This move is a major escalation in the U.S.-China trade war, potentially crippling Huawei's smartphone sales and delaying China's 5G network build. Analysts warn of potential retaliation from China against American tech companies operating within the country.

title: We learn more about Huawei's Google ban from memes than recent news reports
summary: Google is withdrawing the licensing of the Android Operating System to Huawei's devices, prompting panic amongst Huawei users despite a temporary reprieve. Huawei states it is prepared with stockpiled components, while the internet has reacted with an array of memes humorously theorizing about the implications of the ban. These memes reflect the market situation, the company's difficult period, and the timeline of events leading up to the blacklisting.

title: How to test 5G: From millimeter-wave to massive MIMO to beamforming
summary: This article explains the essential technologies behind 5G networks, including millimeter-wave, massive MIMO, and beamforming. It details the challenges and testing methodologies for each technology, such as using handheld analyzers for mmWave path loss and over-the-air measurements for phased array antennas. The piece emphasizes the importance of robust testing equipment and adaptation to evolving 5G standards.

title: Three Factors Reshaping RF Transceivers in the 5G Era
summary: RF transceivers are undergoing a significant transformation in the 5G era, driven by the need for wider bandwidths, higher integration, and miniaturization. Key semiconductor players like Analog Devices Inc., MaxLinear, and Texas Instruments are developing single-chip solutions that combine multiple functionalities and reduce size and power consumption. These advancements are crucial for supporting the demanding requirements of 5G infrastructure, including massive MIMO and beamforming.

title: CrowdStrike IPO: 5 things to know about the cybersecurity unicorn
Broadcom results to provide clear insight into trade war impact
summary: Broadcom's upcoming earnings report is expected to offer crucial insights into the impact of the U.S.-China trade war on the semiconductor industry, especially given its significant ties to China and key customers like Huawei and Apple. Analysts are closely watching for commentary on second-half revenue recovery, cloud capital expenditures, and smartphone unit trends, as expectations for the company's performance have recently been lowered. Despite the trade tensions, some analysts view Broadcom's stock as attractive due to its strong long-term growth and profitability prospects.

title: Opinion: Broadcom slaps down hopes for a second-half rebound in chips
summary: Broadcom Inc. has dampened expectations for a semiconductor market recovery in the latter half of the year, attributing this to U.S. sanctions on Huawei Technologies Co. and general trade-related jitters among customers. The company revised its full-year guidance, projecting a 10% drop in revenue for its semiconductor-solutions business. This outlook suggests a challenging environment for the chip industry due to geopolitical tensions.

title: Hewlett-Packard and Fort Collins grew up together, but they've also grown apart
summary: This article details the evolving relationship between Hewlett-Packard (HP) and Fort Collins, Colorado, over four decades. While HP was once the city's largest employer and a significant community partner, its presence has diminished since the 2015 split into HP Inc. and Hewlett Packard Enterprise, leading to a reduced workforce and a less visible community role. Despite these changes, both companies continue to contribute to the city through philanthropy and job creation, and their legacy has fostered an entrepreneurial spirit in Fort Collins.

title: Broadcom's Symantec Play Goes Too Far
summary: This article discusses Broadcom's strategy of acquiring older technology companies and pruning them for value, a strategy typically employed by private equity firms. The author, Shira Ovide, suggests that Broadcom's move to apply this blueprint to software companies like Symantec risks damaging its reputation. The piece questions whether extending this approach beyond hardware into the software sector might prove to be an overreach for the company.

title: Symantec shares jump on Broadcom buyout rumors
summary: Shares of Mountain View-based Symantec rose significantly due to rumors of a potential buyout by Broadcom. The company has faced challenges including increased competition, waning interest in consumer products, and executive leadership changes, with three CEOs since 2016. This comes as Broadcom is reportedly shifting its merger and acquisition strategy away from strictly chip companies.

title: IBM mainframes face competitive pressures inside and out
summary: IBM's mainframe business is facing increasing competitive pressure from cloud-based solutions and even its own Power servers, despite strong legacy customer loyalty. While IBM continues to invest in mainframe modernization, analysts debate its long-term strategic emphasis given the company's focus on cloud, analytics, and other distributed platforms. The article highlights migrations of mainframe workloads to the cloud by companies like Swisscom and Sabre Corp, and discusses the challenges of cost, agility, and skills shortages affecting mainframe adoption, alongside IBM's efforts to innovate and maintain market relevance.

title: Intel (INTC) Q2 2019 earnings preview
summary: Intel is expected to report a decline in Q2 2019 earnings and revenue, with analysts forecasting a 13% drop in EPS and a 7.5% drop in revenue. Investors will be keenly watching the company's guidance for the third quarter and the second half of 2019 after a weaker-than-expected 2019 outlook previously hit the stock. Recent reports indicate an easing of Intel CPU shortages, which alongside new product plans for AI, 5G, and autonomous driving, and long-term revenue targets, will also be of interest.

title: Skype for Business Online 3PIP IP Phones will work with Microsoft Teams until July 31st 2023
summary: Microsoft announced that 3rd Party IP (3PIP) phones certified for Skype for Business Online will continue to function with Microsoft Teams, albeit with limited functionality, until July 31, 2023. An update released on August 3, 2020, extended this support beyond 2023. This article clarifies the implications for users migrating from Skype for Business Online or Server who use these devices, noting that this applies to 3PIP phones and not newer Microsoft Teams IP Phones.

title: C-suite shuffle: Synaptics taps former Finisar, Broadcom exec as its new CEO, while former chief exec heads to AMD
summary: Synaptics, a San Jose-based company, has appointed the former CEO of Finisar as its new chief executive. Concurrently, Synaptics' previous CEO, Rick Bergman, is transitioning to Sunnyvale-based AMD to lead its largest business segment. This move highlights a significant leadership change for both technology companies.

title: Broadcom to buy Symantec enterprise security business for $10.7 billion
summary: Broadcom has officially announced its acquisition of Symantec's enterprise security business for $10.7 billion. This announcement came shortly after Symantec reported better-than-expected earnings for its fiscal first quarter. Both Symantec and Broadcom saw their stock prices rise following the news.

title: Week In Review: Manufacturing, Test
summary: This article provides an overview of developments in the manufacturing and test sectors, highlighting new tools for 3D NAND production, financial results from KLA, and key partnerships and acquisitions in the silicon carbide and semiconductor industries. It also touches on market research for IC products and the competitive landscape between Intel and Samsung.

title: Broadcom to Buy Symantec Enterprise Division
summary: Broadcom has agreed to acquire Symantec's enterprise division for $10.7 billion in cash, marking its second major software acquisition after CA Technologies. This deal will refocus Symantec on its consumer products and aims to generate $2 billion in sustainable revenue for Broadcom, along with $1.3 billion in EBITDA. Symantec plans to return $8.2 billion after taxes to shareholders via a special dividend of $12 a share.

title: The Gartner 2019 Magic Quadrant for Unified Endpoint Management Tools
summary: This article discusses Gartner's 2019 Magic Quadrant for Unified Endpoint Management Tools, defining UEM and highlighting key capabilities and trends. It analyzes the positioning of various vendors, noting shifts in Challengers, Niche Players, Visionaries, and particularly the rise of Citrix to the Leaders quadrant, alongside MobileIron, BlackBerry, IBM, Microsoft, and VMware. The report emphasizes the increasing importance of CMT integration and the evolving UEM market.

title: Apple’s US job footprint grows to 2.4 million
summary: Apple's US job footprint has expanded to 2.4 million, an increase of four times the number of American jobs attributable to the company eight years prior. The company is on track to directly contribute $350 billion to the US economy by 2023, while also supporting numerous American suppliers and fostering growth in the app economy. This growth includes significant expansion plans, such as creating 20,000 new jobs across the US by 2023 and opening new facilities in San Diego and Seattle.

title: VMware buys Carbon Black and Pivotal, valued together at $4.8 billion
summary: VMware announced the acquisition of cybersecurity firm Carbon Black for $2.1 billion and software company Pivotal for $2.7 billion, totaling $4.8 billion. Both Carbon Black and Pivotal are subsidiaries of Dell, like VMware. These acquisitions aim to bolster VMware's capabilities in security and hybrid-cloud infrastructure, with expectations to contribute over $1 billion in incremental revenue within two years.

title: Cover Story: Electrical + electronics moving up the value chain
summary: This article discusses Malaysia's electrical and electronics (E&E) sector, highlighting its historical development and the current challenge of moving up the value chain from manufacturing to design and development. It explores the reasons behind this struggle, including a shortage of entrepreneurial engineers and issues with the local ecosystem, and proposes solutions such as government support for local design firms and incentives for high-skill workers. The importance of intellectual property ownership and the risks of remaining in low-margin manufacturing are also emphasized.

title: What’s Changed: the 2019 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Access Management
summary: Gartner's 2019 Magic Quadrant for Access Management highlights the increasing importance of SaaS delivery, UEBA, and MFA in access management solutions. The report evaluates 14 providers, noting significant movements among visionaries and leaders while identifying key trends and capabilities expected to shape the AM market in the coming years.

title: Broadcom is Title Sponsor of the IRIS National Fair
summary: Broadcom Inc. announced its title sponsorship with IRIS (Initiative for Research and Innovation in STEM) to bolster STEM education in India, aiming to impact 4.5 million students. This partnership supports young Indian innovators, provides a platform for them to showcase projects, and underwrites Team India's participation in the ISEF 2020. The collaboration highlights Broadcom's commitment to corporate social responsibility by fostering the next generation of scientists and engineers.

title: Industrial Sector Moves Higher While Stocks Rally Back From Lows
summary: The industrial sector is showing signs of strength despite a broader market downturn led by tech stocks and Netflix. While the Industrial Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLI) has underperformed the S&P 500, the Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight Industrials ETF (RGI) has outperformed significantly, largely due to Boeing's impact on XLI and better performance from domestically focused industrials and transport stocks. The semiconductor sector, hitting new highs, is also noted as a key leading indicator for market direction.

title: What's driving the Automotive Electronics Market trends? 2024
summary: The automotive electronics market is projected to exceed USD 400 billion by 2024, driven by increasing demand for advanced safety, comfort features, and the development of intelligent vehicle technologies. Stringent regulations, rising electric vehicle sales, and growth in ADAS systems are key factors fueling this expansion. Major players like Lear Corporation, Panasonic, and Continental are investing in R&D to develop advanced electronic systems.

title: Symantec is now NortonLifeLock as Broadcom closes purchase of its enterprise business
summary: Symantec Corp. has officially changed its name to NortonLifeLock Inc. following the completion of Broadcom Inc.'s $10.7 billion acquisition of its enterprise security business. Symantec’s stock symbol shifted from SYMC to NLOK, and shares in the newly named company rose, with analysts issuing a "buy" rating. This acquisition further consolidates Broadcom's move into the software sector, adding significant cybersecurity services and a new revenue stream.

title: Goodbye, Symantec: Consumer business gets rebrand
summary: Broadcom Inc.'s $10.7 billion acquisition of Symantec Corp.'s enterprise security business has closed, granting Broadcom the rights to the Symantec name. As a result, the remaining part of Mountain View-based Symantec, specifically its consumer business, has undergone a rebranding. This change means the Symantec brand will now be associated with Broadcom's enterprise security offerings while the consumer segment operates under a new identity.

title: NortonLifeLock, formerly Symantec, names Vincent Pilette its new CEO
summary: NortonLifeLock, the consumer cybersecurity division formerly known as Symantec, has appointed Vincent Pilette as its new CEO following Broadcom's acquisition of Symantec's enterprise business. Pilette announced plans to eliminate $1.3 billion in costs and expand growth initiatives, including the Norton 360 security suite and international expansion, after the company reported strong financial results that beat Wall Street forecasts. This move focuses on repositioning NortonLifeLock as a pure-play consumer cyber safety company.

title: OMAP processors settlement clears way for German car manufacturers
summary: A global patent dispute over OMAP processors between Innovative Foundry Technologies, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), and United Microelectronics Corporation (UMC) has concluded with a settlement. This resolution offers relief to car manufacturers like VW and Ford, who use infotainment modules containing these chips. The lawsuits primarily targeted chip manufacturers TSMC and UMC, with Texas Instruments also playing a significant role in facilitating the settlement, particularly regarding UMC's processors used in automotive infotainment systems.

title: Kulicke & Soffa Appoints Jeff Richardson to Its Board of Directors
summary: Kulicke & Soffa Industries, Inc. announced the appointment of David Jeffrey Richardson to its Board of Directors. Mr. Richardson brings over 32 years of semiconductor industry experience, previously serving as Chairman of Lattice Semiconductor Corporation and a Director of Ambarella, as well as holding key roles at LSI Corporation and Intel Corporation. The company believes his extensive management and technical background will be invaluable as K&S diversifies and grows.

title: 3 networking startups rearchitect routing
summary: Three networking startups, Arrcus, DriveNets, and Volta Networks, are redefining routing by decoupling software from hardware, enabling it to run on commodity products. This disaggregation reduces operational expenses and adds flexibility, mirroring a trend previously seen in network switching. Industry analysts anticipate these companies could become M&A targets as service providers increasingly look towards white box routing for 5G deployments.

title: Report: McAfee mulls possible merger with NortonLifeLock
summary: McAfee LLC is reportedly considering a merger or "combination" with NortonLifeLock Inc., which would unite the two cybersecurity competitors. This potential deal comes after NortonLifeLock spun off from Symantec Corp. and is seeking to eliminate costs, while McAfee itself is also exploring an outright sale. A merger would make sense in a consolidating consumer cybersecurity market driven by mobile app usage and increased trust in platform security from tech giants.

title: Israeli Court Rejects Regulator Bid for Additional Taxation of Broadcom's Dune Networks Acquisition
summary: Israel's central district court rejected a demand by the Israeli Tax Authority for Broadcom Inc. to pay an additional $29 million in tax related to its 2009 acquisition of Dune Networks. The authority claimed Broadcom emptied Dune of its assets, which the court disagreed with. Broadcom is reportedly facing a similar situation regarding another acquisition.

title: Broadcom outlook for 2020 gives hope for chip-earnings rebound, stock gains
summary: Broadcom Inc. shares rose after its fiscal fourth-quarter earnings report, which included a 2020 revenue outlook that surpassed Wall Street estimates. The chip maker anticipates fiscal 2020 revenue between $24.5 billion and $25.5 billion, exceeding analysts' forecasts of $23.9 billion. This positive outlook suggests a potential rebound in chip-related earnings, providing a boost to the stock.

title: Here are the best-performing stocks of the decade
summary: This article highlights the top-performing stocks of the decade, with Netflix leading the pack with a 3,726.2% return. Other significant performers include semiconductor companies Broadcom and Nvidia, electronic bond trading platform MarketAxess, and Domino's Pizza, which experienced a remarkable turnaround. The article also touches on other companies like Neurocrine Biosciences, Exact Sciences, Cheniere Energy, and DexCom, emphasizing themes of disruption, technological innovation, and strategic business changes that fueled these impressive gains over the last ten years.

title: Cisco to acquire Exablaze for high-performance switching
summary: Cisco plans to acquire Australia-based Exablaze, a manufacturer of high-performance switches and network interface cards used in high-frequency trading and computing. This acquisition mirrors rival Arista's purchase of Metamako and aims to leverage Exablaze's FPGA technology for future AI and machine learning applications. Cisco expects to complete the acquisition by April 2020 and sees it as a move into ultralow-latency switching, complementing its recent Silicon One ASIC announcement.

title: Broadcom quietly acquired a small cyber analytics software company
summary: Broadcom has reportedly acquired cyber analytics software company Bay Dynamics, a move that expands its security business. The acquisition, revealed through regulatory documents, occurred earlier this month. This step aligns with Broadcom's ongoing strategy to build out its security offerings.

title: Accenture to Acquire Symantec’s Cyber Security Services Business from Broadcom
summary: Accenture announced its agreement to acquire Symantec’s Cyber Security Services business from Broadcom, Inc. This acquisition will position Accenture Security as a leading provider of managed security services, enhancing its ability to detect and respond to cyber threats globally. The deal includes Symantec’s global threat monitoring, real-time threat intelligence, and incident response services, supported by over 300 employees and six security operations centers worldwide.

title: 10 things I learned from the 2019 Inari AGM
summary: This article details 10 key takeaways from Inari Amertron Berhad's 2019 Annual General Meeting, covering financial performance, expansion plans, strategic partnerships, and future outlook. It highlights the company's revenue and profit decline in FY2019, the completion of its new P34 plant, and management's strategies for growth amidst industry changes like 5G and fluctuating demand for smartphones. summary: A federal jury has ordered Apple Inc. and Broadcom Inc. to pay $1.1 billion to the California Institute of Technology for infringing on Wi-Fi data transmission patents. The lawsuit focused on Broadcom's computer chips, which were used in various Apple devices including iPhones and iPads, with both companies' headquarters located in California. summary: Self-driving car company Waymo has raised US$2.25 billion in its first external funding round to fuel its global expansion. The capital came from a diverse group of investors including Silver Lake, Canada Pension Plan Investment Board, and Mubadala Investment, alongside its parent company Alphabet Inc. This funding will support the deployment of the Waymo Driver worldwide, as the company competes in the rapidly evolving autonomous driving market.

summary: Broadcom Inc. has withdrawn its revenue forecast for 2020 due to demand and supply disruptions caused by the coronavirus outbreak, joining other chipmakers in revising their outlooks. Despite a slowdown in demand, the company stated its supply chain was not meaningfully impacted. Broadcom expects second-quarter revenue of approximately $5.7 billion, lower than analysts' average estimates.

summary: Broadcom Corporation has filed a patent infringement lawsuit against Netflix, Inc. in the Central District of California, alleging that Netflix's streaming service infringes on nine of Broadcom's U.S. patents. The patents cover technologies crucial for reliable content delivery, efficient server use, and video encoding. Broadcom claims Netflix's infringement has harmed its set-top box business by drawing consumers away from cable television.

title: Intel To Sell Home Gateway Assets For $150 Million
summary: Intel is selling the majority of its Home Gateway Platform Division assets, including SoC products for home gateways, Wi-Fi access points, and Ethernet, to MaxLinear for $150 million in cash. summary: Accenture (NYSE: ACN) has completed its acquisition of the Symantec Cyber Security Services business from Broadcom Inc. (NASDAQ: AVGO). summary: HCL Technologies has expanded its partnership with Broadcom Inc. to include Symantec Enterprise Division (SED) consulting services. summary: Extreme Networks revamped its supply chain processes through automation and centralization to manage rapid growth from acquisitions and mitigate external disruptions like tariffs and COVID-19. By implementing a vendor-managed inventory (VMI) system and consolidating warehouses, the company significantly reduced product constraints and distribution center costs while improving customer request date performance. This strategic overhaul allowed Extreme Networks to absorb increased transaction volumes and maintain stable inventory levels despite substantial revenue growth.

summary: Symantec identified a wave of WastedLocker ransomware attacks targeting U.S. organizations, including eight Fortune 500 companies. The attacks utilized the SocGholish framework, masquerading as software updates, and the Cobalt Strike commodity malware to gain network access and deploy the ransomware. Symantec's proactive detection and outreach helped disrupt these attacks, which could have led to significant financial damages and operational disruptions.

summary: Rocket Lab's 13th Electron rocket launch, named "Pics Or It Didn't Happen," failed the past weekend (July 5th) due to an anomaly causing the second stage to explode, destroying its satellite payload. The mission carried payloads for Canon Electronics, Planet, and In-Space Missions. Rocket Lab is investigating the cause with the FAA and plans a rapid return to flight after corrective actions are identified.

title: NortonLifeLock hires former eBay exec as new CFO
summary: NortonLifeLock has appointed Natalie Derse, a former eBay executive with over 20 years of experience, as its new Chief Financial Officer. summary: Analog Devices is set to acquire San Jose-based Maxim Integrated in a $21 billion chip deal. Analog Devices, based in Massachusetts with operations in Santa Clara, is paying a 22% premium for Maxim Integrated. The acquisition expands Analog Devices' presence in the semiconductor industry.

title: ADI to Acquire Maxim Integrated for $21 Billion in Major Semiconductor Deal
summary: Analog Devices (ADI) announced its intention to acquire Maxim Integrated for $21 billion, continuing ADI's trend of major acquisitions to expand its influence in the semiconductor industry. This deal will bolster ADI's position in signal processing and power management, especially leveraging Maxim's expertise in wearables and medical applications. The acquisition awaits regulatory approval, a process that has historically presented challenges for large-scale mergers.

summary: Innovium Inc., a semiconductor startup specializing in chips for data center switches, has secured a significant $170 million funding round, bringing its total capital raised to $350 million. The company aims to challenge Broadcom Inc.'s dominance in the switching chip market with its Teralynx line of application-specific integrated circuits, boasting rapidly increasing revenue and market share.

title: Ikhwezi Bus Service deploys Africa’s first AI-driven wireless network
summary: Ikhwezi Bus Service has implemented Africa's first AI-driven wireless network, developed by NEC XON and based on Mist Systems (a Juniper Networks company). This network enables the efficient transfer of large CCTV video footage from its bus fleet, improving operational monitoring, safety, and turnaround times, while reducing costs and IT overhead. The system uses AI and WiFi 6 technologies to ensure reliable and fast data transfer, enhancing the bus service's overall efficiency.

title: Koss Sues Apple, Bose, Over Wireless Headphone Patents (2)
summary: Koss Corp. has filed a series of lawsuits in Texas federal court, alleging that Apple Inc., Bose Corp., Plantronics Inc., Skullcandy Inc., and JLab Audio infringe on its wireless headphone patents. The patents cover technology that Koss claims it pioneered, including internal microphones, touch controls, and Wi-Fi connectivity in headphones. These lawsuits assert that the widespread adoption of such features in modern wireless headphones infringes on Koss's early innovations.

title: NortonLifeLock Sells Culver City Offices to Northwood
summary: NortonLifeLock, formerly known as Symantec, has sold its 288,000-square-foot office building in Culver City to Northwood Investors for $120 million. Despite the sale, NortonLifeLock will continue to use the building as its headquarters, having signed a seven-year lease for two floors of the five-story property. The company had developed the property in 2007 as its Southern California headquarters and changed its name in November 2019 after Broadcom Inc. acquired part of Symantec's software business.

title: PRP Acquires Broadcom HQ in Irvine for $355M
summary: PRP, a Washington, DC-based firm, has acquired Broadcom, Inc.'s Southern California headquarters in Irvine for $355 million. This acquisition represents the largest sale in Orange County since 2017. The 660,893-square-foot office complex is 100% leased to Broadcom with 17 years remaining on the lease term.

title: The geopolitical implications of the microchip race
summary: The semiconductor industry has become a critical geopolitical battleground between the United States and China. Both nations recognize that winning the microchip race will confer a significant advantage in the ongoing great power competition. While China's domestic microchip production lags behind Western technology, the country could potentially close the gap by leveraging political power and securing foreign expertise, though U.S. efforts are aimed at thwarting these advancements.

title: Tesla To Equip Vehicles With 7nm HPC Processor In 2022 Built With Broadcom & TSMC
summary: Tesla has partnered with Broadcom and TSMC to develop a 7nm HPC processor, dubbed HW 4.0, for its Full Self-Driving (FSD) computer. This chip will enter production in Q4 2020 and will be available in Tesla vehicles by 2022. The HW 4.0 will utilize TSMC's advanced InFo packaging and System on Wafer (SoW) technology, bypassing the need for a substrate and PCB, directly integrating with the heat dissipation module.

The platforms feature self-learning, self-optimizing, and self-healing capabilities to simplify management and maximize performance in data centers.

In contrast, US chipmakers experienced a downturn, with Nvidia, Broadcom, and Qualcomm shares falling.

title: Broadcom Emulex SAN Manager In-Band Management Application
summary: Broadcom Inc. announced the Emulex SAN Manager, designed to reduce operational costs and complexity for enterprises by providing centralized monitoring, management, and automated performance optimization for storage area networks (SANs). This application allows server and storage administrators to troubleshoot network issues, manage Host Bus Adapters (HBAs) as resource pools, and integrate HBA management into datacenter analytics. It also features adaptive congestion mitigation and in-band HBA management to improve availability and IT efficiency while simplifying SAN management.

title: In a Historic $40 Billion Deal, NVIDIA Acquires Arm Amid Potential Backlash from Chip Industry
summary: NVIDIA has acquired Arm Holdings for $40 billion in a cash and stock deal, aiming to merge Arm's computing ecosystem with NVIDIA's AI leadership. The acquisition, however, faces potential backlash due to concerns about impartiality and neutrality, given NVIDIA's direct competition in the chip industry and Arm's role in licensing architectures to NVIDIA's rivals. Despite assurances from NVIDIA about maintaining Arm's open-licensing model and expanding R&D in the UK, the deal is subject to regulatory approvals and has already sparked political controversy.

title: Nvidia Confident U.S.-China Tech War Won’t Stop It From Buying Arm
summary: Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang expressed confidence in obtaining regulatory approvals for its $40 billion acquisition of Arm Ltd., despite escalating U.S.-China tech tensions. The deal faces skepticism from Chinese experts and opposition from Arm co-founder Hermann Hauser, who warns of potential job losses and compromised business neutrality. Despite these challenges, Nvidia remains optimistic, citing past regulatory successes.

summary: STMicroelectronics has revealed features of its Stellar automotive microcontrollers, co-developed with Bosch, designed to ensure reliable and deterministic execution of multiple independent real-time applications in next-generation automotive architectures. These MCUs offer virtualization capabilities, hardware support for virtualization, quality of service settings, and resource separation to allow independent applications to coexist securely while meeting stringent safety standards. A key feature is the non-volatile Phase-Change Memory (PCM), enabling fast read access and zero-downtime over-the-air updates, even for full memory refreshes.

title: NEC, ADI to provide 5G O-RAN Massive MIMO Radio for Rakuten Mobile
summary: NEC Corporation and Analog Devices (ADI) have partnered to design and provide a 5G Network Massive MIMO Antenna Radio Unit for Rakuten Mobile. The unit uses ADI’s fourth-generation wideband RF transceiver and supports Rakuten Mobile’s virtualized cloud-native network, enabling high-capacity transmission with Massive MIMO and digital beamforming. Rakuten Mobile has already begun receiving these units and plans to expand its 5G service across Japan by March 2021, with a standalone 5G network launching in Q2 2021.

title: STMicroelectronics Introduces World’s First All-in-One, Multi-Zone, Direct Time-of-Flight Module - ST News
summary: STMicroelectronics has launched the VL53L5, the world's first 64-zone direct Time-of-Flight (ToF) sensor, enhancing spatial understanding for imaging systems. This all-in-one module features a 940nm VCSEL light source, a System-on-Chip sensor with SPADs, and a low-power MCU, offering 4m ranging performance and improved laser autofocus, touch-to-focus, presence detection, and gesture interfaces. Already in mass production, the VL53L5 is shipping to leading wireless and computer manufacturers, with Android and Windows device drivers widely available.

title: Marvell to Acquire Inphi - Accelerating Growth and Leadership in Cloud and 5G Infrastructure
summary: Marvell Technology Group Ltd. announced its definitive agreement to acquire Inphi Corporation in a cash and stock transaction, valued at approximately $40 billion, to enhance its leadership in cloud and 5G infrastructure. The STWLC88 offers a comprehensive turnkey solution when paired with the STWBC2 digital controller, ensuring high power delivery safely while remaining Qi compliant.

summary: Eversource Energy is seeking approval to invest $600 million in "smart" meters, prompting Connecticut regulators to investigate whether similar meters contributed to a high rate of service disconnections by United Illuminating (UI) last year. UI, an Avangrid subsidiary, reported a 20.7 percent termination rate in 2019, significantly higher than Eversource's rate and Avangrid's New York subsidiary. Regulators are questioning if UI staff were too quick to disconnect customers for nonpayment and if the remote control capabilities of smart meters played a role.

This prestigious honor highlights his significant global impact and contributions to the field.

summary: Synaptics' Q1 earnings report shows a significant shift towards IoT, with IoT revenue projected to surpass mobile and PC business for the first time. title: Marvell inks $1.1B deal to acquire network chip startup Innovium
summary: Marvell Technologies Inc. announced a $1.1 billion deal to acquire Innovium Inc., a startup specializing in network processors for cloud data centers. The acquisition will be financed entirely with Marvell shares and is expected to add $150 million to annual revenues by fiscal year 2023. Innovium's chips, known for their efficiency and integration, have rapidly gained market share, securing a contract with a Tier 1 cloud customer that will significantly boost its 2022 revenue.

title: Marvell Tech to acquire Innovium for $1.1 Billion
summary: Marvell Technology is set to acquire networking chip startup Innovium for $1.1 billion to enhance its market share in networking chips for large cloud-computing companies and data centers. The acquisition aims to bolster Marvell's portfolio, particularly with Innovium's Teralynx chips, which compete with Broadcom in the market for data center traffic controllers. This move follows Marvell's previous $10 billion acquisition of Inphi Corp, indicating a strategic effort to expand its cloud business offerings amid significant consolidation in the semiconductor industry.

title: Ecopetrol adquirió las acciones del Ministerio de Hacienda en ISA por $14,2 billones
summary: Ecopetrol announced the acquisition of the Ministry of Finance's 51.4% stake in Interconexión Eléctrica S.A. ESP (ISA) for $14.2 trillion. The transaction, priced at $25,000 per share, solidifies Ecopetrol's position as the majority owner of ISA and is considered a significant step for Colombia's energy sector and transition. Both companies will remain state-owned, with the deal aiming to strengthen strategic goals and attract investment.

title: Open code software giant Elastic to buy Israeli startup, open Tel Aviv R&D site
summary: Elastic NV announced its acquisition of Israeli cybersecurity startup Build.security and the establishment of an R&D site in Tel Aviv. Build.security, founded in January 2020, specializes in authorization policy management for cloud-native environments. This acquisition further expands Elastic's presence in the cybersecurity sector and its operations in Israel.

title: T-shirt fundraiser with Tractor Supply and Carhartt supports skilled trades jobs
summary: Tractor Supply Company and Carhartt have partnered to launch a "Support the Trades" T-shirt fundraiser to help address the skilled trades gap in the U.S. Proceeds from the exclusive T-shirt sales at Tractor Supply will benefit SkillsUSA, a nonprofit dedicated to preparing students for careers in trade, technical, and skilled service occupations. Both companies have committed a maximum donation of $50,000 each, totaling $100,000, to support SkillsUSA's mission to expand its reach and training capabilities.

title: Maxim Integrated Products acquired by Analog Devices to bolster semiconductor production
summary: Analog Devices, Inc. has completed its acquisition of Maxim Integrated Products, Inc. Maxim stockholders received 0.63 of a share of ADI common stock for each share of Maxim common stock, and Maxim common stock will no longer be traded on NASDAQ. Tunç Doluca and Mercedes Johnson, former Maxim board members, have joined the ADI Board of Directors.

title: Vertical Cavity Surface Emitting Laser (VCSEL) Market
summary: Market Insights Reports has published a research report on the Vertical Cavity Surface Emitting Laser (VCSEL) market, highlighting its expected growth over the forecast period (2020-2025) with a CAGR over 18%. The report utilizes primary and secondary research methods, including SWOT and Porter's Five Forces Analysis, and provides an in-depth study of geographic regions, revenue forecasts, segmentation, and market share. A key trend identified is the significant share held by Gallium Arsenide (GaAs) in VCSEL applications, driven by its adoption in 3D sensing in consumer electronics like the iPhone and continuous integration in data communications and gesture recognition.

title: Semiconductor ETF
summary: The VanEck Semiconductor UCITS ETF provides targeted exposure to the semiconductor sector, crucial for the ongoing "fourth industrial revolution" encompassing AI, 5G, and IoT. This ETF, the first of its kind in Europe, invests in pure-play semiconductor companies globally, focusing on those generating at least half their revenue from semiconductors. It highlights the high barriers to entry in the semiconductor industry, which protect profit margins for leading manufacturers.

title: Broadcom forecasts upbeat current-quarter sales on 5G bet
summary: Broadcom Inc. forecasted fourth-quarter revenue above Wall Street expectations, driven by strong demand for semiconductors due to 5G adoption and hybrid work models. The company's wireless division, including Apple as a major customer, is also expected to benefit from new iPhone launches. Broadcom's diversification into software business has helped mitigate supply chain disruptions.

title: Intel CEO Predicts Chips Will Be More Than 20% of Premium Vehicle BOM by 2030
summary: Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger predicts that semiconductors will constitute over 20% of the total premium vehicle bill of materials by 2030, a significant increase from 4% in 2019, driven by "the digitization of everything." To meet this escalating demand, Intel plans to expand chip production in Europe and establish dedicated foundry capacity in Ireland. Additionally, the company's subsidiary Mobileye showcased its production autonomous vehicle and announced plans for a robotaxi service in Germany in 2022.

title: Focal Point Names Scott Pomerantz, formerly of Global Locate and Broadcom, as CEO
summary: Focal Point Positioning, a UK-based deep tech startup, has appointed Scott Pomerantz as its new CEO. Pomerantz, who founded Global Locate and later sold it to Broadcom, brings 30 years of experience in positioning and semiconductors. Focal Point's Supercorrelation technology aims to improve GPS chip performance in various devices, and Pomerantz will lead the company's efforts to scale up technical support, customer integration, and commercialization.

title: Time-of-Flight 8x8 Multi-Zone Ranging Sensor from STMicroelectronics Enables Innovative Applications
summary: STMicroelectronics has launched the VL53L5CX, its first multi-zone FlightSense™ time-of-flight sensor for general-purpose applications. This sensor offers up to 64 sensing zones, multi-target detection up to four meters per zone, and a broad 63° diagonal field of view, making it suitable for gesture recognition, 3D room mapping in robotics, and various level monitoring applications. The VL53L5CX supports innovative features like motion indication and selectable sensing array resolutions, including an 8x8 zone mode for AR/VR, and is available for immediate order.

title: Roundup: More 6 GHz Wi-Fi in the US, Liberty Global upgrades with Plume, more 6 GHz Wi-Fi in Europe, & latest from Plume IQ
summary: This roundup covers significant advancements in Wi-Fi technology and adoption. The FCC is moving closer to authorizing standard power 6 GHz Wi-Fi in the US, with conditional approvals for AFC systems expected to start after November 30. Liberty Global is upgrading millions of European homes with Plume's intelligent Wi-Fi services, and more European countries are greenlighting 6 GHz Wi-Fi operation. Additionally, Plume IQ reports a growing preference for Smart TVs over streaming STBs and the rising trend of 4K video consumption.

title: Caixin Explains: What’s at Stake in the Massive Unigroup Restructuring
summary: Tsinghua Unigroup Co. Ltd., a Chinese semiconductor giant, is undergoing a massive bankruptcy restructuring to address its significant debts and revive its promising businesses. Several companies, including Alibaba Group and various government-backed enterprises, have expressed interest in bidding for Unigroup's assets, which include its critical chipmaking and cloud computing units. The restructuring aims to find strategic investors with the financial capacity to take over and further invest in key projects like Yangtze Memory Technologies, crucial for China's semiconductor independence.

title: Shares of this obscure chip component supplier have surged by over 1200% in the past three years
summary: Shares of Nan Ya Printed Circuit Board Corp., an obscure Taiwanese company that supplies essential Ajinomoto build-up film (ABF) substrates for chipmaking, have surged over 1200% in the past three years. This surge is due to ABF substrate becoming a critical bottleneck in the semiconductor industry, with supply expected to remain constrained until at least 2025. Major tech companies are struggling to secure enough of this component, leading to increased profits and investment for substrate manufacturers.

title: 5G Technology Devices for an O-RAN Wireless Solution
summary: This article explores the necessary 5G technology devices for successful and cost-effective O-RAN wireless solutions, particularly focusing on the challenges and technological advancements in massive MIMO and small cell deployments. It details Analog Devices' integrated transceiver family, the RadioVerse, and its components like the ADRV9029, ADRF5545A, and DPD functionality, showcasing their role in enabling high-performance, low-cost O-RAN platforms. The author discusses receiver and transmitter signal chain designs, power management, clocking architectures, and the flexibility of these solutions for various 5G applications.

title: The Chip Crunch Grows Worse as Wait Times Hit Record 21 Weeks
summary: The global chip shortage worsened in August, with lead times for semiconductor orders reaching a record 21 weeks. This delay has significantly impacted industries like automotive and electronics, hindering production and growth. While some chip types saw a slight improvement, overall wait times continue to increase.

title: Symantec Endpoint Security: Protection, Prevention and Innovation
summary: This article highlights Symantec Endpoint Security Complete (SESC) as a leading endpoint protection solution, emphasizing its strong performance in independent evaluations like MITRE ATT&CK and Gartner. It discusses Symantec's continuous innovation through advanced machine learning and its economic value, evidenced by a Forrester study showing a 437% ROI. The piece aims to reassure customers about the product's future following Broadcom's acquisition and to counter competitors' FUD.

title: Broadcom launches its lowest power GNSS receiver for mobile, wearables
summary: Broadcom has launched its BCM4778, the lowest power L1/L5 GNSS receiver chip designed for mobile and wearable applications. This third-generation chip is 35% smaller and consumes five times less power than its predecessor, significantly extending battery life. It features advanced multipath mitigation with new Grid Tracking technology, enabling enhanced accuracy and performance for urban navigation.

title: Cover Story: The rise of test equipment giants amid tech boom
summary: The Malaysian semiconductor industry, historically dominated by OSAT companies, is seeing a significant rise in automated test equipment (ATE) manufacturers due to the Fourth Industrial Revolution and AI. These ATE makers, such as ViTrox, Greatech, and Pentamaster, have outperformed OSAT companies in share price and are now comparable in market capitalization, attracting a premium from investors. The article explores the opportunities and challenges for ATE manufacturers, including views on MNC presence, diversification strategies, and the potential for Malaysia to become a regional hub for advanced technology equipment.

title: New Report Highlights Strength of U.S. Semiconductor Industry and Continued Challenges
summary: A new report from the Semiconductor Industry Association (SIA) details the strong global market share and R&D investment of the U.S. semiconductor industry, while also highlighting significant challenges like the ongoing global chip shortage and decreasing domestic manufacturing capacity. The report urges Congress and the White House to fund the CHIPS for America Act and consider an investment tax credit (FABS Act) to enhance U.S. semiconductor production and innovation. These measures are deemed crucial for maintaining America's economic competitiveness, national security, and technological leadership.

title: Digital Turbine Stock, Builders FirstSource, Cricut Among 19 New IBD Watchlist Stocks
summary: Investor's Business Daily (IBD) has added Digital Turbine, Builders FirstSource, and Cricut to its updated watchlist, which includes 19 new stocks. IBD regularly updates its stock screens, such as the IBD 50 and IBD Sector Leaders, to help investors identify promising stocks, and the article provides a detailed list of these additions and removals.

title: VMware Helps Customers Move to the Cloud With Flexibility and Speed
summary: VMware has announced new advancements for its VMware Cloud platform, designed to help customers modernize applications, increase business agility, and reduce costs. These innovations include a new portfolio of managed Kubernetes services, capabilities to enhance security and simplify running enterprise applications, and an initiative supporting sovereign clouds. The company also showcased future tech previews like Project Arctic and Project Capitola at VMworld 2021.

title: Nvidia offers EU concessions over $54 billion Arm deal
summary: Nvidia has offered concessions to the EU antitrust regulator regarding its $54 billion acquisition of British chip designer Arm. The deal has raised concerns within the semiconductor industry about Arm's neutrality as a technology supplier. The EU will now seek feedback before deciding whether to approve the deal, demand more concessions, or open a formal investigation.

title: PCIe 5.0 controllers now available with zero-latency integrated IDE
summary: Rambus Inc. has released Compute Express Link (CXL) 2.0 and PCI Express (PCIe) 5.0 controllers that feature integrated Integrity and Data Encryption (IDE) modules. These controllers offer zero-latency security, crucial for high-speed data center applications like AI/ML and HPC, by employing AES-GCM symmetric-key cryptographic block ciphers. This development, enhanced by the recent acquisition of PLDA, aims to protect against physical attacks on CXL and PCIe links while ensuring data confidentiality, integrity, and replay protection at full 32 GT/s speed.

title: Emerson to Merge Software Units With AspenTech
summary: Emerson Electric plans to merge two of its software businesses, OSI and Geological Simulation Software, with Aspen Technology in an $11 billion cash-and-stock deal. The new combined entity, valued at $160 a share, will retain AspenTech's name and CEO Antonio Pietri. Emerson will contribute $6 billion in cash and own 55% of the new company.

title: EU to investigate Nvidia's $54 bln ARM bid after remedies fall short - sources
summary: The EU is expected to launch an extended antitrust investigation into Nvidia's $54 billion bid for British chip designer ARM. This comes after remedies offered by Nvidia last week failed to address competition concerns, marking a second setback for the company after a similar warning from Britain's antitrust agency. The European Commission is scheduled to end its preliminary review on October 27, initiating a four-month investigation.

title: Apple likely to slash iPhone 13 production due to chip crunch - Bloomberg News
summary: Apple is expected to reduce its iPhone 13 production by 10 million units this year due to the ongoing global chip shortage. The tech giant's chip suppliers, including Broadcom and Texas Instruments, are struggling to provide necessary components, leading to a 1% drop in Apple's shares after the news. This chip crunch continues to impact various industries, from electronics to automobiles.

title: Apple May Cut iPhone 13 Production Goals Due to Chip Crunch
summary: Apple is reportedly planning to cut its iPhone 13 production targets for 2021 by up to 10 million units due to ongoing chip shortages impacting key suppliers like Broadcom and Texas Instruments. This reduction jeopardizes Apple's expected record-breaking holiday sales quarter, highlighting that even major tech giants are susceptible to global supply chain disruptions exacerbated by the pandemic. The shortages have already led to significant delays in iPhone 13 shipments and are affecting other Apple products as well.

title: Multi-Access Edge Computing: The Future of IoT & Connected Vehicles
summary: The article discusses the growing prevalence of IoT devices and the challenge of processing the vast amount of data they generate, especially in the automotive industry. It highlights how Multi-Access Edge Computing (MEC), originally developed by telecommunications companies, offers a solution by processing data closer to the source, significantly reducing latency and improving reliability. MEC is presented as crucial for the future of connected vehicles, enabling new services, enhancing customer experience, and allowing for new revenue streams for OEMs.

title: Semiconductors Market in Vietnam to grow by USD 1.65 billion| Broadcom Inc. and Hitachi Ltd. among Key Vendors|Technavio
summary: The semiconductors market in Vietnam is projected to grow by USD 1.65 billion, accelerating at a CAGR of 6.52% from 2021 to 2025, driven primarily by the growing use of IoT. Key vendors identified include Broadcom Inc., Hitachi Ltd.,Intel Corp., and Samsung Electronics Co. Ltd., with power management integrated circuits (PMICs) expected to be a significant segment. However, the market growth might be hampered by a lack of skilled labor.

title: Apple likely to cut iPhone 13 production due to chip crunch – Bloomberg News
summary: Apple Inc. is reportedly planning to slash its iPhone 13 production target by as many as 10 million units due to the ongoing global chip shortage, according to Bloomberg News. Chip suppliers like Broadcom Inc. and Texas Instruments are struggling to meet demand, impacting Apple's ability to produce the anticipated 90 million units by year-end. Despite this, some analysts believe Apple is handling the supply crunch better than competitors and maintain healthy sales forecasts for the iPhone 13.

summary: Due to a global chip shortage, Apple expects to produce 10 million fewer iPhone 13 smartphones than planned, impacting deliveries to customers and prompting temporary sales halts in some stores. This shortage, stemming from COVID-19 pandemic-related issues, also affects production of other Apple products like the Apple Watch Series 7 and is causing difficulties across various industries including automotive and electronics. Shares of Apple, Broadcom, Inc., and Texas Instruments, Inc. saw a decline following the news.

title: Smartphone IMU market to grow 5% per year
summary: The mobile inertial measurement unit (IMU) market is projected to reach US$838 million by 2026, growing at an average annual rate of 5% from 2020. This growth is driven by the increasing use of IMUs in smartphones and tablets for user movement analysis, with STMicroelectronics, Invensense, and Bosch leading the market. STMicroelectronics currently holds the largest share, followed by Invensense and Bosch, though Bosch's market share has been increasing.

title: Aruba Fabric Composer unifies and provisions network and security policy configurations
summary: Aruba Fabric Composer, a software-defined orchestration solution, has expanded its capabilities beyond network configuration to also include security policy orchestration with the new Aruba CX 10000 data center switch. This unification, enabled by Pensando Policy and Services Manager technologies, provides a single interface for managing both network and security policies. It allows for operational splits between SecOps and NetOps, supports brownfield environments, and offers a global health dashboard for comprehensive troubleshooting.

title: New RF FPGA solutions transform EW platforms
summary: The article discusses how new RF FPGA solutions from Xilinx, specifically the RFSoC and Versal ACAP families, are transforming Electronic Warfare (EW) platforms. These highly integrated devices combine critical EW functions like data converters and powerful processors into single chips, significantly reducing size, weight, power, and cost (SWaP-C) while improving performance. This technological advancement enables new system architectures, addresses challenges in phased-array antennas, and supports advanced capabilities like AI for more agile and effective EW systems.

title: Aruba Launches Network Switch Armed with Pensando Programmable Chip
summary: Aruba has partnered with silicon startup Pensando to launch the CX 10000 Series network switch, integrating Pensando's Elba DPU to provide various network services as distributed functions. This new switch aims to help enterprises manage east-west traffic more efficiently and cost-effectively, bringing hyperscaler networking capabilities to their own data centers. It promises significant improvements in performance and scalability by offloading tasks typically handled by separate appliances directly into the network fabric.

title: A Look Inside The Apple iPhone 13 Pro
summary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the Apple iPhone 13 Pro, model A2636, revealing its internal components, estimated build costs, and design wins. It highlights the A15 Bionic processor, image sensor specifications, and contributions from various suppliers like Qualcomm, KIOXIA, and STMicroelectronics. The report also compares the iPhone 13 Pro's cost and features to its predecessor, the iPhone 12 Pro, and a competitor, the Samsung Galaxy S21+.

title: Renesas’ Innovative Automotive Chips Drive Next-Generation Multimedia System for Toyota Lexus
summary: Renesas Electronics Corporation's R-Car H3 and R-Car M3 system-on-chips (SoCs) have been adopted by Toyota Motor Corporation for their new multimedia systems. These chips power advanced infotainment features, including large touch displays, voice recognition, and OTA updates, for Lexus and Toyota vehicles, starting with the Lexus NX in November 2021. The R-Car family's software compatibility streamlines development across various vehicle models, contributing to an enhanced user experience in the "CASE era."

title: Chipmaker GlobalFoundries valued at $26 bln in lackluster Nasdaq debut
summary: GlobalFoundries Inc. made a lackluster Nasdaq debut, with shares opening flat and finishing slightly below its IPO price, valuing the chipmaker at approximately $26 billion. Despite raising $2.6 billion, the company faces lower gross margins compared to competitors, though it plans significant investments to boost capacity and future margins amid a global chip shortage. CEO Thomas Caulfield expects demand to remain high for years, with acute shortages potentially easing in 2023.

title: Indian American student wins $25,000 top award in science competition
summary: Akilan Sankaran, a 14-year-old Indian American student from New Mexico, won the $25,000 Samueli Foundation Prize in the Broadcom MASTERS competition for his math project on antiprime numbers. He created a computer program to calculate highly divisible numbers over 1,000 digits long, aiming to accelerate software performance. Other notable winners included students focusing on wildfire prevention, aquatic drone technology, and obesity research.

title: KLA Corp expands India presence for semiconductor-based R&D
summary: KLA Corporation is expanding its presence in India by opening two new facilities in Chennai to boost semiconductor-based research and talent development. This includes an AI-Advanced Computing Lab in partnership with IIT-Madras and a new office space for operations and talent expansion. These efforts aim to advance AI, software, image processing, and physics modeling for the global semiconductor industry.

title: FedEx, S&P Global discuss cloud edge use cases
summary: This article discusses how companies like FedEx and S&P Global are adopting cloud edge strategies to move data and applications closer to users, devices, and remote sites. The move is driven by the need to support real-time applications like robotics, IoT, and autonomous processing, especially exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic and the shift to remote work. Experts highlight the importance of connectivity, security like ZTNA, and automation for seamless operation and developer experience in these distributed environments.

title: GaN and SiC Power Semiconductor Market Size, Growth, Forecast to 2034
summary: The GaN and SiC Power Semiconductor Market is projected for significant growth through 2034, driven by the superior efficiency and performance of gallium nitride (GaN) and silicon carbide (SiC) over traditional silicon-based devices in applications like automotive electronics, industrial motors, and PV inverters. Despite high manufacturing costs and the established use of conventional silicon, government initiatives and the increasing adoption of electric vehicles are key market drivers. Notable industry developments include product introductions from major players like Alpha and Omega Semiconductor and ON Semiconductor.

title: Arista Gains Big on Cloud Boom
summary: Arista Networks experienced significant stock gains following strong earnings and boosted guidance, driven by increased capital spending from hyperscalers like Meta and Microsoft. The company also continues to gain market share from competitors like Cisco in both data center, cloud, and campus networking segments, indicating a robust cloud boom across the industry. Other infrastructure vendors like NVIDIA, Amazon Web Services, and Broadcom are also seeing growth.

title: Inari Amertron hedging its bets in China
summary: Inari Amertron, the largest OSAT player in Malaysia, is expanding into China through a joint venture with China Fortune-Tech Capital Co Ltd (CFTC). This move aims to diversify its income stream and reduce reliance on its major customer, Broadcom, while tapping into China's ambitious semiconductor market. The JV, leveraging Inari's expertise and CFTC's backing by SMIC, is seen by analysts as a strategic step to accelerate growth and mitigate risks in a highly competitive industry.

title: American Industrial Icon To Emerge As Aviation Pure-Play After 3-Way Split
summary: General Electric (GE) announced plans to split into three separate public companies, focusing on healthcare, power/renewable energy, and aviation. This restructuring aims to streamline the American industrial conglomerate after a period of significant change. Following the split, GE will emerge as an aviation pure-play, with its healthcare business spinning off in 2023 and the power and renewable energy businesses combining and separating in early 2024.

title: NVIDIA DRIVE Hyperion Combines Orin With Best-in-Class Sensor Architecture for Production-Ready Platform
summary: NVIDIA has announced its DRIVE Hyperion 8 platform, a production-ready computer architecture and sensor set for full self-driving systems, available for 2024 vehicle models. The platform leverages two NVIDIA DRIVE Orin systems-on-a-chip for redundancy and ample compute, supported by a comprehensive sensor suite from leading suppliers like Continental, Hella, Luminar, Sony, and Valeo. Designed to be open and modular, DRIVE Hyperion 8 aims to accelerate the development and deployment of safe and robust autonomous vehicles.

title: Meta Stitches Cisco, Arista to Open Compute Project Switches
summary: Meta has integrated Cisco and Arista Networks into its Open Compute Project (OCP) efforts by announcing new top-of-rack switches and improvements to its data center fabrics. This expansion includes the introduction of the OCP Switch Abstraction Interface (SAI) to standardize APIs for network hardware. Meta also shared future goals, including an open die-to-die interface and a commitment to net-zero emissions by 2030.

title: Ex-Broadcom engineer charged in US with stealing secrets for Chinese firm
summary: A former Broadcom engineer, Peter Kisang Kim, has been charged in the US with 18 counts of trade-secret theft for allegedly stealing chip designs for data centers and taking them to a China-based start-up. Kim, who worked at Broadcom for over 20 years, pleaded not guilty and faces a potential 10-year prison sentence for each count if convicted. This case highlights escalated US efforts against Chinese industrial espionage, while also drawing criticism about potential bias against Asian-Americans.

title: Broadcom’s 6-GHz Wi-Fi accelerates the future of connectivity
summary: Broadcom is at the forefront of enabling Wi-Fi 6E, which utilizes the 6 GHz spectrum band to significantly enhance connectivity speeds, reduce latency, and increase network capacity. This advancement is crucial for supporting demanding applications like virtual reality, 8K video streaming, and real-time gaming, as well as addressing the growing density of connected devices in homes and enterprises. By providing a "greenfield" spectrum, Wi-Fi 6E minimizes interference and allows for wider channels, ensuring a more robust and efficient wireless experience.

title: TI to construct new 300 mm chip fab
summary: Texas Instruments (TI) plans to build a new 12-inch semiconductor wafer fab in Sherman, Texas, to manufacture analog and embedded processing chips. The fab, with construction starting in 2022 and production by 2025, is part of a potential four-fab site representing an investment of up to $30 billion. This initiative aligns with the broader U.S. push to increase domestic semiconductor manufacturing, spurred by recent chip shortages and government legislation like the CHIPS for America Act.

title: Middle School Students Win Science Fair Prizes
summary: Middle school students competed virtually in the annual Broadcom MASTERS science competition, where $100,000 in prizes were awarded. Akilan Sankaran, 14, won the top prize for his math project, showcasing the power of mathematics in solving complex problems. Despite the virtual format, finalists bonded through various social activities and were praised for their innovative spirit by the Society for Science.

title: This company may overtake LG as OLED supplier for Apple iPhones
summary: Chinese display manufacturer BOE is reportedly set to overtake LG as an OLED panel supplier for Apple iPhones. BOE is increasing its production, aiming to supply 50 million OLED units by 2022, potentially surpassing LG's projected 70 million units in 2023. Samsung remains Apple's largest OLED supplier, expected to provide 150 million units by 2022.

title: Storage Management Software Market to grow by USD 10.64 bn from 2020 to 2025 |Evolving Opportunities with Broadcom Inc., Cisco Systems Inc. & Data Dynamics Inc|17000+ Technavio Reports
summary: The Storage Management Software Market is projected to grow by USD 10.64 billion from 2020 to 2025, driven by an increasing volume of data and with significant growth originating from APAC. Key players like Broadcom Inc., Cisco Systems Inc., and Data Dynamics Inc. are contributing to the market's fragmented yet competitive landscape. The report also highlights upcoming trends and competitive analysis based on financial performance and growth strategies.

title: 6 GHz readies for new users as AFC wannabees stack up
summary: A growing number of companies have applied to become Automated Frequency Coordination (AFC) system operators for the unlicensed 6 GHz band, a crucial step to enable standard power operations for new applications. These AFC systems will facilitate outdoor operations, highly directional indoor antennas, and higher power indoor uses, with applicants including major tech and telecom firms. The market for AFC operators is expected to allow for diverse business models and innovation, particularly with the adoption of a standardized interface for device makers.

title: U.S. FTC sues to block Nvidia deal to buy Arm
summary: The U.S. Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has sued to block Nvidia Corp's more than $80 billion acquisition of British chip technology provider Arm, citing concerns that the deal would give Nvidia undue control over crucial computing technology and designs. This move complicates an already challenging regulatory path for the acquisition, which has faced opposition from the chip industry and scrutiny from British and European Union regulators. The FTC argues the merger would harm competition, reduce innovation, and lead to higher prices by giving Nvidia the ability and incentive to undermine competitors who rely on Arm's technology.

title: AppNeta Acquired by Broadcom in Order to Bring Its Award-Winning Visibility Platform to the World's Largest Enterprises
summary: AppNeta, a leading network performance monitoring solution, announced its acquisition by Broadcom. This acquisition will combine AppNeta's end-to-end visibility platform with Broadcom's DX NetOps to provide large enterprises with a unified solution for monitoring network performance and application delivery, especially critical for cloud and SaaS transformations. The integration aims to eliminate blind spots for IT teams regarding end-user experience for business-critical applications in a decentralized work environment.

title: Microsoft Expands Azure Space Partnerships with Azure Orbital Preview
summary: Microsoft unveiled a public preview of Azure Orbital, its groundstation-as-a-service offering for satellite communication and data processing, emphasizing its integration with Azure's hyperscale computing resources. The company is expanding its Azure Orbital network through new partnerships, including ST Engineering iDirect for virtualized modems and an enhanced collaboration with KSAT for groundstation access. Additionally, Microsoft announced new partnerships with Airbus for satellite imagery integration into Azure Maps and Blackshark.ai, Esri, and Orbital Insight for geospatial intelligence and data analytics solutions within Azure.

title: 10 Technology Vendors Affected By The Log4j Vulnerability
summary: The critical Log4j vulnerability has impacted numerous technology vendors, including prominent names like Cisco, IBM, VMware, and MSP-focused companies such as ConnectWise and N-able. This zero-day exploit allows attackers to execute arbitrary code due to vulnerable Java logging package Log4j, prompting vendors to rapidly develop patches and workarounds, though some fixes may not be available until early 2022. Several companies, including Amazon Web Services, Broadcom, Fortinet, HCL, and Okta, have issued advisories and remediation steps for their affected products, warning customers to update or implement temporary mitigations.

title: Wise Road Drops $1.4 Billion Buyout of Magnachip
summary: Chinese private equity firm Wise Road Capital has terminated its $1.4 billion all-cash merger agreement with U.S. chipmaker Magnachip Semiconductor Corp. The termination was due to the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (CFIUS) failing to approve the deal, citing national security risks. Wise Road Capital will pay Magnachip a $70.2 million termination fee.

title: Apple Builds New Team in Southern California to Bring More Wireless Chips In-House
summary: Apple is expanding its in-house chip development by hiring engineers for a new office in Irvine, Southern California. This team will focus on creating wireless chips, potentially replacing components currently supplied by companies like Broadcom and Skyworks Solutions. The move is part of Apple's broader strategy to reduce reliance on third-party suppliers and produce more of its own components, following similar efforts with modems and other chip technologies.

title: 17 Semiconductor Companies Forecast to Have >$10B Sales in 2021
summary: According to IC Insights, 17 companies are projected to achieve over $10 billion in worldwide semiconductor sales in 2021, with AMD, NXP Semiconductors, and Analog Devices joining this "megasuppliers" list. The combined sales of these companies are expected to grow by 26% year-over-year, outpacing the overall industry's 25% growth. Samsung is forecast to be the largest semiconductor supplier, with sales nearing $83.1 billion, driven by a strong memory market.

title: DIVS Outperforms Benchmark Despite Bumpy Month
summary: The Guinness Atkinson SmartETFs Dividend Builder ETF (DIVS) outperformed its benchmark despite a 1.41% loss in November, primarily due to solid stock selection in industrials, healthcare, and financials. The loss was attributed to resurfacing COVID variant fears and hawkish statements from the Fed, which erased robust gains from October. Despite the bumpy month, DIVS is up 15.23% YTD and 20% over a one-year period, benefiting from its focus on healthy companies with strong fundamentals that consistently provide dividend growth.

title: New TI Sensor Tech Drives Toward a Collision-Free Future, Advancing Autonomous Driving and Vehicle Safety
summary: Texas Instruments (TI) unveiled a new AWR2944 radar sensor at CES 2022, designed to enhance autonomous driving and vehicle safety. This sensor can detect objects up to 40% farther away, is 30% smaller, and offers 33% higher resolution than existing radar sensors, specifically improving blind spot monitoring and turn navigation. The technology aims to contribute to a "collision-free future" by addressing challenges in processing large amounts of data for advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) and improving visibility around corners, particularly important for automated parking and driving.

title: Micron Technology searches for site for $40B factory. Is Boise among the contenders?
summary: Micron Technology is reportedly scouting locations for a new $40 billion manufacturing plant, with sites in Arizona, California, Texas, and North Carolina under consideration, though Boise is apparently not on the list. This search is part of Micron's larger plan to invest over $150 billion in chip production over 10 years to address a global chip shortage and meet growing demand driven by AI, 5G, and autonomous vehicles. The company is evaluating locations based on factors like site availability, talent pool, utility services, sustainability, and regulatory environment, with a focus on domestic production potentially spurred by the CHIPS Act.

title: Optical lovebirds eye a $14 billion market opportunity
summary: The merger between ADTRAN and ADVA is nearing completion, with ADTRAN shareholders approving the deal. The combined company anticipates a significant increase in its total addressable market to almost $14 billion, driven by growth opportunities in North America and Europe, and expects to boost sales by 50% in a few years. Despite the challenges of integration, both CEOs are optimistic about building a global leader in fiber networking solutions.

title: Datto Hires Splunk, Qlik Veteran Brooke Cunningham as CMO -
summary: Datto has appointed Brooke Cunningham, a veteran from Splunk and Qlik, as its new Chief Marketing Officer. This strategic hire aligns with Datto's ongoing expansion beyond its traditional storage offerings into cloud-based software and security solutions for Managed Service Providers (MSPs). Cunningham's experience in scaling businesses and nurturing partner ecosystems, particularly in the security technology sector, is expected to support Datto's accelerated growth and its commitment to the MSP community.

title: Comcast Announces World-First Test of 10G Modem Technology Capable of Delivering Multigigabit Speeds to Homes
summary: Comcast successfully tested a prototype 10G modem using Full Duplex DOCSIS 4.0 technology, achieving upload and download speeds faster than 4 Gbps. This marks a significant milestone in Comcast's 10G initiative, demonstrating the capability to deliver multigigabit speeds over existing network connections and promising increased reliability, performance, and lower latency for customers.

title: DevOps Tool Market 2022 Outstanding Growth Scope Witnessed
summary: The global DevOps Tool market is projected to reach USD 6881.6 million by 2026, growing from USD 4092.1 million in 2020 at a CAGR of 13.9% over five years. This report by Infinity Business Insights analyzes key players, market trends, and the impact of COVID-19, providing insights for investors and businesses to achieve market growth. The study covers product types like DevOps Ready, Enabled, and Capable, and applications across various sectors including IT, Telecom, BFSI, and Government.

title: The Threat Landscape in 2021
summary: Symantec, a division of Broadcom Software, reviewed the major cyber threats of 2021, highlighting ransomware, supply chain attacks, exploitation of public-facing application vulnerabilities, and attacks on critical infrastructure. While ransomware attack numbers decreased, targeted ransomware incidents increased significantly, fueled by initial access brokers and ransomware-as-a-service models. The report details prominent attacks like SolarWinds, Kaseya, and Colonial Pipeline, emphasizing the evolving tactics of threat actors and the rising impact on organizations and society.

title: Siemens collaborates with UMC on design kits for automotive and power applications
summary: Siemens Digital Industries Software has partnered with United Microelectronics Corporation (UMC) to create process design kits (PDKs) for UMC's 110-nanometer and 180-nanometer BCD technology platforms. These PDKs are optimized for Siemens EDA’s Tanner custom design flow software, enabling the creation of integrated circuits for automotive and power applications. The collaboration aims to provide customers with the necessary tools to develop sophisticated power management solutions amidst increasing market demand.

title: Silicon Labs Announces BG24, MG24 TinyML 2.4GHz SoCs — and Boasts of a Fourfold Performance Gain
summary: Silicon Labs has unveiled its new BG24 and MG24 system-on-chip (SoC) range, targeting edge AI projects with a claimed fourfold performance boost and six-times energy efficiency improvement. These SoCs feature an Arm Cortex-M33 processor, dedicated AI/ML accelerators, and support for TensorFlow workloads. The BG24 offers Bluetooth 5.3 Low Energy, while the MG24 adds OpenThread, Zigbee, and Matter compatibility, with general availability expected in April.

title: Tech firms connect for nature conservation
summary: Ericsson, PLDT Inc., and Smart Communications Inc. have partnered to use technology and AI-enabled solutions for the conservation of a 405-hectare mangrove wetland in Sasmuan, Pampanga. This collaboration aims to protect endangered wildlife and marine biodiversity in the area, which was designated an internationally important wetland under the Ramsar Convention in 2021. The project involves deploying AI-enabled CCTV cameras to identify bird species, with PLDT hosting the cloud system for data and Smart providing internet connectivity for environmental monitoring.

title: CRDO Stock Price, Forecast & Analysis | CREDO TECHNOLOGY GROUP HOLDI (NASDAQ:CRDO)
summary: The article provides a detailed analysis of CREDO Technology Group Holding (NASDAQ:CRDO), covering its stock price, forecast, and various analytical ratings. It highlights CRDO's strong performance in the past year, its technical and fundamental ratings from ChartMill, and analysts' expectations for significant future growth in both EPS and revenue. The company specializes in high-speed connectivity solutions for the data infrastructure market.

title: Juniper Guns for Cisco, Nokia With Revamped Routing Silicon
summary: Juniper Networks has announced new routing silicon, Express 5 and Trio 6, claiming superior performance and power efficiency compared to Cisco's and Nokia's offerings. The Express 5 chips, designed for core routing, offer up to 28.8 Tb/s throughput, while the Trio 6, for edge routing, features machine learning capabilities and a 70% improvement in power efficiency. Dell'Oro Group analyst Shin Umeda notes that direct comparison of ASICs is challenging due to varying vendor development cycles and deployment timelines.

title: Reference design offers wireless docking over Wi-Fi 6E for PCs
summary: Synaptics Incorporated has introduced Gemini, a reference design that offers wireless docking over Wi-Fi 6E for PCs, claiming it's the world's first true Wi-Fi 6/6E wireless docking experience for laptops. This technology enables full dual-4K display capability and ultra-low latency, comparable to wired connections, and integrates hardware and software components like the BCM43752 Wi-Fi 6/6E radio and DL-1950 video interface IC. While initially focused on PC docking, Gemini's applications extend to tablets, gaming, and VR, with analyst Patrick Moorhead highlighting its potential to revolutionize connectivity in hybrid work environments.

title: VAST Data Accelerates Global Expansion Plans Across Europe and Asia
summary: VAST Data, a storage software company, is expanding its global operations across Europe and Asia, following previous launches in several countries. This expansion aims to meet the growing demand for its Universal Storage platform, offering a modern alternative to traditional HDD storage systems, especially for AI computing, big data, and analytics. The company has partnered with leading distributors in various regions to support this growth.

title: Apple, Broadcom win new trial in $1.1 bln Caltech patent case
summary: A U.S. appeals court has invalidated a $1.1 billion jury verdict against Apple and Broadcom in a patent infringement case brought by the California Institute of Technology (Caltech). The court deemed the damages "legally unsupportable" and ordered a new trial on the amount of damages, while upholding the infringement findings for two of Caltech's patents.
