The lawsuit also names Occidental's CEO, former CFO, several directors, and banks that underwrote its bonds, alleging inadequate due diligence.

title: Christine Y. Zhao Celebrated for Dedication to the Field of Finance
summary: Christine Y. Zhao has been recognized by Marquis Who's Who for her extensive and accomplished career in finance, spanning more than two decades. She currently serves as a Board Director for Nasdaq-listed BeyondSpring Inc. and a Venture Partner at YuanMing Capital, having previously held significant roles at JPMorgan, Bank of America Merrill Lynch, and as CFO for private equity-backed companies including Best Inc. Her career highlights include driving strategy, business execution, and successful financial initiatives across various global institutions and industries, in addition to her significant community involvement.

title: Chinese Gaming Firm NetEase to Launch $2.5 Billion Hong Kong Stock Sale
summary: Chinese game developer NetEase Inc. is preparing to launch a $2.5 billion stock offering in Hong Kong, following a trend of U.S.-listed Chinese companies seeking secondary listings in the city amid rising U.S.-China tensions. This move, along with JD.com Inc.'s planned $3 billion offering, highlights a shift towards Hong Kong as a listing destination, especially after a proposed U.S. bill could force Chinese companies to delist from American markets. NetEase plans to use the proceeds for expansion into music streaming and online education, with its Hong Kong debut expected on June 11.

title: Embrace Disruption to Tenth Degree With This ETF
summary: The article highlights the ALPS Disruptive Technologies ETF (DTEC) as a solution for investors to gain broad exposure to 10 themes reshaping the technological landscape, including Healthcare Innovation, Cloud Computing, and FinTech. It emphasizes the significant growth potential of themes like cloud computing and fintech, as well as the importance of 3D printing in industries like defense and healthcare. The ETF offers a way to embrace the transformative power of disruptive technologies.

title: Capital One Announces Capital One, National Association and Capital One Bank (USA), National Association Any and All Cash Tender Offers for $7.55 Billion of Notes
summary: Capital One announced cash tender offers for approximately $7.55 billion of notes issued by its subsidiaries, Capital One, National Association, and Capital One Bank (USA), National Association. The offers allow holders to sell certain securities back to Capital One for cash, with varying purchase prices depending on the note series. The tender offers are set to expire on June 5, 2020, with a settlement date expected on June 10, 2020.

title: Charles Schwab lands DOJ approval to buy TD Ameritrade
summary: The U.S. Justice Department's antitrust division has approved Charles Schwab's proposed $26 billion acquisition of TD Ameritrade, clearing the way for the merger. This combination is expected to solidify Schwab's dominant position in the discount-brokerage market and help both firms manage costs in a zero-commission trading environment. The deal is anticipated to close in the latter half of the year, with integration taking 18 to 36 months.

title: No quiet retirement for longtime Webster Financial chief
summary: James Smith, former CEO of Webster Financial, is actively involved in developing an economic action plan for Connecticut, even in retirement, demonstrating a continued commitment to public service. His work, initially derailed by COVID-19, now focuses on reopening, recovery, and reimagining the state's economy, with a particular concern for small businesses and urban centers. Smith advocates for retired bankers to invest their career knowledge back into their communities, emphasizing the noble nature of banking and civic responsibility.

title: U.S. Bancorp pledges $116 million to address racial inequality
summary: U.S. Bancorp announced a $116 million pledge to combat racial and economic inequality following the death of George Floyd. The initiative includes significant capital for African American-owned businesses, a new fund for grants addressing systemic inequities, and a community development financial institutions partnership program. The bank also plans to increase partnerships with African American suppliers, promote people of color to leadership, and rebuild damaged branches in Minneapolis

title: Bank of America, U.S. Bank, PNC and others pledge millions toward racial equality
summary: Several major financial institutions, including Bank of America, U.S. Bank, and PNC, have pledged millions to racial equality initiatives. These commitments involve boosting loans to Black-owned businesses, funding community grants, and investing in organizations that address economic inequality, with some pledges specifically addressing anti-Asian hatred. The efforts are a response to the ongoing focus on racial justice and the disproportionate impact of systemic issues on communities of color.

title: Morgan Stanley's Gorman 'thrilled' with ETrade purchase
summary: Morgan Stanley CEO James Gorman expresses immense satisfaction with the acquisition of ETrade, highlighting the online trading firm's technology, digital banking capabilities, and management team. He plans to retain the ETrade brand, possibly as "ETrade powered by Morgan Stanley," recognizing its value to clients. Gorman believes the deal expands Morgan Stanley's online platform, diversifies the company, and strengthens its digital offerings, particularly appealing to a younger demographic.

title: Could a Western Union–MoneyGram deal help two giants fend off fintech disrupters?
summary: Western Union is reportedly considering an acquisition of rival MoneyGram, a move that could help both remittance giants better compete against fintech disruptors. MoneyGram has struggled financially since a failed acquisition attempt in 2018, making it a potentially attractive target for Western Union to expand its global retail network and digital capabilities. However, such a deal faces challenges including MoneyGram's debt, potential antitrust issues, and Western Union's mixed history with large acquisitions.

title: The 20-Year Bond Is Changing The Shape Of The Yield Curve
summary: The U.S. Treasury's re-issuance of 20-year bonds in May 2020, for the first time since 1986, is significantly altering the shape of the yield curve. This new issuance has created a "kink" in the curve, with front-end rates indicating lower interest rates while longer-dated rates have moved higher. As liquidity in this sector builds, experts anticipate that the kink will moderate, influencing futures trading and overall market liquidity.

title: Banking by appointment could stick as a post-COVID-19 customer habit
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic has led financial institutions to implement appointment-based banking to manage social distancing, a practice that some bankers believe will continue post-pandemic. This system helps banks manage staff levels, triage customers, and offer convenience for customers working from home. It also complements digital banking options for those who still prefer a personal touch, with banks like Regions seeing a significant increase in appointment volume.

title: PFPC Selected by Franklin Templeton Investments to Service New Jersey 529 Plans
summary: PFPC Inc., a member of The PNC Financial Services Group, Inc., has been selected by Franklin Templeton Investments to provide investor servicing for both the Franklin Templeton 529 College Savings Plan and the NJBEST 529 College Savings Plan. This multi-year contract involves PFPC providing recordkeeping, reporting, and investor servicing for these plans, expanding its role in the growing 529 college savings plan market. The collaboration will leverage PFPC's Global Enterprise Platform to support expanded distribution goals and complex servicing needs for these college savings programs.

title: Japan's SoftBank unloads a $21 billion stake in T-Mobile US as the great sell-off commences
summary: SoftBank Group Corp. is selling a $21 billion stake in T-Mobile US Inc. as part of a larger $42 billion asset sale to finance stock buybacks and reduce debt, motivated by record losses in its Vision Fund. This move comes after significant write-downs in investments like WeWork and Uber. The complex transaction involves T-Mobile holding a public offering and transferring nearly 200 million shares owned by SoftBank.

title: CoreLogic Weighs Unsolicited Bid from Cannae Holdings, Senator Investment Group
summary: Cannae Holdings Inc. and Senator Investment Group LP have proposed acquiring CoreLogic Inc. for $5.16 billion, or $65 a share in cash, representing a 37% premium over CoreLogic's stock price on June 15. CoreLogic stated it would review the unsolicited bid, with the bidders criticizing CoreLogic's current strategy and recent guidance change as a defensive move. The firms are calling for CoreLogic to hire advisers and form a special committee to negotiate the transaction.

title: Netflix will move $100 million into Black-owned banks
summary: Netflix Inc. is pledging $100 million to Black-owned banks and financial institutions to support African-American communities. This initiative involves an initial $25 million investment in the Black Economic Development Initiative and $10 million to Hope Credit Union, with an ongoing commitment to steer 2% of its cash to these organizations. This move follows calls for corporate support for racial equality and aims to address systemic inequality by boosting historically underfunded institutions.

title: First look: JPMorgan Chase's downtown branch to open next week
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. is opening its newest Nashville branch next week at the base of the ServiceSource Tower in downtown Nashville. This will be the bank's flagship Nashville location, situated near Broadway and several competitors like Regions Bank, Fifth Third Bank, and SunTrust Bank.

title: BBVA brings ‘banker bar’ to new branches in Texas expansion
summary: BBVA USA is expanding its presence in Texas by opening 15 new branches, despite the coronavirus pandemic. These new branches will feature a "personal banker bar" instead of traditional tellers, aiming to merge digital and physical banking experiences. The bank plans to retrain existing tellers and new employees to facilitate digital onboarding and account origination, with a goal to complete this re-skilling by 2021.

title: Waterstone Mortgage Head Andy Peach To Resign
summary: Andy Peach, President and CEO of Waterstone Mortgage Corporation, has announced his resignation. Peach, who was appointed last August, is leaving the role with over 30 years of industry experience. A replacement has not yet been named.

title: Lululemon acquisition Mirror could generate $700 million and reach 600,000 subscribers by 2023: Bank of America
summary: Bank of America analysts project that Lululemon Athletica's newly acquired at-home fitness company, Mirror, could generate $700 million in revenue and attract 600,000 subscribers by 2023. This projection is based on the increased interest in digital fitness, partly due to the coronavirus pandemic. If achieved, Mirror's revenue would account for approximately 10% of Lululemon's total annual revenue.

title: USDA Rural Dev.’t awards 5 Puerto Rico banks for $109M in lending
summary: The U.S. Department of Agriculture Rural Development office in Puerto Rico recognized five local banks with "Top Lenders Awards" for collectively approving $109 million in home loans. This initiative celebrates "Homeownership Month" and highlights the partnership between USDA Rural and local lenders, which has helped over 3,700 families purchase homes in 2020. Despite challenges, USDA Rural Development has invested nearly $447 million in Puerto Rico for homeownership and provided additional funds for home repairs and housing preservation grants.

title: Credicorp emite bonos por 500 millones de dólares en el mercado internacional
summary: Credicorp, a Peruvian financial services holding company, issued $500 million in bonds in international markets with a coupon rate of 2.750% and maturity in 2025. The proceeds from this operation will be used to finance corporate purposes. Various law firms advised Credicorp and the initial purchasers, Bank of America Securities, J.P. Morgan Securities, and Goldman Sachs.

title: Valley National Bank views today's business environment as a glass half full
summary: Valley National Bank's Tampa-based commercial real estate lending team is cautiously optimistic about the region's economic rebound despite the COVID-19 pandemic. They are implementing stricter lending practices, including requiring more equity and increased due diligence, but have also processed over $2.3 billion in PPP loans. The bank is buoyed by falling unemployment claims, rising consumer confidence, and anticipates growth in certain commercial real estate sectors.

title: Banks Could Get $24 Billion in Fees From PPP Loans
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. and Bank of America Corp. are projected to earn between $1.5 billion and $2.6 billion in fees from the government's Paycheck Protection Program (PPP), acting as leading conduits for small-business aid during the coronavirus shutdown. The two largest banks by assets processed more emergency loans than other lenders and are poised to receive the largest fees, according to recent disclosures by the Trump administration.

title: White & Case Advises the Underwriters on Lemonade, Inc.'s Initial Public Offering
summary: White & Case LLP advised the underwriters on Lemonade, Inc.'s US$367 million initial public offering and listing on the New York Stock Exchange. Lemonade (NYSE: LMND) offers homeowners and renters insurance and has expanded globally, with the offering including the full exercise of the underwriters' option to purchase additional shares. Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC, Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC, and Allen & Company LLC acted as managing bookrunners for the offering.

title: Bank of America exec Aditya Bhasin talks virtual assistant Erica's progress — and how Covid-19 accelerated growth
summary: Bank of America's virtual assistant, Erica, has processed over 150 million requests since its 2018 launch. The article, featuring an interview with exec Aditya Bhasin, discusses Erica's evolution and how the Covid-19 pandemic significantly accelerated its growth and usage among customers.

title: Exxon vs Chevron Which Is The Smartest Buy
summary: The article compares ExxonMobil (XOM) and Chevron Corp. (CVX) amidst the shale bust, evaluating which company presents a smarter investment. It highlights Chevron's stronger resilience due to more modest capital investment plans and lower debt-to-equity ratio, contrasting it with Exxon's aggressive spending that has strained its balance sheet and dividend. The analysis suggests Chevron is better positioned to weather the industry's downturn.

title: Bank of America blows out its solar energy commitment with 10 deals in 3 states
summary: Bank of America has signed 10 agreements to purchase solar electricity for its operations in North Carolina, Texas, and South Carolina, totaling 200 megawatts (MWAC) of new solar capacity. These deals will supply over 340,000 megawatt-hours (MWh) of Green-e-certified renewable energy certificates annually, covering a significant portion of the bank's U.S. electricity use. A unique feature of many of these projects is the inclusion of pollinator habitats to support local biodiversity and agriculture in low-to-moderate-income communities.

title: Rocky Mountain Institute launches the Center for Climate-Aligned Finance
summary: Rocky Mountain Institute (RMI) has launched the Center for Climate-Aligned Finance in collaboration with major financial institutions like Wells Fargo, Goldman Sachs, Bank of America, and JPMorgan Chase. The Center aims to facilitate the financial sector's role in guiding the global economy to net-zero emissions by mid-century by developing practical solutions and frameworks for carbon-intensive industries. It will work with financial institutions and corporations to accelerate the transition to a sustainable energy platform and foster climate alignment initiatives across various sectors.

title: PPP in CNY: Top 20 banks, lenders that doled out most loans to local businesses
summary: This article identifies the top 20 banks and lenders that distributed the most Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) loans to local businesses in Central New York. It highlights that independent community banks and credit unions performed the majority of lending, with M&T Bank leading. The article also provides a list of the top lenders and details about loan size distribution.

title: ING Groep to Shut Branches Amid Shift Toward Digitalization
summary: ING Groep announced plans to close 42 branches in the Netherlands due to a decline in foot traffic, accelerated by the coronavirus pandemic and a broader shift towards digital banking. The bank, led by CEO Ruud van Dusschoten, intends to transfer services to existing service points and offer affected employees other positions within the company. This move aligns with ING's long-term strategy of focusing on digital capabilities, a trend also seen in other major banks.

title: nCino prices IPO above price range at $31 a share
summary: nCino Inc., a cloud-based software provider for financial institutions, priced its initial public offering at $31 a share, exceeding its proposed range due to strong investor demand. The company sold 8.06 million shares, raising $249.86 million, and plans to use the proceeds for general corporate purposes and working capital. Shares are expected to begin trading on Nasdaq under the ticker 'NCNO' with BofA and Barclays leading the underwriting.

title: BofA Clients Keep Tight Grip on Cash Amid Ebullient Stock Rally
summary: Despite a significant stock market rally, Bank of America's client survey shows fund managers are maintaining high cash levels, boosting average cash holdings to 4.9% in July from 4.7% in June. This suggests that managers, who oversee $570 billion, view stocks as overvalued and are preparing for potential market volatility, anticipating "bad news on virus, macro, election."

title: How Banks Artwash the Funds that Enable Police Brutality
summary: This article argues that major banks "artwash" their image by sponsoring cultural institutions while simultaneously profiting from municipal bonds issued to pay for police brutality settlements. It highlights how these bonds increase the cost of settlements, divert funds from public services to wealthy investors, and lack transparency, effectively transferring wealth from over-policed communities to financial institutions. The piece suggests that the art world, by accepting these sponsorships, is implicated in a system that financially benefits from racist oppression.

title: BBVA, the best bank in Latin America according to Euromoney
summary: Euromoney magazine has named BBVA the best bank in Latin America for 2020, also recognizing it as the best in sustainable finance for the second consecutive year. The publication highlighted BBVA's successful integration of digitization across the region and its strong financial performance, with Latin American operations contributing significantly to the group's overall results. Additionally, BBVA was named the best bank in Mexico and Argentina, lauded for its digital transformation efforts, efficiency, customer satisfaction, and commitment to sustainable development.

title: FD interest rate revised by ICICI Bank! Compare latest rates with SBI, HDFC Bank – July 2020
summary: ICICI Bank has revised its fixed deposit (FD) interest rates downwards, effective July 14, making it the only leading bank to do so in July. This article compares the latest FD rates of ICICI Bank with those of SBI and HDFC Bank, highlighting that HDFC Bank offers the highest interest on 1-year FDs, while ICICI Bank leads for longer tenures (5-10 years). Both ICICI Bank and SBI have special "Golden Years" or "Wecare" FD schemes offering additional benefits for senior citizens for a limited period.

title: SEC charges former Morgan Stanley rep with stealing $6 million from clients
summary: The SEC has charged Michael Barry Carter, a former Morgan Stanley representative, with stealing approximately $6 million from brokerage customers and an elderly investment advisory client through unauthorized transfers between 2007 and 2019. Carter has pleaded guilty to parallel criminal charges and was fired by Morgan Stanley in 2019, with the firm stating that impacted clients have been reimbursed. He used the misappropriated funds to support a lavish lifestyle and concealed the fraud with false account statements.

title: Notre Dame elects three new Trustees
summary: The University of Notre Dame has elected three new members to its Board of Trustees: Justin R. Liu, Michael G. O’Grady, and Jennifer F. Scanlon. All three are Notre Dame alumni with significant leadership roles in their respective industries. Additionally, three former Trustees were elevated to Emeritus status, and two individuals were elected as Fellows of the University.

title: More Wells Fargo customers say the bank decided to pause their mortgage payments without asking
summary: Numerous Wells Fargo customers across 14 states claim the bank unilaterally placed their mortgages into forbearance plans, affecting their credit reports and ability to refinance, without their consent. The bank attributes these incidents to misinterpretations of customer intentions, while critics like Sen. Sherrod Brown denounce the bank's "sloppy service and shoddy management." This practice has drawn comparisons to Wells Fargo's past scandals of enrolling customers in unwanted services.

title: BTG Pactual obtém 514,1 milhões de dólares em emissão de unidades locais e internacionais
summary: BTG Pactual successfully raised $514.1 million through a primary public offering of 35,625,000 units, with each unit equivalent to one common share and two Class A preferred shares. The funds will be allocated to strategic initiatives within its digital retail business and to bolster its capital indicators. Several law firms advised on the transaction, which involved both local and international placement agents.

title: Macy’s, Kohl’s suffer as brands, competitors and e-commerce step in to replace department stores
summary: Macy's and Kohl's have been downgraded to "sell" by UBS due to a shift in retail power towards brands and e-commerce. Department stores were already struggling before the pandemic, and their positions have further weakened, according to Bank of America. UBS also significantly reduced the price targets for Macy's and Kohl's.

title: Morning Coffee: The hot new finance job that’s actually really old. Can you trust the interns with your computer network?
summary: The article discusses the resurgence of "direct lending" in finance, exemplified by Apollo Global Management's new business, noting its similarity to traditional banking functions that banks divested from due to regulatory changes. It also covers Morgan Stanley's in-office virtual internship in Shanghai due to new cybersecurity laws and touches on other finance-related news, including legal disputes, academic research, and green bond market activity.

title: A few of Charlotte’s largest companies just told employees they’ll work from home for the rest of 2020. Will others follow?
summary: Several major Charlotte-based companies, including Red Ventures, LendingTree, Ally, and Brighthouse Financial, have announced that employees will work remotely until at least early 2021 due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic and related logistical challenges. This decision, influenced by school system changes and health concerns, raises questions about whether other large companies in the area will adopt similar long-term work-from-home policies, potentially reshaping the future of white-collar workplaces. Other large companies like Bank of America, Wells Fargo, Truist, and Duke Energy are still evaluating their return-to-office plans, largely maintaining remote work for most employees for the time being.

title: HSBC launches ESG solutions team | HSBC news | HSBC Holdings plc
summary: HSBC has established a dedicated Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) Solutions unit to assist clients in transitioning to more sustainable business models, especially in the post-COVID-19 recovery. This new team will offer advice, expertise, and financing ideas to various clients globally, including businesses, governments, and asset managers. The initiative aims to solidify HSBC's position as a leader in sustainable finance and support the move towards a net-zero economy.

title: Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway Inc. adds another $400M to investment in Bank of America
summary: Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway Inc. has significantly increased its investment in Bank of America, adding another $400 million to its holdings. This latest purchase brings Berkshire Hathaway's total investment in the bank to over $1.2 billion in just eight days. Bank of America, headquartered in Charlotte, employs approximately 16,000 people in the area.

title: Regions to close 37 branches, including two in Tampa Bay
summary: Regions Bank is closing 37 branches, including two in Tampa Bay, as part of its network optimization strategy. This decision aligns with changing consumer preferences, which have been accelerated by the Covid-19 pandemic. The closures reflect a broader trend of banks adjusting their physical footprints in response to evolving customer banking habits.

title: Strategic Education, Inc. to Acquire Laureate Education, Inc.’s Australia and New Zealand Academic Operations, Including Torrens University
summary: Strategic Education, Inc. announced its definitive agreement to acquire Laureate Education, Inc.'s Australia and New Zealand academic operations, including Torrens University, for $642.7 million in cash. This acquisition will expand Strategic Education's global presence, diversify its offerings, and is expected to be immediately accretive to its earnings. The transaction is anticipated to close by the first quarter of 2021, subject to regulatory approvals.

title: Citi, Bank of America join Morgan Stanley in carbon-disclosure group
summary: Bank of America and Citi have joined the Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financials (PCAF), an organization aiming to standardize how banks measure and reduce their climate impact. Citi pledged $250 billion over the next five years for low-carbon solutions and aims to reduce CO2 emissions by 45% by 2025. These moves follow Morgan Stanley also joining PCAF, highlighting a growing trend among major U.S. banks to improve their green profiles and address climate change.

title: CECL versus IFRS9: It Looks like U.S. Regulators Got it Right for Credit Cards
summary: This article examines the differences between U.S. CECL and international IFRS9 accounting standards for loan loss provisioning, particularly for credit cards. It argues that U.S. regulators made a better choice with CECL, which requires banks to provision for lifetime expected losses, compared to IFRS9's 12-month horizon. The piece highlights how U.S. banks, under CECL, are significantly more reserved than their Canadian counterparts following IFRS9, leading to greater financial stability, especially during crises like COVID-19.

title: Goldman, BofA Left Off Ant IPO for Work With Alibaba Rivals
summary: Goldman Sachs and Bank of America were excluded from Ant Group's upcoming Hong Kong IPO due to their prior work with Alibaba's competitors. Alibaba, which owns a significant stake in Ant, has reportedly advised banks to avoid working with its rivals to secure future business. Ant Group is planning dual listings in Hong Kong and Shanghai, aiming for an IPO size that could exceed Saudi Aramco's record-setting offering.

title: Trump fires Tennessee Valley Authority chair, cites hiring of foreign workers
summary: President Donald Trump announced the firing of Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) chair, Skip Thompson, and another board member, citing the authority's practice of hiring foreign workers under H1-B visas. Trump also threatened to remove other board members and mandated that the new CEO's salary should not exceed $500,000, significantly less than the previous CEO's $8 million. The decision followed a TV ad criticizing the TVA for replacing American workers with foreign contractors, a move that Senator Lamar Alexander disputes, stating the TVA operates without taxpayer money and has competitive rates.

title: Buffett's Berkshire bought $2.07 billion BofA stock since mid-July, has 11.9% stake
summary: Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway Inc. has acquired an additional $2.07 billion in Bank of America Corp. shares since mid-July, increasing its stake to 11.9%. The move follows regulatory approval from the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond to boost its holding up to 24.9% and helps Berkshire reduce its substantial cash reserves. This makes Bank of America Berkshire's largest common stock holding after Apple Inc.

title: Bank of America Says It Has Display Issue Following $0 Balance Complaints
summary: Bank of America experienced a temporary display issue causing some online and mobile banking customers to see inaccurate, zeroed-out account balances. The bank confirmed the issue has been resolved, stating that account balances are restored and customer information remains secure with no impact on accounts.

title: Bank of America Stocks Chief Gallo Considers Leaving After Snub
summary: Fab Gallo, Bank of America's head of global equities, is reportedly considering leaving the firm after being excluded from a recent promotion of senior executives. This snub occurred despite his division achieving record revenue earlier in the year, following public scrutiny over his communication style and business turbulence. An internal recording of Gallo's conference call was leaked, contributing to the decision to omit him from the new class of senior executives.

title: 4 Silver Stocks to Add Pizzazz to Your Portfolio HL PAAS FSM EXK
summary: This article highlights four silver stocks—Hecla Mining (HL), Pan American Silver (PAAS), Fortuna Silver Mines (FSM), and Endeavour Silver (EXK)—as strong investment opportunities given the bullish outlook for silver prices. It emphasizes that a surge in silver to $30-$35 an ounce would significantly boost EBITDA margins and free cash flow for these companies, supported by expansionary monetary policies. Each company is analyzed for its financial health, production capabilities, and potential for future growth and dividends.

title: US Exim backs exports to Argentina’s YPF with credit guarantee facility
summary: The US Export-Import Bank (US Exim) has provided a $75 million credit guarantee facility to Argentina's state-backed energy company YPF. This facility, backed by a loan from Bank of America, will support YPF's capital expenditure for upstream and downstream activities, involving the purchase of equipment and services from US companies across multiple states. The deal is expected to support approximately 500 US jobs in the petroleum equipment and services industry, which has been impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Amazon and Google among big US companies pledging to hire 100,000 people from marginalized New York communities
summary: Major US companies including Amazon, Google, and Goldman Sachs have pledged to hire 100,000 people from New York City's low-income and minority communities by 2030. This initiative, called the New York Jobs CEO Council, aims to address racial and economic inequities worsened by COVID-19 by providing entry-level positions, apprenticeships, and on-the-job learning. While the effort is praised as a good start, experts emphasize the need for specific interventions like mentoring programs and performance reviews to ensure career advancement for employees from underrepresented backgrounds beyond entry-level roles.

title: Vertafore to be Acquired by Roper Technologies
summary: Vertafore, an insurtech leader, announced its acquisition by Roper Technologies, Inc. (NYSE: ROP), a diversified technology company. The acquisition, expected to close in the third quarter subject to regulatory approval, will see Roper acquire Vertafore from Bain Capital Private Equity and Vista Equity Partners. Vertafore CEO Amy Zupon will continue to lead the company, which has significantly grown its employees and customer satisfaction since 2016.

title: Warren Buffett’s Stock Portfolio Saw Massive Recovery, Big Bank and Gold Changes
summary: Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway filed its Q2 13F report, revealing significant shifts in its equity portfolio as of June 30, 2020. The portfolio saw a massive recovery in the second quarter, contributing $26.3 billion in earnings, primarily driven by investment gains. Notable changes include increased stakes in Apple and Bank of America, a new position in Barrick Gold, and reduced holdings in JPMorgan Chase, PNC, Wells Fargo, Visa, Mastercard, and a complete exit from Goldman Sachs and airline stocks.

title: Pampa Energía destina fondos de colocación para refinanciar pasivos
summary: Pampa Energía, una compañía argentina con intereses en petróleo, gas, energía eléctrica y petroquímica, emitió obligaciones negociables Clase 6 por 86,9 millones de dólares para refinanciar pasivos y financiar inversiones. La emisión, asesorada por Salaverri, Burgio & Wetzler Malbrán y Marval O’Farrell Mairal, se realizó en el mercado local y fue calificada como "AA-(arg)". Los fondos se utilizarán para refinanciar obligaciones negociables anteriores, deuda con vencimiento en 2021, inversiones y capital de trabajo.

title: Banco de Chile advierte sobre nuevo intento de estafa al cobrar el 10% de las AFP
summary: Banco de Chile has issued a warning regarding a new scam attempt targeting individuals withdrawing 10% of their AFP pension funds. Scammers are sending fake text messages claiming successful withdrawal requests and prompting users to click a link to check their balance, which is a phishing attempt. The bank advises customers to ignore these messages, never click links from unknown sources, avoid sharing personal keys, and only rely on official bank channels for information and transactions.

title: Chipotle managers refused nursing mom pumping breaks, class-action suit alleges
summary: A class-action lawsuit alleges that managers at an Arizona Chipotle violated federal law by denying a worker, Noel Hendrix, breaks to pump breast milk. Hendrix's complaint claims managers cited business demands and told her any corporate complaint would be futile, leading to visible leakage and discrimination based on sex. This incident highlights the requirements of Title VII of the Civil Rights Act and the Fair Labor Standards Act, which protect nursing mothers' rights to pump at work.

title: ADM bags $850m from Wilmar block, EB combo
summary: Archer-Daniels-Midland Co (ADM) has raised $850 million through a dual equity capital markets transaction, marking its first such move in over a decade. The deal involved a concurrent block sale of Wilmar International shares and an exchangeable bond, both linked to the same underlying stock. This strategy allowed ADM to efficiently raise significant capital.

title: Ambipar faz IPO na B3 e capta 197 milhões de dólares
summary: Ambipar, a Brazilian company specializing in waste management and disaster response, successfully completed its Initial Public Offering (IPO) on the B3 stock exchange, raising US$197 million. The offering involved 43,733,334 ordinary shares at US$4.50 per share. Ambipar plans to use the capital for international expansion through acquisitions, investments in new operational bases in Brazil, and strengthening technical cooperation alliances.

title: Banks fined for improper disclosure and charges on credit cards
summary: Canada's financial consumer watchdog has fined Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce over $1.2 million for errors that improperly charged 1.3 million credit card customers over 15 years, an issue the bank had previously disclosed and refunded for. Additionally, Canadian Western Bank and its subsidiary Canadian Western Trust were fined $200,000 each for failing to disclose non-interest costs and fees on various credit products and mortgages, affecting thousands of clients. These penalties highlight a lapse in proper disclosure and fee transparency by the sanctioned banks.

title: KBR to Buy Centauri for $800M; Stuart Bradie Quoted
summary: KBR has announced its agreement to acquire Centauri for approximately $800 million in cash, aiming to bolster its intelligence, military space, defense modernization, and cybersecurity capabilities. The acquisition will integrate Centauri into KBR's government solutions segment and is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2020. This strategic move aligns with KBR's goal of expanding its highly technical, mission-focused services and enduring customer relationships.

title: Chinese Crowdfunding, Insurance Site Waterdrop Raises $230 Million, Plans U.S. IPO
summary: Chinese online insurance technology platform Waterdrop Inc. has raised $230 million in a new funding round led by Swiss Re and Tencent Holdings. The company, valued at nearly $2 billion, plans an initial public offering in the United States as early as this year, bringing in Bank of America and Goldman Sachs to manage the float. Waterdrop, which distributes insurance policies and provides illness insurance crowdfunding, will use the new capital to invest in AI and big data initiatives for its products and services.

title: UBS to update legal structure at wealth management unit to cut costs
summary: UBS Group plans to restructure its wealth management unit by transferring large customer deposits to its primary legal entity, a project known as "Rigi." This move aims to cut costs and free up billions of dollars for loans outside Switzerland, partly reversing measures taken after the 2008 financial crisis. The restructuring is also part of a broader revamp of the wealth management business, including job cuts and managerial changes, set to be completed by 2022.

title: John Edward Mack
summary: This obituary details the life of John Edward Mack, who passed away on August 22, 2020, in Charlotte. He was a distinguished individual with a long and successful career in finance, holding senior positions at Bank of America, Shinsei Bank, and serving on numerous corporate boards. Mack was also an active alumnus of Davidson College, establishing a scholarship in his father's honor.

title: La discriminación de género impide a las mujeres en Chile conseguir préstamos bancarios
summary: A study by the Inter-American Development Bank (BID) and CAF reveals that women in Chile are 18% less likely to have loan applications approved than men, despite being more responsible with payments. This gender discrimination, often perpetuated by male executives, results in significant lost profits for banks and highlights a deep-seated bias. The research, which is unprecedented globally, suggests that eliminating this discrimination could inject an additional $12 billion into the financial system through women's loans.

title: North Charleston chemical maker Ingevity Corp. names a new CEO
summary: Ingevity Corp., a chemical manufacturer based in North Charleston, has announced the promotion of its chief financial executive, John C. Fortson, to CEO and president, effective September 1. Fortson will also join the company's board of directors and his promotion follows a six-month search for a replacement for the previous CEO. The company, one of South Carolina's largest publicly traded firms, emphasized Fortson's vision for "Ingevity 2.0" and his commitment to sustainability, customer centricity, and innovation.

title: Wells Fargo asset cap has hit bank hard
summary: The Federal Reserve's asset cap imposed on Wells Fargo in early 2018 has become a significant financial burden, costing the bank an estimated $4 billion in missed profits. This sanction, intended to address various scandals, has proven to be one of the costliest regulatory punishments, far more impactful than traditional fines. The bank's inability to grow its assets has hindered its ability to offset lower interest rates, resulting in an 18% drop in net interest income during the second quarter and a loss of over $200 billion in market value since the restriction began.

title: Chase and Capital One to close local branches
summary: Two major bank branches, Chase and Capital One, are scheduled to close their locations on Chambers Street in the coming months. The Chase branch will close in the fourth quarter of 2020, while the Capital One branch will close on October 21, 2020. This decision contributes to a broader trend of bank branch closures in New York City, drawing mixed reactions from residents.

title: Pullman Cargo refinancia deuda para enfrentar la pandemia
summary: Chilean cargo transportation company Pullman Cargo secured a $105 million refinancing deal with local banks to mitigate the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. Garrigues-Chile advised the consortium of banks in the negotiation, which involved the restructuring of debt for Pullman Cargo and its subsidiaries. This agreement is expected to help the group absorb the pandemic's effects and prepare for market recovery.

title: Banco de Chile obtiene primer lugar en ranking Merco Talento Chile 2020
summary: Banco de Chile has achieved the top position in the Merco Talento Chile 2020 ranking, recognizing it as the best company in the country for attracting and retaining talent. This marks the first time the bank has led the general ranking, while also maintaining its leadership in the Banks and Financial Institutions category for the seventh consecutive year. The achievement was highlighted by CEO Eduardo Ebensperger and Division Manager Cristián Lagos, who emphasized the bank's commitment to its employees and clients, attributing this recognition to their focus on continuous development, teamwork, and strong corporate values.

title: Banks eye layoffs as short-term crisis ends, long-term costs emerge
summary: As the immediate crisis of the pandemic subsides, U.S. banks are planning layoffs, reversing earlier pledges not to cut jobs in 2020. This shift is driven by expectations of an extended recession, rising loan losses, prolonged low-interest rates, and increased efficiency from remote work. Industry experts anticipate a 5-10% reduction in bank staff, particularly in technology, HR, and finance departments, with institutions like JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo, Standard Chartered, and HSBC already initiating or planning significant job cuts.

title: Boeing aims to increase Black employees by 20%, CEO says in memo
summary: Boeing CEO Dave Calhoun announced in a memo that the company aims to increase its Black U.S. employees by 20% and establish benchmarks for hiring people of color. These changes come amid a summer of anti-racism protests and will be guided by an internal Racial Justice think-tank. The company is also donating $10 million to social justice nonprofits following a racist incident at one of its factories.

title: CORRECTED-Banks eye layoffs as short-term crisis ends, long-term costs emerge
summary: U.S. banks, which had pledged not to cut jobs in 2020 at the pandemic's outset, are now considering layoffs due to economic recovery taking longer than expected, high unemployment, and sustained low interest rates. Consultants and industry insiders suggest a 5-10% reduction in staff at mid- and lower levels. This shift comes as remote work has demonstrated increased efficiency and banks grapple with the need to cut costs in the face of anticipated credit issues and regulatory pressure.

title: Berlusconi Holding Hires BofA Banker to Lead Its M&A Division
summary: Fininvest SpA, the investment company of former Italian Premier Silvio Berlusconi, has hired Gianluca Iuliano from Bank of America Merrill Lynch to head its strategic planning, M&A, and business development division. Iuliano, 42, is expected to join Fininvest, which is chaired by Marina Berlusconi, in mid-September. The appointment has not yet been publicly announced.

title: Stop the presses: McGraw publishing heir sells Gulf Stream house for $8M
summary: John L. McGraw, former chairman of McGraw Hill, and his wife Marjorie, sold their Gulf Stream waterfront house for $8 million to Keith E. Rowling, a managing director at Merrill Lynch. The McGraws had purchased the 6,000-square-foot property in 2006 for $7 million. Rowling is a highly ranked wealth advisor at Merrill Lynch, recognized by Forbes.

title: Global Banking Services Industry Market Analysis, Trends, and Forecasts, 2019-2024 by SpendEdge
summary: The Global Banking Services Industry market is projected to grow by over USD 1 trillion at a CAGR of 6.0% between 2019 and 2024, driven by digital technology adoption among service providers. North America and Europe are expected to be the leading spending regions. Key suppliers include JPMorgan Chase & Co., Bank of America Corp., and Wells Fargo & Co.

title: Which coding languages are used by the world’s top companies?
summary: This article examines the most popular and highest-paying coding languages used by major companies, highlighting an infographic from Flyaps that details the languages adopted by 25 Fortune 500 companies. It discusses how choices in programming languages depend on factors like speed, reliability, and scalability, and contrasts findings from other studies on popular and high-paying languages. Examples of specific companies and the languages they use are also provided.

title: Just 2 Banks, 2 CUs Still Participating in TARP Program
summary: As of September 2020, only two banks and two credit unions remained in the Troubled Asset Relief Program (TARP), which initially included 763 institutions. Carver Bancorp Inc. recently exited the program, leaving OneUnited Bank, Harbor Bank of Maryland, Berkeley-based Cooperative Center FCU, and Washington-based DC FCU as the remaining participants. The investments in these institutions are relatively small compared to the overall program, and it's possible the government could force an exit for the remaining participants.

title: Black-owned SC lender lands investment from Bank of America
summary: Bank of America has invested in Optus Bank, a Black-owned financial institution in South Carolina, as part of its $1 billion commitment to racial equality and economic opportunity. This investment gives Bank of America a 5 percent stake in Optus Bank's parent company, SCCB Financial Corp., and is one of several similar deals with minority-owned lenders aimed at increasing lending capacity in underserved communities. Optus Bank, founded in 1921, will celebrate its 100th anniversary next year and serves minority businesses and consumers.

title: Warren Buffett, Berkshire Set to Plow $550 Million Into Snowflake
summary: Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway plans to invest over $550 million in Snowflake's IPO, purchasing 3.1 million Class A shares in a private placement and an additional 4 million shares from former CEO Robert Muglia. This investment is notable given Buffett's historical aversion to tech stocks and follows other recent unusual moves by Berkshire Hathaway. Salesforce's venture arm will also invest $250 million in Snowflake.

title: Bank of America outlines $300 million investment plan for racial equality
summary: Bank of America has announced a $300 million investment as part of its broader $1 billion commitment to advance racial equality and economic opportunity. These funds will be directed towards enhancing training opportunities, specifically mentioning community colleges like Atlanta Technical College. The initiative aims to address systemic issues and foster economic empowerment within communities.

title: UBS and Barclays' Digital Settlement Coin Project Delayed
summary: The Fnality International project, backed by major banks like UBS and Barclays, aimed to create digital versions of several fiat currencies for faster and cheaper settlements. Originally slated for 2020, the project has been delayed until at least 2021 as it awaits regulatory approvals. This initiative seeks to revolutionize interbank settlements by leveraging tokenized global currencies on enterprise blockchains.

title: Bank of America backs Black-owned banks, including one in Detroit, in $300 million equality drive
summary: Bank of America has invested $50 million in three Black-owned banks, including First Independence Corp. in Detroit, as part of its $1 billion commitment to racial equality. This initiative is part of a larger $300 million allocation that includes job programs, community outreach, and direct equity investments in Black- and Hispanic-owned businesses. The goal is to create jobs, increase lending to minority-owned businesses, and build wealth within these communities.

title: Citi names Jane Fraser as first female CEO of big Wall St bank
summary: Citigroup announced Jane Fraser will succeed Michael Corbat as CEO in February, making her the first woman to lead a major Wall Street bank. Fraser, currently head of Citi's global consumer banking division, has a distinguished career in the financial industry and her promotion was widely anticipated. This move is seen as a significant step for diversity in finance.

title: Fidelity National Financial Prices $600 Million Of 2.450% Notes Due March 15, 2031
summary: Fidelity National Financial (FNF) has priced an issuance of $600 million of 2.450% senior notes due March 15, 2031. The notes were priced at 99.642% of their principal amount to yield 2.489% per annum, with interest paid semi-annually. The net proceeds will be used to repay outstanding indebtedness related to the FGL Holdings acquisition and for general corporate purposes.

title: Lightspeed Announces Pricing of Initial Public Offering in The United States
summary: Lightspeed POS Inc. announced the pricing of its initial public offering in the United States and Canada, with underwriters agreeing to purchase 10 million subordinate voting shares from the Company and 1.65 million from Caisse de dépôt et placement du Québec at US$30.50 per share. The shares are expected to begin trading on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol "LSPD" on September 11, 2020. The offering aims to strengthen Lightspeed's financial position and support its growth strategies.

title: Bank of America Adopts AI, Finds ‘More Significant Credit Stresses’ From Covid-19
summary: Bank of America is now using artificial intelligence, specifically natural language processing, to analyze corporate credit and predict loan defaults. This AI approach has identified "more significant credit stresses" in COVID-19 impacted sectors like energy, transportation, and media compared to the bank's traditional models. While the AI increases the overall default forecast slightly, the bank plans to observe its behavior independently before full integration.

title: Who’s the Next Woman to Take Over on Wall Street? (Published 2020)
summary: Following Jane Fraser's historic appointment as CEO of Citigroup, becoming the first woman to lead a major Wall Street bank, this article profiles several women who are potential candidates to break banking's glass ceiling. It highlights executives like Marianne Lake, Jennifer Piepszak, and Cathy Bessant, who are seen as top contenders at their current companies, as well as rising stars such as Thasunda Duckett, Susan Huang, and Dina Powell McCormick.

title: Citigroup has just appointed the first female CEO of a Wall Street bank
summary: Jane Fraser has been appointed the next chief executive officer of Citigroup, making her the first woman to lead a major Wall Street bank. Her promotion is seen as a significant step towards greater gender diversity in the financial industry, where only a small percentage of top leadership roles are held by women. Fraser's career spans various critical roles within Citigroup and is credited with helping the bank recover after the financial crisis.

title: Coca-Cola FEMSA recauda más de 700 millones de dólares con bono verde
summary: Coca-Cola FEMSA, the largest Coca-Cola bottler by sales volume, successfully issued its inaugural green bond in the international market, raising $705 million. This issuance, with a 12-year term and a coupon rate of 1.850%, is noted as the largest of its kind for a Latin American issuer and will fund green projects related to climate change, water care, and circular economy initiatives. Legal counsel for the transaction included Cleary Gottlieb Steen & Hamilton for the issuer and Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom, alongside Galicia Abogados, for the underwriters BofA Securities, J.P. Morgan Securities, and Morgan Stanley.

title: -Citigroup hires BofA executive to run institutional client group compliance
summary: Citigroup Inc has announced the hiring of Jennifer Taylor, a Bank of America Corp executive, to lead compliance for its Institutional Clients Group (ICG). Taylor will commence her role as chief compliance officer for the ICG in December, based in the UK, bringing extensive product knowledge and a track record of embedding compliance culture. Her appointment comes as regulators are scrutinizing Citi's operations following a significant error involving nearly $1 billion of its funds.

title: Weekly S&P 500 Chart Storm: All Eyes On Mega Cap Tech Stocks
summary: This article analyzes the S&P 500's recent pullback, highlighting the impact on mega-cap tech stocks and examining various market indicators. It delves into sentiment, seasonality, and the implications of the upcoming US presidential election on market trends, suggesting potential continued volatility. The author also discusses the shift towards intangible assets in corporate balance sheets and the declining equity risk premium.

title: Deutsche Bank appoints Loïc Voide and Kees Hoving as Co-CEOs for the Middle East and Africa
summary: Deutsche Bank announced the appointment of Loïc Voide and Kees Hoving as Co-Chief Executive Officers for the Middle East and Africa (MEA), based in Dubai. Voide will also head the International Private Bank (IPB) MEA and serve as Chief Country Officer for the UAE, while Hoving will oversee the Corporate Bank MEA and Corporate Coverage MEA. These appointments aim to leverage synergies and enhance client services in a region identified for significant growth by Deutsche Bank.

title: Leading global advisory, broking and solutions company
summary: J.P. Morgan helped Willis Towers Watson create an innovative Treasury Centre in the Netherlands, significantly improving visibility and transparency in their treasury function. This solution addressed challenges arising from the merger of Willis and Towers Watson and the acquisition of Gras Savoy, establishing an in-house bank for foreign exchange and cash concentration. The new structure has led to improved working capital, optimized liquidity through cross-border sweeps, and a scalable framework for future growth.

title: PNC Bank Appoints New Regional Leadership for Washington State and Portland
summary: PNC Bank announced new regional leadership appointments for its Washington State and Portland markets. Laura MacNeil will serve as regional president for Washington State, Jennifer Hare as head of Corporate Banking for Washington State, and JT Hutchinson as regional president and head of Corporate Banking for Portland. These appointments are part of PNC's strategic national expansion and aim to strengthen its presence and service delivery in the Pacific Northwest.

title: JFrog Announces Pricing of Its Initial Public Offering
summary: JFrog Ltd. announced the pricing of its initial public offering of 11,568,218 ordinary shares at $44.00 per share. Of these, 8,000,000 shares are offered by JFrog and 3,568,218 by existing shareholders. The shares were expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol "FROG" on September 16, 2020.

title: ‘It has to have an impact’: What Citi’s new CEO means for other women on Wall Street
summary: Jane Fraser's appointment as CEO of Citigroup marks a historic milestone as the first woman to lead a major Wall Street bank, sparking optimism about the future for other senior women in finance. This promotion, while significant, highlights that increasing female representation in top executive roles is a slow process requiring intentional effort from companies and boards. Despite progress, there is still a considerable journey ahead to achieve true gender diversity, especially for women of color, in corporate leadership.

title: CEO Kelly King talks Truist Financial's strategy for merger-related cost cuts
summary: Truist Financial Corp. CEO Kelly King discusses the company's strategy for achieving cost cuts related to its merger. The financial institution is nearing the end of its first year post-merger and is focused on optimizing expenses.

title: ¿Cómo crear una empresa en Colombia? Hazlo todo digital
summary: This article explains how to create a company in Colombia digitally through the Ventanilla Única Empresarial (VUE). The VUE simplifies the process by unifying all required steps for registering a business, from mercantile registration to tax and social security affiliations, making it faster and more cost-effective for entrepreneurs. It highlights the platform's features, including information on business types, name verification, and digital affiliation to ARL and health services.

title: Why are bank branches gobbling up Charlotte’s hottest real estate?
summary: Despite a national trend of bank branch closures since the recession and increased digital banking, new bank branches, including Fifth Third Bank and JPMorgan Chase, are rapidly opening in Charlotte's fast-growing and expensive neighborhoods. Banks view these high-tech, modern branches as crucial for connecting with customers, building loyalty, and attracting newcomers to the competitive Charlotte banking market even as they acknowledge a shift towards digital transactions for basic needs. The article also notes how even Bank of America and Wells Fargo are adapting their physical presence, with BofA modernizing existing centers and Wells Fargo opening "digital-first" Express Centers.

title: CBK bars digital mobile lenders from CRB listing
summary: The Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) has prohibited unregulated digital mobile lenders from submitting names of loan defaulters to credit reference bureaus (CRBs) and has halted the blacklisting of borrowers with debts under Sh1,000. This decision comes in response to widespread public complaints about the misuse of the credit information sharing mechanism by digital lenders. Consequently, only regulated financial institutions can now blacklist defaulters, and a stimulus package introduced during the pandemic has suspended CRB listing for defaults from April 1 for six months, requiring clearance for those previously blacklisted for amounts below Sh1,000.

title: Morgan Stanley Narrows Recruiting-Attrition Gap, Hires $5 Mln UBS Duo
summary: Morgan Stanley is close to reversing its net outflow of financial advisors, with CFO Jon Pruzan highlighting that net recruiting is now "much closer to zero." The firm recently hired a $4.8 million producing duo from UBS, Gerald Crum and Darren Hugo, as part of its selective re-entry into the recruiting market. This increased focus on recruiting high-producing advisors aims to make Morgan Stanley a "destination of choice" for financial advisors again.

title: Bank with the largest market share in Atlanta changes for the first time since 2005
summary: Bank of America has taken the top spot for the largest market share of deposits in the metro Atlanta area in 2020, marking the first change since 2005. This shift was revealed by newly released data from the FDIC and reflects the impact of recent mergers and acquisitions within the banking industry.

title: Old-School Regions Bank Lobby Set to Close
summary: Regions Bank is closing the lobby of its two-story branch at 400 W. Capitol Ave. in Little Rock, effective November 6th, and relocating branch operations to the second floor of the same building. This move signifies the end of another spacious old-school bank lobby, following a similar downsizing by Bank of America in 2018. The bank, headquartered in Birmingham, Alabama, reported a second-quarter loss of $214 million, primarily due to an $882 million increase in its provision for potential losses.

title: Pittsburgh becomes a battleground for national banking powerhouses
summary: Pittsburgh is becoming a battleground for national banking giants Bank of America and JPMorgan Chase, which are expanding their physical presence in the market historically dominated by PNC. While PNC still holds the largest market share, its dominance has slightly decreased. Smaller community banks in the area are relying on strong customer relationships and personalized service to compete against the national powerhouses, who offer a more complete product suite.

title: Truist changes landscape of local banking
summary: Truist Bank, formed from the merger of SunTrust and BB&T, has become the third-largest bank in the Tampa-St. Petersburg-Clearwater metropolitan market by deposit market share. This shift, reported by the FDIC, moved long-time No. 3 Wells Fargo Bank down to fourth place. The local banking market overall saw a strengthening, with an increase in institutions, offices, and total deposits as of June 30, 2020.

title: Banks bludgeoned by $2 trillion suspicious transfers bombshell
summary: A cache of leaked documents revealed that several major global banks, including HSBC, Standard Chartered, Deutsche Bank, and JPMorgan Chase, transferred over $2 trillion in suspect funds between 1999 and 2017. The FinCen files sparked fresh concerns about money laundering and led to calls for industry reforms, with some banks' shares falling significantly. Despite the revelations, some analysts believe the reports may not have a lasting impact on the banking sector, while banks stressed their efforts to enhance compliance.

title: Byline Bank to Consolidate 20% of Branches
summary: Byline Bancorp, the parent company of Byline Bank, plans to consolidate 11 of its 57 full-service branch offices, representing about 20% of its network. This consolidation, starting December 31, 2020, is a response to customers' increased adoption of digital banking channels during the COVID-19 pandemic. The bank aims to focus its remaining branch network on sub-markets with significant growth opportunities and where a physical presence adds the most value to new business development.

title: Bank of America making presence known in central Ohio
summary: Bank of America has rapidly expanded its presence in central Ohio, becoming the fifth-largest bank in the region by deposits within a year of opening its first Columbus office. This growth is attributed to its focus on supporting clients and the community, with plans for further expansion across Ohio. The article also notes a significant increase in total deposits across central Ohio, indicating consumers and businesses are hoarding cash due to economic uncertainty.

title: Goldman Sachs names new heads of global M&A
summary: Goldman Sachs has appointed Stephan Feldgoise and Mark Sorrell as co-heads of its global mergers and acquisitions practice. They succeed Michael Carr, Dusty Philip, and Gilberto Pozzi, who will now serve as co-chairs of the bank’s global M&A unit. The appointments come as global deal volumes are down almost 40% year-to-date, despite a recent uptick in activity.

title: ODNI Blamed Syrian Banks, but Did the West’s Deutsche Bank Facilitate ISIL Finances in Mosul?
summary: This article investigates suspicious money transfers totaling billions of dollars through Deutsche Bank and Bank of America to Iraqi banks during the peak of ISIS's control in Iraq. It questions why these transfers were permitted despite ISIL's financial activities and sanctions, especially given Deutsche Bank's history of fines for money laundering and sanctions violations. The report highlights the bank's deep ties with the Iraqi government and Kurdistan, scrutinizing its continued involvement despite recurring controversies.

title: JD.com Healthcare Unit Plans Hong Kong IPO
summary: JD.com's healthcare division, JD Health, plans to spin off and list in Hong Kong, following JD.com's own secondary listing. This move is part of an ongoing trend of U.S.-traded Chinese companies seeking listings closer to home. JD Health aims to raise at least $1 billion through the IPO and has already secured over $830 million in Series B financing from Hillhouse Capital.

title: HSBC Stock Pummelled by Financial Crimes Report, China ‘Unreliable Entity’ List
summary: HSBC's Hong Kong-listed shares plunged to a decade-low after reports of the bank's involvement in facilitating criminal activities and concerns it might be added to China's "Unreliable Entity List." The bank was named in a report by the International Consortium of Investigative Journalists for allegedly aiding a massive Ponzi scheme, even while on probation with U.S. regulators. Additionally, investors fear potential sanctions from the Chinese government due to claims HSBC provided information related to the detention of Huawei's CFO.

title: Gold prices are slumping – could they fall further?
summary: Gold prices have been slumping after reaching record highs in early August, leading investors to question if this is a temporary dip or a sharper decline. While some banks predict higher prices, a resurgent dollar has put pressure on gold, despite expansive Federal Reserve policies. Several factors, including dollar dominance, plateauing real rates, technical trading signals, ETF investor behavior, and the impending volatile U.S. election, will influence gold's future trajectory.

title: Two locals make annual list of top performing U.S. small-cap banks and thrifts
summary: Two local banks, Meridian and Parke, have been named to investment firm Piper Sandler’s annual list of top-performing U.S. small-cap banks and thrifts. This exclusive list includes only 35 U.S. banks with a market cap below $2.5 billion that meet rigorous criteria related to growth, profitability, credit quality, and capital strength.

title: Keep Calm and Stay Long: This Gold Price Correction Is Normal and Healthy
summary: Frank Holmes argues that the recent gold price correction is normal and healthy, attributing it to the metal's inherent volatility and short-term market dynamics. He highlights significant inflows into gold-backed ETFs during the dip, negative real rates, and unprecedented money printing as factors supporting gold's long-term outlook. The article also discusses the robust economic activity in Texas, advancements in the precious metals streaming industry, and other market updates.

title: Mapa del sector bancario: las crisis fomentan una mayor concentración del mercado
summary: The article discusses the increasing concentration in the Spanish banking sector, driven significantly by the 2008 financial crisis and the current economic impact of the coronavirus. It highlights how the number of banks and savings banks has drastically reduced through mergers, acquisitions, and absorptions, leading to a few large entities dominating the market. Experts suggest this trend will continue, with implications for employment, branch closures, and customer services, though opinions vary on the impact on competition.

title: Morgan Stanley Hires $265-Mln Asset Merrill Team in Florida
summary: Morgan Stanley has hired a four-person team from Merrill Lynch in Ponte Vedra Beach, Florida, managing $265 million in client assets. This move is part of Morgan Stanley's aggressive hiring efforts, contrasting with Merrill Lynch's continued freeze on experienced advisor recruitment. The article highlights the ongoing shift of advisors between major wealth management firms.

title: PNC opens first retail branch in Greater Boston
summary: PNC Bank has opened its first retail branch in Greater Boston, located at 55 Boylston St. in Chestnut Hill. This is the first of five planned locations for the Pittsburgh-based banking giant in the region for 2020, signaling an expansion into the Boston market.

title: Truist, BofA among banks with largest Orlando market share
summary: The article discusses how Truist and Bank of America hold the largest banking market shares in metro Orlando. The merger of BB&T and SunTrust was a key factor in establishing Truist as one of the largest banks in the market. The content highlights the competitive landscape of the banking sector in the Orlando area.

title: IRSA buscará reestructurar su deuda en dólares
summary: IRSA will present a proposal to its creditors to restructure its debt of US$181 million, which matures on November 15, adhering to BCRA regulations. This comes as the BCRA has called on companies with foreign currency debt exceeding US$1 million monthly to present restructuring plans. The proposal must include a maximum 40% access to the exchange market and a two-year extension for the remaining payments.

title: Goldman Sachs to go ahead with "modest" job cuts after coronavirus pause
summary: Goldman Sachs Group Inc plans to proceed with a "modest number of layoffs" after pausing job cuts due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The bank is reportedly looking to cut about 400 jobs, or roughly 1% of its workforce, primarily targeting back-office roles as part of an earlier reorganisation aimed at improving efficiency. This comes as the U.S. Federal Reserve curbed big bank capital distributions through the end of the year, affecting share buybacks and dividends for major banks.

title: Lithia Announces Pricing of Public Offering of Common Stock
summary: Lithia Motors, Inc. announced the pricing of its public offering of 3,181,819 shares of Class A common stock at $220.00 per share, with an option for underwriters to purchase additional shares. Concurrently, Lithia announced a private offering of $550 million aggregate principal amount of 4.375% senior notes due 2031, an increase from the previously announced size. The offering is expected to close on October 5, 2020.

title: Bank of America Stands by Pledge of No Layoffs This Year
summary: Bank of America plans to uphold its promise of no staff layoffs in 2020, as stated by CEO Brian Moynihan. This commitment stands in contrast to several other major banks, including Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase, which have resumed job cuts amidst the pandemic. The bank will continue to manage its headcount through attrition alone.

title: As Goldman, JPMorgan resume cuts, Bank of America reiterates no-layoff vow
summary: As Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase resume job cuts, Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan reiterated the bank's commitment to no layoffs for the year. This comes as other major banks like Citi and Wells Fargo have also restarted workforce reductions, with the industry on pace to cut over 80,000 positions in 2020. Moynihan highlighted Bank of America's strategy of relying on attrition and its progress in diversity initiatives.

title: KKR-backed Academy Sports and Outdoors raises $203 million in IPO - source
summary: Academy Sports and Outdoors, backed by KKR, raised $203 million in its IPO by selling shares at $13 each, below its target range of $15-$17. The IPO valued the company at $1.1 billion, despite a surge in demand for at-home leisure activities during the coronavirus pandemic which significantly boosted its e-commerce sales. Shares are expected to begin trading on Nasdaq under the symbol "ASO".

title: USAA sues PNC over alleged infringement of mobile deposit tech
summary: USAA has sued PNC in federal court, alleging that PNC infringed on two patents related to mobile check deposit technology. This lawsuit follows USAA's prior nine-figure judgments against Wells Fargo for similar patent infringements. USAA seeks reasonable compensation for the use of its remote deposit capture patents, which are also used by over 6,500 financial institutions that utilize Mitek Systems' technology.

title: Lightsource bp Secures Financing on Bighorn Solar Project in Colorado
summary: Lightsource bp has secured $285 million in financing for its Bighorn Solar project in Pueblo, Colorado. The project, located on the Evraz Rocky Mountain Steel mill property, will supply power to the steel mill via a long-term contract with Xcel Energy, helping to preserve 1,000 local jobs and support Colorado's renewable energy goals. Construction has begun and is expected to create 300 direct jobs, with commercial operation slated for late 2021.

title: Bank of America, Wells Fargo and Truist remain deposit leaders in Sarasota-Manatee
summary: Bank of America maintained its lead as the largest bank by customer deposits in the Sarasota-Manatee region, marking its tenth consecutive year at the top. Despite its merger, Truist Bank narrowly missed unseating Wells Fargo for the second position, with only a $90.3 million difference in deposits. The region saw an overall increase of $3.1 billion in deposits, partly attributed to investors seeking the security of insured bank deposits.

title: Bank of America wades into digital financial planning space
summary: Bank of America is launching "Life Plan," a new digital financial planning tool to compete with fintech companies. This tool allows customers to set financial goals and receive personalized recommendations by leveraging existing client data, making financial planning accessible beyond high-net worth individuals. The initiative aims to provide a fuller financial picture to customers and potentially increase engagement with the bank's services.

title: Today In Digital-First Banking: BoA Launches Life Plan; United Airlines, Chase Roll Out United Gateway Card
summary: Bank of America has introduced its Life Plan program for digital financial planning. Concurrently, United Airlines and Chase Card Services have launched a new no-annual-fee United Gateway credit card, offering travel miles for various purchases. Additionally, NCR Corp. has upgraded its ATM operating software with the "Activate Enterprise NextGen ATM infrastructure," aiming to integrate ATMs further into the digital age.

title: What's next for TD after completing Ameritrade sale to Charles Schwab
summary: TD Bank has completed the sale of Ameritrade to Charles Schwab, resulting in TD holding a 13.5% stake in Charles Schwab. After an eight-month holding period, analysts believe TD may sell this stake to fund the acquisition of another U.S. bank. This move could significantly alter TD's strategic presence in the American banking market.

title: Morgan Stanley’s Eaton Vance Acquisition Could Mean More Asset Management Mergers Are Coming
summary: Morgan Stanley is acquiring asset management firm Eaton Vance for $7 billion, increasing its assets under management to $1.2 trillion and solidifying a trend of consolidation in the asset management industry. Analysts believe more mergers are likely as firms seek to fill product gaps and benefit from historically low valuations. This acquisition follows Morgan Stanley's earlier purchase of E-Trade, indicating a strategic shift towards expanding its investment management business.

title: Bank of America enters the small-dollar loan fray
summary: Bank of America announced it will begin offering "Balance Assist" loans of up to $500 for a flat $5 fee. This initiative, rolling out in January and expanding nationwide in early 2021, aims to provide an alternative to high-interest payday loans, aligning with recent regulatory encouragement for banks to enter the small-dollar lending space. The loans can be repaid in three equal installments over 90 days and consumers can only take out one loan at a time.

title: Bank of America's plan in Columbus: Keep going
summary: Bank of America is continuing its expansion in Central Ohio, having opened its first Columbus branch on Morse Road in July 2019. The bank's market leader discussed plans for further growth in the region, focusing on a technology-centered design to attract customers.

title: Symcor helps to accelerate digital transformation in the COVID-19 era and beyond
summary: Symcor, a joint venture of Canada's top financial institutions, played a crucial role in helping the Canadian financial services sector respond to the COVID-19 pandemic by quickly deploying fraud detection solutions and digitizing operations. The company specializes in payment processing, customer communications, and fraud detection, assisting large organizations across various sectors. Symcor anticipates a continued acceleration of digital transformation and aims to be a key player in the future of open banking in Canada, ensuring data security and accessibility.

title: Actualización: Cemex recauda fondos en emisión internacional para pagar deuda
summary: Cemex, a Mexican cement company, issued $1 billion in senior guaranteed notes in the international market at a 5.200% rate with a 10-year term to pay down debt and for general corporate purposes. This private placement, which closed on September 17, involved several legal advisors for Cemex and the initial purchasers. The company plans to list these notes on the Irish Stock Exchange for trading on Euronext Dublin, following a similar bond issue in June.

title: China’s Ping An-Backed Lufax Files for $3 Billion U.S. IPO
summary: Lufax Holding Ltd., a Chinese online wealth management platform backed by Ping An Insurance Group, has filed for a U.S. IPO aiming to raise about $3 billion. This move comes as the company shifts away from its P2P lending origins and follows another Ping An-backed fintech listing (OneConnect Financial Technology), amidst a backdrop of rising U.S.-China tensions. The company reported a net profit of 7.27 billion yuan for the first half of 2020.

title: Eastern Bank Prepares for $1.8B IPO
summary: Eastern Bank, the oldest mutual bank in the US, is set to go public on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on October 14, with shares launching at $10 each, valuing the company at nearly $1.8 billion. The capital raised from the IPO will be used for technology investments, new services, and acquisitions in banking and insurance. Additionally, former CEO Ken LaRoe announced plans to launch Climate First Bank in Florida, focusing on an impact-based "triple bottom line" approach.

title: Credit Suisse Hires Veteran Meissner to Lead New Unit Serving Wealthy Clients
summary: Credit Suisse has hired Christian Meissner, a former veteran of Bank of America and Goldman Sachs, to lead a new unit aimed at connecting its wealthiest clients with its investment bank. Meissner will serve as co-head of international wealth-management investment banking advisory and vice chairman of investment banking. This strategic move is intended to enhance revenue from affluent clients by offering them exclusive access to deals and business opportunities through Credit Suisse's investment banking services, amidst increasing competition in banking the ultra-rich.

title: Americold acquires Agro Merchants Group in $1.74 billion deal
summary: Americold Realty Trust has announced its acquisition of Agro Merchants Group, the world's fourth-largest temperature-controlled operator, for $1.74 billion.
