title: Banks Fined for Price-Rigging
summary: Mexico's antitrust authority COFECE fined several major banks, including Barclays, Deutsche Bank, Santander, Citibanamex, Bank of America, BBVA, and JP Morgan, a total of over MX$35 million (US$1.74 million) for collusion on the peso bond market between 2010 and 2013. The fines concluded a four-year investigation that uncovered 142 illegal agreements to manipulate prices and negatively impacted the market by MX$29.39 million (US$1.46 million). Despite the penalties, the fines represent a fraction of what the banks could have faced, especially when compared to similar fines imposed by European and US regulators.

title: Capital One Fined Millions for Ineffective Money-Laundering Protections
summary: Capital One was fined $390 million by FinCEN for willfully failing to maintain an effective anti-money laundering program, stemming from its dealings with high-risk check-cashing businesses from 2008 to 2014. Despite warnings and internal assessments, the bank failed to detect and report suspicious activities, including thousands of suspicious activity reports and over 50,000 currency transaction reports totaling more than $16 billion. Capital One has since paid the penalty, enhanced its AML program, and resolved the matter related to a now-defunct business unit.

title: Foley-backed SPAC agrees to $7.3 billion deal with Blackstone's Alight
summary: A blank-check company backed by investor Bill Foley has agreed to take Alight Solutions LLC, a U.S. benefits services provider owned by Blackstone Group, public through a $7.3 billion deal. Foley Trasimene Acquisition Corp will list Alight on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol "ALIT." This agreement follows a previous deal where Blackstone and CVC Capital Partners merged Paysafe Group with another Foley Trasimene SPAC.

title: Obituary: PennyMac founder Stanford Kurland
summary: Stanford Kurland, founder of PennyMac Financial Services, passed away at age 68 from complications related to COVID-19 and brain cancer. Kurland had a significant impact on the mortgage industry, previously serving in key roles at Countrywide Financial before founding PennyMac, which grew to become a major player in residential mortgage lending and servicing.

title: NCR and Cardtronics Announce Definitive Acquisition Agreement at $39.00 Per Share
summary: NCR Corporation has announced a definitive agreement to acquire Cardtronics for $39.00 per share in an all-cash transaction valued at approximately $2.5 billion, including debt. This acquisition aims to accelerate NCR's "NCR-as-a-Service" strategy, shift its revenue mix towards software, services, and recurring revenue, and expand opportunities in payments. The transaction is expected to be accretive to NCR's non-GAAP EPS in the first full year post-closing and is anticipated to generate $100-$120 million in run rate operating cost synergies by the end of 2022.

title: UK banks freeze accounts to claw back ill-gotten Bounce Back loans
summary: UK banks, including HSBC, Barclays, NatWest, and Lloyds Banking Group, have started seizing business accounts to recover fraudulently obtained Bounce Back loans. These loans, part of a scheme to support small businesses during COVID-19, total £43.5bn, but an estimated £26bn may not be repaid due to fraud and defaults. Banks are using a legal tactic to reclaim funds, citing clauses that allow them to take money from current accounts without consent, though these actions typically follow an investigation.

title: The largest bank in Massachusetts is awarding $750 cash bonuses to employees as pandemic continues
summary: Bank of America is distributing $750 cash bonuses to eligible employees earning up to $100,000 annually, and stock grants to those earning between $100,001 and $500,000, as a gesture of support during the ongoing pandemic. The initiative will benefit 97% of its workforce, totaling over 206,000 employees. This follows previous actions by the bank, including raising its minimum wage to $20 per hour and providing supplemental pay for certain workers.

title: Jude Pinto, Former President, Intria Items Inc.; SVP Retail Client Services at CIBC joins Perativ as a Senior Advisor
summary: Jude Pinto, former President of Intria Items Inc. and SVP of Retail Client Services at CIBC, has joined Perativ as a Senior Advisor. Perativ offers a SaaS platform for retail banks to optimize cash forecasting and compliance in ATM and branch distribution networks. Pinto brings over 25 years of experience in retail bank operations and cash distribution leadership, which he will leverage to enhance Perativ's global services.

title: Bank of America sets aside $150M for minority financial institutions as part of previous $1B, four-year pledge
summary: Bank of America has allocated $150 million towards minority financial institutions, as part of a larger $1 billion, four-year commitment. This initiative aims to foster economic opportunity. The announcement provides more details on how the bank is deploying its previously announced pledge.

title: The LBO Value Equation
summary: This article explains the LBO value equation, detailing how private equity firms identify and value potential leveraged buyout targets. It outlines the characteristics that make a company attractive for an LBO, such as low leverage and stable cash flow, and illustrates the valuation process with real-world examples like Fidelity National Information Services. The content also provides a method for investors to spot potential LBO candidates and value the upside.

title: Morgan Stanley Hires $2.6-Mln Merrill Lifers in Maryland
summary: Morgan Stanley has hired Gregory Blair and Peter J. Della-Croce, a team from Merrill Lynch in Maryland, who were generating $2.6 million in annual revenue. This move continues Morgan Stanley's strategy of recruiting experienced brokers, contrasting with Merrill Lynch's focus on retaining existing advisors and hiring novices. The article also notes other recent advisor movements, including a team leaving Morgan Stanley for Janney Montgomery Scott.

title: U.S. private prison revenue under pressure from new Biden rules
summary: President Biden's new executive order targeting private prisons could cost CoreCivic and GEO Group, the two largest U.S. private prison companies, up to a quarter of their combined revenue, equating to about $1 billion annually. The order applies to federal contracts with the Justice Department, affecting Bureau of Prisons and U.S. Marshals Service facilities, but not those under the Department of Homeland Security, such as ICE facilities. This policy shift exacerbates financial pressures already faced by these companies due to declining occupancy during the Trump administration and a growing reluctance from major Wall Street banks to finance the industry.

title: GameStop stock market surge captures attention, enriches Michigan billionaire Donald Foss
summary: The article details the significant surge in GameStop's stock price, highlighting how it substantially increased the wealth of Michigan billionaire Donald Foss, who held a 5.3% stake. It describes the phenomenon as a battle between day traders and Wall Street short sellers, driven by activity on Reddit, and notes the skepticism of financial analysts regarding the company's underlying fundamentals. The piece also mentions the broader market impact, the involvement of figures like Elon Musk, and warnings about the irrationality of the market.

title: Bank of America's Pittsburgh market president taking role in Houston
summary: Brian Ludwick, who has been Bank of America's Pittsburgh market president since December 2017, is taking on a new role as market executive in Houston for the bank. This move was announced on January 28, 2021.

title: Bank of America's Pittsburgh market president leaving
summary: Bank of America's Pittsburgh market president, Brian Ludwick, is leaving his current role to take on a new post in Houston, Texas. Ludwick was the first Pittsburgh market president for Bank of America, and a successor is expected to be named soon.

title: Bank of America’s New Managing Directors Are Less White, Male
summary: Bank of America Corp. announced the appointment of 279 new managing directors, with a significant push for diversity reflected in the selections. Approximately half of the new managing directors are women or people of color, according to a person familiar with the matter. This move highlights the bank's commitment to increasing diversity within its leadership ranks, with 86 of the new managing directors coming from sales and trading.

title: BPI AMTC launches “Wealth Radio” podcast channel on Spotify — Technology
summary: BPI Asset Management and Trust Corporation (AMTC) has launched "Wealth Radio" on Spotify, a podcast channel designed to provide accessible financial education to a wider Filipino audience. The initiative aims to help Filipinos navigate their finances and investment journeys through bite-sized content, expert interviews, and market updates. BPI AMTC president Sheila Marie U. Tan emphasized that the podcast seeks to engage younger Filipinos and demystify investing concepts, leveraging the popularity of audio listening in the Philippines.

title: BofA’s Merrill Raises Margin to 100% to Trade Certain Stocks
summary: Bank of America Corp.'s Merrill Lynch raised margin requirements to 100% for wealth-management and self-directed brokerage clients to trade certain stocks. This move comes as financial firms impose limits amidst significant price volatility, which was sparked by investors on social media platforms. Typically, stock trading margins are around 30%, but these can fluctuate based on the concentration of client holdings.

title: Bank of America executive on how bank is drawing customers to digital services
summary: Bank of America's head of digital, David Tyrie, stated that the pandemic significantly accelerated the bank's digital banking goals. The article highlights BofA's success in attracting customers to its digital services, attributing this largely to changes brought about by the pandemic.

title: Stifel Nabs Merrill Team Managing $1.35 Billion in Dallas
summary: Stifel has successfully recruited a Merrill Lynch team from Dallas managing $1.35 billion in assets, marking its largest hire by assets in over a year. The team, including four brokers and a junior advisor, generated around $4.6 million in annual production and cited Stifel's client-focused approach over Merrill Lynch's bank-driven objectives as their reason for moving. This move highlights Stifel's robust recruiting efforts in a competitive market, as noted by CEO Ron Kruszewski.

title: Ventas Closes $2.75B Credit Facility
summary: Ventas, Inc., a Chicago-based healthcare REIT, successfully closed a new four-year $2.75-billion unsecured credit facility, which was oversubscribed by 24 financial institutions. This facility enhances Ventas's liquidity, extends debt maturities, and improves borrowing costs, with nearly $2.7 billion of available borrowing capacity and a $1-billion accordion feature. BofA Securities and JPMorgan Chase Bank served as joint bookrunners.

title: Pat Chiefalo departing as head of BlackRock’s iShares Canada
summary: Pat Chiefalo, a prominent figure in Canada's ETF industry and head of BlackRock's iShares Canada, is leaving the company on February 5th. Chiefalo played a significant role in the growth of ETFs in Canada, joining BlackRock in 2014 and taking over iShares Canada in 2017. His departure comes as BlackRock strives to maintain its market share in the increasingly competitive Canadian ETF landscape, where it has partnered with RBC to manage over $80.4 billion in ETF assets.

title: Wire Wars: Morgan Stanley Hires $500 Million-Asset Merrill Team in NJ
summary: Morgan Stanley Wealth Management recruited a Merrill Lynch team managing $500 million in client assets, comprising Todd C. Gray and Rosa M. Quartuci, along with client associate Janyve Almanzar. This move is part of a trend after Morgan Stanley re-entered the recruiting market, often drawing from Merrill Lynch, which has seen several veteran departures. The article highlights Morgan Stanley's increased advisor count and Merrill Lynch's challenges in retaining brokers despite its Protocol membership.

title: Tech company plans to double staff as it moves HQ to Calgary
summary: A Vancouver-based tech company, mCloud Technologies Corp., is relocating its head office to downtown Calgary, where office vacancy rates are at a record high. The company, which uses artificial intelligence to mitigate energy waste, plans to double its Alberta staff, seeking chemical and mechanical engineers, as well as finance, sales, and marketing professionals. CEO Russ McMeekin cited Calgary's talent pool, proximity to innovative oil and gas clients, and favorable space costs as key factors for the move.

title: BBVA accepts an offer to sell Holvi to Keru Fintech Investments
summary: BBVA has agreed to sell its Finnish neobank Holvi to Keru Fintech Investments, a new company founded by Holvi's co-founder Tuomas Toivonen. Holvi will continue its operations in European markets under new leadership. Concurrently, BBVA announced a new investment of up to $150 million in Propel, bringing its total investment to over $400 million, emphasizing its commitment to digital transformation and collaboration with startups.

title: Bank stocks jump as yields rise, but one trader says questions remain about the group longer term
summary: Bank stocks have seen a significant short-term boost due to rising bond yields and the prospect of further fiscal stimulus, with the Financial Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLF) and SPDR S&P Bank ETF (KBE) showing strong gains. However, Mark Newton of Newton Advisors suggests that for a sustained longer-term rally, the sector needs to break through key resistance levels. Conversely, Chad Morganlander of Washington Crossing Advisors is overweight financials, citing improving net interest margins, credit growth, declining loan loss provisions, and robust buybacks and dividend growth as reasons for optimism.

title: As Silver Mania Fades, Focus on the Fundamentals, 'SLV'
summary: As the initial excitement around Reddit users driving up silver prices dwindles, investors are encouraged to refocus on the fundamentals of silver. The iShares Silver Trust (SLV) is highlighted as a suitable ETF for exposure to silver bullion, offering portfolio diversification and inflation protection. Bank of America remains bullish on silver, forecasting prices could reach $35, with a potential spike to $50, despite recent volatility.

title: Vor Biopharma Announces Pricing of Initial Public Offering
summary: Vor Biopharma announced the pricing of its initial public offering of 9,828,017 shares of common stock at $18.00 per share, expecting to raise approximately $176.9 million in gross proceeds. The shares are anticipated to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Market under the ticker symbol "VOR" on February 5, 2021, with the offering expected to close on February 9, 2021. Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC, Evercore ISI, Barclays, and Stifel are acting as joint book-running managers.

title: Tackling Prison Profiteers Will Take More Than Banning Private Prisons
summary: President Biden's executive order to phase out federal private prisons is a positive step, but it overlooks the significant issue of private immigration detention centers. These facilities, which house over 70% of individuals in ICE custody, represent a major source of profit for private prison companies and have been linked to numerous human rights abuses. To truly end profiteering from incarceration, the administration must address the financial incentives throughout the entire prison and detention industrial complex, including those operating immigration facilities.

title: Klein's seventh SPAC Churchill Capital Corp VII more than triples deal size ahead of $1 billion IPO
summary: Churchill Capital Corp VII, a blank check company founded by dealmaker Michael Klein, has increased its proposed IPO deal size to $1.0 billion, up 233% from initial plans. The company aims to offer 100 million units at $10 each, with each unit comprising one share and one-fifth of a warrant. This SPAC, like Klein's others, intends to target businesses with stable free cash flow and strong management, and will list on the NYSE under the symbol CVII.U.

title: Cross-Currency Credit Spreads: Mind the Gap
summary: This article examines the divergence in corporate-bond spreads between USD and EUR markets, particularly during and after the COVID-19 crisis. It highlights that while Federal Reserve interventions addressed acute liquidity shortages, smaller discrepancies persisted, presenting both risks and opportunities for investors. The research suggests that the spread differential was largely driven by U.S. companies and potentially reflects a greater "home bias" among U.S. investors.

title: Canadian banks urged to disclose race, gender, income data to ensure equitable credit, loan access
summary: Business groups are calling on the Canadian government to mandate that banks disclose race, gender, income, and neighbourhood data to ensure equitable access to credit and loans. Proponents argue that a similar system already exists in the US through the Community Reinvestment Act, which four of Canada's big banks currently adhere to for their US operations. Despite some banks' claims of not collecting such data, advocates believe it's a necessary step to address discrimination and identify existing gaps in financial inclusion, particularly for minority and Black entrepreneurs.

title: Morgan Stanley Hires $7.5 Mln Merrill Private Wealth Team
summary: Morgan Stanley Wealth Management has recruited a significant Private Wealth Management team from Merrill Lynch, generating $7.5 million annually. The team, led by Lawrence W. Catena, his son Steven, Erik Beiermeister, and Mercedes Fonte, managed $1.2 billion in client assets and will join Morgan Stanley's private wealth group for high-net-worth clients. This move follows Morgan Stanley's aggressive re-entry into the recruiting market, having hired at least five multi-million dollar teams from Merrill Lynch recently.

title: JP Morgan's board rejects switch to stakeholder-focused entity
summary: JPMorgan Chase's board, chaired by CEO Jamie Dimon, has rejected a proposal to convert the bank into a "public benefit corporation." This decision highlights that despite Dimon's previous calls for companies to consider all stakeholders, JPMorgan prioritizes shareholder interests, as stated in a legal review commissioned by the board. Activist investor John Harrington, who proposed the change, views this rejection as evidence that corporate leaders' statements about stakeholder capitalism are largely symbolic.

title: Gerald Klein to Retire from Tompkins Mahopac Bank
summary: Gerald J. Klein, Jr. is set to retire as president and CEO of Tompkins Mahopac Bank after 26 years of service, with his retirement anticipated mid-year. David DeMilia, currently senior vice president, has been appointed as his successor. Klein will support the transition process during the first half of the year, ensuring a smooth leadership handover.

title: Citigroup, Bank of America Cut CEO Pay
summary: Citigroup and Bank of America both announced cuts to their CEOs' 2020 pay following a drop in profits last year. Citigroup CEO Michael Corbat's pay was reduced by 21% to $19.04 million, attributed to a consent order from regulators regarding deficiencies in the bank's risk-management systems. Other executives at Citigroup also saw pay reductions for similar reasons.

title: BofA, Citi Trim CEO Compensation for 2020 in Year of Restraint
summary: Bank of America and Citigroup both reduced their CEO's compensation for 2020, reflecting a year of economic restraint due to the pandemic. Brian Moynihan's pay at BofA was cut by 7.5% to $24.5 million, while outgoing Citigroup CEO Michael Corbat saw a 21% reduction to $19 million. This move highlights ongoing efforts by banks to manage executive payouts conservatively during a challenging economic period.

title: Citigroup slashes CEO's pay by 21%, to $19 million
summary: Citigroup announced that outgoing CEO Mike Corbat's 2020 compensation would be $19 million, a 21% decrease from the previous year. This reduction was due to his failure to address regulatory concerns regarding risk and control, following a $400 million penalty and operational lapses. Other Wall Street banks also showed restraint in executive compensation, reflecting the financial impact of the coronavirus pandemic, with some CEOs experiencing pay cuts while Morgan Stanley's CEO saw an increase.

title: Auxílio faz Caixa ter mais força em sociedade com BB e Bradesco na Elo
summary: The article discusses the ongoing dispute between Caixa, Banco do Brasil, and Bradesco over their ownership stakes in Elo, a Brazilian card brand. The key point of contention is whether the emergency aid payments distributed by Caixa should count towards its share in Elo, as these payments significantly boosted Caixa's card issuance and transaction volumes. This re-evaluation of ownership occurs every four years, with the next one due soon, and the other banks are questioning the inclusion of emergency aid data, arguing it distorts the true market share generation.

title: Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan takes a pay cut
summary: Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan has taken a pay cut, with his total compensation package for the year amounting to $24.5 million, including stock awards. His base salary of $1.5 million remains unchanged. This news follows a similar announcement about Wells Fargo's CEO also taking a significant pay cut.

title: Buffett's Berkshire reveals big stakes in Verizon, Chevron
summary: Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway Inc revealed significant new investments, including an $8.6 billion stake in Verizon Communications Inc and a $4.1 billion stake in Chevron Corp, according to a regulatory filing. The conglomerate also disclosed a new $499 million stake in Marsh & McLennan Cos while reducing investments in companies like Apple and several banks. These moves signal where Buffett and his portfolio managers see value, deploying some of Berkshire's substantial cash hoard.

title: Silver as a Store of Value? Why Analysts Are Growing Bullish on the Metal
summary: Analysts are growing bullish on silver as a store of value, similar to gold, leading to increased interest in silver exchange-traded funds and trusts like the Sprott Physical Silver Trust (PSLV). Despite recent volatility influenced by retail traders, Bank of America maintains a bullish outlook, supported by easy monetary policies, a weak U.S. dollar, and emerging demand from renewable energy sectors. Moody's highlights silver's price sensitivity and its historical role as a medium of exchange, while also noting its smaller, less liquid market compared to other commodities.

title: Berkshire Hathaway Discloses $499M Investment in Marsh & McLennan
summary: Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway announced significant new investments in Verizon Communications ($8.6 billion) and Chevron Corp. ($4.1 billion), along with a new $499 million stake in Marsh & McLennan Cos., as detailed in a recent regulatory filing. These moves indicate where Buffett and his portfolio managers see value, deploying some of Berkshire's substantial cash reserves. The company also reduced holdings in several banks and Apple Inc., while increasing investments in pharmaceutical companies.

title: BofA, Goldman Sign Leases at Tower Owned by Vornado, Trump
summary: Bank of America Corp. and Goldman Sachs Group Inc. have signed new leases at the 555 California Street skyscraper in San Francisco, which is jointly owned by Vornado Realty Trust and the Trump Organization. Bank of America, a long-standing tenant, will remain in the building despite having previously reduced its office footprint. This news comes as Vornado has explored selling its stake in the property.

title: Talis Announces Closing of Initial Public Offering and Full
summary: Talis Biomedical Corporation announced the closing of its initial public offering, which included the full exercise of the underwriters' option to purchase additional shares. The company sold 15,870,000 shares of common stock at $16.00 per share, generating approximately $253.9 million in gross proceeds. The shares began trading on Nasdaq under the symbol "TLIS" on February 12, 2021.

title: Asian Stocks Have Momentum in The Year of the Ox
summary: The article highlights China's economic resilience during the pandemic, with a surging export business and significant foreign direct investment, positioning it to potentially overtake the U.S. economy earlier than expected. Asian stock markets, particularly South Korea, Taiwan, and China, demonstrated strong performance in 2020 and continue to show momentum in the new year, driven by increased investor interest and massive infrastructure projects requiring substantial metal demand. The author predicts a strong outlook for Asian markets in the "Year of the Metal Ox," especially in sectors related to advanced technology and electric vehicles.

title: Wells Fargo Advisors Embraces More Execs from Private Bank
summary: Wells Fargo Advisors has appointed Kent Caldwell-Meeks, Connie Degler, and Adam Taback to its management operating committee, signaling increased integration of private bank services into its financial advisory operations. This move is part of the company's broader strategy to enhance cross-selling opportunities for wealthy clients and better manage risk and costs under new leadership. The appointments reflect a significant push to combine private banking and advisory services, a shift that reverses previous leadership migrations within the company.

title: AHM IPO News - Mortgage servicer AmeriHome withdraws $250 million IPO in favor of acquisition by Western Alliance
summary: Mortgage servicer AmeriHome has withdrawn its plans for a $250 million initial public offering. This decision follows an announcement that the company will instead be acquired by Western Alliance Bancorp for approximately $1 billion. AmeriHome had initially filed for its IPO in October 2020 and revived its plans earlier this year before the acquisition news.

title: BofA Names New Leaders in Fixed Income, FX After Departures
summary: Bank of America Corp. has appointed Michael Maras as the new head of global fixed-income, currencies, and commodities research, following David Woo's departure. Maras will continue to oversee research in the EMEA region from London and the bank also named a new head of currency trading for Brazil. These changes were communicated to staff via an internal memo.

title: Bain hires banks to revive IPO of French car parts group Autodis -sources
summary: Bain Capital is attempting to revive the IPO of its French car parts group Autodis, hiring Goldman Sachs, BNP Paribas, and Barclays as global coordinators for a share sale in Paris this year. The move capitalizes on strong investor demand in a record-breaking start to the year for stock listings, after an aborted IPO attempt in 2018. Autodis, valued at over 1.5 billion euros, specializes in aftermarket spare parts distribution and expects core earnings of approximately 200 million euros by March.

title: Chinese InsurTech firm Waterdrop gears up for US IPO
summary: Chinese InsurTech firm Waterdrop Inc. is preparing for its initial public offering (IPO) in the United States in the next quarter. The company has raised approximately $495 billion through five rounds of financing, with the most recent Series D round in August 2020 bringing in $230 million. Waterdrop, which provides online insurance policies and illness crowdfunding, has seen its valuation multiply significantly since its angel financing in 2016.

title: Robert McSpadden Obituary (1944 - 2021) - Southaven, MS - The Daily Memphian
summary: Robert A. "Bob" McSpadden, 76, of Southaven, MS, passed away on February 19, 2021. He was born in Memphis, TN, and had a long career in finance, culminating in his own mortgage title research company, The Alpha Group. McSpadden was a devoted family man and a dedicated member of Whitehaven Presbyterian Church and later Idlewild Presbyterian Church.

title: M&T Bank Agrees To Acquire People’s United Financial In Latest Tie-Up Of Regional Lenders
summary: M&T Bank announced its agreement to acquire People's United Financial in a $7.6 billion deal, continuing a trend of regional bank mergers driven by low interest rates and the need for technological investments. This acquisition will create a bank with $200 billion in assets and over 1,100 branches across 12 states, with M&T expecting the transaction to significantly boost its earnings per share by 2023. The merger reflects a broader strategy among regional lenders to scale up and compete more effectively with larger U.S. banks while adapting to evolving customer demands for digital banking.

title: M&T Bank acquiring Bridgeport-based People’s United in $7.6B deal
summary: M&T Bank is acquiring Bridgeport-based People's United Bank in a $7.6 billion deal. M&T aims for $330 million in cost savings and synergies and plans to maintain People's United's Bridgeport office as its New England regional headquarters. The acquisition would end People's United's 179-year run as an independent Connecticut-based bank.

title: Ingreso Solidario: ¿Cómo consultar su saldo en Nequi, Daviplata, Bancolombia y demás entidades?
summary: This article provides information on how beneficiaries of the "Ingreso Solidario" program can check their balances in various Colombian banking platforms, including Nequi, Daviplata, and Bancolombia. It emphasizes that the Department for Social Prosperity is the only authorized entity to provide official information regarding payment dates and channels. The content focuses on guiding users through the process of balance inquiry for this government aid.

title: Merrill Lifer and His $4.4-Mln Alabama Team Jump to Morgan Stanley
summary: A Merrill Lynch team led by 38-year Merrill veteran Robert Runkle, managing $1.3 billion in assets and generating $4.4 million in annual revenue, has moved to Morgan Stanley. The team, known as The Runkle Group, includes Runkle's children and will operate out of Montgomery, Atlanta, and Destin. This move is part of Morgan Stanley's continued efforts to recruit experienced financial advisors from competitor wirehouses.

title: Reconnecting to CT: M&T Bank gets fresh start in state with People’s United acquisition
summary: M&T Bank, which previously struggled in Connecticut after acquiring Hudson City Savings Bank in 2015, is poised for a fresh start with its proposed $7.6 billion acquisition of People’s United Financial. The acquisition will significantly expand M&T's presence in Connecticut, where People's United has the largest branch network after Bank of America. M&T aims to preserve community relationships and customer-facing employees from People's United to ensure success in the new combined entity.

title: Largest lenders deny home loans for Black applicants up to three times more often than whites
summary: A WCNC Charlotte analysis reveals that major lenders in the Charlotte market denied home loans for Black applicants two to three times more often than white applicants in 2018 and 2019. This disparity persists across all income brackets. The article explores reasons behind the disparities, including socio-economic factors and current lending rules, and highlights efforts by banks, advocates, and government agencies to address the issue.

title: Bank of America emphasizes diversity, employee wellness in annual financial filing
summary: Bank of America (BAC.N) has incorporated new sections on "Diversity and Inclusion," "Fair and Equitable Compensation," and "Health and Wellness" into its annual financial filing. This move highlights the increasing importance of non-financial topics for executives and investors, reflecting a broader corporate shift following social justice movements. These inclusions formalize the bank's priorities and provide investors, including prominent figures like Warren Buffett, with greater insight into the company's social impact.

title: Bank of America retail president on building industry diversity, key growth strategies
summary: Steve Boland, president of retail at Bank of America, discussed the importance of diversity, the bank's future retail strategy, and consumer spending outlook for 2021. He highlighted the ongoing work needed to promote diversity within the industry. The article also touches upon BofA's investment in digital banking and its commitment to community development and affordable homeownership.

title: JPMorgan exits Mexico private banking, refers clients to BBVA
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. is exiting its private banking business in Mexico, referring its local clients to BBVA Mexico. This move follows a similar decision in Brazil and reflects a trend of wealthy Latin American clients shifting their assets to international financial centers. JPMorgan will continue to operate its other businesses in Mexico, including investment banking, trading, and treasury services, and will still serve Mexican clients through its offshore platform.

title: Big U.S. Banks’ Vows to Halt Job Cuts End as Virus Endures
summary: Major U.S. banks, including Bank of America, are ending their pledges to halt job cuts made at the beginning of the pandemic. This marks a return to typical staffing adjustments, especially after bonuses, and reflects a broader shift as Wall Street banks also push to end remote work arrangements. Wells Fargo, Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, JPMorgan Chase, and Morgan Stanley had previously either initiated cuts or not fully committed to no reductions.

title: Big 5 Sporting Goods Enters Into New Five-Year Credit Facility
summary: Big 5 Sporting Goods Corporation announced a new five-year loan agreement with Bank of America, N. A., maturing in February 2026. This agreement provides a secured revolving credit facility of up to $150 million, with an option to increase to $200 million. CFO Barry Emerson highlighted the favorable terms and the company's strong financial condition, anticipating that the facility will provide crucial financial flexibility.

title: Equitable Financial Inks 130 KSF Manhattan Lease
summary: Equitable Financial Life Insurance Co. has signed a 15-year lease for 130,000 square feet at 1345 Avenue of the Americas in Midtown Manhattan, moving its headquarters. This move reflects a broader trend among financial services firms to embrace office space, despite the increase in remote work options. The new location, owned by Fisher Brothers, is undergoing a $100 million-plus renovation to include high-end amenities.

title: EDD tax call center chaos: Few people getting the answers they need
summary: California's Employment Development Department (EDD) launched a new call center to address tax issues related to billions of dollars in fraudulent unemployment claims. However, the call center is plagued with technical problems, including frequent call disconnections and overwhelmed operators, leading to few people getting the answers they need. Many callers are victims of identity theft receiving tax forms for benefits they never received, while the EDD insists it has sufficient resources and will staff up by the end of March despite ongoing technological issues.

title: Sanciones a empresas por incumplimiento de los acuerdos con consumidores
summary: Six companies in Argentina were sanctioned a total of $4.4 million for failing to uphold agreements reached in conciliation hearings with consumers. The companies, including Telefónica, Banco Galicia, BBVA, Plan Rombo, VW Ahorro Previo, and Falabella, were penalized under Article 46 of the Consumer Defense Law for not complying with the terms set by the COPREC system. This action underscores the government's commitment to protecting consumer rights and ensuring businesses adhere to established conciliation agreements.

title: Citi’s ties to Saudi royal family to remain intact after Khashoggi link
summary: Despite a new US government report linking Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman to the murder of journalist Jamal Khashoggi, Citigroup plans to maintain its long-standing business ties with the Saudi royal family. The bank, under new CEO Jane Fraser, reportedly cannot afford to sever the relationship due to its relatively weaker financial condition compared to rivals and the substantial earnings derived from its Saudi dealings. Major financial institutions like BlackRock and Goldman Sachs also continue to do business with Saudi Arabia, indicating the significant economic benefits outweigh other concerns.

title: Bank of America, Morgan Stanley win dismissal of metals spoofing litigation
summary: A federal judge dismissed a lawsuit against Bank of America and Morgan Stanley accusing them of manipulating the precious metals futures market through "spoofing." The judge ruled the litigation, filed in June 2019, was beyond the two-year statute of limitations, as evidence of harm was known by December 2016. While two traders involved face a separate criminal trial, both banks had previously settled civil and criminal probes related to spoofing activities.

title: Bank of America, Morgan Stanley win dismissal of metals spoofing litigation
summary: A federal judge has dismissed a lawsuit against Bank of America Corp and Morgan Stanley accusing them of "spoofing" in the precious metals futures market. The judge ruled that the 2019 lawsuit was filed too late, past the two-year federal statute of limitations, as similar litigation had commenced in 2016. While two individuals from the banks involved in the alleged spoofing face criminal charges, the banks previously settled with the Department of Justice and the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission over the matter.

title: Aramco $75 Billion Payout No Problem as Oil Recovers, BofA Says
summary: Bank of America believes Saudi Aramco will easily meet its $75 billion dividend payout next year due to the recovery in oil prices. The bank maintains a neutral rating on the company. Rising oil prices and increased output could even enable Aramco to raise its 2022 dividend.

title: Gold Is at a Critical Juncture Now
summary: Technical analyst Clive Maund examines gold's recent price decline and its potential future movements, suggesting a likely imminent rally based on technical indicators and market behavior. The article analyzes various charts, including Larry's gold chart and broader market indices like the Wilshire 5000, to predict whether gold will break out or form a "Cup & Handle" pattern, and discusses the Fed's role in market stability.

title: Desconto de 8% no IPTU de Rio das Ostras prossegue até 31 de março
summary: A Prefeitura de Rio das Ostras oferece um desconto de 8% no IPTU de 2021 para quem realizar o pagamento em cota única até o dia 31 de março. Os contribuintes também têm a opção de parcelar o imposto em nove vezes. Para emissão da guia ou agendamento de atendimento presencial, há canais online, e-mail e telefone disponíveis.

title: BofA Widens Lead in Muni Business With Almost 20% Market Share
summary: Bank of America Corp. has significantly expanded its dominance in the municipal bond underwriting business in 2021, leading the sale of $13.2 billion in bonds. This represents a 19% market share, nearly triple that of its closest competitor, Citigroup Inc. This marks BofA's largest market share in the sector since at least 2013, demonstrating a substantial lead in the underwriting of long-term state and local government debt.

title: Hilton Grand Vacations to acquire Diamond Resorts in $1.4B transaction
summary: Hilton Grand Vacations Inc. (HGV) has entered a definitive agreement to acquire Diamond Resorts International Inc. for approximately $1.4 billion in a stock-based transaction. This acquisition will combine HGV's brand strength with Diamond's independent timeshare operations, creating a premier vacation ownership company with expanded offerings and an anticipated $125 million in run-rate cost synergies. The transaction is expected to close in the summer, pending regulatory and shareholder approvals.

title: Goldman Sachs Unveils $10 Billion Push to Invest in Black Women
summary: Goldman Sachs announced a $10 billion commitment over the next decade to invest in businesses and organizations that benefit Black women, aiming to narrow the wealth gap. This initiative will focus on housing, healthcare, and other programs, alongside a $100 million philanthropic contribution. This move is part of a broader trend among major financial institutions addressing their historical role in racial wealth disparities.

title: Timeline of Bryn Mawr Trust's 132-year path to a $976 million acquisition
summary: This article provides a timeline of Bryn Mawr Trust's 132-year history, culminating in its $976 million acquisition. It highlights the bank's long-standing roots in the Philadelphia Main Line area and references related articles concerning its acquisition and other business activities.

title: Rockefeller Hires $4.6-Mln Morgan Stanley Private Wealth Team in Los Angeles
summary: Rockefeller Capital Management has hired a two-advisor team, Hans Maentz and Bernard Machlovitch, from Morgan Stanley's private wealth unit in Los Angeles. The team managed approximately $1.5 billion in assets and specialized in serving Native American Tribes and Alaskan Native Corporations. This move marks the 48th team to join Rockefeller under Greg Fleming's leadership, further expanding their presence.

title: Value is finally outpacing growth this year but will still falter long term, traders say
summary: Value stocks are currently outperforming growth stocks, with some traders like Steve Chiavarone of Federated Hermes expecting this trend to continue in 2021 due to economic reopening. However, Danielle Shay of Simpler Trading believes growth will ultimately win out long term, though she acknowledges value's current appeal for long-term investors. Both traders highlight the ongoing debate between investing in growth versus value and the difficulty of trading options in value stocks due to lower premium and momentum.

title: New office buildings in Coral Gables sign five tenants, including bank HQ, Naples payments firm
summary: The Plaza Coral Gables has secured five new tenants for its office spaces, including the relocation of BAC Florida Bank's headquarters and ACI Worldwide, a payments firm from Naples. Other significant clients include Raymond James, HIG Capital, and PNC Bank. This indicates strong activity in the commercial real estate market in Coral Gables.

title: On the Value-Growth Fence? TILT Into Value with This ETF
summary: The FlexShares Morningstar U.S. Market Factor Tilt Index Fund (TILT) offers investors a way to capitalize on the resurgence of value stocks without completely abandoning growth exposure. The ETF tilts towards small-cap and value stocks, aiming to reflect the performance of the Morningstar U.S. Market Factor Tilt Index. This approach is particularly relevant as value-related ETFs are seeing significant inflows and some financial stocks, to which TILT allocates over 16%, still appear undervalued.

title: Ex-BofA, Carlyle Dealmakers Plan $300 Million Consumer SPAC
summary: Former senior dealmakers from Bank of America and Carlyle Group are launching a special purpose acquisition company (SPAC) aiming to raise $300 million. This SPAC, Transformational CPG Acquisition Corp., will target consumer-sector businesses and is backed by Wadih Boueiz and Nadim Barakat through a new investment firm. The initiative was formalized with a filing on Monday.

title: Seeking return to normal, JPMorgan Chase is planning for summer interns to go to the office. (Published 2021)
summary: JPMorgan Chase is planning for summer interns in New York and London to work from the office, signaling a move towards pre-pandemic working life for big financial firms. The bank also intends to allow some employees to return to its London offices starting March 29, though at no more than 50% capacity. This decision reflects the eagerness of banks to re-establish in-office working, despite challenges, with leaders like Jamie Dimon and David Solomon expressing concerns about prolonged remote work.

title: Patriotic Canadian venture capital firm Inovia raises $450-million to back domestic tech champions
summary: Inovia Capital, a prominent Canadian venture capital firm, has successfully raised US$450-million for its second growth equity fund, aiming to invest in emerging Canadian technology companies. The firm's strategy emphasizes backing domestic champions, with 90% of the new fund coming from Canadian investors. Co-managed by Chris Arsenault, Patrick Pichette, and Dennis Kavelman, this fund builds on Inovia's track record of supporting high-profile Canadian tech firms and preventing foreign takeovers, notably with Lightspeed.

title: Morgan Stanley becomes the first big U.S. bank to offer its wealthy clients access to bitcoin funds
summary: Morgan Stanley is the first major U.S. bank to offer its wealthy clients access to bitcoin funds, responding to client demand despite the cryptocurrency's volatility. The bank will provide access to three bitcoin funds with significant investment minimums and strict eligibility criteria, allowing investments up to 2.5% of a client's net worth. This move signifies a notable step for bitcoin's acceptance as an asset class within traditional finance.

title: JPMorgan, BofA Condemn Racism Against Asian Americans
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. and Bank of America Corp. have condemned racism against Asian Americans following a shooting in Atlanta that killed eight people, including six Asian women. JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon stated in a staff memo that these racist acts, including physical assault and verbal harassment, will not be tolerated. This stance comes amidst a rise in anti-Asian sentiment impacting communities and businesses.

title: Goldman takes heat for first-year analysts’ 100-hour workweeks
summary: Goldman Sachs is under scrutiny after a survey revealed its first-year analysts are working nearly 100-hour weeks, leading to deteriorating health and a souring outlook. CEO David Solomon responded by promising to strengthen the firm's "Saturday rule" and accelerate hiring for junior bankers. Meanwhile, Jefferies offered its junior employees perks like Peloton bikes, which some see as a subtle recruitment jab in light of Goldman's controversy.

title: Morning Coffee: 41 year-old banker now amply avenged on all who wronged him. Standard Chartered's new hiring plan
summary: This article details how former Bank of America Merrill Lynch banker Omeed Malik, unjustly fired and accused of misconduct, received a substantial settlement and is now launching a successful SPAC. It also discusses Standard Chartered's new growth strategy to expand into Western markets, shifting focus from its traditional Asian base, and touches on various other banking industry news and societal observations.

title: Bitcoin Rally Stirs BofA Alarm on ‘Enormous’ Surge in Energy Use
summary: Bank of America (BofA) has raised concerns about the environmental impact of Bitcoin's energy consumption, noting that the cryptocurrency's network uses significant amounts of power comparable to developed countries. The report highlights that Bitcoin's energy use has soared, contributing to a substantial increase in emissions, especially when its price is high, consuming about 0.4% of global energy.

title: JPMorgan Chase: The Real Winner Of The Fintech Micro-Bubble
summary: JPMorgan Chase is highlighted as the true winner in the fintech micro-bubble, leveraging its scale, cash flow, and existing customer base to outperform fintech startups like Square. The article argues that big banks, particularly JPM, have significant competitive advantages in the financial services industry due to their resources, regulatory approvals, and customer relationships, which allow them to integrate technology efficiently and maintain superior profitability. Despite Square's rapid growth, its lack of consistent profitability and high valuation expectations are contrasted with JPMorgan Chase's undervalued stock and strong fundamentals.

title: Despite calls for change, Canada's RBC is one of world's top bankers to fossil fuel industry
summary: A new report shows that despite commitments to align with the Paris climate accord, 60 of the world's largest banks have increased fossil fuel funding to $3.8 trillion US over the past five years. Canada's RBC, along with three other Canadian banks, ranks among the top 20 global financiers of fossil fuel projects. The article highlights the challenge banks face in transitioning away from fossil fuel investments due to economic and political pressures, despite warnings of systemic financial risk from figures like Mark Carney.

title: BBVA en Asia: productos y servicios para 'corporates' e inversores
summary: BBVA has maintained a presence in Asia for over 40 years, establishing a comprehensive network of branches and representative offices to serve corporate and institutional clients. The bank focuses on supporting Asian multinational clients, fulfilling demand for Asian products from global clients, and distributing investment solutions to institutional and public sector clients, all while emphasizing sustainability and digital transformation. BBVA aims to be a key partner for "nearshoring" initiatives, leveraging its strong franchises in countries like Mexico and Spain to assist Asian companies in their international expansion.

title: Schwab puts political activity in deeper freeze by leaving Chamber
summary: Charles Schwab Corp. has withdrawn from the U.S. Chamber of Commerce, further reducing its political activity after previously shutting down its corporate political action committee following the Jan. 6 Capitol riot. This move is part of Schwab's re-evaluation of its engagement with policymakers, though the company states it is unrelated to the Chamber's political donations. Other financial firms are also reassessing their PAC contributions and political involvement in response to increased scrutiny and polarization.

title: House flippers in the US are awash in cash after record year
summary: House flippers in the US are experiencing a record year with high profits due to a red-hot real estate market and increasing interest from lenders. This influx of cash, primarily from second-tier regional banks and shadow lenders, is driving up home prices and raising concerns about market speculation, although experts don't foresee another housing bust. The phenomenon is fueled by low housing inventory and urban dwellers moving to suburbs, making flipping an attractive short-term investment for lenders.

title: Conheça todos os códigos dos bancos no Brasil
summary: Este artigo lista os códigos de identificação únicos para bancos no Brasil, o que é crucial para diversas transações financeiras. O TecMundo compila uma extensa lista desses códigos para auxiliar os usuários na identificação das instituições bancárias. A lista detalha centenas de bancos, incluindo grandes nomes e cooperativas de crédito.

title: Who is Behind Archegos?
summary: The article identifies Bill Hwang, a "tiger cub" hedgie with a past insider trading conviction, as the figure behind Archegos Capital Management, whose colossal margin calls are impacting major banks. Archegos's forced liquidation of an estimated $30 billion in block trades, including shares in Chinese firms, affected banks like Credit Suisse and Nomura after prime brokers demanded more collateral.

title: Airstream Launches Innovative RV Financing Program
summary: Airstream has launched a new financing program in partnership with Bank of America, called Airstream Financial, to streamline RV financing for its customers. This program offers simplified one-stop shopping at dealerships, with terms up to 20 years and potential tax deductibility as a second home. The initiative aims to make Airstream ownership more accessible and affordable, strengthening customer-dealer relationships.

title: Black Media Execs Demand More Business From General Motors' Multi-Billion Dollar Ad Budget
summary: Black media executives are demanding that General Motors significantly increase its advertising spending with Black-owned media companies, pointing out that GM spent an allegedly abysmal 0.5% (or 2% according to GM) of its multi-billion dollar ad budget with them in 2019. The article highlights the financial capacity of GM and compares its investment in Black businesses to other major companies and individuals who have pledged substantial funds to racial justice and Black-owned enterprises. The author argues that a larger allocation of GM's ad budget to Black-owned media would create Black jobs and significantly change the landscape of these companies while still reaching Black audiences.

title: UWNYC Honors Women Board Leaders
summary: In honor of Women's History Month, United Way of New York City (UWNYC) recognized its extraordinary women board leaders. The article highlights the professional achievements and philanthropic contributions of 14 influential women who are at the forefront of strengthening New York City's underserved communities. These leaders come from diverse sectors including finance, marketing, law, and corporate operations, showcasing their dedication to both their careers and community service.

title: Kosciusko County Court News
summary: This article provides a detailed list of various court proceedings in Kosciusko County, including small claims, civil collections, evictions, marriage licenses, and marriage dissolutions. It itemizes the parties involved and the awarded amounts or case details for events occurring in Kosciusko Superior Courts I, II, III, and IV. The report covers cases presided over by Judges Chad Miner, Chris Kehler, Karin McGrath, and Torrey Bauer, along with marriage licenses filed with Clerk Ann Torpy.

title: Former JPMorgan executive quits board of company that collected data for Trump 2020 campaign
summary: Blythe Masters, formerly a top executive at JPMorgan Chase, is resigning from the board of Phunware, a company known for developing a data collection app for Donald Trump's 2020 re-election campaign. Her departure, effective May 1, is reportedly due to her recent nomination to the board of Credit Suisse, requiring her to step down from other board positions. Masters' tenure at Phunware also involved controversy surrounding the company's receipt of a PPP loan arranged by JPMorgan, leading to a class-action lawsuit which Phunware was later dismissed from.

title: Turkey fines 10 foreign firms for illegal short selling
summary: Turkey's capital markets watchdog has imposed fines totaling $3.25 million on 10 foreign financial firms for unlawful short selling transactions. The fines were issued because the firms failed to notify brokerage houses that their transactions were short selling. Credit Suisse, Barclays, and Merrill Lynch BofA International received the largest penalties.

title: An Acquisition of AxiaMed Helps BofA’s Effort to Rebuild Its Acquiring Business
summary: Bank of America acquired Axia Technologies Inc. (AxiaMed) to bolster its merchant-acquiring business, specifically targeting the healthcare sector. AxiaMed offers integrated payment solutions for healthcare providers, supporting various payment methods and omnichannel integration. This acquisition is part of BofA's strategy to rebuild its acquiring services post-First Data partnership, aiming to compete effectively with financial-technology providers.

title: BofA Acquires Health-Care Tech Startup Axia in Payments Push
summary: Bank of America Corp. has acquired health-care technology company Axia Technologies Inc., also known as AxiaMed, to enhance its merchant payment processing capabilities. This acquisition follows BofA's move to build its own proprietary payment platform after dissolving a previous merchant-services joint venture. The terms of the deal were not disclosed.

title: Turkey fines 10 foreign firms for illegal short selling
summary: Turkey's capital markets watchdog has fined 10 foreign financial firms a total of 26.4 million Turkish liras ($3.25 million) for unlawful short-selling transactions. The firms, including Credit Suisse, Barclays Capital, and Merrill Lynch, failed to notify their brokerage houses that their transactions were short selling.

title: Fifth Third Bancorp stock rises Monday, still underperforms market
summary: Fifth Third Bancorp stock (FITB) rose 0.66% on Monday, closing at $38.23, although it still underperformed the broader market, with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average seeing larger gains. The stock remained below its 52-week high and showed mixed performance compared to competitors like Bank of America and Wells Fargo. Trading volume was also below its 50-day average.

title: Bank Of America Adds AxiaMed To Its Merchants Payments Regimen
summary: Bank of America has acquired Axia Technologies, also known as AxiaMed, to enhance its merchant payments regimen, specifically targeting the healthcare sector. AxiaMed provides an integrated payments platform for healthcare providers, addressing the industry's historical lag in payment advancements and expanding Bank of America's merchant services capabilities. This acquisition follows Bank of America's decision to build its own proprietary payments platform after dissolving its joint venture with Fiserv.

title: Achilles Therapeutics Announces Closing of $175.5 million Initial Public Offering
summary: Achilles Therapeutics plc (NASDAQ: ACHL), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on T cell therapies for solid tumors, announced the closing of its initial public offering in the United States. The offering, consisting of 9,750,000 American Depositary Shares at $18.00 per share, generated gross proceeds of approximately $175.5 million for the company. J.P. Morgan, BofA Securities, and Piper Sandler acted as joint book-running managers.

title: Morgan Stanley dumped $5 billion in Archegos’ stocks the night before massive fire sale hit rivals
summary: Morgan Stanley reportedly sold off $5 billion in Archegos' shares to a select group of hedge funds on March 25, the day before a broader market fire sale commenced. The bank, with Archegos' consent, offered the shares at a discount, framing it as a move to prevent a client's collapse. This early action allowed Morgan Stanley to avoid substantial losses, unlike other banks such as Credit Suisse, which faced significant hits from the Archegos unwind.

title: AmEx's purchase of online lender Kabbage left desperate PPP borrowers in the cold
summary: American Express's acquisition of Kabbage in August 2020 created significant problems for small businesses seeking second-round PPP loans. While AmEx bought Kabbage's lending technology, it left behind the PPP loan book, which became K Servicing. This orphaned entity is now plagued with customer complaints, delays, and a lack of support, leaving many desperate borrowers without critical funding and struggling to navigate the complex process.

title: BMO CEO Darryl White urges regulators to prepare measures to cool the housing market
summary: BMO CEO Darryl White advises policymakers and regulators to urgently plan for potential interventions to cool overheating Canadian housing markets, though he suggests waiting a few weeks to assess the impact of new lockdown measures. Despite concerns about housing, White remains optimistic about a robust economic recovery later this year, driven by pent-up demand and increased savings, predicting significant GDP growth for Canada and the U.S.

title: RBC and TD CEOs Give Staff an Extra Day Off to Avoid Burnout
summary: The CEOs of Royal Bank of Canada and Toronto-Dominion Bank are granting employees an extra paid day off this year to combat burnout exacerbated by the ongoing pandemic. RBC CEO Dave McKay noted that staff are more exhausted than ever and emphasized the need to remove the stigma around taking time to recharge. This initiative comes as Canada faces a potentially worsening pandemic situation.

title: Duke Energy, Wells Fargo, NextEra Energy Resources join forces on major solar expansion in North Carolina
summary: Wells Fargo has joined Duke Energy's Green Source Advantage (GSA) program, partnering with NextEra Energy Resources to develop a 58-megawatt solar power plant in Catawba County, North Carolina. This project, known as Blackburn Solar, is expected to come online in 2022 and will offset about 50 percent of Wells Fargo’s energy usage in the state. The GSA program allows large customers to achieve sustainability goals by securing renewable energy from projects connected to the Duke Energy grid, contributing to North Carolina's solar expansion.

title: Morgan Stanley Star Who Exited in Partnership Fracas Joins N.J. RIA
summary: David S. Weinerman, a former top-ranked Morgan Stanley broker managing $1 billion in assets, has joined Summit Financial, a New Jersey-based RIA, after a controversial departure from Morgan Stanley. Weinerman allegedly left the firm due to policy violations involving a listening device he hid in his former partner's office. This incident highlights the challenges in advisor team partnerships, especially heightened during the pandemic, and large firms' decreasing tolerance for policy breaches.

title: Citi, BofA Want to Save Traders’ Time With Fixed-Income Platform
summary: Citigroup Inc. and Bank of America Corp. are developing a new fixed-income trading platform aimed at making CLO traders more productive. The platform will initially focus on streamlining the manual process of compiling bid lists for "bid wanted in competition" (BWICs) auctions, a time-consuming task that currently generates little revenue for banks. The two banks plan to invite other dealers to participate in the new trading venue.

title: BTFL IPO News - Wellness products supplier The Bountiful Company files for a $100 million IPO
summary: The Bountiful Company, a supplier of vitamins and wellness products, has filed for an initial public offering to raise $100 million. The company, founded in 1971, reported $2.2 billion in sales for the 12 months ending December 31, 2020, and plans to list on the NYSE under the symbol BTFL. Morgan Stanley, J.P. Morgan, and KKR are among the joint bookrunners for the deal.

title: Cadence Bank agrees to merge with Mississippi lender in $6B deal
summary: Cadence Bank has announced an all-stock merger with BancorpSouth Bank, creating an entity with a market value exceeding $6 billion and assets around $44 billion. The combined company, to be named Cadence Bank, will have dual headquarters in Tupelo, Miss., and Houston, with shareholders of Cadence Bank receiving 0.70 shares of BancorpSouth stock and a cash dividend of $1.25 per share. The transaction is expected to finalize in the fourth quarter, establishing the fifth-largest institution in Texas and the Southeast.

title: JPMorgan Chase wants to be the commercial bank for ‘green economy’ companies
summary: JPMorgan Chase is establishing a new Green Economy team within its commercial banking division to deepen relationships with companies focused on environmentally-friendly products, services, and conservation. This initiative aims to provide capital and expertise to businesses across renewable energy, efficiency solutions, agriculture and food technology, and sustainable finance. The move aligns with the broader financial industry's shift towards a low-carbon economy, as highlighted by CEO Jamie Dimon.

title: BMO sells EMEA asset management business for $1.1-billion to Ameriprise Financial
summary: Bank of Montreal is selling its European, Middle East, and Africa (EMEA) asset management business to Ameriprise Financial Inc. for $1.1-billion. This divestiture is part of BMO's strategy to focus on North America and improve its efficiency ratio, despite the sale price being lower than its original acquisition cost. The deal is expected to boost BMO's capital levels and marks a new strategic relationship with Ameriprise's asset management arm, Columbia Threadneedle Investments.

title: Reuters names Alessandra Galloni as its next editor-in-chief
summary: Reuters News has appointed Alessandra Galloni as its first female editor-in-chief in its 170-year history. Galloni, 47, will succeed Stephen J. Adler and faces challenges common to the news industry, as well as those specific to Reuters' complex structure as part of Thomson Reuters Corp. Her priorities include maintaining Reuters' relationship with Refinitiv, its largest customer, and boosting the news agency's digital and events businesses.

title: Lloyds Shares: Dividend Outlook for 2022 and 2023
summary: This article examines the dividend outlook for Lloyds shares for 2022 and 2023, analyzing its recent share price performance and future dividend payments. It details the interim 2022 dividend and predicts the final 2022 dividend's ex-dividend and payment dates, along with implications for investors. The article also provides historical dividend data and context regarding the PRA's previous directive to suspend bank dividends during the pandemic.

title: Firstrust, M&T participate in grant programs to help local small businesses
summary: Firstrust and M&T Bank are participating in grant programs designed to assist local small businesses in their expansion efforts. This initiative comes as several local banks are finding ways to provide assistance to businesses beyond the Paycheck Protection Program. The article highlights these banks' commitment to supporting the local business community.

title: Gap to Replace Longtime Credit-Card Issuer Synchrony With Barclays
summary: Gap Inc. is ending its 22-year partnership with Synchrony Financial, its longtime credit-card issuer, and moving its business to Barclays PLC. Barclays will now manage Gap's private-label and co-branded credit cards, including those for Athleta, Banana Republic, and Old Navy. The portfolio includes approximately 11 million open card accounts with a total balance of roughly $3.8 billion as of the end of March.

title: Morgan Stanley Drafts Merrill’s Willie Thomas for Menlo Park Post
summary: Morgan Stanley has hired William "Willie" Thomas, a former Merrill Lynch manager and NFL player, to lead its Menlo Park, California branch. Thomas previously oversaw Merrill's "Boca Tropics" market and will join Morgan Stanley after a garden leave, filling a role whose previous occupant, John Harsch, shifted to managing a private wealth branch. This move highlights Morgan Stanley's renewed recruiting efforts, contrasting with Merrill Lynch's focus on internal growth from its market executives.

title: CPI data Buy the Rumor Sell the Fact DXY EURUSD
summary: The article discusses the impact of the US March CPI data on the DXY and EUR/USD, noting that while the year-over-year figure was strong (2.6%), it was distorted by the low CPI prints from March-May of the previous year due to lockdowns. Traders anticipated this distortion, leading to a "buy the rumor, sell the fact" reaction. This resulted in the US Dollar Index (DXY) falling and EUR/USD rising immediately after the data release, despite the seemingly dramatic inflation jump.

title: CIBC CEO urges action on increasing rental housing supply
summary: CIBC CEO Victor Dodig emphasized the urgent need for increased housing supply in Canada, particularly rental stock, to address rising house prices and accommodate immigration. While supporting regulatory measures like toughening mortgage stress tests, Dodig stressed that long-term solutions lie in building more purpose-built rental housing and increasing density in urban areas. He also noted that low interest rates and generational wealth transfers contribute to the current housing market dynamics.

title: JPMorgan Chase’s mortgage margins narrow in Q1
summary: JPMorgan Chase saw its mortgage margins narrow in the first quarter of 2021 despite a 21% increase in originations over the previous quarter. Production revenue from mortgage fees declined, and gain-on-sale margins fell significantly due to market factors and a shift towards lower-margin correspondent lending. CEO Jamie Dimon anticipates a "Goldilocks moment" for the economy.

title: Goldman, JPMorgan Traders Show the Reddit Crowd How It’s Done
summary: Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase & Co. reported massive revenue windfalls from trading and dealmaking, kicking off bank earnings season with surprisingly strong results. Despite predictions that good times for Wall Street were over, particularly after retail investor activity early in the year, these major banks demonstrated their continued profitability. The strong performance was partly fueled by the renewed optimism of small investors.

title: Consumers Shifted Credit Payment Behaviors in the U.S. and Other Global Markets as a Result of COVID-19
summary: A TransUnion Global Payment Hierarchy study revealed that the COVID-19 pandemic significantly altered consumer credit payment behaviors in the U.S. and other global markets. The study found that consumers prioritized different credit products during the pandemic, with mortgage payments becoming paramount in the U.S. and credit cards gaining importance in various regions, especially for those with limited card access. These shifts highlight the critical role of accessible credit and the impact of economic crises on financial decision-making.

title: BofA Shares Slide as Tepid Loan Growth Counters Trading Bonanza
summary: Bank of America (BAC) saw its shares decline by as much as 4.2% despite strong performance from its trading and investment banking divisions. This drop was attributed to a decrease in loan balances and higher-than-expected pandemic-related costs, which outweighed the revenue surge from trading and banking fees. The bank also released $2.7 billion of reserves, signaling an improving economic outlook.

title: Bank of America management offers optimistic outlook on economy, reserves
summary: Bank of America executives expressed an optimistic outlook for economic growth, citing strong consumer spending and financial markets after better-than-expected first-quarter profits. The bank released $2.7 billion in loan loss reserves and expects to release more as the economy improves, despite challenges from low interest rates and one-off expenses. Analysts remain positive on the bank’s future growth prospects, anticipating a rise in net interest income.

title: KKR-backed AppLovin raises $2 billion in U.S. IPO at over $28 billion valuation
summary: Mobile app and gaming company AppLovin Corp successfully priced its initial public offering at $80 per share, raising $2 billion and valuing the company at $28.64 billion. Backed by KKR & Co Inc, AppLovin is listing on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol "APP." This IPO highlights the surging demand for video games during the COVID-19 pandemic, with AppLovin boasting over 410 million daily active users and more than 200 free-to-play mobile games.

title: Bank of America Profit Doubles After It Releases Reserves for Bad Loans
summary: Bank of America announced its profit doubled in the first quarter of the year, reaching $8.05 billion, largely due to releasing reserves previously set aside for bad loans. This marks a significant increase from $4.01 billion a year prior when banks were building up reserves at the start of the pandemic. The first-quarter results surpassed analysts' expectations, despite revenue remaining flat.

title: Bank of America Profit Doubles After It Releases Reserves for Bad Loans
summary: Bank of America announced a doubling of its profit in the first quarter of the year, reaching $8.05 billion, largely due to releasing reserves previously set aside for potential bad loans. This performance significantly surpassed its earnings of $4.01 billion from a year prior, when banks were heavily provisioning for the economic impact of the pandemic. While profits soared, the bank's revenue remained flat, beating analysts' expectations.

title: Morgan Stanley had $911 million in first-quarter losses tied to Archegos fund meltdown
summary: Morgan Stanley reported a nearly $1 billion loss in the first quarter of 2021 stemming from its prime brokerage relationship with Bill Hwang's Archegos Capital Management. The loss included $644 million from a "credit event" and an additional $267 million in related trading losses as the firm rapidly de-risked its positions. CEO James Gorman defended the decision to quickly unwind positions as "necessary and money well spent," while CFO Jon Pruzan suggested the bank might have been misled by Archegos.

title: Northern Trust to launch FX trading engine in Singapore
summary: Northern Trust is set to launch an electronic FX pricing and trading engine in Singapore, becoming the latest major bank to join the Monetary Authority of Singapore's (MAS) initiative to develop the region into a global FX trading hub. This move expands Northern Trust's FX solutions in Asia-Pacific, following prior efforts to grow its FX trading business through acquisitions and partnerships with firms like BEx and Lumint. The new eFX platform aims to benefit regional market participants with improved speed, enhanced pricing discovery, and more efficient execution.

title: Bank of America CEO Moynihan says supports ‘a well-focused infrastructure plan’ - CNN interview
summary: Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan stated in a CNN interview that he supports a "well-focused infrastructure plan" for the U.S. He also commented on the potential impact of a 28 percent corporate tax rate, noting it would depend on the new tax law's details.

title: Bank of America tops charts with $15 billion bond deal, the biggest ever from a bank
summary: Bank of America Corp. raised $15 billion in the corporate bond market, marking the largest bond deal ever issued by a bank. This six-part sale surpassed a previous record and saw strong investor demand, allowing for a reduction in interest rate spreads.

title: Citibank: Why one of the world's largest and most iconic banks is wrapping up its retail business in India
summary: Citigroup announced its plan to exit the retail banking business in India, a market it has been in for 119 years. This move is part of the bank's global strategy to reallocate resources to higher-returning opportunities in wealth management and institutional businesses in four key locations (Singapore, Hong Kong, UAE, London). The exit also reflects the intense competition faced by foreign banks in India from domestic heavyweights, and comes amidst a trend of other foreign banks scaling back or leaving the Indian market due to high capital and regulatory requirements.

title: Bank of America to Set Record for Largest Bank Bond Sale at $15 Billion
summary: Bank of America is preparing to issue $15 billion in bonds, which would be the largest bond sale ever by a bank. This move comes shortly after JPMorgan Chase & Co. set a record with a $13 billion bond offering. The significant investor demand, totaling around $25 billion, suggests BofA will secure favorable borrowing rates.

title: Bank of America, Goldman Sachs, and JPMorgan Chase Had Huge Bond Sales
summary: Bank of America, Goldman Sachs, and JPMorgan Chase conducted significant bond sales this week, capitalizing on a decrease in Treasury yields. JPMorgan Chase alone issued $13 billion in bonds. These sales occurred following their earnings reports, indicating a strategic move to raise capital in a favorable market.

title: Morgan Stanley reveals $911 million Archegos loss as profit jumps
summary: Morgan Stanley reported a $911 million loss due to the collapse of Archegos Capital Management, which impacted its first-quarter profit, despite a 150% overall jump fueled by strong trading and deal-making. The bank lost $644 million from selling Archegos-related stocks and $267 million in derisking efforts. While the Archegos event overshadowed its otherwise stellar performance, Morgan Stanley's profit comfortably beat expectations thanks to record capital markets activity and an unprecedented boom in dealmaking.

title: Broadway Financial Completes Merger to Create Largest Black-Owned Bank in the US
summary: Broadway Financial Corp. completed its merger with Washington, D.C.-based CFC Banc Corp. on April 1, forming CityFirstBroadway, now the largest Black-led bank in the U.S. with over $1 billion in assets. The new institution plans to expand commercial lending, develop affordable housing, and offer loans to small businesses in underserved urban areas. This merger occurred despite a significant decline in the number of Black-owned financial institutions nationwide.

title: Bank of America looks to expand Leader on Loan program in new markets
summary: Bank of America is planning to expand its "Leader on Loan" program into new markets. This program allows bank executives to assist local organizations, leveraging their business expertise for community benefit. The expansion aims to accelerate work at various non-profit and community-focused groups.

title: XPO Logistics Announces Mark Manduca as Chief Investment Officer for GXO Logistics Spin-Off
summary: XPO Logistics announced the appointment of Mark Manduca as Chief Investment Officer for GXO Logistics, its intended spin-off logistics business. Manduca will be responsible for analyzing GXO's growth opportunities, optimizing its asset portfolio, overseeing UK pension investments, and communicating GXO's investment case globally. He brings extensive experience as a top-ranked European transport research analyst from leading investment banks.

title: Herman Miller, Knoll $1.8B deal to create furniture leader
summary: Herman Miller Inc. announced its acquisition of Knoll Inc. for $1.8 billion in a cash-and-stock deal. This merger aims to bolster Herman Miller's market position as offices globally prepare for employees' return, and as companies reconfigure workspaces for social distancing or permanent work-from-home setups. The combined entity will boast 19 brands and operate across over 100 countries.

title: U.S. Banks: Goldman Sachs reveals Black workforce numbers for the first time
summary: For the first time, Goldman Sachs has released detailed numbers on its Black workforce in the U.S. The report, part of its sustainability efforts, shows that 24 Black men and 25 Black women are among the 1,548 U.S. executives, senior officials, and managers, accounting for 6.8% of the total U.S. workforce, a slight increase from the previous year. CEO David Solomon acknowledged that there is "still a long road ahead" but committed to making diversity a personal priority.

title: Barclays Drops $630 Million Prison Finance Deal After Pressure from Investors and Sustainability Orgs
summary: Barclays has withdrawn from a $630 million municipal bond deal for private prison company CoreCivic Inc. and the State of Alabama. This decision followed intense pressure from sustainability organizations and investors who highlighted the financial and reputational risks associated with financing private prisons, particularly given Barclays' prior commitment not to do so.
