AAA Cooper will continue to operate independently under CEO Reid Dove, who has also been appointed to Knight-Swift's board of directors.

title: SentinelOne Announces Underwriters’ Full Exercise of Greenshoe Option and Closing of Initial Public Offering
summary: SentinelOne announced the closing of its initial public offering, including the full exercise of the underwriters' overallotment option. The company sold 40,250,000 shares of Class A common stock at $35.00 per share, generating approximately $1.33 billion in net proceeds. Concurrently, SentinelOne sold an additional 1,428,568 shares to existing stockholders in a private placement at the same public offering price.

title: Bank of America, Citigroup, and Other Major Banks Manipulate Credit Default Swap Market, Class Action Alleges
summary: A new class action lawsuit, filed by New Mexico's State Investment Council, alleges that major banks including Bank of America, Citigroup, and Deutsche Bank manipulated the credit default swap (CDS) market for over a decade. The lawsuit claims these banks exploited their market power and rigged CDS auctions by coordinating submissions and sharing sensitive pricing information, ultimately driving down auction prices to their benefit. This alleged scheme allowed them to illegally accumulate billions of dollars at the expense of the CDS market and other investors.

title: Authentic Brands Group Files For IPO
summary: Authentic Brands Group (ABG), owner of numerous fashion and sports brands, has filed for an initial public offering (IPO). The company plans to sell $100 million worth of stock, though this is a placeholder amount. ABG generates over $14 billion in annual retail sales and reported net income of $225 million in 2020.

title: Banks in U.S. are poised for weaker results after a pandemic windfall
summary: U.S. banks are expected to report weaker second-quarter results compared to their pandemic windfalls, primarily due to an anticipated 28% tumble in trading revenue. While a strong mergers and acquisitions market might provide some offset, overall revenue for the six largest U.S. banks is projected to fall by about 5% from the previous year. Analysts view this period as an "intermission," with hopes for improving loan growth in the future and continued benefits from reserve releases.

title: Top 5 Banks in Canada
summary: This article lists the top five banks in Canada, ranked by revenue. It highlights key facts about each institution, including their founding dates, customer base, number of branches, and notable services. The Canadian banking sector is described as one of the safest globally, comprising various financial entities.

title: VTEX Announces Launch of Initial Public Offering
summary: VTEX, a software-as-a-service digital commerce platform provider, announced the launch of its initial public offering. The offering comprises 19,000,000 Class A common shares, with an expected price between $15.00 USD and $17.00 USD per share, and VTEX intends to list its shares on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol "VTEX". The company plans to use the net proceeds for general corporate purposes and will not receive proceeds from shares sold by selling shareholders.

title: Shinhan promises a human touch at new Digilog branches
summary: Shinhan Bank has launched a new "Digilog" branch concept, aiming to combine digital technology with a human touch in a cafe-like setting. These branches offer digital services, financial seminars, and traditional banking counters, intending to differentiate Shinhan from big tech companies entering finance. The first three Digilog branches have opened in Seoul and Incheon, with another planned for Hanyang University.

title: La Bolsa porteña logró un alza de 3 por ciento en el comienzo semanal
summary: The Buenos Aires Stock Exchange (Bolsa porteña) saw a 3% increase at the start of the week, with the Merval index reaching 64,215.26 points. Argentine shares also rose sharply on Wall Street, led by BBVA, while public bonds showed a slight improvement. This positive movement aligns with global market gains and anticipated strong Q2 earnings reports from major US banks.

title: JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs to kick off earnings week
summary: JPMorgan Chase and Goldman Sachs are scheduled to release their second-quarter earnings on Tuesday, kicking off a week of major bank earnings reports. Analysts are anticipating strong year-over-year growth, with a consensus for earnings per share up 7% over the last three months. Despite some concerns about peaking earnings due to slowing trading activity and low interest rates, experts like Brian Belski of BMO Capital Markets remain optimistic about the overall market trajectory.

title: Buy, Borrow, Die: How Rich Americans Live Off Their Paper Wealth
summary: Wealthy Americans are increasingly using low-interest, securities-backed loans to fund their lifestyles and minimize tax liabilities. This "buy, borrow, die" strategy allows them to access cash without selling assets, thus avoiding capital-gains taxes, and is becoming a common practice among clients of major banks like Morgan Stanley and Bank of America. The trend is driven by rising stock markets and low interest rates, enabling the rich to leverage their paper wealth for various expenditures.

title: Around the house: newly-public Utz Brands names first general counsel
summary: Newly-public US snacks maker Utz Brands has appointed Theresa Robbins Shea as its first general counsel as part of a broader leadership team expansion since going public last August. The article also highlights other significant in-house legal appointments, including Matthew Martin as chief counsel for First Citizens Bank, Michael Garson as general counsel for SOS International, Hannah Kim as chief legal officer for Neiman Marcus Group, Alan Halfenger as general counsel for Arctaris Impact Investors, and Andrea Soria as director of legal for Tonal Systems. These appointments reflect a trend of companies bolstering their legal and compliance departments with experienced professionals.

title: Merrill Lynch adviser head count drops as self-directed investing soars
summary: Merrill Lynch saw a 6% decrease in its adviser head count, reaching 19,385 advisers by the end of June, partly due to a small number of trainee advisers not accepting positions in a new development program. Despite this, the firm's self-directed investing platform, Merrill Edge Guided Investing, gained significant traction with over 80,000 clients and $45 billion in assets. Merrill Lynch plans for low single-digit annual growth in its adviser population and has invested heavily in technology to enhance client services and attract new assets.

title: Envestnet taps UBS, iCapital to offer alternatives
summary: Envestnet has partnered with UBS and iCapital to launch an "Alternatives Exchange," providing curated alternative investment products to 106,000 advisors on its platform. This initiative addresses the growing demand for alternative assets, aiming to streamline access to investments like hedge funds, private equity, and venture capital, and democratize investment management for affluent investors. The exchange will also support Envestnet's new Private Wealth Consulting service for high-net-worth clients.

title: Japan's SMFG to buy nearly 5% of Jefferies for $386 million
summary: Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group Inc (SMFG) plans to acquire nearly 5% of Jefferies Financial Group Inc shares for $386 million to bolster its U.S. presence. The two companies will also form a partnership for cross-border M&A opportunities involving Japanese firms, and SMFG will provide substantial credit facilities to support Jefferies' lending. This move is part of SMFG's broader international expansion strategy, driven by limited growth opportunities in Japan.

title: Bank of America reports a big profit, and Citi and Wells Fargo beat expectations. (Published 2021)
summary: Bank of America reported a significant profit increase in the second quarter of 2021, more than doubling its earnings from the previous year, partly due to releasing funds set aside for loan losses. Citigroup and Wells Fargo also surpassed analysts' expectations, benefiting from consumers' increased spending and a recovering economy. Despite these strong earnings, Bank of America's revenue dropped, and its stock price fell as investors questioned the sustainability of loan growth amidst a potentially slowing economic rebound.

title: Core & Main Has Filed to Go Public, IPO Date and Price Explained
summary: Core & Main, a company specializing in fire protection and water infrastructure products, has filed initial documents with the SEC to go public under the symbol CNM. The IPO is expected to offer nearly 34.9 million shares at a price range of $20–$23 apiece, aiming for a valuation of up to $7.5 billion and potentially raising $802.3 million. Investment funds of private equity firm Clayton, Dubilier & Rice (CD&R) currently own Core & Main and will control about 79.6 percent of the company after the IPO is completed.

title: Stifel Announces Pricing of $300 Million of Non-Cumulative Perpetual Preferred Stock
summary: Stifel Financial Corp. announced the pricing of a $300 million public offering of 12,000,000 depositary shares, each representing a 1/1000th interest in a share of 4.50% Non-Cumulative Perpetual Preferred Stock, Series D. Dividends will be payable quarterly at an annual rate of 4.50%, and the offering is expected to close on July 22, 2021. Stifel plans to use the proceeds to redeem its outstanding Series A Preferred Stock and for general corporate purposes.

title: Dow drops nearly 300 points on Friday, snaps 3-week winning streak
summary: U.S. stocks, including the Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq Composite, fell on Friday, snapping three-week winning streaks, as inflation fears overshadowed strong retail sales and earnings. The Dow lost 299.17 points, or 0.86%, closing at 34,687.85 and ending the week down 0.52%. Consumer sentiment declined in early July, with inflation expectations rising to levels not seen since August 2008, contributing to the market sell-off.

title: Nomura Joins Wall Street Rivals in Boosting Pay for Juniors
summary: Nomura Holdings Inc. is increasing the starting salaries for its entry-level bankers to $100,000. This move aligns the Japanese brokerage with other major banks like Bank of America, Barclays, and JPMorgan Chase, which have also raised junior pay. The industry-wide pay hikes come as financial institutions strive to retain young talent amid a surge in deal activity and intense work-from-home demands.

title: Ruta de la Araucanía consigue un financiamiento con acreedores chilenos
summary: Ruta de la Araucanía Sociedad Concesionaria secured $23.8 million in financing from a syndicate of Chilean creditors, including Banco de Chile, Itaú Corpbanca, and Banco del Estado de Chile. This funding, obtained through a "Financing Opening and Modification Contract," will be used for project accounts and general corporate purposes. The concessionaire, a subsidiary of Intervial Chile, manages a 144.1-kilometer stretch of highway in southern Chile and was advised by Morales & Besa, while Larrain y Asociados Abogados represented the banks.

title: Huntington Bancshares Inc. stock underperforms Monday when compared to competitors
summary: Huntington Bancshares Inc. (HBAN) stock declined by 4.48% on Monday, closing at $13.23, amid a broad market downturn where the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average also fell. The stock's performance lagged behind some competitors but was comparable to others. This marks the second consecutive day of losses for the company, placing it $3.68 below its 52-week high.

title: UBS Wealth Americas’ Profit Hits Record, Execs Promise Improvement in Margin
summary: UBS Wealth Management Americas achieved a record profit of $505 million in the second quarter, a 136% increase year-over-year, driven by higher recurring fees and transaction income. Despite rising expenses, primarily due to advisor compensation, UBS executives, including CEO Ralph Hamers, assured analysts of future margin improvements by focusing on lending, fee-based assets, and affluent clients. The firm also saw significant inflows into its fee-based assets and lending services, while continuing to manage its broker headcount for increased productivity.

title: The newest addition to the Charlotte skyline just opened near Bank of America Stadium
summary: The 29-story FNB Tower, a mixed-use development, officially opened in uptown Charlotte near Bank of America Stadium. It will serve as the regional headquarters for First National Bank, offering luxury apartments, office space, retail, and a sky-deck terrace. The environmentally-friendly building, which began construction in January 2019, is designed to achieve LEED Certification and Three Green Globes for sustainability.

title: Derek Ellington, former BoA Triad market president, joins Wells Fargo as head of small business banking
summary: Derek Ellington, previously the Triad market president for Bank of America, has joined Wells Fargo as the new head of small business banking. He officially began his role at Wells Fargo on October 18, 2021. This move marks a significant career change for Ellington, transitioning from a regional leadership position at BoA to a national role at Wells Fargo.

title: Canada’s big banks need to show rebound in lending to avoid fate of U.S. counterparts: analysts
summary: Canadian banks are under pressure to demonstrate a rebound in their core lending business to avoid the negative investor reaction experienced by U.S. banks. While U.S. banks reported strong profits due to reserve recoveries and advisory fees, falling revenues and tepid loan demand caused their stock prices to drop. Analysts believe Canadian banks, reporting their fiscal third-quarter earnings in August, need to show better net interest income, with some hope for gradual loan growth evident in recent regulatory data, particularly in mortgages.

title: Traders should have fundamentals in place for better banking
summary: An expert panel organized by the Vidarbha Management Association (VMA) emphasized that traders and businessmen need to maintain good track records and strong fundamentals for successful negotiations and better banking benefits. The discussion, titled 'Banking on Banks', highlighted the importance of clear records, documentation, and technology in modern banking, while also touching upon interest rates and non-performing assets. VMA also recently conducted a workshop on Google Tools and aims to provide business management and leadership learning to its members.

title: MUFG Union Bank avoids closures with bare-bones branches
summary: MUFG Union Bank is transforming over 80% of its U.S. branches into smaller, stripped-down locations to reduce costs while maintaining customer accessibility, according to its new CEO. This move serves as a trial for its Japanese parent company. The bank aims to balance cost efficiency with customer reach in its U.S. operations.

title: Why are so many Merrill Lynch advisers leaving?
summary: Merrill Lynch is experiencing a significant departure of top advisers due to accelerating changes initiated by Bank of America. These changes, including shifts in recruiting, revamping training programs, direct outreach to clients, client retention teams, and limitations on portfolio management, suggest a new era where Bank of America asserts more control. Advisers are questioning their future at the firm as they perceive a diminished emphasis on their unique value and independence.

title: It's Looking Like a Fine Time to Consider Covered Call ETFs
summary: The article suggests that covered call ETFs, specifically the Global X Nasdaq 100 Covered Call ETF (QYLD), are an attractive investment option for income-focused investors, especially given potential market volatility. QYLD offers a substantial yield by selling covered calls on Nasdaq-100 components and can provide monthly income. While covered call strategies may underperform in rapidly rising markets, they tend to outperform in flat, down, or slightly up markets, making QYLD a credible long-term income alternative.

title: CAD explained: A guide to the Canadian dollar
summary: The Canadian dollar, also known as the 'loonie', is the national currency of Canada and consistently ranks among the top ten most traded currency pairs globally. This guide explores Canada's economy, the history of its currency, and key factors influencing its price, such as monetary policy, oil prices, and economic data releases. It also details popular CAD currency pairs like USD/CAD, EUR/CAD, and AUD/CAD, advising traders on considerations for each.

title: Leveraged Muni Funds Face Losses as Bond Rout Drags On
summary: Leveraged municipal bond funds are experiencing double-digit losses due to the worst bond rout in decades. Rising interest rates are impacting fund-share prices and reducing income payouts to investors. High net worth households had previously invested in these closed-end muni mutual funds, which hold approximately $60 billion, seeking tax-free income.

title: BlackRock, AmEx extend hybrid work plans as Omicron spreads across U.S.
summary: BlackRock and American Express are extending their hybrid work arrangements in response to the spread of the Omicron COVID-19 variant across the United States. BlackRock is offering employees flexibility to work remotely until January 28, while AmEx has delayed the launch of its "Amex Flex" program. This move mirrors actions by other Wall Street firms that have paused return-to-office plans due to rising infection rates.

title: MAS investigates online trading platform
summary: The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and the Commercial Affairs Department (CAD) are investigating Samtrade FX, an overseas online trading platform, for potential breaches of local securities laws related to operating without a capital markets services licence. Three men have been arrested in connection with the probe, which also revealed suspicions of irregular trading activities on the platform. Samtrade FX and its related entities have been on MAS’s Investor Alert List since July 2021.

title: BAC Credomatic completa fusión interna en Costa Rica
summary: BAC Credomatic has completed the merger of its businesses in Costa Rica, integrating several affiliated companies into Banco BAC San José, S.A. This move

title: Regions Financial Corp. stock rises Tuesday, outperforms market
summary: Regions Financial Corp. (RF) saw its stock rise 4.46% on Tuesday, closing at $23.68, outperforming the mixed market performance where the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose and the S&P 500 Index fell. The stock also surpassed several competitors and closed just below its 52-week high, with trading volume exceeding its 50-day average. This marks the second consecutive day of gains for the company.

title: European Energy Bills to Rise 54% From 2020 Level, BofA Says
summary: Bank of America Corp. predicts that European households will see their energy bills increase by an average of 54% compared to 2020 levels, primarily due to surging natural gas and power prices. This translates to an average residential consumer spending 1,850 euros this year, up from 1,200 euros in 2020. Italy and the U.K. are expected to experience the steepest rises, with bills jumping by approximately 950 euros.

title: FactSet and S&P’s CUSIP Global Services Enter $1.925B Deal
summary: FactSet announced a $1.925 billion all-cash acquisition of CUSIP Global Services (CGS) from S&P Global. This strategic move aims to enhance FactSet's role in global capital markets by integrating CGS's securities identification platform into its Content and Technology Solutions division. The deal is expected to be accretive to FactSet's adjusted diluted EPS in the first year and is contingent on regulatory approval and the completion of the S&P Global and IHS Markit merger.

title: Morgan Stanley, Robinhood Further Blur Traditional Brokerage and Self-Directed in Latest Branding Tweaks
summary: Morgan Stanley and Robinhood Financial have both taken steps that further blur the lines between traditional full-service brokerages and self-directed platforms. Morgan Stanley rebranded E*Trade to "E*TRADE from Morgan Stanley" and unified its logo colors, aiming to integrate its advisor force with self-directed clients. Concurrently, Robinhood launched "First Trade Recommendations," a tool designed to guide new customers to personalized ETF portfolios based on their risk profiles, signaling its move further into wealth management.

title: Cementos Pacasmayo recibe préstamo por 214,6 millones de dólares
summary: Cementos Pacasmayo has secured a medium-term loan of up to $214.6 million (860 million soles) from Scotiabank del Perú and Banco de Crédito del Perú. Miranda & Amado Abogados advised Credicorp Capital Servicios Financieros and Scotiabank del Perú as structuring agents. The company, a major cement producer in northern Peru, did not disclose the intended use of the funds.

title: Pinnacle Financial Partners Opens Full-Service Office in Huntersville
summary: Pinnacle Financial Partners has opened a new full-service office in Huntersville, NC, expanding its presence in Mecklenburg County with a team of veteran financial services professionals. The new office at 16633 Birkdale Commons offers a full range of banking and financial services, building on Pinnacle's significant growth in the greater Charlotte MSA. The team includes new additions and experienced advisors, solidifying Pinnacle's commitment to community-focused service with comprehensive financial solutions.

title: American Express Personal Loans Review
summary: This Bankrate review evaluates American Express personal loans, highlighting their competitive APRs, fully online application process, and minimal fees. However, it notes that loans are exclusive to existing American Express card members who receive a preapproval offer, limiting accessibility. The article details loan amounts, terms, and permissible uses, comparing American Express's offerings with those of other lenders like Wells Fargo and Discover.

title: Analyst Coverage | Investor Relations | Workday
summary: This Workday Investor Relations page lists the research analysts who cover the company. It explicitly states that analyst opinions, estimates, and forecasts are their own and do not represent Workday's views or endorsement. The page provides a comprehensive list of firms and their respective analysts covering Workday.

title: Lionsgate Studios Set to Open With Student Partnership Program
summary: Lionsgate Studios is opening its $500 million facility in Yonkers, NY, which will expand to 12 soundstages and a million square feet by mid-2023, making it one of the largest production facilities on the East Coast. Great Point Studios (GPS), which owns and manages the campus for Lionsgate, is partnering with Syracuse University to create a hands-on filmmaking course, providing students with experience across various production departments and internship opportunities. The initiative aims to address the shortage of film infrastructure in the region due to high demand from streaming and cable outlets.

title: Subsidiarias de peruana Urbanova reciben préstamo de 190 millones de dólares
summary: Subsidiaries of the Peruvian real estate company Urbanova secured a $190 million secured loan from a syndicate of banks to refinance a previous credit. The beneficiaries, Inmuebles Limatambo, Inversiones San Borja, and Urbanizadora Jardín, used the funds to repay an earlier loan and backed the new credit with a mortgage on their properties. Legal counsel for the transaction included Simpson Thacher & Bartlett and Rodrigo, Elías & Medrano Abogados for Urbanova, and Clifford Chance and Garrigues for the syndicate of banks led by Banco Santander.

title: Citigroup prepares to fire unvaccinated employees at the end of January. (Published 2022)
summary: Citigroup announced it will dismiss unvaccinated employees by the end of January, requiring all U.S. staff to submit proof of vaccination by January 14 or face unpaid leave and termination by January 31. This mandate is among the strictest on Wall Street, with over 90% of Citi's U.S. employees already complying, while other major banks have varying policies. The decision comes amidst broader discussions about vaccine mandates for large employers, with some employees resisting the policy.

title: BlackRock Inc. stock falls Friday, still outperforms market
summary: Shares of BlackRock Inc. (BLK) experienced a 0.36% decline on Friday, closing at $892.27, despite a generally dismal day for the stock market, which saw the S&P 500 Index and Dow Jones Industrial Average also fall. The company's stock, however, underperformed compared to some competitors like Bank of America Corp., INVESCO Ltd., and Affiliated Managers Group Inc., which all saw gains. BlackRock Inc. closed $80.89 short of its 52-week high, and its trading volume surpassed its 50-day average.

title: Deep Jaggi elevated as CEO of IndoStar
summary: Deep Jaggi has been promoted to CEO of IndoStar Capital Finance Ltd, an NBFC promoted by Brookfield and Everstone. Jaggi previously served as Chief Business Officer, where he was responsible for retail business development and collections, expanding the company's presence across India. He brings over two decades of experience from financial institutions like HDB Financial, Cholamandalam, and Apollo Tyres.

title: Bank OZK to Offer Peachtree Branch in Atlanta
summary: Bank OZK of Little Rock is expanding its presence in Atlanta's $115 billion-deposit market by opening its second full-service branch at 3215 Peachtree Road NE. Despite minimal deposits in Atlanta, Bank OZK holds the 10th-biggest total in Georgia with $5.7 billion and operates 68 full-service locations in the state, second only to Arkansas. Concurrently, Bank OZK is selling its Magnolia office to Peoples Bank of Magnolia for approximately $7.1 million.

title: These 14 bank stocks are in the best position to benefit from rising interest rates
summary: This article identifies 14 bank stocks poised to benefit from rising interest rates, based on a screen of various banks. It highlights Huntington Bancshares Inc. (HBAN) as a top performer expected to significantly increase its earnings per share through 2023, outpacing the S&P 500 Index. The piece delves into why these select few banks are projected to achieve double-digit earnings growth.

title: Bank of America to Cut Overdraft Fees to $10 From $35
summary: Bank of America announced it will cut its overdraft fees from $35 to $10 starting in May, following similar moves by other major banks. Regulators and politicians have been scrutinizing these fees, arguing they unfairly impact financially vulnerable families. This change comes after the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau highlighted overdraft fees charged by Bank of America, JPMorgan Chase, and Wells Fargo in a recent report.

title: Bank of America Slashes Fees for Account Overdrafts
summary: Bank of America announced significant reductions to its overdraft fees and the complete elimination of fees for non-sufficient funds (bounced checks), effective in May. The changes are expected to cut the bank's overdraft fee revenues by 97% compared to 2009 levels, following years of incremental steps to curb such charges. This move positions BofA among a growing number of banks, including Ally, PNC, Santander, and Capital One, that have recently eliminated or significantly reduced overdraft fees due to increased scrutiny from consumer advocates and regulators.

title: Nelson Bradshaw joins Farther’s investment office
summary: Nelson Bradshaw, former BBVA North Florida CEO, has joined Farther, a New York City-based digital family investment office, as managing director of Banking Strategies in Northeast Florida. He will focus on building the organization's regional banking strategy and a team of financial advisers for the Southeast market alongside Daniel Gilham. Farther aims to pair advisers with technology to manage client finances and capitalize on fintech growth in Jacksonville.

title: Looking to Trim $500-Mln Book, Merrill Vet Jumps to Morgan Stanley in Palo Alto
summary: Christina Yuni, a top-ranked Merrill Lynch broker with approximately $500 million in assets under management, has moved to Morgan Stanley's Palo Alto office. Yuni, who produced around $2.7 million annually at Merrill, aims to service a smaller client base with deeper relationships, a model she found untenable under Merrill's growth-based compensation grid. She was joined by Randi Wang and two support staff, while her husband is also a broker at Morgan Stanley.

title: US Banks Form Group to Offer USDF Stablecoin
summary: A consortium of U.S. banks, including New York Community Bank and FirstBank, plans to launch its own stablecoin called USDF. This initiative aims to provide a bank-minted alternative to existing stablecoins like Tether's USDT and Circle's USDC, addressing concerns about the reserves backing nonbank-issued stablecoins and potentially offering additional consumer protection. USDF will operate on the Provenance blockchain and be redeemable 1:1 for cash from member banks.

title: Morgan Stanley Quietly Embraces New Source of Broker Trainees
summary: Morgan Stanley has implemented a "Virtual Engagement Associates" (VEA) program to cultivate new broker talent and support its existing advisors. The program, launched in 2020, trains associates in client onboarding and technology, after which they can advance to formal advisor training, with alumni showing higher success rates. VEA also aims to increase diversity within its advisor ranks by providing a less risky and cost-effective talent pipeline for the firm.

title: JANELLE CURTIS NAMED CHIEF ENTERPRISE TRANSFORMATION OFFICER FOR WARNER MUSIC GROUP
summary: Janelle Curtis has been appointed as Chief Enterprise Transformation Officer for Warner Music Group. Her role will focus on driving tech-enabled evolution across the company's global corporate operations, business structures, processes, and digital solutions. Curtis brings extensive experience from Bank of America and Goldman Sachs to her new position.

title: HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Infosys and more...in a blockchain ETF's portfolio? That's possible
summary: This article discusses the misconception that Blockchain ETFs are solely for investing in cryptocurrencies, pointing out that cryptocurrencies are just one application of blockchain technology. The author suggests that a blockchain ETF's portfolio could include traditional financial powerhouses like HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, and Infosys. The article highlights how this broader understanding of blockchain technology can impact investment strategies.

title: Focus: Citigroup CEO Fraser fights to sell turnaround plan to investors
summary: Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser is struggling to convince investors and analysts that her radical overhaul of the bank will succeed, despite efforts to simplify the firm and exit non-core businesses. The bank's share price continues to lag rivals, reflecting skepticism after years of previous failed restructuring attempts. Fraser aims to transform Citigroup into a premier bank for institutions with cross-border needs, but market participants remain unconvinced by the progress so far.

title: NewcrestImage portfolio sale completed; Aimbridge to manage
summary: Summit Hotel Properties Inc. has completed the initial closing of its portfolio acquisition from NewcrestImage affiliates, with NewcrestImage transferring hotel management rights to Aimbridge Hospitality and gaining a minority stake in Aimbridge. This collaboration aims for growth, with NewcrestImage developing new hotels and Aimbridge expanding its operator services. The transaction involved 26 hotels initially, totaling $776.5 million for the portfolio, and is expected to be immediately accretive to adjusted FFO per share for Summit.

title: Wells Fargo Mortgage Production Fades As It Closes Branches
summary: Wells Fargo's mortgage loan production declined significantly in 2021, with an 8 percent overall fall and 27 percent fewer loans to homebuyers, coinciding with the closure of 270 branches and 16,000 layoffs. The bank originated $205 billion in home loans, down from $223 billion in 2020, even as it increased reliance on its retail branches for loan origination. Despite these declines in home lending revenue, the bank reported a stronger fourth quarter overall, with a 13 percent increase in total revenue to $20.9 billion and a $5.8 billion profit.

title: Proyecto vial Cambao - Manizales alcanza el cierre financiero
summary: The Cambao-Manizales road infrastructure project in Colombia has achieved financial close after obtaining a $114 million loan from Bancolombia and the CAF-AM Ashmore I Senior Debt Fund for Infrastructure in Colombia. This financing will enable the Concesionaria Alternativas Viales to fund the construction of the Ibagué-Honda and Cambao-Manizales corridor. The project is part of Colombia's 4G road concession program and has already reached 48.77% completion.

title: Truist reduces overdraft fees, joining other big banks
summary: Truist Bank announced it is reducing overdraft fees and implementing new checking account options to better serve vulnerable customers, expecting to save customers $300 million annually by 2024. This move follows similar actions by other major banks like Bank of America, Wells Fargo, Capital One, and Ally Bank, indicating an industry-wide shift away from reliance on overdraft fees. The bank plans to introduce a new checking account with a $100 buffer and a line of credit, along with a product for unbanked individuals that prevents overdrawing.

title: Frost Tower in downtown San Antonio is up for sale
summary: The Frost Tower, San Antonio's first new downtown office tower since 1989, is currently on the market. Completed in 2019 and valued at $99.5 million, the 24-story building is 80 percent leased, with Frost Bank occupying 61% of the space for its corporate headquarters until 2039. The sale does not impact Frost Bank's long-term lease or its commitment to downtown San Antonio.

title: Morgan Stanley CEO Boosts Wealth Margin Target to 30%-Plus
summary: Morgan Stanley CEO James Gorman announced a new target for the company's wealth management unit, aiming for a 30%-plus pre-tax profit margin. This ambitious goal is driven by unprecedented net new asset growth and anticipated rising interest rates. The wealth division achieved a 27% margin in 2021 (excluding acquisition costs) and brought in a record $438 billion in client assets the same year.

title: Bank of America Corp. stock falls Thursday, underperforms market
summary: Bank of America Corp. (BAC) shares fell 1.49% to $45.75 on Thursday, underperforming the broader market as the S&P 500 Index and Dow Jones Industrial Average also declined. The stock closed $4.33 below its 52-week high. Competitors JPMorgan Chase & Co. and Wells Fargo & Co. also saw declines, while Citigroup Inc. rose slightly.

title: Bank of America Adds Neal Nisargand, Citi’s Kaushik Banerjee for Tech Investment Banking
summary: Bank of America Corp. has expanded its technology investment-banking team by adding Kaushik Banerjee and Neal Nisargand. Banerjee, previously from Citigroup, rejoins as a managing director focusing on the semiconductor sector, while Nisargand joins as a director to support the global enterprise business. Both will be based in Palo Alto, California, strengthening BofA's tech investment banking capabilities.

title: Survey: Financial Advisors Increasingly Allocating to Crypto
summary: A new survey by Bitwise Asset Management and ETF Trends reveals that financial advisors are increasingly integrating crypto into client portfolios, with 15% already doing so and an additional 14% planning to this year. The trend is driven by high client interest, as 94% of advisors fielded crypto questions in 2021, and personal crypto holdings by nearly half of advisors. Despite concerns about volatility and regulatory uncertainty, many advisors anticipate significant growth in Bitcoin's value and prefer spot Bitcoin ETFs over futures-based alternatives for investment.

title: Cómo funcionará Nequi después de separarse de Bancolombia
summary: Bancolombia announced on December 15 its decision to separate from the Nequi platform. This article from January 24, 2022, discusses how Nequi will operate following this separation. The specific details of Nequi's new operational structure are expected to be outlined, clarifying its future independence from Bancolombia.

title: Bank of America Says a Digital U.S. Dollar Is ‘Inevitable’
summary: Bank of America strategists believe a digital U.S. dollar is "inevitable" and expect its issuance between 2025 and 2030. They consider central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) a natural progression of current electronic currencies. In the interim, privately issued digital currencies are anticipated to see increased adoption.

title: OCC approves national bank charter applications of fintech company
summary: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) has conditionally approved applications from Social Finance Inc. (SoFi) to establish SoFi Bank, National Association. This move brings SoFi under federal bank regulatory supervision, subjecting it to comprehensive regulations including the Community Reinvestment Act. The approval requires the new bank not to engage in crypto-asset activities, and SoFi Technologies is seeking to become a bank holding company.

title: Bank of America Employees to Share Stock Award of $1 Billion
summary: Bank of America is distributing $1 billion in restricted stock to almost all of its employees, with staff earning up to $500,000 annually eligible for the award. This move is part of an ongoing effort by financial firms to attract and retain talent in a competitive market. This marks the fifth consecutive year the bank has issued such compensation awards, bringing the total to $3.3 billion.

title: JPMorgan Chase: Driving Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion
summary: JPMorgan Chase is leveraging its supply chain and a US$30 billion commitment to enhance diversity, equity, and inclusion, particularly for Black, Hispanic, and Latino suppliers. The firm aims to increase spending with diverse businesses, requiring its top suppliers to do the same, and is addressing barriers such as cyber-readiness and access to capital through new programs and partnerships. These initiatives are designed to foster economic inclusion and drive cultural shifts across the business community.

title: JPMorgan Chase: Driving Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion
summary: JPMorgan Chase is actively promoting diversity, equity, and inclusion by focusing on its supply chain and committing to increased spending with Black, Hispanic, and Latino-owned businesses. The firm aims to spend an additional US$750 million with these businesses by 2025 and is partnering with TruSight to enhance the cybersecurity readiness of diverse suppliers. This initiative seeks to break down barriers to opportunity and foster sustainable diversity programs across the business community.

title: JPMorgan Chase: Driving Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion
summary: JPMorgan Chase is leveraging its supply chain to drive diversity, equity, and inclusion, particularly focusing on supporting Black, Hispanic, and Latino suppliers through a US$30bn commitment to close the racial wealth gap. The firm aims to increase diverse supplier spend by US$6bn, with US$1.2bn dedicated to Black, Hispanic, and Latino-owned businesses, and is developing initiatives like a cyber-readiness program with TruSight and a grant program to help diverse businesses meet industry requirements. These efforts demonstrate JPMorgan Chase's commitment to making diversity an integral part of its procurement strategy and fostering inclusive growth within the business community.

title: Bank of America Names 314 Managing Directors in One of Most Diverse Classes
summary: Bank of America has promoted 314 executives to managing director roles, marking one of the most diverse classes in the bank's history. Over 55% of the promotions were awarded to women or minorities, aligning with the bank's strategy to reward and retain talent amidst increasing competition. This move highlights Bank of America's focus on diversity within its leadership structure.

title: CRDO IPO News - Connectivity solutions provider Credo Technology Group prices downsized IPO at $10 low end
summary: Credo Technology Group Holding, a provider of semiconductor solutions for optical and electrical Ethernet applications, raised $200 million in its downsized IPO. The company offered 20 million shares, including an 8% secondary offering, at $10, which was the low end of its anticipated range. Credo Technology Group Holding will list on the Nasdaq under the symbol CRDO.

title: CAF grants A/B loan for USD 300 million to YPF S.A. to support its climate change adaptation and mitigation strategy
summary: CAF has granted an A/B loan of USD 300 million to YPF S.A. to support its climate change adaptation and mitigation strategy. This loan marks YPF’s return to the international financial market and is one of its first financings focused on emissions reduction and green projects. The transaction, involving several international financial institutions, aligns with CAF's goal of promoting green financing in Latin America.

title: TD Bank to add 2,000 technology roles in 2022, expanding workforce by 2%
summary: TD Bank announced plans to hire over 2,000 technology professionals in 2022 to boost its capabilities in engineering, automation, AI, cloud technology, and cybersecurity. This expansion will increase TD's current workforce by approximately 2.2% and comes as other industries are also competing fiercely for technology talent. The move addresses growing demand for online banking services and aligns with the bank's focus on prioritizing projects that drive growth, despite increased expenses.

title: BofA (BAC) Names 105 Managing Directors in Corporate, Investment-Banking Unit
summary: Bank of America (BAC) has promoted 105 executives to the managing director level within its global corporate and investment banking unit. This promotion recognizes the hard work and commitment of these individuals, positioning them for new levels of leadership and contribution to the firm. The selection process is highly competitive, as noted by Matthew Koder, president of global corporate and investment banking.

title: Estos son los bancos que conforman el Grupo Aval
summary: Grupo Aval, the largest financial group in Colombia, formally known as Grupo Acciones y Valores S.A., controls four major banks: Banco de Bogotá, Banco de Occidente Credencial, Banco AV Villas, and Banco Popular. The article highlights that three of these banks—Banco de Bogotá, Banco Popular, and Banco de Occidente—are among the best performing in the Colombian financial system based on various metrics. Grupo Aval serves approximately 10 million clients, generates over 50,000 direct jobs, and operates with around 2,000 offices, nearly 6,000 ATMs, and more than 45,000 banking correspondents.

title: Goldman Sachs leads U.S. banks in return to office
summary: Goldman Sachs led U.S. banks in recalling staff to the office on Tuesday as COVID-19 cases declined, with other major firms like Jefferies, Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, Citigroup, Bank of America, BNP Paribas, and Deutsche Bank following suit. Many banks had previously allowed staff to work from home during the winter Omicron wave. Several banks have implemented specific return-to-office policies, including vaccination requirements at Citi and regular testing at Deutsche Bank.

title: Bank of America Is Refusing to Forgive Some PPP Loans in Full, Giving Small Businesses Little Recourse
summary: Bank of America is reportedly denying full forgiveness for some Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) loans, leaving small business owners in a difficult position. Despite following initial rules, many found their loan forgiveness amounts pre-populated lower by the bank, preventing them from applying for full forgiveness or appealing directly through the SBA. Business owners affected by this issue have formed a support group, as their attempts to resolve the situation with the bank and federal regulators have been largely unsuccessful.

title: US and Chinese Banks Dominate the Top 10
summary: The Brand Finance Banking 500 2022 report indicates that the world's top 500 banking brands have seen a 9% year-on-year brand value growth, reaching an all-time high of US$1.38 trillion after three years of contraction. US banks account for five of the top ten most valuable brands, with Bank of America leading in the US. Chinese banks collectively represent one-third of the total brand value, and ICBC remains the world's most valuable banking brand at US$75.1 billion.

title: Bank of America plans to open 6 Columbus branches through 2023, a 50% increase
summary: Bank of America's first Columbus market president, Kelly D'Ambrosia, outlined plans for significant growth in the region. The bank aims to open 6 new branches in Columbus by the end of 2023, representing a 50% increase. This expansion is part of a larger strategy to boost hiring and internal employee development.

title: BofA (BAC) Chief Brian Moynihan Gets a 31% Raise to $32 Million
summary: Bank of America's CEO, Brian Moynihan, received a 31% increase in his compensation for 2021, bringing his total pay to $32 million. This raise follows a record year for profitability for the firm and reverses a pay cut he took in 2020 due to the pandemic. His package comprises a $1.5 million salary and $30.5 million in stock-based incentive awards.

title: Bank of America CEO receives 31% pay bump in 2021
summary: Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan received a 31% pay increase in 2021. Moynihan has served as CEO since 2010 and also took on the chairman role in 2014. The article briefly mentions related banking news from 2021, including local stories, credit union growth, branch closures, and the bank's minimum wage increase.

title: U.S. Bancorp stock falls Monday, still outperforms market
summary: U.S. Bancorp (USB) stock fell 0.20% on Monday to $59.58, despite a mixed trading session where the Dow Jones rose and the S&P 500 fell. The stock closed below its 52-week high but underperformed compared to competitors like Bank of America Corp., Citigroup Inc., and Wells Fargo & Co. Trading volume was also below its 50-day average.

title: Pinnacle Expands to North Fulton County in Atlanta
summary: Pinnacle Financial Partners is expanding its operations to North Fulton County in Atlanta, establishing a temporary presence and planning a full-service location for summer. The firm has hired a team of banking veterans, led by Scott Jordan as area manager, to serve clients in North Fulton, Gwinnett, and Forsyth Counties. This expansion is part of Pinnacle's broader growth strategy in Atlanta, building on its entry into the market two years prior.

title: After Turbulence, BofA’s Stocks Unit Finds Success With New Peacemaker Leader
summary: Bank of America's equities unit, led by Soofian Zuberi, posted a 19% jump in revenue in his first year, despite previous turbulence, personnel strife, and market swings. This performance helped the unit maintain its market share and narrowed the gap with the firm's fixed-income division. Zuberi's leadership is seen as crucial for future growth after a period of scrutiny and defections in the stocks business.

title: Bank of America Helping Employees at More Than 200 Companies Manage Everyday Financial Needs Through Corporate Employee Banking and Investing Program
summary: Bank of America's Corporate Employee Banking and Investing program, launched in 2020, has been adopted by over 200 corporate and commercial clients, covering nearly 3 million employees. This initiative helps employees manage everyday banking, lending, and investing needs, enhancing their financial wellness. The program is part of the broader Financial Life Benefits®, addressing a wide range of financial topics beyond traditional retirement planning, highlighting employers' growing responsibility for employee financial well-being.

title: Australia drops landmark cartel case against Citi, Deutsche Bank
summary: Australian prosecutors have dropped a landmark cartel case against Citigroup and Deutsche Bank, along with several former executives, concluding there were no longer reasonable prospects of conviction. The case, which centered on a 2015 share issue worth $1.8bn, would have been the country's biggest white-collar criminal trial and challenged the practices of investment banks in capital raisings. The banks and individuals involved maintained their innocence, stating they acted responsibly and in the interest of clients.

title: SoFi is ‘not just another neobank,’ Bank of America analyst says
summary: Bank of America analyst Mihir Bhatia initiated coverage of SoFi Technologies Inc. with a buy rating and a $17 price target, expressing a bullish view on the fintech company. Bhatia highlighted SoFi's broad range of financial services and its Galileo platform, which serves other neobanks, as key differentiators that make it more than just another neobank. SoFi went public in June 2021 through a SPAC merger.

title: Marcus & Millichap Arranges $5.8 Million Sale of Retail Strip Center in Orlando
summary: Marcus & Millichap has facilitated the $5.8 million sale of Shoppes at Lee, a 19,970-square-foot retail strip center in Orlando, Florida. The property, located at 1084 Lee Road, is home to tenants including FedEx Office, Boost Mobile, Little Caesar’s, and Trustco Bank. Nick Ledvora of Marcus & Millichap represented both the seller, Peak 14 LLC, and the buyer, Malhan Investments LLC, in the transaction.

title: Mobility or dexterity impairment
summary: Barclays Private Bank provides various accessibility features for customers with mobility or dexterity impairments, offering solutions across their app, online banking, telephone banking, and in-branch services. These include flexible login options, adjustable display settings, assistance for signing documents, and tailored communication preferences to ensure a comfortable and accessible banking experience.

title: Citigroup raises Fraser's pay by 32% after appointing her as CEO
summary: Citigroup increased CEO Jane Fraser's total compensation for 2021 by 31.6% to $22.5 million, citing her efforts to define priorities for boosting long-term shareholder value. This pay raise occurred after she formally took the helm in February 2021. Despite the increase, her compensation is lower than that of more experienced CEOs at rival, more profitable banks, such as JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, and Bank of America.

title: Regulators probe block trading at Wall Street banks, hedge funds- WSJ
summary: Federal investigators are reportedly probing block trading practices at major Wall Street firms, including Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs, and various hedge funds. The investigation, led by the SEC and Department of Justice, centers on whether bankers improperly shared confidential information about large share sales with hedge funds before public disclosure. Regulators are examining trading records and communications, suspecting some funds may have benefited from these early tips.

title: Axis Bank set to buy Citigroup’s India retail unit
summary: Axis Bank is nearing a deal to acquire Citigroup’s India retail banking business for an estimated $2.5 billion. The agreement, expected to be announced in the coming weeks, is contingent on approval from the Reserve Bank of India and would include a cash component of less than $2 billion after accounting for liabilities. This move is part of Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser's restructuring efforts to exit retail banking in 13 countries and focus on high-growth businesses.

title: Charlie Munger's Daily Journal scored a 15x return on a stock — and used margin debt to invest $87 million last quarter
summary: Charlie Munger's Daily Journal reportedly made a 15x return on BYD stock, selling $50 million worth and using the proceeds combined with $37 million in margin debt to acquire new securities last quarter. Despite Munger's previous warnings against using leverage, the investment immediately faced an unrealized loss of $30 million. Shareholders are anticipating Munger's explanation for this strategy at the upcoming annual meeting.

title: WSJ News Exclusive | Regulators Probe Block Trading at Morgan Stanley, Goldman, Other Wall Street Firms
summary: Federal investigators, including the SEC and Justice Department, are probing block trading practices at Wall Street firms like Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs. The investigation focuses on whether bankers improperly tipped off hedge-fund clients about large share sales before public disclosure. Regulators are examining communication records and trading activities to determine if funds benefited from such insider information.

title: Axis Bank set to buy Citigroup’s India retail unit
summary: Axis Bank is reportedly close to acquiring Citigroup Inc’s retail banking business in India for an estimated $2.5 billion. The agreement is expected to be announced within weeks, pending RBI approval, with Axis Bank prioritizing job security for current Citigroup employees. This acquisition follows Citigroup's announcement last year to exit its consumer banking business in India as part of a global strategic review.

title: MoneyGram Enters into Agreement to be Acquired by Madison Dearborn Partners
summary: MoneyGram International, Inc. announced a definitive agreement to be acquired by funds affiliated with Madison Dearborn Partners, LLC for $11.00 per share in an all-cash transaction valued at approximately $1.8 billion. This acquisition aims to accelerate MoneyGram's digital growth strategy and strengthen its market-leading cross-border capabilities. The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2022, after which MoneyGram will become a private company.

title: Goldman Sachs Appoints AlphaSense as the Exclusive Distributor of its Aftermarket Research
summary: AlphaSense, a leading market intelligence platform, announced an exclusive partnership with Goldman Sachs to distribute its aftermarket research through the AlphaSense platform. This collaboration will make Goldman Sachs' Global Investment Research (GIR) division's insights available to AlphaSense's broad customer base, including S&P 500 companies and major financial institutions. The integration of Goldman Sachs' research into AlphaSense's Wall Street Insights® (WSI) offering enhances the platform's ability to provide valuable market intelligence and support informed decision-making across various industries.

title: BofA Clients Are Most Underweight on Tech Stocks Since 2006
summary: A Bank of America survey reveals that fund managers are the most underweight on technology stocks since 2006, reflecting concerns over aggressive Federal Reserve policy tightening. This sentiment was evident even before a significant U.S. inflation report, which led investors to anticipate numerous Fed rate hikes in 2022. The net allocation to the tech sector has reached its lowest point in nearly 16 years.

title: ABG Shipyard Ltd Loan Fraud: LIC Grazed; ICICI, IDBI Worst-hit in Rs 22,842 cr Scam
summary: The Rs 22,842 crore loan fraud by ABG Shipyard Ltd has impacted several banks, with ICICI Bank and IDBI Bank being the worst hit, losing Rs 7,089 crore and Rs 3,639 crore respectively. Even IPO-bound LIC was grazed for Rs 136 crore, although this amount is reportedly secured. Other major lenders defrauded include SBI, Bank of Baroda, EXIM Bank, and Punjab National Bank, indicating widespread financial damage across both public and private sectors.

title: ICICI, IDBI, SBI, LIC hit in Rs 22,842 cr ABG scam State Bank of India had first reported the scam
summary: The article reports on the Rs 22,842 crore loan fraud allegedly committed by Gujarat-based ABG Shipyard Ltd (ABGSL), impacting several major banks and LICI. ICICI Bank suffered the largest loss, followed by IDBI Bank and SBI, which was the first to report the scam. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman noted that the ABG Shipyard account became a Non-Performing Asset (NPA) during the previous UPA regime, and banks detected the fraud faster than average.

title: Bloomberg Lab opens at Jones Leadership Academy
summary: Jones Leadership Academy of Business in Toledo, Ohio, has opened a new Bloomberg Lab Terminal, featuring a dozen monitoring units connected to the New York Stock Exchange. This initiative provides middle and high school students with hands-on experience in real-world business practices and opportunities to earn banking certifications. Toledo Public Schools partnered with the University of Toledo for this project, making it only the second urban district in the U.S. to receive such an investment.

title: HSBC appoints first Independent Board Chairman
summary: HSBC Bank (Singapore) Ltd has appointed Mrs. Penny Goh as its first Independent Board Chairman, succeeding Mr. Mervyn Fong. Mrs. Goh, who joined as an Independent Non-Executive Director in August 2019, previously served as Co-Chairman and Senior Partner of Allen & Gledhill LLP and holds other significant board positions. Her appointment is seen as crucial for HSBC Singapore's strategic growth, particularly in its ambition to double the total wealth balances of its Wealth and Personal Banking business in the next five years.

title: Canada's major banks go offline in mysterious hours-long outage
summary: Major Canadian banks, including RBC, BMO, Scotiabank, and CIBC, experienced a widespread hours-long outage, affecting online and mobile banking, as well as e-transfers. The cause of the outage is unknown but its timing is notable, occurring just days after the Canadian Prime Minister invoked the Emergencies Act, broadening anti-money laundering rules and authorizing banks to freeze accounts linked to illegal blockades. While some speculate a connection, banks like TD Bank denied widespread issues and the exact reason for the downtime remains unconfirmed.

title: Arch to up cyber underwriting
summary: Arch Capital Group plans to increase its cyber underwriting exposure, driven by market demand and corporate focus on security. CEO Marc Grandisson noted that "fear is driving the market right now," leading to minimized moral hazard as corporate and insurer interests align. Despite potential for widespread losses, Arch aims to remain prudent by tracking aggregates while expanding its cyber insurance offerings.

title: Celanese to buy DuPont’s materials arm for $11 billion
summary: Celanese Corp. has agreed to acquire the majority of DuPont de Nemours Inc.'s mobility and materials arm for $11 billion in cash, marking Celanese's largest-ever acquisition. This strategic move aims to establish Celanese as a leading global specialty materials company, expecting to generate significant synergies and boost earnings per share by 2026. DuPont plans to use the proceeds to fund its acquisition of Rogers Corp. and other M&A opportunities, as it transforms into a company focused on electronics, automotive, and water and industrial technologies.

title: Barclays Named Prime Broker of the Year in 2022 Risk Magazine Awards
summary: Barclays has been honored as the Prime Broker of the Year in the 2022 Risk Magazine Awards, recognized for its overall strategy, focus, and significant gains over the last five years. The award highlights Barclays' integrated approach, technology, and selectivity, which have contributed to its success in the prime brokerage market, moving it to the #5 global ranking from joint #9 in 2016. The firm's global prime brokerage services encompass financing for various asset classes, strategic consulting, and capital introductions.

title: Raymond James says buy the dip in Fastly, stock can rebound more than 80%
summary: Raymond James believes the drop in Fastly's stock was an overreaction to its fourth-quarter results and 2022 revenue projections, despite the company forecasting less revenue and wider losses. Analyst Frank Louthan upgraded Fastly to "strong buy" from "outperform," maintaining a price target that suggests an 84% rebound, emphasizing the stock's undervaluation and strong growth potential. The firm expects the stock to climb back to its historical trading range assuming no further widespread customer outages and consistent execution.

title: Officials warn of new phishing scam to get bank information
summary: Officials are warning about a new type of phishing scam, known as smishing, where scammers send fake text messages appearing to be from banks like Huntington and PNC to steal banking information. Two local women nearly fell victim to these sophisticated scams. The article advises contacting banks directly to verify suspicious messages and provides resources from the FBI, FCC, Huntington Bank, and PNC on how to identify and protect against such fraudulent attempts.

title: CSB Bank appoints Sharad Kumar Saxena as Additional Director for 3 years term
summary: CSB Bank has appointed Sharad Kumar Saxena as an Additional Director (Non-Executive & Independent) for a three-year term, effective February 19, 2022, pending shareholder approval. Saxena brings over 30 years of IT experience from the Railways and Banking sectors, having held significant leadership roles at ICICI Bank and Bank of Baroda. At the time of the announcement, CSB Bank's shares were trading up by 1.05% on the BSE.

title: Waterstone Mortgage Review: Home Purchase Loan Experts Who Strive to Close On Time
summary: This article reviews Waterstone Mortgage, highlighting its unique position as a subsidiary of a large bank with a local feel, offering an expansive range of loan products. It emphasizes their expertise in home purchase loans, especially in competitive markets, and their commitment to timely closings while noting the absence of online rate disclosures as a potential drawback.

title: Banking giant asks court to strike out part of AXA’s multimillion-dollar lawsuit
summary: Santander Group has requested a London court to dismiss portions of a £624 million lawsuit filed by AXA concerning mis-sold payment protection insurance (PPI). Santander claims that AXA's argument of a binding settlement agreement is "disingenuous" as no such agreement was finalized or executed, citing email correspondence. AXA, however, argues that the settlement is binding based on the conduct of both parties, despite the lack of signed paperwork, and seeks a trial to resolve the issue.

title: Bank of America, Capital One Rake In Billions While Denying Customers COVID Hardship Relief
summary: Bank of America and Capital One are facing class-action lawsuits for allegedly denying customers COVID-19 hardship relief despite promising assistance. The lawsuits claim the banks continued to charge late fees and interest while generating billions in revenue, breaching good faith and violating consumer protection laws. Plaintiffs seek restitution for fees and damages, arguing the banks failed to provide meaningful financial aid during the pandemic.

title: Zevia Announces Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2021 Results
summary: Zevia PBC reported strong financial results for the fourth quarter and full year 2021, with net sales increasing by 23% and 26% respectively, driven by broad-based volume gains. The company outlined its strategic plan for continued growth, including channel expansion and innovation, and provided optimistic net sales guidance for 2022. Despite inflationary pressures impacting gross margin, Zevia maintained its commitment to providing affordable, zero-sugar, plant-based beverages and demonstrated significant progress in its ESG metrics.

title: Citigroup to Get Rid of Overdraft Fees, the Biggest Bank to Do So (Published 2022)
summary: Citigroup announced it will eliminate overdraft and returned item fees by summer, becoming the largest bank to do so. This decision follows similar moves by smaller lenders like Capital One and Ally Financial, and comes amidst increasing pressure from regulators who argue these fees disproportionately affect financially vulnerable customers. Other banking giants like Bank of America have cut their overdraft fees, but none have fully eliminated them.

title: Rocket Companies Report Down Earnings, But Issue Special Dividend
summary: Rocket Companies reported a significant drop in annual revenue and net income for 2021 compared to 2020, as well as lower fourth-quarter results. Despite the decrease in earnings, the company announced a special dividend of $1.01 per share and a share repurchase program worth $300 million. CEO Jay Farner highlighted a record year in loan origination and the strategic importance of the Truebill acquisition for client engagement and long-term goals.

title: List of Banks and Lenders with SBA Loan Guarantee Agreements
summary: This article provides a comprehensive list of banks and lenders in New Hampshire that offer small business loans under SBA loan guarantee agreements. It details contact information including addresses, phone numbers, and websites for each institution. The list serves as a valuable resource for small businesses seeking financing options in the region.

title: Goldman Probed by SEC Over Messages Sent Using Unapproved Services
summary: Goldman Sachs Group Inc. is being investigated by the SEC for employees' use of unapproved messaging services for business communications. This probe follows similar actions against other major financial institutions, including JPMorgan, which faced $200 million in fines, and HSBC, which is also being investigated by the CFTC for similar issues. Goldman Sachs is cooperating with the SEC and providing requested documents.

title: SunTrust Bank Permanently Closed
summary: The SunTrust bank branch at 8700 Georgia Ave. in downtown Silver Spring has permanently closed following the consolidation of operations into Truist after BB&T Bank acquired SunTrust in 2019. This closure is part of Truist's "core conversion" process, which has led to some customer issues, including temporary loss of access to debit cards and bank accounts. These conversions are affecting all former BB&T and SunTrust customers as they transition to Truist products and digital platforms.

title: Safehold Announces Public Offering and Concurrent Private Placement
summary: Safehold Inc. announced a public offering of 1,750,000 shares of its common stock, with underwriters having an option to purchase an additional 262,500 shares. Concurrently, Safehold will sell shares to iStar Inc. in a private placement. The net proceeds will be used for additional ground lease investments, to repay borrowings, and for general corporate purposes.

title: Morgan Stanley Forgoes Subtlety in Recruiting Video Targeting Merrill Lynch Brokers
summary: Morgan Stanley Wealth Management created a nearly five-minute recruiting video directly targeting Merrill Lynch brokers using testimonials from former Merrill advisors. The video critiques Merrill Lynch's culture and product offerings while praising Morgan Stanley's support for its wealth management division. This aggressive tactic is seen as an attempt by Morgan Stanley to capitalize on its positive recruiting trend and Merrill Lynch's recent attrition.

title: BlackRock Inc. stock underperforms Friday when compared to competitors
summary: BlackRock Inc. (BLK) shares fell 4.95% on Friday to $696.59, underperforming the broader market as the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average also declined. This marked the second consecutive day of losses for the stock, placing it significantly below its 52-week high. Competitors like Bank of America Corp., INVESCO Ltd., and Affiliated Managers Group Inc. also saw their shares fall, although BlackRock's decline was substantial.

title: SERNAC lanza primer comparador de tarjetas de crédito
summary: SERNAC has launched the first-ever Credit Card Comparator in Chile, a tool designed to help consumers compare all associated charges of credit cards available in the market. This tool aggregates information from 194 cards, highlighting significant differences in maintenance fees, cash advance charges, and foreign transaction fees. The initiative aims to empower consumers to make more informed financial decisions, prevent over-indebtedness, and encourage competitive practices among financial institutions.

title: International Arbitration After the Pandemic
summary: The article discusses the resurgence of international arbitration after the COVID-19 pandemic, driven by growth in cross-border trade and investment. It highlights the rapid expansion of international disputes and the rebalancing of dispute resolution activity towards Asian centers. The publication also anticipates new disputes from COVID-19 disruptions, energy transition, and financial distress, while noting reforms in Investor State Dispute Settlement.

title: SIRIANNI: Morgan Stanley’s Moment
summary: Tony Sirianni discusses Morgan Stanley's revamped recruiting strategy and unique position in the wealth management industry. He highlights Morgan Stanley's success in attracting advisors, contrasting its approach with Merrill Lynch and other wirehouses, particularly its focus on a strong, advisor-centric culture. The article suggests Morgan Stanley has carved out a distinct identity as a large full-service firm, appealing to veteran wire advisors who might be dissatisfied with bank-owned platforms.

title: The Buzz Online
summary: This article, "The Buzz Online," highlights various professional appointments, promotions, and achievements in New Hampshire. Key updates include new hires and promotions at banks like St. Mary's Bank, Meredith Village Savings Bank, and Merrimack County Savings Bank, as well as academic honors at Plymouth State University and a significant medical appointment at Dartmouth-Hitchcock's Norris Cotton Cancer Center. Additionally, it announces a donation to NHTI's Paramedic Emergency Medicine program and the launch of the 41st Annual Prouty.

title: Huntington Bancshares Inc. stock outperforms competitors despite losses on the day
summary: Huntington Bancshares Inc. (HBAN) shares fell 4.54% on Monday, closing at $14.09, amidst a broader market decline where the S&P 500 and Dow Jones also experienced losses. Despite this, HBAN outperformed several competitors, including Bank of America Corp. (BAC), Fifth Third Bancorp (FITB), and F.N.B. Corp. (FNB), which saw larger percentage drops. The stock closed $3.70 below its 52-week high, with trading volume exceeding its 50-day average.

title: Onnet Fibra Colombia, de KKR y Telefónica, recibe financiamiento
summary: Onnet Fibra Colombia, a joint venture between KKR and Telefónica Colombia, secured a syndicated loan equivalent to $221 million from several banks including Scotiabank Colpatria S.A., Bancolombia S.A., BBVA Colombia, and The Bank Of Nova Scotia. These funds will finance KKR's acquisition of Telefónica Colombia's fiber optic assets for $500 million. Onnet Fibra Colombia, which began operations in January 2022, provides a neutral fiber-to-the-home (FTTH) network with a current coverage of 1.2 million homes and aims to reach 4.3 million customers by the end of 2024.

title: Regulators put UnitedHealth-Change Healthcare Merger on Life Support
summary: The Department of Justice has filed a lawsuit to block UnitedHealth Group's $13 billion acquisition of Change Healthcare, Inc., disagreeing with the companies' claim that the merger would benefit consumers through streamlined healthcare processes and reduced costs. The DOJ argues that the deal would allow UnitedHealth to gain unfair access to competitors' sensitive information and control healthcare technology innovations, highlighting a shift in antitrust enforcement under the Biden administration.

title: ‘Black Panther’ Director Ryan Coogler Mistaken for Bank Robber in Atlanta
summary: Ryan Coogler, the director of "Black Panther," was briefly detained by police in Atlanta after Bank of America employees mistook him for a bank robber. Coogler was attempting to discreetly withdraw a large sum of cash, which led the teller to incorrectly believe a robbery was in progress. Bank of America has since apologized to Coogler for the incident.

title: Huntington to cut overdraft fees from $36 to $15 starting in July
summary: Huntington Bank announced it would reduce overdraft and non-sufficient funds fees from $36 to $15 starting in July, following similar moves by other major banks. Additionally, the bank will introduce a feature in April allowing customers immediate access to up to $500 from check deposits. This strategy, estimated to cost the bank $14 million per quarter initially, is expected to attract new customers and reduce attrition in the long term.

title: Russia risks "imminent" default on its debt, Wall Street analysts say
summary: Russia is facing an "imminent" default on its debt due to groaning under Western sanctions, according to credit ratings agencies and Wall Street firms. Fitch downgraded Russia's debt for the second time in a week, citing the high likelihood of default and the impact of sanctions on its ability and willingness to repay. With $700 million in payments due in March and a 30-day grace period, a default could occur as early as mid-April, further isolating Russia from international financial flows.

title: Goldman Sachs CEO Says Ostracizing Russia Isn’t the Finance Industry’s Job
summary: Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon stated that it is not the finance industry's job to ostracize Russia, but rather to follow government sanctions. He emphasized that businesses should implement policies set by the government, agreeing with the sanctions against Russia's actions in Ukraine. Despite this stance, the article highlights Goldman Sachs's historical involvement in Russia's economic policy and its mixed record on activism.

title: New agriculture practices are preserving Brazil’s forests
summary: CHS Brazil is implementing new agricultural practices and participating in programs to combat deforestation in Brazil. They are committed to ensuring crops are grown on existing agricultural land, not illegally cleared forest land, and have received a "green" loan for their sustainable sourcing practices. The company also collaborates with NGOs and involves employees in reforestation efforts.

title: Old-School Leveraged Loan Market Is a Step Closer to Ditching Faxes
summary: A consortium of Wall Street banks, including Bank of America, Citigroup, and JPMorgan Chase, has launched Versana, a new platform aimed at modernizing the $1.38 trillion U.S. leveraged loan market. This initiative seeks to centralize data management for lenders, moving away from current manual tracking methods that still occasionally involve faxes. Credit Suisse has also joined the portal, which is expected to improve efficiency and reduce settlement times in the notoriously complex market.

title: EXCLUSIVE: Morgan Stanley Calls Brokers Back to Offices, Sets 90-Day Cap on WFH
summary: Morgan Stanley Wealth Management is implementing a new policy limiting most of its 16,000 brokers to 90 days of remote work per year, effective July 1. This move aims to bring staff back to offices and ensure compliance with supervisory obligations. Brokers can apply for alternative remote work locations based on criteria like length of service or production club membership, subject to additional supervision.

title: Why Mubadala Bought Taco Bell's K-Mac in History-Making Deal
summary: Mubadala Investment Co., a state-owned holding company from Abu Dhabi, made a significant investment in K-Mac Enterprises, a U.S.-based Taco Bell operator. This deal, which occurred last October, marks the first time a Middle East sovereign wealth fund has invested in a U.S. restaurant franchisee. The move highlights Mubadala's strategy to diversify investments away from oil and signals a growing trend of sovereign wealth funds seeking premier platforms in the U.S. restaurant sector.

title: Bank of America Adviser Ousted After Rant Is Hired by Brokerage Aegis Capital
summary: James Iannazzo, a former Bank of America financial adviser who was fired after a widely circulated video showed him in a tirade at a smoothie shop, has been hired by Aegis Capital Corp. FINRA data confirms his registration with the New York-based broker-dealer as of March 15. His specific role at the new company was not disclosed.

title: Lloyds share price: to break the 100p resistance barrier?
summary: The Lloyds Banking Group share price has struggled since the 2008 financial crisis, remaining a "penny stock" below the 100p resistance level. However, recent strong full-year results and rising UK interest rates, particularly from the Bank of England, could help the bank break this psychological barrier. While increasing rates pose some risks of mortgage defaults, historically, Lloyds' share price has closely tracked UK interest rates, suggesting a potential recovery closer to pre-crisis norms.

title: Expedia Group CPO on risk management & strategic sourcing
summary: Reagan Smith, Head of Global Corporate Procurement at Expedia Group, discusses his journey into procurement, his biggest career influences, and his passion for elevating the indirect procurement function. He emphasizes continuous learning, challenging established practices, and aligning procurement strategies with business needs for success. Smith also shares personal anecdotes, including his pride in advocating for the LGBTQ community.

title: Georgia Power Foundation pledges $2.5 million to the HUB for Community Innovation project
summary: The Georgia Power Foundation has pledged $2.5 million to the HUB for Community Innovation project, bringing its total funding to $21 million out of a $33.5 million goal. This investment is part of Georgia Power's five-year, $87 million commitment to advancing racial equity and social justice. The HUB will house four local nonprofits and aims to revitalize the Harrisburg and Laney Walker neighborhoods.

title: Alaska Air Group and Bank of America Renew Long-Term Partnership Agreement
summary: Alaska Air Group and Bank of America have renewed their co-branded credit card agreement through 2030, extending a decades-long partnership. This collaboration aims to enhance guest benefits and further drive strategic growth for both companies, particularly in West Coast regions. Additional cardholder benefits are anticipated to be introduced in the latter half of 2022.

title: Alaska Air Group provides update on long-term growth strategy
summary: Alaska Air Group is hosting its Investor Day to outline its long-term growth strategy, emphasizing successful pandemic recovery, industry outperformance in guest experience, and financial strength. The company plans to grow 4-8% annually through 2025 by deepening its network, transitioning to a single, more efficient fleet, and enhancing its loyalty program through an extended partnership with Bank of America. They also reiterate commitments to sustainable practices and provide a positive full-year 2022 outlook with specific financial metrics.

title: JD.com’s logistics unit seeks up to US$1.1 billion via placement
summary: JD Logistics, the logistics unit of JD.com, is seeking to raise up to US$1.1 billion through a new share placement.
