The page also features recent articles related to shares and client reviews of the Capital.com platform.

title: Costco’s results will show us how important bargains still are for shoppers
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. is set to release its quarterly earnings, which are anticipated to highlight the continued importance of value for consumers. The results will also shed light on the performance disparity between warehouse retailers like Costco, Walmart, and Amazon compared to other retailers. This earnings report is expected to provide key insights into current retail trends.

title: Costco’s Popular Kirkland Baby Diapers Are Shifting Suppliers
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. is changing the manufacturer for its Kirkland Signature brand diapers from Kimberly-Clark Corp. to First Quality. This change, effective in January, comes as Kimberly-Clark scales back its private label businesses to improve profitability.

title: Costco’s Extremely In-Demand Item Will Drop In Quality, Insiders Say
summary: Costco's popular Kirkland Signature Diapers are reportedly switching manufacturers from Kimberly-Clark Corp. (Huggies) to First Quality (Cuties) starting in January due to Kimberly-Clark's desire to focus on premium brands. This change has led to fears among shoppers that the quality of the beloved and affordable Kirkland diapers may decline, despite currently being lauded for their similarity to Huggies. Customers and experts suggest that any change in product quality following the supplier switch will be noticeable to consumers.

title: Schwab Fundamental U.S. Large Company ETF (FNDX) Stock Price Quote Today & Current Price Chart
summary: This article provides the current stock price quote and chart for the Schwab Fundamental U.S. Large Company ETF (FNDX), highlighting its current trading data, key statistics, and CFD trading conditions. It details aspects like spread, overnight funding adjustments, margin requirements, and commission. The page also features a section with related market articles and customer reviews for the trading platform.

title: Albertsons sues Kroger after judge rules against grocery merger
summary: Albertsons has formally terminated its proposed $25 billion merger with Kroger and is suing its competitor, alleging Kroger violated their contract regarding the deal's approval process. This legal action follows a judge blocking the planned tie-up and highlights a dispute over responsibility for legal fees and a potential $600 million termination fee. Kroger has called Albertsons' allegations "baseless and without merit."

title: Albertsons gives up on Kroger merger, sues grocery chain
summary: Albertsons is suing Kroger and abandoning their $24.6 billion merger after judges halted the deal, citing Kroger's alleged failure to secure regulatory approval. Albertsons claims Kroger did not exert "best efforts" to overcome antitrust objections, which Kroger denies, accusing Albertsons of breaching the merger agreement. The lawsuit follows preliminary and permanent injunctions issued in federal courts in Oregon and Washington.

title: GROCERY MEGA-MERGER: Day after court rulings, Albertsons/Safeway bags the plan
summary: Albertsons has officially terminated its merger agreement with Kroger following injunctions issued by courts in Oregon and Washington state on December 10, 2024. Albertsons announced its decision while also filing a lawsuit against Kroger, accusing Kroger of willfully breaching the merger agreement. Kroger, in turn, called the lawsuit "baseless and without merit."

title: What’s ahead for Kroger & Albertsons after their failed merger
summary: Following the failed $24.6 billion merger between Kroger and Albertsons due to regulatory blocking, both companies are now seeking individual strategies to gain market share. Key areas of focus include investing in e-commerce and advertising platforms, expanding private label brands, and potentially pursuing smaller, non-overlapping mergers or acquisitions. The Federal Trade Commission and state attorneys general hailed the merger's failure as a victory for consumers, preventing higher grocery prices.

title: Genetically Engineered Salmon Production Ends as AquaBounty Shutters Last Facility
summary: AquaBounty Technologies (NASDAQ: AQB) has announced the cessation of all genetically engineered AquAdvantage® salmon production, the culling of remaining fish, and the closure of its last North American facility in Prince Edward Island, Canada. This decision follows decades of controversy, market rejection, and legal challenges, with the company citing insufficient liquidity to maintain operations. Environmental groups, Indigenous communities, and allies celebrate this as a victory against GE food animals and emphasize the importance of sustainable wild salmon and ecosystem protection.

title: Kroger to move on from failed Albertsons merger 'from a position of strength'
summary: Kroger has terminated its $24.6 billion agreement to acquire Albertsons Cos. after regulatory injunctions, stating it is no longer in its best interests to pursue the merger. Following the termination, Kroger plans to resume share repurchases with a new $7.5 billion buyback program, leveraging its strong balance sheet to invest in business growth and return capital to shareholders. The company will continue with its "Leading with Fresh and Accelerating with Digital" strategy, focusing on investments in lower prices, higher associate wages, and store network expansion.

title: Costco Goes Greener in Latest Fiscal Year
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. has released its annual update on sustainability commitments, detailing progress in operations, people and communities, and merchandising. The company is actively working on its Climate Action Plan, expanding its workforce dashboard, and increasing sustainable merchandise offerings by engaging directly with suppliers and partnering with organizations like the Seafood Task Force. These efforts align with an evolving regulatory landscape and Costco's commitment to a more sustainable future for its stakeholders.

title: Is Moderna Stock Underperforming the Dow?
summary: Moderna (MRNA) stock has significantly underperformed the Dow Jones Industrials Average, plummeting 75.5% from its 52-week high and 57.9% year-to-date. This underperformance is attributed to declining COVID-19 vaccine sales and uncertainty surrounding future revenue growth, despite the company's large market cap and mRNA technology advantage. Wall Street analysts are cautious, giving MRNA a "Hold" rating with an 88.2% potential upside from current levels.

title: Luxury furniture designer to open in shuttered NW 23rd space
summary: King Living, a luxury furniture designer, is set to open its third U.S. showroom in the former Williams Sonoma storefront in Northwest Portland next summer. This expansion marks a new development for the area, utilizing a previously shuttered retail space. The article was written by Sara Edwards for the Portland Business Journal.

title: 5 lessons for grocers from the Kroger-Albertsons saga
summary: The collapse of the Kroger-Albertsons merger offers five critical lessons for the grocery industry, ranging from effective merger messaging to the risks of mega-mergers and the importance of strategic divestiture partners. Analysts suggest that Albertsons must now redefine its competitive strategy, while Kroger may pursue smaller acquisitions. The saga underscores the ongoing vulnerability of traditional supermarkets against giants like Walmart and Costco, potentially leading to more M&A activity driven by the need for scale.

title: Join the club: The economics of membership retail
summary: The article discusses the growing trend of membership retail, highlighting how warehouse clubs like BJ's and Costco have recently increased their membership fees and continue to see high renewal rates. It also explores the expansion of subscription models beyond traditional clubs, noting how giants like Amazon and Target are leveraging subscriptions for delivery and perks, and how niche lifestyle brands like Fabletics and Liquid I.V. are entering this space to cater to younger consumers' hobbies and interests. The piece emphasizes the benefits for both consumers, who receive convenience and extras, and companies, which gain recurring revenue and engaged customers.

title: Liberty Hill moves closer to reeling in its 'whale': Costco
summary: Costco is reportedly moving closer to opening its seventh Austin-area location in Liberty Hill, Texas. The retail giant appears to have a site under contract, although the construction timeline remains unclear. This expansion signifies continued growth for Costco in the Austin metropolitan area.

title: Christmas Eve 2024: Store hours for Costco, Walmart, Walgreens, Target and more
summary: This article provides a comprehensive list of Christmas Eve 2024 store hours for numerous major retailers including Walmart, Target, Costco, and Walgreens. Many stores will close early on Christmas Eve, with some, like Big Lots and Party City, facing store closures and liquidation sales, highlighting the compressed shopping season. Shoppers are advised to check local store websites or apps for the most accurate hours.

title: What Stores Are Open and Closed on Christmas Eve and Christmas Day?
summary: This article provides a comprehensive guide to the operating hours of various stores, financial institutions, pharmacies, and postal services on Christmas Eve and Christmas Day 2024. Many businesses will be closed or have reduced hours, particularly on Christmas Day, to allow employees to celebrate the holiday. Shoppers are advised to check local store hours, especially for independently owned businesses.

title: The Walmart Effect
summary: New research suggests that Walmart has a broadly negative economic impact on the communities it operates in, challenging the long-held belief that its low prices significantly benefit consumers. Two papers indicate that the costs of lower earnings and higher unemployment outweigh the savings for shoppers, ultimately making communities poorer. The findings also question the consumer-welfare standard used in antitrust regulation, suggesting it overlooks broader economic impacts beyond price.

title: 3 Stocks With Rising Prices That Are Likely to Split in 2025
summary: The article identifies Broadcom (AVGO), Casey's General Stores (CASY), and Costco (COST) as companies whose stock prices are high enough to warrant a stock split in 2025. Stock splits make shares more affordable, increase market liquidity, and signal company confidence, often leading to outperformance. The author details the financial health and growth drivers for each company, reinforcing the likelihood of future splits.

title: Costco Drops Amid Yield Concerns: Why $900 Could Be the Next Big Opportunity
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. (COST) experienced a 3% drop due to rising 10-year Treasury yields, signaling investor concerns about inflation and consumer spending. Despite a strong 43% gain in 2024, the selloff highlights macroeconomic headwinds. Analysts are watching the stock's 50-day moving average, with a potential short-term target of $900, which could be a buying opportunity for long-term investors.

title: Costco defends DEI program as other major retailers drop controversial diversity push
summary: Costco's board of directors is urging shareholders to vote against a proposal to eliminate its Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) program, defending its practices as beneficial for employees, members, and suppliers. This comes as other major retailers have scaled back similar initiatives following a Supreme Court ruling and warnings from state attorneys general. The National Center for Public Policy Research is challenging Costco's DEI program, alleging it involves discriminatory practices and rebrands rather than eliminates problematic policies.

title: Costco to shut down 500 stores for 24 hours with Aldi and Sam's Club also closed
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp will close all 500+ of its U.S. stores on New Year's Day, January 1, 2025, following a Christmas Day closure. Other major retailers like Aldi and Sam's Club will also be closed, while Walmart, Target, and Kroger will maintain normal operating hours. All affected retailers will resume regular operations on January 2.

title: 3 Reasons Costco Stock Will Have More Room to Run in 2025
summary: Costco (NASDAQ: COST) stock, despite a recent dip, is poised for further growth in 2025 due to strong customer retention, ambitious expansion plans including e-commerce, and a robust cash balance. The company's recent membership fee increase has not impacted its high retention rate, and ongoing store openings and digital growth, alongside a significant cash position and potential future stock split, suggest continued upside.

title: How Vending Kiosks Curb Store Shrink and Optimize Labor
summary: Cantaloupe, Inc. has expanded its Smart Store vending machine line (600 and 700 models) for grocery stores, aiming to reduce shrink, optimize labor, and offer convenient shopping for shelf-stable and fresh items. These machines use weighted shelves and cameras for inventory monitoring and allow various payment methods. According to Cantaloupe's chief revenue officer, Jeff Dumbrell, the kiosks can nearly eliminate theft and improve customer experience by speeding up transactions, even for high-cost items typically prone to theft.

title: 3 new Costco stores are coming to this booming area of North Texas
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. plans to open three new stores in Collin County, North Texas, in 2025, specifically in Celina, Prosper, and Allen. These new locations are driven by the area's robust population growth and existing Costco stores operating at full capacity. The expansion underscores major retailers' significant investment in this rapidly growing part of the Metroplex.

title: Retailers Try on More Tech
summary: Retailers are entering a new phase of growth driven by AI and automation, according to Morgan Stanley. Key technologies like retail media, AI, and automation are expected to boost profitability and growth, particularly for larger retailers who can invest more in these advancements. This technological adoption will lead to margin expansion and consolidation within the retail sector.

title: Innovators in alcohol-free: TÖST
summary: TÖST is a non-alcoholic beverage founded in 2017 by Brooks Addington, offering an elevated drink experience with a blend of white tea and botanicals. The brand has gained significant traction, including a minority investment from Constellation Brands, and is expanding its reach with new canned formats and flavors in 2025. TÖST aims to provide a sophisticated alternative for consumers seeking alcohol-free options in a growing moderation movement.

title: EXEC: Hydro Flask Adds Velocity with Expanding Amazon, Target and Costco Programs
summary: Helen of Troy Limited, parent company of Hydro Flask, Osprey, and OXO brands, reported positive momentum in its Home & Outdoor segment for Q3 fiscal year 2025, partially offsetting declines in Beauty & Wellness. Hydro Flask saw significant distribution gains at Target and Costco, alongside strong e-commerce performance, including being Amazon's #1 Best Seller during Prime Day. The company also detailed its Project Pegasus restructuring plan, aimed at improving operating margins, and provided an updated fiscal 2025 outlook including the acquisition of Olive & June.

title: News | Albertsons steps up streamlining of stores, including closings
summary: Albertsons is moving forward with streamlining its store portfolio, which will include both opening and closing locations, after its proposed merger with Kroger was blocked. The company aims to cut $1.5 billion in costs over the next three years and will focus on optimizing its real estate footprint. While there may be more closures than previously seen due to "general hygiene of the real estate portfolio," Albertsons also plans for new store openings and will consider strategic transactions to create long-term shareholder value.

title: What to know about Costco memberships, food court, rewards, location, returns, refunds
summary: This article provides key information on Costco ahead of its Treasure Coast opening, covering membership benefits, the popular food court, and the store's generous return policy. It details the differences between Gold Star and Executive memberships, lists popular food court items and prices, and clarifies exceptions to their refund policy for electronics and certain high-value items.

title: ACVF - Conservative Values ETF - Divests from Costco and Allstate expanding its fight against corporate 'Woke-ism” and DEI
summary: The American Conservative Values ETF (ACVF) has divested its holdings in Costco and Allstate, citing the companies' commitment to Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) initiatives. Simultaneously, ACVF has removed its boycott of Walmart and added the retailer to its portfolio, praising Walmart's move away from DEI efforts. This action is part of ACVF's broader strategy to combat corporate "woke-ism" and reward companies that align with conservative values.

title: Here’s what’s being built along Riverside Boulevard near Costco in Loves Park
summary: A new Valvoline Instant Oil Change is currently under construction in Loves Park, near the Costco and Burger King interchange at Interstate 90 and Riverside Boulevard. The 2,028-square-foot facility will feature three oil change bays at 4020 Stadium Drive, though a grand opening date has not yet been set. This addition continues the development in Loves Park's growth corridor, following the recent opening of a new four-story extended-stay hotel.

title: BJ's Wholesale Reaches 250 Clubs With Latest Opening in Kentucky
summary: BJ's Wholesale Club Holdings, Inc. announced the opening of its 250th club in Louisville, KY, marking its first location in Kentucky and expanding its presence to the 21st state. The company continues to drive growth through strategic initiatives like expanding its own-brand portfolio and enhancing omnichannel capabilities, which has resulted in increased membership and strong sales performance. Despite the stock trading at a premium, its strong performance and strategic focus position it for long-term success.

title: Once Upon a Farm debuts protein bars
summary: Once Upon a Farm has launched new Refrigerated Protein Bars, now available nationwide. These organic and Non-GMO Project Verified bars are designed for active kids, offering 8 grams of protein from milk and whey concentrate, real fruit and vegetables, and whole-grain oats with no added sugar. The company, co-founded by Jennifer Garner, aims to provide nutritious and delicious snack options in flavors like Oatmeal Chocolate and Cinnamon Roll.

title: New Sprouts Farmers Market location draws crowds to Delaware town
summary: A new Sprouts Farmers Market has opened in Middletown, Delaware, attracting crowds to the town. Host Ashley Harder reported on the new grocery store, highlighting its contribution to enabling a consciously healthy lifestyle for residents.

title: Costco to make major change to food courts this summer
summary: Costco announced a significant change for its food courts, switching from Pepsi to Coca-Cola products starting in the summer. This decision was revealed by CEO Ron Vachris during an investor meeting, though no specific reason for the change was given. The popular $1.50 hot dog and soda combo price will remain unchanged despite this beverage swap.

title: Costco confirms major food court changes
summary: Costco is making a significant change to its food courts by switching back to Coca-Cola products after more than a decade of serving Pepsi. This decision was announced by CEO Ron Vachris during the company's annual shareholders meeting. Importantly, the price of the famous $1.50 hotdog combo will remain unchanged.

title: The clock is ticking for Costco and Teamsters to unite on a new contract
summary: Costco and the Teamsters Union are nearing a deadline for a new contract affecting approximately 18,000 workers nationwide. Teamsters have authorized a strike if an agreement isn't reached, citing Costco's failure to bargain constructively. Costco's CEO claims good relations with the union and highlights the company's "superior" employee benefits and wages.

title: QQQ vs ONEQ: Is There Any Real Difference Between These ETFs?
summary: This article compares two ETFs, Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) and Fidelity Nasdaq Composite Index ETF (ONEQ), for investors looking to bet on big tech and AI. While both offer exposure to tech-heavy indices, QQQ tracks the Nasdaq 100 (100 largest non-financial firms) and ONEQ follows the Nasdaq Composite (over 1,000 stocks). The author notes QQQ's higher returns over 10 years but suggests ONEQ might be a better pick for broader exposure and potential future performance driven by mid-cap and financial sector holdings.

title: Complaint Filed Against Grocery Outlet
summary: A class-action lawsuit has been filed against Grocery Outlet Holding Corp. in Northern California, alleging investor losses due to misleading disclosures related to a tech upgrade. The complaint, filed as Liberato v. Grocery Outlet Holding Corp., focuses on the period from November 2023 to May 2024, during which investors reportedly sustained losses. The company attributed worse-than-expected results in May 2024 to tech challenges.

title: Celebrating Black History Month: Best practices for social media and beyond
summary: This article explores how brands can authentically celebrate Black History Month and integrate Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Accessibility (DEIA) initiatives year-round, especially as companies reduce their DEIA efforts. It emphasizes that cultural heritage months are crucial for building authentic connections and amplifying underrepresented voices. The piece provides five best practices for brands, including recognizing Black history 365 days a year, using social data for intentional campaigns, avoiding performative activism, participating in relevant industry events, and partnering with diverse influencer agencies.

title: Consumers Rank Speed as Top Reason for Self-Checkout
summary: A report by NCR Voyix, "2025 Commerce Experience Report," reveals that speed is the primary reason shoppers opt for self-checkout, with 77% preferring it for faster transactions and shorter lines. The study also highlights generational differences, with Gen Z and millennials being the biggest self-checkout adopters. Additionally, the report touches on consumer loyalty programs, the rising importance of convenience stores, and inflation's impact on dining habits, noting a growing demand for smart technology and personalization in customer experiences.

title: Conmed, McKesson, Veralto
summary: This article summarizes changes in analyst ratings and price targets for various U.S. companies announced on Thursday. Key updates include JP Morgan downgrading Conmed Corp to Neutral, Baird increasing McKesson Corp's price target to $729, and RBC lowering Veralto Corp's price target to $110. Multiple other companies also saw adjustments to their ratings and price targets from different financial institutions.

title: First Solar bars use of deep-sea minerals, early win for ESG group
summary: First Solar has committed to excluding deep-sea mined minerals from its supply chain, marking a significant win for environmental, social, and governance (ESG) shareholder activists. This decision, prompted by a shareholder resolution from As You Sow, signals continued corporate attention to environmental concerns despite potential political headwinds. The agreement highlights an ongoing receptiveness among some companies to ESG principles, even as overall resolution filings might slightly decrease.

title: Costco Just Brought Back This Customer-Favorite Garden Gem for Spring
summary: Costco has brought back its customer-favorite self-watering raised cedar planter for $149.99, the same price as the previous year. This planter is ideal for "lazy-girl gardeners" and those with small spaces, offering a convenient way to cultivate vegetables or herbs with less frequent watering. It also prevents dogs from disturbing plants and allows for good drainage.

title: BJ's Wholesale Harnessing Digitization & Membership for Growth
summary: BJ's Wholesale Club is set to sustain its growth momentum by focusing on digital innovation and expanding its membership base. The company has invested in its digital infrastructure to enhance customer experience, offering services like same-day delivery and curbside pickup, which has led to increased engagement and higher average purchase values from digitally-enabled members. BJ's strong membership model, supported by successful acquisition efforts, increased renewal rates, and a recent membership fee hike, is expected to continue driving revenue growth.

title: This huge chain closed all its stores; smaller-format locations are coming back in 2025
summary: Bed Bath & Beyond, which filed for bankruptcy in 2023, is making a retail comeback with smaller-format stores. This return is due to a multi-million-dollar investment from Kirkland’s Inc., which will operate the new stores as part of a strategic partnership with Beyond, the parent company of Bed Bath & Beyond. The first new store is expected to open later in 2025, focusing on a more efficient, neighborhood-focused format.

title: Canned Tuna From Walmart, Costco Recalled Over Botulism Risk
summary: Tri-Union Seafoods has issued a voluntary recall of canned tuna products sold at major retailers like Walmart, Costco, Trader Joe's, and Harris Teeter. The recall is due to a defect in the can's pull tab, which could lead to leakage or contamination with Clostridium botulinum, a potentially fatal bacteria. The company advises customers to discard affected products immediately.

title: CVS Q4 tops Street; revenue up 4.2%
summary: CVS Health Corp. reported better-than-expected fourth-quarter earnings and revenue, despite a drop in net income and adjusted earnings per share due to cost pressures in its insurance business. Total revenue increased by 4.2% to $97.71 billion, exceeding analyst estimates. The company anticipates full-year adjusted earnings in the range of $5.75 to $6 per share for the upcoming fiscal year.

title: Kroger names new CFO
summary: Kroger has appointed David Kennerley, formerly Senior Vice President and CFO for PepsiCo Europe, as its new chief financial officer, effective April 3. He will succeed interim CFO Todd Foley, who plans to retire at the end of the fiscal first quarter. Kennerley's appointment is a significant C-suite change for Kroger, occurring as the company navigates its business strategy after its unsuccessful merger attempt with Albertsons.

title: Costco Was Just Dethroned As the Top Warehouse Club for Customer Service
summary: Sam's Club has surpassed Costco to become the top warehouse club for customer service, according to the latest American Customer Satisfaction Index (ACSI) report. Sam's Club's rise is attributed partly to its adoption of new technology like Scan & Go and a focus on curbside pickup. Costco, while maintaining its ACSI score, dropped to second place as Sam's Club's score significantly increased.

title: 3 Consumer Staples ETFs for Stability in a Volatile Market
summary: In a market experiencing volatility due to inflation and tariff uncertainties, consumer staples ETFs can offer stability and defensive investment options. This article highlights three specific ETFs: the Invesco Dorsey Wright Consumer Staples Momentum ETF (PSL) for those seeking momentum within the sector, the iShares Global Consumer Staples ETF (KXI) for broad global exposure, and the Invesco Food & Beverage ETF (PBJ) for a focused investment in US food and beverage companies. Each ETF presents different expense ratios, diversification approaches, and performance characteristics for investors to consider during periods of market caution.

title: Gold Mining ETFs, NEM & COST Option Trading Ideas
summary: As gold prices reach record highs, the article explores two high-volatility option trading opportunities: a Newmont (NEM) mining strangle and a Costco (COST) skewed iron condor. It details the composition of gold mining ETFs (GDX and GDXJ) and offers insights on the gold/silver ratio and gold futures. The author, Michael "Dr. Data" Rechenthin, provides specific trade ideas for NEM and COST based on implied volatility and market conditions.

title: Retail Insights® 2025 Retail Universe for U.S. Premium Natural, Organic Foods, Supplements & Personal Care
summary: In 2024, the U.S. natural organic products market saw significant growth, adding $7.137 billion in sales to reach $110.75 billion, outpacing conventional grocery channels. Supernaturals like Whole Foods and Sprouts maintained their lead, while compact grocers and club stores experienced the highest percentage growth in natural organic sales. The report details the performance of eight retail channels, highlighting the increasing market share and productivity of natural organic products.

title: 'Makes sense why my daughter has been getting rashes': Costco shopper issues warning to parents who rely on Kirkland diapers
summary: Costco's decision to switch manufacturers for its Kirkland Signature diapers, from Kimberly-Clark Corp. to First Quality, has sparked concern and backlash among parents. Many shoppers, including one mother in a viral TikTok video, report that the new diapers are causing rashes and discomfort in their children, leading them to abandon the Kirkland brand despite its affordability. This change is reportedly part of Costco's strategy to prioritize name brands over its less profitable private label products.

title: Costco chairman reveals surprising luxury items that are selling out
summary: Costco's chairman, Hamilton "Tony" James, highlighted that the retailer successfully sells a surprising range of luxury items, from Porsches to Rolex watches, Dom Perignon, and gold bars. He noted that despite a generally average-income customer base, the presence of affluent members with double the average income allows Costco to move high-end products rapidly due to their appreciation for good deals. James also mentioned the recent quick sale of gold bars, questioning whether affluent individuals or those wary of the economy are driving these purchases.

title: QVCGA - QVC Group Inc Stock Price and Quote
summary: This article provides comprehensive stock information for QVC Group Inc (QVCGA), including its current price, financial metrics, and recent news. It details analyst ratings, insider transactions, and a timeline of corporate announcements, highlighting financial results, strategic moves like a reverse stock split, and management changes. The company operates through QxH, QVC International, and CBI segments, focusing on video and online commerce.

title: 98% of John Deere & Apple Shareholders Reject Anti-Diversity Proposals
summary: Shareholders of Deere & Co (NYSE:DE) and Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) overwhelmingly rejected shareholder proposals aimed at undermining diversity and inclusion programs, with votes against reaching over 98% at both companies. This follows a similar rejection at Costco, indicating a strong shareholder belief that diversity and inclusion are material to profitable growth and financial outperformance. Andrew Behar, CEO of As You Sow, stated that these votes signal a rejection of attempts to inject political culture wars into standard business practices, reinforcing the business rationale for diverse workforces.

title: Costco announces 9 new stores opening in 2025, starting with 6 in March
summary: Costco plans to open nine new warehouse stores globally in 2025, with six locations in the U.S. slated to open by March. These new U.S. stores will be located in California, Texas, Michigan, and Massachusetts, and additional international expansion is planned for Japan and Australia. Costco CEO Ron Vachris also reported strong January sales, with net sales increasing by 9.2% from the previous year.

title: Apple and John Deere reject anti-DEI proposals amid corporate walkbacks
summary: Apple and John Deere shareholders have voted against anti-DEI proposals, contrasting with other companies that are dismantling or softening their diversity, equity, and inclusion efforts amidst a changing political and legal landscape. A recent executive order and Department of Justice memo signal federal opposition to DEI programs, prompting many brands like Bank of America, Google, and Disney to walk back their initiatives. However, some companies like e.l.f. and Patagonia are reaffirming their DEI commitments, while those that have scaled back, like Target, have faced public criticism and boycotts.

title: After Earnings, Is Walmart Stock a Buy, a Sell, or Fairly Valued?
summary: Morningstar maintains a fair value estimate of $58 per share for Walmart (WMT) and rates it as significantly overvalued following its fiscal first-quarter earnings report. Despite strong performance in key metrics like comparable sales and high-margin profit streams, underwhelming fiscal 2026 guidance led to a stock sell-off. Morningstar believes Walmart possesses a wide economic moat due to its brand, cost advantage, and extensive physical footprint, but faces risks from e-commerce competition.

title: Blink Charging Remains Bullish on the EV Supply Equipment Sector
summary: Despite potential changes in government policy regarding electric vehicles, Blink Charging expressed optimism about the continued growth of the EV supply equipment sector. The company's officials noted that state and local efforts, combined with increasing private investment and consumer demand for affordable EV models, are expected to sustain momentum. They also highlighted the increasing use of polycarbonate in charging station enclosures due to its performance benefits over traditional metal.

title: Pardon the Disruption: Where does Kroger go from here?
summary: Rodney McMullen's unexpected resignation as Kroger CEO leaves the supermarket giant facing significant challenges, including stiff competition from discounters, an uncertain omnichannel strategy, and the failed Albertsons merger. The new CEO will need to innovate and revitalize Kroger's core grocery business, digital presence, and explore further acquisitions to maintain relevance in a rapidly evolving market. Despite its strengths in private label and alternative profit streams, Kroger must adapt to customer demands and differentiate itself beyond traditional supermarket advantages.

title: Walmart Launched a Video Game. Are Shoppers Sold on It?
summary: Walmart has launched "Walmart Unlimited," a gamified miniseries developed with Unity and Spatial, marking its expansion into gamified shopping after a successful Roblox e-commerce channel. The series features three young characters on quests, integrating real Walmart supplier products into each episode. This initiative builds on Walmart's existing collaborations with Unity, aiming to empower developers to integrate Walmart's commerce APIs into games and apps, allowing users to purchase physical products without leaving the virtual environment.

title: The company that commissioned Wall Street's 'Fearless Girl' statue radically adjusts diversity policies for its index funds
summary: State Street, known for commissioning the "Fearless Girl" statue, has reversed its diversity policies for companies in its index funds. Previously requiring 30% female board representation, the company now encourages boards to determine their own composition with diverse experiences and perspectives. This move, which also drops requirements for DEI goals and disclosure of gender/racial board makeup, aligns with a broader trend of companies walking back DEI programs.

title: Albertsons CEO to step down after Kroger merger fails. What he says about grocer’s future
summary: Albertsons CEO Vivek Sankaran is set to retire on May 1st after the failed merger attempt with Kroger. He will be succeeded by Susan Morris, current executive vice president and chief operations officer. This announcement follows Kroger CEO Rodney McMullen's resignation and comes after Albertsons sued Kroger for billions due to the merger's collapse.

title: Outpace Traditional Bond Yields With Calamos ETFs
summary: This article highlights how Calamos ETFs, specifically the Calamos CEF Income & Arbitrage ETF (CCEF) and the Calamos Alternative Nasdaq & Bond ETF (CANQ), can offer investors higher yields and diversification compared to traditional bond strategies. CCEF invests in discounted closed-end funds, while CANQ combines fixed income with Nasdaq-100 exposure, both demonstrating competitive yields and strong annual returns. The piece also provides crucial disclosure information and investment risks associated with these funds.

title: BJ’s Q4 Performance Contributes to Record Year
summary: BJ's Wholesale Club Holdings Inc. reported better-than-anticipated Q4 results, contributing to a record year, with comparable-club sales up 4.0% and membership fee income increasing by 7.9%. The company achieved its 12th consecutive quarter of traffic growth, driven by merchandising, digital conveniences, and strong performance in perishables. Looking ahead to fiscal year 2025, BJ's remains cautiously optimistic and plans to expand its footprint with new clubs and an ambient distribution center.

title: Montanans weigh in on how 25% tariff on Mexico and Canada will increase grocery prices
summary: New tariffs of 25% on Mexican and Canadian goods, alongside a 10% tariff on Chinese imports, are expected to significantly impact grocery prices in Montana, according to economist Robert Sonora. Montana heavily relies on imported goods from these countries, especially produce from Mexico. While some view the tariffs as a negotiation tactic, experts suggest 80-90% of the cost will be passed to consumers, leading to higher prices, and prompting calls to support local food sources as a more stable alternative.

title: BJ’s Wholesale stands out by not warning on sales due to tariffs. Stock soars.
summary: BJ’s Wholesale Club Holdings Inc. saw its stock soar after reporting a triple earnings beat and providing a full-year outlook that met expectations, bucking the trend of companies issuing warnings due to tariff uncertainties. The retailer achieved its fastest comparable-club sales growth in nearly two years, driven by consistent traffic growth, increased digital sales, and record-high membership. BJ's attributes its ability to mitigate tariff impacts to its "muscle" in negotiating with suppliers.

title: Costco says customers could stay cautious due to inflation and tariffs. ‘When it rains, it rains on everyone,’ CEO says.
summary: Costco reported mixed second-quarter results and warned that inflation and tariffs could make shoppers more cautious, impacting consumer spending. The CEO noted that retailers, including Costco, are all facing the same challenging economic environment. Despite this, larger retailers have seen increased business from wealthier consumers seeking value amid rising costs.

title: Costco Posts Quarterly Profit That Misses Market Expectations
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. reported quarterly profit that missed Wall Street's expectations, with earnings of $4.02 per share against an estimated $4.11. The big-box retailer's shares fell 7% after the announcement, attributed to macroeconomic uncertainties and higher supply chain costs.

title: Costco Earnings: Top-Line Growth Is Still Best in Class, but Shares Have Lofty Expectations
summary: Morningstar plans to increase its fair value estimate for Costco Wholesale after the company reported strong fiscal 2025 second-quarter results, driven by expected higher comparable sales growth and improved operating margins. Despite the positive outlook on Costco's competitive position and a planned increase in fair value, Morningstar considers Costco shares to be very overvalued, trading at approximately 55 times its fiscal 2025 earnings estimate. The market's high valuation is seen as extrapolating past growth into the distant future, whereas Morningstar anticipates a moderation in comparable sales growth long-term.

title: The Case for Costco Stock Hitting $1,000 in the Next Year
summary: Costco (COST) stock has significantly outperformed the broader market, even with its high valuation and a recent dip from an all-time high of $1,078.23. Analysts are optimistic about its future, with one setting a price target of $1,205, driven by the company's strong business model, loyal customer base, and investments in e-commerce and recent membership fee hikes. While there are concerns about its high P/E ratio, its consistent growth and strong earnings performance are seen as justifying its premium.

title: Ross Stores opens 19 new stores in 14 states
summary: Ross Stores announced the opening of 19 new stores across 14 states, including 16 Ross Dress for Less and 3 dd's Discounts locations. This expansion is part of the company's plan to open approximately 90 new stores in fiscal year 2025 and aims to eventually grow to 2,900 Ross locations and 700 dd's Discounts stores. The company reported nearly $21.13 billion in sales for fiscal 2024, a 3.7% increase from the prior year.

title: Market outlook: How investors with US shares should respond to tariffs, uncertainty in March
summary: This article advises investors with US shares to focus on fundamentals and valuations amid the uncertainty of potential tariffs in March 2025. It suggests overweighting value and small-cap stocks, while underweighting growth stocks and certain large-cap stocks. The author also predicts potential negative impacts of tariffs on several sectors and companies, highlighting the importance of strategic portfolio positioning.

title: Time to 'pass the baton': CIBC CEO's retirement leaves some analysts surprised
summary: Victor Dodig, CEO of Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce (CIBC), is set to retire in October after a decade in the top position, to be replaced by Harry Culham, head of CIBC’s capital markets segment. This announcement has surprised some analysts, who expected Dodig to remain longer given CIBC's strong performance and his significant pay increase. Dodig is lauded for transforming CIBC and leading key acquisitions, while Culham brings solid capital markets experience, though some note his limited background in personal commercial banking and wealth.

title: Costco Wholesale Becomes Oversold (COST)
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp (COST) shares have entered oversold territory with an RSI reading of 28.4. This technical indicator suggests that the stock has experienced heavy selling, potentially signaling an upcoming buying opportunity for bullish investors. The article highlights Costco's current stock price relative to its 52-week range and advises considering the RSI as a measure of market sentiment.

title: Lumicera Secures Purchase Agreement for Stelara® Biosimilar, Delivering Major Cost Savings
summary: Lumicera Health Services has secured a purchase agreement for ustekinumab-aekn, a biosimilar version of Stelara, which is expected to generate $120 million in annualized savings for clients and reduce per-patient costs by up to $336,000 annually. This move reflects Lumicera's commitment to making critical medications more affordable through its cost-plus model. Lumicera, a subsidiary of Navitus Health Solutions, will begin dispensing the biosimilar on July 1, 2025, and Navitus will remove Stelara from its formulary.

title: Consumer Staples ETFs: Defensive Strength in Uncertain Times
summary: The consumer staples sector has shown resilience in 2025 due to its defensive nature, outperforming the consumer discretionary sector despite economic uncertainties. This sector benefits from consistent consumer spending on essential goods and the ability to pass on some costs. Various ETFs offer investors exposure to consumer staples, each with different holdings, expense ratios, and investment strategies.

title: Looking for Exposure to NFLX? Try These Two ETFs
summary: This article suggests two ETFs, Global X Millennial Consumer ETF (MILN) and iShares Nasdaq Top 30 Stocks ETF (QTOP), for investors seeking exposure to Netflix (NFLX) due to its recent stock surge and growth potential. Both ETFs offer indirect investment in NFLX, thereby reducing risk compared to direct stock investment, and include Netflix as a significant holding alongside other major companies. The article provides details on each ETF's holdings, AUM, expense ratio, and performance.

title: ‘Improving sleep all around the world’: UK alum becomes a brand leader at Tempur Sealy
summary: Virginia Groppo, a University of Kentucky alumna, has risen to become an associate brand manager at Tempur Sealy International, specializing in the Stearns & Foster mattress brand. Her career trajectory is attributed to her academic foundation at UK, particularly her involvement in the Textile Testing Lab and internships with the Walt Disney Company, which honed her brand management skills. Groppo emphasizes the multifaceted nature of brand management, requiring creativity and a deep understanding of evolving customer needs to improve sleep globally.

title: Five Guys and Ramen Restaurant Coming to Jodeco Road
summary: Two new restaurants, Five Guys and Minano Ramen, are set to open in the Bridges at Jodeco development on Jodeco Road, McDonough. Five Guys will be located at 1060 Chen Parkway, Suite A, offering its popular burgers and fries. Minano Ramen, known for Japanese cuisine, will be in Suite B of the same building, expanding its presence from Tampa, FL.

title: Target Corp named second-strongest grocery brand in U.S. for 2025 - Bizwomen
summary: Target Corp. has been named the second-strongest grocery store brand in the U.S. for 2025 by YouGov's survey, trailing only Walmart. The retailer performs well across demographics and generations, with 42.5% of consumers considering shopping there for groceries. Target also ranked highly in perceived quality and has increased its focus on grocery due to the segment's resilience to economic downturns.

title: Target Corp named second-strongest grocery brand in U.S. for 2025 - Bizwomen
summary: Target Corp. has been recognized as the second-strongest grocery store brand in the U.S. for 2025 by YouGov, based on consumer consideration, ranking only behind Walmart. The company performed particularly well among millennials and was also noted for being the second most improved grocery store in terms of consideration. While grocery is not its primary revenue driver, Target is strategically investing in this segment due to its resilience against economic fluctuations, enhancing offerings like home delivery and supply chain infrastructure.

title: Walmart to Invest in Convenience & Gas Growth in 2025
summary: Walmart plans to expand its convenience and gas services in 2025 by opening or remodeling over 45 fuel stations across the U.S., increasing its total to more than 450 locations in 34 states. title: Costco’s Internal Investigation Confidentiality Restrictions Deemed Unlawful
summary: An Administrative Law Judge for the NLRB ruled that Costco violated the National Labor Relations Act by requiring employees involved in an internal investigation to sign a confidentiality agreement and by broadly prohibiting discussion or recording of the investigation. The deal also gives Disney a controlling stake in Hulu and reunites Marvel characters like the X-Men with the Avengers for future projects.

title: Disney Closes Acquisition of 21st Century Fox
summary: The Walt Disney Company has officially completed its historic $71.3 billion acquisition of 21st Century Fox, creating an unprecedented collection of content and talent. This deal grants Disney ownership of major film and TV assets, including Twentieth Century Fox, FX Networks, and a 30 percent stake in Hulu, aiming to enhance Disney's direct-to-consumer strategy and global presence. Disney CEO Robert A. Iger acknowledged the challenging integration ahead but expressed confidence in the long-term value and growth opportunities.

title: Disney closes $71 billion acquisition of Twenty-First Century Fox's assets
summary: Walt Disney Co completed its $71 billion acquisition of Twenty-First Century Fox Inc's film and television assets. This deal expands Disney's content library, including franchises like X-Men and Avatar, to bolster its upcoming streaming service, Disney+. The acquisition follows a bidding war with Comcast Corp.

title: Here’s what Disney owns after the massive Disney/Fox merger
summary: The article details the implications of Disney's $71.3 billion acquisition of 21st Century Fox's film and TV assets, highlighting how it reshapes the media landscape. It covers Disney's new ownership of a vast library of movies and shows, its majority stake in Hulu, and Marvel regaining access to X-Men and Fantastic Four characters, while also noting the continuation of Fox Corp as a news and sports entity. The author raises concerns about media consolidation and potential job losses stemming from the merger.

title: None of BlackBerry’s top executives work out of its Waterloo headquarters anymore
summary: BlackBerry no longer has any top executives based at its iconic Waterloo headquarters or anywhere else in Canada, with its entire executive team now operating out of Bay Area offices in California. This shift has occurred under CEO John Chen, who took over in 2013, despite BlackBerry continuing to brand itself as a Waterloo-based company and receiving Canadian government funding. While the executive presence has moved south, BlackBerry maintains a significant Canadian workforce, especially in R&D, and is still viewed as a symbol of Canadian innovation.

title: Disney Shutters Fox 2000
summary: Following its acquisition of Fox, Disney has announced the closure of the Fox 2000 label, which often produced a mix of art house films and mainstream popcorn fare. This move comes with the first wave of layoffs, including several key executives from the Fox studio system. While current projects will be completed and released, and the Fox 2000 catalog will be available on Disney's streaming services, the studio will cease to exist.

title: Viacom, AT&T reach deal that keeps Nickelodeon, MTV and Comedy Central on DirecTV
summary: Viacom and AT&T reached a new distribution agreement, preventing a blackout of Viacom's channels like Nickelodeon, MTV, and Comedy Central on AT&T's DirecTV service. The deal was struck after tense negotiations, reportedly involving fee reductions from Viacom's side, as AT&T, heavily in debt, sought to cut costs. This resolution avoids a significant disruption for 24.5 million AT&T TV subscribers and addresses concerns from both companies facing industry shifts and subscriber challenges.

title: Disney Earns Perfect Score for LGBTQ Workplace Equality
summary: The Walt Disney Company achieved a perfect score of 100 on the 2019 Corporate Equality Index (CEI) for LGBTQ workplace equality, marking its 13th consecutive year of top marks. Administered by the Human Rights Campaign Foundation, the CEI evaluates corporate policies and practices, recognizing Disney as a "Best Place to Work for LGBTQ Equality." Disney's commitment includes comprehensive benefits, support for transitioning employees, LGBTQ business employee resource groups, and contributions to diverse organizations.

title: How Netflix plans on owning your kids’ screen time
summary: Netflix is heavily investing in children's animation, spending an estimated $1.1 billion this year, to appeal to its broad global subscriber base and fend off competition. Unlike traditional studios, Netflix aims for a diverse range of content without a singular "brand" to cater to every household member's viewing preferences. The company is encouraging creators to pursue unique visions and is experimenting with new interactive features to engage young viewers.

title: How Lachlan Murdoch Went From Studying Philosophy at Princeton to Exploiting White Nationalism at Fox News
summary: This article traces Lachlan Murdoch's journey from a philosophy student at Princeton, where he wrote a thesis on morality, to his current role overseeing Fox News, which the author contends exploits white nationalism. It explores his upbringing, his conservative leanings, and the family dynamics, including his brief departure from his father's business and the succession struggle among the Murdoch children, culminating in Lachlan's ascent to leadership. The piece contrasts his early intellectual pursuits with his later actions as a media proprietor, suggesting a transformation shaped by his relationship with his powerful father.

title: Chart: Everything That Disney Owns
summary: This article details the extensive list of companies, brands, and franchises owned by The Walt Disney Company following its acquisition of significant parts of 21st Century Fox. It highlights key acquisitions like Fox Family, Fox Animation, and Fox Networks, alongside existing properties such as Marvel, Lucasfilm, ESPN, and Pixar. The article also mentions Disney's major competitors in the media landscape.

title: ‘Captain Marvel’ Crosses $1 Billion Worldwide
summary: Captain Marvel has crossed the $1 billion mark globally, becoming the seventh Marvel Studios film to achieve this milestone. The movie earned $358 million domestically and $645 million internationally as of April 2, 2019, with a strong opening weekend of $153 million in the U.S. and a $455 million global debut. This success contributes to the Marvel Cinematic Universe's collective box office earnings of over $18.5 billion.

title: How Rupert Murdoch’s Empire of Influence Remade the World (Published 2019)
summary: This article details Rupert Murdoch's vast media empire and its significant influence on politics and world affairs across continents. It explores the family dynamics, particularly the rivalry between his sons Lachlan and James for succession, and Murdoch's strategic use of his media outlets to shape political outcomes, including the rise of Donald Trump and Brexit. The piece highlights Murdoch's consistent push for right-wing ideologies and his transactional relationships with political leaders over decades.

title: 'Treated as cheap labor': Disney underpays women, lawsuit alleges
summary: The Walt Disney Company is facing a class-action lawsuit alleging systematic underpayment of women and "widespread" discrimination. The lawsuit comes just after Disney's acquisition of 21st Century Fox and follows a report that the company pays men 22% more on average than women in the UK. Two longtime female employees, LaRonda Rasmussen and Karen Moore, allege significant pay disparities compared to male counterparts despite similar roles and experience.

title: Disney Spotlights Comprehensive Direct-to-Consumer Strategy at 2019 Investor Day
summary: The Walt Disney Company's Investor Day showcased its comprehensive direct-to-consumer strategy, highlighting Disney+, Hulu, Hotstar, and ESPN+. Disney+ is set to launch on November 12, 2019, at $6.99 a month, featuring content from Disney, Pixar, Marvel, Star Wars, and National Geographic, including original series and films. The company detailed a robust content slate and global expansion plans, aiming to deliver significant value to consumers and shareholders.

title: Disney CEO Robert Iger announces 2021 retirement
summary: Walt Disney CEO Robert Iger announced his plan to step down from his role when his current contract expires at the end of 2021. Iger, who became CEO in 2005, has previously extended his tenure but stated that 2021 will be his time to finally depart, following the company's significant acquisitions like Pixar, Marvel, and Lucasfilm. The 2021 extension was contingent on the successful $71.3-billion acquisition of 21st Century Fox's entertainment assets.

title: Live Blog: The Walt Disney Company Investor Day 2019 — Disney+ Reveal and More
summary: The Walt Disney Company announced an Investor Day event to unveil details about its upcoming streaming services, particularly Disney+. The event was scheduled to begin at 2 p.m. PDT/5 p.m. EDT, with a live blog covering all emerging news from the special presentation. Key topics expected included Disney+, ESPN, Hotstar, and Hulu.

title: Netflix’s Market Value Dropped $8 Billion After the Disney Plus Announcement
summary: Netflix Inc. experienced an $8 billion drop in market capitalization after Disney announced its new, cheaper streaming service, Disney+, slated to launch in November. Disney's stock, conversely, surged to a record high, adding $25 billion in market value, as the company detailed its content-rich streaming offering designed to compete directly with Netflix.

title: Disney CEO Bob Iger lays out details on company's Netflix competitor
summary: Disney CEO Bob Iger discussed the company's new streaming platform, Disney+, and its position against competitors like Netflix during an interview with CNBC's David Faber. The discussion also touched upon impending job cuts resulting from consolidation efforts. The interview followed Disney's investor day, providing insights into their strategy moving forward.

title: Netflix Just Dropped $8 Billion in Market Value on Disney+ News
summary: Netflix Inc. experienced an $8 billion drop in market capitalization following Walt Disney Co.'s announcement of its new, cheaper streaming service, Disney+. Disney+ is set to launch on November 12 at a price point significantly lower than Netflix's most popular U.S. plan, causing investor concern for Netflix.

title: Marcella Regniault
summary: Marcella Regniault is the Vice President, Digital Sales Planning and Client Services at ESPN, where she oversees digital client services strategy to optimize advertising inventory and revenue. Before joining ESPN, she held significant roles at JP Morgan Chase Inc., focusing on ad operations, and at Ziff Davis, managing marketing and sales operations. Her extensive career also includes leadership positions at TVGuide.com, The Wall Street Journal Digital Network, and Time, Inc.

title: Hulu buys AT&T’s stake for $1.43 billion
summary: Hulu has repurchased AT&T's nearly 10% equity stake for $1.43 billion, valuing the streaming service at $15 billion. This transaction positions AT&T to focus on its own WarnerMedia streaming service, while Disney solidifies its control over Hulu with a 60% stake. Hulu aims for profitability by fiscal year 2023 or 2024, despite an anticipated $1.5 billion operating loss in fiscal year 2019.

title: AT&T sells Hulu stake in deal that values streaming service at $15 billion
summary: AT&T has sold its minority stake in Hulu back to the streaming service, a deal that valued Hulu at $15 billion. AT&T's 9.5% interest was valued at $1.43 billion, and the company plans to use the sales proceeds to pay down debt. Hulu's CEO expressed gratitude for AT&T's support.

title: With Disney in Control, Hulu Buys Out AT&T Stake for $1.4 Billion
summary: Hulu, now majority-controlled by Disney, has bought out AT&T Inc.'s 9.5 percent stake for approximately $1.43 billion. This deal values Hulu at $15 billion and leaves Walt Disney Co. and Comcast Corp. as the sole owners of the streaming service. Disney gained majority control last month after acquiring Fox assets.

title: Hulu Buys AT&T’s Minority Stake in Joint Venture
summary: AT&T has sold its 9.5% minority stake in Hulu back to the streaming video joint venture for $1.43 billion, valuing Hulu at $15 billion. The transaction was signed and closed simultaneously without needing third-party approvals. AT&T plans to use the proceeds to reduce its debt.

title: Walt Disney in control, Hulu buys out AT&T for $1.4 billion
summary: Hulu has bought out AT&T's 9.5% stake for about $1.43 billion, valuing the company at $15 billion, leaving Walt Disney Co. and Comcast Corp. as the sole owners. Disney, which now has majority control, is considering an international rollout for Hulu, which is projected to lose $1.5 billion this year but aims for profitability by FY23 or FY24. AT&T plans to use the proceeds to reduce its substantial debt load.

title: Texas Children’s and Disney partnership brings the magic of the mouse to patients
summary: Texas Children’s Hospital and The Walt Disney Co. have launched a pilot program called Disney Team of Heroes, bringing the magic of Disney to hospitalized children. This initiative aims to create "moments of joy" and provide delightful distractions through Disney-themed murals, hospital gowns, play spaces, mobile movie theaters, and an app. The partnership seeks to enhance patient experiences and may expand to other children's hospitals globally.

title: Netflix is opening a production hub in NYC
summary: Netflix is expanding its presence in New York City by opening a new production hub, which is expected to create hundreds of jobs and involve up to $100 million in investments. This move follows Amazon backing out of Long Island City and comes as Netflix faces increased competition from other streaming services like Disney, demonstrating its strategy to grow beyond Hollywood. The state of New York is offering Netflix up to $4 million in performance-based tax incentives for job creation.

title: Opinion | Abigail Disney: It's time to call out my family's company — and anyone else rich off their workers' backs
summary: Abigail Disney, president of Fork Films and co-founder of Level Forward, addresses wage inequality at The Walt Disney Co. She contends that the Disney brand holds a unique place in the economic landscape due to its reliance on emotion and sentiment, suggesting it has the potential to lead the way in humane business practices if its leaders chose to do so. She emphasizes that her comments are personal views and not representative of her family.

title: Disney heiress calls CEO Bob Iger’s $65 million pay package ‘insane’
summary: Disney heiress Abigail Disney criticized CEO Bob Iger's $65.6 million pay package as "insane," highlighting the vast disparity between his salary and that of the median Disney employee. She advocated for significant pay raises for the company's lowest-paid workers, arguing that Disney's profitability leaves no excuse not to do so.

title: Abigail Disney Urges Walt Disney Co. to “Lead” in Op-Ed About Wage Inequality
summary: Abigail Disney, great-niece of Walt Disney, published an op-ed in The Washington Post criticizing wage inequality at The Walt Disney Co., specifically highlighting CEO Bob Iger's "insane" 2018 compensation of over $65 million. She urges the company to lead in improving employee wages and promoting a more humane way of doing business, contrasting CEO pay growth with minimal worker pay increases. Disney also criticized the company's $3.6 billion share buyback, arguing it dwarfed employee raises and primarily enriched shareholders.

title: Variety, iHeartMedia Launch New Film Podcast ‘The Big Ticket’ With Marc Malkin
summary: Variety and iHeartMedia have launched a new weekly film-focused podcast called "The Big Ticket," hosted by Marc Malkin. The podcast will feature interviews with Hollywood stars and filmmakers, with its debut episodes focusing on "Avengers: Endgame" and upcoming guests including Halle Berry and Keanu Reeves. This partnership aims to expand the reach of Variety's journalism to wider audiences through iHeartMedia's platforms.

title: Disney heir calls on company to give 50% of exec bonuses to lowest-paid employees
summary: Abigail Disney, granddaughter of co-founder Roy Disney, is advocating for Disney to dedicate 50% of executive bonuses to its lowest-paid employees. She points out the significant disparity between executive compensation, such as CEO Bob Iger's $66 million pay package, and the median employee salary of $46,127, arguing that a portion of executive bonuses could significantly benefit lower-paid workers without impacting executives' quality of life. The company, Disney (DIS), has responded by highlighting its investments in employee wages and benefits, and defending Iger's performance-based pay.

title: Disney heiress calls out wage inequality at Walt Disney Company
summary: Abigail Disney, granddaughter of Roy Disney, publicly criticized wage inequality at the Walt Disney Company, highlighting that CEO Bob Iger's 2018 compensation was 1,424 times the median worker's pay. She urged executives to donate 50% of their bonuses to the lowest-paid employees to address the widening gap between top management and the average worker. Disney argued that despite a $1,000 bonus to some employees, the company prioritized stock buybacks over significant worker compensation improvements.

title: Marvel Studios’ ‘Avengers: Endgame’ Makes History with $1.2 Billion Global Debut
summary: Marvel Studios' Avengers: Endgame set a new global box office record with an unprecedented $1.209 billion debut, becoming the first film to surpass $1 billion in its opening weekend. The film achieved this milestone in just five days and broke numerous domestic and international records, including an estimated $350 million domestically and $859 million internationally. This monumental success solidifies the Marvel Cinematic Universe's dominance, with critical acclaim and significant contributions to The Walt Disney Studios' financial performance.

title: Disney and Make-A-Wish Launch #FriendLikeMe Challenge in Celebration of ‘Aladdin’
summary: The Walt Disney Company and Make-A-Wish have launched the #FriendLikeMe Challenge in celebration of the new Aladdin movie, starring Will Smith. For every public social media post with #FriendLikeMe through May 24, 2019, Disney will donate $5, up to $1 million, to Make-A-Wish to help grant wishes for children with critical illnesses. This initiative highlights the long-standing collaboration between Disney and Make-A-Wish, which has granted over 130,000 wishes since 1980.

title: Disney Touches Record High as ‘Endgame’ Dominates Box Office
summary: Walt Disney Co. shares reached record levels after its film "Avengers: Endgame" shattered box-office records. The film's success is expected to significantly boost the studio division's contribution to overall profit and is seen as a positive indicator ahead of the Disney+ streaming service launch. Analysts also anticipate upside for theater companies due to the film's performance.

title: Vice Media Gets $250 Million in Debt Funding From George Soros, Other Investors
summary: Vice Media has secured $250 million in debt funding from an investment consortium including George Soros, led by 23 Capital, to revitalize its business. This capital infusion is intended to accelerate Vice's growth plans and execute the strategic vision of CEO Nancy Dubuc, who aims for profitability within the next fiscal year. The funding comes after a period of revenue shortfalls, employee layoffs, and a significant drop in the company's valuation.

title: ‘Avengers: Endgame’ is Fastest Ever to $2 Billion
summary: ‘Avengers: Endgame’ achieved a historic milestone by crossing $2 billion at the global box office in just 11 days, becoming the fastest film to reach this threshold. It is now the second highest-grossing film of all time, surpassing "Avengers: Infinity War," "Star Wars: The Force Awakens," and "Titanic." The film also set numerous international records, including becoming the highest-grossing non-local film in China and the highest-grossing Hollywood film in India, among other territories.

title: Target rebrands digital-advertising business as Roundel
summary: Target has rebranded its digital advertising business from Target Media Network to Roundel, signaling an aggressive push into the digital advertising sector. The company aims to leverage its customer data and "exceptional branding" to offer personalized ad campaigns for its 1,000 clients, including major brands like Disney and Coca-Cola. This move positions Target to compete more directly with other retailers like Amazon and Walmart, which have also seen success in their advertising businesses.

title: Marvel Studios’ Avengers: Endgame Sets New Record for IMAX China’s Highest-grossing Title Ever With 496 Million Rmb
summary: Marvel Studios’ Avengers: Endgame has become IMAX China’s all-time highest-grossing title in just 12 days, reaching approximately RMB 496 million. The film nearly doubled the entire run of Avengers: Infinity War in IMAX China and set multiple records, including the best midnight, opening day, three-day opening, and biggest opening week for IMAX in China. IMAX contributed nearly 13% of the film’s overall gross in China from only 1% of the total screens, highlighting the success of the film shot entirely with IMAX cameras.

title: Fox Corp. Won’t Reunite With News Corp, CEO Lachlan Murdoch Says
summary: Fox Corp. CEO Lachlan Murdoch stated at an investor day that the company will not reunite with News Corp, despite speculation after its split from Fox entertainment assets. He emphasized that the new Fox Corporation, focusing on news, entertainment, and sports, will pursue growth through deals that align closely with its core businesses and expertise. The company also recently adopted a "poison pill" to protect against hostile takeover attempts, clarifying it's not intended to block board-approved transactions.

title: How DisneyResearch|Studios’ Technology and Industrial Light & Magic Artistry Helped Reinvent Hulk in Marvel Studios’ ‘Avengers: Endgame’
summary: This article details how DisneyResearch|Studios (DRS) technology, Anyma, and Industrial Light & Magic (ILM) artistry were crucial in reinventing the Hulk for Marvel Studios’ ‘Avengers: Endgame’. Anyma, an advanced motion capture system, allowed for the nuanced performance of Mark Ruffalo to be captured and translated to the character, enabling the depiction of a merged Banner-Hulk entity. This collaboration highlights a long-term strategy for technological innovation within Disney to enhance film production.

title: Netflix Acquires Children’s Education Company StoryBots
summary: Netflix has acquired StoryBots, a children's media content brand founded by the creators of JibJab. The acquisition aims to expand Netflix's children's programming and establish StoryBots as a global educational entertainment brand, leveraging Netflix's scale for distribution, merchandising, and licensing. The deal terms were undisclosed, but Netflix stated they were "immaterial," and the StoryBots founders will continue to work within Netflix's animation department.

title: Safety-sense with Spider-Man™: United Airlines Launches New Safety Video Featuring Superhero
summary: United Airlines is launching a new inflight safety video featuring Spider-Man as part of a broader promotional partnership with Sony Pictures for the movie Spider-Man™: Far From Home. The collaboration will also include Spider-Man-themed Polaris business class amenity kits and MileagePlus Exclusives experiences. The video aims to engage customers with an entertaining mini-drama while emphasizing United's commitment to safety.

title: NBC is expected to take Netflix favorite ‘The Office’ to its new streaming service
summary: NBCUniversal is strongly hinting that "The Office," currently a popular Netflix favorite, will be moving to its new, as-yet-unnamed streaming service launching in mid-2020. This move is seen as NBCU's strategy to take control of its valuable properties and a potentially significant blow to Netflix, which saw "The Office" streamed for 52 million minutes in 2018. The new NBCU service will be ad-supported, and the company is actively seeking sponsors for its launch.

title: Disney to buy full control of Hulu from NBC owner Comcast
summary: Disney is taking full operational control of the streaming service Hulu from Comcast in a deal that values Hulu at $27.5 billion U.S. This move positions Disney to better compete with Netflix, especially as Disney prepares to launch its own streaming service, Disney+. The agreement allows Disney to acquire Comcast's remaining 33 percent stake after January 2024.

title: Communication Services XLC ETF Closes Up 2.24%
summary: The Communication Services Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLC) closed up 2.24% on Wednesday, amidst a strong market performance and news of delayed automotive tariffs. The XLC ETF, composed of major communication services companies like Facebook, Google, and Netflix, represents a relatively new sector formed in late 2018. The sector's constituents include significant growth drivers, though some analysts express caution about potential over-regulation.

title: Eleven New Disney Legends to Be Honored During D23 Expo 2019
summary: The Walt Disney Company announced that 11 new individuals will be honored with the Disney Legends Award during the D23 Expo 2019. The honorees include Robert Downey Jr., Jon Favreau, James Earl Jones, Bette Midler, Kenny Ortega, Ming-Na Wen, and Hans Zimmer, recognized for their significant contributions across film, television, and theme parks. The awards ceremony will be hosted by Disney Chairman and CEO Bob Iger and will involve a handprint ceremony for the recipients.

title: Jefferies Financial has highest-paid CEO among NY companies
summary: Richard Handler, CEO of Jefferies Financial Group, was the highest-paid CEO among New York-based companies, earning $44.7 million in 2018, a 105% increase from the previous year. His compensation included a $26 million stock award and $18.7 million in base pay. This places him fourth overall on The Wall Street Journal's list of highest-paid S&P 500 CEOs, despite a general trend of falling shareholder returns.

title: Lions Gate offered to sell Starz to CBS for $5.5 billion - sources
summary: Lions Gate Entertainment reportedly offered to sell its cable channel Starz to CBS Corp for $5.5 billion, after previously rejecting an informal $5 billion bid from CBS. This move highlights CBS's ambition to compete more aggressively in the media landscape, potentially ahead of merger discussions with Viacom Inc. The news led to a rise in Lions Gate shares and a marginal decline for CBS shares.

title: New Coke Was a Debacle. It’s Coming Back. Blame ‘Stranger Things.’ (Published 2019)
summary: New Coke, the famously failed soft drink from 1985, is making a limited-time comeback due to a promotional partnership with Netflix's "Stranger Things." The vintage beverage will be available starting Thursday and will appear in the show's upcoming third season, which is set in summer 1985. This collaboration is part of Netflix's broader strategy to ramp up corporate partnerships and merchandising to attract new subscribers and generate revenue without commercials.

title: Coca-Cola Will Revive New Coke in Alliance With Netflix, ‘Stranger Things’
summary: Coca-Cola is reviving New Coke for a limited time as part of a partnership with Netflix, integrating the infamous beverage into the third season of "Stranger Things," which is set in 1985. This marketing initiative aims to promote both the return of the series and gives Coca-Cola a unique way to connect with streaming audiences, despite New Coke's historical marketing failure. Coca-Cola will make 500,000 cans available online and in select locations, also releasing limited-edition original Coke with "Stranger Things" designs.

title: Coca-Cola is bringing back New Coke in honor of ‘Stranger Things’
summary: Coca-Cola is bringing back a limited number of New Coke cans as a promotion for the third season of "Stranger Things," which is set in 1985 when New Coke originally debuted and famously flopped. This partnership with Netflix allows Coca-Cola to engage with consumers in changing media landscapes and aims to "break the internet" with the nostalgic product, which will be available through various promotional channels. Netflix is also partnering with several other companies for show promotion, leveraging physical products to reach wider audiences.

title: Walt Disney CEO Bob Iger Says It's “Very Difficult” To Do Georgia Business With New Abortion Law
summary: Walt Disney CEO Bob Iger stated it would be "very difficult" for the company to continue doing business in Georgia if the new "heartbeat" abortion law takes effect. He expressed doubts about continued filming in the state, citing potential reluctance from employees to work there. This sentiment echoes concerns from other companies like Netflix, despite Georgia's significant tax credits and film production industry.

title: Star Wars: Galaxy’s Edge is Dedicated at Disneyland Park
summary: Disneyland Park officially dedicated Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge, the largest single-themed land expansion in Disney Parks history, with a grand opening ceremony attended by Disney CEO Bob Iger, George Lucas, and Skywalker Saga actors. The new land, opening to guests tomorrow, offers immersive experiences including two attractions, advanced technology integrated with the Play Disney Parks mobile app, and unique retail and culinary adventures designed to deepen guest engagement with the Star Wars universe. Walt Disney Imagineering and Lucasfilm collaborated extensively to ensure authenticity and realism, redefining the Disney park experience by allowing guests to become active participants in the Star Wars galaxy.

title: SETTING THE STAGE
summary: The article discusses the resurgence of film and television production in Los Angeles, driven by streaming services and tax incentives, which has led to a boom for soundstage owners. It highlights that studio spaces are near 100% occupancy, making it a lucrative but operationally intensive business for property owners. Key players like Hudson Pacific Properties, Occidental Entertainment Group, and Hackman Capital are expanding their soundstage portfolios, with long-term leases becoming more common due to high demand.

title: 'Merch by Amazon' t-shirt business increasing orders from Disney to Dr. Seuss
summary: Amazon's 'Merch by Amazon' on-demand t-shirt printing service is increasingly being used by major entertainment companies like Walt Disney Co and Dr. Seuss. This service allows brands to produce merchandise closer to the point of sale, eliminating the need for large upfront inventory commitments and traditional supply chains. The trend is contributing to Amazon's growing influence in the clothing industry and allows for more niche and timely product offerings.

title: How to watch the 2019 NBA Finals live on ABC or TSN without cable
summary: This article provides a guide for cord-cutters in the United States and Canada looking to stream the 2019 NBA Finals live. It outlines various options for watching ABC's coverage in the U.S. and TSN's coverage in Canada, including free over-the-air broadcasts and paid streaming services. The article also lists the schedule for the remaining games between the Golden State Warriors and the Toronto Raptors.

title: Is a construction company right in suing a cafe over the word cat?
summary: Caterpillar, the multi-billion dollar construction equipment giant, has filed a cease-and-desist order against a small Santa Cruz coffee shop, Cat & Cloud Coffee, for using the word "Cat" on its apparel. The article questions the company's decision, comparing it to Disney's inaction against a small dry-cleaning business using a Disney character, and highlights the public and the coffee shop's frustration. It suggests that such disputes often come down to economic sense rather than who is "right or wrong."

title: Clorox Brand Has a (Toy) Story to Tell
