Despite challenges, Disney's streaming services, particularly Disney+, are surging in subscribers, and its cable networks like ESPN are seeing reduced costs, offering some resilience amidst the widespread impact.

title: Special Feature: YouTube’s Evolution in the OTT Streaming Landscape...
summary: This article by Comscore and YouTube examines YouTube's significant growth within the evolving OTT streaming landscape, highlighting its increased reach in ad-supported households and substantial growth in CTV watch time. It also details how YouTube's unique user-generated content and extensive library are providing new opportunities for advertisers to target diverse audiences. The piece further explores emerging content consumption trends on the platform, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: fuboTV follows YouTube's lead, increases monthly subscription rate
summary: FuboTV is raising its monthly subscription rate from $60 to $65 for its family plan, and existing standard plan subscribers will be automatically moved to the family plan, increasing their rates from $55 to $65. This price hike comes alongside significant content changes, as fuboTV has dropped all Turner channels but added Disney channels, including ESPN, which will be available in August. The move follows a similar price increase by YouTube TV and suggests a potential trend in the streaming service market.

title: VOD Transactions Peaked in the Month of April 2020
summary: Comscore reports that Video on Demand (VOD) transactions, including Transactional on Demand (TOD), Subscription Video on Demand (SVOD), and Free on Demand (FOD), all peaked in April 2020 during the initial months of the coronavirus pandemic. While TOD and FOD remained steady or saw slight declines in May, SVOD transactions showed a more pronounced decline. The report specifically highlights significant year-over-year increases in Sports and Fitness VOD categories, suggesting a strong consumer interest in these areas during lockdown.

title: Crowds flock to Six Flags Great Adventure ready to have some fun, masks in place
summary: Six Flags Great Adventure reopened its gates after a coronavirus pause, drawing large crowds despite new safety protocols. Guests were required to wear masks, have their temperatures checked, and practice social distancing, with rides operating at reduced capacity. The park, a major seasonal employer, implemented these measures after Governor Phil Murphy allowed amusement parks to open at 50% capacity.

title: Lucie Quenneville Appointed General Manager, Programming and Strategies Acquisition, Bell Media
summary: Bell Media has appointed Lucie Quenneville as General Manager, Programming and Strategies Acquisition for its French-language content in Québec, effective July 20. Quenneville will oversee programming and acquisition strategies for V, Bell Media's French-language specialty channels, and Crave's French-language content. She brings 25 years of experience, including her recent role at CBC/Radio-Canada, and her appointment aims to strengthen Bell Media's French-language offerings.

title: The Walt Disney Company Announces Overall First-Look Deal with Colin Kaepernick
summary: The Walt Disney Company has announced an overall first-look deal with Colin Kaepernick's production company, Ra Vision Media. This partnership will focus on developing scripted and unscripted stories exploring race, social injustice, and equity, while providing a platform for Black and Brown directors and producers across all Disney platforms. The first project in development is an exclusive docuseries chronicling Kaepernick's journey, utilizing new interviews and never-before-seen archives.

title: Why Disney wants to reopen its theme parks now
summary: Walt Disney World Resort in Florida is reopening amidst a surge in COVID-19 cases because other Disney enterprises like Disney+ and ESPN are not generating enough revenue. The company needs its theme parks, which serve as a crucial interactive PR tool and revenue source despite the pandemic's impact on other business segments. Disney has prior experience with reopening its Shanghai resort during the pandemic.

title: Cracker Barrel Old Country Store® Elects Gilbert Dávila to Board of Directors
summary: Cracker Barrel Old Country Store, Inc. (Nasdaq: CBRL) announced the election of Gilbert Dávila to its Board of Directors, effective immediately. Mr. Dávila, founder and CEO of DMI Consulting, brings extensive experience in multicultural marketing, diversity & inclusion, market segmentation, and digital marketing from his leadership roles at The Walt Disney Company, Sears & Roebuck Company, Coca-Cola USA, and Procter & Gamble. This appointment supports Cracker Barrel's strategic focus on digital and multicultural engagement.

title: Disney Parks Boss ‘Pretty Pleased’ With Demand on Reopening Day
summary: Josh D’Amaro, chairman of Walt Disney Co.'s theme parks business, expressed satisfaction with booking trends as Magic Kingdom and Animal Kingdom reopened to the public after a four-month coronavirus shutdown. Disney is taking reservations through September 2021, with Epcot and Disney’s Hollywood Studios parks set to reopen later. This indicates strong initial demand for theme park visits following the reopening.

title: EA Sports UFC 4 coming in August on PS4 and Xbox One
summary: EA Sports UFC 4 is set to release on PS4 and Xbox One on August 14, featuring Jorge Masvidal and Israel Adesanya on the cover. The game will prioritize accessibility and expand beyond strict realism, particularly in its career mode and customization options. While no next-gen versions are confirmed, the Xbox One version will support Smart Delivery for Xbox Series X.

title: Disney+ Honored by American Council of the Blind for Achievement in Audio Description
summary: Disney+ has received the 2020 Achievement Award in Audio Description from the American Council of the Blind (ACB) for its commitment to providing audio description tracks for its original programming and extensive back catalog. The streaming service was recognized for its high standards in audio description scripts, quality voicing, and outreach to the blindness community. Disney+ is noted as the only streaming service with such a large number of titles available with audio description from its inception, showcasing The Walt Disney Company's long-standing dedication to accessibility.

title: Disney+ Honored by American Council of the Blind for Achievement in Audio Description
summary: Disney+ received the 2020 Achievement Award in Audio Description from the American Council of the Blind (ACB) for its commitment to adding audio description tracks to its entire slate of original programming and a significant portion of its back catalog. The service was recognized for its high standards in audio description scripts, quality voicing and audio mix, and outreach to the blindness community. Disney+ emphasizes accessibility and inclusiveness, treating it as an ongoing principle rather than a one-time project.

title: PepsiCo jumps after Cheetos-Hungry Americans stock up on comfort
summary: PepsiCo's sales surged due to increased at-home snacking on comfort foods like Tostitos, Fritos, and Cheetos during COVID-19 lockdowns, despite a decline in beverage sales. This article also covers Moderna's inclusion in the Nasdaq-100, Australia's push for tech giants to share revenue with news publishers, a strike at Bath Iron Works, RTW Retailwinds' bankruptcy, a projected fall in global coffee consumption, Southwest Airlines' warning of layoffs, Netflix surpassing Disney in market capitalization, Heathrow Airport closing a runway for repairs, and Huawei's sales growth despite restrictions.

title: Blerg, Most NBC Stations Won’t Air the 30 Rock Reunion
summary: Major NBC affiliate groups, including Gray Television and Sinclair Broadcast Group, have decided not to broadcast the upcoming 30 Rock reunion special, meaning about half the country won't see it when it debuts. The reason appears to be that station owners view the special, produced by NBCUniversal's ad-sales division, as too much of a promotion for the company’s new Peacock streaming platform. Despite the preemption, viewers in major markets will still be able to watch, and the special will be available on NBC.com, Peacock, and other NBCU cable networks.

title: NBCUniversal wades into streaming wars with Peacock
summary: NBCUniversal is launching its Peacock streaming service nationwide, offering a tiered service with free, ad-supported, and ad-free options. The company is betting on a hybrid model that includes news, sports, and a vast library of TV shows to differentiate itself from competitors like Netflix and Disney+. Peacock aims to attract consumers by replicating traditional TV economics while facing challenges like late entry into the streaming wars and distribution hurdles with major platforms.

title: Irving Azoff, Chairman and CEO, The Azoff Company
summary: Irving Azoff, Chairman and CEO of The Azoff Company, discusses the devastating impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the live music industry. He shares insights into how his company and artists are adapting, including the successful ESPN broadcast of an Eagles concert, and expresses pessimism about a full return to touring before summer 2021 due to economic and health uncertainties. Azoff emphasizes resilience and advises artists to protect their employees and crews.

title: Disney Executive Michael Colglazier Leaving Disney to Become CEO of Virgin Galactic
summary: Michael Colglazier, President and Managing Director of Disney Parks International, is leaving Disney to become Chief Executive Officer of Virgin Galactic Holdings, effective July 20th, 2020. Colglazier brings over thirty years of experience at Disney, including overseeing international parks and resorts and leading the Disneyland Resort during its 60th Anniversary. George Whitsides, Virgin Galactic's former CEO, will transition to Chief Space Officer, focusing on future business opportunities like hypersonic and orbital space travel.

title: Virgin Galactic hires Disney veteran as new CEO
summary: Virgin Galactic has appointed Michael Colglazier, a Walt Disney Company veteran, as its new CEO, effective July 20. Colglazier previously led Disney Parks International and was instrumental in the Star Wars: Galaxy’s Edge expansion. Current CEO George Whitesides will transition to chief space officer, focusing on future business opportunities like hypersonic and orbital space travel.

title: NEWS! More Shakeups in the Walt Disney Company’s Leadership Team
summary: The Walt Disney Company is undergoing leadership changes with Michael Colglazier stepping down as Disney Parks International’s President and Managing Director to become Virgin Galactic’s new CEO. Additionally, Jackie Swisher has replaced Phil Holmes as the Vice President of Disney’s Hollywood Studios. These shifts follow Bob Chapek's recent appointment as CEO of The Walt Disney Company.

title: Abigail Disney slams Disney World reopening as coronavirus spreads
summary: Walt Disney Co. heiress Abigail Disney has criticized the reopening of Disney World amidst the ongoing coronavirus pandemic, expressing concern for the health and safety of workers and guests. She also reiterated her earlier criticisms regarding executive compensation and the furloughing of park employees, suggesting executives should have forgone pay to support workers. The article details Disney's safety measures for reopening, as well as the indefinite delay of Disneyland's reopening in California.

title: Barr condemns Disney and Hollywood for 'kowtowing' to China | William Barr
summary: US Attorney General William Barr criticized Disney and other Hollywood studios for allegedly "kowtowing" to the Chinese Communist Party, accusing them of prioritizing short-term profits over American values. Barr highlighted instances where Disney reportedly apologized for a film about the Dalai Lama and allowed Chinese officials a role in Shanghai Disneyland, while Hollywood studios allegedly tweaked scripts to appease Beijing. He also extended his criticism to US technology companies, calling them "pawns of Chinese influence" for their operations in China.

title: Virgin Galactic announces Michael Colglazier as CEO
summary: Virgin Galactic announced the appointment of Michael Colglazier as its new chief executive officer and George Whitesides as chief space officer, effective July 20, 2020. Colglazier, formerly of The Walt Disney Company, brings extensive experience in consumer-oriented multi-billion dollar businesses. Whitesides, the former CEO, will focus on future business opportunities like hypersonic and orbital space travel, while also chairing the company's space advisory board.

title: Summer Blockbusters Were Slated for This Weekend. Most People Aren’t Ready to Go Back to the Movies
summary: New polling data indicates that between two-thirds and three-quarters of adults in every U.S. state are uncomfortable returning to movie theaters, despite Hollywood's plans to release major blockbusters. Experts suggest that opening theaters prematurely could be detrimental, as low audience comfort combined with increased operating costs from safety measures would lead to razor-thin profit margins. The industry faces significant challenges, including staggered reopenings across states and studios' unwillingness to release big films if returns are low, highlighting a complex interplay between government regulations, studio decisions, and audience readiness.

title: Slideshow: What’s new from General Mills, Kellogg, Three Wishes
summary: General Mills, Kellogg Co., and Three Wishes Cereal are introducing new ready-to-eat cereal products. General Mills is launching a Mandalorian-themed cereal, Kellogg is releasing a Mashups Cereal combining Frosted Flakes and Froot Loops, and Three Wishes is expanding its grain-free portfolio with a new cocoa flavor. These innovations aim to cater to diverse consumer preferences in the breakfast cereal market.

title: Looking for an escape: Younger people more likely to say entertainment costs rose since COVID-19
summary: A global Ipsos survey reveals that a quarter of people in 26 countries believe entertainment costs (electronics, movies, books) have increased since COVID-19, with younger individuals (under 35) being most likely to report this. The article highlights the boom in streaming services and gaming during the pandemic, noting that companies quickly adapted to deliver content to homes. While some changes in consumer behavior, like higher Premium VOD use, are expected to persist, there are concerns about content production shutdowns and "streaming fatigue."

title: U.S. Attorney General Accuses The Walt Disney Company of "Kowtowing" to Chinese Government; 300 of Shanghai Disneyland's Cast Members Active Members of Communist Party
summary: U.S. Attorney General William Barr accused The Walt Disney Company of "kowtowing" to the Chinese government, citing the presence of 300 active Communist Party members among Shanghai Disneyland's 11,000 employees and the Chinese government's role in managing the resort. Barr also referenced Disney's past apology for the film "Kundun" and the company's efforts to appeal to the Chinese film market, which generated significant revenue. Disney has not commented on Barr's remarks.

title: Fortune 500 Tapestry CEO Jide Zeitlin Quits For Personal Reasons After Less Than A Year On Job
summary: Jide Zeitlin, CEO of Fortune 500 Tapestry Inc., resigned for personal reasons after less than a year, amidst allegations of an inappropriate personal relationship predating his tenure. His departure reduces the number of Black CEOs in Fortune 500 companies to three. Zeitlin had also been a vocal advocate against racism and for Black Lives Matter.

title: Fox Will Fill Empty Baseball Stadiums With Virtual Fans
summary: Fox Sports plans to use virtual fans to fill seats in MLB stadiums during its broadcasts to create a more traditional viewing experience amidst the coronavirus pandemic. This digital augmentation will allow for custom crowd reactions and appearances, aiming to make games look and sound authentic despite empty stands. The move is a response to the challenge faced by broadcasters in making sports look appealing without live audiences, with other networks exploring similar innovations.

title: AT&T calls launch of streamer HBO Max a success despite business challenges posed by COVID-19
summary: AT&T declared the launch of HBO Max a success despite COVID-19 challenges, with 4.1 million subscribers in its first month and targets for 50 million by 2025. The service's broad content and existing library attracted customers despite initial delays in original series production caused by the pandemic. While revenue across AT&T's businesses fell due to COVID-19, HBO Max's performance was a positive note, though big theatrical releases like "Tenet" are still planned for cinemas.

title: Streaming service Philo adds TV One to lineup, won't raise price
summary: Philo is adding TV One to its lineup of 60 pay TV networks, making it the first time the channel is available without a traditional cable or satellite subscription. This addition is part of Philo's commitment to diverse programming and will not result in a price increase for customers, maintaining its $20 a month subscription package. The move also benefits Urban One, as Philo becomes the first streaming cable TV alternative to offer both TV One and Cleo TV in its basic package.

title: Disney Company Acquisitions: The Miramax Deal
summary: This article details The Walt Disney Company's acquisition of Miramax in 1993, highlighting it as one of Disney's first major acquisitions aimed at expanding into non-family-friendly content for young adults. It explores the tumultuous relationship between Disney and Miramax founders Bob and Harvey Weinstein due to creative differences and financial disputes, ultimately leading to Miramax's sale in 2010. The piece evaluates the acquisition as a learning opportunity for Disney, paving the way for future major deals under Iger, despite its own challenges.

title: 'Tenet' to hit international theaters on Aug. 26, some U.S. cinemas over Labor Day weekend
summary: Christopher Nolan's "Tenet" will have a staggered release, debuting internationally on August 26, 2020, followed by a limited release in select U.S. cities over Labor Day weekend. This unusual strategy aims to recoup its substantial budget and support international theaters, as Hollywood blockbusters often generate a significant portion of their revenue from overseas markets. The domestic movie theater industry has been severely impacted by the coronavirus pandemic, leading to multiple delays for anticipated blockbusters like "Tenet" and "Mulan."

title: Disney Launchpad: Shorts Incubator Unveils 2020 Directors
summary: Disney Launchpad: Shorts Incubator, a program aimed at amplifying underrepresented voices, has announced its six directors for the inaugural 2020 year: Ann Marie Pace, Aqsa Altaf, Hao Zheng, Jessica Mendez Siqueiros, Moxie Peng, and Stefanie Abel Horowitz. These directors will develop original live-action short films centered on the theme "Discover," with the potential for their works to be featured on Disney+. The program provides mentorship, script development, and classes, with the ultimate goal of empowering a new generation of filmmakers and reflecting diverse global perspectives.

title: James Murdoch resigns from news publisher News Corp’s board
summary: James Murdoch, son of News Corp founder Rupert Murdoch, has resigned from the company's board, citing disagreements over editorial content and strategic decisions. He is known as the more liberal Murdoch brother, contrasting with his conservative sibling Lachlan, who is co-chairman of News Corp and CEO of Fox Corp. James has previously criticized News Corp's editorial stance, including its outlets' coverage of climate change.

title: Rupert Murdoch’s Son James Resigns From News Corp. Due To ‘Disagreements’
summary: James Murdoch, the youngest son of Rupert Murdoch, resigned from the News Corp. board, citing "disagreements over certain editorial content" and "strategic decisions." This marks his final departure from formal roles within his family’s media empire. Murdoch had previously criticized the family's news outlets for their stance on climate change and has supported Democratic candidates and sustainability causes.

title: James Murdoch cuts ties with father Rupert’s News Corp empire
summary: James Murdoch has resigned from the board of his father Rupert Murdoch's News Corp., citing "disagreements over certain editorial content" and strategic decisions. This move further distances him from the conservative-leaning media empire, particularly after recent tensions over the Wall Street Journal's opinion section. Murdoch, who said he doesn't watch Fox News, has been critical of the company's coverage of issues like global warming and is pursuing investments through his firm Lupa Systems that counter the family's main media outlets.

title: Here’s how PayPal hopes to turn Venmo into the next PayPal
summary: PayPal is looking to increase revenue from its Venmo brand, which is popular with younger consumers, by introducing new features like a credit card. Darrell Esch, the new general manager of Venmo, is tasked with leading this initiative as digital wallets become increasingly important. PayPal itself has experienced significant growth during the COVID-19 pandemic, surpassing the market capitalization of several major companies.

title: 16 AMC Cinemas locations to offer Dolby experience in KSA
summary: AMC Entertainment Holdings Inc. and Dolby Laboratories, Inc. announced a partnership to bring the Dolby Cinema experience to 16 AMC Cinemas locations in Saudi Arabia over the next four years, with the first expected by the end of 2020. This expansion aims to provide moviegoers with a premium experience featuring Dolby Vision's ultravivid picture and Dolby Atmos' immersive sound. AMC plans to significantly increase its presence in Saudi Arabia, with eight new sites by the end of 2020 and an additional 14 in 2021.

title: Live-action 'Mulan' will be released on Disney+ for added $29.99
summary: Disney announced that its live-action "Mulan" film will bypass a major theatrical release and instead debut on Disney+ on September 4th. Subscribers will need to pay an additional $29.99 to rent the film, beyond their monthly subscription. This decision was made to bring the family-friendly film to a broad audience during an unpredictable period when many cannot go to movie theaters.

title: NBCUniversal Chairman Steve Burke Extends Comcast Deal As Advisor
summary: NBCUniversal chairman and former CEO Steve Burke has extended his tenure with parent company Comcast, transitioning from chairman to a senior adviser role beginning January 2021. His new contract runs through 2025, paying him $350,000 annually for the part-time position, with stipulations against working for other companies. This move follows a common practice at Comcast of retaining top executives in advisory capacities after they step down from their primary roles.

title: Disney Parks Pandemic Closures Result in $3.5 Billion Loss
summary: The Walt Disney Co. announced a $3.5 billion loss in its fiscal third quarter due to the closure of its theme parks worldwide caused by the novel coronavirus pandemic. Parks, Experiences and Products revenues decreased by 85 percent to $1.0 billion, resulting in a $2.0 billion operating loss for the segment. While Disney World in Florida has reopened, Disneyland in California remains largely closed, with its reopening dependent on state guidelines.

title: BREAKING: Parks, Experiences and Products Loses $2 Billion in Third Quarter, The Walt Disney Company Reports Historic Losses in Revenue Due to COVID-19 Pandemic
summary: The Walt Disney Company announced a significant revenue loss in its Q3 FY20 earnings report, primarily due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The Parks, Experiences and Products segment alone lost $2.0 billion, impacting overall revenue which was down 41.8% year-over-year to $11.78 billion. Despite the financial setbacks in its physical parks, Disney's streaming services, Disney+ and ESPN+, showed strong subscriber growth during the quarter.

title: Powering the Magic with Renewable Energy
summary: The Walt Disney Company is making continuous investments in renewable energy across its global operations to achieve its long-term goal of net-zero greenhouse gas emissions. This includes expanding solar arrays at corporate campuses, utilizing geothermal energy at Disneyland Paris, and opening a new 270-acre solar facility near Walt Disney World Resort capable of powering two theme parks. These efforts highlight Disney's commitment to clean electricity and increasing its renewable energy portfolio.

title: Novavax Stock Soars, Beyond Meat Drops and the Dow Keeps Marching Higher
summary: U.S. markets saw widespread gains as investors processed new earnings reports and monitored discussions in Washington regarding the next COVID-19 relief package. Novavax shares surged following positive clinical trial results for its Covid-19 vaccine, while Beyond Meat's stock fell due to higher-than-expected pandemic-related costs despite beating financial estimates. Disney and CVS Health also reported stronger-than-anticipated results, contributing to the overall market optimism.

title: Power Moves | Condé Nast Entertainment Hires President From Walt Disney Company, Gucci Global Head of Diversity Departs
summary: Condé Nast Entertainment has hired Agnes Chu, previously from Walt Disney Company, as its new president. Renée Tirado, Gucci's global head of diversity, equity, and inclusion, has departed to launch her own consulting firm. The article also highlights other significant executive appointments and departures in the fashion and media industries.

title: Judge Approves Ending Paramount Antitrust Consent Decrees
summary: A federal judge has approved the Justice Department's request to end the Paramount Consent Decrees, which previously barred movie studios from owning theaters. These antitrust rules, in place since the golden age of cinema, are now considered anachronistic given the rise of streaming and the challenges facing movie theaters. The decision is not expected to significantly alter Hollywood's business landscape, though it will eventually remove restrictions on "block booking" and "circuit dealing" after a two-year sunset period.

title: Walt Disney World to Reduce Theme Park Hours Next Month
summary: Walt Disney World is set to reduce operating hours at all four of its theme parks starting September 8th, following their phased reopening amidst a surge in COVID-19 cases in Florida. This decision comes after the Walt Disney Co. reported a significant fiscal third-quarter loss of $3.5 billion due to park closures. The parks had previously implemented safety measures like mandatory masks and social distancing, but faced criticism for reopening too early.

title: Disney World scaling back hours of operation in September
summary: Due to higher-than-anticipated cancellations and a surge in coronavirus cases in Florida, Disney World is reducing its operating hours starting September 8th. Parks like Magic Kingdom, Hollywood Studios, Epcot, and Animal Kingdom will close 1-2 hours earlier, while Animal Kingdom will also open an hour later. Despite the cancellations, Disney reported that the park is meeting its financial criteria for reopening.

title: WarnerMedia’s New CEO Says HBO Max Has One Clear Edge Over Netflix
summary: WarnerMedia CEO Jason Kilar believes HBO Max has a distinct advantage over competitors like Netflix, focusing on quality content despite lacking an early breakout hit. Kilar, who previously led Hulu, aims to use this strategy to thwart rivals in the streaming landscape. The article notes his past experience at Hulu and Amazon and touches on the historical context of media companies' hesitance to embrace streaming.

title: Breaking: Unicorp starts construction on O-Town West near Walt Disney World
summary: Unicorp has begun construction on its O-Town West development near Walt Disney World in Orlando. This major project, valued at $1 billion, will feature a Marriott Vacations Worldwide global corporate headquarters, a hotel, retail spaces, and apartments. The development is also anticipated to include establishments like Portillo's and White Castle.

title: Saukville cinema remains closed during pandemic
summary: The Marcus Saukville Cinema remains closed due to the coronavirus pandemic, with no set reopening date, as Marcus Corp. awaits the release of new movies. Six Marcus theaters in Wisconsin temporarily reopened in June to test new safety protocols, and the company hopes to reopen more locations by Labor Day. Marcus is also offering curbside pickup for concessions like popcorn and pizza at some of its other Wisconsin locations to cater to demand.

title: All in the Family: The Morrison Family
summary: The Morrison family's journey in the toy industry began with Doug Morrison's work on speech products for companies like Hasbro, including Star Wars toys. Doug, with his wife Christine, later founded So Sound Ltd., focusing on toy product recording and editing, and now involves their sons, TJ and Charlie, in the business. The article highlights the evolution of sound in toys, from gimmicks to integral learning aids, and offers advice on embracing new ideas and encouraging creativity within a family business.

title: Disney, Netflix Sue Streaming Service for Copyright Infringement
summary: Disney, Netflix, and other major media companies have filed a lawsuit against Florida-based Crystal Clear Media, alleging copyright infringement. The lawsuit, filed in a U.S. District Court in California, claims that Crystal Clear Media illegally offers copyrighted movies and television programs online for a fee, including popular titles like "Frozen II" and "The Amazing Spider-Man."

title: ‘Be Prepared’ to Order This NEW Build-a-Bear Scar Plush!
summary: Build-a-Bear Workshop has released a new Scar plush from Disney's "The Lion King." This special plush includes a sound chip that plays Scar's iconic song "Be Prepared" and features the Disney The Lion King logo on its paw. Customers can purchase the Scar plush for $43.00, choosing to receive it pre-stuffed or unstuffed, and personalize it further at a Build-a-Bear Workshop.

title: Ninth Circuit Affirms Dismissal of Copyright Infringement Claim Against Disney’s Inside Out Movie
summary: The Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed the dismissal of a copyright infringement claim against Disney's "Inside Out" movie. The court found no substantial similarity between Masterson's literary works and Disney's film, emphasizing that generic themes and unprotectable elements, even in combination, do not warrant copyright protection without a novel arrangement. This ruling highlights that literary works are not entitled to special treatment in copyright infringement cases and expert testimony is not always necessary to determine substantial similarity.

title: Bay Park Cinema reopens Friday for new Russell Crowe thriller; Green Bay East Cinema to open Aug. 28
summary: Marcus Theatres Corp. is reopening 17 more movie theaters in Wisconsin, including two in Green Bay: Bay Park Cinema and Green Bay East Cinema. Bay Park Cinema reopens Friday with new releases like "Unhinged" and classic films, while Green Bay East Cinema will open on August 28. Safety protocols such as face masks, social distancing, and advance ticket/concession purchases will be implemented.

title: Saudi Arabia's $300 billion sovereign wealth fund sold off 50% of its stake in Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway
summary: Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF), a $300 billion sovereign wealth fund, halved its stake in Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway during the second quarter of this year, an SEC filing revealed. This move reduced its investment in Berkshire Hathaway by about $40 million, leaving it with approximately $39 million worth of stock. The PIF also divested entirely from major US corporates like Facebook, Boeing, Disney, Citigroup, Bank of America, and European energy firms, while making new investments of about $4.7 billion into real estate and utilities focused funds.

title: Vera Bradley Creates New Limited-Release Patterns for Disney Parks, “Mickey’s Sweet Treats” and “Sweet Treat Ditsy”
summary: Vera Bradley has launched two new limited-release patterns for Disney Parks: "Mickey’s Sweet Treats" and "Sweet Treat Ditsy." These patterns feature Mickey and friends along with iconic Disney sweet treats like ice cream bars and cupcakes. The collection includes 18 items such as backpacks, totes, and accessories, available at Vera Bradley in Disney Springs and on shopDisney.com.

title: NEW Disney Vera Bradley Designs Launch at Disney Springs
summary: Vera Bradley has launched two new Disney patterns, "Mickey’s Sweet Treats" and "Sweet Treat Ditsy," available at Disney Springs and online. "Mickey’s Sweet Treats" features Disney Parks snacks on a light purple background, while "Sweet Treat Ditsy" is a paisley design with classic characters and subtle mini treat accents. Disney fans can find these new collections at the Vera Bradley store in Disney Springs starting August 20.

title: 24 Awesome Chapter Book Series for Kids
summary: This article lists 24 popular chapter book series for children, ranging from classics to more recent hits. It provides a brief description of each series, target age group, author, and an image of the book cover, making it a useful resource for parents and educators looking for reading recommendations. The selections cover various genres like fantasy, mystery, and humor, ensuring there's something for every young reader.

title: ‘Unhinged’ earns $4M in biggest movie release since theaters closed
summary: The Russell Crowe thriller "Unhinged" grossed $4 million in North American box-office sales, marking the biggest new movie release since COVID-19 theater closures began in March. While these numbers are modest compared to pre-pandemic standards, the film's performance indicates a growing willingness among consumers to return to cinemas. The true test for the industry's recovery will come with major releases like Warner Bros.' "Tenet" on September 3.

title: Disney World will continue to have reduced hours in November
summary: Disney World will maintain reduced operating hours into November, significantly cutting back daily schedules compared to 2019. This continues a trend that began in September, following the park's reopening after its closure due to the coronavirus pandemic. The article also notes the cancellation of the Halloween celebration and uncertainty surrounding Christmas events.

title: Pearson appoints Andy Bird as next CEO
summary: Pearson PLC announced the appointment of Andy Bird as its next chief executive, effective October 19. He will succeed John Fallon, who will step down from the board on the same date. Bird previously served as chairman of Walt Disney Co.'s international operations and is currently a nonexecutive director at Pearson.

title: Pearson Taps Former Disney Official as Incoming CEO
summary: Pearson, the global education company, has appointed Andy Bird, a former Walt Disney International official known for leading a digital-first strategy, as its new CEO. Bird will replace retiring CEO John Fallon and is expected to further Pearson's transition to a digital-first learning company with a focus on direct-to-consumer sales. His appointment is pending shareholder approval of a unique compensation package that includes a significant personal investment in Pearson shares.

title: Disney, Hilton, Southwest Airlines target travel planners on Pinterest
summary: Disney, Hilton, Southwest Airlines, Accor, and California's tourism board are targeting travel planners on Pinterest with branded content and campaigns. This comes as Pinterest saw elevated interest in travel-related searches during the summer, particularly for socially distanced options like RV camping and road trips. Brands are developing content that balances health and safety recommendations with "dream vacation" ideas to help users plan for future travel.

title: The Walt Disney Studios’ StudioLAB (Virtually) Hosts Tech Leaders at Inaugural Partner Summit
summary: The Walt Disney Studios' StudioLAB held its first virtual partner summit on August 13, bringing together over 100 participants from its Innovation Partners and Disney teams. The summit, themed "The New Normal—Operating in Our Current Reality," focused on how advanced technology is being used to adapt to current operating environments. StudioLAB aims to advance storytelling through cutting-edge tools and collaboration with industry partners, with significant progress noted in technology deployments since its inception.

title: Tegna Relaunching Justice as True Crime Net with Streaming | Next TV | Broadcasting+Cable
summary: Tegna is relaunching its Justice Network multicast channel as True Crime Network on July 27, offering its programming as both a broadcast channel and an on-demand streaming service. This move aims to tap into the growing over-the-top viewing market and the popularity of the true crime genre, competing with established networks like Discovery's ID and Court TV. The streaming service will launch with hundreds of hours of content, including popular true crime series and safety tips.

title: Marvel Super War is a 5v5 MOBA from NetEase, now available in more regions
summary: NetEase and Marvel Entertainment's 5v5 MOBA, Marvel Super War, expanded its regional availability beyond its initial closed beta territories to include South Korea, Japan, Australia, and New Zealand. The game, which features popular Marvel heroes and villains, aims for fair combat and balanced gameplay unlike traditional mobile MOBAs. While initially facing skepticism due to NetEase's history with "reskins," the game continues to grow its presence, though a Western release date remains unannounced.

title: Harry Potter comes to Build-A-Bear Workshop the same week of Q2 earnings call
summary: Build-A-Bear Workshop is launching a Harry Potter collection exclusively online on September 2nd, with in-store availability later in the fall. The collection features themed bears and Hogwarts house apparel, following the success of their Baby Yoda plush toys. This announcement comes just ahead of Build-A-Bear's Q2 earnings call on September 1st, after a significant drop in Q1 revenues due to the coronavirus pandemic.

title: Adventure to the Edge of the Galaxy in The Sims™ 4 Star Wars™: Journey to Batuu Game Pack
summary: Electronic Arts announced the release of The Sims 4 Star Wars: Journey to Batuu Game Pack, available September 8 for PC and consoles. This new game pack allows players to create their own Star Wars story in the galaxy, featuring iconic locations like Black Spire Outpost and characters such as Rey and Kylo Ren. Players can align with factions, customize droids and lightsabers, and bring these items back to their Sims' home worlds.

title: New ‘ Harry Potter’ Collection Arrives at Build-a-Bear!
summary: Build-a-Bear Workshop is launching a new Harry Potter collection online on September 2nd, featuring bears dressed in Hogwarts house uniforms complete with wands. This new line follows the success of their Baby Yoda plush and arrives shortly after their Q2 earnings call, with hopes that the magical bears will help the company recover from recent losses experienced during the coronavirus pandemic. Fans can customize their bears to reflect their favorite Hogwarts house.

title: Marriott International Debuts JW Marriott, Anaheim Resort
summary: Marriott International announced the opening of the JW Marriott, Anaheim Resort on August 19, 2020, offering a luxury experience near Disneyland and the Anaheim Convention Center. The resort features 466 rooms, extensive indoor and outdoor event spaces, and unique amenities like an augmented reality sculpture garden. The hotel emphasizes guest safety with a "Safe Meeting" protocol and enhanced cleanliness standards in line with Marriott's commitment to clean.

title: Kartoon Channel! Acquires “Sonic The Hedgehog” and “PAC-MAN” Animated Series
summary: Kartoon Channel! has acquired the rights to two人気 animated children's series, "Adventures of Sonic The Hedgehog" and "PAC-MAN and The Ghostly Adventures," from 41 Entertainment. These classic shows will be available on Kartoon Channel! and its apps starting in October. This move aims to deliver high-quality, popular children's entertainment and expands Kartoon Channel!'s growing library of content.

title: Economics of Film: Changing Dynamics & COVID-19
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic severely disrupted the film industry in March 2020, leading to production halts and cinema closures, which forced studios to explore direct-to-consumer digital alternatives. This article by FTI Consulting examines how these changes impact the economics of film production, the significance of cinema theatre contributions, and the shift toward premium video-on-demand (PVoD) platforms. It also discusses the implications for marketing spend under a direct-to-consumer model.

title: Disney’s Epcot revamp, Cirque du Soleil renovations begin
summary: Walt Disney World continues to advance major renovation projects at Epcot and Disney Springs. These updates include a significant revamp of Epcot and renovations for the Cirque du Soleil show. The theme park had reopened in July with limited capacity amid ongoing pandemic concerns.

title: Peloton launching cheaper treadmill, cutting bike price
summary: Peloton is introducing a more affordable treadmill, the "Tread," priced at $2,495, and cutting the price of its original stationary bike to $1,895 while launching a premium "Bike+" for $2,495. These strategic price adjustments come as demand for at-home fitness equipment surges due to gym closures during the coronavirus pandemic. The company aims to make its offerings more accessible to a wider audience, building on its 2.6 million members.

title: Jessica Alba to Receive Hispanic Heritage Business Award
summary: Jessica Alba will be honored with the Business Award at the 33rd Annual Hispanic Heritage Awards. The award, presented by Nationwide, recognizes her achievements as an entrepreneur and philanthropist through The Honest Company. Alba will join other honorees including Bad Bunny and farmworkers, celebrating Hispanic accomplishment and culture.

title: 'Million Dollar Listing LA': John Barrymore's $15.9M Beverly Hills mansion with opium den is up for sale
summary: The article features the historic Beverly Hills mansion of acting legend John Barrymore, which is currently for sale at $15.9 million and was showcased in the finale of 'Million Dollar Listing LA'. Real estate agents Josh Altman and Tracy Tutor are handling the sale of the Spanish-style estate, notable for its dramatic fireplaces, lush gardens, and a unique opium den located above the main bedroom. Originally listed for $42.5 million in 2015 with more acreage, the property has since been downsized and re-listed.

title: 'Mulan' reboot, once a sure thing, becomes a headache for Disney
summary: Disney's live-action "Mulan" reboot, initially expected to be a blockbuster, has instead become a political controversy. Released online in some regions and set to open in China, the $200 million film faced production issues exacerbated by the coronavirus pandemic. Its struggles highlight the fraying relationship between the U.S. and China.

title: Netflix isn't a media company or a technology company -- it's an entertainment company, CEO Reed Hastings says
summary: Netflix co-founder and co-CEO Reed Hastings argues that Netflix should be classified as an "entertainment company" rather than a media or technology company, despite its roots in Silicon Valley and technology-driven operations. He explains that Netflix's primary focus, employee distribution, and spending are entertainment-centric. Hastings also commented on how traditional media companies can compete by fully committing to streaming and predicted continued industry consolidation.

title: Debut of Disney Cruise Line's newest ship, Disney Wish, to be delayed amid pandemic
summary: The debut of Disney Cruise Line's newest ship, the Disney Wish, has been delayed due to disruptions caused by the coronavirus pandemic. The ship, originally slated for a late 2021 debut and a January 2022 inaugural trip, is awaiting new finalized dates from the shipyard, Meyer Werft. Other Disney projects, including the Star Wars Hotel and Avengers Campus, are also facing potential delays, while Disney Cruise Line has canceled all trips until October 31, 2020.

title: ‘September Is the New October’ for Political Advertising | Next TV | Multichannel News
summary: The 2020 political advertising landscape is undergoing significant changes due to early voting and the COVID-19 pandemic, leading to "September being the new October" for campaign spending. Political campaigns are front-loading their ad buys, particularly for "get-out-the-vote" messages, and are increasingly utilizing multi-platform and programmatic advertising, especially on connected TV and news channels. This shift is creating challenges for non-political advertisers as inventory tightens in swing states.

title: ESPN Enters into Co-Exclusive Agreements with Caesars Entertainment and DraftKings
summary: ESPN has signed separate multi-year co-exclusive agreements with Caesars Entertainment and DraftKings. These deals integrate links to sportsbooks from Caesars Entertainment's partner William Hill and DraftKings across ESPN's digital platforms, expanding ESPN's commitment to sports betting. Caesars will also become a sponsor of ESPN's Fantasy products and the exclusive odds provider, while DraftKings will be the exclusive daily fantasy sports provider and power integrations across ESPN content.

title: New Safety Standards for Moviegoing as U.S. Theaters Reopen (Published 2020)
summary: Major U.S. movie theater chains, including AMC Entertainment, Cinemark, Marcus Theaters, and Regal Cinemas, announced uniform health protocols under the "CinemaSafe" campaign to encourage moviegoing as theaters reopen after the pandemic shutdown. These measures include mask requirements, limited capacity, and enhanced air filtration, aiming to assure patrons of a safe viewing experience. Despite the reopening efforts, several states like New York and California had not yet allowed theaters to resume operations due to ongoing safety concerns.

title: Exclusive: -AT&T considers cellphone plans subsidized by ads
summary: AT&T is exploring offering wireless phone plans partially subsidized by advertising as early as next year, according to CEO John Stankey. This move aligns with AT&T's commitment to advertising and its efforts to reduce debt by potentially selling assets like its advertising-technology unit Xandr. The company believes that a segment of its customer base would accept ads for a reduction in their mobile bill, leveraging better ad targeting and its upcoming ad-supported HBO Max service.

title: Jakks Pacific Unveils ‘Treats at Home: Halloween’ with Super Mario, Frozen II Characters
summary: Jakks Pacific is launching a new product range called "Treats at Home: Halloween" featuring Super Mario and Frozen II characters, designed to facilitate virtual trick-or-treating experiences during the COVID-19 pandemic. These sets include figures and accessories, along with postcard invitations for families to host virtual Halloween events via video conferencing. The initiative aims to blend seasonal celebration with product engagement and costume promotion.

title: Cable Adds a Playbook To Addressable Ad Push | Next TV | Broadcasting+Cable
summary: Comcast, Charter Communications, and Cox Communications have launched a "playbook" for addressable advertising, aiming to simplify the buying and selling of targeted ads for distributors, programmers, media buyers, and advertisers. The initiative, part of their "On Addressability" program started in 2019, seeks to standardize practices and achieve scale in addressable TV. This effort comes as the industry adapts to changing advertising spending patterns, exacerbated by the recent pandemic, making it easier for marketers to utilize targeted TV campaigns.

title: The Walt Disney Company’s Major Recent Acquisitions, Ranked By Cost
summary: This article details The Walt Disney Company's major acquisitions, ranking them by cost and highlighting their strategic importance under former CEO Bob Iger. It covers the financial impact and strategic reasoning behind acquiring Marvel, Lucasfilm, Pixar, Hulu, and Fox, emphasizing how these deals reshaped Disney's market presence, especially in direct-to-consumer entertainment.

title: Father Sues Universal After Son Jumps From Aventura Hotel
summary: Alfred Bahna is suing Universal Orlando Resort, Loews Corp., and others after his 27-year-old son, Matthew Bahna, committed suicide by jumping from the Bar 17 Bistro at Universal's Aventura Hotel in 2019. The lawsuit alleges wrongful death, claiming hotel employees overserved Matthew alcohol and that the open-air rooftop bar lacked sufficient safety barriers. Bahna seeks over $30,000, stating the hotel should have foreseen the danger posed by the bar's design to intoxicated patrons.

title: E.W. Scripps Buys ION Media For $2.65B, With Berkshire Hathaway Investment
summary: E.W. Scripps announced it will acquire ION Media for $2.65 billion, with a significant $600 million investment from Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway. This acquisition will combine ION's broadcast spectrum and reach with Scripps' existing assets, aiming to create a stronger national media company. The deal positions Scripps to be the largest holder of broadcast spectrum, leveraging new ATSC 3.0 standards.

title: Walt Disney Co loses right to expand Hong Kong Disneyland
summary: The Walt Disney Company has lost the option to expand Hong Kong Disneyland as the Hong Kong Government decided not to renew an agreement for an adjacent land plot. This decision was influenced by the current economic conditions amid COVID-19, with the government advising the park to focus on its existing multi-expansion plan rather than geographical growth. Disney expressed disappointment but stated it would continue investing in the park, which is majority-owned by the local government.

title: Disneyland Resort Final Walt Disney Co. Property To Reopen
summary: Disneyland Resort is the last Walt Disney Company property awaiting reopening, as Hong Kong Disney reopened and other Disney parks worldwide began operating. The closure has caused significant economic impact, with 32,000 direct employees and 80,000 related jobs affected, leading to calls for clear reopening guidelines from California's Governor amid declining COVID-19 cases in Orange County. Local businesses and chambers of commerce are urging the state for an economic recovery roadmap for theme parks.

title: New Star Wars The Black Series and Vintage Collection Toys Revealed During Hasbro PulseCon 2020
summary: Hasbro revealed new Star Wars toys from both the Vintage Collection and The Black Series during its inaugural PulseCon 2020 virtual event. The announcements included new 3 ¾-inch Vintage Collection figures like Anakin Skywalker and Captain Rex, 6-inch Black Series figures such as Dark Side Rey and Jar Jar Binks, and additions to the Black Series Archive Collection. A Black Series Holiday Edition and a new Ahsoka Tano Force FX Elite lightsaber were also unveiled.

title: Star Wars The Mandalorian Razor Crest Ship Arrives at Hasbro HasLabs
summary: Hasbro has launched a new HasLabs campaign for an incredibly detailed, large-scale replica of the Razor Crest ship from "The Mandalorian" for its Vintage Collection. This 30-inch long ship will feature numerous screen-accurate details, detachable parts for recreating scenes, and will come with an exclusive Beskar-armored Mandalorian figure. Priced at $349.99, the campaign has unlockable tiers after reaching its 6,000 backer goal, with the ship expected to ship in Fall 2021.

title: Walt Disney Co (DIS) Hires Diane Jurgens As CIO
summary: Walt Disney Co (NYSE: DIS) has announced the hiring of Diane Jurgens as its new Chief Information Officer, effective October 5. Jurgens brings extensive global technology leadership experience from her previous roles at BHP, SAIC General Motors, and General Motors. She will oversee Disney’s Enterprise Technology operations and report to CFO Christine McCarthy, succeeding Susan O’Day.

title: Sonos and Disney+ team for Mandalorian tie-in
summary: Sonos and Disney+ have partnered for the second season premiere of The Mandalorian, aiming to enhance the at-home sound experience through Sonos Arc and Beam soundbars. From October 1-31, 2020, customers purchasing eligible Sonos home theatre systems will receive six months of Disney+ for new subscribers. Additionally, Sonos Radio will launch a new station, "Things That Stuck," curated by The Mandalorian composer Ludwig Göransson, featuring the show's soundtrack and exclusive commentary.

title: The Mandalorian Partners With Sonos For Audio Goodies
summary: The Mandalorian is partnering with Sonos to enhance the viewing experience for its second season through improved audio and a curated musical playlist. Sonos is offering 5.1 surround sound with Dolby Atmos integration for iconic Star Wars sounds and a six-month free Disney+ subscription with select Sonos product purchases. Additionally, composer Ludwig Göransson has curated a station on Sonos Radio featuring music from the show and other genres.

title: AMC’s “The Walking Dead” Invades Magic: The Gathering on October 4th
summary: Wizards of the Coast announced a limited-edition Magic: The Gathering Secret Lair crossover with AMC's "The Walking Dead," launching October 4th. This drop will feature all-premium-foil cards depicting iconic characters from the TV series, with pre-orders available for a limited time. The launch coincides with AMC's "We Are The Walking Dead Weekend" events.

title: Disney Sells Ad Tech Firm TrueX To Marketing Data Company Gimbal
summary: The Walt Disney Co. has sold its advertising technology firm TrueX to Gimbal, a marketing data company. Disney had acquired TrueX as part of its $71 billion purchase of 21st Century Fox's entertainment assets the previous year. This sale is part of Disney's ongoing effort to divest "non-core" assets obtained during the Fox acquisition, having previously sold Fox's regional sports networks and the FoxNext video game division.

title: Walt Disney Company to lay off 28,000 at Disney World in Florida, Disneyland in California
summary: The Walt Disney Co. announced it would lay off 28,000 workers in its theme parks division in California and Florida due to the prolonged impact of the COVID-19 pandemic and restrictions on park attendance. Two-thirds of the layoffs will impact part-time workers, but salaried and hourly employees are also affected. The layoffs are exacerbated by California's unwillingness to lift restrictions allowing Disneyland to reopen.

title: Walt Disney sheds 28,000 jobs at theme parks as pandemic bites
summary: Walt Disney announced the layoff of 28,000 employees from its theme park business, attributing the decision to limited attendance at reopened parks and the continued closure of others due to the coronavirus pandemic. The company, which reported a $4.72 billion loss in the second quarter, stated that despite cost-cutting measures, they could not remain fully staffed with limited capacity. The majority of the cuts affect part-time positions, with Disneyland in California remaining closed.

title: Disney Lays Off 28,000, Mostly at Its 2 U.S. Theme Parks (Published 2020)
summary: Disney announced the layoff of 28,000 employees in the United States, predominantly affecting its theme park division in Florida and California, as a result of the prolonged impact of the Covid-19 pandemic. The job cuts include both part-time hourly workers and salaried employees. Disney attributed the layoffs in California partly to the state's unwillingness to lift restrictions that would allow Disneyland to reopen.

title: HGTV HOME® by Sherwin-Williams Announces Its 2021 Color Collection of the Year
summary: HGTV HOME® by Sherwin-Williams has unveiled its 2021 Color Collection of the Year, "Delightfully Daring," and the distinguished 2021 Color of the Year, "Passionate." This collection, available exclusively at Lowe's, features earthy tones with vibrant accents, designed to create energizing yet calming spaces inspired by both virtual and real-world experiences. The colors aim to help consumers streamline and personalize their homes while infusing fun and emotion through thoughtful design.

title: Disney announces 28,000 layoffs amid continued closure of Disneyland
summary: Disney announced the layoff of approximately 28,000 employees in its Parks, Experiences and Products division due to the prolonged impact of COVID-19 and the continued closure of Disneyland. The company attributed the decision partly to California's restrictions preventing Disneyland from reopening, despite Walt Disney World in Florida having reopened. These layoffs primarily affect domestic, with about two-thirds being part-time employees.

title: Disney leads companies announcing layoffs; big airline job cuts loom
summary: Several major companies, including Disney, Royal Dutch Shell, and Dow Inc., have announced significant job cuts due to the ongoing impact of the coronavirus pandemic. Disney is laying off 28,000 employees, primarily from its parks and experiences divisions, while Shell will cut 7,000 to 9,000 jobs. The airline industry also faces looming job losses, with over 30,000 potential cuts if additional federal aid is not provided.

title: When sports and financial markets collide
summary: The article discusses the increasing intersection of sports and financial markets, driven largely by the legalization of sports betting. It highlights the launch of sports betting and esports ETFs by Roundhill Investments and introduces the JohnWallStreet Sports Stock Index by Sportico, which tracks the growth of the domestic sports industry through 40 publicly traded companies.

title: Disney's Bob Iger leaves California coronavirus task force as parks remain idle
summary: Walt Disney Co. Chairman and CEO Bob Iger has resigned from California Gov. Gavin Newsom's COVID-19 economic task force as Disneyland's reopening remains stalled. His departure comes after Disney announced it would lay off 28,000 employees in its Parks, Experiences and Products segment, citing the state's unwillingness to lift restrictions. Disney has incurred a $3.5 billion financial blow during the third quarter due to park closures.

title: Dole Healthy-Cooking Initiative With Disney and Pixar’s Ratatouille Seeks to Get More Cooks in the Kitchen
summary: Dole Food Company launched a new healthy-cooking initiative inspired by Disney and Pixar’s Ratatouille to encourage more people to cook at home using fresh ingredients. The "Now We’re (All) Cooking" program features 20 new recipes, digital activations, and family-friendly activities, working in collaboration with Disney and Pixar. This initiative is part of Dole's larger nutritional alliance with The Walt Disney Company, aiming to make healthy eating more fun and accessible.

title: Studios “Must Be Willing to Take a Hit” to Keep Cinema Chains From “Falling Apart”: Analyst
summary: A Wall Street analyst, Eric Wold of B. Riley, stated that Hollywood studios must be willing to take a financial hit to support cinema chains, which are struggling due to film delays caused by the coronavirus pandemic. The postponement of the new James Bond film has left the upcoming months as a "virtual ghost town" for cinema schedules. Wold also criticized state-level restrictions on theaters, arguing that safety protocols there are "not well appreciated," leading to significantly stricter regulations compared to other indoor entertainment options.

title: Halloween happenings around the Central Florida theme parks
summary: This article details the various Halloween-themed events and attractions available at Central Florida's theme parks in 2020, despite changes due to the year's circumstances. It covers offerings at Universal Orlando Resort, SeaWorld Orlando, Walt Disney World Resort, and Busch Gardens Tampa, highlighting options for both families and those seeking more intense scares.

title: Disney cast member union says full-time employees to avoid layoffs; 8,800 part-time to face layoffs
summary: The Service Trades Council Union announced an agreement with Disney to prevent layoffs for full-time union cast members, despite original plans for thousands of layoffs. While full-time employees are spared, approximately 8,800 part-time employees will still be laid off due to reduced park attendance and resort occupancy stemming from the coronavirus pandemic. Both full-time employees potentially laid off in the future and part-time employees will have contractual recall rights to their previous jobs until October 1, 2022.

title: Lewis Hamilton against plan to build new Rio track in Camboata Forest
summary: Lewis Hamilton has voiced his opposition to plans for a new Formula 1 track in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, which would require building on the Camboata Forest. The six-time world champion emphasized that the most sustainable action would be to avoid tearing down trees, especially given the global crisis of deforestation. While organizers claim the Deodoro circuit would be zero-carbon and involve replanting, Hamilton prefers existing circuits like Interlagos.

title: How Dividend Funds Can Add Income, and Risk, to Your Portfolio
summary: Dividend funds can offer higher income than Treasuries and investment-grade bonds but come with the inherent volatility of underlying stocks. The article highlights that while dividends can be dependable, stock prices are not, and the pandemic has increased the risk of dividend cuts, citing examples like Disney and the increased number of cuts in 2020. Investors should weigh the potential for income against the risks of stock market fluctuations and dividend suspensions.

title: The Walt Disney Company Announces Strategic Reorganization of Its Media and Entertainment Businesses
summary: The Walt Disney Company has announced a strategic reorganization of its media and entertainment businesses to accelerate its direct-to-consumer (DTC) strategy following the success of Disney+. The new structure centralizes distribution and commercialization activities into a single global Media and Entertainment Distribution organization, led by Kareem Daniel, while creative engines will focus on producing original content across three distinct groups: Studios, General Entertainment, and Sports. This move aims to optimize content delivery and monetization across all platforms, including Disney+, Hulu, and ESPN+.

title: In The Pitlane: Liberty Media takes back control in Brazil
summary: Liberty Media is moving the Brazilian Grand Prix from Interlagos to a new purpose-built track in Rio de Janeiro, despite significant public opposition regarding deforestation. The decision stems from Liberty discovering that Brazil did not pay hosting fees, a situation Bernie Ecclestone had secretly arranged. This move allows Liberty to control a crucial revenue stream, particularly by launching its F1 TV OTT streaming service in Brazil, which is F1's top TV market.

title: The Walt Disney Company Announces Strategic Reorganization of Its Media and Entertainment Businesses
summary: The Walt Disney Company announced a strategic reorganization of its media and entertainment businesses to accelerate its direct-to-consumer (DTC) strategy following the success of Disney+. The new structure centralizes distribution and commercialization into a single global Media and Entertainment Distribution organization, while creative engines will focus on content production for both DTC and legacy platforms. This aims to increase shareholder value and allow creative teams to focus on content creation, while the distribution team monetizes it across platforms like Disney+, Hulu, ESPN+, and the upcoming Star international streaming service.

title: Disney’s Streaming Reorganization Cheers Investors but Confuses Insiders
summary: The Walt Disney Company announced a major reorganization of its film and television teams to bolster its streaming services, which was well-received by investors, causing shares to rise. However, the internal reaction among employees was one of confusion regarding the timing and content of the announcement, particularly concerning new leadership roles and the apparent omission of some key creative executives. This strategic shift underscores Hollywood's accelerated move towards direct-to-consumer ventures, driven by the impact of COVID-19 on traditional revenue streams like theme parks and box office.

title: Walt Disney restructures entertainment businesses to boost streaming
summary: Walt Disney Co (DIS.N) announced a restructuring of its media and entertainment businesses to prioritize the growth of its streaming services like Disney+. This move follows pressure from activist investor Daniel Loeb to increase programming investment in streaming. The reorganization separates content creation from distribution to be more responsive to consumer demands, with the company planning to increase content investments.

title: Disney says it’s shifting its business around. And it’s going to impact you
summary: Disney is undertaking a major restructuring to prioritize its streaming business, creating a single organization for media content distribution. This shift will allow content executives to focus on creation while distribution teams decide the best platform for release, including Disney Plus, Hulu, or other services. CEO Bob Chapek stated this move was always planned but accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic, aiming to increase shareholder value and meet consumer content consumption preferences.

title: Coronavirus: A Cruise Timeline of Events
summary: This article provides a detailed timeline of events related to the impact of the SARS-CoV-2 virus on the cruise industry, beginning from December 2019 through May 2021. It covers significant actions taken by health organizations, governments, and cruise lines, including no-sail orders, financial struggles, fleet reductions, and the eventual cautious resumption of sailings with new health protocols. The timeline highlights the evolving challenges and responses of the industry to the global pandemic.

title: Global TV & Streaming News Bytes
summary: This article provides a comprehensive overview of recent global television and streaming news within the animation industry. It details numerous new international broadcast and distribution deals for various animated series, including "The Curious World of Linda," "Remy & Boo," "Pikwik Pack," "True and the Rainbow Kingdom," "Brave Bunnies," and titles from WowKidz, DreamWorks Animation, and Pokémon. The developments highlight the ongoing expansion of children's animated content across different platforms and regions worldwide.

title: Are you still watching? Netflix misses subscriber target by 1.2m
summary: Netflix Inc reported its weakest subscriber gains in four years, adding 2.2 million globally, significantly missing both Wall Street's and its own target of 3.4 million for the quarter ending September 30. This shortfall is attributed to increased streaming competition, easing pandemic restrictions, and the return of live sports. The company's shares dropped by nearly 6 percent in after-hours trading, with domestic subscriber growth being almost flat, hinting at saturation in the US market.

title: Disney Debuts New Trailer for ‘Raya and the Last Dragon’
summary: Walt Disney Animation Studios has released a new trailer for "Raya and the Last Dragon," a film starring Kelly Marie Tran as Raya, a lone warrior. Her mission is to find the last dragon to save and unite the lands of Kumandra, which were fractured after dragons sacrificed themselves to save humanity from an evil force 500 years ago. The movie, set to open in U.S. theaters on March 12, 2021, emphasizes themes of trust and teamwork alongside the quest for the dragon.

title: As Quibi Shutters, So Goes Nearly $2 Billion in Major Hollywood Investments
summary: Quibi, the mobile streaming startup led by Jeffrey Katzenberg and Meg Whitman, is shutting down just six months after launching, resulting in the loss of nearly $2 billion in investments from major Hollywood studios and other financial entities. The company struggled to attract subscribers, falling far short of its targets, partly due to its launch coinciding with the COVID-19 pandemic which disrupted its intended use case. Quibi plans to wind down operations, sell its assets, and return remaining funds to its investors.

title: Mattel Crushes Estimates for Pandemic-Fueled Q3 Earnings Boom
summary: Mattel reported a surprisingly strong third quarter, exceeding analyst expectations with a 10% increase in overall sales due to significant growth in North America (13%) and international markets (8%). The company's adjusted earnings per share reached $0.95, significantly higher than the expected $0.39, driven by strong sales in categories like dolls (up 24%, led by Barbie) and vehicles (up 8%, led by Hot Wheels). Mattel reinstated its financial guidance, expecting to finish the year flat to a modest 1% increase, and continues to focus on its long-term strategy of leveraging its intellectual property across gaming and entertainment.

title: Executive Turntable: Beasley Elected Chairman of BMI Board; Reservoir Deepens Creative Team
summary: Caroline Beasley has been elected as the new chairman of BMI's board of directors, and BMI has extended Mike O’Neill’s contract as president & CEO for six years. Additionally, Reservoir has expanded its creative team with multiple promotions and hires, including Donna Caseine, Annette Barrett, and Faith Newman in new leadership roles. Bell Media will see Wade Oosterman take operational leadership following Randy Lennox's departure, and Spirits Music Group has restructured its synch team with Amy Hartman as senior vp creative services.

title: Media executives are finally accepting the decline of cable TV as they plot a new path forward
summary: Major media companies anticipate a significant decline in traditional pay-TV subscribers, expecting the number to drop to around 50 million households in the U.S. within the next five years. This shift has prompted large-scale reorganizations and a pivot towards streaming services, as companies aim to offset projected losses in cable subscription revenue and advertising. However, the economic viability of streaming as a replacement for the cable bundle remains uncertain, with challenges including subscriber growth, content budgets, and password sharing affecting the new business model.

title: Disney Announces More Christmas 2020 Merchandise
summary: Disney is gearing up for Christmas 2020 by releasing a new merchandise collection in stores at Disney parks and on shopDisney.com. The collection includes items such as Christmas face masks, plush toys, kitchenware, ears and hats, and jewelry. The article provides a visual preview of some of these festive products.

title: LG TV launches Shop Time app featuring QVC, HSN
summary: LG has launched its Shop Time app, a free shopping platform available on LG Smart TVs made between 2016 and 2020. The app allows users to purchase directly from retailers like QVC and HSN, offering tailored product recommendations and incentives like coupons for new customers. This initiative reflects a broader trend of companies, including Qurate Retail Group, experimenting with shoppable content on smart TVs and other digital platforms, especially accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Walt Disney World lays off live show entertainers, casts a dark shadow on popular Disney attractions
summary: Walt Disney World has initiated a new round of layoffs, primarily affecting live show entertainers and casting uncertainty over many popular attractions such as "Beauty and the Beast – Live on Stage" and "Festival of the Lion King." This move follows an earlier announcement by Disney Chairman Josh D'Amaro in September, where the company indicated plans to reduce its workforce by approximately 28,000 employees due to the prolonged impact of the COVID-19 pandemic and associated operational restrictions. The Actors' Equity Association expressed deep sorrow for the affected cast members, emphasizing the need for robust national strategies against the virus and continued support for arts workers.

title: Apple's subscription bundle of news, music and services to launch Friday
summary: Apple Chief Executive Tim Cook announced that the Apple One bundle, which includes news, music, video, and cloud storage, would launch on Friday, October 30, 2020. This move increases Apple's competition with services like Spotify and Netflix, and Cook also noted that Apple Fitness+ would launch later in the year. Apple has already exceeded 585 million subscribers on its platforms and anticipates surpassing 600 million for the calendar year, with services revenue up by 16.3% to $14.5 billion.

title: Dole Food Company Continues Cooking Collaboration With Disney and Pixar’s Ratatouille
summary: Dole Food Company is continuing its collaboration with Disney and Pixar’s Ratatouille to inspire healthy cooking at home. The initiative provides free downloadable resources, recipes, and activities to encourage consumers to create French-inspired dishes. This partnership is part of Dole's long-term nutritional alliance with The Walt Disney Company, aiming to make healthy eating more accessible and fun.

title: Thinking of cutting the cord with T-Mobile's new streaming service TVision? What you need to know
summary: T-Mobile has launched its new streaming service, TVision, offering cord-cutting options starting at $10 monthly for 30 networks. The service is initially available to T-Mobile postpaid customers, with wider access planned for Sprint subscribers later in the month and other customers next year. TVision provides various packages, including live news and sports, and allows users to add premium channels, though the total cost can rise with additional services.

title: Sony Wants a Bite of Anime Streamer Crunchyroll (Report)
summary: Sony is reportedly in exclusive negotiations to acquire anime streaming platform Crunchyroll from AT&T for an estimated $960 million. This potential acquisition would significantly bolster Sony's position in the anime market, following a previous investment in Bilibili, and increase its rivalry with other streaming giants like Netflix and Hulu. The deal would also raise questions about the future integration of Crunchyroll with Sony's existing anime properties like Funimation.

title: Disney Recovers 45%, But Company Is Not Out of the Woods
summary: The Walt Disney Company has seen its stock price recover by 45% from its March lows after significant struggles due to the COVID-19 pandemic, although it still underperforms the broader S&P 500. This recovery, or lack thereof compared to the market, could have wide-ranging implications for its theme park expansions, film production strategies, particularly a shift towards Disney+, and potential for further job layoffs. Despite these challenges, CEO Bob Chapek maintains hope for the company's future.

title: New Disney Content Head Elaborates on Restructuring
summary: Peter Rice, Chairman of Disney General Entertainment Content (DGE), detailed the ongoing restructuring of Disney's television division, emphasizing a shift to focus DGE's resources on developing content for both streaming and linear platforms. The new structure aims to make the company more effective and flexible in content creation, with a strong focus on Disney+ and other streaming services. Rice also outlined the leadership team supporting this new content-centric approach and highlighted the company's commitment to adapting to industry changes.

title: Ulta Beauty will open hundreds of shops inside Target stores
summary: Ulta Beauty plans to open hundreds of mini-shops, each approximately 1,000 square feet, inside Target stores. These shops will be located next to Target's existing beauty sections and are about one-tenth the size of a typical Ulta store.

title: Disney+ subscribers hit nearly 74 million as COVID-19 brings big losses
summary: Despite significant financial losses across its other divisions due to the COVID-19 pandemic, Disney announced its Disney+ streaming service reached 73.7 million subscribers by October 3, 2020, just one year after its launch. The company's overall revenue fell by 6% for the fiscal year, with its parks segment experiencing an $81-million operating loss. Disney executives are prioritizing streaming and are restructuring the company to focus on direct-to-consumer content, emphasizing the success of shows like "The Mandalorian"

title: Disney Quarterly Losses Mount, Even as Company Beats Expectations
summary: The Walt Disney Company reported significant quarterly losses due to the coronavirus pandemic, with revenues falling 23% to $14.7 billion and a loss of $710 million. Despite these losses, the company beat Wall Street expectations, largely driven by the strong performance of Disney Plus, which reached 73 million paid subscribers. Disney CEO Bob Chapek emphasized the direct-to-consumer business as the primary catalyst for future growth and announced the suspension of semi-annual cash dividends to prioritize streaming investments.

title: Disney Takes $6.9 Billion Hit Amid Park Closures In 2020
summary: The Walt Disney Co. reported a $6.9 billion hit in 2020 due to global park closures and reduced capacities caused by the pandemic. CEO Bob Chapek expressed disappointment with California Governor Gavin Newsom's "arbitrary standard" for reopening Disneyland, highlighting the company's implemented health and safety measures. The Parks department saw a 61 percent revenue decrease and a $1.1 billion operating loss for the quarter.

title: Aflac Offered Disney Millions of Dollars to Cast Its Mascot in a Movie
summary: Aflac offered Disney a multi-million dollar deal to feature its mascot, the Aflac Duck, in background shots of the 2005 film *Chicken Little*. However, director Mark Dindal rejected the offer, aiming to maintain the film's creative integrity despite numerous studio-mandated changes during production. The animation team faced extensive notes, including a late decision to make it a 3D movie and changing the lead character's gender.

title: Mountain Dew, AMC partner for ‘Walking Dead’ product placement
summary: Mountain Dew has partnered with AMC for in-show product placement in an upcoming episode of "The Walking Dead: World Beyond." This new placement builds on a prior marketing relationship between the brands from 2017 and was facilitated by AMC Networks’ Content Room and Omnicom Group's The Content Collective. The move reflects a growing trend in product integration as a way to reach audiences who often skip traditional TV commercials.

title: Celebrate 80 Years of "Fantasia" WIth New Urban Outfitters Collection
