summary: Urban Outfitters has launched a new collection to celebrate the 80th anniversary of Disney's "Fantasia." The collection features graphic tees and sweatshirts inspired by the iconic film and Mickey Mouse as the Sorcerer's Apprentice, with prices ranging from $24-$69. It is available in stores and online, offering street-style aesthetic items for Disney and Urban Outfitters fans.

title: The Walt Disney Company Reports Fourth Quarter and Full Year Earnings for Fiscal 2020
summary: The Walt Disney Company reported higher-than-expected revenue of $14 billion for its fourth quarter and fiscal year ended October 3, 2020, despite a net loss of $2.83 billion. The company's direct-to-consumer business, particularly Disney+, was a bright spot, surpassing 73 million paid subscribers. COVID-19 significantly impacted operating income, especially in the Parks, Experiences and Products segment, resulting in an estimated $7.4 billion adverse impact across all businesses for the full year.

title: Urban Outfitters, Disney Link for ‘Fantasia’-Inspired Collection
summary: Urban Outfitters has launched an exclusive men's collection inspired by Walt Disney's "Fantasia" to celebrate the film's 80th anniversary. The collection features graphic T-shirts and sweatshirts that combine Disney's classic artwork with Urban Outfitters' street-style aesthetic. Items are available in stores and online, with prices ranging from $34 for T-shirts to $69 for hoodies.

title: DoorDash boosts IPO size: What to know
summary: DoorDash has increased its IPO offering price to $90.00-$95.00 per share, up from an earlier range, aiming to raise an estimated $2.96 billion and value the company at around $30 billion. The San Francisco-based delivery service, which will list on the NYSE under DASH, has seen significant growth during the pandemic, although it continues to incur net losses. This IPO positions DoorDash to compete aggressively with rivals like UberEats and GrubHub, with plans for future expansion beyond food delivery.

title: Aflac Offered Disney Millions to Cast Duck Mascot in Movie
summary: During the production of Disney's "Chicken Little," Aflac reportedly offered the studio millions of dollars to feature its iconic duck mascot in the film, even in small cameo roles. Producer Randy Fullmer revealed this offer, which director Mark Dindal ultimately rejected, despite Disney Animation facing a challenging period at the time. The article raises the question of whether Aflac might pursue such a cross-promotional opportunity with Disney again in the future.

title: WebToon Launches WebToon Studios
summary: Digital comic publisher WebToon has launched WebToon Studios, a new multi-platform production division aimed at expanding its library and creators into various entertainment mediums including film, television, and interactive entertainment. This expansion includes new partnerships with Vertigo Entertainment, Bound Entertainment, and Rooster Teeth Studios, with more collaborations anticipated. The studio will leverage its existing pool of writers and artists to build franchises across all media platforms.

title: Taylor Swift’s Old Catalog Is Now Owned by an Investment Fund
summary: Shamrock Holdings has acquired the rights to Taylor Swift's old music catalog from Scooter Braun, a move that occurred without Swift's knowledge or involvement. Swift had previously been in a dispute with Braun over the ownership of her master recordings. In response to the sale, Swift reiterated her intention to re-record her earlier albums, hoping fans will support the new versions to redirect profits back to her.

title: Exclusive | Sinclair Broadcast Group to rename sports channels after Bally’s casinos
summary: Sinclair Broadcast Group and Bally's Corp. have partnered in a deal that will see Sinclair rename its 21 sports networks to Bally Sports. Bally's will pay Sinclair $85 million over 10 years for naming rights, gaining exclusive access to fans of 42 major teams, and Sinclair will receive a 15 percent stake in Bally's. The partnership aims to integrate online sports betting directly into game broadcasts, with Bally's also acquiring sports-betting software company Bet.Works.

title: Disney Parks Receives Industry Honors
summary: The Themed Entertainment Association (TEA) awarded Star Wars: Rise of the Resistance and Mickey & Minnie’s Runaway Railway with Thea Awards for Outstanding Achievement – Attraction. TEA also honored Walt Disney Imagineering President Bob Weis with the Buzz Price Thea Award. Additionally, Disney Parks' chief safety officer Greg Hale and former Imagineer Tony Baxter were inducted into the International Association of Amusement Parks and Attractions’ Hall of Fame.

title: SiriusXM is the New Destination for Original, Exclusive, and Popular Podcasts
summary: SiriusXM is launching a new podcast destination featuring original, exclusive, and popular podcasts from creators like Marvel, Kevin Hart, and FOX News, alongside content from Stitcher, NBC News, and NPR. Subscribers with streaming access can now enjoy a diverse array of audio content through the SiriusXM mobile app or online. This initiative follows SiriusXM's acquisitions of Simplecast and Stitcher, solidifying its position as a major player in podcast hosting, production, and distribution.

title: Bally's Goes All-In On Sports Betting With Bet.Works And Sinclair Deals
summary: Bally's Corporation is making a significant move into sports betting and online gambling by acquiring Bet.Works for $125 million. This acquisition will power the launch of Bally Bets and establish a new interactive division. Additionally, Bally's secured naming rights for over 20 regional sports networks through a separate agreement with Sinclair Broadcast Group, aiming for national brand recognition and an omni-channel customer experience.

title: Disney Parks Receives Industry Honors
summary: Disney Parks recently received several prestigious industry honors, including Thea Awards for Outstanding Achievement for "Star Wars: Rise of the Resistance" and "Mickey & Minnie’s Runaway Railway." Walt Disney Imagineering President Bob Weis was recognized with the Buzz Price Thea Award, and top safety officer Greg Hale and former Imagineer Tony Baxter were inducted into the IAAPA Hall of Fame. These accolades highlight Disney's ongoing innovation in technology and storytelling within its theme parks.

title: Williams-Sonoma Will Deliver Baby Yoda’s Macarons to Your Doorstep
summary: Williams-Sonoma is now selling "Nevarro Nummies," blue French macarons identical to those eaten by Baby Yoda (The Child) in The Mandalorian Season 2. These treats, inspired by a scene in the popular Disney+ series, are available for $49.99 and are described as hand-piped with a rich, creamy vanilla filling. They are shipped frozen or chilled and can be stored for up to one month unopened in the refrigerator, making them a festive holiday indulgence for Star Wars fans.

title: Walt Disney Television CFO & President Of Business Operations Ravi Ahuja To Exit
summary: Ravi Ahuja, President of business operations and CFO at Walt Disney Television, is stepping down from his role. This decision follows a major Disney restructure that significantly changed his responsibilities within the company. Ahuja will remain as a consultant during the transition period while a new head of operations and finance is identified, with Trisha Husson managing day-to-day operations immediately.

title: Omaha’s AMC Oakview Plaza 24 closes permanently
summary: AMC's Oakview Plaza 24 movie theater in Omaha has permanently closed its doors on November 8, after nearly 23 years of operation. The closure is a result of financial strains exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic, leading landlords to terminate leases with AMC. This specific theater is one of six nationwide affected by an agreement with landlord EPR Properties, though other AMC locations in the Omaha-Council Bluffs area remain open.

title: Global Over the Top Market - Featuring 8*8 Inc., Alphabet Inc., and Amazon.com Inc. Among Others | Technavio
summary: The global Over the Top (OTT) market is projected to grow by USD 88.85 billion during 2020-2024, at a CAGR of almost 14%. This growth is primarily driven by the increasing demand for cloud streaming services and the rising adoption of target advertisement-based streaming applications. Technavio's report provides a comprehensive analysis including market sizing, forecast, trends, growth drivers, challenges, and vendor analysis featuring key players like 8x8 Inc., Alphabet Inc., Amazon.com Inc., and Netflix Inc.

title: Nets star Deron Williams sells Tribeca penthouse for $16.4M after slashing ask
summary: Former NBA star Deron Williams has sold his Tribeca penthouse at 35 North Moore St. for $16.4 million, less than half its original asking price of $33.5 million from 2015. Williams had purchased the property in 2013 for $15.8 million. The 7,200-square-foot penthouse includes six bedrooms, a climate-controlled wine room, and 3,000 square feet of outdoor space.

title: Not the happiest place: Disney to lay off 32,000 workers in 2021
summary: Walt Disney Co. announced plans to lay off 32,000 workers, primarily in its theme parks, by the first half of 2021. This figure is an increase from the 28,000 layoffs previously announced in September, as the company continues to struggle with reduced customer numbers due to the coronavirus pandemic. Theme parks outside the US have reopened with strict measures, while others, like Disneyland Paris, have faced new closures.

title: Disney expands layoffs, bringing total to 32,000 workers as theme parks take biggest hit from pandemic
summary: The Walt Disney Co. is increasing its planned layoffs to a total of 32,000 employees, primarily impacting its Parks, Experiences and Products division, due to the ongoing impact of the coronavirus pandemic. The company estimates COVID-19 has caused approximately $7.4 billion in adverse effects on its full-year segment operating income, with the theme park sector alone losing $6.9 billion. In addition to park closures, Disney's merchandise licensing, studio entertainment, and advertising sales have also suffered, leading to delays in theatrical releases and content production.

title: Universal Studios’ long-awaited Super Nintendo World finally gets an opening date
summary: Universal Studios Japan announced that its $580 million Super Nintendo World attraction will open on February 4, after being delayed due to the pandemic. The park will feature life-sized replicas of Nintendo's popular games, including a Mario Kart ride in Bowser’s Castle, and allows visitors to collect virtual coins with special wristbands. The opening faces challenges as Japan grapples with a new COVID-19 outbreak and the theme-park industry struggles with falling revenue.

title: Walt Disney Company Cast Members Offered "Disney Streaming Bundle" As A Perk
summary: The Walt Disney Company is offering its Cast Members a choice between a year's subscription to the "Disney Streaming Bundle" (Disney+, ESPN+, and Hulu, valued at over $155) or a "Main Entrance Pass" to one of their theme parks as a yearly perk. This continues a long-standing tradition for Cast Members, allowing them to bring family and friends to the parks with some restrictions. Cast Members who chose the bundle last year will have their subscription extended until their 2021 perk is activated, and they will still receive complimentary park tickets and discounts.

title: Sanjay Sharma: Remixing the Mainstream From the Margins?
summary: In this interview, Sanjay Sharma, Founder and CEO of Marginal MediaWorks, discusses his journey from being a lawyer and screenwriter to a serial entrepreneur. He emphasizes how focusing on "fringe" cultures and underserved audiences has led to outsized value creation in the media landscape. Sharma covers his experiences building successful ventures like Machinima and All Def Digital, and how these inform his current work at Marginal MediaWorks, which focuses on genre storytelling from marginalized voices for a changing demographic.

title: Columbia Sportswear’s Mandalorian-inspired Star Wars outerwear collection releases today: How to buy the limi
summary: Columbia Sportswear has launched a limited-edition Star Wars outerwear collection inspired by "The Mandalorian" characters, Din Djarin and Grogu. The collection features technologically advanced jackets, fleece hoods, and accessories, incorporating intricate details and fan-favorite elements from the series. These items are available online and in select stores, and are designed for warmth and protection rather than just costumes.

title: Warner Bros. to release movies on HBO Max for the next year
summary: Warner Bros. announced it will release its entire 2021 film slate simultaneously in U.S. theaters and on HBO Max, a move sparked by the COVID-19 pandemic. This bold strategy, which includes major potential blockbusters like "Dune" and "Matrix 4," is a temporary measure to address the challenging theatrical market and boost HBO Max subscriptions. The decision has drawn sharp criticism from cinema chains, who view it as a sacrifice of profitability for the streaming service.

title: Online Travel Booking Platform Market to Grow by Almost $ 205 Billion Despite Pandemic | Technavio
summary: Technavio projects that the global online travel booking platform market will grow by USD 204.81 billion during 2020-2024, despite the COVID-19 pandemic, progressing at a CAGR of almost 5%. The "packages" segment led the market in 2019, and the market is driven by increasing internet and smartphone penetration. Key players include Airbnb Inc., Booking Holdings Inc., Expedia Group Inc., and Trip.com Group Ltd.

title: Radio Disney to shut down in first quarter of 2021 amid Walt. Disney Co.'s restructuring
summary: Radio Disney and Radio Disney Country are scheduled to cease operations in the first quarter of 2021, affecting 36 employees. This decision is part of Walt Disney Co.'s restructuring to focus on content for Disney+ and Disney Channels, and comes amid broader layoffs within the company, particularly in its Parks, Experiences and Products segment, due to the COVID-19 pandemic's impact. The closures reflect an evolving media environment and ongoing public health crisis affecting in-person music events.

title: Peter Rice | Next TV | Broadcasting+Cable
summary: This article profiles Peter Rice, Chairman of Disney General Entertainment Content, highlighting his role in overseeing Disney's vast television programming output and its pivot towards streaming. It discusses the recent reorganization at Disney that separates content creation from distribution and monetization, allowing Rice's team to focus solely on developing and producing content for various platforms. The piece emphasizes that this new structure leverages Rice's strengths in storytelling and creative leadership to drive Disney's streaming ambitions.

title: Mando Mondays Roundup Week 7 – New “The Mandalorian” Merchandise from Hasbro and More
summary: This article provides a roundup of new "The Mandalorian" merchandise released during Mando Mondays Week 7, featuring products from popular Star Wars licensees like Hasbro, Funko, and Her Universe. Highlights include a NERF Star Wars The Mandalorian Amban Phase-Pulse Blaster, several Star Wars Mission Fleet figure and vehicle packs, new Funko Pop! Bobbleheads of Moff Gideon and Mando, and a Her Universe long-sleeve tee.

title: Kareem Daniel
summary: Kareem Daniel, chairman of Media and Entertainment Distribution at The Walt Disney Co., started as an intern and rose to become the first Black person to head a division, reporting directly to CEO Bob Chapek. He previously played a key role in the acquisitions of Marvel Studios and Lucasfilm and oversaw Consumer Products, Games, and Publishing. In his new role, Daniel manages P&L, distribution, operations, sales, advertising, and data worldwide, including the operations of Disney's crucial streaming services.

title: Hasbro Crowdfunders React: Company Took $10 Mil. to Create Razor Crest Toy
summary: Hasbro faced backlash from Star Wars fans who crowdfunded nearly $10 million for a Razor Crest toy, only for the ship to be destroyed in a recent episode of The Mandalorian. Many backers expressed disappointment, believing Hasbro may have known the ship's fate while collecting funds. Despite the controversy, the toy is now considered a rare collector's item.

title: Variety’s Dealmakers Impact Report 2020: Top Negotiators That Have Kept Hollywood Humming
summary: This report highlights the top lawyers, financiers, executives, and entrepreneurs who have driven major deals in Hollywood throughout 2020, navigating the challenges of a pandemic and economic disruption. It showcases key transactions, client representations, and insights from these dealmakers on the evolving media landscape, including the acceleration of streaming and changes in production and financing. The article details how these individuals and firms adapted their strategies to continue shaping the entertainment industry despite unprecedented circumstances.

title: Nature Conservancy Hooked Corporate America on an Empty Climate Solution
summary: The Nature Conservancy, the world's largest environmental group, is accused of selling "meaningless" carbon offsets to major corporations like JPMorgan, Disney, and BlackRock. These offsets are based on preserving forestland that was never actually threatened with deforestation. Critics argue that this practice allows companies to claim significant emissions reductions without making genuine changes to their operations, undermining efforts to combat climate change.

title: Will K-Dramas Come to Disney+? Disney May Expand to Korea & Taiwan!
summary: Disney+ is reportedly in negotiations to expand its streaming service to South Korea and Taiwan, following an instant success since its launch. This expansion could lead to the inclusion of family-friendly K-Drama content for these regions, similar to how Disney partnered with Hotstar in India to bring Bollywood movies to that audience. The move to Taiwan is seen as a strategic step towards potentially entering the Chinese market, after a previous venture with Alibaba in China was short-lived.

title: Disney Sets Comcast Xfinity Distribution Deal For Disney+ And ESPN+, New Bundle With Ad-Free Hulu
summary: Disney has finalized a distribution agreement with Comcast to integrate Disney+ and ESPN+ into Comcast's Xfinity X1 and Flex broadband services. Additionally, Disney announced a new bundle option in 2021 that will include the ad-free version of Hulu for an additional $6 per month, prompted by customer feedback. This expansion builds on Disney+'s rapid growth, which had already reached 86.8 million global subscribers by December 2, 2020.

title: Disney Lays Out Multi-Billion Dollar Plan to Dominate the Streaming Wars
summary: The Walt Disney Company announced a multi-billion dollar plan to significantly expand its streaming services, including Disney Plus, Hulu, and ESPN Plus, with an estimated $8 billion to $9 billion allocated for Disney Plus content alone in fiscal 2024. The company projected subscriber growth for Disney Plus to 230 million to 260 million by the end of fiscal 2024, emphasizing a focus on quality content with plans for over 100 new titles annually across its brands. Disney also addressed its theatrical release strategy, indicating that while tentpole films will largely maintain cinema debuts, several titles will go directly to Disney Plus or offer "premium access" simultaneously with theatrical release.

title: Every Disney+ Announcement and More From the Disney Investor Day 2020
summary: The Disney Investor Day 2020 unveiled a massive slate of new content for Disney+, Hulu, and ESPN+, significantly expanding the direct-to-consumer services. Key announcements included plans for approximately 10 Star Wars and 10 Marvel series, alongside 15 Disney live-action, Disney Animation, and Pixar series and features. Upcoming content includes new series for established franchises like Beauty and the Beast and Percy Jackson, Marvel series like Secret Invasion and Ironheart, Pixar films such as Turning Red and Lightyear, and new international branding with "Star."

title: Your Guide to 2020 Holiday Viewing from Across The Walt Disney Company
summary: This article provides a comprehensive guide to holiday viewing across The Walt Disney Company's various platforms for 2020. It lists beloved classics and new favorites available on Disney+, Hulu, Disney Channel, Disney Junior, Disney XD, ABC, FX, FXX, and ESPN. The guide includes original shows, holiday episodes, and movies to help families plan their seasonal screenings.

title: Imax CEO Rich Gelfond On Warner-HBO Max Theatrical Plan: “It’s a Real Issue”
summary: Imax CEO Rich Gelfond views Warner Bros.' plan to release its 2021 film slate day-and-date on HBO Max and in theaters as a "real issue" that Hollywood will not quickly overcome. He believes that WarnerMedia misunderstands how the theatrical business and creative community operate, emphasizing that filmmakers envision their movies for the big screen. Gelfond anticipates that Warner will likely reverse its decision later in the year, especially given the expected rebound of theatrical attendance post-pandemic, as seen in other countries.

title: Stocks making the biggest moves midday: Tesla, Nio, Airbnb, Disney & more
summary: This article details the midday stock movements of several notable companies on December 11, 2020. Key movements include Snowflake and Nio sliding after downgrades and a new share offering, respectively, while Disney soared due to projections for its streaming service. Other companies like Airbnb, Tesla, Qualcomm, UPS, Vail Resorts, Lululemon, and American Airlines also experienced significant shifts, driven by analyst ratings, earnings reports, or industry news.

title: Movie Theaters Need New Films and Sanguine Customers. What Will Next Year Bring?
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic severely impacted movie theaters in 2020, with foot traffic at only 25% of pre-COVID levels and only 24% of adults comfortable attending. Studios like Warner Bros. and Disney adapted by releasing films concurrently in theaters and on streaming platforms, leading to concerns about the future of traditional distribution. While individual theater chains secured lifelines, the industry faces an uncertain 2021, dependent on new film releases and increased consumer comfort, with ongoing discussions about distribution models.

title: Disney’s stock rises after monumental Investor Day announcements
summary: The Walt Disney Company's stock increased significantly after its Investor Day event, where it announced major expansion plans for Disney+. The company plans to add over 50 original titles, including numerous Marvel and Star Wars series, to Disney+ in the coming years and reported substantial subscriber growth across its streaming services. Disney is also continuing its Premier Access strategy for new film releases, underscoring its shift to focus on streaming content.

title: Greening Production on Disney+ Film, "Safety"
summary: The Disney+ film "Safety" implemented significant sustainability efforts during its production, including hiring an Environmental Steward, partnering with Clemson University for waste management, and using solar-powered trailers to reduce diesel fuel reliance. The production successfully diverted waste from landfills, donated excess food and furniture, and avoided the use of 22,000 single-use plastic bottles, setting new environmental benchmarks for Walt Disney Studios.

title: Microsoft and Warner Bros. Pictures Assemble All-Star Team in LeBron James, Bugs Bunny and Xbox to Celebrate Gaming and Coding Education Inspired By The Upcoming Animated, Live-Action Adventure 'Space Jam: A New Legacy'
summary: Microsoft and Warner Bros. are launching a partnership with LeBron James, Bugs Bunny, and Xbox to promote coding education, inspired by the upcoming movie 'Space Jam: A New Legacy'. This initiative includes a fan contest to design an Xbox arcade-style video game, free coding workshops, and Microsoft Learn lessons focusing on game design and real-time decision-making using player stats. These efforts align with Microsoft's broader goal to help 25 million people acquire new digital skills.

title: Texas Bowl lands new sponsor
summary: The Texas Bowl announced Mercari, Inc., the U.S. subsidiary of a Japanese e-commerce company, as its new title sponsor for the New Year's Eve game at NRG Stadium. This marks the fourth title sponsor in the bowl game's 15-year history. Attendance for the game between Big 12 and Southeastern Conference schools will be limited to 13,300 due to COVID-19 restrictions, with no fan-related events planned.

title: Greening Production on Disney+ Film, "Safety"
summary: The production of the Disney+ film "Safety" focused heavily on sustainability, employing an Environmental Steward and partnering with Clemson University for waste management and composting. Key initiatives included using solar-powered cast trailers, implementing a no-idling policy, and donating leftover food and furniture. These efforts significantly reduced the film's environmental impact both on set and in various locations.

title: COVID-19 canceled your cruise. Here’s how you can use that money for a future vacation
summary: Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, many cruise lines have canceled trips, leaving passengers with credits for future travel. Companies like Carnival Corp., Royal Caribbean Group, Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings, and Disney Cruise Line are working to meet the CDC's conditional sail order requirements. This article provides guidance on how affected customers can utilize their money for future vacation plans.

title: Samba TV Grows Revenue Over $100 Million Globally, Adds TiVo Data Deal 12/16/2020
summary: Samba TV, a TV data measurement company, announced it has exceeded $100 million in global revenue for 2020. The company has secured several major worldwide TV data deals this year, including agreements with Walt Disney, Comscore, and most recently, TiVo. This partnership with TiVo is expected to enhance Samba TV's targeting technology by incorporating time-shifted data from multichannel video programming distributors.

title: Walt Disney Company Announces Annual Shareholder Meeting
summary: The Walt Disney Company announced its annual shareholder meeting will be held virtually on March 9th, 2021. The meeting is expected to provide updates on Disney+ subscriber counts, the international rollout of Star, and financial details for Disney+, Hulu, and other segments of the company, with a focus on the impact of the Coronavirus on Disney's earnings.

title: Sony’s Crunchyroll purchase puts anime at the core of its streaming play
summary: Sony acquired Crunchyroll for $1.2 billion, positioning anime at the center of its direct-to-consumer streaming strategy to compete with giants like Netflix and Disney. This move follows Sony's aggressive anime buying spree and aims to capitalize on the rapidly growing global demand for animation, significantly boosted by the COVID-19 pandemic. The deal signals Sony's intent to become a major player in the streaming wars, leveraging the massive popularity of anime, despite prior Japanese corporate hesitations in international markets.

title: Walt Disney Co: A Lesson On Overvaluation
summary: This article argues that Walt Disney Co (NYSE: DIS) is dangerously overvalued, despite being a great company with strong expected earnings recovery. The author, known as "Mr. Valuation," emphasizes the importance of attractive valuation in investing and warns against the potential losses of time and money associated with overvalued stocks. The piece recommends investors avoid obvious valuation mistakes even for beloved companies.

title: Alan Bergman Named Chairman, Disney Studios Content; Alan Horn To Continue As Chief Creative Officer
summary: Alan Bergman has been appointed Chairman, Disney Studios Content, and Alan Horn will remain the Chief Creative Officer, effective January 1, 2021. This announcement was made by Disney CEO Bob Chapek, emphasizing continuity in leadership for the studios. Bergman will oversee creative, production, marketing, and operations for all Disney Studios, while Horn will focus on the creative aspects of the content pipeline.

title: The Walt Disney Company ‘Needs To Be Saved From Itself,’ Says Abigail Disney
summary: Abigail Disney, granddaughter of co-founder Roy O. Disney, criticizes The Walt Disney Company's corporate behavior and widening pay gap between executives and employees. She argues that the company's internal culture, particularly under Bob Iger, is self-destructive and unsustainable despite its financial success. Disney also shares her views on the Fox acquisition, Bob Chapek's leadership, and the need for meaningful regulation.

title: The Walt Disney Company Sets New 2030 Environmental Goals
summary: The Walt Disney Company has announced ambitious new environmental goals for 2030, focusing on five key areas: greenhouse gas emissions, water, waste, materials, and sustainable design. CEO Bob Chapek emphasized the company's commitment to building on its environmental legacy and making a lasting positive impact. These goals include achieving net-zero greenhouse gas emissions, sourcing 100% zero-carbon electricity, implementing sustainable design for new construction, and reducing its plastics footprint.

title: Walt Disney Company releases 2030 environmental goals
summary: The Walt Disney Company has publicly released its comprehensive environmental goals for the year 2030, targeting five key areas: greenhouse gas emissions, water usage, waste reduction, sustainable materials, and building design. The company aims for net-zero greenhouse gas emissions, 100% zero-carbon electricity, and significant reductions in plastic and landfill waste across its global operations. These ambitious targets build upon Disney's historical commitment to environmental stewardship, with current initiatives already in place at its theme parks and cruise lines.

title: Hasbro’s Darksaber Deemed ‘Most Dangerous’ Toy of the Year
summary: Hasbro's Darksaber toy has been labeled one of the "most dangerous" toys of 2020 by the consumer watchdog World Against Toys Causing Harm (W.A.T.C.H.), despite being made of plastic. The group argues that the toy, inspired by the Mandalorian Darksaber, encourages aggressive play and carries a risk of facial and other impact injuries due to its rigid plastic construction. The article notes the toy has no official safety recalls and is rated for children aged 5 and up.

title: Buyer or Seller? How Each Film Studio Tackled Dealmaking Amid the Pandemic
summary: This article examines how various film studios adapted their dealmaking strategies during the 2020 pandemic, which caused significant disruptions like production halts, theatrical window changes, and a shift towards streaming. It details key moves made by major studios such as Amazon, Apple, Disney, Lionsgate, MGM, Netflix, Paramount, Sony, Universal, and Warner Bros., including acquisitions, production adjustments, and executive changes. The report highlights each studio's unique approach to navigating the unprecedented challenges and opportunities presented by the altered entertainment landscape.

title: Don't make the same mistake I did by visiting Disney World during the pandemic. It's just not worth it.
summary: The author recounts his family's November 2020 trip to Disney World during the pandemic, expressing regret despite personal precautions. He found the park unexpectedly crowded and felt the "magic" was lost due to safety measures like suspended character interactions, plexiglass dividers on rides, and restaurant closures, leading to long wait times. While acknowledging some positive aspects like resort services and mask enforcement, he concluded the experience wasn't worth the cost and effort, wishing they had waited for a safer and more enjoyable time.

title: Univision plans ad-supported streaming service launch in 2021: report
summary: Univision is reportedly planning to launch a new ad-supported streaming service in the first half of 2021, filling it with library content from Grupo Televisa SAB. The move is a high priority for CEO Wade Davis, who recently led an investment group to acquire a majority stake in Univision. The service will reportedly hold back new episodes of current TV shows to avoid issues with pay TV partners.

title: Delta Air Lines, Airbnb, Peloton: Stocks That Defined the Week
summary: This article highlights major companies whose stocks were influenced by recent news events. Delta Air Lines announced a $200 monthly surcharge for unvaccinated employees, while Pfizer's Covid-19 vaccine received full FDA approval, boosting its shares. Walmart introduced "Walmart GoLocal," expanding its Spark Driver delivery platform for other businesses.

title: Walt Disney Company Announce Next Quarterly Financial Results Webcast
summary: The Walt Disney Company announced its next quarterly financial results meeting for the fiscal first quarter of 2021 will be held on Thursday, February 11th, 2021, at 4:30 p.m. ET / 1:30 p.m. PT. The event will be broadcast as a live audio webcast and will include updates on Disney+ subscribers and the launch of Star on Disney+. Disney often makes a significant announcement before releasing results to generate shareholder interest.

title: Disney in Talks to Move Some Operations From CA to FL
summary: The Walt Disney Company is reportedly considering moving some operations from California to Florida, according to the Orlando Business Journal. This consideration comes amidst California's strict restrictions on reopening Disneyland Resort, while Walt Disney World in Florida has been operational since July 2020. The potential move is seen as a reflection of Disney's increasingly difficult relationship with California and an opportunity for Orlando to attract a major corporate relocation.

title: The Walt Disney Company
summary: This page from Newsweek compiles various news articles related to The Walt Disney Company. It covers topics ranging from leadership changes, theme park updates, streaming content, financial performance, and political disputes primarily with Florida Governor Ron DeSantis, showcasing a wide array of company-related news.

title: The Walt Disney Company Reportedly Considering Moving Some Divisions to Lake Nona, Florida
summary: The Walt Disney Company is reportedly considering moving several of its divisions from California to Lake Nona, Florida, a master-planned community in southeastern Orlando. This potential relocation is driven by Florida's more tax-friendly and business-supportive environment, especially in contrast to California's strict COVID-19 restrictions that have impacted Disney's operations. While not a complete relocation of all operations, it is speculated that theme park support and operational departments would be among those considered for the move.

title: Disney Could Be Considering Moving Some Corporate Divisions to Florida
summary: The Walt Disney Company is reportedly considering relocating some of its corporate divisions from California to Lake Nona, Florida, a move that would shift headquarters operations closer to their Central Florida theme parks. This potential relocation aligns with a trend of companies moving to more business- and tax-friendly Southeastern states, with Florida's CFO Jimmy Patronis welcoming such a move. Industry analysts suggest that if a move occurs, it would likely involve the theme parks division due to existing operations in Central Florida and potential frustrations with California's government policies.

title: Walt Disney Commits to Net-Zero Emissions and Sustainability
summary: The Walt Disney Company has announced ambitious environmental goals for 2030, building on its nearly century-long commitment to eco-friendly initiatives. These goals include achieving net-zero greenhouse gas emissions, purchasing 100% zero-carbon electricity, and implementing sustainable practices across five key areas: greenhouse gas emissions, water, waste, materials, and sustainable design. CEO Bob Chapek emphasized the company's strong legacy in environmental protection and its excitement to build upon these efforts to make a lasting positive impact.

title: Walt Disney Co., Motion Picture Association To Halt Contributions
summary: The Walt Disney Co. and the Motion Picture Association announced they would halt political contributions to lawmakers who voted to reject the certification of electoral votes for Joe Biden. This decision follows the January 6th Capitol insurrection. Other major companies like Comcast and AT&T have made similar announcements.

title: Disney won’t donate to Congress members who challenged Joe Biden’s win
summary: The Walt Disney Company announced it will cease political contributions in 2021 to members of Congress who voted against certifying Joe Biden's electoral college win. This decision is significant for Florida, where Disney has a major presence, and particularly impacts Senator Rick Scott, who objected to electors and recently took over as chairman of the National Republican Senatorial Campaign. The move could impede Scott's fundraising efforts, though Disney's statement only covers 2021, leaving future donations open.

title: It's official: Disney's long-standing exclusivity deal on 'Star Wars' games just ended
summary: Disney has ended its exclusive deal with Electronic Arts for "Star Wars" games, allowing other publishers like Ubisoft to develop new titles. This change is part of a renewed push into video games by Disney's Lucasfilm group, which also announced an "Indiana Jones" game by Bethesda. Despite opening up to new partners, Disney states it will continue to work with EA as a strategic partner.

title: Disney Analyst Boosts The Walt Disney Company Stock Price Target to $200 Based on Theme Park Projections
summary: Guggenheim Securities analyst Michael Morris has increased his stock price target for The Walt Disney Company to $200, up $15. This projection accounts for a slower revenue recovery in theme parks for fiscal years 2021-2023 but anticipates stronger long-term economic potential from 2024 onwards. Morris's valuation highlights Disney+ at $132 per share, linear media at $28 per share, and theme parks and consumer products at $80 per share, with an expected gradual increase in park attendance through fiscal year 2022.

title: Disneyland Resort to end Annual Passport program amid uncertainty of the pandemic
summary: Disneyland and California Adventure are ending their Annual Passport program due to the ongoing uncertainty of the pandemic and expected restrictions on park reopenings. The resort plans to offer refunds for eligible passports and is developing new membership options that aim to provide more choice and flexibility for guests. The parks have been closed since March 2020, and the future reopening date remains unclear.

title: Disney Downsize
summary: Walt Disney Co. is transforming into a streaming-centric business, which prompted questions on its impact on Burbank's commercial real estate, where Disney occupies massive office spaces. Despite a challenging 2020 due to the pandemic, Disney's successful Disney Plus streaming service is expected to keep its real estate footprint in Burbank stable, although rumors of relocating some operations to Florida persist. The article also highlights the growing competition in the streaming market and the potential for Disney to seek more business-friendly states for its operations.

title: Disney Leaders Bob Iger, Bob Chapek Forgo Bonuses, but Still Rake in Millions
summary: Top Disney executives Bob Iger and Bob Chapek saw their 2020 pay packages significantly reduced due to their decision to forgo bonuses amid the COVID-19 pandemic. Although their compensation decreased, they still earned millions, while Disney laid off 32,000 employees, primarily in its parks division. Other senior leaders also went without bonuses, with their total compensation including salary and stock options.

title: Netflix shares rise on strong subscriber growth, considers share buybacks
summary: Netflix (NFLX) reported strong Q4 2020 earnings, beating revenue and subscriber expectations, leading to a stock rise. The company announced it is nearing free cash flow positive status and will consider returning cash to shareholders through buybacks, no longer needing external financing for daily operations. This marks a significant shift as Netflix also surpassed 200 million paid subscribers and detailed its content successes despite increased streaming competition.

title: Netflix will consider buybacks as it returns to positive cash flow after 2021
summary: Netflix announced it expects to be cash-flow positive after 2021 and will no longer require external financing, ending a decade of significant debt. The company also stated it would consider share buybacks, a practice not seen since 2011. This shift validates Netflix's long-term content spending strategy and comes as its market capitalization has grown significantly.

title: Two new 401(k) lawsuits and one big settlement
summary: Two new 401(k) lawsuits have been filed against VALIC and Associated Banc-Corp, alleging ERISA violations and breaches of fiduciary duty, respectively. Meanwhile, a class-action lawsuit against DST Systems, Ruane Cunniff & Goldfarb, and Robert Goldfarb regarding losses in Valeant Pharmaceuticals stock has been settled for $79 million. These cases highlight ongoing scrutiny of fees, investment choices, and fiduciary responsibilities within retirement plans.

title: Naver to acquire web novel platform Wattpad for $593 mn
summary: South Korean internet giant Naver Corp. is set to acquire Wattpad, the world's largest web novel platform, for $593 million. This acquisition aims to bolster Naver's storytelling content and secure a leading position in the global content market, combining Wattpad's 90 million users with Naver Webtoon's 160 million monthly active users. Naver plans to apply its successful webtoon business model to Wattpad, including adapting popular web novels into webtoons, and this move is also seen as a strategic play for the global streaming market by providing a rich source of adaptable content.

title: Double oh-no: James Bond film No Time to Die postponed again
summary: The global release of the James Bond movie "No Time to Die" has been postponed again, moving from April to October 8, 2021. This marks another significant setback for the struggling movie theatre industry, which has been severely impacted by the coronavirus pandemic. The film, which cost an estimated $200 million and is Daniel Craig's last as James Bond, was originally slated for April 2020.

title: Fox Corporation appoints Varun Narang as Chief Product Officer
summary: Fox Corporation has appointed Varun Narang as its new Chief Product Officer. In this role, Narang will oversee the company's FOX-branded streaming products and platforms, working to drive digital priorities and accelerate the growth of current and future digital streaming offerings. He previously served as Chief Product Officer of Disney+Hotstar and held senior positions at Hulu, Amazon, and Xerox.

title: Levi’s first home collection deepens Target relationship
summary: Levi Strauss & Co. is expanding its partnership with Target by launching its unique, denim-inspired home collection. The limited-time 100-item collection, featuring tableware, quilts, and pillows, will be available online and in most Target stores starting February 28. This collaboration reflects Levi's strategy to diversify beyond department stores and Target's focus on strategic brand partnerships to drive sales and differentiate itself from competitors.

title: Toy Store Chain Selects Bridgeline's Celebros Search to Power Their New Magento eCommerce Store
summary: Bridgeline Digital, Inc. announced that the largest toy store chain in Indonesia has chosen its Celebros Conversion Engine to power their new Magento 2 eCommerce site. The toy retailer aims to enhance customer experience and generate new revenue opportunities by leveraging Celebros's AI technology, which offers advanced search, conversion optimization, and intelligent machine learning for its extensive catalog of global brands. Bridgeline's CEO, Ari Kahn, expressed confidence that the Celebros software will boost revenue and provide a high-quality shopping experience for the toy store's customers.

title: Hulu, Peacock to Share Streaming Rights to ‘Modern Family’
summary: Hulu and Peacock have agreed to share streaming rights for the popular sitcom "Modern Family," a rare move given the industry's trend for exclusive content. All 11 seasons will be available on both platforms starting February 3rd. This partnership highlights the intense competition among streaming services for established comedies.

title: Fox Sports Ohio, SportsTime Ohio get new names: Bally Sports Ohio and Bally Sports Great Lakes
summary: Fox Sports Ohio and SportsTime Ohio will be rebranded as Bally Sports Ohio and Bally Sports Great Lakes, respectively. This change is due to a 10-year, $85 million naming rights deal between Sinclair, the owner of the regional sports networks, and casino operator Bally’s. The rebrand signifies Sinclair's intention to "gamify" the viewing experience of live sports, introducing more personalized and interactive programming, with future plans for in-game betting and a standalone streaming service.

title: Fox Sports Ohio Changing To Bally Sports Ohio
summary: Sinclair Broadcast Group is rebranding its Fox Sports regional networks, including Fox Sports Ohio, as Bally Sports. This change follows Sinclair's acquisition of the networks from Disney in 2019 and a strategic partnership with Bally's Corporation, which aims to integrate sports betting and gaming content with live game coverage. Fox Sports Ohio will become Bally Sports Ohio, continuing to broadcast games for teams like the Cincinnati Reds and Columbus Blue Jackets, among others.

title: Disney Company To Cut Ties With Its Founder, Walt Disney?
summary: The article discusses the idea, proposed by a blogger, that the Walt Disney Company should distance itself from its founder, Walt Disney, to address past racist leanings and succeed in markets like China. The author refutes this, arguing that Disney's recent changes to rides and content warnings are attempts to modernize and atone for past mistakes, not an indication of abandoning its founder. The article concludes that distancing from Walt Disney would be financially detrimental and that his name is integral to the brand.

title: Ryan Coogler’s Proximity Media Sets Exclusive Television Deal with The Walt Disney Company
summary: The Walt Disney Company has signed a five-year exclusive television deal with Ryan Coogler’s Proximity Media. As part of this deal, Proximity Media will develop new television series for Disney+, including one based in the Kingdom of Wakanda, and will also develop content for other Disney divisions. This builds on Coogler's successful collaboration with Disney on Marvel Studios' "Black Panther."

title: ‘Black Panther’ Helmer Ryan Coogler Stakes His Proximity Media Banner To 5-Year Exclusive Disney Television Deal; Wakanda Series In Works For Disney+
summary: Ryan Coogler, director of "Black Panther," has signed a five-year exclusive television deal with The Walt Disney Company through his production company, Proximity Media. As part of this agreement, Coogler will develop new TV series for Disney, including a drama set in the Kingdom of Wakanda for Disney+. This deal strengthens Coogler's relationship with Disney and extends Proximity Media's reach to develop content for various Disney divisions.

title: The Walt Disney Company Ranks 4th on Fortune’s 2021 List of “World’s Most Admired Companies”
summary: The Walt Disney Company has been ranked 4th on Fortune’s 2021 list of “World’s Most Admired Companies,” marking its third consecutive year in the top five and its 18th consecutive year leading the entertainment industry. Despite a challenging 2020 due to the pandemic, Disney received high marks for product quality, global competitiveness, people management, social responsibility, and long-term investment value. The company hopes for a more positive 2021 with vaccine distribution, park reopenings, and new content releases.

title: Apple (AAPL), Microsoft (MSFT), Disney (DIS) Are Top Admired Companies
summary: Apple, Microsoft, and Disney have been recognized as the top admired companies in Fortune Magazine's 2021 list, securing the first, third, and fourth spots respectively. This ranking, compiled in partnership with Korn Ferry, surveyed executives, directors, and analysts on various criteria. While direct financial impact is minimal, such accolades are valuable as recruiting tools to attract top talent.

title: Bally Sports: A guide to the changes and gambling coming to regional sports TV - The Athletic
summary: The article details the rebranding of Fox Sports regional channels to Bally Sports following Sinclair's acquisition and partnership with Bally's. This change integrates sports betting content and technology into live game broadcasts and a new streaming app, reflecting a broader trend towards merging sports media with legal gambling. The piece also discusses the financial aspects of the deal, Sinclair's strategy to boost viewership and revenue through sports wagering, and the acquisition history of Bally's.

title: Netflix raises prices for Japanese customers
summary: Netflix has increased its monthly subscription prices in Japan for its standard and basic plans. This move comes as the streaming giant invests heavily in original content to compete with a growing number of rivals. The price of the premium plan in Japan remains unchanged, while earlier price hikes were also implemented in the United States.

title: Jenefer Brown
summary: Jenefer Brown is the Executive Vice President and Head of Global Live, Interactive & Location Based Entertainment at Lionsgate. She oversees the development of themed entertainment experiences based on Lionsgate's intellectual properties, such as The Hunger Games, The Walking Dead, and SAW. Brown aims to expand the Lionsgate Entertainment World format globally, focusing on adult-led licensed properties.

title: Tom Gayner Top 10 Holdings (Q4 2020)
summary: This article details the top 10 holdings of superinvestor Tom Gayner's portfolio as of Q4 2020, based on his 13F-HR filing. The total market value of his portfolio was over $6.7 billion, with his top 10 holdings accounting for 42.79% of the total. The article also lists his top buys and sells during that period, including significant holdings in Berkshire Hathaway, Brookfield Asset Management, and The Walt Disney Co.

title: Exclusive: For Streaming Value, Amazon Prime Video Offers Best Bang for Consumers’ Buck, Report Says
summary: A new Reelgood report, shared exclusively with Morning Consult, indicates that Amazon Prime Video offers the best value for money among streaming services, providing the most movies and TV shows per dollar. While Prime Video excels in quantity per dollar, Netflix leads in original series content, and Disney+ boasts the highest percentage of exclusive content. The report helps consumers navigate the crowded streaming landscape based on budget and content preferences.

title: Disney World extends hours for first week of March
summary: Disney World has announced extended operating hours for all four of its theme parks during the first week of March. This decision comes nearly a year after the park's temporary closure due to the coronavirus pandemic, though parks will still operate under reduced hours compared to pre-pandemic schedules. Enhanced safety measures, including limited capacity, mask policies, and social distancing, remain in effect.

title: Disney Smashes Expectations, Company Poised to "Thrive"
summary: The Walt Disney Company exceeded financial expectations in its first fiscal quarter of 2021, largely due to the success of its streaming service, Disney+. Analysts believe Disney is well-positioned for recovery in a post-pandemic world, with significant growth planned for streaming content and rising demand for its theme parks despite ongoing closures and restrictions.

title: As Chinese film goers pivot to local content, Hollywood loses out
summary: China's film market is becoming increasingly lucrative, with box office takings expected to return to near pre-pandemic highs in 2021. However, Hollywood studios are facing challenges as Chinese audiences show a growing preference for local productions and increased sensitivity towards portrayals of China in Western films. The expiration of a bilateral agreement that mandated a minimum number of American movie imports further complicates market access for Hollywood.

title: The (Not So?) Wonderful World of Disney : It's Been a Minute
summary: Abigail Disney, granddaughter of Disney co-founder Roy O. Disney, discusses her criticism of The Walt Disney Company, focusing on corporate greed, executive compensation, and the disparity between executive pay and low-wage worker conditions. She advocates for Disney to prioritize its employees and community by adopting practices similar to a "B Corp" certification, emphasizing stakeholder primacy over shareholder primacy. Disney also reflects on the company's historical issues, including racial insensitivity in earlier works, and cautions against romanticizing the past.

title: Former Disney Accountant is Now Suing the Walt Disney Company in Federal Court After Filing a Series of SEC Complaints
summary: A former Walt Disney Company senior financial analyst, Sandra Kuba, is suing Disney in federal court. Kuba claims she was fired after raising concerns about the company's accounting practices and previously filed complaints with the SEC and a whistleblower-retaliation complaint. Disney denies the allegations, stating Kuba was terminated for workplace complaints lacking reasonable basis and calls the current lawsuit "meritless."

title: Cruise lines, mayor say shore power coming to PortMiami ‘as expeditiously as possible’
summary: Miami-Dade Mayor Daniella Levine Cava, six cruise companies, and Florida Power & Light have signed a letter of intent to bring shore power to PortMiami, allowing cruise ships to plug into the local electrical grid while docked and reduce emissions. This initiative follows a Miami Herald report on cruise ship pollution, with a task force formed to address logistics and funding, aiming for at least one hookup within a year or two. While some residents express skepticism about the lack of a firm timeline, officials state new terminals will be constructed with shore power in mind or retrofitted, promising significant environmental benefits.

title: Jessica Alba Signs With UTA
summary: Actress, author, and entrepreneur Jessica Alba has signed with UTA in all areas. Alba's extensive career includes roles in "Fantastic Four" and "Sin City" films, and she is set to host a docuseries for Disney+ and star in a Netflix action thriller. She also founded The Honest Company in 2011, focusing on baby and beauty products.

title: Walt Disney World announces 'Beacons of Magic' park transformation to celebrate 50th anniversary
summary: Walt Disney World is preparing for its 50th anniversary, which begins on October 1, 2021, marking five decades since its opening day. The resort will celebrate with an 18-month transformation, starting with Cinderella Castle and extending to other park icons like the Tower of Terror, Tree of Life, and Spaceship Earth, which will all receive special embellishments and sparkle. Mickey and Minnie Mouse also revealed special anniversary costumes to kick off the celebration.

title: If COVID rules allow, Six Flags Magic Mountain aims to open in spring
summary: Six Flags Magic Mountain plans to reopen its parks in the spring of 2021, contingent on government-issued coronavirus rules. The company, which operates 26 parks, aims to open all its locations for the 2021 season and is actively hiring staff and collaborating with officials to set reopening dates in various regions. Reopening in California and Los Angeles County specifically depends on significant easing of COVID-19 restrictions, requiring the county to reach the least restrictive “yellow” tier of the state's reopening guidelines.

title: Walt Disney Co. Taps Susan Fox For Top Government Relations Post
summary: Susan Fox has been appointed as the senior vice president of government relations for The Walt Disney Co., succeeding Richard Bates who passed away in December. Fox, with 20 years at the company, will lead Disney's government relations efforts in Washington, D.C., a high-profile role given Disney's extensive presence and influence. She previously served as vice president of government relations focusing on federal policy issues and brings a strong background including legal advisory roles with the FCC.

title: Charbel J. Barakat
summary: Charbel J. Barakat is the Vice President and Counsel for Public Policy at D.R. Horton, Inc., the largest homebuilder in the nation, where he manages government interactions. He has an extensive legal background, including serving as Chief Counsel for D.R. Horton's Florida, Gulf Coast, and Mid-Atlantic Regions, and specializing in corporate, real estate, and project finance transactions at major law firms. Barakat also holds significant public service roles, such as a member of the University of South Florida Board of Trustees and the Florida Supreme Court Judicial Nominating Commission, and notably served as Vice Chair and acting Chair of the Central Florida Tourism Oversight District, where he presided over key litigation settlements and a large development agreement.

title: AT&T to spin off troubled satellite TV unit DirecTV
summary: AT&T is spinning off its troubled DirecTV satellite TV unit into a new company with private equity firm TPG Capital. AT&T will retain 70% ownership, with TPG paying $1.8 billion for a 30% stake, valuing the new entity at $16.25 billion including debt, a significant drop from the $49 billion AT&T paid in 2015. This move allows AT&T to offload a declining business and focus on its streaming service, HBO Max, while using proceeds to reduce debt.

title: Lionsgate Teams With Sony In New Multi-Year Home Entertainment Pact
summary: Lionsgate and Sony Pictures Home Entertainment have entered a multi-year agreement for Sony to distribute Lionsgate's physical home entertainment releases in the U.S. and Canada. This new partnership follows the expiration of Lionsgate's previous deal with 20th Century Fox after its acquisition by Disney. Lionsgate will maintain its own sales and marketing teams, leveraging Sony's supply chain and distribution services.

title: Can ‘Modern Family,’ ‘The Office’ give Peacock the lift it needs?
summary: Interest in "Modern Family" and "The Office" has surged since the shows became available on Peacock, which is an unusual phenomenon for library titles. This trend suggests these popular sitcoms could provide a significant boost to Peacock's viewership. The article highlights that unlike other older shows, "Modern Family" and "The Office" have seen increased demand after switching streaming platforms.

title: Royal Caribbean will offer 'fully vaccinated' cruise with sailings starting in Israel
summary: Royal Caribbean's newest ship, Odyssey of the Seas, will debut in May with sailings from Israel, offering fully vaccinated cruises for passengers and crew over 16. These cruises, ranging from three to seven nights, will visit the Greek Isles and Cyprus and are exclusively for Israeli residents. This initiative marks Royal Caribbean's first departures from Israel and is a response to Israel's effective COVID-19 management.

title: Universal Orlando: Epic Universe starts construction again, promising ‘thousands’ of jobs
summary: Universal Orlando has restarted construction on its Epic Universe theme park, a multibillion-dollar project that was previously delayed due to the pandemic. The company expects the park to create thousands of jobs in Central Florida, with an estimated 14,000 jobs upon opening. While grand opening is anticipated for early 2025, the full construction speed will take several months to achieve as Universal re-staffs and reassembles its teams.

title: Discover the future of work management at Adobe Summit
summary: The Collaborative Work Management Track at Adobe Summit will showcase the integration of Workfront with Adobe enterprise solutions, emphasizing their combined power for marketing lifecycle management. Attendees will hear from Adobe and Workfront leadership, customers like Stanley Black & Decker and The Walt Disney Company, and explore various sessions on work visibility, agile management, and technology adoption. The article highlights the increased productivity and creativity expected from this integration, providing a single system for planning, collaboration, and governance.

title: Philips and Disney join forces to improve the healthcare experience of children
summary: Philips and The Walt Disney Company EMEA are collaborating on a clinical research pilot program to reduce fear and anxiety in children during MRI exams. The project will incorporate custom-made Disney animations and characters into Philips Ambient Experience solutions across six European hospitals. This initiative aims to improve the patient and clinician experience by making medical procedures more comforting and engaging for pediatric patients.

title: Disney to close at least 60 Disney Stores in US and Canada, as shopping shifts to online
summary: The Walt Disney Co. announced it will close at least 60 Disney Stores in North America this year, representing about one-third of its stores in the region, to emphasize e-commerce. This move comes as shopping habits shift online, accelerated by the pandemic, and the company plans to create a more flexible, interconnected e-commerce experience. Despite the closures, Disney Parks stores and locations within Target will remain, with new merchandise offerings expected.

title: Disney to Sell Its Stake in German Kids Channel Super RTL
summary: The Walt Disney Company is selling its 50 percent stake in Super RTL, a German kids channel, to RTL Group. This move aligns with Disney's strategy to focus on its streaming platform, Disney+, which launched in Germany the previous year. RTL Group will gain full control of Super RTL, further consolidating its broadcasting presence and expanding its online activities.

title: Bob Iger Talks About Making Acquisitions at the Walt Disney Company on the Podcast “Masters of Scale”
summary: Bob Iger discussed his strategy for acquisitions at The Walt Disney Company on the podcast "Masters of Scale". He outlined his three priorities as CEO: quality branded content, embracing technology, and global expansion, detailing how these led to the successful acquisitions of Pixar, Marvel, and Lucasfilm. Iger emphasized preserving the acquired companies' identities and cultures to ensure continued success.

title: Discovery Inc. Series C stock rises Thursday, outperforms market
summary: Discovery Inc. Series C stock (DISCK) surged 2.06% to $51.44 on Thursday, marking its fifth consecutive day of gains and setting a new 52-week high. This performance occurred despite a broader market downturn, with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average both falling. DISCK also outperformed several competitors, although Comcast Corp. Cl A (CMCSA) also saw a slight gain.

title: Disney downsize: Company plans to close 20 percent of shops
summary: The Walt Disney Company plans to close over 60 of its North American Disney stores, representing about 20% of its global retail footprint, to focus more on e-commerce. The company is also evaluating the closure of its European stores. This strategic shift comes as consumer behavior increasingly moves online, a trend accelerated by the pandemic, which contributed to a 7% decline in sales for its merchandise licensing and retail business last year.

title: Four Investments of Nancy Pelosi and Her Husband Reveal Much
summary: The article discusses four significant investments made by House Speaker Nancy Pelosi and her husband, Paul Pelosi, on December 22. These investments include shares in AllianceBernstein (AB) and call options in Apple (AAPL), Tesla (TSLA), and Walt Disney Co (DIS), totaling between $1,751,003 and $3,500,000. Experts weigh in on the implications of these bullish trades, noting that while the Pelosis are wealthy, their investment choices align with market opportunities, although the full scope and reasoning behind the trades are not publicly known.

title: Tech-heavy Nasdaq hits correction with 10.5% fall from peak
summary: The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite has entered correction territory, falling 10.5% from its February peak, as technology shares experienced a significant sell-off. This downturn was driven by concerns over rising bond yields and inflation fears stemming from a new $1.9 trillion COVID-19 relief bill. While financial, restaurant, and travel stocks rose on reopening hopes, they couldn't offset the weight of declining big tech shares like Apple, Nvidia, and Tesla.

title: Disney Executive Chairman Bob Iger Confirms He Will Leave the Walt Disney Company on December 31, 2021
summary: During the 2021 Annual Meeting of Shareholders, Disney Executive Chairman Bob Iger reaffirmed his plan to leave The Walt Disney Company on December 31, 2021. He had previously stepped down as CEO in February 2020, with Bob Chapek taking over, but temporarily resumed a greater leadership role due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Iger has expressed interest in other ventures and is involved in California's COVID-19 Business Recovery Task Force.

title: New “Minnie’s Garden Party” Vera Bradley Pattern Dropping Tomorrow
summary: Vera Bradley is launching a new "Minnie's Garden Party" pattern featuring Minnie Mouse surrounded by spring-colored flowers. This new collection will be available starting March 11th at Vera Bradley stores, shopDisney, and the Vera Bradley website. The article also mentions previous Disney-inspired patterns and other new Disney merchandise from brands like Ravensburger Games and Funko Games.

title: The Walt Disney Company, ESPN and National Hockey League Reach Groundbreaking Long-Term Agreement
summary: The Walt Disney Company, ESPN, and the National Hockey League have reached a historic seven-year television, streaming, and media rights deal, bringing the NHL back to Disney platforms from the 2021-22 through 2027-28 seasons. This agreement includes exclusive coverage of the Stanley Cup Final on ABC in four of the seven years, 25 exclusive national regular-season games, and 75 national regular-season games streaming exclusively on ESPN+ and Hulu. Additionally, ESPN+ subscribers will gain access to over 1,000 out-of-market games.

title: NHL, ESPN, Walt Disney Company Agree to Groundbreaking Long-Term Agreement
summary: The NHL, ESPN, and The Walt Disney Company have announced a seven-year broadcasting rights agreement. This deal brings the Stanley Cup Final, regular-season games, and extensive streaming coverage to ESPN, ABC, ESPN+, and Hulu, marking a significant return of the NHL to ESPN's platforms. NHL Commissioner Gary Bettman and ESPN Chairman Jimmy Pitaro both emphasized the groundbreaking nature of the deal for fans and the sports media landscape.

title: Vera Bradley Just Released a Minnie Mouse Garden Party Collection for Disney Fans
summary: Vera Bradley has teamed up with Disney Parks to launch a new Minnie Mouse Garden Party collection, featuring two spring-ready patterns inspired by Minnie Mouse and Epcot's Flower & Garden Festival. The collection includes 20 different items, from backpacks to smaller accessories, with prices ranging from $20 to $140. These limited-time designs are available at Vera Bradley at Disney Springs, shopDisney, and Vera Bradley's online store.

title: Netflix password sharing crackdown underway with new test and warning
summary: Netflix is implementing a new test to curb password sharing, requesting users to verify account ownership to ensure they are authorized to use the service. This move comes as the streaming market has become increasingly competitive, with password sharing costing providers billions in lost revenue, an amount expected to rise to $12.5 billion by 2024. Users who do not verify their account will be asked to create a new one, as Netflix aims to enforce its terms of service that limit sharing to individuals within the same household.

title: Los Angeles movie theaters could open next week to limited capacity
summary: Los Angeles County movie theaters could reopen as early as next week, operating at 25% capacity, which is expected to provide a significant boost to the struggling theater industry. This reopening hinges on the county reaching the "red tier" in California's coronavirus risk assessment. Major theater operators anticipate that this will allow them to show blockbuster films scheduled for the summer, helping to recover from prolonged closures.

title: Subscription E-Commerce Market: 3 Bold Projections for 2021 |
summary: HTF Market Intelligence Consulting Pvt. Ltd. has released a detailed research study on the Global Subscription E-Commerce Market, offering a product outlook and market review until 2026. The report segments the market by regions, types (Beauty and Personal Care, Food and Beverage, Clothing and Fashion, Entertainment & Health and Fitness), and applications (Online & Offline), highlighting key players such as Dollar Shave Club, Netflix, and Hello Fresh. It provides competitive analysis, financial ratios, and strategic recommendations to help businesses understand market dynamics and identify growth opportunities.

title: NEW Disney x Vera Bradley Collection Has Officially Arrived in Disney World!
summary: A new Disney x Vera Bradley collection featuring Minnie Mouse in spring colors and floral patterns has launched. The collection, which includes totes, crossbody bags, and sling backpacks, is available at the Vera Bradley store in Disney Springs at Walt Disney World and online. Prices range from $65 to $120.

title: ‘Avatar’ Reclaims All-Time Box Office Crown Following Imax China Re-Release
summary: The 2009 sci-fi epic "Avatar" has reclaimed its title as the highest-grossing theatrical release of all time, surpassing $2.8 billion in ticket sales, largely due to a successful re-release in Imax China. The re-release generated $6.2 million over the weekend, with Imax theaters accounting for a significant portion despite a small screen count. This resurgence highlights the strong demand for theatrical blockbusters, particularly in the Chinese market.

title: American Tower enters Dish mix, reaches lease deal for up to 20K sites
summary: American Tower has finalized a long-term lease agreement with Dish Network for up to 20,000 sites, making it the last of the "Big Three" tower companies to secure a deal for Dish's 5G network build. This agreement completes Dish's essential infrastructure portfolio, with revenue generation for American Tower expected to begin in 2022. The deal supports Dish's aggressive 5G rollout, aiming for 70% U.S. population coverage by June 2023.

title: The Walt Disney Company Earns 15 Academy Award Nominations
summary: The Walt Disney Company received a total of 15 Academy Award nominations for hits like Nomadland, Mulan, Soul, and Onward. Nomadland led the nominations with six nods, including Best Motion Picture, while Disney+ original content secured several first-time Oscar nominations. The article details all the nominations by film, highlighting Disney's strong performance in a unique year for the movie industry.

title: Kevin Mayer Speaks Out On Getting Passed Over for CEO of The Walt Disney Company
summary: Kevin Mayer, former head of Disney+, discusses his disappointment at being passed over for the CEO position of The Walt Disney Company when Bob Iger stepped down. Mayer, who successfully launched Disney+ and other streaming services, explains his perspective on why Bob Chapek was chosen instead, citing Chapek's extensive experience across various Disney divisions and the timing of Iger's departure. Mayer later left Disney for TikTok and is now chairman of DAZN.

title: Mr. Potato Head officially drops the “Mr.”
summary: Hasbro Inc. has decided to rebrand its iconic Mr. Potato Head toy to the gender-neutral title "Potato Head" to promote gender equality and inclusivity. This move follows a trend of toy companies, like Mattel with Barbie, adapting their products to become more modern and inclusive, allowing children to assign gender or no gender to their toys. The change aims to encourage children to be their authentic selves outside of traditional gender norms.

title: The Walt Disney Company, ESPN and National Football League Reach Landmark Long-Term Agreement
summary: The Walt Disney Company, ESPN, and the NFL have signed a new 10-year agreement starting in 2023, significantly expanding ESPN's NFL coverage. This landmark deal includes ABC/ESPN joining the Super Bowl rotation, additional playoff games, exclusive national ESPN+ matchups, and a 35% increase in regular-season Monday Night Football games. The agreement also provides enhanced schedule flexibility and comprehensive content rights across various platforms.

title: Roblox stock: meteoric growth, but what happens when the lockdowns end?
summary: Roblox Corporation experienced significant user and revenue growth in 2020 due to pandemic lockdowns, leading to a successful direct listing on the NYSE. While analysts predict continued strong performance, the article discusses potential hurdles such as the return to normalcy post-pandemic, unsophisticated graphics, platform bugs, and safety concerns, alongside strategies for future growth such as expanding to teenage demographics and international markets.

title: The Walt Disney Company and NFL Reach an Agreement Bringing the Super Bowl Back to ABC and More
summary: The Walt Disney Company and the NFL have reached a 10-year agreement starting in 2023, bringing the Super Bowl back to ABC/ESPN in 2026 and 2030. The deal also expands ESPN's regular-season NFL schedule by 35% and includes exclusive international games on ESPN+. This partnership leverages Disney's extensive platforms, including ESPN+, to reach more NFL fans.

title: Walt Disney Employees to Start Returning to the Office After July 4
summary: The Walt Disney Co. is planning a phased reopening of its U.S. offices after the July 4 weekend, with employees gradually returning as vaccinations increase. This move makes Disney the latest media conglomerate to begin its return to office strategy, following a year of remote work due to the pandemic. Other companies like ViacomCBS are also planning post-Independence Day returns, while Fox Corp has deferred its reopening until at least September.

title: Check Out Godzilla vs. Kong’s IMAX, RealD and Dolby Posters
summary: The article highlights the visually striking IMAX, RealD, and Dolby posters for the movie "Godzilla vs. Kong," noting their superior artwork compared to the mainstream promotional materials. It describes unique aspects of each poster, such as neon-tinted titans for IMAX, the iconic smack reimagined for RealD, and a bird's-eye city view from Godzilla's perspective for Dolby. The film's release dates in India, internationally, and the US are also mentioned.

title: Hasbro Unveils New ‘Baby Yoda’ Grogu Animatronic
summary: Hasbro has launched a new "Star Wars Galactic Snackin' Grogu" animatronic, an updated version of their popular "Baby Yoda" toy from The Mandalorian. This animatronic features sounds, animated motions, interactive accessories that trigger eating sounds, and Force activation inspired by the Disney+ series. It is currently available for pre-order at major retailers.

title: T-Mobile to wind down live TV services, offer YouTube TV
summary: T-Mobile is discontinuing its live TV service, TVision, on April 29th and will instead direct its wireless customers towards Google's YouTube TV. This decision comes after the company struggled to make its "skinny bundle" profitable, facing rising fees from programmers and intense competition in the virtual pay-TV market. This marks T-Mobile's second failed attempt to establish itself in the pay-TV industry.

title: Televisa desmiente rumores de unión con Univisión
summary: Grupo Televisa has denied rumors of a full merger with Univision, stating that such reports are false. However, Televisa confirmed that both companies are in discussions about a potential combination of certain content assets to expand their partnership and achieve efficiencies. The Mexican group emphasized that there's no certainty the operation will occur, nor are the terms or timing finalized.

title: Red Robin Gourmet Burgers, Inc. Appoints Darla Morse as Executive Vice President and Chief Information Officer
summary: Red Robin Gourmet Burgers, Inc. announced the appointment of Darla Morse as Executive Vice President and Chief Information Officer, effective April 12, 2021. Ms. Morse, with over 25 years of experience from companies like Walt Disney World and CKE Restaurants, will lead Red Robin's enterprise technology strategy, including digital platforms and data management. This strategic hire aims to accelerate the company's transformation and technology evolution for sustained growth.

title: Nexon invests $874 mn in Hasbro, Japan’s game giants
summary: South Korea’s Nexon Co. invested $874 million in global entertainment companies in 2020, including Hasbro Inc. and major Japanese game companies like Bandai Namco Holdings Inc., Konami Holdings Co., and Sega Sammy Holdings Inc. These investments represent less than 5% stakes and are described as long-term friendly investments aimed at strengthening business partnerships rather than acquisitions. Nexon plans to invest the remaining $626 million of its authorized funds in 2021, potentially targeting The Walt Disney Company, Electronic Arts Inc., and Nintendo Co.

title: Comcast Launches Disney+ and ESPN+ on Xfinity
summary: Comcast and The Walt Disney Company have announced the rollout of Disney+ and ESPN+ on Xfinity, making these streaming services available to X1 and Flex customers. This integration allows subscribers to access a wide range of content, including movies, shows, live sports, and original programming, directly through their Xfinity platforms using voice commands. The launch aims to provide an enhanced user experience and timely access to popular new and upcoming series and sporting events.

title: Deluxe Acquires Sony Electronics’ New Media Solutions Division
summary: Deluxe has acquired Sony New Media Solutions, a division of Sony Electronics, to enhance its digital media supply chain capabilities for studios and streaming services. The acquisition is expected to strengthen Deluxe's technology and workflows, providing NMS customers with full access to Deluxe's integrated supply chain solutions, including localization and distribution. This deal follows Deluxe's earlier acquisition of Sundog Media Toolkit, further expanding its cloud automation resources.

title: Josh D’Amaro Discusses the Fresh, Technology-Focused Future of Disney Parks
