summary: Disney Parks Chairman Josh D’Amaro discussed the future of Disney Parks, emphasizing the preservation of Walt Disney’s legacy while integrating new technologies and intellectual properties. He highlighted the potential of a "metaverse" concept to enhance park experiences and the role of new IPs from Disney+ in driving attractions like Avengers Campus. D'Amaro also noted how technology, such as MagicMobile and Disney Genie, will personalize guest experiences and improve operational efficiency.

title: Avengers Campus Opening at Disneyland Resort on June 4, 2021
summary: Disneyland Resort's new immersive land, Avengers Campus, is set to open on June 4, 2021, inside Disney California Adventure Park. The campus invites guests to team up with Super Heroes, experience attractions like WEB SLINGERS: A Spider-Man Adventure, and enjoy themed dining at Pym Test Kitchen and Shawarma Palace. This expansion aims to recruit and train the next generation of heroes, bringing the Marvel universe to life with innovative technology and character interactions.

title: Walt Disney Company Selling Vista Way Aparment Complex
summary: The Walt Disney Company is selling its 468-unit Vista Way apartment complex, previously used for the Walt Disney World College Program. The complex, valued at $63.1 million in 2020, is expected to sell for tens of millions more due to its location near Walt Disney World and amenities. Future College Program participants will be housed in the new Flamingo Crossings Village complex.

title: ‘Top Gun’ sequel delayed in summer movie setback for theaters
summary: Paramount Pictures has delayed the release of "Top Gun: Maverick" from July to November, depriving theaters of a major summer blockbuster. This move also pushed back Tom Cruise's seventh "Mission: Impossible" film to May 2022. The delay is a setback for movie theaters hoping for a strong summer rebound following COVID-19 closures, though other major films like "Fast & Furious 9" and "Black Widow" are still scheduled for summer release.

title: Visible Tattoos Among Inclusive Changes Coming for Cast Members & Disney Company
summary: The Walt Disney Company is introducing inclusive changes for its cast members, primarily allowing visible tattoos and offering greater flexibility in appearance guidelines. These updates, part of the new "Fifth Key of Inclusion," aim to foster a culture of belonging and allow cast members to express their individuality and cultures, as well as making guests feel more welcome with diverse representation. The changes also extend to attractions like Jungle Cruise and Splash Mountain.

title: Disney’s LAUNCHPAD Brings a New Generation of Storytellers to Disney+
summary: Disney's LAUNCHPAD initiative is set to release its first season of six live-action short films on Disney+ on May 28, featuring diverse filmmakers and stories centered around the theme "Discover." The program aims to empower underrepresented storytellers and will open applications for its second season, themed "Connection," on May 10, 2021, including a new writers' track. The inaugural films explore unique perspectives on living in America and personal journeys.

title: The VIG ETF: From Dividend Maintenance to Dividend Growth
summary: The VIG ETF, managed by Vanguard, focuses on companies with a history of increasing dividends over time, rather than just maintaining them. It tracks the Nasdaq US Dividend Achievers Select Index and offers exposure to large-cap equities with a low expense ratio of 0.06%. The fund includes companies that have increased dividends for at least ten consecutive years, making it suitable for long-term, dividend-focused investors.

title: Are FYC Billboards DOA? Studios Pull Back on Outdoor Marketing Amid Pandemic
summary: Studios significantly reduced their "For Your Consideration" (FYC) billboard advertising in Los Angeles during the early part of 2021 due to the pandemic, as Oscar voters were no longer commuting or attending in-person screenings. While out-of-home advertising for the cinema sector saw a 90 percent drop in 2020, the FYC market for billboards began recovering near the end of the awards season, with a projected return to full swing for Emmy season, partly driven by sustained investment from streaming companies. The pandemic also shifted billboard placement strategies, with advertisers becoming more open to suburban locations to target executives and talent in their homes.

title: Netflix reports dramatic slowdown in subscribers
summary: Netflix shares fell significantly after the company reported a large miss in subscriber numbers for Q1 2021, adding only 3.98 million paid net subscribers against an expectation of 6.2 million. The company attributed the slowdown to the "Covid-19 pull forward" in 2020 and production delays affecting its content slate, despite beating earnings per share and revenue estimates. Netflix expects content to pick up in the second half of the year and plans to spend over $17 billion on content, while also approving a $5 billion stock buyback program.

title: Netflix’s Dominance Starts to Slow as Rivals Gain (Published 2021)
summary: Netflix reported a slowdown in subscriber growth for the first quarter of 2021, adding only four million new customers compared to a forecast of six million. This modest growth, coupled with a decline in its share of global demand for original programming, indicates that competitors like Disney+, HBO Max, and Paramount+ are beginning to challenge Netflix's long-standing market dominance. The company anticipates adding even fewer subscribers in the current quarter.

title: Declare Your Rebel or Imperial Allegiance With Columbia Sportswear’s New Star Wars Jackets
summary: Columbia Sportswear is releasing a special collection of Star Wars-themed jackets, allowing fans to show allegiance to either the Rebel Alliance or the Galactic Empire. These collectible jackets, retailing for $200, feature subtle Star Wars references and iconic symbols, ensuring fans stay warm while displaying their chosen side of the Force.

title: Netflix tanks as subscriber growth cools
summary: Netflix shares fell significantly after reporting only 4 million new subscribers in Q1 2021, a miss compared to its 6 million projection. The company attributed the slowdown to COVID-19 related production delays and faces growing competition from services like Disney+. Despite the subscriber miss, Netflix saw a 24% year-over-year revenue increase to $7.16 billion and expects growth to re-accelerate in the latter half of 2021 with new content.

title: Netflix subscriber growth slows after pandemic boom, shares fall 11%
summary: Netflix reported significantly lower-than-expected subscriber growth in the first quarter of 2021, with only 3.98 million new sign-ups compared to an average projection of 6.25 million. This slowdown, attributed to slower content production during the pandemic, caused the company's shares to fall 11% and wiped $25 billion off its market capitalization. Netflix anticipates growth to accelerate in the second half of the year with new content releases, but analysts suggest subscribers might decrease streaming time as global vaccinations progress.

title: Netflix Not-So-Secretly Wants to Be Disney, But Is It Placing the Right Bets?
summary: Netflix is increasingly attempting to emulate Disney's strategy by focusing on key content verticals like animation, Hollywood blockbusters, and foreign shows. This shift comes as Netflix faces accelerating competition and a shrinking share of original digital demand, despite its large content budget. The article questions if these targeted investments will yield the same success and branding power as Disney's established intellectual property.

title: Here's how much money you'd have if you bought $1,000 worth of Netflix stock in 2011
summary: This article examines the significant return on investment for Netflix stock over the past decade. A $1,000 investment in Netflix in 2011 would have grown to over $15,000 by April 2021, far outpacing the S&P 500, Google, and Apple. Despite recent subscriber growth concerns, analysts believe Netflix is well-positioned for the long term due to its first-mover advantage and extensive content investments, even amidst increasing competition from other streaming services.

title: The Walt Disney Company Presents the 2021 NFL Draft
summary: The Walt Disney Company will present the 2021 NFL Draft across multiple platforms including ESPN, ABC, ESPN Deportes, ESPN Radio, and the ESPN App, starting April 29. The coverage will feature extensive camera setups, numerous analysts, and specialized pre- and post-event programming across various ESPN networks and digital platforms. Additionally, unique collaborations with Marvel Entertainment for custom comic book covers and comprehensive social media integration are planned.

title: Cambria Opens Orlando Airport Hotel
summary: Cambria Hotels, an upscale brand by Choice Hotels International, has opened its Cambria Hotel Orlando Airport location, marking its fourth opening this year with two more airport-area hotels planned for Austin and Nashville. The 108-room hotel is strategically located near Orlando International Airport, major theme parks, and convention centers. It offers upscale amenities and contactless services, reflecting Cambria's expansion strategy in key travel destinations.

title: Oscars 2021: Netflix and Disney dominate in streaming’s biggest year
summary: The 93rd Academy Awards saw Netflix and Disney dominate, reflecting the streaming-centric year. Netflix, despite losing Best Picture to Disney-owned Searchlight's “Nomadland,” secured seven awards, making it the top distributor. Disney, including wins from Searchlight and Pixar, also performed strongly with five trophies, solidifying streaming services' significant presence in the awards landscape.

title: Comcast Advertising Appoints Rick Mandler as VP
summary: Comcast Advertising has appointed Rick Mandler as Vice President, Growth Strategy. In this new role, Mandler will be responsible for developing growth marketing strategies across the Comcast Advertising portfolio, aiming to advance revenue growth and market share, and will report to Chief Growth Officer Pooja Midha. Mandler brings extensive experience from true[X], ABC, and Walt Disney, where he specialized in advanced advertising and strategic initiatives.

title: Disney Earns Five Oscars®, Including Best Motion Picture and Best Animated Feature
summary: The Walt Disney Company received five Academy Awards, with Searchlight Pictures' "Nomadland" securing three Oscars, including Best Motion Picture, Best Actress (Frances McDormand), and Best Director (Chloé Zhao). Disney and Pixar's "Soul" won two awards, Best Animated Feature and Best Original Score. Chloé Zhao made history as the first Chinese woman and second woman ever to win Best Director.

title: Netflix wins 7 Oscars, beating out other streaming services
summary: Netflix secured seven Oscar wins at the 93rd Academy Awards, outperforming other streaming services. Despite these wins, including awards for "Mank," "My Octopus Teacher," and short films, Netflix did not receive the top award for Best Picture. Disney+ competitor, however, claimed Best Picture with "Nomadland," directed by Chloé Zhao, who also made history as the first woman of color to win Best Director.

title: TNT, TBS to Share NHL Rights With ESPN in Seven-Year Deal
summary: AT&T's TNT and TBS networks will air NHL regular games and Stanley Cup playoffs for seven years, joining ESPN in broadcasting the league's games. This deal, along with Disney's previously announced agreement, means the league's fees increased by 200%. The rights also include streaming on AT&T’s HBO Max service.

title: Hasbro Reports First Quarter 2021 Financial Results
summary: Hasbro Inc. reported a strong first quarter for 2021 with revenues of $1.11 billion, up 1%, driven by growth in Consumer Products and Wizards of the Coast segments. The company's chairman and CEO, Brian Goldner, expressed confidence in achieving full-year double-digit revenue growth. Despite a decline in the Entertainment segment due to COVID-19 related theater shutdowns, Hasbro is targeting a return to 2019 revenue levels for the full year in its TV and film business.

title: Byron Allen Buys 7 Gray Divestiture TV Stations for $380M
summary: Byron Allen's Allen Media Broadcasting has acquired seven TV stations from Gray Television for $380 million. This acquisition is part of Gray Television's deal to acquire Quincy Media. Allen Media Group now owns 23 network affiliate stations nationwide and plans to acquire more ABC, CBS, NBC, and Fox stations in the next two years.

title: Walt Disney Co. Taps ESPN’s Paul Richardson As Chief Human Resources Officer
summary: The Walt Disney Co. has appointed Paul Richardson as Senior Executive VP and Chief Human Resources Officer, effective July 1, 2021. Richardson, previously ESPN's HR head and Disney's first Chief Diversity Officer, will report to CEO Bob Chapek and oversee global HR strategy. He succeeds Jayne Parker, who is retiring after 33 years with the company.

title: Walt Disney Company confirms AWS as preferred cloud partner for Disney+ streaming service
summary: The Walt Disney Company has designated Amazon Web Services (AWS) as its preferred cloud partner for the Disney+ streaming service, which has garnered over 100 million subscribers globally. Disney+ leveraged AWS for its rapid international expansion and will further integrate AWS's machine learning, database, storage, and analytics services. This partnership highlights AWS's broader strategy to offer sector-specific cloud services for the media and entertainment industry.

title: The Walt Disney Company partners AWS for Disney+ expansion
summary: The Walt Disney Company has partnered with Amazon Web Services (AWS) for the global rollout and expansion of its Disney+ streaming service. AWS has been Disney's preferred public cloud infrastructure provider, supporting Disney+'s growth to over 100 million subscribers in 59 countries. This expanded partnership will see Disney+ leverage more than 50 AWS technologies, including machine learning, database, storage, and analytics, to enhance its content delivery and platform efficacy.

title: Trump pitched on launching a "conservative media powerhouse"
summary: Donald Trump was presented with a proposal to launch a multi-billion dollar media and technology company called Trump Media Group. The "conservative media powerhouse" would include subscription content, social media, and technology divisions, aiming to rival liberal media and combat "Big Tech" censorship. Although the idea seems to have stalled, it indicates the types of business ventures being pitched to the former president.

title: Disney+ chooses Amazon Web Services for global expansion
summary: The Walt Disney Company has selected Amazon Web Services (AWS) as its preferred public cloud infrastructure provider for the global expansion of Disney+. Leveraging AWS's fault-tolerant and highly performant infrastructure, Disney+ has rapidly grown to over 100 million subscribers in 59 countries. The streaming service utilizes more than 50 AWS technologies, including machine learning, databases, and analytics, to handle content ingestion, manage customer actions, and ensure high-quality video delivery.

title: The Disney Wish to Bring Immersive Disney Storytelling to the High Seas in New and Innovative Ways
summary: The Disney Wish, launching its maiden voyage on June 9, 2022, will introduce innovative new experiences including the first-ever Disney attraction at sea, AquaMouse, a Marvel cinematic dining adventure, and a Star Wars-themed lounge. The ship aims to elevate the cruise experience with immersive storytelling inspired by various Disney brands. It will also feature a Frozen-themed dining experience, a Toy Story waterplay district, and a restaurant named 1923 celebrating the company's legacy.

title: Video game brands win big for Jakks Pacific
summary: Jakks Pacific experienced a significant boost in its Q1 2021 net sales, growing by 26% to US$83.8 million, largely driven by popular video game brands like Sonic the Hedgehog and Super Mario. This marks the toymaker's biggest Q1 jump since 2015, following a challenging year in 2020. The company plans to continue expanding its offerings for key video game brands and Disney properties.

title: What Animation Does Fox Corporation Own?
summary: This article details Fox Corporation's animation assets, which were retained after Disney's 2019 acquisition of 21st Century Fox. It highlights key acquisitions like Bento Box Entertainment and Tubi, new ventures such as Princess Bento Studio and Blockchain Creative Labs, and mentions the animated shows airing on its Fox Broadcasting Company's Animation Domination block, many of which are co-productions with other studios.

title: The Rise of Streaming Services and the Role of 3rd Party Measurement...
summary: The article analyzes the profound impact of the 2020 pandemic on streaming service viewership, detailing the advertising spend by major players like Netflix and Disney+ to attract subscribers. It presents Comscore's insights into streaming service rankings, day-of-week viewership trends, and an unsupervised cluster analysis categorizing services into Fully-Established, Somewhat-Established, and Emerging types, highlighting the evolving streaming landscape and the role of third-party measurement.

title: A Conservative ETF That Boycotts Liberal Companies Is Beating the S&P 500
summary: The American Conservative Values ETF ($ACVF), which boycotts companies supporting a "liberal agenda," has outperformed the S&P 500 since President Biden took office, gaining 9.1% compared to the S&P 500's 8.7%. The fund's founder, Bill Flaig, believes politically active companies negatively impact shareholder returns and aims to provide conservative investors with an option that aligns with their values. While acknowledging the subjectivity in defining "hostile" companies, the fund seeks to balance advocacy with predictable large-cap performance.

title: Crocs are making a pandemic comeback, thanks to Gen Z and Justin Bieber
summary: Crocs, the brightly-colored rubber clogs, have seen a resurgence in popularity during the pandemic, largely due to Generation Z and celebrity endorsements from figures like Justin Bieber and Questlove. Despite their divisive aesthetic, the company's stock price has soared, and collaborations are driving significant growth. Critics remain puzzled by their comeback, but acknowledge the comfort factor and the influence of pandemic fashion trends.

title: Disneyland Resort Theme Parks Welcome Back Guests
summary: Disneyland Park and Disney California Adventure Park reopened to the public, welcoming back guests with joy and excitement. The CEO of The Walt Disney Company, Bob Chapek, expressed gratitude to cast members for their spirit and dedication. The reopening marks a historic moment for the Disneyland Resort, following a soft opening for cast and community members.

title: AT&T shareholders vote against approving executive compensation
summary: AT&T shareholders have voted against approving executive compensation during the company's annual meeting, with only 49% of votes cast in favor. This advisory vote comes as executive pay packages have grown, and highlights shareholder concerns, particularly regarding the more than $52 million compensation for WarnerMedia CEO Jason Kilar, which was double that of AT&T CEO John Stankey. AT&T's board acknowledged the vote and stated they would consider it to ensure their compensation approach aligns with company principles.

title: GMA Network ties up with iQiyi for global video streaming service
summary: GMA Network has partnered with Singapore-based iQiyi International, a global video streaming service, to bring GMA's content to a wider audience. This multi-year agreement will see 12 new GMA titles with over 1,000 catch-up episodes available on iQiyi, expanding the platform's Asian entertainment portfolio and GMA's reach. The partnership aims to adapt to changing viewer habits and capitalize on iQiyi's massive user base, following a successful 2020 for GMA Network with significant profit growth.

title: Walt Disney Co. marks Star Wars Day by ringing New York Stock Exchange opening bell
summary: The Walt Disney Company celebrated Star Wars Day by virtually ringing the New York Stock Exchange's opening bell on Tuesday, May 4, 2021. The celebration included help from Baby Yoda and marked the release of new Star Wars content on Disney+. This annual observance of "May the Fourth Be With You" has evolved into "Star Wars Day" for global recognition.

title: Televisa y TV Azteca se recuperan en publicidad, pero toca impulsar el contenido
summary: Televisa and TV Azteca are seeing a recovery in advertising revenue after a challenging 2020, with Televisa's ad income up 28.1% and TV Azteca's up 8% in Q1 2021. However, despite increased viewership during the COVID-19 pandemic, both companies face the challenge of migrating advertising investment to digital platforms and the need to innovate content to retain audiences and compete with streaming services. Experts emphasize that investing in new, high-quality content is crucial for the future of open television.

title: May the 4th be with you: Star Wars fans storm downtown Panama City
summary: Downtown Panama City celebrated "May the Fourth" with a Star Wars-themed event that drew hundreds of fans, including members of the 501st Legion costuming group. The event featured trivia, a scavenger hunt, activity stations, and lightsaber displays, and organizers plan for it to become an annual tradition. The celebration aimed to bring the community together and highlight the city's evolving downtown area.

title: New Facilities Insider | Disney’s Digital Center 3 Centralizes Hardware, Allows Control From Anywhere
summary: Disney has consolidated its broadcast and entertainment network operations into a new 187,000-square-foot facility, Digital Center 3 (DC3), in The Woodlands, Texas. This hub centralizes playout, transmission, and media functions, previously spread across multiple locations, and connects directly to ESPN headquarters for redundancy. DC3 is based on a private cloud architecture, utilizing software-defined playout systems and allowing remote control of hardware, a strategy proven effective during the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: ViacomCBS Inc. Cl B stock rises Friday, outperforms market
summary: ViacomCBS Inc. Class B stock (VIAC) rose 3.25% to $39.39 on Friday, outperforming the broader market which also saw gains in the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average. This gain broke a two-day losing streak for the stock, though it remained significantly below its 52-week high. Competitors like Walt Disney Co., Netflix Inc., and Comcast Corp. Cl A also saw increases.

title: Cinemark, Studios Reach Deals on How Movies Are Shown as Theaters Reopen
summary: Cinemark Holdings Inc. has reached agreements with major Hollywood studios including Warner Bros., Disney, Paramount, and Sony, building on a previous deal with Universal. These agreements aim to establish the exclusive theatrical window for films before they become available on at-home streaming platforms, as theaters begin to reopen.

title: The Wokest Place on Earth
summary: This article criticizes The Walt Disney Corporation's "Reimagine Tomorrow" diversity and inclusion program, which it argues has introduced critical race theory concepts like "white privilege," "white fragility," and "systemic racism" into the company's corporate culture. The author, citing whistleblower documents and anonymous employee accounts, claims the program promotes racially segregated affinity groups and discourages dissenting viewpoints, transforming Disney into a "wokest place on Earth."

title: Peloton Strive Score: Everything you need to know
summary: Peloton has introduced the Strive Score, a new personal metric announced during their Homecoming Event, which measures workout intensity based on time spent in different heart rate zones. This score aims to provide a comparable performance metric across various types of Peloton workouts, including those without power-based output. While it offers an interesting way to gauge effort, the article suggests it's best used as a weekly or monthly metric and notes its limitations, particularly for strength training where heart rate doesn't directly correlate with strength gains.

title: Disguise to Launch Bluey Costumes at Walmart this Fall
summary: Disguise, Inc., the Halloween costume division of JAKKS Pacific, Inc., announced it secured U.S. rights for the children's animated television program "Bluey." The company will design, manufacture, and distribute costumes and accessories for the property, with a first-to-market launch at Walmart in the U.S. this fall. The partnership with BBC Studios aims to bring the popular "Bluey" characters to life for fans, particularly capitalizing on the show's significant reach and themes of family life and imaginative play.

title: What Animation Does Sony Own?
summary: This article details the extensive animation holdings of Sony Group Corporation, covering its presence in Hollywood, video games, and anime. It lists various Sony-owned companies and divisions, such as Sony Pictures Animation, Sony Pictures Imageworks, and Silvergate Media. The article also highlights Sony's ownership of classic theatrical shorts, numerous character franchises like Peanuts, and anime-related entities such as Aniplex and Funimation.

title: Norwegian Cruise Line unveils Norwegian Prima, set to debut summer 2022 (Renderings)
summary: Norwegian Cruise Line (NYSE: NCLH) has unveiled its new ship, Norwegian Prima, which is scheduled to debut in summer 2022 and arrive in Miami in November 2022. This vessel will be the first of six in the cruise line's new class, measuring 965 feet long and accommodating 3,215 guests at double occupancy. The announcement includes renderings of the new ship.

title: Streaming Giants Are Spending Billions Overseas. Here Comes the Pushback.
summary: U.S.-based streaming services like Netflix, Amazon, Disney+, and HBO Max are investing billions in overseas markets to produce local-language content, leading to a boom for local talent and increased competition. However, this global expansion is also generating pushback from established international broadcasters, local lawmakers, and producers who are raising concerns about equal pay and content ownership. This development occurs as Disney+ has boosted its parent company's stock, highlighting the significant impact of streaming in the entertainment industry.

title: The Walt Disney Company, ESPN and Major League Baseball Reach Long-Term Rights Extension for Fully Exclusive, Marquee Schedule
summary: The Walt Disney Company, ESPN, and Major League Baseball have agreed to a new seven-year rights extension through the 2028 season. This agreement grants ESPN exclusive rights to 30 regular-season games annually, including "Sunday Night Baseball," the Home Run Derby, and potential expanded MLB Wild Card Series. It also includes simulcast rights for ESPN+, extensive Spanish-language telecast rights for ESPN Deportes, and increased highlight rights for ESPN platforms.

title: Disney's streaming growth slows as pandemic lift fades, shares fall
summary: Walt Disney Co.'s shares fell 3.7% after its streaming service, Disney+, showed disappointing growth, overshadowing better-than-expected overall profits. The slowdown is attributed to the fading "pandemic boost," although the company expects subscriber growth to rebound with upcoming content. Despite the decline in streaming subscribers and overall revenue, Disney's theme parks are showing strong reservation numbers as they begin to recover from COVID-19 related closures.

title: China's streaming giant iQiyi may turn a profit in 5 yrs - CEO
summary: iQiyi, China's Netflix-like streaming platform, expects to turn a profit within five years by leveraging "intelligent production" and AI to cut costs. The company, which is majority-owned by Baidu, plans to increase its self-produced content to 60%-70% and eventually build an entertainment park, despite facing declining user subscriptions and advertising revenue due to competition from short video platforms. CEO Gong Yu also stated that reported acquisition talks with Tencent and Alibaba were "largely market's imagination" due to antitrust constraints.

title: Walmart, Starbucks Among Retailers Dropping Mask Requirement
summary: Walmart Inc. has announced that fully vaccinated staff and customers no longer need to wear masks, a decision likely to influence other businesses. Starbucks Corp. followed suit for vaccinated customers, while Walt Disney World Resort made masks optional in common outdoor areas. These changes reflect a response to updated government guidance regarding mask use.

title: Disney World, Disneyland to increase park capacity; CEO hints that mask mandates could be lifted by summer
summary: Disney is increasing capacity at its California and Florida theme parks, with CEO Bob Chapek expecting an immediate rise in admissions. He also suggested that mask mandates could be lifted by summer, believing this would boost attendance and enhance the visitor experience. This announcement follows the CDC easing mask-wearing guidance for fully vaccinated individuals.

title: Disney World no longer requires masks outdoors, but you'll still need to wear a mask to enter parks and inside
summary: Walt Disney World announced that masks will no longer be required outdoors starting Saturday, May 15, 2021, but will still be necessary for entering parks and inside attractions, theaters, and transportation. This change follows new CDC guidelines for vaccinated individuals and aims to improve the guest experience, especially during the summer months in Florida. Despite a drop in revenue for parks, demand is increasing, and park capacities are being raised.

title: Is an AT&T-Discovery media marriage in the works?
summary: Dallas-based AT&T Inc. is reportedly in talks to spin off its media business and merge it with Discovery Inc. This potential deal would combine Discovery’s reality-TV empire with AT&T’s media holdings, aiming to create a formidable competitor to Netflix and Walt Disney. The move signals a major shift in AT&T's strategy, which previously focused on integrating telecommunications and media assets, and comes amid efforts to reduce debt and invest in 5G.

title: AT&T Is Preparing to Merge Media Assets With Discovery
summary: AT&T Inc. is reportedly preparing to spin off its media business and merge it with Discovery Inc. in a tax-friendly deal, a surprising move given its significant previous investment. This merger would combine WarnerMedia assets with Discovery's reality-TV empire, creating a new entertainment giant. A deal could be announced as early as this week and is expected to be structured as a Reverse Morris Trust.

summary: AT&T and Discovery Inc. have officially announced their plan to merge their media assets, including WarnerMedia and Discovery, to create a global leader in entertainment and streaming. Discovery CEO David Zaslav will lead the new company, which is expected to generate $52 billion in revenue by 2023 and aims to compete globally with major streaming services. summary: AT&T announced it is spinning off WarnerMedia to merge with Discovery Inc. in a $43 billion all-stock deal, creating a new media giant led by Discovery CEO David Zaslav. summary: AT&T has agreed to merge its WarnerMedia division with Discovery Communications Inc., creating a new streaming giant to compete with Disney+ and Netflix. summary: David Zaslav, the longtime CEO of Discovery Communications Inc., will lead the combined media company formed by AT&T Inc. and Discovery's $43 billion tie-up. summary: AT&T is preparing to spin off its media business and merge it with Discovery Inc. in a tax-friendly deal, reversing an $85 billion acquisition made less than three years ago. title: WarnerMedia, Discovery unveil new global streaming giant
summary: AT&T and Discovery have announced a merger to create a new standalone global entertainment company, combining WarnerMedia's premium entertainment with Discovery's non-fiction and international content. title: Canadian TV networks face rising costs for U.S. programming in wake of AT&T-Discovery merger
summary: Canadian television networks anticipate higher costs and potential loss of popular shows following the US$43-billion merger of WarnerMedia and Discovery Inc. title: Michael Bair Hones Spectrum Networks’ Local Edge | Next TV | Broadcasting+Cable
summary: Michael Bair, head of Spectrum Networks, is navigating the company's 30 regional news and sports channels through a changing media landscape. He emphasizes the importance of local news and sports programming as retention tools, noting the high ratings for Dodgers and Lakers telecasts and the expansion of local news networks during the pandemic. Bair also discussed carriage deals, including the recent agreement with AT&T for SportsNet LA.

title: WarnerMedia, Discovery unveil new global streaming giant
summary: AT&T Inc. and Discovery, Inc. have partnered to create a new, standalone global entertainment company, combining WarnerMedia's premium content with Discovery's non-fiction and international assets. title: AT&T signing $43B deal to combine media business with Discovery
summary: AT&T announced a $43 billion deal to spin off its WarnerMedia content unit and merge it with Discovery, creating a new media giant. Discovery CEO David Zaslav will lead the combined entity, marking a significant strategic shift for AT&T.

title: Marvel Entertainment and SiriusXM to Premiere First Original Scripted Podcast Series 'Marvel's Wastelanders: Old Man Star-Lord' on June 1
summary: Marvel Entertainment and SiriusXM announced they will premiere their first original scripted podcast series, 'Marvel's Wastelanders: Old Man Star-Lord,' on June 1, 2021. The 10-episode series will launch with its first two episodes and will feature a star-studded cast including Timothy Busfield, Chris Elliott, Nadine Malouf, Vanessa Williams, and Danny Glover. This podcast marks the beginning of a multi-part series set in a dystopian Marvel Universe where villains have triumphed, with future installments focusing on other "Old Man" heroes.

title: Condé Nast may have a place in the Warner Media/Discovery merger
summary: The upcoming merger of Discovery and WarnerMedia could potentially include Condé Nast, given the Newhouse family's significant stake in Discovery. Such a union could provide Condé Nast with much-needed scale and distribution for its multimedia content, especially as its print revenues decline. While Steven Newhouse denies plans to divest, industry experts see potential strategic advantages and a possible "smart exit strategy" for the family.

title: The CW Renews Agreement With Top Affiliate Nexstar Media Group
summary: The CW has renewed its affiliation agreements with Nexstar Media Group, its largest affiliate group, covering 37 markets and over 31% of the U.S. audience. This multi-year deal includes key stations in top markets like New York and Los Angeles, arriving just before The CW's 2021-22 schedule unveiling. The agreement leverages a recent "time slot swap" expanding CW network programming to Saturday nights while returning an afternoon hour to affiliates, and highlights the importance of The CW's digital strategy and in-season streaming rights since the Netflix output deal ended.

title: Netflix users dip in S. Korea amid growing competition
summary: Netflix's monthly active users in South Korea have declined for three consecutive months, reaching 8.08 million in April, down from a peak of nearly 9 million in January. This dip comes as Netflix faces increased competition from local streaming services like Wavve and Tving, which are investing heavily in content, and ahead of Disney+'s anticipated launch in the region. Despite a global slowdown in subscriber growth for Netflix, the company plans to invest $500 million in original Korean content to boost its presence.

title: John Malone sees merged WarnerMedia-Discovery becoming No. 3 global streamer behind Netflix, Disney+
summary: Billionaire media mogul John Malone believes the merged WarnerMedia-Discovery will become the third global streaming powerhouse, competitive with Netflix and Disney+. He sees "great upside" for HBO Max in this merger, especially for international expansion, and supports Discovery CEO David Zaslav's leadership and AT&T CEO John Stankey's decision to spin off WarnerMedia. Malone also confirmed he was comfortable giving up his super-voting Discovery shares as part of the deal.

title: Behind the Scenes at Sinclair’s New Media Operations Center Powering Bally Sports, Marquee Sports, and YES Network
summary: Sinclair Broadcast Group has established a new 25,000-sq.-ft. SMPTE ST 2110-based Media Operations Center in Atlanta to handle master-control for 19 Bally Sports RSNs, YES Network, and Marquee Sports Network. This initiative replaces the former Fox RSN master-control center and involves building a new Sinclair Video Network (SVN) to connect RSN studios and venues. The project was completed under tight deadlines and during the COVID-19 pandemic, showcasing a collaborative effort to transition complex broadcast infrastructure.

title: AT&T Breaks Off WarnerMedia
summary: AT&T is spinning off WarnerMedia to merge with Discovery Inc., a move that will provide AT&T with $43 billion in cash and debt relief, allowing it to focus on 5G wireless services. This decision marks a significant shift from AT&T's previous strategy of acquiring major media properties and is supported by prominent investors like John Malone and Elliott Management Corp. The new combined WarnerMedia and Discovery entity aims to become a major player in the streaming market, similar to Netflix and Disney.

title: MGM to Be Acquired by Amazon for $8.45 Billion
summary: Amazon announced its acquisition of Beverly Hills-based Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer Studios Inc. for $8.45 billion. This deal gives Amazon access to MGM's extensive library of 4,000 films and 17,000 television shows, aiming to enhance Prime Video's competitive edge against other streaming services. The acquisition, subject to regulatory approval, will allow Amazon to "reimagine and develop" MGM's intellectual property for the 21st century.

title: American Tower is convinced Crown Castle’s early Dish builds is not a long-term concern
summary: American Tower (ATC) is not concerned by Crown Castle's larger initial share of Dish Network's site co-locations. ATC's CFO Rod Smith believes Dish will eventually utilize a similar percentage of ATC's sites as other carriers, and that short-term revenue spikes don't impact long-term value. American Tower expects to see revenue from Dish in 2022.

title: Amazon brings James Bond, Rocky to fight Netflix with $8.5 bln MGM buy
summary: Amazon is acquiring MGM, the studio behind James Bond and Rocky, for $8.45 billion to expand its content library and compete more effectively with streaming rivals like Netflix and Disney+. This acquisition will bolster Amazon's Prime Video service by adding a vast catalog of films and TV shows, including valuable intellectual property that Amazon plans to reimagine for the 21st century. The deal, Amazon's second-largest after Whole Foods, highlights the ongoing consolidation in the media industry as companies vie for compelling content to attract and retain streaming subscribers.

title: Sony Pictures Not for Sale, Says CEO Yoshida Kenichiro
summary: Sony Group CEO Yoshida Kenichiro has stated that Sony Pictures is not for sale and will not be spun off, despite industry speculation fueled by recent mergers and acquisitions like Amazon's purchase of MGM. Sony's strategy involves operating as an independent studio, supplying content to streamers, and leveraging its various entertainment divisions, such as gaming and anime, to create content. The company has secured licensing deals with Netflix and Disney+ and plans to produce more films for direct release on streaming platforms while retaining ownership.

title: Amy Chang, Calvin McDonald Elected to The Walt Disney Company Board of Directors
summary: The Walt Disney Company has announced the election of technology executive Amy Chang and lululemon CEO Calvin McDonald to its Board of Directors, effective immediately. Both new members bring extensive experience in technology, consumer experience, and scaling major brands. Their appointments are expected to enhance Disney's focus on innovation and connecting with consumers.

title: Amy Chang and Calvin McDonald Elected to The Walt Disney Company Board of Directors
summary: The Walt Disney Company announced the election of Amy Chang and Calvin McDonald to its Board of Directors, effective immediately. Robert A. summary: The Walt Disney Company has appointed two new members to its board of directors: Silicon Valley veteran Amy Chang and Lululemon CEO Calvin McDonald. title: Electronic Arts Inc. stock remains steady Friday, underperforms market
summary: Electronic Arts Inc. (EA) stock remained unchanged on Friday despite an overall strong market performance, with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average both seeing gains. summary: The 2021 "Jeopardy!" Tournament of Champions concluded with Sam Kavanaugh, a substitute teacher from Carlton, Minn., claiming the $250,000 grand prize. Jennifer Quail and Veronica Vichit-Vadakan placed second and third, respectively. title: ‘Quiet Place’ and ‘Cruella’ Fuel Biggest Weekend of Covid Era
summary: The Memorial Day weekend box office saw a significant resurgence with the release of "A Quiet Place Part II" and "Cruella," marking the biggest weekend for movie theaters since early 2020. title: The Walt Disney Company’s Board Of Directors Adds Two
summary: The Walt Disney Company has appointed Amy Chang and Calvin McDonald to its Board of Directors, expanding the board from 10 to 12 members. Chang, a former Google executive and current Cisco executive, brings tech experience, while McDonald, CEO of Lululemon Athletica Inc., contributes trade expertise. title: With theme parks set to rebound this summer, travel advisors share trip tips
summary: As theme parks prepare for a rebound this summer, propelled by loosening restrictions and pent-up demand, experts predict a return to 2019 attendance levels as early as next year. Travel advisors are urging prospective visitors to book early, secure required reservations, and manage expectations, as the industry navigates a fluid post-pandemic landscape with new attractions and evolving safety measures. Despite some challenges, many parks are focusing on outdoor experiences and electronic transactions to maintain safety standards while offering a "fun" and "safe" environment.

title: 10 Things You Didn’t Know about Christopher Hopper
summary: This article details 10 lesser-known facts about Christopher Hopper, head of Aurora Solar, highlighting his extensive career in renewable energy, finance, and academia. summary: On the first day of Pride Month, a longtime executive, Joel Hopkins, filed a sexual orientation discrimination lawsuit against Disney, ABC Signature Studios, and Riverside Television Services. summary: Lionsgate has acquired the film rights to Steven Rowley's novel "The Guncle" for a movie adaptation. title: Disney Develops New Spider-Man Attraction Using Technology that Empowers Guests to Discover Web-Slinging Super Powers
summary: Disney's new attraction, WEB SLINGERS: A Spider-Man Adventure, opening on June 4, 2021, at Disney California Adventure park, allows guests to experience web-slinging like Spider-Man. Developed by Walt Disney Imagineering and part of the Avengers Campus, this interactive experience uses advanced technology, including AI, machine learning, and computer vision, to render virtual webs without the need for wearable tech beyond 3D glasses. summary: Disney Parks is launching a reimagined line of educational experiences called Disney Imagination Campus for student groups, based on their popular franchises and Walt Disney Imagineering. title: LDC’s “Mastergold” Cooking Oil E-store Live on JD.com
summary: Louis Dreyfus Company (LDC) has launched its first-ever e-store on JD.com, a major Chinese B2C online retailer, to sell its Mastergold cooking oils to Chinese consumers. title: Growth Stocks: Roku Inc.
summary: Roku Inc. (ROKU.US) is a US-based company known for its digital media players and streaming platform, which has seen significant growth in active users and revenue per user, especially during the COVID-19 pandemic. title: Will Disney Stock Split This Year? (NYSE:DIS)

title: Post-Pandemic Media Consumption: Online Streaming Accelerates A New Content Experience
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic significantly accelerated the shift to online media consumption, with streaming services becoming a primary source of entertainment. This trend has reshaped consumer expectations, leading to continued heavy TV/video consumption, a decline in offline media use, and a move away from movie theaters towards at-home viewing. Consumers are also seeking to replicate public viewing experiences within private social circles.

title: Blockbusters are back: New 'Fast & Furious' aims to jolt US movie-going
summary: Hollywood is releasing "F9," the ninth installment of the "Fast & Furious" saga, exclusively in theaters, marking the return of major blockbusters after COVID-19 impacted the movie business. Cinema operators hope the film will boost domestic ticket sales, which plummeted in 2020, as about 20% of U.S. theaters remain closed and capacity limits persist. Despite challenges, Universal Pictures is optimistic that "F9" will ignite the domestic box office, with predictions of $50 million to $70 million for its opening weekend.

title: Report: Comcast Considering Merger With ViacomCBS To Create Mega-Streamer
summary: Comcast is reportedly considering a merger with ViacomCBS to bolster its streaming strategy and compete with industry giants like Netflix and Disney. This speculation comes as ViacomCBS itself is undergoing internal restructuring to prioritize its streaming service, Paramount+. A potential merger would combine assets like Peacock and Paramount+, and Universal Pictures and Paramount Pictures, but would likely face significant regulatory challenges.

title: Why Steven Spielberg’s Netflix deal is not as groundbreaking as Netflix wants you to think
summary: Steven Spielberg's production company, Amblin Partners, struck a deal with Netflix, leading to significant media attention. While Netflix aims to leverage Spielberg's name for content and subscribers, the article argues the deal is not as groundbreaking as it seems, as Amblin's existing theatrical commitments with Universal remain unaffected, and Spielberg's personal directing projects are not exclusive to Netflix. The financial details and number of films in the Netflix deal also remain unspecified, dampening its perceived impact.

title: Storyland Studios welcomes veteran Disney Imagineer Jim Clark
summary: Storyland Studios has appointed veteran Disney Imagineer Jim Clark as its new Executive Director. Clark, who spent 27 years with the Walt Disney Company, including 20 years at Walt Disney Imagineering, contributed to projects at Walt Disney World, Disneyland, and Tokyo Disneyland, notably the Tokyo Disneyland Expansion. He brings extensive experience in themed entertainment design and a passion for creating immersive attractions, having worked alongside Imagineering legends like Marty Sklar.

title: Disney uses HPE for private cloud
summary: The Walt Disney Company continues to utilize Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) technology for its internal private cloud infrastructure, even as it has adopted Amazon Web Services (AWS) for its Disney+ streaming service. Disney maintains this long-running partnership due to the need for responsive internal servers, particularly for its diverse operations ranging from theme parks to stage shows. The company leverages HPE's Synergy composable infrastructure and VMware Cloud Foundation to provide cloud-like experiences with local resources for its "cast members" and support data-intensive operations at its theme parks.

title: Disney World offering $1,000 hiring bonuses to new staff
summary: The Walt Disney Company is offering $1,000 hiring bonuses for new housekeepers and culinary cast members at Walt Disney World to fill job openings for the summer season. To be eligible, new hires must stay on the job for at least 90 days, with the bonus paid in two installments after 90 and 150 days respectively. This initiative follows previous layoffs and aims to rehire staff, with other attractions like Six Flags and Universal Orlando also offering hiring incentives.

title: Visalia man participating in Nathan's Hot Dog Eating Contest
summary: Visalia resident Pablo Martinez is preparing for his seventh appearance at Nathan's Famous Hot Dog Eating contest on Coney Island. Ranked 21st in the world, he uses a "two dog and two bun technique" and hopes to consume close to his personal record of 32 hot dogs despite short notice for the event. Martinez describes the competition as an amazing experience with a mix of excitement and nervousness.

title: Target to remodel Franklin store that could include in-store shop by Ulta Beauty, Apple or Disney
summary: Target plans to remodel its Franklin, Wisconsin store as part of a larger initiative to renovate approximately 150 stores in 2021. title: Save Up to 40% Off Build-A-Bear Workshop Star Wars Toys And Check Out the New Jawas and Loth-Cats
summary: Build-A-Bear Workshop is having a sale on Star Wars merchandise, offering up to 40% off various items. This promotion coincides with the release of new Jawas and Loth-Cats plush toys. title: Seven members of Wake family, three others plead guilty in identity theft ring
summary: Ten individuals, including seven members of a Wake County family, have pleaded guilty to fraud charges stemming from a phony credit repair service. The ring defrauded Capital One, Discover, and Synchrony Bank by creating fictitious credit profiles, opening accounts with fraudulent identities, and defaulting on payments. All 10 face significant prison sentences, while charges are still pending against three other individuals, including the alleged ringleader Michael Anthony Griffin.

title: Kay Jewelers Follows the Way of ‘The Mandalorian’
summary: Kay Jewelers has launched a new limited-edition jewelry collection inspired by Disney's hit series "The Mandalorian." The six-piece collection features designs referencing characters like Grogu (Baby Yoda) and Ahsoka Tano, with prices ranging from $299 to $399. Each item comes in Star Wars-branded packaging.

title: Getting to Know Safra A. Catz: Oracle CEO, Newest Board Member of The Walt Disney, and Things We Did Not Know
summary: This article profiles Safra A. Catz, the CEO of Oracle and a board member of The Walt Disney Company. The piece also touches on her political involvement and some of the controversies Oracle faced during her leadership.

title: The Walt Disney may reinstate Bangladesh as Permitted Sourcing Country
summary: The Walt Disney Company is reportedly considering reinstating Bangladesh as a Permitted Sourcing Country, according to the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA). This move comes after Disney stopped sourcing from Bangladesh in 2013 following fire and building collapse disasters, and recognizes significant progress in workplace safety, social standards, and environmental sustainability within the industry. Factories participating in the ILO’s Better Work Bangladesh programme will be eligible to become vendors, provided they also participate in Nirapon or RMG Sustainability Council (RSC) and fulfill specific remediation criteria.

title: Universal movies to move to Peacock streaming service on quicker timeline

Additionally, Universal Pictures will begin producing original films specifically for Peacock to enhance its streaming content.

The film features original songs by Lin-Manuel Miranda and Carlos Vives and is set to release on November 24, 2021.

title: Top 30 Station Groups: Nexstar Still No. 1; Gray, Scripps, Allen Busy Buyers

Significant M&A activity, including Gray Television's acquisitions of Meredith and Quincy Media stations and E.W. Scripps' purchase of Ion Media, led to substantial shifts in the top 10 rankings. Gray Television climbed to second place, while Allen Media made the biggest jump, moving up eight spots to No. 14, propelled by station acquisitions.

title: |‘Black Widow’ Spins Up Big Debut at the Box Office
summary: |Marvel Studios' "Black Widow" achieved a strong box office debut, setting a pandemic-era record for Thursday night previews domestically with $13.2 million. The film earned $22.4 million in its first two international days and is receiving positive audience and critic reviews. It is now playing in theaters worldwide and on Disney+ with Premier Access.

title: La Bolsa porteña logró un alza de 3 por ciento en el comienzo semanal
summary: The Buenos Aires Stock Exchange (Bolsa porteña) saw a 3% increase at the start of the week, with the Merval index reaching 64,215.26 points. Argentine shares also rose sharply on Wall Street, led by BBVA, while public bonds showed a slight improvement. This positive movement aligns with global market gains and anticipated strong Q2 earnings reports from major US banks.

title: Netflix extends deal for animation films with Universal Pictures
summary: Netflix Inc. and Universal Pictures have extended their multi-year exclusive rights deal in the U.S. for animated film franchises like "Minions" and "Puss in Boots." This agreement allows Netflix to stream these DreamWorks Animation movies after a four-month window on Peacock, Universal's streaming service. The deal aims to retain Netflix's younger subscriber base, especially as other studios are bolstering their own streaming platforms.

title: Breaking: Disney confirms plans to build campus in Lake Nona and relocate 2,000 jobs here
summary: Walt Disney Co. has confirmed its plans to build a campus in Lake Nona, Orlando, and relocate 2,000 jobs from California. This move marks what is likely the biggest corporate relocation in Orlando's history.

title: Vera Bradley Announces a New Collaboration With Disney
summary: Vera Bradley has announced a new collaboration with Disney, launching "The Disney Collection by Vera Bradley." This collection features Disney's "Sensational Six" characters in hand-drawn designs across various Vera Bradley products. Available in stores and online, this marks an expanded distribution for their Disney-inspired merchandise, previously mostly limited to Disney Parks and their Disney Springs store.

title: Movie Theater Stocks Take Hit Amid Rising COVID-19 Cases, Streaming Uncertainty
summary: Movie theater stocks, including AMC, Cinemark, and Imax, experienced a significant sell-off due to rising concerns over the Delta variant of COVID-19 and Disney's disclosure of $60 million in Premier Access revenue for "Black Widow." Analysts noted that investor sentiment was affected by both macro-driven fears about the pandemic's impact on reopening businesses and anxieties about the future of theatrical distribution amidst increasing premium video-on-demand releases. Despite the downturn, some analysts believe the market is overlooking factors such as revenue sharing for PVOD platforms and piracy issues, suggesting that strong theatrical demand still exists.

title: Jonathan Katz Leaving Scripps To Start New Business Venture | Next TV | Broadcasting+Cable
summary: Jonathan Katz, who founded Bounce TV and Katz Networks, has resigned from Scripps to launch a new business venture. Katz Networks, which includes Bounce, Court TV, Grit, and Laff, was sold to Scripps for $302 million in 2017 and generated $257.5 million in revenue last year. Katz plans to create a new company focused on consumer needs, similar to his previous successful ventures.

title: Only at Applebee’s® Get a FREE* Movie Ticket to See Disney’s Jungle Cruise for the Ultimate Dinner and a Movie
summary: Applebee's is partnering with Disney to offer free movie tickets to Disney's Jungle Cruise with any $25 purchase. This promotion, running from July 19 through August 15, allows guests to receive up to four tickets, each valued at up to $15, for dine-in, To Go, or delivery orders. The initiative aims to revive the family tradition of dinner and a movie, coinciding with the film's release on July 30.

title: Formula One TV Ratings Up Big Amid Liberty Media Turnaround
summary: Formula One's TV ratings have significantly increased, particularly in the U.S., under Liberty Media's ownership, validating their modern approach to managing the sport. This growth is attracting investor interest and is expected to lead to substantial increases in broadcast, advertising, and sponsorship revenues, although some experts temper expectations for rights fee increases. The Netflix docuseries "Drive to Survive" and relaxed social media guidelines are credited with boosting F1's popularity and brand awareness.

title: When Will Cruises Resume in 2021?
summary: This article from July 2021 provides an extensive overview of when various cruise lines planned to resume operations globally, detailing the phased restart following the COVID-19 shutdown. It covers the situation in major markets like the UK, US, Canada, and Australia, highlighting restart dates for dozens of cruise lines and the challenges faced, including evolving health protocols and government regulations. The piece acknowledges the dynamic nature of the situation, with many dates subject to change.

title: Ulta to open first Target shop-in-shop locations in August
summary: Ulta Beauty and Target are set to launch their first shop-in-shop locations in August, with plans for 800 nationwide. These 1,000 square-foot Ulta at Target spaces will offer premium beauty brands and provide specialized training for Target employees. This partnership aims to expand both retailers' customer reach and enhance Target's presence in the beauty market.

title: Walt Disney Company To Receive Nearly $600M In Tax Credits To Relocate 2,000 Jobs To Florida
summary: The Walt Disney Company announced it will relocate approximately 2,000 jobs from Burbank/Glendale, California, to Orlando, Florida, in exchange for $580 million in tax credits over 19 years. The move is attributed to Florida's business-friendly climate, lower taxes, and better housing prices. This relocation is expected to impact local businesses in California and cause many current employees to lose their jobs, as corporations prioritize financial benefits over employee loyalty.

title: The Walt Disney Company Announces Participating Companies for 2021 Disney Accelerator Program
summary: The Walt Disney Company announced the eight participating companies for its 2021 Disney Accelerator program, which focuses on various innovative B2C technologies including messaging, frontier tech, e-commerce, data, and personalization. The selected companies will engage in a three-month mentorship connecting them with Disney's leadership and expertise to accelerate their growth. Bonnie Rosen has been appointed as the new General Manager for the program.

title: Exclusive: Jakks Pacific Unveils 2021 A Christmas Story, Super Mario Advent Calendars
summary: Jakks Pacific is expanding its seasonal offerings with two new advent calendars for 2021, exclusively revealed by The Toy Book. One calendar is based on "A Christmas Story," featuring figurines and artifacts from the film in a pop-up diorama of the Christmas Story House. The other is a Nintendo Super Mario advent calendar, an Amazon exclusive, that includes 24 characters and accessories, with special Santa Mario and Snowman Mario figures.

title: YouTube is a proven juggernaut that rivals Netflix in the streaming wars
summary: YouTube is emerging as a significant contender in the streaming wars, with its ad revenue growing at a much faster rate than Netflix's overall revenue. Despite the focus on subscription services, YouTube's substantial growth in ad revenue and increasing viewership on television sets position it as a key rival to traditional paid streaming platforms. The platform also shows potential for further expansion, with its short-form video service, YouTube Shorts, gaining traction and a large portion of the population still on traditional TV, offering ample room for all streamers to grow.

title: Disney Strikes Back Over Scarlett Johansson’s ‘Black Widow’ Lawsuit, Reveals Her $20 Million Payday – Update
summary: The Walt Disney Co. has responded to Scarlett Johansson’s lawsuit regarding the release of 'Black Widow', stating that the litigation shows a “callous disregard” for the Covid-19 pandemic and revealing she has received $20 million from the project to date. Johansson claims Disney breached her contract by releasing the film simultaneously on Disney+ and in theaters, impacting her potential box office-based compensation. The lawsuit highlights concerns within Hollywood about the financial implications for talent from day-and-date streaming releases.

title: Scarlett Johansson Is Suing Disney For Its Streaming Release Of 'Black Widow'
summary: Scarlett Johansson is suing Disney for releasing her movie 'Black Widow' simultaneously on streaming and in theaters, alleging a breach of contract. She claims her salary was partly based on box office performance, which was negatively impacted by the Disney+ release. Disney states it has complied with her contract and that the streaming release enhanced her earning potential.

title: The Walt Disney Co. Will Require That Salaried And Non-Union Hourly Employees In U.S. Be Vaccinated
summary: The Walt Disney Co. has announced a new requirement for all salaried and non-union hourly employees in the U.S. to be fully vaccinated against COVID-19. Unvaccinated employees working on site will have 60 days to comply, while new hires will need to be fully vaccinated before starting employment. The company is also discussing the mandate with unions representing its collectively bargained workers, citing health and safety as a top priority.

title: Walt Disney Co. announces mandate for workers to be vaccinated against COVID-19
summary: The Walt Disney Co. has announced a mandate requiring all salaried and non-union hourly workers in the United States to be vaccinated against COVID-19. This decision comes as Disneyland reopened with new mask requirements for all visitors indoors, regardless of vaccination status. The company is also negotiating with employee unions regarding vaccination requirements and will mandate vaccines for all new hires.

title: Walt Disney Co., Walmart adopt Covid vaccine requirements for employees
summary: Walmart and The Walt Disney Co. on Friday announced new policies requiring certain employees to be vaccinated against Covid-19. Walmart's mandate applies to headquarters staff and traveling managers, while Disney's covers all salaried and non-union hourly employees in the U.S., with a 60-day vaccination window. These moves come amid a rise in private employer vaccine mandates and a surge in Covid cases due to the delta variant.

title: Textbook Publisher Pearson Bets Big on Online Learning
summary: Pearson CEO Andy Bird is leading the textbook publisher's pivot towards online learning, aiming to attract college students with a new app and retain them for lifelong learning. The company saw significant growth in its online business, including a 40% enrollment increase in its K-12 Connections Academy, during the Covid-19 pandemic. This strategy capitalizes on the increasing need for new skills throughout careers.

title: Reese Witherspoon's Hello Sunshine to be sold to Blackstone-backed media company for $900 million
summary: Reese Witherspoon's media company, Hello Sunshine, is being sold to a Blackstone-backed media company for approximately $900 million. This new venture, spearheaded by former Disney executives Kevin Mayer and Tom Staggs, aims to build an independent entertainment company focused on content for the streaming era. Witherspoon will maintain an ownership stake and continue to oversee operations, with the goal of expanding content focused on women's stories.

title: Reese Witherspoon's Hello Sunshine gets scooped up by a Blackstone-backed media company
summary: Hello Sunshine, Reese Witherspoon's media company known for "Big Little Lies" and Reese's Book Club, has been acquired by a Blackstone-backed company led by former Disney executives Kevin Mayer and Tom Staggs. This deal allows Hello Sunshine to significantly increase its output of women-created stories across various platforms. Witherspoon emphasized that the partnership will enable the company to tell more entertaining, impactful, and illuminating stories globally.

title: Reese Witherspoon's media firm to be sold to Blackstone-backed company
summary: Reese Witherspoon's media company, Hello Sunshine, is being sold to a new media firm backed by Blackstone Group Inc. The deal, which values Hello Sunshine at about $900 million, comes amid a video streaming war and strong demand for high-quality content. Witherspoon and Hello Sunshine's CEO, Sarah Harden, will maintain significant equity and continue to oversee operations.

title: Roanoke’s Major Player in U.S. Electrical Power Industry Celebrates Half Century of Service
summary: Roanoke-based Virginia Transformer Corporation (VTC) celebrated its 50th anniversary, marking its growth from a small power transformer producer to the largest U.S.-based power transformer OEM. CEO Prabhat K. Jain announced two new corporate initiatives: an employee financial aid fund and a scholarship award for employees' children, aimed at attracting and retaining talent. VTC, an American-owned, Minority Business Enterprise, has supplied transformers for major clients like Tesla, NASA, and Walt Disney, and continues to be a key player in updating the U.S.'s aging energy infrastructure.

title: Disney Moves More Ops Out of California With NEW Vancouver Studio
summary: The Walt Disney Company's Walt Disney Animation Studios is opening a new studio in Vancouver, British Columbia, to focus on long-form series for Disney+. This move shifts some operations from their Burbank, California headquarters and follows news of Disney relocating over 2,000 jobs from California to Lake Nona, Florida. The Burbank studio will continue to lead feature films, while Vancouver's facility will concentrate on Disney+ series like the anticipated "Moana" musical series.

title: Walt Disney Imagineering Among Fast Company’s 2021 Best Workplaces for Innovators
summary: Walt Disney Imagineering has been recognized as one of Fast Company’s 2021 Best Workplaces for Innovators, an honor that highlights companies fostering cultures of innovation. This recognition stems from Imagineering's approach of combining diverse backgrounds and expertise, encompassing over 100 different disciplines, to create imaginative and technologically advanced experiences for Disney parks and attractions. The article cites the Spider-Man animatronic at Avengers Campus as a recent example of their innovative spirit.

title: Royal Caribbean expands mask requirement to Adventure of the Seas sailings
summary: This collection of articles from the Royal Caribbean Blog covers various aspects of cruising with Royal Caribbean, including a live blog from Navigator of the Seas, updates on vaccine policies for children with Disney Cruise Line, changes to COVID-19 testing for consecutive cruisers, future plans for Royal Caribbean ships and private destinations, and tips for cruising to Alaska in September. It also features a guide to sailing in Star Class and an interview with Royal Caribbean CEO Michael Bayley addressing health protocols, future plans, and mask policies. The articles provide detailed insights into the cruise experience, company strategies, and evolving health guidelines.

title: Disney’s Ultimate Princess Celebration Interactive Vanity and Rapunzel Doll Coming Soon from JAKKS Pacific
summary: JAKKS Pacific is releasing two new Disney Princess products for the holidays as part of Disney’s Ultimate Princess Celebration. These include the Enchanted Messages Musical Vanity, which features interactive messages from seven princesses and the theme song "Starting Now," and the Magic in Motion Hair Glow Rapunzel Doll, which talks, sings "I See the Light," and has glowing hair. Both toys are designed for ages 3 and up and will be available for pre-order.

title: Hasbro Inc. stock outperforms market on strong trading day
summary: Hasbro Inc. (HAS) stock increased by 0.49% to $98.68 on Tuesday, outperforming the S&P 500 Index and the Dow Jones Industrial Average. This marks the second consecutive day of gains for the stock, placing it $6.21 below its 52-week high. Hasbro's performance was mixed compared to competitors, with Walt Disney Co. rising and Nintendo Co. Ltd. ADR falling, while Activision Blizzard Inc. also saw gains.

title: Reese Witherspoon's $900-million deal
summary: Reese Witherspoon recently sold a majority stake in her production company, Hello Sunshine, to a group backed by Blackstone, valuing the company at $900 million. This deal is part of a larger trend in Hollywood, driven by the streaming boom, where private equity firms are investing heavily in content creation and talent. The move allows creators like Witherspoon to maintain more control over their projects and maximize their value in a competitive market dominated by streaming giants.

title: Disney to Pay NHL $350M for Stake in Streaming Tech Platform
summary: The Walt Disney Co. will acquire the National Hockey League's 10 percent stake in Disney Streaming Services for $350 million. This move will increase Disney's ownership in the technology platform, which powers its streaming services like Disney+ and ESPN+, to 85 percent, with Major League Baseball retaining the remaining 15 percent. The NHL exercised its buyout option, and the deal is expected to close by the end of fiscal 2021.

title: Disney reports post-Covid rebound as theme parks reopen
summary: Disney reported a significant post-pandemic recovery, driven by the reopening of its theme parks in the US, France, and China, which returned the parks and consumer products division to profit. The company also saw substantial growth in its streaming service Disney+, attracting 12 million new subscribers and surpassing analyst expectations with a total of 116 million global users. Overall, Disney's revenue increased by 45% year-on-year to $17bn, exceeding analyst estimates.

title: Jakks Pacific Bounds Into Fall With Disney ily 4EVER Fashion Doll Line
summary: Jakks Pacific has launched its new Disney ily 4EVER Fashion Doll Line, featuring 18-inch dolls inspired by Disney characters and the trend of "DisneyBounding" by adult fans. The initial wave includes characters like Olaf, Cinderella, Tinker Bell, Ariel, and Minnie Mouse, with more beloved characters planned for future releases. These dolls will be exclusively available at Target starting August 15.

title: ‘Free Guy,’ Disney Gaming Comedy, Tops Weekend Box Office
summary: The Walt Disney Co. film "Free Guy" topped the U.S. box office during its opening weekend, likely boosted by its exclusive theatrical run without concurrent streaming release. Starring Ryan Reynolds and Jodie Comer, the comedy's strong performance highlights the potential advantage of traditional theatrical windows. The movie's success comes amidst a competitive landscape for film releases.

title: Disney Stock Stalls Despite Impressive Earnings, The Reason Is Simple
summary: Despite impressive Q3 earnings and positive news from its various divisions, Disney's stock has stalled and reset to pre-earnings report numbers. The primary reason for this lack of sustained momentum is attributed to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, particularly the rise of new variants and vaccine hesitancy. While Disney's direct-to-consumer streaming services have thrived, its major revenue streams like theme parks and box office are highly susceptible to the pandemic's impact, making investors wary.

title: China Poised To Play A Larger Role In Global Entertainment Business: IMAX CEO
summary: IMAX CEO Richard Gelfond states that China is poised to play a larger role in the global entertainment business due to its large population, increasing demographics, and growing film quality and budgets. IMAX's success in China is attributed to its long-standing presence, focus on local film studios, and the rising popularity of animated and local language films. Gelfond anticipates the Chinese box office for Hollywood films will normalize once global release patterns resume post-pandemic, while local film trends in China will likely continue to strengthen.

title: Comcast, ViacomCBS to launch streaming service SkyShowtime in Europe
summary: Comcast and ViacomCBS are partnering to launch a new streaming service called SkyShowtime in various European markets. This joint venture aims to compete with major players like Netflix and Disney+ by offering content from Nickelodeon, Paramount+, Sky, and Peacock. The collaboration allows both companies to cost-effectively expand their reach into smaller European territories where they currently lack a strong presence.

title: Disney World replaces free FastPass system with paid reservation service
summary: Walt Disney World is replacing its free FastPass+ system with a new paid service called Disney Genie+, which will allow guests to purchase attraction reservations through Lightning Lane. The new service offers different tiers, including a $15 per day option for multiple rides and a separate pay-per-ride option for individual popular attractions. Disney Genie will also offer free features like personalized itineraries and forecasted wait times, aiming to enhance the guest experience by reducing planning and waiting times.

title: Netflix and Hulu Failed to Register, Pay Fees Required Under New Jersey Law
summary: A class action lawsuit alleges that Netflix and Hulu have failed to register and pay required fees under the New Jersey Cable Television Act (CTA). The lawsuit, filed by the Borough of Longport and Township of Irvington, claims that both streaming giants operate in New Jersey without proper authorization, depriving municipalities of revenue. The plaintiffs contend that Netflix and Hulu's subscription services are comparable to cable television, making them subject to the CTA's franchise fees and registration requirements.

title: Naver to create webtoons of DC Comics' series, HYBE artists
summary: Naver Webtoon Corp. is collaborating with DC Comics and HYBE Co. to produce webtoons based on their content and artists, including original DC Comics series and exclusive content featuring BTS. This move intensifies competition with Kakao Corp., which has also partnered with DC Comics and Marvel Studios for similar webtoon projects, reflecting the expanding rivalry between the two South Korean platform giants. The article also highlights the significant earnings of Naver's webtoon creators, with one earning 12.4 billion won last year.

title: How Stryve Foods Plans to Make Biltong a Household Name
summary: Stryve Foods, a healthy snack brand, saw a 65% increase in year-over-year sales in the first half of 2021, capitalizing on the heightened demand for snacks, particularly dried meat, during the pandemic. The company is focused on making biltong, a South African dried meat snack, a mainstream household name in the growing market for meat snacks. The article highlights the broader trend of increased snacking globally and its impact on consumer eating habits and the snack industry.

title: Target to add more than 100 Disney shops to stores as holiday season approaches
summary: Target plans to nearly triple the number of Disney shops within its stores to over 160 by year-end, turning its locations into "mini-malls" to drive foot traffic ahead of the holiday season. This expansion positions Target to capitalize on toy sales, following Macy's similar move to open Toys R Us shops. The retailer also announced an exclusive toy collection with FAO Schwarz, reinforcing its strategy to create unique shopping experiences and elevate its merchandising.

title: Disney Store closings: Is your closest location holding a liquidation sale? See new closures list.
summary: The Walt Disney Co. is closing nearly 60 of its full-size retail locations across the U.S. by September 15, 2021, while Target plans to open over 100 new Disney shops within its stores. This move is part of Disney's strategy to shift focus towards its e-commerce business, recognizing changing consumer behavior. The article provides an extensive list of Disney Store locations slated for closure across various states.

title: Official Disney Castle Posted on Zillow For Only $157.99
summary: Hasbro has launched a unique marketing campaign for its new Disney Princess Ultimate Celebration Castle by listing it on Zillow as an official home. This initiative, part of Disney's Ultimate Princess Celebration and World Princess Week, allows "buyers" to browse an interactive listing complete with intricate details, room descriptions, and fictional previous visitors. The toy, standing four feet tall, is available for purchase on Amazon for $157.99, blending real estate fantasy with product promotion.

title: Here's when SeaWorld Orlando's delayed new Ice Breaker roller coaster finally will debut
summary: SeaWorld Orlando's new Ice Breaker roller coaster, originally delayed due to the pandemic, is now set to open in February 2022. The highly anticipated attraction will finally welcome guests almost two years after its initially planned debut. This announcement comes as SeaWorld navigates ongoing changes in its executive team and records strong revenue performance.

title: Target expands its Disney partnership
summary: Target Corp. is expanding its partnership with Disney, tripling the number of Disney shop-in-shops within its stores. This expansion comes as the retailer also released its list of "must-have" toys for the 2021 holiday season, signaling a focus on toys and partnerships. The article also mentions related news about other toy retail collaborations.

title: Synovus Bank Provides $45M Construction Loan on Orlando Rental Project
summary: Synovus Bank has provided a $45 million construction loan to The Cornerstone Group for the development of Urbon at Nona, a 360-unit multifamily community in Orlando, Florida. This four-year, fixed-rate loan will finance the construction of the large-scale residential and commercial property, with vertical construction slated to begin in August. The project aims to meet the high demand for quality housing in the growing Lake Nona area, near major employment centers and the Orlando International Airport.

title: Delta Air Lines, Airbnb, Peloton: Stocks That Defined the Week
summary: This article highlights major companies whose stocks were influenced by news events during the week. Delta Air Lines announced a monthly $200 health-insurance surcharge for unvaccinated employees, leading to a 1.9% rise in its shares. The piece also mentions vaccination policies from Goldman Sachs and Walt Disney Co.
