title: Power Rangers ‘ Mother of All Megazords Leads the Week’s Biggest Toys
summary: This article highlights new toy releases, including Hasbro's Power Rangers Lightning Collection Zord Ascension Project Mighty Morphin Dino Megazord, a full-size replica of Bo-Katan Kryze’s helmet from Star Wars, and Lego's Creator 3-in-1 Majestic Tiger. It also features McFarlane Toys' second wave of Disney Mirrorverse figures. The Power Rangers Megazord is presented as a lavish, transformable collector's item, and the Lego tiger is noted for a surprising anatomical detail that caused a stir among fans.

title: Houston, We Have a NextGen TV Launch
summary: Ten local TV stations in Houston, the eighth-largest TV market in the U.S., have launched ATSC 3.0 broadcasts, marking the largest NextGen TV rollout to date. This collaborative effort by various station groups aims to enhance the viewing experience with improved audio and video quality, and explore new business opportunities. The launch merges over-the-air antenna TV with the internet, bringing advanced features to viewers.

title: Score! Cinemark Teams Up with ESPN to Bring College Football Playoff Games to the Big Screen
summary: Cinemark and ESPN are partnering to bring College Football Playoff Semifinals and the National Championship to select Cinemark theaters. Fans can watch the games, including pre-game programming, in an immersive environment for $10, which includes a concessions package and special prizes. This collaboration offers a unique viewing experience for college football enthusiasts across various U.S. markets.

title: Disney Extends CFO Christine McCarthy’s Contract Through 2024
summary: Walt Disney Co. has extended Christine McCarthy's contract as Senior Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer through June 30, 2024. McCarthy, a 22-year Disney veteran, has served as CFO since 2015 and oversees the company’s worldwide finance organization. CEO Bob Chapek praised her leadership as instrumental during a period of disruption and transformation for the company.

title: ‘Spider-Man’ $260 million debut smashes pandemic-era record
summary: “Spider-Man: No Way Home” shattered pandemic-era box office records with a $260.1 million debut in North America, marking the second-highest domestic opening weekend of all time. This success, driven by a core demographic of 18-to-34-year-old fans, offers hope for the theater industry's recovery in 2022, despite ongoing challenges like the Omicron variant and uneven audience return. Sony's decision for a theatrical-only release underscored the cultural impact of exclusive cinematic experiences.

title: The Walt Disney Company Extends Chief Financial Officer Christine M. Mccarthy’s Contract Through June 30, 2024
summary: The Walt Disney Company has extended the contract of Chief Financial Officer Christine M. McCarthy through June 30, 2024. CEO Bob Chapek highlighted McCarthy's indispensable leadership during a period of disruption and transformation, praising her contributions to the company's growth and navigation through the pandemic. McCarthy, a 22-year Disney veteran and CFO since 2015, expressed her privilege in the role and her commitment to delivering shareholder value.

title: The Walt Disney Company Names Horacio Gutierrez as General Counsel and Secretary
summary: The Walt Disney Company has appointed Horacio Gutierrez as Senior Executive Vice President, General Counsel, and Secretary, effective February 1, 2022. Gutierrez, previously Spotify's Head of Global Affairs and Chief Legal Officer, will oversee all legal affairs for Disney worldwide and report directly to CEO Bob Chapek. He succeeds Alan Braverman, who is retiring after nearly two decades in the role.

title: Sony, Zee finalise merger even as courtroom feud continues
summary: Sony's India unit and local rival Zee Entertainment have finalized a merger deal to combine their television channels, film assets, and streaming platforms. This alliance aims to compete with major streaming players like Netflix and Disney in India and will create the country's largest media entity, with Sony holding the majority stake. title: The Walt Disney Company Names Horacio Gutierrez as General Counsel and Secretary
summary: The Walt Disney Company announced the appointment of Horacio Gutierrez as Senior Executive Vice President, General Counsel and Secretary, effective February 1, 2022. Gutierrez joins Disney from Spotify, where he was Head of Global Affairs and Chief Legal Officer, and will succeed the retiring Alan Braverman. He will oversee Disney's global legal affairs, serving as the chief legal officer and strategic advisor to executive leadership and the Board of Directors.

title: The definitive ranking of streaming services as we head into 2022
summary: This article ranks the top streaming services as of late 2021, evaluating their performance and strategies during the "streaming wars." HBO Max emerged as a strong contender due to its day-and-date movie releases and popular original series, while Amazon Prime Video expanded its focus with major event films and Netflix saw a resurgence with global hits like "Squid Game." Apple TV+ demonstrated growth with acclaimed originals, though Disney Plus and Hulu faced challenges related to content strategy and corporate interests, respectively.

title: Pelosi's husband bets big on Google, Salesforce, Disney after speaker defends lawmaker transactions
summary: Weeks after House Speaker Nancy Pelosi defended stock trading by lawmakers and their spouses, her husband, Paul Pelosi, made significant purchases in Google, Salesforce, and Disney call options. title: Fare thee well, Mr. Iger. And also, thank you. For everything.
summary: This article serves as a farewell and thank you to Robert Iger on his last day with The Walt Disney Company. title: Disney in Danger of Losing Copyright Protection For Many Beloved Characters
summary: The Walt Disney Company is facing challenges with copyright law as several beloved characters, including the original Winnie the Pooh and friends from A.A. Milne's books, are set to enter the public domain. Investors should note the significant revenue Winnie the Pooh generates for Disney, though other companies may now use the original stories as inspiration for new creations.

title: Hasbro Promotes Chris Cocks to CEO
summary: Hasbro has named Chris Cocks as its new CEO, succeeding the late Brian Goldner and interim CEO Rich Stoddart. Cocks, previously president and COO of Wizards of the Coast and digital gaming, will focus on evolving Hasbro’s brand blueprint strategy and generating growth. Eric Nyman has been appointed president and COO of Hasbro, while Stoddart will become chair of the board.

title: Watch the Beatles' final performance at the Indiana State Museum Imax for one night only
summary: The Indiana State Museum Imax will host a one-night-only screening of "The Beatles: Get Back -- The Rooftop Concert" on January 30, 2022, to celebrate the 53rd anniversary of their final performance. The event will include restored footage and a Q&A with filmmaker Peter Jackson. Tickets are $25, and the Imax manager expects the show to sell out.

title: Disney and Pixar’s ‘Turning Red’ to Premiere Exclusively on Disney+ on March 11
summary: Disney Media & Entertainment Distribution announced that Disney and Pixar’s new film, "Turning Red," will premiere exclusively on Disney+ worldwide on Friday, March 11, 2022. This decision was made due to the delayed box office recovery, especially for family films, allowing Disney to prioritize delivering content to its global audience. The movie tells the story of Mei Lee, a 13-year-old who transforms into a giant red panda when she gets too excited.

title: Walt Disney Co. stock outperforms market on strong trading day
summary: Walt Disney Co. (DIS) stock rose 0.59% to $157.83 on a generally down trading day for the market, outperforming the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average. This marks the second consecutive day of gains for Disney, though its stock remains $45.19 below its 52-week high. The company also outpaced competitor Comcast Corp. Cl A (CMCSA).

title: Bob Chapek’s Memo to Staff: Disney Has Three “Strategic Pillars” Moving Forward
summary: Walt Disney Co. CEO Bob Chapek outlined three key strategic pillars for the company's future in a memo to staff as Disney approaches its 100th anniversary. These pillars include "storytelling excellence" with a focus on new monthly creative meetings, "innovation" leveraging the company's franchise ecosystem and exploring new "canvases like the metaverse," and a "relentless focus on our audience" by evolving with changing consumer entertainment behaviors. Chapek emphasized adapting to how technology and the pandemic are rapidly altering audience preferences while also thanking employees for their resilience.

title: The Walt Disney Company Celebrates Black Culture, Voices and Experiences at AfroTech World 2021
summary: The Walt Disney Company participated in AfroTech World 2021 as a diamond sponsor, reiterating its commitment to Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion by celebrating the Black community and actively recruiting diverse talent. Disney hosted virtual events, engaged with attendees, and facilitated discussions on Black life experiences and technological advancements within the company. The company emphasizes AfroTech World as a crucial platform for Black technologists to find representation and opportunities within Disney.

title: New Digital Dimensions in MSG Sports and Entertainment
summary: Infosys has partnered with Madison Square Garden (MSG) as the Official Digital Innovation Partner for properties like the New York Knicks, New York Rangers, and the Madison Square Garden Arena. This partnership aims to enhance fan experiences through digital technologies, including real-time operational updates, in-depth game statistics, and data-powered solutions for eSports. Infosys will leverage applied AI, data analytics, and digital experiences to transform entertainment.

title: Big Leadership Changes at Gelson’s
summary: Gelson's Markets has announced significant leadership changes, promoting John Bagan to COO and Ron Johnson to CIO. Additionally, the Southern California grocer has hired Clare Bogle as its new CFO. These appointments aim to strengthen the executive team as the company continues to operate its 27 specialty grocery stores.

title: China's YouTube Bilibili Reveals New Banned Games List & Bans GTA
summary: Bilibili, China's largest video sharing platform, has published a new list of over 70 banned games that cannot be streamed or shared on its platform. This list includes popular titles like the entire GTA and Battlefield series, Resident Evil games, and nearly all visual novels not rated for "all-ages." The ban follows recent self-regulation by Genshin Impact which modified character outfits on Chinese servers to avoid stricter censorship.

title: NBCUniversal partners with iSpot.tv for alternate ratings measurement
summary: NBCUniversal has partnered with iSpot.tv in a multi-year deal to measure its audience, moving away from traditional TV measurement methods. This comes amidst widespread dissatisfaction with Nielsen's ability to accurately capture evolving viewing habits, especially with the rise of streaming. The partnership aims to provide second-by-second measurement for linear, streaming, and time-shifted viewing, starting with the Beijing Olympics and Super Bowl LVI.

title: Tickets for D23 Expo: The Ultimate Disney Fan Event Presented by Visa® Go on Sale January 20, 2022
summary: Tickets for D23 Expo 2022, presented by Visa, will go on sale January 20, 2022, with a presale for Visa cardholders who are also D23 Members starting January 19. The event, hosted by D23: The Official Disney Fan Club, will take place September 9-11 at the Anaheim Convention Center, celebrating Disney entertainment and kicking off Disney100, the company's centennial celebration. It will feature over 50 shows, presentations, and panels, including the Disney Legends Awards Ceremony, the Mousequerade costume contest, and an exhibit of Walt Disney's restored Grumman Gulfstream I company airplane.

title: A Tinder Revenge Story
summary: This article details the legal battle between Tinder co-founder Sean Rad and media mogul Barry Diller’s company, IAC, over the valuation of Tinder. Rad accused IAC of deliberately undervaluing the company, costing him a significant portion of his stock options. The contentious lawsuit, marked by personal animosity and accusations, ultimately concluded with a $441 million settlement for Rad and his co-plaintiffs, highlighting the emotional and financial stakes involved in the tech industry's ownership disputes.

title: Experience Chloé Zhao's Full Vision For 'Eternals' at Home with IMAX
summary: Marvel Studios' "Eternals," directed by Chloé Zhao, is now streaming on Disney+ with IMAX's Expanded Aspect Ratio, allowing viewers to experience the film closer to the filmmaker's original vision. The article highlights how IMAX's technology enhances the storytelling, particularly showcasing the vast scale of the Celestials and the immersive quality of select scenes. Bruce Markoe of IMAX and Evan Jacobs of Marvel Studios explain the technical adaptations made for home viewing while preserving Zhao's artistic intent.

title: Netflix raises monthly subscription prices in U.S., Canada
summary: Netflix has increased its monthly subscription prices in the U.S. and Canada by $1 to $2, depending on the plan, to fund new programming and maintain competitiveness in the streaming market. The standard U.S. plan now costs $15.49, up from $13.99, while the Canadian standard plan rose to C$16.49 from C$14.99. These increases, the first since October 2020 in these markets, reflect Netflix's pricing power as it faces growing competition from other major streaming services.

title: Here’s How Warren Buffett Persuaded Google’s Reluctant Founders to Go Public
summary: Google co-founders Sergey Brin and Larry Page were initially hesitant to take their company public due to fears of losing control. A serendipitous meeting with Warren Buffett, who shared his strategy of a two-tier stock structure used at Berkshire Hathaway, convinced them that they could go public while retaining control. This led Google to adopt a similar stock structure for its IPO and publish an "Owner's Manual" outlining their long-term philosophy for shareholders.

title: Disney+ Debuts Trailer and Poster for Marvel Studios’ ‘Moon Knight’
summary: Disney+ has released a new trailer and poster for Marvel Studios’ upcoming series, 'Moon Knight,' which is set to premiere on March 30. The series follows Steven Grant, a mild-mannered employee who discovers he shares a body with mercenary Marc Spector due to dissociative identity disorder, leading them into a dangerous mystery involving Egyptian gods. Oscar Isaac, Ethan Hawke, and May Calamawy star, with Jeremy Slater as head writer and Kevin Feige among the executive producers.

title: Netflix earnings to set the pace for 2022 streaming wars
summary: Netflix is set to report its fourth-quarter earnings this week, which will provide insight into the growth of streaming services in 2022. The company, along with competitors like Disney and Amazon, is investing heavily in new content amid intensifying "streaming wars." Analysts expect Netflix's growth to stabilize in 2022, primarily driven by international markets, as competition for subscribers increases, especially in the U.S.

title: The Walt Disney Company Promotes a Handful of Executives to New Positions to Support the Newly Created International Content Group
summary: The Walt Disney Company announced promotions for several executives to bolster its direct-to-consumer business and international content creation. Rebecca Campbell will lead the newly formed International Content Group as Chairman, focusing on localized content for Disney's streaming services. Additionally, Michael Paull is now President of Disney Streaming, overseeing Disney+, Hulu, ESPN+, and Star+ globally, with Joe Earley appointed as President of Hulu.

title: Disney CEO Bob Chapek's pay doubles to $32.5 million as cash bonuses return to the Mouse House
summary: Walt Disney Co. CEO Bob Chapek's compensation doubled to $32.5 million in fiscal year 2021, driven by a return of cash bonuses for executives as the company recovered from the pandemic. This package included a $14.3 million bonus, a $2.5 million salary, and significant stock awards and options. Former executive chairman Bob Iger also saw substantial compensation, earning $45.9 million in the same period for his creative oversight.

title: Netflix misses subscriber target, shares fall on weak forecast
summary: Netflix Inc fell short of analyst predictions for new subscribers in the fourth quarter of last year, adding 8.3 million customers against a projected 8.4 million. This, along with a weaker forecast for early 2022 due to increased competition, caused its shares to drop by 10 percent in after-hours trading. The company's global subscriber count reached 221.8 million, and it is now focusing on overseas growth after raising prices in the US and Canada.

title: Hudi powering data lake efforts at Walmart and Disney+ Hotstar
summary: Apache Hudi, an open-source data lake platform, is gaining significant adoption among large enterprises like Uber, Walmart, and Disney+ Hotstar. The article highlights how these companies are leveraging Hudi for scalable data management, improved performance, and efficient analytics, addressing challenges previously faced with other data management systems. Walmart and Disney+ Hotstar specifically detail their migration to Hudi and its benefits, while Uber continues to utilize and contribute to the project.

title: Netflix stock drops after streaming giant predicts subscriber slowdown. (Published 2022)
summary: Netflix's stock dropped nearly 20 percent after the company announced it added 8.3 million subscribers in Q4 but forecast only 2.5 million additions for the current quarter. This projection signals one of the slowest growth periods for the streaming giant in years, despite strong performance in the U.S. and Canada. Co-chief executive Reed Hastings expressed frustration, attributing the slowdown potentially to COVID-19 effects or increased competition from services like Disney+ and HBO Max.

title: Netflix tanks again as investors question growth prospects
summary: Netflix shares continued to fall after the company announced a significant slowdown in subscriber growth, missing analyst forecasts and marking its slowest annual growth pace since 2016. Despite these challenges, some Wall Street analysts remain optimistic, viewing the subscriber shortfall as a forecasting issue rather than an existential threat, particularly given Netflix's strong international expansion prospects.

title: The Walt Disney Company Announces New Leadership Roles for Trisha Husson, Eric Marcotte with Disney General Entertainment
summary: The Walt Disney Company has announced new leadership roles within its Disney General Entertainment (DGE) division. Trisha Husson has been named head of Strategy, Business Operations and Finance for DGE, overseeing financial planning, content analytics, and other strategic functions. Eric Marcotte will take on Husson's previous role as senior vice president overseeing the Strategy & Business Operations team for DGE.

title: Liberty Media Is World’s Largest Sports Empire
summary: Liberty Media leads as the world's largest sports empire, valued at $17.2 billion, significantly outpacing its competitors. The sports empire landscape is expanding, with the top 20 empires now collectively worth $124 billion, a 22% increase from the previous year. This growth is fueled by major media deals for leagues like the NFL and NHL, alongside a trend of multi-team ownership, especially in soccer, as investors seek more diverse portfolios.

title: For Netflix stock, it's like the pandemic never happened
summary: Netflix shares have fallen to their lowest level since April 2020, erasing gains made during the pandemic, due to concerns over subscriber growth. The company reported a much lower subscriber forecast for the first quarter, spooking investors and raising concerns for other media companies that have transitioned to streaming. This decline signals a potential revaluation for streaming competitors as well.

title: Abigail Disney Directing New Movie Criticizing Treatment of Cast Members
summary: Abigail Disney, granddaughter of Disney co-founder Roy O. Disney, has co-directed a new film, "The American Dream and Other Fairy Tales," which critically examines economic inequality in the U.S. and Disney's treatment of its cast members. The film highlights the disparity between executive compensation and cast member wages, with Disneyland and Walt Disney World cast members earning significantly less per hour than the combined $80 million earned by CEOs Bob Chapek and Bob Iger last year. While Disney has not yet secured a distributor, the film aims to spark a conversation about a more equitable future.

title: Electronic Arts and Lucasfilm Games Announce New Star Wars Titles in Development From Respawn Entertainment
summary: Electronic Arts and Lucasfilm Games have announced an expanded collaboration to develop three new Star Wars titles through Respawn Entertainment. These include the next game in the Star Wars Jedi franchise, a new Star Wars first-person shooter led by Peter Hirschmann, and a Star Wars strategy game developed in partnership with Bit Reactor. Vince Zampella of Respawn will oversee these projects, and work has already begun on all three.

title: Electronic Arts and Lucasfilm Games Announce New Star Wars Titles in Development From Respawn Entertainment
summary: Electronic Arts and Lucasfilm Games announced the development of three new Star Wars titles by Respawn Entertainment: the next game in the Star Wars Jedi franchise, a new Star Wars first-person shooter directed by Peter Hirschmann, and a Star Wars strategy game in collaboration with Bit Reactor. Vince Zampella of Respawn will oversee these projects, emphasizing Respawn's history in game development and storytelling within the Star Wars universe. Work has already begun on all three games, and Respawn is actively seeking new talent.

title: Mattel Rises After Winning Back Disney Princess Toys From Hasbro
summary: Mattel Inc. shares jumped after the company announced it won back the global licensing agreement to produce toys based on Walt Disney Co.’s princesses and the "Frozen" movies. This marks a significant comeback for Mattel, which lost these rights to Hasbro Inc. in 2016. The new toy collection is expected to be available for sale at the beginning of 2023.

title: Mattel wins back Disney Princess toys from Hasbro
summary: Mattel has reacquired the licensing rights for Disney Princess toys from Hasbro. This move signifies a notable shift in the competitive landscape of the toy industry, with Mattel regaining a valuable franchise.

title: Mattel Wins Back Disney Princess and ‘Frozen’ Toys Licensing Deal From Hasbro
summary: Mattel has reacquired the licensing rights for Disney Princess and 'Frozen' toys from Hasbro, a deal it lost in 2016. This multiyear global pact allows Mattel to produce a new line of dolls and figures for early 2023, building on their existing relationship with Disney for Pixar franchises. The news led to a 6.63% increase in Mattel's stock during pre-market trading.

title: Mattel Stock Soars After Regaining License to Make ‘Frozen,’ Disney Princess Toys
summary: Mattel's stock surged after the company announced it had regained the global licensing rights to produce toys based on Walt Disney's Princess and Frozen franchises, lines it previously lost to Hasbro in 2016. The new agreement expands on Mattel's existing relationship with Disney for other properties like Toy Story and Cars, with new products expected in 2023. Meanwhile, rival Hasbro also had positive news, renewing its Star Wars licensing deal and securing rights for Indiana Jones toys.

title: Netflix: Why the world's biggest streaming service is frustrated with India
summary: Netflix, despite its global success, is struggling to gain significant traction in the competitive Indian streaming market. With 5.5 million subscribers, it lags far behind rivals like Disney+ Hotstar and Amazon Prime Video, which have focused on local content, sports, and bundled services. Experts suggest Netflix needs to localize its content more deeply and move beyond its "international playbook" to attract a wider Indian audience.

title: Genius Brands Promotes Industry Leader Kerry Phelan to Chief Brand Officer
summary: Genius Brands International, Inc. (Nasdaq: GNUS) has promoted Kerry Phelan to the newly created position of Chief Brand Officer. This move follows the company's significant expansion, including acquisitions of WOW! Unlimited Media, Inc. and Ameba TV, and a major investment in Your Family Entertainment. Phelan, who has a distinguished 30-year career in consumer products and retail with major studios, will now spearhead global brand strategy, consumer products, and partnerships for Genius Brands' growing portfolio of children's properties.

title: Wall Street gains evaporate, S&P 500 ends lower on Fed tightening timeline
summary: The S&P 500 ended lower after the U.S. Federal Reserve indicated it would soon raise interest rates to combat persistent inflation. All three major U.S. stock indexes swung wildly, with the Dow and S&P 500 closing in negative territory, while Nasdaq saw a nominal gain. The market reacted strongly to Fed Chair Jerome Powell's comments about inflation and supply problems being more severe and long-lasting than anticipated.

title: Universal Studios Orlando Leads NBCU Theme Parks, Epic Universe Next
summary: NBCUniversal's theme parks had their most profitable fourth quarter ever, driven by strong performance at Universal Studios Orlando, Hollywood, and Japan. Despite some limitations from COVID-19, especially in Beijing, the division saw significant revenue and EBITDA growth. Construction on the new Epic Universe theme park in Orlando is progressing rapidly, with an opening planned by summer 2025, representing Comcast/NBCUniversal's largest theme park investment to date.

title: Reddit 'antiwork' forum implodes, goes private after train wreck interview with Fox News
summary: The popular Reddit forum /r/Antiwork went private after a moderator, Doreen Ford, gave a widely criticized interview to Fox News's Jesse Watters. The interview, where Ford appeared disheveled and stated "laziness is a virtue," caused an internet backlash and led to accusations from users of misrepresenting the subreddit's goals. Consequently, Ford was removed from her moderation duties, and many users migrated to a new subreddit, /r/WorkReform.

title: Revolving Door Roundup: Havas Media Group, Joan, Shadow and More
summary: This article summarizes recent noteworthy developments in the advertising and marketing agency world. It details new partnerships, rebrands, and agency launches, including Havas Media Group becoming Edgewell's media agency of record, Joan being selected by S&P Global, and Dolphin Entertainment creating a new Web3-focused agency. The roundup also highlights marketing campaigns featuring celebrity endorsements and innovative technological activations.

title: Disney Names Former J.P. Morgan Analyst Alexia Quadrani As Head Of Investor Relations
summary: The Walt Disney Co. has appointed Alexia Quadrani, a former J.P. Morgan media analyst, as its new head of investor relations. She replaces Lowell Singer and will report directly to CFO Christine McCarthy. Quadrani will be the company's liaison with Wall Street, managing relationships with analysts and investors, and advising senior management on financial matters.

title: Univision cerró acuerdo con Televisa para una nueva plataforma de streaming
summary: Univision and Televisa have finalized a $4.8 billion merger, creating a new Spanish-language media giant called TelevisaUnivision Inc. This agreement paves the way for a new streaming service, which will feature both free and premium tiers with a wide range of entertainment, sports, and news content. Despite growing competition in the streaming market, Univision aims to leverage its extensive programming library and vast network of broadcast and cable channels to promote the new platform.

title: AT&T opts for WarnerMedia spinoff in Discovery merger, cuts dividend
summary: AT&T announced it will spin off WarnerMedia in a $43 billion transaction to merge its media properties with Discovery Inc., and subsequently cut its dividend by nearly half. AT&T shareholders will own 71% of the new Warner Bros. Discovery company and receive 0.24 shares for each AT&T share. The move aims to reduce AT&T's debt and positions the new entity, Warner Bros Discovery, to compete in the streaming market against rivals like Netflix.

title: Televisa y Univision se fusionan para lanzar nueva empresa de streaming y competir con Netflix
summary: Televisa and Univision have merged to create TelevisaUnivision, Inc., a new streaming company aimed at becoming the dominant Spanish-language content producer globally. This new venture seeks to compete with major streaming platforms like Netflix and Amazon Prime Video by targeting the "underserved" Hispanic digital market. The new company, with Televisa as the majority shareholder, will offer a vast catalog of content from both media giants, including a free and premium subscription model, expected to launch in 2022.

title: Disney Ranks High on Fortune’s 2022 List of “World’s Most Admired Companies”
summary: The Walt Disney Company has been recognized on Fortune's 2022 list of "World's Most Admired Companies," ranking No. 5 overall and retaining its position as the top-ranked media and entertainment company for the 19th consecutive year. Disney received high marks across various areas including innovation, quality of management, financial soundness, and social responsibility. The list was compiled by Fortune in partnership with Korn Ferry, surveying executives, directors, and analysts.

title: PHOTOS: Columbia Sportswear "Star Wars: Boba Fett Collection" Apparel Lands at Disney Springs
summary: The new Columbia Sportswear "Star Wars: Boba Fett Collection" apparel is now available at Disney Springs. This collection includes a women’s jacket for $450, men’s graphic tees in white and black for $50 each, and a men’s hoodie for $120. The merchandise can be found at the Columbia Sportswear store, capitalizing on the recent focus on Boba Fett in Star Wars content.

title: My first stock: Arlene Dickinson on investing in IBM
summary: Arlene Dickinson recounts her first stock purchase of IBM in 1983 with $500, an experience that caused significant stress and led her to sell the stock quickly. This initial investment taught her valuable lessons about market volatility, the importance of understanding what you invest in, and the necessity of not investing more than one can afford to lose. These lessons shaped her long-term investing style, emphasizing diversification and calculated risks with blue-chip stocks.

title: Want Exposure To Google? 2 Communication Services ETFs Holding Alphabet Shares
summary: This article discusses two Communication Services ETFs, the Fidelity MSCI Telecommunication Services Index ETF (FCOM) and the iShares Global Comm Services ETF (IXP), that offer significant exposure to Alphabet shares. It highlights Alphabet's strong Q4 and FY 2021 results, including a 20-for-1 stock split, and reviews the holdings, performance, and key metrics of each ETF for investors looking to capitalize on the growth in this sector.

title: Disney Q1 FY2022 Earnings Report Preview: What to Look For
summary: The Walt Disney Co. (DIS) is set to report its Q1 FY 2022 earnings, with analysts expecting significant growth in adjusted EPS and revenue as the company recovers from the pandemic. Key metrics to watch include revenue from its Parks, Experience and Products segment, which is projected to see robust growth, and Disney+ subscriber numbers, although subscriber growth is expected to decelerate. Despite the overall recovery, Disney's stock has underperformed the broader market over the past year.

title: Growth Stocks: Walt Disney Co
summary: This article analyzes Walt Disney Co (DIS.US) ahead of its Q1 fiscal year 2022 earnings report, focusing on key growth metrics. It highlights the importance of subscriber growth in Disney's streaming services, particularly Disney+, and reviews performance in its theme parks and efforts to reduce debt. The author advises caution given a challenging technical context for Disney's stock and investor expectations after Netflix's recent subscriber miss.

title: Norwegian Cruise Line set to drop mask requirement, update testing and vaccine protocols
summary: Norwegian Cruise Line announced significant changes to its COVID-19 protocols, effective March 1, including dropping the onboard mask requirement for passengers. The cruise line will also allow unvaccinated children under five years old to board and will shift pre-departure testing responsibilities to guests, who will need to secure their own tests before sailing. These updates come as coronavirus cases decline and aim to streamline the check-in process while maintaining health and safety standards.

title: Walt Disney Co. theme parks kick off fiscal-year 2022 with big growth
summary: The Walt Disney Co. theme parks, including Walt Disney World in Orlando, have started fiscal year 2022 with strong growth. This positive performance is largely attributed to the theme park giant driving much of the local travel recovery. The article highlights this strong start in the current fiscal year.

title: Discovery’s merger with WarnerMedia clears antitrust scrutiny. (Published 2022)
summary: Discovery and AT&T have cleared a significant regulatory hurdle, with their merger satisfying the antitrust review by the Department of Justice. This development paves the way for the creation of one of the largest media companies, combining assets like HBO, Warner Bros., TNT, and TBS with Discovery's extensive nonfiction programming. The deal is expected to close in the next few months, with Discovery's CEO, David Zaslav, set to lead the new combined entity.

title: Meyer Werft Floats Out First New Disney LNG-Fueled Cruise Ship
summary: Germany’s Meyer Werft has completed the float out of the Disney Wish, the first of three new LNG-fueled cruise ships for Disney Cruise Line. The 144,000 gross ton vessel emerged from the building hall on February 11 and is scheduled for its maiden voyage in July 2022. This ship marks Disney's first new cruise ship in a decade and will incorporate unique features like a water ride and innovative digital media, expanding on Disney's family-focused cruise experience.

title: ‘Our turnaround is now complete’: Mattel takes victory lap after year of turbulence and growth
summary: Mattel CEO Ynon Kreiz has declared the company's multi-year turnaround complete after a strong performance in 2021, despite global supply chain disruptions. The toy manufacturer reported a 22% increase in North American sales for 2021 and gained market share, driven by a surge in consumer demand during the pandemic. Moving forward, Mattel projects further revenue growth for the upcoming fiscal year.

title: Disney Taps Mike White to Lead Metaverse Strategy
summary: Disney CEO Bob Chapek has appointed Mike White to a new role as SVP of next-generation storytelling and consumer experiences, leading the company's metaverse strategy. White will coordinate efforts across Disney's brands to blend physical and digital worlds, aiming to enhance audience engagement with stories through interactive experiences. This move reflects Disney's belief that the metaverse is the "next great storytelling frontier" and an opportunity to innovate.

title: Disney Launches New Business to Develop Residential Communities
summary: The Walt Disney Company has announced Storyliving by Disney, a new business venture to develop master-planned residential communities infused with Disney's magic and attention to detail. The first community, Cotino, will be built in Rancho Mirage, California, an area with historical ties to Walt Disney. These communities will offer unique amenities, curated experiences, and will include sections for residents aged 55 and over, with Disney Imagineers playing a key role in their creative concept.

title: DISH Network Corp. Cl A stock underperforms Wednesday when compared to competitors
summary: DISH Network Corp. Cl A (DISH) stock dropped 0.94% to $31.59 on Wednesday, underperforming a mixed trading session where the S&P 500 rose and the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell. The stock closed significantly below its 52-week high and showed mixed performance against competitors like Walt Disney Co. (DIS) and Netflix Inc. (NFLX). Trading volume was also below its 50-day average.

title: Salaam Coleman Smith joins Scopely Board of Directors
summary: Salaam Coleman Smith, an entertainment industry veteran with over 20 years of leadership experience from Disney and Comcast NBCUniversal, has been appointed to the Scopely Board of Directors. She brings extensive expertise in navigating the digital landscape and balancing creative vision with business acumen, having also served on the boards of Pinterest and Gap Inc. Scopely's Co-CEOs Walter Driver and Javier Ferreira anticipate that her audience-first thinking and insights will be invaluable as the company continues to expand its mobile gaming business.

title: TelevisaUnivision Unveils Plans for Streaming Service in Spanish (Published 2022)
summary: TelevisaUnivision announced its new Spanish-language streaming platform, ViX, which will offer both a free ad-supported tier and a premium subscription service. The free tier will launch on March 31 with over 100 channels and 40,000 hours of on-demand content, while the premium ViX+ service will follow later in the year with over 60 original productions. This move positions TelevisaUnivision to compete for the large global Spanish-speaking audience, joining other major players like Netflix, Disney+, and WarnerMedia who are also investing heavily in Spanish-language content.

title: How to Buy Disney Stock
summary: This article provides guidance on investing in Disney stock, detailing its business segments, financial performance, and how it might fit into an investment portfolio. It covers the company's history, recent earnings, stock splits, and considerations for potential shareholders, including valuation and diversification. The article also explains the process of buying Disney stock through a brokerage account and offers advice on long-term investment strategy.

title: 02/22/22 NickALive!
summary: This NickALive! post from February 22, 2022, covers a range of Nickelodeon news. Key announcements include Paramount Consumer Products partnering with Culture Kings for an Avatar: The Last Airbender streetwear line and the launch of a new Australian tour for PAW Patrol Live! 'The Great Pirate Adventure'. It also mentions Nickelodeon's plan to register SpongeBob NFTs and programming highlights for Nickelodeon CEE and UK, including the movie "Hook" and Carnevale celebrations for "The Smurfs" in Italy.

title: Disney and State Farm Team Up to Create Good Neighbor Magic
summary: The Walt Disney Company and State Farm have announced a new multi-year relationship focusing on Disney Parks and Resorts and Disney Advertising Sales. This collaboration, driven by shared values of community and helping people achieve their dreams, will manifest in exciting events, sponsorships, and venue naming rights at Walt Disney World Resort. The alliance aims to create magic and give back to communities, with initial activations including the Disney Dreamers Academy and the Walt Disney World Marathon Weekend.

title: State Farm and Disney Team Up to Create Good Neighbor Magic
summary: State Farm and The Walt Disney Company announced a new multi-year strategic alliance, building on their shared values of community and helping people achieve their dreams. This collaboration will involve various events and sponsorships, including a Disney Dreamers Academy event, Good Neighbor Month celebrations, and the Walt Disney World Marathon Weekend. State Farm will also sponsor specific venues at Walt Disney World Resort and present Disney podcasts.

title: Sony Pictures, Disney, BBC Studios Join DEG International
summary: BBC Studios, Sony Pictures Entertainment, and The Walt Disney Company, EMEA, have joined Digital Entertainment Group International (DEGI), expanding its global membership. This move comes as home entertainment is experiencing a "global renaissance," with significant growth in VOD and digital transactions, especially in the United Kingdom. The new members aim to collaborate on driving category growth and sharing insights to benefit the evolving digital content market.

title: What is Brian Roberts' Secret Plan?
summary: The article discusses the perceived underperformance of NBCUniversal's Peacock streaming service within the intensely competitive streaming wars, especially following the least-watched Olympic Games in history. It questions Comcast's strategy, suggesting that given their reputation for strategic and careful moves, there might be a hidden plan behind Peacock's seemingly nonchalant approach rather than a simple failure to compete. The author argues that Peacock's minimal impact is puzzling for one of the major legacy entertainment studios known for its capable leadership.

title: Statement from The Walt Disney Company in Response to the Crisis in Ukraine
summary: The Walt Disney Company announced it is pausing the release of theatrical films in Russia, including Pixar's "Turning Red," due to the ongoing invasion of Ukraine and the resulting humanitarian crisis. The company stated it would base future business decisions on the evolving situation and is actively working with NGO partners to provide humanitarian aid to refugees.

title: Comcast Corp. Cl A stock outperforms competitors despite losses on the day
summary: Comcast Corp. Cl A (CMCSA) shares dropped 0.79% to $46.39 on a down trading day for the broader market, with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones also falling. Despite the loss, Comcast's stock performed better than some competitors like Walt Disney Co. (DIS) and DISH Network Corp. Cl A (DISH), although it closed $15.41 below its 52-week high. Trading volume was slightly below its 50-day average.

title: Apple, Netflix, TikTok strike back against Russian state media content
summary: Several major tech and entertainment companies, including Apple, Netflix, and TikTok, are taking action against Russian state media and suspending services in Russia following the invasion of Ukraine. This includes Netflix refusing to carry Russian federal channels, Apple pausing product sales and limiting services, and social media platforms restricting access to and demoting content from outlets like RT and Sputnik due to concerns about propaganda and disinformation. The moves reflect a global condemnation of Russia's actions and a united front from U.S. businesses.

title: Abigail Disney Calls Out Disney Donations to Florida’s ‘Don’t Say Gay’ Supporters
summary: Abigail Disney, filmmaker and activist, has publicly criticized The Walt Disney Company for its financial contributions to Florida politicians who support the "Don't Say Gay" bill. She expressed her strong disapproval via Twitter, advocating for a law requiring all corporations to disclose their funding and lobbying activities. This isn't the first time Disney has spoken out against the company, having previously criticized former CEO Bob Iger's salary in 2019.

title: Sony Pictures TV to Acquire Industrial Media, Production Company Behind ‘American Idol,’ in $350 Million Deal
summary: Sony Pictures Television is set to acquire Industrial Media, the production company behind popular non-fiction shows like "American Idol" and "90 Day Fiancé," in a deal valued at $350 million. The acquisition aims to expand SPT's nonfiction content capabilities, with Industrial Media's CEO, Eli Holzman, and President, Aaron Saidman, joining Sony Pictures Television to lead the newly formed nonfiction entertainment division. This move highlights Sony's strategy to bolster its presence in the growing nonfiction television market.

title: ESPN Announces Content for Fifty/50 Initiative Celebrating Fifty Years of Title IX with Elements Across The Walt Disney Company
summary: ESPN and The Walt Disney Company are launching "Fifty/50," a major initiative to commemorate the 50th anniversary of Title IX. This initiative will feature content across various platforms, including a four-part documentary series "37 Words," the 30 for 30 film "Dream On" about the 1996 U.S. Women’s Olympic basketball team, and five short films from W. Studios and Google. The programming aims to highlight the civil rights journey of women in sports and culture, reflecting both past progress and the work still needed for equality.

title: After protests, Disney CEO speaks out against Florida's 'Don't Say Gay' bill
summary: Following internal and external protests, Disney CEO Bob Chapek announced the company's opposition to Florida's "Don't Say Gay" bill, which limits discussions of sexual orientation and gender identity in schools. Chapek stated Disney would reassess its advocacy approach and pledge five million dollars to LGBTQ+ rights organizations, though the Human Rights Campaign initially declined the donation, urging more substantive action. Critics argue Disney's stance is "a day too late," highlighting past political contributions to bill sponsors.

title: The Pros and Cons of Variable Dividends
summary: This article explores the growing trend of variable dividend policies, particularly in the energy sector, comparing them to traditional fixed quarterly dividends. It discusses the advantages, such as providing more cash to shareholders in commodity-driven industries, and disadvantages, like increased uncertainty for investors. The author also speculates on the future adoption of variable dividends in other sectors with fluctuating cash flows.

title: ‘Black Panther’ Director Ryan Coogler Mistaken for Bank Robber in Atlanta
summary: Ryan Coogler, the director of "Black Panther," was briefly detained by police in Atlanta after Bank of America employees mistook him for a bank robber. Coogler was attempting to discreetly withdraw a large sum of cash, which led the teller to incorrectly believe a robbery was in progress. Bank of America has since apologized to Coogler for the incident.

title: Disney ‘Taking Steps to Pause’ All Business in Russia
summary: The Walt Disney Company announced it is "taking steps to pause" all other businesses in Russia, beyond its initial halt on new movie releases, due to the "unprovoked invasion of Ukraine" and escalating humanitarian crisis. This includes content and product licensing, Disney Cruise Line activities, National Geographic magazine and tours, local content productions, and linear channels. Disney stated that while some activities can be paused immediately, others will take time due to contractual complexities, and staff in Russia will remain employed.

title: The Walt Disney Company Celebrates 6 Wins At The 2022 EE British Academy Film Awards
summary: The Walt Disney Company achieved significant success at the 2022 EE British Academy Film Awards, securing a total of six awards. Wins included "Encanto" for Animated Film, "West Side Story" for Casting and Supporting Actress, "Cruella" for Costume Design, and "The Eyes of Tammy Faye" for Make Up & Hair, alongside "Summer Of Soul" for Best Documentary. Many of these award-winning films are currently available on Disney+, with "The Eyes of Tammy Faye" joining the platform later in March.

title: Netflix stock has now lost all its gains from the pandemic
summary: Netflix's stock has lost all its gains from the pandemic, with shares falling to a 52-week low of around $332 and being more than 50% down from its mid-November high of $700.99. This decline is attributed to consumers returning to out-of-home entertainment, increased competition from other streaming platforms, and underwhelming subscriber growth forecasts, prompting Netflix to rethink its strategy and raise prices. Analyst Michael Pachter suggests that competition makes it harder to retain customers and increases content costs, while competitors are less likely to license content to Netflix now that they have their own platforms.

title: Omnicom is first agency to integrate with NBCUniversal’s data clean room
summary: Omnicom Media Group (OMG) has become the first agency to integrate with NBCUniversal's Audience Insight Hub, a proprietary data clean room, to enhance measurement capabilities while preserving data privacy. This collaboration allows OMG to run permissioned measurement queries across both NBCU's first-party data and Omnicom's Omni system without exposing personally identifiable information. The move underscores the growing importance of data, technology, and advanced measurement solutions in the media industry, especially as global data privacy regulations tighten and legacy measurement platforms face challenges.

title: PHOTOS: Vera Bradley’s NEW ‘The Little Mermaid’ Collection Has Arrived at Disney World
summary: Vera Bradley has launched a new "The Little Mermaid" collection at Disney World, featuring a whimsical "Under The Sea" pattern and a variety of items made from recycled cotton. The collection includes popular Vera Bradley styles like weekender travel bags, crossbody bags, and wristlets, as well as unique items like shell cosmetic cases, pajamas, socks, and lotion bags. Shoppers can find the collection at the Vera Bradley store in Disney Springs, Uptown Jewelers in Magic Kingdom, Legends of Hollywood in Disney’s Hollywood Studios, and online.

title: Electronic Arts stops sales in Russia, bans Russian teams from esports events
summary: Electronic Arts has ceased sales of its games, content, and virtual currency in Russia and Belarus in response to the ongoing conflict in Ukraine. The company has also removed Russian teams from its sports video games FIFA 22 and NHL 22, and banned teams from both Russia and Belarus from competing in official esports events. This action comes amidst a broader trend of companies, including Microsoft and CD Projekt Group, pulling out of the Russian market and following an appeal from Ukraine's deputy prime minister.

title: Thursday's Top Analyst Upgrades and Downgrades: Adobe, American Airlines, Coupa Software, Disney, Host Hotels, Nio, Roblox, SentinelOne and More
summary: This article details top analyst upgrades, downgrades, and initiations for various companies on Thursday, March 17, 2022. It covers a range of sectors, providing updated price targets and ratings from major financial institutions like Stifel, Goldman Sachs, BofA Securities, Raymond James, Citigroup, Deutsche Bank, J.P. Morgan, Needham, Truist Securities, UBS, and Baird. The analysis follows a general market rally and the Federal Reserve's recent interest rate hike.

title: Amazon.com closes deal to buy MGM movie studio
summary: Amazon.com Inc has finalized its $8.5 billion acquisition of MGM, integrating the renowned movie studio known for "Rocky" and James Bond into its ecosystem. This move aims to enhance Amazon's Prime streaming service by adding over 4,000 film titles and numerous television shows to better compete with rivals like Netflix and Disney+. The deal closed after clearing regulatory hurdles in both the U.S. and Europe, with Amazon welcoming all MGM employees and leadership.

title: Exclusive: The Walt Disney Company and Lightstorm Entertainment on 'Avatar 2' Collaborations and Consumer Products
summary: The Walt Disney Company and Lightstorm Entertainment are collaborating on numerous projects for the upcoming "Avatar 2" film, including consumer products, gaming, and location-based entertainment. This exclusive interview reveals plans for highly detailed figures, apparel, home decor, publishing, and two new video games, "Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora" and "Avatar: Reckoning." The strategy focuses on celebrating Pandora's world and characters, with global retail activations planned.

title: Disney workers walk out over the company's response to so-called 'Don't Say Gay' bill
summary: Hundreds of Disney employees staged a full-scale walkout to protest the company's handling of Florida's "Don't Say Gay" bill, which restricts discussions of gender and sexuality in schools. Employees are demanding that Disney cease political donations to certain Florida politicians and commit to a plan protecting LGBTQIA+ staff. Disney CEO Bob Chapek apologized for not speaking out sooner and is engaging in a "listening tour" with employees.

title: Disney Walkout Spurs In-Person Action in Burbank, Social Media Response From Disney Stars
summary: Disney employees and supporters participated in physical and virtual walkouts to protest Florida’s "Don't Say Gay" bill, with in-person demonstrations occurring at the Burbank studios and social media support from Disney stars like Mark Ruffalo. While Burbank workers chanted slogans like "Say Gay" and received support from their divisions, parks employees in Florida and California expressed feeling unsafe to participate fully due to company policies. The walkouts followed internal apologies and policy changes from CEO Bob Chapek regarding the company's prior silence and political funding.

title: The Walt Disney Company Earns 6 Academy Awards® Including Best Animated Feature Film and Best Documentary
summary: The Walt Disney Company received six Academy Awards at the 94th annual ceremony. "Encanto" was named Best Animated Feature Film, and "Summer of Soul" won Best Documentary Feature, marking significant firsts for several creators and Disney divisions. Other wins included Best Actress in a Leading Role for Jessica Chastain in "The Eyes of Tammy Faye," Best Actress in a Supporting Role for Ariana DeBose in "West Side Story," and Best Costume Design for Jenny Beavan in "Cruella."

title: Disney Vows to Help Repeal Florida’s ‘Don’t Say Gay’ Bill: ‘It Should Never Have Passed’
summary: The Walt Disney Company has vowed to work towards the repeal of Florida's "Don't Say Gay" bill, stating it "should never have passed." This public opposition follows internal backlash from employees and Pixar for CEO Bob Chapek's initial handling of the controversial legislation. Disney is committed to supporting LGBTQ+ rights organizations and aims to see the law overturned by the legislature or the courts.

title: Disney Says Florida’s “Don’t Say Gay” Bill Should Be Repealed as Gov. DeSantis Signs It Into Law
summary: The Walt Disney Co. has issued a statement condemning Florida Governor Ron DeSantis's signing of the "Don't Say Gay" bill into law, calling for its repeal. The company stated its commitment to supporting organizations working to overturn the legislation and standing up for the rights of LGBTQ+ individuals within and outside the company. Disney's CEO, Bob Chapek, had previously faced backlash from employees for not speaking out sooner against the bill, leading to an apology, a pause on political donations in Florida, and a commitment to fight similar legislation in other states.

title: Walt Disney Co. Denounces Florida's ‘Don't Say Gay' Bill, Now a Law
summary: The Walt Disney Company has publicly denounced Florida's "Parental Rights in Education" bill, dubbed the "Don't Say Gay" bill by critics, following its signing into law by Gov. Ron DeSantis. Disney expressed its commitment to supporting organizations working to repeal the law and stands in solidarity with the LGBTQ+ community. This stance comes after earlier criticism of Disney's initial silence on the bill and an apology from CEO Bob Chapek for not being a stronger ally.

title: Operator of Domino’s Pizza China Files for Hong Kong Listing amid Three-year Net Loss
summary: DPC Dash, the exclusive master franchisee for Domino’s Pizza in mainland China, Hong Kong, and Macao, has applied for a Hong Kong stock exchange listing. Despite reporting increasing net losses for the past three years due to expansion costs and the 30-minute delivery promise, the company plans to open 120 new stores in 2022, primarily in Beijing and Shanghai. The filing also highlighted that over 73% of its revenue comes from delivery orders and acknowledged business risks related to Covid-19 restrictions.

title: Measurement Giant Nielsen Sold to Private-Equity Group for $16 Billion
summary: Nielsen has been sold to a private-equity group led by Evergreen Coast Capital Corporation and Brookfield Business Partners for $16 billion, including debt. The all-cash deal offers $28 per share, a 10% premium over a previous offer, and comes as Nielsen faces scrutiny over its measurement methodologies and is working on a new cross-stream viewership system. Nielsen's CEO, David Kenny, is expected to remain with the company, and the deal is anticipated to close in the second half of 2022.

title: National CineMedia's New Target Crowd: TV's "Unreachables"
summary: National CineMedia (NCM) held its annual Upfront presentation, targeting advertisers with the message that cinema advertising can reach a new generation of 18-34 year-olds dubbed "unreachables" who avoid traditional TV. NCM highlighted data showing the younger demographic's strong movie attendance and higher recall of cinema ads, introducing new initiatives like Noovie Studios for original content and NCMx for targeted advertising. The company emphasized the unique engagement of the cinema experience for brands.

title: Why you need a total experience strategy to drive CX and EX
summary: This article discusses the growing importance of a "total experience" strategy, which integrates customer experience (CX), employee experience (EX), user experience (UX), and multiexperience (MX). Companies like Lumen Technologies and Fidelity Investments are adopting this approach to enhance both customer satisfaction and employee productivity, recognizing that these aspects are deeply intertwined. The strategy aims to create exponential business value by addressing experiences holistically rather than in silos, despite the current lack of a single, all-encompassing platform.

title: Why Formula 1 U.S. Expansion to Las Vegas Should Raise the Bar for IndyCar
summary: Formula 1's expansion into the U.S. with a third race in Las Vegas starting in 2023, alongside existing events in Miami and Austin, is raising questions about its impact on IndyCar. While some, like former F1 and current IndyCar driver Alexander Rossi, don't foresee an "outright war," they acknowledge a competition for race fans and call for IndyCar to evolve and differentiate its product. The article highlights F1's growth in the U.S. and the potential challenges this presents for IndyCar, despite its unique racing diversity and fan access.

title: The Rise of Anti-ESG Shareholder Proposals
summary: This article discusses the increasing number of "anti-ESG" shareholder proposals, which aim to disrupt the efforts of pro-ESG investors. These proposals often mimic the language of pro-ESG resolutions but serve opposing intentions, and their rise, alongside changes in SEC rules, could significantly impact the proxy voting landscape. The author highlights the tactics used by anti-ESG groups, including submitting proposals early and leveraging new SEC thresholds for support, and suggests shareholders carefully scrutinize the intent behind proposals.

title: Mastech Digital Appoints Mr. Vlad Rak As Board Member
summary: Mastech Digital, a provider of Digital Transformation IT Services, has appointed Mr. Vlad Rak as an independent member of its Board of Directors, effective April 1, 2022. Mr. Rak, currently the Executive Vice President & Chief Technology Officer of Dick’s Sporting Goods, brings over 24 years of technology experience from premier organizations like Nike, Disney, and Merck. He will serve on the Audit, Compensation, and Nominating & Corporate Governance Committees.

title: WarnerMedia’s CEO departs in advance of Discovery merger
summary: Jason Kilar is stepping down as CEO of WarnerMedia just days before its merger with Discovery Inc. to form a new media company. His departure paves the way for Discovery CEO David Zaslav to build his own management team at the combined entity. Kilar, who oversaw the launch of HBO Max and made controversial decisions regarding film distribution during the pandemic, expressed pride in his achievements in transforming WarnerMedia into a direct-to-consumer global company.

title: Williams Sonoma Partners with the Kentucky Derby® to Inspire At-Home Race Day Celebrations
summary: Williams Sonoma has partnered with the Kentucky Derby and Woodford Reserve to inspire at-home race day celebrations for the 148th Kentucky Derby. This partnership includes a curated line of merchandise, co-branded cocktail mixes, special recipes from Chef Kelsey Barnard Clark, and virtual and in-person cooking events. The collaboration aims to bring the authentic charm of the Derby into homes and offers a sweepstakes for a trip to the 149th Kentucky Derby in 2023.

title: Global Video Streaming Market to Boost in Coming Years –
summary: The global video streaming market is projected to reach USD 213.1 Billion by 2028, growing from USD 60.1 Billion in 2021 at a CAGR of 19.9%. This growth is driven by technological advancements like AI and blockchain, widespread smartphone adoption, and the increasing popularity of streaming platforms, especially exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic. North America currently dominates the market, but the Asia-Pacific region is expected to show the highest growth rate during the forecast period.

title: Walt Disney World Earmarks 80 Acres for New Affordable Housing Development
summary: Walt Disney World Resort has designated 80 acres in southwest Orange County, Florida, for a new affordable housing development. This project, expected to include over 1,300 units, aims to address the shortage of affordable housing in Central Florida and will be developed by a third-party on Disney's land. The initiative builds on Disney's broader commitment to community investment and sustainable development, with similar efforts already underway at Disneyland Resort.

title: UFC, Formula 1 and WWE could be the next acquisition targets for streaming giants
summary: Streaming giants like Disney and Netflix may eye sports organizations such as UFC, WWE, and Formula One as acquisition targets. Owning a league could help control rising licensing fees and provide exclusive content, making these global properties attractive despite few being available for sale. WWE, with its aging controlling shareholder, is highlighted as a particularly strong potential takeover candidate.

title: House Republicans want to axe Citi contracts over bank's abortion benefits
summary: House Republicans are calling for the cancellation of government contracts with Citigroup after the banking giant announced it would cover travel costs for employees seeking abortions. Republican Rep. Mike Johnson and 44 other lawmakers argue that continuing the contract would violate the policy of not funding abortions with taxpayer money. This controversy highlights the increasing focus on companies' stances on political and social issues, with other corporations also facing scrutiny for their policies on reproductive healthcare and other contentious matters.

title: Turning Red's Best Buy Exclusive SteelBook Cover Revealed
summary: Screen Rant has unveiled Best Buy's exclusive SteelBook cover for Pixar's "Turning Red," which will be released digitally on April 26th and on 4K Ultra HD, Blu-ray, and DVD on May 3rd. The article highlights the unique animation style and re-watchability of the film, focusing on the SteelBook's design that reflects protagonist Meilin Lee's transformation into a red panda. It also details the extensive bonus features included in the home release, offering fans more reasons to purchase a physical copy.

title: CNN Officially Has a New Parent Company: Warner Bros. Discovery, Inc.
summary: Discovery, Inc. and WarnerMedia's parent company AT&T officially closed a $43 billion merger to form Warner Bros. Discovery, Inc. This new entity, uniting WarnerMedia (including CNN) and Discovery's portfolio, began trading on Nasdaq under the ticker "WBD" on April 11. The merger creates a new streaming-centric media company, with AT&T shareholders holding 71% of the new company and Discovery shareholders 29%.

title: WarnerMedia, Discovery complete merger, become Warner Bros Discovery
summary: AT&T Inc's WarnerMedia unit and Discovery Inc have completed their merger, forming Warner Bros Discovery Inc, which will begin trading on Nasdaq under the ticker "WBD" on Monday. This merger allows AT&T to focus on 5G and fiber while Discovery aims to enhance its content library and make streaming profitable under CEO David Zaslav. The new company's portfolio includes major brands like HBO, CNN, and popular franchises.

title: DeFiChain Adds New dTokens Corresponding to Disney, Intel, MicroStrategy, and iShares MSCI China ETF
summary: DeFiChain has announced the addition of four new decentralized tokens, or dTokens, following a community vote. These new dTokens correspond to Walt Disney Co ($dDIS), iShares MSCI China ETF ($dMCHI), MicroStrategy Incorporated ($dMSTR), and Intel Corporation ($dINTC), allowing users to gain price exposure to these traditional assets without ownership. DeFiChain, a blockchain built on the Bitcoin network, aims to provide decentralized financial applications and services, expanding its dToken universe to offer an alternative to traditional financial brokers.

title: 'B+C', 'MCN', 'NextTV' Name L.A. TV Week 40 Under 40
summary: Broadcasting+Cable, Multichannel News, and Next TV have announced the 2022 L.A. TV Week 40 Under 40 honorees. These individuals are recognized for their innovative contributions to the industry and will be celebrated on June 7 at the Sofitel Los Angeles at Beverly Hills. The full list of honorees will also be featured in the May issue of B+C Multichannel News.

title: Warner Bros Discovery shares gain on first trading day
summary: Shares of Warner Bros Discovery Inc (WBD.O) rose on their first trading day following the $43-billion merger of Discovery Inc and AT&T's content assets. The new company, led by CEO David Zaslav, faces strong competition in the streaming market, while AT&T is expected to focus on its core telecom business and debt reduction.

title: IMDb TV will be renamed Amazon Freevee, says Amazon
summary: Amazon's free streaming service IMDb TV will be rebranded as Amazon Freevee starting April 27, 2022. The platform will significantly expand its original programming by 70% in 2022, including spin-offs and new movies. This move is part of Amazon's broader strategy to enhance its streaming services, following its acquisition of MGM.

title: Posts Spread Unfounded Claims About Disney Company’s Financial Health
summary: Social media posts have been circulating with unsubstantiated claims about The Disney Company's financial health, alleging significant declines in Disney+ subscribers, theme park visitors, and stock value. These claims arose after Disney opposed Florida's "Parental Rights in Education" law. FactCheck.org found these claims to be largely unfounded or highly exaggerated, with Disney's stock experiencing a modest decline, and the company reporting strong revenue and rebounding park attendance.

title: Who's who: Meet the Murdoch Family
summary: This article provides an in-depth look at the Murdoch family, chronicling Rupert Murdoch's seven-decade career building News Corp into a global media empire and the ongoing speculation about his succession. It details the roles and relationships of his six children—Lachlan, James, Elisabeth, Prudence, Grace, and Chloe—and his four wives, highlighting their involvement and influence within the family business and their personal lives. The piece also touches on significant controversies faced by News Corp, such as phone hacking scandals and sexual harassment allegations.

title: It’s Disney vs. Florida
summary: The Walt Disney Co. is embroiled in a political battle with Florida Governor Ron DeSantis over the state's Parental Rights in Education Law, leading to calls to revoke Disney's unique self-governing status in Florida. While some experts believe the financial impact on Disney will be minimal and the conflict is largely "political theater," the dispute—coupled with Disney's political donations—has alienated both conservative and liberal groups. The company's stock has seen a decline since the controversy, and its standing with some customers, particularly moderates and conservatives, may be affected.

title: Disney Tops MBLM’s Most Intimate Brands Survey
summary: For the second time since 2019, Disney has been ranked No. 1 in MBLM's Brand Intimacy Study, which analyzes how consumers connect emotionally with global brands using artificial intelligence. This achievement highlights Disney's resilience and ability to form deep relationships with consumers, particularly in the media and entertainment sector.

title: Netflix Loses 200,000 Subscribers in Q1, Predicts Loss of 2 Million More in Q2
summary: Netflix lost 200,000 subscribers in Q1 2022, marking its first subscriber loss in 10 years, and forecasts an additional loss of 2 million in Q2. The company attributes this decline to increased competition, password sharing, and macro factors, leading to a significant drop in its stock price and a reevaluation of future strategies including ad-supported plans and content spending adjustments. Despite beating earnings per share expectations, revenue fell short of analyst forecasts.

title: Niles: Will Warner Bros. take the next step in the theme park business?
summary: This article discusses whether Warner Bros. Discovery will significantly expand its presence in the theme park industry after AT&T spun off Warner Bros. to merge with Discovery, Inc. Currently, Warner Bros. licenses its IPs to various parks like Six Flags and Universal and operates successful studio tours. The author questions if the new company will leverage its expanded intellectual property portfolio to create more world-class immersive experiences beyond its existing licensing agreements.

title: Netflix Loses Subscribers For The First Time In Ten Years, Shares Plunge 35%
summary: Netflix shares plummeted over 35% after the company reported its first subscriber loss in over a decade, signaling a significant slowdown in revenue growth. The streaming giant lost 200,000 subscribers in Q1 and expects to lose another 2 million, attributing the decline to password sharing, increased competition, and the suspension of service in Russia. Co-CEO Reed Hastings announced plans to explore lower-priced, ad-supported subscription tiers to attract new customers.

title: Netflix loses 200,000 subscribers in first quarter
summary: Netflix reported a loss of 200,000 subscribers in the first quarter, missing its own projections and marking its first decline in over a decade. The company attributes the subscriber loss to password sharing, increased competition from other streaming services, and geopolitical events. Netflix is exploring new strategies to regain subscribers, including a lower-priced ad-supported service and cracking down on password sharing.

title: Netflix Reports Loss of Subscribers for the First Time in a Decade
summary: Netflix reported a loss of 200,000 subscribers in Q1 2022, marking its first subscriber decline in a decade, and anticipates losing 2 million more in the next quarter. This decline is attributed to rising inflation, increased competition from rivals like Amazon and Disney, and account sharing among users. The news led to a significant drop in Netflix's share price and negatively impacted other entertainment stocks.

title: Netflix just lost $50 billion in market cap
summary: Netflix's stock plummeted by 35% after the company reported a loss of 200,000 subscribers in the first quarter of 2022, wiping out $50 billion in market cap. The streaming giant attributed the decline to increased competition, widespread password sharing, and macroeconomic factors, and expects to lose another two million subscribers in the second quarter. In response, Netflix plans to enhance content quality, monetize password sharing more effectively, and is now open to introducing an ad-supported, lower-priced tier to boost revenue and subscriber growth.

title: Uber, Lyft and Disney end mask mandates as COVID cases fall
summary: Uber Technologies Inc and Lyft Inc have ended face mask mandates for their riders and drivers in the United States, citing a sharp fall in COVID-19 cases from their January peak. Walt Disney Co also made masks optional for fully vaccinated visitors at its indoor and outdoor locations, aligning with a broader trend among transportation companies following a federal judge's ruling against a U.S. mask mandate on public transportation.

title: Why Is Procter & Gamble (PG) Stock Up Today?
summary: Procter & Gamble (PG) stock is rising today after its fiscal Q3 2022 earnings report, which saw the company beat Wall Street estimates for both adjusted diluted earnings per share ($1.33 vs. $1.29 expected) and revenue ($19.4 billion vs. $18.73 billion expected). The company also reported a 10% organic sales growth, its largest in 20 years, and updated its full-year core EPS guidance despite increased costs and foreign exchange challenges.

title: Disney UNCF Corporate Scholars Named for 2022 Cohort
summary: The Walt Disney Company and the United Negro College Fund (UNCF) announced the 2022 Disney UNCF Corporate Scholars, a program providing $5,000 annual scholarships, paid summer internships, and mentorship to students from four-year institutions, including Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs). This initiative is funded by Disney's multi-year commitment, expanding on previous support, and aims to develop a robust pipeline of Black talent in various fields. The program was recognized with the "Corporation of the Year" award by UNCF Leadership Councils, highlighting Disney's dedication to educational and career opportunities for underrepresented communities.

title: Netflix shares fall more than 35% after streamer loses over 200,000 subscribers
summary: Netflix shares plummeted over 35% after the company announced a loss of more than 200,000 subscribers in Q1 2022 and projected a further 2 million loss. This significant drop, wiping $50bn off its value, is attributed to increased competition, market saturation post-pandemic, inflation, and account sharing. Netflix plans to address this by tackling account sharing, improving programming quality, and considering an advertiser-supported subscription tier.

title: Is Now the Time to Buy Netflix Stock?
summary: Netflix reported its first quarterly subscriber loss since 2011 and expects further declines, causing its stock to plummet. Despite this, Morningstar's senior equity analyst Neil Macker lowered his fair value estimate but noted the stock is now deeply undervalued, while some investors like Bill Nygren still see value in the company given its market multiple and industry dominance. The company plans to reaccelerate growth through improved content, tackling password sharing, and potentially introducing an ad-supported, lower-priced tier.

title: Netflix’s Stumble Could Be a Warning Sign for Streaming Industry (Published 2022)
summary: Netflix reported losing more subscribers than it gained in Q1 2022, reversing a decade of growth and causing its stock to plummet by 35% and its market cap to shed $50 billion. This reversal raises questions about the sustainability and profitability of the streaming business model, especially as traditional media companies invest heavily in similar subscription services. Industry executives and analysts are re-evaluating the "streaming wars" and the long-term viability of an industry built on numerous paid streaming options.

title: Netflix shares slide after it loses 200,000 subscribers
summary: Netflix shares plummeted after the company reported losing 200,000 subscribers in the first quarter of 2022, its first subscriber loss in over a decade. The decline was attributed to increased competition, economic headwinds, market saturation, and the withdrawal from Russia, leading to a significant drop in stock price and concerns about future growth. Netflix plans to address the issue by cracking down on password sharing and exploring new revenue streams like video games.

title: Florida state Senate passes bill that would eliminate Walt Disney World's district
summary: The Florida state Senate passed a bill to eliminate Walt Disney World's special district, Reedy Creek Improvement District, which operates as its own municipality. This move comes after Disney opposed Florida's Parental Rights in Education Law, dubbed the "Don't Say Gay" bill. If signed into law, the legislation could lead to a legal battle over the theme park's future.

title: When Worlds Collide: Moelis & Co.’s Carlos Jimenez on the Emerging Metaverse Economy
summary: Carlos Jimenez, managing director at Moelis & Co., believes the entertainment business is undergoing a massive transformation into a metaverse economy where various leisure activities merge. He predicts a surge in investment in metaverse infrastructure and content due to booming content spending, noting an opportunity for investors to consolidate small and medium-sized content development assets. Jimenez also suggests that new ventures similar to Candle Media will emerge to become scaled suppliers of content to the expanding ecosystem.

title: Columbia’s Star Wars jackets let us dress like the rebel scum we are
summary: Columbia Sportswear has partnered with Lucasfilm to release a line of limited edition Star Wars jackets inspired by costumes from the movie Rogue One. The collection includes three jackets: the Jyn Erso Rebel Jacket, the Imperial Death Trooper Jacket, and the Captain Cassian Andor Rebel Parka, ranging from $400 to $500. These jackets incorporate design elements from the film's costumes while also featuring Columbia's signature outdoor technology for warmth and weather protection.

title: News | How the Unraveling of Walt Disney World’s Special Tax Status in Florida Affects Commercial Property
summary: Florida Governor Ron DeSantis signed a bill to abolish Walt Disney World's special tax district, Reedy Creek Improvement District, which grants the park governmental privileges. This move is a response to Disney's opposition to a Florida law regarding gender and sexuality education. The dissolution of the district could lead to significant financial burdens for Orange and Osceola counties, potentially impacting commercial development and local taxpayers.

title: Professor: Walt Disney Co. Chose Values Over Politics; Other Corporations May Face Similar Dilemmas
summary: The Florida legislature voted to end Walt Disney Co.'s special tax district following Disney's criticism of the "Don't Say Gay" bill. Business law Professor Robert Bird discusses the implications, highlighting that corporations are increasingly expected to take stances on public policy and face potential retaliation from governments.
