He suggests this event signals a trend where companies must balance their values with political relationships.

title: Formula 1’s American Conundrum (Published 2022)
summary: Formula 1's popularity is rapidly growing in the United States, marked by record ratings, popular Netflix series "Drive to Survive," and new U.S. races. Despite this expansion, there hasn't been a prominent American driver in the series for a long time, raising questions about the lack of U.S. representation on the track. The article explores the reasons behind this "American conundrum," highlighting the traditional European path to F1 and the lack of financial backing for American drivers.

title: Florida Battles Disney World Over ‘Don’t Say Gay’ Bill
summary: Florida Governor Ron DeSantis challenged Disney World's special tax status in retaliation for the company's opposition to the state's "Parental Rights in Education" bill, dubbed the "Don't Say Gay" law. Disney, initially silent, eventually criticized the law, leading DeSantis to revoke the company's 50-year-old self-governing district. The move sparked mixed reactions, with some conservatives supporting the warning to corporations, while others raised concerns about free speech implications and the potential financial burden on local counties.

title: Judge invites Walt Disney Co. to bring Disney World to Texas amid new passed law
summary: A Texas judge has formally invited Disney to relocate Walt Disney World to Fort Bend County, Texas, following Florida lawmakers' decision to dissolve Disney World’s private government. This invitation comes amid the ongoing dispute between Disney and Florida over the "Don't Say Gay Bill," which Disney publicly criticized. The judge highlighted Fort Bend County's diversity, economic development, and business-friendly climate as reasons for a potential move.

title: Cityneon Holdings reveals new Marvel experience
summary: Cityneon Holdings is launching an updated Marvel experience called MARVEL AVENGERS STATION: EVOLUTION, premiering in Dallas this summer. This new immersive exhibition will incorporate content from all four phases of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, including recent series and films, and builds upon the success of the original MARVEL AVENGERS S.T.A.T.I.O.N. experience. Guests will be able to interact with characters, weapons, and technologies, and see original costumes and props.

title: HURRY! Disney’s ‘Little Mermaid’ Vera Bradley Collection is Now Online!
summary: The new "The Little Mermaid" Vera Bradley collection, previously launched in Disney Springs, is now available online at shopDisney. The collection features 37 items, including various bags like the Weekender Travel Bag, Crossbody Bag, Backpack, and Tote, as well as smaller accessories like the ID Case and Lanyard. Fans of Ariel and her undersea friends can purchase these items online while supplies last.

title: Analytics Unite 2022: Procter & Gamble's David Dittman Joins Loyalty Talk
summary: David Dittman, vice president and chief analytics officer at Procter & Gamble, will join the "Innovative Loyalty: Identify the Data that Creates Obsessed Consumers" session at Analytics Unite 2022. The event will focus on creating impactful loyalty strategies that strengthen existing consumer relationships and incentivize new customers. Dittman will share insights from his 12+ years of experience at P&G in leveraging analytics for marketing, product supply, and customer business development.

title: With Trump and Rumble, Florida becomes conservative media HQ
summary: Florida is emerging as a major hub for conservative media, with Donald Trump's Truth Social establishing a presence in Sarasota County. Canadian video platform Rumble, which powers Truth Social's technology, also moved its U.S. headquarters to Longboat Key, despite local backlash. This shift aligns with other conservative media companies like Newsmax and The Daily Wire relocating to Florida and Nashville, respectively.

title: Disney, DeSantis, and Corporate Dilemmas
summary: This article discusses the conflict between Disney and Florida Governor Ron DeSantis, following Disney's opposition to state legislation. Professor Robert Bird of UConn explains how the dispute highlights the increasing expectation for corporations to take stances on public policy issues, especially for a company like Disney which has a history of supporting LGBTQ+ rights. The situation also sends a message to other CEOs about balancing corporate values with political relationships.

title: Award-Winning Actor Michael Greyeyes Joins Directing Team for CTV Comedy Channel’s Original Series, ACTING GOOD
summary: Award-winning actor, director, and choreographer Michael Greyeyes is set to direct five episodes of CTV Comedy Channel's new original series, *ACTING GOOD*. The half-hour scripted comedy, loosely based on the life of Anishinaabe stand-up comedian Paul Rabliauskas, is currently in production in Winnipeg and surrounding areas. Darlene Naponse, Amber-Sekowan Daniels, and Eric Toth will also direct episodes for the debut season.

title: Charter and Comcast Announce Joint Venture to Develop and Nationally Offer a Next Generation Streaming Platform
summary: Charter Communications and Comcast Corporation have formed a 50/50 joint venture to develop and nationally offer a next-generation streaming platform. This platform will leverage Comcast's Flex streaming technology, XClass TVs, and Xumo, with Charter making an initial contribution of $900 million. The venture aims to provide a world-class user experience with top apps and greater choice in the streaming market, reaching customers nationwide through various branded 4K streaming devices and smart TVs.

title: Toymaker Mattel explores sale, has held talks with Apollo, L Catterton - source
summary: Toymaker Mattel Inc. is reportedly exploring a sale and has engaged in discussions with buyout firms Apollo Global Management Inc. and L Catterton. This news comes just months after Mattel's CEO stated the company had completed its turnaround and entered a "growth mode," buoyed by strong demand for brands like Barbie and recent wins like reacquiring the Disney princess doll license from rival Hasbro.

title: The Happiest Place on Earth? A Look Inside Disney’s Tax and Non-Tax Battle with the State of Florida
summary: Florida Governor Ron DeSantis signed a bill to revoke Walt Disney Company's special status, which allowed it to function as its own municipal government. This move follows Disney's public opposition to Florida legislation, including the "Don't Say Gay" bill. Accounting professors Nathan Goldman and Christina Lewellen examine the implications for Disney's taxes and Florida residents, noting that Disney might actually experience a tax decrease while the burden of services shifts to Orange and Osceola counties.

title: Imax Sets Up Special ‘Avatar’ Task Force To Capitalize On December Release
summary: Imax announced the formation of a special internal "Avatar" task force to maximize the impact of the upcoming "Avatar: The Way of Water" release in December, following the original film's success as Imax's top-grossing movie. This initiative comes as Imax reported first-quarter earnings, including a $6.9 million provision for uncertainty in its Russian receivables due to the ongoing conflict in Ukraine, while also noting increased box office revenue driven by films like "The Batman" and "Spider-Man: No Way Home." CEO Rich Gelfond expressed optimism for a strong box office recovery, dismissing day-and-date streaming as an ineffective model for studios.

title: Chief communications officer Joe Quenqua to exit WW International in July
summary: Joe Quenqua, Chief Communications Officer at WW International (formerly Weight Watchers), is set to leave the company at the beginning of July after a three-year tenure. During his time, Quenqua managed communications strategy and oversaw worldwide teams for internal and external communications, including corporate, crisis, consumer, financial, and executive positioning. His departure follows the recent change in CEO at WW International, with Sima Sistani joining the company in March.

title: Build-A-Bear Has A NEW Exclusive Disney World 50th Anniversary Bundle!
summary: In celebration of Disney World's 50th Anniversary, Build-A-Bear Workshop has released an exclusive online "50th Anniversary Celebration Gift Bundle." This bundle includes an unstuffed Mickey Mouse, a "I'm Going to Walt Disney World" outfit, a 1st Visit button, a 5-in-1 sound chip, and a special 50th anniversary bag. The bundle costs $64.95, and customers can also enter a sweepstakes for a chance to win a 5-day/4-night Disney World vacation.

title: Disney’s National Geographic Hires Nathan Lump as Editor in Chief
summary: Nathan Lump, a veteran journalist who previously led editorial for Expedia and served as editor-in-chief of Travel + Leisure, has been appointed as the new editor-in-chief of National Geographic. In his new role, Lump will be responsible for aligning the editorial strategy with both Disney, which acquired Nat Geo in 2019, and the National Geographic Society, focusing on the brand's scientific and educational mission while expanding its reach across Disney's global properties. He succeeds Susan Goldberg, who departed earlier this year.

title: The Game Awards, Summer Game Fest Events To Air Live In Imax Theaters Via New Partnership
summary: The Game Awards and Summer Game Fest producer Geoff Keighley has partnered with Imax to broadcast both annual gaming events live in Imax theaters across the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom. This collaboration aims to diversify Imax's content and offer an immersive viewing experience for gaming fans, starting with Summer Game Fest Live! on June 9. The partnership will also include The Game Awards, providing audiences with live game reveals, celebrity appearances, and musical performances in a shared cinema setting.

title: WPP partners with Epic Games to boost metaverse offering
summary: WPP has partnered with Epic Games to enhance its metaverse offerings for brands. This collaboration involves a training program for WPP's creative and technical staff on building brand experiences in Fortnite and utilizing Epic's Unreal Engine for 3D creation. Additionally, WPP will work with Epic Games' SuperAwesome to ensure online safety and privacy, especially when engaging younger audiences in the metaverse.

title: Kellogg's Just Gave Frosted Flakes A Star Wars-Inspired Twist
summary: Kellogg's has launched a limited-edition Obi-Wan Kenobi version of Frosted Flakes, combining original and Chocolate Frosted Flakes to represent the light and dark sides of the Star Wars universe. The cereal features Tony the Tiger dressed as both a Jedi and a Sith. While the "Obi-Wan Kenobi" series airs in May, the cereal will be released nationwide in July, with Walmart stocking mystery boxes as early as June.

title: The Chernin Group-Led Consortium to Acquire $263 Million in Funko, a Leading Pop Culture Lifestyle Brand
summary: A consortium led by The Chernin Group (TCG) will acquire a $263 million strategic investment in Funko, a pop culture lifestyle brand, taking an 80% stake from ACON Investments. This all-secondary transaction values Funko shares at $21.00 each, with TCG and its consortium owning 25% of the company post-acquisition. The investment includes commercial agreements with eBay Inc. and strategic advising for Funko's growth in content, commerce, and new product categories.

title: Walt Disney Company Builds Entertainment Empire Worth $97 Billion
summary: The Walt Disney Company has grown into a $97 billion entertainment empire by diversifying its holdings across five major segments: media networks, resorts and parks, studio entertainment, consumer products, and interactive media. The company owns over 200 subsidiaries, including well-known names like Marvel Entertainment, Pixar, Lucasfilm (Star Wars), and Hulu. Disney's strategic acquisitions, such as Marvel and Lucasfilm, have proven highly profitable, significantly contributing to its massive net worth and global influence.

title: The Disney Company’s recent controversy
summary: This article criticizes The Disney Company for its handling of controversial political issues, particularly its initial silence and subsequent actions regarding Florida's Parental Rights in Education Act. The author highlights inconsistencies between Disney's public image of diversity and its financial support for politicians backing anti-LGBTQ+ legislation. It urges consumers to stay informed about the company's political influence but acknowledges that enjoying Disney products doesn't make consumers culpable for the company's decisions.

title: SeaWorld parks enjoy highest first-quarter attendance since 2013
summary: SeaWorld Entertainment reported its highest first-quarter attendance since 2013, hosting 3.4 million guests in Q1 2022. The company also announced a significant increase in revenue compared to the same period in 2021 and 2019, driven by new rides and attractions. SeaWorld CEO Marc Swanson highlighted ongoing business model improvements and strong guest reception to new park offerings.

title: PHOTOS: ‘Star Wars’ Vera Bradley Collection Available in Disney Springs
summary: Vera Bradley has released a new Star Wars collection, which is now available at their Disney Springs location. The collection features a variety of items including blankets, bags, accessories, and smaller items like pouches and luggage tags, all adorned with Star Wars patterns and characters. This merchandise allows fans to celebrate the galaxy far, far away with everyday use items.

title: The Real Meaning Behind Hasbro's Brand Name
summary: Hasbro, a renowned toy company, started as a textile business called Hassenfeld Brothers Incorporated in 1923, founded by brothers Herman, Hilal, and Henry Hassenfeld. Initially selling fabric remnants, the company eventually shifted to toy manufacturing in the 1930s, producing iconic items like Mr. Potato Head. In 1968, the company shortened its name to Hasbro Industries Incorporated, continuing its legacy with popular toy lines such as G.I. Joe, Star Wars, Monopoly, and Play-Doh.

title: Disney hasn’t found itself in this much trouble since 1941
summary: The article discusses how the Walt Disney Co., typically controversy-averse, has recently become embroiled in the American culture wars due to its stance on a Florida law. This current situation is compared to a major internal revolt in 1941, when Walt Disney faced a strike by his animators demanding better working conditions and union representation. The article details the historical conflict, Disney's fervent anti-union stance, and his eventual testimony before the House Un-American Activities Committee where he accused union leaders of being communists.

title: ‘Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness’ Opens to $450 Million Worldwide
summary: Marvel Studios' "Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness" achieved a global opening of $450 million, securing the No. 1 spot in all markets and marking the highest global opening of 2022 to date. The film garnered $187 million domestically and $262.4 million internationally, making it the second-highest domestic opening of the pandemic era. It also ranks as the 11th highest domestic opening in history and the seventh-highest MCU opening weekend ever.

title: SHUTTERSTOCK ACQUIRES POND5, THE WORLD'S LARGEST VIDEO MARKETPLACE
summary: Shutterstock, Inc. has announced the acquisition of Pond5, the world's largest video-first content marketplace, for $210 million in cash. This acquisition significantly strengthens Shutterstock's position in premium editorial and commercial video and music content, expanding its content library and editorial offerings. The deal is expected to be immediately accretive to Shutterstock's 2022 adjusted EBITDA.

title: Disney Takes $1B Hit For Ending License Deals To Send Content To Streaming; Quarterly Sales Up, Profit Falls
summary: The Walt Disney Company reported a $1.023 billion hit in its second fiscal quarter due to terminating content license agreements early to bring film and television content to its direct-to-consumer streaming services. While overall revenue increased by 23% to $19.2 billion, profit fell 48% to $470 million. The company's parks division saw significant recovery, with sales more than doubling and swinging to an operating profit, helping to offset losses in its streaming sector, which are widening.

title: 2 Dozen-Plus NHL Partners in Canada, US Set 2022 Stanley Cup Playoffs Activations
summary: Over two dozen NHL partners in Canada and the U.S. are launching various activations for the 2022 Stanley Cup Playoffs. Notable new partners this year include Chipotle, Clutch, and TikTok. Viewership for the playoffs is significantly up from previous years, averaging 668,000 viewers across ESPN, ESPN2, TBS, and TNT.

title: Shutterstock Acquires Pond5 for $210 Million
summary: Shutterstock has acquired Pond5, the world's largest video-centric stock agency, for $210 million in cash. This acquisition expands Shutterstock's offerings in video, music, and editorial content, further positioning itself as a leading provider of stock assets. Pond5's extensive library and global network of contributors will become accessible to Shutterstock clients, enhancing their content options.

title: Hulu expands partnership to stream music festivals through 2023
summary: Hulu has expanded its partnership with Live Nation to stream several major music festivals, including Bonnaroo, Lollapalooza, and Austin City Limits, from 2022 through 2023. This collaboration aims to bring live music performances to a wider audience, with Hulu offering two distinct live streams for each festival weekend. The move further solidifies Hulu's position as a streaming destination for live events, adding to its growing content library for its over 45 million subscribers.

title: The Walt Disney Company Shares First Look at the Disney Pride Collection
summary: The Walt Disney Company announced the launch of its new Disney Pride Collection, with all profits from sales through June 30, 2022, being donated to organizations supporting LGBTQIA+ youth and families. This initiative builds on Disney's history of supporting LGBTQIA+ charities and features new branding designed by community members and allies. Various organizations across the U.S. and local charities worldwide will benefit from the collection's sales.

title: The Walt Disney Company, ESPN & XFL Reach Exclusive Multi-year Agreement
summary: The Walt Disney Company, ESPN, and the XFL have signed an exclusive multi-year agreement to broadcast all XFL regular-season and playoff games across Disney/ESPN platforms, beginning with the league's return season in February 2023. The deal includes coverage on ABC, ESPN networks, FX, and digital/DTC outlets like ESPN+, with global rights also included. This partnership aims to leverage ESPN and Disney's reach with the XFL's vision for competitive action and entertainment.

title: Disney Chiefs Deliver Stars and Muscle of ‘Most Powerful Force in the Industry’ at Upfront
summary: During Disney's upfront presentation, CEO Bob Chapek declared the Walt Disney Company "the most powerful force in the industry," highlighting its wide range of storytelling options and distribution platforms. The event featured appearances from numerous stars and executives promoting shows and films across Disney's linear networks, digital channels, and streaming services, including ABC, Hulu, Disney+, ESPN, and Marvel Studios. Key announcements touched on new series, film sequels, and sports programming, while also subtly addressing various industry topics.

title: XFL reaches multiyear agreement to air all games on ESPN and other networks owned by The Walt Disney Company
summary: The XFL has signed a multiyear agreement to broadcast all its regular-season and playoff games on ESPN, ABC, and FX, starting in February 2023. This deal also includes content rights for Disney's digital, social, and streaming platforms like ESPN+. The league, under new ownership including Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson, previously partnered with the NFL to focus on innovation and player health.

title: Amusement Park Market Analysis| Global Industry Trends & Forecast |CAGR - 3.18% by 2026 | Technavio segmentation based on Type and Geography
summary: The global amusement park market is projected to grow by USD 9.97 billion from 2021 to 2026, exhibiting a CAGR of 3.18%. This growth will be primarily driven by the increasing construction of new amusement parks, despite potential challenges like inherent hazards. North America is expected to contribute 54% of this growth, with the "Tickets" segment poised to gain significant market share.

title: Lovesac and Disney+ Team Up to Enhance Consumer Viewing Experiences
summary: Lovesac and Disney+ have partnered to enhance at-home viewing experiences for consumers, launching with the release of Disney's "Chip 'n Dale: Rescue Rangers." The collaboration will highlight Lovesac's StealthTech Sound + Charge system, which offers immersive surround sound and wireless charging integrated into their Sactionals. This partnership aims to bring a cinematic audio-visual experience directly into customers' living rooms through product demos, watch parties, and custom premiere lounges.

title: Disney boosts LGBTQ support, debuts “Pride Collection”
summary: Disney has launched its "Pride Collection" merchandise, featuring items like T-shirts and Mickey Mouse ears, with profits being donated to LGBTQ+ advocacy organizations through June. This move signifies increased support for the LGBTQ+ community, coming amid conservative backlash against the company for its progressive stances, particularly regarding Florida's "Don't Say Gay" law. While facing criticism, Disney states the collection was conceived months ago as part of its ongoing evolution towards inclusion, and is an expansion of its long-standing efforts to recognize and cater to LGBTQ+ visitors and employees.

title: Sony readies for metaverse revolution with cross-platform push
summary: Sony Group Corp is positioning itself to be a leading player in the metaverse, seeing it as a social and live network space where its various entertainment assets like games, music, movies, and anime can intersect. The company's strategy involves expanding beyond its traditional focus on single-player console games to embrace cross-platform and multi-platform offerings, as evidenced by its acquisition of Bungie and support for cross-play in games like Fortnite. Additionally, Sony is exploring opportunities in mobility, aiming to transform cars into new entertainment spaces, similar to the Walkman's impact on personal audio.

title: Mobile Gaming Market Size to grow by USD 66.43 billion | 47% of the growth will originate from APAC| Technavio
summary: The mobile gaming market is projected to grow by USD 66.43 billion at a CAGR of 12.26% between 2021 and 2026, with 47% of this growth coming from the APAC region. The market's expansion is driven by the increasing popularity of multiplayer mobile games and the development of advanced smartphones, encouraging online platform growth. However, the rise of alternative gaming platforms like consoles poses a challenge to market growth.

title: Netflix addresses content that runs counter to employees’ personal values
summary: Netflix updated its workplace culture document, stating that employees must support the company's diverse content offerings, even if some titles conflict with their personal values. The update follows controversy and employee walkouts over Dave Chappelle's comedy special "The Closer" and comes amidst declining subscriber counts and revenue growth for the company. Netflix's stance indicates that if employees find it difficult to support content breadth, the company "may not be the best place for you."

title: Report: EA Almost Merged With NBC Universal Before Deal With Comcast Dissolved
summary: A report indicates that Electronic Arts (EA) was close to merging with NBC Universal, with talks dissolving in April over monetary and corporate structure disagreements. Comcast's chairman and CEO, Brian Roberts, reportedly sought to bring EA under NBCUniversal's umbrella for new IP. Despite this failed deal, EA is also reportedly exploring a "more meaningful relationship" with Disney, potentially uniting ESPN and EA Sports.

title: The Walt Disney Company Stock Drops to $100
summary: The Walt Disney Company's stock dropped to $100.08 on May 20, 2022, closing at $102.42. This follows a previous low of $119 last month and a peak of $201.91 in March 2021. Despite reporting $19.2 billion in total revenue for Q2, the stock continues to decline.

title: Netflix scraps shows from left-wing creators amid tumbling stock price
summary: Amid a significant drop in its stock price and a loss of subscribers, Netflix has canceled several shows by creators associated with the social justice movement, such as Ibram X. Kendi and Ava DuVernay. Sources indicate these cancellations were due to creative reasons, shortly after Netflix reportedly told employees to embrace ideological diversity or leave. This move, combined with recent layoffs affecting diversity-focused projects, comes as the company faces financial challenges and increasing scrutiny from companies regarding "woke" risks, following Disney's battle with Florida Republicans.

title: NBC Universal acquisition of Electronic Arts fell apart at the last second
summary: A proposed merger between Comcast/NBC Universal and Electronic Arts fell through due to disagreements over price and structure. The deal would have seen NBCUniversal spun off and combined with EA, with EA's CEO Andrew Wilson potentially leading the new entity. This acquisition was considered in the wake of other major gaming industry mergers, highlighting the ongoing consolidation trend.

title: Walt Disney Co. stock underperforms Friday when compared to competitors
summary: Walt Disney Co. (DIS) stock dropped 0.70% on Friday, closing at $102.42, underperforming the broader market which saw the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average rise. This marks the third consecutive day of losses for Disney, putting its stock significantly below its 52-week high. Competitors such as Comcast Corp. Cl A also fell slightly, while Sony Group Corp. ADR saw a gain.

title: Apple's Steve Jobs: An Extraordinary Career
summary: This article chronicles the extraordinary career of Apple co-founder Steve Jobs, highlighting how his vision propelled the PC revolution and Apple's success. It covers his early life, his initial departure from Apple, his ventures with NeXT and Pixar, and his triumphant return to Apple, where he spearheaded groundbreaking products like the iMac, iPod, iPhone, and iPad. The piece concludes with his health struggles, resignation, and passing, emphasizing his lasting legacy as a visionary leader.

title: Remembering Disney Legend Tom Murphy
summary: This article commemorates the life and legacy of Thomas S. Murphy, a Disney Legend and former Chairman and CEO of Capital Cities/ABC, who passed away at 96. Murphy was renowned for his ethical leadership, business acumen, and philanthropic efforts, overseeing the mergers of Capital Cities with ABC and later with The Walt Disney Company. His career highlighted his commitment to decentralization, cost control, and strong ethical standards within the media industry.

title: Licensing International Announces Nine New Board Members
summary: Licensing International has announced the election of nine new executives to its Board of Directors for three-year terms, effective July 1, 2022. The new board members bring diverse expertise from companies such as Hasbro, Netflix, Warner Bros. Discovery, and more, aiming to support the expansion of brand licensing globally. Steve Scebelo will serve as chairperson and Veronica Hart as vice chairperson, as the organization welcomes new leadership and thanks outgoing members.

title: Lights! Camera! Action! Pier 94 Could Make the Movies —If Developer Vornado Fulfills Promises
summary: Developer Vornado proposes a new 212,000-square-foot film and television studio at Pier 94 in Hell's Kitchen, complete with public amenities. However, Manhattan Community Board 4 is skeptical given Vornado's history of unfulfilled promises regarding the disrepair of adjacent Pier 92 and other community requests. The board insists Vornado address these structural issues and implement promised public amenities before approving the new project.

title: PPG Named Official Paint of WALT DISNEY WORLD® Resort and DISNEYLAND® Resort
summary: PPG has announced a multi-year parks alliance agreement with Disney Parks, Experiences and Products, designating PPG as the Official Paint of Walt Disney World® Resort and Disneyland® Resort. This partnership builds on over 50 years of collaboration, with PPG providing a wide range of paints and coatings to enhance the guest experience and maintain the aesthetic of the parks, including specific products used in attractions like Guardians of the Galaxy: Cosmic Rewind and on Main Street, U.S.A.

title: Here are this year’s Fortune 500 companies by region
summary: The 2022 Fortune 500 companies collectively generated $16.1 trillion in revenue, reflecting a 19% increase from 2020. This article breaks down the geographical distribution of these companies across the U.S. and highlights dominant industries in the Western, Midwest, Northeast, and Southern regions. Insights into key companies and financial performances specific to each region are also provided.

title: \'Top Gun\' stays aloft with $86M in its 2nd weekend
summary: “Top Gun: Maverick” continued its strong theatrical run, earning $86 million in its second weekend, marking a modest 32% drop from its opening, an unusually steady performance for a blockbuster. The film has grossed $548.6 million worldwide and is Tom Cruise’s best performer in domestic ticket sales, contributing significantly to the current recovery of movie theaters. It faces upcoming competition from other major summer releases like "Jurassic World: Dominion" and "Lightyear."

title: Netflix Gearing Up for Formula 1 Rights Push
summary: Netflix is reportedly vying for the U.S. broadcast rights to Formula 1, marking its first potential move into live sports. The streaming giant is competing with ESPN, Amazon, and NBCUniversal for the rights, which are sought at around $100 million annually by F1's parent company, Liberty Media. This interest comes as F1's popularity in the U.S. has surged, partly due to Netflix's "Drive to Survive" docuseries, and coincides with Netflix's plans to introduce an ad-supported tier.

title: Warner Bros. Discovery Taps Luis Silberwasser as Chairman/CEO of Sports Division
summary: Luis Silberwasser has been appointed as Chairman and CEO of Warner Bros. Discovery Sports, where he will lead the company's domestic sports portfolio and global sports strategy. He previously held leadership roles at TelevisaUnivision and Discovery Communications, bringing extensive experience in building successful global businesses and content strategies. His immediate tasks will include negotiating the renewal of NBA broadcast rights, as Warner Bros. Discovery aims to leverage its combined assets and global distribution capabilities to become a major player in sports rights acquisition.

title: With 'Jurassic World 3,' dinosaurs rule again at box office
summary: “Jurassic World: Dominion” achieved a massive box office success, pulling in $143.4 million in North American ticket sales and $389 million globally. This strong performance, alongside "Top Gun: Maverick," signals a robust rebound for the summer box office, challenging the notion that only superhero films are pandemic-proof blockbusters. The film's success highlights audience enthusiasm for big-screen spectacles despite critical reviews, making it a significant milestone for the cinematic industry.

title: Thor: Love and Thunder Releases Its Most Epic Poster Yet
summary: Marvel Studios released a new IMAX poster for Thor: Love and Thunder, featuring Thor, Jane Foster, Valkyrie, and Gorr the God Butcher. The film will include almost 35 minutes of Expanded Aspect Ratio footage in IMAX. The article also mentions the film's runtime of 1 hour and 59 minutes, and details about Thor and Jane's comical breakup and Jane's role as the new God of Thunder.

title: Walt Disney Imagineering Move to Lake Nona Delayed to 2026
summary: The Walt Disney Company has postponed the relocation of Walt Disney Imagineering and other departments to Lake Nona, Florida, until mid-2026. This move was originally slated for completion in 2023. The delay has caused frustration among some employees who had already begun relocation efforts, while others were already opposed to the move, particularly in light of political developments in Florida.

title: Demi Busatta Cabrera adds $42K in May for HD 114 defense
summary: Rep. Demi Busatta Cabrera, a Republican, raised $42,000 in May for her House District 114 campaign, bringing her total war chest to over $259,000. Her donations came from corporations, a fellow Republican, and business associations, including $15,000 from the Florida Prosperity Fund. Her Democratic opponent, Adam Benna, raised about $6,000 in May, accumulating nearly $83,000 in his campaign funds.

title: American Express and Delta Air Lines Debut First-Ever Limited-Edition Boeing 747 Credit Card Design
summary: American Express and Delta Air Lines have launched a limited-edition credit card design made with metal from a retired Boeing 747 aircraft. This unique card, available for Delta SkyMiles Reserve and Reserve Business Card Members from June 16 to August 3, 2022, offers an augmented reality experience detailing the history of the 747 and Delta's transformation of Ship #6307. The initiative celebrates aviation history and provides premium travel benefits for cardholders, coinciding with increased consumer interest in summer travel.

title: Mattel Names Josh Silverman Global Head of Consumer Products and Chief Franchise Officer
summary: Mattel Inc. has appointed Josh Silverman as its global head of consumer products and chief franchise officer, effective September 1, 2022. Silverman, who previously worked for The Walt Disney Co.'s consumer products division for over a decade, will be responsible for global consumer products licensing, franchise management, retail development, publishing, live experiences, and location-based entertainment. This move aims to leverage Silverman's extensive experience to unlock the potential of Mattel's intellectual property and iconic brands.

title: Disney delaying Florida campus – but not because of tensions
summary: The Walt Disney Co. is delaying the opening of a new campus in central Florida, which will house 2,000 relocated workers from Southern California, until 2026. Despite recent political tensions with Florida Governor Ron DeSantis, Disney officials stated the delay is due to the extended time needed for construction and to provide employees more flexibility for relocation. The campus will be located near Walt Disney World, and Disney aims to align the relocation period with the campus's completion.

title: Disney Cruise Line's newest ship Disney Wish prepares for maiden voyage - Bizwomen
summary: The Disney Wish, Disney Cruise Line's fifth ship, has arrived at Port Canaveral and is preparing for its maiden voyage on July 14, offering 3- and 4-day Bahamian trips. The 4,000-passenger ship features areas themed around Marvel, Star Wars, and Pixar. The cruise industry is vital to Port Canaveral, representing 80% of its revenue and significantly contributing to regional tourism and the local economy.

title: Cinemark Reinforces the Power of the Big Screen with XD Campaign
summary: Cinemark Holdings, Inc. has launched a new multi-platform campaign to promote its premium large format offering, Cinemark XD. The campaign emphasizes the immersive experience of XD auditoriums with brighter colors, deeper sound, and a larger picture. It aims to attract moviegoers seeking an enhanced out-of-home entertainment experience for anticipated Hollywood films.

title: Netflix lays off 300 workers amid subscriber losses
summary: Netflix announced it has laid off 300 employees as it grapples with a significant revenue slowdown and its first subscriber loss in over a decade. These cuts, representing about 3% of its global workforce, primarily impacted staff in the U.S. and Canada but also extended to other regions and affected various roles from vice presidents to individual contributors. The company attributes these actions to the need to align costs with slower revenue growth and address increased competition in the streaming market, aiming to maintain profit margins while also planning to expand its workforce and introduce new revenue strategies like paid sharing and an ad-supported tier.

title: Disney tells employees it will provide ‘comprehensive access’ for reproductive care
summary: The Walt Disney Company informed its employees via an internal memo that it would cover travel expenses for pregnancy-related care if they needed to seek services out of state following the Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade. The memo, signed by chief human resources officer Paul Richardson and vice president Pascale Thomas, emphasized the company's commitment to comprehensive, affordable care, including family planning and reproductive care, regardless of where employees live.

title: Companies paying for abortion-related travel include Dick's Sporting Goods, Google, Disney
summary: Following the Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade, several major corporations, including Dick's Sporting Goods, Google, and Disney, are offering to cover abortion-related travel expenses for their employees. This move comes as at least 26 states are expected to ban or significantly restrict abortion access, prompting companies to take a stance on reproductive rights despite previously avoiding the issue.

title: ‘A great loss but not a new one’: Lizzo pledges big bucks for abortion organizations
summary: Lizzo announced she will donate $500,000 from her upcoming tour proceeds to Planned Parenthood and other abortion rights organizations in response to the overturning of Roe v. Wade. Live Nation has pledged to match her donation, bringing the total to $1 million. The company also stated it would cover travel expenses for employees seeking reproductive healthcare outside their home state and support community activism related to the issue.

title: JP Morgan, Disney join wave of companies that'll cover employee abortion travel costs
summary: Following the Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade, numerous companies, including JPMorgan Chase and Disney, announced they would cover travel expenses for employees needing to go out-of-state for abortion services. This decision aligns with a prior trend seen among other corporations after a leaked opinion indicated the potential overturning of the federal protection. Companies like Dick's Sporting Goods and Condé Nast also detailed their plans to support employees' access to reproductive healthcare, with some even extending support to include bail for peaceful protestors.

title: Walt Disney Co. tells employees it will pay for travel costs for their reproductive care
summary: The Walt Disney Company announced it will cover travel costs for employees seeking reproductive care, including those related to pregnancy decisions, if they cannot access such care in their current location. This decision comes in response to the Supreme Court's ruling to overturn Roe v. Wade, with Disney emphasizing its commitment to providing healthcare access regardless of location. Specific details of the benefit are yet to be released, but Disney joins several other major companies in expanding healthcare coverage to include travel expenses for reproductive services.

title: Disney, other U.S. companies offer abortion travel benefit after Roe decision
summary: Following the U.S. Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade, numerous U.S. companies, including Walt Disney Co. and Meta Platforms Inc., announced they would cover travel expenses for employees seeking abortion services. This move comes as many states are expected to restrict or ban abortions, making it necessary for employees to travel to states where the procedure remains legal. Companies like Dick's Sporting Goods, Lyft, Yelp, Microsoft, Tesla, Apple, Alaska Air Group, Johnson & Johnson, OkCupid, Bumble, Netflix, and JPMorgan Chase & Co. are also offering similar benefits or legal protections.

title: As Chapek weathers Disney drama, board gathers in Florida
summary: As CEO Bob Chapek faces mounting pressure from various controversies and a struggling stock price, Disney's board of directors is meeting in Orlando for its annual retreat. While the board is expected to reaffirm its support for Chapek, whose leadership during the pandemic has been praised by the CFO, the series of public relations challenges and investor doubts about subscriber goals have put his leadership under intense scrutiny. The article details Chapek's missteps, including conflicts with Scarlett Johansson and Florida Governor Ron DeSantis, alongside the company's strong performance in theme parks and Disney+ subscriber growth, questioning his suitability despite a lack of obvious internal successors.

title: BREAKING NEWS: The Walt Disney Company Board Votes to Extend Bob Chapek's Contract as CEO for Three Years
summary: The Walt Disney Company's Board of Directors has unanimously voted to extend CEO Bob Chapek's contract for another three years, running until 2025. This decision, following a statement expressing the board's confidence in Chapek and his leadership, comes after he took over from the popular Bob Iger. This news may be received negatively by some Disney fans, given widespread sentiments about his leadership.

title: Target completes 1,000th store remodel — here’s what it means
summary: Target Corp. has completed its 1,000th store remodel, a key milestone in its "stores-first" strategy, which has shown a 2% to 4% sales bump in updated stores. The company's 2022 remodel program is its most ambitious yet, including full-store remodels, fulfillment remodels to boost same-day services, and the addition of Drive Up canopies. These renovations incorporate welcoming elements, consistent layouts, and shop-in-shop experiences, while also focusing on sustainability and improving customer loyalty.

title: Target's massive overhaul of stores reaches halfway point
summary: Target has completed the remodeling of its 1,000th store, signifying the halfway point in a chainwide renovation program that began before the pandemic and has cost billions. The retailer plans to complete nearly 200 full-store remodels and 200 fulfillment-related remodels this year, with commitments to remodel almost all of its 1,900 locations. These renovations aim to enhance the customer experience, improve ease of shopping, and have historically led to sales bumps of 2 to 4% for updated stores.

title: Disney's board backs CEO Chapek, extends his contract for three years
summary: The Walt Disney Co. board of directors unanimously voted to extend CEO Bob Chapek's contract for three years, signaling strong confidence in his leadership despite recent controversies. Chapek, who became CEO in February 2020, navigated the company through the COVID-19 pandemic, leading to significant growth in its streaming service, Disney+. This extension comes after some criticism regarding his handling of a Florida bill concerning LGBTQ+ discussions in schools and a high-profile executive ousting.

title: Disney unveils first new cruise ship in a decade, dips toe into metaverse
summary: Disney has launched its first new cruise ship in a decade, the 4,000-passenger "Disney Wish," marking a significant expansion for its cruise line. CEO Bob Chapek highlighted the ship's integration of characters, stories, and innovative technology, including interactive experiences that hint at Disney's venture into the metaverse. The launch comes as Disney's theme parks unit rebounds from pandemic closures and Chapek looks to solidify his leadership.

title: Most Powerful Women 2022
summary: Cablefax celebrates its 2022 Most Powerful Women in Broadband in Media, recognizing top-performing female executives across various sectors. The magazine highlights "Glass Breakers" who have overcome barriers, along with Women’s Advancement Champions, a Mentor of the Year, and the "Rising Tide" Class, featuring up-and-coming women making significant contributions. The publication includes insights from honorees on their evolving definitions of success and experiences as the sole women in a room.

title: Starz could turn into an 'acquisition machine' after Lionsgate spins it off
summary: Lionsgate is planning to spin off Starz, potentially as early as next year, with bids already in place for a 20% stake from Vivendi's Canal Plus and a consortium of Apollo Global and Roku. This separation could enable Starz, once an independent company, to pursue acquisitions of other subscale media companies like AMC Networks and A&E Networks, a vision previously espoused by media mogul John Malone. The move comes as Lionsgate (LGF.A) has seen its market capitalization shrink, and investors view Starz as needing to gain significant scale to compete in the evolving streaming landscape.

title: Nathan’s Famous Hot Dog-Eating Contest to Air July 4 on ESPN Networks
summary: The Nathan's Famous Hot Dog-Eating Contest will air live on ESPN Networks on July 4, marking the 19th consecutive year for ESPN to televise the event. World Champion Joey Chestnut aims for a new record, while top-ranked female Miki Sudo returns after missing last year to reclaim her title. The event, returning to Coney Island, will feature ESPN SportsCenter Anchor John Anderson on play-by-play and Major League Eating’s Richard Shea providing analysis.

title: Travel Apps Offering Ultimate Convenience to Travelers
summary: Travel apps have become one-stop shops for travelers, enabling instant bookings, personalized itineraries using AI, and seamless management of travel logistics. The report highlights key technology, macroeconomic, and regulatory trends impacting the travel app theme, as well as leading public and private companies in the space. It emphasizes how these apps provide convenience and are crucial for companies to stay competitive in the evolving tourism industry.

title: The Walt Disney Company extends Bob Chapek’s CEO Contract
summary: The Walt Disney Company's Board of Directors has unanimously voted to extend Bob Chapek's contract as CEO for three years. Susan Arnold, Chairman of the Board, cited Chapek's leadership in navigating the company through the pandemic and positioning it for a strong future. Chapek expressed gratitude for the opportunity to lead Disney, highlighting his nearly 30-year career with the company and his focus on storytelling, innovation, and audiences.

title: Amazon, Disney, AT&T Gave to Abortion Foes Like DeSantis While Vowing to Help Employees
summary: Amazon, Disney, and AT&T, despite pledging to cover travel costs for employees seeking reproductive medical care, have also contributed financially to anti-abortion governors and political figures like Ron DeSantis. State campaign-finance records show these corporate giants supported leaders actively working to reduce access to abortions, creating a contradiction between their public stances and political donations.

title: Dole Food Company Expands "Dole Healthy Heroes: Assemble!" Campaign; Melanie Marcus Comments
summary: Dole Food Company is expanding its "Dole Healthy Heroes, Assemble!" campaign by partnering with Marvel Studios' Thor: Love and Thunder. This third chapter, "Heroes of the Heart," aims to celebrate everyday acts of kindness and first responders, featuring new Thor-inspired recipes, collectible stickers, and digital content. The initiative seeks to drive consumer interest in the produce department with Marvel-themed merchandising.

title: Disney Launches Howard University Fund to Support Black Storytellers
summary: The Walt Disney Company has partnered with Howard University to establish the "Disney Storytellers Fund," a multiyear program aimed at supporting underrepresented students in media and entertainment. This initiative will provide stipends for student projects across various creative fields, fund a new collaborative space, and offer access to speakers, mentors, and internships. The program aligns with Disney's broader efforts to amplify underrepresented voices and increase access to careers in storytelling.

title: 'Minions' set box office on fire with $108.5 million debut
summary: The film "Minions: The Rise of Gru" debuted with an estimated $108.5 million in North America, with projections to exceed $127.9 million by the end of the July Fourth holiday, making it one of the biggest openings for that weekend. Its worldwide gross reached $202.2 million through Sunday. This success highlights the strong return of family audiences to movie theaters, as the film attracted a wide demographic, including many young viewers.

title: Disney’s $56.2B in Retail Sales Leads Global Brand Licensing Race
summary: The Walt Disney Co. topped global brand licensors in 2021 with $56.2 billion in retail sales of licensed merchandise worldwide, an increase from $54 billion in 2020. This achievement occurred despite the pandemic's disruption, showcasing Disney's strong portfolio including Pixar, Marvel, and Star Wars. Other major players in brand licensing included WarnerMedia, The Pokemon Company, Hasbro, NBCUniversal, Mattel, and Paramount Global, contributing to a total of $260.8 billion in retail sales for licensed consumer products globally.

title: ARK’s Expected Value For Roku in 2026: $605 Per Share
summary: ARK Invest projects Roku's stock price to reach $605 per share by 2026, representing a 53% annual growth rate. This forecast is based on an open-source model incorporating various factors like active accounts, daily streaming hours, and platform monetization rates. The report also provides bull and bear case scenarios, highlighting video advertising as a key driver for future growth.

title: How a Disney and P&G Director Found Her Own Direction
summary: Amy Chang, a board member at Disney and P&G, overcame initial intimidation to navigate critical corporate challenges, including a major proxy fight at Procter & Gamble. She shares her experience of relying on trusted advisors for guidance on management decisions and moral dilemmas.

title: The Unstoppable Rise of Formula 1
summary: Formula 1 has experienced a remarkable resurgence, transitioning from declining viewership in 2016 to a global phenomenon by 2022. This growth is attributed to strategic marketing efforts by Liberty Media, particularly the Netflix series "Drive to Survive," and a new media rights deal with ESPN. The sport's increasing popularity is also reflected in increased viewership, significant revenue growth, and high-profile entertainment projects, making it a case study in effective content marketing for sports leagues.

title: Disney to Produce Three Projects Featuring K-Pop Supergroup BTS
summary: Disney and K-Pop supergroup BTS' agency, Hybe, have announced a multiyear content collaboration, which includes three exclusive projects featuring BTS for Disney's streaming services. These projects aim to boost Disney's global subscriber count and offer bankable Korean entertainment, with titles like a concert film, a travel reality show, and a docuseries about the band's journey. The collaboration comes as Disney+ expands its Korean content slate and BTS members explore solo endeavors while remaining together as a group.

title: 'Las Vegas of Asia' tells casinos to grow beyond gambling
summary: Macao, the "Las Vegas of Asia," is urging American casino giants to diversify beyond gambling by investing in non-gaming attractions like theme parks, a new requirement for renewing their expiring licenses. This push comes as Macao seeks to reduce its reliance on its dominant industry amid COVID-induced financial losses and pressure from Beijing. Major casino operators like MGM Resorts, Las Vegas Sands, and Wynn Resorts, which have invested billions, face a new challenge in balancing profitability with the government's development ambitions.

title: Two BTS Series to Play on Disney Streaming Services Following Deal With Hybe
summary: The Walt Disney Company Asia Pacific and Hybe Corporation have signed a content agreement to bring two BTS-related series to Disney's international streaming platforms. The deal includes a 4K concert film "BTS: Permission to Dance On Stage – LA" and a docuseries "BTS Monuments: Beyond the Star," following the K-pop group's rise. This partnership also includes a travel show "In the Soop: Friendcation" featuring BTS member V.

title: BTS brings streaming titles to Disney+ in content coup
summary: K-pop group BTS has signed a content deal with Disney+ to bring three new titles to the streaming platform. These include a concert film, a docuseries, and a travel reality series featuring BTS member V. The partnership aims to expand HYBE's content reach and tap into the growing K-content demand on streaming services.

title: Netflix in talks with Hollywood studios for new tier with ads - WSJ
summary: Netflix is reportedly engaging in discussions with major Hollywood studios like Warner Bros., Universal, and Sony Pictures Television to adjust existing programming agreements. These talks are crucial for Netflix to launch a new, lower-priced ad-supported subscription tier. This move comes as Netflix faces declining subscriber numbers and increased competition, following its announcement in April regarding the consideration of an ad-supported option.

title: Netflix names Microsoft as partner for ad-supported subscription plan
summary: Netflix has selected Microsoft as its technology and sales partner for its upcoming ad-supported subscription plan. This move comes as Netflix seeks to boost subscriber growth after experiencing losses, aligning with other streaming services that offer ad-supported tiers. Microsoft's strong advertising revenue and recent acquisition of Xandr Inc. make it a suitable partner, with Netflix's Chief Operating Officer emphasizing increased consumer choice and a premium advertiser experience.

title: Disney+ to run two BTS shows in HYBE's 1st global content collaboration
summary: HYBE Co., the K-pop label behind BTS, has announced its first global content collaboration with Walt Disney Company. Disney+ will produce and distribute five major titles worldwide, two of which will feature members of the septet. These shows include a 4K film of BTS's live performance in Los Angeles and "In the Soop: Friendcation," a travel show featuring V from BTS and other celebrities.

title: The Walt Disney Company Announces 2022 Disney Accelerator Participants
summary: The Walt Disney Company has announced the six companies selected for its 2022 Disney Accelerator program. This year's program focuses on immersive experiences using technologies like AR, NFTs, and AI characters, aiming to build on Disney's legacy of leveraging technology for entertainment. The participating companies, including Flickplay, Inworld, and Polygon, will receive guidance and mentorship from Disney, culminating in a Demo Day in the fall.

title: ‘Netflix Thinks Exactly Like an Old Movie Studio’
summary: In response to declining subscriber numbers and a volatile stock price, Netflix is shifting its strategy from filling niche content gaps to focusing on expensive, large-scale, and risky blockbusters with A-list stars. This pivot aims to compete directly with traditional Hollywood studios by creating new, wide-reaching franchises, despite lacking the same intellectual property. The company hopes these "event" films will re-engage audiences and solidify Netflix's position in the streaming landscape.

title: Netflix, Microsoft And The Rapidly Blurring Lines Between Media And Tech
summary: The article discusses the increasing convergence of media and technology industries, highlighted by Netflix's partnership with Microsoft for its ad-supported tier and Disney's ad tech collaboration with The Trade Desk. It also points to Apple TV+'s exclusive streaming deal for Major League Soccer as another example of tech companies making significant moves into content. The author uses the metaphor of Certs mints to illustrate how Netflix and Microsoft are becoming "two industries in one," emphasizing the blurring lines between these sectors.

title: Korean Streamer TVING to Acquire Rival Seezn to Better Compete With Netflix, Disney+
summary: Korean streaming platforms TVING and Seezn are set to merge, creating a more powerful domestic service controlled by CJ ENM. This strategic move aims to enhance competitiveness against global giants like Netflix and Disney+ and accelerate the growth of K-content. The merger reflects a broader industry trend where local players are consolidating to better compete in a fierce streaming market.

title: Hulu Is Driving More Streaming Subscribers to Disney Than Marvel or Star Wars
summary: Hulu has become Walt Disney Co.'s fastest-growing U.S. streaming service, attracting more new subscribers than Disney+ in 18 of the past 24 months. Total new subscriptions to Hulu have also surpassed Disney+ in each of the last six quarters, according to data from subscriber-measurement firm Antenna. This growth is attributed to Hulu's focus on more adult-oriented entertainment, expanding Disney's reach to a broader audience.

title: Mattel Opens Its Vault to Revitalize Dormant Brands (Published 2022)
summary: Mattel is reintroducing three dormant action figure lines—Major Matt Mason, Big Jim, and Pulsar—at Comic-Con as part of CEO Ynon Kreiz's strategy to leverage the company's intellectual property. This move is part of the toymaker's broader effort to revive older brands and expand legacy franchises into films and other media, contributing to its recent sales growth. The new line will be released under the "Back in Action" umbrella.

title: Netflix Loses Nearly 1 Million Subscribers, Vows Rebound
summary: Netflix reported a loss of 970,000 paid subscribers in the June quarter, marking its first consecutive quarterly subscriber decline in its history, though this was less than the 2 million it had projected. The streaming giant announced plans to introduce an ad-supported tier and crack down on password sharing next year to boost revenue and subscriber growth. Despite the losses, Netflix anticipates adding 1 million net new subscribers in the current quarter.

title: Disney Aspire Adds California State University, Fullerton and Fullerton College
summary: Disney Aspire, The Walt Disney Company's education program, has expanded its network by adding California State University, Fullerton and Fullerton College. This partnership brings almost 70 new degree and program offerings, making education more accessible to over 29,500 eligible hourly employees in California. The program covers 100% tuition upfront, along with reimbursements for books and fees, and provides student success coaching to support career mobility.

title: For Netflix stock, it's no longer subscribers or content. It's all about the cash
summary: The article highlights a shift in focus for Netflix (NFLX) stock from subscriber numbers and content investment to cash flow generation. It notes that years of debate about content spending are over as the company achieved positive operating cash flow, which is expected to double or triple by 2023. This change is driven by leveling off content spending and the upcoming addition of an advertising-supported tier, though top-line growth is slowing and subscriber growth potential is now seen as lower.

title: Netflix Lost Nearly 1 Million Subscribers Last Quarter. Here’s What That Means for Its Future
summary: Netflix reported a loss of nearly 1 million subscribers in the second quarter of 2022, compounding its 200,000 subscriber loss from the previous quarter. Despite this, the total loss was less than projected, leading to a temporary stock surge, though shares remain significantly down for the year. In response, Netflix is pursuing efforts like an ad-supported tier and focusing on high-quality original content to drive future growth and revenue.

title: Disney’s Reputation Is Plummeting Fast, According to New Survey
summary: A new survey indicates that The Walt Disney Company's reputation has significantly declined, dropping 28 spots to No. 65 on the Axios Harris Poll 100 list. This plummet is attributed to various controversies, including Disney's stance on Florida's "Don't Say Gay" bill, the box office failure of "Lightyear," and fan dissatisfaction with price increases and the new Genie+ system at its Parks. The company's overall score has shifted from "excellent" to "very good" as a result of these issues.

title: Jordan Peele's 'Nope' debuts at No. 1 with $44 million
summary: Jordan Peele's latest film, "Nope," secured the top spot at the North American box office in its opening weekend, grossing an estimated $44 million. While this figure is less than his previous film "Us," it represents a significant achievement for an original, R-rated movie and is the biggest original screenplay debut of the pandemic era. The film, starring Daniel Kaluuya, Keke Palmer, and Steven Yeun, was made on a $68 million budget and received largely positive reviews, with an 83% rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

title: Vrbo named new title partner for Fiesta Bowl
summary: Vrbo, the vacation rental site owned by Expedia Group, has been named the new title partner for the Fiesta Bowl, replacing PlayStation. ESPN, owned by Disney, will also be a title sponsor. The newly named Vrbo Fiesta Bowl will take place on December 31st and will be a semifinal game in the College Football Playoff, with Vrbo also becoming the official travel sponsor of the College Football Playoff.

title: Christmas in July: LEGO, Funko, Mattel, Hasbro announce new products at SDCC to score ahead of the holidays
summary: Major toy manufacturers LEGO, Funko, Mattel, and Hasbro unveiled new products at San Diego Comic-Con, aiming to attract holiday shoppers early with their latest offerings. LEGO celebrated its 90th anniversary with new "Avatar" and "The Office" sets, and a massive Super Mario Bros. Bowser build. Funko highlighted its expanded lifestyle brand with acquisitions like Loungefly and Mondo, while Mattel showcased its "Masters of the Universe" 40th anniversary and upcoming "Barbie" film, and Hasbro introduced new Dungeons & Dragons merchandise and a customizable Selfie Series.

title: Are Hobson and Rice Mere Pawns for the NFL?
summary: Mellody Hobson and Condoleezza Rice made history by joining the Denver Broncos ownership group as the first Black women involved in an NFL team's ownership. While lauded for bringing diversity, their roles have also drawn criticism, with some questioning if their additions are merely a public relations move by the NFL, especially amidst a discrimination lawsuit filed by former coach Brian Flores. The article explores both the historical significance of their appointments and the controversy surrounding their past affiliations and the implications for the league's diversity efforts.

title: BUILD-A-BEAR WORKSHOP CONTINUES 25TH ANNIVERSARY CELEBRATION WITH NEW VAULT RELEASE AND SPECIAL POKÉMON AND DISNEY PRINCESS COLLABORATIONS
summary: Build-A-Bear Workshop is extending its 25th-anniversary celebration with new limited-edition releases, including the Floppy Kitty from "The Vault" and special collaborations with Pokémon and Disney Princesses. The event also features a "Beary Big Adventure Sweepstakes" offering a trip to the World Bearquarters in St. Louis and exclusive access to the Silver Celebration Gala. Customers are encouraged to share their Build-A-Bear memories and join the Bonus Club for exclusive offers and updates.

title: The Walt Disney Company Joins Propel Education Center in Support of the Next Generation of Diverse Storytellers and Innovators
summary: The Walt Disney Company has partnered with Propel, an education hub for Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs), as the lead sponsor for arts, media, entertainment, and hospitality. This collaboration aims to expand opportunities for underrepresented students to pursue careers as storytellers and innovators. Disney will help create curriculum, provide guest speakers, and offer mentorship and internship placements, focusing initially on technology and hospitality to bridge academic training with industry job opportunities.

title: The Future of Modern Payments Processing is Here: Moov Financial Joins Forces with Visa and Pathward to Improve Payments and Onboarding Experience for ISV's
summary: Moov Financial has announced its launch as a direct merchant acquiring processor on the Visa network, partnering with Pathward N.A. This collaboration aims to enhance payment processing and onboarding experiences for platform, vertical SaaS, and fintech companies by providing a streamlined path to card processing and other services. Moov's modern and modular technology enables quick merchant onboarding and direct connection to the Visa network.

title: Next wave of Disney campaign donations could signal whether the Mouse is mad at Florida Republicans
summary: This article explores whether The Walt Disney Company's political donations to Florida Republicans will resume after tensions arose over Disney's opposition to the "Parental Rights in Education" bill and the subsequent dissolution of the Reedy Creek Improvement District. Historically, Disney has been a major donor to Florida Republicans, giving millions each election cycle, but paused donations indefinitely following the conflict. The article suggests that the upcoming donation period will indicate if Disney plans to renew its support for the GOP or pursue a different political strategy.

title: Comcast Corp. Cl A stock rises Tuesday, outperforms market
summary: Comcast Corp. Cl A (CMCSA) stock increased by 0.45% on Tuesday, closing at $37.68, despite a broader market downturn where the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average both fell. This rise ended a three-day losing streak for Comcast and allowed it to outperform competitors like Walt Disney Co., Rogers Communications Inc. Cl B, and DISH Network Corp. Cl A. The stock is currently $24.12 short of its 52-week high reached on September 3rd.

title: Disney class action alleges Visa, Mastercard charge high transaction fees
summary: The Walt Disney Co. has filed a class action lawsuit against Visa and Mastercard, alleging that the payment companies colluded to force merchants to pay excessively high transaction fees for over a decade, violating antitrust laws. Disney claims these "interchange fees" are supracompetitive and seeks damages, fees, and costs, arguing that more competition between card-issuers would benefit both merchants and consumers. This action follows Disney's decision to opt out of a previous $6 billion multidistrict litigation settlement with Visa and Mastercard regarding similar fee-fixing allegations.

title: The World of Warcraft mobile game was officially canceled
summary: Blizzard and NetEase have officially canceled the World of Warcraft mobile game, which had been in development for three years, due to disagreements over financial terms. This cancellation, along with another Warcraft-based augmented reality project, raises questions about Blizzard's mobile strategy and its partnership with NetEase, despite their co-creation of the commercially successful Diablo Immortal. The situation highlights challenges in adapting existing franchises to mobile platforms and the complexities of international gaming partnerships.

title: Chairman Of World’s Hottest Stock AMTD Now Worth Nearly $37 Billion, More Than Li Ka-Shing
summary: Calvin Choi, chairman of AMTD Digital, has seen his stake in the company surge to nearly $37 billion, making him Asia's sixth-richest person on paper. This valuation, driven by a 14,000% stock increase, is largely unexplainable by the company's financial performance or small employee base. Despite concerns about the stock's stability and comparisons to meme stocks, Choi continues to expand AMTD Group's ventures, including into the metaverse, while facing scrutiny over past financial practices.

title: Why a former Netflix executive joined the Deluxe leadership team
summary: Anna Lee, a former Netflix executive, joined Deluxe as Chief Strategy Officer following Platinum Equity's acquisition of Deluxe Entertainment's distribution business. Lee's expertise from Netflix is being leveraged to expand Deluxe's content distribution and localization services, particularly through its Showcase platform, targeting emerging opportunities in streaming and virtual events. The strategic hire aims to enhance Deluxe's ability to serve content creators across various platforms, regardless of traditional cinema attendance.

title: Guardians Of The Galaxy: Should You Buy Disabler Or Not
summary: This article discusses whether players should buy the "disabler" item in Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy. While the item is a scam within the game's narrative and Rocket will mock the player for purchasing it, buying it does contribute to achieving 100% game completion and unlocking the "Lore Hoarder" trophy/achievement. Players are advised to consider their in-game currency before making the purchase for trophy hunting purposes.

title: Walmart Ponders Streaming Deal With Paramount, Disney and Comcast (Published 2022)
summary: Walmart is reportedly in discussions with major media companies, including Paramount, Disney, and Comcast, to integrate a streaming service into its Walmart+ membership program. This initiative aims to expand Walmart's relationship with customers beyond its physical stores, similar to how wireless providers have bundled streaming services. The move is seen as an effort to compete with Amazon.com's Prime and maintain its influence in the entertainment sector as consumption shifts online.

title: 20th Century Studios’ ‘Prey’ Is the No. 1 Premiere on Hulu to Date
summary: 20th Century Studios' film "Prey" has become the most-watched premiere on Hulu to date, surpassing all other film and TV series debuts. It also achieved the top spot for film premieres on Star+ in Latin America and Disney+ under the Star Banner across other territories, based on hours watched in its first three days. The movie is a new installment in the Predator franchise, set 300 years ago in the Comanche Nation, and follows a young warrior named Naru as she confronts an advanced alien predator.

title: Ad-Supported Disney+ Subscription Tier To Launch In The U.S. On December 8
summary: The Walt Disney Company announced that an ad-supported Disney+ subscription tier will launch in the U.S. on December 8, 2022, offering consumers more choices and price points. Alongside this, new subscription plans across Disney+, Hulu, ESPN+, and the Disney Bundle will be introduced, providing flexibility in streaming options. Kareem Daniel, Chairman, Disney Media & Entertainment Distribution, emphasized that these services offer unparalleled content and value with a vast library of movies, TV episodes, original shows, sports, and live events.

title: Disney edges past Netflix in streaming subscribers as it raises ad-free prices
summary: Disney has surpassed Netflix in total streaming subscribers, reaching 221 million across Disney+, Hulu, and ESPN+, while Netflix reported 220.7 million. In response to subscriber growth driven by content like "Obi-Wan Kenobi," Disney announced an ad-supported Disney+ tier priced at $7.99/month, with the ad-free version increasing to $10.99/month as of December 8. Despite the subscriber increase, Disney's streaming services reported a $1.1 billion loss for the quarter.

title: Disney tops Netflix on streaming subscribers, sets higher prices
summary: Walt Disney Co. surpassed Netflix Inc. in total streaming subscribers, reaching 221 million customers globally. Following this milestone, Disney announced price increases for its ad-free Disney+ and Hulu services, while introducing an ad-supported Disney+ option at the current price point. The company also adjusted its long-term subscriber forecast for Disney+ downwards due to the loss of cricket streaming rights in India, although it still expects its streaming unit to be profitable by fiscal year 2024.

title: HBO Max: Everything You Need to Know About the Big OTT Service From Cost to Content
summary: This article provides an overview of HBO Max, covering its subscriber growth, content strategy, pricing, and the impact of its spin-off from AT&T and merger with Discovery. It details the company's shift towards streaming content, its financial performance, and future plans for combining with Discovery Plus and international expansion changes.

title: The FIFA 23 Pitch Will Be Legendary With EA Sports x Marvel Collab
summary: EA Sports and Marvel Entertainment are collaborating for FIFA 23, introducing new FIFA Ultimate Team Heroes reimagined and inspired by Marvel Comics. This partnership will feature special illustrations by Marvel artists, untradeable FUT items for World Cup FUT Heroes, and various Marvel-themed vanity items for players. Additionally, an online Marvel Heroes comic book will be released, with limited edition physical versions available later.

title: Tony the Tiger® Tackles Twitch and Becomes the First-Ever Brand Mascot Working with Twitch to Transform into an Interactive VTuber
summary: Kellogg's Frosted Flakes and Tony the Tiger are collaborating with Twitch to transform Tony the Tiger into an interactive VTuber for a livestreamed gaming event. This marks the first time a brand mascot will engage with Twitch in this capacity, with Tony competing against popular streamers in a battle royale game. The event aims to connect with new audiences and deepen engagement with fans through an innovative gaming experience.

title: U.S. Toy Industry Sales Grow 2% as Unit Sales Decline
summary: The U.S. toy industry saw a 2% increase in dollar sales to $11.4 billion in the first half of 2022, despite a 6% decline in unit sales. This growth is attributed to an 8% rise in average selling price and indicates the industry's resilience amidst inflation and challenging comparisons to the pandemic-driven boom of 2020-2021. Plush, Explorative and Other toys (including trading cards), Action Figures & Accessories, and Building Sets were the top-performing categories.

title: Watch the newest commercials from T-Mobile, Acorns, Cîroc and more
summary: This article highlights new commercials from various brands, including T-Mobile, Acorns (featuring Christopher Walken), Cîroc, Subway, and Principal Financial Group. It briefly mentions other topics covered by Ad Age, such as AI in campaigns and marketing winners and losers.

title: I Am Groot Comes to Build A Bear Workshop with Adorable New Plush
summary: Build-A-Bear Workshop has released a new 17-inch plush of Baby Groot, an online exclusive tied to the "I Am Groot" shorts now streaming on Disney+. This pre-stuffed plush features leaves and bark design but does not offer custom additions like scents or sounds. It's priced at $32, joining other Marvel characters like Thor and Vision in the Build-A-Bear collection.

title: In Sports Streaming Milestone, Sinclair’s Bally Sports+ Sets Nationwide Launch Date
summary: Sinclair Broadcast Group's regional sports unit, Diamond Sports Group, has announced that its direct-to-consumer streaming service, Bally Sports+, will launch nationwide on September 26. Priced at $19.99 a month or $189.99 a year, the service aims to attract sports fans who don't have pay-TV subscriptions, offering access to Major League Baseball, NBA, and NHL games, among others. This launch marks a significant step in transferring the regional sports network model to the digital age, despite challenges with major streaming platforms like Roku and Amazon Fire TV.

title: Environmental sustainability: going green at Disney
summary: The Walt Disney Company announced ambitious environmental sustainability goals for 2030, focusing on greenhouse gas emissions, water, waste, materials, and sustainable design. Emily Dow and Caitlin Krasovic from Walt Disney Imagineering discussed the progress, including efforts to achieve net-zero Scope 1 & 2 emissions, 90% construction waste diversion, and defining science-based targets for Scope 3 emissions by the end of 2022. They also highlighted specific projects like Lighthouse Point and the Epcot transformation, emphasizing the integration of sustainable design and collaboration across teams and with suppliers.

title: Insider: Fox, Big Ten made a big bet on TV future; it paid off Thursday
summary: The Big Ten's long-term bet on its media future through a joint venture with Fox paid off significantly with a new seven-year, multi-network media rights package worth over $1 billion annually, excluding ESPN. This deal positions Fox as a dominant player in college sports broadcasting, alongside ESPN, and is expected to push annual per-school distributions for the Big Ten to $100 million or more. The arrangement also brings in CBS and NBC, expanding their college football and basketball inventory, with significant content streaming exclusively on NBC's Peacock.

title: Charlie Collier's Driving Force
summary: Charlie Collier, CEO of Fox Entertainment, is celebrated for his visionary leadership in transforming Fox Broadcasting into a multifaceted entertainment company after Disney's acquisition of 20th Century Fox. He emphasizes the "power of broadcast" and strategically leverages it to build new businesses and platforms, including acquisitions like Tubi, MarVista Entertainment, and Bento Box, while preserving Fox's "rebel roots" in programming. Collier's approach is marked by a deep trust in creators and a commitment to bold, original content, reflecting his belief that "Nobody Knows Anything" with certainty in Hollywood.

title: Moonbug Entertainment Announces First Deal Across EMEA with the Walt Disney Company for Go Buster and Lellobee City Farm
summary: Moonbug Entertainment has secured its first distribution deal with The Walt Disney Company across the Europe, Middle East, and Africa region for its series Go Buster and Lellobee City Farm. Both shows, spin-offs of Little Baby Bum, will be available on Disney+ starting September in multiple languages. This collaboration expands Moonbug's partnership with Disney and aims to broaden its reach in the EMEA market.

title: Miko announces Disney and Pixar collaboration
summary: Miko, a consumer robotics company, has announced an historic collaboration with Disney and Pixar, bringing animated storybooks and content featuring beloved characters to its Miko robot. This partnership marks the first official Disney app on a kids' robot platform, suggesting a growing role for AI in children's entertainment. Families can access select Disney stories for free or subscribe to Miko Max for full content access, enhancing playful learning experiences for children aged 5 to 10.

title: McDonald's Appoints Jon Banner as Executive Vice President and Global Chief Impact Officer
