summary: McDonald's has appointed Jon Banner as Executive Vice President and Global Chief Impact Officer, reporting directly to CEO Chris Kempczinski. In this role, Banner will oversee Sustainability & ESG, Government Relations and Public Policy, Communications, International Corporate Relations, and Ronald McDonald House Charities. He brings extensive experience from PepsiCo and Disney/ABC, where he led communications and sustainability initiatives.

title: Marcus Theatres Chief Rolando Rodriguez to Retire
summary: Rolando Rodriguez, the chief executive of Marcus Theatres, announced his retirement effective October. He will be succeeded by Mark Gramz and will remain chairman of the National Association of Theatre Owners. The company reported strong financial results for its second quarter, with theatre admission revenues reaching $63 million and concessions at $58 million, despite a 24 percent drop in admission revenue compared to pre-pandemic 2019.

title: ESPN Events Joins Forces with Marvel Studios and The Walt Disney Company on “Black Panther: Wakanda Forever” Collaboration at 2022 Cricket MEAC/SWAC Challenge Kickoff – Saturday in Atlanta
summary: ESPN Events is collaborating with Marvel Studios and The Walt Disney Company for a "Black Panther: Wakanda Forever" promotion at the 2022 Cricket MEAC/SWAC Challenge Kickoff. The college football game between Howard University and Alabama State University will feature film elements in the stadium and during the ESPN telecast. This initiative aims to connect the spirit of Wakanda with the cultural significance of Atlanta and HBCUs, coinciding with the film's November 11 release.

title: Disney’s theme park price hike nets more profit from fewer visitors: report
summary: Despite fewer visitors, Disney's theme parks have achieved record sales and profits due to price increases and new revenue strategies. The company's Genie+ app and additional charges for popular rides have contributed to increased costs for guests. Disney attributes its pricing to "pure supply and demand," while some parkgoers feel the company is overcharging.

title: Netflix shakes up film team as senior executive exits
summary: Netflix is restructuring its film team, leading to the departure of senior executive Tendo Nagenda, who was a vice president of original film for four years and worked on movies like "The Harder They Fall" and "Da 5 Bloods." This change aims to simplify the film team's structure, leaving Kira Goldberg and Ori Marmur to lead the studio film group. The reshuffle occurs as Netflix faces increased competition and seeks to cut costs and boost its subscriber base.

title: Rogue One IMAX Re-Release Propels Film Into IMAX All-Time Top 10
summary: The IMAX re-release of "Rogue One: A Star Wars Story" has grossed an additional $1 million, pushing its lifetime IMAX earnings to $105 million and placing it among the top 10 highest-grossing films in the format. This re-release, which included a preview of the upcoming "Andor" series, aimed to build anticipation for the spin-off show. "Andor," a prequel to "Rogue One," is set to debut on Disney+ with its first three episodes on September 21st.

title: Horror movie 'The Invitation' tops lukewarm weekend at box office
summary: The horror film "The Invitation" led the North American box office with a modest $7 million, marking the weakest weekend of the summer. Despite the overall lackluster performance, the year-to-date box office remains strong compared to 2021. The industry anticipates a rebound with major releases in October, while a "National Cinema Day" offering $3 tickets is set for the upcoming Saturday to boost attendance.

title: Movie tickets to cost just $3 on 'National Cinema Day' across U.S.
summary: Movie tickets will be available for just $3 across most cinemas in the United States on September 3, as part of 'National Cinema Day'. This initiative, spearheaded by The Cinema Foundation, aims to encourage moviegoers back to theaters after a significant lull during the pandemic. Over 3,000 theaters and 30,000 screens will participate, offering tickets at the discounted price, excluding tax, for all formats and show times.

title: The Walt Disney Company Hosting Q&A at the 2022 Bank of America Securities Media, Communications & Entertainment Conference
summary: The Walt Disney Company announced that Christine McCarthy, Senior Executive Vice President and CFO, and Josh D’Amaro, Chairman of Disney Parks, Experiences and Products, will participate in a Q&A session. This event will take place at the 2022 Bank of America Securities Media, Communications & Entertainment Conference on September 7th, 2022, at 1:30 p.m. ET/10:30 a.m. PT. A live stream and archive of the session will be available online.

title: Hudson Pacific buys Quixote Studios in $360-million deal
summary: Hudson Pacific Properties has acquired Quixote Studios for $360 million, significantly expanding its soundstage business to meet growing demand. Quixote, founded in 1995, provides production services in multiple cities and operates studios in Los Angeles, serving clients like HBO and Walt Disney. This acquisition occurs amid an intensifying competition to provide soundstages and production facilities fueled by a content boom, with existing soundstages in Los Angeles County almost fully rented for years.

title: Procter & Gamble Is Doing The Unified ID 2.0 Thing
summary: Procter & Gamble publicly announced its support for Unified ID 2.0, an open-source initiative led by The Trade Desk aiming to replace third-party cookies with hashed, encrypted email-based identifiers. P&G has already been using UID 2.0 since last year for activating anonymized identifiers linked to its first-party data in the bidstream. Attracting marketers like P&G is crucial for UID2's success, although scaling the initiative and finding an administrator remain ongoing challenges.

title: The Untold Truth Of Steak 'N Shake
summary: Steak 'n Shake, a burger and milkshake chain founded in 1934, has experienced significant transformations and challenges despite its longevity. Changes include its parent company, Biglari Holdings, also owning Maxim magazine, a unique and inexpensive franchise partner program, and efforts to operate internationally. The chain has faced recent struggles with numerous store closings, a shift from full-service dining to self-service kiosks, lawsuits from franchisees and employees, and a near bankruptcy experience.

title: Pixar Fest Kicks Off with New Products from Crocs, Mattel, and More!
summary: Disney is celebrating Pixar Fest throughout September, coinciding with Lightning McQueen Day on September 5th. This month-long event includes weekly activities, watch parties, and new merchandise releases. Fans can expect new products from Crocs and Mattel for "Cars On The Road," "Lightyear," "The Incredibles," and "Coco."

title: Box CEO Aaron Levie, who taught Stanford class on digital disruption, admires Disney's evolution
summary: Box CEO Aaron Levie discusses how incumbent companies have successfully adapted to digital disruption, highlighting Disney's response to the streaming threat with Disney+. He also expresses skepticism about Web3's economic implementation despite its idealistic promises of digital asset ownership and open systems. Levie emphasizes that many CEOs learned from the failures of companies like Kodak and Blockbuster, driving them to innovate.

title: The Walt Disney Company Announces 103 Exclusive National Hockey League Games Across ESPN, ESPN+, Hulu and ABC Beginning October 11
summary: The Walt Disney Company announced its schedule of 103 exclusive National Hockey League games for the 2022-23 season, to be broadcast across ESPN, ESPN+, Hulu, and ABC. The season kicks off on October 11 with a doubleheader featuring the Tampa Bay Lightning vs. New York Rangers and Vegas Golden Knights vs. Los Angeles Kings. The coverage also includes the NHL All-Star Weekend, the Stadium Series, and over 1,050 out-of-market games on ESPN+.

title: Disney Advertising Hits the Road for 2022-23 College Football Season with Strong Slate of College GameDay Built by The Home Depot Sponsors
summary: Disney Advertising has secured nine sponsors for College GameDay Built by The Home Depot for the 2022-23 college football season, including returning brands like The Home Depot, Aflac, and AT&T, plus new additions DoorDash and Old Dominion Freight Line. These sponsors will integrate into the show through various activations, segments, and creative campaigns, leveraging College GameDay's high viewership. This strong lineup underscores the program's appeal to brands looking to connect with passionate college football fans.

title: Apple’s iPhone 14 launch sets off competing wireless promotions
summary: The launch of Apple's iPhone 14 has ignited fierce promotional competition among major U.S. wireless carriers, including AT&T, T-Mobile, and Verizon. These promotions involve free phones, discounts, and bundled services like Apple One to attract and retain customers. The competitive landscape is impacting carrier subscriber growth and profit margins as they vie for market share.

title: Netflix looks to control cloud computing costs with AWS - WSJ
summary: Netflix is reportedly working to control its rising cloud computing costs with Amazon Web Services as part of a broader effort to reduce expenses. The streaming giant is also hiring more junior staff, reducing its real-estate footprint, and minimizing data storage globally following subscriber losses and increased competition. These measures aim to help Netflix manage costs and achieve its goal of 500 million global subscribers in the next three years.

title: Disney Live Action, Pixar, and Walt Disney Animation Studios Present Upcoming Slate of Films and Series at D23 Expo 2022
summary: The D23 Expo 2022 showcased upcoming films and series from Walt Disney Studios, Pixar, and Walt Disney Animation Studios. Highlights included new live-action adaptations like "Hocus Pocus 2", "Disenchanted", "The Little Mermaid", and "Snow White", as well as Pixar's "Elemental", "Win or Lose", "Elio", and "Inside Out 2". Walt Disney Animation Studios also unveiled "Zootopia+", "Iwájú", "Strange World", and the new original film "Wish", set to release in 2023.

title: Disney Legends Awards Ceremony and Disney 100 Years of Wonder Kick Off D23 Expo 2022
summary: The Walt Disney Company honored 14 talents as Disney Legends at D23 Expo 2022, continuing a 35-year tradition, with the ceremony hosted by Tamron Hall. CEO Bob Chapek also launched the Disney 100 Years of Wonder celebration, marking the company's 100th anniversary with new content, experiences, and programming. Honorees included Chadwick Boseman, Tracee Ellis Ross, and the cast of Frozen, recognized for their significant contributions to Disney's legacy.

title: New Details About Disney 100 Years of Wonder Revealed to Fans During D23 Expo
summary: During the D23 Expo 2022, Disney unveiled extensive plans for its "Disney 100 Years of Wonder" celebration, marking the largest global celebration in the company's history. This included new entertainment like the animated musical "Wish" and live-action films, the Disney100: The Exhibition set to tour internationally, and special events and nighttime spectaculars at Disney Parks worldwide. Additionally, new merchandise collections and publishing titles are being released to commemorate the 100th anniversary.

title: Studios Become Hot Commodities
summary: Quixote Studios, a 27-year-old provider of content production services, was acquired by Hudson Pacific Properties Inc. for $360 million. The acquisition enhances Hudson Pacific's studio business by adding sound stages and production services, capitalizing on the high demand for studio space driven by the streaming wars. Other major real estate developers are also investing heavily in new soundstage projects across Los Angeles.

title: Crunchyroll class action alleges company shares user data with Facebook
summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Sony Group Corporation, owner of Crunchyroll, alleging that the streaming service shared its digital subscribers' personally identifiable information and video viewing data with Facebook without consent. Plaintiff Lisa Cuevas claims Crunchyroll violates the Video Privacy Protection Act (VPPA) by using a Facebook Pixel to collect and disclose this data. The lawsuit seeks injunctive relief, declaratory relief, and punitive damages for a nationwide class of affected Crunchyroll subscribers.

title: The Walt Disney Company Wins 26 Primetime Emmy® Awards
summary: The Walt Disney Company earned 26 Primetime Emmy Awards across its various content brands and studios, including 19 wins for its streaming platforms, Hulu and Disney+. Notable wins include "The Beatles: Get Back" sweeping its categories, "Chip ‘n’ Dale: Rescue Rangers" making history as the first animated film to win Outstanding Television Movie, and several acting awards for stars from Hulu Originals. ABC and 20th Television's "Abbott Elementary" also secured three wins.

title: Grindr Appoints George Arison as Chief Executive Officer and Vanna Krantz as Chief Financial Officer
summary: Grindr has appointed George Arison as its new Chief Executive Officer, effective October 19, 2022, and Vanna Krantz as Chief Financial Officer, effective September 26, 2022. These appointments are part of a planned leadership transition as Grindr prepares for its public listing. Arison brings experience as the founder and CEO of Shift Technologies, Inc., while Krantz previously served as CFO of Disney Streaming Services.

title: Comcast CEO Brian Roberts: NBCUniversal Would Love to Buy Hulu Outright From Disney
summary: Comcast CEO Brian Roberts expressed NBCUniversal's strong interest in purchasing Hulu outright from Disney, rather than selling its 33% stake. Speaking at a Goldman Sachs conference, Roberts highlighted Hulu's significant value and scale, suggesting a "robust auction" would occur if Disney decided to sell the platform. This statement comes ahead of Comcast's 2024 right to sell its stake to Disney for at least $27.5 billion.

title: Disney’s Pandemic Recovery Is Bringing Digital Innovation to Forefront of Theme Parks
summary: During the D23 Expo, Josh D'Amaro, chairman of Disney Parks, Experiences and Products, highlighted digital innovation as central to Disney's future. He announced significant updates to the theme park experience, which will likely integrate Disney+ content into the parks to enhance the visitor experience. D'Amaro emphasized Disney's commitment to constantly reinventing itself and telling new stories for future generations.

title: Disney+ Hotstar delivers unique headphone experience in Dolby Atmos
summary: Disney+ Hotstar has partnered with Dolby Laboratories to bring Dolby Atmos immersive audio to its users. This new feature, which launched after Dolby Vision support, provides a multidimensional, spatial sound experience on compatible devices. The collaboration aims to enhance entertainment by making content more immersive and is available for a wide range of Disney+ Hotstar titles and upcoming releases.

title: OTT Platform DISNEY+ HOTSTAR now supports Dolby Atmos on compatible TVs, AVRs, soundbars, Android smartphones and iOS devices
summary: Disney+ Hotstar has expanded its audio support to include Dolby Atmos for its users, delivering a multidimensional, spatial sound experience on compatible devices. This new feature, complementing existing Dolby Vision support, aims to immerse users more deeply in their favorite movies and shows. A wide range of titles, including Hotstar Specials and Multiplex content, are now available with Dolby Atmos.

title: Disney focuses on local content for global expansion
summary: Disney is shifting its focus to local content for global expansion, particularly in the Asia-Pacific region, to attract more subscribers to its streaming services. The company has invested a significant portion of its production budget in South Korea and Japan, with a particular emphasis on K-content due to its broad global appeal. This strategy has already led to substantial subscriber growth, surpassing Netflix in total streaming subscribers.

title: Netflix and Disney+ Are About to Get Ads. What It Means for Streaming Stocks.
summary: Netflix and Disney+ are soon launching ad-supported tiers, a move that is expected to significantly impact the future of streaming. This shift marks a new era for these streaming giants, as the success of their shares may hinge on the adoption and performance of these new ad-supported options. The introduction of commercials could redefine the streaming experience for subscribers and potentially boost the companies' financial performances.

title: Here's how to watch or stream Saturday's Nevada-Iowa football game
summary: This article provides details on how to watch or stream the Nevada-Iowa football game scheduled for Saturday. The game will be broadcast nationally on the Big Ten Network, with various streaming options available through Fox Sports. It also lists the broadcast crew and local radio information, along with related articles to prepare for the game.

title: Sinclair may sell Bally Sports channels to MLB, NBA and NHL, report claims
summary: A new report suggests that Major League Baseball (MLB), the National Basketball Association (NBA), and the National Hockey League (NHL) may bid for Sinclair Broadcast Group's 21 Bally Sports-branded regional sports networks. Sinclair, which acquired the channels from Disney for $10.6 billion, has faced challenges with carriage agreements and recently launched a direct-to-consumer streaming service, Bally Sports Plus. The company is reportedly seeking to sell the entire sports group for about $3 billion, including debt, to avoid potential bankruptcy for its subsidiary, Diamond Sports Group.

title: ACE South Central Celebrates Frontier Fest
summary: American Coaster Enthusiasts (ACE) recently held their Frontier Fest event at Frontier City, the first such event since 2018. The park, owned by EPR Properties and operated by Six Flags, was highlighted by its Director of Operations and Maintenance, Zach Vobornick, for its unique feel and growth potential, emphasizing infrastructure's importance. Marketing and Public Relations Manager Aileen Garcia praised the park's distinct theming, friendly environment, and unique position within the Six Flags family.

title: DISH Network Corp. Cl A stock falls Tuesday, underperforms market
summary: DISH Network Corp. Cl A (DISH) stock fell 5.11% on Tuesday, closing at $16.16, significantly underperforming the broader market. This marked the second consecutive day of losses for the company, which is $30.15 below its 52-week high. The stock also performed worse than competitors like Walt Disney Co. (DIS), Netflix Inc. (NFLX), and Comcast Corp. Cl A (CMCSA).

title: Strive launches Strive 500 ETF
summary: Strive Asset Management has introduced its second index fund, the Strive 500 ETF (NYSE: STRV), designed to mirror the Solactive GBS United States 500 Index. The ETF aims to provide diversified large-cap exposure to US corporations and seeks to unlock investor value through pro-fiduciary shareholder engagement, moving companies to prioritize value maximization over other agendas. Strive emphasizes its commitment to clients' financial interests, independent of social or political objectives.

title: WPP acquires leading communications agency JeffreyGroup
summary: WPP has acquired JeffreyGroup, a prominent independent corporate communications, public affairs, and marketing consulting firm in Latin America. The acquisition will integrate JeffreyGroup into WPP's Hill+Knowlton Strategies network, creating the largest global communications agency presence in the region. This move aligns with WPP's accelerated growth strategy and aims to strengthen its services in the important Latin American market.

title: Why IMAX is acquiring AI-driven video company SSIMWAVE
summary: IMAX is acquiring SSIMWAVE, an AI-driven video quality solutions company, for $20.5 million to expand its business beyond theaters and focus on streaming capabilities. This acquisition will allow IMAX to leverage SSIMWAVE's technology for video optimization across various platforms, reduce content compression costs, and pursue research and development for next-generation video experiences. The move reflects IMAX's strategy to diversify revenue and adapt to changes in content consumption, particularly after the pandemic.

title: Charlie Collier Exits Fox Corp. to Join Roku as President of Media
summary: Charlie Collier, CEO of Fox Entertainment, is leaving to become president of Roku Media, overseeing advertising sales and content for Roku's owned-and-operated channels. This move is part of Roku's strategy to evolve into a "next-generation media company" amidst pressure from Wall Street regarding its stock price. Collier's appointment, alongside other executive promotions, aims to strengthen Roku's content strategy and relationships with key partners.

title: How Marvel's digital comics strategy (including Webtoons) intersects with the mainstream popularity of the MCU
summary: Marvel has expanded its global reach by leveraging the mainstream popularity of the MCU through digital comics strategies like Webtoons and Marvel Unlimited's Infinity Comics. These initiatives aim to attract new international audiences and MCU fans to Marvel Comics by creating mobile-friendly, vertically scrolling content and primers for characters appearing in films and shows. The strategy involves both international partnerships, such as the Marvel WEBTOON Project in Korea, and exclusive domestic content on Marvel Unlimited.

title: Abigail Disney takes on family's company in new documentary: 'We have lost the plot'
summary: Abigail E. Disney, granddaughter of co-founder Roy O. Disney, has released a documentary titled "The American Dream and Other Fairy Tales," criticizing The Walt Disney Co. for losing its moral compass. The film highlights pay inequity and the struggles of theme park employees on minimum wage, arguing the company has strayed from its benevolent origins. Disney expresses her love for the company but believes she cannot remain silent as it "goes off the rails."

title: WWE Expands Exclusive Deal With Foxtel in Australia
summary: WWE has expanded its exclusive deal with Foxtel Group in Australia, making the pay-TV giant the sole destination for WWE content in the country. This multi-year partnership will see WWE Network content become available exclusively through Foxtel's streaming service Binge from January 2023, while Foxtel channels FOX8 and a new dedicated 24/7 WWE channel will air live events and weekly shows. The agreement aims to grow WWE's audience in Australia and provides Foxtel subscribers with access to premium live events at no extra cost.

title: Lovesac and Disney+ Give Customers a Front Row Seat to Salem for Hocus Pocus 2
summary: Lovesac is partnering with Disney+ for the release of Hocus Pocus 2, launching a campaign to enhance the at-home streaming experience with its StealthTech Sound + Charge System. This system, integrated into Lovesac's Sactionals, offers immersive surround sound and wireless charging. The collaboration also includes a "Watch With Your Witches Ultimate Movie Night Sweepstakes" where customers can win a customized Sactionals setup and a special Hocus Pocus 2 Footsac Blanket with purchases of StealthTech.

title: Lionsgate Targets Spinning Off Studio While Rebranding Starz Streamer Overseas
summary: Lions Gate Entertainment Corp. announced its intention to spin off its Lionsgate studio business and rebrand its Starz streaming service outside the U.S. to Lionsgate+. This strategic move aims to create two distinct companies for investors, allowing for separate valuation of Starz assets and the film/TV production studio, despite previous speculation that the streaming service would be spun off to reduce debt.

title: Abigail Disney Criticizes Labor Practices at the Company Her Family Founded
summary: Abigail Disney, Walt Disney Company co-founder Roy Disney's granddaughter, has released a new documentary titled "The American Dream and Other Fairy Tales" which critiques the labor practices of the company. The film highlights income inequality and the struggles of Disney employees, some of whom work for $15 an hour and face challenges meeting basic needs. While primarily focusing on broader issues of workers' rights in America, the documentary notably criticizes the Walt Disney Company for deviating from its once "kinder" image.

title: Fast Facts: Rihanna and the Super Bowl
summary: Comscore announced "Fast Facts: Rihanna and the Super Bowl" on September 28, 2022, highlighting the social media anticipation surrounding Rihanna's confirmed performance for the 2023 Super Bowl Halftime Show. Fans expressed excitement not only for her performance but also for the potential release of a new album. The piece emphasizes the intersection of music, social media, sports, and television analytics.

title: American Electric Power crews heading to Florida to help with Hurricane Ian
summary: American Electric Power (AEP) is deploying approximately 600 workers from AEP Ohio to Florida to assist with power restoration following Hurricane Ian's anticipated "total devastation." However, AEP West Virginia crews are remaining in their state due to a potential local weather threat. Meanwhile, Disney World in Orlando is shutting down as the hurricane is expected to bring over a foot of rain to the area, impacting residents like Kaley Morris who are unfamiliar with a storm of this magnitude.

title: The Walt Disney Company Appoints Veteran Media and Technology Executive Carolyn Everson to Its Board of Directors
summary: The Walt Disney Company announced the appointment of Carolyn Everson, a seasoned media and technology executive, to its Board of Directors, effective November 21. This decision reinforces Disney's commitment to a strong, independent board and has the support of Third Point LLC, an investment firm. Everson's extensive experience from companies like Facebook (Meta) and Instacart is expected to bring valuable perspective to Disney's global brand expansion and long-term growth strategies.

title: How ‘Hocus Pocus 2’ Weaves Disney History into the Sanderson Sisters’ New Costumes
summary: This article explores the costume design process for Disney's "Hocus Pocus 2," focusing on how costume designer Salvador Perez updated the iconic looks of the Sanderson sisters. Released 29 years after the original, the filmmakers aimed for refreshed yet familiar outfits, incorporating Disney archival research, Wiccan mythology, and modern craftsmanship. The piece details specific design choices for Winifred, Sarah, and Mary, highlighting elements like hand-embroidery, custom boots, and symbolic rings.

title: Kareem Daniel Elected to McDonald's Board of Directors
summary: McDonald's Corporation announced the election of Kareem Daniel to its Board of Directors as an independent Director, effective October 1, 2022. Daniel currently serves as Chairman, Disney Media and Entertainment Distribution at The Walt Disney Company, bringing extensive experience in brand building, consumer expertise, and leadership from his 15-year tenure at Disney. His appointment expands the board to 15 members, enhancing its collective experience.

title: DISH Network And Walt Disney Company Do A Rare ‘Handshake’ Carriage Agreement For Cable Networks
summary: DISH Network and The Walt Disney Company reached a "handshake agreement" to restore Disney's cable networks, including ESPN, to DISH's platform after a brief blackout. This rare event occurred before a formal contract was signed, allowing viewers to access channels like ESPN for "Monday Night Football." The terms of the agreement, particularly regarding ESPN's carriage on non-sports programming packages, were not disclosed, but both parties are working to finalize a new deal.

title: Marvel Studios Debuts ‘Black Panther: Wakanda Forever’ Trailer
summary: Marvel Studios has released a new trailer and poster for "Black Panther: Wakanda Forever." The film returns to Wakanda, where a new threat from the undersea nation of Talokan emerges after King T’Challa’s death. The Wakandan heroes, joined by War Dog Nakia and Everett Ross, must unite to protect their nation and forge a new path.

title: Build-A-Bear Entertainment and Hello Sunshine Partner on Reimagined Goldilocks and the Three Bears Feature Film
summary: Build-A-Bear Entertainment and Hello Sunshine, founded by Reese Witherspoon, are partnering to develop a reimagined feature film of "Goldilocks and the Three Bears." This modern take will present Goldilocks as a powerful female protagonist and marks the first children's feature from Hello Sunshine's Kids and Animation division. Executives from both companies, including Reese Witherspoon and Sharon Price John, will executive produce the project.

title: Walt Disney Company to celebrate 100th anniversary with special events, experiences at Disneyland Resort
summary: The Walt Disney Company plans to celebrate its 100th anniversary, dubbed "100 Years of Wonder," with special events and experiences launching January 27, 2023, at Disneyland Resort in Anaheim. The celebration will include two new nighttime spectaculars, the early opening of Mickey & Minnie's Runaway Railway, and the return of the "Magic Happens" parade, alongside platinum décor throughout the park. More details are expected to be announced closer to the kick-off date.

title: ‘LofyGang’ hacking group targets Discord, Disney+ and Minecraft accounts
summary: Security researchers at Checkmarx Ltd. have exposed a hacking group named "LofyGang" responsible for over 200 malicious packages and thousands of installations in 2022. The group, believed to be Brazilian, targets online accounts to steal credit card information and premium accounts for services like Discord, Disney+, and Minecraft. LofyGang operates openly, promoting tools on GitHub and having a Discord server, highlighting the risks of untrusted open-source code.

title: Major Theme Park Company Introduces Nationwide Changes to Security Policy, Guests Worried
summary: Six Flags has implemented new nationwide security policies, including a strict bag policy and X-ray screening of all bags, causing concern among guests. Bags must now be no larger than 12″x 12″ x 6″ for entry, with exceptions for medical reasons and diaper bags. These changes follow a series of violent incidents at various theme parks, and similar measures have been adopted by other parks like Knott's Berry Farm and Carowinds.

title: Disney’s ESPN and DraftKings near deal as views on sports gambling change
summary: ESPN, a Walt Disney Co. subsidiary, is reportedly close to finalizing a major partnership with sports-betting company DraftKings Inc. This move would allow Disney to capitalize on the growing legalized sports betting market, despite its historical aversion to gambling due to its family-friendly brand. The potential collaboration is seen as a strategic step for both companies, enabling them to expand their audiences and integrate betting odds directly into broadcasts.

title: NewsNation, other Nexstar channels could disappear from Verizon Fios
summary: Verizon is warning its Fios customers that they may lose access to Nexstar Media Group's local stations and NewsNation by the end of the week. This potential outage stems from ongoing negotiations over a significant fee increase requested by Nexstar, which Verizon describes as "unreasonable." Nexstar, however, states it is seeking "fair market rates" for its programming and hopes to reach an agreement to avoid service interruptions.

title: Fox's Tubi touts over 200 streaming channels — but is anyone watching them?
summary: Tubi, Fox Corporation's free ad-supported streaming service, now offers over 200 linear content streams, including news, sports, and general entertainment. Despite an impressive roster of channels and contribution to Fox's $3 billion revenue, a survey by Interpret Research suggests only 20% of Tubi users regularly engage with its linear channels, with the majority preferring on-demand content. Tubi has aggressively pursued local news deals, a strategy differentiating it from competitors like Pluto TV and the Roku Channel.

title: IGN Acquires Agency 1TwentyFour in Brand Partnership Push
summary: IGN, a prominent entertainment and gaming publisher, has acquired brand partnership agency 1TwentyFour to enhance its service offerings for clients. This acquisition grants brands access to IGN's audience across various platforms and countries, leveraging shared resources. 1TwentyFour will operate as a standalone division, with co-founder Karl Stewart taking on a new role to develop brand partnerships across multiple sectors.

title: How much Netflix’s new ad-supported plan will cost and what you get (and don’t)
summary: Netflix is launching a cheaper, ad-supported plan for $6.99 a month starting November 3rd in the U.S., which will include 4 to 5 minutes of commercials per hour. While this plan offers a discount, some shows and movies will be unavailable due to licensing, and downloads won't be permitted. This move comes as Netflix faces increased competition and investor pressure to grow its subscriber base and revenue.

title: Netflix to get Nielsen ratings as streaming giant rolls out ad-supported plan
summary: Netflix will begin using Nielsen ratings for its ad-supported plan in the U.S. starting in 2023, offering advertisers better insights into audience reach. This move coincides with the launch of Netflix's $6.99 monthly ad-supported tier in November, aimed at boosting revenue after recent subscriber losses. Other streaming services like Amazon Prime and Disney+ also offer ad-supported plans, with varying price points and advertisement loads.

title: Netflix ad-supported plan to launch in November at $7 a month
summary: Netflix announced it will launch an ad-supported streaming plan for $6.99 per month in November, aiming to attract new subscribers after a period of customer losses. This "Basic with Ads" tier, which is $3 cheaper than the current lowest-priced ad-free option, will roll out in 12 countries. While it will include four to five minutes of advertising per hour, some programming will be unavailable due to licensing restrictions, and newly released films will have limited ads to preserve their cinematic experience.

title: Murdochs Mull New Combination of Fox, News Corp.
summary: Rupert Murdoch is exploring a potential re-merger of Fox Corp. and News Corp., the two media companies his family split in 2013. Special committees have been formed by both companies to consider the combination, which would reunite assets like Fox News and Harper Collins under one umbrella again, though the entities are now smaller than before the original split. The move comes as traditional media companies face pressure to gain scale against tech giants.

title: Rupert Murdoch explores reuniting Fox and News Corp.
summary: Rupert Murdoch is exploring the possibility of combining his media companies, News Corp. and Fox Corp., which he split in 2013. News Corp. has formed a special committee to consider a potential deal, though a merger is not certain. A reunification could consolidate leadership and cut costs, particularly as both print media and cable television face declining audiences.

title: Breakingviews - Rupert Murdoch’s odd reunion simplifies succession
summary: Rupert Murdoch's family trust is seeking to recombine News Corp and Fox, nearly a decade after their split. While the business logic is unclear, given the differing nature of publishing and TV news, the move is seen as a way to simplify future succession plans for the Murdoch empire. The boards of both companies have formed independent committees to explore a potential merger.

title: U.S. Speaker Pelosi's husband sold Nvidia, Micron options at a loss
summary: U.S. House Speaker Nancy Pelosi's husband, Paul Pelosi, sold call options in chipmakers Micron Technology and Nvidia, incurring losses close to $1 million. The transactions were disclosed in a transparency filing, which also showed he exercised call options for Alphabet shares and allowed Walt Disney call options to expire at a loss. This comes amid scrutiny over stock trading by lawmakers and their families, leading to legislative efforts to restrict such activities.

title: TEA releases 2021 Theme Index and Museum Index
summary: The Themed Entertainment Association (TEA) has released its 2021 Theme Index and Museum Index, reporting encouraging signs of recovery for the global visitor attraction sector. The report highlights significant attendance increases in North America and improved revenues for operators like Merlin Entertainments, showing resilience despite pandemic impacts. While Asia-Pacific's recovery is slower due to China's Zero COVID policy, the industry globally is seeing a return to normality with increased per capita spending and investment in new attractions.

title: Third Point takes stake in Colgate-Palmolive, urges pet food spinoff
summary: Activist investor Third Point, led by Daniel Loeb, has acquired a significant stake in Colgate-Palmolive Co. The firm is advocating for the spinoff of Colgate's Hill's Pet Nutrition business, believing it could be worth around $20 billion as a standalone entity and would unlock significant hidden value. Third Point views Colgate as a defensive investment with pricing power amid inflation and expects mid to high teens returns over the next several years.

title: Netflix reverses subscriber slump, shares surge 14%
summary: Netflix Inc. reported a significant reversal in customer losses, adding 2.4 million subscribers in the third quarter and forecasting 4.5 million new customers in Q4, leading to a 14% surge in its shares. The company plans to introduce an ad-supported streaming option in November and achieved $7.9 billion in revenue with $3.10 earnings per share for the quarter. This positive outlook signals renewed growth for the streaming giant after a challenging first half of the year.

title: Comcast Corp. Cl A stock falls Wednesday, underperforms market
summary: Comcast Corp. Cl A (CMCSA) shares decreased by 1.17% on Wednesday, closing at $30.39, while the broader stock market (S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average) also experienced declines. The stock underperformed compared to some competitors, such as Walt Disney Co. and Rogers Communications Inc. Cl B, but outperformed DISH Network Corp. Cl A. This was its second consecutive day of losses, placing it significantly below its 52-week high.

title: ‘Caesars Palace Times Square’ Proposal Vies for a Downstate Retail Casino License
summary: Caesars Entertainment and SL Green Realty Corporation have announced plans for "Caesars Palace Times Square" at 1515 Broadway, seeking one of three downstate retail casino licenses in New York. The project, which would redevelop One Astor Plaza, aims to appeal to both tourists and New Yorkers, promising economic and infrastructure improvements. The proposal faces competition from other contenders like Resorts World Casino and Empire City Casino.

title: VI Delegation Attends 28th Annual Cruise Conference
summary: The Virgin Islands delegation, led by Deputy Premier Honourable Kye M. Rymer, attended the 28th annual Florida-Caribbean Cruise Association (FCCA) Cruise Conference and received positive reviews on the cruise tourism industry's outlook. Discussions focused on certified transportation training, integrating local products onto ships, employment opportunities for Caribbean nationals on cruise lines, and strengthening supply chains for product consistency. The delegation is optimistic about the Virgin Islands' position in delivering exceptional cruiser experiences.

title: The Walt Disney Company, ESPN, Formula 1 Extend Relationship with New, Multi-Year Contract
summary: The Walt Disney Company, ESPN, and Formula 1 have extended their broadcasting agreement, ensuring F1 races remain on ESPN Networks in the U.S. through the 2025 season. The new multi-year contract includes increased race coverage on ABC and ESPN, continuation of commercial-free presentations, and expanded direct-to-consumer rights for content distribution. This extension comes amid record-breaking viewership for F1 in the U.S. and reflects the sport's growing popularity.

title: Walt Disney Co. Grants $1 Million to Exceptional Minds Nonprofit
summary: The Walt Disney Company has committed a $1 million multi-year grant to Exceptional Minds, a nonprofit creative arts academy for young adults with autism, as part of its Future Storytellers initiative. The grant aims to enhance the academy's technology and curriculum, preparing neurodivergent talent for careers in storytelling and potentially within Disney. Exceptional Minds leadership expects the funding to significantly advance infrastructure, particularly in virtual production, and support the employment of alumni within the academy and its VFX studio.

title: ESPN and F1 announce new U.S. broadcast deal through 2025
summary: ESPN and Formula 1 have extended their U.S. broadcast deal through 2025, continuing ESPN's commercial-free coverage of F1 races. This agreement comes amidst a significant surge in F1's popularity and viewership in the United States, marked by record viewership figures and an expanded race calendar. Additionally, the announcement coincided with news that Logan Sargeant is likely to become the first American F1 driver since 2015, further fueling U.S. interest in the sport.

title: Disney Announces $1 Million Multi-Year Grant to Exceptional Minds in Support of Inclusion and Diversity in Entertainment
summary: The Walt Disney Company has granted $1 million to Exceptional Minds, a nonprofit academy for young adults on the autism spectrum, to support inclusion and diversity in the entertainment industry. This multi-year grant, part of the Disney Future Storytellers initiative, will fund curriculum development and training for neurodivergent individuals in animation, visual effects, and 3D gaming. The partnership highlights Disney's long-standing collaboration with Exceptional Minds, which has placed graduates in roles at Marvel Studios and worked on numerous Disney productions.

title: Mastercard Teams up With Marvel Studios’ Black Panther: Wakanda Forever to Spotlight Small Business Superheroes
summary: Mastercard has partnered with Marvel Studios' "Black Panther: Wakanda Forever" to celebrate Black excellence and the strength of Black women, both on and off-screen. This collaboration spotlights Black women small business owners, like Egypt Otis of Comma Bookstore & Social Hub, through a Wakanda-inspired commercial and various initiatives. Mastercard's efforts extend its $500 million commitment to close the racial wealth and economic gap in the U.S. by supporting Black women-owned businesses through the Strivers Initiative, exclusive screenings, and new digital platforms like the Mastercard Small Biz Marketplace on Instagram and a Small Business Metaverse platform.

title: Outlets at Tejon to hold outdoor movie screening at night
summary: The Outlets at Tejon are bringing back their "Cinema Under the Stars" event with a Halloween theme, featuring a screening of "The Nightmare Before Christmas" on October 29th. The event will include trick-or-treating at participating stores before the movie and food provided by the local nonprofit The League of Dreams. Attendees are encouraged to wear costumes, and the event aims to provide a safe and festive Halloween celebration for families.

title: Announces $1 Million Multi-Year Grant for the Disney Storytellers Fund at Florida A&M University | The Walt Disney Company
summary: The Walt Disney Company announced a $1 million multi-year grant to Florida A&M University's School of Journalism & Graphic Communication (SJGC), establishing the Disney Storytellers Fund at FAMU. This grant, part of the Disney Future Storytellers program, aims to support students from underrepresented communities with scholarships, stipends, and mentorship to pursue careers in storytelling and innovation. ABC News President and FAMU alumna Kim Godwin highlighted the initiative's potential to empower future Black journalists and media executives.

title: The Walt Disney Company Announces A $1 Million Multi-Year Grant For Disney Storytellers Fund At Florida A&M University
summary: The Walt Disney Company has committed a $1 million multi-year grant to Florida A&M University's (FAMU) School of Journalism & Graphic Communication (SJGC) to establish the Disney Storytellers Fund. This initiative, part of the Disney Future Storytellers program, aims to support journalism students from underrepresented communities with scholarships, mentoring, and specialized training over the next five years. The grant seeks to foster diversity in storytelling and empower the next generation of Black journalists and media executives.

title: Man of the cloth: Wallstrom departs Vera Bradley
summary: Rob Wallstrom, CEO of Vera Bradley, is departing the company after leading it for nearly a decade to pursue seminary studies and focus on speaking and writing. During his tenure, Vera Bradley saw significant partnerships, received high rankings on Forbes' Best Midsize Employers list, and contributed millions to breast cancer research through its foundation. Wallstrom will be succeeded by Jacqueline Ardrey and plans to remain active in the Fort Wayne community through faith-based non-profit Love Fort Wayne.

title: EA and Marvel Entertainment Announce Multi-Title Collaboration to Make Action Adventure Games
summary: Electronic Arts and Marvel Entertainment have announced a long-term collaboration to develop at least three new action-adventure games for consoles and PC. The first title confirmed is a single-player, third-person Iron Man game developed by Motive Studios, featuring an original narrative focused on Tony Stark. This partnership aims to create unique Marvel Universe experiences for players.

title: Electronic Arts Strikes Three-Game Deal With Marvel
summary: Electronic Arts (EA) has secured a deal with Marvel to develop three video games based on Marvel comic book characters. The first announced game will be a single-player action-adventure title featuring Iron Man for PCs and consoles. EA has not yet revealed details about other characters or a release timeline for the games.

title: EA and Marvel Entertainment Announce a Multi-Title Collaboration to Make Action Adventure Games
summary: Electronic Arts (EA) and Marvel Entertainment have announced a multi-title collaboration to develop at least three new action-adventure games for consoles and PC. The first title in development is a single-player, third-person Iron Man game being created by Motive Studios, featuring an original narrative within the Marvel universe. This collaboration highlights EA's long-standing admiration for Marvel and Marvel's commitment to finding top-tier teams to bring their characters to life in new ways.

title: EA to develop three Marvel games, beginning with Iron Man
summary: Electronic Arts (EA) has announced a deal to develop three action-adventure games based on Marvel characters, starting with an Iron Man title. The games will feature original narratives and be available on consoles and PC, expanding EA's presence in the popular superhero gaming market. This move comes as EA faces a slowdown in demand after pandemic highs.

title: Disney Receives 86 Children’s & Family Emmy® Award Nominations
summary: The Walt Disney Company has received 86 nominations for the inaugural Children's & Family Emmy® Awards across its various content brands and studios. Disney+ and Hulu platforms alone garnered 62 and 7 nominations, respectively. The awards ceremony is scheduled for December 10 and 11 in Los Angeles.

title: FuboTV to Stream Select World Cup Matches in 4K/HDR
summary: FuboTV announced it will stream select FIFA World Cup games in 4K/HDR, starting November 20 with the Qatar vs. Ecuador match. All 64 matches will be broadcast by Fox Sports and Telemundo, with FuboTV offering English language 4K/HDR coverage to its Ultimate and Elite subscribers. FuboTV was the first vMVPD to stream in 4K during the 2018 World Cup and has continued to innovate in live sports viewership.

title: McDonald's launches 'Black Panther: Wakanda Forever' Happy Meal
summary: McDonald's has launched a special "Black Panther: Wakanda Forever" Happy Meal to promote the upcoming Marvel Studios film. The Happy Meal includes toys modeled after characters from the movie and will be available nationwide for a limited time. The initiative aims to celebrate the film's powerful story and representation, bringing the experience to McDonald's customers.

title: David Zaslav defends Warner Bros. Discovery cuts: 'We did not get rid of any show that was helping us'
summary: Warner Bros. Discovery CEO David Zaslav defended significant cuts made at the company, stating that no show "that was helping us" was removed and framed the actions as part of a fundamental "rethinking and reimagining." The company increased its synergy goal to $3.5 billion in savings and plans to launch a combined streaming service in spring, while also beefing up franchises like DC amidst a $50-billion debt load and a challenging economic environment. Zaslav criticized the prior strategy of growing subscriptions at all costs, emphasizing a focus on the bottom line and the importance of theatrical releases.

title: Infographic: Walt Disney Company (DIS) Q4 revenue up 9%, earnings miss
summary: The Walt Disney Company reported its fourth-quarter results, showing a 9% increase in revenue to $20.15 billion, which missed expectations. Adjusted earnings, however, decreased to $0.30 per share from $0.37 per share a year earlier, also falling short of forecasts. CEO Bob Chapek expressed optimism for the future, citing cost realignment, price increases, and the upcoming Disney+ ad-supported tier as drivers for profitable streaming and shareholder value.

title: Growth Stocks: The Walt Disney Company
summary: The Walt Disney Company (DIS.US) is preparing to release its Q4 2022 financial results, with investors closely watching the performance of its streaming service, Disney+, despite a challenging market and a 36% year-to-date stock decline. While the company lowered its 2024 Disney+ subscriber target, it still expects significant growth, alongside a strong recovery in its Parks and Experiences division and improvements in theatrical distribution. The article highlights the importance of cash flow generation, debt reduction, and forecasted revenue and earnings per share for the company's future outlook.

title: Disney+ Debuts Trailer for Documentary ‘Idina Menzel: Which Way to the Stage?’
summary: Disney+ has released the official trailer for its upcoming documentary, "Idina Menzel: Which Way to the Stage?". The film follows Disney Legend Idina Menzel as she pursues her lifelong dream of headlining Madison Square Garden, documenting her national tour and the challenges of being a working mom. The documentary is set to premiere on Friday, December 9, exclusively on Disney+.

title: Disney Awards $1 Million In Grants To Support Youth In STEM And The Arts In Honor Of Marvel Studios’ "Black Panther: Wakanda Forever"
summary: In celebration of Marvel Studios' "Black Panther: Wakanda Forever," Disney has committed $1 million in grants to nonprofit organizations focusing on STEM and arts education for underrepresented youth. This initiative, part of Disney Future Storytellers, aims to inspire young people and increase their access to careers in media, entertainment, technology, and hospitality. Additionally, Disney and Target hosted community screenings of the film for nearly 25,000 young people.

title: LBE Will Abound at IAPPA
summary: The article discusses the resurgence of location-based entertainment (LBE) offerings, many delayed by the pandemic, set to be unveiled at the International Association of Amusement Parks and Attractions (IAPPA) show. It highlights new attractions from companies like Lotte World Adventure, Triotech, Mattel, and Hasbro licensee Rockafella Leisure, indicating a shift where LBE is becoming its own significant business sector. Despite an increase in new LBE projects, the industry faces challenges such as inflation, supply chain issues, and tightening consumer budgets for entertainment, making the future profitability and consumer reception of these ventures uncertain.

title: The Walt Disney Company’s Heroes Work Here Program Celebrates 10-Year Milestone
summary: The Walt Disney Company is celebrating the 10th anniversary of its Heroes Work Here program, an initiative launched in 2012 to hire, train, and support U.S. military veterans. The program has successfully onboarded over 12,500 veterans and led to the creation of the Veterans Institute, which helps other companies establish veteran-hiring programs. Additionally, Disney's Heroes Supply Here initiative has significantly increased spending with veteran-owned businesses, reflecting the company's long-standing commitment to servicemen and women.

title: The Walt Disney Company Explores the Future of Immersive Experiences at 2022 Disney Accelerator Demo Day
summary: The Walt Disney Company hosted its 2022 Disney Accelerator Demo Day, showcasing six growth-stage companies focusing on technologies such as AR, NFTs, and AI virtual characters. CEO Bob Chapek highlighted Disney's commitment to using technology to enhance storytelling and connect with audiences. The event celebrated collaborations between Disney and the participating companies, aiming to redefine the media landscape and create new immersive experiences for fans.

title: Disney plans to freeze hiring and cut some jobs, memo shows
summary: The Walt Disney Co will freeze hiring and implement some job cuts as it aims to make its Disney+ streaming service profitable amid economic uncertainties. CEO Bob Chapek sent a memo outlining these cost-management measures, following Disney missing Wall Street earnings estimates and accumulating significant losses from its direct-to-consumer business. A task force has been formed to make "critical big picture decisions" on spending without sacrificing content quality.

title: Hasbro Inc. stock rises Friday, outperforms market
summary: Hasbro Inc. (HAS) stock rose 5.00% on Friday to $63.41, outperforming the broader market which also saw gains with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average rising. The stock closed significantly below its 52-week high but showed mixed performance compared to competitors like Walt Disney Co. and Activision Blizzard Inc. Trading volume was slightly below its 50-day average.

title: ‘Wakanda Forever’ Tops Box Office With $180 Million Debut
summary: Disney's "Black Panther: Wakanda Forever" achieved a significant box office success, grossing $181.3 million in its opening weekend in the US and Canada and $330 million globally. This performance exceeded expectations and was a boost for theaters like AMC. The film's appeal, particularly to women through its Black female heroes, contributed to its strong debut.

title: Bob Greenblatt, Allison Janney Partner to Adapt ‘Confident Women’ Into Anthology Series for Amazon (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Bob Greenblatt and Allison Janney are collaborating with writer Alexa Junge to develop an anthology series called "Confident Women" for Amazon Prime Video. The series will be based on Tori Telfer's book, which explores the stories of female con women throughout history. Janney is attached as a non-writing executive producer, and each season will focus on a different woman's story, starting with Sante Kimes.

title: Court told Musk's $56 billion pay wasn't for punching a clock
summary: A Delaware court heard arguments regarding Elon Musk's $56 billion Tesla pay package, with a director and former executive defending it against a shareholder's claim that Musk dictated terms. The shareholder alleges Musk used his dominance to craft the 2018 package and duped investors, while defendants argue the package incentivized Musk during a critical growth period for Tesla. The trial examines the board's latitude in setting executive compensation, especially for a controlling shareholder, and will impact the future of Musk's compensation from Tesla.

title: Hasbro to Sell eOne TV, But Keep Family Brands Such as 'Peppa Pig', 'Transformers' and 'Power Rangers'
summary: Hasbro is initiating a sale process for the non-core parts of its eOne TV and film business while retaining key family brands like Peppa Pig, Transformers, and Power Rangers. This move is part of the company's Blueprint 2.0 strategy to focus strategic investment on core Hasbro brands including gaming, direct-to-consumer, franchise brands, and licensing. J.P. Morgan and Centerview Partners have been retained to assist with the sale, which is expected to take several months.

title: Disney Parks, Experiences and Products Awarded for Industry Excellence
summary: Disney Parks, Experiences, and Products received three Thea Awards and nine Brass Ring Awards at the 2022 IAAPA Expo. Awards recognized innovations like Star Wars: Galactic Starcruiser, the Main Street Electrical Parade, and Tokyo DisneySea. Additionally, Disney Live Entertainment Creative Director Susana Tubert was honored with the Thea Catalyst Award for her significant contributions to the industry.

title: Netflix Still on Top in Terms of Original Content, with 37% of All Movies and Shows
summary: A study by BB Media, commissioned by Media Play News, found that Netflix leads all streaming services in original content, offering 3,260 titles, which accounts for nearly 37% of the total original content across 41 platforms in the U.S. HBO Max and Yupp TV follow, with Amazon Prime Video ranking among the top five. When considering hours of original content, Prime Video displaces IQIYI for fourth place.

title: ‘Transformers: Earthspark’ Features Non-Binary Bot
summary: Hasbro, Paramount Plus, and Nickelodeon have introduced a non-binary Autobot named Nightshade in the animated children's show "Transformers: Earthspark," voiced by Z Infante. The character uses they/them pronouns, though the article notes some fan dissatisfaction and criticism regarding character changes and perceived "wokeness" in Hasbro's recent projects. The author points out that Nightshade was previously depicted as a female character and highlights other instances of Hasbro making gender-neutral changes to its brands.

title: Robert A. Iger Appointed CEO by Disney Board of Directors
summary: The Walt Disney Company announced the immediate return of Robert A. Iger as Chief Executive Officer. Iger, who previously served as CEO for 15 years, will lead the company for two years to set strategic direction for growth and help identify his successor. He replaces Bob Chapek, who has stepped down from the position.

title: Columbia Sportswear Has a New Line of Winter Star Wars Gear for Clone Wars Fans
summary: Columbia Sportswear has launched a new "Defenders of Justice" line of Star Wars-themed winter gear, inspired by the Clone Wars animated series. The collection features jackets designed after Anakin, Obi-Wan, and Ahsoka's attire during the Orto Plutonia campaign, intended for extremely cold weather. In addition to the parkas, the line also includes matching pullovers and ball caps.

title: Bob Iger returns as CEO of Walt Disney Company, board announces
summary: Bob Iger has returned as CEO of The Walt Disney Company, effective immediately, replacing Bob Chapek who has stepped down. Iger will serve for two years with a mandate to set new strategic directions for growth and work with the board to develop a successor. He previously served as CEO from 2005 and oversaw major acquisitions like Marvel, Pixar, and Lucasfilm.

title: Walt Disney CFO, Others Brought Concerns to Board Over Bob Chapek
summary: The sudden replacement of Disney CEO Bob Chapek by former chief Robert Iger was driven by growing discontent among investors and top executives, including CFO Christine McCarthy. Concerns about Chapek's leadership were reportedly brought to the board after a poor fiscal-fourth-quarter earnings report. In the wake of Iger's return, a key Chapek lieutenant was dismissed, and Iger announced plans for organizational restructuring to prioritize creativity.

title: Bob Iger In, Bob Chapek Out as Walt Disney Company CEO
summary: In a surprising move, Bob Iger has returned as CEO of The Walt Disney Company, replacing Bob Chapek, effective immediately. Chapek's tenure was marked by controversies including a stock price drop and public disputes, while Iger, who previously led a period of significant growth, is tasked with navigating the company through current industry transformations. The announcement led to an immediate 8% jump in Disney's stock price.

title: Former Twitter Employees Sue Company Alleging WARN Act Violations
summary: Former Twitter employees have filed a lawsuit against the company, alleging violations of both California's and the federal Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification (WARN) Acts. The lawsuit claims that Twitter failed to provide the legally required 60 days' notice before mass layoffs, impacting approximately 3,700 employees. This action seeks to prevent further unlawful layoffs and secure back pay and benefits for affected workers, though potential arbitration clauses similar to those in a Tesla case could complicate the class action.

title: Roku, Vix, Warner Bros. Discovery Execs Join Gen Z Entertainment Panel
summary: Top executives from Vix, Roku Inc., and Warner Bros. Discovery will participate in a virtual panel discussion on December 6, focusing on "Gen Z Entertainment – Finding the Next Wave of Consumers in TV Streaming." The panel will explore how to reach, attract, and retain Gen Z consumers, who are digitally native and have unique entertainment habits, discussing key insights across search, content affinity, and audience behavior. Registration for the B2B event, moderated by Variety's Todd Spangler, is free and required for access.

title: Potential News Corp, Fox reunion faces opposition from large shareholder
summary: Rupert Murdoch's proposed recombination of News Corp and Fox Corp. is facing notable opposition from large shareholders like Independent Franchise Partners and Irenic Capital Management. These shareholders argue that a merger would not realize News Corp's true value, advocating instead for alternatives such as breaking up News Corp or selling off specific assets. The opposition highlights concerns about undervaluation and the strategic disadvantages of recombining the companies.

title: Fox Corp. Cl A stock rises Wednesday, still underperforms market
summary: Shares of Fox Corp. Cl A (FOXA) rose 0.58% to $31.08 on Wednesday, despite the broader market also seeing gains, with the S&P 500 Index rising 0.59% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average rising 0.28%. The stock, however, underperformed compared to competitors like Walt Disney Co., Netflix Inc., and Comcast Corp. Cl A. Fox Corp. Cl A closed $13.87 below its 52-week high of $44.95.

title: News Corp-Fox merger plan opposed by big shareholder
summary: A major investor, Independent Franchise Partners, has expressed opposition to Rupert Murdoch's plan to recombine News Corp and Fox Corp, raising a potential hurdle to the merger. This follows earlier dissent from another investor, Irenic Capital, suggesting alternatives like spinning off digital real estate or Dow Jones. Analysts and some close to the Murdochs view the reunion attempt as driven by succession planning, despite the companies previously being split in 2013.

title: Apple's interest in Manchester United would mark a major escalation in the ‘streaming war’
summary: Reports that Apple is interested in buying Manchester United could signal a significant shift in the streaming wars. Apple TV, currently a minor player, could leverage football's massive global audience to become a major streaming power. Acquiring a club like Manchester United would give Apple a crucial negotiating position for future broadcast rights, combining commercial opportunities with strategic content acquisition in the highly competitive streaming market.

title: House Republicans target U.S. Chamber of Commerce as GOP battle against ‘woke capitalism’ revs up
summary: House Republicans are intensifying their campaign against "woke capitalism," targeting corporations that have embraced environmental, social, and governance (ESG) goals or supported Democratic candidates. This has put the U.S. Chamber of Commerce in the crosshairs, with House Speaker Kevin McCarthy reportedly pushing for a leadership change after the Chamber endorsed some Democrats. The growing rift between the GOP and big business stems from differing views on social issues, immigration, and climate change, threatening legislative gridlock and increasing scrutiny on corporate practices.

title: "Twelve Days of Christmas" - 12 companies for the Santa Claus Rally
summary: This article discusses the "Santa Claus Rally," a stock market phenomenon typically occurring in late December and early January, where the S&P 500 historically sees an average rise of 1.3%. It examines past rallies, their occurrence during bear markets, and potential reasons for the phenomenon, such as tax optimization and investor sentiment. The article then highlights 12 companies, including Amazon, Alphabet, and NVIDIA, that could benefit from this rally and provide investment opportunities based on their current valuations and market positions.

title: Scholastic Names Mary Beech as Chief Marketing & Transformation Officer
summary: Scholastic has appointed Mary Beech as its new Chief Marketing & Transformation Officer, effective January 1, 2022. Beech, who previously served as an independent director on Scholastic’s board, will report directly to CEO and president Peter Warwick in this newly created role. She brings experience from her most recent position as CEO of Sarah Flint and prior roles at MRB Brand Consulting, Kate Spade New York, and The Walt Disney Company.

title: Bring Home the Galaxy With Vera Bradley's New 'The Mandalorian' Collection [Exclusive]
summary: Vera Bradley has launched an exclusive "The Mandalorian" collection, offering 32 Grogu-themed items ranging from luggage tags to a quilt set. The new line features a unique color palette inspired by the series, departing from Vera Bradley's traditional bright florals. This release coincides with anticipation for Season 3 of "The Mandalorian."

title: Apple TV's Lloyd Sam talks money — from a $50 dare to when he won’t pay extra
summary: Lloyd Sam, an Apple TV MLS commentator, shares his financial perspective in an interview with Ally's "Money Clips" series. Sam discusses his early savings habits which led to accidental real estate development, his current savings goals for a Range Rover, and his refusal to pay extra for first-class travel. He also reflects on financial lessons learned from his accountant father, emphasizing value and hard work.

title: ‘Indiana Jones and the Dial of Destiny’ Teaser Trailer Released
summary: The Walt Disney Company has released the teaser trailer and poster for "Indiana Jones and the Dial of Destiny," the highly anticipated fifth installment in the iconic franchise. Starring Harrison Ford and directed by James Mangold, the film is set to open in theaters on June 30, 2023. John Williams is composing the score once again.

title: Gray Names Curtis Miles as the General Manager of KCTV and KSMO in Kansas City
summary: Gray Television, Inc. announced the appointment of Curtis Miles as the General Manager of KCTV (CBS) and KSMO (MyNetwork) in the Kansas City market, effective January 3, 2023. Miles brings extensive experience in news, marketing, research, and sales, previously leading WAOW in Wausau, Wisconsin, to increased ratings and revenues. His background also includes 13 years with Disney ABC O&O group, where he notably re-launched "Eyewitness News" at WLS-TV in Chicago.

title: After Disney’s ‘Strange World’ bombs, film critic says ‘go woke, go broke’
summary: Disney's animated movie "Strange World," which features an openly LGBTQ+ teenage character, is set to lose an estimated $147 million at the box office. Film critic Christian Toto attributes this underperformance to the "go woke, go broke" phenomenon, suggesting that parents are avoiding content with sexual conversations in children's movies. Toto believes poor box office results may eventually force companies like Disney to re-evaluate their content strategies.

title: Recapping Bob Chapek's Time As CEO Of The Walt Disney Company, And What Went Wrong
summary: This article examines Bob Chapek's turbulent tenure as CEO of The Walt Disney Company, highlighting key events from February 2020 to November 2022 that led to his replacement by Bob Iger. It details challenges such as the Covid-19 pandemic, strategic shifts towards streaming, controversies surrounding LGBTQ+ issues, and financial struggles. The piece concludes with Iger's return and the immediate positive market reaction, emphasizing his task to reverse Disney's declining share value.

title: Disney offers SoCal residents discounted Disneyland tickets next year
summary: Disneyland is offering a discounted ticket offer for Southern California residents to celebrate the Walt Disney Co.'s 100th anniversary in 2023. Residents can purchase three-day, mid-week tickets for Disneyland or Disney California Adventure for as low as $73 per day, valid from January 9 to May 25. The celebration will include platinum decorations, two new nighttime spectaculars, and the debut of the Mickey and Minnie's Runaway Railway ride.

title: New Products on shopDisney Celebrating 100 Years of The Walt Disney Company
summary: shopDisney is launching limited-release collections to celebrate The Walt Disney Company's 100th anniversary, starting with the Disney Platinum Celebration Collection on December 12, 2022. Additional collections, including the Disney100 Oswald Collection, The Eras Collection, and Decades Collection, will roll out throughout the year. Fans are encouraged to join the social media celebration using #ShareTheWonder and #Disney100.

title: Former Disney CEO Michael Eisner Buys Up IAC Stock
summary: Former Disney CEO Michael Eisner has acquired a substantial block of shares in IAC, the internet and media company. Eisner, who founded Tornante and previously led Walt Disney, made the purchase amidst IAC's recent struggles.

title: Watching FIFA World Cup 2022 on FuboTV: how to get soccer streams for every game
summary: This article provides a comprehensive guide on how to watch the FIFA World Cup 2022 using FuboTV for US subscribers, covering pricing plans, features like 4K streaming and DVR, and compatible devices. It also explains how to bypass geo-restrictions using a VPN for those outside the US and offers alternative streaming services like Sling TV and Hulu + Live TV.

title: Disney Advertising enhances clean room capabilities with VideoAmp partnership
summary: Disney Advertising is upgrading its data clean room technology through a partnership with VideoAmp, integrating measurement, planning, and optimization tools to help advertisers with audience-based matches across platforms. This move comes ahead of the Disney+ ad-supported tier launch and addresses the growing need for meaningful advertising measurements in connected TV and the deprecation of third-party cookies. The collaboration aims to provide advertisers with better insights into audience reach and frequency across Disney's properties, with initial brand tests already underway with Omnicom Media Group.

title: Ad-Supported Disney+ Plan Now Available In The U.S. With More Than 100 Advertisers Across All Major Categories At Launch
summary: Disney+ has launched its ad-supported subscription plan in the U.S., featuring over 100 advertisers across various major categories. This new "Basic" plan offers the full content catalog and key features available on the Premium plan, but at a lower price point and without premium features like downloads. The initiative aims to provide consumers with more flexible options and connect advertisers with Disney's extensive content library.

title: Will TNT Walk Away From The NBA?
summary: Warner Bros. Discovery CEO David Zaslav's recent comments questioning the necessity of the NBA for TNT have sparked industry speculation about the future of their 33-year partnership. As the NBA seeks significantly increased media rights—potentially $50 billion to $75 billion—from incumbents TNT and ESPN, the possibility of tech giants like Amazon entering the bidding process looms. While an NBA-TNT divorce seems unlikely due to their deep integration and the network's commitment to "Inside the NBA," the evolving media landscape and WBD's cost-cutting measures could lead to a reevaluation of the relationship, possibly involving a split package with streaming services.

title: Build-A-Bear Introduces New “Monsters, Inc.” Plush Friends
summary: Build-A-Bear Workshop has released new plush friends featuring Mike and Sulley from Disney and Pixar's "Monsters, Inc." These plush figures are available online and in stores. The James P. Sullivan plush is priced at $36.00 and stands 17 inches tall, while the Mike Wazowski plush costs $26.00 and is appropriately scaled at 11 inches.

title: Dow Jones Sustainability Indices Results Announced: Walmart, Disney In, Starbucks, UPS Out
summary: S&P Dow Jones Indices (S&P DJI) announced the results of its annual rebalancing of the Dow Jones Sustainability Indices (DJSI), which track companies based on ESG criteria. Notable changes to the DJSI North America index include the addition of Walmart and Disney, while Starbucks and UPS were removed. The 2022 review incorporated significant methodology changes, focusing on net-zero commitments, decarbonization strategies, and circular economy principles.

title: CalChamber Board Elects Greg Bielli, President and CEO of Tejon Ranch Company, as 2023 Chair
summary: The California Chamber of Commerce Board of Directors has elected Greg Bielli, President and CEO of Tejon Ranch Company, as its 2023 chair. Bielli emphasized the CalChamber's ongoing role in advocating for California businesses and addressing critical challenges such as housing shortages, water issues, energy costs, and income inequality to promote economic growth. The article also lists other key officers and executive committee members elected for 2023.

title: ESPN and Cinemark Once Again Team Up to Bring College Football’s Biggest Games to the Big Screen, This Time Expanding Theater Count
summary: ESPN and Cinemark are partnering again to show college football playoff games and the National Championship in theaters, expanding the number of participating Cinemark locations. Following last year's success, fans can purchase $10 concession packages to watch the College Football Playoff Semifinals and the National Championship live on the big screen with pre-game studio programming. The initiative aims to provide an immersive, shared viewing experience for college football enthusiasts.

title: Another Major Cruise Line to Raise Gratuity Rates
summary: Holland America Line is set to increase its daily gratuity rates by $0.50 per guest starting February 1, 2023, following a trend seen across other major cruise lines like Princess Cruises, Norwegian Cruise Line, Royal Caribbean International, and Disney Cruise Line. This adjustment will raise rates to $17.50 for suites and $16.00 for non-suite staterooms. The article speculates that other cruise lines under the same corporate umbrellas might also follow suit, as such increases are historically common in the industry.

title: 13 Years After ‘Avatar,’ More Than Half of Americans Still Plan to See Its Sequel
summary: Thirteen years after the original "Avatar," over half of U.S. adults (58%) plan to see its sequel, "Avatar: The Way of Water," with 21% intending to watch it in theaters. While streaming remains the preferred viewing method overall, the film leads other blockbusters in intent for theatrical viewing, especially in non-standard formats like IMAX and 3D. This indicates a potential glimmer of hope for the theatrical industry against the rising tide of streaming, particularly for visually immersive films.

title: Disney+ Debuts ‘Encanto at the Hollywood Bowl’ Trailer
summary: Disney+ has unveiled the trailer for "Encanto at the Hollywood Bowl," a live-to-film concert experience featuring the original voice cast of the Academy Award-winning film. The special, which includes an introduction by Lin-Manuel Miranda and performances by special guests, will be available to stream exclusively on Disney+ starting Wednesday, December 28. It transforms the Hollywood Bowl into the world of Encanto with an 80-person orchestra, 50 dancers, and special effects.

title: Netflix Shares Sink After Report of Weaker Ad Demand
summary: Netflix shares dropped significantly after a report indicated weaker-than-expected ad demand for its new advertising-supported tier, with some advertisers able to reclaim money due to unfulfilled audience targets. Analysts, however, view this as an early-stage issue for the product, expecting audience growth and improved ad tech to resolve it in the long run. The ad tier, launched in November, is still seen as a significant catalyst for subscriber growth and revenue boost for Netflix and other streamers.

title: Adobe mostly unscathed by economic downturn
summary: Adobe has shown resilience amidst an economic downturn, reporting 14% year-over-year revenue growth in Q4, reaching $4.5 billion. Its Adobe Experience platform achieved $1 billion in subscription revenue for the first time, marking a 16% annual increase. While other tech companies like Salesforce have faced layoffs and executive changes, Adobe's strong performance, attributed to its vertical supply chain and healthy balance sheet, positions it favorably despite a recent acquisition of Figma for an estimated $20 billion awaiting regulatory approval.

title: How ‘Avatar: the Way of Water’ Revolutionizes Underwater Cinematography
summary: James Cameron and his team developed groundbreaking filmmaking technology for 'Avatar: The Way of Water' to capture actors' performances underwater, a cinematic first. This involved constructing a massive custom tank and training the cast in free diving to enable realistic motion capture while ensuring water clarity. The innovative techniques, combining separate underwater and air performance capture volumes and advanced virtual camera systems, set a new standard for photo-real visual effects and are expected to impact future Hollywood productions.

title: Scripps Sees Opportunity in ‘Broken’ RSN Business | Next TV | Broadcasting+Cable
summary: The E.W. Scripps Co. is positioning itself to capitalize on the struggling regional sports network (RSN) business model by engaging in a two-pronged strategy. They plan to seek national deals to integrate sports into their Ion network and pursue local deals, especially in markets where they own multiple stations. Scripps aims to offer a new model that leverages their broadcast reach to provide leagues and teams with broader audience access than traditional RSNs.

title: ‘Avatar’ Sequel Brings In $134 Million in Domestic Opening
