summary: Disney and Pixar's "Inside Out 2" made a record-breaking premiere on Disney+, achieving 30.5 million views globally within five days and becoming the No. 1 film premiere on the platform in 2024. The film also holds the record for the No. 1 theatrical film premiere on Disney+ since "Encanto" and the No. 1 film premiere of all time in EMEA and LATAM. Its success also led to over 121 million views of the original "Inside Out" movie on Disney+ as viewers revisited the first installment.

title: Sony Pictures CEO Tony Vinciquerra to step down, succeeded by Ravi Ahuja
summary: Tony Vinciquerra, the current Chairman and CEO of Sony Pictures Entertainment, will step down in January 2025, handing over the reins to Ravi Ahuja. Ahuja, who previously ran Sony’s global television studios and has a background with Disney and Fox, was promoted to COO in April, signaling this succession. Vinciquerra is credited with turning Sony Pictures into a profitable "arms dealer" in the streaming wars by producing content for various platforms rather than launching its own

title: Focus: MercadoLibre, Latam's Amazon.com rival, rides high with AI, loans, drones
summary: MercadoLibre, Latin America's e-commerce giant, is expanding rapidly by leveraging AI, offering loans, and exploring drone delivery to enhance its ecosystem for shoppers and sellers. The company is using its extensive user data to provide instant credit, fueling its growth and solidifying its position as the region's most valuable firm despite competition from other fintechs. Investors are bullish on MercadoLibre's outlook, with strong growth in areas like credit and plans to triple active users.

title: Steph Curry, Chinese Stimulus Revive Under Armour, Amer as Stocks Gain
summary: Under Armour and Amer Sports experienced significant stock gains in September, contributing to the Sportico Sports Stock Index reaching a 13-month high. This surge was primarily driven by Steph Curry's successful tour of China for Under Armour, which boosted brand heat and sales, and substantial Chinese government stimulus measures that encouraged consumer spending. Additionally, sports betting companies also saw double-digit gains due to a strong start to the NFL season and favorable interest rate conditions.

title: ESPN BET Retail Sportsbook Unveiled at Hollywood Casino Columbus
summary: Hollywood Casino Columbus has unveiled its new ESPN BET Sportsbook, enhancing the sports betting and viewing experience for guests. This rebranding strengthens the connection between PENN Entertainment's retail casino and its online sports betting platform, ESPN BET, which launched in November 2023 and is available in 19 jurisdictions. The new sportsbook features numerous betting kiosks and windows, large TV walls, and a gameday menu.

title: Another Round of Layoffs on the Way for The Walt Disney Company
summary: The Walt Disney Company is planning another round of layoffs, impacting approximately 75 employees from ABC News and local stations, following previous reductions in corporate employees and Disney Entertainment Television. This move is part of ongoing efforts to streamline operations amidst a challenging operating environment. Company executives expect the layoffs will not affect national or local programming or specific employee teams.

title: The Walt Disney Company’s Shift Away From Walt Disney’s Vision
summary: The Walt Disney Company is experiencing a significant decline in fan loyalty, particularly among "Disney adults," due to past leadership decisions, notably under former CEO Bob Chapek, and a perceived shift away from Walt Disney's original vision. Despite Bob Iger's return, skepticism remains as fans feel the company is prioritizing financial recovery over the cherished legacy and visitor experience, leading to an erosion of the "Disney magic." The company faces challenges in reconnecting with its core values and fanbase amidst a competitive market.

title: How Disney Consumer Products Delivers Culture-Driving Collaborations
summary: Disney Consumer Products (DCP) leverages Disney's rich legacy and intellectual property to create high-impact collaborations with modern fashion, beauty, and lifestyle brands like Coperni, Pleasing, Balmain, Kith, and Gap. These partnerships aim to connect with global audiences, inspire artists, and offer unexpected products that introduce Disney to new demographics. The collaborations are launched with unique campaigns, showcasing creativity and artistry to maximize their reach and cultural impact.

title: Disney+, Hulu, or ESPN+ Now Included with Boost by Kroger Plus Annual Membership
summary: The Kroger Co. announced that its Boost by Kroger Plus annual membership will now include Disney streaming options at no additional cost. Members can choose between Disney+ Basic (With Ads), Hulu (With Ads), or an ESPN+ subscription, enhancing the existing savings on fuel and groceries. This collaboration aims to provide greater value and convenience for Boost members.

title: Kartoon Channel and Samsung TV Plus Launch Kids Free Streaming Channel in India, the United Kingdom, Italy, and Spain
summary: Kartoon Studios has launched a new "Video Game Heroes" FAST channel for kids through Samsung TV Plus in the UK, Italy, and Spain, and in India via a joint venture with Power Kids. This expansion will reach over 1.5 billion new viewers with gaming-led content, including shows like *Kidaverse Roblox Rumble*, *Sonic X*, and *Donkey Kong Country*, all curated to be family-friendly and child-safe. The initiative aims to provide safe and entertaining content that caters to children's interest in gaming, aligning with parents' desire for secure viewing environments.

title: Kroger gives its membership program a streaming boost
summary: Kroger has enhanced its annual Kroger Boost membership program by adding Disney streaming options, allowing members to choose between Disney+ Basic with ads, Hulu with ads, or ESPN+. This move aligns Kroger with competitors like Walmart and Amazon, who also incorporate streaming perks into their subscription services to increase perceived value and member engagement. The new benefit provides added value at no extra cost for members, with different subscription options depending on their annual Boost plan.

title: The world's top 10 theme park operators
summary: This article identifies the top 10 theme park operators globally based on 2023 attendance figures from the TEA/AECOM Theme Index and Museum Index. It details each company's portfolio of parks, their visitor numbers, and recent developments or future expansion plans, highlighting the industry's shift towards multinational corporations focused on immersive experiences.

title: Advertisers are targeting horror-loving younger audiences in theaters
summary: Advertisers are increasingly targeting younger, horror-loving audiences in theaters, recognizing that this demographic is often difficult to reach through traditional advertising channels. The success of indie horror films like "Longlegs" highlights the effectiveness of out-of-home and in-theater advertising for engaging these cord-cutting, ad-avoiding consumers. Cinema advertising companies like Screenvision Media and National CineMedia are capitalizing on this trend, as horror films create cultural moments that attract a young and engaged audience.

title: Instagram and TikTok Remain the Most Popular Social Apps Among Teens
summary: A Piper Sandler survey of over 13,000 U.S. teens indicates that Instagram is still the most used social app, despite TikTok being preferred for entertainment. While Snapchat has declined, Pinterest and Facebook have seen slight resurgences in teen interest. These insights suggest that targeting young audiences should still primarily focus on Instagram and TikTok, with potential to explore Pinterest and Facebook's AI ads.

title: Disney, Hershey execs share how holiday marketing campaigns are evolving
summary: Executives from Disney and Hershey discussed at Advertising Week how they are evolving holiday marketing campaigns to engage audiences through cultural moments beyond traditional advertising. Hershey partners with Disney for its key seasonal events like Halloween, focusing on impressive content integration rather than just ad spots. Both companies emphasize creating authentic, real-time campaigns and leveraging unique cultural moments to drive significant ROI and revenue growth.

title: NetEase Games and Marvel Games Reveal MARVEL Mystic Mayhem, A Mobile, Team-Based Tactical RPG Set in the Heart of the Marvel Universe
summary: NetEase Games and Marvel Games have announced MARVEL Mystic Mayhem, a new free-to-play mobile tactical RPG. Players will assemble teams of Super Heroes to battle Nightmare, the lord of the Dream Dimension, as he turns dreams into dangerous dungeons. The game will feature characters like Scarlet Witch, Moon Knight, and Captain America, with Doctor Strange and Sleepwalker assisting the heroes.

title: Macy's and Disney Celebrate Magic and Legacy with a New Holiday Collaboration and the Balloon Debut of Minnie Mouse at the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade
summary: Macy's and Disney are collaborating on a new holiday collection and the debut of a Minnie Mouse character balloon at the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade. This partnership celebrates a 90-year relationship between the two brands, featuring exclusive artwork by Disney's Jeff Shelly and a limited-edition product line available at Macy's stores nationwide. Dedicated Mickey and Minnie Shops will open in 200 Macy's stores, including a special interactive experience at the Herald Square flagship.

title: Mandalorian N-1 Starfighter Official Images & Details for Transformers x Star Wars Collaborative
summary: Hasbro has unveiled official images and details for the new Transformers x Star Wars Collaborative The Mandalorian N-1 Starfighter. This exclusive 7.5-inch figure converts from character mode to starfighter alt mode in 37 steps and comes with multiple accessories, including blast effects, blasters, a shield, and a cape that doubles as a display stand. It is available for pre-order at $54.99 USD and is expected to ship in February 2025.

title: Into The Cineverse With 'Terrifier 3's Distributor: How A Six-Figure Investment Turned Into Tens Of Millions In Box Office
summary: Cineverse, the distributor of 'Terrifier 3,' turned a six-figure marketing investment and a multi-million-dollar loan into nearly $30 million in box office revenue for the film. The company, formerly a cinema equipment seller, has pivoted to a streaming-centric operation with a "Moneyball approach" to film distribution, focusing on cost controls and leveraging its horror-centric assets like Screambox and Bloody Disgusting. This strategy demonstrates a successful model for indie distribution, emphasizing partnerships with producers and de-risking P&A and marketing spend.

title: The Walt Disney Company Board Names James P. Gorman as Chairman, Effective January 2, 2025
summary: The Walt Disney Company Board of Directors has named James P. Gorman as Chairman, effective January 2, 2025, succeeding Mark G. Parker. Gorman, currently Executive Chairman of Morgan Stanley and Chair of Disney's Succession Planning Committee, will lead the ongoing search for a new CEO, with an announcement expected in early 2026. This appointment comes as Disney aims to ensure a smooth leadership transition before Bob Iger's contract concludes in December 2026.

title: Airbnb Debuts Iconic Beetlejuice House Recreation — and Yes, You Can Go Inside, If You Dare (Exclusive)
summary: Airbnb has created an immersive recreation of the iconic Deetz residence from "Beetlejuice," located in New Jersey, offering fans a spooky experience complete with film-inspired details. While not an overnight stay, guests can participate in "otherworldly escapades," art classes, and photo ops for free. This initiative is part of Airbnb's "Icons" program, bringing beloved pop culture locations to life for unique fan experiences.

title: Gail Evans Obituary - Charlotte, NC
summary: Gail Evans, a distinguished executive who held leadership roles at Eastman Kodak, Bank of America, HP, Microsoft, Mercer, and Disney, passed away on October 29, 2024, at the age of 65. Born in Rochester, NY, she diligently pursued education, earning degrees from Hobart William Smith, Nazareth University, and the University of Rochester. Evans was celebrated for her professional achievements and her dedication to her family, leaving behind a legacy of warmth, joy, and purpose.

title: Walt Disney Co. Wins Rights to Broadcast Grammys From 2027, Ousting CBS
summary: Walt Disney Co. has secured the rights to broadcast the Grammy music awards for 10 years, starting in 2027, taking the event from Paramount Global’s CBS. The Grammys will be simultaneously broadcast on Disney’s ABC network and its streaming platforms Hulu and Disney+. Financial terms of the deal were not disclosed.

title: The Walt Disney Company Acquires Exclusive Broadcast & Streaming Rights to 'The GRAMMYS'
summary: The Walt Disney Company has secured exclusive broadcast and streaming rights for "The GRAMMYS" under a new 10-year global deal with the Recording Academy, effective 2027. This agreement means ABC, Hulu, and Disney+ will become the new home for the annual awards show, along with GRAMMY-branded specials, marking a significant shift after 50 years. Disney's co-chairman, Dana Walden, highlighted the importance of live events in their portfolio, while Recording Academy CEO Harvey Mason Jr. expressed excitement for the partnership's role in the Academy's growth and mission.

title: Excitement Soars During the World-Renowned Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade
summary: Macy's announced details for its 98th Thanksgiving Day Parade, featuring new character balloons, floats, and a star-studded lineup of performers. The parade, which will take place on November 28, 2024, will be broadcast live on NBC and Peacock, with actress Alison Brie serving as the kickoff ribbon cutter. This year's event will highlight new inflatables, floats from various brands, and performances by renowned musical artists, Broadway casts, and marching bands.

title: Exclusive: Walt Disney forms business unit to coordinate use of AI, augmented reality
summary: Walt Disney is establishing a new business unit, the Office of Technology Enablement, to coordinate the company's application of artificial intelligence and mixed reality across its film, television, and theme park divisions. The unit will be led Jamie Voris, the former CTO of the film studio, and will ensure various projects align with Disney's broader strategy in these fast-evolving technological areas. The initiative highlights Disney's commitment to exploring opportunities and navigating risks associated with AI and extended reality to impact consumer experiences and creative endeavors.

title: Is this cruising's 'golden era'?
summary: The cruise industry is currently experiencing a "golden era" marked by strong demand, record-breaking bookings, and favorable pricing compared to other vacation types. Analysts and executives note an increase in younger and first-time cruisers, extended booking curves, and significant investments in new ships and private destinations. While concerns exist about potential oversupply and future economic slowdowns, the industry appears resilient despite past challenges and current geopolitical conflicts.

title: Disney to Become New Home of 'The GRAMMYS®' Under 10-Year Global Deal with The Recording Academy
summary: The Walt Disney Company announced a 10-year global deal with The Recording Academy to make Disney the exclusive home for The GRAMMYS starting in 2027. This agreement includes simulcasts on ABC, Hulu, and Disney+, and will also feature GRAMMY-branded music specials and new programming across Disney's platforms through 2036. The deal marks a significant expansion of Disney's live event programming, adding Music's Biggest Night to its portfolio which already includes The Oscars and The CMA Awards.

title: Federal Lawsuit Filed Against Disney: Streaming Platforms at Risk
summary: Technology company Adeia has filed a federal lawsuit against Disney, alleging that Disney's streaming services (Hulu, ESPN+, and Disney+) infringe on six of Adeia's patents related to video streaming technology. Adeia, formerly the intellectual property licensing division of Xperi and TiVo, claims its patents cover crucial advancements in streaming functionalities and is seeking monetary damages and an injunction. This lawsuit highlights the growing intellectual property disputes in the competitive streaming industry.

title: Marvel Rivals Unveils Moon Knight At D23 Brazil, Set to Join Launch Roster of All-Star Characters on December 6th
summary: NetEase Games announced at D23 Brazil that Moon Knight will join the launch roster of Marvel Rivals, a team-based PVP shooter set to release on December 6th. The game will feature an evolving cast of Marvel heroes and villains, with all characters unlocked and free to play at launch. Additionally, Shota Nakama was revealed as the music producer and arranger, and Masahiro Aoki as the composer for the game, with Nakama performing selections at the event.

title: The Potential New CEO Candidates for The Walt Disney Company Stink
summary: This article criticizes the leading candidates for the CEO position at The Walt Disney Company, arguing that each lacks the comprehensive experience and vision needed for the role. It analyzes Andrew Wilson, Josh D’Amaro, Dana Walden, and Alan Bergman, highlighting their strengths in specific areas but pointing out their major deficiencies concerning Disney's diverse operations, particularly theme parks and family-centric branding. The author concludes that Disney needs a visionary leader, not just a corporate operator, to maintain its core values and connection with fans.

title: Diving Off the Screen: Masterful ‘Little Mermaid’ Product Art
summary: This article celebrates the enduring legacy of Disney's "The Little Mermaid" by showcasing rarely seen merchandising artwork beyond the film itself. It highlights illustrations from Little Nugget Books, "How to Draw The Little Mermaid" guides, and classic VHS packaging, demonstrating the extensive artistic effort consistently applied to Disney products. The piece emphasizes how Disney's commitment to storytelling extends throughout the company's various offerings.

title: Diving Off the Screen: Masterful ‘Little Mermaid’ Product Art
summary: This article celebrates the enduring legacy of Disney's "The Little Mermaid" beyond its animated film, focusing on the extensive and often unseen product artwork. It highlights a collection of merchandising illustrations from the Walt Disney Archives, including those for Golden Press storybooks, Walter Foster "How to Draw" books, and various home video releases. The piece underscores the consistent care and artistry Disney applies across all its productions and consumer products.

title: Mattel Bets Big On Its IP
summary: Mattel Inc. is shifting its strategy to heavily capitalize on its intellectual property by expanding into movies, TV shows, and theme parks. This move, spearheaded by CEO Ynon Kreiz, aims to leverage iconic brands like Barbie and Hot Wheels beyond traditional toy sales, creating new revenue streams and engaging adult fans. The strategy appears to be paying off, with significant net income growth and positive analyst outlooks, despite the company's stock price being lower than its all-time high.

title: Netflix stock recovers from losses after technical glitches disrupt the Jake Paul, Mike Tyson boxing match
summary: Netflix shares rebounded after technical issues plagued its highly anticipated Jake Paul, Mike Tyson boxing match, raising concerns about its ability to handle future live events, including upcoming NFL Christmas Day games. Despite the glitches, an Oppenheimer analyst suggested viewership likely exceeded expectations, a "high quality problem" fixable before the NFL games. The company also announced Beyoncé as the halftime performer for one of the Christmas Day NFL games, and its ad-supported tier now boasts 70 million global monthly active users.

title: Disney, ESPN, and the NBA Team Up to Present 'Dunk the Halls' - the First Real-Time, Animated NBA Game
summary: Disney, ESPN, and the NBA are collaborating to present "Dunk the Halls," the first real-time animated NBA game, on Christmas Day, December 25, at noon ET. This special broadcast will feature the New York Knicks hosting the San Antonio Spurs, with players appearing as motion-enabled animated figures using Sony's Beyond Sports technology, set in a virtual Magic Kingdom® Park. The event, streaming on ESPN2, Disney+, and ESPN+, will also include iconic Disney characters, an animated commentary team, and a storyline involving Mickey's Christmas wish.

title: Americans Spend More on Streaming Services Than Retirement
summary: A new study by First Merchants Bank reveals that Americans, particularly Millennials and Gen Xers, prioritize spending on short-term services like streaming and food delivery over long-term financial goals such as retirement savings. The study indicates that 47% of respondents prioritize streaming, while only 26% prioritize retirement savings, leading to overspending for many due to economic challenges. Financial assistance tools and budgeting strategies are suggested to help individuals balance immediate enjoyment with future investments.

title: Kentucky Derby Futures: Odds for 2-Year-Olds from Churchill and Vegas
summary: This article analyzes the current Kentucky Derby futures market for 2-year-old thoroughbreds, highlighting betting options from Caesars Sportsbook in Nevada and Churchill Downs' parimutuel pools. It discusses key contenders, particularly those trained by Bob Baffert following his lifted ban, and offers insights into other promising horses and potential value plays for the 2025 Kentucky Derby.

title: ‘Moana 2’ Directors on What to Expect from the Exciting Sequel
summary: Directors David Derrick Jr., Jason Hand, and Dana Ledoux Miller discuss the highly anticipated sequel "Moana 2," highlighting its themes of growth, community, and Moana's expanded adventures. The filmmakers emphasize their close collaboration with the Oceanic Cultural Trust to ensure authenticity and pride in the character's journey. They note the film places Moana in challenging situations, features memorable music, and builds on the enduring popularity of the original film and its presence across Disney platforms.

title: Disney Agrees to $43M Deal to Settle Class Action Over Women’s Pay
summary: Disney has agreed to pay $43.25 million to settle a class-action lawsuit brought by approximately 9,000 female employees in California who accused the company of pay discrimination. The settlement also mandates Disney to retain experts to address significant pay differences and conduct annual pay equity reviews. This agreement, which is awaiting judicial approval, aims to promote equitable treatment for women at the company.

title: Inside Paramount’s Search for a Buyer: Apollo’s Letters, Redstone’s Rejections and ‘Party F’
summary: This article details the complex and prolonged search for a buyer for Paramount, revealing how controlling shareholder Shari Redstone and a special committee navigated offers from over 50 parties. It highlights Apollo Global Management's persistent but ultimately unsuccessful bids, along with interest from Warner Bros. Discovery, Comcast, and undisclosed private equity firms, including "Party F," before the Skydance Media deal was settled. The article also touches on investor accusations that the Skydance deal primarily benefited Redstone, despite the extensive process to find a suitable offer.

title: The Artistry & Technology Behind 'Moana 2'
summary: This article details the advanced artistry and technology used by Walt Disney Animation Studios in creating "Moana 2," highlighting the challenges and innovations involved in bringing characters like Nalo to life and updating Moana's appearance. It emphasizes the collaborative effort between artists and technologists, the importance of cultural authenticity through choreographers like Tiana Liufau, and the seamless integration of CG and hand-drawn animation, particularly with Mini Maui. The creators express their excitement to revisit Moana's story and evolve her character.

title: Inside The Walt Disney Company’s New NYC Headquarters
summary: The Walt Disney Company has opened a new headquarters in New York City, named the Robert A. Iger building, at 7 Hudson Square. This state-of-the-art facility will serve as a collaborative hub for various Disney businesses, including news, streaming, and production, and features numerous amenities and eco-friendly designs. The building honors Robert A. Iger's 50th anniversary with the company and continues Disney's long-standing connection with NYC, which dates back to the debut of Steamboat Willie and its significant presence on Broadway.

title: PokerStars partners the NHL’s Philadelphia Flyers
summary: PokerStars, owned by Flutter Entertainment, has announced a partnership with the NHL's Philadelphia Flyers, making it the first poker brand to team up with the Pennsylvania-based NHL team. This collaboration will feature PokerStars' branding at Flyers home games and offer players opportunities to win tickets and signed memorabilia. This expands PokerStars' presence in North American sports, following similar partnerships with the Detroit Red Wings and Maple Leaf Sports and Entertainment.

title: Walt Disney Company Rewarding Shareholders With Increased Cash Dividend
summary: The Walt Disney Company's Board of Directors has approved a cash dividend of $1.00 per share, a 33% increase from the previous $0.75 dividend, signaling a focus on shareholder returns and long-term investment. CEO Bob Iger highlighted a successful year and renewed strength for the company. The dividend will be issued in two payments in early and mid-2025, following Disney's reported annual revenue of $91.4 billion for fiscal year 2024.

title: MIDiA’s 2025 predictions It’s social’s stage now
summary: MIDiA's 2025 predictions anticipate that social platforms, which have reshaped entertainment through the creator economy, will continue to dominate. The report suggests that the "second-order effects" of this shift will become more apparent, characterized by attention saturation and content commodification. Traditional entertainment companies are expected to adapt and reinvent themselves to secure a share of the evolving entertainment landscape.

title: The Walt Disney Company Earns 35 Golden Globe® Award Nominations Across its Film and Television Studios, Streaming Services and Broadcast
summary: The Walt Disney Company has proudly received 35 Golden Globe® Award nominations across its various content brands and studios, including Pixar, Marvel, 20th Century Studios, and Searchlight Pictures. Hulu and Disney+ together garnered a total of 23 nominations, with shows like "The Bear" and "Only Murders in the Building" leading in television categories. Searchlight Pictures earned 10 nominations for its film productions, including "A Complete Unknown" and "A Real Pain," and several acting nominations for its stars.

title: How indie agencies could benefit as Omnicom’s mega-deal for IPG shakes up adland
summary: Omnicom Group's impending $13 billion-plus acquisition of Interpublic Group of Companies (IPG) is set to reshape the advertising landscape, creating the industry's largest holding company. This mega-deal is expected to open opportunities for independent agencies, which are positioning themselves as more nimble and less complex alternatives. While the consolidation offers scale for data-driven marketing, it also pressures Omnicom to integrate IPG's assets efficiently, potentially prompting other major agency networks to accelerate M&A activities.

title: Marvel Rivals Version 20241210 Patch Notes
summary: This article details the patch notes for Marvel Rivals Version 20241210, focusing on bug fixes across all platforms. Key improvements address character becoming stuck in maps, display errors in highlights and mission progress, game crashes, and desynchronization issues in specific game modes. Several hero-specific bugs related to costumes, voice lines, energy recovery, and ultimate abilities have also been resolved.

title: WBD Secures Comcast Deal, Preps for Future Without NBA Rights
summary: Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) has finalized a crucial distribution agreement with Comcast, securing carriage for its key networks in the U.S., UK, and Ireland. This deal, following a similar one with Charter, is part of WBD's strategic reorganization in anticipation of losing domestic NBA media rights from the 2025-2026 season. The company has also expanded significantly into college sports rights and settled a lawsuit with the NBA, leading to a more than 60% increase in stock value since August.

title: The Walt Disney Company to Pay $233 Million Settlement in Disneyland Wage Theft Lawsuit
summary: The Walt Disney Company has agreed to a $233 million settlement in a wage theft lawsuit at Disneyland Resort, affecting over 50,000 current and former cast members. The lawsuit stemmed from Disney's alleged violation of Anaheim's Measure L minimum wage law, which required businesses receiving tax rebates to pay employees at least $15 an hour. The settlement covers lost wages and interest dating back to January 1st, 2019, after years of legal battles that saw the California Supreme Court refuse Disney's final appeal.

title: Liberty Media €4.2 billion MotoGP takeover subject to EU probe – report
summary: Liberty Media's €4.2 billion takeover of MotoGP from Dorna Sports is facing an intensive investigation by the European Union. Concerns have been raised by new antitrust chief Teresa Ribera about potential monopolies and the impact on competition in broadcasting and streaming markets. This follows Liberty Media's earlier acquisition of Formula 1 rights in 2016, and the EU is set to begin a secondary probe by December 19th.

title: BBC Studios, The Walt Disney Company Announce ‘Bluey’ Movie
summary: BBC Studios and The Walt Disney Company have announced their collaboration on the first-ever animated feature film for the popular children's show "Bluey." The Walt Disney Company has acquired the global theatrical rights and will release the film in cinemas in 2027, with "Bluey" creator Joe Brumm involved in the project. The movie will feature the original vocal cast and is supported by the Australian and Queensland governments.

title: BBC Studios and The Walt Disney Company Announce First-Ever ‘Bluey’ Animated Feature Film
summary: BBC Studios and The Walt Disney Company have announced the first-ever animated feature film for the Emmy® and BAFTA Award-winning series "Bluey." Disney has acquired the global theatrical rights for the film, set to release in cinemas in 2027 and later stream on Disney+. Written and directed by "Bluey" creator Joe Brumm, the movie will continue the adventures of Bluey, Bingo, Mum, and Dad, aiming to bring the characters to the big screen as an experiential event for families worldwide.

title: Surf Air Mobility Appoints David Anderman to Board of Directors
summary: Surf Air Mobility Inc. has appointed David Anderman to its board of directors, effective December 17, 2024. Anderman previously served as General Counsel of SpaceX and COO/General Counsel of Lucasfilm Ltd., bringing extensive experience in legal, operational, and technology sectors to the regional air mobility platform. He is also co-founder of Stellar Ventures and will contribute to the development of SurfOS AI-powered software with Palantir.

title: Top 11 Disney Alternatives & Competitors in 2026
summary: This article identifies and details the top 11 competitors and alternatives to Disney across entertainment, theme parks, and comic books, as of 2026. It provides financial data, founding information, and key insights for major companies like Time Warner Inc., Fox, Paramount Global, Comcast, Sony, AMC Network, Lionsgate, Universal Studios, Cedar Fair, Six Flags Entertainment, and DC. The article highlights Disney's continued dominance despite robust competition and its significant investment in its Parks, Experiences and Products division.

title: Standalone Hollywood Online Casino App Live In Pennsylvania
summary: Penn Entertainment has launched its standalone Hollywood Casino online casino app in Pennsylvania, separating it from the ESPN Bet online sportsbook. This move comes after previous offerings were described as "messy" by Penn CEO Jay Snowden, disrupting the user experience with its land-based casino database. The company plans to extend this enhanced Hollywood Casino experience to other iCasino markets like Michigan and West Virginia in early 2025, anticipating regulatory approvals.

title: TelevisaUnivision Pulls Spanish-Language Programming From Fubo Impacting Thousands of Hispanic Consumers
summary: FuboTV announced that TelevisaUnivision has pulled its Spanish-language programming from the platform, affecting thousands of Hispanic consumers who have lost access to local news, weather, sports, and entertainment. Fubo attributes this to TelevisaUnivision's refusal to accept fair and competitive rates, attempting to increase prices by 25% and imposing unfair bundling practices. Fubo remains open to negotiation but emphasizes the need for a fair and equitable agreement for its subscribers.

title: Gray Renews All ABC Affiliation Agreements
summary: Gray Television, Inc. (NYSE: GTN) has renewed its network affiliation agreements with The Walt Disney Company for all its ABC affiliated television stations across 25 markets, extending through December 31, 2028. This extension continues a decades-long relationship, ensuring that these stations will keep delivering ABC's programming alongside their local content to their communities. The agreement covers a wide range of markets, from Tampa-St. Pete to Meridian, solidifying Gray's position as a major media company in the U.S.

title: Disney's streaming business is profitable for first time, but slowing US park business ups anxiety
summary: Disney's streaming business achieved profitability for the first time in the third quarter, driven by strong performances from its movie studio and streaming services like Disney+, Hulu, and ESPN+. Despite this success, the company is facing anxiety due to slowing growth in its U.S. park business, with domestic park operating income seeing a decline. Disney anticipates this moderation in demand at its U.S. parks to persist for the next few quarters.

title: James P. Gorman Begins Role as Walt Disney Company Board Chairman this Week
summary: James P. Gorman has officially taken over as chairman of The Walt Disney Company Board of Directors, succeeding Mark G. Parker, who served for nine years. Gorman, previously executive chairman of Morgan Stanley, will lead the Board's Succession Planning Committee in identifying Disney's next CEO, with an announcement expected in early 2026. Both Parker and Disney CEO Bob Iger expressed confidence in Gorman's leadership as the company focuses on its future and CEO transition.

title: Fubo And Disney’s Hulu + Live TV Virtual MVPD Businesses To Combine
summary: Fubo and The Walt Disney Company announced a definitive agreement to combine Disney's Hulu + Live TV business with Fubo, forming a new virtual MVPD company. Disney will own 70% of the combined entity, which will operate under the Fubo name with existing Fubo management. The deal, which includes a settlement of all litigation between Fubo and Disney, is expected to enhance consumer choice and create a new Sports & Broadcasting service featuring Disney's premier sports and broadcast networks.

title: Fubo’s stock skyrockets as Disney Hulu + Live TV deal creates YouTube TV rival
summary: Fubo's stock price surged over 250% after the company announced a deal to combine its service with Walt Disney Co.’s Hulu + Live TV. This merger aims to create a stronger virtual multichannel video programming distributor with a combined 6.2 million North American subscribers, positioning it as the second-largest online pay-TV provider, second only to Google’s YouTube TV.

title: Billionaire Nelson Peltz Shifts Focus: Sells Ferguson Enterprises Stake While Investing in Troubled Financial Services Stock
summary: Billionaire activist investor Nelson Peltz's Trian Fund Management has shifted its investment focus, completely exiting its significant stake in Walt Disney after a 16-month battle. Trian has also been selling off its Ferguson Enterprises stock, moving some of the proceeds into financial services company Janus Henderson. This strategic reallocation demonstrates Peltz's method of generating profit through active portfolio management.

title: Fubo And Disney’s Hulu + Live TV Virtual MVPD Businesses To Combine
summary: FuboTV Inc. and The Walt Disney Company announced a definitive agreement to combine Disney's Hulu + Live TV business with Fubo, forming a new virtual MVPD company. Disney will own 70% of the combined entity, which will retain the Fubo public company name and be led by Fubo's existing management. This merger aims to enhance consumer choice, offering flexible programming with over 6.2 million North American subscribers, and includes a new carriage agreement allowing Fubo to create a Sports & Broadcast service featuring Disney's premier sports networks.

title: We Might See A Profit From Dolphin Entertainment, Inc. (NASDAQ:DLPN) Soon
summary: Dolphin Entertainment, Inc. (NASDAQ:DLPN) is expected to become profitable soon, with analysts forecasting a breakeven in 2024 and positive profits of US$333k in 2025. The company has reduced its losses and will need an average annual growth rate of 111% to meet these forecasts. However, its high debt-to-equity ratio of 152% is a concern for investors.

title: ESPN, Fox, Warner Bros. Discovery Drop Venu Sports Joint Venture
summary: ESPN, Fox, and Warner Bros. Discovery have decided to shut down their joint venture, Venu Sports, before its public launch. This decision comes shortly after Disney, ESPN's parent company, settled an antitrust lawsuit with Fubo Inc. by acquiring a majority stake in Fubo and forming a new joint venture with them. The companies stated that they opted to focus on existing products and distribution channels, citing an "ever-changing marketplace."

title: CEO Of Barry Diller’s IAC Steps Down As Company Announces Spinoff Of Angi Stake
summary: Barry Diller is reasserting his leadership role at IAC, a diversified digital company, as CEO Joey Levin steps down to become executive chairman of Angi following its spinoff. This move, expected to finalize in the first half of 2025, positions Angi for greater independence and caused IAC's shares to jump 5% after hours. Diller emphasizes Levin's desire to lead his own venture, while also highlighting Levin's significant contributions to IAC and Angi's transformation.

title: The Walt Disney Company Board Names James P. Gorman As Chairman, Effective January 2, 2025
summary: The Walt Disney Company Board has named James P. Gorman as its new Chairman, effective January 2, 2025, succeeding Mark G. Parker. Gorman, currently Executive Chairman of Morgan Stanley, will lead the Succession Planning Committee tasked with identifying Disney's next CEO, with an announcement expected in early 2026. This transition ensures a successful handover before Bob Iger's contract concludes in December 2026.

title: Top 13 trends to watch in the visitor attractions industry in 2025
summary: This article outlines the top 13 trends predicted for the visitor attractions industry in 2025, covering diverse areas from the expansion of gaming brands in location-based entertainment to immersive wellness experiences. Key themes include the increasing integration of AI for personalized guest experiences and operational efficiency, growing emphasis on sustainability in ride innovation and conservation efforts, and the rising popularity of family-friendly attractions and unique themed accommodations. The article also highlights the continued growth of permanent horror attractions and immersive technologies such as AR and projection mapping.

title: The Top Thirty Companies That Diamond Owes Money To
summary: Diamond Comic Distributors has declared bankruptcy, owing over $31.7 million to its top thirty non-secured creditors. Penguin Random House is the largest creditor with a $9.2 million debt, demonstrating the impact of its subdistribution deals for Marvel, Dark Horse, and IDW. The list also reveals significant debts to various toy companies like Bandai and Hasbro, and graphic novel/comic publishers such as Simon & Schuster and Titan, indicating a broad financial fallout across the industry.

title: Comscore Announces Unified Content Measurement
summary: Comscore has launched Comscore Content Measurement (CCM), a new solution within The Comscore Platform that unifies content measurement across various channels and platforms. This advanced self-service tool provides content owners and creators with a holistic view of consumer behavior, enabling them to understand viewing habits and commercialize their offerings more effectively. CCM integrates measurement across linear TV, CTV/Streaming, PC, Mobile, and Social, offering deduplicated audience reach insights and enhancing content and ad monetization strategies for brands like Google, NBCUniversal, and Paramount.

title: Webtoon Entertainment Invests in Japanese Webcomic & Manga Studio No. 9
summary: Webtoon Entertainment's Japanese subsidiary, LINE Digital Frontier, has made its first investment in a Japanese studio by acquiring a minority stake in webcomic and manga studio No. 9. This strategic move aims to enhance Webtoon Entertainment's content pipeline in Japan, its fastest-growing market, and foster global hits. No. 9 will appoint a director from LINE Digital Frontier to its board, strengthening the collaboration and supporting the localization of Japanese webcomics for international audiences.

title: Active ETFs vs Mutual Funds: What to Know Before Picking a New Fund
summary: This article discusses the pros and cons of active ETFs versus traditional mutual funds, highlighting their similarities and differences in tax advantages, fees, and trading flexibility. It also delves into Netflix's strategy to expand into live sports streaming and advertising, and how these moves could impact its future profitability and stock performance. The article features insights from Morningstar experts Russel Kinnel and Matthew Dolgin, CFA.

title: Research: Video streaming is twice as bad as aviation for carbon emissions
summary: A report by InterDigital and Futuresource Consulting reveals that the video streaming industry accounts for 4% of global carbon emissions, double that of the aviation industry's 2%. The research highlights the significant environmental impact of TV and video consumption, from production to delivery, and explores emerging solutions like IP-based virtual production and more energy-efficient devices to mitigate this footprint. The report emphasizes the industry's responsibility to improve sustainability, noting the potential for significant energy savings through technologies like PVR.

title: Walt Disney Company (DIS) Stock: Global Investment Opportunity
summary: The article analyzes Walt Disney Company (DIS) stock as a global investment opportunity, highlighting its strong brand, business diversification across film, theme parks, and streaming, and its blue-chip status. It details Disney's stock performance, fundamental strengths, challenges in the competitive streaming market, and offers technical analysis and tips for investors. The article concludes by recommending Disney as an attractive long-term investment, especially for beginners, due to its stability and growth potential.

title: Beijing welcomes back international blockbusters
summary: Facing a slumping domestic movie market and a cooling economy, China is increasingly re-opening its doors to international blockbusters from Hollywood, Bollywood, and Japan. This shift aims to boost consumer spending, especially as cinemas are often located in malls, encouraging additional purchases. The move also reflects China's efforts to mend international relations and diversify film offerings, following a period where foreign cultural influence was viewed with suspicion.

title: InterDigital, Inc. Files Lawsuit Against The Walt Disney Company Over Intellectual Property Infringement
summary: InterDigital, Inc. has filed lawsuits against The Walt Disney Company, including its streaming services Disney+, Hulu, and ESPN+, alleging intellectual property infringement related to its video streaming technologies. While preferring amicable licensing negotiations, InterDigital's Chief Legal Officer, Josh Schmidt, stated their commitment to fair compensation for their innovations that enhance streaming efficiency and user experience. The litigation has been initiated in multiple jurisdictions, including the U.S., Brazil, and Germany, as InterDigital, a leader in wireless and video technology since 1972, seeks to protect its foundational technologies.

title: ESPN BET, PGA TOUR LIVE on ESPN+ team up to launch new betting stream
summary: The PGA TOUR, PENN Entertainment, and ESPN have partnered to launch a new live betting stream, "ESPN BET on PGA TOUR LIVE," on ESPN+. This stream will provide real-time data, insights, and betting analysis during six major FedExCup events in the 2025 season, starting with the WM Phoenix Open. The initiative aims to enhance the fan experience by integrating betting content into live golf coverage.

title: InterDigital begins action against Disney to enforce patents
summary: InterDigital has initiated legal action against The Walt Disney Company, including Disney+, Hulu, and ESPN+, alleging ongoing infringement of its intellectual property, specifically concerning advanced video compression technology. InterDigital states that amicable negotiation is preferred but enforcement is sometimes necessary to ensure fair compensation for their innovations, which allows them to continue developing future technologies. Cases have been filed in multiple international courts.

title: Disney Comes Together to Support Los Angeles Fire Relief Efforts
summary: The Walt Disney Company has committed $15 million and numerous initiatives to support Los Angeles fire relief and rebuilding efforts. These initiatives include providing immediate aid to vital organizations, opening a wardrobe warehouse for affected employees, bolstering the Disney Employee Relief Fund, assembling comfort kits for children, hosting community screenings, conducting donation drives, and honoring first responders and heroes with complimentary theme park tickets and special events. Disney’s Imagineers are also assisting in reimagining community spaces damaged by the fires, and KABC volunteers helped rebuild a home with Habitat for Humanity.

title: Disney Tops Estimates on Gains From Streaming and ‘Moana 2’
summary: Walt Disney Co. (DIS) exceeded analysts' fiscal first-quarter estimates, driven by the success of the film "Moana 2" and improved profitability from its streaming services. The company reported earnings of $1.76 per share, surpassing the $1.42 average estimate, and revenue increased by 5% to $24.7 billion. This marks the third consecutive quarter of streaming profitability for Disney.

title: Magical Savings Coast to Coast: Disney Parks Deals for Walt Disney World & Disneyland
summary: This article details various Disney Parks deals for Walt Disney World and Disneyland in 2026, targeting different visitor types. It includes discounts on resort stays, special ticket offers for Florida and California residents, military personnel, and Disney+ subscribers, along with new attractions and returning festivals. The aim is to provide flexible savings for a wide range of guests across both iconic Disney destinations.

title: Bath & Body Works and Disney Collaborate to Launch Disney Princess Fragrance Collection
summary: Bath & Body Works has announced a collaboration with Disney to launch a new Disney Princess-inspired fragrance collection. The extensive 85-product collection features six new fragrances inspired by Ariel, Belle, Cinderella, Jasmine, Moana, and Tiana, with items ranging from $1.95 to $99.95. Rewards program members will have early access on February 11 and 12, before the official launch on February 16, 2025.

title: After Earnings, Is Disney Stock a Buy, a Sell, or Fairly Valued?
summary: Morningstar maintains its fair value estimate of $125 per share for Disney, believing the stock is fairly valued despite growth in revenue and operating profit from streaming and experiences, alongside a decline in linear networks. The company's wide economic moat, driven by iconic characters and content, is expected to ensure strong returns on invested capital, while its financial health is sound, with an improving debt leverage and a reinstituted dividend. While risks from the evolving media landscape exist, Disney's diverse revenue streams and strong brand appeal position it well for the future.

title: Comcast and NBCUniversal receive FCC inquiry on DEI initiatives
summary: The FCC has launched an investigation into Comcast and NBCUniversal's Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) practices, following a new executive order from President Donald Trump aimed at ending DEI initiatives in corporations. FCC Chairman Brendan Carr initiated the inquiry, citing concerns that the companies' DEI programs might not comply with FCC regulations. This move has drawn criticism from FCC Commissioner Geoffrey Starks and comes as other media entities like Disney and PBS are also re-evaluating or dismantling their DEI programs.

title: Comcast Under Federal Investigation for DEI Initiatives
summary: Comcast is currently under federal investigation for its Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) initiatives, a probe initiated by the Federal Communications Commission following a directive from the Trump administration. This investigation is part of a broader effort by the Trump administration to scale back DEI programs across various sectors. Despite the probe and ongoing restructuring efforts, Comcast has stated its commitment to DEI, considering it a central element of its corporate philosophy.

title: Outrage Erupts as Major Orlando Theme Park Sneaks in New 9% Fee—Effective Now
summary: SeaWorld Parks & Entertainment has introduced a new, unannounced 9% sales tax on specific in-park purchases, primarily for its 7 Seas Festival, sparking considerable outrage among guests and annual passholders. This move, which contrasts with the tax-inclusive pricing at competitors like Disney and Universal, is raising concerns about the affordability of visiting SeaWorld and its affiliated parks. Fans are questioning if the park is losing its competitive edge as a budget-friendly alternative in the Orlando theme park market.

title: NEW Monsters Inc. Crocs Arrive at Walt Disney World
summary: The Monsters Inc. Crocs, including Sulley-inspired fuzzy sandals and Mike Wazowski classic clogs, have arrived at Walt Disney World Resort. Both pairs feature unique character details like Sulley's horns and work badge, and Mike's eye and horns. While not yet available online from Disney, they can be purchased at Beverly Sunset Boutique in Disney’s Hollywood Studios and at Disney Springs.

title: Dave Portnoy says he is not going to sell Penn Entertainment stake at current price
summary: Dave Portnoy, founder of Barstool Sports, has stated he will not sell his stake in Penn Entertainment Inc., despite the company registering 1.25 million of his shares for possible sale. Penn, which recently sold Barstool Sports back to Portnoy for $1, registered his shares after agreeing to a $2 billion deal to license ESPN for its sports betting operations. Portnoy's current holdings amount to 1.48 million shares, worth approximately $35 million.

title: Bath & Body Works launches Disney Princess product line
summary: Bath & Body Works has launched a new product line in partnership with Disney, featuring Disney Princess-themed scents. This collaboration allows consumers, particularly children, to enjoy products inspired by Disney Princesses. The news was reported by Dan Eaton for Columbus Business First.

title: eVTOL Evolution
summary: Boeing recognized the need to accelerate innovation and address urban mobility challenges. This led to the creation of HorizonX and later Boeing NeXt, which fostered partnerships with startups like Kittyhawk. These initiatives ultimately contributed to the formation of Wisk Aero, a wholly-owned Boeing subsidiary focused on developing autonomous eVTOL air taxis, leveraging Boeing's extensive resources and expertise.

title: China likely to lift ban on South Korea’s K-wave as early as May
summary: China is expected to lift its ban on Hallyu (Korean popular culture) as early as May, signaling a shift from its "wolf warrior" diplomacy to "smile diplomacy." This move, eight years after the ban was imposed in retaliation for South Korea's THAAD deployment, aims to strengthen cooperation ahead of the 2026 APEC summit in China and boost cultural exchanges. The lifting of restrictions is anticipated to benefit Korean content distribution and consumer goods sales, which previously suffered an estimated 22 trillion won in damages.

title: ‘Win or Lose’ Co-Creators on Bringing Pixar’s First-Ever Original Series to Disney+
summary: Carrie Hobson and Michael Yates, co-creators of Pixar's first-ever original series "Win or Lose" on Disney+, discuss the challenges and inspirations behind the show. The series features intertwined stories of eight characters preparing for a championship softball game, aiming to incorporate Pixar's hallmarks while pushing storytelling boundaries with multiple protagonists and nonlinear narratives. Hobson and Yates hope the show encourages viewers to see the world from different perspectives, inspired by their own varying views during meetings.

title: The Walt Disney Company To Participate In The Morgan Stanley Technology, Media, And Telecom Conference
summary: The Walt Disney Company announced that Dana Walden, Co-Chairman, Disney Entertainment, will participate in a Q&A session at the Morgan Stanley Technology, Media, and Telecom Conference on March 4, 2025. The session will be streamed live on the Disney Investor Relations website, with a recording also made available.

title: NetEase CEO William Ding Restructures Company with Layoffs and Studio Closures Amid Profit Push
summary: NetEase, China's second-largest gaming company, is undergoing a significant restructuring led by CEO William Ding, involving hundreds of layoffs and studio closures. These changes are aimed at boosting profitability amidst stagnating growth and intense competition. The company is now prioritizing high-revenue, "evergreen" titles and focusing on domestic hits while scaling back international investments.

title: Kartoon Studios, Samsung TV Plus Partner on Kartoon Channel!
summary: Kartoon Studios has partnered with Samsung TV Plus to launch Kartoon Channel! in the United States and Canada, making free kids' streaming content available to connected Samsung TVs. The channel features video game-themed content like 'Kidaverse: Roblox Rumble,' original shows such as 'Rainbow Rangers,' and classics like 'Yu-Gi-Oh!' and 'Bakugan.' This partnership aims to expand Kartoon Channel!'s reach, offering families a safe and curated streaming option while driving growth for Kartoon Studios.

title: 1 telling stat: ESPN Bet trails in parlays
summary: ESPN Bet, a sports betting platform, is significantly lagging behind market leaders DraftKings and FanDuel in the highly profitable parlay betting segment. Only about 30% of bets on ESPN Bet are parlays, compared to 50% or more for its competitors. This underperformance challenges ESPN Bet's initial goal of achieving 20% U.S. market share by 2027, with executives now expecting to reach just over 5% by Q4, despite ongoing product improvements.

title: Earnings call transcript: Bath & Body Works Q4 2024 tops EPS forecast, shares fall
summary: Bath & Body Works (NYSE: BBWI) announced Q4 2024 earnings per share (EPS) of $2.09, exceeding the forecasted $2.04, despite a 4% decline in net sales to $2.8 billion year-over-year. The company's stock dropped 12.07% in pre-market trading, reflecting investor concerns over sales performance and future growth challenges amidst competitive pressures. For 2025, Bath & Body Works anticipates modest sales growth of 1% to 3% and EPS between $3.25 and $3.60, focusing on product innovation, marketing, technology, and international expansion while maintaining cost discipline.

title: Chief legal and compliance officer at The Walt Disney Co. to speak on AI at esteemed speaker series
summary: Horacio Gutierrez, J.D. '98, and current Chief Legal and Compliance Officer at The Walt Disney Co., is set to speak at the Alan S. Becker and Gary A. Poliakoff Preeminent Leaders in Law Speaker Series on March 18 at the University of Miami School of Law. Gutierrez will deliver a lecture titled "Artificial Intelligence and the Creative Industries," drawing on his extensive experience in corporate law and compliance, including previous roles at Spotify and Microsoft. The series, created by Becker & Poliakoff, honors its founders and aims to provide insights into the legal field, with this event also celebrating the University of Miami's centennial.

title: Fubo Closed 2024 with Record Revenue, Subs
summary: FuboTV Inc. announced record total revenue and paid subscribers for the fourth quarter and full year ended December 31, 2024, achieving its first quarter of positive free cash flow. The company reported full-year 2024 North America revenue of $1.588 billion, up 19% year-over-year, and 1.676 million subscribers, up 4% year-over-year. Despite these record results, Fubo projects a decline in subscribers for 2025, attributing it to a carriage dispute with TelevisaUnivision.

title: ESPN Bet Could Shut Down In 2026
summary: ESPN Bet, a partnership between ESPN and Penn National, is facing potential closure in 2026 due to underperforming market share goals. The initial $2 billion deal aimed for a 20% gambling market share by 2027, but ESPN Bet currently holds only 2.35%. Penn National's CEO has indicated that a three-year clause in the contract allows either party to exit if performance targets are not met.

title: Comcast CEO Brian Roberts Says Peacock Will Live-Stream NBA 'Tonnage' Beginning in 2025-26 Season
summary: Comcast CEO Brian Roberts announced that Peacock will live-stream "tonnage" of NBA and WNBA games starting in the 2025-26 season as part of a new 11-year, $76 billion media rights deal. Peacock plans to offer 100 NBA games and 50 WNBA games, marking a significant expansion into live sports content for the streaming service. Roberts also emphasized the company's focus on internet connectivity to support streaming, with 98% of Peacock's viewing coming from non-NBCUniversal cable networks.

title: Lionsgate Studios, Starz Split On Track For Mid To Late April Close, CFO Says – Update
summary: Lionsgate CFO James Barge announced that the company is on track to complete the separation of Lionsgate Studios and Starz by mid-to-late April. The split, which has faced delays due to various unforeseen events, aims to unlock greater shareholder value by allowing each entity to be valued independently. This move comes as Lionsgate reports strong third-quarter 2025 earnings, driven by television production and library revenue, despite a dip in motion picture business and Starz revenue.

title: Mattel, Inc. Share Price Target '$25.58', Now 21.7% Upside Potential
summary: Mattel, Inc. has a new share price target of $25.58, representing a 21.7% upside potential based on the consensus of 13 market analysts who rate the stock as a 'buy'. The company's current market capitalization is $6.75 billion, with analysts projecting a potential market cap of over $8.2 billion. Key financial metrics include a P/E ratio of 13.28 and revenue per share of $15.80, though the company currently does not pay dividends.

title: Netflix Stock Slides Amid Analyst Forecast of Slowing Sub Growth, Broader Market Turmoil Over Trump Tariffs
summary: Netflix shares dropped 8.5% due to analyst predictions of slowing subscriber growth after a record year spurred by its password-sharing crackdown. The decline was exacerbated by broader market turmoil following President Trump's fluctuating decisions on tariffs with Canada and Mexico. While Netflix has experienced strong subscriber growth in late 2024, analysts expect the benefits from the password sharing crackdown to diminish, and noted a decline in average daily engagement per global subscriber despite increased overall viewing hours.

title: ‘The Future of World-Building at Disney’: Josh D’Amaro and Alan Bergman Preview Exciting Session at SXSW
summary: Josh D’Amaro, chairman, Disney Experiences, and Alan Bergman, co-chairman, Disney Entertainment, will present "The Future of World-Building at Disney" at SXSW, highlighting the convergence of imagination, innovation, and experiential storytelling. They discuss how Disney's integration of artistry and technology has created an everlasting storytelling legacy, spanning films, parks, and other consumer experiences. The session will cover how studios and Disney Experiences fuel each other's innovation, creating immersive worlds that resonate across generations.

title: Man Utd reveal fixtures on USA pre-season tour as Ruben Amorim prepares for huge summer
summary: Manchester United has confirmed a three-game pre-season tour of the USA this summer as Ruben Amorim prepares for his first full season in charge. The Red Devils will participate in the Premier League's Summer Series, playing against West Ham, Bournemouth, and Everton in New Jersey, Chicago, and Atlanta, respectively. This marks the third consecutive year United has toured the US during the summer, concluding with a match on August 3rd, 13 days before the new Premier League season begins.

title: Six Flags, Dendur strike deal for four board seats
summary: Six Flags has reached a settlement with investor Dendur Capital to add four new directors to its board, ending months of private negotiations. Dendur Capital, which owns approximately 3% of Six Flags, had been pushing for improved margins, governance, and investor communications, especially following the company's merger with Cedar Fair. The new board members include Felipe Dutra, former CFO of AB Inbev, who is noted for his M&A strategy and zero-based budgeting experience, and is seen as a potential CEO candidate.

title: Will More Cruise Lines Launch River Brands?
summary: Royal Caribbean Group's Celebrity Cruises is set to launch 10 new riverboats in Europe by 2027, signaling a growing trend for major ocean cruise lines to enter the river cruising market. This move, following similar strategies by Viking and efforts by Crystal (now Riverside Luxury Cruises), is expected to increase the visibility of river cruising and offers new opportunities for travel advisors to cross-sell to loyal clients. The article also explores the potential for other brands like Disney and Silversea to follow suit, as well as the importance of design and service in this expanding segment.

title: Roomba vacuum maker to up China investment, expand the market
summary: US-based iRobot Corp, known for its Roomba robot vacuum cleaners, plans to increase investment in research and development and expand its manufacturing operations in China, recognizing the country's significance to its growth strategy. China is currently iRobot's fastest-growing and fourth-largest market, prompting the company to tailor products for the local market and establish a dedicated commercial team in Shanghai. The company is also collaborating with Google LLC to integrate robotic and smart home technologies, while rival Xiaomi Corp is also expanding its smart home offerings in China.

title: Netflix Just Made a Truly Radical Change Affecting Millions of New Subscribers, and It's Totally Brilliant. (Or Maybe Insane--Time Will Tell)
summary: Netflix has implemented a significant change by no longer allowing new subscribers to pay via iTunes, aiming to avoid the substantial "Apple tax" of 15% to 30% on subscription revenue. This strategic move, which could save Netflix hundreds of millions, shifts new users to subscribe directly through the Netflix app, cutting Apple out of its commission. While potentially risking some new subscribers, Netflix is betting that its strong demand across platforms will outweigh any losses and make the decision financially brilliant in the long run.

title: Is Apple Still a ‘forever’ Company? How About Facebook?
summary: This article questions the "forever company" thesis for tech giants like Apple and Facebook, highlighting recent market shifts and challenges. It discusses how Apple's plunging shares due to demand issues in China and Nokia's past trajectory suggest even dominant companies face significant hurdles. The piece also explores the concept of S-curves in technology, suggesting that while current tech giants are strong, a new S-curve, potentially augmented reality or AI, could reset the competitive landscape.

title: For Many Builders, Smart Homes Now Come Standard
summary: New-home builders are increasingly integrating smart home technology as a standard feature due to its widespread adoption and affordability. Companies like Meritage Homes and Lennar are partnering with tech giants such as Amazon, Google, and Apple to offer various smart devices and services, aiming to meet consumer demand and differentiate new constructions from existing homes. This shift is driven by consumer expectations and the decreasing cost of smart home tech, making it a compelling baseline amenity for new builds.

title: Philips Cares digitizes the aging and caregiving experience
summary: Royal Philips launched Philips Cares in the U.S. at CES 2019, a new digital experience designed to support family caregivers and their aging loved ones. This service creates a care circle of trusted contacts, provides insights into a loved one's well-being, and allows for managing Philips Lifeline personal alert services. The aim is to ease the caregiving journey by leveraging digital technology, allowing caregivers to stay informed and connected.

title: Resideo Unveils A New Degree Of Whole Home Comfort At CES 2019
summary: Resideo announced its new Honeywell Home T-Series Smart Thermostats (T9 and T10 Pro) at CES 2019, featuring innovative wireless smart room sensors. These thermostats aim to provide whole-home comfort by adjusting temperatures where and when needed, optimizing for sleep at night and energy savings when away. The T9 model offers DIY installation, while the T10 Pro is professionally installed and includes humidity and ventilation controls.

title: Google Signs Lease For Once Bustling Westside Pavilion Shopping Center
summary: Google has signed a 14-year lease for the entire 584,000-square-foot redevelopment of the former Westside Pavilion shopping mall in Los Angeles, transforming it into a "creative office campus" called One Westside. The lease is set to begin in 2022 after construction completion, marking Google's continued expansion following other significant real estate investments in New York City. This move highlights the growing tech and media industries in Los Angeles and the repurposing of traditional retail spaces for modern office needs.

title: With Google project, Minnesota joins the boom in megasized data centers
summary: Minnesota is set to join the growing trend of megasized data centers with Google Inc.'s proposed project near the Sherco power generating station in Becker, Minn. This $600 million facility will consume significant electricity and contribute to the regional boom in "hyperscale" data centers being built by major tech companies. While these centers employ few people once operational, their construction phases provide hundreds of jobs, particularly for skilled electricians, and are critical for the infrastructure of cloud-based computing.

title: TVA announces solar farms to serve Google data centers
summary: The Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) announced new solar farm deals with NextEra Energy Resources and Invenergy to power Google's data centers in Alabama and Tennessee. These two solar farms will provide 300 megawatts of carbon-free renewable power, contributing to Google's commitment to 100% renewable energy. The initiative is part of TVA's efforts to attract and retain top-tier companies by providing cleaner, low-cost electricity and significantly increases solar capacity in the region.

title: Google spends $40 million on Fossil smartwatch tech
summary: Google has agreed to acquire smartwatch technology and personnel from Fossil Group Inc. for US$40 million. This move aims to bolster Google's presence in the smartwatch market, where its Wear OS platform has lagged behind competitors like Apple. The acquisition includes intellectual property not yet released to the market and transfers an unspecified number of Fossil's R&D employees to Google, while Fossil retains 200 people in its smartwatch division.

title: Developers of Driverless Cars Taking A More Cautious, Low-Key Approach
summary: The driverless car industry is adopting a more cautious and low-key approach after previous bold claims and incidents like the fatal Uber crash. Companies like Aptiv, Toyota, and Waymo are emphasizing safety and more restrained deployments, focusing on specific routes and lower speeds, with full autonomy taking longer to achieve. The article highlights the increased recognition of the complexity and challenges involved in industrializing autonomous vehicle technology.

title: The No. 1 Airline App Just Got Better - United Airlines Introduces Upgraded App
summary: United Airlines has launched a reimagined mobile app to enhance customer experience, building on its position as the top-downloaded airline app. The updated app features a dynamic design to provide relevant information throughout the travel journey, new navigation and "My Trips" tab, an inbox for notifications, and personalized content, all based on extensive customer and employee feedback. This initiative reinforces United's commitment to using technology to make travel easier and more intuitive for its customers.

title: Google Cloud Acquisition Targets: ServiceNow, Atlassian, Splunk? Pure Speculation
summary: This article speculates on potential acquisition targets for Google Cloud Platform (GCP) to help it close the revenue gap with AWS and Azure, specifically mentioning ServiceNow, Atlassian, Splunk, and Zayo. It analyzes the pros and cons of each potential deal, highlighting challenges related to market capitalization, sales models, and integration for each company. The author concludes that while Wall Street speculates, there are no credible reports of actual takeover discussions.

title: January 2019 Newsletter: 4 Charts Every Investor Should Know
summary: This January 2019 newsletter by Lyn Alden discusses major market drivers for 2019, highlighting high asset valuations and global leverage. It presents four key charts investors should know: corporate debt, central bank balance sheets, net worth to income, and the U.S. federal deficit and debt to GDP, to help balance risk and reward. The article also provides detailed portfolio updates and investment strategy recommendations focusing on dividends and defensive positioning.

title: Why You Should Include ETFs in Your Portfolio
summary: ETFs offer a convenient and easy way to diversify a portfolio, combining features of individual stocks and mutual funds. They allow investors to participate in entire sectors, avoid single stock risk, and benefit from lower fees and greater tax efficiency compared to traditional mutual funds. The article also covers how to choose and purchase ETFs, as well as several investing strategies.

title: What’s Changed: 2019 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Data Management Solutions for Analytics
summary: This article reviews the 2019 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Data Management Solutions for Analytics (DMSA), highlighting key changes since the previous report. It discusses shifts in vendor positions, new entrants, and removals, focusing on the evolution of major players like Oracle, Microsoft, Amazon Web Services, SAP, Teradata, IBM, Snowflake, Google, and MarkLogic. The article also touches upon the general trends in DMSA, emphasizing the growing importance of cloud and the diverse approaches taken by niche and leading providers.

title: Taiwanese manufacturers are expecting an increase in OLED production and demand
summary: Taiwanese manufacturers like AU Optronics and Novatek Microelectronics are anticipating a massive surge in OLED display demand and are adjusting their production to meet it. The growth is leading established players to ramp up output for Android devices and iPhones, while newcomers like Novatek Microelectronics and Himax Technologies are entering the market focusing on OLED driver ICs. This trend is also observed with other Asian companies, highlighting a widespread belief in the continued expansion of the OLED market.

title: Silicon Valley's highest-paid CEOs may surprise you
summary: This article from the Silicon Valley Business Journal reveals the highest-paid CEOs in Silicon Valley for 2019, highlighting some lesser-known executives at the top of the list. John Donahoe of ServiceNow Inc. is identified as the highest-paid CEO with total compensation of $41.52 million. The piece suggests that the typical highest-paid CEOs might not be the most obvious names.

title: Amazon Eases Into Self-Driving Tech By Joining Aurora's $530 Million Funding Surge
summary: Aurora, a self-driving technology startup founded by leading researchers, secured over $530 million in Series B funding, with Amazon making a significant investment. The company aims to develop autonomous vehicle technology for other manufacturers rather than building its own fleet. This substantial funding injection underscores the capital-intensive nature of autonomous driving development and Amazon's interest in logistics and goods movement.

title: A Storm Is Coming to the Global Music Industry — and More than $100 Billion Is at Stake
summary: Vivendi is selling up to 50% of Universal Music Group, and its projected astronomical valuation could significantly impact the valuations of rivals Sony Music and Warner Music Group. Analysts from Deutsche Bank, Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs, and Exane BNP Paribas have provided valuations for UMG ranging from $29 billion to $42 billion, with a "bull case" scenario for Morgan Stanley suggesting even higher figures based on streaming growth. This potential Universal Music Group supersale could lead to a combined valuation for the "big three" music companies exceeding $100 billion, driven by intense market demand and optimistic streaming forecasts.

title: Dandelion Energy Raises $16 Million Led by Google Ventures and Comcast
summary: Dandelion Energy, a leading home geothermal company, has completed a Series A funding round of $16 million, bringing its total funding to $23 million. The round was co-led by GV (formerly Google Ventures) and Comcast Ventures, with participation from Lennar Corporation and existing investors. Dandelion plans to use the funding to accelerate growth, invest in R&D, and expand operations across New York State, aiming to make geothermal heating and cooling economically viable for millions of homeowners by reducing installation costs.

title: Google selects Equinix for submarine cable landing station in LA
summary: Google has chosen Equinix's LA4 data center as the landing point for its upcoming Curie submarine cable, which will connect the US with Chile. This marks the first direct submarine link between the two countries in 20 years. The cable, named after Marie Skłodowska Curie, will stretch over 10,000 km and aims to meet the increasing demand for high-capacity, low-latency global connectivity.

title: Johnson & Johnson to buy surgical robotics firm Auris for $3.4 billion
summary: Johnson & Johnson announced its acquisition of Auris Health Inc for $3.4 billion in cash, marking its expansion into the rapidly growing healthcare robotics market. This strategic move aims to bolster J&J's medical device business and leverage Auris's surgical robotic scope used in respiratory procedures and lung cancer detection. The deal is expected to create a formidable competitor, particularly for current market leader Intuitive Surgical.

title: Google confirms plans to expand in Cambridge's Kendall Square
summary: Google has confirmed its plans to expand its presence in Kendall Square, Cambridge, by occupying a new glass tower. This expansion marks a significant development for the technology giant in the area. The article references previous related developments and proposals for Google's presence in Kendall Square.

title: Alphabet Dethrones Amazon As Top U.S. Internet Company: Citi Report
summary: Citigroup has re-ranked Alphabet as the top U.S. internet company, surpassing Amazon, due to its strong growth in mobile search and YouTube, stock buybacks, and high valuation. Amazon's downgrade to fourth place is attributed to slower growth, regulatory challenges in India, and distractions from its HQ2 plans and CEO's personal issues. This re-ranking coincides with Google Cloud's aggressive investment in its sales division and increased competition with Amazon Web Services and Microsoft Azure.

title: Microsoft boosts HoloLens performance, seeking corporate users
summary: Microsoft is launching an improved version of its HoloLens augmented reality goggles, the HoloLens 2, aimed at corporate users, with a lower price point and enhanced features. The company is positioning the device as a tool for various industries, including healthcare and manufacturing, and is also offering it via a monthly subscription. This move reflects Microsoft's strategy to democratize AI and mixed reality technology and generate revenue beyond device sales through cloud software.

title: Special report: Sophisticated ad fraud permeates the mobile app ecosystem
summary: This report details how sophisticated ad fraud has become an endemic problem within the mobile app ecosystem, affecting both Android and iOS platforms. It covers various fraudulent techniques such as unviewable ads, bad traffic, synthetic audiences, and click injection, highlighting the significant financial and personal costs to users, advertisers, and the industry. Case studies including apps from Cheetah Mobile, Kika Tech, and GOMO illustrate the pervasive nature of these fraudulent activities and the challenges in detection and regulation.

title: Here are the top 10 self-made richest women in India
summary: The Hurun’s India Rich List of 2018 highlights the top 10 self-made richest women in India, led by Biocon's Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw. The list features prominent figures such as PepsiCo's ex-CEO Indra Nooyi and Jayshree Ullal of Arista Network, showcasing women who have built significant wealth through their entrepreneurial ventures and leadership roles. Companies represented include biopharma, networking, healthcare technology, and consumer goods.
