summary: Equinix is expanding into India, one of the world's fastest-growing digital services markets, through a $161 million acquisition of a two-data center campus in Mumbai from GPX Global Systems. The acquisition is strategic as the campus already hosts major cloud service providers, networks, and internet exchanges, giving Equinix a strong foothold in the country. This move aligns with increased investment in India's digital infrastructure by both specialist data center providers and international cloud giants.

title: FuboTV begins streaming some content in 4K with HDR10
summary: FuboTV has started streaming select content, specifically main broadcasts of the 2018 FIFA World Cup, in 4K resolution with HDR10 support. This feature is initially available on Chromecast and Amazon Fire TV 4K devices, with support for Apple TV and Roku devices coming soon. FuboTV is the first virtual MVPD to launch 4K HDR in beta, requiring users to have compatible 4K HDR TVs, HDMI 2.0/2.2 ports, and sufficient bandwidth.

title: PPP likely saved 35 million jobs, says JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon
summary: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon estimates that the government's Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) saved between 30 to 35 million jobs by providing loans to small businesses affected by the coronavirus pandemic. Dimon praised the swift action of lawmakers and the administration, but also highlighted the need to extend the program, especially for minority-owned businesses that may not have initially received adequate funds. He also discussed the formation of the New York Jobs CEO Council to address the racial wealth gap and economic inequality, anticipating a delayed economic recession and stressing the importance of safely reopening the economy.

title: iShares MSCI All Country Asia ex Japan ETF (AAXJ) Short Interest & Short Float | Updated Feb 2026
summary: This article provides an updated overview of the short interest for the iShares MSCI All Country Asia ex Japan ETF (AAXJ) as of August 15, 2025. It details that AAXJ had 1.24 million shares sold short, a 1.64% increase from the prior report, and a short interest ratio of 2.3 days to cover. The report also includes historical short interest data, a comparison to competitors, and explanations of short selling metrics.

title: Hyundai, Aptiv Dub Autonomous Venture ‘Motional,’ Increase Hiring
summary: Hyundai Motor Group and Aptiv Plc have named their autonomous-driving joint venture "Motional" and plan significant expansion. The company aims to increase staffing by 45% to over 1,000 people and have a self-driving car ready for testing by 2022. Motional seeks to sell its software to robotaxi fleets, leveraging Hyundai's backing to compete with tech giants entering the autonomous vehicle space.

title: Android phones with Qualcomm Snapdragon processors may have security worry
summary: Security researchers at Check Point have discovered over 400 code vulnerabilities in Qualcomm Digital Signal Processor (DSP) chips used in Android phones. These vulnerabilities could allow an attacker to turn the phone into a spying tool, exfiltrating personal data, or even render the device permanently unresponsive. Qualcomm has acknowledged the findings and released mitigations, encouraging users to update their devices.

title: Two beverage giants choose cloud partners
summary: PepsiCo and Keurig Dr Pepper have each signed long-term cloud technology contracts with Microsoft and Google Cloud, respectively, to modernize their digital networks. PepsiCo's partnership with Microsoft aims to improve service delivery, innovation, and sustainability, while Keurig Dr Pepper's agreement with Google Cloud supports its digital transformation by migrating major applications and retiring data centers. Both companies are leveraging cloud solutions for greater agility, data insights, and operational resilience.

title: Developers v. Apple: Outlining Complaints about the App Store
summary: This article examines the various complaints developers have against Apple regarding its App Store policies, including the 30% revenue cut, Apple's alleged favoritism towards its own apps, the effectiveness of App Store ads, and issues with counterfeit apps. It also discusses Apple's arbitrary judgments against developers and its controversial stance on game streaming services. The author suggests potential solutions for Apple to improve its relationship with developers and avoid increased regulation.

title: Amazon and Google among big US companies pledging to hire 100,000 people from marginalized New York communities
summary: Major US companies including Amazon, Google, and Goldman Sachs have pledged to hire 100,000 people from New York City's low-income and minority communities by 2030. This initiative, called the New York Jobs CEO Council, aims to address racial and economic inequities worsened by COVID-19 by providing entry-level positions, apprenticeships, and on-the-job learning. While the effort is praised as a good start, experts emphasize the need for specific interventions like mentoring programs and performance reviews to ensure career advancement for employees from underrepresented backgrounds beyond entry-level roles.

title: Apple Sells $5.5 Billion of Bonds in Tech Borrowing Boom
summary: Apple Inc. has sold $5.5 billion in bonds, joining a trend of tech giants leveraging low borrowing costs. This marks Apple's second bond issuance in a single calendar year since 2017, a strategy also pursued by companies like Amazon and Alphabet. The move highlights the current environment where cash-rich companies are taking advantage of historically low yields to raise capital.

title: GIB - CGI Inc Latest Stock News & Market Updates
summary: This page provides the latest news and insights on CGI Inc. (GIB), a global IT and business consulting firm. It covers company announcements on technology initiatives, government contracts, acquisitions, and regulatory disclosures. Recent updates include CGI's expansion in Atlanta, director election results, Q1 Fiscal 2026 earnings, renewal of its Normal Course Issuer Bid, and strategic collaborations with OpenAI and Google Cloud for advanced AI solutions.

title: Nvidia Expands Partner Program With New Incentives, Training
summary: Nvidia has enhanced its Partner Network with new incentives, industry-specific training, and improved sales tracking for its growing channel of over 1,500 members. Key additions include a fixed back-end rebate for Elite partners, dedicated market development funds, and an expanded "AI Champions Club." The company is also planning future expansions, such as integrating Mellanox and Cumulus Networks' partner programs and introducing a cloud service provider program.

title: Exclusive: Amazon in talks to invest in cloud services company Rackspace - sources
summary: Amazon.com Inc. is reportedly in preliminary discussions to acquire a minority stake in U.S. cloud services provider Rackspace Technology Inc. This potential investment would strengthen ties between the two companies, as Rackspace already assists businesses in migrating data to Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, and VMware. Rackspace's shares surged following the news of the possible deal, which would be the second such investment by a major tech company into an Apollo-owned firm this year, following Google's investment in ADT Inc.

title: SoftBank builds $1.2 billion Amazon stake; invests in Netflix, Tesla
summary: SoftBank Group Corp has built a $1.2 billion stake in Amazon and also invested in Netflix, Tesla, Microsoft, and Alphabet, marking a strategic shift towards liquid stocks. This move comes as the company expands its investment activities beyond unlisted startups and its Vision Fund, which has recently seen its holdings fall below acquisition prices. The group is leveraging a massive asset sale program to buy shares in these tech giants, whose values are currently rising amidst a tech stock rally.

title: The race to quantum advantage
summary: This article discusses the global race toward quantum advantage, highlighting how quantum computing promises to solve currently intractable problems across various industries. It details the fundamental concepts of quantum computing, including qubits and modalities like superconducting and trapped ion qubits, and outlines the technological stack required. The authors emphasize that while significant progress has been made by companies like IBM, Google, and Honeywell, the journey to scalable, error-free quantum computers capable of widespread application is still a marathon.

title: Apple Becomes First U.S. Company Worth More Than $2 Trillion
summary: Apple achieved a new financial milestone, becoming the first publicly traded U.S. company to reach a market capitalization of over $2 trillion. This valuation marks a doubling in just two years, driven by a strong stock performance, especially during the pandemic due to work-from-home trends and robust online sales. The company's market cap now surpasses that of other U.S. tech giants and the GDP of several developed countries, with a four-for-one stock split planned to make shares more accessible.

title: BlackBerry Phones Live Again, As Texas Startup Promises 5G Device
summary: A Texas-based startup named OnwardMobility has announced plans to release a new BlackBerry smartphone in 2021, featuring 5G connectivity and a physical keyboard. This comes after BlackBerry and TCL Communication had previously ceased their partnership for branded phones. OnwardMobility justifies the revival by citing the increasing need for secure, productivity-enhancing 5G devices for remote enterprise professionals.

title: To get skin tones right, Pinterest’s AI went way beyond facial recognition
summary: Pinterest has updated its AI to more accurately detect skin tones in a wider array of images, moving beyond facial recognition. This helps users find more relevant beauty and style tips, and supports features like their augmented-reality Try On tool. The new system avoids biases associated with facial recognition and can analyze images beyond just faces, such as close-ups of body parts or accessories.

title: Google parent company Alphabet weighed buying small TikTok stake as a part of a group bid
summary: Google's parent company, Alphabet, considered joining a group bid to acquire a minority, non-voting stake in TikTok, but the effort ultimately fell through. TikTok, owned by China's ByteDance, is facing a US government order to sell its American assets amid national security concerns. The popular video-sharing app is a significant rival to Google's YouTube, attracting both creative talent and advertising revenue.

title: Google, T-Mobile, Silicon Labs among partners with ioXt Alliance to secure IoT devices
summary: The ioXt Alliance, a global standard for IoT security, announced that major technology companies like Google, T-Mobile, and Silicon Labs have certified a wide range of their devices through the ioXt Alliance Certification Program. This initiative aims to address increasing consumer and retailer demand for secure IoT products by providing a comprehensive and scalable security compliance program. The certified devices span various categories, from cell phones and smart home devices to automotive technology, ensuring transparency and assurance in IoT security.

title: (08/25/20) Dan Sullivan: Technical Talk from The Chartist
summary: Despite high price-to-earnings multiples and near-historic valuations, technical expert Dan Sullivan believes the bull market has further to run, supported by bullish chart patterns and strong AIII sentiment indicators. He notes the significant outperformance of FAANG stocks relative to the S&P 500 and recommends Veeva Systems (VEEV) and DexCom (DXCM) in the medical sector for traders.

title: Alphabet’s Google Appoints Halimah DeLaine Prado as New General Counsel
summary: Alphabet Inc.'s Google has appointed Halimah DeLaine Prado, a long-time company veteran and one of its highest-ranking Black executives, as its new general counsel. This promotion aligns with CEO Sundar Pichai's pledge earlier this year to increase leadership diversity among underrepresented groups by 30% by 2025. DeLaine Prado's appointment is expected to be well-received by Black employees advocating for greater diversity within the company.

title: Unity Software Prepares To Become Publicly Owned
summary: Unity Technologies is planning its initial public offering (IPO), having filed an S-1 statement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, revealing significant revenue alongside ongoing losses. The Unity engine is widely used by over 1 million active users for games and animations, with its diverse application extending beyond gaming to architecture and filmmaking. Going public is expected to help Unity address financial losses and expand into new markets, improving its competitive position.

title: TUBI NOW AVAILABLE ON NEW TIVO STREAM 4K DEVICE AND STREAMING ON TIVO+
summary: Tubi, a division of FOX Entertainment, has announced that its library of over 23,000 movies and TV shows is now available on the new TiVo Stream 4K device and streaming on the TiVo+ content network. This renewed agreement allows TiVo customers to access Tubi's on-demand content for free, including new titles like Magic Mike XXL and The Family That Preys. The partnership aims to enhance content discovery and expand Tubi's reach across various platforms.

title: How to Invest In Telehealth and Digital Medicine
summary: The article discusses investment opportunities in telehealth and digital medicine, highlighting the accelerated adoption due to the COVID-19 pandemic. It differentiates between telehealth and telemedicine, and provides examples of public companies and ETFs for investors looking to capitalize on this growing sector. The piece emphasizes the long-term growth potential in virtual healthcare, driven by demographic trends and technological advancements.

title: Cetus: Cryptojacking Worm Targeting Docker Daemons
summary: A new cryptojacking worm named Cetus has been discovered, specifically targeting unsecured Docker daemons to mine Monero. Cetus, created by TeamTnT, disguises itself as legitimate Docker binaries like Portainer and uses Masscan to spread across networks. Palo Alto Networks customers are protected through Prisma Cloud Compute's host compliance protection feature.

title: Coronavirus Recovery: A Tale of Two Markets
summary: This article examines the differing impacts of market concentration on the recovery of the U.S. and Canadian markets from the coronavirus pandemic. It highlights how the concentration of FAANG-type stocks boosted the U.S. market's recovery, while Canada's concentration in underperforming companies and the energy sector hindered its rebound. The author emphasizes the importance of portfolio diversification to mitigate risks associated with market concentration.

title: Exclusive: -Facebook says Apple rejected its attempt to tell users about App Store fees
summary: Facebook stated that Apple rejected its attempt to inform users about the 30% App Store fee on sales from a new online events feature, citing a rule against "irrelevant" information. Facebook had sought a fee waiver from Apple for small businesses using the feature to recover COVID-19 related revenue losses, but Apple declined. This incident aligns Facebook with other developers, like Epic Games, who are criticizing Apple's App Store commissions and facing scrutiny over alleged anti-competitive behavior.

title: Tesla, Apple stock splits pave way for more gains
summary: Apple and Tesla's recent stock splits may lead to further share price gains by increasing affordability for smaller investors, despite splits not changing a company's overall market capitalization. Historically, major brands have seen an average 33% share price rally within 12 months post-split. While some experts caution about increased volatility and diluted earnings, others predict continued growth for mega-cap tech stocks.

title: ANALYSIS - WPP's path out of the pandemic
summary: WPP, the world's largest advertising company, has outlined a strategy for prosperity after what it believes was the economic low point of the pandemic. Despite an 11.5% fall in first-half revenue, WPP announced a dividend to shareholders, signaling confidence in its performance. CEO Mark Read highlighted accelerated digital transformation, the rise of e-commerce, and increased focus on ESG issues as key trends shaping the industry and WPP's future approach.

title: Big Oil Faded. Will Big Tech?
summary: This article questions whether Big Tech companies, currently dominant, face a similar fate to Big Oil, specifically Exxon Mobil, which was once the world's most valuable company but has since declined. The author draws parallels between the economic and political influence of past oil superpowers and current tech giants, suggesting that while Big Tech seems invincible now, history shows that even dominant industries can lose relevance due to changing global dynamics and a failure to adapt.

title: Zoom posts another stellar quarter, with revenue up 355 percent
summary: Zoom reported exceptional second-quarter financial results, with revenue soaring 355% year-over-year, significantly surpassing market expectations. This growth is attributed to the widespread shift to remote work during the COVID-19 pandemic and organizations planning for long-term remote operations. The company saw a massive increase in customers and is projecting substantial revenue for the full fiscal year 2021.

title: Apple and Tesla shares spike after stock splits kick in
summary: Apple and Tesla shares surged on Monday after their stock splits took effect, attracting significant investor buying. Apple jumped over 4 percent after its 4-for-1 split, while Tesla rallied 10 percent following its 5-for-1 split, elevating its market capitalization to over $440 billion and showcasing the impact of increased affordability for individual investors. The success of these splits may encourage other companies with high-priced stocks to consider similar moves, as both Silicon Valley companies have strong individual investor followings.

title: Amazon’s Drone Delivery Fleet Hits Milestone With FAA Clearance
summary: Amazon Prime Air has received certification from the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to operate as an "air carrier," allowing it to begin commercial drone deliveries under a trial program. This certification signifies the FAA's confidence in Amazon’s drone operating and safety procedures, placing it alongside Wing (Alphabet Inc. subsidiary) and UPS as companies approved for such operations. While this is a significant step, routine drone deliveries are still years away due to the need for further regulatory frameworks regarding autonomous flights, design standards, and a new air-traffic system for low-altitude drones.

title: What Enabled Adobe to Raise Its Digital Media ARR?
summary: Adobe's Digital Media ARR increased due to the continued migration of its Creative Suite and the addition of new Creative Cloud subscriptions. The company saw significant growth in its Digital Media segment, with Creative Cloud revenues rising 44% year-over-year, leading Adobe to raise its fiscal 2016 Digital Media ARR guidance to $4.0 billion. Fiscal 1Q16 was the last quarter Adobe provided specific Creative Cloud subscriber figures.

title: AT&T explores sale of its digital advertising business Xandr
summary: AT&T Inc. is reportedly exploring the sale of its Xandr digital advertising unit as it focuses on entertainment and debt reduction. This potential sale signals a shift away from challenging Alphabet Inc. in online ads, with the unit not generating robust revenue growth after being acquired as AppNexus for approximately $1.6 billion in 2018.

title: Marvell exits the general purpose Arm server business
summary: Marvell Technology Group has announced it is discontinuing its ThunderX3 Arm-based server processor for general-purpose server use. The company will instead focus on vertical markets and hyperscalers, customizing silicon for major cloud providers. This move allows Marvell to secure up-front commitments and reduce risk by co-funding custom chip development with customers.

title: 10 Most Visited Websites by Internet Users in India
summary: This article identifies the top 10 most visited websites in India based on unique visitor data from July 2020. Google Sites, encompassing YouTube, Gmail, and Google Search, leads the list with over 396.9 million unique visitors and a 97.8% reach among Indian internet users. Facebook and Amazon Sites follow, securing the second and third positions respectively.

title: Apple delays iPhone change that's expected to make it harder for Facebook and other apps to target ads
summary: Apple announced a delay until early 2021 for a planned change to the iPhone operating system that would impact how mobile advertisers track users. This privacy-focused update, previously set for iOS 14, gives developers more time to adapt to new rules requiring user permission to track their activity. The change is expected to significantly affect mobile advertising, with Facebook warning of potential revenue drops for publishers.

title: Oatly is defending itself after selling stake to Trump donor Schwarzman's Blackstone Group
summary: Oatly, the vegan milk brand, is facing backlash and potential boycotts from its customers and the coffee industry after selling a 10% stake to a group of investors led by Blackstone Growth. The controversy stems from Blackstone CEO Stephen Schwarzman's significant donations to Donald Trump's reelection campaign, and past accusations against Blackstone-owned Hidrovias regarding Amazon deforestation. Oatly is defending its decision, stating the partnership helps expand its sustainable mission and influences leading private equity to invest in sustainability.

title: Axis Global Equity Alpha Fund of Fund Review: Should You Invest?
summary: This article reviews the Axis Global Equity Alpha Fund of Fund, which invests in Schroder International Selection Fund Global Equity Alpha. The author discusses the underlying fund's performance against its benchmark, highlighting a poor track record and high expense ratios, especially for the regular plan. The article concludes by recommending investors consider alternatives with lower expenses, such as the Motilal Oswal S&P 500 Index Fund, for international diversification.

title: Fossil Gen 5 Garrett HR review: Style and substance
summary: The Fossil Gen 5 Garrett HR smartwatch blends classic chronograph style with modern features like hands-free calls, activity tracking, and contactless payments. Its improved hardware provides a smooth user experience, addressing previous Wear OS sluggishness. While battery life is typical for smartwatches, and Google Fit has some limitations, the Garrett HR is praised for its design, vibrant display, and multi-functional capabilities, making it a strong lifestyle-focused smartwatch.

title: Google Pixel 4a – a back to basics 4G phone with lots of features
summary: The Google Pixel 4a is reviewed as a strong "value" offering with pure Android and guaranteed updates, praised for its computational camera and 3.5mm audio jack. While it excels in software and photography for its $599 price, it receives average marks for battery life and screen readability in daylight. The review concludes it's a class leader in its segment, especially for those prioritizing a basic, well-featured 4G phone.

title: Montana GOP lawmakers made fortunes at tech giant Oracle — and became its best friends in D.C.
summary: Montana Republicans Senator Steve Daines and Representative Greg Gianforte accrued significant wealth through their past association with tech giant Oracle, leveraging their positions to promote legislation and initiatives that benefited the company. Their financial ties stemmed from Gianforte's sale of RightNow Technologies to Oracle and shared real estate ventures, while both lawmakers supported Oracle's lobbying efforts on cybersecurity, AI, and other policy issues, often opposing Oracle's competitors like Google. This close relationship has also seen Oracle contribute to their political campaigns, highlighting a pattern of mutual financial and legislative support.

title: TikTok data could be gold mine for ERP, HR systems
summary: TikTok's vast user data and its powerful AI-driven recommendation engine could be highly valuable for enterprise resource planning (ERP) and human resources (HR) systems, attracting interest from companies like Microsoft and Oracle. This data could offer insights into consumer trends, improve advertising integration, and enhance job matching capabilities. The potential acquisition of TikTok's U.S. operations by a U.S. company could alleviate governmental concerns about data ownership by China.

title: The Taboola/Outbrain Merger Is Off – Here’s Why
summary: The planned merger between content recommendation companies Taboola and Outbrain has been called off. The primary reasons cited are Taboola's shift from publisher guarantees to a revenue share model, leading to breaches of publisher agreements and loss of major clients, which in turn hindered its ability to secure new financing. This development comes after a lengthy engagement period and a Justice Department antitrust review that ultimately cleared the merger.

title: Helium Is Soaring on Red-Hot Demand, Shrinking Supply
summary: This article discusses the increasing demand and shrinking supply of helium, highlighting its critical role in various high-tech applications beyond balloons. It points out that new large helium deposits are becoming rare and existing reserves, like the U.S. National Helium Reserve, are projected to be depleted soon. The piece also suggests investment opportunities in helium exploration companies like Desert Mountain Energy, comparing the commodity's rarity to gold.

title: The ABCs of AI
summary: This article provides a primer on artificial intelligence (AI) and its applications, particularly within the printing industry. It explains what AI is, its historical context, and how it can help print businesses optimize operations, cut costs, and streamline workflows, especially in the context of increasing automation and customization demands accelerated by COVID-19. Kodak's PRINERGY Software and On Demand Platform are highlighted as examples of AI-powered solutions in print.

title: Taboola, Outbrain merger collapses, ending bid to form rival to walled gardens
summary: The planned $850 million merger between ad-tech firms Taboola and Outbrain has fallen through after nearly a year of negotiations. The deal's collapse, influenced by Taboola reportedly seeking to pay less than half the agreed price and antitrust scrutiny, highlights the challenges in creating a digital advertising entity capable of rivaling Google and Facebook. Despite the combined entities' potential to reach 2 billion users monthly, various obstacles including the pandemic's impact on digital advertising and the changing terms led to the dissolution of the agreement.

title: Russian Intelligence Hackers Are Back, Microsoft Warns, Aiming at Officials of Both Parties (Published 2020)
summary: Microsoft has warned that Russian military intelligence hackers, previously responsible for the Democratic National Committee attack, are targeting campaign staff, consultants, and think tanks associated with both Democrats and Republicans with new, stealthier methods. This assessment follows a whistle-blower claim about suppressed intelligence regarding Russian interference. While Microsoft also found Chinese and Iranian hacker activity, the Chinese attacks were primarily focused on Biden campaign staff members' private email accounts and other prominent individuals, potentially complicating previous government assessments.

title: Digital Billboards: A Game Changer for Auto Advertisers in the Out-of-Home Market
summary: This article discusses the increasing importance of digital billboards (DOOH) for auto advertisers in the Out-of-Home (OOH) market. It highlights the growing revenue generated by DOOH, its effectiveness in driving consumer action, and the innovative ways auto companies like Porsche and Kia are utilizing this advertising medium. The article also touches on the challenges of quantifying OOH impact and the advantages DOOH offers over traditional advertising methods, including affordability and flexibility.

title: HP CFO departs for Google after two years of service
summary: HP Inc. announced that its Chief Financial Officer, Steve Fieler, will be leaving the company in October to take on the role of business finance officer at Google. He had served as HP's CFO since 2018. Marie Myers, the current Chief Transformation Officer, will serve as the interim finance head until a permanent successor is found.

title: Inside Adobe’s employee-focused COVID-19 response roadmap
summary: Adobe successfully transitioned its 22,000+ global workforce to remote work within a single weekend during the COVID-19 crisis, leveraging previous contingency planning experience and existing cloud infrastructure. The company prioritized employee experience by enhancing collaboration tools, implementing a Zero-Trust Enterprise Network (ZEN) for secure access, and providing "desktop as a service" solutions. This focus on employee well-being and productivity ensured business continuity and a smooth transition to long-term remote work.

title: -ByteDance picks Oracle as partner to try to save TikTok U.S.
summary: ByteDance has chosen Oracle as its technology partner to keep TikTok operating in the United States, sidestepping an outright sale but structuring the deal as a partnership. This decision comes after intense pressure from the U.S. government, with Oracle expected to manage TikTok's U.S. user data and potentially acquire a stake in its U.S. operations. The proposal will undergo review by the U.S. Treasury Department and CFIUS to address national security concerns.

title: What to Expect with the Release of Apple iOS14
summary: Apple's iOS14 update introduces significant privacy changes, requiring consumer opt-in for sharing personal data with third-party apps for ad targeting, primarily affecting the use of the IDFA. This shift presents challenges for app advertisers and platforms like Outbrain, which are adapting by participating in Apple’s SKAdNetwork framework, working with Mobile Measurement Partners, and leveraging their extensive network on the open web. The changes are expected to have a massive impact on in-app advertising, particularly for social platforms like Facebook, making it crucial for advertisers to diversify their media mix.

title: More Risk, More Reward for U.S. Equity Funds
summary: U.S. equity funds with "High" Morningstar Risk ratings significantly outperformed during the market rebound from March to September 2020, demonstrating higher up-capture ratios compared to lower-risk counterparts. However, these high-risk funds also experienced larger declines during the initial COVID-19-driven market collapse. The article highlights specific funds like Baron Partners and Miller Opportunity that benefited greatly from concentrated holdings in strong-performing stocks and sectors.

title: Oracle (ORCL) Trading Lower After TikTok Download Ban
summary: Oracle (ORCL) stock is trading lower after the U.S. Commerce Department banned TikTok and WeChat downloads, effective Sunday. The announcement creates uncertainty around Oracle's potential deal for TikTok's U.S. operations, with the stock needing to hold the $57 to $57.50 price zone to maintain a bullish technical outlook. Long-term patterns suggest only modest upside even if a deal is finalized, and a failed deal could trigger a bearish double top pattern.

title: Goldman Sachs: Labor Day Weekend Total Beer Sales +7%; Hard Seltzer Sales +137%
summary: A Goldman Sachs report indicates that total beer sales increased 7% over Labor Day weekend 2020 compared to the previous year, with distributors anticipating a strong finish to the year for off-premise beer sales. Hard seltzer sales surged an impressive 137% over the same period, despite widespread out-of-stock issues for both categories. The report highlights that Boston Beer's Truly Hard Seltzer and Mark Anthony Brands' White Claw continued to dominate the hard seltzer market, with breweries actively increasing capacity to meet demand.

title: The biggest semiconductor deal in history should have been even bigger
summary: Nvidia's acquisition of Arm Holdings for $40 billion marks the semiconductor industry's largest deal, yet Arm's valuation is considered surprisingly low, lagging SoftBank's investment goals. Analysts believe Nvidia's ownership could help Arm realize its full potential, providing resources to a company whose technology is integral to various processors. The deal also highlights Europe's struggle to retain its tech giants, with many being acquired by US companies, though some European firms are now achieving significant market capitalization.

title: Trump Blesses Oracle’s TikTok Deal, Delaying Potential U.S. Ban
summary: President Trump approved Oracle Corp.'s bid for TikTok's American operations, delaying a potential U.S. ban on the video-sharing app. The deal involves the creation of TikTok Global, with Oracle taking a 12.5% stake and Walmart Inc. taking 7.5%, and includes a $5 billion contribution to a U.S. education fund as well as the creation of 25,000 jobs. This agreement aims to address U.S. national security concerns while allowing TikTok to continue operating in the country.

title: TikTok Ban Averted: Trump Gives Oracle-Walmart Deal His 'Blessing'
summary: President Trump has tentatively approved a deal involving Oracle and Walmart to keep TikTok operational in the U.S., averting a ban set for midnight, Sunday. The agreement aims to address national security concerns regarding American user data, even though Chinese company ByteDance is expected to retain a majority ownership stake. This deal is expected to boost Oracle's cloud computing business and allow Walmart to integrate e-commerce into the app.

title: Wall Street-Backed Exchange Launches as Rival to NYSE, Nasdaq
summary: A new exchange, Members Exchange (MEMX), backed by major Wall Street firms and BlackRock Inc., launched on Monday to compete with NYSE and Nasdaq. MEMX aims to offer a low-cost alternative, initiating trading with seven stocks and planning to expand to all U.S. exchange-listed securities by September 29. This launch follows years of dissatisfaction among banks and trading firms regarding fees charged by existing major exchanges.

title: Wall Street-Backed Exchange Launches as Rival to NYSE, Nasdaq - WSJ
summary: Members Exchange (MEMX), a new low-cost competitor backed by Wall Street firms and BlackRock Inc., launched Monday to rival NYSE and Nasdaq. The exchange aims to attract trading activity with an aggressive pricing strategy, starting with trades in seven stocks and planning to expand to all U.S. exchange-listed securities by Sept. 29. This launch follows years of frustration among banks and trading firms with existing exchanges' fees.

title: Peacock Now Available on the Roku Platform
summary: Peacock announced its app is now available nationwide on the Roku® platform, reaching an estimated 100 million people. This partnership expands Peacock's reach and provides Roku users with access to over 20,000 hours of on-demand movies, shows, live news, and sports programming, including a free tier offering 13,000 hours of premium content. Both companies expressed excitement about delivering high-quality content to engaged streamers.

title: COVID-19 Recovery Analysis: Automotive Software
summary: Technavio reports that the automotive software market is expected to grow by $10.70 billion between 2020 and 2024, with a CAGR exceeding 9%, despite the COVID-19 pandemic. This growth is primarily driven by the increased adoption of Advanced Driver-Assistance Systems (ADAS) in mass-produced vehicles. The report provides an in-depth analysis of market trends, drivers, and the competitive landscape, highlighting key market participants and potential challenges like increasing software complexity.

title: Oracle is a distant laggard in cloud infrastructure market even after TikTok deal
summary: Despite recent high-profile customer wins like TikTok and Zoom, Oracle remains a "niche player" in the cloud infrastructure market, significantly trailing leaders Amazon, Microsoft, and Google. Gartner estimates Oracle's market share at around 2%, and analysts note that its growth is still heavily reliant on traditional database software, with its stock performance lagging behind major cloud competitors. The TikTok deal, while a "shot in the arm," is viewed by some analysts as politically motivated rather than a testament to Oracle's competitive cloud capabilities.

title: What happened to Baidu, once China's golden boy of innovation?
summary: Baidu's decline in innovation and market dominance is largely attributed to Google's exit from China in 2010, which removed a fierce competitor and led to complacency. The article suggests that while Baidu initially excelled in technology, the lack of competition caused its search engine to deteriorate with commercial and misleading content. Now, Baidu is making risky, rushed gambles into new sectors like biotech, potentially repeating IBM Watson's mistakes, rather than careful exploration like Google.

title: Nasdaq 100 Is Just Halfway Through Its Plunge, Says Morgan Stanley
summary: Morgan Stanley's chief US equity strategist, Michael Wilson, believes the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 is only halfway through its market correction despite a recent bounce. He points to continued overvaluation, strong call option interest, successful tech IPOs, and hedge fund commitment as signs that bullish sentiment for major tech companies like FAANGs and Microsoft remains too high, indicating further declines are likely. The Nasdaq 100 has already seen a significant drop this month, underperforming the S&P 500.

title: ClassEDU Launches to Bring "Class for Zoom" Product to Market to Help Millions of Teachers and Students Learning Online Due To COVID
summary: ClassEDU Inc. announced its launch and secured $16 million in seed financing to bring its "Class for Zoom" product to market. This platform aims to enhance online learning by adding features like attendance tracking, assignment distribution, and quizzes to Zoom, making virtual classrooms feel more like in-person ones. The funding round saw participation from key Zoom investors and prominent education leaders, recognizing the critical need for improved remote learning solutions hastened by the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: BBVA permitirá realizar consultas a través de WhatsApp
summary: BBVA is launching a new feature that allows customers to conduct inquiries via WhatsApp through an adapted version of its virtual assistant, Blue. This service will enable users to check account movements, income, expenses, and receive information on products without needing to visit a physical branch. The initiative aims to provide an accessible and secure channel for financial queries, especially benefiting those less familiar with traditional banking apps, and aligns with the bank's efforts to enhance customer support during the Covid-19 crisis.

title: Vitality: Delivering a valuable experience for customers
summary: Vitality, founded in 2004, distinguishes itself in the insurance market by integrating wellness into its offerings, aiming to improve customers' lives and encouraging 100 million people to be 20% more active by 2025. Chief Digital Officer Dave Priestley explains how the company uses digital transformation, including an innovative member app, to deliver value and a superior customer experience. Despite initial challenges with legacy systems, Vitality has leveraged technology and partnerships, such as with TCS, to create a unified customer platform and adapt rapidly to new demands like the COVID-19 pandemic, all while focusing on customer-centric outcomes.

title: Joker Playing Hide-and-Seek with Google Play
summary: The article discusses how the Joker malware continuously bypasses Google Play's vetting process by changing its code and payload retrieval methods. It details three scenarios Joker uses to deliver its malicious payload, including direct downloads, one-stage, and two-stage downloads, all designed to steal SMS, contacts, and subscribe users to premium services. The author recommends users pay close attention to app permissions and reviews to avoid such compromised applications.

title: Spotify, Match Launch Coalition to Protest App Store Rules
summary: Spotify, Match Group, Epic Games, and 10 other organizations have formed the Coalition for App Fairness to challenge the app store rules of Apple and Google. The coalition introduced "App Store Principles," advocating against platform owners using developer data to compete and requiring exclusive use of their app stores or payment systems. This move aims to pressure Apple and Google into modifying their existing app store guidelines.

title: To Fight Apple and Google, Smaller App Rivals Organize a Coalition (Published 2020)
summary: Smaller app developers like Spotify, Match Group, and Epic Games have formed the "Coalition for App Fairness" to challenge the dominance and app store practices of Apple and Google. This move comes as scrutiny intensifies on major tech companies for alleged antitrust violations. The coalition aims to advocate for changes in app store policies and "protect the app economy."

title: Amazon’s Drone Delivery Fleet Hits Milestone With FAA Clearance
summary: Amazon Prime Air has received certification from the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to operate as a drone airline, allowing it to begin commercial deliveries under a trial program in the U.S. This makes Amazon one of only a few companies, alongside Wing and UPS, to achieve this crucial step towards widespread drone delivery. While this is a significant milestone, routine deliveries are still years away as regulatory and technical hurdles, such as autonomous flight standards and low-altitude air traffic systems, still need to be addressed.

title: Alphabet settles shareholder suit over sexual misconduct cases
summary: Alphabet Inc. has settled a shareholder lawsuit accusing it of mishandling sexual misconduct cases, agreeing to significant changes in its workplace policies. The company will prohibit severance for employees under sexual misconduct investigation, form a new diversity council including CEO Sundar Pichai, and invest $310 million over a decade in diversity initiatives. These measures aim to enhance transparency, increase oversight, and improve accountability regarding sexual misconduct and diversity efforts.

title: Mediaweek Roundup: Simon Reeve, Netflix, Dean Jones, ABC + more
summary: This Mediaweek Roundup covers several key media industry stories, including a coalition of smaller app companies forming to challenge Apple and Google's app store policies, former Seven Network presenter Simon Reeve suing the network for over $500,000, and a call for Netflix to contribute more to Australian content production. It also touches on celebrity manager Sam Mangan's "virtual" LA office, Peter V'landys suing ABC, and the passing of cricket legend Dean Jones.

title: This Is the Best Performing Stock of 2020
summary: Carrier Global Corp. (NYSE: CARR), a company in heating and refrigeration products, is identified as the best-performing stock of 2020 among S&P 500 companies, having risen 153% since going public on April 3rd. Despite a drop in revenue and earnings during Q2, the company's shares are performing well due to increased demand for its air quality and circulation products, driven by the COVID-19 pandemic. Carrier raised its full-year revenue and operating profit forecasts, signaling confidence in continued demand.

title: Google's $310 million sexual harassment settlement aims to set new industry standards
summary: Google's parent company Alphabet has agreed to a $310 million settlement regarding sexual misconduct and harassment, which includes over 80 policy updates aiming to set new industry standards. The settlement addresses gaps executives allegedly exploited and seeks to be a bellwether for Silicon Valley, particularly concerning NDAs and arbitration. The company plans to introduce new oversight, training, and accountability measures, with a focus on diversity, equity, and inclusion, and will formalize policies preventing severance for executives under investigation.

title: D-Wave Systems unveils new hardware, business model in race to commercialize quantum computing
summary: D-Wave Systems Inc. has unveiled a re-engineered quantum computer chip and a retooled business model, shifting from selling hardware to offering online access to its capabilities. The company is now focusing on practical applications for customers' immediate needs, promoting a hybrid computing model. This move aims to address past criticisms and demonstrate value beyond achieving "quantum supremacy," with applications being explored by companies like Save-On-Food, Menten AI, and Volkswagen.

title: Birthday week: Cloudflare turns 10
summary: Cloudflare celebrated its 10th birthday with a "Birthday Week" featuring several significant announcements. Key updates included advancements in their Workers platform with Durable Objects and Cron Triggers, a new privacy-focused Web Analytics product, and the launch of Cloudflare Radar for real-time internet traffic insights. The company also introduced API enhancements like gRPC support and API Shield, and Automatic Platform Optimization for improved website performance, starting with WordPress.

title: Google parent company to pay $310M to settle shareholder sex harassment suit
summary: Alphabet, Google's parent company, has agreed to pay $310 million to settle a shareholder lawsuit concerning alleged sexual harassment and misconduct. This settlement, deemed the largest of its kind for a shareholder derivative case related to sexual misconduct, will fund diversity, equity, and inclusion initiatives over ten years. Additionally, the agreement eliminates mandatory arbitration for harassment disputes within Alphabet companies and enforces new employment policies and training.

title: Apple pulls rival products from stores ahead of launch
summary: Apple Inc. has removed rival products from its retail and online stores ahead of the anticipated launch of its new iPhone, speakers, and headphones. This strategic move impacts brands like Bose Corp., Sonos Inc., and Logitech International SA, and is a recurring practice for Apple, previously seen when it launched the Apple Watch in 2014. The company stated this is part of its regular curation of third-party accessories to complement its own products.

title: Arm CEO Simon Segars discusses AI, data centers, getting acquired by Nvidia and more
summary: Arm CEO Simon Segars discusses the 2020 acquisition by Nvidia for $40 billion, highlighting the strategic alignment of both companies in AI and data centers. He emphasizes that the merger will accelerate Arm's trajectory into new markets like automotive and data centers, while also expanding their IP offerings. Segars addresses regulatory hurdles and concerns about licensing to Chinese companies, asserting that the deal is pro-competitive and will not alter Arm's licensing approach.

title: Customer Wins Power Bike After Ordering 1kg Milo Refill from Jumia
summary: A Lagos-based forex trader, Mr. Emeka Oscar Chukwumanjo, won a Suzuki Power Bike in a Jumia-Nestle raffle draw after purchasing a 1kg Milo Refill. Mr. Chukwumanjo, a frequent Jumia customer, expressed his surprise and delight at winning such a significant prize. The Head of Marketing at Jumia Nigeria, Ms. Olajumoke Bolu-Kujero, highlighted that this prize is one of many benefits customers receive when shopping on Jumia, emphasizing their partnerships with brands like Nestle to offer affordable products and incentives.

title: Enhancing Serverless Security with Check Point CloudGuard and AWS Lambda Extensions
summary: This article discusses how Check Point CloudGuard and AWS Lambda Extensions enhance serverless security. It highlights the inherent security improvements with serverless computing due to a minimal attack surface and shared responsibility model, while still emphasizing the need for robust visibility, posture management, and application security. The integration of CloudGuard with AWS Lambda Extensions enables deeper monitoring and protection of serverless functions by analyzing application activity, remediating posture issues, and providing customized defense strategies.

title: Pinched by Politics, XLC Still Merits Consideration
summary: The article discusses how political scrutiny on tech giants like Facebook and Alphabet, while a recurring theme, has not damaged the long-term prospects of the communication services sector and the Communication Services Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLC). XLC, being the largest ETF in this growth-oriented sector, continues to attract institutional investors, with its performance suggesting that political headwinds are often short-lived. The article also touches upon the potential for a less aggressive regulatory stance under a Biden administration, given Silicon Valley's support for some Democrats.

title: Damco Solutions added monday.com to its partnership pool to prioritize workplace transformation
summary: Damco Solutions Inc. has announced a partnership with monday.com, a SaaS-based collaboration and productivity platform, to help businesses create future-ready digital workplaces. This strategic alliance aims to simplify project management and supercharge workforces with custom workflows, easy collaboration, automation, real-time reporting, and integrations. The partnership leverages Damco's IT services expertise and monday.com's platform to drive transformational experiences for global teams, especially expanding monday.com's presence in North America.

title: Private equity giant Blackstone set to open tech office in Miami
summary: Private equity firm Blackstone plans to open a technology-focused headquarters in Miami, creating up to 215 tech jobs with an average salary of $200,000. Miami-Dade County will provide up to $650,000 in job incentives, anticipating $910,303 in new tax revenue. This move signifies Miami's growing appeal as a tech hub, attracting other companies like Google, Microsoft, and Softbank.

title: Ford to keep office workers at home through at least next June
summary: Ford Motor Co. has announced that its North American white-collar workers will continue to work from home through at least June of next year, extending a policy put in place at the start of the coronavirus pandemic. This decision mirrors similar extended remote work plans by other major companies like General Motors, Rocket Companies, Google, Facebook, and Amazon, as COVID-19 cases continue to rise across the U.S. By the time these policies expire, many employees will have been working remotely for approximately 15 months.

title: Foreign cloud service providers led by Amazon, MS play big in Korea
summary: Foreign cloud service providers, spearheaded by Amazon Web Services and Microsoft, are increasingly dominating South Korea's cloud computing market, capturing over half of it in 2019. Their aggressive expansion and investment in data centers in Korea are leading to higher growth rates compared to domestic providers. This trend is pushing local companies like Naver and Kakao to step up their own cloud infrastructure development and services.

title: These British Columbian billionaires are among the richest people in Canada
summary: CEOWORLD Magazine released its 2020 Canada Rich List Index, identifying the 46 wealthiest Canadians whose combined wealth reached a record high of $185.2 billion U.S. dollars. Several British Columbians made it into the top 20, including Google early investor David Cheriton, Lululemon founder Chip Wilson, business magnate Jim Pattison, beverage entrepreneur Anthony von Mandl, and Northland Properties founder Bob Gaglardi. The list highlights significant wealth growth for some individuals, particularly in the e-commerce sector.

title: Bandwidth to Acquire Voxbone, Propel Global Expansion
summary: Bandwidth announced its plan to acquire Voxbone for approximately $527 million, with the aim of expanding its global reach and creating a single cloud communications platform spanning over 60 countries. This acquisition is expected to accelerate Bandwidth's international expansion, leveraging Voxbone's strong presence in Europe and Asia, and enable extensive cross-selling opportunities and a simplified "one-stop shop" for cloud communication services. The deal reflects the increasing momentum in cloud communications, expedited by the pandemic, making time more valuable than money for market expansion.

title: Google adds new partners to its BeyondCorp Alliance
summary: Google has announced new partners for its BeyondCorp Alliance, an initiative designed to expand its "zero-trust" security model. With remote work becoming common, the alliance aims to help organizations embrace zero-trust security. The new partners include Citrix Inc., CrowdStrike Holdings Inc., Jamf Software LLC, and Tanium Inc., enhancing secure remote access, endpoint assessment, device management, and endpoint identity services.

title: Total and Google Cloud develop Solar Mapper, a tool for estimating the solar energy potential of houses’ roofs
summary: Total and Google Cloud have collaborated to develop "Solar Mapper," an AI-powered tool designed to accurately estimate the solar energy potential of residential roofs. This innovation aims to accelerate the deployment of solar panels for individuals, initially in Europe and globally thereafter. The tool leverages artificial intelligence to provide sharper estimations and broader geographical coverage, contributing to Total's goal of becoming a leader in renewable energies.

title: Apple Announces First 5G Smartphone, iPhone 12
summary: Apple has announced its first lineup of 5G-enabled smartphones, the iPhone 12 series, which includes four models: the iPhone 12, iPhone 12 Mini, iPhone 12 Pro, and iPhone 12 Pro Max. While these new phones support 5G technology for faster wireless speeds, the full benefits may not be immediately available to all users as 5G networks are still under construction in many regions. Aside from the phones, Apple also revealed a smaller, more affordable HomePod Mini smart speaker.

title: BBVA launches Aqua, the first card without numbers or a CVV
summary: BBVA has launched Aqua, a new line of credit cards in Spain that enhances security by featuring a dynamic CVV code and omitting printed card numbers or expiration dates. This innovation aims to prevent fraudulent use both online and physically. The associated BBVA app also provides renewed payment management, allowing customers to easily access card details and control expenses, with plans for a global rollout of this experience.

title: Augmented Reality (AR) Market Will Showcase Positive
summary: Technavio predicts that the Augmented Reality (AR) market is poised to grow by USD 76.99 billion during 2020-2024, driven significantly by the adoption of AR-enabled smart glasses. The market is concentrated with major players like Alphabet Inc. and Facebook Inc., and is expected to decelerate in concentration over the forecast period. The report highlights the increasing popularity of AR in smartphones and tablets as a key growth driver, offering detailed market analysis and segmentation.

title: Free Apple 5G iPhones are offered by carriers to lure upgraders
summary: US carriers such as AT&T and Verizon are offering free Apple iPhone 12 devices to new and existing customers to attract subscribers during the 5G upgrade cycle. These promotions require qualifying trade-ins and unlimited plans. The carriers are gambling that by covering the phone cost, subscribers will sign up for higher-priced unlimited data plans, despite potential economic headwinds and initial limited 5G network speeds.

title: How to Switch from AWS EBS to Cloud Volumes ONTAP for LVM Storage
summary: This article explains how to migrate LVM storage from AWS EBS to Cloud Volumes ONTAP with zero downtime. It provides an overview of LVM, Cloud Volumes ONTAP, and a practical demonstration of the migration process using iSCSI. The article highlights the benefits of using Cloud Volumes ONTAP for data management, including advanced features like snapshots, data compression, and high availability.

title: Zoom opens marketplace to apps that run within its platform
summary: Zoom is expanding its platform by opening a new marketplace for "Zapps," which are third-party applications deeply integrated into its video conferencing service. This initiative allows users to access collaboration, productivity, and education tools directly within Zoom, enhancing functionality and offering a best-of-breed approach. Additionally, Zoom introduced OnZoom, an event-hosting software, and announced SDK enhancements and broader hardware support.

title: Fisker closes deal for supplier Magna to build its SUV, take stake in startup
summary: Fisker Inc. announced a deal with Magna International Inc. for Magna to supply the vehicle platform and build its Ocean SUV, with Magna also receiving warrants for up to a 6% stake in Fisker. This partnership marks Magna's first entry into contract manufacturing for an EV startup and is seen as critical for Fisker's future, targeting significant sales volumes for the Ocean SUV starting in 2022. Fisker's merger with Spartan Energy Acquisition Corp. is expected to close on Oct. 30, with shares trading as "FSR" on the NYSE.

title: What’s up with… Juniper Networks, Telefónica, Nokia
summary: Juniper Networks acquired 128 Technology for $450 million to enhance its automated, AI-enabled enterprise services platform. Telefónica is reportedly close to forming a €5 billion fiberoptic joint venture with Allianz's private equity arm for a German FTTX rollout. Nokia has been selected by NASA to build the first-ever cellular network on the Moon as part of the 'Tipping Point' technologies initiative.

title: Chrome Enterprise Recommended Program Includes Palo Alto Networks App
summary: Palo Alto Networks announced that its GlobalProtect App has been included in Google's Chrome Enterprise Recommended program. This designation highlights their commitment to providing world-class network security for Chrome OS users, enabling secure remote access, consistent policy enforcement, and visibility into users and applications. The app offers features like zero-touch provisioning, always-on security, seamless access, and enhanced troubleshooting for Chrome OS devices.

title: MongoDB Atlas now enables multi-cloud database clusters
summary: MongoDB has enhanced its Atlas cloud database service to support multi-cloud clusters, allowing databases to run simultaneously across AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure. This new capability addresses customer demand for data portability across different cloud providers, enabling features like live replication and proximity-based query routing for improved performance and compliance. The change shifts from running separate applications on different clouds to truly integrated, distributed databases across multiple cloud environments.

title: A lot more goes into good smartphone haptics than you'd think
summary: This article delves into the intricacies of smartphone haptics, explaining the technology behind the vibrations and tactile feedback users experience. It distinguishes between older eccentric rotating mass (ERM) motors and modern linear resonant actuators (LRAs), highlighting how LRAs provide crisper and more precise sensations. The piece also emphasizes the crucial role of software, like those developed by Cirrus Logic, in controlling and enhancing haptic performance, even suggesting that Apple's Taptic Engine sets the benchmark for superior haptic feedback in mobile devices.

title: Expedia Group CEO on Google antitrust case: 'Very pleased to see the government finally taking action'
summary: Expedia Group CEO Peter Kern expressed satisfaction with the U.S. Justice Department's antitrust complaint against Google, hoping it will lead to a fairer marketplace for online travel companies. Kern stated that Expedia has "no axe to grind against Google" but believes the current market is not equitable, pointing out Google's dual role as a search platform and competitor. He emphasized that Expedia's goal is merely "a fair fight" in the industry.

title: Apple, Google Worked as ‘One Company’ on Search Deal, U.S. Says
summary: The U.S. Justice Department has filed an antitrust lawsuit against Alphabet Inc.'s Google, accusing it of abusing its monopoly in search through a multibillion-dollar deal with Apple Inc. This agreement makes Google the default search engine on iPhones and other Apple devices. Documents from Google reportedly describe the potential loss of this deal as a "Code Red."

title: Protecting the Great Barrier Reef
summary: HSBC and the Queensland government are jointly investing in Reef Credits to improve water quality around the Great Barrier Reef, a vital ecosystem threatened by climate change and pollution. This initiative, part of HSBC's broader sustainable finance goals, aims to reduce sediment, nutrients, and contaminants by compensating farmers for implementing better management practices. The partnership highlights a collaborative effort between the public and private sectors to safeguard this natural wonder and its significant economic contributions.

title: TripAdvisor CEO says Google uses its 'dominance in internet gatekeeping' against travel sites
summary: TripAdvisor CEO Stephen Kaufer supports the Department of Justice's antitrust lawsuit against Google, echoing sentiments from Expedia's CEO. Kaufer argues that Google leverages its internet dominance to disadvantage other businesses, specifically in the travel sector, by preferentially ranking its own travel services in search results. This practice has reportedly hurt the ability of online booking sites like TripAdvisor, Expedia, and Booking Holdings to drive organic traffic and has forced them to increase advertising spending.

title: SanDisk IXpand Wireless Charger Sync Can Also Backup Smartphone Data
summary: SanDisk, a Western Digital company, has introduced two new wireless charging accessories: the SanDisk Ixpand Wireless Charger Sync and the Ixpand Wireless Charger 15W. The "Sync" model offers integrated data backup for contacts, photos, and videos while charging, available in up to 256GB, ideal for users without microSD slots. The 15W model provides traditional fast wireless charging without the backup feature; both include safety features and come with a 2-year warranty, with the Sync starting at $99.99 and the 15W at $49.99.

title: Microsoft's SpaceX partnership sends Azure to the final frontier
summary: Microsoft has launched its Azure Space initiative, partnering with SpaceX to integrate Azure with low-orbiting satellites and introduce a new Azure Modular Datacenter (MDC). This move positions Microsoft to compete in the space and satellite segment of the IaaS market, particularly targeting telecommunications, government, and energy industries. The venture will put Microsoft head-to-head with AWS, which already has similar cloud-based space offerings, requiring both companies to address the persistent issue of latency in satellite communications.

title: ExxonMobil Deploys QR Codes And NFC Tags for Streamlined Mobile Payment at the Pump
summary: ExxonMobil is implementing QR codes and NFC tags at over 11,500 U.S. stations to enable streamlined mobile payments with Apple Pay and Google Pay. This system leverages Apple App Clips for iPhone users without the ExxonMobil app and provides a web-based solution for Android users, enhancing contactless payment options at the pump. The initiative is part of ExxonMobil's ongoing efforts to innovate and offer secure, convenient payment methods, building on prior contactless payment solutions like "Alexa, Pay for Gas."

title: AT&T Has The Most Disappointing Big Company Stock This Year
summary: AT&T Inc. (NYSE: T) has recorded the worst stock performance among large-cap companies this year, dropping 27% while the S&P 500 gained 7%. This decline is significant compared to top companies like Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, and Facebook, which have seen substantial gains. The company also reported a 5% fall in operating revenue and a 22% drop in EPS, coupled with massive long-term debt, despite an impressive dividend yield.

title: How to invest in the S&P 500 without betting hard on the ‘FAAMG’ stocks that are 20% of the index
summary: This article discusses a strategy to invest in the S&P 500 without being overly exposed to the "FAAMG" stocks (Facebook, Apple, Amazon.com, Microsoft, and Google/Alphabet) which collectively represent 20% of the index's valuation. It suggests that when investing in a typical S&P 500 index fund, one is inherently making a significant bet on the continued success of these five dominant companies. The piece broadly hints at an "equal-weight S&P 500 ETF" as a potential solution for investors seeking diversification away from these outsized positions.

title: Apple, Google and a Deal That Controls the Internet (Published 2020)
summary: The Justice Department has filed a landmark antitrust lawsuit against Google, targeting a secretive partnership with Apple worth billions where Google's search engine is the preselected choice on Apple devices. This alliance, seen as "co-opetition" by former Apple counsel, is now under scrutiny for potentially stifling competition and preventing smaller companies from flourishing. The lawsuit highlights the complex relationship between the two tech giants and their role in controlling web search.

title: Microsoft Tunnel Makes Connecting to Corporate Apps Easier from Android and iOS
summary: Microsoft Tunnel is a new VPN gateway solution for Intune, announced at Ignite in September 2020, designed to make connecting to on-premises corporate resources easier from Android and iOS devices. Differentiating itself from existing VPN solutions, it integrates fully with Microsoft 365, supporting single sign-on and Azure Active Directory Conditional Access policies. The solution aims to be enterprise-ready with simple deployment, automatic updates, and an app for users, although always-on VPN is limited to Android due to iOS restrictions.

title: Facebook, Google and Microsoft 'avoiding $3bn in tax in poorer nations'
summary: ActionAid estimates that Google, Facebook, and Microsoft are avoiding up to $2.8bn (£2.2bn) in tax revenue in developing nations, a sum that could significantly boost public services like healthcare and education. The charity is advocating for a new global tax system, ideally under the United Nations, requiring large corporations to pay a minimum tax rate based on their "real economic presence." This initiative highlights long-standing concerns about tech giants' tax contributions and their impact on global south countries, especially as these companies have seen soaring revenues during the pandemic.

title: Waymo, Daimler to partner in developing self-driving semi trucks
summary: Daimler AG's commercial truck unit and Alphabet Inc's Waymo announced a partnership to develop self-driving Class 8 semi trucks, integrating Waymo's automated system into Daimler's Freightliner Cascadia. This collaboration aims to accelerate the deployment of automated heavy-duty trucks, a market where several companies are competing to reduce reliance on human drivers. Despite the partnership, Daimler will continue its in-house development of robotic truck drivers, offering a dual-strategy approach for its customers.

title: Daimler and Waymo partner on self-driving trucks
summary: Daimler, parent company to Mercedes-Benz and a leading truck manufacturer, has partnered with Alphabet Inc.'s Waymo to integrate Waymo's Level 4 self-driving system into Freightliner Cascadia Class 8 semi-trailer trucks for the U.S. market. Despite the partnership, Daimler will continue developing its own self-driving technology, adopting a "dual-strategy approach" to accelerate the deployment of autonomous trucking solutions. The initiative aims to offer Waymo Driver-equipped Cascadias to customers in the U.S. in the coming years, with potential expansion to other markets, while acknowledging the complex demands self-driving technology faces in heavy-duty commercial vehicles.

title: Rackspace Technology opens new Singapore office
summary: Rackspace Technology has opened a new 4,876-square-foot office in Singapore's Central Business District, quadrupling its previous office size and anticipating a 25% increase in headcount. This expansion is part of the company's continued investment in the APAC region and its strategy to enhance digitization plans for businesses globally, especially for its cloud solutions following its IPO. The new office will serve as a base for expansion into ASEAN markets, focusing on helping businesses leverage cloud technology for efficiency, productivity, and cost optimization.

title: Entertainment and Media Market to Witness Huge Growth by 2026 | Warner Media, Viacom, Alphabet
summary: A new research study by HTF MI titled "Global Entertainment and Media Market Report 2020" predicts significant growth in the entertainment and media sector by 2026. The report evaluates market trends, drivers, and investment structures, covering key players like Viacom, Alphabet, and Warner Media. It provides forecasts based on segments like product types (Amusement Park/Facilities, Animation, Films) and applications (Wire, Wireless) across various regions.

title: Marvell to buy Inphi in $10bn semiconductor deal
summary: Semiconductor company Marvell Technology Group is set to acquire Inphi Corp in a $10 billion cash-and-stock deal. The acquisition aims to strengthen Marvell's leadership in cloud infrastructure and expand its 5G presence, leveraging Inphi's expertise in fiber-optic data traffic and its customer base including Amazon, Google, Microsoft, and Facebook. This move is part of a broader trend of consolidation within the semiconductor industry.

title: A Look Behind the Vimeo Brand
summary: This article explores Vimeo's unique position in the crowded video platform market, highlighting its focus on community, storytelling tools, and value proposition compared to competitors like YouTube. Author Bryan Elliott shares insights from his professional experience and an interview with Vimeo CMO Harris Beber, discussing Vimeo's features, OTT capabilities, and a new service connecting creators with video professionals. The piece also delves into the author's personal journey in content creation, including his early experiences in the entertainment industry and the inspiration behind his career path, concluding that now is an optimal time for video storytelling.

title: Analysis: In an epic pivot to the cloud, Microsoft makes Azure the linchpin of its future
summary: Microsoft's Azure cloud computing service is a central component of the company's innovation strategy, driving significant revenue growth and serving as a key differentiator from competitors focused on advertising. The company's overall financial performance is strong, with impressive growth across its three main business segments: Productivity and Business Process, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing. Microsoft's successful pivot to the cloud and its developer-centric approach have made it a leader in the tech industry, demonstrating remarkable spending momentum among its customers despite its large size.

title: Mukesh Ambani versus Jeff Bezos: A fight or a waiting game?
summary: The article details the struggle between Mukesh Ambani and Jeff Bezos for dominance in the Indian consumer market. This centers around Amazon's attempt to block Reliance Industries' $3.4 billion acquisition of Future Group assets, stemming from a previous agreement where Amazon had rights to acquire shares in Future Retail and a non-compete clause with Reliance. The dispute highlights potential issues for foreign investors in India and questions whether Amazon prefers rivalry or a sweeter deal with Ambani.

title: IndianoriginCEOs
summary: This article highlights 13 individuals of Indian origin who hold significant leadership positions in global IT companies. It showcases their roles, companies, and key achievements, underscoring the growing presence and influence of Indian-origin executives in the international tech industry.

title: Smart Offers: Sabre Partners With Google on AI-Powered Personalized Travel Tech
summary: Sabre, in partnership with Google, is launching an AI-powered "Smart Retail Engine" in early 2021 to offer personalized travel options. This technology aims to customize offerings for travelers, increase satisfaction, and boost industry revenue by leveraging AI and machine learning. The partnership seeks to transform customer experience and pricing in the travel sector.

title: Toyota-backed startup Pony.ai raises $267 mln in latest fundraising
summary: Pony.ai, a self-driving startup backed by Toyota, announced it raised $267 million in the initial phase of its latest fundraising round, valuing the company at $5.3 billion. This investment, led by Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan Board, aims to boost its presence in the United States and China and explore mobility services with Toyota. The company plans to use the funds for technology development and fleet expansion, including autonomous trucks.

title: Nest Wifi vs. Ubiquiti AmpliFi HD: Which should you buy?
summary: This article compares Google's Nest Wifi and Ubiquiti AmpliFi HD mesh Wi-Fi systems, detailing their strengths, weaknesses, and key differences. While Nest Wifi offers Google Assistant integration and WPA3 support, AmpliFi HD excels in coverage, QoS options, wired backhaul, and a free VPN solution. The article concludes that AmpliFi HD is generally the superior product due to its broader feature set and performance advantages.

title: Prisma Access: SASE Architected for Unprecedented Security and Scale
summary: Palo Alto Networks' Prisma Access service, combined with CloudGenix SD-WAN, offers a comprehensive SASE platform designed for unprecedented security and scale. Leveraging cloud-native architecture on AWS and Google Cloud, it provides extensive global coverage and ultra-fast security processing, proven by its ability to support massive increases in remote workers during the COVID-19 pandemic. The service has demonstrated rapid scalability, enabling major organizations like PwC, Schlumberger, and Flex to transition significant portions of their workforce to remote operations without disruption.

title: Google parent Alphabet turns to cat bonds for earthquake insurance
summary: Alphabet, Google's parent company, has entered the catastrophe bond market for the first time, seeking $237.5 million in earthquake insurance protection. This is facilitated through a Phoenician Re Ltd. cat bond transaction with capital market investors. The move highlights how major tech companies are utilizing the insurance-linked securities (ILS) market for efficient capacity to manage significant catastrophe exposures like California earthquakes.

title: 10 Websites to Make $100 per Day Working From Home (Without Investment!)
summary: This article lists ten websites that can help individuals earn $100 per day working from home without an upfront investment. It covers various online opportunities like freelancing, affiliate marketing, content creation, and online tutoring, detailing how each platform works and payment methods. The goal is to provide readers with diverse options to supplement their income or make a full-time living online.

title: Buy now! COVID-19 sparks Southeast Asian e-commerce boom
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic has significantly accelerated e-commerce growth in Southeast Asia, with spending expected to triple to over $300 billion by 2025. While online travel and transport were hit, overall digital adoption surged, bringing 40 million new internet users online in the region in 2020. Indonesia's digital economy is also projected to nearly triple despite the wider economic downturn.

title: Yelp CEO is encouraged by antitrust case against Google
summary: Yelp CEO Jeremy Stoppelman expressed encouragement regarding the U.S. antitrust case against Google, stating that it validates his long-held belief in Google's monopoly in internet search. Stoppelman alleges that Google abuses its dominant position by prioritizing its own content, harming competition and consumers. Despite initial pandemic-related challenges, Yelp reported better-than-expected sales in the third quarter and anticipates further improvement with a vaccine rollout.

title: How Microsoft and Sony’s new consoles improve game technology
summary: Penn professors and lecturers discuss the technological advancements in the new PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X consoles. Key improvements include solid-state hard drives (SSDs) for faster loading times and hardware-based ray tracing for photo-realistic graphics. The article also touches on the potential impact of streaming services on the gaming industry.

title: The Snowflake Story
summary: Snowflake Inc., founded in 2012, is a cloud-based data-warehousing company that came out of stealth mode in 2014. The company offers a data warehouse-as-a-service, running on major cloud platforms and enabling data storage and analytics for corporate users. Snowflake had a historic IPO on September 16, 2020, with shares more than doubling in value, leading to a $70.4 billion market valuation on its first day of trading.

title: Amazon shifts some voice assistant, face recognition computing to its own chips
summary: Amazon is transitioning some of the computing for its Alexa voice assistant and Rekognition facial recognition service to its custom-designed "Inferentia" chips. This strategic move aims to improve speed and reduce costs by moving away from third-party chip providers like Nvidia. The company reports a 25% improvement in latency and 30% lower costs for Alexa's text-to-speech tasks with the new chips.

title: Apple, Google, and LG Start Working on 6G Technology
summary: Apple, Google, and LG have joined the Next G Alliance, a group focused on developing sixth-generation (6G) communication technology. Established in October by ATIS, the Alliance aims to position North America at the forefront of 6G innovation, even as 5G technology has yet to become mainstream. The group is working towards making 6G a reality potentially ahead of Samsung's 2028 estimate.

title: Why Google, Amazon, and Nvidia are all building AI notetakers for doctors
summary: Google, Amazon, and Nvidia are developing AI-powered notetaking tools for doctors to address the time-consuming and often inaccurate process of medical transcription. These tools aim to improve the efficiency and accuracy of recording patient interactions and medical records, moving beyond existing methods that doctors find cumbersome or overly generalized. While some solutions are already available, tech giants are focusing on delivering more precise and sophisticated AI to streamline healthcare documentation.
