title: Behind the Scenes at the John Deere Horicon Works Factory
summary: Wayne Southall, a factory manager at John Deere's Horicon Works, discusses the company's journey in the riding lawn equipment market, including successes, challenges, and lessons learned over his 20-year career. The article highlights product development, such as the airless Tweel tire, the missteps with the SpinSteer mower, and how the company adapted to changes like the mass market entry and the COVID-19 pandemic's impact on supply chains. Southall emphasizes John Deere's continuous efforts to innovate and maintain flexibility in manufacturing.

title: Home Depot names company vet to CIO role
summary: Home Depot has announced the appointment of Matt Carey as the new executive vice president of customer experience and Fahim Siddiqui as the new executive vice president and chief information officer. Carey will lead strategies to enhance customer experience in stores and digital channels, while Siddiqui will manage digital strategy, infrastructure, and software development. Both promotions highlight Home Depot's focus on internal talent and technology to improve customer interaction and differentiate itself in the home improvement market.

title: Tractor Supply Makes the Case for Investing in BIPOC, LGBTQ and Women Farmers
summary: Tractor Supply Co. is increasing its focus on ESG initiatives, including reducing its carbon footprint and boosting diversity. Through its foundation, it partners with the American Farmland Trust to support small farmers, particularly women, BIPOC, and LGBTQ individuals, providing grants and aiming to improve their viability and resilience in the face of various challenges. This initiative addresses the struggles faced by these farmers, such as declining farm numbers, low-profit margins, and historical inequities.

title: The Home Depot Awards 30 HBCUs Retool Your School Campus Improvement Grants
summary: The Home Depot is investing an additional $1 million in its Retool Your School program, providing grants to 30 Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs) for campus improvements. This marks the 13th year of the program, which has supported almost 70 percent of the nation's HBCUs with over 180 grants totaling more than $5 million since its launch in 2009. Alabama State University was awarded Campaign of the Year, alongside grants for the 30 winning institutions.

title: RBC, CIBC to lend Elon Musk $1.5 billion for Twitter takeover
summary: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) and Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce (CIBC) have pledged a combined $1.5 billion to help finance Elon Musk's $56-billion bid to acquire Twitter. This contribution is part of a larger $32.5 billion financing package from 12 banks, with RBC providing $956.5 million and CIBC contributing $510 million. The article also touches on other recent financing deals, including increased investment by The Home Depot Canada Foundation for youth homelessness, funding for QuadFi to offer personal loans to underserved groups, and Mavrck's acquisition of Later.

title: Home Depot Canada Foundation Increases Investment To $125 Million In Support Of Youth Experiencing Homelessness
summary: The Home Depot Canada Foundation is increasing its investment to combat youth homelessness to $125 million by 2030, exceeding its initial $50 million pledge. This renewed commitment will focus on expanding stable housing, providing community support, and increasing youth employment readiness through various grants and strategic partnerships. The funding will emphasize an equity framework, significantly supporting organizations that assist underrepresented youth, and will also boost the TradeWorx program to provide skilled trades training.

title: The Home Depot Announces $150 Million Venture Capital Fund to Fuel Innovation in Retail and Home Improvement
summary: The Home Depot has launched Home Depot Ventures, a $150 million venture capital fund aimed at investing in early-stage companies to foster innovation in retail and home improvement. The fund will support technologies that enhance customer experience, improve associate efficiency, and drive operational excellence, building on the company's history of successful startup investments like Afero and Loadsmart. These investments are intended to create a seamless interconnected shopping experience and strengthen Home Depot's market position.

title: This Company’s Earnings Have Bad News for Home Depot and Lowe’s Stock
summary: Emerson Electric reported better-than-expected earnings, but its results contained a warning for investors in Home Depot and Lowe's. The industrial company's performance, coupled with higher prices, suggests potential negative impacts on retail demand for home improvement stores. This could imply a challenging outlook for Home Depot and Lowe's stock.

title: Home Depot Kids Workshops Return to Stores
summary: The Home Depot is bringing back its in-store Kids Workshops starting May 7, 2022, after shifting to virtual offerings in 2020 due to safety concerns. These workshops will occur on the first Saturday of each month, featuring seasonal-themed DIY projects like a Picket Fence Planter, and aim to foster creativity and learning in children. Participants will receive an apron, a collectible pin, and a certificate, continuing a 25-year tradition of community engagement.

title: Neo Financial Announces $185 Million Series C Raise at a Unicorn Valuation
summary: Neo Financial, a Canadian fintech company, announced a $185 million Series C fundraising round, valuing the company at over $1 billion. This brings their total funding to $299 million. The company has grown to over 1 million customers since its 2019 inception and plans to use the new funding to expand its product offerings, including a mortgage product, and strengthen its presence across Canada.

title: Urban Edge grows food, wellness offerings with new leases at Bergen Town Center
summary: Urban Edge Properties is enhancing its Bergen Town Center property in Paramus with new leases for diverse tenants, including Kohl's, Chick’n Cone, Ani Ramen, V/O Med Spa, and Pandora Jewelry. These additions, alongside ongoing renovations to improve walkability and light, aim to provide a high-quality retail experience. Hackensack Meridian Health is also establishing an 80,000-square-foot medical office facility at the center.

title: New TA Express franchise opens today off I-45 in Fairfield, Texas
summary: TravelCenters of America Inc. has opened a new franchised TA Express travel center in Fairfield, Texas, located off Interstate 45, exit 198. The 17,000-square-foot facility offers various amenities for professional drivers and motorists, including dining options, truck parking, fueling positions, showers, and laundry facilities. This opening expands TA's nationwide network to 276 sites, strategically serving a key route between Dallas and Houston.

title: Duke Realty Rejects Nearly $24 Billion Buyout Offer From Prologis
summary: Duke Realty Corp. has rejected a nearly $24 billion buyout offer from warehousing giant Prologis Inc., deeming the unsolicited proposal insufficient. Prologis made its all-stock offer public after more than five months of private overtures. The acquisition would have significantly expanded Prologis's industrial real estate footprint, which already includes over 1 billion square feet used by major e-commerce companies.

title: Home Depot busts woman for half-dozen thefts at 4 Palm Beach County store locations
summary: A woman identified as Maria Matias was arrested after Home Depot loss prevention officers and the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office linked her to six separate thefts across four different store locations in Palm Beach County. The incidents, documented through video surveillance and fraudulent returns/purchases, involved Matias illicitly obtaining various items including door kits, ceiling fans, and seasonal decorations, often by using fake receipts or manipulating returns. Matias faces multiple charges including organized fraud and retail theft, and was released on bail after spending time in jail.

title: Home Depot's Stock Is Down, but It's Not Cheap
summary: Despite a significant drop from its December high, Home Depot's stock is still considered pricey by Morningstar analysts, trading at a premium to its fair value estimate. The retailer faces pressure from inflation, rising interest rates, and a shift in consumer spending toward travel, making its outlook challenging for 2022. Alternative home improvement stocks like Lowe's, Restoration Hardware, and Williams-Sonoma offer more compelling valuations.

title: Home Depot Sees Record First-Quarter Sales. The Stock Is Rising.
summary: Home Depot reported record first-quarter sales, exceeding expectations. This positive financial performance led to an increase in the company's stock value. The article highlights the strong sales figures for the quarter.

title: Home Depot raises annual profit forecast as demand holds up
summary: Home Depot Inc increased its full-year profit forecast and reported a surprise increase in quarterly same-store sales, driven by higher prices and steady demand for tools and building materials, particularly from home-improvement professionals. The company's shares rose 4% following the announcement, as it expects comparable sales to increase about 3% in fiscal 2022. This positive outlook helps allay concerns about easing consumer spending, with earnings per share also beating estimates.

title: Walmart: Profits dragged down by inflation, supply chain woes
summary: Walmart reported stronger sales in its fiscal first quarter but saw its profits decline due to surging inflation, particularly in food and fuel, and higher costs from global supply chain disruptions. The company subsequently cut its full-year earnings forecast, leading to an over 8 percent drop in shares. CEO Doug McMillon noted that inflation created more pressure on margin mix and operating costs than anticipated, despite overall sales holding up as shoppers shifted to lower-priced items and private brands.

title: After decades of producing chemicals, Westlake makes a material shift
summary: Westlake Corp., a Houston-based chemical and materials manufacturer, has undergone a significant transformation, shedding the word "chemical" from its name to reflect its expansion into material manufacturing. Following a series of nearly $4 billion in acquisitions since 2020, the company is now earning record profits, with revenue increasing by over 70 percent in the first quarter of 2022. CEO Albert Chao discusses the company's growth strategy, its move closer to consumer products in the housing and construction sectors, and its commitment to sustainability and emission reduction.

title: Home Depot raises full-year forecasts as demand stays firm
summary: Home Depot Inc. raised its annual profit and sales forecasts, easing concerns about demand despite surging inflation. The company's first-quarter comparable sales increased, driven by professional home-improvement demand and higher sales in certain categories, indicating favorable underlying housing metrics. This forecast raise was seen as "unexpected" by some analysts given the volatile economic environment.

title: After heightened demand during the pandemic, growth at Home Depot and Lowe's begins to normalize
summary: Following two years of elevated sales during the pandemic, growth in the home improvement sector is normalizing. Home Depot reported increased net sales and operating income for Q1, outperforming Lowe's, largely due to strong performance from its Pro customers. Lowe's experienced a slight decline in sales and comps, attributed to a cooler spring and its larger DIY customer base, prompting expectations of more subdued growth for the retailer.

title: Dramatic shift in sales mix leaves Target overloaded with inventory
summary: Target is grappling with an oversupply of inventory, particularly in large home goods categories like kitchen appliances and outdoor furniture, due to an unexpected shift in consumer spending habits. Following the end of federal stimulus payouts, shoppers moved away from major home makeovers and are now prioritizing smaller decor items, essentials, and experiences. To address this, Target plans to cut prices and right-size its assortments, anticipating global supply chain issues to persist until early 2023.

title: Target earnings fall short as supply chain struggles persist
summary: Target Corp. reported a significant miss on Q1 2022 earnings, with net profit more than halving despite strong comparable sales growth. The shortfall was attributed to higher-than-expected freight and transportation costs, excess inventory, and a dramatic shift in consumer spending away from discretionary goods. This mirrors similar struggles faced by competitor Walmart, highlighting the ongoing challenges for big box retailers amid supply chain disruptions and changing consumer habits.

title: Lowes vs Home Depot – Which Store is Better?
summary: This article compares Lowe's and Home Depot across various aspects like company size, customer service, power tool brands, and building materials, aiming to determine which store is "better." While acknowledging that both are strong contenders in the home improvement market, the authors provide insights based on their experience and polling, concluding that the preference often comes down to specific needs, brand loyalty, and the quality of local store employees. The comparison highlights their respective strengths and offers guidance for both Pros and DIYers.

title: Our Ultimate Stock-Pickers' Top 10 High-Conviction Purchases
summary: The article highlights the top 10 high-conviction purchases by Morningstar's Ultimate Stock-Pickers, focusing on significant additions to portfolios. Despite market volatility and inflation in early 2022, managers found value across various sectors, with Sherwin-Williams, T-Mobile, and Home Depot being particularly notable. Many of these high-conviction and new-money purchases received positive economic moat ratings from Morningstar analysts.

title: Sherwin-Williams Co. stock underperforms Tuesday when compared to competitors
summary: Shares of Sherwin-Williams Co. (SHW) dropped 3.01% on Tuesday, closing at $268.04, underperforming the broader market and its competitors. This decline ended a three-day winning streak for the company, which is currently $86.11 below its 52-week high. Competitors like Home Depot Inc., PPG Industries Inc., and Masco Corp. also saw declines but generally fell less than Sherwin-Williams.

title: Suspect in San Jose Home Depot Fire Appears in Court
summary: Dillyn Jaycruz Gogue, accused of intentionally setting a Home Depot store on fire in San Jose on April 9, appeared in court to face numerous charges including arson. His public defender indicated a conflict in representing him, likely due to other alleged crimes like thefts on the same day. Gogue is expected back in court on June 29 to determine if an alternate defender's office can take the case.

title: Walmart is using its thousands of stores to battle Amazon for e-commerce market share
summary: Walmart is leveraging its extensive network of nearly 4,700 stores across the U.S. as "shoppable fulfillment centers" to boost its e-commerce market share and compete with Amazon. The retailer is transforming its physical locations into hubs for drone deliveries, automated online grocery order fulfillment, and direct-to-fridge drop-offs, aiming to provide faster and more efficient service. This strategy also involves wooing third-party sellers by offering fulfillment services from its stores and expanding its delivery and membership programs like GoLocal and Walmart+.

title: Home Improvement Market Size & Share | North America, Europe, & APAC Industry Forecasts 2027: Graphical Research
summary: The global home improvement market is projected to grow significantly through 2027, driven by homeowners seeking to enhance comfort, style, and value, particularly influenced by the COVID-19 pandemic's impact on living spaces. Key trends include the rise of DIY projects in APAC, increasing renovations across the region, and a surge in DIFM projects and exterior replacements in North America. Europe is also seeing momentum in property and kitchen upgrades due to an aging housing stock and demand for smart home technologies.

title: Beyond the distribution center
summary: The article discusses how evolving customer demands and e-commerce growth are pushing retailers to rethink traditional distribution center models. It introduces three new fulfillment horizons: within the store, around the store, and in the neighborhood (Q-commerce), detailing how retailers are using existing assets, strategic partnerships, and rapid delivery services to meet modern customer expectations for speed and agility. The authors urge retailers to act quickly, invest in future-proof models, and foster cross-functional and external partnerships to stay competitive.

title: Home Depot Upgrades 2.3K Retail Edge Locations Using SUSE Rancher, K3s
summary: Home Depot has transitioned its 2,300+ retail locations to a new architecture leveraging SUSE's Rancher and K3s technology. This shift aims to automate the maintenance of containerized applications at edge locations, eliminating the manual effort previously required. The K3s, a lightweight Kubernetes version, combined with Rancher's management capabilities, enables efficient deployment; updates of operating systems and Kubernetes layers; and management of thousands of remote clusters with limited IT resources.

title: Hold the Presses: H-E-B Grocery Store Not Yet Coming to Fort Worth at Parkside at Alliance Town Center
summary: News that H-E-B would anchor the Parkside at Alliance Town Center in Fort Worth was prematurely announced. While Hillwood initially indicated an H-E-B as the anchor, public relations officials later clarified that the grocery store has not yet agreed to build there. However, four other dining and retail concepts — Torchy’s Tacos, CAVA, Black Rifle Coffee Company, and Dash Nail Spa — are confirmed and under construction, with planned openings for early 2023.

title: Home Depot Wins Suit Prohibiting Employees From Wearing BLM Logos
summary: A judge has ruled in favor of Home Depot, prohibiting its employees from wearing Black Lives Matter apparel while on the job. The administrative law judge stated that the BLM message does not meet the requirements for legal protection as it primarily addresses the unjustified killings of Black individuals and acts as a political umbrella for social concerns. This decision follows a complaint by the US National Labor Relations Board against Home Depot for allegedly interfering with employees' rights by banning BLM messaging on aprons.

title: 8 Money-Saving Secrets Home Depot Employees Want You to Know
summary: This article reveals eight money-saving secrets when shopping at Home Depot, directly from employee insights. Key tips include returning dead plants within a year, renting expensive tools instead of buying, and utilizing free DIY workshops. Additionally, shoppers can find deeply discounted cull lumber and "mistake paint," check online for coupons, time purchases during major sales, and benefit from their 110% price match guarantee.

title: Home Depot, Costco and 3 More Retail Stocks to Buy
summary: The article identifies five retail stocks poised for success despite recent declines in retail sales. It highlights companies like Home Depot, Costco, AutoZone, Academy Sports + Outdoors, and Dollar General, explaining why each is a promising investment opportunity in the current economic climate.

title: How Home Depot’s Pro Xtra Program Alone Helped Me Save $1,400 This Year
summary: The author details how Home Depot's Pro Xtra program helped him save $1,400 this year through perks, coupons, and special offers, highlighting that individuals don't need to be licensed contractors or business owners to sign up. The article also suggests exploring similar discount programs at other retailers and leveraging small business status for additional savings. It emphasizes asking for volume discounts and considering licensing for industry-specific benefits.

title: $210M loan secured for Inland Empire industrial development
summary: JLL Capital Markets has arranged a $210 million construction loan for the first phase of Ontario Ranch Business Park, a 1.68-million-square-foot industrial development in California's Inland Empire. The project, a joint venture between Real Estate Development Associates, LLC and Clarion Partners, LLC, will include seven buildings, with its largest preleased to The Home Depot. The Inland Empire industrial market is experiencing extremely low vacancy rates, indicating strong demand.

title: The Home Depot Adopts HPE GreenLake for Aruba Networking and Aruba ESP to Drive Enhanced Customer and Associate Experiences
summary: The Home Depot has selected Aruba ESP delivered via HPE GreenLake for Aruba networking to enhance customer and associate experiences across its U.S. stores. This partnership aims to provide a solid network foundation with speed, scale, and flexibility, supporting interconnected capabilities and streamlining IT management. The technology investment will enable features like in-store navigation and easy product look-up for associates, improving the overall retail experience.

title: Home Depot Refreshes Tech To Boost Customer Service
summary: Home Depot is partnering with Aruba, a Hewlett Packard Enterprise company, to enhance in-store connectivity and improve customer and employee experiences. They are implementing Aruba ESP via HPE GreenLake for Aruba networking, and Zebra Technologies’ handheld devices, to provide a seamless omnichannel retail experience. This technology refresh aims to streamline IT management, proactively monitor network health, and enable features like in-store navigation and image search, ultimately making home improvement projects easier for customers.

title: The 13 Best Grill Brands
summary: This article identifies and reviews 13 top grill brands, highlighting what makes each manufacturer stand out in the market. It discusses various types of grills, including charcoal, gas, pellet, and griddles, outlining their price ranges, top products, and unique features. The selection criteria prioritize durability, performance, versatility, and availability across different retailers, catering to diverse user needs and budgets.

title: New externship program gives law students taste of in-house legal work with businesses
summary: Mercer Law School is launching a new Corporate Counsel Externship Program this fall to provide students with hands-on experience in in-house legal work. Led by former Tractor Supply general counsel Ben Parrish, the program addresses the growing demand for in-house legal professionals and will partner students with companies like Home Depot and Aflac. Students will gain practical skills in areas such as contract drafting, compliance, and negotiation, preparing them for diverse legal career paths.

title: Lowe's Cos. stock underperforms Thursday when compared to competitors
summary: On Thursday, Lowe's Cos. stock experienced a decline of 0.81%, closing at $174.67, amidst a broader market downturn. This performance meant Lowe's underperformed its competitors, such as Home Depot Inc. and Kingfisher PLC ADR, which saw gains. The stock closed significantly below its 52-week high, and its trading volume was higher than its 50-day average.

title: A new ETF investing in disaster relief launches in time for hurricane season
summary: A new exchange-traded fund (ETF) called Procure Disaster Recovery Strategy ETF (ticker: FEMA) has launched, focusing on companies involved in disaster recovery and risk reduction. The ETF's creation was inspired by Hurricane Katrina and invests in a diversified basket of companies across various sectors, including those that provide communications tech, risk assessment, engineering, and cloud computing services. Since its launch on June 1, the FEMA ETF is down about 11%.

title: Fire breaks out in Home Depot in Williston
summary: A fire broke out in the Williston Home Depot on Thursday afternoon after a stove caught fire in the receiving area, igniting nearby boxes. An employee extinguished the initial blaze before firefighters arrived, who then ventilated moderate smoke from the rear of the store. The fire was deemed accidental, and no injuries were reported.

title: The Homer Fund: Supporting Associates in Need with the Annual Orange at Heart Campaign
summary: The Homer Fund, The Home Depot's employee assistance program, aids associates facing hardship through grants. Funded by both associates and the company, it's celebrated by the annual Orange at Heart campaign, ensuring every dollar donated directly helps fellow employees. Since its inception in 1999, the fund has distributed nearly $233 million to over 165,000 associates, including support during the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Evernote, Home Depot outsource network management
summary: Evernote and Home Depot have outsourced their network management to vendors like Meter and Aruba, respectively. This strategy allows their in-house IT staff to focus on business-critical projects rather than the daily tasks of network maintenance. Both companies found that a subscription-based "network as a service" (NaaS) model was more cost-effective and agile for adapting to changing business needs.

title: Pace is attracting new people and businesses, while trying to maintain the same ol' charm
summary: Pace, Florida, is experiencing significant economic and population growth, transforming from a bedroom community to a commercially vibrant suburb. While residents appreciate the increased availability of goods and services, concerns are rising about traffic congestion and the proliferation of chain stores. Local officials and residents are looking for infrastructure improvements and more diverse entertainment options to manage this rapid development while retaining the area's community feel.

title: Celebrating 30 Years of Business and Partnership with American Carpet South
summary: American Carpet South (ACS), The Home Depot’s largest carpet provider, is celebrating 30 years in business. Joe Santagata, CEO, invested his college fund to partner with his father, Bob, and expand their flooring services, eventually becoming CEO in 2007. ACS has been recognized as National Flooring Service Provider of the Year by The Home Depot and attributes its success to strategic partnerships and a focus on customer service.

title: Home Depot taps Aruba platform to power customer, associate experiences
summary: The Home Depot is expanding its partnership with Aruba by deploying Aruba ESP and HPE GreenLake for Aruba networking across its U.S. stores. This initiative aims to enhance both customer and associate experiences by providing a robust, flexible, and fast network. The upgrade supports interconnected capabilities like in-store navigation and image search for customers, and empowers associates with handheld devices for efficient inventory management.

title: Bath & Body Works changes return policy
summary: Bath & Body Works is updating its return policy, effective September 14, to limit non-receipted returns or exchanges to $250 within a 90-day period at select U.S. stores. The company will use an electronic system for tracking these returns, requiring customers to show a government-issued ID. While maintaining a 100% satisfaction guarantee, the updated policy will no longer accept products showing excessive wear and tear.

title: Two single-tenant North Carolina retail properties sell for $23.93M
summary: JLL Capital Markets announced the $23.93 million sale of two single-tenant retail properties in Durham, North Carolina: a 120,000-square-foot Home Depot and a 148,663-square-foot Costco. Armada Hoffler Properties sold the properties to a New York-based buyer at a blended 4.0 percent cap rate. Both retailers operate under long-term absolute NNN ground leases in a high-visibility location near Duke University.

title: Home Depot’s 12-foot $300 skeleton is back in stock for Halloween
summary: Home Depot has brought back its popular 12-foot skeleton, "Skelly," along with other Halloween decor, for the spooky season. The $300 skeleton, which features animated LCD eyes, first went viral and sold out in 2020. The Halloween items launched online and will be available in brick-and-mortar stores from late August to early September.

title: This family moved into a Home Depot shed after going into debt ⁠— then made a huge profit selling it
summary: A Georgia couple, Nick and Meghan Lucido, got out of significant debt by moving into an 860-square-foot Home Depot shed. After paying off $82,000 in nine months, they sold the shed for $312,000, making a substantial profit. This allowed them to build their dream farmhouse and achieve financial freedom.

title: Make Your Halloween Set-Up Haunted AF With A 15-Foot Phantom & 12-Foot Flying Witch
summary: Home Depot's Halloween 2022 decorations are back in stock, featuring the 12-foot skeleton, Skelly, and a new 15-foot phantom. This article highlights some of the Halloween items available to help enthusiasts create a spooky setup.

title: The Home Depot signs on for major distribution operation at new Childress Klein Steele Creek development
summary: The Home Depot is set to occupy a large industrial facility of over 603,000 square feet at The Concourse, Childress Klein's mixed-use development in the Steele Creek area of Charlotte. This marks another significant industrial presence for the home improvement retailer in the Charlotte region. Sources indicate this is a major distribution operation.

title: Jose "Pepe" Rodriguez | President – Mexico
summary: This article profiles Jose "Pepe" Rodriguez, the President of The Home Depot Mexico. It details his responsibilities, which include overseeing sales, operations, online platforms, and over 18,000 associates across 140 stores. The profile also highlights his career trajectory, from joining Home Depot in 2001 as a financial analyst to his various leadership roles in finance and operations both in Mexico and the U.S.

title: The Home Depot Announces Latest Carbon Emission Reductions, New Supplier Diversity Spending Goal and Progress on Community Investments in 2022 ESG Report
summary: The Home Depot announced significant progress in its 2022 ESG Report, detailing a reduction of approximately 172,000 metric tons in combined Scope 1 and 2 carbon emissions in 2021 and a 50 percent cut in U.S. store electricity usage since 2010. The company also set a new goal to spend $5 billion annually with diverse suppliers by 2025 and highlighted over $400 million contributed to veterans' causes by The Home Depot Foundation since 2011. These achievements underscore the company's commitment to its environmental, social, and governance pillars.

title: HOME DEPOT TAKES A WIN: Home Depot Barely Dodges TCPA Class Action Suit in Georgia
summary: Home Depot successfully had a TCPA class action suit dismissed with prejudice, despite failing to compel arbitration. The plaintiff, Melissa Carson, alleged Home Depot sent unwanted text messages after an unsubscribe request, but the court found she did not plausibly allege Home Depot itself sent the messages or assert an alternate theory of liability against the company. The court rejected Home Depot's attempt to enforce an arbitration clause through equitable estoppel, but ultimately dismissed the case because Carson's claims were not directly against Home Depot.

title: Thieves steal zero-turn mower, trailer from Tractor Supply Co., sheriff says
summary: Thieves reportedly stole a zero-turn mower, a trailer, and a grill from a Tractor Supply Co. in Denver early Friday morning, as stated by the sheriff. The incident, valued at $8,500, was caught on video surveillance, showing the culprits fleeing in a pickup truck. Authorities were alerted by an alarm company after a break-in was reported.

title: DeWALT recall announced for 1.4M miter saws due to injury, laceration hazards
summary: DeWALT has recalled over 1.4 million 12-inch Sliding Compound Miter Saws in the U.S. and Canada due to a safety hazard. The saws' rear safety guard can break or detach, posing injury and laceration risks from projectiles or direct blade contact. The company has received 571 reports of guard failure, including nine laceration injuries, and advises consumers to stop using the saws immediately and contact DeWALT for a free repair kit or service center repair.

title: Burberry appoints ex-Tesco CFO as Non-Executive Director
summary: Burberry Group has appointed Alan Stewart, former Chief Financial Officer of Tesco PLC, as its new Non-Executive Director, effective September 1, 2022. He will also become a member of Burberry's Audit and Nomination committees and is expected to replace Matthew Key as Audit Committee Chair. Stewart brings extensive experience from his previous roles at major public companies like Tesco, Marks & Spencer PLC, and WH Smith PLC.

title: A The Home Depot Joins Billion Dollar Roundtable, Continues to Expand Supplier Diversity Programs
summary: The Home Depot has joined the Billion Dollar Roundtable Inc. (BDR), a nonprofit recognizing corporations that spend over $1 billion annually with minority and woman-owned suppliers. In fiscal year 2021, the company spent $3.3 billion with diverse suppliers, demonstrating its commitment to expanding its supplier diversity program to foster growth, reflect customer diversity, and strengthen communities. This move aims to leverage innovative and unique products and perspectives from diverse businesses, ultimately meeting customer needs and increasing shareholder value.

title: The Home Depot unifies customer experiences with Adobe
summary: The Home Depot has successfully unified its online and in-store customer experiences using Adobe products, leading to a 62% increase in personalized campaigns and a 14% rise in net sales year over year. The company leverages Adobe Real-Time Customer Data Platform and Adobe Experience Platform to create unified customer profiles, enabling highly relevant messaging and inspiration for customers' home improvement projects. This data-driven approach, along with innovative tools like a mobile app for in-store navigation and AI-powered product search, allows The Home Depot to cater to diverse customer journeys, from project-based customers to item buyers and contractors.

title: News | Home Depot Plugs Into Duke Realty's Most Energy Efficient Warehouse to Date
summary: Home Depot has leased a 529,000-square-foot energy-efficient warehouse in Irwindale, California, developed by Duke Realty. This "smart" industrial building, the most energy-efficient to date for Duke Realty, features advanced technologies expected to save significant electricity and reduce its carbon footprint. The lease represents one of the largest industrial deals in Los Angeles County, highlighting the growing demand for sustainable commercial properties.

title: Victoria Town Center to open Boot Barn, Burlington Coat Factory
summary: Victoria Town Center, a new shopping development in Victoria, Texas, has announced Boot Barn and Burlington Coat Factory as its first two tenants. Boot Barn is expected to open by the end of the year, with Burlington Coat Factory following early next year. The city anticipates the $31 million private investment will generate significant property and sales tax revenue, with the developer needing to meet a $54.4 million sales revenue target by 2027.

title: The Home Depot Announces Second Quarter Results; Reaffirms Fiscal 2022 Guidance
summary: The Home Depot announced record-breaking second-quarter results for fiscal 2022, reporting sales of $43.8 billion and net earnings of $5.2 billion. The company reaffirmed its fiscal 2022 guidance, expecting total sales growth and comparable sales growth of approximately 3.0 percent. This strong performance reflects continued high demand for home improvement projects.

title: Introducing Vining Ivy: GLIDDEN Paint by PPG’s ‘bluish, greenish’ 2023 Color of the Year
summary: PPG announced Vining Ivy (PPG1148-6) as the joint 2023 Color of the Year for both its Glidden and PPG paint brands. This versatile "bluish-greenish" teal is described as energizing yet grounding, suitable for diverse design aesthetics and spaces. The color is available in various PPG products, including Glidden Diamond paint and Speedhide Pro-EV Zero interior latex paint.

title: Home Depot pushes ahead of Lowe’s as it leans on pro customers
summary: Home Depot reported record quarterly sales and earnings, driven by its strong performance with pro customers, which helped offset a shortened spring selling season that negatively impacted DIY sales. In contrast, competitor Lowe’s experienced lower-than-expected sales, primarily due to its heavier reliance on DIY customers, whose spending has moderated. While both companies reaffirmed their annual outlooks, Home Depot's focus on pro customers appears to be a key differentiator in a challenging economic environment.

title: The Home Depot Names Ted Decker Chair of the Board
summary: The Home Depot announced that its Board of Directors has elected CEO and President Edward "Ted" Decker as chair of the board, effective October 1, 2022. Decker, a 22-year veteran of the company, will succeed Craig Menear, who is retiring. Greg Brenneman, the board's lead director, praised both Decker's passion for customers and associates and Menear's visionary leadership.

title: The Home Depot proposes a third St. Johns County store
summary: The Home Depot plans to open its third St. Johns County store in the World Commerce Center, near the intersection of I-95 and International Golf Parkway. This proposed 136,014-square-foot facility includes a garden center, tool rental, and seasonal sales area. The move comes as Lowe's Home Centers also proposes a second location in northern St. Johns County, intensifying competition in the region's home improvement market.

title: Tractor Supply Co. plows into Clayton for grand opening
summary: Tractor Supply Co. celebrated its grand opening and ribbon-cutting in Clayton on July 29, 2022, in partnership with Forward Rabun and the Rabun County Chamber of Commerce. The new store, located at 1563 Highway 441 South, features a greenhouse and a dog/pet washing station. The grand opening was extended with events including an adoption day with Rabun County Paws 4 Life and local vendors on August 6.

title: Home Depot finally coming to this Lehigh County shopping center
summary: After more than a decade, Home Depot is set to open a 136,058-square-foot store in the Macungie Crossings shopping center in Lower Macungie Township, Lehigh County. The township board of commissioners approved the development, which includes design customizations and plans for shared parking with future retailers, aiming for a summer 2023 opening. This project is part of a larger vision to create a walkable, village-like atmosphere at Macungie Crossings.

summary: Despite potential economic challenges like a recession and decreasing home prices, Home Depot is projected to achieve another sales record. summary: A Home Depot manager is urging shoppers, especially in hurricane-prone areas, to purchase essential storm supplies well in advance of a storm or hurricane season's peak. Due to ongoing inventory challenges and the impending Hurricane Ian, many crucial items like extension cords, tarps, flashlights, and generators can quickly sell out, leaving last-minute shoppers unprepared. The manager advises checking hurricane checklists and ensuring all necessary hardware and functioning batteries are acquired early.

summary: Best Buy and Home Depot are locking up more merchandise to combat high rates of theft, which remain elevated above pre-pandemic levels. Stores are using methods like replacing products with QR codes or signs indicating items are in secured locations, requiring shoppers to seek assistance from staff. This strategy aims to deter theft without alienating customers or investors.

summary: PPG's Glidden paint brand has launched a new line of floor and concrete coatings featuring Cool Surface Technology, designed to limit surface temperatures by up to 20%. summary: Hurricane Ian's weather bands caused significant damage even on Florida's east coast, with strong winds uprooting and overturning trees outside a Home Depot in Delray Beach. title: Forward momentum for Roche and Wave in latest news about huntingtin-lowering trials
summary: Roche announced plans for a new clinical trial, GENERATION-HD2, for its huntingtin-lowering drug tominersen, specifically targeting younger people in earlier stages of Huntington's disease. Simultaneously, Wave Life Sciences released early data from its SELECT-HD trial showing that its selective ASO drug, WVE-003, successfully lowered mutant huntingtin levels while preserving normal huntingtin, though some participants showed unexpected increases in neurofilament. Both advancements offer cautious optimism for the Huntington's disease community, despite previous setbacks and the unproven long-term efficacy of huntingtin-lowering.

summary: A federal judge has ruled in favor of The Home Depot in an ERISA class action lawsuit. summary: Home Depot's 12-foot skeleton decoration, affectionately known as Skelly, has become a massive Halloween hit since its debut in 2020. title: Kidde smoke alarm protection events at The Home Depot
summary: The Home Depot and Kidde are collaborating to raise fire safety awareness through events in October, coinciding with Fire Prevention Week and the cooler months when home fires are more common. For every Kidde alarm purchased at The Home Depot through November 2022, a $1 contribution will be made towards donating alarms to communities in need. The article highlights key Kidde products available, including smoke alarms, fire extinguishers, and combination smoke and carbon monoxide detectors, emphasizing their role in protecting homes from fires and CO leaks.

title: Home Depot Philadelphia Store to Vote on Unionizing in First for Chain
summary: Employees at a Home Depot store in Philadelphia are scheduled to vote on November 2 and 5 on whether to unionize, marking a potential first for the company's US stores. The election will be supervised by the National Labor Relations Board and held in person on company premises. This vote could establish the first unionized Home Depot location in the United States.

title: Smoke detector sale: Chicago Home Depot stores selling 99-cent smoke alarms this weekend
summary: The Chicago Fire Department and Home Depot are offering smoke detectors for 99 cents this weekend at 11 Home Depot stores in Chicago. This initiative is part of National Fire Prevention Week, encouraging residents to replace old or expired smoke alarms. This is the fourth consecutive year for this partnership.

title: The Home Depot launches jobseeker portal
summary: The Home Depot has expanded its Path to Pro professional skills initiative by launching a new jobseeker portal, PathtoPro.com. This platform connects skilled tradespeople with hiring professionals in the construction and home improvement industries, allowing jobseekers to create profiles, upload resumes, and showcase their work. The initiative aims to address the skilled labor shortage by providing training, networking opportunities, and information on trade professions.

summary: Broe Real Estate Group (BREG) has announced that Micron Technology, Inc. will be the lead tenant at its 25-acre MAX Technology Center in Longmont, Colorado. summary: This article details the enduring popularity and fervent demand for Home Depot's 12-foot Halloween skeleton, affectionately known as "Skelly," since its introduction in 2020. summary: Home Depot shoppers are raving about the new 9.5-foot "Animated Immortal Werewolf Halloween Animatronic," which is being sold at a 50 percent discount for $199. title: Plug Power adding jobs locally to deliver green hydro energy worldwide by 2028
summary: Plug Power's Henrietta gigafactory is now at full production, creating new jobs to support the company's goal of supplying 1,000 tons of green hydrogen daily worldwide by 2028. The facility, which manufactures fuel cell stacks and electrolyzers, also serves as a model for future global expansion. Despite supply chain challenges impacting 2022 revenue projections, Plug Power remains committed to its growth in New York and its mission to build the green hydrogen economy.

title: Popular, tech-infused furniture brand to open store in this bustling Columbia shopping area
summary: Lovesac, a furniture brand known for its "Sac" chairs and adaptable "Sactional" couches with tech features, is opening a new store at 201 Harbison Blvd. in Columbia, South Carolina. The new showroom will be located in the busy Harbison Crossing shopping center, a popular retail district near the Columbiana Centre mall and other major stores. Lovesac currently operates a kiosk inside the Columbiana Centre.

summary: This article lists recent career changes and promotions within the lighting industry for October 2022. summary: The 12-foot Home Depot skeleton, despite debuting during the pandemic, has achieved perennial hit status, fostering a passionate community and even inspiring merchandise and a short film. title: California Court of Appeal Reverses Summary Judgment in Time-Rounding Case Involving Electronic Timekeeping System
summary: The California Sixth Appellate District Court recently reversed a summary judgment in *Camp v. Home Depot*, ruling against an employer that rounded employee work-time to the nearest quarter-hour despite using an electronic system that recorded time to the minute. The court's decision, limited to the specific facts, emphasized that employees must be paid for all work performed, inviting the California Supreme Court to address the validity of time-rounding standards given modern timekeeping technology. Employers are advised to consult legal counsel regarding their rounding policies, especially if using electronic timekeeping systems, as conflicting decisions exist at the appellate level.

title: Floor & Decor executives say home equity continue to boost sales even as market slows

summary: A new 65,000-square-foot ShopRite supermarket, owned and operated by the Greenfield family, is set to open on December 11th in Huntington Commons. This new store occupies part of the space previously held by a Kmart and is part of major renovations at the shopping center by Urban Edge Properties. Huntington Commons will also see new businesses like GOLFTEC, CycleBar, and iStretchPlus.

title: New Jacksonville Tractor Supply Company store to open this week
summary: A new Tractor Supply Company store is scheduled to open in Jacksonville this week. The store will feature a garden center and a pet wash. This opening is part of a broader retail movement in the area, as other stores like Old Navy are also expanding.

title: California Wage and Hour Issues for Employers to Watch in 2023: Is My Time-Rounding System Still Compliant? (US)
summary: A recent California Court of Appeal decision, Camp v. Home Depot USA, Inc., questioned the compliance of employer time-rounding systems, especially when precise timekeeping technology is available. The court reversed a lower court's ruling in favor of Home Depot, stating that employers able to capture exact work times must pay for all time worked, urging caution for California employers using time-rounding. A petition for review has been filed with the California Supreme Court, indicating potential further developments in 2023.

title: Global Power Tool Market is Expected to Reach $43B by 2030 – IndexBox
summary: The global power tool market, valued at $32.2 billion in 2022, is projected to reach $42.7 billion by 2030, driven by increasing demand from construction, automotive, and DIY projects. Key players like Stanley Black & Decker and Robert Bosch dominate a fragmented market, with sales primarily through indirect channels and online retail gaining importance. The market faces challenges such as rising raw material costs and competition from low-cost manufacturers, alongside opportunities in cordless tools and industrialization.

title: HD Supply to close Cobb County office, move jobs to other states
summary: HD Supply, a subsidiary of Home Depot, is closing one of its offices in Cobb County, Georgia, and relocating 57 jobs out of the state. This move involves shifting some positions to other states.

summary: Under Armour announced the appointment of Stephanie Linnartz, formerly president of Marriott International, as its new President, CEO, and a member of its Board of Directors, effective February 27, 2023. Kevin Plank, Under Armour's Executive Chair, highlighted Linnartz's extensive experience in brand strategy, omnichannel execution, and driving consumer loyalty from her 25-year career at Marriott. Colin Browne, who served as interim President and CEO, will resume his role as Chief Operating Officer.

title: 5 Warnings to Shoppers From Ex-Dick’s Sporting Goods Employees
summary: Former Dick's Sporting Goods employees share five warnings for shoppers. These include anticipating chaotic back stockrooms, pressure to sign up for credit cards and the Scorecard rewards program, a surprisingly lenient return policy for some items, and vigilance against email scams. Understanding these points can help customers navigate their shopping experience more effectively.

title: Home Depot will be there to fix up your virtual house in the metaverse
summary: The Home Depot is exploring a venture into the metaverse, aiming to capitalize on the potential for virtual home renovation projects. This move comes as the company has seen significant sales growth from physical home renovations in recent years. The article suggests that virtual renovations could provide a similar boost to Home Depot's business.

title: Walmart, Home Depot and Gap Execs Honored by NRF Foundation
summary: The NRF Foundation has announced its "People Shaping Retail’s Future 2023" honorees, recognizing five retail executives for their contributions to communities and the industry. Among those honored are leaders from Walmart, Home Depot, Gap Inc., Ministry of Supply, and Steve Madden. These individuals will be celebrated at an event in New York City during NRF 2023: Retail’s Big Show.

summary: The Home Depot is opening a new 417,000-square-foot distribution center in Rosemount, creating more than 100 new jobs. The company is hiring for positions to operate lift equipment and prepare orders for delivery at the new facility.

title: Home Depot to launch new distribution center in Minnesota
summary: Home Depot is opening a new 417,000-square-foot distribution center in Rosemount, Minnesota. The Atlanta-based company plans to hire over 100 people for this new facility.

summary: Detectives are searching for three men who stole approximately $2,800 worth of power tools from a Home Depot in North Lauderdale, Florida. Surveillance video captured the men loading about 10 power drills into a shopping cart and calmly walking out of the store without paying. They then placed the items into a dark-colored four-door vehicle occupied by a fourth person, last seen leaving the plaza.

title: Home Depot Executive Adolfo Villagomez to Be New CEO of Progress Residential
summary: Adolfo Villagomez, an executive from Home Depot Inc., has been appointed as the new Chief Executive Officer of Progress Residential, a single-family rental arm of Pretium Partners. Mr. Villagomez, 49, will succeed Chaz Mueller, who retired last year after serving as CEO since 2018. Progress Residential is a major rental-home manager in the country.

title: Tractor Supply Co. stock underperforms Wednesday when compared to competitors
summary: Tractor Supply Co. (TSCO) stock fell 0.76% on Wednesday, closing at $221.49, despite a generally positive trading session for the broader market. The company's stock underperformed against competitors like Home Depot Inc., Lowe's Cos., and AutoZone Inc., all of which saw gains. This marked the third consecutive day of losses for Tractor Supply Co.

title: The Home Depot Adds New Enhancements to Pro Xtra Loyalty Program
summary: The Home Depot has expanded its Pro Xtra loyalty program to include new membership tiers (Member, Elite, and VIP) and improved benefits for professional contractors and builders. These enhancements offer specialized perks, business tools, exclusive sales, and personalized support, aiming to remove friction for Pros who account for approximately half of the company's sales. The program, which launched in 2012, continues to evolve to better support the growing needs of its Pro customers.

title: Family Succession Story: Longtime business operations prove that some things never change - Aug/Sept 2022
summary: This article details the succession stories of three multi-generational flooring businesses—Myers Carpet, Howard’s Rug Co., and Airbase Carpet & Tile Mart—highlighting how they have adapted and thrived over decades. It emphasizes the importance of finding a niche, cultivating relationships, and remaining flexible to navigate industry changes and competition. The businesses demonstrate that while market dynamics evolve, core principles of family ownership and customer focus remain crucial for long-term success.

title: The Home Depot Launches New In-Store Application to Help Associates Provide Better Customer Experience
summary: The Home Depot has launched a new in-store application called "Sidekick" to enhance customer experience by helping associates prioritize tasks more effectively. Powered by machine learning, Sidekick guides associates on restocking and product location, leveraging cloud-enabled algorithms and machine vision. This app is an addition to their hdPhones and is being rolled out to all U.S. stores following a successful initial deployment.

title: Home Depot will now pay its hourly employees to the minute
summary: Home Depot is changing its payroll policy for hourly employees to pay them to the nearest minute based on exact time punches, effective January 16, 2023. This change moves away from the common industry practice of "time clock rounding" where total shift time was rounded to the nearest 15 minutes. The decision follows legal challenges and evolving workplace practices, with the Department of Labor allowing rounding only if it doesn't favor the employer.

title: Sonos One Gen 2 and One SL – the backbone of the Sonos sound system (AV review)
summary: This review highlights the Sonos One Gen 2 and One SL speakers as the foundational components of any Sonos sound system, excelling as stereo pairs or rear speakers for soundbars. It details their sound quality, features like voice assistant support and Trueplay, and connectivity caveats. The article concludes that despite being a tad expensive, they offer quality, performance, and flexibility within the Sonos ecosystem.

title: Home Depot co-founder warns the 'woke generation' is ignoring the economy's 'bottom line'
summary: Home Depot co-founder Bernie Marcus criticized the "woke generation" of leaders for allegedly ignoring the economy's "bottom line" and focusing on issues like climate control at events such as the World Economic Forum, rather than prioritizing shareholders and employees. Marcus also expressed concern about a perceived lack of work ethic among some individuals, attributing it to entitlement and government assistance, and warned that small businesses are struggling due to inflation and difficulties in finding workers. He argued that current leaders are pushing a "socialistic society" that discourages work and negatively impacts the economy.

title: Lowe's Cos. stock falls Thursday, underperforms market
summary: Lowe's Companies (LOW) stock experienced a 3.06% decline on Thursday, closing at $202.13. This performance lagged behind the broader market, with both the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average also seeing losses. title: For $837 worth of Home Depot merch, man faces murder charge, life in prison
summary: A man has been arrested and charged with first-degree murder and robbery after an 82-year-old Home Depot employee, Gary Rasor, died weeks after being pushed to the concrete floor during a shoplifting incident. The suspect, Terry McAnthony McMillian Jr., stole pressure washers valued at $837 and faces a possible life sentence without parole. Rasor, beloved by customers, suffered severe injuries and his family stated his health deteriorated rapidly after seeing surveillance footage of the assault.

title: Lowe's Cos. stock falls Thursday, underperforms market
summary: Lowe's Cos. (LOW) stock fell 2.09% on Thursday, closing at $201.81, despite a positive trading session for the broader market with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average both rising. The stock underperformed competitors like Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) but fared better than Home Depot Inc. (HD) and Walmart Inc. (WMT), which also saw slight declines. This marked the second consecutive day of losses for Lowe's, with its trading volume exceeding its 50-day average.

title: Home Depot Canada found sharing customer personal data with Meta - privacy regulator
summary: Canada's privacy regulator found that Home Depot's Canadian arm shared customer e-receipt details, including encoded email addresses and purchase information, with Meta Platforms Inc without customer knowledge or consent. The practice occurred through Meta's offline conversions program. Home Depot Canada ceased sharing this data in October 2022, following recommendations from the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada, until it can ensure valid consent.

title: Home Depot didn't get customer consent before sharing data with Facebook's owner, privacy watchdog finds
summary: Canada's privacy watchdog found that Home Depot shared customer data from electronic receipts with Meta (Facebook and Instagram) without customer knowledge or consent since 2018. The information, potentially sensitive, was used for targeted advertising and user profiling, not just to gauge ad effectiveness. Home Depot stopped the practice in October 2022 and has agreed to implement recommendations for better consent measures, despite initially citing "consent fatigue" as a reason for not notifying customers.

title: Stanley Black & Decker stock rises on Q4 earnings beat
summary: Stanley Black & Decker (SWK) saw its stock rise after beating Q4 earnings expectations, despite a 5% drop in organic sales for its tools and outdoor segment due to lower consumer demand for DIY products. The company announced a new $1 billion cost-cutting program, which analysts noted as a recurring theme for the efficient company. The market reacted positively to the cost-cutting initiatives, even as sales figures indicated weakness in the housing and DIY markets.

title: The Home Depot and Ecolab Launch Ecolab® Scientific Clean
summary: The Home Depot has partnered with Ecolab, a global leader in hygiene and infection prevention, to launch Ecolab Scientific Clean, a new line of retail cleaning products. This collaboration marks Ecolab's first entry into the retail market, making their professional-grade cleaning solutions available to both Pro and DIY customers at The Home Depot stores and online. The product range includes degreasers, pressure wash concentrates, bathroom cleaners, and floor cleaners, bringing Ecolab's 100 years of expertise directly to consumers.

title: Hoka: The Chunky, Ugly Sneaker Craze
summary: Hoka, known for its super-thick soled sneakers, has become the fastest-growing running brand globally, with sales exceeding $1 billion in 2022. The brand's success is attributed to its comfort, functional benefits for runners, and its appeal across various demographics, including celebrities, hikers, and older individuals. Hoka has embraced an anti-fashion, "ugly shoe" aesthetic, setting it apart from competitors and contributing to its widespread popularity.

title: The Home Depot and Ecolab Launch Ecolab® Scientific Clean
summary: The Home Depot has partnered with Ecolab Inc. to launch "Ecolab Scientific Clean," a new line of cleaning products for retail. This marks the first time Ecolab's commercial-grade solutions are available to both Pro and DIY customers in stores and online at The Home Depot, offering products like degreasers, pressure wash concentrates, bathroom cleaners, and floor cleaners. The collaboration makes Ecolab's 100 years of expertise accessible for residential use.

title: State Street Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLY) Stock Price, Holdings, Dividend Yield
summary: This article provides a detailed overview of the Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLY), including its stock price, key statistics, top holdings, and dividend information. summary: Major retailers and distributors like 84 Lumber, Builders FirstSource, Lowe’s, and Floor & Decor showcased their offerings at the 2023 International Builders’ Show (IBS). Companies emphasized services for professional customers, with Lowe's collaborating on a new paint with Sherwin-Williams, 84 Lumber highlighting its expansion, and Builders FirstSource focusing on digital tools like myBLDR.com. Floor & Decor also noted its strong catering to both small and large pro builders.

summary: BlackRock has increased its ownership in Home Depot (HD) to 76.26 million shares, representing 7.5% of the company, up from 6.70% previously. title: The Home Depot Foundation Celebrates Black History Month with New Grants for Atlanta-Based Nonprofit Partners
summary: The Home Depot Foundation is celebrating Black History Month by awarding $185,000 in grants to three Atlanta-based Black-led and Black-benefitting nonprofit organizations. The grants will support student scholarships, memorialize a civic engagement leader, and fund scholarships for Black entrepreneurs, reinforcing the Foundation's commitment to social equity and community development.

title: 4.9 Million Fabuloso Bottles Recalled for Bacteria Risk (Published 2023)
summary: Colgate-Palmolive has recalled approximately 4.9 million bottles of Fabuloso cleaning products due to a bacteria risk. The recall affects products sold between December and January, as an inadequate amount of preservative during manufacturing may have allowed bacteria like Pseudomonas aeruginosa to grow. While generally not harmful to healthy individuals, this bacteria can cause serious infections in those with weakened immune systems or underlying health conditions.

title: What happened to In-N-Out coming to Lubbock? Company responds
summary: In-N-Out Burger has confirmed it has no immediate plans to expand to Lubbock, Texas, despite past hopes for a location in the city. The company's strategy focuses on slow and controlled growth within existing operating markets. This means Lubbock fans will continue to travel approximately 300 miles to the Dallas-Fort Worth area for the nearest In-N-Out.

title: Don’t use these cleaners: Millions of bottles recalled because of bacteria
summary: Colgate-Palmolive has recalled almost 5 million bottles of Fabuloso multipurpose cleaner due to concerns about bacterial contamination, specifically Pseudomonas species bacteria. The recall was initiated because a preservative was not added at intended levels during manufacturing, posing a risk of serious infection to individuals with weakened immune systems or underlying health conditions. Consumers are advised to stop using the recalled products immediately and contact Colgate-Palmolive for a refund or replacement.

title: Fabuloso recall: Colgate-Palmolive recalls 4.9M cleaners over bacteria risk
summary: Colgate-Palmolive has recalled 4.9 million bottles of its Fabuloso Multi-Purpose Cleaner due to a risk of bacteria exposure, specifically Pseudomonas species bacteria. The recall affects certain scents and bottle sizes sold nationwide since December 2022. Consumers are advised to stop using the product and contact Colgate-Palmolive for a refund or replacement.

title: Colgate-Palmolive recalls 4.9 million bottles of Fabuloso
summary: Colgate-Palmolive has recalled approximately 4.9 million bottles of Fabuloso Multi-Purpose Cleaners due to a risk of exposure to Pseudomonas species bacteria. The recall affects products sold between December 2022 and January 2023 at various retailers, posing a serious infection risk for individuals with weakened immune systems. Consumers are advised to immediately stop using the recalled products, take a picture of the UPC and lot code, and contact Colgate-Palmolive for a full refund or replacement.

title: 4.9 million Fabuloso cleaning products recalled due to bacteria risk
summary: Colgate-Palmolive Company has recalled approximately 4.9 million units of Fabuloso Multi-Purpose Cleaner products in the U.S. and 56,000 in Canada due to a risk of bacteria contamination, specifically Pseudomonas species bacteria. The recall, impacting products produced between December 14, 2022, and January 23, 2023, is due to inadequate preservative levels during manufacturing. Consumers are advised to stop using the recalled products, which were sold at major retailers, and contact the company for a refund or replacement.

summary: Colgate-Palmolive has issued a voluntary recall for 4.9 million bottles of Fabuloso multi-purpose cleaning liquids due to potential bacterial contamination, specifically Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Pseudomonas fluorescens. The Department of Licensing and Consumer Affairs (DLCA) has instructed all retailers in the U.S. Virgin Islands to remove affected products from shelves. Consumers who purchased recalled items from Home Depot can return them for a refund, and others can submit an online form and dispose of the product for a refund.

title: What to Watch for in Home Depot’s Q4 Earnings
summary: Home Depot investors should prepare for potential challenges in their Q4 earnings due to economic pressures in the housing market and shifting consumer spending habits. The home improvement retailer saw significant growth in 2020 and 2021, but now faces headwinds from rising interest rates and declining home sales. Analysts predict slow revenue growth and a decrease in net income for the fourth quarter.

summary: West Fraser's Riegelwood lumber mill stands out through its operational robustness and commitment to workforce development, despite market fluctuations. General Manager D.J. Russell Jr. and Superintendent Lyle Kindig emphasize the mill's strategic focus on being a low-cost producer and investing in its employees. The Riegelwood facility has seen advancements in technology, transitioning from manual grading to AI-optimized production, while maintaining its core manual labor needs and strong local sourcing.

title: Home Depot's starting pay rises to $15 an hour
summary: Home Depot is increasing its starting pay for employees to $15 an hour, part of a $1 billion investment in raises across its U.S. and Canadian stores. This move comes as major retailers boost wages in a competitive job market with low unemployment. Despite the wage increase, Home Depot reported mixed fourth-quarter earnings and a tepid outlook due to inflation and a cooling housing market.

title: Home Depot flags profit hit from slowing demand, rising wages in 2023
summary: Home Depot warned of an expected decline in annual profit for 2023, missing Street expectations, due to slowing demand for home improvement goods and increased labor costs. The company plans to spend an additional $1 billion on annual wages for its hourly workers while facing inflation that is reducing consumer spending on remodeling projects. This outlook caused Home Depot's shares to tumble, reflecting a broader trend of cautious forecasts from major retailers like Walmart amid a challenging economic environment.

title: Target plans to boost next-day delivery service with more sortation centers
summary: Target Corp. is expanding its next-day delivery capabilities through Shipt by building more than half a dozen new sortation centers. These new facilities will add to the nine sortation centers Target currently operates across the U.S. This initiative aims to enhance the speed and efficiency of Target's delivery service for customers.

title: Walmart and Home Depot are spending heaps of cash on pay raises because they can't afford to lose workers
summary: Walmart and Home Depot are significantly increasing worker wages to combat high turnover and a tight labor market in retail. Home Depot is investing $1 billion to raise hourly wages to at least $15, while Walmart is raising its minimum wage to $14 per hour. These moves are a strategy to retain and attract employees, as retail workers are quitting at higher rates and job openings remain abundant.

title: THE HOME DEPOT COUNTS DOWN TO SPRING WITH DAILY DEALS, EXPERT TIPS AND NEW INTERACTIVE WORKSHOPS
summary: The Home Depot has launched its "Countdown to Spring," offering daily deals, a dedicated online hub, and new interactive workshops to help customers with their spring projects. The initiative includes online-only "Special Buys of the Day," a "Countdown to Spring Hub" featuring product categories and inspiration, and both virtual interactive workshops for adults and free in-person Kids Workshops. These efforts aim to support customers with everything from gardening to home improvement as the spring season begins.

title: The dirty truth about your fake wood floors
summary: The article discusses the hidden dangers of "luxury" vinyl plank flooring, which is often made from PVC and is the most common type of flooring in the U.S. It highlights the toxicity of PVC production, its environmental impact during manufacturing and disposal, and potential health risks from additives, despite the material's popularity due to its low cost and appearance. The author suggests that consumers and designers should opt for safer alternatives like linoleum or porcelain.

title: Target warns of dull 2023 profit as heavy discounts sap margins
summary: Target (TGT.N) predicted subdued profit growth for 2023 due to increased discounting efforts aimed at attracting shoppers who are reducing discretionary spending amidst high inflation. Despite beating market expectations for sales and profit in the holiday quarter through these discounts, the strategy is expected to weigh on gross margins in the coming year. The retailer also announced a pause on share buybacks until cash flow improves, while still planning significant investments in store remodels and same-day fulfillment.

title: XLY Top Holdings List & Exposure (Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR Fund)
summary: This article details the top holdings and exposure breakdown for the Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLY). title: Is Time Rounding Over for California Employers? The California Supreme Court Will Weigh In
summary: The California Supreme Court is set to rule on the legality of neutral time-rounding practices for calculating employee wages in the case of Camp v. Home Depot, USA. This decision could significantly impact California employers who currently use such policies for payroll. Employers are advised to consult legal counsel and prepare for potential changes, as a ruling against time rounding could apply retroactively and necessitate immediate adjustments to timekeeping methods.

title: These 4 retailers will move into the former Wisconsin Rapids Shopko. Here's what they'll offer.
summary: Four new retailers, Big Lots, Marshalls, Harbor Freight, and Five Below, are set to occupy the former Shopko building in Wisconsin Rapids, with construction beginning in early spring 2023 and openings planned for late 2023 and early 2024. These businesses aim to fill gaps in community needs by offering a variety of goods and services previously unavailable in the area. The developer, Cool Investment LLC, emphasized creating a lasting retail hub and committed to the project before securing all tenants.

title: California Supreme Court to Address Rounding of Employee Time
summary: The California Supreme Court has agreed to review the Court of Appeal's decision in *Camp v. Home Depot U.S.A., Inc.*, which departed from prior precedent regarding the rounding of employee time. The case addresses whether employers with precise timekeeping systems must compensate employees for all actual time worked, even if a neutral rounding policy is in place. Employers are advised to exercise caution with rounding policies during this review period, especially if their systems capture exact work times.

title: Home Depot Distribution Center coming to Warren
summary: Home Depot plans to build a new, state-of-the-art distribution center in Warren, Michigan, at the former GM Warren Transmission Plant property. This project, supported by a $480,000 Michigan Business Development Program grant, is expected to create 80 jobs and generate $6.1 million in capital investment. It is part of a larger redevelopment aimed at bringing economic growth and jobs to the area.

title: The Home Depot built a store in Roblox and is hosting virtual Kids Workshops there
summary: The Home Depot has created a virtual store within the Roblox platform. In this virtual space, the company is hosting its popular Kids Workshops, bringing its community activities to a digital audience. This initiative allows The Home Depot to engage with younger consumers in an interactive online environment.

title: Home Depot is hiring more than 150 people across Indianapolis
summary: Home Depot is looking to hire more than 150 full-time and part-time employees across its Indianapolis locations. The company offers various benefits, including tuition reimbursement, performance-based cash bonuses, paid family leave, and a 401(k) savings plan. Applicants may receive a job offer within one day of applying, either in-person or online.

title: Supplier Profile: Exclusive Home Depot Partner RYOBI on Leading the Cordless Power Lawn and Garden Industry to a More Sustainable Future
summary: RYOBI, an exclusive partner of The Home Depot, has been a leader in the cordless power lawn and garden industry for nearly 30 years, focusing on sustainable practices. The company's Innovation Center in South Carolina produces over 430,000 units of battery-powered outdoor power equipment annually, aiming to reduce carbon footprint, lower noise pollution, and eliminate gas-powered equipment. RYOBI is expanding its facility in South Carolina to produce the majority of its walk-behind mowers there, demonstrating its commitment to innovation and sustainability.

title: Inside the never-ending softwood lumber trade war between Canada and the U.S.
summary: The article details the ongoing softwood lumber trade war between Canada and the U.S., which dates back to the 1980s. It highlights how Canadian lumber companies have strategically established significant sawmill capacity within the U.S. to bypass tariffs and access faster-growing timber supplies, especially in the U.S. South. The dispute stems from differing views on public versus private forest ownership and stumpage fees, with Canadian producers having paid over $8-billion in duties since 2017 despite international rulings often favoring Canada.

title: The U.S. Duopoly of Home Improvement: The Home Depot vs Lowe’s
summary: This article analyzes the duopoly of the U.S. home improvement market, comparing the two dominant players: The Home Depot and Lowe's. The comparison also touches on their ability to manage inflation, operational efficiency, and vulnerability to economic downturns.

title: The 7 Best Plumbing Supply Stocks To Buy Now
summary: This article identifies the seven best plumbing supply stocks to consider for investment, highlighting companies like Ferguson PLC, The Home Depot Inc, and W.W. Grainger. title: W.W. Grainger Inc. stock rises Tuesday, outperforms market
summary: W.W. Grainger Inc. (GWW) stock rose 0.62% to $675.84 on Tuesday, outperforming the broader market which saw the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average decline. This marked the second consecutive day of gains for the stock, placing it $33.37 short of its 52-week high. The company also outperformed competitors like Amazon.com Inc., Home Depot Inc., and Lowe's Cos.

title: City Known for Agriculture Gets Long-Awaited First Sprouts Farmers Market
summary: Stockton, California, a major agricultural hub, has finally welcomed its first Sprouts Farmers Market, located in the Sherwood Place mall. This 26,800-square-foot lease earned a 2023 CoStar Impact Award for its role in revitalizing the long-struggling mall. Brixton Capital's redevelopment plans for the property included Sprouts as a prominent tenant, aiming to better serve the community's grocery needs.

title: Fabuloso recall 2023: Full list of products that have been recalled
summary: Colgate-Palmolive issued a voluntary recall in February 2023 for millions of bottles of Fabuloso multi-purpose cleaners in the US and Canada due to potential bacterial contamination. Customers are advised to stop using and dispose of recalled products and can claim a refund, though no infections have been reported to date.

title: The Home Depot Announces Grants for 36 HBCUs at 2023 Retool Your School Awards Celebration
summary: The Home Depot awarded over $2 million in grants to 36 Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs) through its 2023 Retool Your School program.
