The program has invested over $9.25 million in HBCUs since its inception in 2009.

title: Nordstrom Rack coming to Jacksonville Beach
summary: Nordstrom Inc. announced it will open a new 30,000-square-foot Nordstrom Rack store in Jacksonville Beach in spring 2024. The store will be located in the South Beach Regional shopping center, taking over the former Stein Mart space. This addition will mark Nordstrom's 18th Nordstrom Rack store in Florida, alongside six full-line stores.

title: Fastenal Sales Up 9% in First Three Months of 2023
summary: Fastenal reported a 9% increase in sales to $1.86 billion in the first three months of 2023, exceeding Wall Street projections. The company's gross profit, operating income, and net earnings also saw significant increases. Fastenal attributed its strong performance to broad pricing actions, robust demand in industrial capital goods, and the expansion of its "Digital Footprint" operations.

title: How an American Logging Giant Bills Itself as a Climate Hero
summary: Weyerhaeuser, one of the world's largest timber companies, is promoting its logging activities as sustainable and a solution to climate change, despite plans to increase lumber production. The company is investing in carbon offsets from its vast forest holdings, claiming that replanting trees and using wood for products stores carbon. However, critics argue that the math is "fuzzy," as regrowing forests take decades to reach full sequestration strength and logging can lead to continued carbon emissions.

title: Pleasanton Home Depot employee Blake Mohs identified as victim shot, killed during shoplifting confrontation
summary: Blake Mohs, a 26-year-old Home Depot loss prevention employee, was shot and killed while confronting a shoplifting suspect in Pleasanton, California. He was engaged to be married in the summer. Two suspects have been arrested and face charges including murder and child endangerment.

title: Home Depot dog bite case should have been comp exclusive: State high court
summary: The Pennsylvania Supreme Court has ruled that a Home Depot dog bite case, where an employee was injured by a customer's dog, should fall under the exclusive jurisdiction of workers' compensation. This decision reverses lower court rulings that allowed the employee to pursue a negligence lawsuit against Home Depot, asserting that the workers' compensation law provides immunity to employers in such third-party actions. The court found that the case did not meet the criteria for exceptions to the workers' compensation exclusivity rule.

title: Stanley Black & Decker recalls about 2.2 million sledgehammers due to injury risk
summary: Stanley Black & Decker has issued a recall for approximately 2.2 million DeWALT, Stanley FATMAX, and Craftsman Fiberglass Sledgehammers due to a risk of the hammer heads detaching unexpectedly. This defect has led to 192 reported incidents, including two resulting in face and head injuries. Consumers are advised to stop using the recalled sledgehammers and contact Stanley Black & Decker for a refund.

title: Home Depot to open new location in Katy’s Cane Island
summary: The bustling Cane Island area of Katy, Texas, is set to welcome a new Home Depot store. The Katy City Council approved an economic development agreement with Home Depot USA Inc. for the new location. This development follows the city's annexation of a 24-acre plot of land to facilitate the project, which Mayor Dusty Thiele highlighted as an example of smart economic development for Katy.

title: Bed Bath & Beyond Files for Bankruptcy With Plan to Shut Stores
summary: Bed Bath & Beyond Inc. has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in New Jersey, planning to liquidate its 360 Bed Bath & Beyond stores and 120 Buy Buy Baby shops. The company is actively seeking a buyer for its assets, with the possibility of halting store closures if a successful sale occurs. This move puts thousands of jobs at risk as the retailer struggled to adapt to evolving consumer behaviors.

title: After Dog Bite at Work, Exclusivity Leashes Home Depot Employees Tort Claims
summary: The Pennsylvania Supreme Court ruled that a Home Depot employee bitten by a customer's dog at work could not sue the company beyond workers' compensation benefits due to the state's exclusivity provision. The court found that the injury was inextricably linked to the workplace incident, even though the employee argued Home Depot's negligence prevented a third-party suit against the dog owner. This decision upholds the principle that workers' compensation is generally the sole remedy for workplace injuries in Pennsylvania.

title: Long Island retail center anchored by ShopRite and Home Depot sold
summary: JLL Capital Markets facilitated the sale of Riverhead Centre in Riverhead, New York. This retail center is prominently anchored by major tenants ShopRite and Home Depot. The transaction highlights investment activity in the retail real estate sector.

title: Tractor Supply Is the Home Improvement Stock to Buy Now, Analyst Says
summary: An analyst suggests buying Tractor Supply stock, arguing it's a better home improvement play than Home Depot or Lowe's, despite a tough year for the sector. While first-quarter earnings for home improvement retailers might not be strong, the outlook for later in the year could improve.

title: The Home Depot Announces First Quarter Fiscal 2023 Results; Updates Fiscal 2023 Guidance
summary: The Home Depot reported first-quarter fiscal 2023 sales of $37.3 billion, a 4.2% decrease from the prior year, with comparable sales declining 4.5%. Net earnings were $3.9 billion, or $3.82 per diluted share. The company updated its fiscal 2023 guidance, expecting sales and comparable sales to decline between 2% and 5%, citing lumber deflation, unfavorable weather, and softening demand.

title: Home Depot Earnings Take a Hit as Company Sticks with ‘Woke’
summary: The National Legal and Policy Center (NLPC) presented a proposal at Home Depot's annual shareholder meeting to require an independent board chair, coinciding with a 4.2% drop in the company's Q1 revenue. NLPC attributes Home Depot's lagging performance compared to Lowe's and recent financial hits to its continued emphasis on ESG priorities. The organization warns that "woke agenda politics" could negatively impact Home Depot's business, citing examples like Disney and Anheuser-Busch.

title: The Home Depot Partners with Army & Air Force Exchange Service to Offer Tax-Free Major Appliances
summary: The Home Depot is partnering with the Army & Air Force Exchange Service (Exchange) to provide tax-free major appliances to eligible military shoppers. This program allows active-duty service members, their dependents, retirees, DoD civilians, and honorably discharged veterans to purchase appliances online through ShopMyExchange.com and in up to 60 planned Home Depot appliance showrooms at various military bases. The initiative reflects The Home Depot's commitment to supporting military families, with 100% of Exchange earnings benefiting military communities.

title: Lowe's stock bounces back, as U.S. same-store sales beat rival Home Depot for first time in more than 2 years
summary: Lowe's Companies Inc. saw its stock reverse to a gain after reporting fiscal first-quarter profit that exceeded expectations. Despite same-store sales missing forecasts, they surpassed those of rival Home Depot Inc. for the first time in over two years. Although Lowe's lowered its full-year guidance for earnings and revenue, the revised outlook still aligned with Wall Street's projections.

title: Costco earnings miss estimates as shoppers curb discretionary spending
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp (COST) missed quarterly earnings estimates as consumers reduced non-essential spending due to inflation and economic uncertainties. The retailer experienced a drop in demand for high-margin products like home furnishings and electronics, despite a rise in membership revenue. This trend also impacted other major retailers such as Target and Home Depot.

title: Costco earnings miss estimates as shoppers curb discretionary spending
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp missed quarterly earnings estimates as shoppers reduced discretionary spending due to high inflation and economic uncertainty. The warehouse retailer, like others, saw a decline in demand for high-margin non-essential items, leading to lower-than-expected profits and revenue. Despite this, membership revenue, which accounts for most of Costco's gross margin, increased.

title: The Home Depot to Host 2023 Investor and Analyst Conference on June 13
summary: The Home Depot announced it will host its 2023 Investor and Analyst Conference on Tuesday, June 13, at 9 a.m. ET. A webcast of the event will be available on the company's investor relations website, with a replay accessible approximately two hours after the event concludes. The company also provided details on its store count and market performance.

title: Gary Rasor | Son of Hillsborough Home Depot worker killed wants crackdown on theft, he tells 'Nightline'
summary: The son of Gary Rasor, a Home Depot employee who died after confronting a shoplifter, is calling for a crackdown on organized retail crime. Rasor, 83, was fatally injured while trying to stop someone stealing pressure washers. His son, Jeff Rasor, told "Nightline" that there need to be severe consequences for such crimes, emphasizing that no merchandise is worth a human life.

title: Home Depot Files Opening Brief in California Supreme Court Case Set to Determine Validity of Time Clock Rounding
summary: Home Depot has filed its opening brief in a California Supreme Court case challenging a Sixth District Court of Appeal ruling that found the company's total time rounding for non-exempt employees unlawful. The appellate court's decision in Camp v. Home Depot U.S.A., Inc. ignored prior precedent, asserting that employers must pay for all exact time worked if they can capture it. Critical to the appeal, the California Employment Law Council and the Employers Group have enlisted Sheppard Mullin to draft an amicus brief arguing for the continued validity of time rounding practices for employers in California.

title: The Home Depot now sells surprisingly stylish build-it-yourself tiny homes – for under $50,000
summary: The Home Depot is now selling surprisingly stylish build-it-yourself tiny homes for under $50,000. These pre-fabricated, one-bedroom homes range from $4,000 to $40,000 and can serve as an addition or a primary residence, offering a compact and accessible housing solution. While the initial price is attractive, buyers need to factor in additional costs for essential features like doors, windows, and electrical/plumbing systems.

title: The Home Depot Provides Update on Strategic Objectives; Reaffirms Fiscal 2023 Guidance; Establishes Market Stability Outlook
summary: The Home Depot held its 2023 Investor and Analyst Conference to discuss strategic objectives, reaffirming its fiscal 2023 guidance, which projects a sales and comparable sales decline of 2% to 5%. The company also established a "Market Stability Base Case" outlook, anticipating low-single-digit overall market growth and 3% to 4% annual sales growth once the home improvement market stabilizes. CEO Ted Decker highlighted the company's strong competitive advantages and significant growth opportunities within the fragmented home improvement market.

title: Big Changes Inside New York Home Depot Stores
summary: Home Depot stores in New York, including the Wappingers Falls location, are increasingly locking up various items like power tools and copper wire. This change is a response to high rates of shoplifting, making it necessary for customers to request employee assistance to handle or purchase these products. The new policy aims to deter theft, but it also means that shopping at Home Depot now takes longer for items that are under lock and key.

title: Glen Carbon panel approves Dick's Sporting Goods concept plan
summary: A Glen Carbon building and development committee approved the concept plan for Dick's Sporting Goods at the Orchard Town Center (OTC). This marks the first step toward bringing the store to Glen Carbon, with the company slated to occupy over 6.5 acres of the development. The approval also provided updates on the two-phase development, traffic improvements, remaining outlots, and plans for a greenspace with a stage and amphitheater.

title: P&G’s Vanished Forest Degradation Commitment
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) has removed its commitment to prohibit forest degradation from its latest forest sourcing policy, despite previous investor pressure. This move suggests a backtracking on responsible sourcing claims, leaving P&G as a continued driver of degradation in Canada's boreal forests, which has significant climate and biodiversity impacts. The NRDC highlights that P&G's previous claims were misleading and calls for a genuine commitment to eliminate forest degradation.

title: First Trust Exchange-Traded Fund III - First Trust Morningstar Dividend Leaders Index Fund (FDL) News, Articles, Events & Latest Updates
summary: This article provides recent news and updates for the First Trust Morningstar Dividend Leaders Index Fund (FDL). It highlights several financial articles discussing FDL and other dividend ETFs outperforming the S&P 500, offering current income, and gaining investor interest amid market volatility and sector rotations. The feed includes news from Zacks and Stocktwits discussing various dividend-focused investment strategies and company-specific financial reports impacting dividend stocks.

title: The Home Depot launches $500M cost-savings plan
summary: The Home Depot is implementing a $500 million cost-savings plan expected to be completed in fiscal year 2024. This initiative involves reducing excess supply chain holding capacity that was expanded due to increased demand during 2020 and 2021. The company is also optimizing its downstream supply chain through forecasting, labor management, and technology, while continuing to leverage past investments in supply chain infrastructure.

title: Home Depot adds automatic fee and customers need to watch out where they shopped
summary: Home Depot has introduced a 15% restocking fee on returned or canceled special orders, a policy that can lead to substantial charges due to the often high cost of these customized items. This policy differs from their standard no-fee return for most purchases. Other retailers like Levi's, Urban Outfitters, and Kohl's also have return fees, with some offering ways to avoid them such as in-store returns or membership programs.

title: Home Depot Wages Settlement
summary: Home Depot employees are seeking preliminary approval for a $72.5 million settlement in a California wage and hour class-action lawsuit. The lawsuit, brought under California's Private Attorneys General Act, alleges that Home Depot failed to pay employees for off-the-clock work, including time spent locked in stores after shifts, and for tasks like putting on aprons, impacting over 272,000 workers since March 2012. The settlement aims to resolve these allegations, with Home Depot denying wrongdoing but settling to avoid the costs of litigation.

title: Riot leverages Texas power strategy to fund operations as BTC balance increases
summary: Riot Platforms reported producing 460 Bitcoin in June 2023, a 40% decrease from May, but successfully leveraged its power strategy in Texas to generate $10 million in revenue, equivalent to an additional 361 BTC. This strategy, which involves participating in ERCOT's ancillary services and the Four Coincident Peak program, allowed Riot to avoid solely relying on Bitcoin sales for funding operations during a heatwave. The company also announced plans to significantly boost its hash rate with an order for 33,280 new MicroBT miners.

title: Rabina completes $13.5M refinance of Home Depot warehouse in Auburn
summary: New York real estate investment company Rabina has secured a $13.5 million refinancing for its 210,000-square-foot distribution center in Auburn, Massachusetts. The property at 26 Millbury St. is fully leased by an affiliate of The Home Depot. The refinancing, arranged by Kelleher & Sadowsky Associates with Rockland Trust, was sought due to existing debt maturity and current interest rate volatility.

title: Top Women: Meet the Class of 2023
summary: HBSDealer has announced the "Class of 2023" for its annual Top Women in Hardware & Building Supply event, recognizing leaders and rising stars in the industry. The honorees, selected from a record number of nominations, will be celebrated at a live event in Chicago on November 15-16. The initiative aims to promote the role of women and amplify their contributions to the hardware and building supply sector.

title: Beating the benchmark? How AI-driven ETFs stack up
summary: The article discusses the performance of AI-driven ETFs and whether they offer an information advantage in stock selection compared to traditional benchmarks. It highlights examples like the QRAFT AI-Enhanced U.S. Large Cap Momentum ETF (AMOM) and the AI Powered Equity ETF (AIEQ), noting AMOM's outperformance against a momentum benchmark while AIEQ trails the S&P 500. The piece also explores the potential benefits of AI in portfolio management, such as a lack of emotion and more frequent rebalancing.

title: Ahead of Earnings, Is Home Depot Stock a Buy, a Sell, or Fairly Valued?
summary: Ahead of its second-quarter earnings report on August 15, Morningstar assesses Home Depot (HD) stock as overvalued with a 2-star rating and a fair value estimate of $259. The analysis highlights concerns about slowing top-line momentum and discretionary spending, while also noting the company's wide economic moat due to its brand intangible asset and cost advantage. Investors are advised to watch for trends in consumer spending, pro backlog, and potential trade-downs in upcoming earnings.

title: $72.5M Settlement in California Home Depot Wage & Hour Class Action
summary: Home Depot has agreed to a $72.5 million settlement in a California wage and hour class action lawsuit. The lawsuit, filed by Utne in 2016, alleged the company violated labor laws by underpaying over 272,000 employees. The settlement aims to resolve claims ranging from unpaid "off the clock" work for closing shifts and shift preparation to lost pay due to the company's rounding policy for hours worked.

title: Markets News, Aug. 15, 2023: Dow Drops More Than 350 Points on U.S. Banking Concerns, Weakening Chinese Economy
summary: U.S. stocks, including the Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq, fell due to concerns over the creditworthiness of U.S. banks, a potential downgrade by Fitch Ratings, and a weakening Chinese economy. The Chinese central bank cut a key interest rate, while the U.K. saw record wage growth. Individual stock movers included Amgen and Home Depot rising, while JPMorgan Chase, American Express, Goldman Sachs, Dow Inc., Caterpillar, 3M, Chevron, and Walt Disney Co. declined.

title: O’Reilly Auto Parts opens new store in Caguas
summary: O’Reilly Auto Parts has opened its third store in Puerto Rico, located in Caguas, expanding its presence which includes two other stores and a distribution center. The new 15,000-square-foot store at Las Catalinas Mall will offer sale prices from August 16-29, with a grand opening celebration on August 19. This expansion represents a significant investment by the company in Puerto Rico, creating jobs and ensuring quick parts delivery from its Bayamón distribution center.

title: A Class Action Lawsuit Against Amazon & Wayfair Was Approved In Quebec & You Could Be Owed Money
summary: A class action lawsuit against Amazon, Wayfair, and Home Depot has been approved in Quebec, potentially entitling consumers who purchased extended warranties between 2019 and 2023 to compensation. The lawsuit alleges that these companies violated Quebec's Consumer Protection Act by not adequately informing customers about existing warranties. While Home Depot has already reached a settlement, Amazon and Wayfair's cases are still pending, with affected customers in Quebec eligible for reimbursement and punitive damages.

title: Walmart and Target executives speak out on retail crime
summary: Executives from Walmart and Target are raising concerns about the persistent issue of retail crime and organized retail theft, which continues to impact company profits and employee safety. Both CEOs, Doug McMillon of Walmart and Brian Cornell of Target, highlighted the financial strain ("shrink") caused by these thefts, with Target expecting a half-billion-dollar hit to profits. They emphasized the need for action, particularly at the local jurisdictional level, to combat this growing problem.

title: Introducing Limitless: GLIDDEN Paint by PPG’s ‘Anything but Yellow’ 2024 Color of the Year
summary: PPG's Glidden paint brand has announced "Limitless" (PPG1091-3) as its 2024 Color of the Year. This warm honey beige hue is described as a versatile neutral, suitable for various design styles and applications in both residential and commercial spaces. Glidden color experts state that this modern neutral signals the end of cool grays, embracing a new era of warmer tones.

title: Advance Auto Names New CEO Shane O’Kelly
summary: Advance Auto Parts Inc. has appointed Shane O’Kelly, formerly of Home Depot Inc.’s HD Supply unit, as its new CEO, effective September 11, following a quarter where profits missed estimates and the company lowered its outlook. The company also initiated a strategic review of its business as it grapples with inflation and a significant drop in its stock value this year. O’Kelly replaces Tom Greco, who will remain as an adviser for an unspecified period.

title: Advance Auto Parts Announces Executive Leadership Changes
summary: Advance Auto Parts has announced key executive leadership changes, appointing Shane O’Kelly as the new president and CEO, effective September 11, 2023. O’Kelly, former CEO of HD Supply and PetroChoice, succeeds Tom Greco, who is retiring. Additionally, Tony Iskander has been named interim chief financial officer following Jeff Shepherd's departure, with a search initiated for a permanent CFO.

title: Boise Cascade agrees to purchase door and millwork company
summary: Boise Cascade has announced its agreement to acquire Brockway-Smith Co. (BROSCO), a wholesale distributor specializing in doors and millwork, for $172 million. This acquisition will expand Boise Cascade's millwork business with BROSCO's two distribution centers and extensive product offerings. The transaction is expected to finalize in early Q4 2023, pending customary closing conditions and antitrust approval.

title: Advance Auto Parts falls out of the S&P 500 and names new CEO
summary: Advance Auto Parts is undergoing significant leadership changes and an operational review following a sharp drop in its stock price and removal from the S&P 500. Shane O'Kelly will replace Tom Greco as CEO, and CFO Jeffrey Shepherd is also departing. The company, facing supply shortages and wage inflation, aims for profitable growth within a year, while analysts note competitors have not experienced similar issues.

title: Home Depot SWOT Analysis (2026)
summary: This article provides a comprehensive SWOT analysis of Home Depot, examining its strengths such as helpful staff, online shopping, and strong brand, alongside weaknesses like inadequate store layout and high prices. It also explores opportunities in the home renovation market and smart technology, and threats including intense competition and economic fluctuations. The analysis concludes that strategic planning and customer-centric approaches are crucial for Home Depot to maintain its market leadership.

title: Dollar Tree Threatens to "Discontinue" Products Over Theft Concerns
summary: Dollar Tree is considering drastic measures, including discontinuing products, to combat rising retail theft that has impacted its recent profits. The company's CFO attributed a decline in financial results to "unfavorable shrink trends" and other factors. CEO Rick Dreiling announced new anti-theft strategies, potentially leading to fewer items on shelves or products being removed from inventory entirely.

title: Shoppers Are Abandoning Dick’s Sporting Goods, Data Shows—Here’s Why
summary: Dick's Sporting Goods recently reported a 23 percent drop in profits and failed to meet Wall Street expectations for its second fiscal quarter, despite an overall increase in sales driven by the back-to-school season. Factors contributing to this decline include macroeconomic uncertainties such as the upcoming student loan payment resumptions, a decrease in outdoor gear sales, and a significant impact from "shrink" (theft, damage, and cashier error). The company has reduced its global workforce by less than 1 percent, primarily in customer support, and expects flat to 2 percent sales growth for 2023.

title: The Top Fifty, revisited
summary: This article revisits the HBSDealer Top 150 Industry Leaderboard, focusing on observations beyond just sales figures for the top fifty companies. It highlights key strategic moves, financial performances, and leadership changes for major players like Home Depot, Lowe's, and Builders FirstSource, as well as significant developments for companies ranging from 11th to 50th on the list.

title: The Home Depot Introduces Decor Days to Offer Big Style Savings for Holiday Prep
summary: The Home Depot is launching its first-ever "Decor Days" event from October 5-9, 2023, offering significant savings on home decor, furniture, and other related products. This event aims to help customers prepare their homes for the holiday season with stylish updates and DIY projects at competitive prices. Exclusive discounts of up to 60% will be available on national and proprietary brands through HomeDepot.com/decor.

title: Residential demand for lawn equipment plummets, leading to rare Toro quarterly loss
summary: Toro experienced a rare quarterly loss due to plummeting residential and professional lawn equipment demand, attributed to dry weather, economic uncertainty, and pandemic-era purchases. To address this, the company announced a new retail partnership with Lowe's for next spring. Despite stronger performance in other business segments, Toro's stock dropped, and the company reduced its sales and earnings guidance for the remainder of the year.

title: Homesense building-out at Riverplace Shopping Center
summary: Homesense, an off-price home decor retailer owned by TJX Companies, is building out its new store at Riverplace Shopping Center in Mandarin, Jacksonville. The city issued a permit for the $2.14 million remodel of the former Stein Mart store. Homesense is actively hiring for various positions at the new 36,076-square-foot location, which will offer a wide array of home goods at discounted prices.

title: Home Depot Slammed Over Botched Appliance Delivery
summary: A Massachusetts man is accusing Home Depot of a botched appliance delivery after paying for premium "white glove" service for over $10,000 worth of appliances. The man claims the appliances were left on his front lawn, leading to mold growth and damage, despite his efforts to facilitate easy access. Home Depot has since apologized, acknowledging a miscommunication regarding shipping options for the specific brand purchased, and is working to replace the damaged units.

title: The Zacks Analyst Blog Highlights Walmart, The Home Depot and Costco Wholesale
summary: The Zacks Analyst Blog highlights Walmart, Home Depot, and Costco Wholesale as top blue-chip retail stocks for stable, long-term investment. These companies are praised for their financial resilience, consistent growth, and ability to weather economic downturns, making them dependable choices for investors. Each company's strategic initiatives, market capitalization, earnings expectations, and dividend payouts are detailed to showcase their strong investment potential.

title: Lowe's Cos. stock falls Friday, underperforms market
summary: Lowe's Cos. (LOW) stock fell by 4.70% on Friday, closing at $220.02, underperforming the broader market as both the S&P 500 Index and Dow Jones Industrial Average also declined. The stock closed $17.19 below its 52-week high reached on July 27th.

title: The Home Depot Announces 2023 Innovation Award Winners
summary: The Home Depot announced the winners of its 2023 Innovation Awards, recognizing products that enhance efficiency for both Pros and DIYers. Leviton's Decora Edge™ was named the overall winner for its safer and more efficient light switch and outlet installations. Other top honors went to Ecolab Scientific Clean Line for bringing professional-grade cleaning solutions to homes and Glidden Cool Touch Exterior Floor Paint for its temperature-reducing technology.

title: Home Depot is selling a tiny home for $6,000 - customers say it's 'very sturdy'
summary: Home Depot is selling a Colonial Williamsburg DIY shed kit that can be converted into a tiny home for just over $6,000. Customers praise its sturdiness and ease of assembly. The kit measures 8 by 12 feet, includes a floor, and features fungal decay and termite-resistant paneling with a 50-year rot-resistant warranty.

title: Target announces nine store closures, cites 'organized retail crime'
summary: Target announced it would close nine stores in major cities across the U.S., explicitly blaming retail theft and organized retail crime for the decision. The closures, representing less than 1% of Target's total stores, will affect locations in New York City, Seattle, San Francisco, Oakland, and Portland. This move comes after Target's CEO previously noted a worsening trend in retail theft affecting safety, product availability, and business performance.

title: PPG receives top honors for product innovation, DE&I at The Home Depot’s 2023 Innovation Awards
summary: PPG has been recognized with two top honors at The Home Depot’s 2023 Innovation Awards: a second runner-up Innovation Award for its GLIDDEN® floor paint and concrete stain featuring COOL SURFACE TECHNOLOGY™ and the first-time Supplier Diversity Tier II Partner of the Year award. These accolades highlight PPG's commitment to delivering innovative products that simplify projects for both professionals and DIY customers, as well as its dedication to advancing diversity, equity, and inclusion within its business practices and supply chain. The Cool Surface Technology formulation limits surface temperatures by up to 20 percent, while the diversity award recognizes PPG's consistent performance in supporting diverse suppliers.

title: Home Depot Tracked a Crime Ring and Found an Unusual Suspect
summary: Home Depot and Florida law enforcement busted an organized retail crime ring led by Robert Dell, a pastor who ran a drug recovery program. Dell allegedly instructed individuals in his program to steal tools from Home Depot stores, which he then resold online for profit. The operation, which involved $3 million in stolen goods sold since 2016, resulted in Dell and four others being arrested and charged with racketeering and dealing in stolen property.

title: Tractor Supply’s Unsung Apparel Edge
summary: Tractor Supply Co. is actively expanding its apparel business, which already accounts for $1.2 billion to $1.3 billion in annual sales. The retailer is focusing on workwear and Western-inspired fashion, utilizing social media, brand partnerships, and shops-in-shop to attract a younger, more suburban customer base. Despite solid financial performance, the potential of its apparel segment is often underrated compared to other business strategies.

title: Greener Pastures for the Housing Market
summary: The U.S. housing market is projected to recover, driven by eased pressures from high interest rates, prices, and supply shortages, with new-home construction expected to rise 2% in 2024. This recovery presents significant opportunities for sustainable investing, particularly in green home construction and renovation, bolstered by environmentally conscious consumers, government incentives, and decreasing costs of clean technologies. Equity strategists anticipate growth in sustainable housing as demand for eco-friendly building practices aligns with the broader market's resurgence.

title: Papa Johns Appoints John Garratt And Stephen Gibbs To The Board
summary: Papa John's International, Inc. (PZZA) has appointed John Garratt, former President and CFO of Dollar General, and Stephen Gibbs, former Chief Accounting Officer and Corporate Controller at The Home Depot, to its Board of Directors. These appointments expand the board to 10 directors, with eight being independent. Both individuals bring extensive financial leadership and corporate strategy experience to help guide Papa Johns' growth plans.

title: Dallas-Based Spirit Realty Capital Acquired in $9.3 Billion Deal
summary: Dallas-based Spirit Realty Capital is being acquired by San Diego-based Realty Income Corporation in an all-stock transaction valued at $9.3 billion. This merger will create a combined company with an enterprise value of approximately $63 billion, enhancing Realty Income's size, scale, and diversification. Spirit shareholders will receive 0.762 newly-issued Realty Income common shares for each Spirit common share they own, resulting in them owning approximately 13% of the combined company.

title: Homesense Opens New Store in Jacksonville, FL
summary: Homesense, part of the TJX family of brands, is opening a new store in Jacksonville, FL on November 2nd at the Riverplace Shopping Center. The store offers a wide range of home furnishings, decor, and seasonal items at discounted prices, with new merchandise regularly arriving. To celebrate the opening, Homesense will donate $10,000 to Habitat for Humanity of Jacksonville.

title: Why Home Depot is evolving its media strategy, starting with branded content
summary: Home Depot is changing its media strategy by focusing on branded content, beginning with a shoppable CTV series on Vizio for the holiday season. The series, titled ‘Merry & Bright,’ stars Jordin Sparks and aims to engage early holiday shoppers. This move signifies Home Depot's evolving approach to reaching consumers through diverse media channels.

title: Home Depot co-founder: My customers are 'getting killed' by Biden’s inflation
summary: Home Depot co-founder Bernie Marcus criticized President Biden's economic policies, stating that inflation is severely impacting American consumers and Home Depot customers. He highlighted that despite a decline from its peak, inflation remains nearly double the Federal Reserve's target, causing hardship for middle-class Americans struggling with the rising costs of necessities. Marcus also mentioned the Federal Reserve's decision to keep interest rates unchanged while leaving open the possibility of further hikes to combat persistent inflation.

title: Days before investor call, Kohl's board chair announces he's not seeking re-election in 2024
summary: Kohl's board chair Peter Boneparth is stepping down in May 2024 after 15 years, with Michael Bender appointed as his successor. This announcement comes days before the company's quarterly investor call, following past proxy fights and a CEO change. Additionally, Adolfo Villagomez has been appointed as a new independent director, bringing e-commerce and marketing expertise.

title: Target earnings up, food sales slip
summary: Target Corporation reported a 36% increase in net earnings for the third quarter ending October 28, despite a 4.2% drop in revenue. The company's CEO, Brian C. Cornell, attributed the earnings growth to lower freight costs, efficient inventory management, and operational efficiencies, which helped offset a decline in discretionary spending. While overall sales decreased, Target's food and beverage category saw only a slight dip, with seasonal snacks performing well, and the company plans to offer holiday deals on turkeys and side dishes.

title: Best Pellet Grill Black Friday & Cyber Monday Deals (2023): Weber, Traeger, Pit Boss & More Savings Highlighted by Retail Egg
summary: Retail Egg has compiled a list of the best Black Friday and Cyber Monday 2023 deals on pellet grills from various brands, including Weber, Traeger, Pit Boss, Z Grills, and Camp Chef. Shoppers can find significant savings, with discounts reaching up to $450 on some models. The article directs consumers to retailer websites like ZGrills.com, Walmart.com, Traeger.com, Weber.com, BBQGuys.com, PitBoss-Grills.com, GrillaGrills.com, and TractorSupply.com to access these deals.

title: The electric revolution is coming for your lawn mower
summary: California is set to ban the sale of new gasoline-powered lawn mowers and other landscaping tools starting in 2024, aiming to reduce emissions from small off-road engines that pollute more than all cars in the state combined. This move highlights a broader push towards electric technologies in daily life, impacting manufacturers and consumers alike. While electric alternatives offer environmental benefits, challenges such as higher upfront costs and performance concerns are debated.

title: Final Thoughts From Charlie Munger on Apple, Warren Buffett, and the Big Costco Error
summary: This article compiles insights from Charlie Munger's final interviews, focusing on his investment philosophy, partnership with Warren Buffett, and specific investments. It covers his views on Apple, the "big Costco error" by Buffett, and Munger's perspectives on retailing, China, and company valuations. The article highlights how Munger influenced Buffett's investment strategy and his own unique approach to identifying valuable companies.

title: Home Depot highlights trade labor gap in new campaign
summary: Home Depot has launched a new campaign to address the significant labor gap in the construction industry. The company, which has a substantial business catering to construction professionals, is drawing attention to this issue. The article briefly mentions other related marketing news, including AI in campaigns and weekly marketing winners and losers.

title: Costco, Home Depot and Floor & Decor: Diverging Outcomes From a Similar Model
summary: This article analyzes the business models and operational efficiencies of Costco, Home Depot, and Floor & Decor, highlighting their diverging outcomes despite similar approaches. Costco excels in efficiency, profitability, and customer loyalty through its volume-driven strategy and superior inventory turnover and cash conversion cycles. While Home Depot shows strong profitability and ROI, and Floor & Decor faces challenges in inventory and cash conversion.

title: She conceived of Pottery Barn Kids. Now Williams Sonoma’s CEO is expanding another new business—furnishing hotels and stadiums
summary: Laura Alber, CEO of Williams Sonoma, is recognized as the longest-serving female CEO in the Fortune 500, having led the company for 13 years after starting as a senior buyer in 1995. Despite various market challenges like the retail apocalypse and housing slowdown, Williams Sonoma's stock has outperformed the market under her leadership. Alber is now focusing on new growth opportunities, including expanding the company's B2B business to furnish hotels and stadiums, international expansion, and integrating AI into home design services.

title: 8 Retail Stocks Whose Price and Fundamentals Don’t Line Up
summary: This article discusses eight retail stocks where the market price does not align with the underlying financial fundamentals, particularly following a significant stock market rally. It suggests that some recent gains in these stocks might be less stable than others.

title: Traeger Pellet Grills Recalls Flat Top Propane Grills Due to Fire Hazard
summary: Traeger Pellet Grills has issued a recall for approximately 37,000 Flatrock Flat Top Propane Grills due to a fire hazard. This move sets a higher standard in the industry, aiming to reduce forest degradation, particularly in critical northern forests, and includes commitments to Indigenous communities' rights. The policy puts pressure on competitors like Procter & Gamble and aligns with increasing global regulatory scrutiny on deforestation and forest degradation.

title: The Home Depot Announces Expiration of Hart-Scott-Rodino Act Waiting Period
summary: The Home Depot announced the expiration of the Hart-Scott-Rodino (HSR) Act waiting period for its acquisition of SRS Distribution Inc. This satisfies a key condition for the transaction, which is now expected to close around June 18, 2024, subject to customary closing conditions. The company also included a comprehensive forward-looking statements disclaimer detailing potential risks.

title: Resideo Completes Acquisition of Snap One
summary: Resideo Technologies, Inc. announced the completion of its acquisition of Snap One for approximately $1.4 billion. This acquisition is expected to expand Resideo's presence in smart living products and distribution, enhance its growth and margin profile, and be accretive to non-GAAP Adjusted EPS in the first full year of ownership. Following the closing, Nate Sleeper and John Stroup of Clayton, Dubilier & Rice LLC joined Resideo's Board of Directors.

title: Weil Advises The Home Depot in its $18.25B Acquisition of SRS
summary: Weil, Gotshal & Manges LLP advised The Home Depot on its acquisition of SRS Distribution Inc. for approximately $18.25 billion. The transaction involves Home Depot acquiring SRS, a leading residential specialty trade distribution company serving professional roofers, landscapers, and pool contractors. A large Weil team, including partners Michael J. Aiello and Eoghan Keenan, handled various aspects of the deal.

title: The Home Depot Completes Acquisition of SRS Distribution
summary: The Home Depot has finalized its acquisition of SRS Distribution, Inc. for approximately $18.25 billion, as announced on March 28, 2024. This acquisition significantly expands The Home Depot's addressable market and strengthens its position in serving residential professional customers across various specialty trade verticals, including roofing, landscaping, and pool contracting. The integration of SRS is expected to accelerate Home Depot's growth in this segment and enhance its service offerings.

title: Home Depot Buys SRS Distribution As DIY Giants Turn To Pro Market
summary: Home Depot has acquired SRS Distribution Inc. for approximately $18.25 billion, aiming to expand its reach in the professional contractor market, which it estimates will increase its total addressable market to $1 trillion. This acquisition is part of a strategy to better serve residential professional customers for complex projects, especially as DIY sales have softened. The move reflects a broader trend among DIY giants to focus on pro markets to bolster growth.

title: Home Depot (HD) Buys SRS Distribution, Reaches $1 Trillion TAM
summary: Home Depot (HD) has finalized its acquisition of SRS Distribution for $18.25 billion, expanding its total addressable market to $1 trillion. This acquisition is expected to boost Home Depot's Pro business by offering more fulfillment and service options to residential professional customers. The company continues to invest in strategic initiatives, including its "One Home Depot" plan, to enhance its interconnected retail strategy and Pro capabilities.

title: Shares of swimming-pool makers slide after warning about weakening demand
summary: Pool Corp. issued a profit warning for 2024, citing weak demand for new pools, causing shares of swimming-pool makers to decline. The company projects new-pool construction activity to fall 15% to 20% and remodel activity to decrease by as much as 15%. This grim outlook from an industry leader indicates a slowdown in consumer spending on swimming pools and related equipment.

title: Home Depot and Lowe’s Target the Pros
summary: Home Depot and Lowe's are increasingly focusing on professional builders and contractors, a segment that accounts for a significant portion of their revenue, despite individual consumers driving the majority of sales. This shift comes as the general home improvement market slows down due to high mortgage rates and changing consumer spending habits post-pandemic. Both companies are implementing strategies, including acquisitions and specialized services, to capture a larger share of the pro market, which collectively represents nearly $100 billion in annual sales for the two giants.

title: EXCLUSIVE: Home Depot builds retail media network around DIY needs
summary: The Home Depot has developed its retail media network, Orange Apron Media, to better connect brands with its unique DIY customer base. Launched in 2018 and upgraded in March 2024, the network helps suppliers like Scotts target residential and professional customers at crucial points in their buying journeys. Home Depot plans to expand its focus to multicultural and pro audiences, leveraging its brand trust for greater impact.

title: How A Broken Furnace Led To An Innovative New Power Solution
summary: Entrepreneurs Pierre Delforge and Jane Melia, both Ph.D. Cambridge University engineers, founded Harvest Thermal after their home furnace broke in 2018. Their company developed the Smart Thermal Battery, which combines heat pump technology with thermal energy storage to reduce home emissions, lower heating bills, and provide superior comfort. Harvest Thermal's system has gained recognition and awards, securing nearly $11 million in funding, and is expanding its reach in new construction, home retrofits, and multi-family housing.

title: Tractor Supply Co. Just Made a Bold Change to Drop DEI at the End of Pride Month
summary: Tractor Supply Co. announced it would be eliminating its DEI department at the end of Pride Month, a decision influenced by a conservative activist campaign. This move follows similar quiet cutbacks in DEI funding by other major companies, despite general public support for DEI initiatives, highlighting a correlation between DEI support and political affiliation. The article suggests that for companies with a conservative customer base, pulling back on DEI might be a smarter business move to avoid controversy.

title: 4 Reasons to Buy Home Depot Stock Like There's No Tomorrow
summary: This article argues for investing in Home Depot stock, highlighting four key reasons. It emphasizes Home Depot's market dominance and vast network, its reliable dividend history despite occasional growth pauses, the current 14% discount from its recent high making it a good buying opportunity, and the anticipated recovery in the homebuilding market which will benefit the company.

title: Beloved retail chain with 400 locations to close down store after 24 years - and enters 'final phase' sales up to 70%
summary: A Bassett Furniture franchisee in Redmond, Washington, is closing its store after 24 years, offering final sales with discounts up to 70% on rugs and up to 65% on other furniture. The liquidation sale began in April, with the last day for shoppers being July 7, 2024. This closure follows Bassett Furniture Industries, Inc. reporting an operating loss, though no new corporately owned stores are planned for 2024.

title: Home Depot fined $1.6M for allegedly selling environmentally harmful refrigerant in Washington
summary: The Home Depot has been fined $1.6 million by the Washington State Department of Ecology for allegedly selling banned products containing environmentally harmful hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs). Despite repeated attempts by the Department of Ecology to ensure compliance between 2001 and 2003, Home Depot continued to sell an automotive HFC refrigerant called R-134a through its website in Washington, with 1,058 units sold during that period. The company has 30 days to appeal the penalty.

title: Report: North American furniture market to experience significant growth
summary: A report by Allied Market Research predicts significant growth in the North American furniture market, with its value projected to reach over $400 billion by 2030. The residential segment, driven by increased consumer spending, urbanization, and work-from-home trends, is expected to maintain the largest market share. The commercial segment is also forecast to grow rapidly due to companies investing in comfortable office environments, though raw material price increases pose a potential challenge.

title: Macy’s hires new CIO from within
summary: Macy's Inc. is promoting Keith Credendino to Chief Information Officer, effective August 4, 2024. He will replace Laura Miller, who is retiring. Credendino has been with Macy's for over two years, having previously held positions at Inspire Brands, The Home Depot, and other companies. His promotion comes at a turbulent time for Macy's, which is facing a takeover bid, board changes, and plans to close 150 locations.

title: Home Depot overcharges customers for rentals class action claims
summary: A new class action lawsuit alleges that Home Depot systematically overcharged customers using its tool rental service by charging excessive late fees and inflated Damage Protection costs. The lawsuit claims Home Depot's practices violate consumer laws and breach its own rental contracts from two distinct periods: 2015-2019 and 2022-present. E&G Enterprise Inc. is seeking to represent all impacted Home Depot customers nationwide to recover damages and legal costs.

title: VCR: Consumer Discretionary Sector Dashboard For July (NYSEARCA:VCR)
summary: This monthly article series provides a dashboard with aggregate subsector metrics in the Consumer Discretionary sector, highlighting that consumer services are the most attractive subsector based on value and quality scores. It also points out that the auto and components industry is below its baseline for both scores. The article suggests Vanguard Consumer Discretionary Index Fund ETF Shares (VCR) as an alternative to XLY and identifies nine stocks that were cheaper than their peers in July 2024.

title: Conn's HomePlus stores closing nationwide after company filed bankruptcy
summary: Conn's HomePlus, a home goods retailer, is closing several stores after filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy on July 23. This move follows three consecutive years of fiscal losses and an over 80 percent drop in shares in 2023. The company, founded over 130 years ago, has listed 174 stores for closure, including six in Tennessee and two in Mississippi, and is holding a going-out-of-business sale.

title: Dollar Tree selling $1.25 dinner essential - 94% cheaper than Williams-Sonoma
summary: Dollar Tree is selling Royal Norfolk Stoneware Dinner Plates for $1.25, which are a dupe for Williams-Sonoma's Le Creuset Vancouver Dinner Plates that cost $20 each. This makes the Dollar Tree plates 94% cheaper. Shoppers are praising the quality of these budget-friendly plates and Dollar Tree is also noted for its other popular dupes, including beauty products from Five Below.

title: Going Into Earnings, Is Home Depot Stock a Buy, a Sell, or Fairly Valued?
summary: Ahead of its Q2 earnings report, Morningstar assesses Home Depot stock as overvalued with a 1-star rating despite increasing its fair value estimate to $270 after incorporating the SRS acquisition. The article details what to watch for in the Q2 earnings, the impact of the SRS acquisition on financial outlook, and Home Depot's competitive advantages, financial strength, and risk profile. Morningstar rates Home Depot with a wide economic moat and a low uncertainty rating.

title: 11th Circuit Sides With Home Depot in 401(k) Excessive Fee Lawsuit
summary: The 11th Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed a lower court's decision in a 401(k) excessive fee lawsuit against The Home Depot Inc. The ruling places the burden of proof on workers to show how the company's conduct caused them to suffer losses, diverging from rulings in several other circuits. The case, Pizarro et al. v. The Home Depot Inc. et al., involved allegations that Home Depot offered imprudent investment options with higher fees than similar plans.

title: Michaels bolsters same-day delivery with DoorDash, Uber Eats
summary: Michaels is expanding its same-day delivery services by partnering with DoorDash and Uber Eats, making crafting supplies and home decor available from over 1,200 stores nationwide. This move aims to enhance omnichannel experience, convenience, and reach new audiences, mirroring a broader trend of retailers using on-demand delivery platforms beyond restaurant services. Other businesses like Home Depot and Lowe's have also ramped up their same-day delivery offerings.

title: 11th Circuit Appeals Court Rules With Home Depot on 401(k) Fee Suit
summary: The U.S. 11th Circuit Court of Appeals sided with Home Depot in an excessive 401(k) fee lawsuit, affirming a lower court's decision that the plaintiffs failed to prove Home Depot's conduct caused their losses. This ruling highlights a circuit split, as other appellate courts and the Department of Labor place the burden of proof on fiduciaries once a breach and loss are established. The court reiterated that plaintiffs must demonstrate that a hypothetical prudent fiduciary would not have made the same investment choices, concluding that Home Depot's decisions were "objectively prudent."

title: Investors - Governance - Board of Directors - Person Details
summary: This page introduces Keith Credendino as the Chief Information Officer of Macy's, Inc., a role he assumed in August 2024. It details his responsibilities, which include overseeing information technology applications, infrastructure, and operations that support Macy's' data-first modernization strategy. The article also highlights his previous experience at Macy's as Senior Vice President, Technology Product Development, Customer Experience, and prior roles at Inspire Brands, The Home Depot, InterContinental Hotels Group, and Cox Enterprises, emphasizing his expertise in large-scale e-commerce, loyalty systems, and cloud-native infrastructure.

title: Home Depot reports another quarter of soft earnings as potential rate cut comes into view
summary: Home Depot reported soft earnings for the seventh consecutive quarter, with revenue of $43.18 billion and adjusted EPS of $4.67, missing revenue expectations. The decline is attributed to high interest rates and cautious consumer spending on major home improvement projects. The company anticipates a turnaround with potential interest rate cuts, with fiscal 2024 guidance updated to expect total sales to increase by 2.5% to 3.5%, while comparable sales are projected to decline between 3% and 4%.

title: Home Depot’s stock bounces as home improvement demand may have just bottomed
summary: Shares of Home Depot Inc. bounced on Tuesday despite the company reporting worse-than-forecast fiscal second-quarter comparable sales and a cut in its full-year profit outlook. The rebound was driven by an implication that lower interest rates could stimulate interest in large home improvement projects, leading the company to raise its total sales growth guidance. This suggests that the demand for home improvement services might be nearing a bottom, potentially driven by anticipated monetary policy shifts.

title: Stocks of Lowe's, Behr paint seller Masco get a boost after Home Depot earnings
summary: Shares of home improvement companies, including Lowe's and Masco, saw a boost after Home Depot's earnings report and favorable inflation data. While Home Depot missed sales expectations due to high interest rates impacting demand for larger projects, optimism grew that demand would improve once the Federal Reserve starts lowering rates. This led to stock gains across the sector, including paint sellers and building material suppliers.

title: Qualified Remodeler's ‘TOP 500’ Residential Remodelers Offers Insights on $500 billion R&R Market
summary: Qualified Remodeler has released its 46th annual TOP 500 list, highlighting that the largest residential remodelers generated $21.7 billion in sales from 2.1 million jobs, an increase from $19.9 billion the previous year. This growth occurred despite challenging market conditions, with specialty home improvement firms showing the fastest expansion. The article also announces the upcoming TOP 500 LIVE conference in October.

title: Walmart Overtakes PepsiCo on Top 100 Private Carriers List
summary: Walmart Inc. has become the largest private motor carrier in North America, reaching No. 1 on Transport Topics' Top 100 Private Carriers list for the first time since 2002. This move unseats longtime leader PepsiCo Inc., driven by Walmart's expansion of its fleet to 12,663 power units and investments in its driver training programs. The updated list also highlights significant changes due to mergers and acquisitions, introducing several new companies to the Top 100 rankings.

title: Conn’s Closures Leave Behind A Swath Of Empty Retail, Industrial Space In Texas
summary: Conn’s Inc.'s Chapter 11 bankruptcy filing will result in 174 Conn’s HomePlus stores and 380 Badcock Home Furniture stores closing, leaving millions of square feet of retail and industrial space empty across Texas. The closures are expected to have a significant impact on Texas's commercial real estate market, particularly given Conn's large existing footprint in the state, including 83 locations and nearly 4M SF of industrial space. Despite the potential for landlords to re-tenant spaces and raise rents due to strong market fundamentals, the large floor plates of Conn's stores and the possibility of a "domino effect" on smaller tenants could present challenges.

title: Lowe’s Cuts Full-Year Guidance Amid Soft Housing Market
summary: Lowe's has lowered its full-year guidance due to a softened housing market, leading to reduced consumer spending on home renovations and DIY projects. The retailer now anticipates comparable sales to fall by 3.5% to 4%, a steeper decline than its previous forecast, and expects lighter adjusted earnings. Despite this, Lowe's reports making progress with professional customers.

title: New: Roofing Material Market to Increase 57% by 2034
summary: A new report by Future Market Insights forecasts the global roofing material market to reach over $231 billion by 2034, growing at a CAGR of 4.6%. The U.S. domestic market is expected to hit $29 billion in the same period. This growth is attributed to increasing global construction, rising demand for energy-efficient solutions, and technological advancements in materials.

title: Unlock Homebuilder Gains: ITB vs. XHB—Which ETF Is Your Golden Ticket to Housing Market Success ?
summary: This article provides a detailed comparison of two homebuilder ETFs, ITB and XHB, to help investors decide which is better suited for their portfolios. It analyzes their fund composition, performance, expense ratios, and risk profiles, highlighting ITB's concentrated exposure to home builders and XHB's diversified approach. The piece aims to guide investors in aligning their ETF choice with their investment goals and risk tolerance in the dynamic U.S. housing market.

title: Hertz adds former Home Depot CEO and ex-GM general counsel to its board
summary: Hertz Global Holdings has appointed Frank Blake, former CEO of The Home Depot, and Lucy Clark Dougherty, former GM deputy general counsel, to its board of directors. These additions aim to strengthen the board with their extensive experience in business, government, law, and driving business transformation. Their diverse backgrounds are expected to help steer the company toward future success.

title: Home Depot Sued Over Use of Plan Forfeitures
summary: Home Depot Inc. is facing a lawsuit from a former employee alleging misuse of 401(k) plan forfeitures. The complaint, filed in U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Georgia, claims the company breached ERISA duties by using forfeited funds to reduce employer contributions instead of covering administrative expenses. This case follows similar lawsuits against other major employers regarding 401(k) forfeiture practices.

title: The Home Depot Inc (HD): Is It a Buy? – Acquirer’s Multiple Stock Screener Analysis
summary: This article analyzes The Home Depot Inc (HD) using The Acquirer's Multiple stock screener, highlighting its position as the world's largest home improvement retailer. It details the company's operational footprint, recent strategic acquisitions, and key financial metrics that suggest it may be undervalued. The analysis points to the stock's 14.32% increase over the past year and provides several financial indicators supporting its potential as a 'buy'.

title: Mandarin Kmart building cleared for demolition for new Home Depot
summary: The former Kmart building at 9600 San Jose Blvd in Mandarin, which has been closed since 2016, is approved for demolition. Home Depot plans to build a new 132,975-square-foot store, including a large garden center, on the 11.64-acre site. The Jacksonville City Council rezoned the property for this purpose in May, and the demolition permit was issued on September 6, 2024.

title: Wood Products Market Opportunities and Strategies to 2033:
summary: The global wood products market is projected to grow from $788.45 billion in 2023 to $1.58 trillion by 2033, driven by increasing focus on home renovation, infrastructure development, demand for energy-efficient buildings, and rapid urbanization. The report highlights key segments like finished wood products and the offline distribution channel as major growth areas, with Asia-Pacific dominating the market and the Middle East and Africa showing the fastest growth. Strategies for companies include focusing on sustainable materials, AI integration, automation, and strategic acquisitions to capitalize on market opportunities.

title: Home Depot places huge Valley warehouse on sublease market
summary: The Home Depot Inc. has put its 1.3-million-square-foot warehouse in Goodyear, Arizona, on the sublease market. This move comes after the company rapidly expanded its industrial footprint to meet increased demand during the COVID-19 pandemic. Home Depot had signed a 10-year lease for the facility in late 2021.

title: New Report Finds Shoppers Value In-store Shopping
summary: A new report by Ryder System reveals that despite the flourishing e-commerce market, consumers are increasingly valuing in-store shopping experiences. The study found that 61% of shoppers enjoy the in-store experience, a significant increase from last year, and many use their mobile devices while shopping in physical stores for price comparisons and product information. Additionally, 55% of consumers now prefer to return online purchases in-store, often leading to additional purchases during their visit.

title: Big problems for big furniture store chain with 14 NJ locations
summary: Bob's Discount Furniture is facing significant online problems, including a network disruption that began on Thursday and escalated by Friday. Although their physical stores remain open for business, customers expecting deliveries are advised to check emails for updates, as the company cannot provide real-time information or adjustments. The issue has also made it impossible to contact the company via phone, affecting its 14 New Jersey, 16 Pennsylvania, and 180 nationwide locations.

title: 2 Dividend Growth ETFs That You Can Count on for Recurring Income for Decades
summary: This article highlights two dividend growth ETFs, the WisdomTree U.S. Quality Dividend Growth Fund (DGRW) and the Vanguard Dividend Appreciation ETF (VIG), as excellent long-term investment options for recurring income. It details their holdings, expense ratios, dividend yields, and past performance, making a case for why they are suitable for investors looking for consistent cash flow. The author also provides a brief comparison between the two, noting DGRW's slightly higher returns due to more tech exposure and VIG's greater safety and diversification.

title: RPM International Thrives in Rate-Cut Driven Construction Rally
summary: RPM International, a specialty chemicals and building materials manufacturer, is experiencing a surge to all-time highs, driven by an anticipated construction rally fueled by interest rate cuts. Despite a slight revenue decline, the company reported record earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT) in Q1 2025, showcasing improved efficiencies across its diverse brand portfolio. The article highlights RPM's strong market position, mixed guidance, and technical analysis suggesting further growth potential, making it a potential buy for investors seeking construction sector exposure.

title: Home Depot to Force Corporate Staff to Work Shifts in Stores
summary: Home Depot plans to require its corporate staff, including senior management and remote workers, to work 8-hour shifts in retail stores each quarter. This initiative aims to help corporate employees understand the challenges faced by in-store associates and improve employee retention amid rising labor activism and a sales slump. The move is considered unusual for the retail sector.

title: Prime San Antonio retail center changes hands
summary: JLL Capital Markets announced the sale of Village at Stone Oak, a 476,371-square-foot retail center in San Antonio, Texas, from SITE Centers to Sterling Organization. The center, a high-performing asset ranking in the top 5% of U.S. shopping centers, boasts an 84% occupancy rate and a diverse tenant mix. Its strategic location in Bexar County and proximity to an affluent community and major attractions make it an attractive investment.

title: Fastenal Ends 3Q with Momentum
summary: Fastenal reported improved sales metrics for September and the third quarter of 2024, indicating a demand uptick in the industrial supply sector. While gross margin continued to slide, the company demonstrated solid cost discipline and management amidst a challenging demand environment. The sales gains suggest July might have been the low-point for industrial demand, pointing towards a potential acceleration period.

title: Home Depot Plans to Make Every Employee, Including Executives, Work in Stores. It's an Absolutely Brilliant Move
summary: Home Depot plans to implement a policy requiring all employees, including executives, to work an eight-hour shift in a store once per quarter. This initiative is lauded as brilliant for providing corporate staff with hands-on experience and a deeper understanding of the core business, improving decision-making, and fostering respect between employees and executives. The author emphasizes the importance of humility from corporate staff during these shifts for the program to be successful and advocates for similar cross-training in other businesses.

title: City issues building permit for The Home Depot in Mandarin
summary: The City of Jacksonville has issued a building permit for a new Home Depot store in Mandarin, to be constructed on the former Kmart site at 9600 San Jose Blvd. The $8 million project will be undertaken by Ordner Construction Co. Inc., creating a 132,975-square-foot facility including a large retail space and a garden center. The demolition of the Kmart store, which closed in 2016, was completed in September.

title: XLY: Consumer Discretionary Dashboard For October
summary: This article analyzes the consumer discretionary sector, focusing on fundamental and momentum metrics, and identifies consumer services as the most compelling subsector due to its slight undervaluation and excellent quality score. It provides fast facts on the XLY sector benchmark and lists nine stocks that are cheaper than their peers in October.

title: Deals of the Year: AGCO closes joint venture with technology company Trimble - Atlanta Business Chronicle
summary: AGCO Corp. has finalized a joint venture with Trimble Inc., acquiring an 85% interest in Trimble's Ag assets and technologies. This deal was recognized as a "Deals of the Year" by the Atlanta Business Chronicle. The acquisition aims to expand AGCO's portfolio as an agricultural machinery and equipment manufacturer and distributor.

title: Cohen & Steers and Acadia Realty Trust Acquire Open-Air Shopping Center in Tampa, FL
summary: Cohen & Steers and Acadia Realty Trust have formed a joint venture to acquire The Walk at Highwoods, a 141,000 square foot open-air shopping center in Tampa, Florida. This acquisition aligns with their shared view that open-air shopping centers are well-positioned for a new economic cycle due to robust demand and limited new retail construction, especially within Tampa's high-growth market. The center is fully occupied by national and local retailers and benefits from Tampa's strong economic and population growth.

title: I’m a Former Maintenance Worker—This Is The Only Brand of Cleaner I Need For My Whole House
summary: A former New York City luxury high-rise janitor, Anthony O'Reilly, tested a suite of Ecolab cleaning products for 30 days and found them to outperform other brands while being significantly more affordable. He highlights six specific Ecolab products—Heavy-Duty Citrus Degreaser, Industrial Degreaser, Mold and Mildew Stain Remover, Foaming Tub and Tile Cleaner, Hardwood and Laminate Floor Cleaner, and Fast Action Foaming Degreaser—detailing their effectiveness on various household cleaning challenges, from stubborn grease to mold and hard water stains. O'Reilly concludes that Ecolab is now the only cleaning brand he needs for his entire home.

title: Urban Edge sells Home Depot property in Union for $71 million
summary: Urban Edge Properties has sold a 232,000-square-foot Home Depot property in Union Township, New Jersey, for $71 million as part of a Section 1031 like-kind exchange. The company simultaneously acquired a 382,000-square-foot upscale retail center in Gambrills, Maryland, for $126 million. This move is part of Urban Edge's strategy to acquire high-quality retail assets in core markets and divest noncore properties.

title: 11 Recycled Building Materials Made From Trash
summary: This article highlights 11 innovative building materials created from post-consumer waste, tackling the significant problem of landfill-bound trash. Companies are transforming items like old jeans, fishing nets, glass bottles, and tires into durable, cost-effective, and eco-friendly construction products. From insulation and carpet tiles to countertops and roofing shingles, these recycled materials offer sustainable alternatives for various building needs.

title: Home Depot co-founder, GOP donor Bernie Marcus dead at 95
summary: Bernie Marcus, the co-founder of Home Depot and a prominent Republican donor, has passed away at the age of 95. A self-made billionaire, Marcus co-founded Home Depot in 1978 and later established the Job Creators Network and the Marcus Foundation, which has given over $2 billion to charitable causes. He was also a staunch critic of President Biden's economic policies.

title: How To Earn $500 A Month From Home Depot Stock Ahead Of Q3 Earnings
summary: This article discusses how an investor can earn $500 a month from Home Depot stock through its dividends, ahead of its Q3 earnings report. It details the number of shares and investment required to achieve this monthly income based on Home Depot's current dividend yield. The article also provides analyst expectations for Home Depot's Q3 earnings and revenue.

title: The Home Depot Announces Third Quarter Fiscal 2024 Results; Updates Fiscal 2024 Guidance
summary: The Home Depot reported third-quarter fiscal 2024 sales of $40.2 billion, a 6.6% increase from the prior year, though comparable sales nationally decreased by 1.3%. The company updated its fiscal 2024 guidance, anticipating a total sales increase of approximately 4% and a diluted earnings-per-share decline of about 2%. This performance exceeded expectations despite macroeconomic uncertainty.

title: Home Depot’s Q3 results top Wall Street as pullback in consumer spending eases a bit
summary: Home Depot's fiscal third-quarter results surpassed Wall Street expectations, despite an ongoing pullback in consumer spending that was less severe than in previous quarters. The company reported a 6.6% increase in revenue to $40.22 billion and raised its full-year revenue outlook, now expecting a rise of about 4%. While sales at stores open at least a year still declined, the drop was less significant than in the second quarter, leading to a rise in Home Depot's shares in premarket trading.

title: Savvy acquisition saves Home Depot from third-quarter revenue decline
summary: Home Depot Inc. reported third-quarter sales exceeding Wall Street expectations and upgraded its full-year guidance, largely due to its acquisition of SRS Distribution. While total sales increased by 6.6% to $40.2 billion, comparable sales dropped 1.3% year-over-year. The acquisition of SRS Distribution for $18.25 billion is projected to add $6.4 billion in full-year sales, offsetting an expected sales decline for Home Depot without the acquisition.

title: Home Depot Raises Outlook on Hurricane-Fueled Demand
summary: Home Depot Inc. (HD) has raised its sales forecast for a key metric, driven by increased demand for home-improvement materials following adverse weather in the latest quarter. Despite high interest rates impacting the housing market, the company's comparable sales decline of 1.3% was better than Wall Street expectations and represented its best quarterly sales performance in nearly two years. This uptick suggests that hurricane-fueled demand is providing a significant boost to Home Depot's business.

The article highlights pre-market movers, with Shopify and Amprius Technologies among the top gainers, and several companies, including Home Depot and Live Nation, seeing their stock movements noted based on recent financial updates and analyst actions.

title: Home Depot grows online sales in Q3
summary: The Home Depot reported a 4% year-over-year increase in online sales for its fiscal Q3, which ended October 27, 2024. Nearly half of these web orders were fulfilled through its physical stores, reflecting the company's focus on an interconnected retail experience. Despite slight declines in average order value and customer transactions, the company highlighted the success of annual sales events and ongoing efforts to improve delivery speeds and expand fulfillment capabilities.

summary: Home Depot's $18.25 billion acquisition of SRS Distribution is an effort to expand its pro business, especially as DIY demand slows. The deal has already boosted Home Depot's sales and is seen as a way to enter new specialty markets and differentiate itself from competitors like Lowe's. This strategic move aims to accelerate Home Depot's growth by catering to professional contractors in the roofing, pool, and landscaping segments.

title: Top IoT Stocks: Why Samsara and Digi Are Thriving in 2025
summary: This article examines why Samsara (IOT) and Digi International (DGII) are poised for continued thriving in the Internet of Things (IoT) market in 2025. Samsara is highlighted for its hypergrowth in fleet management and industrial IoT, driven by strong financial results and AI integration.
