title: After Earnings, Is Home Depot Stock a Buy, a Sell, or Fairly Valued?
summary: Morningstar raised its fair value estimate for Home Depot to $292 per share following its Q3 earnings report, driven by stronger professional product demand despite a decline in DIY sales due to high interest rates. However, shares are still considered overvalued at 25 times next year's earnings. The company maintains a "wide moat" rating due to its brand and cost advantage, but faces risks from weak consumer spending and economic downturns.

title: Here's why Dollar Tree and Dollar General stocks have plummeted
summary: Dollar Tree and Dollar General stocks have fallen approximately 50% this year, facing a mix of economic and self-inflicted problems. Lower-income Americans, who constitute a large portion of their customer base, are prioritizing consumables due to high inflation, while middle and upper-middle income shoppers are not trading down to dollar stores because of a strong job market. Additionally, these companies lag in e-commerce capabilities compared to larger retailers and have faced worker safety violations, further contributing to their struggles.

title: Stanley Black & Decker CEO on potential Trump tariffs: Tool prices will go up
summary: Stanley Black & Decker CEO Don Allan believes that new tariffs proposed by Donald Trump could significantly increase the cost of tools, making products up to 60-70% more expensive if manufacturing were moved from China to the U.S. The company has already begun discussing potential pricing actions with customers in anticipation of these changes. Despite tariff concerns, Stanley Black & Decker provided an upbeat long-term outlook, targeting $16.5 billion to $17 billion in sales by fiscal year 2027, although the company's recent performance has been impacted by consumer weakness and a challenging housing market.

title: ‘Everything is on the table’: Williams-Sonoma preps for tariff hikes
summary: Williams-Sonoma is preparing for potential new U.S. tariffs on China imports by evaluating various mitigation options, including reducing sourcing from China and shifting production to other countries. The company has already significantly decreased its reliance on China for goods since 2020. Its vertically integrated supply chain and U.S. manufacturing hubs provide strategic flexibility in responding to changes in the tariff landscape.

title: Holiday crime crackdown: An inside look at Billings police detective sting operations
summary: Billings Police Department detectives conducted a sting operation at Home Depot to combat a seasonal spike in theft. Senior Det. Jeff Chartier noted that the first Wednesday after Thanksgiving is a common period for theft. At least three individuals were arrested, with two found to have illegal drugs and outstanding warrants worth approximately $70,000, underscoring the police's vigilance against retail crime during the holidays.

title: Home Depot accused of faking Black Friday deals by masking original prices with holiday sale stickers showing the same cost
summary: Home Depot is facing accusations of false advertising for its Black Friday sales, after a viral TikTok video showed an item with a "holiday sale" sticker revealing the exact same original price underneath. Retail experts suggest this practice could be considered false advertising and might further erode customer trust, especially given current concerns about shrinkflation. While proving false advertising can be difficult, consumers are likely to feel misled by such tactics, which contribute to the perception that Black Friday deals are not as significant as they once were.

title: What’s new: Amazon Fresh coming to Corona; Murrieta gets another Home Depot
summary: This article highlights new developments in the Inland Empire, including the opening of an Amazon Fresh grocery store in Corona and a second Home Depot in Murrieta, both set for December 12. It also covers the groundbreaking for Southern California Edison's new Edison Training Academy in Corona, the sale of Summit Business Center in Riverside for $19 million, and the opening of a new EV supercharging station at the Lebec Travel Center.

title: Verrado Marketplace, Teravalis: Key Buckeye developments to look for in 2025
summary: Buckeye, Arizona, a rapidly growing city, is set for significant developments in 2025 despite ongoing water supply challenges. Key projects include the Verrado Marketplace, a large shopping center expected to open in early 2026, and Teravalis, a massive master-planned community whose first village, Floreo, will have its grand opening. Additionally, the city is revitalizing its downtown area to attract businesses and improve walkability.

title: Builders FirstSource to acquire Alpine Lumber
summary: Builders FirstSource, Inc. announced its definitive agreement to acquire Alpine Lumber Company, expanding its presence in Colorado and New Mexico. The acquisition, valued at approximately $500 million in trailing twelve months sales, is expected to be accretive to Builders FirstSource's adjusted earnings per share in 2025 and will be financed through existing cash and credit facilities. This move aligns with Builders FirstSource's strategy to invest in high-growth areas and enhance its footprint in the West Division.

title: Home Depot’s $9.5 Million Meal Break Settlement Gets Final Nod
summary: A federal court has approved a $9.5 million settlement involving Home Depot and over 32,000 associate workers. The lawsuit alleged that the company's administrative and staffing policies prevented these employees from taking their legally required full meal and rest breaks between 2018 and 2024. This settlement resolves claims brought against the home improvement retailer.

title: 1 Vanguard Index Fund Could Turn $375 Per Month Into a $569,400 Portfolio That Pays $17,200 in Annual Dividend Income
summary: This article highlights how consistent small investments in the Vanguard High Dividend Yield ETF (VYM) can lead to a substantial retirement portfolio. Investing $375 monthly could result in a nearly $570,000 portfolio yielding over $17,000 in annual dividend income over 30 years. The ETF's low expense ratio, lower volatility compared to the S&P 500, and historical performance are key attractive features for risk-averse investors.

title: The Walmart Effect
summary: New research suggests that Walmart has a broadly negative economic impact on the communities it operates in, challenging the long-held belief that its low prices significantly benefit consumers. Two papers indicate that the costs of lower earnings and higher unemployment outweigh the savings for shoppers, ultimately making communities poorer. The findings also question the consumer-welfare standard used in antitrust regulation, suggesting it overlooks broader economic impacts beyond price.

title: Who Owns Ridgid Tools And Where Are They Made?
summary: This article explains the ownership and manufacturing origins of Ridgid Tools. It details that Ridgid is owned by Emerson Electric since 1966, an American company founded in Elyria, Ohio, which still maintains its headquarters there. While some tool components are made in Pennsylvania, various power tools are manufactured by Hong Kong-based Techtronic Industries (TTI), and Ridgid maintains an exclusive sales relationship with Home Depot.

title: Who Owns Home Depot? Owner, CEO and Key Data (2026)
summary: Home Depot is a public company with shares listed on the New York Stock Exchange, meaning it has no single owner. Its major shareholders include The Vanguard Group and BlackRock, who influence strategic decisions. Edward 'Ted' Decker serves as the Chairman, CEO, and a member of the Board of Directors, focusing on integrating digital and physical channels for an improved customer experience. The company, founded in 1978, has expanded significantly through strategic acquisitions and is recognized for its philanthropy and commitment to sustainability.

title: Home Depot buys former Wells Fargo building
summary: Home Depot has acquired a former Wells Fargo building in Pembroke Park, Florida, as part of its plan to open 80 new stores. This move aligns with the Atlanta-based retailer's strategy to expand its footprint for home repair goods. The announcement comes after Home Depot revealed its expansion intentions earlier in the year.

title: Home Depot Buys Roofing Distributor in Deal Valued at $18 Billion Including Debt
summary: Home Depot announced its acquisition of SRS Distribution for $18 billion, including debt. This strategic move aims to expand Home Depot's reach into supplying professional contractors and large construction projects, diversifying its business beyond traditional do-it-yourself sales, which have been slowing. The acquisition reflects a significant bet on the professional segment of the home improvement market.

title: Investment bank Jefferies’ profit more than triples: CEO says the ‘cherry on top’ is that ‘financial stars are aligning’ after crippling inflation
summary: Jefferies Financial Group reported exceptionally strong performance in 2024, with net revenues reaching $7.03 billion and fourth-quarter profits more than tripling. The company increased its quarterly dividend and attributed its success to market share gains, improved market conditions, and significant growth across all business lines, positioning it as the world's 6th largest investment bank. CEO Richard Handler and President Brian Friedman expressed optimism for 2025, noting the firm is in its best position in its 62-year history.

title: B.C. court authorizes class action against Home Depot over sharing of customer data with Meta
summary: The B.C. Supreme Court has certified a class action lawsuit against Home Depot over the alleged sharing of customer email addresses and purchase details with Meta Platforms, Inc. The plaintiff, Lasse Hvitved, argues that customers had a reasonable expectation of privacy, which Home Depot violated by using an offline conversions tool service with Meta. While the court allowed the privacy breach claims, it struck down causes of action related to contract and unjust enrichment.

title: Nation's fastest-growing city to add another major retailer
summary: Home Depot is opening a new 105,000-square-foot store in Celina, Texas, America's fastest-growing city, following approval of a $1.39 million sales tax grant. The investment is expected to boost the local economy, create jobs, and support infrastructure, as Celina's population continues to rapidly expand with other major retailers like Costco and Lowe's also establishing a presence. This development reflects Celina's significant growth and its appeal to businesses due to new infrastructure, schools, and housing projects.

title: The Home Depot adds two new online delivery partners
summary: The Home Depot is expanding its online delivery options by partnering with DoorDash and Uber Eats. These new collaborations will allow customers to order Home Depot products for on-demand or scheduled delivery, complementing existing partnerships with Instacart and Walmart's GoLocal service. The initiative is aimed at providing greater flexibility and convenience for both DIY customers and professionals.

title: The Home Depot, Inc. (NYSE:HD) is a favorite amongst institutional investors who own 72%
summary: Institutional investors own 72% of The Home Depot, Inc. (NYSE:HD), indicating their significant influence on the company's stock price and decisions. The Vanguard Group, Inc. is the largest shareholder, holding 9.6% of outstanding shares, while insiders own less than 1% but represent a substantial monetary value. The general public holds a 28% stake, suggesting widely disseminated shares without a single dominant shareholder.

title: Duopoly Discount: Lowe's Is A Better Deal Than Home Depot For DCA Investors (NYSE:LOW)
summary: Lowe's expects a decline in comparable sales for fiscal 2024 due to reduced discretionary DIY spending. Despite short-term challenges, Lowe's has a strong long-term outlook driven by factors like aging homes and remote work trends. For dollar-cost averaging investors, Lowe's is presented as a better value than Home Depot due to a lower growth premium embedded in its stock price, despite similar long-term growth drivers for both companies.

title: Coca-Cola, Home Depot, Walmart To Announce Dividend Increases In Second Half Of February
summary: This article predicts upcoming dividend increases for 10 long-term dividend growth companies in the latter half of February. Notable companies expected to announce increases include Coca-Cola (for its 63rd consecutive year), Walmart, and Home Depot. The author, an individual investor focused on dividend growth stocks, details their investment strategy and disclosures.

title: Class I Briefs: NS, BNSF
summary: Norfolk Southern (NS) has been named to FORTUNE Magazine's list of World's Most Admired Companies for 2025, ranking as the highest railroad in its category. Separately, BNSF received The Home Depot Rail Carrier of the Year award for 2025, recognizing its commitment to service and a pilot project that improved routing and transit time. BNSF also celebrated its Stockton, California team completing a full year without a single injury, an achievement mirrored across other major terminals in the region.

title: Kontoor Brands to buy Helly Hansen from Canadian Tire Corporation
summary: Kontoor Brands, the company behind Wrangler and Lee, is set to acquire the Canadian outdoor workwear brand Helly Hansen from Canadian Tire Corporation. This strategic acquisition aligns with Kontoor Brands' global expansion plans and follows a strong financial performance in the previous quarter. The transaction is expected to be finalized in the second quarter of the current year, pending regulatory approvals.

title: Prologis CEO Hamid Moghadam to retire next year
summary: Hamid Moghadam, co-founder and CEO of Prologis, plans to retire on January 1, 2026, after more than four decades with the company and its predecessor. Dan Letter, current president, will succeed him as CEO, while Moghadam will transition to executive chairman. This succession plan has been in the works for over two years, with Letter having joined AMB in 2004 and becoming president of Prologis in January 2023.

title: Saham The Home Depot, Inc. (HD): Prospek dan Analisis 2025
summary: Artikel ini membahas prospek dan analisis saham The Home Depot, Inc. (HD) untuk tahun 2025, menyoroti posisi perusahaan sebagai ritel perbaikan rumah terbesar di AS. Analisis mencakup data historis pergerakan harga saham, laporan keuangan terkini dengan pendapatan dan laba yang kuat, serta proyeksi masa depan dan tips investasi bagi pemula, termasuk potensi dan risiko. Home Depot dianggap menarik bagi investor karena pertumbuhan stabil, strategi bisnis solid, dan kebijakan dividen yang konsisten.

title: Earnings call transcript: Floor & Decor Q4 2024 beats estimates, stock surges
summary: Floor & Decor Holdings Inc. (FND) reported strong Q4 2024 results, surpassing analyst expectations with an EPS of $0.44 and revenue of $1.11 billion, leading to a 10.94% stock surge in aftermarket trading. The company plans to open 25 new stores in fiscal 2025 and projects sales growth of 6.5% to 10%, maintaining stable gross margins despite facing a cyclical downturn in the flooring industry. Executives highlighted market share gains, supply chain diversification, and increased investments in new stores, technology, and customer service.

title: Going Into Earnings, Is Home Depot Stock a Buy, a Sell, or Fairly Valued?
summary: Morningstar maintains a fair value estimate of $292 per share for Home Depot (HD), viewing the stock as overvalued going into its Q4 earnings report. The analysis highlights an expected sales decline when accounting for an extra week and acquired sales, with focus shifting to professional demand as DIY customers pause big-ticket projects due to high interest rates. While tariffs pose a wild card, Home Depot's scale is expected to help absorb incremental costs, and its wide economic moat provides a competitive edge despite current market challenges.

title: Nvidia, Home Depot, Lowe's, TJX and Salesforce are part of Zacks Earnings Preview
summary: Zacks.com previews upcoming earnings reports from major companies including Nvidia, Home Depot, Lowe's, TJX Companies, and Salesforce. The report highlights the challenging environment for home improvement retailers due to elevated mortgage rates and discusses Nvidia's critical role in AI-focused buildouts, despite recent sentiment shifts. It also provides an overview of the Q4 earnings season scorecard for the Retail sector and the S&P 500.

title: The Home Depot Announces Fourth Quarter and Fiscal 2024 Results; Increases Quarterly Dividend by 2.2%; Provides Fiscal 2025 Guidance
summary: The Home Depot reported strong fourth quarter and fiscal 2024 results, with sales exceeding expectations and a 2.2% increase in its quarterly dividend. The company also provided its fiscal 2025 guidance, forecasting modest sales and comparable sales growth. Despite ongoing macroeconomic pressures, the retailer emphasized continued investments in strategic initiatives.

title: Home Depot, Sempra Energy, American Tower to report earnings Tuesday By Investing.com
summary: Investing.com reports that a diverse group of companies, including Home Depot, Sempra Energy, and American Tower, are scheduled to release their earnings on Tuesday. The article provides a detailed list of companies reporting both before and after market close, along with their estimated EPS and revenue figures. This information offers investors key insights into various economic sectors.

title: The Home Depot Announces Fourth Quarter and Fiscal 2024 Results; Increases Quarterly Dividend By 2.2%; Provides Fiscal 2025 Guidance
summary: The Home Depot announced its fourth quarter and fiscal year 2024 results, reporting an increase in quarterly sales and diluted earnings per share for Q4, despite a decrease in comparable sales for the full fiscal year. The company also declared a 2.2% increase in its quarterly dividend to $2.30 per share and provided its fiscal 2025 guidance, projecting total sales growth of approximately 2.8% and a slight decline in diluted earnings per share. These results exceeded expectations due to greater engagement in home improvement, even amidst a challenging macroeconomic environment.

title: Ninja Disrupts the Outdoor Grilling Market with Launch of FlexFlame™
summary: SharkNinja (NYSE: SN) has launched the Ninja™ FlexFlame™, an innovative outdoor cooking system. This revolutionary propane-powered device combines five cooking methods—grilling, smoking, roasting, griddling, and pizza-making—into a single unit, designed to simplify outdoor cooking and deliver high-quality results. The FlexFlame™ utilizes Ninja’s CyclonicHeat-iQ™ technology, integrating rapid convection airflow, precision propane flame control, and Woodfire Technology to enhance its performance.

title: Home Depot says consumers postponing renovation projects, citing high interest rates
summary: Home Depot executives report that consumers are postponing large renovation projects due to high interest rates and uncertain macroeconomic conditions. This has led to a decline in demand for major home improvement projects, with customers increasingly resorting to financing options for those they do undertake. The housing market is also impacted by high mortgage rates and a "golden handcuff" effect, where homeowners with low rates are reluctant to sell, leading to limited supply and dampening pending home sales.

title: Top Stock Movers Now: Sempra, Zoom, Home Depot, and More
summary: U.S. equities declined midday due to a drop in consumer confidence. Sempra (SRE) shares fell after missing estimates and cutting its outlook, while Zoom Communications (ZM) also slumped due to weak guidance. Home Depot (HD) and Solventum (SOLV) saw gains, with Home Depot benefiting from hurricane-related demand and Solventum from selling a business unit.

title: Lowe’s earnings, sales top estimates amid ‘challenging’ home improvement market
summary: Lowe's reported better-than-expected fourth-quarter earnings and sales, including its first same-store sales increase in two years, despite a challenging home improvement market. The company saw net income rise to $1.13 billion and comparable sales edge up 0.2%, driven by Pro customers and online sales. However, Lowe's issued weaker-than-expected full-year guidance for 2025 due to continued high borrowing rates impacting discretionary spending.

title: Lowe's forecasts muted 2025 profit on economic uncertainty, cautious spending
summary: Lowe's (LOW.N) has predicted subdued sales and profits for 2025, mirroring rival Home Depot's outlook, as the home improvement sector faces a downturn due to high interest rates and cautious consumer spending. The retailer expects comparable sales to be flat to up 1% and earnings per share between $12.15 and $12.40, both below analyst estimates. Despite the conservative forecast, driven by economic uncertainty and potential tariff impacts, Lowe's shares rose about 3% following a surprise rise in same-store sales due to hurricane-related demand.

title: Ecolab Celebrates Two-Year Anniversary of Partnership with Home Depot and the Launch of the Ecolab® Scientific Clean™ Product Line
summary: Ecolab is celebrating the two-year anniversary of its partnership with The Home Depot and the successful expansion of its Ecolab® Scientific Clean™ product line. The collaboration began in February 2023, making professional-grade cleaning solutions available to commercial, industrial, and residential customers. Ecolab plans to launch new products and expand its market presence throughout North America in 2025, reinforcing its commitment to innovation and customer needs.

title: Home Depot plans to open new Valley store in Surprise
summary: Home Depot announced its plan to open a new store in Surprise, Arizona, as part of its expansion across the country, which includes over a dozen new locations this year. This new West Valley location will mark another addition to the region's growing retail landscape.

title: After 6-year renovation, Nora Plaza unveils new restaurants, modern look on far north side
summary: Nora Plaza has completed a six-year, modernizing renovation by Kite Realty Group, bringing new restaurants like Culinary Dropout and Flower Child to the Indianapolis food scene. While some original tenants moved, the overhaul is contributing to local growth and attracting new businesses, with further developments such as The Milkshake Factory and Potbelly planned. The transformation has been recognized by local community groups and officials as a significant improvement for the far north side neighborhood.

title: Blink Charging Remains Bullish on the EV Supply Equipment Sector
summary: Despite potential changes in government policy regarding electric vehicles, Blink Charging expressed optimism about the continued growth of the EV supply equipment sector. The company's officials noted that state and local efforts, combined with increasing private investment and consumer demand for affordable EV models, are expected to sustain momentum. They also highlighted the increasing use of polycarbonate in charging station enclosures due to its performance benefits over traditional metal.

title: Home Depot Surprise expansion with new location in 2025
summary: Home Depot Inc. is set to open a new 109,651-square-foot store with an attached garden center in Surprise, Arizona, in April 2025. This new location, situated along Loop 303 at 16601 Cactus Road, is part of 13 new stores the company plans to open this year. The retailer acquired the 18-acre site for $8.4 million last year, positioning it next to the Sycamore Farms project.

title: Home Depot Gets Workers’ Back Pay Interest Lawsuit Thrown Out
summary: A federal court has dismissed a lawsuit against Home Depot U.S.A. Inc. that alleged the company improperly listed interest for workers’ back pay from a previous case on incorrect tax forms, leading to unlawful withholding. The US District Court for the District of Oregon found that the claim under the federal false-information statute was invalid because it requires a defendant to willfully misrepresent payment amounts, which was not alleged. Additionally, the workers' claim of over-deducted state income tax was also rejected by the court.

title: 6th Circuit Rules Data Breach Claims Not Covered by CGL Policies
summary: The 6th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals ruled that Home Depot's commercial general liability (CGL) insurance policies do not cover losses from its 2014-2015 data breach due to an explicit electronic data exclusion. The court affirmed that CGL policies are distinct from cyber insurance and do not indemnify costs associated with data breaches, including those for reissued payment cards or lost usage. This decision highlights the critical difference between cyber and general liability coverage for the insurance industry.

title: THE HOME DEPOT NAMES MICHAEL ROWE EVP OF PRO; STEPHANIE SMITH TO BECOME EVP OF HUMAN RESOURCES
summary: The Home Depot announced new executive appointments, naming Michael Rowe as Executive Vice President of Pro and promoting Stephanie Smith to EVP of Human Resources. Rowe will lead the company's strategy to expand its business with professional customers. Smith will succeed Tim Hourigan, who is retiring, and will be responsible for culture, associate engagement, and leadership development for the company's 470,000 associates.

title: Home Depot turns to AI to answer online shoppers’ questions
summary: Home Depot is integrating generative AI into its online platform to enhance the shopping experience by answering product and project questions. This move aims to replicate in-store customer service online, offering features like design ideas and product comparisons, as the company seeks to revive sales amidst shifting consumer spending habits. Home Depot anticipates improved demand as customers adapt to higher interest rates, focusing on professional contractors and leveraging AI for functions like summarizing product reviews.

title: EXEC: VF Corp. Shares Fall Following Investor Day Part 2
summary: VF Corp. shares fell significantly following its "Reinvent to Grow" Part 2 Investor Day in New York City. The company emphasized introducing new brand leaders and outlined strategic objectives for brands like The North Face, Timberland, Dickies, Altra, and Vans, but lacked specific projections which concerned some analysts. Despite reaffirming targets for 10%+ operating margins by Fiscal 2028, investor sentiment was negative, possibly due to concerns about a brewing trade war.

title: Stock Market Today: Dow Sinks 537 Points On Tariff Threats As S&P 500 Corrects; Gold Miners Jump, Meta Triggers Sell Rule (Live Coverage)
summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 537 points, and the S&P 500 corrected amid new tariff threats from the Trump administration. Gold miners rallied while Home Depot and Meta Platforms experienced sell-offs, with Meta triggering a sell rule. Despite a late attempt by traders to cover short positions, major indexes ended the trading day lower.

title: I tested the Traeger Woodridge Pro, and it's ideal for set-it-and-forget-it smoking
summary: The Traeger Woodridge Pro is a hybrid pellet grill that excels at smoking, offering a "set-it-and-forget-it" experience with an intuitive app. While it provides decent grilling capabilities, particularly for lower-heat cooking, it has limitations regarding high-heat searing due to the lack of direct flames. The grill features a stout build, ample cooking space, and user-friendly design, making it a strong choice for frequent smokers.

title: Survey reveals Georgia's 34 most trustworthy companies. Georgia Power, Coca-Cola make cut
summary: A new survey by Newsweek and Statista identified 34 Georgia-based companies among the 700 most trustworthy in the United States. The survey considered 97,000 evaluations from potential customers, investors, and employees. Notable companies like Georgia Power, Coca-Cola, and The Home Depot are included in the list, spanning various sectors from automotive to financial services.

title: UPS CEO Carol Tomé to deliver 2025 Oglethorpe Commencement address
summary: Oglethorpe University announced that UPS CEO Carol B. Tomé will deliver the 2025 Commencement address on May 3. Tomé, who is the 12th CEO in UPS's history and previously served as CFO of The Home Depot, will also be awarded an honorary doctor of letters degree. The ceremony will be presided over by President Kathryn McClymond and Board of Trustees Chair Tammy Pearson, and will include speeches and awards for graduates.

title: Home Depot Inc. (HD) reports earnings
summary: Home Depot Inc. (HD) has filed its 10-K report for the fiscal year ended February 2, 2025, reporting net sales of $159.5 billion, a 4.5% increase from the previous year, partly due to the acquisition of SRS. The company achieved net earnings of $14.8 billion and increased its quarterly cash dividend by 2.2%. Strategic investments will continue in its supply chain, technology, and customer experience, with approximately $4 billion planned for capital expenditures in fiscal 2025.

title: Byte-Sized AI: Walmart Announces Gen AI Merchant Tool; Oxford Industries Partners With Exotec
summary: Walmart has launched a new generative AI tool called Wally to help its merchants automate tasks, generate insights, and improve decision-making. Simultaneously, Oxford Industries has partnered with Exotec to implement AI-enabled robotics in its new distribution center, aiming to streamline warehouse operations and returns processing. The article also highlights Augment securing $25 million in funding for its AI-powered logistics assistant, Augie, and Lowe's introducing a gen AI chatbot, Mylow, for home improvement assistance.

title: Williams-Sonoma Joins The S&P 500
summary: Williams-Sonoma, Inc. has been added to the S&P 500, a significant milestone for the retailer that acknowledges its brand portfolio and growth strategies. The company's CEO, Laura Alber, stated their commitment to innovation, customer experience, and long-term stakeholder value. This announcement follows a strong fiscal year 2024 finish, with increased net revenue and net earnings in the fourth quarter.

title: JAMES HARDIE ACQUIRING AZEK
summary: James Hardie Industries plc has agreed to acquire The AZEK Company Inc. for $8.75 billion in cash and shares, creating a leading exterior and outdoor living building products growth platform. The acquisition aims to accelerate growth, enhance customer solutions, and drive shareholder value by combining complementary products like siding, exterior trim, decking, and railing. The transaction is expected to close in the second half of calendar year 2025, pending regulatory and AZEK shareholder approvals, and promises significant cost and commercial synergies, targeting over $1 billion in annual free cash flow.

title: Home Depot, world's largest home improvement chain, plans to build its fifth Polk County store
summary: Home Depot is planning to build its fifth store in Polk County, a 135,632-square-foot retail store in Davenport on U.S. 27. The project will include a 28,000-square-foot garden center and will be reviewed by Polk County's Development Review Committee on March 27. This new location will provide jobs and serve the growing Davenport area, which is seeing numerous new housing and commercial developments.

title: News | Intermodal transportation network, population growth convince Home Depot to expand in Edmonton
summary: The Home Depot has expanded its distribution network in Edmonton, Alberta, with a new 206,000-square-foot facility developed by Qualico Properties. This expansion, prompted by Edmonton's intermodal transportation network and population growth, supports Home Depot's 11 stores in the region. The project, completed in two phases for $36.9 million, earned a 2025 CoStar Impact Award for commercial development for Edmonton.

title: Home Depot nears completion on South Hill
summary: Home Depot's new South Hill store, located at 4515 S. Regal in Spokane, is nearing completion with an expected opening in June. The $17.8 million project includes a 108,000-square-foot building and a 26,000-square-foot garden center, creating nearly 200 jobs. This new development comes after a previous plan in 2008 was canceled due to neighborhood objections.

title: Despite environmental concerns, Stockton City Council enters 20-year partnership with Home Depot
summary: The Stockton City Council approved a 20-year partnership with The Home Depot, projecting $500,000 to $1 million in annual revenue for the city. This agreement will facilitate the expansion of Home Depot's e-commerce and distribution operations in a new 600,000 to 700,000 square foot facility at the Port of Stockton, creating 80-100 permanent jobs. Despite environmental concerns raised by the Delta-Sierra Group regarding the health impacts on nearby residents from increased emissions, the council voted 6-1 in favor, with Mayor Christina Fugazi noting the facility is already near completion and the potential revenue is crucial for community reinvestment.

title: XLY ETF Holdings List — AMEX:XLY
summary: This article provides a detailed list of the top holdings for the XLY ETF (State Street Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR ETF) as of February 27, 2026. It includes the weight percentage, number of shares, and market value for each company held within the ETF. Key holdings include Amazon.com, Inc., Tesla, Inc., Home Depot, Inc., and McDonald's Corporation, among others.

title: The Zacks Analyst Blog Highlights Walmart, Costco Wholesale and The Home Depot
summary: The Zacks Analyst Blog highlights blue-chip retail stocks Walmart, Costco Wholesale, and The Home Depot as stable investment options amidst global trade war uncertainties. These companies are noted for their financial strength, market dominance, and adaptability, which allow them to navigate rising tariffs and economic turbulence. The article details each company's strategies, financial performance, and dividend payouts, positioning them as reliable choices for investors seeking stability and sustained growth.

title: Home Depot subsidiary Construction Resources Co. buys stone slab and tile company
summary: The Home Depot subsidiary Construction Resources Co. has acquired Opustone, a stone slab and tile distributor. This acquisition expands the Decatur-based company's luxury design offerings. The deal was reported by the Atlanta Business Chronicle.

title: Hilton Stock Faces Challenges: Insights Unveiled
summary: Hilton Worldwide Holdings Inc. (HLT) stock has dropped by -3.69% due to investor reactions to potential regulatory challenges. Jefferies lowered its price target for Hilton to $228 from $277 but maintained a Hold rating, influencing investor sentiment. Despite robust revenue and a strong gross margin, the company faces pressures on profitability margins and has a leaner liquidity position, alongside significant long-term debt and capital outflows.

title: The Home Depot, Inc. (NYSE:HD) is favoured by institutional owners who hold 73% of the company
summary: Institutional investors hold a significant 73% ownership in The Home Depot, Inc. (NYSE:HD), indicating their strong preference for the company and influence on its stock price. The Vanguard Group, Inc., BlackRock, Inc., and State Street Global Advisors, Inc. are among the largest shareholders, while insiders own less than 1% but have been recently buying shares. The general public accounts for 27% ownership.

title: Home Depot in Buckeye coming up due to recent purchase
summary: Home Depot is moving forward with plans to open a new store in Buckeye, Arizona. The company recently purchased 11.14 acres at the Buckeye Commons shopping center for $7.7 million and applied for a building permit for a 137,347-square-foot store. This development positions Home Depot as another major retailer alongside Costco in the Buckeye Commons center.

title: Lowe’s extends brand into digital gaming
summary: Lowe's has announced a new partnership with EA Sports to integrate its brand into popular digital game titles such as EA Sports FC, Madden NFL, and College Football. This collaboration aims to engage sports fans and new generations of home improvers through in-game branding and a real-life "On the Road" interactive gaming experience. title: News | Construction equipment giant calls workers back for a five-day workweek

It details his strategic approach, including consolidation, rigorous management, and the acquisition of Smith Barney, which significantly boosted Morgan Stanley's wealth management division. The piece emphasizes Gorman's foresight in recognizing wealth management as a high-margin, stable business and his commitment to strong management and client care, leading to substantial growth in revenues and assets under management.

title: Opinion: BB&T-SunTrust merger signals more bank deals are coming
summary: The $66 billion combination of BB&T Corp. and SunTrust is the largest U.S. bank merger since the 2008 credit crisis, potentially signaling a wave of future mergers among large regional banks. This trend is driven by the necessity for banks to grow to increase profits and to lower expenses in the face of rising regulatory costs. Investors have reacted positively to the deal and are anticipating which banks might be next to merge.

title: JPMorgan Chase Moves to Be First Big U.S. Bank With Its Own Cryptocurrency (Published 2019)
summary: JPMorgan Chase, despite its CEO Jamie Dimon's previous skepticism about Bitcoin, has become the first major U.S. bank to introduce its own digital token for real-world use. This move expands the bank's exploration of blockchain technology and aims to make digital currencies more accessible to its corporate clients. The initiative follows JPMorgan's earlier blockchain platform, Quorum, demonstrating an evolving strategy towards digital assets within the financial system.

title: Paramount Completes $227M Acquisition of Historic San Francisco Building
summary: Paramount Group, Inc. acquired 111 Sutter Street, a historic 22-story office property in San Francisco, from JLL Income Property Trust for $227 million. A joint venture partner was brought in to acquire 51% of the equity interest, with Paramount managing the 70%-leased asset. Paramount expects to significantly increase net operating income by managing existing vacancy and upcoming lease expirations through 2021.

title: JP Morgan is rolling out the first US bank-backed cryptocurrency to transform payments business
summary: JP Morgan Chase is launching "JPM Coin," the first cryptocurrency created by a major U.S. bank, to instantly settle transactions for its wholesale payments business. This digital token will initially be used for international payments, securities transactions, and treasury services for large corporate clients, not for retail investors. While CEO Jamie Dimon has been critical of bitcoin, the bank sees promise in blockchain technology and regulated digital currencies.

title: Can JPMorgan Chase's JPM Coin knock off Ripple and Swift?
summary: JPMorgan Chase has introduced JPM Coin, a stablecoin designed to facilitate faster and cheaper cross-border payments on its Quorum blockchain, aiming to compete with Ripple and Swift. While JPM Coin offers the speed of cryptocurrencies without the volatility of XRP, its adoption hinges on other institutions trusting JPMorgan and potentially being compelled to use it due to JPMorgan's extensive network. The initiative challenges traditional correspondent banking and the Swift network, pushing the financial industry towards a more real-time, blockchain-based payment infrastructure.

title: High Dividends, Low Taxes: A Careful Investor's Guide To Preferred Stocks
summary: This article provides a guide to preferred stocks for investors seeking high dividends and favorable tax treatment. It highlights the hybrid nature of preferred stocks, their tax implications, and the complexities involved in selecting and trading them. The author emphasizes diversification, careful trading practices, and understanding call provisions and qualified dividend income (QDI).

title: JPM Coin From JPMorgan Chase Vs. Crypto Fans: Who's Missing The Point?
summary: JPMorgan Chase introduced JPM Coin, a prototype digital coin for instantaneous payments using blockchain technology, sparking immediate consternation among crypto fans who argue it doesn't align with traditional cryptocurrency characteristics like decentralization and permissionless access. The article explores whether JPM Coin is truly "crypto" or a "stablecoin," highlighting its purpose to streamline interbank transactions and challenge existing systems like Swift and Ripple. It also discusses the potential for other banks to adopt or compete with JPM Coin, raising questions about the future of interbank digital currencies.

title: Those Credit Card Bonuses May Be Taxable (Published 2019)
summary: Credit card bonuses received from referring friends or family for new cards may be taxable, prompting recipients to receive 1099 tax forms from major card brands like Chase, American Express, and Discover. Tax experts clarify that rewards tied to spending on the card, such as cash back or bonus points for meeting spending requirements, are generally not considered taxable by the IRS. However, bonuses not linked to spending, like referral incentives, can be classified as miscellaneous income and therefore subject to taxation.

title: A Local Wells Fargo Bank in Georgia Refused to Cash My Hurricane María Insurance Check Because It Was Written in Spanish (OPINION)
summary: A Puerto Rican woman in Georgia encountered significant difficulty attempting to deposit a Hurricane María insurance check written in Spanish at a local Wells Fargo branch. Despite initial acceptance, the check was later reversed, with bank staff claiming their systems couldn't process Spanish and suggesting she obtain an English check. The incident sparked outrage from the customer and online commenters, highlighting issues of discrimination and outdated banking policies.

title: PNB Metlife IPO likely next fiscal, says CEO Sunil Mehta
summary: PNB Metlife's CEO Sunil Mehta indicated that the company's IPO is likely to take place next fiscal year, as the current market conditions are subdued. Punjab National Bank is currently selling a 4% stake in PNB Metlife as part of a price discovery process for the potential IPO. The American financial services major Metlife Inc. has plans to exit the company, necessitating the public offering.

title: Bank of America said to drop Merrill Lynch name from investment bank
summary: Bank of America is rebranding its investment banking arm as BofA Securities and its wealth management unit as Merrill, while renaming U.S. Trust to Bank of America Private Bank. This move is part of a larger campaign to remake the bank's image following crisis-era acquisitions. CEO Brian Moynihan's leadership has been praised by investor Warren Buffett for the company's strong performance, including a record net income in 2018.

title: Walmart Acquires Israeli Consumer Data Tech Startup Aspectiva
summary: Walmart has acquired Aspectiva, an Israeli startup specializing in leveraging machine learning and natural language processing to analyze consumer opinions for valuable insights. Aspectiva will join Walmart’s incubation arm, Store No 8, and continue to operate from its Tel Aviv offices. This acquisition marks Walmart's latest venture with Israeli technology companies, highlighting the country's innovation.

title: Top AI researcher leaves Morgan Stanley for academia
summary: Sasha Luccioni, an AI researcher specializing in natural language processing, has left Morgan Stanley to become a postdoctoral researcher at The Mila-Quebec Artificial Intelligence Institute. Her departure highlights the strong appeal of academia for high-level machine learning researchers. Morgan Stanley, along with other financial institutions like JPMorgan, is actively working to recruit top AI talent despite such exits.

title: First look: Chase moves into new East Valley campus
summary: JPMorgan Chase is expanding its new Tempe campus in the East Valley as its banking operations grow and the business model evolves. Some 2,000 employees have already relocated to the new facility at 2118 E. Elliot Road in Tempe, with more expected to move in. The expansion reflects the bank's growth and the changing landscape of the banking industry.

title: Texas Instruments prices $750 million of investment grade notes
summary: Texas Instruments announced the pricing of $750 million in 3.875% senior unsecured notes due March 15, 2039. The company plans to use the net proceeds for general corporate purposes, with the offering expected to close on March 11, 2019. Barclays Capital Inc., J.P. Morgan Securities LLC, MUFG Securities Americas Inc., Citigroup Global Markets Inc., Merrill Lynch, Pierce, Fenner & Smith Incorporated, Mizuho Securities USA LLC, and Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC are serving as joint book-running managers.

title: JPMorgan Chase Enters A Hot Fintech Space: Point-Of-Sale (POS) Financing
summary: JPMorgan Chase is entering the point-of-sale (POS) financing market with "My Chase Plan" and "My Chase Loan," allowing customers to finance purchases over time. This move comes as consumer demand for POS financing is growing, driven by younger consumers, with fintech startups transforming the space with new digital capabilities and business models. The article suggests that many banks and credit unions might be overlooking this significant market shift.

title: JPMorgan to stop financing private prisons and detention centers after protests
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co has decided to stop financing private operators of prisons and detention centers due to ongoing evaluations and pressure from activists. This decision follows similar moves by other banks, like Wells Fargo, which are reducing their involvement with the private prison industry. The move by JPMorgan, while potentially symbolic, highlights increasing public scrutiny and financial risks associated with companies profiting from detention centers, especially those involved in immigration policies.

title: Goldman Sachs Tells Its Bankers to Loosen Their Neckties (Published 2019)
summary: Goldman Sachs has relaxed its dress code for bankers, moving towards a "flexible" common sense approach that aligns with evolving industry standards. This change follows similar moves by competitors like JPMorgan Chase and is seen as an attempt to appeal to younger workers and bridge the gap with Silicon Valley's casual attire, though the firm advises employees to still exercise good judgment in their choice of dress. The new policy reflects broader shifts in corporate culture on Wall Street.

title: What Goldman’s New Dress Code Says About the Millennial Workplace
summary: Goldman Sachs loosened its employee dress code, following a 2017 change for its tech department and other financial institutions. This move reflects a broader trend of companies adapting to a more casual, millennial-driven workplace culture, emphasizing the importance of internal consistency between espoused values and employee preferences to positively impact the bottom line. The article suggests that understanding employee preferences and explaining company changes can strengthen brand reputation and customer loyalty.

title: JPMorgan Chase Stops Funding Private Prison Companies, and Immigration Activists Applaud (Published 2019)
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Company announced it would no longer finance private operators of prisons and detention centers, a move celebrated by immigrant rights advocates. This decision comes after years of public pressure and protests against the bank's involvement with companies like CoreCivic and GEO Group, which had borrowed substantial sums from banks including JPMorgan Chase. The article notes that while private companies house a small percentage of the overall prison population, they hold about three-quarters of immigrant detainees.

title: The Biggest Banks in America
summary: This article examines the size of the biggest banks in America, highlighting that the top 10 U.S. banks control a combined $12.2 trillion in assets. It lists the top 10 banks by asset size as of Q3 2018, noting that even "smaller" banks hold hundreds of billions in assets, posing potential systemic risks. The piece emphasizes the massive scale of the U.S. banking sector and compares it to global economic indicators.

title: HarborOne tops list of fastest-growing Mass. banks
summary: HarborOne has topped the list of fastest-growing banks in Massachusetts. The article notes that Bay State banks overall saw their lowest year-over-year increase since the beginning of the decade, highlighting HarborOne's growth as an anomaly in a slower market.

title: HSBC's Major: U.S. 10-Year Yield Stuck Between 2.40% and 2.90%
summary: HSBC's Steven Major discusses the outlook for global bond markets, while JP Morgan ETFs' Samantha Azzarello highlights the continued appeal of short-duration bonds for income and the importance of having more duration for portfolio balance in volatile times. Azzarello also suggests a more active and granular approach within fixed income than reliance on broad indexes like the Bloomberg Barclays U.S. Aggregate Bond Index. The article emphasizes the need for smarter implementation within fixed income to achieve better duration profiles and income.

title: 2019 Chief Investment Officer Summit
summary: The 2019 Chief Investment Officer Summit, held on May 16-17, 2019, in New York City, gathered leading investment professionals to discuss topics such as asset allocation, risk management, and manager selection. The article features detailed profiles of numerous speakers, including CIOs from major corporations, foundations, and public retirement systems, highlighting their professional backgrounds and areas of expertise. It provides a comprehensive overview of the event's participants and their significant contributions to the investment industry.

title: MercadoLibre, Inc. Announces Closing of Follow-on Offering
summary: MercadoLibre, Inc. announced the closing of its underwritten public offering of US$1.15 billion in common stock, including the full exercise of the underwriters’ option for additional shares. The company also closed a $750 million private offering to PayPal and expects to close a $100 million preferred stock offering to Dragoneer, totaling $2 billion in offerings. This significant capital raise was managed by Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan, and Morgan Stanley as joint bookrunners.

summary: Wells Fargo is facing

title: The Story Behind the Real (And Fake) Names on Credit Cards
summary: This article delves into the origins of placeholder names seen on credit card marketing materials, revealing whether they belong to real people or fictional identities. It uncovers the stories behind names like CF Frost on American Express cards, D. Barrett on Chase cards, and Chris L Martin on Bank of America promotions. The piece explains why banks use these names to engage potential customers and reflects on the broader practice of displaying a name on a credit card.

title: Ripple vs. JPMorgan – 1:0: Citigroup Shelves Its Stablecoin
summary: Citigroup has reportedly shelved its plans to issue a bank-backed stablecoin, indicating that such "bank coins" are considered useless for streamlining cross-border payments, echoing criticism from Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse. While Citi is exploring blockchain technology, it seeks short-term results that stablecoins cannot provide. This development follows JPMorgan's introduction of its JPM Coin, amidst a broader industry discussion on the utility of bank-issued cryptocurrencies.

title: ETFs Can Boost Your Liquidity Management Strategy
summary: This article discusses how Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) can be used as a liquidity management strategy, particularly focusing on cash equitization. It explains how using ETFs to invest excess cash can prevent "cash drag" and improve portfolio returns, especially for institutional investors and bond portfolios. The piece highlights that ETFs offer significant liquidity, making them an efficient tool for managing cash positions.

title: JP Morgan Leads ETF Issuers in In-House Assets
summary: JP Morgan is at the forefront of the "bring your own assets" (BYOA) trend within the ETF issuer sector, directing its own clients towards its ETF products. This strategy, which involves proper disclosure, allows for lower costs for in-house clients compared to competitors and can rapidly increase an ETF's asset base, as seen with the JPMorgan BetaBuilders Japan ETF. In 2018, JP Morgan reportedly raised $15.6 billion from in-house affiliates, making clients account for 53% of its ETF assets.

title: JPMorgan Chase gives $350M to workforce training, community colleges
summary: JPMorgan Chase announced an investment of $350 million over five years into community colleges and career training programs, extending a previous $250 million initiative. This funding aims to improve economic mobility for underserved groups and address skill gaps, particularly in light of community colleges being underfunded despite their critical role in workforce development. The initiative coincides with federal efforts to prioritize workforce training, though challenges such as covering non-tuition expenses for students remain.

title: Mobile Software Firm Movius Raises $45M From JPMorgan Chase, Adds Silicon Valley CEO
summary: Movius, an Atlanta-based mobile communications software provider, has secured $45 million in Series D funding led by JPMorgan Chase & Co., bringing its total equity raised to $91 million. The company also announced the appointment of John Loiacono, a seasoned Silicon Valley technology executive, as its new CEO. Movius plans to use this funding to expand its global enterprise client acquisition, leveraging its cloud-based software that enables secure personal and professional communication on a single mobile device for highly regulated industries.

title: Global Banks, Led by JPMorgan Chase, Invested $1.9 Trillion in Fossil Fuels Since Paris Climate Pact
summary: A new report reveals that 33 global banks have invested $1.9 trillion in fossil fuel projects since the 2016 Paris Agreement, with JPMorgan Chase leading the pack. U.S. banks, including Wells Fargo, Citi, and Bank of America, account for the top four investors, despite growing awareness of climate change and past pledges to support a low-carbon economy. This continued investment occurs as climate-related disasters intensify globally.

title: Bank of Montreal picks Irish unit as post-Brexit EU hub
summary: Bank of Montreal (BMO) has chosen its existing Irish unit to serve as its future European hub following Brexit. This restructuring will allow its fully-licensed Bank of Montreal Ireland (BMI) subsidiary to become its sole EU-based entity, securing passporting rights across the European Economic Area and access to European Central Bank funding. Standard & Poor's has assigned an A+ long-term rating to the Irish unit, recognizing it as a "core subsidiary" despite its small contribution to BMO's overall revenues and assets.

title: Hellman & Friedman led group agrees $11bn Ultimate Software deal
summary: An investor group led by private equity firm Hellman & Friedman is set to acquire Ultimate Software, a human capital management solutions provider, in an $11 billion deal. All Ultimate Software stockholders will receive $331.50 in cash per share, and the company will continue to operate under its current leadership, while also making additional investments in products and services for its customers. This transaction, which has been unanimously approved by Ultimate Software's board, expects to close in mid-2019.

title: BlackRock to buy risk platform in $1.3 billion wager
summary: BlackRock, the world's largest money manager, is set to acquire French software provider eFront for $1.3 billion in cash. This acquisition aims to expand BlackRock's private equity and real estate analytics capabilities, integrating eFront's technology with its existing Aladdin risk management platform. The deal reflects BlackRock's strategy to grow its business in technology and alternative investments.

title: Steiner sells majority stake in DoBro rental tower to JPMorgan fund
summary: Steiner NYC has sold a majority stake in the Hub, its 55-story Downtown Brooklyn rental tower, to a JPMorgan real estate equity fund for $253 million, valuing the building at $408 million. This sale coincided with a $330 million refinancing of the property at 333 Schermerhorn Street by Nuveen Real Estate, replacing an older construction loan. The 750-unit tower was completed in 2017 and includes residential and retail spaces.

title: BlackRock invests in pot stock
summary: Five BlackRock funds have become the largest institutional investor in Curaleaf Holdings Inc., a cannabis dispensary operator. This makes BlackRock an early mover in the cannabis sector, which has struggled to attract institutional investment due to the federal prohibition of marijuana in the U.S. Despite the challenges, Curaleaf's shares have risen significantly this year, particularly after announcing a deal to sell hemp-derived products in CVS Health Corp. stores.

title: Fund debuts in Norwalk with U.S. housing as foundation
summary: Hoya Capital Real Estate, based in Norwalk, launched HOMZ, a new exchange-traded fund (ETF) focused on the U.S. housing sector. The fund, designed by Alex Pettee, aims to provide everyday investors with a way to profit from the projected growth in the housing industry due to a national shortage. HOMZ is indexed to 100 publicly traded companies involved in various aspects of housing, from construction and financing to home improvement and insurance.

title: Bank of America tech chief is skeptical on blockchain even though BofA has the most patents for it
summary: Bank of America's tech and operations chief, Cathy Bessant, expresses skepticism about blockchain's immediate utility, despite the bank holding more blockchain-related patents (82) than any other financial firm. Bessant views blockchain as a technology still searching for a clear use case that scales beyond individual transactions. While the bank is "future-proofing" with patents, Bessant is particularly doubtful about public blockchains and wary of projects like JPM Coin's actual usage volume.

title: Morgan Stanley Fills Manager Seats in New York and Florida
summary: Morgan Stanley has moved Bernardo “Bernie” Duque to manage its Penn Plaza branch in New York City and brought in Vincent Colucci as the new complex manager in Naples, Fla., following Gregg Stupinski's departure. These changes reflect the challenges wirehouses face in filling high-pressure branch manager roles as the focus shifts from recruiting to retaining advisors and promoting bank products. The firm is still searching for managers to fill several other vacated positions in New England and Boston.

title: Goldman Sachs CEO turns up in Saudi Arabia as uproar fades over Khashoggi killing
summary: Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon is making his first trip to Saudi Arabia, signaling that Wall Street's hesitations about doing business with the kingdom are diminishing after the murder of Jamal Khashoggi. Other major banks like JPMorgan Chase and Morgan Stanley are also resuming or strengthening their ties. Goldman Sachs aims to expand its presence, with several significant deals already underway in the country.

title: UBS considers sale, acquisition and other options for its asset management business
summary: UBS Group AG is evaluating various options for its asset management unit, including a partial sale or merger, and potentially acquiring Deutsche Bank's DWS Group. The unit, which has been impacted by investors shifting to cheaper funds, oversees about $800 billion, and UBS is exploring ways to ensure its long-term survival and compete with U.S. rivals. Discussions are ongoing, and the bank may still decide to keep the unit unchanged.

title: US Bank updates iPhone app to help millennials
summary: U.S. Bank updated its iPhone mobile app to include a "money mentorship" feature aimed at helping millennials analyze spending habits in real time and manage their finances. The app now allows Face ID for secure access and provides a comprehensive view of a user's financial portfolio. This update, which will also be released for Android, coincides with a national ad campaign highlighting the bank's role in customers' everyday financial lives.

title: Long/ Short Equity Hedge Funds Are Back To Winning
summary: Hedge funds, particularly long/short equity funds, are showing a significant turnaround in performance, with the Eurekahedge Hedge Fund Index climbing 0.89% in February. Despite continued investor redemptions, long/short equity funds achieved $4.9 billion in performance-based gains in February due to strength in global equities, especially consumer discretionary and technology stocks. North American funds also exhibited strong performance-based growth, though they, like other regions, still faced substantial investor outflows.

title: Lyft is threatening litigation against Morgan Stanley, accusing the firm of supporting short-selling
summary: Lyft is threatening legal action against Morgan Stanley, accusing the firm of enabling short-selling by pre-IPO investors who were subject to lock-up agreements. Lyft sent a letter to Morgan Stanley questioning its alleged role in marketing products that would allow investors to bet against the stock, while Morgan Stanley has strongly denied the accusations, stating its activities were normal market-making. The dispute comes as many tech companies prepare for IPOs, with Morgan Stanley also slated to underwrite Lyft's rival Uber's IPO.

title: SL Green Secures $455M from Wells Fargo for NY Tower Development
summary: SL Green Realty Corp. has secured an additional $455 million in debt financing from Wells Fargo for the ongoing development of One Vanderbilt, a 67-story tower in New York. This latest financing brings the total debt load for the $3.2-billion project to $2.2 billion. The tower, which is 54% leased and expected to be completed by the end of 2020, has also recently signed leases with several major tenants.

title: Apple and Goldman Sachs Dive Head-First Into Crowded $175 Billion Credit Card Pool
summary: Apple and Goldman Sachs have launched a new credit card, entering the competitive $175 billion industry. While Apple aims to revolutionize the credit card experience, both companies are new to consumer credit and must quickly master customer service, dispute resolution, and statement management, areas where Apple typically maintains end-to-end control. They are implementing strategies like iMessage support and machine learning for transaction clarity to address these challenges.

title: Ron Redell Discusses the Birth, Growth and Culture of DoubleLine on The Sherman Show Podcast
summary: Ron Redell, president of DoubleLine Group, discussed his career, the establishment of DoubleLine's operational infrastructure, and the firm's culture on The Sherman Show podcast. He shared insights into his transition from a professional football hopeful to a leader in asset management, touching upon DoubleLine's rejection of asset growth fixation and its independent, private company structure. The podcast also covered the importance of consistent management and cultivating younger talent within the firm.

title: Financial Sector ETF 'XLF' Mutes CEO Questioning on Capitol Hill
summary: Despite big bank CEOs facing intense questioning on Capitol Hill regarding executive compensation and banking system stability, the Financial Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLF) showed minimal reaction, down only 0.19 percent. Investors are bracing for a less-than-stellar first-quarter earnings season for banks, with a projected 4.3 percent year-over-year reduction in earnings growth for the S&P 500. The focus will be on corporate guidance for the rest of the year to allay investor fears amid these financial challenges.

title: Bank of America to raise minimum wage to $20 per hour by 2021
summary: Bank of America announced on Tuesday that it plans to raise its minimum wage to $20 per hour by 2021. The first increase will be on May 1st, when the hourly wage will rise by $2 to $17. This move follows other Wall Street banks that have raised wages after the 2017 corporate tax cuts, with Bank of America having previously raised its minimum wage to $15 two years prior.

title: Wells Fargo CEO drama eclipses struggling business
summary: Wells Fargo is conducting a search for a new CEO, but this drama is overshadowed by the bank's struggling business operations and ongoing regulatory scandals. The company's revenue in its consumer division fell, and its wholesale and investment banking divisions also saw declines, leading to significant cost-cutting measures including job eliminations and branch closures. Analysts do not expect significant improvement in the near future, emphasizing that the biggest challenge for Wells Fargo is to convince the Fed to lift the asset cap imposed in 2018.

title: Parsons Corporation Files Registration Statement for Proposed Initial Public Offering
summary: Parsons Corporation announced it has filed a registration statement on Form S-1 with the SEC for a proposed initial public offering of its common stock. The number of shares and price range are yet to be determined, and Parsons plans to list its common stock on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol "PSN." Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC, BofA Merrill Lynch, and Morgan Stanley are serving as joint lead book-running managers for the offering.

title: Outsize pay for CEO of small online bank
summary: Gregory Garrabrants, CEO of the small online bank Axos Financial Inc., earned $34.5 million in 2018, outstripping the CEOs of much larger banks like JPMorgan Chase and Goldman Sachs. This compensation, tied to Axos's significant share gains (up 72% last fiscal year), stemmed from a complex pay structure likened to hedge fund incentives, sparking debate among shareholders and analysts about its fairness relative to the bank's size and the CEO's actual performance contributions. While some argue it aligns with shareholder interests, others view it as an example of short-term incentives gone awry and an out-of-touch board.

title: Marcella Regniault
summary: Marcella Regniault is the Vice President, Digital Sales Planning and Client Services at ESPN, where she oversees digital client services strategy to optimize advertising inventory and revenue. Before joining ESPN, she held significant roles at JP Morgan Chase Inc., focusing on ad operations, and at Ziff Davis, managing marketing and sales operations. Her extensive career also includes leadership positions at TVGuide.com, The Wall Street Journal Digital Network, and Time, Inc.

title: What’s the Second Best Performing Asset Since 1999?
summary: This article highlights gold as the second-best performing asset since 1999, according to JPMorgan data, only surpassed by REITs. It discusses gold's negative correlation with the market, its role in diversifying portfolios, and the investment strategies of figures like Ray Dalio. The article also notes the continued accumulation of gold by central banks, particularly China.

title: SL Green snags huge bank lease
summary: SL Green's investment in the Hudson Yards area is paying off as First Republic Bank signs a 212,000-square-foot lease at 460 W. 34th St. SL Green will soon control the office tower, having purchased a majority stake from the Kaufman Organization for $440 million. The building will undergo redevelopment to give it a "Midtown South-style creative vibe," with work scheduled to finish by late 2021.

title: JPMorgan Shuffles Executive Ranks, Promoting Two Women (Published 2019)
summary: JPMorgan Chase promoted Marianne Lake and Jennifer Piepszak to key executive roles, positioning them as potential successors to CEO Jamie Dimon. Ms. Lake will become CEO of consumer lending, while Ms. Piepszak will take over as chief financial officer. This move comes amidst discussions on diversity in leadership succession across major banks.

title: Deutsche Bank faces action over $20bn Russian money-laundering scheme
summary: Deutsche Bank is facing potential fines, legal action, and prosecution of senior management due to its alleged role in a $20bn Russian money-laundering scheme, according to a confidential internal report. The bank admits a high risk of significant disciplinary action from US and UK regulators, which could damage its global brand, investor confidence, and market value. The scheme, dubbed the Global Laundromat, involved Russian criminals moving money into the western financial system between 2010 and 2014, with detectives estimating the total cash involved could be up to $80bn.

title: TD Ameritrade to Transition $35 Billion in Retirement Plan Assets to Broadridge
summary: TD Ameritrade has agreed to sell $35 billion in retirement plan custody and trust assets to Broadridge's Matrix Financial Solutions. This deal will make Matrix one of the largest independent service providers of custodial solutions with approximately $420 billion in assets under administration. While it will provide advisors with more options, analysts note potential risks due to client questions and changes in pricing.

title: Pampa Energía analiza vender su participación mayoritaria en Edenor
summary: Pampa Energía, Argentina's most diversified energy company, is considering selling its 51.4% majority stake in Edenor. JPMorgan Chase & Co. has been selected to advise on the potential operation, which is still in early exploration stages. The move comes as the country approaches a presidential election, with the re-election of Mauricio Macri uncertain, and Edenor's market capitalization stands at around USD 825 million.

title: Verint Systems' Anil Chawla on how speech analytics is bettering customer experience
summary: Anil Chawla, India managing director of customer engagement solutions at Verint Systems, discusses how speech analytics is enhancing customer experience. Verint is expanding its market in India by targeting insurance, digital wallet providers, and the fintech sector, leveraging its solutions to bridge gaps between front-end and back-office operations and provide actionable insights from unstructured data. The company's speech analytics tools help address customer complaints, offer real-time agent guidance, and improve several key performance indicators for clients across various sectors.

title: Equinor strengthens its commitment to climate leadership
summary: Equinor announced new steps to demonstrate industry leadership on climate change, including setting climate-related ambitions beyond 2030 and assessing its portfolio against a well below 2°C scenario. This commitment builds on Equinor's existing climate strategy and involves collaboration with investors participating in Climate Action 100+. The company also plans to strengthen the link between climate targets and executive remuneration and review memberships in industry associations with active climate and energy policy positions.

title: The Two Women Executives Leading JPMorgan Chase Into The Future
summary: JPMorgan Chase is advancing two senior women, Marianne Lake and Jennifer Piepszak, into key leadership roles, positioning them as potential successors to CEO Jamie Dimon. Lake will become CEO of Consumer Lending, while Piepszak will take over as CFO, marking a significant step for women in the banking industry given their decades of experience and the company's succession planning. Their appointments come as Dimon continues to lead the bank, with Wall Street closely watching who will eventually take the helm of the U.S.'s largest bank.

title: Here are the executive power moves that help explain everything that's going on in finance, tech and retail
summary: This article details significant executive appointments and promotions across finance, tech, and retail sectors. Key moves include JPMorgan appointing Jennifer Piepszak as CFO and Marianne Lake to CEO of Consumer Lending, Google Cloud hiring former SAP executive Robert Enslin, and Flexport onboarding a Chief Data Officer and Chief Information Security Officer. Best Buy also announced Corie Barry as its first female CEO, and Robinhood made changes to its compliance team, featuring Scott Friedman stepping down and John Castelly taking over as Chief Compliance Officer.

title: After years serving CEOs, Goldman's Ayco also wants other workers
summary: Goldman Sachs' Ayco unit, traditionally serving top executives, is expanding its financial advisory services to target millions of other affluent employees at major U.S. companies. This expansion, which includes offering high-yield savings accounts and personal loans through its Marcus online bank, is part of Goldman's strategy to reposition itself as a traditional bank and reach a wider customer base to meet its $5 billion new annual revenue target by 2020. Despite some investor concerns about entering new territory, Goldman views Ayco's growth into the mass affluent market as a cost-effective way to acquire new clients.

title: Bank of Morgan Stanley?
summary: Morgan Stanley's CEO James Gorman has restructured the leadership of its wealth management and institutional banking units, leading to speculation that the firm is aiming to expand into a full-service bank. This move, which includes Shelley O’Connor overseeing both banking parts of the business, suggests a future where Morgan Stanley might resemble Bank of America or JPMorgan. The article highlights that Morgan Stanley has already shifted significantly in the past decade, with half its revenues coming from wealth management.

title: Real Estate
summary: This article from The Boston Globe's "Real Estate" section features various news items focusing on commercial and residential real estate developments in greater Boston. Key topics include concerns over sea level rise in the Seaport, major life science company moves and tax incentives in Somerville and Alewife, significant investments in commercial properties to attract tenants, and large corporate lease deals like JPMorgan at South Station Tower and Hasbro's move to Boston. The articles also touch on local zoning changes, debates over city taxes on office buildings, and planned residential projects.

title: Investors Sue to Block Mellanox-Nvidia Deal, Report Says
summary: A shareholder of Mellanox Technologies Ltd. has filed a class-action lawsuit to block the company's acquisition by Nvidia Corp. for $6.9 billion. The suit alleges that Mellanox failed to provide sufficient information to the SEC regarding Nvidia's bid and criticized JP Morgan's analysis of the deal. The transaction, announced in March, is expected to be completed later this year.

title: Meet the woman leading Chase's branch expansion in Pittsburgh
summary: JPMorgan Chase hired Sandra Reiman from Citizens Bank to lead its branch expansion efforts in Pittsburgh. Reiman's move to Chase signifies a strategic shift from competing against the bank to joining its operations. This hiring is part of a larger initiative by the nation's biggest bank to expand its presence in the Pittsburgh market.

title: Vornado, Rudin mull 1,450-foot tower in Midtown East
summary: Vornado Realty Trust and Rudin Management are considering a 1,450-foot, 1.68 million-square-foot office tower at 350 Park Avenue in Midtown East, taking advantage of the area's rezoning. This potential joint venture would involve demolishing existing buildings owned by both companies at 51st and 52nd streets. The proposed tower includes extensive amenities and would be among the tallest new developments in Midtown East, following the city's 2017 rezoning initiative.

title: Lehman’s London ghost office nears wind-down after 12 years| Gulf Times
summary: The European arm of Lehman Brothers is finally nearing its complete wind-down in London, almost 12 years after the Wall Street giant's collapse. Administrators from PwC, who have overseen the process since 2008, are preparing to leave their office by June 2020, with fewer than 20 people now working to conclude the remaining legal cases and asset distributions. Creditors of the European unit have already received £26.4bn ($34.6bn), with many repaid interest, marking a significant milestone in winding up the firm's legacy.

title: Midtown East could get another supertall on Park Avenue
summary: Vornado Realty Trust and Rudin Management are reportedly exploring a partnership to construct a 1,450-foot supertall skyscraper at 350 Park Avenue in Midtown East, following the neighborhood's rezoning. This proposed tower would include nearly 1.7 million square feet of space and various amenities, potentially requiring the demolition of two existing buildings. While plans are currently speculative, this project would join several other major developments announced in the area.

title: Tesla may be about to lose a key group of investors that have stuck with the struggling stock
summary: Tesla's recent pivot towards autonomous driving, highlighted by CEO Elon Musk's statements during an investor call, may alienate long-term growth investors who anticipated profitability from high-volume auto sales. While a recent $2.7 billion stock and bond offering provided a temporary relief rally, Barclays analyst Brian Johnson suggests the focus on autonomy pushes out the timeline for investor payoff, potentially causing "rational bulls" to reassess their investment in the struggling stock.

title: Tech Moves: F5 Networks lands former Marketo and J.P. Morgan execs; AI2 adds managing director; Groupon snags REI vet; and more
summary: F5 Networks announced two new senior executives: Mika Yamamoto as EVP and chief marketing & customer experience officer, and Geng Lin as CTO. AI2 appointed Bryan Hale as managing director of its incubator, while Groupon hired REI veteran Craig Rowley as chief marketing officer. The article also details several other notable tech hires and promotions across various Seattle-area companies, including EagleView, Adaptive Biotechnologies, Reverb, Genesys, Olis Robotics, and HNTB Corporation.

title: Private Prison Company GEO Group Says Activists Pose Risk to Bottom Line
summary: GEO Group, a private prison company, has warned investors that activist pressure leading to financial institutions divesting from the private prison industry poses a material adverse risk to its business. Both JP Morgan Chase and Wells Fargo have ceased new financing for private detention facilities in response to activist campaigns, impacting GEO Group's stock. Despite these challenges, GEO Group reported increased net income and revenues, expanding operations with new contracts.

title: Sallie Mae Is Launching Three New Credit Cards
summary: Sallie Mae is launching three new credit cards called Accelerate, Evolve, and Ignite, marking its expansion into the consumer banking industry beyond student loans. While these cash-back cards offer some benefits like cell phone protection and free FICO scores, their earning potential and perks are considered less competitive than existing cards from other issuers.
