The article suggests Sallie Mae needs to enhance its offerings to stand out in the crowded credit card market.

title: 20s Maurice Goodman
summary: Maurice Goodman, 27, is a risk and settlement manager at Seed CX, a cryptocurrency trading platform, where he helps attract clients and manages risk. Before joining Seed CX, he honed his skills at CME Group and Bank of America Merrill Lynch. Goodman is also an active real estate investor, co-founding Goodman & Przybyl Properties, and is inspired by his parents' hard work and entrepreneurial spirit.

title: Weatherford Reaches Agreement With Senior Noteholders On Terms Of Comprehensive Financial Restructuring To Create Sustainable Capital Structure And Greatly Enhance Liquidity
summary: Weatherford International plc has reached an agreement with its senior noteholders on a comprehensive financial restructuring plan. This plan aims to significantly reduce the company's long-term debt by over $5.8 billion, provide new financing, and establish a more sustainable capital structure. The restructuring is expected to be implemented through a "pre-packaged" Chapter 11 process, allowing the company to continue operations without interruption for customers, vendors, partners, or employees.

title: The Good, The Bad, & The Ugly Of US Mobile Banking Experiences In 2019
summary: Forrester's 2019 review of US mobile banking apps found that while banks excel at log-in and money movement features, they are only "just OK" at self-service and financial management. A significant weakness identified was their failure to provide actionable financial advice and adequately reassure users on security and privacy. The report highlights Bank of America and USAA as leading providers in money management and service features.

title: Sempra Energy and partners begin production from Cameron LNG project
summary: Sempra Energy and its partners have commenced production from the Cameron LNG project's first liquefaction train in Hackberry, Louisiana. This milestone is a precursor to the first cargo, expected in the coming weeks, bringing the project closer to delivering 12 million tonnes per annum (Mtpa) of LNG. McDermott International and Chiyoda International were responsible for the engineering, procurement, and construction of the $6bn LNG export facility.

title: Meridian Bank delays 1Q earnings report due to mortgage snafu
summary: Meridian Bank has delayed its first-quarter earnings report because it originated residential mortgage loans in a neighboring state where it was not licensed. The bank disclosed that this oversight would result in a material weakness.

title: JP Morgan buys health-care payments firm InstaMed in the bank's biggest acquisition since the financial crisis
summary: J.P. Morgan Chase is acquiring InstaMed, a healthcare payments technology firm, for over $500 million, making it the bank's largest acquisition since the financial crisis. This move aims to deepen J.P. Morgan's presence in the $3.5 trillion U.S. health-care spending market and underscores the bank's aggressive strategy in the evolving world of payments. InstaMed, founded in 2004, automates medical billing and processed $94 billion in transactions last year.

title: JPMorgan to buy healthcare payments technology firm InstaMed
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. announced its plan to acquire InstaMed, a U.S. healthcare payments technology firm, for over $500 million. This acquisition is part of JPMorgan's deeper dive into the $3.5 trillion healthcare market, aiming to expand its payment services for healthcare consumers, providers, and payers, and to leverage InstaMed's established network and platform to address inefficiencies in healthcare payments. The deal is expected to integrate JPMorgan’s payment infrastructure into InstaMed, potentially also leveraging the bank's healthcare venture, Haven, with Amazon and Berkshire Hathaway.

title: JPMorgan to acquire healthcare payments company InstaMed
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. announced its acquisition of InstaMed, a U.S. healthcare payments technology company, for over $500 million. This acquisition allows JPMorgan to expand its wholesale payments business into the growing healthcare sector. InstaMed specializes in processing payments between patients, healthcare providers, and payers through a private, cloud-based platform.

title: Chase CEO Denies Debanking Conservatives
summary: During a JPMorgan Chase shareholder meeting, a shareholder activist questioned CEO Jamie Dimon about allegations of "debanking" conservatives for their political views. Dimon denied the claims, stating Chase does not debank individuals due to political beliefs but rather for regulatory reasons. The activist, David W. Almasi, urged conservatives to consider other banking options if Chase cannot guarantee protection from such actions.

title: Protesters Disrupt Chase Shareholder Meeting Over Financing of Controversial Pipeline
summary: Environmental activists protested outside and inside JPMorgan Chase's annual shareholder meeting in Chicago, May 21, 2019, to condemn the bank's extensive financing of fossil fuel projects, particularly the controversial Line 3 pipeline by Enbridge Energy. Organizers highlighted that Chase has provided nearly $200 billion in financing for fossil fuel projects since 2016, a figure significantly higher than other banks. Both Chase and Enbridge issued statements defending their positions, emphasizing sustainable solutions and community engagement, respectively.

title: BNY Mellon lays off staff in Pittsburgh
summary: BNY Mellon has continued making job cuts in its Pittsburgh office, following earlier layoffs in January. This move is part of a broader trend of layoffs among asset managers like BlackRock, State Street, Legg Mason, JP Morgan, Goldman Sachs, Invesco, and AllianceBernstein, who are struggling with outflows, price pressure, and market volatility. The company states it is optimizing its business structure for efficiency and better client service.

title: Exclusive: JPMorgan cuts ties with OxyContin maker Purdue Pharma - sources
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co has cut ties with Purdue Pharma LP due to the OxyContin maker's alleged role in the U.S. opioid crisis, forcing Purdue to find a new bank to manage cash and bill payments. This move makes JPMorgan the most high-profile corporation to distance itself from Purdue and the Sackler family amidst thousands of lawsuits. Purdue has since tapped Comerica Inc to handle its financial transactions and accounts.

title: New Zealand gets thematic and ESG ETFs, with help from iShares
summary: Smartshares, New Zealand's sole ETF provider, is expanding the Kiwi ETF market by listing eight new funds in early June, including thematic and ESG options. These new funds, which offer exposure to areas like AI, robotics, and innovative healthcare, will gain market exposure via iShares' Dublin-based UCITS ETFs, making them accessible to New Zealand retail investors in NZD-denominated ETFs. This strategy allows Smartshares to offer diverse investment opportunities cost-effectively while aiming to tap into institutional market segments currently dominated by banks.

title: Global Payments Agrees to Buy Total System Services
summary: Global Payments Inc. announced its agreement to acquire Total System Services Inc. for $21.5 billion, marking the payment industry's third major merger of the year. This all-stock deal aims to create a significant player providing payment technology and software to millions of merchants and financial institutions globally. The transaction is expected to generate $300 million in cost savings and combine Global Payments' merchant acquiring strength with Total System Services' issuer processing capabilities.

title: TRADING UP: Stifel Promotes Spensieri; Mrak to Refinitiv
summary: Stifel Financial Corp. appointed John Spensieri as Head of U.S. Equity Trading, while Refinitiv named Joseph Mrak as global head of wealth management. Other notable appointments include Stacey Gilbert as Portfolio Manager at Glenmede Investment Management and Bruce Savage as FIA's new head of Europe. The article details various leadership changes and new hires across several financial firms, highlighting significant career moves within the industry.

title: SeaWorld Entertainment, Inc. Announces Buyback and Hill Path Capital to Increase Investment
summary: SeaWorld Entertainment, Inc. announced a share buyback plan to acquire approximately 5.6 million shares for $150.0 million from an affiliate of Pacific Alliance Group (PAG). Concurrently, Hill Path Capital LP is increasing its investment by purchasing approximately 13.2 million shares from PAG, which will boost its equity stake in SeaWorld to about 34.5%. This move also includes the appointment of up to three Hill Path director designees to SeaWorld's Board of Directors, reinforcing the commitment of both the company and Hill Path Capital to SeaWorld's future growth and value for shareholders.

title: Global Payments to buy peer Total System for $21.5 billion in stock — CEO touts the benefits
summary: Global Payments announced its acquisition of Total System Services for approximately $21.5 billion in stock, marking the third major deal in the payment technology industry this year. The acquisition premium represents more than 20% to Total System's previous closing price. Global Payments CEO Jeff Sloan emphasized that the merger will enable continued investment to stay ahead in the evolving digital payments market.

title: Global Payments to buy Total System Services in $21.5B deal
summary: Global Payments announced its plan to acquire Total System Services for approximately $21.5 billion in stock, aiming to enhance its scale in the competitive payment technology industry. This deal marks Global Payments' largest acquisition and the third major consolidation within the sector this year, driven by the increasing shift to digital payments and growing competition from banks and fintech startups. The merged entity, which will operate under the Global Payments name, is expected to process over 50 billion transactions annually and immediately contribute to Global Payments' adjusted profit.

title: JPMorgan Chase settles class-action lawsuit after dad demands equal parental leave for men
summary: JPMorgan Chase settled a class-action lawsuit after an employee, Derek Rotondo, challenged the company's parental leave policy which he argued discriminated against fathers. Rotondo initially was told that only mothers would be eligible for the full 16 weeks of paid leave unless he could prove his wife had returned to work or was medically incapable. This settlement stems from his demand for equal parental leave for men.

title: J.P. Morgan Chase EEOC Complaint
summary: The ACLU and Outten & Golden LLP filed a discrimination charge against J.P. Morgan Chase on behalf of a male employee, Derek Rotondo, who claimed the company denied fathers paid parental leave on the same terms as mothers. The case settled in June 2019, with Chase agreeing to maintain a gender-neutral parental leave policy, train staff on its application, and pay $5 million to fathers who were denied equal parental leave. This settlement marks the first private class action lawsuit rectifying sex discrimination claims for fathers regarding parental leave.

title: JPMorgan Chase settles case with fathers over paid parental leave
summary: JPMorgan Chase has reached a $5 million settlement in a class-action lawsuit filed by male employees who alleged they were denied paid parental leave on terms equal to women. The American Civil Liberties Union, representing the fathers, stated that the settlement addresses claims from 2011 to 2017 and ensures JPMorgan maintains a gender-neutral parental leave policy. This marks the first class-action lawsuit settlement of its kind, and the agreement awaits court approval.

title: JPMorgan Chase to pay $5 million to male employees in parental-leave discrimination settlement
summary: JPMorgan Chase has agreed to a $5 million settlement in a class-action lawsuit alleging parental-leave discrimination against male employees. This marks the largest-ever settlement for such a case, where male workers were allegedly denied the same parental leave opportunities as female workers. The outcome could prompt other companies to re-evaluate their own family leave policies.

title: Pega Customer Service adds digital messaging capabilities
summary: Pegasystems has integrated digital messaging capabilities into its Pega Customer Service platform, allowing users to offer support through popular messaging apps like Facebook Messenger, Twitter's Direct Message, and Apple Business Chat. This move, stemming from the acquisition of In The Chat, aims to address increasing demand for text-based customer support, especially among younger demographics. Additionally, Pegasystems launched Enterprise Low-Code Factory, a new low-code development environment designed to enable non-software developers to create enterprise applications with built-in governance.

title: Synovus picks Regions exec as new CFO
summary: Synovus has named Jamie Gregory, formerly of Regions, as its new executive vice president and CFO. This appointment follows the previous CFO, Kevin Blair, being named COO in late 2018.

title: Brinks CEO: The $160 billion cannabis industry, much of it still illegal, makes for a 'beautiful opportunity'
summary: Brinks CEO Douglas Pertz sees a "beautiful opportunity" in the global cannabis industry, which he estimates to be $160 billion, despite most of it being illegal. Brinks currently provides cash and logistics services to Canopy Growth in Canada, but not in the U.S. due to federal prohibition. Pertz supports legislation like the SAFE Banking Act and STATES Act to integrate the cannabis industry with federally regulated banks and free states from federal penalties.

title: Santander pays US$50mn to end São Paulo tax probe
summary: Santander's Brazilian unit agreed to pay 196mn reais (US$49.7mn) to settle a tax evasion investigation in São Paulo. The probe focused on allegations that banks' leasing and factoring companies registered headquarters in other cities for tax benefits. Santander made the payment without admitting guilt, closing the case after a court ordered its CEO to attend a commission hearing.

title: JPMorgan Chase Seeks to Prohibit Card Customers From Suing (Published 2019)
summary: JPMorgan Chase is reintroducing arbitration provisions for about 47 million credit card accounts, including its popular Sapphire card, preventing customers from participating in class-action lawsuits or suing in court. Customers must object in writing by mail by August 7th to avoid the new individual arbitration agreement, though small-claims court remains an option. The bank claims arbitration is faster, less expensive, and yields better outcomes for customers, aligning with a broader Wall Street trend to avoid large settlements and negative publicity from class-action suits.

title: Northpointe Bank parent company raises $25 million from PE firm
summary: Northpointe Bancshare Inc., the parent company of Northpointe Bank, successfully raised $25 million in capital through a private placement of common stock with private equity firm Castle Creek Capital LLC. The Grand Rapids-based company plans to use these funds to support further growth and for general corporate purposes, with Castle Creek now owning 27 percent of Northpointe's outstanding equity. This investment is expected to help Northpointe, primarily a mortgage lender with $1.57 billion in assets, pursue organic growth opportunities and expand its market share.

title: JPMorgan Chase will bring 4,000 more workers to Plano with new tower project
summary: JPMorgan Chase is expanding its Plano campus with a new 12-story office tower, which will accommodate an additional 4,000 workers. This expansion will bring the total workforce at its Legacy West development to almost 11,000 employees. The more than $100 million project signifies Chase's continued investment in the Dallas-Fort Worth market and will make the campus over 1.5 million square feet.

title: Jamie Dimon shows the JPMorgan Chase flag at Philly’s big BIO meeting
summary: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon spoke at the BIO 2019 conference in Philadelphia, expressing concerns about the "self-inflicted" U.S.-China trade war and the potential for a broader "economic war." He also discussed his company's expansion in Philadelphia, efforts to cut healthcare costs, and the importance of immigration reform and higher minimum wages. Dimon touched on the soundness of the U.S. financial system despite problematic government policies and the need for stronger leadership and tougher journalists.

title: Wendy's sponsoring a $1B whole-biz refinancing transaction
summary: Wendy's International LLC is returning to whole-business securitization investors to refinance its existing asset-backed debt, planning a $1 billion, 2019-1 series of notes with staggered maturities. This refinancing could maintain the burger-chain franchisor's high operations leverage, with $869 million of the proceeds designated to pay outstanding securitization debt. The notes include a $150 million variable funding note and two $425 million term notes, all carrying preliminary investment-grade BBB ratings.

title: JPMorgan Scraps New App Service for Young People
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. is discontinuing Finn, its digital banking app designed to attract younger customers, just one year after its nationwide launch. The bank is transferring funds from Finn accounts to new Chase checking and savings accounts for existing clients. This move marks a quick reversal for a product JPMorgan had hoped would help secure new clientele.

title: BBVA Banco Francés y el Santander Río cambian de nombre
summary: BBVA Banco Francés and Santander Río are changing their names to BBVA Argentina and Banco Santander, respectively, as part of a global rebranding strategy focused on digital transformation. This change will see two long-standing financial brands in Argentina disappear, with the new names being presented to the public at the Martín Fierro awards ceremony. The move aims to enhance digital credibility, create global synergies, and facilitate expansion into new markets.

title: Credit ratings
summary: This article provides details on UBS's requested credit ratings from agencies such as Moody's, S&P, and Fitch. It lists the long-term, short-term, and outlook ratings for UBS Group AG, UBS AG, UBS Switzerland AG, UBS Europe SE, Credit Suisse International, Credit Suisse USA (LLC), and Credit Suisse Bank (Europe) S.A. The article emphasizes that these ratings reflect the agency's view at the time of issuance and are not a recommendation to buy, sell, or hold securities.

title: Fidelity custody business hooks up with lender to finance RIAs
summary: Fidelity Clearing & Custody Solutions has partnered with Merchant Investment Management to provide its RIA clients with preferential access to business loans for acquisitions and succession planning. This alliance aims to offer RIAs a capital alternative without requiring them to give up equity, with a discounted loan origination fee for Fidelity's clients. The move is designed to help RIAs access the capital needed for growth and scale through M&A.

title: Amazon launches a credit card for the 'underbanked' with bad credit
summary: Amazon, in partnership with Synchrony Financial, has launched "Amazon Credit Builder," a secured credit card program aimed at individuals with no credit history or bad credit. This initiative offers the same 5% cash back perks as the popular Amazon Store card and includes financial literacy tools, allowing users to build credit and eventually "graduate" to an unsecured card. The program addresses a significant market segment of underbanked Americans and comes with a 28.24% APR for the starter card.

title: Inside BlackRock’s ‘Once in a Lifetime’ Deal With Barclays, 10 Years Later
summary: This article reflects on BlackRock's acquisition of Barclays Global Investors (BGI) 10 years later, highlighting the transformative impact on BlackRock, particularly through its iShares ETF business. It details Barclays' regret over selling BGI to fund its Lehman Brothers acquisition and the initial cultural challenges during integration. The piece concludes that the deal, initially perceived as costly, proved to be a "once-in-a-lifetime opportunity" that cemented BlackRock's market dominance.

title: JPMorgan Years Away From Seeing Quantum-Computing Dividends
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. is years away from deploying quantum computing despite seeing potential in using the technology to speed up financial calculations. The bank has been collaborating with IBM researchers since late 2017 and has achieved minor successes, including theoretical proof that quantum computing can accelerate certain financial models. JPMorgan has been running tests on IBM’s 20-qubit machine via the cloud.

title: Wells Fargo is reportedly struggling to find a new CEO
summary: Wells Fargo is reportedly having difficulty finding a new chief executive officer. Several top candidates, including William Demchak of PNC and former U.S. Bancorp CEO Richard Davis, have turned down offers. Gordon Smith of J.P. Morgan also indicated he is likely staying with his current company.

title: South Korean firm Yanolja that reinvented love hotels gets Booking, GIC funding
summary: South Korean firm Yanolja, known for reinventing "love hotels" into modern budget accommodations, has secured $180 million in funding from Booking Holdings Inc and Singapore's sovereign wealth fund GIC Pte Ltd, pushing its valuation over $1 billion. CEO Kim Jong-yoon announced plans for an IPO as early as next year, aiming for global expansion, particularly in Southeast Asia, to compete with Oyo. The company's success highlights a shift in the accommodation market by targeting millennials and short-term tourists, moving past the stigma associated with traditional love hotels.

title: 'It's a free-for-all' PNC CEO says of big bank branch expansion
summary: PNC CEO William Demchak states that national retail expansion is a learning process, anticipating that newcomers Bank of America and Chase will take market share in Pittsburgh. He discussed this strategy at a Morgan Stanley conference, alongside related topics such as PNC's early childhood education program and comments about Wells Fargo.

title: Chart Industries Prices Offering of 3,500,000 Shares of Common Stock
summary: Chart Industries, Inc. announced the pricing of an underwritten public offering of 3,500,000 shares of its common stock at $73.50 per share, with an option for underwriters to purchase an additional 525,000 shares. The company estimates net proceeds of approximately $248.8 million, which it intends to use for a portion of the purchase price of its pending acquisition of Harsco Corporation's Industrial Air-X-Changers business, to repay indebtedness, and to cover related fees and expenses. J.P. Morgan Securities LLC, Credit Suisse Securities (USA) LLC, and Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC are acting as joint lead book-running managers for the offering.

title: BB&T, SunTrust announce merger to become Truist
summary: BB&T and SunTrust Banks announced their merger to form Truist, which will become the sixth-largest U.S. bank holding company, serving over 10 million households. The merger is expected to close in the third or fourth quarter of 2019, pending regulatory and shareholder approvals. Leadership roles in the new company have been outlined, with Kelly S. King becoming Chairman and CEO, and Bill Rogers becoming President and COO before succeeding King in 2021.

title: T. Rowe Price appoints Dina Dublon, Robert J. Stevens to board - Bizwomen
summary: T. Rowe Price Group Inc. has appointed Dina Dublon, former CFO at JPMorgan Chase & Co., and Robert J. Stevens, former CEO at Lockheed Martin Corp., as independent directors to its board. These appointments bring the money manager's board to 11 members, filling vacancies left by recent retirements. Dublon’s appointment increases the number of women on the board to four, aligning with efforts to promote more female representation in boardrooms.

title: See you at the ‘Truist’: BB&T, which scrapped Susquehanna, Nat Penn names, picks new brand
summary: BB&T and SunTrust announced their merged entity will be named "Truist," combining "trust" with an "I." The new name will brand the sixth-largest bank in the U.S. with approximately $450 billion in assets, but it is facing skepticism from branding experts and the public. The merger is driven by the need for bank automation and technology, according to analyst Stephen Scouten, who currently rates the shares as "neutral."

title: Morehouse College Entrepreneurship Center Shares In $640,000 Donation From JPMorgan Chase & Company
summary: The Morehouse College Entrepreneurship Center will receive a $640,000 donation from JPMorgan Chase & Company, contributing to a total investment of $820,500 over two years, to support the training of minority and women business owners in metro Atlanta through the Ascend Atlanta initiative. This funding will expand outreach to include community-based micro-businesses and small-to-midsize firms, alongside continued support for technology startups and access to capital and market opportunities for minority and women-owned businesses. JPMorgan Chase's total investment in the Ascend Atlanta initiative has reached approximately $1 million since 2017, aiding entrepreneurs in opening businesses and improving services.

title: How this Charlotte executive is getting Bank of America ready for what's next
summary: Wyatt Smith, Bank of America's market executive for commercial banking in the Carolinas, discusses cybersecurity, growth markets, and other significant trends impacting the bank. This conversation comes as Bank of America (NYSE: BAC), headquartered in Charlotte, is experiencing some of its best financial results. The article highlights how a Charlotte executive is preparing Bank of America for future challenges and opportunities.

title: American Assets Trust Acquires UTC Office Towers for $525M
summary: American Assets Trust, Inc. has acquired La Jolla Commons, a two-tower trophy office property in San Diego’s University Town Center submarket for $525 million. The property includes 724,000 square feet of office space, an entitled development parcel, and two parking structures. The seller was reportedly JP Morgan Asset Management, which had developed the project with Hines.

title: “Play It Cool” and Get Paid: How Wall Street Got Rich Off the Fresh Market Deal
summary: A shareholder lawsuit alleges that the 2016 Fresh Market buyout by Apollo Global Management, with assistance from JPMorgan Chase and various legal advisers, was designed to benefit the acquirers at the expense of public shareholders. The lawsuit claims that conflicts of interest were rampant, with JPMorgan Chase having significant financial ties to Apollo and allegedly manipulating financial analyses to justify a lower purchase price. This case highlights how Wall Street dealmaking can be riddled with conflicts that favor private equity firms and bankers over ordinary investors.

title: A delicate balance (sheet)
summary: Nonbank lenders are increasingly dominating the mortgage market, particularly in South Florida, by offering quicker loan approvals than traditional banks. This trend, while filling a market void, raises concerns about liquidity issues for nonbanks during economic downturns, as they lack the capital reserves and government backing of traditional banks, potentially leaving the housing market vulnerable. Financial experts and former regulators express worry about the potential for widespread defaults and the impact on the housing market if these nonbanks face financial distress.

title: Fifth Third Bank closing 44 Chicago-area branches
summary: Fifth Third Bank plans to close 44 branches in the Chicago area following its acquisition of MB Financial. The consolidation, set for July 9 or 10, will result in 190 remaining branches in the region and a "relatively small" number of job cuts. This move positions Fifth Third Bank close to Northern Trust in terms of Chicago-area banking market share, vying for fourth place.

title: DOJ settles redlining lawsuit against First Merchants Bank
summary: The U.S. Department of Justice has settled a redlining lawsuit against First Merchants Bank, alleging discriminatory residential mortgage lending practices in Indianapolis-Marion County. The settlement requires the bank to take several corrective actions, including opening new branches in majority-Black census tracts, investing in a special subsidy fund of $1.12 million, and increasing advertising and outreach in underserved areas. This marks the second fair lending settlement under the Trump administration, notably without a civil money penalty.

title: FOMC Recap Doves Play Catchup With Markets
summary: The Federal Reserve hinted at interest rate cuts, with nearly half of voting members now anticipating two cuts this year, largely due to ongoing trade disputes. Markets are pricing in a high probability of a cut in July, and potentially a second in September. This shift led to falling bond yields, a slight rise in equities, and significant moves in gold, USD/JPY, and USD/CHF.

title: Insight Acquires PCM for $581M in Cash and Debt
summary: Insight Enterprises Inc. has acquired El Segundo-based PCM Inc. for approximately $581 million, including cash and debt. This acquisition will add PCM’s 40 offices and 4,000 employees globally to Insight, creating a combined entity offering a wide range of technology hardware, software, and services. The merger is expected to generate around $70 million in savings by the end of 2021 and close in the second half of the year.

title: Lloyds Bank Freezes Offshore Accounts in Money Laundering Crackdown
summary: Lloyds Banking Group Plc has frozen accounts of some offshore banking customers in Jersey as part of a crackdown on money laundering. The Financial Times reported that 8,000 accounts were frozen, though the bank did not confirm the exact number. This action is part of the bank's efforts to tighten controls and meet anti-money-laundering requirements on the island.

title: Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan on Why the U.S. Will Avoid a Recession
summary: Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan believes the U.S. economy will avoid a recession, expecting GDP growth to flatten out at 2%. He emphasizes the bank's "responsible growth" mantra, which includes direct consumer lending, tolerating market-share declines in mortgages for safer operations, and offering no-fee checking accounts with direct deposit. Moynihan's leadership has been praised for turning BofA around, increasing profitability and stock value, despite some past decisions.

title: Coinbase Has More Users Than Schwab
summary: In October 2017, Coinbase, a popular U.S. cryptocurrency exchange, surpassed Charles Schwab Corp. in total user accounts, reaching over 13.3 million users. This surge in users coincided with bitcoin's rapid price increase and growing mainstream acceptance, despite skepticism from some financial figures. The article highlights the significant growth of Coinbase's user base compared to the long-established brokerage firm, though Schwab still managed significantly higher assets under management.

title: Dimon to Bank of America: We’re Coming for You in Branch-Expansion Battle
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. CEO Jamie Dimon has declared a competitive battle with Bank of America Corp., as both banks plan significant branch expansions across the U.S. Each bank aims to add at least 400 branches in new and existing markets over the coming years, with 90 new retail locations opened by each in 2019 alone. This strategic move intensifies competition for consumer deposits in rapidly growing U.S. cities.

title: JPMorgan Chase expands Seattle engineering center to 100 people, plans to add hundreds more
summary: JPMorgan Chase is significantly expanding its technology engineering center in Seattle, growing to 100 people in its first year and signing a new lease to accommodate hundreds more. This expansion is part of the financial services giant's major investment in cloud technology, partnering with AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud, and signals Seattle's growing potential as a fintech hub. The bank's CEO, Jamie Dimon, initially skeptical, is now fully committed to cloud adoption and integrating AI into operations.

title: JPMorgan Chase CEO says student debt crisis a "disgrace" that's "hurting America"
summary: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon has again criticized the student debt crisis, calling it a "disgrace" that is "hurting America." While not endorsing Bernie Sanders' plan for debt elimination, Dimon suggested fixing broken parts of student lending, forgiving those in need, and making universities more responsible. He also pointed blame at the government for making "irresponsible" loans since 2010.

title: Bank of America Will Stop Lending to Private-Prison Firms
summary: Bank of America, the second-biggest U.S. bank, announced its decision to stop lending to companies that operate private prisons and detention centers. This move follows an internal due diligence process and discussions with civil rights leaders. JPMorgan and Wells Fargo had previously indicated they would also exit this business space.

title: Expanded Fiduciary Duties for Directors of CBCA Companies
summary: The Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA) was amended on June 21, 2019, to codify the fiduciary duties of directors as outlined in the BCE Inc. v. 1976 Debentureholders Supreme Court case. The amendment expands the list of stakeholders directors may consider to include shareholders, employees, retirees and pensioners, creditors, consumers, governments, the environment, and the long-term interests of the corporation. This change requires directors of CBCA companies to be more aware of the broader impact of their decisions.

title: RealWear raises $80M from Teradyne, Qualcomm, others for industrial augmented reality headset
summary: RealWear, a Vancouver, Wash.-based company specializing in industrial augmented reality headsets, announced an $80 million Series B equity and debt round. This funding comes from investors like Teradyne, Qualcomm, and Bose, and will fuel the company's significant growth in providing ruggedized, voice-controlled AR devices to industrial workers globally. RealWear's devices are used by major companies to improve remote video calling, document navigation, and data visualization, with strong revenue growth and projections for a nine-figure year.

title: American Express Travel Insurance Review (Coverage, Policies) [2020]
summary: This article reviews American Express travel insurance, detailing its coverage, policies, and pricing as of 2020. It compares Amex's offerings with protections provided by other major credit cards like the Chase Sapphire Reserve and explains how to sign up for policies and file claims. The review also covers American Express rental car insurance, highlighting its benefits and limitations.

title: Northern Trust lists yet more quality ETFs
summary: Northern Trust's FlexShares is launching three new smart beta ETFs focused on quality and low volatility factors for US, Developed Markets ex-US, and Emerging Markets. The article also discusses the "bring your own assets" (BYOA) strategy used by asset managers like JPMAM and reportedly FlexShares, where existing client assets are channeled into new ETFs to rapidly build AUM and liquidity, thereby minimizing closure risk. FlexShares reportedly sources 67% of its ETF assets from existing Northern Trust clients.

title: Deutsche Bank outlines significant strategic transformation and restructuring plans
summary: Deutsche Bank announced a significant strategic transformation and restructuring plan aimed at improving long-term profitability. Key measures include exiting Global Equities, reducing Fixed Income operations, and creating a Capital Release Unit to wind down non-strategic assets. The bank also plans a cost reduction program, expects cumulative charges of EUR 7.4 billion by 2022, and will not pay common equity dividends for 2019 and 2020 to fund the transformation.

title: Streaming Platform Douyu Updates US IPO Terms
summary: Douyu TV, the largest game-centric live streaming platform in China, has updated its US IPO terms. It plans to offer 67.4 million shares, including American Depository Shares (ADS) to be listed on Nasdaq under "DOYU" priced between $11.50 and $14.00. The company's expected valuation ranges from $3.73 billion to $4.54 billion.

title: SunTrust joins wave of banks cutting ties with private prison industry
summary: SunTrust announced it will no longer provide financing to companies managing private prisons or immigration holding facilities, joining a trend among major banks. This decision follows similar moves by JPMorgan Chase and Bank of America, driven by stakeholder views and increased scrutiny of the private prison industry. The timing of SunTrust's announcement is significant as the bank faces a House Financial Services Committee hearing regarding its proposed acquisition by BB&T.

title: Cargo ship owned by JPMorgan Chase seized by US with 20 tons of cocaine
summary: US authorities seized the cargo ship MSC Gayane in Philadelphia in June with nearly 20 tons of cocaine aboard. The ship is owned by a transportation strategy fund run by JPMorgan Chase's (JPM) asset management unit, though JPMorgan Chase has no operational control of the vessel. The US Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania announced the seizure of the ship itself on July 4, calling it unprecedented due to the massive amount of drugs found.

title: Cargo ship involved in $1.3B cocaine bust in Philadelphia owned by JPMorgan Chase
summary: A cargo ship carrying nearly 20 tons of cocaine, valued at $1.3 billion, and seized in Philadelphia last month, was owned by a fund run by JPMorgan Chase. The bank, however, had no operational control over the vessel, which was managed by Swiss firm MSC Mediterranean Shipping Co. This bust was the largest cocaine seizure in U.S. Customs and Border Protection's 230-year history and comes amidst a series of large drug seizures in the Northeast, including incidents involving fentanyl-laced cocaine.

title: JP Morgan Chase owns ship seized in $1.3 billion cocaine bust
summary: A cargo ship seized with nearly 20 tons of cocaine, valued at an estimated $1.3 billion, is owned by clients of JP Morgan Asset Management through a transportation fund. JP Morgan leased the ship to Mediterranean Shipping Co., which is responsible for its operations. Neither JP Morgan Chase nor MSC are targets of the ongoing criminal investigation, which has resulted in several crew members being charged. US Customs and Border Protection called this the largest vessel ever seized in the agency's history.

title: Report: Bank of America's Cathy Bessant in talks for Wells Fargo CEO job - Bizwomen
summary: Cathy Bessant, Bank of America's chief operations and technology officer, is reportedly in talks for the Wells Fargo CEO position, according to a Bloomberg report. She joins a list of potential candidates, including industry figures from JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs, and Bank of New York Mellon, to replace former CEO Tim Sloan who stepped down in March. The new CEO will face the challenge of addressing Wells Fargo's ongoing scandals stemming from improper business practices and a federal asset cap implemented in 2018.

title: JP Morgan AM expands ETF range with triple launch
summary: JP Morgan Asset Management (JPMAM) has expanded its ETF offerings with the launch of two multi-factor equity ETFs, the JPMorgan Global Equity Multi-Factor UCITS ETF (JPGL) and the JPMorgan US Equity Multi-Factor UCITS ETF (JPUS). Additionally, JPMAM introduced the JPM BetaBuilders US Treasury Bond 0-1 yr UCITS ETF (BBIL) to broaden its fixed income ETF range. These new products are listed on major European exchanges and aim to provide diversified exposure at competitive total expense ratios.

title: FinTech Trends: M&A and Mobile Payments Driving Recent Growth
summary: This article examines the key drivers behind FinTech's growth, specifically focusing on the increasing M&A activity and the rising adoption of mobile payments. Despite low overall penetration, FinTech firms are experiencing rapid growth and outperforming traditional financial services, prompting major M&A deals as established companies seek to capitalize on this disruption. The reduced reliance on cash globally, particularly in countries like China, highlights the vast potential for mobile payments to continue expanding and reshape the financial landscape.

title: Bank of America CFO warns that falling rates will hit net interest income
summary: Bank of America's CFO, Paul Donofrio, warned that the projected growth in net interest income for 2019 could fall from 3% to 1% due to anticipated interest rate cuts by the Federal Reserve. This potential reduction in NII is attributed to lower yields on floating rate assets, reduced coupons on new bonds, and mortgage refinancing at lower rates. Despite this, Bank of America shares rose after the bank posted record profits exceeding analysts' estimates.

title: Best Visa credit card in India: Types, features and benefits
summary: This article provides a comprehensive guide to Visa credit cards in India, outlining different card types such as Classic, Gold, Platinum, Signature, and Infinite, along with their respective features and benefits. It also explains how to obtain a Visa credit card, how the Visa network operates, and essential tips for secure usage. Additionally, the article lists several Indian banks offering Visa credit cards and highlights options with no annual fee.

title: Navient plans full-Earnest loan pool in $535.2M student-loan ABS
summary: Navient plans a $535.2 million student-loan asset-backed security (ABS) backed entirely by loans primarily issued to advanced-degree professionals by Earnest, an online lender Navient acquired in 2017. The securitization, Navient Private Education Refi Loan Trust 2019-E, will include triple-A rated Class A notes and a AA-rated Class B offering. The offering is backed by 8,092 seasoned private student loans with strong borrower profiles.

title: Phreesia Announces Pricing of Initial Public Offering
summary: Phreesia announced the pricing of its initial public offering of 9,288,194 shares of common stock at $18.00 per share. The shares are expected to begin trading on the New York Stock Exchange under "PHR" on July 18, 2019, with the offering closing on July 22, 2019. J.P. Morgan, Wells Fargo Securities, and William Blair are acting as joint book-running managers.

title: Here's why Bank of America's CEO likes his execs on other companies' boards
summary: Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan encourages his executives to serve on the boards of other companies. He views this experience as valuable for developing future leaders, including his own potential successor. Moynihan believes diverse board experience is crucial for those aspiring to CEO roles.

title: Chinese game-streaming platform DouYu prices U.S. IPO
summary: Chinese game-streaming platform DouYu International successfully priced its Nasdaq IPO, raising $775 million by selling 67.4 million American depositary shares at $11.50 each. This makes it the largest Chinese IPO in the U.S. for 2019. The company, which specializes in streaming eSports and other gaming events, started trading under the ticker symbol DOYU with a $3.73 billion valuation by market close on its first day.

title: Phreesia has strong public debut as 2nd digital health IPO in 2019
summary: Healthcare software company Phreesia (PHR) had a strong public debut, closing its first day of trading about 40% above its set price of $18 per share after being priced at $18. The company, which offers a patient intake management platform, raised $167 million in its IPO. Phreesia CEO Chaim Indig hopes their successful IPO will pave the way for more digital health companies to go public, noting the market's need for more digital innovation in healthcare.

title: Intercorp empezó a cotizar en la Bolsa de Nueva York
summary: Intercorp Financial Services (IFS) successfully launched its initial public offering on the New York Stock Exchange, raising US$ 414 million. This marks the largest IPO in New York this year by a Latin American company. The offering involved the placement of approximately 9,000,000 common shares at US$ 46 per share.

title: TripAdvisor Calls Out ‘Straight Pride’ Organizers for Alleging Sponsorship, Threatens Legal Action
summary: TripAdvisor has issued a cease-and-desist letter to the organizers of a "Straight Pride Parade" for falsely claiming the travel company was in negotiations for sponsorship. The letter, penned by Bradford Young, TripAdvisor's associate general counsel, highlights the company's commitment to equality and diversity, citing its perfect score on HRC's Corporate Equality Index. Other companies like Netflix, Lyft, Gillette, and State Street have also taken action against the organizers for similar unauthorized use of their branding.

title: Banco Santander
summary: Banco Santander's blockchain laboratory, initially focused on the technology itself, has shifted its focus to real-world use cases, particularly in online payments and smart contracts. Through its participation in the we.trade consortium and leveraging IBM Blockchain Platform, Santander is developing solutions to facilitate international trade and individual payments, especially in areas with underdeveloped payment infrastructures. This initiative aims to address the growing demand from corporate banking customers for blockchain-based solutions.

title: Bond ETFs hit $1 trillion, now set for takeoff
summary: Bond ETFs have reached a milestone of $1 trillion, signaling a potential period of significant growth. The article highlights that Susan E. Oh believes using bond ETFs was a brilliant move for her fund.

title: Bank of America to open branches in Cincinnati, Columbus
summary: Bank of America announced plans to open 30 branches in Ohio over the next two years, including 15 in Cincinnati, marking its first retail presence in the state. The expansion is part of a broader strategy to open 350 new branches across various U.S. markets and builds upon the bank's existing commercial, business banking, and wealth management services in Ohio. The move aims to better serve clients and demonstrates a commitment to responsible growth in the region.

title: Charities and not-for-profits
summary: Barclays Private Bank offers specialized financial advice and management services for charities and not-for-profit organizations, leveraging over 60 years of experience. They provide tailored investment strategies including discretionary portfolio management, treasury services, and credit facilities, catering to various entities like higher education institutions and social housing providers. Clients need to meet minimum investment thresholds of £3 million in the UK or £5 million internationally to access these services.

title: Clear Channel Outdoor Holdings, Inc. Announces Pricing of its Offering of Common Stock
summary: Clear Channel Outdoor Holdings, Inc. announced the pricing of its public offering of 100 million shares of common stock at $3.50 per share. The company also granted underwriters a 30-day option for an additional 15 million shares. Proceeds from the offering will be used to redeem a significant portion of its 9.25% Senior Subordinated Notes due 2024.

title: Ex-Corporate Lawyer’s Idea: Rein In ‘Sociopaths’ in the Boardroom (Published 2019)
summary: Jamie Gamble, a retired corporate lawyer from Simpson Thacher & Bartlett, has concluded that corporate executives are "legally obligated to act like sociopaths." He argues that corporations are structured to care only about maximizing their own profits, viewing this as a "textbook case of antisocial personality disorder." Gamble's epiphany, which he developed while working on a novel, led him to write an essay about the "complex network of horribles" in corporate America.

title: CIM Group refinances Central Loop tower after completing renovation
summary: CIM Group refinanced its 425 South Financial Place tower in Chicago's Central Loop with a $170 million loan from KKR Real Estate Finance Trust after completing extensive renovations. CIM acquired the 950,000-square-foot office building in 2016 for $189 million and rebranded it following renovations that included lobby and plaza improvements. This refinancing follows other significant development projects by CIM in Chicago, including the Tribune Tower redevelopment.

title: JPMorgan Chase inks 5-year deal to generate marketing copy via AI
summary: JPMorgan Chase has signed a five-year deal with Persado to use its AI technology for generating marketing copy across various banking segments and digital advertising. This expanded partnership follows successful pilot programs demonstrating significant increases in click-through rates for AI-generated ads compared to human-written copy. The move signifies JPMorgan Chase's increasing investment in automating key marketing processes to improve personalization and campaign performance.

title: Spanish banking giant charged with corruption
summary: Spain's National Court has charged Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria (BBVA) with "corruption and breach of confidence" for allegedly contracting disgraced former police chief Jose Manuel Villarejo to illegally tap phones in 2004. The suspicions relate to BBVA's efforts to prevent a takeover bid by construction company Sacyr, and nine current or former managers are under investigation. BBVA denies wrongdoing, despite admitting to using Villarejo's firm Cenyt, and its former executive chairman, Francisco Gonzalez, resigned due to the probe.

title: Capital One touted the data cloud’s safety. Then a hacker breached it
summary: Capital One, a prominent advocate for cloud-based data storage, experienced a significant data breach affecting over 100 million customers. The incident, which involved a former Amazon Web Services employee exploiting a misconfigured firewall, has raised concerns about the security of financial data in the cloud despite Capital One's assertions of its safety and benefits. The breach is expected to cost Capital One between $100 million and $150 million, primarily for credit monitoring and legal support.

title: Review: TWA Hotel at JFK
summary: This article reviews the TWA Hotel at JFK, highlighting its success in recreating the glamorous "golden age" of air travel. Despite minor issues like limited in-room storage and a windy rooftop bar, the hotel is praised for its spectacular design and unique experience, particularly for aviation enthusiasts. The review encourages visitors to explore the lobby and amenities even without staying overnight.

title: HSBC Ousts CEO John Flint After Just 18 Months
summary: HSBC CEO John Flint's tenure ended abruptly after just 18 months, with the bank announcing his departure. The board sought to accelerate change amid a complex environment and challenges from low interest rates and trade tensions. Noel Quinn, head of global commercial banking, will serve as interim CEO as the bank conducts a search for a permanent replacement.

title: Asset managers farm out trading as costs and complexity climb
summary: Asset managers are increasingly outsourcing their trading operations to specialized firms to cut costs and navigate rising regulatory complexity, particularly after the introduction of MiFID II. This trend is driven by the fact that outsourcing can be significantly cheaper than maintaining in-house trading desks, offering savings of up to 40% for small to medium-sized fund firms. The outsourced trading sector is experiencing rapid growth, with a rising number of new firms and even large banks entering the market to capitalize on this demand, while offering advantages like extensive broker networks crucial for best execution under new regulations.

title: Quality or minimum volatility?
summary: This article analyzes whether quality ETFs or minimum volatility ETFs are a better investment strategy during volatile and downward-trending markets. It compares the performance of specific ETFs, discusses the criteria used to select quality stocks, and highlights the considerations and risks associated with both investment approaches during different market conditions.

title: Mesa Laboratories, Inc. Announces Pricing of Public Offerings of Common Stock and Convertible Senior Notes
summary: Mesa Laboratories, Inc. announced the pricing of concurrent public offerings, including 375,000 shares of common stock at $210.00 per share and $150 million aggregate principal amount of 1.375% convertible senior notes due 2025. The company expects net proceeds of approximately $73.9 million from the stock offering and $145.4 million from the notes, which it intends to use for its acquisition strategy and general corporate purposes. The notes will be convertible into cash, common stock, or a combination thereof, with an initial conversion price of approximately $283.50 per share.

title: Assured Guaranty to Take Over BlueMountain Capital for $160 Million
summary: Assured Guaranty Ltd. has agreed to acquire BlueMountain Capital Management for $160 million from majority shareholder Affiliated Managers Group Inc. and the founders. The insurer will also invest an additional $590 million in BlueMountain and its funds, while BlueMountain's founders will take on new roles within Assured Guaranty's asset management division. This acquisition provides Assured Guaranty with an alternative credit platform and a strong collateralized loan obligations business.

title: ‘Take It Like a Gift’: Chase Erases Canadian Credit Card Debts (Published 2019)
summary: JPMorgan Chase announced it has forgiven all remaining debt on its Canadian credit card accounts, which it closed last year. This unusual decision came as the bank exited the Canadian market, surprising cardholders who saw their balances reduced to zero. The move is being hailed by some as a "gift" and an opportunity for a fresh start for affected consumers.

title: Puerto Rico insurer sues 5 US SIFIs for $720M in debt defaults
summary: An insurer, MBIA Inc., has sued five out of the eight U.S. systemically important financial institutions (SIFIs) for $720 million in damages stemming from defaulted Puerto Rico bonds. The lawsuit, filed in San Juan, names subsidiaries of JPMorgan Chase, Citigroup, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, and Bank of America, alleging they "inflicted a financial tragedy" on the island and enriched themselves through massive fees from underwriting over $66 billion in debt. MBIA claims its subsidiary relied on "materially false or misleading" disclosures and has already paid over $720 million in claims due to these defaults.

title: Broadcom to Buy Symantec Enterprise Division
summary: Broadcom has agreed to acquire Symantec's enterprise division for $10.7 billion in cash, marking its second major software acquisition after CA Technologies. This deal will refocus Symantec on its consumer products and aims to generate $2 billion in sustainable revenue for Broadcom, along with $1.3 billion in EBITDA. Symantec plans to return $8.2 billion after taxes to shareholders via a special dividend of $12 a share.

title: Brighton chairman Tony Bloom wants Albion to be top 10 Premier League club
summary: Brighton chairman Tony Bloom aims for the club to become a top 10 Premier League team after securing a 12-year, £100m sponsorship deal with American Express. This deal bolsters their financial standing significantly, moving them into the top tier for club sponsorships in the league. Despite finishing 17th last season, the club is investing in infrastructure and personnel to achieve this ambitious goal, highlighting their growth over the past decade.

title: BlackRock buys $875M stake in brand-management giant
summary: BlackRock's private equity vehicle, Long-Term Private Capital, made its first deal by investing $875 million in Authentic Brands Group, the company behind brands like Sports Illustrated, Marilyn Monroe, and Juicy Couture. This investment makes BlackRock the largest shareholder in Authentic Brands Group, valuing the company at over $4 billion including debt. The move is part of BlackRock's strategy to expand its alternative assets business.

title: Main yield curve inverts as 2-year yield tops 10-year rate, triggering recession warning
summary: The main U.S. yield curve inverted as the 2-year Treasury yield surpassed the 10-year rate, a phenomenon historically preceding economic recessions. This inversion, along with the 30-year bond yield hitting an all-time low, signals increasing investor concern about a slowdown in global economies. While the inversion is a reliable indicator, a recession typically follows 22 months later, and the S&P 500 often sees gains in the year following such an event.

title: Warren Buffett Is a Huge Backer of U.S. Banks
summary: Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway holds nearly $100 billion in financial-services stocks, demonstrating his significant commitment to the U.S. economy. These holdings, which include banks, payment companies, insurers, and a ratings firm, now constitute about one-fifth of Berkshire's total market capitalization. This represents a substantial increase from 2010, when financial-sector investments made up 12% of the company's market cap.

title: US 30-year bond yield falls below 2% for first time
summary: The US 30-year bond yield fell below 2% for the first time ever, driven by investors seeking safety amidst growing fears over the global economy and renewed trade tensions. This rally in government bonds, alongside weak data from Germany and China, indicates rising recession risks and has led to an inversion of the yield curve, historically a harbinger of economic downturn. The stock of global negative-yielding debt also surged past $16 trillion, reflecting the high price money managers are willing to pay for secure sovereign bonds.

title: Genuine Parts Company Announces Sale of Electrical Specialties Group to Audax Private Equity
summary: Genuine Parts Company announced it has entered into a definitive agreement to sell its wholly-owned subsidiary EIS, Inc., the Electrical Specialties Group of Motion Industries, to Audax Private Equity. GPC plans to use the net cash proceeds from the transaction for investments, share repurchases, and debt repayment. The sale is expected to streamline GPC's operations and strengthen its focus on value-driving initiatives, while Audax aims to support EIS in expanding its customer base and offerings.

title: Big health plans pledge to look beyond shareholders. Critics aren’t so sure
summary: Major health plans, including CVS Health, Anthem, and Cigna, have signed a Business Roundtable statement indicating a shift from prioritizing only shareholders to considering all stakeholders. However, critics and political figures like Sen. Elizabeth Warren remain skeptical, calling for concrete actions. Kaiser Permanente CEO Bernard Tyson declined to sign, stating that as a non-profit, Kaiser does not have shareholders to prioritize.

title: Apple, JPMorgan CEOs Say Companies Must Serve More Than Shareholders
summary: 181 CEOs of major public companies, including Apple, JPMorgan Chase, and Walmart, have declared their companies' purpose extends beyond just shareholders to include all stakeholders like customers, employees, and communities. This new stance, articulated by the Business Roundtable, signifies a shift away from the "shareholder primacy" theory that has guided corporate governance for decades, reflecting growing public and generational expectations for corporate responsibility. The declaration suggests that capitalism, when adjusted, can be a force for broader societal good.

title: Makeover at Wells Fargo Advisors well-received
summary: Wells Fargo Advisors is undergoing a reorganization of its wealth management business, reducing its corporate structure and cutting about a dozen market manager positions. This move is seen by some as a necessary step to cut waste and duplicative management, leading to 91 markets within the firm. The firm is also consolidating its bank brokerage channel into the wirehouse channel as part of a $4 billion cost-cutting plan.

title: As Americans Stick With Cards, JPMorgan Drops Its Chase Pay App
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. is discontinuing its Chase Pay app for in-store smartphone payments early next year due to slow consumer adoption in the U.S. While other parts of the world embrace mobile payments, Americans prefer traditional credit cards and cash. The service will still be available for payments on retailer websites and apps.

title: JPMorgan to shutter stand-alone Chase Pay app
summary: JPMorgan Chase is closing its stand-alone Chase Pay app in early 2020 due to shifts in the online payments market and customer behavior. Despite the closure, customers can still use Chase Pay on merchant websites and apps, with new merchants like Grubhub adopting the platform. This move is part of JPMorgan's broader strategy of re-evaluating digital initiatives, following the closure of its Finn banking app and the end of a small-business loan partnership with OnDeck.

title: Waltermire joins Colliers International's retail practice
summary: Erica Waltermire has left CBRE Inc.’s Tampa office to join Colliers International Tampa Bay, Central and Southwest Florida as an Executive Managing Director specializing in retail properties. Waltermire, who has handled $250 million in retail real estate deals, was attracted to Colliers' team-based environment and dominance in the retail market.

title: JPMorgan’s First Majority-Owned Brokerage Names New Head
summary: JPMorgan has appointed Li Yi, also known as David, as chairman of its new majority foreign-owned securities firm in China, JPMorgan Securities (China) Co. Ltd. JPMorgan International Finance Ltd. holds a 51% stake in the new firm. This move follows China's relaxation of foreign ownership caps in joint-venture securities companies.

title: Key yield curve inverts to worst level since 2007, 30-year rate under 2%
summary: A key yield curve inverted to its worst level since 2007, with the 30-year Treasury rate falling below 2%. This inversion, particularly the 10-year yield falling below the 2-year yield, is seen by fixed-income traders as a significant indicator of a potential recession. The market's unease is attributed to investor expectations regarding Federal Reserve policy and delays in the U.S.-China trade agreement.

title: Peloton IPO: 1.4 Million Users, $195 Million in Losses, and an Uncertain Valuation
summary: Peloton Interactive Inc. has filed for an initial public offering, anticipating it will be one of the year's largest. The company, which sells interactive fitness equipment and subscriptions, reported 1.4 million members but also $196 million in losses on $915 million in sales for the year ended June 30. Despite its growth and "sticky" service, Peloton faces an uncertain valuation, intense competition, and potential tariff risks.

title: SEC penalizes embattled Deutsche Bank more than $16 million to settle graft failings tied to China, Russia ‘referral hires’ – third bank to fall
summary: The SEC has fined Deutsche Bank over $16 million for violating U.S. Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (FCPA) by hiring relatives of foreign government officials in China and Russia to secure investment banking business. This practice, known as "referral hires," involved bypassing standard hiring processes and offering positions to less qualified individuals to improperly influence officials. Deutsche Bank is the third major bank to face penalties for similar "princelings" scandals, following JPMorgan and Credit Suisse.

title: Citigroup raises minimum wage to $15 following political pressure
summary: Citigroup announced it has raised its minimum wage to $15 per hour, a move that comes after significant political pressure from U.S. lawmakers regarding the pay gap between its executives and lower-level employees. This decision follows similar actions by other major banks like Wells Fargo and JPMorgan, with Bank of America also vowing to increase its minimum wage. The bank's CEO, Michael Corbat, faced scrutiny over his $24.2 million salary, which was 486 times the median employee salary.

title: Hiring more workers, investing in communities — should corporations focus on more than shareholders?
summary: This article discusses the debate sparked by the Business Roundtable's new statement that corporations should serve all stakeholders, not just shareholders. It explores arguments for and against this shift, highlighting concerns about income inequality, CEO compensation, and the long-term impact on society versus short-term profit motives. Experts from various fields weigh in on whether this is a genuine change or merely PR, and the challenges of balancing diverse interests.

title: GM now has more workers in China than UAW employees in the U.S.
summary: General Motors now employs more workers in China than members of the United Auto Workers in the U.S., with approximately 58,000 workers in China compared to 49,000 UAW employees in the U.S. This comes amid President Trump's criticism of GM for its shrinking U.S. workforce, although experts suggest the decline is due to reduced car sales rather than job relocation overseas. The article also notes that nearly all GM vehicles made in China are sold within that country.

title: Why Big Companies Are Thinking Like Startups
summary: Large corporations like JPMorgan Chase are adopting startup methodologies to foster innovation and maintain competitiveness in a rapidly changing market. This involves minimizing waste, maximizing customer value, embracing Agile development, and implementing a "three horizons" framework for innovation, with a focus on continuous customer feedback. These strategies aim to accelerate product development and deliver value faster, much like their smaller, more nimble counterparts.

title: The Power of Scarcity
summary: This article discusses the economic principle of scarcity and its impact on investment value, highlighted by the popularity of the Popeyes chicken sandwich. It examines how limited supply drives up demand and value in various markets, including gold, municipal bonds, and even affects stock dilution in companies. The author also touches on global economic factors like the U.S.-China trade war and the rise of free trade zones in China, linking them to investment opportunities in precious metals and government debt.

title: Industry Headwinds, Fallout Of Recent Data Breach To Weigh On Capital One's Stock
summary: Capital One's stock is expected to be negatively impacted by industry headwinds, including a slowdown in consumer activity, and the fallout from a recent data breach. The article forecasts revenue trends for Capital One's commercial loans, consumer loans, and credit card segments, with an overall expected increase in revenues from $27.8 billion in 2018 to $31.4 billion by 2021. Despite challenges, Trefis estimates Capital One's valuation to be $103 per share, higher than the market price at the time of publication.

title: Con Ed on defense as pols ponder public takeover
summary: Con Edison executive Timothy Cawley defended the company's performance and structure during a hearing with state legislators who are questioning the merits of privately run utilities after summer power outages. Mayor Bill de Blasio and state lawmakers like Sen. Michael Gianaris raised the idea of a publicly owned power grid, citing high customer costs and conflicts between profit motives and public accountability. Cawley attributed the outages to specific equipment flaws and pre-emptive measures, emphasizing Con Edison's significant investments and reliability compared to national averages.

title: JPMorgan Says China to Be Included in Benchmark Bond Indexes
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. announced a phased inclusion of Chinese government debt into its benchmark emerging-market indexes, starting February 28, 2020. This move, following Bloomberg Barclays' earlier inclusion, caps China's weight at 10% of the GBI-EM global diversified and narrow diversified indexes. Analysts from Goldman Sachs Group Inc. estimate this could lead to approximately $3 billion in monthly inflows into China's bond market.

title: Dow jumps more than 200 points as Hong Kong tensions ease, tech shares rally
summary: U.S. stock markets surged on Wednesday, with the Dow gaining over 200 points, driven by easing tensions in Hong Kong after the withdrawal of a controversial extradition bill and a rally in tech shares. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq also saw significant gains, while bank stocks benefited from the U.S. yield curve uninverting. Positive news from China's services sector and comments from the New York Fed President further boosted investor sentiment.

title: iRhythm unveils $13m Verily afib deal, readies $100m offering
summary: iRhythm Technologies announced a nearly $13 million deal with Alphabet's Verily to develop AI-based technology for atrial fibrillation screening, diagnosis, and management. Concurrently, iRhythm is preparing a $100 million stock offering to fund growth initiatives, including a significant portion for the Verily collaboration. The partnership aims to enhance cardiac care through data analytics and patient-centric solutions.

title: Citigroup doubles down on credit cards even as U.S. economy softens
summary: Citigroup is heavily investing in its credit card business, particularly through zero-interest balance transfers, despite concerns about a softening U.S. economy. While this strategy carries risks from higher-risk borrowers, Citigroup asserts that tough underwriting standards and low delinquency rates will protect the bank. The credit card unit has become a crucial driver of revenue and profit growth for the bank following the 2007-2009 financial crisis.

title: Morgan Stanley Eyes $4 Trillion in Client Assets Held Away
summary: Morgan Stanley Wealth Management is making progress in capturing client assets held away from the firm, estimating it has uncovered $60 billion through new asset aggregation and financial planning technology. The firm believes clients hold an additional $4 trillion outside of Morgan Stanley. Efforts include integrating its recent Solium Capital acquisition and incentivizing brokers to utilize financial planning tools.

title: The Yield Curve Inversion May Be Different This Time
summary: The article discusses the recent inversion of the treasury yield curve and argues that this instance might be different from historical inversions. It suggests that short-term factors, such as global recession fears driving investors to safe assets and the Federal Reserve's reluctance to aggressively cut interest rates, are primarily responsible for the current inversion, rather than a fundamental economic outlook. The author posits that aggressive rate cuts by the Fed could eliminate the inversion and spur investment.

title: 20 Things You Didn’t Know About MarketAxess
summary: This article details 20 facts about MarketAxess, a leading electronic trading platform for fixed-income markets. It covers the company's history, its market dominance in US corporate bond trading, significant acquisitions like LiquidityEdge and Trax, key partnerships with companies like BlackRock, and its innovative use of AI technology. The article highlights MarketAxess's growth, global reach, and comprehensive solutions for financial professionals.

title: Sebi imposes Rs 12 lakh fine on ICICI Bank, compliance officer for disclosure lapses
summary: SEBI has imposed a total fine of Rs 12 lakh on ICICI Bank Ltd and its compliance officer, Sandeep Batra, for disclosure lapses. The fine was levied due to the delayed disclosure of a binding agreement signed with Bank of Rajasthan for its amalgamation, which was deemed price-sensitive information. ICICI Bank was fined Rs 10 lakh, and Sandeep Batra was fined Rs 2 lakh for failing to ensure timely disclosure.

title: 10x Genomics CEO Calls IPO a Validation of the Company’s Years-Long Strategy
summary: Shares of 10x Genomics surged over 35% on its Nasdaq debut, validating the company's long-term strategy in gene sequencing and genomic analysis. CEO Serge Saxonov views the successful IPO as a testament to their execution and scale, positioning the company to continue advancing human health. The company plans to use the funds to expand its research and maintain its leadership in the rapidly growing genomics market.

title: Time for a Trade on Financials, But Which Way?
summary: This article discusses the financial sector's performance in August 2019, a period of heightened volatility due to trade tensions and inverted treasury yields. Despite recession fears and an interest rate cut, major banks reported better-than-expected Q2 earnings, indicating underlying health in lending and liquidity. The piece suggests that while market anxiety persists, the fundamental strength of financials offers potential for both bullish and bearish trades using Direxion's leveraged ETFs.

title: Finance start-up SoFi strikes deal to put its name on new LA stadium for the Rams and Chargers
summary: Financial technology start-up SoFi has secured a 20-year naming rights deal for the new Los Angeles football stadium, which will be home to both the Rams and the Chargers. The "SoFi Stadium" deal is reportedly worth $400 million and aims to increase brand awareness for the eight-year-old venture capital-backed company. This move makes SoFi the first Silicon Valley start-up to have its name on a major NFL sports arena, strategically expanding its reach beyond its financial services offerings.

title: Greenlight raises $54 million for a debit card that teaches kids financial literacy
summary: Greenlight, a startup cofounded by Timothy Sheehan, has raised $54 million in Series B funding to expand its debit card service designed to teach kids financial literacy. The Greenlight card, managed by parents via a smartphone app, allows kids to monitor spending, set savings goals, and receive allowances, with future plans for educational layers and investing functionality. The funding round was led by Drive Capital, with participation from JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo, and existing investors.

title: Assessing the Gender Pay Gap in the Finance Sector
summary: The finance sector exhibits one of the largest gender pay gaps, with women earning significantly less than men despite making up a majority of the workforce. This gap is an international problem, exacerbated by men holding more senior roles and receiving promotions faster. While initiatives are underway to address this through recruitment, retention, advancement strategies, and technology, progress remains slow.

title: Blackstone CEO Steve Schwarzman on Bitcoin: “I Was Raised in a World Where Someone Needs to Control Currencies”
summary: Blackstone CEO Steve Schwarzman discusses his views on Bitcoin, artificial intelligence, and investment strategies in an interview with Fortune. He expresses skepticism about cryptocurrencies due to the lack of central control and potential for illicit activities but views blockchain technology favorably for other applications. Schwarzman also highlights AI as a major growth area and discusses the ethical challenges associated with technological advancements.

title: ETF People - Katherine Magee
summary: Katherine Magee is an Executive Director and Investment Specialist in J.P. Morgan Asset Management's US Equities business, based in London. She works with clients across EMEA, LatAm, and Asia, positioning the firm's US Equity investment strategies. Magee previously focused on factor-based, sustainable, and thematic investment strategies and supported the CEO of Asset Management, EMEA.

title: JPMorgan Chase And Wells Fargo Invest In Debit Card For Kids Company Greenlight
summary: Greenlight Financial Technology, a company offering a debit card for kids with parental controls, announced it raised $54 million in Series B funding. The round was led by Drive Capital with participation from JPMorgan Chase and Wells Fargo, along with existing investors. This funding will be used to drive growth, accelerate development, and enhance the educational features of the app for promoting financial literacy in children.

title: New Capital One Café Opens on M Street
summary: A new Capital One Café is opening on M Street in Georgetown, Washington, D.C., blending banking services with a coffee shop and communal workspace concepts. This location aims to attract a younger demographic, including Georgetown students, by offering study spaces, financial education, and a relaxed environment with Peet's coffee. While it provides traditional banking services, the cafe emphasizes community engagement and financial wellness, with analysts noting that prior Capital One Cafes see more patrons working and buying coffee than engaging in traditional banking.

title: MetLife to stay at Highwoods Preserve
summary: Metropolitan Life Insurance Co. has renewed its 176,000-square-foot lease in Highwoods Properties' Highwoods Preserve VII and V buildings in Tampa, representing one of the largest office commitments in the area since early 2018. This renewal secures steady cash flow for Highwoods and reduces near-term lease rollover risk for the company. The buildings occupied by MetLife are the last of a seven-building cluster owned by Highwoods in Highwoods Preserve.

title: Post Holdings Active Nutrition Business to be Named
summary: Post Holdings announced that its active nutrition business will be named BellRing Brands, Inc. following its proposed initial public offering (IPO) of approximately 20% ownership. BellRing Brands has filed a registration statement with the SEC for the IPO of its Class A common stock and expects the offering to be completed in the fall of 2019, with its shares to be listed on the NYSE under the symbol "BRBR". This move establishes BellRing as a holding company in the global convenient nutrition category with primary brands Premier Protein, PowerBar, and Dymatize.

title: A shift in strategy
summary: This article discusses the growing presence of actively managed ETFs in the Canadian market, traditionally dominated by passive indexing. Despite their increasing numbers, active ETFs still represent a smaller portion of total ETF assets, indicating significant potential for expansion. The piece details various types of active ETF strategies, including strategic beta, rules-based quantitative approaches, covered-call options, and fully discretionary management, highlighting their role in different asset classes, especially fixed-income.

title: Jeffrey Epstein’s fortune has passed from Deutsche Bank to Toronto-Dominion Bank
summary: Jeffrey Epstein's fortune has been transferred from Deutsche Bank to Toronto-Dominion Bank (TD) after Deutsche Bank severed ties with him. Deutsche Bank began closing Epstein's accounts earlier this year, prompting TD to accept his money. This move followed JPMorgan Chase's previous decision to end its relationship with Epstein after his 2008 arrest.

title: Morgan Stanley Hires $1 Billion-Asset Texas Team from UBS
