summary: This article identifies the top 20 banks and lenders that distributed the most Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) loans to local businesses in Central New York. It highlights that independent community banks and credit unions performed the majority of lending, with M&T Bank leading. The article also provides a list of the top lenders and details about loan size distribution.

title: ING Groep to Shut Branches Amid Shift Toward Digitalization
summary: ING Groep announced plans to close 42 branches in the Netherlands due to a decline in foot traffic, accelerated by the coronavirus pandemic and a broader shift towards digital banking. The bank, led by CEO Ruud van Dusschoten, intends to transfer services to existing service points and offer affected employees other positions within the company. This move aligns with ING's long-term strategy of focusing on digital capabilities, a trend also seen in other major banks.

title: Golpeado por la pandemia, IRSA sale a buscar fondos para refinanciar deuda
summary: IRSA Inversiones y Representaciones, heavily impacted by the economic effects of the COVID-19 pandemic, is seeking to raise up to $300 million in fresh funds from capital markets to refinance its debt. The real estate holding company, led by Eduardo Elsztain, faces significant foreign currency debt maturities of $450 million between July and November this year. Rating agencies like S&P have warned about the risks IRSA faces due to its exposure to Argentina's economic conditions and the uncertainty generated by the coronavirus on its businesses, particularly its shopping centers, hotels, and offices.

title: HP Enterprise to buy Silver Peak for about $925 million
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co announced its intention to acquire Silver Peak, a developer of wide area network (WAN) performance tools, for approximately $925 million in cash. This acquisition aims to bolster HPE's software-defined wide-area network (SD-WAN) capabilities, integrating Silver Peak into its Aruba business unit. The move is particularly relevant given the increased demand for remote work solutions due to the COVID-19 pandemic, with HPE anticipating significant growth in the SD-WAN market.

title: Despite a massive recession, JPMorgan Chase just posted record revenue — here's how the bank did it
summary: JPMorgan Chase achieved record quarterly revenue of $33.8 billion in Q2 2020 despite a recession, largely thanks to its investment bank, which posted a record $5.5 billion profit. Shrewd moves made under CEO Jamie Dimon to build up the investment bank after the financial crisis, combined with surging market volatility and Federal Reserve actions, created an excellent environment for trading and advisory services. This strong performance in its Wall Street division helped offset significant losses in the bank's consumer and commercial banking segments, which were impacted by loan default provisions related to the pandemic.

title: BBVA, the best bank in Latin America according to Euromoney
summary: Euromoney magazine has named BBVA the best bank in Latin America for 2020, also recognizing it as the best in sustainable finance for the second consecutive year. The publication highlighted BBVA's successful integration of digitization across the region and its strong financial performance, with Latin American operations contributing significantly to the group's overall results. Additionally, BBVA was named the best bank in Mexico and Argentina, lauded for its digital transformation efforts, efficiency, customer satisfaction, and commitment to sustainable development.

title: Goldman Traders’ Best Result in Years Spurs Surprise Profit Gain
summary: Goldman Sachs Group Inc. saw a surprise profit gain in the second quarter, driven by a 93% surge in revenue from trading stocks and bonds. This performance, significantly exceeding analyst expectations, comes as the bank also achieved record underwriting fees amid a historic market rebound and Federal Reserve stimulus efforts. CEO David Solomon noted that recent market turbulence reinforced the bank's commitment to its strategy.

title: Morgan Stanley beats estimates for second-quarter profit on strong trading results
summary: Morgan Stanley reported its second-quarter 2020 earnings, significantly surpassing analysts' estimates due to robust trading results. The bank achieved a record profit of $3.2 billion, or $1.96 a share, and revenue climbed 30% to a record $13.4 billion, driven by strong performances in fixed income and equities trading, as well as wealth management. CEO James Gorman highlighted the success of the bank's business transformation in providing stability during stressful times and indicated potential future dividend increases and share buybacks.

title: Freeport freezes workers’ pensions
summary: Freeport-McMoRan Inc. announced it would freeze employee pension plans, ceasing all benefit accruals as of September 1, 2020, though existing benefits remain protected. This move has sparked speculation that the company might be up for sale, with past rumors involving Barrick Gold and Newmont Corporation. An financial advisor from Ash Creek Financial Advisors provided advice for employees on managing their retirement plans in light of these changes.

title: Berkeley Lights Announces Pricing of Initial Public Offering
summary: Berkeley Lights, Inc. announced the pricing of its initial public offering of 8,100,000 shares of common stock at $22.00 per share, expecting to raise approximately $178.2 million. The company's common stock is set to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol "BLI" on July 17, 2020. J.P. Morgan, Morgan Stanley, and Cowen are serving as lead book-running managers for the offering.

title: Wilson Sonsini Advises Ascentage Pharma in HK$702 Million Placing
summary: Wilson Sonsini Goodrich & Rosati advised Ascentage Pharma Group International in a private placement that raised HK$702 million. The biotechnology company, focused on novel therapies for cancers, HBV, and age-related diseases, placed 15,000,000 shares at HK$46.80 per share through Citi and J.P. Morgan. The Wilson Sonsini team was led by partner Wanda Woo.

title: Kidney diagnostics developer Renalytix AI prices US IPO at $13.50
summary: Renalytix AI, a developer of AI-powered diagnostic tests for kidney disease, priced its US IPO at $13.50 per ADS equivalent, raising $74 million. The company will list on the Nasdaq under the symbol RNLX. J.P. Morgan and Stifel were the lead managers for the offering.

title: Indigenous Resistance Expels Oil Company GeoPark from Peruvian Amazon
summary: The oil company GeoPark (NYSE:GPRK) announced its departure from Block 64 in the Peruvian Amazon following years of fierce opposition from the Achuar People of the Pastaza and the Wampis Nation. This withdrawal is a result of sustained indigenous resistance, involving protests, lawsuits, and advocacy campaigns targeting investors and the company's CEO. Indigenous leaders and Amazon Watch emphasized this as a victory for territorial rights and a call for investors to divest from destructive resource extraction in the Amazon.

title: FD interest rate revised by ICICI Bank! Compare latest rates with SBI, HDFC Bank – July 2020
summary: ICICI Bank has revised its fixed deposit (FD) interest rates downwards, effective July 14, making it the only leading bank to do so in July. This article compares the latest FD rates of ICICI Bank with those of SBI and HDFC Bank, highlighting that HDFC Bank offers the highest interest on 1-year FDs, while ICICI Bank leads for longer tenures (5-10 years). Both ICICI Bank and SBI have special "Golden Years" or "Wecare" FD schemes offering additional benefits for senior citizens for a limited period.

title: KB Kookmin to own 67% of Indonesia's Bank Bukopin
summary: KB Kookmin Bank announced its plan to become the largest shareholder of Indonesia's Bank Bukopin, aiming for a 67% stake by the end of August. This acquisition, approved on July 16, will be one of the lowest-priced Indonesian bank purchases in the last five years. KB Kookmin Bank plans to enhance Bank Bukopin's risk-management and digital finance capabilities.

title: SEC charges former Morgan Stanley rep with stealing $6 million from clients
summary: The SEC has charged Michael Barry Carter, a former Morgan Stanley representative, with stealing approximately $6 million from brokerage customers and an elderly investment advisory client through unauthorized transfers between 2007 and 2019. Carter has pleaded guilty to parallel criminal charges and was fired by Morgan Stanley in 2019, with the firm stating that impacted clients have been reimbursed. He used the misappropriated funds to support a lavish lifestyle and concealed the fraud with false account statements.

title: Wells Fargo Names Mike Santomassimo as New Chief Financial Officer
summary: Wells Fargo & Company announced that Mike Santomassimo will join the company in fall 2020 as Chief Financial Officer, succeeding John Shrewsberry. Santomassimo previously served as CFO at BNY Mellon and held key finance leadership roles at JPMorgan Chase. John Shrewsberry will retire after a 22-year career with Wells Fargo, including six years as CFO, and will assist with the transition.

title: What BlackRock's continued dominance means for other ETF issuers
summary: BlackRock continues its dominance in the ETF market, fueled by increased interest in its fixed-income and cash management services and strategic fee cuts. While BlackRock and Vanguard account for a significant portion of ETF assets, smaller firms like Ark Invest are growing rapidly by offering specialized, actively managed funds. This creates a dual market where investors rely on large firms for passive index products and on niche players for alpha generation and diversification.

title: More Wells Fargo customers say the bank decided to pause their mortgage payments without asking
summary: Numerous Wells Fargo customers across 14 states claim the bank unilaterally placed their mortgages into forbearance plans, affecting their credit reports and ability to refinance, without their consent. The bank attributes these incidents to misinterpretations of customer intentions, while critics like Sen. Sherrod Brown denounce the bank's "sloppy service and shoddy management." This practice has drawn comparisons to Wells Fargo's past scandals of enrolling customers in unwanted services.

title: Morgan Stanley is starting to come clean about climate change
summary: Morgan Stanley is the first U.S.-based global bank to join the Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financials (PCAF), an international collaboration aimed at standardizing carbon accounting for the financial sector. This move signifies a commitment from the finance giant to disclose how its investments and loans contribute to climate change, following increasing pressure from climate activist groups and previous steps towards more environmentally friendly investments. The bank has financed over $91 billion in fossil fuel ventures since 2016, highlighting the significance of its new commitment to transparency.

title: BTG Pactual obtém 514,1 milhões de dólares em emissão de unidades locais e internacionais
summary: BTG Pactual successfully raised $514.1 million through a primary public offering of 35,625,000 units, with each unit equivalent to one common share and two Class A preferred shares. The funds will be allocated to strategic initiatives within its digital retail business and to bolster its capital indicators. Several law firms advised on the transaction, which involved both local and international placement agents.

title: Deutsche Bank to invest in financing platform Traxpay
summary: Deutsche Bank AG has announced its investment in the Frankfurt-based fintech Traxpay GmbH, aiming to expand its supply chain finance offering through Traxpay's platform technology. Traxpay provides dynamic discounting and reverse factoring solutions to corporate clients, and seeks to become a leading player in Europe, encouraging other banks to join as investors and partners. This strategic move highlights the growing market for supply chain finance, with both companies advocating a "fintech AND bank" approach.

title: HSBC launches ESG solutions team | HSBC news | HSBC Holdings plc
summary: HSBC has established a dedicated Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) Solutions unit to assist clients in transitioning to more sustainable business models, especially in the post-COVID-19 recovery. This new team will offer advice, expertise, and financing ideas to various clients globally, including businesses, governments, and asset managers. The initiative aims to solidify HSBC's position as a leader in sustainable finance and support the move towards a net-zero economy.

title: Black financial advisor accuses JPMorgan Chase of racism, retaliation over firing
summary: A former JPMorgan Chase financial advisor, Ricardo M. Peters, has accused the bank of institutional racism, alleging he was passed over for promotions, subjected to microaggressions, and ultimately fired in retaliation for blowing the whistle on discriminatory practices. Peters claims he experienced racial discrimination throughout his 10-year tenure, despite high performance rankings. He has since founded Guardian Financial Wealth Management Inc., aiming to educate clients on financial literacy and wealth building.

title: Why Invest in Ultra-Short, Active Strategies in Today’s Markets
summary: This article discusses the benefits of investing in ultra-short, active strategies, specifically J.P. Morgan’s Ultra-Short Income ETF (JPST) and Ultra-Short Municipal Income ETF (JMST), in current market conditions. It highlights their role in navigating COVID-19 related market volatility, offering attractive yield-to-duration profiles due to a flat yield curve and the Federal Reserve's low-rate policy. The piece also explains how these ETFs can be used to step up from cash for higher income or step down from longer-term bonds to reduce risk, emphasizing their active management approach in selecting financially strong securities.

title: A shoddy succession plan at HDFC Bank
summary: HDFC Bank is facing uncertainty regarding the succession plan for its long-serving managing director, Aditya Puri, who is set to retire. Despite Puri's significant financial gains from the bank and its success under his leadership, the lack of a clear successor is causing concern among investors, especially as the bank is India's third-most valuable company. The article suggests that a robust succession strategy is crucial for HDFC Bank's future stability and continued growth in a competitive banking landscape.

title: JPMorgan Chase partners with fintech start-up Marqeta to launch 'virtual' credit cards
summary: JPMorgan Chase is partnering with fintech start-up Marqeta to offer "virtual" credit cards for its commercial cardholders, allowing immediate use in mobile wallets. This eliminates the need for physical plastic cards and helps address needs intensified by the pandemic, such as remote work and contactless payments. Marqeta, which provides similar technology to DoorDash and Instacart, offers speed and modern technology that would take established financial institutions years to develop in-house.

title: Pharmapacks Announces Growth Financing by GPI Capital and JPMorgan Chase Bank
summary: Pharmapacks, a leading e-commerce enablement platform, has secured up to $150 million in growth financing from GPI Capital and JPMorgan Chase Bank to accelerate its expansion plans. This funding will allow Pharmapacks to significantly expand its warehouse footprint, invest in brands and inventory, and deepen its offerings across major e-commerce platforms. The company, which achieved over $250 million in sales in 2019, anticipates achieving 70% year-over-year growth and potentially 100% year-over-year growth in Q4 with the opening of a new replenishment center.

title: Chicago's Enova acquiring OnDeck Capital for $90 million
summary: Online consumer lender Enova International is acquiring OnDeck Capital for $90 million, a deal primarily structured with Enova shares and some cash. This acquisition significantly boosts Enova's presence in small business lending, making it a stronger player in the online lending sector. The combined entity will see 60% of Enova's loans directed to small businesses, up from 15%, with both CEOs maintaining leadership roles.

title: Regency Centers Evolving and Adapting With CEO Lisa Palmer
summary: Lisa Palmer discusses her journey to becoming CEO of Regency Centers and how the company has grown and adapted over her 24-year tenure. She highlights the importance of the company's culture, community involvement, and strategic advantages, while also touching on her personal experiences with sports and mentorship. Palmer outlines Regency's future goals amidst a rapidly changing retail real estate industry and the company's response to the pandemic and calls for racial justice.

title: State Street launches ESG version of its mammoth S&P 500 ETF
summary: State Street Corp. has launched its SPDR S&P 500 ESG ETF (EFIV), an environmentally, socially, and governance-focused version of its flagship S&P 500 ETF. The new ETF tracks S&P 500 companies meeting specific ESG criteria, excluding those involved in tobacco, weapons, or with low ESG scores from S&P Dow Jones Indices or the United Nations Global Compact. This launch reflects a growing investor interest in ESG strategies, especially during the COVID-19 pandemic, with ESG ETFs already attracting $14.7 billion in 2020.

title: JPMorgan Chase, Marqeta partner to launch virtual corporate cards
summary: JPMorgan Chase is collaborating with fintech firm Marqeta to introduce virtual credit cards for its commercial clients, utilizing Marqeta's tokenization technology. This new functionality, set to launch early next year, will allow instant issuance of virtual cards into mobile wallets, enhancing payment streamlining for businesses and expanding use cases like travel expenses for interview candidates or payments for disaster relief volunteers. The partnership addresses a growing need for contactless and virtual payment solutions, a trend accelerated by the coronavirus pandemic.

title: Israel's Enlight Renewable gets financing for Golan Heights wind farm
summary: Enlight Renewable Energy Ltd has secured 1.05 billion shekels in financing for a 1.25 billion shekel wind farm project in the Israeli-controlled Golan Heights. The project, which will include 39 turbines generating 189 megawatts of electricity, is expected to produce annual revenues of 140-160 million shekels for 20 years and power 60,000 households. General Electric Co will supply the turbines and provide maintenance.

title: El Paso Electric's $4.3B sale to JPMorgan-tied fund completed; new CEO named
summary: El Paso Electric's $4.3 billion sale to the JPMorgan Chase-tied Infrastructure Investments Fund (IIF) has been completed, with IIF assuming $1.5 billion of the utility's debt. Kelly Tomblin, formerly of INTREN LLC, has been named the new CEO, replacing interim CEO Adrian Rodriguez. The sale drew mixed reactions from community leaders and environmental groups due to JPMorgan's ties to IIF, despite regulator approvals.

title: Strategic Education, Inc. to Acquire Laureate Education, Inc.’s Australia and New Zealand Academic Operations, Including Torrens University
summary: Strategic Education, Inc. announced its definitive agreement to acquire Laureate Education, Inc.'s Australia and New Zealand academic operations, including Torrens University, for $642.7 million in cash. This acquisition will expand Strategic Education's global presence, diversify its offerings, and is expected to be immediately accretive to its earnings. The transaction is anticipated to close by the first quarter of 2021, subject to regulatory approvals.

title: CECL versus IFRS9: It Looks like U.S. Regulators Got it Right for Credit Cards
summary: This article examines the differences between U.S. CECL and international IFRS9 accounting standards for loan loss provisioning, particularly for credit cards. It argues that U.S. regulators made a better choice with CECL, which requires banks to provision for lifetime expected losses, compared to IFRS9's 12-month horizon. The piece highlights how U.S. banks, under CECL, are significantly more reserved than their Canadian counterparts following IFRS9, leading to greater financial stability, especially during crises like COVID-19.

title: JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon's morning routine: Wake up at 5 a.m. and 'read tons of stuff'
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. CEO Jamie Dimon wakes up at 5 a.m. to read various publications and analyst reports for nearly two hours. He prefers physical newspapers to online ones to expose himself to a wider range of stories. After reading, he typically exercises for 45 minutes, though he generally doesn't eat breakfast until later in the morning.

title: Here’s how PayPal hopes to turn Venmo into the next PayPal
summary: PayPal is looking to increase revenue from its Venmo brand, which is popular with younger consumers, by introducing new features like a credit card. Darrell Esch, the new general manager of Venmo, is tasked with leading this initiative as digital wallets become increasingly important. PayPal itself has experienced significant growth during the COVID-19 pandemic, surpassing the market capitalization of several major companies.

title: Goldman, BofA Left Off Ant IPO for Work With Alibaba Rivals
summary: Goldman Sachs and Bank of America were excluded from Ant Group's upcoming Hong Kong IPO due to their prior work with Alibaba's competitors. Alibaba, which owns a significant stake in Ant, has reportedly advised banks to avoid working with its rivals to secure future business. Ant Group is planning dual listings in Hong Kong and Shanghai, aiming for an IPO size that could exceed Saudi Aramco's record-setting offering.

title: Latham & Watkins Advises GCM Grosvenor on Transaction to Become a Public Company
summary: Latham & Watkins advised GCM Grosvenor, a global alternative asset management firm, on its merger with CF Finance Acquisition Corp. to become a public company. The transaction values GCM Grosvenor at $2 billion, and the combined entity will operate as GCM Grosvenor Inc., with its Class A common stock expected to be listed on NASDAQ. GCM Grosvenor's existing senior management team will continue to lead the business.

title: Trump fires Tennessee Valley Authority chair, cites hiring of foreign workers
summary: President Donald Trump announced the firing of Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) chair, Skip Thompson, and another board member, citing the authority's practice of hiring foreign workers under H1-B visas. Trump also threatened to remove other board members and mandated that the new CEO's salary should not exceed $500,000, significantly less than the previous CEO's $8 million. The decision followed a TV ad criticizing the TVA for replacing American workers with foreign contractors, a move that Senator Lamar Alexander disputes, stating the TVA operates without taxpayer money and has competitive rates.

title: Capital One: What’s in an Empty Wallet?
summary: Capital One (COF) stock has been significantly impacted by the pandemic, with shares collapsing and only partially recovering. The company reported a net loss of $918 million in Q2, cut its marketing budget, and reduced its dividend by 75%. This financial distress, coupled with a major data breach, reflects the broader challenges faced by banks deeply involved in the credit card business during economic downturns.

title: Vital Farms Announces Closing of Initial Public Offering
summary: Vital Farms (Nasdaq: VITL) announced the closing of its initial public offering of 10,699,573 shares of common stock at $22.00 per share, including the full exercise of the underwriters' option to purchase additional shares. The offering consisted of shares sold by both the company and selling stockholders. Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC, Morgan Stanley, and Credit Suisse Securities (USA) LLC acted as joint lead bookrunning managers for the offering.

title: Elaine Szeto joins consulting firm CCG as principal consultant
summary: Elaine Szeto has joined Phoenix-based Catalyst Consulting Group (CCG) as a principal consultant, bringing over 25 years of financial services industry experience. Szeto previously served as chief product officer at Western Alliance Bancorporation and held leadership roles at Omaha Bank and PNC Bank. She will focus on payments and assisting financial institutions and fintechs in navigating the disruptive industry landscape.

title: ‘Change Agent’ To CEO: Sashidhar Jagdishan Set To Bring Continuity To HDFC Bank
summary: Sashidhar Jagdishan has been appointed as the new CEO of HDFC Bank, succeeding Aditya Puri, who led the bank for 26 years. Jagdishan, an internal candidate with 25 years at HDFC Bank, is expected to bring continuity to the bank's leadership. The article discusses his background, the positive market reception of his appointment, the challenges he faces, and the legacy of his predecessor, Aditya Puri.

title: Buffett's Berkshire bought $2.07 billion BofA stock since mid-July, has 11.9% stake
summary: Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway Inc. has acquired an additional $2.07 billion in Bank of America Corp. shares since mid-July, increasing its stake to 11.9%. The move follows regulatory approval from the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond to boost its holding up to 24.9% and helps Berkshire reduce its substantial cash reserves. This makes Bank of America Berkshire's largest common stock holding after Apple Inc.

title: Banking Regulator Fines Capital One $80 Million Over 2019 Hack
summary: A top banking regulator, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), has fined Capital One Financial Corp. $80 million. The fine is a result of a 2019 data breach that exposed the personal information of about 106 million card customers and applicants. The OCC stated that Capital One failed to establish effective risk assessment processes and correct deficiencies in a timely manner.

title: HDFC Bank's delayed reports to draw in Indian regulator
summary: One of India's largest credit bureaus, Experian Plc, has informed the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) about consistent delays from HDFC Bank Ltd. in providing details of its loans, including the repayment status of millions of retail borrowers. This tardiness has allegedly been an issue for about two years and is expected to draw the attention of the Indian regulator.

title: JPMorgan Rejects Threat to Dollar Status Flagged by Goldman
summary: JPMorgan strategists disagree with Goldman Sachs' assessment of a structural decline in the dollar, despite acknowledging potential near-term downside. They argue against the idea that the U.S. is losing its reserve currency status or that the euro is experiencing a full "rehabilitation." The strategists believe the dollar’s issues are not indicative of a long-term, secular downtrend driven by structural factors.

title: Buffett buys back record $5.1 billion in Berkshire stock as coronavirus hits operating earnings
summary: Berkshire Hathaway repurchased a record $5.1 billion of its own stock in May and June, the largest single buyback period for Warren Buffett's conglomerate. This occurred as operating profits fell 10% in the second quarter due to the coronavirus pandemic impacting businesses like Geico and Precision Castparts, though net earnings surged to $26.3 billion primarily from unrealized gains in public market investments. Buffett warned against focusing solely on these volatile net earnings due to the pandemic's ongoing uncertainties.

title: Dow jumps 350 points to start week, S&P 500 inches closer to all-time high
summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average rallied over 350 points on Monday, driven by gains in economically sensitive stocks. The S&P 500 also rose, closing less than 1% away from its all-time high, while the Nasdaq Composite struggled as investors trimmed positions in mega-cap tech stocks. The market moves followed President Trump's executive orders for extending coronavirus relief benefits amidst ongoing stimulus package negotiations in Congress.

title: Swissport gets new owners with debt-for-equity deal
summary: Swissport has secured new ownership through a debt-for-equity swap, including significant debt facilities, to ensure its financial stability. Senior secured creditors like SVP Global and Apollo Global Management will take ownership, while the former owner, HNA Group, will benefit from future value creation. This restructuring aims to position Swissport to gain market share from weaker competitors in the aviation services industry, which has been severely impacted by COVID-19.

title: Blackstone to Boost Mobile-Home Bet With $550 Million Deal
summary: Blackstone Group Inc. is expanding its investment in mobile-home parks with a reported $550 million deal to acquire approximately 40 parks from Summit Communities. This move reflects a broader trend of investors turning to mobile-home parks during the pandemic, as this sector has proven more resilient than others like retail and hotels. The investment will be made through Blackstone Real Estate Income Trust (BREIT), with plans for upgrades to the properties.

title: Banks and tech giants including JPMorgan and Amazon pledge to hire 100,000 minority and low-income New Yorkers
summary: A new organization called the New York Jobs CEO Council, comprising leaders from 27 firms including JPMorgan, IBM, and Amazon, has pledged to hire 100,000 people from low-income Black, Latino, and Asian communities by 2030. The initiative aims to address inequality exacerbated by the coronavirus pandemic, providing entry-level jobs and apprenticeships, with 25,000 specifically for CUNY students. Co-chairs include Jamie Dimon, Arvind Krishna, and Julie Sweet, with support from other tech and finance giants.

title: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon weighs in on how to help the economy
summary: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon discusses strategies to support the economy amidst the pandemic, acknowledging the recession but expressing confidence in recovery. A new initiative is highlighted where large companies are collaborating to create 100,000 jobs to address the high unemployment rate. The report emphasizes the role of corporate efforts in economic revitalization.

title: PPP likely saved 35 million jobs, says JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon
summary: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon estimates that the government's Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) saved between 30 to 35 million jobs by providing loans to small businesses affected by the coronavirus pandemic. Dimon praised the swift action of lawmakers and the administration, but also highlighted the need to extend the program, especially for minority-owned businesses that may not have initially received adequate funds. He also discussed the formation of the New York Jobs CEO Council to address the racial wealth gap and economic inequality, anticipating a delayed economic recession and stressing the importance of safely reopening the economy.

title: MicroStrategy buys $250M in Bitcoin as CEO says it's superior to cash
summary: MicroStrategy has purchased $250 million worth of Bitcoin, with CEO Michael Saylor asserting its superiority as a long-term store of value compared to cash. Saylor, who holds significant voting power in the Tysons company, has been a vocal proponent of cryptocurrency. This move reflects his vision for MicroStrategy's financial strategy.

title: Jamie Dimon of JP Morgan Chase and other CEOs aim to hire 100,000 New Yorkers by 2030
summary: A group of CEOs, led by Jamie Dimon of JPMorgan Chase and the head of Google, formed the New York Jobs CEO Council with the goal of hiring 100,000 disadvantaged New Yorkers or people of color by 2030. This initiative aims to provide training, apprenticeships, and entry-level positions to address economic inequities exacerbated by the COVID-19 crisis, particularly in communities of color. The program, which includes companies like Goldman Sachs and Amazon, also plans to expand beyond entry-level roles and potentially to other cities.

title: Amazon and Google among big US companies pledging to hire 100,000 people from marginalized New York communities
summary: Major US companies including Amazon, Google, and Goldman Sachs have pledged to hire 100,000 people from New York City's low-income and minority communities by 2030. This initiative, called the New York Jobs CEO Council, aims to address racial and economic inequities worsened by COVID-19 by providing entry-level positions, apprenticeships, and on-the-job learning. While the effort is praised as a good start, experts emphasize the need for specific interventions like mentoring programs and performance reviews to ensure career advancement for employees from underrepresented backgrounds beyond entry-level roles.

title: BNY Mellon creates head of front-to-back solutions role through new buy-side appointments
summary: BNY Mellon has appointed Mark McKeon, formerly of State Street, to lead its new global front-to-back solutions role. This strategic move aims to enhance the company's open architecture strategy and expand its data and analytics capabilities for investment managers. The firm also hired two new relationship managers, Kevin Keefe and Cathy-Jo Reed, to strengthen its investment manager segment.

title: Allianz PNB Life launches new wealth protection fund
summary: Allianz PNB Life has introduced a new fixed-income product, the Peso-Hedged Diversified Income Dividend Paying Fund, tailored for HSBC clients. This fund aims to maximize returns with prudent investment management, investing in a PIMCO-managed dollar-denominated fund with a peso-hedging mechanism to mitigate exchange rate fluctuations. It is designed for moderate risk-takers seeking wealth protection and quarterly dividends.

title: Warren Buffett’s Stock Portfolio Saw Massive Recovery, Big Bank and Gold Changes
summary: Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway filed its Q2 13F report, revealing significant shifts in its equity portfolio as of June 30, 2020. The portfolio saw a massive recovery in the second quarter, contributing $26.3 billion in earnings, primarily driven by investment gains. Notable changes include increased stakes in Apple and Bank of America, a new position in Barrick Gold, and reduced holdings in JPMorgan Chase, PNC, Wells Fargo, Visa, Mastercard, and a complete exit from Goldman Sachs and airline stocks.

title: Pampa Energía destina fondos de colocación para refinanciar pasivos
summary: Pampa Energía, una compañía argentina con intereses en petróleo, gas, energía eléctrica y petroquímica, emitió obligaciones negociables Clase 6 por 86,9 millones de dólares para refinanciar pasivos y financiar inversiones. La emisión, asesorada por Salaverri, Burgio & Wetzler Malbrán y Marval O’Farrell Mairal, se realizó en el mercado local y fue calificada como "AA-(arg)". Los fondos se utilizarán para refinanciar obligaciones negociables anteriores, deuda con vencimiento en 2021, inversiones y capital de trabajo.

title: Wireless tower operator may deliver Africa’s biggest IPO in the US
summary: IHS Holding, a wireless tower operator, is exploring a potential initial public offering (IPO) in the US, which could be the largest listing by an African company with an estimated valuation of $7bn. The company, backed by shareholders like Wendel, Goldman Sachs, and MTN, had previously stalled IPO plans due to political uncertainty in Nigeria. MTN, a significant shareholder, values its stake in IHS at R30.7bn and views the potential IPO as an opportunity to divest non-core assets.

title: Chase Bank Opens New Branch in Ventura Village
summary: JPMorgan Chase opened a new Chase Bank branch in the Ventura Village neighborhood of south Minneapolis, a lower-income area. This new branch is a "community center pilot concept" designed to provide access to opportunities for an underserved community and is only the second such location among Chase’s 4,900 U.S. branches. The company also announced $1.75 million in philanthropic commitments with a focus on helping local minority business owners in the Twin Cities.

title: Scotiabank to pay over $127 million for precious metals price manipulation
summary: Scotiabank has agreed to pay over $127 million to resolve U.S. regulatory charges related to alleged price manipulation of precious metals futures contracts. The settlement includes a deferred prosecution agreement and requires an independent compliance monitor for three years. The charges stem from illegal "spoofing" by four Scotiabank traders over eight years, involving gold, silver, and other metals futures contracts.

title: One year ago, the Business Roundtable pledged to reshape the culture of business. Has anything changed?
summary: One year after the Business Roundtable's pledge to broaden corporate responsibility beyond just shareholder value, a Fast Company article investigates whether meaningful change has occurred. While some see the pledge as a mere PR move with little board-level commitment, others argue it formalized an ongoing shift towards stakeholder focus, especially as recent crises highlight corporate social responsibility. However, tangible, measurable changes remain elusive, and U.S. corporate leaders still lag behind global counterparts in embracing a fundamental shift in capitalism.

title: Brokers Notch Mixed Results in TRO Battles with JPMorgan, Edward Jones
summary: Two Ameriprise Financial brokers experienced conflicting outcomes in their non-solicitation disputes with former employers, JPMorgan Chase & Co. and Edward Jones. A federal judge dissolved a temporary restraining order against Ryan Riley, a former JPMorgan broker, denying a preliminary injunction, while another judge granted Edward Jones a TRO against Samuel "Ed" Clyburn, Jr., preventing him from soliciting former clients. The cases highlight the differing legal interpretations of client solicitation and "irreparable harm" in broker transitions.

title: Arista will charge a premium for CloudVision as a service
summary: Arista Networks is introducing CloudVision as a service, a cloud-based version of its network management software for data centers and campuses, which will carry a higher subscription price than its on-premises counterpart. The company justifies the premium by eliminating the hassle of software security, updates, and server management for customers. Arista also plans to leverage anonymized customer telemetry data in the cloud to provide enhanced insights and more effective problem-solving recommendations.

title: Banks fined for improper disclosure and charges on credit cards
summary: Canada's financial consumer watchdog has fined Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce over $1.2 million for errors that improperly charged 1.3 million credit card customers over 15 years, an issue the bank had previously disclosed and refunded for. Additionally, Canadian Western Bank and its subsidiary Canadian Western Trust were fined $200,000 each for failing to disclose non-interest costs and fees on various credit products and mortgages, affecting thousands of clients. These penalties highlight a lapse in proper disclosure and fee transparency by the sanctioned banks.

title: KBR to Buy Centauri for $800M; Stuart Bradie Quoted
summary: KBR has announced its agreement to acquire Centauri for approximately $800 million in cash, aiming to bolster its intelligence, military space, defense modernization, and cybersecurity capabilities. The acquisition will integrate Centauri into KBR's government solutions segment and is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2020. This strategic move aligns with KBR's goal of expanding its highly technical, mission-focused services and enduring customer relationships.

title: Chinese Crowdfunding, Insurance Site Waterdrop Raises $230 Million, Plans U.S. IPO
summary: Chinese online insurance technology platform Waterdrop Inc. has raised $230 million in a new funding round led by Swiss Re and Tencent Holdings. The company, valued at nearly $2 billion, plans an initial public offering in the United States as early as this year, bringing in Bank of America and Goldman Sachs to manage the float. Waterdrop, which distributes insurance policies and provides illness insurance crowdfunding, will use the new capital to invest in AI and big data initiatives for its products and services.

title: Bids open as a dozen firms vie for airport contract
summary: Twelve firms, including a consortium led by Williams Industries and VINCI Airports, are vying for a contract to operate, finance, develop, and maintain the Grantley Adams International Airport (GAIA) in Barbados. The bidding process, advised by the International Finance Corporation (IFC), is for a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model where the government retains ownership while a private partner manages the airport for up to 30 years. The tender is expected to be awarded in the first half of 2021, following an evaluation of bids adjusted for the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the aviation industry.

title: UBS to update legal structure at wealth management unit to cut costs
summary: UBS Group plans to restructure its wealth management unit by transferring large customer deposits to its primary legal entity, a project known as "Rigi." This move aims to cut costs and free up billions of dollars for loans outside Switzerland, partly reversing measures taken after the 2008 financial crisis. The restructuring is also part of a broader revamp of the wealth management business, including job cuts and managerial changes, set to be completed by 2022.

title: Bank's COVID relief turned to financial pain for BMO customer, now reimbursed for her trouble
summary: A Vancouver woman faced significant financial distress after BMO's COVID-19 relief program application was mishandled, leading to mounting debt and a damaged credit score. After being contacted by CBC News, BMO agreed to waive her entire credit card balance, lower her interest rate, and rectify the negative impact on her credit, using her case for future staff training. This resolution brought immense relief to the customer, who was already struggling with unemployment during the pandemic.

title: Postal banking may soon be here! But there’s a catch
summary: Progressive politicians have long advocated for the return of postal banking in the U.S. A recent report indicates that the USPS is considering a pilot program with JPMorgan Chase to place ATMs and other banking services in post offices. While this could expand access, critics raise concerns about private partnerships undermining the original goal of public banking and potential antitrust issues.

title: Mizuho becomes first Japan megabank to set fee for new passbooks
summary: Mizuho Bank announced it will charge new customers under 70 a ¥1,100 fee for paper passbooks starting January 18, aiming to promote digital alternatives and cut costs. This makes Mizuho the first Japanese megabank to implement such a fee, potentially influencing other banks to follow suit. The bank will encourage customers to use its free online passbook service and will also change transaction processes to reduce the need for hanko seals and physical passbooks.

title: La discriminación de género impide a las mujeres en Chile conseguir préstamos bancarios
summary: A study by the Inter-American Development Bank (BID) and CAF reveals that women in Chile are 18% less likely to have loan applications approved than men, despite being more responsible with payments. This gender discrimination, often perpetuated by male executives, results in significant lost profits for banks and highlights a deep-seated bias. The research, which is unprecedented globally, suggests that eliminating this discrimination could inject an additional $12 billion into the financial system through women's loans.

title: Warren Buffett's Gold Bet Helps Thomas Kaplan Again: 'I Owe Him Two!'
summary: Warren Buffett's investment in Barrick Gold has once again benefited billionaire Thomas Kaplan, chairman of NovaGold, which co-owns a major gold deposit with Barrick. This marks the second time Buffett's market actions have favored Kaplan, the first being his silver purchase in the late 1990s. Kaplan suggests Buffett's indirect endorsement could "detoxify" gold, making it more appealing to mainstream investors.

title: Chinese Company Signs Large Industrial Lease in Vernon
summary: US Elogistics Service Corp., a China-based ecommerce company, has signed a 232,000-square-foot industrial lease in Vernon, making it the largest industrial lease in central L.A. this year. The company will use the space as a fulfillment center, drawn by its proximity to the ports of L.A. and Long Beach and its state-of-the-art construction. This deal highlights the growing demand for industrial space, particularly from the ecommerce sector, which has been further accelerated by Covid-19.

title: Alphonse Valbrune Joins Clearwater as Chief Legal Officer
summary: Clearwater Analytics announced that Alphonse Valbrune has joined the company as Chief Legal Officer. Valbrune brings extensive experience in advising high-growth technology companies, including leadership roles at Genpact and Headstrong, and will contribute to Clearwater's continued expansion. Clearwater is a leading SaaS solution for investment data aggregation, reporting on over $4 trillion in investments daily for numerous institutional investors.

title: Chase and Capital One to close local branches
summary: Two major bank branches, Chase and Capital One, are scheduled to close their locations on Chambers Street in the coming months. The Chase branch will close in the fourth quarter of 2020, while the Capital One branch will close on October 21, 2020. This decision contributes to a broader trend of bank branch closures in New York City, drawing mixed reactions from residents.

title: Your 5-Point Stress-Free Money Plan.
summary: This article presents a 5-point stress-free money plan, drawing insights from Charles Schwab's SVP and Chief Fixed Income Strategist, Kathy A. Jones. It discusses strategies for navigating a volatile financial landscape, including maintaining cash reserves, diversifying investments, shortening bond terms, and focusing on creditworthy corporate and municipal bonds. The conversation highlights risks related to junk bonds, emerging markets, and potential US credit downgrades, emphasizing the importance of understanding one's investments and having a well-thought-out financial plan.

title: Management consulting firm inks big lease at Minskoff’s 1166 Sixth
summary: FTI Consulting has signed one of Midtown Manhattan's largest office leases since the COVID-19 pandemic began, securing over 120,000 square feet at Edward Minskoff's 1166 Sixth Avenue. The 15-year deal involves FTI consolidating several Manhattan offices into the newly renovated building. This transaction is notable given the significant slowdown in leasing activity experienced in Manhattan during the pandemic.

title: LGIM may take 'action' against KEPCO on coal projects
summary: Legal & General Investment Management (LGIM), a major UK asset manager and KEPCO shareholder, is considering "investment action" against Korea Electric Power Corp. (KEPCO) due to its continued investment in overseas coal-fired power plants. LGIM's head of sustainable investment strategies, Meryam Omi, stated that KEPCO is the lowest-scoring company in its sector under their Climate Impact Pledge program and expressed concerns about the financial viability and environmental impact of these projects in Vietnam and Indonesia. LGIM has already removed KEPCO from its ESG-themed Future World Funds and may take further voting and investment action, underscoring a growing trend among investors to prioritize environmental and financial sustainability.

title: El Banco Santander deja de financiar el 100% de sus pisos embargados tras la crisis
summary: Banco Santander has changed its policy for selling foreclosed properties, now limiting financing to 90% of the property's value, a departure from the previous 100% financing model. This decision comes amidst the economic crisis caused by the coronavirus pandemic and follows a general tightening of lending criteria by Spanish banks, as reported by the Bank of Spain. While the general limit is 90%, the bank may still offer 100% financing on a case-by-case basis depending on the client's profile and the operation's viability.

title: J.P. Morgan Chase Bank's South Minneapolis branch manager aims to promote financial literacy
summary: Hodan Ahmed, the branch manager for Chase Bank's new Ventura Village location in South Minneapolis, aims to promote financial literacy within the community. Ahmed lives in the neighborhood and understands the specific needs of the local residents. This initiative comes as Chase Bank is expanding its presence in the Twin Cities with new branches.

title: ConsenSys acquires JPMorgan blockchain platform Quorum
summary: ConsenSys has acquired Quorum, JPMorgan Chase's blockchain platform, and rebranded it ConsenSys Quorum. JPMorgan, which uses Quorum for its Interbank Information Network and JPM Coin, has also made a strategic investment in ConsenSys and will continue to utilize the platform. This acquisition is seen as a move to broaden Quorum's adoption among financial institutions as a technology firm, rather than a rival bank.

title: Pullman Cargo refinancia deuda para enfrentar la pandemia
summary: Chilean cargo transportation company Pullman Cargo secured a $105 million refinancing deal with local banks to mitigate the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. Garrigues-Chile advised the consortium of banks in the negotiation, which involved the restructuring of debt for Pullman Cargo and its subsidiaries. This agreement is expected to help the group absorb the pandemic's effects and prepare for market recovery.

title: Banco de Chile obtiene primer lugar en ranking Merco Talento Chile 2020
summary: Banco de Chile has achieved the top position in the Merco Talento Chile 2020 ranking, recognizing it as the best company in the country for attracting and retaining talent. This marks the first time the bank has led the general ranking, while also maintaining its leadership in the Banks and Financial Institutions category for the seventh consecutive year. The achievement was highlighted by CEO Eduardo Ebensperger and Division Manager Cristián Lagos, who emphasized the bank's commitment to its employees and clients, attributing this recognition to their focus on continuous development, teamwork, and strong corporate values.

title: Banks eye layoffs as short-term crisis ends, long-term costs emerge
summary: As the immediate crisis of the pandemic subsides, U.S. banks are planning layoffs, reversing earlier pledges not to cut jobs in 2020. This shift is driven by expectations of an extended recession, rising loan losses, prolonged low-interest rates, and increased efficiency from remote work. Industry experts anticipate a 5-10% reduction in bank staff, particularly in technology, HR, and finance departments, with institutions like JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo, Standard Chartered, and HSBC already initiating or planning significant job cuts.

title: CORRECTED-Banks eye layoffs as short-term crisis ends, long-term costs emerge
summary: U.S. banks, which had pledged not to cut jobs in 2020 at the pandemic's outset, are now considering layoffs due to economic recovery taking longer than expected, high unemployment, and sustained low interest rates. Consultants and industry insiders suggest a 5-10% reduction in staff at mid- and lower levels. This shift comes as remote work has demonstrated increased efficiency and banks grapple with the need to cut costs in the face of anticipated credit issues and regulatory pressure.

title: ‘New’ Medtronic the goal of CEO Geoff Martha’s plans for surgical robotics maker
summary: Medtronic CEO Geoff Martha aims to transform the company into a more agile and competitive entity, emphasizing a "new Medtronic" with a strong focus on surgical robotics and artificial intelligence. Martha plans to aggressively expand market share with products like the Hugo surgical system and integrate AI through acquisitions like Digital Surgery and Medicrea International to enhance surgical planning and delivery. The strategy involves playing offense and leveraging a robust product pipeline to drive growth and establish Medtronic as a leader in "medtech."

title: Historic Buildings Made New With the Help of Low-Cost Capital
summary: JPMorgan Chase is actively involved in the preservation and revitalization of historic buildings across the U.S. through investments in projects that qualify for the Historic Tax Credit (HTC) program. This program provides low-cost capital to developers who agree to maintain historic elements, leading to the transformation of abandoned properties into modern living and commercial spaces. Since 2017, JPMorgan Chase has invested equity in over 3 million square feet of historic buildings, repurposing them for affordable housing, commercial spaces, and industrial use, thereby contributing to community development.

title: Charts of the Day: Overseas Mutual Funds Ride the High in China Stocks
summary: Major overseas mutual funds significantly increased their investments in Chinese stocks during the second quarter, indicating strong performance in the region's equities. This surge, led by top fund managers, was primarily in A-shares, H-shares, and U.S.-listed Chinese companies, with particular interest in nonessential consumption, communication, and financial industries. China is also actively working to make its financial markets more accessible to foreign investors, including scrapping quota restrictions on major inbound investment systems and unifying its bond market.

title: Stop the presses: McGraw publishing heir sells Gulf Stream house for $8M
summary: John L. McGraw, former chairman of McGraw Hill, and his wife Marjorie, sold their Gulf Stream waterfront house for $8 million to Keith E. Rowling, a managing director at Merrill Lynch. The McGraws had purchased the 6,000-square-foot property in 2006 for $7 million. Rowling is a highly ranked wealth advisor at Merrill Lynch, recognized by Forbes.

title: JPMorgan hires Vanguard veteran to lead call center wealth managers
summary: JPMorgan Chase has hired Boaz Lahovitsky, formerly the head of Vanguard Group's robo-adviser, to lead its phone and video-based financial advice unit. Lahovitsky will oversee the expansion and hiring of hundreds of new advisers for JPMorgan's U.S. National Branch for Wealth Management, a key part of the bank's strategy to grow its wealth management business through remote advice channels. This move underscores JPMorgan's commitment to strengthening its digital and remote financial advisory services.

title: JPMorgan hires Vanguard veteran to lead call center wealth managers
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co has hired Boaz Lahovitsky, formerly head of Vanguard's Personal Advisor Services, to lead its U.S. National Branch for Wealth Management. Lahovitsky will oversee the expansion of JPMorgan's phone and video-based financial advice unit, including the hiring of hundreds of new advisers. This move aligns with JPMorgan's strategy to expand its wealth management business by focusing on accessible advice channels.

title: $217 Million Pour Into Grayscale's Crypto Funds Following Bitcoin TV Ad Campaign
summary: Grayscale Investments reported a significant influx of $217 million into its cryptocurrency funds during the third quarter of 2020, bringing its assets under management (AUM) to over $5.9 billion. This surge in investment is largely attributed to the company's recent Bitcoin TV ad campaign, which aimed to educate mainstream investors about Bitcoin's potential as a store of value. The campaign appears to have successfully attracted institutional investors, as 81% of the investments came from this sector.

title: JetBlue makes credit card deal with Puerto Rican bank Popular
summary: JetBlue has announced a new credit card agreement with Puerto Rican bank Popular. The airline will be launching two new Mastercard options in Puerto Rico: one with no annual fee and another with a $99 annual fee. This deal expands JetBlue's credit card offerings in the region.

title: Key appointments across South West including Lloyds Bank, Hargreaves Lansdown and Bevan Brittan
summary: This article details recent key appointments and promotions across various companies in the South West region of the UK. It highlights new hires and internal advancements at firms like Lloyds Bank, Hargreaves Lansdown, Bevan Brittan, Meade King, Brunelcare, Smith & Williamson, Pall-Ex, The Family Law Co, PKF Francis Clark, GA Solicitors, SSG Training & Consultancy, and Wildworks, showcasing significant movements in the business and legal sectors.

title: -MOVES-Citi hires ex-Deutsche Bank M&A boss Rousseau for France advisory push
summary: Citigroup has appointed Robin Rousseau, formerly Deutsche Bank's M&A boss for EMEA, as a vice chairman of investment banking for Europe, the Middle East, and Africa. Based in Paris, Rousseau will concentrate on Citi's French client franchise and provide financial advisory services across the region. His role aims to enhance strategic client coverage and help companies identify opportunities amidst a challenging environment for French M&A, which has seen a 40% decline this year due to the coronavirus crisis.

title: -JPMorgan to exit private banking business in Brazil, Bradesco says
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co has agreed with Brazil's Banco Bradesco SA to potentially transfer its Brazilian private banking clients, representing approximately 20 billion reais ($3.71 billion) in assets under management, to the Brazilian bank. JPMorgan will continue to offer international products and services to Brazilian clients, and clients have the option to migrate to Bradesco. The agreement highlights JPMorgan's move to exit its private banking unit in Brazil.

title: PIMCO: fully engaged on ESG
summary: PIMCO's CIO of US Core Strategies, Scott Mather, discusses the firm's deep integration of ESG into its investment processes, emphasizing engagement as crucial for improving issuer sustainability performance. The article highlights PIMCO's approach to ESG in conventional and dedicated funds, its collaborative engagement strategy with issuers, and how fixed income serves as an ideal asset class for driving change. It also covers PIMCO's Climate Bond Strategy, the impact of the Covid-19 pandemic on ESG focus, and the firm's involvement with UN Sustainable Development Goals and Coronabonds.

title: Global Banking Services Industry Market Analysis, Trends, and Forecasts, 2019-2024 by SpendEdge
summary: The Global Banking Services Industry market is projected to grow by over USD 1 trillion at a CAGR of 6.0% between 2019 and 2024, driven by digital technology adoption among service providers. North America and Europe are expected to be the leading spending regions. Key suppliers include JPMorgan Chase & Co., Bank of America Corp., and Wells Fargo & Co.

title: General Electric is now worth less than companies you've may have never heard of
summary: General Electric, once the world's largest public company, is now valued less than much smaller entities and its stock might be worth nothing, according to a JPMorgan analyst. GE's decline is attributed to financialization under Jack Welch, risky acquisitions like Alstom, and massive share buybacks under Jeff Immelt. The company's core power unit faces further challenges as the world shifts toward greener energy solutions.

title: Mastercard partners with Global Payments’ TSYS to expand installment offerings
summary: Mastercard has partnered with TSYS, a Global Payments company, to offer consumers more flexible payment options by enabling them to split transactions into installments before, during, or after checkout. This collaboration aims to meet the growing demand for flexible payment solutions amidst economic uncertainties, enhancing Mastercard's buy-now-pay-later ecosystem and benefiting issuers and merchants. The partnership focuses on increasing consumer choice, control, and simplicity at checkout, ultimately aiming to boost consumer acquisition, loyalty, and approval rates while decreasing cart abandonment.

title: Monroe Chamber names top 20 young professionals
summary: The Monroe Chamber of Commerce, Northeast Louisiana Young Professionals, BayouLife Magazine, Origin Bank, and JPMorgan Chase honored 53 regional young professionals at the Top 20-Under 40 celebration. This event recognized individuals for their outstanding accomplishments professionally, personally, and in community service. The article lists the 20 young professionals who received the "Top 20-Under 40" award, along with other nominees and sponsoring organizations.

title: More Investors Are Exiting Cash and Turning Up the Risk
summary: Investors are moving out of cash positions, specifically short-duration Treasury ETFs, and increasing their risk exposure by investing in equities and other higher-yielding assets. This shift is attributed to the Federal Reserve's commitment to near-zero interest rates, making cash less attractive, and the consistent gains seen in major stock indexes. The article highlights significant outflows from Treasury ETFs like SHV and BIL, contrasting with increased capital flows into equities, with the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY) being a prime beneficiary.

title: Just 2 Banks, 2 CUs Still Participating in TARP Program
summary: As of September 2020, only two banks and two credit unions remained in the Troubled Asset Relief Program (TARP), which initially included 763 institutions. Carver Bancorp Inc. recently exited the program, leaving OneUnited Bank, Harbor Bank of Maryland, Berkeley-based Cooperative Center FCU, and Washington-based DC FCU as the remaining participants. The investments in these institutions are relatively small compared to the overall program, and it's possible the government could force an exit for the remaining participants.

title: JPMorgan Dethrones Pimco With the Biggest Actively Managed ETF
summary: JPMorgan's Ultra-Short Income ETF (JPST) has surpassed Pimco's Enhanced Short Maturity Active ETF (MINT) to become the largest actively managed ETF with $13.94 billion in assets. This marks a significant achievement for JPMorgan, a relatively new entrant to the ETF market. JPST's strong performance and lower fees, especially during market downturns, have contributed to its rapid growth and investor appeal.

title: CMA stops Lloyds ‘bundling’ business accounts with loans
summary: The Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) has stopped Lloyds Banking Group from forcing small business customers to open business current accounts when taking out Bounce Back Loans. Lloyds breached legal undertakings designed to prevent anti-competitive practices by requiring approximately 30,000 customers to open a business current account to access the Bounce Back Loan Scheme. Lloyds has agreed to rectify this by offering affected customers the option to switch to a fee-free loan servicing account and ensuring new applicants have a choice.

title: UBS and Barclays' Digital Settlement Coin Project Delayed
summary: The Fnality International project, backed by major banks like UBS and Barclays, aimed to create digital versions of several fiat currencies for faster and cheaper settlements. Originally slated for 2020, the project has been delayed until at least 2021 as it awaits regulatory approvals. This initiative seeks to revolutionize interbank settlements by leveraging tokenized global currencies on enterprise blockchains.

title: A New Take on the Earnings-Surprise Strategy
summary: Morgan Stanley's quantitative equity research suggests a new strategy for investors to find alpha in earnings surprises, especially amidst unpredictable guidance fueled by events like the COVID-19 pandemic. By focusing on high-quality stocks that beat consensus estimates and shorting low-quality stocks that miss, investors can potentially achieve better returns than strategies focusing solely on surprise magnitude. This approach leverages the firm's proprietary "Quali-SURE" score, emphasizing earnings and revenue quality, and is shown to be effective across various capitalization levels and market environments.

title: Citi names Jane Fraser as first female CEO of big Wall St bank
summary: Citigroup announced Jane Fraser will succeed Michael Corbat as CEO in February, making her the first woman to lead a major Wall Street bank. Fraser, currently head of Citi's global consumer banking division, has a distinguished career in the financial industry and her promotion was widely anticipated. This move is seen as a significant step for diversity in finance.

title: Citigroup’s Fraser to Be First Woman to Lead a Big Wall Street Bank (Published 2020)
summary: Jane Fraser will become the first woman to lead a major Wall Street bank, taking over as CEO of Citigroup in February. This move is seen as groundbreaking in an industry historically dominated by men, with Ms. Fraser succeeding Michael Corbat after his eight years at the helm. She joins a small group of female leaders among large American corporations, highlighting the ongoing effort for greater diversity in finance.

title: Israeli Fintech company Capitolis raises $11 million from three financial powerhouses
summary: Fintech company Capitolis has raised $11 million from Citi, J.P. Morgan, and State Street, bringing its total funding to $81 million. This strategic investment from three major financial institutions serves as a strong endorsement of Capitolis' platform, which helps financial institutions optimize their balance sheets and free up capital. The company, founded in 2016, has already eliminated $5 trillion in overall positions for over 50 financial institutions, including many of the world’s largest banks, and plans further expansion.

title: Citigroup picks Jane Fraser as first female CEO of a major Wall Street bank
summary: Citigroup has named Jane Fraser as its next chief executive, making her the first woman to lead a major Wall Street bank. Fraser, who was president of the company, will succeed Michael Corbat and faces significant challenges including improving profitability and addressing past operational issues. Her appointment is seen as a pivotal moment for the bank, which has lagged behind competitors in key financial metrics.

title: Exclusive: Goldman Sachs to Buy Out Partner in China Securities Venture
summary: Goldman Sachs is moving to acquire full ownership of its Chinese securities joint venture, Goldman Sachs Gao Hua Securities Co. Ltd., by buying the remaining 49% stake from its partner, Beijing Gao Hua Securities Co. Ltd. This move follows China's relaxation of foreign ownership restrictions in financial sectors and coincides with a significant shake-up in the joint venture's top management, including the appointment of a new chair and general manager. The acquisition price is expected to be substantially higher than previous valuations, reflecting the growing interest of foreign financial institutions in leveraging China's market opening policies.

title: JPMorgan Chase fires employees over possible coronavirus aid fraud
summary: JPMorgan Chase has fired several employees for allegedly pocketing funds from a federal program designed to aid companies hurt by the coronavirus shutdown. An internal investigation, prompted by a government inquiry, found that a number of employees improperly applied for and received money from the Small Business Association's Economic Injury Disaster Loan (EIDL) program and deposited it into personal accounts. The bank sent an all-staff memo signed by CEO Jamie Dimon urging employees to report suspicious conduct and uphold high standards.

title: Fidelity National Financial Prices $600 Million Of 2.450% Notes Due March 15, 2031
summary: Fidelity National Financial (FNF) has priced an issuance of $600 million of 2.450% senior notes due March 15, 2031. The notes were priced at 99.642% of their principal amount to yield 2.489% per annum, with interest paid semi-annually. The net proceeds will be used to repay outstanding indebtedness related to the FGL Holdings acquisition and for general corporate purposes.

title: Citi names Jane Fraser CEO
summary: Citigroup Inc. has appointed Jane Fraser as its next chief executive, making her the first woman to lead a major global bank. Fraser will succeed Michael Corbat, who is retiring in February after more than eight years. She is tasked with improving returns and leveraging the bank's global network in a changing economic landscape.

title: Successful With Chinese Startups, Sequoia China Launches a Hedge Fund
summary: Sequoia Capital China, led by Neil Shen, has launched a new hedge-fund business, the Sequoia Capital Equity Partners fund. Starting with over $300 million in initial capital from investors, the U.S.-dollar-denominated fund plans to invest in publicly traded stocks globally, leveraging the firm's successful track record with Chinese technology startups.

title: Who’s the Next Woman to Take Over on Wall Street? (Published 2020)
summary: Following Jane Fraser's historic appointment as CEO of Citigroup, becoming the first woman to lead a major Wall Street bank, this article profiles several women who are potential candidates to break banking's glass ceiling. It highlights executives like Marianne Lake, Jennifer Piepszak, and Cathy Bessant, who are seen as top contenders at their current companies, as well as rising stars such as Thasunda Duckett, Susan Huang, and Dina Powell McCormick.

title: Morgan Stanley fends off JPMorgan to keep top spot in Japan
summary: Morgan Stanley maintained its position as Japan's most profitable foreign securities firm for the fourth consecutive year, reporting a 5% increase in net income to ¥22.4 billion ($211 million) in the year ended March. This achievement was largely attributed to successful trading for hedge funds, allowing it to surpass JPMorgan Chase & Co. The U.S. bank anticipates continued momentum despite the economic impact of the novel coronavirus pandemic.

title: Citigroup has just appointed the first female CEO of a Wall Street bank
summary: Jane Fraser has been appointed the next chief executive officer of Citigroup, making her the first woman to lead a major Wall Street bank. Her promotion is seen as a significant step towards greater gender diversity in the financial industry, where only a small percentage of top leadership roles are held by women. Fraser's career spans various critical roles within Citigroup and is credited with helping the bank recover after the financial crisis.

title: Coca-Cola FEMSA recauda más de 700 millones de dólares con bono verde
summary: Coca-Cola FEMSA, the largest Coca-Cola bottler by sales volume, successfully issued its inaugural green bond in the international market, raising $705 million. This issuance, with a 12-year term and a coupon rate of 1.850%, is noted as the largest of its kind for a Latin American issuer and will fund green projects related to climate change, water care, and circular economy initiatives. Legal counsel for the transaction included Cleary Gottlieb Steen & Hamilton for the issuer and Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom, alongside Galicia Abogados, for the underwriters BofA Securities, J.P. Morgan Securities, and Morgan Stanley.

title: Huntington extends ‘fair play banking to business customers
summary: Huntington Bancshares has extended its "fair play banking" initiative, which includes a 24-hour grace period to cover overdrafts, to its business customers. This program, previously available to consumers for a decade, is intended to help small businesses, especially during the pandemic, by saving them millions in potential overdraft fees. The bank's CEO, Steve Steinour, stated this move helps businesses allocate funds to payroll or inventory and signals strong customer support.

title: Morgan Stanley Lands $8-Million RBC Wealth Team in New York
summary: Morgan Stanley has recruited a team of advisors, Ira H. Mark and Michael J. Berger, from RBC Wealth Management, marking a strategic move to regain talent. This team generated nearly $8 million in revenue over the past year and managed approximately $1.4 billion in client assets. Their return to Morgan Stanley, where they previously worked, signals Morgan Stanley's renewed focus on recruiting veteran brokers after a period of reduced activity.

title: AmEx reopens its city offices at 10% capacity
summary: American Express has begun reopening its New York City offices at 10% capacity, while simultaneously extending its work-from-home policy for employees worldwide through June 2021. This move aims to offer colleagues greater flexibility with work and family obligations, particularly concerning childcare and public transportation concerns. AmEx joins other major New York employers in gradually bringing workers back to boost the local economy while accommodating employee needs.

title: At JPMorgan, Productivity Falls for Staff Working at Home
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. CEO Jamie Dimon discussed with KBW analysts that productivity among employees working from home slipped, particularly on Mondays and Fridays. This decline in performance, coupled with concerns about organic interaction, is a key reason the bank is encouraging more staff to return to the office. The bank observed a "troubling pattern" as most employees transitioned to remote work due to the Covid-19 pandemic.

title: Leading global advisory, broking and solutions company
summary: J.P. Morgan helped Willis Towers Watson create an innovative Treasury Centre in the Netherlands, significantly improving visibility and transparency in their treasury function. This solution addressed challenges arising from the merger of Willis and Towers Watson and the acquisition of Gras Savoy, establishing an in-house bank for foreign exchange and cash concentration. The new structure has led to improved working capital, optimized liquidity through cross-border sweeps, and a scalable framework for future growth.

title: The digital transformation: speed and convenience drive B2C payments
summary: Digital transformation is rapidly changing B2C payments, driven by customer demand for speed and convenience, especially among Millennials. The article highlights how technological advancements, particularly mobile technology and payment networks, are enabling businesses to digitize low-value consumer payments like refunds and rebates, significantly reducing costs and enhancing customer satisfaction. This shift leverages network effects, contextual remittance, and enhanced security measures to create a strong value proposition for both payers and customers.

title: New funding mechanism fuels growth for JERA global markets
summary: JERA Global Markets (JERAGM), facing challenges with fragmented banking across multiple banks and time zones, partnered with J.P. Morgan for a treasury transformation. J.P. Morgan implemented a three-phase global liquidity solution, including notional pooling in Asia, the U.S., and Europe, and a cross-border "follow-the-sun" sweep. This automated system delivered an estimated US$1 million in annual benefits by improving scalability, operational efficiency, and security for JERAGM's treasury operations.

title: Offshore driller Noble enters Chapter 11
summary: Offshore drilling contractor Noble Corporation plc has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy due to a significant crash in crude oil prices, compounded by the coronavirus pandemic. The company plans to restructure its operations by exchanging $3.4bn in debt for new equity, securing a new $675m revolving credit facility, and receiving a $200m investment from bondholders. Noble expects to emerge from Chapter 11 before the end of 2020, aiming for a stronger balance sheet and enhanced liquidity to support future growth and continue operations without interruption.

title: REFILE-JPMorgan and BlackRock tap AI startup to automate opening custody accounts
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co and BlackRock Inc have partnered with AI startup Saphyre to automate the process of opening custody accounts, which promises to streamline a heavily manual process involving extensive paperwork and faxes. This AI-powered system remembers previously uploaded documents, accelerating the time it takes for new funds to reach the market. The collaboration highlights a growing trend of large financial institutions leveraging tech startups to digitize and automate burdensome procedures, especially in a post-COVID-19 world where manual processes have become even more challenging.

title: JFrog Announces Pricing of Its Initial Public Offering
summary: JFrog Ltd. announced the pricing of its initial public offering of 11,568,218 ordinary shares at $44.00 per share. Of these, 8,000,000 shares are offered by JFrog and 3,568,218 by existing shareholders. The shares were expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol "FROG" on September 16, 2020.

title: Paul Ryan's SPAC Executive Network Partnering Corp. prices upsized $360 million IPO at $25
summary: Executive Network Partnering Corp., a SPAC co-founded by Paul Ryan, Alex Dunn, and Solamere Capital, successfully priced an upsized $360 million IPO, offering 14.4 million units at $25 each. The company, led by CEO Alex Dunn, plans to focus on businesses where its network and operational background will provide a competitive advantage. It will list on the NYSE under the symbol ENPC.U, with Evercore ISI acting as lead manager.

title: -Morgan Stanley doesn't expect trading boom to continue
summary: Morgan Stanley's CFO Jonathan Pruzan stated that the bank does not anticipate its sales and trading and investment banking business to perform as well in the third quarter as it did in the second quarter, despite good August activity. The bank expects net interest income in its wealth management business to decline slightly but is on track to complete its E*Trade acquisition in Q4. Pruzan also noted the bank's capital strength offers flexibility for future strategic opportunities in investment management.

title: Broadstone Net Lease, Inc. Announces Pricing of Initial Public Offering
summary: Broadstone Net Lease, Inc. (BNL), an internally-managed real estate investment trust, announced the pricing of its initial public offering of 33,500,000 shares of Class A Common Stock at $17.00 per share. Trading on the NYSE under "BNL" was expected to begin on September 17, 2020, with the offering closing on September 21, 2020. The net proceeds are intended for debt repayment and general business purposes, including future acquisitions.

title: Webull Review (2023): A Free Stock App — But Better Than Robinhood?
summary: This article provides a comprehensive review of Webull, a free stock trading app known for $0 commissions on stock, options, and ETF trades. It highlights Webull's impressive technology, advanced trading platforms, and research tools, comparing it to competitors like Robinhood and TradeStation. The review also covers Webull's pros and cons, fee structure, safety measures, and account opening process, concluding that it's ideal for active DIY investors and those focused on stocks and ETFs.
