summary: JPMorgan Chase has consolidated its $400 million global media account, appointing WPP and Dentsu as its media agencies of record after a review that began in late September. WPP will establish a dedicated team known as Team JPMC, powered by GroupM, to manage the account. This change follows a marketing department leadership shake-up in April and sees incumbent Zenith losing the account after 15 years.

title: Leveraged Muni Funds Face Losses as Bond Rout Drags On
summary: Leveraged municipal bond funds are experiencing double-digit losses due to the worst bond rout in decades. Rising interest rates are impacting fund-share prices and reducing income payouts to investors. High net worth households had previously invested in these closed-end muni mutual funds, which hold approximately $60 billion, seeking tax-free income.

title: 2021's top local financial stock may surprise you
summary: Byline Bancorp significantly outperformed other Chicago financial firms in 2021, with a 77% return for investors, far exceeding larger banks like Wintrust Financial and Northern Trust. Despite its smaller size and the ongoing consolidation in the banking market, Byline's CEO maintains the company is focused on organic growth rather than seeking a sale, challenging investor speculation about a takeover premium. The success is attributed to strong loan growth, avoidance of pricey acquisitions, and a robust SBA lending business.

title: Jefferies staff to go remote until end Jan, financial offices empty out
summary: Jefferies Financial Group has instructed its staff to work remotely until January 31 due to the spread of the Omicron variant, a move mirrored by other major investment banks like Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase. This decision reflects the ongoing challenges financial firms face in managing the pandemic's impact on office work, despite earlier efforts to bring employees back. Banks are re-evaluating their return-to-office plans amid rising COVID-19 cases, with varying deadlines for staff to return onsite.

title: JPMorgan Chase Appoints Ben Ratner Executive Director, Sustainability
summary: JPMorgan Chase has appointed Ben Ratner as its new Executive Director, Sustainability. Ratner, previously with the Environmental Defense Fund, will focus on integrating sustainability into the firm's growth strategies, including low-carbon technology and community climate resilience. This appointment follows JPMorgan Chase's significant sustainability commitments, such as aligning with the Paris Agreement and facilitating $2.5 trillion in sustainable finance.

title: MAS investigates online trading platform
summary: The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and the Commercial Affairs Department (CAD) are investigating Samtrade FX, an overseas online trading platform, for potential breaches of local securities laws related to operating without a capital markets services licence. Three men have been arrested in connection with the probe, which also revealed suspicions of irregular trading activities on the platform. Samtrade FX and its related entities have been on MAS’s Investor Alert List since July 2021.

title: Fast-charging battery startup StoreDot hits $1.5 billion valuation in Series D
summary: Fast-charging battery startup StoreDot has achieved a $1.5 billion valuation in its Series D funding round, having raised $60 million to date, led by Vietnamese EV manufacturer VinFast. The company aims to bring additional automotive giants on board and plans to use the funds to further its silicon-dominant extreme fast charge (XFC) battery cells for EVs and commence scale-up operations for mass production by 2024. StoreDot's technology promises to fully charge an EV in just five minutes, revolutionizing the electric vehicle market.

title: SIMON PROPERTY GROUP SELLS $1.2 BILLION OF SENIOR NOTES
summary: Simon Property Group, through its operating partnership subsidiary, has announced the sale of $1.2 billion in senior notes, comprising $500 million in Floating Rate Notes due 2024 and $700 million in 2.650% Notes due 2032. The proceeds from this offering are intended to repay indebtedness under its $3.5 billion revolving credit facility and for general corporate purposes. The offering is expected to close on January 11, 2022.

title: Private equity firm TPG seeks $9.5 bln valuation in U.S. IPO
summary: Private equity firm TPG is targeting a $9.5 billion valuation in its upcoming U.S. initial public offering this month. The firm plans to sell about 28.3 million shares between $28 and $31 apiece, aiming to raise approximately $877.6 million, with 40% going to existing shareholders. TPG, an investor in companies like Airbnb and Uber, has recovered from past poor investments and seen a significant jump in net income and revenue in the nine months leading up to September 2021.

title: Driven Brands Acquires Auto Glass Now, Expands US Presence
summary: Driven Brands Holdings, Inc. has acquired Auto Glass Now (AGN) for $170 million, significantly expanding its U.S. presence in the auto glass repair market. The acquisition adds 75 locations to Driven Brands' Paint, Collision, and Glass segment, making it one of North America's largest providers of auto glass services. Analysts maintain a "Strong Buy" consensus rating for DRVN, with an average price target implying a 35% upside potential.

title: Iberdrola optimizes working capital with SAP® Real-Time Treasury
summary: Iberdrola, a global leader in renewable energy, has partnered with J.P. Morgan to implement the SAP® Real-Time Treasury app. This integration provides Iberdrola with real-time visibility into their global cash positions, streamlines treasury operations, and enhances their ability to respond to market changes. The solution, powered by J.P. Morgan's Treasury Services APIs, has migrated Iberdrola from daily reporting to instant access to financial data, optimizing their working capital management.

title: Santander finds itself in a Citi moment with $175M error
summary: Santander mistakenly paid out $175 million in duplicate payments to 75,000 customers on Christmas Day, creating a situation reminiscent of Citi's $900 million error in 2020. The bank is now working to claw back the funds, expecting varying levels of cooperation from other financial institutions and potentially facing regulatory scrutiny over its risk management systems. The incident highlights the challenges banks face in recovering erroneous payments, especially when funds have been disbursed to accounts at other banks or potentially spent by recipients.

title: JPMorgan Chase: The Gold Standard in Diverse Spend
summary: JPMorgan Chase is promoting diverse spend throughout its supply chain by dedicating approximately $2bn annually to diverse-owned and managed companies and committed to increasing spend with Black, Hispanic, and Latino businesses by an additional $750 million. The company's strategy involves mobilizing key suppliers, mentoring those with emerging diversity programs, and enhancing the discoverability of diverse suppliers, aiming for a significant increase in diverse spend over the next three years. This initiative is a core part of its ESG agenda, viewing supplier diversity as both a moral imperative and smart business practice to foster economic growth and strengthen communities.

title: Jim Connell
summary: Jim Connell, CPO and Head of Global Supplier Services at JPMorgan Chase, discusses the importance of diverse spend and maximizing its impact throughout the supply chain. JPMorgan Chase is committed to supporting diverse suppliers, dedicating approximately US$2bn annually, and made a further commitment in October 2020 to increase spend with Black, Hispanic, and Latino businesses by $750 million. Through their Gold Supplier program, they encourage strategic suppliers to develop growth plans to improve supplier diversity, aiming for a significant increase in diverse spend over the next three years.

title: Pinnacle Financial Partners Opens Full-Service Office in Huntersville
summary: Pinnacle Financial Partners has opened a new full-service office in Huntersville, NC, expanding its presence in Mecklenburg County with a team of veteran financial services professionals. The new office at 16633 Birkdale Commons offers a full range of banking and financial services, building on Pinnacle's significant growth in the greater Charlotte MSA. The team includes new additions and experienced advisors, solidifying Pinnacle's commitment to community-focused service with comprehensive financial solutions.

title: Analyst Coverage | Investor Relations | Workday
summary: This Workday Investor Relations page lists the research analysts who cover the company. It explicitly states that analyst opinions, estimates, and forecasts are their own and do not represent Workday's views or endorsement. The page provides a comprehensive list of firms and their respective analysts covering Workday.

title: Rockefeller Plucks $9.1-Mln Atlanta Team from Morgan Stanley
summary: Rockefeller Capital Management has hired a six-person team from Morgan Stanley in Atlanta, generating $9.1 million in annual revenue and managing $1.3 billion in client assets. The team, led by Hunter Hamm, will operate as Southeastern Wealth Management Group and reports to a new divisional director for the Southeast. This move marks Rockefeller's 68th team addition to its private wealth unit since its 2018 recapitalization, continuing its aggressive recruiting strategy.

title: Subsidiarias de peruana Urbanova reciben préstamo de 190 millones de dólares
summary: Subsidiaries of the Peruvian real estate company Urbanova secured a $190 million secured loan from a syndicate of banks to refinance a previous credit. The beneficiaries, Inmuebles Limatambo, Inversiones San Borja, and Urbanizadora Jardín, used the funds to repay an earlier loan and backed the new credit with a mortgage on their properties. Legal counsel for the transaction included Simpson Thacher & Bartlett and Rodrigo, Elías & Medrano Abogados for Urbanova, and Clifford Chance and Garrigues for the syndicate of banks led by Banco Santander.

title: Citigroup prepares to fire unvaccinated employees at the end of January. (Published 2022)
summary: Citigroup announced it will dismiss unvaccinated employees by the end of January, requiring all U.S. staff to submit proof of vaccination by January 14 or face unpaid leave and termination by January 31. This mandate is among the strictest on Wall Street, with over 90% of Citi's U.S. employees already complying, while other major banks have varying policies. The decision comes amidst broader discussions about vaccine mandates for large employers, with some employees resisting the policy.

title: WSFS nets $15M in lawsuit settlement tied to acquisition 12 years ago
summary: WSFS Financial Corp. announced it will receive $15 million from a settlement resolving a long-standing legal dispute. This dispute originated from the bank's 2010 acquisition of Christiana Bank & Trust. The settlement covers all legal costs associated with the case.

title: Rocket Grew Into America’s Biggest Mortgage Lender, but Now Comes the Hard Part - WSJ
summary: Rocket Companies became the largest mortgage lender in the U.S. during the pandemic, significantly increasing its mortgage originations. However, the company now faces the challenge of convincing investors that it can sustain growth even if mortgage refinancings decline. Rocket's past success relied heavily on a favorable interest rate environment, and it needs to adapt to a potentially sleepier mortgage market.

title: JPM 2022: New Johnson & Johnson CEO Duato points out 5 pipeline meds that can generate $5B-plus
summary: Johnson & Johnson's new CEO, Joaquin Duato, outlined the company's pharmaceutical strategy for the coming decade at the J.P. Morgan Healthcare Conference, aiming for $60 billion in pharma sales by 2025. He highlighted five pipeline drugs—Carvykti, nipocalimab, Rybrevant, milvexian, and the Taris bladder cancer platform—each with the potential to generate $5 billion or more in peak sales. These new therapies, alongside expanded indications for existing blockbusters, are crucial for future growth, especially as the company prepares for a consumer health spinoff and faces patent expiration for Stelara.

title: At least $5 billion was spent on music rights acquisitions in 2021. Could 2022 be even bigger?
summary: In 2021, the music industry saw an estimated $5.05 billion spent on catalog and music rights acquisitions, involving over 60 significant deals. This included sales directly from artists and songwriters, which accounted for approximately $2.33 billion of the total, with December alone seeing $720 million in such deals. The article questions if 2022 will surpass this record, pointing to early 2022 deals like Warner Chappell's acquisition of David Bowie's catalog for $250 million and John Legend's previously undisclosed 2021 catalog sale.

title: Owens & Minor to buy home healthcare provider Apria for $1.45 bln
summary: Owens & Minor Inc. announced its acquisition of home healthcare provider Apria Inc. for approximately $1.45 billion in cash. This strategic move aims to strengthen Owens & Minor's position in the growing home healthcare services market, reflecting increased demand due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic. The deal, valued at $37.50 per share for Apria, is expected to close in the first half of 2022.

title: AI Startup Speeds Up Derivative Models for Bank of Montreal
summary: Riskfuel, a Toronto-based AI startup, has partnered with Bank of Montreal (BMO) to accelerate its derivative models using NVIDIA DGX systems. This technology significantly improves the performance of complex financial calculations, enabling BMO to make faster and more accurate investment decisions and expand its client base. Riskfuel's solution allows banks to run derivative portfolio models in seconds, offering both speed and accuracy.

title: These 14 bank stocks are in the best position to benefit from rising interest rates
summary: This article identifies 14 bank stocks poised to benefit from rising interest rates, based on a screen of various banks. It highlights Huntington Bancshares Inc. (HBAN) as a top performer expected to significantly increase its earnings per share through 2023, outpacing the S&P 500 Index. The piece delves into why these select few banks are projected to achieve double-digit earnings growth.

title: Bank of America to Cut Overdraft Fees to $10 From $35
summary: Bank of America announced it will cut its overdraft fees from $35 to $10 starting in May, following similar moves by other major banks. Regulators and politicians have been scrutinizing these fees, arguing they unfairly impact financially vulnerable families. This change comes after the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau highlighted overdraft fees charged by Bank of America, JPMorgan Chase, and Wells Fargo in a recent report.

title: Nelson Bradshaw joins Farther’s investment office
summary: Nelson Bradshaw, former BBVA North Florida CEO, has joined Farther, a New York City-based digital family investment office, as managing director of Banking Strategies in Northeast Florida. He will focus on building the organization's regional banking strategy and a team of financial advisers for the Southeast market alongside Daniel Gilham. Farther aims to pair advisers with technology to manage client finances and capitalize on fintech growth in Jacksonville.

title: Goldman Sachs Stock (GS): Is It A Good Buy?
summary: This article analyzes whether Goldman Sachs stock (GS) is a good investment, focusing on its current price, market capitalization, P/E ratio, EPS, and PEG ratio. It highlights that the company's favorable ratios and strong business position, combined with a "Buy" rating from Zacks Rank System, suggest it is a worthy investment. However, it advises investors to await the upcoming earnings report before making significant investment decisions.

title: Omar Siddiq first Malaysian to head HSBC local unit
summary: HSBC Holdings Plc has appointed Omar Siddiq from CIMB Group Holdings Bhd to lead its Malaysian unit, making him the first Malaysian to hold this position. Siddiq, who was the head of CIMB Group’s wholesale banking division, will replace the retiring CEO Stuart Milne after a garden leave period. HSBC has had a presence in Malaysia since 1884, with over 60 branches and 4,000 employees.

title: At Wall Street firm Jefferies, bonuses clock in at nearly $450,000—on average
summary: Jefferies Financial Group reported average bonuses of $443,000 for bankers for 2021, significantly higher than the Wall Street average. This reflects a highly profitable year for investment banking due to soaring stock markets and low interest rates. The lavish pay is expected to face increased scrutiny from politicians amidst broader economic struggles.

title: US Banks Form Group to Offer USDF Stablecoin
summary: A consortium of U.S. banks, including New York Community Bank and FirstBank, plans to launch its own stablecoin called USDF. This initiative aims to provide a bank-minted alternative to existing stablecoins like Tether's USDT and Circle's USDC, addressing concerns about the reserves backing nonbank-issued stablecoins and potentially offering additional consumer protection. USDF will operate on the Provenance blockchain and be redeemable 1:1 for cash from member banks.

title: JPM 2022: Morgan Health, Kaiser Permanente partner on health equity
summary: Morgan Health and Kaiser Permanente are partnering to focus on health equity for JPMorgan Chase's California employees, beginning this month. They plan to jointly collect and report health equity metrics and introduce performance guarantees tied to health equity for JPMorgan employees starting in 2023. Morgan Health also aims to expand into new markets and integrate digital capabilities through its investment in Vera Whole Health, which is merging with Castlight Health.

title: Ao menos três agências bancárias estão fechadas no Alto Tietê por causa da contaminação de funcionários com Covid-19
summary: Ao menos três agências bancárias no Alto Tietê, incluindo unidades do Itaú Unibanco em Suzano e Poá, e uma do Bradesco em Suzano, foram fechadas temporariamente devido à contaminação de funcionários por Covid-19. O Sindicato dos Bancários da região relata um aumento significativo nos casos, com cerca de 20 bancários afastados atualmente e 45 já tendo retornado ao trabalho desde o início de janeiro. Os bancos envolvidos afirmam ter implementado protocolos de segurança, como sanitização e afastamento de equipes, e instam os clientes a priorizarem os canais digitais.

title: JANELLE CURTIS NAMED CHIEF ENTERPRISE TRANSFORMATION OFFICER FOR WARNER MUSIC GROUP
summary: Janelle Curtis has been appointed as Chief Enterprise Transformation Officer for Warner Music Group. Her role will focus on driving tech-enabled evolution across the company's global corporate operations, business structures, processes, and digital solutions. Curtis brings extensive experience from Bank of America and Goldman Sachs to her new position.

title: HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Infosys and more...in a blockchain ETF's portfolio? That's possible
summary: This article discusses the misconception that Blockchain ETFs are solely for investing in cryptocurrencies, pointing out that cryptocurrencies are just one application of blockchain technology. The author suggests that a blockchain ETF's portfolio could include traditional financial powerhouses like HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, and Infosys. The article highlights how this broader understanding of blockchain technology can impact investment strategies.

title: Lifestance CEO Doesn’t See Digital Mental Health Providers as Competitors
summary: LifeStance Health CEO Michael Lester states that digital mental health providers are not significant competitors, as LifeStance focuses on higher-acuity patients with diagnoses and bills third-party payers. The company differentiates itself by largely providing in-network care through its extensive network of 4,400 clinicians and also sees its staffing model as appealing to a different, larger subset of clinicians. LifeStance also reported that while it saw an uptick in cancellations due to the omicron variant, its hybrid model helped it navigate COVID-related challenges.

title: Focus: Citigroup CEO Fraser fights to sell turnaround plan to investors
summary: Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser is struggling to convince investors and analysts that her radical overhaul of the bank will succeed, despite efforts to simplify the firm and exit non-core businesses. The bank's share price continues to lag rivals, reflecting skepticism after years of previous failed restructuring attempts. Fraser aims to transform Citigroup into a premier bank for institutions with cross-border needs, but market participants remain unconvinced by the progress so far.

title: Wells Fargo Rally Shows Warren Buffett's Mistake in Selling Big Stake in Bank
summary: The article suggests that Warren Buffett made a significant investment mistake by selling Berkshire Hathaway's large stake in Wells Fargo, JPMorgan Chase, and Goldman Sachs in 2020. This is highlighted by the subsequent rally in Wells Fargo's stock. The piece frames this as one of Buffett's less successful decisions in an otherwise illustrious career.

title: Citigroup results show restructuring has its costs
summary: Citigroup reported a 26% drop in fourth-quarter profit, largely due to $1.1 billion in after-tax expenses related to its ongoing divestitures of consumer banking businesses outside the U.S. CEO Jane Fraser's "strategy refresh" involves shedding non-U.S. consumer operations to focus more tightly on institutional businesses. Despite a profit drop, the company's shares pared losses after CFO Mark Mason confirmed the resumption of share buybacks, and its investment banking business showed a 43% jump in revenue.

title: Wage inflation has arrived in a big way and Jamie Dimon says CEOs 'shouldn't be crybabies about it'
summary: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon stated that while megabanks initially benefited from inflation through higher interest rates, rising employee wages are now impacting earnings. Dimon acknowledged that wage inflation is a significant expense for banks, especially for their professional staff, and advised CEOs to "just deal with it" rather than complain, calling rising wages "a good thing for the people who have the wages going up."

title: The Student Has Become The Master
summary: Wells Fargo, under CEO Charlie Scharf, significantly improved its fourth-quarter profit, suggesting a turnaround for the bank previously mired in scandal. This performance contrasts with dips in fourth-quarter profits reported by JPMorgan Chase and Citigroup, the latter continuing to divest its Asian consumer banking operations. The article highlights Wells Fargo's resurgence and the varying fortunes of major U.S. banks.

title: StubHub Explores Going Public, Valued at $13B
summary: StubHub Holdings is considering a direct listing that could value the company at over $13 billion, following other ticket platforms going public. The parent company of StubHub and Viagogo has filed paperwork with the SEC and is working with Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase. Despite facing scrutiny over its merger and carrying significant debt, StubHub expects to rebound to pre-pandemic revenue levels in 2022, though the Omicron variant poses a potential challenge.

title: DI People: JCPenney, 7-Eleven, Recode Therapeutics, Hawkeye, PCCI, and Others Make Moves
summary: This article details numerous executive appointments and promotions across various companies in North Texas, including JCPenney, 7-Eleven, Recode Therapeutics, Hawkeye, and PwC. Key moves include new CEOs for Hawkeye, Harver, and Recode Therapeutics, and significant leadership changes in e-commerce, technology, and operations at other notable firms, reflecting a dynamic period of innovation and growth in the region.

title: Stock Market News For Today, January 14th, 2022
summary: This article provides a stock market update for January 14th, 2022, highlighting that penny stocks and blue chips were expected to start lower. It discusses key economic factors like falling retail sales and upcoming political nominations, and features five trending penny stocks to watch: Guardforce AI (GFAI), Nextplay Technologies (NXTP), China SXT Pharmaceuticals (SXTC), Kaival Brands Innovations Group (KAVL), and Vinco Ventures (BBIG), detailing their recent performance and news.

title: Pay on Wall Street will surge after a bumper year. (Published 2022)
summary: JPMorgan Chase and Citigroup reported strong annual profits for 2021, leading to increased compensation on Wall Street despite rising costs and a slight dip in quarterly earnings for JPMorgan. The banks are focused on competitive pay to attract and retain talent in a tight labor market. JPMorgan Chase posted a record $48.3 billion in profit for the year, even as its fourth-quarter profit declined due to higher employee compensation and technology investments.

title: JPMorgan shares fall as mixed outlook sours profit beat
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co's shares declined by as much as 6% despite exceeding fourth-quarter profit estimates, as analysts reacted negatively to the bank's future profitability forecasts. The largest U.S. bank warned that a key metric, return on tangible capital equity (ROTCE), might drop below its 17% medium-term target for the current year due to a slowdown in capital markets, investment costs, and rising expenses. Despite this, JPMorgan maintained its 17% ROTCE target beyond 2022, anticipating benefits from rising interest rates and business growth stemming from its investments.

title: Wells Fargo Mortgage Production Fades As It Closes Branches
summary: Wells Fargo's mortgage loan production declined significantly in 2021, with an 8 percent overall fall and 27 percent fewer loans to homebuyers, coinciding with the closure of 270 branches and 16,000 layoffs. The bank originated $205 billion in home loans, down from $223 billion in 2020, even as it increased reliance on its retail branches for loan origination. Despite these declines in home lending revenue, the bank reported a stronger fourth quarter overall, with a 13 percent increase in total revenue to $20.9 billion and a $5.8 billion profit.

title: StubHub Reportedly Considers Going Public
summary: StubHub Holdings, which operates ticket resale platforms StubHub and viagogo, is reportedly exploring going public via a direct listing as early as 2022. This move could value the company at over $13 billion, with JPMorgan Chase & Co. and Goldman Sachs Group Inc. advising. The decision to pursue a direct listing means selling existing shares without issuing new ones, distinguishing it from a traditional IPO.

title: Three Takeaways from the J.P. Morgan Health Care Conference
summary: The article summarizes three key takeaways from the J.P. Morgan Health Care Conference, highlighting Morgan Health's efforts to lower healthcare costs through reshaped accountable care models and partnerships with Kaiser Permanente and Vera Whole Health. It also discusses how provider organizations like Intermountain Healthcare and Mass General Brigham are pursuing growth strategies amid the pandemic, emphasizing shifts to value-based care and investments in virtual care and cutting-edge therapies. Finally, the article underscores the ongoing impact of COVID-19 on hospitals, increased workforce expenses, and the permanent integration of COVID-19 testing into lab services.

title: Frost Tower in downtown San Antonio is up for sale
summary: The Frost Tower, San Antonio's first new downtown office tower since 1989, is currently on the market. Completed in 2019 and valued at $99.5 million, the 24-story building is 80 percent leased, with Frost Bank occupying 61% of the space for its corporate headquarters until 2039. The sale does not impact Frost Bank's long-term lease or its commitment to downtown San Antonio.

title: Brazil-based Hashdex Expects to Launch First DeFi ETF Next Month
summary: Brazil-based Hashdex has received approval to launch the world's first decentralized finance (DeFi) ETF, which is expected to be listed on the Brazilian stock exchange, B3, on February 17. The ETF will track the CF Benchmarks' DeFi Composite Index, comprising 12 assets including decentralized applications, service protocols, and the Ethereum network. Hashdex aims to provide global investors with a new way to access the growing crypto ecosystem through this innovative product.

title: Morgan Stanley outperforms rivals with profit beat
summary: Morgan Stanley reported fourth-quarter profit that exceeded market expectations, driven by its focus on advising wealth clients and a boom in global dealmaking. The investment bank's shares rose as it outmaneuvered rivals who faced challenges like rising expenses and weak trading. The record full-year profit and revenue, along with a raised target for return on tangible capital equity, underscore the success of CEO James Gorman's strategy of transforming the bank into a more balanced institution with a strong wealth management focus.

title: World’s first DeFi ETF to be listed on the Brazilian stock exchange in February
summary: Hashdex, the largest crypto asset manager in Latin America, announced that its DeFi exchange-traded fund (ETF) would be listed on the Brazilian stock exchange, B3, under the ticker DEFI11 on February 17th. This ETF, the first of its kind globally, will track the "CF DeFi Composite Index," covering 12 assets across major dApps, service protocols, scalability solutions, and Ethereum as a settlement network. Hashdex aims to provide investors with regulated exposure to the DeFi market and believes in DeFi's potential to significantly impact the financial sector.

title: JPMorgan Chase to use NextEra Energy Resources' Optos software platform to optimize energy and sustainable operations
summary: JPMorgan Chase is implementing NextEra Energy Resources' Optos software platform to enhance its energy optimization and reduce its carbon footprint. The Optos platform utilizes AI and blockchain to provide real-time and forecasted energy data, helping companies match energy demand with clean energy resources. This initiative supports JPMorgan Chase's sustainability goals, including a significant reduction in greenhouse gas emissions and increased reliance on renewable energy.

title: Billioniare Joe Tsai outed as buyer of $190M penthouse
summary: Alibaba co-founder Joe Tsai, through his Hong Kong-based family firm Blue Pool Capital, has been identified as the buyer of billionaire Daniel Och's penthouse at 220 Central Park South for $188 million. This purchase adds to Tsai's existing real estate portfolio in the same building, bringing his total investment there to $345 million. Och made a significant profit, having bought the penthouse for $93 million in 2019.

title: ESR Completes Takeover of ARA Asset Management
summary: ESR has completed its $5.2 billion acquisition of Singapore-based ARA Asset Management, establishing the enlarged ESR Group as the world's third-largest listed real estate investment manager with $140 billion in gross assets under management. The merger, which includes ARA subsidiary Logos, significantly expands ESR's network, adding 59 new capital partners and strengthening its position as APAC's leading real asset manager. This strategic move aims to leverage the combined platform's scale and diversified offerings to deliver integrated solutions to a consolidated global investor base.

title: Bank of America Corp. stock falls Thursday, underperforms market
summary: Bank of America Corp. (BAC) shares fell 1.49% to $45.75 on Thursday, underperforming the broader market as the S&P 500 Index and Dow Jones Industrial Average also declined. The stock closed $4.33 below its 52-week high. Competitors JPMorgan Chase & Co. and Wells Fargo & Co. also saw declines, while Citigroup Inc. rose slightly.

title: News | Marriott Resort Owner in Palm Desert, California, Gets $128 Million Loan
summary: Kam Sang Co. secured a $128 million, five-year, interest-only loan from Goldman Sachs Bank USA for its JW Marriott Desert Springs Resort & Spa in Palm Desert, California. This financing, arranged by JLL’s Hotels & Hospitality Group, was used to repay the debt from the 2017 acquisition of the 286-acre property. The resort recently underwent a $40 million renovation and conditions in the Coachella Valley hotel market are improving after pandemic-related declines.

title: U.S. banks close record number of retail branches in 2021, Wells Fargo shutters most
summary: U.S. banks closed a record 2,927 net retail branches in 2021, driven by increased digital banking adoption and industry consolidation. Wells Fargo led the closures by shuttering 267 net locations. Despite widespread closures, JPMorgan Chase opened the most new branches, expanding into new markets.

title: JPMorgan Latest Lender to Call Staff Back to London Offices
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. has joined other major banks like HSBC and Lloyds in calling staff back to their London offices following the U.K. government's decision to drop work-from-home guidance. This move signals a significant return to in-person work for the City of London's financial sector.

title: Why JPMorgan is spending $12 billion on tech
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. announced a 26% increase in its annual tech budget, pushing technology investments to $12 billion for 2021, up from $9.5 billion in 2020. This spending covers software development, data and analytics, artificial intelligence, and physical infrastructure like data centers, with the goal of securing future growth against competition. CEO Jamie Dimon and CFO Jeremy Barnum emphasized the importance of these investments for maintaining market leadership and delivering strong returns, despite potential impacts on short-term profit expectations.

title: Silknet Will Issue $300 Million Worth of Eurobonds by the End of January
summary: Silknet, a major Georgian communications company, plans to issue $300 million worth of 5-year eurobonds with an 8.375% interest rate by January 31, 2022. The proceeds will be used to repay existing bonds and fund corporate goals. This issuance is considered competitive regionally, with Moody's upgrading Silknet's rating outlook to stable and Fitch likely assigning a "B" credit rating to the new bonds.

title: Goldman Sachs boss David Solomon playing it ‘cool’ with mergers
summary: Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon is reportedly waiting for asset prices of potential merger targets to cool off before making a "transformative" acquisition. Despite Goldman's strong performance in M&A and trading, the firm lacks the broad business model of competitors like JPMorgan and needs to address internal weaknesses through a strategic merger. Potential partners like Charles Schwab, PNC Bank, US Bancorp, and asset managers like T. Rowe Price are considered, but valuation and cultural integration pose significant challenges.

title: OCC approves national bank charter applications of fintech company
summary: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) has conditionally approved applications from Social Finance Inc. (SoFi) to establish SoFi Bank, National Association. This move brings SoFi under federal bank regulatory supervision, subjecting it to comprehensive regulations including the Community Reinvestment Act. The approval requires the new bank not to engage in crypto-asset activities, and SoFi Technologies is seeking to become a bank holding company.

title: Throwing up the white flag? Retail investors dumped stocks at Monday's open, JPMorgan analysis finds
summary: A JPMorgan analysis found that retail investors aggressively dumped stocks at Monday's open, leading to a retail order imbalance of $1.36 billion by noon. This suggests a potential surrender by retail investors in the current market. The analysis was conducted by markets strategist Peng Cheng.

title: Strategas launches first ETFs after institutional clients express interest
summary: Strategas has launched its first exchange-traded funds (ETFs) in response to interest from institutional clients. The article also touches on related financial topics such as hedge fund performance and institutional appetite for diversification, EU-India trade pacts, endowments investing in volatile crypto ETFs, and NYC pension funds' legal actions.

title: Morgan Stanley CEO James Gorman’s Broker Exits Firm Abruptly–Sources
summary: Joshua Gully, a top-ranked Morgan Stanley broker who managed accounts for CEO James Gorman and other senior executives, has unexpectedly left the firm after 30 years. Gully co-led a nine-person team managing $4.8 billion in assets. The firm has stated that other members of Gully's team are now handling the accounts.

title: JPMorgan buys 49% stake in Greek payments company
summary: JPMorgan Chase has acquired a 49% stake in the Greek fintech Viva Wallets as part of its ongoing acquisition strategy. The Athens-based company provides payment solutions to small and medium-sized businesses across 23 European countries. This investment, valued over $1.15 billion, will help Viva Wallets expand its localized payment services throughout Europe.

title: JPMorgan buys 49% stake in Greek fintech Viva Wallet
summary: JPMorgan Chase has acquired a 49% stake in the Greek fintech Viva Wallet, continuing its strategy of investing in banking-adjacent businesses, especially internationally. This investment is part of JPMorgan's aggressive acquisition strategy, particularly as regulations limit its ability to acquire more U.S.-based deposit-taking institutions. Viva Wallet, valued at over $2 billion, provides services to small and medium-sized businesses across 23 European countries.

title: Nuveen Names Saira Malik As Chief Investment Officer
summary: Nuveen has promoted Saira Malik to Chief Investment Officer, a newly created role, where she will drive strategic market and investment insights for the firm's $1.2 trillion assets. Malik will also lead the global investment committee and maintain leadership for Nuveen’s $450 billion global equity business. With 26 years of experience, she will continue as lead portfolio manager for the CREF Stock strategy and a listed portfolio manager for CREF Growth and CREF Global Equities strategies.

title: JPMorgan Chase: Driving Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion
summary: JPMorgan Chase is leveraging its supply chain and a US$30 billion commitment to enhance diversity, equity, and inclusion, particularly for Black, Hispanic, and Latino suppliers. The firm aims to increase spending with diverse businesses, requiring its top suppliers to do the same, and is addressing barriers such as cyber-readiness and access to capital through new programs and partnerships. These initiatives are designed to foster economic inclusion and drive cultural shifts across the business community.

title: BBVA, el banco que impulsa la economía del país
summary: BBVA, originally established as Banco Ganadero Popular in 1956, plays a significant role in Colombia's economic development. The bank has grown to become the fourth-largest in Colombia, focusing on fostering agricultural activity and maintaining a strong presence across the country with numerous branches and ATMs. Globally, BBVA is a major financial group with operations in approximately 30 countries and serves over 53 million clients.

title: JPMorgan Chase: Driving Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion
summary: JPMorgan Chase is actively promoting diversity, equity, and inclusion by focusing on its supply chain and committing to increased spending with Black, Hispanic, and Latino-owned businesses. The firm aims to spend an additional US$750 million with these businesses by 2025 and is partnering with TruSight to enhance the cybersecurity readiness of diverse suppliers. This initiative seeks to break down barriers to opportunity and foster sustainable diversity programs across the business community.

title: Inviu, la fintech de inversiones del Galicia, nombró nuevo CFO y ya piensa en regionalizarse
summary: Inviu, the investment fintech of Grupo Financiero Galicia, has appointed Ignacio Clancy as its new CFO. Clancy, with a strong background in financial services and capital markets, will be responsible for regionalizing the company and mitigating project risks. Inviu aims to expand its operations beyond Argentina, building on Clancy's extensive experience, including his tenure at JP Morgan.

title: JPMorgan Chase: Driving Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion
summary: JPMorgan Chase is leveraging its supply chain to drive diversity, equity, and inclusion, particularly focusing on supporting Black, Hispanic, and Latino suppliers through a US$30bn commitment to close the racial wealth gap. The firm aims to increase diverse supplier spend by US$6bn, with US$1.2bn dedicated to Black, Hispanic, and Latino-owned businesses, and is developing initiatives like a cyber-readiness program with TruSight and a grant program to help diverse businesses meet industry requirements. These efforts demonstrate JPMorgan Chase's commitment to making diversity an integral part of its procurement strategy and fostering inclusive growth within the business community.

title: CAF grants A/B loan for USD 300 million to YPF S.A. to support its climate change adaptation and mitigation strategy
summary: CAF has granted an A/B loan of USD 300 million to YPF S.A. to support its climate change adaptation and mitigation strategy. This loan marks YPF’s return to the international financial market and is one of its first financings focused on emissions reduction and green projects. The transaction, involving several international financial institutions, aligns with CAF's goal of promoting green financing in Latin America.

title: The power of risk taking
summary: Rebecca Minkoff, co-founder of her namesake global company, discusses how taking risks can lead to great things, especially for women entrepreneurs. She emphasizes the importance of embracing discomfort, setting boundaries, and leveraging educational resources, citing her partnership with the Female Founder Collective and JPMorgan Chase's Women On The Move program to empower female business owners. Minkoff also shares insights on adapting her business during the pandemic and her predictions for the future of entrepreneurship, particularly the rise of solo entrepreneurs.

title: Nearly 80 Percent of Financial Firms Use AI to Improve Services, Reduce Fraud
summary: A survey by NVIDIA reveals that 78% of financial services professionals use accelerated computing for AI-enabled applications, driving innovation across the industry. Fraud detection, conversational AI, and algorithmic trading are key use cases, with significant year-over-year growth in AI adoption for various applications. Despite challenges like budget constraints and a shortage of data scientists, executives view AI as critical for future business success, with focuses on hiring AI experts, identifying new use cases, and investing in infrastructure.

title: SAP to Acquire Leading Working Capital Management Company Taulia
summary: SAP SE announced its intent to acquire a majority stake in Taulia, a leading provider of working capital management solutions. This acquisition aims to enhance companies' access to liquidity and improve cash flows by expanding SAP's Business Network and CFO solutions. Taulia will continue to operate as an independent company within the SAP Group, with SAP CFO Luka Mucic becoming Chairman of the Board.

title: TD Bank to add 2,000 technology roles in 2022, expanding workforce by 2%
summary: TD Bank announced plans to hire over 2,000 technology professionals in 2022 to boost its capabilities in engineering, automation, AI, cloud technology, and cybersecurity. This expansion will increase TD's current workforce by approximately 2.2% and comes as other industries are also competing fiercely for technology talent. The move addresses growing demand for online banking services and aligns with the bank's focus on prioritizing projects that drive growth, despite increased expenses.

title: WOTM :sam-sapertein
summary: Sam Saperstein, Head of Women on the Move at JPMorgan Chase, discusses the theme of resilience at the 2021 Women on the Move Leadership Day. She highlights inspiring stories of women who have reinvented themselves in the face of adversity, including a Paralympian and a small business owner who pivoted during the pandemic. The article also showcases JPMorgan Chase's achievements in supporting women, such as exceeding its $10 billion lending goal to women-owned small businesses and implementing programs to support female employees and underserved segments.

title: Fidelity Plots Crypto Industry, Metaverse ETFs
summary: Fidelity Investments has filed proposals with the SEC for two new ETFs: the Fidelity Crypto Industry and Digital Payments ETF, and the Fidelity Metaverse ETF. These filings come shortly after the SEC denied Fidelity's application for a spot bitcoin trust, highlighting the company's continued efforts to expand its offerings in the digital asset space without directly investing in cryptocurrencies for these new ETFs. The proposed ETFs will track indices of companies involved in the crypto industry and those developing metaverse-related products or services.

title: CAF grants A/B loan for USD 300 million to YPF S.A. to support its climate change adaptation and mitigation strategy
summary: CAF has granted an A/B loan of USD 300 million to YPF S.A. to support its climate change adaptation and mitigation strategy. This financing marks YPF's return to the international financial market and aligns with its emissions reduction goals. The loan structure mobilized private capital from Santander, Itau Unibanco, Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited, and Cargill Financial Services International.

title: Disney Names Former J.P. Morgan Analyst Alexia Quadrani As Head Of Investor Relations
summary: The Walt Disney Co. has appointed Alexia Quadrani, a former J.P. Morgan media analyst, as its new head of investor relations. She replaces Lowell Singer and will report directly to CFO Christine McCarthy. Quadrani will be the company's liaison with Wall Street, managing relationships with analysts and investors, and advising senior management on financial matters.

title: What to do if your company stock options are underwater
summary: This article provides advice on managing company stock options when they are "underwater" due to disappointing stock performance, particularly after recent IPOs. Financial experts suggest strategies such as adjusting the stock option exercise strategy, using hedging techniques like collars, and considering tax-loss harvesting. The main goal is to help employees navigate volatility and optimize their equity compensation.

title: loanDepot Announces Closing Of $597M Securitization
summary: loanDepot announced the closing of Mello Mortgage Capital Acceptance 2022-INV1, a $597 million securitization of agency-eligible mortgages originated through its retail and partner channels. This transaction marks over $3 billion in private label residential mortgage-backed securities sponsored by loanDepot entities over the past twelve months. The securitization consists of 1,442 prime mortgage loans made to borrowers with strong credit profiles, demonstrating the company's resilient business model and capital-raising strategy.

title: Citigroup is hiring across Gulf, awaits another record IPO year
summary: Citigroup is expanding its presence in the Gulf region, anticipating that 2022 will surpass 2021 as a record year for activity, including initial public offerings. The bank is adding resources in Saudi Arabia and Dubai to capitalize on the region's booming IPO market and diversifying economies. Amid a wider war for talent in the banking industry, Citigroup believes it can continue to attract skilled professionals due to its strong institution and management.

title: Estos son los bancos que conforman el Grupo Aval
summary: Grupo Aval, the largest financial group in Colombia, formally known as Grupo Acciones y Valores S.A., controls four major banks: Banco de Bogotá, Banco de Occidente Credencial, Banco AV Villas, and Banco Popular. The article highlights that three of these banks—Banco de Bogotá, Banco Popular, and Banco de Occidente—are among the best performing in the Colombian financial system based on various metrics. Grupo Aval serves approximately 10 million clients, generates over 50,000 direct jobs, and operates with around 2,000 offices, nearly 6,000 ATMs, and more than 45,000 banking correspondents.

title: Goldman Sachs leads U.S. banks in return to office
summary: Goldman Sachs led U.S. banks in recalling staff to the office on Tuesday as COVID-19 cases declined, with other major firms like Jefferies, Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, Citigroup, Bank of America, BNP Paribas, and Deutsche Bank following suit. Many banks had previously allowed staff to work from home during the winter Omicron wave. Several banks have implemented specific return-to-office policies, including vaccination requirements at Citi and regular testing at Deutsche Bank.

title: Digital Wallets and Financial Services Disruption
summary: Digital wallets are significantly disrupting traditional financial services, including banking, brokerage, and lending, due to superior user experiences and lower customer acquisition costs. ARK Investment Management predicts substantial growth for digital wallets, projecting their market capitalization to reach $5.7 trillion in the U.S. and $20 trillion globally within five years. Companies like Block (Square) and PayPal, which are major holdings in the ARK Fintech Innovation ETF (ARKF), are leading this disruption by acquiring customers at a fraction of the cost of traditional banks.

title: Future Returns: How Goldman Sachs Approaches Direct Indexing
summary: The article discusses the growing trend of direct indexing in asset management, highlighted by Fidelity's new low-minimum product and previous acquisitions by major firms. It explains how Goldman Sachs, a long-time provider of direct indexing, personalizes portfolios for tax efficiency and individual values, managing $118 billion in this strategy. The piece also delves into the differences between direct indexing and traditional active management, emphasizing its tailored approach to client goals rather than purely seeking market outperformance.

title: Crypto Lending and the Search for Yield
summary: This article explores the landscape of crypto lending, detailing how investors can earn yield by lending digital assets like Bitcoin and stablecoins to various entities. It discusses the primary sources of this yield, including futures-based "cash and carry" trades and arbitrage opportunities, while also analyzing the macro and micro risks involved, such as market volatility and counterparty risk. The author emphasizes the importance of traditional credit analysis in navigating this evolving financial market.

title: Income Is The Outcome
summary: The article discusses the JPMorgan Equity Premium Income Fund, an income-oriented fund that uses equity-linked notes (ELNs) and options premiums to generate substantial income for investors. Despite underperforming market benchmarks in total return, its strategy prioritizes income generation and aims to reduce volatility, allowing investors to stay invested in equities in a more defensive manner. The fund's co-portfolio manager, Hamilton Reiner, explains how the use of ELNs converts options premiums into bona fide income and how market volatility influences the income generated.

title: US and Chinese Banks Dominate the Top 10
summary: The Brand Finance Banking 500 2022 report indicates that the world's top 500 banking brands have seen a 9% year-on-year brand value growth, reaching an all-time high of US$1.38 trillion after three years of contraction. US banks account for five of the top ten most valuable brands, with Bank of America leading in the US. Chinese banks collectively represent one-third of the total brand value, and ICBC remains the world's most valuable banking brand at US$75.1 billion.

title: Top professionals, business people on the move in Palm Beach County
summary: This article highlights key professional movements and appointments across various sectors in Palm Beach County, including finance, arts, healthcare, legal, charity, and hospitality. It details promotions and new hires at organizations like ConnectOne Bank, Homrich Berg, Lighthouse ArtCenter, St. Mary’s Medical Center, Lewis, Longman & Walker, Nonprofits First, and Mizner Country Club. The piece showcases individuals advancing in their careers and contributing to their communities in the region.

title: HDFC Bank Revises Savings Account Interest Rates W.e.f. 2nd February 2022
summary: HDFC Bank has revised its savings account interest rates effective February 2, 2022, offering 3.00% p.a. for balances under Rs 50 lakh, 3.50% p.a. for balances between Rs 50 lakh and Rs 1000 crore, and 4.50% p.a. for balances over Rs 1000 crore. The article compares these new rates with those offered by other major Indian banks like SBI, ICICI Bank, and Axis Bank. Interest rates will be calculated daily and paid quarterly.

title: JPMorgan Chase to open first Birmingham branch this summer
summary: JPMorgan Chase, the largest bank in the U.S. by total assets, announced plans to open its first branch in Birmingham, Alabama, this summer. This move signifies the bank's continued expansion of its presence in the Alabama region. The Birmingham Business Journal reported on this development.

title: Mortgage Stocks are in Free Fall, Losing $36 Billion
summary: Nonbank mortgage stocks have experienced a significant free fall, losing approximately $36 billion in combined market capitalization since mid-2020. This decline is attributed to rising interest rates, reduced refinance volumes, and intensified competition, with analysts anticipating further challenges in 2022. While some large companies like Rocket, United Wholesale Mortgage, and Pennymac are expected to weather the storm due to their scale and efficient operations, smaller players and those with higher cost structures are in a more precarious position.

title: Mujer del día: Ana Botín, presidenta de Banco Santander
summary: Ana Botín, Presidenta de Banco Santander, lideró la entidad a un beneficio atribuido de 8.124 millones de euros en 2021, revirtiendo las pérdidas del año anterior. Santander planea distribuir el 40% del beneficio ordinario de 2022 en dividendos y recompra de acciones, reflejando su compromiso con la retribución al accionista. Botín ha estado al frente de la transformación cultural, comercial y tecnológica del Grupo Santander desde 2014, buscando impulsar la confianza y fidelidad de los clientes.

title: Yelp’s 2021 update on Black-owned Businesses
summary: Yelp's 2021 update highlights continued strong support for Black-owned businesses, with over 45,000 businesses self-identifying as Black-owned on the platform. Consumer searches for these businesses increased by 5%, and mentions in reviews rose by 165% from 2019, indicating a sustained interest in supporting them. Yelp continues its commitment by investing in Black-owned financial institutions and hosting events like the Black in Business Summit.

title: Building a New Sustainability Model for the Food Industry
summary: Maple Leaf Foods, a major protein company, is striving to become the most sustainable in the world by setting science-based targets like reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 30% by 2030 and achieving carbon neutrality. The company is investing in environmentally conscious production facilities, sustainable meat practices, and plant-based proteins, including using an ESG-linked credit facility from J.P. Morgan to support its growth initiatives. Maple Leaf Foods emphasizes a "shared value" framework where business and social decisions are intertwined, aiming to prove that carbon neutrality can be both possible and profitable in the food industry.

title: BlackRock enters the TikTok fray with ‘financial wellness’ account
summary: Asset management giant BlackRock has launched a TikTok account to provide "financial wellness" tips, aiming to engage with a new generation of investors. This move reflects a broader trend among financial firms to connect with younger audiences through platforms popular with Gen Z, leveraging TikTok's extensive user base and demand for finance-related content. BlackRock's initiative aligns with its boss Larry Fink's emphasis on financial inclusion and follows similar efforts by other financial institutions to tap into the youth market.

title: Senators Ask JPMorgan Chase to Explain Its Lawsuit Blitz Against Credit Card Customers
summary: Six Senate Democrats have requested an explanation from JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon regarding the bank's credit card debt collection practices. This inquiry follows ProPublica's reporting that Chase has reignited its controversial "robo-signing" practices in lawsuits against indebted credit card customers. The senators are asking for details on the bank's affidavit quality checks, measures to prevent racial disparities in debt collection, and promises of hardship exemptions during the pandemic.

title: Pinnacle Expands to North Fulton County in Atlanta
summary: Pinnacle Financial Partners is expanding its operations to North Fulton County in Atlanta, establishing a temporary presence and planning a full-service location for summer. The firm has hired a team of banking veterans, led by Scott Jordan as area manager, to serve clients in North Fulton, Gwinnett, and Forsyth Counties. This expansion is part of Pinnacle's broader growth strategy in Atlanta, building on its entry into the market two years prior.

title: American Express to offer debit card that will accrue rewards points
summary: American Express has launched a new checking account with a debit card that allows customers to earn Membership Rewards points, a feature that became rare after the Dodd-Frank Act. This move is significant as most debit cards stopped offering rewards after the Durbin Amendment capped transaction fees for banks. AmEx, operating a "closed system," is exempt from this amendment, enabling them to reintroduce such benefits for existing credit card holders.

title: Empowering change on Black History Month
summary: J.P. Morgan's North America Head of Public Sector Payments, Eva Robinson, discusses the critical role of minority-owned banks, especially during Black History Month, in achieving financial freedom and supporting underserved communities. The article highlights J.P. Morgan's support for Liberty Bank through the Treasury Bank Mentor-Protégé Program and direct equity investment, enabling the bank to grow, provide alternatives to high-interest payday loans, and promote economic development in Black communities. It also emphasizes the importance of providing tools and support to address historical disparities and close the wealth gap.

title: JPMorgan Chase: The Gold Standard in Diverse Spend
summary: This article highlights JPMorgan Chase as a leader in diverse spend practices within the sustainability sector. It mentions key executives involved in their supplier assurance services, indicating the company's commitment to diverse and sustainable supply chains. The article positions JPMorgan Chase as a benchmark for other organizations in this domain.

title: Your Daily Asia Gaming eBrief: Macau CNY visitation registers first growth since pandemic
summary: Macau's Lunar New Year visitation registered its first year-on-year growth since the pandemic, with over 113,000 visitors. While these numbers are below pre-pandemic levels and government forecasts, they represent an improvement compared to 2021 in terms of visitation, hotel occupancy, and spending. The article also provides updates on various gaming companies including Studio City, Nagacorp, Star Entertainment, and GGR forecasts for Macau.

title: Alcon’s Flagship Store Ranks in JD.com’s “Top 100 Stores” of 2021
summary: Alcon, the world's largest eye care device company, was recognized as one of JD.com's "Top 100 Stores" of 2021. This achievement followed 26 consecutive "straight-A" ratings in JD's bi-weekly store management examinations, which assess stores on 28 customer-experience-oriented criteria. Alcon's success on JD.com is attributed to its diverse product offerings, innovative marketing strategies like free trials and collaborations with brands like Pop Mart, and excellent customer service leveraging JD's logistics and rigorous staff training.

title: Chubb Singapore allows no-questions-asked cancellation of travel cover
summary: Chubb Singapore announced a "no-questions-asked" cancellation and refund policy for individual single-trip travel insurance policies issued between December 16, 2021, and March 31, 2022, due to the uncertainties of international travel amidst the COVID-19 pandemic. This initiative aims to reduce stress for consumers planning international trips by allowing them to easily cancel policies if plans change. The eligible policies, including those distributed through partners like American Express and DBS Bank, also cover COVID-19 related expenses such as overseas medical and quarantine costs.

title: PNC Financial Services Group Inc. stock underperforms Wednesday when compared to competitors
summary: PNC Financial Services Group Inc. (PNC) stock fell 0.28% on Wednesday, closing at $210.76, despite a strong overall market performance where the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average rose. The stock underperformed several competitors, including JPMorgan Chase & Co. and Wells Fargo & Co. which saw gains, though it outperformed Fifth Third Bancorp. Trading volume for PNC exceeded its 50-day average.

title: Aptiv Announces Pricing of Senior Notes Offering
summary: Aptiv PLC announced the pricing of a senior notes offering, including $700 million of 2.396% Senior Notes due 2025, $800 million of 3.250% Senior Notes due 2032, and $1 billion of 4.150% Senior Notes due 2052. The proceeds from these notes will primarily fund a portion of the cash consideration for the acquisition of Wind River Systems, Inc., with any remaining funds allocated for general corporate purposes. The offering is expected to close on February 18, 2022, subject to customary conditions.

title: Korean bank profits at record-high as borrowers struggle under debt
summary: South Korea's major banks reported record earnings in 2021 due to higher interest income, even as borrowers face increasing debt burdens. Analysts warn that this strong performance could deteriorate if rising interest rates lead to a surge in bad debt from financially vulnerable households and smaller companies. The central bank's interest rate hikes, aimed at taming inflation and soaring household debt, are making debt repayment harder for retail borrowers.

title: Australia drops landmark cartel case against Citi, Deutsche Bank
summary: Australian prosecutors have dropped a landmark cartel case against Citigroup and Deutsche Bank, along with several former executives, concluding there were no longer reasonable prospects of conviction. The case, which centered on a 2015 share issue worth $1.8bn, would have been the country's biggest white-collar criminal trial and challenged the practices of investment banks in capital raisings. The banks and individuals involved maintained their innocence, stating they acted responsibly and in the interest of clients.

title: A Move to T+1 Settlement: What it Would Mean for Funds and Their Administrators
summary: The financial industry is preparing for a transition to T+1 securities settlement by 2024, aiming to shorten the settlement cycle from the current T+2. This move, supported by organizations like DTCC, SIFMA, and ICI, is expected to reduce market risk and exposure, improve data transparency, and offer investors quicker access to funds. However, it will require significant operational adjustments for fund administrators, prime brokers, and clearinghouses, including compressed timelines for trade affirmations and updates to regulatory frameworks.

title: Deaf, hearing loss or speech impairment
summary: Barclays Private Bank offers extensive accessibility features and support for clients with hearing loss, deafness, or speech impairment. These services include an accessible mobile app and online banking, Relay UK for Textphone users, telephone banking for lip readers, and in-branch accommodations like private meeting rooms and hearing induction loops. The bank also provides BSL interpretation options (video or in-person) and allows clients to confidentially note their specific accessibility requirements for tailored service.

title: Citigroup raises Fraser's pay by 32% after appointing her as CEO
summary: Citigroup increased CEO Jane Fraser's total compensation for 2021 by 31.6% to $22.5 million, citing her efforts to define priorities for boosting long-term shareholder value. This pay raise occurred after she formally took the helm in February 2021. Despite the increase, her compensation is lower than that of more experienced CEOs at rival, more profitable banks, such as JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, and Bank of America.

title: Regulators probe block trading at Wall Street banks, hedge funds- WSJ
summary: Federal investigators are reportedly probing block trading practices at major Wall Street firms, including Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs, and various hedge funds. The investigation, led by the SEC and Department of Justice, centers on whether bankers improperly shared confidential information about large share sales with hedge funds before public disclosure. Regulators are examining trading records and communications, suspecting some funds may have benefited from these early tips.

title: Axis Bank set to buy Citigroup’s $2.5 billion India retail unit
summary: Axis Bank is close to acquiring Citigroup's India retail banking business for approximately $2.5 billion, a deal expected to be announced within weeks, pending Reserve Bank of India approval. The transaction includes a cash component of less than $2 billion, accounting for liabilities, and Axis Bank anticipates a six-month integration period. This acquisition aligns with Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser's strategy to divest retail banking operations in 13 countries and focus on high-growth areas like wealth management, while Axis Bank aims to boost retail loans in India.

title: Axis Bank set to buy Citigroup’s India retail unit
summary: Axis Bank is nearing a deal to acquire Citigroup’s India retail banking business for an estimated $2.5 billion. The agreement, expected to be announced in the coming weeks, is contingent on approval from the Reserve Bank of India and would include a cash component of less than $2 billion after accounting for liabilities. This move is part of Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser's restructuring efforts to exit retail banking in 13 countries and focus on high-growth businesses.

title: WSJ News Exclusive | Regulators Probe Block Trading at Morgan Stanley, Goldman, Other Wall Street Firms
summary: Federal investigators, including the SEC and Justice Department, are probing block trading practices at Wall Street firms like Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs. The investigation focuses on whether bankers improperly tipped off hedge-fund clients about large share sales before public disclosure. Regulators are examining communication records and trading activities to determine if funds benefited from such insider information.

title: UAE Digital Bank Zand Wins Franklin, Aditya Birla Backing
summary: Zand, a digital bank led by Dubai businessman Mohamed Alabbar, has secured investments from prominent firms including Franklin Templeton and Aditya Birla Group. This backing aims to capitalize on emerging opportunities within the fintech sector. Other investors include Abu Dhabi’s Al Hail Holding, Al Sayyah & Sons Investments, Global Development Group, Yusuff Ali of Lulu Group, and Zand co-founder Olivier Crespin.

title: Black Knight Acquires Remaining Interest in Optimal Blue from Thomas H. Lee Partners, L.P. and Cannae Holdings, Inc.
summary: Black Knight, Inc. announced the acquisition of the remaining interests in Optimal Blue Holdco, LLC from co-investors Cannae Holdings, Inc. and Thomas H. Lee Partners, L.P. for a total of $1.156 billion, paid in a combination of Dun & Bradstreet stock and cash. This transaction simplifies Black Knight's organizational structure by making Optimal Blue a wholly-owned subsidiary and is expected to increase 2022 Adjusted EPS by $0.11. Black Knight Chairman and CEO Anthony Jabbour highlighted the strong performance of Optimal Blue and the outstanding returns generated from their initial investment in Dun & Bradstreet.

title: MoneyGram Enters into Agreement to be Acquired by Madison Dearborn Partners
summary: MoneyGram International, Inc. announced a definitive agreement to be acquired by funds affiliated with Madison Dearborn Partners, LLC for $11.00 per share in an all-cash transaction valued at approximately $1.8 billion. This acquisition aims to accelerate MoneyGram's digital growth strategy and strengthen its market-leading cross-border capabilities. The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2022, after which MoneyGram will become a private company.

title: Goldman Sachs Appoints AlphaSense as the Exclusive Distributor of its Aftermarket Research
summary: AlphaSense, a leading market intelligence platform, announced an exclusive partnership with Goldman Sachs to distribute its aftermarket research through the AlphaSense platform. This collaboration will make Goldman Sachs' Global Investment Research (GIR) division's insights available to AlphaSense's broad customer base, including S&P 500 companies and major financial institutions. The integration of Goldman Sachs' research into AlphaSense's Wall Street Insights® (WSI) offering enhances the platform's ability to provide valuable market intelligence and support informed decision-making across various industries.

title: ABG Shipyard Ltd Loan Fraud: LIC Grazed; ICICI, IDBI Worst-hit in Rs 22,842 cr Scam
summary: The Rs 22,842 crore loan fraud by ABG Shipyard Ltd has impacted several banks, with ICICI Bank and IDBI Bank being the worst hit, losing Rs 7,089 crore and Rs 3,639 crore respectively. Even IPO-bound LIC was grazed for Rs 136 crore, although this amount is reportedly secured. Other major lenders defrauded include SBI, Bank of Baroda, EXIM Bank, and Punjab National Bank, indicating widespread financial damage across both public and private sectors.

title: Amazon, Walmart and JPMorgan Chase among companies relaxing employee mask mandates
summary: Several major U.S. companies, including Amazon, Walmart, Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan Chase, HSBC, and Wells Fargo, are relaxing their mask mandates for employees, particularly for fully vaccinated staff, unless local regulations state otherwise. This move follows similar decisions by multiple states to drop indoor mask mandates, citing declining COVID-19 cases and increasing vaccination rates. However, some exceptions remain, such as employees in pharmacies, health clinics, and certain branch offices, who may still be required to wear masks.

title: Bank Of Montreal Commits $78 Million In Financing To Black-Owned Businesses
summary: The Bank of Montreal (BMO) has pledged $78 million in financing for Black-owned businesses through its "Business Within Reach" program. This initiative offers loans up to $196,000 and partners with the Black Opportunity Fund for financial education. BMO's commitment is part of a broader trend among banks to support Black businesses and promote social equity following the Black Lives Matter movement.

title: Databricks extends vertical industry reach with analytics libraries for financial services
summary: Databricks has launched "Lakehouse for Financial Services," a new suite of pre-built analytics tools and open-source libraries aimed at the financial sector. This initiative, which includes partnerships with major financial data providers, seeks to boost innovation in areas like compliance, risk management, and fraud by providing a multi-cloud foundation and addressing limitations of legacy systems. The company is also expanding its Delta Sharing protocol and joining the Fintech Open Source Foundation to support data exchange and standard development.

title: ICICI, IDBI, SBI, LIC hit in Rs 22,842 cr ABG scam State Bank of India had first reported the scam
summary: The article reports on the Rs 22,842 crore loan fraud allegedly committed by Gujarat-based ABG Shipyard Ltd (ABGSL), impacting several major banks and LICI. ICICI Bank suffered the largest loss, followed by IDBI Bank and SBI, which was the first to report the scam. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman noted that the ABG Shipyard account became a Non-Performing Asset (NPA) during the previous UPA regime, and banks detected the fraud faster than average.

title: JPMorgan Chase spent $2 billion on brand new data centers last year
summary: JPMorgan Chase invested $2 billion in new data centers last year, even while actively migrating data and applications to public cloud platforms like AWS, Google, and Microsoft. This investment is part of their broader annual technology spending, which exceeded $12 billion, focusing on cloud capabilities, digital consumer experience, and data analytics. CEO Jamie Dimon emphasized that the new data centers incorporate "cloud capability," and the firm plans to move 30% to 50% of its applications to the cloud this year, driven by the significant value seen in risk management, fraud prevention, and customer satisfaction.

title: XPO Acquires Con-way
summary: XPO, Inc. announced the completion of its acquisition of Con-way Inc., making XPO the second largest less-than-truckload (LTL) provider in North America. This acquisition expands XPO's global logistics, transportation, and freight brokerage businesses. All acquired operations will now operate under the XPO brand, with new financial targets to be issued with the company's third-quarter earnings release on November 4th.

title: Bloomberg Lab opens at Jones Leadership Academy
summary: Jones Leadership Academy of Business in Toledo, Ohio, has opened a new Bloomberg Lab Terminal, featuring a dozen monitoring units connected to the New York Stock Exchange. This initiative provides middle and high school students with hands-on experience in real-world business practices and opportunities to earn banking certifications. Toledo Public Schools partnered with the University of Toledo for this project, making it only the second urban district in the U.S. to receive such an investment.

title: Buyout firm Madison Dearborn to take MoneyGram private in $1.8 billion deal
summary: Private equity firm Madison Dearborn Partners announced it would acquire MoneyGram International Inc for $1.8 billion, taking the debt-laden money transfer platform private. The deal, valued at $11 per share, represents a significant premium to MoneyGram's recent stock prices and aims to revitalize the company amidst stiff competition. Madison Dearborn will also refinance MoneyGram's outstanding debt, with the acquisition expected to close in the fourth quarter of this year.

title: How to restart your career after taking time off
summary: Keita Young, who restarted her career at JPMorgan Chase after an 11-year break to raise her children, shares six tips for others looking to re-enter the workforce. Her advice includes getting involved in outside activities, having a compelling career story, directing one's own path, leveraging a support system, finding a mentor, and not stressing over minor issues.

title: JP Morgan is first bank to enter the metaverse with a virtual 'Onyx lounge'
summary: J.P. Morgan has become the first bank to enter the metaverse by opening a virtual "Onyx lounge" in Decentraland. The bank aims to replicate its real-world services like cross-border payments, trading, and fraud prevention within the virtual economy, which has its own population, GDP, and currencies. J.P. Morgan also plans to support content creators in the metaverse with financial services.

title: HSBC appoints first Independent Board Chairman
summary: HSBC Bank (Singapore) Ltd has appointed Mrs. Penny Goh as its first Independent Board Chairman, succeeding Mr. Mervyn Fong. Mrs. Goh, who joined as an Independent Non-Executive Director in August 2019, previously served as Co-Chairman and Senior Partner of Allen & Gledhill LLP and holds other significant board positions. Her appointment is seen as crucial for HSBC Singapore's strategic growth, particularly in its ambition to double the total wealth balances of its Wealth and Personal Banking business in the next five years.

title: JPMorgan bets the metaverse is a $1 trillion yearly opportunity and opens the first virtual bank
summary: JPMorgan Chase has entered the metaverse by opening a lounge in Decentraland's Metajuku mall, estimating the virtual world market to be a $1 trillion annual opportunity. This move follows the release of a paper by Onyx, the bank's blockchain arm, which highlights the metaverse's potential to infiltrate various sectors. While JPMorgan is the first bank to establish a presence, many other major brands, from retail to entertainment, have already moved into virtual platforms like Decentraland, The Sandbox, and Roblox, viewing it as a growing market for everything from virtual real estate to digital goods and services.

title: JPMorgan Chase, Toshiba and Ciena Build the First Quantum Key Distribution Network Used to Secure Mission-Critical Blockchain Application
summary: JPMorgan Chase, Toshiba, and Ciena have successfully built and demonstrated the first quantum key distribution (QKD) network for metropolitan areas, securing a mission-critical blockchain application. This groundbreaking research proves the viability of QKD to detect and defend against potential quantum computing attacks, supporting 800 Gbps data rates under real-world conditions. The network secured Liink by J.P. Morgan, the world's first bank-led, production-grade, peer-to-peer blockchain network, showcasing the technology's effectiveness against future quantum threats.

title: Carver Federal Savings, unique in New York, survives by investing in underserved communities
summary: Carver Federal Savings, the last Black-operated bank in New York City, is thriving by focusing on underserved communities and small businesses often overlooked by larger banks. Despite facing financial precarity in the past, Carver has seen significant asset growth and capital increases, especially during the pandemic, by prioritizing relationship banking and community reinvestment. The bank's commitment to hyper-local lending and partnerships has helped small businesses flourish in neighborhoods like Harlem.

title: JPMorgan, Toshiba, Ciena find new way to protect blockchain with quantum network
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co, Toshiba Corp, and Ciena Corp have successfully demonstrated a new encryption network using quantum key distribution (QKD) to protect blockchain communications from potential quantum computing attacks. This marks the first time that such a super-secure, quantum physics-powered network has been tested for safeguarding blockchain technology, addressing future threats posed by advanced quantum computers.
