JPMorgan views this as a critical step in preparing banking systems for changes to the security landscape that production-quality quantum computers will bring.

title: Barclays Named Prime Broker of the Year in 2022 Risk Magazine Awards
summary: Barclays has been honored as the Prime Broker of the Year in the 2022 Risk Magazine Awards, recognized for its overall strategy, focus, and significant gains over the last five years. The award highlights Barclays' integrated approach, technology, and selectivity, which have contributed to its success in the prime brokerage market, moving it to the #5 global ranking from joint #9 in 2016. The firm's global prime brokerage services encompass financing for various asset classes, strategic consulting, and capital introductions.

title: JPMorgan sees higher net interest income; return target nears
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co expects its net interest income to increase to $53 billion in 2022, a $3 billion rise from its previous forecast, driven by anticipated interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve and loan growth. The bank's CFO, Jeremy Barnum, stated it is "entirely plausible" to reach a 17% return on tangible common equity by 2023, potentially a year earlier than analyst predictions. Markets revenue for the first quarter is also projected to be better than expected due to increased volatility in fixed-income trading.

title: Morningstar: Active ETFs See Surge in Flows, AUM
summary: Active ETFs experienced a significant surge in investor interest and inflows in 2021, reversing previous trends of outflows for active funds. A Morningstar report highlighted that active ETFs attracted $87 billion in inflows, growing their total assets under management by 44% to $295 billion, despite representing only a small fraction of all active funds and ETFs. Key factors driving this growth included inflation concerns, anticipated Federal Reserve rate hikes, and successful new product launches, with Grayscale Bitcoin Trust (GBTC), JPMorgan Ultra-Short Income ETF (JPST), and ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK) being among the largest active ETFs.

title: Pakistani-American woman appointed CIO of top US firm
summary: Saira Malik, a Pakistani-American, has been appointed as Chief Investment Officer (CIO) of Nuveen, a global asset management firm with $1.2 trillion under management. In her new role, she will lead weekly market and investment insights, client asset allocation views, and chair the Global Investment Committee. Malik has a distinguished career in finance, previously holding senior positions at Nuveen and JP Morgan Asset Management, and is recognized as a top influential woman in US finance.

title: Officials warn of new phishing scam to get bank information
summary: Officials are warning about a new type of phishing scam, known as smishing, where scammers send fake text messages appearing to be from banks like Huntington and PNC to steal banking information. Two local women nearly fell victim to these sophisticated scams. The article advises contacting banks directly to verify suspicious messages and provides resources from the FBI, FCC, Huntington Bank, and PNC on how to identify and protect against such fraudulent attempts.

title: CSB Bank appoints Sharad Kumar Saxena as Additional Director for 3 years term
summary: CSB Bank has appointed Sharad Kumar Saxena as an Additional Director (Non-Executive & Independent) for a three-year term, effective February 19, 2022, pending shareholder approval. Saxena brings over 30 years of IT experience from the Railways and Banking sectors, having held significant leadership roles at ICICI Bank and Bank of Baroda. At the time of the announcement, CSB Bank's shares were trading up by 1.05% on the BSE.

title: Senior J.P. Morgan Bankers Leave Hong Kong
summary: Several senior J.P. Morgan bankers are reportedly leaving Hong Kong due to the city's persistent "dynamic zero-Covid" policy. Ryan Holsheimer, head of cash equity and equity distribution, is returning to Australia, while other bankers are relocating to London or Sydney for similar roles within the firm. This exodus highlights the impact of Hong Kong's strict COVID-19 measures on financial industry professionals.

title: Eli Lilly plans $700M Institute for Genetic Medicine in Boston Seaport
summary: Eli Lilly is investing $700 million to establish an RNA-focused "Institute for Genetic Medicine" in Boston's Seaport district. The institute will occupy 334,000 square feet in a previously intended GE headquarters building at 15 Necco St., with occupancy anticipated in 2024. This facility, alongside a New York City project, aims to develop therapies using RNA and DNA-based technologies to address the root causes of diseases.

title: Waterstone Mortgage Review: Home Purchase Loan Experts Who Strive to Close On Time
summary: This article reviews Waterstone Mortgage, highlighting its unique position as a subsidiary of a large bank with a local feel, offering an expansive range of loan products. It emphasizes their expertise in home purchase loans, especially in competitive markets, and their commitment to timely closings while noting the absence of online rate disclosures as a potential drawback.

title: Breakingviews - Goldman reminds top dogs it can do what it wants
summary: Goldman Sachs is reportedly considering confiscating vested stock from former executives Omer Ismail and David Stark, who left to start a financial business for Walmart. This aggressive move, while potentially legal, is seen as CEO David Solomon's way to dissuade other bankers from leaving, especially since Ismail headed Marcus, a key growth area. The decision highlights Goldman's expanding competition and raises questions about how effective such punitive measures will be in retaining talent amid a talent war.

title: Banking giant asks court to strike out part of AXA’s multimillion-dollar lawsuit
summary: Santander Group has requested a London court to dismiss portions of a £624 million lawsuit filed by AXA concerning mis-sold payment protection insurance (PPI). Santander claims that AXA's argument of a binding settlement agreement is "disingenuous" as no such agreement was finalized or executed, citing email correspondence. AXA, however, argues that the settlement is binding based on the conduct of both parties, despite the lack of signed paperwork, and seeks a trial to resolve the issue.

title: Blackstone Real Estate Launches Affordable Housing Company
summary: Blackstone Real Estate has launched April Housing, a new portfolio company aimed at being a solutions and capital provider for the creation and preservation of high-quality affordable housing across the U.S. This initiative follows Blackstone Real Estate Income Trust's acquisition of a portfolio of over 90,000 affordable housing units. Industry veteran Alice Carr has been appointed CEO of April Housing, and the company plans to invest over $500 million in community improvements while maintaining affordability.

title: Gold prices are popping as Russia invades Ukraine. Why you may want to resist the rush
summary: Gold prices are increasing due to the ongoing conflict between Russia and Ukraine, as investors seek safe havens. However, financial experts advise against a dramatic shift from stocks to gold, noting that while gold offers stability, stocks typically provide greater long-term wealth generation and recover relatively quickly from market corrections. Investors should consider gold only as a small part of their portfolio, rather than a knee-jerk reaction to market volatility.

title: Citigroup to Get Rid of Overdraft Fees, the Biggest Bank to Do So (Published 2022)
summary: Citigroup announced it will eliminate overdraft and returned item fees by summer, becoming the largest bank to do so. This decision follows similar moves by smaller lenders like Capital One and Ally Financial, and comes amidst increasing pressure from regulators who argue these fees disproportionately affect financially vulnerable customers. Other banking giants like Bank of America have cut their overdraft fees, but none have fully eliminated them.

title: JPMorgan Chase Snaps Up $400 Million UBS Team
summary: JPMorgan Chase has hired two financial advisors from UBS who managed over $400 million in assets. This move is part of JPMorgan's strategy to bolster its J.P. Morgan Advisors full-service brokerage by recruiting more talent. The bank is actively increasing its advisor recruiting efforts.

title: Bath & Body Works Appoints Sarah E. Nash As Executive Chair and Interim CEO
summary: Bath & Body Works announced that Andrew Meslow will step down as CEO and board member due to health reasons, effective May 12, 2022. Sarah E. Nash, Chair of the Board, has been appointed Executive Chair immediately and will become Interim CEO upon Meslow's departure. The company plans to conduct a national search for a permanent CEO and announced Q4 2021 financial results in a separate press release.

title: Blackstone Launches April Housing
summary: Blackstone Real Estate Income Trust (BREIT) has formed April Housing, a new portfolio company dedicated to acquiring and preserving affordable housing across the U.S. The new entity will oversee more than 90,000 units and plans to invest over $500 million in property improvements. Alice Carr, formerly of JPMorgan Chase, will lead April Housing as CEO, overseeing Blackstone's commitment to expanding affordable housing solutions.

title: List of Banks and Lenders with SBA Loan Guarantee Agreements
summary: This article provides a comprehensive list of banks and lenders in New Hampshire that offer small business loans under SBA loan guarantee agreements. It details contact information including addresses, phone numbers, and websites for each institution. The list serves as a valuable resource for small businesses seeking financing options in the region.

title: How DBMS is Used by Hulu, JPMorgan Chase, and The Weather Company
summary: This article examines how Database Management Systems (DBMS) are crucial for organizations to efficiently store, retrieve, and manage data. It provides case studies of how major companies like Hulu, JPMorgan Chase, and The Weather Company leverage DBMS to address challenges, optimize operations, and maintain data integrity and security, highlighting the benefits over traditional file systems. The article demonstrates the real-world applications and positive outcomes of integrating DBMS in various industries.

title: U.S. SEC investigating Goldman Sachs over employee communications
summary: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is investigating Goldman Sachs over its employees' use of unapproved communication channels. This probe is part of a broader industry-wide scrutiny into how Wall Street firms track employees' digital communications, especially concerning work-related messages on personal devices during the pandemic era. Goldman Sachs stated it is cooperating with the SEC's investigation.

title: Goldman Probed by SEC Over Messages Sent Using Unapproved Services
summary: Goldman Sachs Group Inc. is being investigated by the SEC for employees' use of unapproved messaging services for business communications. This probe follows similar actions against other major financial institutions, including JPMorgan, which faced $200 million in fines, and HSBC, which is also being investigated by the CFTC for similar issues. Goldman Sachs is cooperating with the SEC and providing requested documents.

title: Announcing JPMorgan Chase & Co.'s Strategic Investment in TRM Labs | TRM Blog
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. has announced a strategic investment in TRM Labs, a company specializing in crypto compliance and risk management technology. This investment highlights the growing significance of the crypto economy and the importance of trust and safety within this ecosystem. TRM Labs provides solutions for financial institutions, cryptocurrency businesses, regulators, and law enforcement agencies to monitor suspicious cryptocurrency transactions and trace illicit funds.

title: Healthcare Realty and Healthcare Trust of America Enter Into $18 Billion Strategic Combination
summary: Healthcare Realty and Healthcare Trust of America announced an $18 billion strategic business combination, creating a preeminent pure-play medical office building REIT. The merger will result in a company with an $11.6 billion equity market capitalization and $17.6 billion total enterprise value, led by Healthcare Realty's management team. HTA shareholders will receive an implied value of $35.08 per share, including a $4.82 special cash dividend, and the combined entity expects significant cost synergies and operational upside.

title: SunTrust Bank Permanently Closed
summary: The SunTrust bank branch at 8700 Georgia Ave. in downtown Silver Spring has permanently closed following the consolidation of operations into Truist after BB&T Bank acquired SunTrust in 2019. This closure is part of Truist's "core conversion" process, which has led to some customer issues, including temporary loss of access to debit cards and bank accounts. These conversions are affecting all former BB&T and SunTrust customers as they transition to Truist products and digital platforms.

title: JLL Capital Markets welcomes Angela Kelcher to head affordable housing debt production team
summary: JLL Capital Markets has appointed Angela Kelcher as Senior Managing Director to lead its affordable housing debt production team. Kelcher brings over two decades of experience in financing affordable housing, making her an industry leader. This strategic hire aims to enhance JLL's capabilities in the affordable housing sector.

title: Secret JPMorgan project aims to push bank deeper into growing market serving private companies
summary: JPMorgan is developing a new fintech business, internally code-named "Project Bloom," to expand its services for start-ups and private companies. This initiative aims to provide a digital network that connects start-ups with investors for fundraising, offers services like share sales and private stake loans, and creates a one-stop digital portal for various financial activities catering to early-stage private firms. The bank is aggressively hiring for this new venture, seeking to establish itself as a dominant player in the private markets before fintech start-ups capture the space.

title: Kennedy Wilson Gets $300M in Preferred Equity
summary: Toronto-based Fairfax Financial Holdings Ltd. has made a $300 million preferred equity investment in Beverly Hills-based Kennedy-Wilson Holdings Inc. This new investment will be used by Kennedy Wilson for its development pipeline, real estate investments, and to pay off unsecured bank borrowings, further expanding their existing partnership which dates back to 2010. Fairfax has also increased its first mortgage target within Kennedy Wilson’s debt investment platform from $2 billion to $5 billion.

title: Wide Moat Stocks Can Get Their Grooves Back
summary: The VanEck Vectors Morningstar Wide Moat ETF (MOAT) has shown durability amid market turbulence in early 2022 and is outperforming the S&P 500. Analysts believe wide moat equities have the ingredients for continued success, with the ETF's valuation methodology identifying stocks trading at attractive multiples despite their inherent quality. MOAT's sector-agnostic approach and diversified holdings, including non-tech stocks, are helping to buffer against current tech sector weaknesses.

title: U.S. SEC investigates Citi over unapproved employee communications
summary: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is investigating Citigroup (C.N) for its employees' use of unapproved communication channels, making it the latest bank to face scrutiny in an industry-wide inquiry. This investigation, which also involves firms like Goldman Sachs, focuses on whether financial institutions are adequately tracking employees' digital communications, especially in the remote work era. The SEC previously fined J.P. Morgan Securities $200 million for similar record-keeping failures related to personal devices and messaging apps.

title: Healthcare Realty Trust, Healthcare Trust of America Agree to Merge, Forming $11.6B Medical Office Building REIT
summary: Healthcare Realty Trust and Healthcare Trust of America have agreed to merge, creating an $11.6 billion medical office building REIT. The combined company will operate under the Healthcare Realty name and will be the largest "pure-play" MOB REIT in the country, with 727 properties totaling 44 million square feet. The deal, valued at $7.75 billion for HTA, is expected to close in the third quarter of 2022 and aims to generate significant synergies and strengthen the combined entity's market position.

title: Japan’s largest bank winds down blockchain payments system over slow growth
summary: Japan's largest financial institution, Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG), has suspended its blockchain payments system, GO-NET Japan, after three years due to slow growth and limited client adoption. Despite initial hopes for its high transaction processing capacity and potential in the IoT market, the platform failed to achieve profitability in a reasonable timeframe, partly due to the COVID-19 pandemic's impact. MUFG, however, remains committed to exploring other digital payment solutions, including its Progmat blockchain platform and the MUFG Coin.

title: Who Owns Progressive Insurance, the Third-Largest Insurance Carrier in the U.S.?
summary: This article details the ownership of Progressive Insurance, identifying its largest shareholders as The Vanguard Group and BlackRock Inc. It also covers the company's history, starting with its founding in 1937, and highlights the career and compensation of current CEO Tricia Griffith.

title: McEwen Mining closes flow-through financing
summary: McEwen Mining Inc. successfully closed a marketed brokered private placement offering on March 2, 2022, raising C$19,212,500 through the sale of 14,500,000 flow-through common shares. Cantor Fitzgerald Canada Corporation acted as the sole bookrunner and agent for the offering. The proceeds are designated for Canadian Exploration Expenditures on McEwen's properties in the Timmins region.

title: U.S. lawmakers demand HSBC explain actions against Hong Kong activists, Americans
summary: U.S. lawmakers are demanding that HSBC explain why it froze the accounts of pro-democracy activists in Hong Kong and restricted accounts of American citizens. A bipartisan group of senators and representatives from the Congressional-Executive Commission on China sent a letter to HSBC's CEO, Noel Quinn, raising concerns about these actions, which could leave the bank liable to U.S. sanctions. HSBC stated it must operate within the legal frameworks of all countries where it has operations.

title: BlackRock suspends purchases of Russian securities in active and index-linked funds
summary: BlackRock Inc. has suspended purchases of all Russian securities in its active and index funds following Russia's invasion of Ukraine, effective Monday. The world's largest asset manager is also advocating for the removal of Russian securities from broad-based indices and consulting with regulators to help clients exit positions where allowed. Russian securities represent a minimal portion of their clients' assets, less than 0.01%.

title: Retirement Industry People Moves
summary: PGIM has appointed Michael Miller as the head of its new Defined Contribution Solutions business, focusing on innovative retirement solutions for maturing DC plans. OneAmerica hired Heather Dawson to lead its Participant Workplace Solutions team, aiming to deliver holistic financial wellness programs to participants. Transamerica expanded its pooled retirement plan capabilities by acquiring TAG Resources, LLC, a company specializing in plan administration for multiple employer plans, to better serve small- and mid-size employers.

title: News | Blackstone Is Still Driving Hotel Portfolio Deals as Investors Mull Inflation, War
summary: Blackstone recently completed $3 billion in hotel portfolio transactions, selling its stake in CorePoint Lodging for $1.5 billion and buying an extended-stay hotel portfolio for $1.5 billion with Starwood Capital. These deals highlight a swift recovery in the hotel sector, driven by abundant capital and the inflation-hedging nature of hotel assets. Investors are closely monitoring inflation and geopolitical events, but the market shows signs of continued robust activity.

title: SERNAC lanza primer comparador de tarjetas de crédito
summary: SERNAC has launched the first-ever Credit Card Comparator in Chile, a tool designed to help consumers compare all associated charges of credit cards available in the market. This tool aggregates information from 194 cards, highlighting significant differences in maintenance fees, cash advance charges, and foreign transaction fees. The initiative aims to empower consumers to make more informed financial decisions, prevent over-indebtedness, and encourage competitive practices among financial institutions.

title: International Arbitration After the Pandemic
summary: The article discusses the resurgence of international arbitration after the COVID-19 pandemic, driven by growth in cross-border trade and investment. It highlights the rapid expansion of international disputes and the rebalancing of dispute resolution activity towards Asian centers. The publication also anticipates new disputes from COVID-19 disruptions, energy transition, and financial distress, while noting reforms in Investor State Dispute Settlement.

title: Driving Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion
summary: JPMorgan Chase is actively promoting diversity, equity, and inclusion by increasing its spend with diverse businesses, particularly Black, Hispanic, and Latino-owned companies, with a commitment of an additional US$6 billion. The firm is also helping these suppliers overcome barriers like cybersecurity readiness through programs with TruSight and providing financial assistance via grants. This initiative aims to foster sustainable diversity programs and drive inclusive growth within the business community.

title: Benchmarking treasury for the energy industry
summary: J.P. Morgan's Head of Global Energy Industry Coverage, Tristan Attenborough, discusses the crucial role of treasury benchmarking in the rapidly evolving energy sector. The article highlights how unprecedented changes, such as the energy transition and macroeconomic variables, require a dynamic approach to treasury strategy, moving beyond traditional long-term implementation plans. It emphasizes the need for agility, technological advancements, and collaborative banking relationships to navigate these challenges and support corporate evolution.

title: SIRIANNI: Morgan Stanley’s Moment
summary: Tony Sirianni discusses Morgan Stanley's revamped recruiting strategy and unique position in the wealth management industry. He highlights Morgan Stanley's success in attracting advisors, contrasting its approach with Merrill Lynch and other wirehouses, particularly its focus on a strong, advisor-centric culture. The article suggests Morgan Stanley has carved out a distinct identity as a large full-service firm, appealing to veteran wire advisors who might be dissatisfied with bank-owned platforms.

title: The Gold Standard in Diverse Spend
summary: JPMorgan Chase is committed to supporting diverse suppliers, dedicating approximately $2 billion annually and aiming for an additional $750 million increase with Black, Hispanic, and Latino businesses as part of its $30 billion racial wealth gap commitment. The firm leverages its Gold Supplier program to promote best practices throughout its supply chain, encouraging key suppliers to increase diverse spending, mentoring those with emerging diversity programs, and enhancing the discoverability of diverse suppliers. This strategy aims to create more inclusive supply chains, foster economic growth, and drive significant financial impact within diverse communities.

title: Stacking up bank CEO pay in Canada vs. the US
summary: Canadian bank CEOs received larger average raises in 2021 (28.2%) compared to their U.S. counterparts (20.9%), but American CEOs still earn significantly more overall, averaging $31.8 million compared to Canada's $10.2 million. This pay disparity existed even before the recent raises, with individual U.S. bank leaders like Morgan Stanley's James Gorman and JPMorgan Chase's Jamie Dimon earning considerably higher compensation. Key Canadian bank CEOs like RBC's Dave McKay and TD's Bharat Masrani also saw substantial pay increases, tied to strong bank performance and strategic deals.

title: Rivian is sued for allegedly misleading investors about electric vehicle prices
summary: Rivian Automotive Inc is facing a class-action lawsuit from a shareholder who claims the company misled investors by initially underpricing its electric vehicles, leading to unpopular price hikes that were later rolled back. The lawsuit alleges Rivian concealed that its R1S SUV and R1T pickup trucks were so underpriced they would require rapid price increases after its November IPO, damaging the company's reputation and risking pre-order cancellations. The plaintiff, Charles Larry Crews, cites the swift rollback of price increases and an apology from CEO R.J. Scaringe as "futile attempts at damage control."

title: JPMorgan Chase Appoints Michael Woodfield as Market Executive for Middle Market Banking in Southern Nevada
summary: JPMorgan Chase Commercial Banking announced the appointment of Michael Woodfield as Market Executive of Middle Market Banking & Specialized Industries in southern Nevada. With 17 years of experience, Woodfield will focus on serving the financial needs of middle market companies in the region, leveraging JPMorgan Chase's global capabilities. This appointment aims to strengthen the bank's commitment to businesses in southern Nevada.

title: Russia risks "imminent" default on its debt, Wall Street analysts say
summary: Russia is facing an "imminent" default on its debt due to groaning under Western sanctions, according to credit ratings agencies and Wall Street firms. Fitch downgraded Russia's debt for the second time in a week, citing the high likelihood of default and the impact of sanctions on its ability and willingness to repay. With $700 million in payments due in March and a 30-day grace period, a default could occur as early as mid-April, further isolating Russia from international financial flows.

title: Tetra Tech Appoints Prashant Gandhi as New Board Member
summary: Tetra Tech Inc., a Pasadena-based consulting and engineering company, has appointed Prashant Gandhi to its Board of Directors, effective May 1. Mr. Gandhi brings over 20 years of experience in digital systems, data analytics, and digital transformation from his roles at McKinsey and Co., JP Morgan Chase, and Melio Payments. He will serve on the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee and the Compensation Committee, contributing his expertise to Tetra Tech's strategic focus on expanding its Delta technologies.

title: Goldman Sachs becomes the first major Wall Street bank to end operations in Russia
summary: Goldman Sachs announced it will wind down its operations in Russia, becoming the first major Wall Street bank to exit the country following the invasion of Ukraine. While exiting, the firm will continue to act as a market-maker for Russian securities to help clients reduce risk, not to speculate, and has been moving some Moscow-based staff to Dubai. Other financial institutions like Citigroup and several European banks are also assessing or halting some operations in Russia due to the conflict and sanctions.

title: Goldman Sachs becomes first Wall St. firm to exit Russia
summary: Goldman Sachs has become the first Wall Street firm to suspend its operations in Russia following the country's invasion of Ukraine, winding down its business in compliance with regulatory requirements. JPMorgan Chase is also actively unwinding its Russian business, while other financial giants like Citigroup, Credit Suisse, and BlackRock have disclosed their exposure and are taking steps to limit their involvement. Several financial service companies, including Visa, Mastercard, American Express, and PayPal, have also suspended operations in Russia.

title: Wall Street banks Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase are pulling out of Russia
summary: Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase are withdrawing from Russia in response to the invasion of Ukraine, making them the first major Wall Street firms to do so. Other financial companies like Western Union and Citigroup are also scaling back or suspending operations in the country. These moves align with global directives and a broader corporate exodus from Russia.

title: JPMorgan says labor shortage requires unconventional hiring, including people with criminal records
summary: JPMorgan Chase is addressing the global labor shortage by adopting unconventional hiring practices, including employing individuals with criminal records and neurodiverse candidates. The bank has hired thousands with criminal backgrounds and hundreds with autism, eliminating questions about criminal history from initial job applications. Brian Lamb, JPMorgan's global head of diversity, equity and inclusion, emphasized the need for such approaches during CNBC's Equity and Opportunity forum.

title: SAP Completes Acquisition of Taulia
summary: SAP has announced the completion of its acquisition of a majority stake in Taulia, a provider of working capital management solutions. This strategic move aims to enhance financial flexibility and stability for companies and strengthen supply chain resilience. Taulia will operate as an independent company within the SAP Group, with its solutions integrated into SAP software while also remaining available standalone.

title: JPMorgan is winding down its Russia operations amid widening business exodus over Ukraine war
summary: JPMorgan Chase is winding down its operations in Russia, following directives from governments globally and amid a broader business exodus due to the Ukraine war. The bank's remaining dealings in Russia are limited to helping global clients manage existing obligations, risks, and taking care of employees, with fewer than 200 staff primarily in the corporate and investment bank. This move by JPMorgan comes shortly after Goldman Sachs also announced its exit from the country.

title: JP Morgan AM to merge global emerging market index fund with ESG ETF
summary: JP Morgan Asset Management (JPMAM) is merging its $47m Global Emerging Markets Research Enhanced Index Equity fund with the $686m JP Morgan Global Emerging Markets Research Enhanced Index Equity ESG UCITS ETF (JREM), effective May 20. This merger aims to benefit shareholders by combining into a larger ETF with lower total expenses, reducing ongoing charges from 0.40% to 0.30% for investors. JREM is an actively managed ESG ETF that seeks to outperform the MSCI Emerging Market index and is classified as Article 8 under SFDR.

title: JPMorgan joins Goldman Sachs in pulling back from Russia
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. and Goldman Sachs Group Inc. are pulling back from Russia in response to the country’s invasion of Ukraine, joining other major companies in halting business operations. JPMorgan specifies its activities are limited to helping clients and managing risk, while Goldman Sachs plans to close operations and has minimal exposure to Russia. This move further isolates Russia economically as other financial and consumer companies also restrict their presence.

title: Commodity ETFs Could Be Overbought After 'Extreme Herding'
summary: Retail investors "herding" into commodity ETFs, as seen by significant inflows, could indicate an overbought market and potential short-term underperformance, according to JPMorgan strategists. This behavior aligns with historical academic data suggesting heightened volatility and subsequent reversals after extreme investor rushes. An ETF analyst also notes that retail investors often enter these markets after much of the performance has already occurred.

title: Stanley Black & Decker shutting down Russian business
summary: Stanley Black & Decker announced it is shutting down its business operations in Russia. The toolmaker, with a significant presence in Greater Baltimore, stated it stands in solidarity with the people of Ukraine. This decision follows similar actions by other major companies in response to the conflict.

title: BlackRock funds take $17 billion loss on Russia exposure, Western banks owed $121 billion
summary: BlackRock funds have incurred a $17 billion loss due to their exposure to Russian assets since the invasion of Ukraine. This loss is part of a larger financial impact on Western banks, which are owed an estimated $121 billion by Russian entities. Many financial institutions, including major U.S. and European banks, are now working to divest from Russian businesses amidst sanctions and regulatory challenges.

title: KWEB Aims to Fully Transition to Hong Kong Shares In Coming Months
summary: The KraneShares CSI China Internet ETF (KWEB) is transitioning its holdings to Hong Kong-listed counterparts to address delisting risks for Chinese American Depository Receipts (ADRs) under the Holding Foreign Companies Accountable Act (HFCAA). KraneShares expects KWEB's portfolio to be solely comprised of Hong Kong listings by the end of the year, providing daily updates on its conversion progress. This strategy aims to protect client interests amidst unresolved regulatory issues between US and Chinese authorities regarding audit paper access.

title: Citigroup expands Russia withdrawal, raising prospect of losses
summary: Citigroup announced it is accelerating its withdrawal from Russia, ceasing new client acquisitions and further reducing its exposure in the country. This decision follows similar moves by other major Wall Street banks like JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs, due to Russia's invasion of Ukraine. With nearly $10 billion in Russian exposure, analysts predict Citigroup could face substantial losses, potentially impacting its share buyback plans, with one analyst forecasting $1.5 billion in charges for Q1.

title: Four ways companies can find the ‘hidden talent’
summary: Many companies struggle to find talent despite a large pool of "hidden workers." This article outlines four strategies for companies to tap into this underserved talent pool. These strategies include implementing "returnships," upskilling current employees, directly collaborating with educational institutions, and removing college degree requirements from job descriptions.

title: Wells Fargo CEO Scharf's 2021 compensation up by 20% at $24.5 mln
summary: Wells Fargo & Co CEO Charles Scharf's total compensation for 2021 increased by nearly 20% to $24.5 million, as disclosed in a regulatory filing. This rise follows a recovery year for the bank, with its shares jumping almost 59% in 2021, and compares to compensation packages of other major Wall Street bank CEOs like JPMorgan Chase & Co's Jamie Dimon and Citigroup Inc's Jane Fraser.

title: Focus: U.S. banks will keep a toe in Russia despite wind-downs
summary: Major U.S. banks, including Citigroup, JPMorgan Chase, and Goldman Sachs, are planning to retain their banking licenses and a limited presence in Russia despite winding down broader operations following the invasion of Ukraine. This strategy allows them to fulfill existing contractual obligations, assist multinational clients, and potentially rebuild business in the future, should geopolitical conditions improve, without needing to re-apply for difficult-to-obtain licenses. The banks face a lengthy withdrawal process, and a complete exit would hinder their ability to return to the Russian market.

title: Wall Street-backed MEMX to launch options exchange
summary: MEMX, a U.S. stock exchange backed by major Wall Street firms, announced plans to launch an options exchange in the fourth quarter, pending regulatory approval. This move aims to reduce industry costs by leveraging technological advancements and competitive pricing, similar to its approach with its stock exchange launched in 2020. The company has gained significant market share by offering lower fees for market data compared to larger incumbent exchanges.

title: JPMorgan to buy Irish fintech firm Global Shares
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co announced its intention to acquire Global Shares, an Irish fintech company specializing in managing employee stock plans. The undisclosed deal is expected to close in the second half of the year, with Global Shares, which manages nearly $200 billion in assets, integrating into JPMorgan's asset and wealth management business while retaining its headquarters in Cork, Ireland.

title: Inside Volatility Trading: Sometimes, Smaller is Better
summary: This article discusses the Cboe's introduction of "Nanos," a smaller, more affordable index option product designed to make options trading more accessible to a wider range of investors. It highlights the historical trend towards shorter-dated maturities and smaller contract sizes in options trading, emphasizing how Nanos can cater to individual traders with smaller portfolios and lower risk tolerances. The author also touches on the concept of "VIX Backwardation" and how starting small is beneficial for learning and adapting in volatile markets.

title: J.P. Morgan agrees to acquire Global Shares, a leading provider of share plan management software
summary: J.P. Morgan announced an agreement to acquire Global Shares, a cloud-based provider of share plan management software, to bolster its services for corporate clients and expand wealth management client acquisition. The acquisition, which is subject to regulatory approvals and expected to close in the second half of 2022, will integrate Global Shares into J.P. Morgan's Asset & Wealth Management business. Global Shares will retain its headquarters in Cork, Ireland, and continue its growth trajectory with J.P. Morgan's support.

title: Webroot sues CrowdStrike, Sophos, others over alleged patent infringement
summary: Webroot and its parent company OpenText are suing Trend Micro, Sophos, Kaspersky, and CrowdStrike for alleged infringement of several malware detection patents, some dating back to 2005. The lawsuits, filed in the Western District of Texas, claim these defendants infringe upon Webroot's intellectual property related to endpoint security products and platforms. Competitors and observers criticized the move, with CrowdStrike calling it typical of a "patent troll" and others viewing it as "patent bullying."

title: Morgan Health joins $23M series B round for Embold Health
summary: Morgan Health, JPMorgan Chase's healthcare arm, invested $5 million in Embold Health's $23 million Series B funding round. Embold Health is a physician-led data analytics company focused on improving healthcare quality and cost. This investment aligns with Morgan Health's mission to enhance employer healthcare by partnering with innovative organizations and making strategic investments in promising health solutions.

title: Metals Acquisition clinches $1.1 billion deal for Glencore’s CSA copper mine
summary: Metals Acquisition Corp has secured a $1.1 billion deal to acquire Glencore's CSA copper mine in Australia, outbidding competitors like IGO Ltd. The acquisition provides access to a high-grade copper mine expected to produce 41,000 to 49,000 tonnes of copper annually, capitalizing on strong demand fueled by electric vehicle production. For Glencore, this sale contributes to its business streamlining efforts, with analysts noting the attractive price received for the asset.

title: BNY Mellon expects $100-mln revenue hit in first quarter from Russia pullback
summary: BNY Mellon anticipates a $100 million revenue impact in the first quarter and an annual reduction of $80 million to $100 million due to pausing new banking business in Russia. This move follows Russia's invasion of Ukraine and aligns with other companies pulling out of the country. The bank has also halted buying Russian securities under its investment management business.

title: Citigroup will pay travel costs for employee abortions in response to the Texas law.
summary: Citigroup announced it will cover travel expenses for employees needing to leave Texas to get abortions, making it the first major U.S. bank to officially respond to the state's restrictive abortion law. The policy change comes after Texas implemented a law banning abortions after six weeks of pregnancy and empowering private citizens to sue those who assist in the procedure. Other companies like Bumble, Salesforce, Lyft, Uber, and Match Group have also implemented policies or funds to support employees affected by similar legislation.

title: Metals Acquisition clinches $1.1 bln deal for Glencore's CSA copper mine
summary: Metals Acquisition Corp has acquired Glencore's CSA copper mine in Australia for $1.1 billion, winning a years-long race for the asset. The deal allows Glencore to continue streamlining its portfolio and provides Metals Acquisition access to a high-grade copper mine, a critical commodity for electric vehicle production and the global energy transition. Metals Acquisition will fund the deal through IPO proceeds and debt, with Glencore receiving both cash and shares.

title: 70% of medical collection debt will soon be removed from credit reports—and it could boost your credit score
summary: The three major credit reporting agencies will remove 70% of medical collection debt from consumer credit reports starting July 2022. This change includes removing paid medical debt, increasing the reporting delay from six months to a year, and eventually removing unpaid medical debt under $500. This initiative aims to improve credit scores for many Americans, as medical debt has been found to be less indicative of future payment problems compared to other forms of debt.

title: ISO 20022: Transformation on the horizon
summary: J.P. Morgan is guiding financial institutions through the migration to the ISO 20022 messaging standard, which is set to become the universal language for cross-border payments by November 2025. The standard promises greater efficiency, enhanced data integration, improved automation for compliance, and the removal of friction points in the global payments industry. J.P. Morgan emphasizes collaboration and transparency in its implementation strategy to help clients prepare for these significant changes.

title: Lloyds share price: to break the 100p resistance barrier?
summary: The Lloyds Banking Group share price has struggled since the 2008 financial crisis, remaining a "penny stock" below the 100p resistance level. However, recent strong full-year results and rising UK interest rates, particularly from the Bank of England, could help the bank break this psychological barrier. While increasing rates pose some risks of mortgage defaults, historically, Lloyds' share price has closely tracked UK interest rates, suggesting a potential recovery closer to pre-crisis norms.

title: Credit reporting agencies Equifax, Experian and TransUnion will wipe out most medical debt
summary: Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion announced they will remove nearly 70% of medical debt from consumer credit reports, amounting to billions of dollars. This change, effective July 1, means paid medical collection debt will no longer appear on reports, and starting in 2023, medical debt under $500 will also be excluded. The move addresses the significant impact of often unpredictable medical debt, which disproportionately affects certain consumer groups.

title: After Bridgewater was defrauded out of nearly $500K, it took Scotiabank to court
summary: The Town of Bridgewater, N.S., was defrauded of almost $500,000 by an Ontario man posing as a construction executive. The town had to pursue legal action against Scotiabank to recover the funds after experiencing frustration with both Scotiabank and BMO's handling of the situation. Despite the financial loss, the mayor emphasized that the town has since implemented stronger internal controls to prevent future incidents of fraud.

title: Does Your Portfolio Need Private Equity?
summary: This article explores whether private equity is a suitable investment for individual investors, highlighting its potential for higher returns but also its complexities and high barriers to entry. It discusses various aspects of private equity, including how its returns are measured, the wide dispersion of returns, and alternative options for gaining exposure to this asset class for different investor profiles. Ultimately, it concludes that while private equity offers potential benefits, its risks and high costs make it generally unsuitable for most individual investors.

title: Lanvin Group, a Global Luxury Fashion Group, to Become Publicly Traded on the NYSE via Business Combination with Primavera Capital Acquisition Corporation
summary: Lanvin Group, a global luxury fashion group, announced its plan to become publicly traded on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) through a business combination with Primavera Capital Acquisition Corporation (PCAC). The transaction values Lanvin Group at a pro forma enterprise value of US$1.5 billion, with up to US$544 million in proceeds expected to accelerate organic growth and fund future acquisitions. This move aims to leverage Primavera's networks and financial strength to expand Lanvin Group's brand portfolio across Europe, North America, and Asia, focusing on key luxury markets.

title: Book Qatar Airways with Avios: Why Its Great
summary: Qatar Airways' adoption of Avios as its mileage currency significantly enhances redemption options for travelers. This change allows greater flexibility in earning and transferring Avios between multiple airlines, including British Airways, Iberia, and Aer Lingus, and opens up more transfer point options from major transferable points programs like American Express and Chase. Travelers can now optimize redemptions between different Avios programs, potentially securing better rates for flights.

title: Alfonso Guzman
summary: Alfonso Guzman of JPMorgan Chase & Co. has been honored with the Diversity in Business Award by the Washington Business Journal. His journey to becoming a top regional executive at JPMorgan Chase was challenging, and he now focuses on giving back. The award recognizes his achievements and commitment to diversity.

title: Southwest’s new fare type is here. What to know about ‘Wanna Get Away Plus’
summary: Southwest Airlines has introduced a new fare class called "Wanna Get Away Plus," offering additional perks beyond its base "Wanna Get Away" fare. This new fare allows flight credits to be transferred to other Rapid Rewards members and includes confirmed same-day flight changes or same-day standby options. It's designed to appeal to both leisure travelers seeking flexibility and business travelers, contributing to Southwest's target of a $1.5 billion revenue boost by 2023.

title: Lloyds Bank to close 60 more branches across UK
summary: Lloyds Banking Group announced the closure of 60 branches across the UK, including Lloyds Bank, Bank of Scotland, and Halifax locations, due to a shift towards online banking. While 124 staff members are affected, the company will attempt to find them new roles. The Unite union criticized the closures, stating they are devastating for local communities.

title: Deal Diary: Wachtell Takes Tegna From Spin to Sale
summary: Tegna Inc.'s $8.6 billion sale to Standard General LP and Apollo Global Management Inc. marks another deal where Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz served as regular counsel to the former Gannett Co. unit. Wachtell Lipton, along with JPMorgan Chase & Co. and Greenhill & Co., advised Tegna on the recent sale, building on their prior work with Tegna, including its 2015 spin-off from Gannett. Standard General was advised by Fried Frank Harris Shriver & Jacobson LLP, Moelis & Co. LLC, and RBC Capital Markets.

title: SoftBank preps Arm IPO, seeking a $60B valuation
summary: SoftBank is preparing for an Initial Public Offering (IPO) of Arm Ltd., aiming for a $60 billion valuation, following the collapse of its proposed sale to Nvidia Corp. The valuation is considered ambitious but potentially realistic due to Nvidia's appreciating stock price since the original acquisition agreement. Analysts suggest the success of the IPO at this valuation could indicate investor confidence in Arm's own growth potential beyond a merger.

title: Bank of America Corp. stock rises Friday, outperforms market
summary: Shares of Bank of America Corp. (BAC) increased by 1.53% to $43.73 on Friday, outperforming the broader market which also saw gains in the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average. This rise ended a two-day losing streak for the company's stock. Despite the positive movement, Bank of America Corp. closed below its 52-week high, and its performance relative to competitors like JPMorgan Chase & Co., Citigroup Inc., and Wells Fargo & Co. was mixed.

title: Wells Fargo & Co. stock outperforms market on strong trading day
summary: Wells Fargo & Co. (WFC) stock rose 2.40% to $52.56, outperforming the broader market with the S&P 500 Index gaining 0.51% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average rising 0.44%. The stock also outperformed its competitors like JPMorgan Chase & Co., Bank of America Corp., and Citigroup Inc. This marks the second consecutive day of gains for Wells Fargo.

title: 2022 Best & Brightest Business Major: Jack Budde, Michigan State (Broad)
summary: This article features Jack Budde, a Finance major from Michigan State University (Broad), as one of the 2022 Best & Brightest Business Majors. It details his academic achievements, extracurricular involvement, internships, and future career plans at Barclays Investment Banking. The piece also includes his reflections on business education, advice for students, and acknowledgements of mentors.

title: KKR, GIP Close $15B Acquisition of CyrusOne
summary: KKR and Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP) have finalized their $15 billion acquisition of data center REIT CyrusOne. The deal, which includes the assumption of existing debt, resulted in CyrusOne's common shares being delisted from Nasdaq and its Senior Notes from the SEC. This acquisition highlights the continued strong investor interest in the data center sector, following other major deals in the previous year.

title: Edward Jones rep managing $135 million goes indie with Raymond James
summary: Samuel Martin, a financial advisor managing $135 million at Edward Jones, has left the firm to establish his own independent practice, SJ Martin Wealth Management, in Beaufort, South Carolina. His new firm is affiliated with Raymond James. Martin, who spent eight years at Edward Jones, is a certified financial planner.

title: Barclays' bankers could have 2021 bonuses clawed back
summary: Barclays faces a potential £450 million loss due to mistakenly overselling securities in an exchange-traded structured note (VXX), leading to an internal investigation. This error could result in the clawback of 2021 bonuses for certain bankers, particularly material risk-takers whose bonuses had previously increased. The incident, deemed "bizarre" and "embarrassing" by analysts, highlights control failures within the bank.

title: Techstars and J.P. Morgan Partner to Invest in Diverse Entrepreneurs
summary: Techstars and J.P. Morgan have partnered to invest over $80 million in diverse entrepreneurs through a new accelerator program, aiming to address disparities in venture capital funding. This multi-year initiative will support more than 400 companies through 37 programs in 9 U.S. cities, focusing on Black, Hispanic and Latino, Indigenous American, and Pacific Islander founders. The program seeks to provide equitable access to capital, mentorship, and customized programming to foster wealth creation and economic opportunity in underserved communities.

title: Barclays ETN snafu could cost it £450 million
summary: Barclays is facing a £450 million after-tax loss due to a blunder in its exchange-traded notes (ETN) business, where it exceeded its US shelf registration for securities issuance. This error has led to the temporary suspension of new ETN issuances, causing significant market disruption and a potential reputational hit for the bank and its CEO, CS "Venkat" Venkatakrishnan. Regulators are now investigating the incident.

title: Verðmetur Alvotech á 540 milljarða skömmu fyrir skráningu á markað
summary: Icelandic biotechnology company Alvotech, founded in 2013, is valued at approximately $4.3 billion (ISK 540 billion) according to a new valuation, which is 90% higher than its previous valuation. The company is preparing for a dual listing on the US and Icelandic stock markets through a merger with SPAC Oaktree Acquisition Corp. II. Alvotech expects to generate over $1 billion in revenue from biosimilar sales after 2025, primarily driven by its biosimilar to Humira, for which it recently reached a settlement with Abbvie, allowing for market entry in the US by mid-next year.

title: Canada’s big five banks increased support for fossil fuels by 70% in 2021
summary: A report reveals that Canada's five largest banks significantly increased their financing of fossil fuels by 70% in 2021, totaling USD 54 billion, despite their net-zero pledges. This increase, particularly in tar sands funding, places Canadian banks among the top global fossil fuel funders and makes them responsible for the largest rise in financed emissions worldwide. Environmental groups and activists criticize these actions, highlighting the contradiction with climate goals and the associated social and environmental risks.

title: BlackRock president warns ’entitled generation’ to ‘put their seatbelts on’ over speeding inflation
summary: BlackRock President Rob Kapito warned that a "very entitled" generation will soon face shortages for the first time due to rising inflation. He described this as "scarcity inflation" affecting various goods and services, urging people to prepare. This comes as inflation hits 40-year highs in the U.S. and accelerates globally, exacerbated by the war in Ukraine and supply chain issues.

title: Inverse, Double VIX ETFs Return
summary: The US ETF market has reintroduced inverse and double VIX funds, four years after the "Volmageddon" event. The new funds, Inverse VIX Futures ETF (SVIX) and 2x Long VIX Futures ETF (UVIX) from Volatility Shares, launched on Cboe Global Markets with specific fee structures and targeted VIX futures exposure. This marks a return to daily short VIX trading after previous products, like Credit Suisse’s inverse VIX note, faced severe losses in 2018.

title: Jugada de Luis Carlos Sarmiento para blindar sus negocios por las elecciones en Colombia
summary: Luis Carlos Sarmiento Angulo, owner of Grupo Aval, has initiated a strategy to reorganize his financial holdings, specifically separating Banco de Bogotá and Grupo Aval from Leasing Bogotá S.A. Panamá, leading to the creation of BAC Holding Internacional. This move involves Rendifin, a Sarmiento-controlled company, attempting to acquire 15% of BAC Holding Internacional through a public acquisition offer. The primary motivation for this restructuring is reportedly the electoral uncertainty in Colombia and the implementation of Bitcoin in El Salvador, aiming to safeguard his businesses in both nations.

title: Charlie Munger warns Gen Z investors: It's 'way harder' for recent college graduates 'to get rich and stay rich'
summary: Billionaire Charlie Munger believes it has become significantly more challenging for young people, particularly recent college graduates, to accumulate and maintain wealth compared to previous generations. He cites the drastically increased cost of living, especially housing, as a primary hurdle. Munger suggests that traditional investment advice might not be as effective now due to the complexity of the market, advocating for either diversified portfolios like the S&P 500 or personalized investment guidance.

title: Dakota Gold Corp. Announces Merger Closing as Part of a Specific Focus on Revitalizing the Homestake District in Lead, South Dakota
summary: Dakota Gold Corp. announced the completion of its merger between Dakota Territory Resource Corp. and JR Resources Corp., focusing on revitalizing the Homestake District in Lead, South Dakota. The company's common stock is expected to begin trading on the NYSE American under the symbol "DC" on or about April 5, 2022, following a significant expansion of its land package and establishment of an ESG fund. This strategic move aims to leverage the Homestake District's 145-year gold mining legacy for new discoveries and opportunities.

title: Amazon renews Prime credit card tie-up with JPMorgan Chase after flirting with American Express
summary: Amazon has renewed its agreement with JPMorgan Chase to issue its flagship Prime rewards credit card, following months of intense negotiations where other financial institutions like American Express and Synchrony also vied for the lucrative partnership. The deal maintains the card's rich 5% rewards rate for Amazon.com and Whole Foods purchases and highlights the significant value these co-brand credit card partnerships hold for issuing banks. This renewal continues a long-standing relationship between Amazon and JPMorgan, dating back to 2002.

title: Jamie Dimon, U.S. Bank and BMO show value is a buyer-led construct
summary: The article discusses how the perceived "value" of executives and acquired companies is largely determined by the buyer, not an intrinsic worth. It highlights Jamie Dimon's substantial compensation package from JPMorgan Chase, which significantly exceeded initial estimates due to stock performance and board decisions, alongside contrasting M&A deals where similar asset sizes yielded vastly different acquisition prices. The piece concludes by noting that value can also depreciate or be withheld, citing examples of executive compensation disputes at Barclays and Goldman Sachs.

title: Former HPE campus in northwest Houston has new owner
summary: JLL Capital Markets has successfully closed the sale of the former Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) campus in northwest Houston to an affiliate of Mexcor International. The nearly two million-square-foot multi-building office/warehouse campus was sold by HPE, which has relocated its corporate campus. The property, built between 1984 and 1988, is situated on a 66-acre site and offers a variety of amenities and connectivity to major Houston roadways.

title: Morgan Stanley spins off $15 billion RIA business
summary: Morgan Stanley is selling its $15 billion registered investment advisory (RIA) business, Eaton Vance WaterOak Advisors, which it acquired last year as part of its Eaton Vance acquisition, to CI Financial and Pathstone. This move signals Morgan Stanley's continued intention to exit the RIA space and focus on core verticals, following a previous sale of ETrade's RIA custody business. The sale involved dividing the assets between two buyers, highlighting a creative approach to acquisitions in the growing RIA sector.

title: J M Baxi Allcargo Lift and Shift
summary: J M Baxi Heavy Pvt. Ltd. has signed a definitive agreement with Allcargo Logistics to acquire its Project Forwarding and Logistics business for INR 98.64 crore. Concurrently, J M Baxi Heavy also made a binding offer, which was accepted, to acquire Lift and Shift India Pvt. Ltd.'s heavy and over-dimension cargo logistics business. These strategic acquisitions aim to integrate the businesses into J M Baxi Heavy Pvt. Ltd., enhancing its capabilities in heavy cargo logistics and expanding its reach across the Indian and African sub-continents.

title: As Wall Street banks embrace crypto, high-flying start-ups look to lure top finance talent
summary: Major Wall Street banks like JPMorgan Chase, Morgan Stanley, and Goldman Sachs are actively building out cryptocurrency and blockchain teams. Despite this, high-flying crypto start-ups are luring top finance talent away from these traditional institutions by offering faster-paced environments, equity, and less bureaucracy, with former executives citing the generational opportunity in Web3 as a key motivator. These start-ups are also looking beyond traditional MBA candidates, seeking self-taught engineers and crypto influencers.

title: Frisco’s Complexity Gaming, Backed by Jerry Jones and John Goff, Partners With Lenovo
summary: Frisco-based Complexity Gaming, co-owned by Jerry Jones and John Goff, has signed a multi-year partnership with Lenovo, renaming its headquarters the Lenovo Legion Esports Center. This collaboration, driven by GameSquare Esports CEO Justin Kenna, aims to expand Complexity's content creation and educational initiatives, especially in DEI. The article also notes Dallas-based cybersecurity firm Zimperium's acquisition for $525M and Sun Holdings gaining control of 90 Papa John's locations.

title: Fidelity Investments strikes right back at Schwab with retail direct indexing that offers two apparent advantages -- it shaves $95,000 off the minimum and already is accepting assets
summary: Fidelity Investments is directly challenging Schwab in the retail direct indexing market. Fidelity's new offering has a significantly lower minimum investment, requiring $95,000 less than Schwab's, and is already accepting assets. This move positions Fidelity to gain a competitive edge in attracting individual investors to direct indexing solutions.

title: The Fed Is on the March. Can Your Bond Fund Keep Up?
summary: This article discusses the impact of the Federal Reserve's aggressive interest rate hikes on bond investors and how they can protect their portfolios. It highlights that while rising rates can lead to bond price declines, they also result in significantly higher future yields for investors. The piece notes the bond market's recent poor performance and the shift in investor flows from bond funds as yields become more attractive.

title: Growth Headwinds - List Gets Longer
summary: This article discusses the growing list of growth headwinds facing emerging markets, including the resurgence of COVID-19 in China, the Russia/Ukraine war's impact on commodity prices and supply chains, and aggressive policy tightening leading to interest rate hikes. It highlights how these factors are leading to growth downgrades in various regions, and how some commodity exporters might benefit from the current market disruptions.

title: China Growth – Withering Greenshoots?
summary: The article discusses the weakening economic activity gauges in China, primarily due to the Omicron outbreak and mobility restrictions, leading to calls for more proactive policy support. It questions the downside risks to China's 2022 growth outlook, the global impact of China's lockdowns on supply chains and inflation, and the extent of additional policy support expected from the central bank. The author suggests that "blanket" measures, like cuts in reserve requirements and policy rates, remain a possibility if growth forecasts drop below 5%.

title: J.P. Morgan Asset Management Hires Ash Williams as Vice Chair
summary: J.P. Morgan Asset Management has appointed Ash Williams, the former Chief Investment Officer and Executive Director of the Florida State Board of Administration (SBA), as Vice Chair, Asset Management. In this part-time role, Mr. Williams will provide extensive experience in institutional investing, offering thought leadership and investment insights to clients and internal teams. He will continue to be based in Tallahassee, Florida, and report to Keith Cahill, Head of North America Institutional.

title: Arkansas Eyes Upon Texas Lending
summary: Arkansas banks are increasingly expanding their operations into Texas, drawn by its larger banking market and growth opportunities. Major players like Home BancShares (Centennial Bank), Simmons First National Corp., and Bank OZK have made significant acquisitions and branch expansions. Other banks like Farmers Bank & Trust, Encore Bank, Bodcaw Bank, and Diamond Bank are also establishing a presence, utilizing both acquisitions and new branch development.

title: Jamie Dimon’s 2021 Letter to Shareholders
summary: Jamie Dimon's 2021 letter to shareholders addresses the significant global challenges of a pandemic, the war in Ukraine, and inflation, while also highlighting JPMorgan Chase's record revenue and strong financial performance in 2021. Dimon emphasizes the company's commitment to clients, employees, and communities, and discusses key themes such as American competitiveness, energy security, and the evolving competitive landscape for banks. The letter underscores the importance of strong leadership, continuous investment, and maintaining a robust balance sheet for sustained success.

title: HDFC Bank creates Indian lending behemoth in $40 billion deal
summary: HDFC Bank is acquiring its largest shareholder, HDFC Ltd, in a $40 billion deal to create India's biggest financial services entity. This merger will expand HDFC Bank's customer base and home loan portfolio, aiming to better compete with rivals and tap into rising credit demand. The combined company will boast a balance sheet of $237 billion and a market value of approximately $160 billion.

title: Citi Hires Four More for Health-Care Banking in Push for Growth
summary: Citigroup Inc. has hired four new health-care investment bankers, signaling a commitment to expanding its market share in the sector. These appointments were announced in an internal memo by Chuck Adams, the global head of the health-care, consumer, and wellness investment banking group. This move demonstrates Citi's strategic focus on the health-care industry as a key growth area.

title: Block by block, building a cleared FX marketplace for asset managers and hedge funds
summary: This article discusses the growing interest from asset managers and hedge funds in using blocks and EFRPs (Exchange for Related Positions) in CME Group's cleared FX products. It highlights the benefits for end-users, such as liquidity, operational, and margin efficiencies, driven by regulatory changes like uncleared margin rules (UMRs) and SA-CCR. The piece also explains how these "ex-pit" trading mechanisms allow clients to leverage OTC liquidity while still benefiting from central clearing.

title: iRhythm builds case for wearable cardiac monitor with data in fainting, TAVR patients
summary: iRhythm Technologies presented new data at the American College of Cardiology's 71st Annual Scientific Session & Expo, strengthening the clinical case for its Zio wearable cardiac monitoring devices. Studies showcased the Zio AT device's ability to reduce hospital stays for fainting patients and identify arrhythmias more effectively, while the Zio XT device was used for atrial fibrillation screening in older, low-risk patients. Analysts believe these presentations will lead to increased adoption and market expansion for iRhythm's technology, particularly in the underpenetrated asymptomatic monitoring market.

title: Liberty Global Decision Invalidates Section 245A Temporary Regulations
summary: A US District Court invalidated temporary regulations related to Section 245A of the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, ruling that the Treasury Department failed to comply with the Administrative Procedure Act's notice-and-comment requirements. The court found that Treasury's "good cause" justification for bypassing these procedures was insufficient. This decision could significantly impact the Treasury's ability to issue immediately effective temporary regulations and makes past and future temporary regulations vulnerable to similar challenges.

title: How Walmart thwarted $4 million in elder gift card scams
summary: Walmart developed technology that helped it identify and freeze nearly $4 million in gift cards that thousands of primarily elderly victims purchased under the direction of con artists. The U.S. Department of Justice seized these funds through a federal court action, making them available for victims to claim. Despite this success, federal authorities note that the recovered amount is a small fraction of the millions lost annually to imposter scams involving gift card purchases.

title: Banking & Finance Roundup: Seacoast to acquire Miami’s Apollo Bank
summary: This article covers the banking and finance news roundup for the week, highlighting Seacoast's acquisition of Apollo Bank in Miami. It also lists other related articles about regional banking news, including Pitcairn hiring a local executive and Amerant Bank joining a blockchain network.

title: These income strategies can help protect your stock investments from inflation and a recession
summary: This article discusses two income strategies for protecting stock investments from inflation and recession. These strategies include selecting stocks of companies with rapidly increasing dividend payouts and augmenting dividend income with covered call options. The author suggests these methods offer downside protection while retaining upside potential in a changing economic environment.

title: BAC Holding International corp inscribió más de 43.220 millones de acciones en la BVC
summary: BAC Holding International (BHI) has registered over 43.22 billion shares on the Colombian Stock Exchange (BVC) following its separation from Banco de Bogotá and Grupo Aval. This move came alongside a tender offer (OPA) by Luis Carlos Sarmiento for up to 15% of BHI's shares at $293 each. The market is awaiting authorization from the Superfinanciera for the OPA, which aims to reduce volatility from currency exchange rates for Grupo Aval and Banco de Bogotá.

title: 10 tendencias del consumo en 2022
summary: This article outlines 10 global consumer trends for 2022, based on a Euromonitor International study. These trends highlight consumers' intentional and conscious decisions, driven by a desire for control and a reflection of their values. The trends range from seeking alternative products due to supply chain issues to prioritizing sustainability, digital solutions for seniors, financial independence, work-life balance, and evolving social interactions in both physical and virtual spaces.

title: JPMorgan allows clients to cancel depositary receipts in Russian companies- sources
summary: JPMorgan has started allowing clients to cancel depositary receipts in Russian companies, providing investors a way to liquidate holdings that were largely frozen after trading was halted and sanctions were imposed following Russia's invasion of Ukraine. This move follows BNY Mellon and comes as Russia considers forcing companies with depositary receipts traded abroad to return to the domestic market.

title: Dave & Buster’s Announces Acquisition of Main Event for $835 Million; Chris Morris to become CEO of Combined Entity Upon Closing
summary: Dave & Buster's Entertainment, Inc. announced its acquisition of Main Event from Ardent Leisure Group Limited and RedBird Capital Partners for $835 million. Chris Morris, the current CEO of Main Event, will become CEO of the combined entity upon closing. This acquisition aims to expand Dave & Buster's demographic reach by targeting families with younger children while also creating significant growth opportunities for both brands.

title: These 7 finance companies have the highest-paid interns on Wall Street and beyond
summary: Glassdoor's 2022 roundup of highest-paying internships reveals that finance companies offer significant compensation, competing with tech giants. Capital One leads the finance sector with $8,333 median monthly pay, ranking third overall. The article highlights other top-paying finance firms like Deutsche Bank, Susquehanna International Group, BlackRock, J.P. Morgan, Citi, and American Express, emphasizing the financial benefits for interns and the companies alike.

title: Johnson & Johnson faces another ballot battle on racial justice audit
summary: Johnson & Johnson is once again facing a shareholder proposal for an independent racial justice audit at its upcoming annual meeting. This proposal, brought by Mercy Investment Services, cites past controversies and political donations, while J&J's board argues that its existing DEI initiatives and racial equity platform make such an audit redundant and resource-diverting. A similar proposal in 2021 saw significant shareholder support, including from BlackRock.

title: Dave & Buster’s To Acquire Main Event for $835 Million
summary: Dave & Buster's Entertainment, Inc. announced its agreement to acquire Main Event for $835 million in an all-cash transaction. Chris Morris, current CEO of Main Event, will become CEO of Dave & Buster’s post-acquisition. This acquisition aims to expand Dave & Buster's demographic reach to include families with younger children, complement existing locations, and generate approximately $20 million in synergies within two years.

title: Fed bans ex-Goldman banker over document leak, 6 others in EIDL fraud
summary: The Federal Reserve banned a former Goldman Sachs managing director, Joseph Jiampietro, from the banking industry for unauthorized use and disclosure of central bank secrets back to 2014. Additionally, the Fed also banned six other former bank employees from Regions Bank and Merrill Lynch Wealth Management for submitting fraudulent applications for Economic Injury Disaster Loan (EIDL) assistance and using the funds for personal expenses. These actions are part of a broader effort by the U.S. government's COVID-19 Fraud Enforcement Task Force to combat fraud.

title: Ryman Hospitality Properties, Inc. Announces Strategic Investment in Opry Entertainment Group by Atairos and NBCUniversal
summary: Ryman Hospitality Properties (RHP) announced that Atairos, an investment company, and NBCUniversal will acquire a 30% minority stake in RHP's subsidiary Opry Entertainment Group (OEG) at a valuation of $1.415 billion. This investment aims to support OEG's growth into an integrated country lifestyle platform, allowing RHP to retain a controlling 70% interest while reducing its leverage and increasing balance sheet flexibility. The partnership is expected to strengthen OEG's iconic brands and expand its influence in country music culture and live entertainment.

title: JPMorgan Chase backs $100M Tech Equity Miami initiative
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. has announced its support for the $100 million Tech Equity Miami initiative, aimed at fostering technological equity opportunities in Miami. This move by the financial services giant highlights a significant investment in the city's tech scene.

title: Michael O’Higgins FX Class Representative Ltd and Mr Phillip Evans v Barclays Bank PLC and others
summary: The Competition Appeal Tribunal (CAT) refused to certify opt-out collective proceedings against several global banks for alleged follow-on competition damages related to foreign exchange trading. The CAT cited concerns about the strength of the proposed claims and the practicability of opt-in proceedings. While neither opt-out application was certified, the CAT indicated it would have granted carriage to Mr Evans had the dispute been relevant for an opt-out claim.

title: Canada’s selfie generations lead the way in financial self-assessments
summary: A BMO Investment Survey reveals that younger Canadians, particularly Gen Z and Millennials, are more engaged in consistently assessing their financial goals than older generations. While these groups are actively tracking their finances and seeking professional advice from recommendations, a significant portion also relies on financial influencers and social media for investing decisions. The survey also highlights that many young Canadians hold predominantly cash savings due to a lack of investment knowledge, yet a good number are contributing to TFSAs for early financial independence.

title: Morgan Stanley aims to serve the richest of the rich as family offices grow to $5.5 trillion in assets
summary: Morgan Stanley has launched a new unit dedicated to serving family offices, which are investment entities for the world's richest individuals and families. The bank is targeting this rapidly growing segment, which has expanded to over $5.5 trillion in assets globally, by offering tailored technology solutions and aims to reach $10 trillion in client assets. This move positions Morgan Stanley to cater to both newly wealthy individuals and established ultra-high net worth clients, differentiating itself through institutional-quality services and a matchmaking platform for private investments.

title: Dow gains, S&P 500 ends lower as market weighs Fed rate hikes
summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite fell on Friday as investors grappled with aggressive Federal Reserve interest rate hikes aimed at tackling inflation. Bank shares, which had significantly declined, saw gains as the 10-year Treasury yield reached a three-year high. Value stocks continued to outperform growth stocks as the market anticipates a potential recession or a "soft landing" engineered by the Fed.

title: Shuffle Board: C-Suite Moves at Nordstrom, Burlington, JD, Zappos, American Textile
summary: This article details significant C-suite personnel changes across several major retail and textile companies, including Nordstrom, Burlington Stores, JD.com, Zappos.com, and American Textile Company. Key appointments and retirements are highlighted, along with new roles aimed at strategic growth, customer experience, and sustainability within these organizations. The changes reflect ongoing efforts by these companies to adapt to market demands and streamline operations.

title: White & Case Advises J.P. Morgan and Evercore on Piedmont Lithium Inc.’s US$130.8 Million Public Offering of Common Stock
summary: White & Case LLP advised J.P. Morgan and Evercore, along with other underwriters, on Piedmont Lithium Inc.'s public offering of common stock. The offering generated gross proceeds of US$130.8 million from the sale of 2.01 million shares, including an over-allotment option. Piedmont Lithium, a dual-listed company, is focused on developing an integrated lithium business to support the clean energy economy in North America.

title: Keurig Dr Pepper announces strategic refinancing, offering
summary: Keurig Dr Pepper (NASDAQ: KDP) announced a strategic refinancing initiative, including a public offering of senior notes and concurrent tender offers, to strengthen its balance sheet and improve liquidity. The proceeds will primarily be used to fund the tender offers and redeem outstanding senior unsecured notes, or for general corporate purposes if the offers are not consummated. This move follows the company's successful deleveraging over the past three years.

title: S&P Global Places Russia in ‘Selective Default’ (Published 2022)
summary: S&P Global has downgraded Russia to "selective default" after Russia attempted to pay a $650 million dollar-denominated debt in rubles, a currency not agreed upon by bond terms. The ratings agency believes sanctions will prevent Russia from converting the ruble payments to dollars within the 30-day grace period, pushing it towards its first foreign currency sovereign debt default in over a century.
