The U.S. Treasury's recent tightening of restrictions on Russian transactions contributed to Russia's inability to use dollars held in American banks for the payment.

title: S&P Global Market Intelligence Global Bank Rankings: European Banks Slid Down Rankings as They Scaled Back Operations in the U.S. amid Competition - Apr 11, 2022
summary: European banks experienced a decline in global asset size rankings in 2021 due to scaled-back operations in the U.S. and slower economic growth in their home markets, with their total assets contracting by 2.16%. In contrast, Chinese banks maintained their top positions with expanded balance sheets, driven by government initiatives to boost lending. Major U.S. banks also saw their asset sizes grow, pushing them higher in the rankings, though future growth may slow due to the absence of government stimulus and the Federal Reserve's efforts to combat inflation.

title: Omaha retail center with Trader Joe’s anchor sells for $34 million
summary: JLL Capital Markets announced the $34 million sale of One Pacific Place in Omaha, Nebraska, a 90,945-square-foot retail center anchored by a Trader Joe's. The property was acquired by Lund Company Investments, Inc. from a joint venture between RED Development and BIG Shopping Centers. The center serves a wide demographic due to housing the only Trader Joe's within a 55-mile radius and includes a diverse mix of tenants.

title: Citigroup Hires Feldkamp, Feige for North America ECM Business
summary: Citigroup Inc. has hired Geoff Feldkamp and Brian Feige as managing directors for its North America equity capital markets business. Feldkamp, formerly of Barclays, will co-lead the real estate and financial ECM business, while Feige, from JPMorgan Chase & Co., will co-lead the industrials ECM business. These hires signal an expansion in Citigroup's ECM division.

title: Morgan Stanley Claws Back $3.1 Million From Ex-Broker in NYC
summary: A FINRA arbitration panel has ordered former Morgan Stanley broker Nicolas P. Lumermann to pay the firm over $3.1 million in a promissory note dispute, denying his claim of constructive discharge. Lumermann, who transitioned to online gaming after leaving the firm, was held liable for the unpaid balance plus interest. The panel did not provide a reason for its decision but denied Morgan Stanley's request for legal fees.

title: VALLEY BANK AND LPGA COGNIZANT FOUNDERS CUP ANNOUNCE THREE-YEAR BRAND AMBASSADOR SPONSORSHIP STARTING WITH THE 2022 TOURNAMENT AT UPPER MONTCLAIR COUNTRY CLUB IN CLIFTON FROM MAY 11-15
summary: Valley Bank has announced a three-year partnership with the LPGA Cognizant Founders Cup as the Brand Ambassador Sponsor, beginning with the 2022 tournament at Upper Montclair Country Club in Clifton, NJ. This sponsorship aims to engage golf fans and local residents to assist with tournament operations and supports the LPGA's mission to empower women through golf. In addition to the Brand Ambassador Program, Valley Bank will also sponsor the Mentor Monday program, connecting students with business leaders in the golf industry.

title: Thoma Bravo to acquire SailPoint for overall $6.9 Billion
summary: Thoma Bravo has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire SailPoint Technologies Holdings, Inc. in an all-cash transaction valued at approximately $6.9 billion. SailPoint stockholders will receive $65.25 per share, representing a 48% premium to its 90-day volume-weighted average price. The acquisition will take SailPoint private, allowing it to leverage Thoma Bravo's resources and expertise to accelerate growth and innovation in the identity security market.

title: Sun Communities Acquires Park Holidays UK
summary: Sun Communities (NYSE: SUI) has completed its previously announced acquisition of Park Holidays UK, acquiring 40 owned and two managed communities for approximately £950 million ($1.3 billion). This acquisition marks a significant expansion for Sun Communities into the highly fragmented UK market, strengthening its presence with a business model complementary to its existing operations. Both companies expressed excitement about leveraging Sun's strategies and Park Holidays' expertise to enhance holiday park experiences and scale opportunities in the UK.

title: JPMorgan Results Marred by $524 Million Loss Tied to Russia
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. reported a $524 million loss in its first-quarter results, attributed to the market fallout from Russia's invasion of Ukraine. This loss was primarily driven by funding spread widening and valuation adjustments for commodities and Russia-linked derivatives, including about $120 million from extreme nickel price movements. Despite this, fixed-income trading revenue exceeded estimates by $1 billion, though CEO Jamie Dimon anticipates significant challenges from inflation and the ongoing war.

title: SPY Stock: Earnings and Key Support Are in Play for SPY ETF
summary: The article discusses the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY) amidst bearish macro drivers, focusing on the upcoming earnings season and key technical support levels. It highlights how investor sentiment is influenced by corporate health reports from SPY constituents like JPMorgan Chase & Co and Delta Airlines, alongside technical indicators such as the 50% Fibonacci retracement and the Chicago Board Options Exchange Volatility Index, to assess potential market bottoms.

title: AmEx takes on banks in bid for new generation of clients
summary: American Express is expanding its services beyond credit cards for affluent individuals by launching all-digital checking accounts and debit cards for small businesses and consumers. This move aims to attract younger generations who prefer debit and to deepen relationships with existing cardholders, as AmEx seeks to compete with traditional banks and fintechs. The company is leveraging its bank holding company status and offering attractive perks like a high annual percentage yield and rewards on debit purchases to gain market share in the digital banking space.

title: Grupo Ergas disuelve su participación en Banco de Chile: vendió acciones por US$96 millones
summary: Grupo Ergas, previously the second-largest shareholder in Banco de Chile, has fully divested its stake by selling 0.93% of the property for approximately US$96 million. This follows an earlier sale in November 2021 where they sold over 198 million shares for US$20 million. The group, controlled by Jacob Ergas and his sons, is also a significant real estate investor in Santiago Centro and created Movicenter.

title: DoubleLine and Barclays Team Up to Market & Distribute ETFs
summary: DoubleLine and Barclays have announced a strategic partnership to market and distribute exchange-traded funds under DoubleLine ETF Adviser LP. This collaboration follows DoubleLine's recent launch of its first ETFs, the DoubleLine Opportunistic Bond ETF (DBND) and the DoubleLine Shiller CAPE U.S. Equities ETF (DCPE). The partnership aims to combine their expertise to further develop the ETF landscape and offer new products to investors.

title: JPMorgan Chase Unveils Plans for New Global Headquarters Building in New York City
summary: JPMorgan Chase has unveiled the design for its new 1,388-foot, 60-story global headquarters at 270 Park Avenue in New York City, designed by Foster + Partners. This will be the city's largest all-electric tower with net-zero operational emissions, emphasizing sustainability, health, and wellness. The skyscraper will accommodate up to 14,000 employees and feature extensive public green spaces, state-of-the-art technology, and flexible office layouts, aiming to set new standards for the modern workplace.

title: Jamie Dimon sees ‘storm clouds’ ahead for U.S. economy later this year
summary: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon believes "storm clouds" are on the horizon for the U.S. economy later this year, citing the risk of the Federal Reserve accidentally triggering a recession while combatting inflation. He noted that while economic growth is expected through Q2 and Q3, inflation and quantitative tightening are significant countervailing factors. Dimon highlighted the bank's decision to increase loan loss reserves as a sign of rising recession probabilities, a stark change from his "Goldilocks moment" prediction a year prior.

title: JPMorgan Chase Unveils Plans for New Global Headquarters Building in New York City
summary: JPMorgan Chase has unveiled the design for its new global headquarters at 270 Park Avenue in New York City. The 60-story skyscraper will be the city's largest all-electric tower with net zero operational emissions, housing up to 14,000 employees. This project is expected to create 8,000 construction jobs and contribute significantly to New York City's economy, while also setting new standards for sustainability and employee wellness in a modern workplace.

title: Leading growth investors acquire minority stake in Coda Payments, the world's leading independent content monetization platform
summary: A consortium of top-tier growth investors, including Smash Capital, Insight Partners, and Singapore's sovereign-wealth fund GIC, has acquired a minority stake in Coda Payments. This US$690 million investment will support Coda Payments, the world's leading independent platform for digital content monetization, during a period of rapid international expansion. Coda Payments operates Codashop and Codapay, enabling content publishers to offer diverse payment methods to millions of consumers globally.

title: JPMorgan Chase plans 60-story NYC tower as new 'all-electric' HQ
summary: JPMorgan Chase announced plans to build a 60-story "all-electric" global headquarters in New York City, which will be powered 100% by renewable hydroelectric energy. The new 1,388-foot tower will replace an older building, housing 14,000 employees and offering expanded outdoor space. This project is expected to create 8,000 construction jobs and contribute significantly to New York City's economy, while also incorporating advanced sustainable and health-focused design elements.

title: Lineage Logistics expands in Canada with VersaCold acquisition
summary: Lineage Logistics LLC, a Novi-based cold storage and logistics company, has announced the acquisition of Canadian firm VersaCold Logistics Services. This strategic move significantly expands Lineage's presence in the North American market, adding 24 temperature-controlled warehouses and 114 million cubic feet of storage space across Canada. The acquisition is expected to close in the third quarter of the year, with financial terms remaining undisclosed.

title: Wells Fargo, JPMorgan and the mortgage storm to come
summary: Wells Fargo and JPMorgan Chase experienced significant declines in their mortgage origination volumes and net earnings in the first quarter of 2022 due to higher interest rates and reduced refinancing activity. While servicing portfolios partially offset these losses, both banks anticipate continued pressure on originations and margins. Executives noted "storm clouds on the horizon" regarding future market volatility, despite some existing customer financial strengths.

title: JPMorgan’s New Manhattan Headquarters to Be All Electric Powered - WSJ
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co.'s new 1,388-foot Manhattan headquarters will be an all-electric skyscraper powered by a hydroelectric source, making it New York's tallest and largest all-electric building. The office tower will operate with net-zero emissions. JPMorgan plans to consolidate its New York offices in this Norman Foster-designed building after its completion around 2025.

title: Wells Fargo commits $210M to racial equity in wake of criticism
summary: Wells Fargo has pledged $210 million to advance racial equity in homeownership following criticism over its low approval rates for Black refinancing applicants. Of this, $150 million will be used to lower rates and costs for Black homeowners seeking to refinance through a new Special Purpose Credit Program. The bank aims to address systemic inequities and will report its progress annually.

title: Fidelity Investments Launches Crypto, Metaverse ETFs — Says 'We Continue to See Demand'
summary: Fidelity Investments has launched two new exchange-traded funds (ETFs) focused on the crypto and metaverse sectors. The company stated that it continues to observe strong demand for digital asset exposure and innovative technologies like the metaverse. This move by Fidelity allows investors to gain exposure to these emerging markets through traditional investment vehicles.

title: “Whatever It Takes” – Whatever That Means
summary: This article discusses the divergent monetary policy approaches of major economies, particularly China's easing against a global tightening trend. It highlights continued hawkish stances in other emerging markets like Korea and Argentina due to high inflation, while noting Turkey's policy limbo despite soaring inflation. The piece underscores the varying interpretations and applications of the "whatever it takes" philosophy in current global economic conditions.

title: Veterans in Business Do What They Love | JPMorgan Chase
summary: This article features interviews with veterans who have successfully transitioned from military service to entrepreneurship, highlighting the unique skills and mission-focused ethos they bring to business. It emphasizes the importance of mentorship, networking, and pursuing one's passion in the post-military career path. The article encourages former servicemembers to leverage their experiences and seek support to achieve their entrepreneurial dreams.

title: Charles Schwab (SCHW) Q1 revenue down 1%; earnings miss estimates
summary: The Charles Schwab Corporation reported lower earnings and revenues for the first quarter of 2022, missing Wall Street's forecasts. Total revenues decreased 1% to $4.67 billion, and adjusted net profit dropped to $0.77 per share. The company's stock experienced a decline following the earnings release.

title: Goldman Sachs Boosts Hiring of Dealmakers in Singapore
summary: Goldman Sachs is increasing its hiring of senior investment bankers in Singapore to strengthen its dealmaking capacity in Southeast Asia. The firm has recruited Chua Hui Yin from JPMorgan Chase & Co. and Andrew Teo from Oversea-Chinese Banking Corp. for key roles in corporate finance and investment banking. These additions aim to capitalize on the growing M&A and IPO activity in the region.

title: BB (BBAS3): 4 bancos brasileiros estão entre os mais rentáveis do mundo
summary: A Economática revelou que quatro bancos brasileiros — Banco do Brasil (BBAS3), Itaú Unibanco (ITUB4), Santander Brasil (SANB11), e Bradesco (BBDC4) — estão entre os dez bancos mais rentáveis do mundo em 2021, considerando instituições com mais de US$ 100 bilhões em ativos. O Santander Brasil liderou entre os nacionais e continuou uma trajetória de crescimento de ROE na última década, enquanto Itaú, Bradesco e Banco do Brasil experimentaram uma queda em sua rentabilidade anual em comparação com 2010. A pesquisa também apontou que, embora a diferença de ROE entre os bancos mais rentáveis e os demais tenha diminuído ao longo dos anos, a rentabilidade mediana dos quatro grandes bancos brasileiros ainda supera a de instituições menores.

title: Treasury Bond Massacre, Mortgage Rates Hit 5.35%, Highest since 2009, and it’s Only April
summary: This article discusses the significant spike in Treasury yields and mortgage rates, with the 30-year fixed mortgage rate reaching 5.35%, the highest since 2009. Author Wolf Richter attributes this to the Federal Reserve's rate-hike plan to combat 8.5% CPI inflation. The bond market is experiencing a "massacre" for long-term bond funds, while future buyers will benefit from higher yields, and the housing market is expected to see a serious impact.

title: See JPMorgan Chase’s big bet on the future of the office
summary: JPMorgan Chase is building a 60-story, all-electric office tower in Manhattan designed with post-pandemic considerations in mind, drawing input from wellness expert Deepak Chopra and Harvard’s Healthy Buildings program director Joseph Allen. The new headquarters, set to be the tallest all-electric building in NYC, emphasizes employee well-being, advanced air quality, and net-zero operational emissions. This project signals a strong commitment to the future of physical office spaces despite skepticism regarding its ambitious environmental goals.

title: WesBanco Named One of the World’s Best Banks by Forbes
summary: For the fourth consecutive year, WesBanco Bank has been recognized by Forbes as one of the World’s Best Banks, ranking 30th globally. The recognition is based on customer satisfaction surveys across various criteria including trust, customer service, digital services, and financial advice. WesBanco's President and CEO, Todd F. Clossin, attributes this success to the company's commitment to delivering large bank capabilities with a community bank feel, focusing on long-term customer relationships and investing in innovative digital technology.

title: Government contracting trends: Surviving economic challenges
summary: Government contractors are currently grappling with significant economic challenges including inflation, supply chain disruptions, and a tight labor market. These issues are particularly problematic for contractors whose existing agreements may prevent them from passing on increased costs to the government. To mitigate these pressures, the article suggests strategies such as employee incentives and a reevaluation of contract types.

title: Addus Hires Former Encompass Health Executive, Gears Up for Major Growth
summary: Addus HomeCare Corporation has appointed Cliff Blessing, former EVP of corporate development for Encompass Health’s home health and hospice business, as its new EVP and chief development officer. This strategic hire signals Addus's intention to aggressively pursue mergers and acquisitions to expand its home health and hospice service lines, moving beyond its traditional Medicaid-based personal care services. The company views acquisitions, combined with a more favorable staffing environment, as crucial for its broader growth strategy and market reach.

title: Canadian megabank CIBC opens startup-focused investment office in Bellevue
summary: Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce (CIBC) is expanding its CIBC Innovation Banking arm by opening a new office in Bellevue. This office will focus on providing growth capital to local startups. CIBC Innovation Banking was established in 2018 following the acquisition of Wellington Financial.

title: Teucrium Bitcoin Futures ETF Now Carries Hashdex Brand
summary: The Teucrium Bitcoin Futures Fund, the first bitcoin futures ETF approved under the Securities Act of 1933, is changing its name to include the Hashdex brand. This move, potentially a result of a new partnership, could help Teucrium differentiate its product and allow Hashdex, a Brazil-based asset manager, to enter the US ETF market. The SEC's approval of this ETF was seen by some as a step towards greenlighting a spot bitcoin ETF, despite other bitcoin futures ETFs being filed under a different act with more investor protections.

title: JPMorgan Chase, Microsoft among growing number of companies turning to neurodiverse workers to help meet need for talent
summary: A growing number of companies, including JPMorgan Chase and Microsoft, are actively recruiting neurodiverse individuals to fill talent needs and leverage their unique skills. This trend is driven by an increasing recognition of the neurodiverse population, their problem-solving abilities, and the ongoing demand for talent, with companies implementing structured programs for interviewing, hiring, and onboarding. These initiatives not only provide career opportunities for neurodiverse workers but also positively impact company culture and team dynamics.

title: First Internet Bank Appoints Genevieve Lua As VP
summary: First Internet Bank announced the appointment of Genevieve Lua as Vice President, Business Development Officer, to its Small Business Administration Lending team. Lua brings extensive lending experience from Bank of America and JPMorgan Chase, and will help entrepreneurs navigate the SBA loan process. First Internet Bank emphasizes providing flexible financial solutions for small businesses.

title: Abbott Labs' profits jump on high winter demand for at-home COVID-19 tests
summary: Abbott Laboratories reported a significant 36% jump in profits for the past quarter, driven primarily by high demand for its at-home COVID-19 test kits, particularly the BinaxNOW test, which contributed $3.3 billion to its revenue. Despite robust first-quarter results, the company's full-year guidance remained conservative due to a recall of its Similac infant formula, which negatively impacted its nutrition division sales. The company also saw strong organic sales growth in medical devices and pharmaceuticals, while its CEO emphasized the strength of its base business when excluding the circumstantial impacts of COVID-19 testing and the formula recall.

title: Kosciusko County Court News
summary: This article details various court proceedings in Kosciusko County, including small claims, civil collections, evictions, marriage licenses, and marriage dissolutions. It lists specific cases, amounts awarded, and names of individuals involved in each category. The infractioins section provides details on several traffic and other minor offenses.

title: Proposal to Remove Warren Buffett as Berkshire Hathaway Chairman Gathers Steam
summary: A proposal in Berkshire Hathaway's 2022 Proxy Statement calls for the separation of the CEO and chairman roles, currently both held by Warren Buffett. This initiative is supported by CalPERS and Sustainalytics, who argue it would strengthen governance by providing independent oversight. Berkshire Hathaway, however, opposes the proposal, stating that Buffett should remain chairman as long as he is CEO, but a non-management director would take over the role once he steps down from the CEO position.

title: JPMorgan Chase is tracking employees through office-entry card swipes: report
summary: JPMorgan Chase is reportedly tracking employees' in-office attendance through badge swipe data, similar to Goldman Sachs. This data is fed into dashboards for managers to monitor compliance with the bank's hybrid work policy, which requires a significant portion of its workforce to be in the office multiple days a week. While CEO Jamie Dimon cited flexibility, some employees express distrust and frustration over the monitoring and rigid requirements.

title: How big banks are building a branch workforce of the future
summary: This article discusses how major banks like U.S. Bank are adapting their retail branch workforces to the evolving digital landscape. It highlights the transformation of retail bank employees to meet the demands of a more digitally-centric banking environment. The piece also includes related articles focusing on banking hiring trends and remote work policies among large financial institutions.

title: News | How the Unraveling of Walt Disney World’s Special Tax Status in Florida Affects Commercial Property
summary: Florida Governor Ron DeSantis signed a bill to abolish Walt Disney World's special tax district, Reedy Creek Improvement District, which grants the park governmental privileges. This move is a response to Disney's opposition to a Florida law regarding gender and sexuality education. The dissolution of the district could lead to significant financial burdens for Orange and Osceola counties, potentially impacting commercial development and local taxpayers.

title: 5 macro sustainability trends to watch
summary: This article outlines five key sustainability trends for businesses to monitor in 2022, including carbon capture technologies, the scaling up of renewable energy sources, and increased corporate capital commitments. It also highlights the growing importance of energy security and the need for improved, standardized data in ESG reporting. JPMorgan Chase experts provide insights into each trend and the bank's own sustainability efforts.

title: Branding Wealth Management for the Averagely Affluent
summary: Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan, and UBS are launching new digital wealth management brands, essentially retail "robo-advisors," targeting "averagely affluent" investors. These platforms offer automated investments with low opening balances and fees, based on personalized risk profiles and financial goals, reflecting a shift towards digital solutions and away from traditional human interaction.

title: Wall Street Firms Make Crypto Push to Catch Up With ‘Cool Kids’
summary: Wall Street firms like Jefferies, BlackRock, and Goldman Sachs are increasing their involvement in cryptocurrencies, expanding services, backing stablecoin firms, and ramping up crypto trading. This shift marks a significant change from their previous skepticism, driven by rising crypto prices and investor interest. The move indicates a push by traditional financial institutions to catch up with the evolving digital asset landscape.

title: RBC and CIBC join banking group helping to finance Elon Musk’s bid for Twitter
summary: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) and Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce (CIBC) have committed US$1.15-billion to finance Elon Musk's US$44-billion takeover of Twitter Inc. The Canadian banks are participating in the lowest-risk part of the financing, a US$12.5-billion loan secured by a portion of Musk's Tesla shares. This indicates their involvement in the major acquisition while taking on the least financial risk among the lenders.

title: 5 Best Business Checking Account Promotions in 2023
summary: This article compiles the top business checking account promotions available in 2023 from various banks, highlighting the bonuses offered, how to earn them, and any restrictions. It also provides guidance on maximizing these promotions, understanding associated fees, and what features business owners should look for in a checking account beyond just sign-up bonuses. The piece emphasizes the importance of reading terms and conditions carefully to ensure eligibility for the offers.

title: Public record: The timeline for Zurn’s acquisition of Elkay
summary: This article details the timeline of Zurn Water Solutions' acquisition of Elkay Manufacturing Co., based on new SEC documents. It outlines the negotiation process, which began in April 2021 between Zurn CEO Todd Adams and Elkay CEO Tim Jahnke, even as Elkay was considering an initial public offering. The timeline highlights key discussions, proposals, and decisions by both companies' leadership and shareholders, leading to the final merger agreement signed in February 2022.

title: Petrucci, PGIM sell 511,000 sq. ft. Phillipsburg warehouse for $110 million
summary: A joint venture between J.G. Petrucci Inc. and PGIM Real Estate has sold a newly constructed 511,200-square-foot industrial building in Phillipsburg for $110 million to Cabot Properties. The transaction, which involved brokers from JLL, marked the largest investment sale in New Jersey’s industrial market during the first quarter. The property at 39 Strykers Road was recently leased to national logistics firm Alan Ritchey.

title: UBS Becomes Third Global Bank to Lose China Boss This Month
summary: UBS Group AG's David Chin is stepping down as China country head, making him the third senior executive at a global lender in China to exit this month. He will be succeeded by Eugene Qian, chairman of UBS Securities Co. The move comes as Covid travel restrictions have made it challenging for international bankers to manage operations from outside mainland China.

title: Barclays warns inflation and cost of living crisis is hurting customers
summary: Barclays has warned that the cost of living crisis and surging inflation are already impacting its customers, leading the bank to set aside an additional £141m for potential loan defaults. These concerns echo those from other major UK banks like Lloyds and HSBC, who are also preparing for tougher economic conditions exacerbated by the war in Ukraine and supply chain issues. Despite these warnings, Barclays still reported a rise in pre-tax profits, though profits were impacted by legal costs related to the over-selling of American financial products.

title: Latest: Morgan Stanley debuts custom index in annuities market
summary: Morgan Stanley has launched a new custom index, the Morgan Stanley Dynamic Global Index, for North American Company for Life and Health Insurance's index annuity products. This index aims to provide diversified exposure across equities, fixed income, and commodities with a rules-based dynamic allocation strategy to manage market volatility. Other financial institutions like Spectrum Markets, J.P. Morgan, Hamburger Sparkasse, and Bloomberg/MSCI are also introducing new services and indices in their respective markets.

title: As Electric Aircraft Approach Takeoff, JP Morgan Picks a Leader
summary: J.P. Morgan Securities analysts Bill Peterson and Mahima Kakani have initiated coverage on three electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) companies: Archer Aviation Inc. (ACHR), Joby Aviation Inc. (JOBY), and Lilium N.V. (LILM). They gave Archer Aviation an "Overweight" rating, citing its strong balance sheet and potential upside, while Joby Aviation and Lilium N.V. both received "Neutral" ratings. The analysts noted the high-risk, high-reward nature of investing in the nascent eVTOL market but estimate it could reach $1 trillion in the long term.

title: FAT Brands Adds Nine Restaurant Chains in $1B Buying Spree
summary: FAT Brands acquired nine restaurant chains over 18 months for $917.5 million, reaching $2.2 billion in system sales from 2,300 restaurants across 17 chains. CEO Andy Wiederhorn plans to "digest" these acquisitions, increase production at their manufacturing business, and refinance debt to lower capital costs, despite concerns raised by a Seeking Alpha analyst about the company's high leverage and ongoing SEC and U.S. Attorney's Office investigations related to Wiederhorn.

title: News | Stream Expands Texas Tenant Team, BBG Launches New Group, Newmark Names Vice Chairman
summary: This article details recent personnel moves and new initiatives within the commercial real estate industry. Key highlights include Stream Realty Partners expanding its Dallas tenant representation team with Greg Biggs, BBG Assessment launching a new seismic services group led by Joshua Marrow, and Newmark promoting Kenneth Cox to vice chairman in its self-storage capital markets group. Other notable appointments include Lauren Nunnally to CAO at Swinerton, Kyle Goehring to US Sustainability Head at Turner & Townsend, and several promotions at Ware Malcomb.

title: Prosecutors search Deutsche Bank HQ in money laundering investigation
summary: German prosecutors, federal police, and financial regulators searched Deutsche Bank's headquarters in Frankfurt in connection with a money laundering investigation. The search is linked to suspicious transactions that Deutsche Bank itself reported to the authorities, and the bank stated it is cooperating fully. This incident is part of a larger effort by Deutsche Bank, under CEO Christian Sewing, to repair its reputation following a history of regulatory failings related to money laundering.

title: The long-shot campaign to get big banks out of fossil fuels
summary: Climate activists are intensifying pressure on major banks like Citigroup, Wells Fargo, Bank of America, and Goldman Sachs to cease financing new fossil fuel projects. Although recent shareholder resolutions failed, gaining only about 10 percent of the vote, advocates see this as a foundational step. They are drawing on the success of the fossil fuel divestment movement and hope to eventually sway large asset managers to support their cause, despite current skepticism from bank boards and the energy market's volatility exacerbated by global events.

title: Buffett reveals big investments, rails against Wall Street excess at Berkshire meeting
summary: Warren Buffett used Berkshire Hathaway's first in-person annual meeting since 2019 to announce significant new investments, including increased stakes in Chevron and Activision Blizzard, totaling over $31 billion. He criticized Wall Street's excess and maintained Berkshire's commitment to holding substantial cash reserves while addressing shareholder inquiries on inflation and nuclear war risks. Shareholders rejected proposals for more diversity disclosure and an independent chairman, with Buffett affirming that "Berkshire is built forever."

title: Frank Sorrentino III Of ConnectOne Bank On The Future Of Money and Banking
summary: Frank Sorrentino III, Chairman, CEO, and Founder of ConnectOne Bank, discusses the evolving landscape of banking and money, emphasizing the role of digitalization and technology in serving small to mid-market clients. He shares insights on ConnectOne Bank's journey, including its IPO and recent Fintech acquisitions, and offers advice for a successful career in the modern finance industry. Sorrentino highlights the importance of innovation balanced with regulation and envisions significant growth in payments and digital asset custody.

title: Banco Galicia y Brubank permiten comprar y vender criptomonedas
summary: Banco Galicia and Brubank have become the first two banks in Argentina to allow customers to buy and sell cryptocurrencies directly through their online banking platforms. This move addresses a growing demand from Argentinians to invest in digital currencies as a hedge against inflation. The services are offered through Lirium, a regulated crypto platform, which partners with banks to enable secure transactions in local currency.

title: Cboe Global Markets Completes Acquisition of ErisX, Entering Digital Asset Market
summary: Cboe Global Markets announced it has completed the acquisition of ErisX, a U.S. based digital asset spot market and regulated derivatives exchange and clearinghouse. This acquisition provides Cboe with an entry into the digital asset market, aiming to build a comprehensive digital asset market data offering and develop further derivative products. Cboe plans to operate ErisX as a subsidiary, with Thomas Chippas remaining as head of the digital asset business, focusing on regulatory compliance and transparency to mature the digital asset market globally.

title: J.P. Morgan Launches Tax Smart SMA Platform to Help Advisors Create Customized Portfolios on Demand
summary: J.P. Morgan Asset Management has launched a new Tax-Smart Separately Managed Account (SMA) Platform, leveraging 55ip's ActiveTax® technology. This platform enables advisors to create customized, tax-efficient portfolios digitally, offering features like custom index SMAs and model portfolios of mutual funds and ETFs. The initial offering is the Custom Invest - U.S. Large Cap Equity strategy, benchmarked to the S&P 500, designed to help advisors enhance after-tax returns for their clients through systematic tax management.

title: México: los principales bancos extranjeros son dueños de las concesiones para la extracción de agua
summary: Major foreign banks hold water extraction concessions in Mexico, allowing them to extract millions of cubic meters annually, often from overexploited aquifers. This financial interest in water is highlighted by the trading of water futures on Wall Street, turning a vital resource into a speculative commodity. The article emphasizes the disparity where a small percentage of users control a large portion of water for profit, exacerbating scarcity and high costs for the general population, especially in marginalized areas, and criticizes government complicity in granting these concessions.

title: Sanctions and their effect on international payments for insurers
summary: This article discusses the profound impact of sanctions imposed on Russia following its invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, especially on international payments for insurers. It details what sanctions are, their implications for the financial sector and businesses, and the challenges faced by the insurance industry, including FX volatility and difficulties in paying suppliers. The article also touches upon the performance of the Russian Ruble and future expectations regarding sanctions.

title: Expanding Economic Opportunity and Mobility for People with Disabilities
summary: A new issue brief from the JPMorgan Chase Policy Center advocates for updating and simplifying asset and income limits for the Supplemental Security Income (SSI) program. The current structure places working individuals with disabilities at risk of losing economic security due to antiquated limits that inhibit their ability to earn more without losing benefits. JPMorgan Chase's head of Disability Inclusion, Jim Sinocchi, emphasizes that these barriers hinder both individuals and employers' diversity and inclusion efforts.

title: Financially Distressed Designer EYP Group Seeks Bankruptcy Protection
summary: EYP Group Holdings, an architecture and engineering firm, has filed for bankruptcy protection in Delaware federal court due to $149 million in debt. The company plans to sell its assets to Ault Alliance for $67 million as part of its restructuring plan. The financial distress originated from financing needed to cash out retiring staff managers and an employee stock ownership plan created five years later, which led to continuous default on bank covenants.

title: What does the future of automotive payments solutions look like?
summary: J.P. Morgan explores the evolving landscape of automotive payments, moving beyond basic in-car purchases to encompass broader mobility experiences. The article highlights how connected cars are transforming into mobile payment sources, enabling new business models and enhancing buying, ownership, and mobility experiences through innovative solutions like subscriptions, EV charging payments, and more streamlined transactions.

title: Klarna borrowing to go on credit reports from June: what it means for you
summary: Klarna will begin reporting the use of its 'Pay in 30' and 'Pay in 3' products to major UK credit reference agencies, Experian and TransUnion, starting June 2022. This means on-time, late, and outstanding payments will appear on credit reports, making it crucial for users to meet repayment obligations. While repayment plans will be marked on credit files, Klarna states that credit scores won't be immediately impacted, awaiting updates to credit scoring mechanisms.

title: Commercial Vehicle Market Size Worth USD 990.5 Billion, Globally, by 2028 at 6.5% CAGR - Light Commercial Vehicle Segment is Expected to Hold the Largest Commercial Vehicle Market Share
summary: The global commercial vehicle market is projected to grow from USD 654.9 billion in 2020 to USD 990.5 billion by 2028, at a CAGR of 6.5%, driven by increasing industrialization and infrastructure development. The Light Commercial Vehicle Segment is expected to dominate the market, with North America emerging as a dominant region and Asia Pacific experiencing outstanding growth. The COVID-19 pandemic severely impacted the market through declined product sales.

title: The Landscape for Digital Asset Custodial Services in 2022
summary: This article discusses the evolving landscape of digital asset custodial services in 2022, highlighting the significant growth of digital assets and the security challenges they present. It explains the need for specialized custody due to the unique nature of cryptocurrencies, contrasting it with traditional asset custody. The piece also outlines various storage mechanisms, client needs, regulatory considerations, and different custody options available to investors and financial institutions.

title: NONPROFIT REGISTER | Colorado Business Hall of Fame adds seven to its roster
summary: The Colorado Business Hall of Fame inducted seven new laureates at its 32nd annual event, hosted by Junior Achievement Rocky Mountain and the Denver Metro Chamber of Commerce. The inductees include entrepreneurs and philanthropists such as Robert Albin, Tim Gill, Robert Newman, Nancy and Curt Richardson, Donald Sturm, and Clara Brown, recognized for their significant contributions to business and society in Colorado.

title: Cinco de Mayo 2022 deals: Find free food, taco specials, discounted margaritas and more savings
summary: This article details various Cinco de Mayo 2022 deals from popular food chains like Chipotle, Taco Bell, and Chili's, offering free food, taco specials, and discounted margaritas. It also includes information on other promotions, such as drink rebates and contests, highlighting that a significant portion of U.S. consumers planned to celebrate the holiday despite inflation concerns. The deals were available nationwide at participating locations, often requiring app usage or loyalty program memberships.

title: Our Target in Action: Expanding Access to Telecommunications in Sub-Saharan Africa
summary: J.P. Morgan Development Finance Institution (JPM DFI) structured a $620 million corporate bond for Liquid Telecom in February 2021 to expand telecommunications access in Sub-Saharan Africa. This initiative aims to connect more homes and buildings to fiber networks, increase LTE coverage, and create employment opportunities in various countries, thereby addressing key development gaps and fostering financial inclusion. The project aligns with United Nations Sustainable Development Goals #8 and #9, focusing on decent work and resilient infrastructure.

title: UK bank and building society overview: who owns who?
summary: This article explains the ownership structures of UK banks and building societies, highlighting how many operate under the same banking licences. Understanding banking groups is crucial for consumers to ensure their money is protected by the Financial Services Compensation Scheme (FSCS), which has an £85,000 limit per banking licence. The article lists major banking groups, single-licence banks, building societies, and foreign-owned banks with UK licences, emphasizing the importance of this knowledge for financial protection and ethical banking choices.

title: Scoping Out Scope 3 Emissions
summary: A report by Citi Research's Anita McBain highlights the growing importance of Scope 3 emissions as new reporting requirements aim to improve transparency in emission reporting across global value chains. The article discusses the complexities of disclosing Scope 3 emissions compared to Scope 1 and 2, and the significant business benefits companies can achieve by addressing them. It also examines current Scope 3 disclosure trends by country, noting that while the U.S. has the largest volume of disclosed emissions, a smaller proportion of its companies consider Scope 3 relevant compared to Japan.

title: Dimensional Completing Largest Mutual Fund To ETF Conversion
summary: Dimensional Fund Advisors is completing its largest mutual fund to ETF conversion, bringing $7.8 billion worth of assets into the ETF wrapper, specifically with the Tax-Managed US Marketwide Value Portfolio II becoming the Dimensional US Marketwide Value ETF (DFUV). This conversion contributes to nearly $10 billion in converted assets in 2022, with more expected from JPMorgan Asset Management. The new ETF retains its 0.23% expense ratio and continues to target U.S.-listed value stocks with a focus on tax efficiency.

title: Revealed: Barclays avoids almost £2bn in tax via Luxembourg scheme
summary: Barclays has avoided nearly £2bn in tax through a Luxembourg arrangement by booking profits from a 2009 sale of a fund management business there instead of in the UK. This controversial decision allowed the bank to pay less than 1% tax on billions in profits for over a decade, raising questions about its investment strategy and impact on UK tax coffers. Despite employing only 54 staff in Luxembourg, it has become one of Barclays' most profitable jurisdictions.

title: Exclusive| HDFC Bank may get RBI glide path to pare holding in HDFC Credila, HDB Financial after merger
summary: HDFC Bank is seeking the RBI's permission to retain all subsidiaries after its merger with HDFC Ltd. However, the RBI has expressed concerns regarding two lending subsidiaries, HDFC Credila and HDB Financial Services, as their operations could be absorbed by the bank. If the RBI does not allow their continuation in current form, HDFC Bank is expected to seek a glide path to divest its stake in these two entities.

title: Strategic Wealth & Advisor Growth News
summary: This article from LPL Financial highlights its "Strategic Wealth & Advisor Growth" news, focusing on the continued success and benefits of its Strategic Wealth model for financial advisors. It details recent advisory firm joins, positive advisor transitions to LPL, and the recognition of 22 LPL-associated advisors on Barron's 2022 list of Top 1,200 Financial Advisors in America, underscoring LPL's commitment to supporting advisor growth and independence.

title: ICICI Bank vs Bank of Baroda vs PNB vs Canara Bank: Comparison of home loan interest rates
summary: Following the RBI's repo rate hike by 40 basis points to 4.40%, several major banks have increased their home loan interest rates. This report compares the new RLLR (Repo Linked Lending Rate) and I-EBLR (ICICI Bank External Benchmark Lending Rate) for ICICI Bank, Punjab National Bank, Bank of Baroda, and Canara Bank, effective primarily in May and June 2022. The hike leads to higher EMIs for existing and new borrowers.

title: These Bond ETFs Are Floating Through Rate Hike Risks
summary: As the Federal Reserve began raising interest rates, investors have shifted towards less rate-sensitive bond ETFs, particularly those focused on floating-rate bonds. Funds like USFR, FLOT, and FLRN have seen significant inflows due to their low duration and ability to adjust coupon rates with rising market rates. These ETFs offer an attractive option for investors looking to trim duration and put cash to work in a rising rate environment, providing downside protection compared to traditional fixed-rate bonds.

title: PE giant Brookfield buys Watermark REIT for $3.8B
summary: Brookfield Real Estate Funds has acquired non-traded REIT Watermark Lodging Trust for $3.8 billion in an all-cash transaction. Watermark's portfolio comprises 25 luxury and upper upscale hotels, including Ritz-Carlton properties, located in U.S. drive-to leisure destinations and gateway urban cities. The acquisition reflects confidence in large-scale hotel deals despite recent interest rate increases and debt capital market volatility.

title: Family offices face scrutiny as CFTC boss vows no Archegos redux
summary: The top U.S. derivatives regulator, Rostin Behnam, is increasing scrutiny on family offices following the Archegos Capital Management collapse. Behnam stated that the Archegos situation highlighted the need to re-evaluate agency rules and the dangers of individual investors building massive, unregulated swaps positions. The CFTC may propose new rules for investors with significant swaps positions and is reviewing risk management practices among private funds, prime brokers, and banks.

title: Byline Bank shutters six more branches, exits DuPage County
summary: Byline Bank has closed six more full-service branches, including its last location in DuPage County, continuing its strategy of reducing its physical footprint. Since 2015, the bank has decreased its number of branches in the Chicago area from 86 to 39. This move aligns with a broader industry trend of branch closures exacerbated by the pandemic, though some larger banks like JPMorgan Chase and Wintrust Financial are still expanding their retail presence.

title: Supporting Consumer Adoption of Electric Vehicles
summary: JPMorgan Chase is actively supporting the adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) by helping consumers understand and finance their purchases. They are developing a new digital resource center to educate first-time EV buyers and are increasing financing options, including private label partnerships with EV manufacturers like Rivian. This initiative responds to the growing consumer interest and complex nature of the evolving EV market.

title: Not working out: Peloton plunges after cutting outlook
summary: Peloton Interactive Inc. shares tumbled after the company reported a deeper loss than analysts predicted, cut its revenue guidance, and secured a $750 million debt deal. The company, which thrived during the early pandemic, is now facing "softer demand" and continued stock decline despite leadership changes and cost-cutting measures. CEO Barry McCarthy is focused on increasing subscribers and expanding the digital app, while some investors are pushing for a sale of the company amidst its financial struggles.

title: Exclusive: Carlyle to acquire NSM Insurance from White Mountains in $1.78 billion deal
summary: Private equity firm Carlyle Group Inc. has agreed to acquire U.S. specialty insurance provider NSM Insurance Group from White Mountains Insurance Group Ltd. for $1.78 billion in cash. This deal is expected to close in the second half of the year and will add $280 per share to White Mountains' adjusted book value. Carlyle plans to invest further in the platform and ramp up mergers and acquisitions activity within NSM Insurance.

title: Dimensional, JPMorgan Flip Billions From Mutual Funds Into ETFs
summary: Dimensional Fund Advisors and JPMorgan Asset Management are converting billions of dollars from mutual funds into ETFs, with a total of about $55 billion in switched assets expected. This move is part of a broader industry trend towards lower-cost, more tax-efficient ETFs, with over $240 billion exiting mutual funds in 2022 so far. Dimensional's ETF assets are set to exceed $54 billion, making it one of the largest issuers.

title: Taking Footsteps Toward a Sustainable Future
summary: The article highlights Allbirds as a successful footwear company built on sustainable practices, using natural, renewable resources and openly sharing its carbon calculation methods. It discusses how Allbirds' financial success, including its IPO led by J.P. Morgan, demonstrates investor confidence in sustainability-driven businesses. The piece emphasizes the growing consumer demand for sustainable products and the fashion industry's need for transformative practices to reduce its environmental footprint.

title: U.S. lawmakers ask JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs for information on Russian debt dealings
summary: U.S. Senator Elizabeth Warren and Representative Katie Porter have requested information from JPMorgan Chase & Co and Goldman Sachs Group Inc regarding their trading of Russian government and corporate debt since the start of the conflict in Ukraine. The lawmakers are seeking details on client lists, transaction types, amounts, and profits made by the banks, arguing that while legal, these dealings may undermine international sanctions against Russia. Both banks had previously announced they were unwinding their Russian businesses, with JPMorgan stating its market-making activities comply with sanctions and aim to help clients reduce risk.

title: Citigroup Head of Asia Pacific FIG Kelvin Goh Is Said to Leave
summary: Kelvin Goh, Citigroup Inc.'s Asia Pacific head of financial institutions group (FIG), has resigned and is reportedly joining JPMorgan Chase & Co. Goh, a Singapore-based banker, is expected to start with JPMorgan in a few months as their head of APAC FIG. This move follows a trend of several Singapore dealmakers changing jobs recently.

title: Rackspace CEO’s comments fuel speculation about another sale of tech company
summary: Rackspace Technology CEO Kevin Jones' recent comments to analysts have sparked speculation about a potential sale or restructuring of the company. Jones indicated that a "sum of the parts valuation" could exceed Rackspace's current enterprise value, leading to considerations of strategic alternatives. While Rackspace later downplayed a full sale, the company is exploring reorganizing its on-premise server and public cloud services into separate entities to "unlock value."

title: nCino announces new partnership with Capitec Bank in South Africa
summary: nCino, a provider of cloud banking and digital transformation solutions, has partnered with Capitec Bank, South Africa's largest digital bank. This collaboration aims to build and optimize Capitec Bank's Business Banking loan management system, enhancing efficiency and simplicity for its rapidly growing client base. The partnership will leverage nCino's technology to streamline processes and improve client and employee experiences in business banking operations.

title: BMO Capital Markets Head Fears Deep Recession on Rate Hikes
summary: The CEO of BMO Capital Markets, Dan Barclay, expressed concerns that rising interest rates, intended to combat inflation, might not be effective due to supply-side issues and could instead lead to a deep global recession. He believes current inflation is driven by post-pandemic supply chain issues and the war in Ukraine, rather than demand. Central banks' shrinking balance sheets further contribute to this risk.

title: Global 2000: Berkshire Hathaway Takes Down JPMorgan As America’s Largest Company
summary: Berkshire Hathaway has surpassed JPMorgan Chase to become America's largest public company in the Forbes Global 2000 list, driven by nearly $90 billion in profits. Despite global volatility, U.S. companies like Amazon and ExxonMobil showed significant growth, with Amazon rising to third in the U.S. and ExxonMobil rebounding strongly due to surging energy prices. The article highlights the resilience of top U.S. companies amid inflation and geopolitical challenges.

title: Star Alliance Plans Credit Card For Redeeming Points Across 26 Airlines
summary: Star Alliance, the largest global airline group comprising 26 member airlines, is set to launch a co-branded credit card this year. This new credit card will enable users to earn points through spending and then redeem those points across the frequent-flyer programs of any of its member airlines, including Singapore Airlines, Lufthansa, and United Airlines.

title: Kosciusko County Court News
summary: This article provides detailed court news from Kosciusko County, Indiana, as of May 12, 2022. It covers small claims, civil collections, evictions, mortgage foreclosures, and various infractions from Superior Courts, including names of parties and financial figures. Additionally, it lists recent marriage licenses issued and marriage dissolutions filed, specifying names, marriage dates, separation dates, and information about minor children involved.

title: KeyCorp stock falls Thursday, underperforms market
summary: KeyCorp's stock (KEY) dropped 0.27% on Thursday, closing at $18.53, underperforming the broader market as the S&P 500 and Dow Jones also experienced declines. This marks the sixth consecutive day of losses for KeyCorp, leaving its stock $8.64 below its 52-week high. The company's performance was mixed compared to competitors like JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo, and PNC Financial Services.

title: Wilks brothers’ oilfield company ProFrac raises $288 million in IPO
summary: ProFrac Holding Corp., an oil services firm founded by brothers Dan and Farris Wilks, raised $288 million in its initial public offering, selling 16 million shares at $18 each. This pricing was below their target range, reflecting a challenging market for new listings. Despite broader market difficulties for IPOs, the company is looking to capitalize on increased demand for oilfield services due to global energy market shifts.

title: Uncover 6 Ways to Reduce Your Tax Bill
summary: This article from Morgan Stanley outlines six strategies to help individuals reduce their tax bill by carefully reviewing their federal income tax return (Form 1040). It suggests analyzing taxable interest, leveraging investment losses through tax-loss harvesting, utilizing Qualified Charitable Distributions, reclaiming foreign taxes, saving for education with 529 plans, and optimizing medical and dental expense deductions. The advice emphasizes year-round tax planning and consulting with a financial advisor.

title: Transcript: Boaz Weinstein
summary: This transcript features an in-depth conversation between Barry Ritholtz and Boaz Weinstein, founder of Saba Capital. Weinstein discusses his background, including his chess and card-counting days, and how he transitioned into finance. The interview covers Saba Capital's investment strategies, such as closed-end fund arbitrage, SPACs, and tail protection, as well as specific trades like the London Whale and Evergrande.

title: JPMorgan Analysts Behind ‘Uninvestable’ Call Upgrade China Tech
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. analysts have upgraded at least 15 Chinese Internet stocks, including Tencent Holdings Ltd. and Alibaba Group Holding Ltd., just two months after their bearish report labeled the sector "uninvestable." This reversal comes after the previous report triggered a market selloff and internal discussions at the US bank.

title: República Dominicana participa en la XI Conferencia BBVA de Latinoamérica
summary: The Dominican Republic, represented by Vice Minister of Public Credit María José Martínez, participated in the XI BBVA Latin America Conference in New York. Martínez presented the Dominican economy's resilience, its management of public debt, and the positive impact of recent bond issuance on debt-to-GDP ratios. The conference gathered public and private debt issuers, analysts, and international investors to discuss economic perspectives and investment opportunities in the region, aligning with the Dominican Republic's strategy to achieve investment grade.

title: Sanofi ordered by French court to compensate for epilepsy drug side effect: report
summary: A French court has ordered Sanofi to pay over 400,000 euros to a family whose child developed autism, linking it to the epilepsy drug valproate (Depakine). The court found that Sanofi failed to adequately warn consumers about the drug's risks, an accusation the company denies and plans to appeal. This ruling is the first in France to directly connect the drug to autism in an individual patient case, following previous estimates of thousands of physical and neuro-developmental defects caused by the medication.

title: Judge Dismisses No-poach Suit Against Live Oak, Apiture; NCino’s Continues
summary: A federal class-action lawsuit alleging a no-hire agreement has been dismissed against Live Oak and Apiture after they settled for $4.65 million. However, the case against nCino, a related financial technology firm, is proceeding. The lawsuit claims that an unwritten "gentlemen's agreement" among executives of these interconnected companies suppressed wages for eligible workers in Wilmington.

title: ETF Leaders Powered by the NYSE: Darek Wojnar
summary: Darek Wojnar of FlexShares, a division of Northern Trust Asset Management, discussed how inflation and ESG are influencing investor allocations. He highlighted FlexShares' diverse ETF lineup, including inflation hedges like the FlexShares Morningstar Global Upstream Natural Resources Index Fund (GUNR A+), and their commitment to ESG investing, leveraging a proprietary scoring mechanism for sustainable portfolio construction.

title: Cashing in on the pandemic: the five highest-paid US executives in 2021
summary: A Wall Street Journal analysis revealed that the highest-paid S&P 500 executives saw record compensation in 2021, with a median of $14.7 million, largely due to stock-based pay capitalizing on the pandemic recovery. Expedia CEO Peter Kern topped the list, earning $296 million primarily in shares and options, followed by David Zaslav of Discovery, William McDermott of ServiceNow, Tim Cook of Apple, and Jamie Dimon of JP Morgan, whose compensations were also heavily tied to stock performance and incentives. This surge in executive pay reflects a strong benefit from the post-pandemic stock market rebound.

title: Globant y Bluecap, una alianza estratégica para los bancos del futuro: "Los datos son el petróleo de este siglo"
summary: Globant acquired Bluecap in December 2020 to revolutionize the financial system through data analysis and AI, focusing on improving customer experience and creating new value propositions for the banking sector. Maite Barrera, CEO of Bluecap and now part of Globant's Executive Committee, highlighted the strategic importance of this alliance for international expansion and leveraging data as "the oil of this century." The collaboration aims to modernize banking, breaking traditional paradigms and adapting to new technologies, while addressing challenges like digitalization and regulatory differences between fintechs and traditional banks.

title: JPMorgan shareholders reject special $52M payout to CEO Jamie Dimon
summary: JPMorgan Chase shareholders rejected a 2021 executive compensation plan, which included a $52.6 million special option award for CEO Jamie Dimon, with only 31% support in a nonbinding vote. This outcome, significantly lower than typical shareholder backing, reflects concerns from proxy advisers Glass Lewis and Institutional Shareholder Services regarding excessive compensation and underwhelming company performance. Although the vote is nonbinding, the board has acknowledged the feedback and indicated it will consider it for future compensation arrangements, particularly as criticism mounts over the bank's spending and the structure of these one-off awards.

title: Paxos and State Street Partner to Deliver Reduced Costs and T+0 Settlement in Innovative Pilot - Paxos | Newsroom
summary: Paxos, a regulated blockchain infrastructure platform, has partnered with State Street to integrate its custodial services into the Paxos Settlement Service. This collaboration, which included Credit Suisse, successfully piloted same-day (T+0) settlement of shares, demonstrating how Paxos' platform can revolutionize market operations by reducing costs and increasing efficiency. The initiative highlights the potential of blockchain technology to automate trade lifecycles and advance towards faster, fairer financial markets.

title: JPMorgan investors hand Jamie Dimon a rare rebuke with disapproval of $52.6 million bonus
summary: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon faced a rare rebuke from shareholders who disapproved of his $52.6 million retention bonus. Only 31% of investors supported the award, which was part of his 2021 compensation and intended to keep him at the bank for another five years. While the vote is nonbinding, the board stated it takes investor feedback seriously and characterized the bonus as a one-time event.

title: JPMorgan shareholders vote disapproval of CEO Dimon's special payout
summary: JPMorgan shareholders have voted to disapprove CEO Jamie Dimon's special $52.6 million stock option award. This advisory "say-on-pay" referendum saw only 31% of votes cast in favor of the bank's executive payments for 2021, a significant drop from previous years. The disapproval was primarily driven by major advisory firms' recommendations against the award, citing a lack of performance criteria for vesting.

title: Digital brokerage Ally Invest launches human wealth management
summary: Ally Invest, the digital brokerage arm of Ally Financial, has launched a new full-service wealth management business offering human financial advice. Investors need a minimum of $100,000 to access financial planning and ongoing guidance from a dedicated adviser, with annual fees ranging from 0.75% to 0.85%. This move marks Ally's first venture into human advisory since its 2016 acquisition of TradeKing, aiming to appeal to clients seeking more personal relationships and comprehensive advice, including on held-away assets.

title: FIS knocks Fiserv out of No. 2 merchant acquirer spot
summary: In 2021, FIS surpassed Fiserv to become the second-largest merchant acquirer by total purchase transactions, following JP Morgan Chase. This shift is attributed to FIS's e-commerce and software strategy, while Fiserv's decline is linked to the dissolution of a joint venture it inherited. Despite the recent change in ranking, Fiserv is expected to regain its position next year due to the growth of its Carat and Clover platforms.

title: JPMorgan CEO Dimon calls for raising minimum wage, more education to address racial gaps
summary: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon has advocated for raising the minimum wage, making mortgages more affordable, and investing in job training to help lower-income workers acquire higher-paying skills. These recommendations come after a report revealed that long-standing racial disparities cost the Columbus economy $10 billion annually. Dimon emphasizes that these initiatives are crucial for addressing racial gaps and improving economic equity.

title: BlackRock, JPMorgan, others tell Texas they don't boycott energy companies
summary: BlackRock, JPMorgan Chase & Co, and other leading financial firms have informed Texas officials that they do not boycott energy companies, responding to inquiries related to a new state law. This law prohibits state agencies from investing funds with firms found to boycott fossil fuel companies. While BlackRock acknowledged participation in initiatives aimed at cutting greenhouse gas emissions, both firms emphasized their fiduciary duty to clients and stressed that their investment decisions are based on business reasons, not boycotts.

title: Santander is the bank that lends the most among its competitors
summary: Banco Santander has emerged as the world's leading bank in lending, excluding Chinese banks, having surpassed one trillion euros in its loan portfolio. This achievement positions Santander ahead of major international competitors like JP Morgan, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, Citi, and HSBC. The bank's strong performance is attributed to growth across individual, corporate, and institutional customer segments, with significant credit investment increases in Europe, North America, and South America, particularly in the UK and Spain.

title: Capital One sets date for hybrid return to office
summary: Capital One announced it will reopen its U.S. offices for all employees on Sept. 6, implementing a hybrid work model. The company encourages employees to work in-office Tuesday through Thursday, though attendance is not mandatory. Capital One has also revised its vaccine policy, permitting unvaccinated staff to return to the office if they comply with regular COVID-19 testing.

title: Mergers & Moves: Raymond James, Focus, LPL, Kestra and Mariner add firms and advisors
summary: This article details recent mergers and acquisitions in the financial advisory industry involving Raymond James, Focus Financial Partners, LPL, Kestra, and Mariner Wealth Advisors. Key moves include Focus firm XML Financial Group acquiring Samson Wealth Management Group with $644 million in assets, Kestra onboarding a former Wells Fargo team managing $590 million, and Mariner purchasing Emerson Wealth with $612 million in assets. Raymond James also added significant client assets through recruited teams, and Emigrant Partners made an international investment in Australian firm Koda Capital.

title: Morgan Stanley's Parametric moves the wirehouse into ETF management
summary: Morgan Stanley's asset management subsidiary, Parametric Portfolio Associates, is entering the ETF market as a subadviser for two new Innovator ETFs, marking Morgan Stanley's first direct involvement in ETF management. This move signifies Parametric's expansion beyond separate accounts and direct indexing, offering strategies designed for downside protection without capping upside potential. Industry experts view this as a significant step for Morgan Stanley given its extensive advisor network, despite its earlier history with ETFs.

title: Kimberly-Clark planning to sell tissue paper assets in Brazil, Latin America -report
summary: Kimberly-Clark Corp is reportedly planning to sell its tissue paper assets in Brazil and other Latin American countries. The company is in talks with JPMorgan to reassess its regional business, with market estimates valuing the assets between $800 million and $1 billion, including about $200 million from Brazil. Several companies, including Suzano SA and Softys, are reportedly interested in acquiring the Brazilian assets.

title: Ecolab's Doug Baker has already started his next chapter
summary: Doug Baker, who recently retired as executive chairman of Ecolab, is embarking on new ventures focusing on economic access and sustainability in Minnesota. Having led Ecolab through significant growth, including a major acquisition and tripling net income, Baker is now investing in companies like JIT Services and co-founding E2SG Partners to accelerate the green economy. He remains committed to his local community engagement, emphasizing the interdependence of healthy businesses and communities.

title: JPMorgan Converts Realty Income Fund Into ETF
summary: JPMorgan Asset Management has converted its JPMorgan Realty Income Fund (JPRE) into an actively managed ETF. This conversion is part of a larger strategy by JPMAM to switch four of its mutual funds into ETFs this year, aiming to broaden the availability of its investment capabilities. The JPMorgan Realty Income ETF (JPRE) invests primarily in real estate investment trusts (REITs), selecting companies based on financial strength, operating revenues, and growth potential.

title: J.P. Morgan Asset Management Hires New Global Data Science Head, Arezu Moghadam
summary: J.P. Morgan Asset Management has appointed Arezu Moghadam as its new Managing Director and Global Head of Data Science. In this role, Moghadam will lead the development of AI and machine learning methods to enhance data-driven investment decisions, client engagement, and operational effectiveness. She brings extensive experience from Point 72, Stone Ridge Asset Management, Oppenheimer Funds, and Goldman Sachs.

title: Santa Monica Rent Controlled Building Sells for Record $330 Million
summary: A former rent-controlled apartment complex in Santa Monica, known as Champagne Towers, has sold for a record-breaking $330 million. Douglass Emmett purchased the 120-unit building at 1221 Ocean Avenue from Irvine Co., making it the most expensive apartment sale in the city's history. The 51-year-old complex, built by Lawrence Welk's firm, offers luxury amenities and has seen its rent-controlled units' prices soar due to the Costa Hawkins Rental Act.

title: Jamie Dimon Hypes J.P. Morgan’s Traditional Brokers
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. CEO Jamie Dimon announced ambitious plans to significantly expand the firm's traditional brokerage unit, J.P. Morgan Advisors, by doubling its headcount to 1,000 top-tier brokers. Dimon emphasized offering superior compensation, research, and resources to attract advisors, aiming to boost market share among affluent investors. Despite management's enthusiasm, recruiters and former advisors expressed skepticism, citing internal competition from the private bank and challenges in attracting high-producing brokers in a competitive market.

title: Innovator ETFs Filed for 2 Managed Floor ETFs
summary: Innovator ETFs has filed for two new actively managed equity ETFs, the Innovator Equity Managed Floor ETF and the Innovator Technology Managed Floor ETF, aiming to address tail risk in stocks. These ETFs will use a custom laddered options strategy designed by Morgan Stanley Investment Management and Parametric to maintain floors against a maximum loss of 10%. Unlike Innovator's existing Defined Outcome ETFs, these new products will be equity-based, comprised mainly of representative stocks from their target indices, and will pay out dividends.

title: JPMorgan’s $30 billion racial-equity commitment was the biggest of any U.S. company. How much progress has it made?
summary: JPMorgan Chase pledged $30 billion over five years to address the racial wealth gap after George Floyd's murder. By the end of 2021, the bank had deployed or committed over $18 billion towards this goal, focusing on initiatives like homeownership, affordable housing, and supporting minority-owned businesses. While JPMorgan considers this substantial progress, some critics argue it's not enough, and activists are pushing for a full racial-equity audit.

title: J.P. Morgan Asset Management Hires New Global Head of Broker Relationship Management, Carissa Biggie
summary: J.P. Morgan Asset Management has appointed Carissa Biggie as Managing Director and Global Head of Broker Relationship Management. Based in New York, Biggie will focus on developing and strengthening relationships with external counterparties. She brings extensive experience from Prudential Financial and Goldman Sachs Asset Management, having previously served in various roles, including global relationship manager and COO of Global Risk Management.

title: How a search for Thai noodles led this Walmart veteran to become CFO of a unicorn
summary: Amanda Whalen, former EVP and CFO at Walmart International, became the new CFO of Klaviyo after a personal experience highlighted the marketing technology unicorn's effectiveness. She discovered Klaviyo through emails from a noodle company she used during the pandemic, which demonstrated how Klaviyo builds digital relationships with customers. Whalen, a veteran in finance, sees similarities between Walmart's customer-first ethos and Klaviyo's approach, and she plans to focus on strengthening the business for future growth, including a potential IPO when the time is right.

title: Mining Billionaire Robert Friedland’s Ivanhoe Electric Seeks Dual Listing In New York, Toronto
summary: Billionaire Robert Friedland's Ivanhoe Electric is seeking a dual listing in New York and Toronto to finance the development of copper mines in the U.S. These mines are intended to supply raw materials for electric vehicle batteries and large-scale energy storage facilities. The company, led by Friedland as CEO, aims to raise $200 million through its initial public offering and emphasizes the strategic importance of developing a domestic U.S. supply of critical minerals for the clean energy transition.

title: MUFG Bank gets IFSCA nod to open a branch at GIFT City
summary: MUFG Bank has received approval from both Indian (IFSCA) and Japanese (FSA) regulators to open a branch at GIFT City, Gujarat, becoming the first Japanese bank to do so. This new branch will allow MUFG Bank to conduct foreign currency-denominated lending business from India, addressing diverse funding needs for clients and simplifying offshore business. The bank, which already operates five branches in India, plans to utilize this expanded network to offer enhanced financial services.

title: JPMorgan's co-head of UK investment banking has quit for PE
summary: David Lomer, co-head of M&A at JPMorgan and co-head of UK investment banking, has resigned to move into private equity. His departure follows the banking industry's bonus season and comes at a time when financial sponsors are a robust area in the M&A market. The move is significant given JPMorgan's fluctuating M&A revenues and his previous leadership roles within the firm.

title: BondBloxx Launches 3 High Yield Corporate Bond ETFs
summary: BondBloxx Investment Management has launched three new High Yield Corporate Bond ETFs, which began trading on NYSE Arca on May 26, 2022. These ETFs focus on specific credit ratings (BB, B, and CCC) within the high yield corporate bond market, building on seven sector-specific high yield ETFs launched earlier this year. The firm aims to provide investors with targeted tools to manage fixed-income exposure, especially in volatile markets.

title: Umivale Activa incorpora a SEAT S.A. a su Junta Directiva
summary: Umivale Activa, a mutual society collaborating with Social Security, held its Board of Directors meeting in Gijón, where Dr. Patricia Such, Director of Health, Safety, and Emergencies for SEAT, CUPRA, and Volkswagen Group companies in Spain, was appointed as the new vice-president. SEAT S.A. now joins the governing body responsible for the Mutua's management and administration. The article also highlights Dr. Such's extensive experience in occupational medicine and her leadership in combating COVID-19 within SEAT S.A., as well as Umivale Activa's key figures and commitment to health and safety management.

title: Retirement Industry People Moves
summary: This article details recent personnel changes and appointments within the retirement industry. Key moves include Eric Kristenson joining Cohen & Steers as a DCIO specialist, Eric Lareau expanding abrdn's institutional team, Aimee DeCamillo becoming Manulife Investment Management's new global head of retirement, Arezu Moghadam joining J.P. Morgan Asset Management as global head of data science, and Jessica Austin Barker being appointed TIAA's chief digital and client experience officer. Additionally, Securian Financial was selected as recordkeeper for the WELLthBUILDER Pooled Employer Plan by Strategic Retirement Partners.

title: Lights! Camera! Action! Pier 94 Could Make the Movies —If Developer Vornado Fulfills Promises
summary: Developer Vornado proposes a new 212,000-square-foot film and television studio at Pier 94 in Hell's Kitchen, complete with public amenities. However, Manhattan Community Board 4 is skeptical given Vornado's history of unfulfilled promises regarding the disrepair of adjacent Pier 92 and other community requests. The board insists Vornado address these structural issues and implement promised public amenities before approving the new project.

title: Concentrated, Yet Fragmented — Indian Banking Has A Split Personality
summary: The Indian banking sector, despite the recent merger of HDFC Bank and HDFC Ltd. leading to increased concentration at the top with SBI and the merged HDFC Bank dominating, remains fragmented beyond the top two players. A BQ Prime analysis indicates that while the two largest banks control a significant portion of advances, the rest of the sector is dispersed among numerous smaller banks. Experts suggest that having a few large "pillar banks" is beneficial for a growing economy, and the presence of many smaller lenders signifies a competitive environment rather than excessive concentration, with continued consolidation expected.

title: Abdul Kahsai Joins Pinnacle's Growing Restaurant and Franchise Team
summary: Pinnacle Financial Partners has expanded its restaurant and franchise finance team by adding Abdul Kahsai as an experienced banker. Based in Phoenix, Arizona, Kahsai will cover the Western U.S., focusing on franchised restaurant and fitness operators. He brings 15 years of financial services experience, having previously worked at JPMorgan Chase and GE Capital.

title: Nomura M&A Banker Chung Said to Join Crypto Firm Riot Blockchain
summary: Riot Blockchain Inc., a Bitcoin infrastructure company, has hired investment banker Jason Chung from Nomura Holdings Inc. as its head of corporate development. Chung, formerly a managing director at Nomura, will help oversee strategic transactions and financing strategy for the crypto firm. This move confirms an earlier Bloomberg News report.

title: PNC changing 1,000-plus branches to automated model - Bizwomen
summary: PNC Bank is converting over 1,000 of its branches, more than 60% of its network, to a new automated model by the end of 2026.
