This initiative will shift basic teller transactions to ATMs and video banking, allowing staff to focus on more in-depth customer conversations and financial guidance. While the conversion cost and savings are not disclosed, PNC emphasizes that overall branch employment is expected to remain consistent despite the changes.

title: Karen Krause Joins TransUnion as Chief Strategy and Communications Officer
summary: TransUnion (NYSE: TRU) has appointed Karen Krause as Executive Vice President, Chief Strategy and Communications Officer, effective June 1, 2022. Krause will be responsible for leading TransUnion’s Global Strategy, Communications, and Branding functions, focusing on transforming global platforms and products. She brings extensive experience from JPMorgan Chase, S&P Global, Goldman Sachs, TCR Private Equity, and McKinsey.

title: JPMorgan CEO Dimon calls for raising minimum wage, more education to address racial gaps
summary: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon advocates for raising the minimum wage, expanding education, and making mortgages more affordable to address racial gaps that cost the Columbus economy $10 billion annually. He also discusses the current economic outlook, noting a strong economy despite "storm clouds" like inflation, and emphasizes the importance of local initiatives and returning semiconductor production to the U.S.

title: AUD/USD Forex Technical Analysis – Sustained Move Under .7143 Puts .7029 on Radar
summary: The Australian Dollar is showing a bearish bias against the US Dollar due to inflation fears, slower economic growth, and warnings from JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon about an economic "hurricane." Technical analysis indicates that a sustained move below .7143 could lead the AUD/USD pair to .7029, while upcoming US economic data, particularly ADP Non-Farm Employment Change, will be crucial for market direction.

title: 2022 40 Under 40: JPMorgan Chase's Paul Drayton leads diversity hiring and engagement efforts
summary: Paul Drayton, an executive director in commercial banking at JPMorgan Chase in Orlando, has been recognized in the 2022 "40 Under 40" list for his leadership in diversity hiring and engagement efforts. The article highlights his professional achievements and includes a personal reflection about overcoming self-doubt. It also acknowledges other individuals from the 2022 "40 Under 40" class across various fields.

title: Jonathan Baliff Named Redwire CFO
summary: Jonathan Baliff, formerly chairman of Redwire’s audit committee, has been appointed as the new Chief Financial Officer of the space infrastructure technology company, succeeding Bill Read. Baliff was previously president of Genesis Park Acquisition, which merged with Redwire in September 2021, and has a background that includes leadership roles at Bristow Group and executive positions at Texas Capital Bancshares and NRG Energy. David Kornblatt will replace Baliff as the head of the board’s audit committee.

title: The SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust Is Still Overvalued
summary: The author argues that the recent surge in the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY) is premature because the S&P 500 remains overvalued. Utilizing the Fed Valuation Model and considering sector weightings, the article suggests that key metrics are not aligned for sustained index success in the near term, anticipating a plateau rather than a continued recovery. Divergent analyst opinions and a low VIX further support the uncertainty in the market.

title: Will Corporate Credits Crack as Growth Slows?
summary: Despite concerns about slowing global growth and central bank rate hikes, the article argues against a wave of corporate downgrades and defaults. It suggests that corporate balance sheets are healthier, the default cycle has cleaned up weaker companies, M&A risk is muted, and maturity runways have been extended, making corporates resilient to a slowdown. The article concludes that strong fundamentals and attractive valuations present a good opportunity for investors in corporate credit.

title: A paradigm shift has begun in markets, says Morgan Stanley's Ted Pick. Here's what to expect
summary: Morgan Stanley co-President Ted Pick states that global markets are experiencing a fundamental paradigm shift after 15 years of low interest rates and cheap corporate debt. This transition, influenced by the pandemic, war, and inflation, is expected to unfold over 12 to 24 months, leading to a new business cycle. Pick anticipates markets will be dominated by concerns of inflation ("fire") and recession ("ice"), requiring careful navigation from clients and impacting various banking businesses differently.

title: Fundos Mútuos de Privatização: o que são e como funcionam?
summary: Os Fundos Mútuos de Privatização (FMP) permitem que recursos do FGTS sejam usados para investir em ações de empresas estatais em processo de privatização ou capitalização, como a Eletrobras. Este mecanismo oferece diversificação para o saldo do FGTS e amplia o capital para ofertas públicas, embora concentre o risco em um único ativo e exija um prazo mínimo de resgate de um ano. A tributação é isenta para rendimentos até o limite do FGTS.

title: NYCB, Flagstar to drop NSF and certain overdraft fees
summary: New York Community Bank (NYCB) and Flagstar Bank are eliminating nonsufficient fund (NSF) fees and making other changes to their overdraft policies, effective August 1. These changes include removing overdraft transfer fees and limiting daily overdraft charges, aligning with an industry trend to move away from punitive fee models. The banks, which announced a merger in October 2021, are still navigating regulatory approvals for the tie-up.

title: Republicans plan legislative assault on ‘woke’ ESG firms
summary: Republicans are set to introduce legislation targeting environmental, social, and governance (ESG) investing, aiming to push corporations away from pro-climate policies and back towards fossil fuels. This move follows a growing anti-ESG sentiment in red states and is spurred by concerns that investment firms like BlackRock are prioritizing social agendas over fiduciary responsibilities. Key proposals include requiring passive investment funds to vote proxies based on individual investor wishes and ensuring retirement plans prioritize financial returns over sustainability.

title: Talkspace CFO: Cerebral's Controlled Substances Pivot Could Create More Daylight in Virtual Mental Health Market
summary: Talkspace CFO Jennifer Fulk believes that Cerebral's pivot away from prescribing controlled substances could create new opportunities for Talkspace in the virtual mental health market. Talkspace has never prescribed controlled substances and sees Cerebral's recent issues as a potential advantage due to its focus on a full-stack behavioral health care platform. The article also touches on Talkspace's financial turnaround plan and analyst speculation about it being an acquisition target.

title: WOTM : Rebecca Thornton
summary: Rebecca Thornton, Head of Director Advisory Services at JPMorgan Chase & Co., discusses the art and science of diversifying corporate boards with Women on the Move host Sam Saperstein. Her team, formed in 2016 by Jamie Dimon, acts as a central clearinghouse connecting diverse board candidates with client needs. Thornton also offers advice for aspiring board members on building their brand and networking, acknowledging practical roadblocks but emphasizing the positive impact of increased diversity.

title: Go Active as Investors Dive Back Into Corporate Bonds
summary: The bond market, particularly corporate bonds, is showing signs of recovery after a downturn, leading investors to cautiously re-enter the market for potential bargains. Active management, such as through the American Century Diversified Corporate Bond ETF (KORP), is suggested as a way for wary investors to navigate the changing corporate bond landscape and balance risk. This approach allows for dynamic adjustments to investment-grade and high-yield components, aiming for current income while managing interest rate and credit risk.

title: Green business models needed for change | JPMorgan Chase
summary: The article discusses the growing trend of green business models, where companies integrate environmental stewardship and social impact with profitability. It highlights how businesses like Daring Foods and Sunnova Energy International are balancing purpose and profits, driven by increasing awareness of climate change and social inequities. JPMorgan Chase is also actively involved in promoting a sustainable economy, aiming to finance and facilitate $1 trillion for green initiatives over ten years.

title: BHP-Woodside: What a block: Why the year’s biggest trade has divided the street
summary: BHP tasked JPMorgan with managing the year's largest block trade, involving the sale of 38 million Woodside shares worth $1.1 billion to BHP investors outside Australia. The transaction has sparked controversy due to its opaque nature and concerns that foreign shareholders were not adequately represented. This event highlights the challenges of large-scale share transfers conducted away from direct stock exchange scrutiny.

title: Bud, an open banking fintech used by HSBC, raises £64m
summary: Bud, a London-based open banking fintech that utilizes AI to automate lending decisions and provide customized financial products, has successfully raised $80m (£63.8m) in a Series B funding round. The capital will be used to enhance its platform and support international expansion. Bud's services are currently employed by major financial institutions like HSBC and Credit Karma.

title: Accepting her inner truth and sparking joy, from iconic toy company co-founder Melissa Bernstein
summary: Melissa Bernstein, co-founder of Melissa and Doug Toys, discusses her journey of self-discovery, fueled by a diagnosis of existential angst. She explains how this led her to co-found LifeLines, a company focused on wellbeing and helping others find meaning through self-expression, stemming from her own experiences of channeling her struggles into creative endeavors.

title: Conservative shareholders attack ‘climate clown show’
summary: Conservative shareholder activists are increasing their efforts to push back against environmental, social, and governance (ESG) initiatives in corporations. They have filed twice as many proposals this year compared to 2021, though most have failed to gain significant shareholder support. These activists aim to counter the influence of sustainable investment advocates by making their voices heard in the press and with corporate leadership, even if their proposals do not pass.

title: S&P Global, Argus invest in oil blockchain VAKT that’s planning tokenization
summary: S&P Global and Argus Media have invested in VAKT, a blockchain-based post-trade solution for the oil sector, which previously raised $57 million. These benchmark pricing firms join existing heavyweight shareholders from the energy and banking sectors. The key motivation for their involvement is VAKT's confirmed plan to tokenize oil contracts in the future, promising enhanced information and intelligence flows for energy and commodity markets.

title: MoneyGram Launches Pioneering Global Crypto-to-Cash Service on the Stellar Network
summary: MoneyGram and the Stellar Development Foundation have launched a pioneering global crypto-to-cash service on the Stellar Network, creating a bridge between cash and cryptocurrencies. This service allows users to convert digital assets like USDC into cash and vice versa through MoneyGram's retail network, initially available in Canada, Kenya, the Philippines, and the U.S. It aims to enhance financial inclusion by enabling seamless transitions between physical and digital currencies for nearly 2 billion people who rely on cash, and will be offered with zero fees for the first 12 months.

title: ¿Cuánto valen las oficinas del Santander en el centro de Santiago?: Banco pondrá a la venta su actual edificio corporativo
summary: Banco Santander plans to sell its current corporate headquarters in downtown Santiago after deciding to relocate to a new building in Las Condes. The fiscal appraisal for the two addresses of the current building, Bandera 140 and Bandera 150, totals approximately $70 billion Chilean pesos. Real estate agents anticipate a challenging sale due to an oversupply of office space in the city center.

title: Bank of New York Mellon Corp. stock outperforms market despite losses on the day
summary: Bank of New York Mellon Corp. (BK) stock experienced a 2.84% drop on Friday, June 10, 2022, closing at $42.79, amidst a general market downturn. Despite its losses and marking its third consecutive day of decline, the stock outperformed major competitors like JPMorgan Chase & Co., Citigroup Inc., and Wells Fargo & Co., which saw larger percentage drops. The company's stock is currently $21.84 short of its 52-week high of $64.63.

title: Walmart struggles to solve consumer needs in China
summary: Walmart has faced persistent challenges in the Chinese market since opening its first store in 1996, struggling to compete with local retailers known for their diverse product offerings and fast home deliveries. The company's large hypermarket format is not appealing to Chinese consumers who prefer online shopping and local products. Additionally, Walmart has found itself navigating complex political tensions, including controversies over product sourcing from Xinjiang and increased regulatory scrutiny, despite China being crucial for its manufacturing supply chain and for observing e-commerce trends.

title: Police investigate Friday morning Anderson bank robbery
summary: Anderson police are investigating an armed bank robbery that occurred Friday morning at Old National Bank. A man in his 20s passed a note demanding money and fled on foot with an undisclosed amount of cash. No arrests have been made, and police are asking for the public's help with information.

title: Morgan Stanley CEO James Gorman sees 50-50 odds of recession ahead
summary: Morgan Stanley CEO James Gorman believes there's a 50-50 chance of a recession, an increase from his previous 30% estimate, but he doesn't expect it to be deep or long. He noted that the Federal Reserve waited too long to raise rates, which limits their options if a recession hits. Despite market downturns, Gorman finds comfort in the strong fundamentals of consumer and corporate balance sheets.

title: West Virginia threatens to bar big banks, Blackrock over perceived fossil fuel boycotts
summary: West Virginia is threatening to bar six major financial institutions, including JPMorgan Chase and BlackRock, from doing business with the state. State Treasurer Riley Moore issued letters to these firms, accusing them of boycotting the fossil fuel industry, which is a significant part of West Virginia's economy. This move is part of a broader pushback by Republican-led states against environmental, social, and corporate governance (ESG) policies that they believe discriminate against certain industries.

title: Citi Hires Hofmann From JPMorgan to Oversee Family-Office Group
summary: Citigroup Inc. has hired Hannes Hofmann from JPMorgan Chase & Co. to lead its family-office group, signaling its intent to expand business with high-net-worth individuals. Hofmann, who previously headed JPMorgan's multifamily office and intermediaries for various regions, will be based in London and report to private-banking chief Ida Liu starting in September. This move highlights Citi's strategic focus on the family-office segment as a critical client base.

title: Six key takeaways from EBAday 2022
summary: EBAday 2022 highlighted six key trends shaping the future of payments: the rapid evolution driven by APIs, the potential of Banking-as-a-Service and Payments-as-a-Service despite integration challenges, the limitations of digital currencies as a complete solution for international payments, and the ongoing improvements by SWIFT initiatives like gpi, Go, and ISO 20022. The conference also discussed the rise of instant and invisible payments and stressed the importance of the new Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) for banks and their technology vendors. These topics are expected to continue to evolve and remain central to future discussions in the payments industry.

title: J.P. Morgan Asset Management Completes Conversion of Four Mutual Funds to ETFs
summary: J.P. Morgan Asset Management has successfully converted four mutual funds into ETFs, including the new JPMorgan International Research Enhanced Equity ETF (JIRE), expanding its active ETF lineup to 22 strategies. This move, which involved approximately $9 billion in combined assets, aims to provide investors with more active investment options offering increased flexibility, transparency, and potentially reduced fees. The firm now manages 44 U.S. ETFs with over $75 billion in assets under management.

title: LATAM Airlines Seeks $2.75b Loan to Exit Chap.11 Bankruptcy Status
summary: LATAM Airlines Group SA is seeking approval for $2.75 billion in new loans to finance its exit from Chapter 11 bankruptcy. The airline has secured commitments from several major banks and an additional agreement to refinance existing loans. This financing is crucial for the company to complete its restructuring plan and proceed with a post-bankruptcy equity offering.

title: Prologis to add 9.6 million square feet in New Jersey with Duke Realty acquisition
summary: Prologis Inc. will acquire Duke Realty Corp. in an all-stock, $26 billion transaction, significantly expanding its industrial footprint in New Jersey by 9.6 million square feet. The merger, unanimously approved by both boards, will add nearly 10 million square feet to Prologis's New Jersey portfolio and includes 150 million square feet of combined industrial space across 19 major U.S. markets. Duke Realty shareholders will receive 0.475 of a Prologis share for each share they own.

title: BNY Mellon Wealth Management Named Tom Assad as Senior Client Strategist in Boston
summary: BNY Mellon Wealth Management has appointed Tom Assad as Senior Client Strategist in Boston. Assad will focus on ultra-high-net-worth families, business owners, and corporate executives, leveraging his over three decades of experience in financial services. He joins BNY Mellon from Wells Fargo Private Bank and will report to Matt Santangelo, head of Client Strategies and Business Development, New England.

title: ACLEDA Bank Plc. Partners with MoneyGram to Enable Cross-Border Remittances via ACLEDA Mobile
summary: ACLEDA Bank Plc. has announced a partnership with MoneyGram International, Inc. to enable cross-border remittances via the ACLEDA mobile app. This collaboration allows customers in Cambodia to send money to over 200 countries and territories and receive international transfers directly through the app, with future plans for cash services at bank branches. The partnership aims to enhance financial inclusion and provide fast, convenient, and reliable money transfer solutions for customers.

title: Crypto bank Protego beefs up advisory board
summary: Protego Trust Bank, a federally chartered crypto bank, has expanded its advisory board with five new Wall Street veterans, including former State Street Corporation chairman and CEO Jay Hooley. This move comes as the company prepares for a full launch later this year and seeks further financing at a reported $2 billion valuation. Protego aims to combine traditional banking knowledge with new financial opportunities for institutional clients.

title: JPMorgan Packed Its Wealthy Clients Into Tiger Global Fund for Private Bets
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. facilitated wealthy clients' investments into Tiger Global Management's private bets, pooling approximately $4.8 billion for venture capital funds with Tiger and Coatue. This strategy, once a point of envy for rivals, is now seen in a different light as Tiger's public investments decline. The article highlights how major banks are helping such vehicles raise significant capital.

title: Associated Banc-Corp recruits two Huntington executives for top posts
summary: Associated Banc-Corp CEO Andy Harmening has hired two former Huntington Bancshares colleagues, Derek Meyer and Bryan Carson, for key executive positions. Meyer will become CFO, and Carson will serve as chief product and marketing officer, bringing decades of combined industry experience to the Green Bay-based company. These appointments aim to strengthen Associated's financial and marketing strategies, with a focus on liquidity, digital innovation, and expanding customer relationships.

title: FTX Acquires Alberta-Based Restricted Dealer to Expand Canadian Presence
summary: FTX Trading Limited announced its agreement to acquire Bitvo, Inc., an Alberta-based crypto asset trading platform registered as a restricted dealer in Canada. This acquisition marks FTX's expansion into the Canadian market, aiming to provide its services to global customers in a regulated manner. The move reflects FTX's proactive approach to working with cryptocurrency regulators internationally and is expected to close in Q3 2022.

title: Visa Inc. completes €3.0bn cross-border offering of senior notes | Vietnam | Global law firm
summary: Visa Inc. has completed a €3.0 billion cross-border offering of senior notes, facilitated by Norton Rose Fulbright's Toronto office. The offering included notes due in 2026, 2029, and 2034, with net proceeds intended for general corporate purposes. The issuance involved a syndicate of underwriters including major financial institutions.

title: Dragon Capital kicks off investment products on MoMo e-wallet
summary: Dragon Capital Vietnam Fund Management (DCVFM) has partnered with MoMo e-wallet to launch fund certificate trading directly on the super-app platform. This collaboration marks the first time open-ended fund certificate trading is available on a super-app in Vietnam, allowing users to open accounts and invest without additional bank accounts or transfer fees. This initiative aims to make diverse investment products accessible to MoMo's over 31 million users.

title: Banks diversity push sees Citigroup recruit associates in U.S. from outside finance
summary: Citigroup has launched a pilot program to recruit U.S. associates from non-traditional backgrounds and underrepresented minorities, aiming to boost diversity and address talent competition. The program brings in individuals without prior banking experience or business degrees, including lawyers, a dentist, and an engineer, with eight out of ten recruits not having attended business school. This initiative is designed to broaden Citi's talent pool and leverage diverse sector-specific expertise within its investment and corporate banking teams.

title: Mining billionaire Robert Friedland launches IPO for Ivanhoe Electric
summary: Billionaire Robert Friedland is launching an initial public offering (IPO) for Ivanhoe Electric Inc., aiming to raise US$180-million. The Vancouver-based company will focus on supplying copper and other critical minerals for electric cars and clean-energy technology, with properties in Arizona and Utah. This IPO marks a significant event in a quiet market, with shares planned for listing on both the Toronto and New York stock exchanges.

title: Activists Target Nelson Peltz’s Trian Over U.K. Fund
summary: A group of investors, including two former targets of Nelson Peltz's activism, is pushing for significant changes at a London-listed investment vehicle managed by Trian Fund Management LP. They argue that the company has strayed from its initial purpose since going public and are seeking an extraordinary general meeting to replace current directors.

title: Big US Banks Led by JPMorgan (NYSE:JPM) Set to Return $80 Billion to Investors
summary: US banking giants, led by JPMorgan Chase & Co., are expected to return $80 billion to shareholders after the Federal Reserve's stress tests. This amount is less than the previous year's elevated returns, which followed a pandemic-induced buyback pause. JPMorgan is projected to lead with $18.9 billion in shareholder returns, with Bank of America and Wells Fargo also making significant returns.

title: Use Alternative ETFs to Hedge Against Further Bumps Down the Road
summary: As financial strategists warn of potential further declines in the S&P 500 amid recession fears and complacent investors, hedge funds are already increasing bearish wagers. The article suggests inverse exchange-traded funds (ETFs) as a strategy for traders to protect their portfolios against market pullbacks. It highlights specific inverse ETFs targeting the S&P 500, Dow Jones Industrial Average, and Nasdaq-100, including both standard and leveraged options.

title: Southern First rolls out new HQ to customers, community
summary: Southern First Bank has unveiled its new five-story, 107,000-square-foot headquarters in Greenville, designed to be warm, welcoming, and progressive, aiming to redefine traditional bank architecture. The new building provides ample space for employees, clients, and community events, reflecting the bank's commitment to its community and its future growth. CEO Art Seaver emphasizes the building as a statement of belief in the future and a tool for recruiting top talent, affirming the bank's long-term vision and client-first mentality.

title: $1.5 Trillion Asset Manager Northern Trust Creates Digital Assets Group To Meet Growing Demand
summary: Northern Trust, a $1.5 trillion asset manager, has established a new Digital Assets and Financial Markets Group to help traditional investors gain exposure to digital assets. This move combines digital asset markets with traditional securities services, demonstrating continued institutional interest in the crypto space despite recent market downturns. The firm has a history of blockchain involvement, including supporting Bitcoin and Ethereum investors and co-launching a crypto administration firm.

title: JPMorgan Chase Reducing Its Mortgage Staff
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. announced layoffs and reassignments in its mortgage business due to slowing housing market conditions caused by inflation and rising mortgage rates. Over 1,000 employees are affected, with about half being moved to other internal divisions. This follows similar job cuts by other real estate companies and comes after the Federal Reserve's significant interest rate hike.

title: Updated: BofA, Morgan Stanley, Wells Join List of Banks Covering Employees’ Abortion Travel Costs
summary: Following the U.S. Supreme Court's overturning of Roe v. Wade, Bank of America, Morgan Stanley, and Wells Fargo have announced they will reimburse employees' travel expenses for abortion-related healthcare. These banks join others like JPMorgan Chase, Deutsche Bank, Goldman Sachs, and Citigroup, in implementing policies to support employees seeking such services in states where they may become restricted. The move aims to align benefits with diverse healthcare needs amidst changing legal landscapes.

title: JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs and Other Big Banks Will Now Cover Travel Expenses for Employee Abortions
summary: Following the Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade, several major banks including JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs, Bank of America, and Morgan Stanley announced they will cover travel expenses for employees seeking abortions. These companies already offer abortion coverage in their medical benefits but are extending it to include travel to ensure equitable access to healthcare for their nationwide workforce, especially considering new state-level restrictions on abortion access. Citigroup had made a similar announcement earlier in the year in response to Texas laws.

title: Dick's Sporting Goods CEO announces travel expense reimbursement to employees seeking abortions in another state
summary: Following the Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade, Dick's Sporting Goods CEO Lauren Hobart announced that the company will provide up to $4,000 in travel expense reimbursement for employees and their dependents who need to travel to another state for abortion access. This benefit is intended to ensure consistent healthcare options regardless of where employees live and will also cover one support person. Pennsylvania Governor Tom Wolf applauded Dick's Sporting Goods for its swift action, and other companies like JPMorgan Chase have also announced similar plans.

title: ICICI Bank Offers Among The Best Risk-Reward Globally, Says Jefferies
summary: Jefferies believes ICICI Bank offers one of the best risk-reward ratios globally due to its high return-on-assets and strong positioning for Indian bank credit growth. The firm maintains a 'buy' rating on the stock with a target price of Rs 1,070, citing projected profit CAGR of 17% over FY22-24 and an ROE of 16%. ICICI Bank is also one of only two Nifty Bank constituents with unanimous 'buy' recommendations from analysts.

title: JPMorgan Chase Joins Companies Paying Employees Who Travel for Abortions
summary: JPMorgan Chase announced it would cover travel expenses for employees needing to travel out of state for abortions, expanding a benefit that covers services unavailable near an employee's home. This decision follows the Supreme Court's overturning of Roe v. Wade and aligns JPMorgan with other companies like Citigroup, Starbucks, Amazon, Tesla, and Yelp making similar pledges. The move addresses the implications of state-level abortion bans, with many states poised to restrict or ban abortions following the ruling.

title: Why Tech Mahindra, Wipro & Other IT Stocks Are Destroying Investor Wealth
summary: Indian IT stocks, including Tech Mahindra and Wipro, have seen a significant correction since early 2022 after two years of strong growth. This downturn is attributed to expensive valuations, margin contraction, high attrition rates leading to salary hikes, and concerns over decelerating revenue growth amid an anticipated US economic slowdown. Despite these challenges, some analysts believe the current valuations present an attractive buying opportunity for long-term investors.

title: JP Morgan, Disney join wave of companies that'll cover employee abortion travel costs
summary: Following the Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade, numerous companies, including JPMorgan Chase and Disney, announced they would cover travel expenses for employees needing to go out-of-state for abortion services. This decision aligns with a prior trend seen among other corporations after a leaked opinion indicated the potential overturning of the federal protection. Companies like Dick's Sporting Goods and Condé Nast also detailed their plans to support employees' access to reproductive healthcare, with some even extending support to include bail for peaceful protestors.

title: JPMorgan, Citi, Goldman, Wells Fargo and Bank of America will cover out-of-state abortion costs for employees
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co., Bank of America Corp., Goldman Sachs Group Inc., Wells Fargo & Co. and Citigroup Inc. have all announced that they will cover out-of-state travel expenses for employees seeking abortions. This decision comes in the wake of the U.S. Supreme Court's ruling to overturn Roe v. Wade. These major banks join other large corporations in offering such benefits.

title: Nike, Alaska Airlines, Dick's Sporting Goods and others covering travel costs for abortions
summary: Following the Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade, numerous major corporations, including Nike, Alaska Airlines, and Dick's Sporting Goods, have announced they will cover travel expenses for employees seeking out-of-state abortions. These companies, such as JPMorgan, Starbucks, Microsoft, and Tesla, emphasize their commitment to supporting employee healthcare and ensuring access to essential medical services regardless of state restrictions. Some companies are also extending these benefits to include travel and lodging for other medical treatments and gender-affirming care if not available locally.

title: Katrina Evans
summary: Katrina Evans, Executive Vice President at KeyCorp, is highlighted for her 30-plus years of adventurous leadership and significant contributions to the company. She has spearheaded growth in marketing, communications, and analytics, orchestrated expansion of a multibillion-dollar community benefits plan, and fostered diversity, equity, and inclusion initiatives. Her leadership style emphasizes authenticity and empowering others.

title: Ivanhoe Electric Announces Pricing of Initial Public Offering
summary: Ivanhoe Electric Inc. has announced the pricing of its initial public offering (IPO) of 14,388,000 shares of common stock at US$11.75 per share, aiming to raise approximately US$169.1 million. The shares are expected to begin trading on the NYSE American and Toronto Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol "IE" on June 28, 2022. Proceeds from the offering will be used to fund payments for mineral and property rights, further metals exploration, construct Typhoon™ electrical pulse-powered geophysical surveying technology, and cover working capital and administrative costs.

title: BlackRock joins Wall Street firms in covering employees' abortion travel costs: Internal memo
summary: BlackRock (BLK) is expanding its health care plan to cover travel expenses for U.S. employees seeking abortion services, following an internal memo. This decision aligns BlackRock with other major Wall Street firms like Jefferies Financial Group, Wells Fargo, JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, and Citigroup, which have made similar commitments in response to the overturning of Roe v. Wade. The firms are covering travel and lodging costs for reproductive services, treating them similarly to other specialized medical care.

title: Are Bank Stocks Undervalued?
summary: Despite fears of a potential recession driving down bank stock prices, many high-quality banks appear undervalued, trading at a significant discount compared to historical recession lows. Rising net interest margins due to Federal Reserve rate hikes could provide a tailwind, which analysts believe is not being fully priced into current valuations. Long-term investors may find attractive opportunities in these undervalued bank stocks, particularly those with wide economic moats like Wells Fargo, JPMorgan Chase, U.S. Bancorp, and Bank of America.

title: Building Wealth and Starting Legacies: Women of Color Shape Their Own Futures
summary: JPMorgan Chase is supporting Zora's House in Columbus, Ohio, a co-working space and leadership incubator for women of color, with two philanthropic investments. These investments launched a financial health program and a 24-month equitable design institute aimed at empowering women of color to build wealth, address systemic inequities, and create sustainable solutions for their communities. The initiative is part of JPMorgan Chase's $30 billion commitment to close the racial wealth gap and advance economic inclusion.

title: JPMorgan Chase walks it like they talk it at the Wealth Summit in Dallas
summary: JPMorgan Chase hosted a Black & Hispanic Wealth Summit in Dallas, demonstrating its commitment to empowering these communities through financial literacy and access to capital. The event featured discussions with financial experts and celebrities on wealth building, entrepreneurship, and addressing systemic financial barriers. This summit is part of Chase's broader Advancing Black Pathways and Advancing Hispanics & Latinos initiatives, including a $30 billion commitment to advancing racial equity.

title: Abortion assistance: Kroger to offer up to $4,000 of out-of-state travel costs for employees seeking abortion
summary: Kroger announced it will offer up to $4,000 to cover out-of-state travel costs for employees seeking abortion and fertility treatments, following the Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade. The company, headquartered in Cincinnati, operates stores in states like Ohio and Kentucky where abortion is now banned or mostly banned. This move aligns Kroger with nearly two dozen other major U.S. companies providing similar assistance.

title: State Street, Wells Fargo to Cover Travel Costs for Employee Abortions
summary: State Street Corp. and Wells Fargo, along with other financial firms, are modifying their employee benefits to include coverage for travel costs associated with abortions. This decision comes in response to the U.S. Supreme Court's overturning of Roe v. Wade, following similar moves by other large corporations like Citigroup and JP Morgan Chase. Many major employers are rethinking benefit plans in states where abortion access is now restricted or unavailable.

title: Fintech Firm PolySign Raises $53M to Expand Staff
summary: Fintech firm PolySign has successfully closed a $53 million Series C funding round with investments from Cowen Digital, Brevan Howard, and GSR, and also secured an additional $25 million credit facility. This capital infusion will primarily be used to significantly increase its workforce by 20% to 30%, recruiting talent from both the crypto and traditional finance sectors. The funding follows PolySign's recent acquisition of fund administrator MG Stover and aims to further expand its institutional-grade custody and fund administration services.

title: Frosch is thrilled about JPMorgan Chase's acquisition of the agency
summary: Frosch executives express excitement and pride regarding JPMorgan Chase's acquisition of the travel agency, viewing it as a strong validation of the travel advisor industry. JPMorgan Chase stated the acquisition makes them a top-five U.S. consumer travel provider and highlights their strategy to own their travel destiny, especially concerning their card business and customer spending habits. The acquisition is expected to provide Frosch with enhanced resources, including cybersecurity, and open up new client opportunities, particularly in high-net-worth categories.

title: JPMorgan Chase Opens First Birmingham Branch, With Help of HBCU Grad
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. has opened its first full-service banking center in Birmingham, with Racquel Oden, Head of Consumer Bank Network Expansion, playing a key role. Oden, who received an MBA from Hampton University, emphasized the bank's commitment to community engagement and financial literacy, reflecting her personal passion and the success of Chase's community-style branches across the country. The new branch aims to be an integral part of the local community, offering banking services while supporting financial health and literacy initiatives.

title: Cleartrace Raises $20 Million Financing Led by ClearSky With Strategic Funding From Brookfield Renewable, EDF Energy North America, Tenaska, and Exelon to Help Companies Reach Decarbonization Goals
summary: Cleartrace, a carbon and energy management software company, has raised $20 million in a financing round led by ClearSky, with strategic investments from Brookfield Renewable, EDF Energy North America, Tenaska, and Exelon. This funding will accelerate the growth of Cleartrace’s advanced carbon and energy management platform, which provides auditable and assurance-ready proof of decarbonization for clients including real estate portfolios, financial institutions, and data centers. The platform offers 100% traceable and actionable hourly energy and carbon records, helping companies achieve and report on their decarbonization goals.

title: JPMorgan Chase Dedicates Resources to Closing Equity Gaps
summary: JPMorgan Chase is dedicating resources to close racial wealth gaps in underserved communities, starting in Bridgeport, Connecticut. The company has hired Eduardo Cabrera as a local ambassador to engage with the community and offer financial literacy workshops as part of its $30 billion Racial Equity Commitment initiative. This effort includes previous investments in affordable housing.

title: BP, Shell to cover employee travel for treatment after Roe v. Wade
summary: BP PLC has joined Shell PLC in committing to cover employee travel expenses for healthcare treatment following the Supreme Court's overturning of Roe v. Wade. Both European oil producers updated their healthcare plans to extend benefits for women needing to travel for services, though neither explicitly named abortion. This move comes as other major companies like Amazon, JPMorgan Chase, Tesla, and Walt Disney also updated their policies to cover travel costs for out-of-state abortion services, while U.S. oil majors have largely remained silent.

title: FGMC owes Customers Bank $25M, bankruptcy filing shows
summary: First Guaranty Mortgage Corp. (FGMC) and its holding company, Maverick II Holdings LLC, have filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy, listing Customers Bank as its largest unsecured creditor with a $25 million claim. Customers Bank, a major warehouse lender, expects to be fully repaid as the debt is guaranteed by a PIMCO entity. FGMC's CEO stated the bankruptcy was necessary due to challenges in the mortgage market, and the company is seeking debtor-in-possession financing from Barclays Bank PLC.

title: BMO and Jefferies Sign On to Platform Bringing AI Auctions to Stocks
summary: OneChronos Markets LLC has launched a new trading platform that uses AI-powered automated auctions for equities, with Bank of Montreal and Jefferies Financial Group Inc. among its initial partners. The platform allows institutional investors to submit "expressive" bids, defining the value they place on stock portfolios, aiming to revolutionize traditional stock trading.

title: PNC Financial Services Group closing branch at PNC Park in Pittsburgh - Pittsburgh Business Times
summary: PNC Financial Services Group is closing its branch located at PNC Park in Pittsburgh as of September 23, 2022. This closure is part of a larger plan by PNC to cut four branches, all of which will cease operations on the same date. The branch closing is notable given that PNC Park shares the bank's name.

title: Walker & Dunlop Adds Betsy Blau, Ryan Smith to Affordable Lending Team in Nashville
summary: Walker & Dunlop has expanded its Nashville affordable housing finance team by adding Ryan Smith as senior director and Betsy Blau as associate director. Smith and Blau bring nearly 30 years of combined experience from Colliers Mortgage, having financed over $2.5 billion in commercial real estate assets. Their addition is part of Walker & Dunlop's strategic expansion in affordable housing debt and equity offerings, following their acquisition of Alliant Capital in 2021.

title: An ecosystem system approach to investing, with Techstars CEO Maëlle Gavet
summary: Maëlle Gavet, CEO of Techstars, discusses the company's ecosystem approach to investing and its commitment to diversifying tech funding, particularly for women and underrepresented founders. Techstars implements accelerators and catalyst programs globally, partnering with various entities to build a supportive environment for entrepreneurs. Gravet also highlights the importance of networking and financial support for female entrepreneurs, referencing a partnership with J.P. Morgan to increase funding opportunities for diverse founders.

title: Podcast avec Caroline DELANGLE
summary: This article announces a podcast featuring Caroline DELANGLE, Head of Cross Asset Solutions at Federal Finance Gestion. The podcast will discuss Federal Indiciel US, a fund created in 2002 to track the performance of the S&P 500. The article also provides extensive financial data for numerous funds across various risk profiles.

title: Banks Get Burned by Risky Debt, Imperiling Buyout Activity
summary: Investment banks, including Bank of America, Credit Suisse, and Goldman Sachs, are facing potential losses of billions of dollars on leveraged buyout loans they committed to finance before market conditions deteriorated. These losses are expected to further cool down deal-making activity in the market. The banks agreed to provide these loans when demand for such debt was high, but the market has since soured.

title: Investors hoard cash at the highest rate in almost a decade
summary: Investors are rapidly accumulating cash, exceeding pandemic-era levels, as they seek refuge from volatile market conditions and prepare for potential opportunities. This shift towards liquid capital, including cash and cash-like ETFs, indicates poor investor sentiment and a preference for cash preservation despite inflation. While some strategists advise against timing the market, the trend highlights deep-seated recession fears and a desire for lower-volatility exposures.

title: MineHub shoots for commercial viability with BHP contract
summary: MineHub has secured its first commercial agreement with global resources company BHP, making BHP a paying customer of its blockchain-based platform for mining logistics. This agreement marks a significant milestone for MineHub, transitioning it into a revenue-generating company and demonstrating the viability of digital industry platforms in the mining sector. The company plans to secure additional commercial agreements with other large industry players this year.

title: TD in talks to buy US brokerage Cowen
summary: TD Bank is reportedly in discussions to acquire Cowen, a Wall Street brokerage firm, as it seeks to expand its U.S. operations further. This potential deal follows TD's earlier announcement to buy First Horizon Bank and aligns with a broader trend of Canadian lenders expanding into the U.S. If the acquisition proceeds, it would significantly boost TD Securities' investment banking capabilities, with Cowen having served as a bookrunner for numerous IPOs.

title: Brookfield Lays Out Infra Secondaries Strategy
summary: Brookfield is launching a "sponsor solutions" secondaries strategy focused on GP-originated deals in the middle market, aiming to provide advisory services and capital deployment to smaller deal originators. This approach, which avoids the need to build a large internal mid-market team, allows Brookfield to invest alongside existing sponsors and leverage their access to deal flow and asset management capabilities. The strategy will target OECD member countries, particularly Europe and North America, with equity checks ranging from USD 100m to USD 500m, and has already executed two deals.

title: Mounting pay pressure at banks as Truist, JPMorgan hike minimum wages
summary: Amidst a tight job market and high inflation, major banks like Truist and JPMorgan Chase are increasing their minimum hourly wages for employees, following a trend set by other large financial institutions. These wage hikes are seen as crucial investments to retain talent and reduce turnover, although they may slightly impact bank earnings. The industry recognizes the need to stay competitive by offering better pay and benefits, while also emphasizing culture and career advancement opportunities.

title: Erin Robert
summary: This article introduces Erin Robert as the Managing Director and Head of Impact Finance at JPMorgan Chase, housed within the company's Corporate Responsibility division. Her role involves executing financial products to advance JPMC's social and environmental impact objectives, including offering low-cost debt to impact-focused financial intermediaries and making equity investments in mission-driven companies. Robert's background includes various roles in J.P. Morgan's Corporate and Investment Bank, starting in Public Finance and later leading the Commodities Structuring team for the Americas.

title: Productos Life de Banco Santander superan el millón de clientes
summary: Banco Santander Chile announced that its Life family of accounts has surpassed one million clients, marking a significant milestone in financial inclusion. The Life products, primarily the Cuenta Corriente Life, aim to provide accessible banking services without minimum income requirements. These products, which include various tiers like Plan Santander Life and Plan Santander Life – LATAM Pass, offer a range of benefits and also incorporate the Meritolife program to reward good financial behavior.

title: Highest FD interest rates: SBI, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, POTD compared, check here
summary: Fixed deposit interest rates are rising after the RBI hiked repo rates to combat inflation. While SBI, HDFC Bank, and ICICI Bank have increased their FD rates, the interest rates on small savings schemes like the Post Office Term Deposit (POTD) remained unchanged for the July-September quarter. This article compares the current FD rates offered by banks with those of POTD, showing that for three-five year FDs, POTD offers significantly better interest rates.

title: Proof Point: Canada’s economy is headed for a recession
summary: RBC Economics predicts Canada's economy will experience a moderate and short-lived recession in 2023 due to inflation, labor shortages, and rising interest rates. While the jobless rate will increase, it is expected to be less severe than in previous downturns, and the higher interest rates are deemed necessary to control inflation. The authors suggest that this economic contraction will be reversible once inflation subsides, allowing central banks to ease rates.

title: UBS, Edward Jones And Others Keep Mum About Covering Abortion Travel Costs
summary: Following the Supreme Court's overturning of Roe v. Wade, many large banks announced they would cover employee travel costs for abortions. However, numerous brokerage firms, including Edward Jones, Ameriprise Financial, Raymond James Financial, Stifel, Nicolaus & Co., Charles Schwab, and UBS Wealth Management USA, have either remained silent or declined to comment on their policies. This silence is attributed to the conservative leanings of many brokers, the "lose-lose situation" of taking a public stance, and legal uncertainties surrounding such benefits in restrictive states.

title: 78% of Americans fear losing their job ahead of recession
summary: A recent survey by Insight Global reveals that 78% of American workers fear losing their jobs due to an impending recession. This fear is more prevalent among managers, and over half of all workers would consider taking a pay cut to avoid layoffs, despite high inflation. Several major companies, including JPMorgan Chase, Coinbase, Netflix, and Tesla, have already conducted significant layoffs, with more expected as economic uncertainty continues.

title: EM Gutsy Policy Moves Keep Coming
summary: This article discusses the "gutsy" policy moves being made in Emerging Markets (EM), highlighting both positive and negative examples. It details significant interest rate hikes in Hungary and Mexico to combat inflation and currency weakness, contrasting them with Poland's more modest increase. The piece also touches on China's infrastructure-oriented bond sales, questioning its impact on balanced recovery and Europe's potential piggybacking.

title: Fully leased, Class A office building in Dallas changes hands
summary: JLL Capital Markets facilitated the sale of 1925 West John Carpenter, a fully leased Class A office building located in Las Colinas, Dallas. The transaction highlights continued investment in the office real estate market. The building is considered a prime asset due to its full occupancy and classification.

title: Payment solutions for fuel providers
summary: J.P. Morgan's article addresses the evolving challenges and opportunities for fuel providers in the payments landscape. It highlights the complexities of managing multiple payment systems in fuel retail, the financial burden of swipe fees and fraud, and the need for modernization. The article suggests that adopting new payment models, leveraging mobile apps, and offering diversified services like EV charging can help fuel retailers attract and retain customers and optimize operational costs.

title: KT pushes ahead with K Bank IPO
summary: KT Corp is proceeding with an Initial Public Offering (IPO) for its digital banking subsidiary, K Bank, aiming to raise up to $1 billion. This move is part of KT's broader strategy to evolve from a traditional telecommunications company into a digital platform operator, diversifying its revenue streams through financial services, content, e-commerce, and cloud offerings. K Bank, in which KT holds a significant stake through BC Card, narrowed its net loss in 2021 and has established a strategic partnership with Shinhan Financial Group to integrate AI, metaverse, NFT, big data, and robotics technologies with financial services.

title: U.S. bank profits to tumble on higher bad loan reserves
summary: U.S. bank profits are expected to fall significantly in the second quarter due to increased loan loss reserves in anticipation of a potential recession. JPMorgan Chase, Citigroup, Wells Fargo, and Bank of America are projected to see substantial profit declines, as they build up reserves after releasing them during the pandemic recovery. While loan growth and higher interest rates are boosting net interest income, concerns about a severe recession and its impact on actual loan losses remain.

title: FIRST HORIZON LAUNCHES SOUTH FLORIDA PRIVATE WEALTH GROUP WITH OFFICES IN CORAL GABLES AND DOWNTOWN MIAMI
summary: First Horizon Corporation announced the formation of the First Horizon Advisors South Florida Private Wealth Group, catering to high net worth clients. Headquartered in Coral Gables with satellite offices in South Miami and Downtown Miami, the group is led by Damian Pardo, Oui Coulson, and Siby Vizoso, focusing on comprehensive financial planning and community involvement.

title: Equities Ownership: Concentration on the Rise?
summary: The article analyzes the increasing concentration of equities ownership, showing that controlled companies constitute nearly 46% of MSCI ACWI Index constituents, a 44% rise since 2015. It highlights the growing influence of "universal managers" like BlackRock and Vanguard, which hold significant stakes in numerous companies, and discusses the implications for corporate governance and shareholder engagement. While seemingly indicating concentration, the article suggests this could also reflect a new way of managing widely dispersed ownership if these managers enable clients to exercise shareholder rights effectively.

title: Vietnam's VinFast taps banks for $4 bln EV factory funding deal
summary: Vietnam's carmaker VinFast is seeking to raise at least $4 billion to fund the construction of its planned electric vehicle factory in North Carolina and support its U.S. expansion. Credit Suisse has been appointed to arrange the issue of offshore securities for $2 billion, while Citigroup Global Markets will advise on transactions of the same value. This funding is crucial for VinFast as it aims to compete in the U.S. EV market, despite potential delays to its initial public offering due to market uncertainty.

title: Chile eleva su tasa de interés a un máximo histórico de 9,75%
summary: Chile's Central Bank has raised its monetary policy rate to a record high of 9.75% in a unanimous decision to combat inflation, which reached 12.5% in June. This marks the ninth consecutive increase since July 2021 and follows a similar move by the US Federal Reserve, contributing to global financial tightening. The country faces economic risks including a significant depreciation of the Chilean peso and falling copper prices, prompting the government to announce a $120 bonus for vulnerable citizens.

title: PPM America’s Commercial Real Estate Team Reaches Significant Milestones
summary: PPM America's Core Plus Real Estate Debt Strategy has achieved significant milestones, including a three-year track record and surpassing $500 million in structured loans. The strategy, developed after Mark Kramer joined in 2018, now manages over $650 million in total assets. This success is attributed to the team's expertise, strong relationships, and strategic focus on enhanced returns in various market conditions.

title: What’s the best way to incentivize supplier sustainability?
summary: The article explores "sustainable supply chain finance" as a method for corporations to incentivize sustainability among their suppliers. This approach, similar to sustainability-linked loans, offers reduced interest rates on credit to suppliers who meet environmental or social criteria. While this method is gaining traction, particularly in the apparel industry, the article questions its effectiveness compared to simply paying suppliers sooner, suggesting that fair purchasing and payment practices might be a more fundamental and impactful solution for fostering a sustainable supply chain.

title: Indian American Naureen Hassan Becomes President of UBS Americas
summary: Naureen Hassan, currently the First VP and COO of the New York Federal Reserve, will become the President of UBS Americas on October 3, 2022. She will also join the UBS Group's Executive Board. Hassan, who has a background in economics and an MBA from Stanford, previously served as Chief Digital Officer at Morgan Stanley.

title: JPMorgan Says Bitcoin Cost of Production May Be Down to $13,000
summary: JPMorgan analysts, led by Nikolaos Panigirtzoglou, report that the estimated cost of Bitcoin production has fallen from $24,000 in early June to about $13,000. This decrease is attributed to more efficient mining rigs using less electricity, rather than a significant departure of less efficient miners. The bank views this reduction in production costs as a potential negative factor for Bitcoin's price appreciation.

title: JPMorgan pauses stock buybacks as profits slump
summary: JPMorgan Chase announced a pause in its stock buyback program following a 28% drop in quarterly earnings, a move its CEO Jamie Dimon attributed to economic uncertainties including the war in Ukraine and inflation. Stock buybacks typically boost share value, but this halt signals the bank's decision to conserve cash. While it's a "cautionary note" from a major bank, analysts suggest it doesn't necessarily set a widespread trend unless other large financial institutions follow suit.

title: Morgan Stanley Misuse of Personal Devices Costs $200 Million
summary: Morgan Stanley announced it expects to pay a $200 million fine for the misuse of unapproved personal devices by its employees, stemming from a broad investigation by the SEC and CFTC across Wall Street. This fine relates to the firm's failure to adequately monitor communications, a challenge amplified by the shift to remote work during Covid-19, and impacts its second-quarter earnings. Other major banks like JPMorgan Chase & Co., Citigroup Inc., and Goldman Sachs Group Inc. are also under scrutiny or have faced similar penalties for similar record-keeping failures.

title: JPMorgan Q2 Profit Down 28%; Results Miss Estimates
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. reported a 28% decline in second-quarter profit, hurt by higher noninterest expenses and a net credit reserve build. Both earnings per share ($2.76 vs. $2.91 expected) and revenues ($30.72 billion vs. $31.95 billion expected) missed analysts' expectations. The provision for credit losses was a net benefit of $1.10 billion, reflecting loan growth and a modest deterioration in the economic outlook.

title: Morgan Stanley sets aside $200M over personal-device misuse probe
summary: Morgan Stanley announced it expects to pay a $200 million penalty for violating record-keeping requirements related to employees' use of unapproved personal devices for business communications. This penalty follows similar probes by regulators into other major financial institutions like JPMorgan Chase, Citi, Goldman Sachs, and HSBC. The charge contributed to Morgan Stanley's second-quarter non-interest expenses, despite an overall 29% decline in profit over the comparable period in 2021.

title: JPMorgan Halts Share Buybacks as Earnings Miss Estimates
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. has temporarily suspended share buybacks after its second-quarter earnings missed analyst estimates, causing its stock to drop. CEO Jamie Dimon stated this decision is necessary to meet higher capital requirements and maintain flexibility across various economic conditions. The bank also increased its reserves for potential loan losses.

title: Morgan Stanley misses analysts’ estimates on worse-than-expected investment banking revenue
summary: Morgan Stanley reported second-quarter earnings and revenue that fell below analysts' expectations, primarily due to a significant 55% decline in investment banking revenue. The bank's profit dropped 29% to $2.5 billion, and revenue fell 11% to $13.13 billion. While trading results partially offset the weakness in investment banking, the disappointing performance underscores broader market challenges impacting Wall Street banks.

title: Morgan Stanley Hit by Banking Slump as Recession Fears Loom
summary: Morgan Stanley's investment banking revenue significantly declined by 55% to $1.07 billion, worse than analyst predictions, as capital markets slowed amidst rising recession fears. The bank also incurred $413 million in mark-to-market losses on corporate loans. This performance highlights a challenging quarter for Wall Street, attributed to a gloomy economic outlook.

title: Mortgages are in free fall at JPMorgan Chase
summary: JPMorgan Chase reported significant declines in mortgage originations, margins, and revenues for the second quarter of 2022, primarily due to higher mortgage rates stemming from the Federal Reserve's tightening monetary policy. The bank's origination volume fell to $21.9 billion, an 11% decline quarter-over-quarter and 45% year-over-year, with the retail channel experiencing the sharpest decrease. Despite a cautious outlook on a potential recession, CEO Jamie Dimon noted that consumers are in a relatively strong financial position compared to previous economic downturns.

title: Blockchain Asset Tokenization with Kinexys
summary: J.P. Morgan's Kinexys Digital Assets platform has completed a significant transaction, utilizing tokenized Money Market Fund (MMF) shares as collateral, marking a first for blockchain in collateral markets. This innovation, through the Tokenized Collateral Network (TCN), aims to enhance liquidity, reduce settlement friction, and enable greater utilization of assets. Kinexys is positioning itself to be a bridge between traditional finance and decentralized finance, with over $300 billion in intraday repo transactions already processed on the platform.

title: UBS, Citi among banks hit by Asia rich clients’ pullback
summary: UBS Group AG and Citigroup Inc. are experiencing a significant drop in wealth management revenues in Asia due to a slump in client trading activity and market volatility exacerbated by China's industry crackdowns. This downturn marks a sharp reversal from previous years, pushing banks to become more cautious with hiring and focus on retaining existing high-net-worth clients, though some continue selective hiring for strategic growth areas like family offices and alternative investments.

title: Why You Need a Rejection Resume (and How to Write One)
summary: The article "Why You Need a Rejection Resume (and How to Write One)" by Eli Joseph discusses the author's extensive experience with failure and rejection throughout his career—from university admissions to job applications and prestigious fellowships. Joseph, who is also the author of "The Perfect Rejection Resume," suggests that individuals should create a "rejection resume" to acknowledge and learn from these setbacks. This document can help in personal growth and career development by reframing failures as stepping stones to success.

title: Wealth management wins, $200M fine highlight Morgan Stanley’s quarter
summary: Morgan Stanley reported sliding net revenues and income for the second consecutive quarter, attributed to a volatile market and significant legal costs. Despite these challenges, CEO James P. Gorman highlighted the strong performance of the wealth management arm, which managed to minimize losses and attract over $50 billion in net new assets. The firm also incurred a $200 million fine related to regulatory investigations into employees' use of unapproved personal devices and recordkeeping requirements.

title: Citigroup shares surge on profit beat, core business strength
summary: Citigroup's shares surged over 10% after the bank reported a better-than-expected quarterly profit, driven by strong performance in its treasury services and trading divisions. Despite a decline in investment banking revenue and an increase in loan loss reserves, the core businesses showed strength, indicating that CEO Jane Fraser's restructuring plan may be gaining traction. However, the bank will pause share buybacks to build regulatory capital and in response to economic threats.

title: Morgan Stanley fined $200 million for WhatsApp use
summary: Morgan Stanley has been fined $200 million for inadequately recording communications made on unapproved personal devices like WhatsApp, mirroring a similar fine against JPMorgan. This highlights the ongoing struggle for financial institutions and even governments to ensure compliance and proper record-keeping as employees use convenient messaging apps for work. The article also touches on a UK High Court ruling that found the use of WhatsApp by government ministers to be legal despite concerns over transparency and record-keeping.

title: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon on potential recession, the business climate and more
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. CEO Jamie Dimon stated the company is not planning drastic pullbacks despite economic turbulence. He noted that customers are generally in a better financial position now compared to previous recessions.

title: India In-Focus — HDFC Bank’s Q2 profit soars; Crop planting ramps up in India; Israel sells Haifa Port to Adani Ports and Gadot for $1.2bn
summary: HDFC Bank reported a 19% rise in net profit for the fiscal first quarter, reaching 91.96 billion rupees (approximately $1.15 billion), driven by reduced bad loan provisions and increased loan growth. Meanwhile, summer crop planting in India is accelerating due to improved monsoon rains in July, although rice planting still lags. Additionally, Israel has sold its Haifa Port to India’s Adani Ports and local group Gadot for $1.18 billion, aiming to boost competition and lower import costs.

title: Why Invest in CLOs?
summary: The article highlights Collateralized Loan Obligations (CLOs) as a compelling investment due to their historical combination of above-average yield, strong risk profiles, and potential for appreciation. It details how CLOs have demonstrated strong risk-adjusted returns compared to other corporate debt categories, particularly through economic crises, and offer lower sensitivity to interest rate changes. The piece also introduces the VanEck CLO ETF (CLOI) as an efficient way for investors to access the largely institutional CLO market.

title: Earnings slide ongoing for banks; BofA Q2 profit dips 32%
summary: Bank of America reported a 32% dip in Q2 2022 profits compared to the previous year, following a trend seen among other major U.S. banks like JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo, and Citigroup. While profits were lower due to robust 2021 results boosted by released loan loss reserves, the bank's revenue increased to $22.7 billion, driven by higher interest rates and increased lending. The outlook for the second half of the year remains a focus due to potential recession risks from inflation and Federal Reserve actions.

title: Splitit strengthens board with appointments of Dan Charron and Nandan Sheth while adding key hires to the executive team
summary: Splitit has announced significant leadership changes, appointing payments industry veterans Dan Charron and Nandan Sheth to its board of directors. Charron joins as an Independent Non-Executive Director, bringing 30 years of experience, while CEO Nandan Sheth will now also serve as Managing Director. The company further bolsters its executive team with three key hires: Colt McCutcheon as Chief Revenue Officer, Collin Flotta as Head of Product, and George Danforth as Head of Operations, aiming to drive revenue growth, product innovation, and operational efficiency for its Installments-as-a-Service platform.

title: Goldman Sachs Beats Rivals, Benefiting From Volatile Markets (Published 2022)
summary: Goldman Sachs exceeded analyst expectations for profit in the second quarter despite a nearly 50% drop, largely due to its traders capitalizing on volatile markets, especially in bond, currency, and commodity trading. However, the company announced it would slow hiring and review stock buybacks, reflecting caution about an "uncertain" economic environment with deeply embedded inflation. The bank, like its rivals, still saw a significant decline in investment banking revenue and increased provisions for loan losses due to inflation and a downturn in deal-making.

title: Jefferies to spin off Vitesse Energy, merge companies and sell unit to focus on core banking business
summary: Jefferies Financial Group Inc. announced plans to spin off its Vitesse Energy LLC holdings to shareholders by the end of the year, aiming to list Vitesse Energy on the New York Stock Exchange. This move is part of an effort to reduce its merchant bank holdings and concentrate on its core investment banking and capital markets units. Additionally, Jefferies will book a $140 million gain from the sale of Idaho Timber, merge Jefferies Group LLC into Jefferies Financial Group Inc., and implement changes in its CFO leadership in 2023.

title: Brazil's Petrobras set to cut gasoline prices Wednesday
summary: Brazil's state-run oil company Petrobras announced it would cut gasoline prices at its refineries by about 5% on Wednesday, marking its first price reduction since late 2021. This decision, influenced by political pressure ahead of an upcoming election, will bring average prices down to 3.86 reais per liter and has led analysts, including JPMorgan, to revise down Brazil's inflation outlook for the year. Petrobras stated the cut aligns with its policy of pegging domestic fuel rates to international prices while allowing for variation during volatility.

title: Morgan Health makes $30M investment in Centivo
summary: Morgan Health, JPMorgan Chase's healthcare arm, has invested $30 million in Centivo, a health plan targeting self-funded employers. Centivo's model focuses on partnering with accountable care organizations to offer affordable, high-quality care, resulting in significant savings for its employer clients. This investment is part of Centivo's extended Series B-1 financing to support its growth and expansion across 13 states.

title: JPMorgan adds former J&J chief Gorsky to board
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co has elected Alex Gorsky, the former chief executive officer of Johnson & Johnson, as a director of the bank. Gorsky, who is currently an executive chairman at J&J, previously led the development of J&J's COVID-19 vaccine and steered the company through significant crises. His appointment to JPMorgan's board is effective immediately.

title: State Street Corp. stock underperforms Wednesday when compared to competitors
summary: State Street Corp. (STT) stock underperformed on Wednesday, July 20, 2022, falling 0.53% to $66.97, despite a generally positive trading session for the broader market. The stock closed significantly below its 52-week high and lagged behind some of its key competitors like JPMorgan Chase & Co., Bank of America Corp., and Citigroup Inc. Trading volume for State Street Corp. was also below its 50-day average.

title: BNY Mellon Wealth Management Named Rob Zaccardi Senior Client Strategist in Boston
summary: BNY Mellon Wealth Management has appointed Rob Zaccardi as Senior Client Strategist in Boston. He will work with ultra-high-net-worth families, business owners, corporate executives, and foundations/endowments on their comprehensive wealth needs. Zaccardi brings over 12 years of financial services experience, previously serving as executive director at JP Morgan Private Bank.

title: ¿Quién es Felipe García Ascencio, el nuevo director general de Santander México?
summary: Felipe García Ascencio has been appointed as the new CEO of Santander Mexico, succeeding Héctor Grisi. García Ascencio, who holds a master's degree in Economics from the London School of Economics, has over 25 years of experience in banking and government roles. He previously served as an advisor to the Ministry of Finance and held positions at IDEA Global and Goldman Sachs before joining Santander Mexico two years prior to this appointment.

title: 2021’s M&A winners BMO, Citizens strike again for smaller deals
summary: Banks like BMO and Citizens, after making significant acquisitions in 2021, are now focusing on smaller, niche deals to drive growth. BMO acquired Radicle Group to build expertise in climate-related services, while Citizens expanded its private-wealth division by acquiring assets from Paladin Advisors. This trend suggests that even after large mergers, banks continue to seek strategic, smaller-scale acquisitions to enhance specific areas of their operations.

title: US Banking Customers Will Soon Demand These Features. Does Your Mobile App Offer Them?
summary: Mobile banking customers are increasingly demanding more sophisticated features in their apps beyond basic tasks, with 54% of US online adults wanting to complete any financial task via mobile. Research from an unnamed source identifies digital wallet integration, customer-facing data management tools, and subscription management tools as three key future "must-have" features. Banks that adopt these features, like Bank of America with its "Erica" tool, can differentiate their offerings and appeal to younger customers.

title: Bank of Montreal Taps North Texas for its Newest Tech Hub
summary: The Bank of Montreal (BMO) is establishing a new tech hub in North Texas, planning to hire 50 new employees to add to its existing 250-person DFW workforce. This move is part of BMO's strategy to expand its U.S. operations and follows similar investments by other major banks like JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, and PNC Bank in the Dallas-Fort Worth region. The Irving tech hub will be BMO's first outside of Toronto and Chicago, focusing on areas like cybersecurity and engineering.

title: State Street Corp. stock underperforms Monday when compared to competitors despite daily gains
summary: State Street Corp. (STT) stock saw a modest gain of 0.35% on Monday, closing at $68.40, marking its third consecutive day of increases amidst a favorable overall market. Despite this, the company's stock underperformed compared to competitors like JPMorgan Chase & Co., Bank of America Corp., and Citigroup Inc., which all recorded higher percentage gains. The stock remained significantly below its 52-week high, and trading volume was below its 50-day average.

title: MasTec Acquires IEA for Wind, Solar Energy Infrastructure Expertise
summary: MasTec has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Infrastructure and Energy Alternatives Inc. (IEA) in a cash-and-stock transaction valued at $14 per IEA share, totaling approximately $1.1 billion. This acquisition aims to expand MasTec's service capabilities in renewable energy infrastructure, particularly wind and solar projects, and is expected to close in late Q4 2022. The deal combines IEA's expertise in utility-scale wind and solar projects with MasTec's existing infrastructure services, anticipating increased scale and capacity to meet growing demand for renewable power generation.

title: Finexio Raises $14 Million in Initial Close of Series B, Company Valued at $100 Million
summary: Finexio announced the initial close of its $30 million Series B funding round, raising $14 million at a pre-money valuation of $100 million. This round was co-led by Mendon Venture Partners and National Bank Holdings Corporation (NYSE: NBHC), with additional participation from Discover Financial Services (NYSE: DFS) and other investors. The funding will accelerate the adoption of Finexio's "B2B Payments-as-a-Service platform," foster team growth, and advance product development.

title: U.S. watchdogs scrutinise UBS over staff messaging
summary: U.S. regulators are investigating UBS Group for not properly documenting staff communications, part of a broader probe into financial institutions. This scrutiny follows similar actions against J.P. Morgan Securities, which was fined $200 million for widespread failures in preserving communications, and Bank of America, which set aside $200 million for a related regulatory matter. UBS is cooperating with the ongoing investigations by the SEC and CFTC.

title: UBS Says It’s Part of US Probe Into Unapproved Staff Messaging
summary: UBS AG has disclosed its cooperation with US regulators, including the SEC and CFTC, in a broad probe concerning the use of unapproved messaging channels by its employees. This investigation into records preservation non-compliance is expected to result in significant fines, potentially totaling about $1 billion across several major investment banks, including UBS, Morgan Stanley, and Citigroup. The probe highlights regulatory efforts to enforce rules requiring financial firms to monitor and store staff communications, especially challenged by the increased use of mobile messaging apps and remote work.

title: Kitchen United CEO, CBO Detail Plans for $100M Investment
summary: Kitchen United has raised $100 million in a Series C funding round, bringing its total fundraising to approximately $175 million. The company plans to expand from 15 to 500 locations, including a partnership with Circle K and expansion into stadium venues, while maintaining a lean operational structure. This investment, largely from industry insiders and existing partners, validates Kitchen United's methodical growth strategy in the ghost kitchen market.

title: ​A fundamental and technical outlook on the Barclays and Lloyds share price
summary: This article provides a fundamental and technical analysis of Barclays (BARC) and Lloyds Banking Group (LLOY) share prices ahead of their H1 2022 earnings releases. It discusses their balance sheets, earnings potential, and the impact of rising interest rates and inflation on their performance. The analysis concludes with price targets and support/resistance levels for both stocks, suggesting they may be undervalued.

title: My Experience Visiting A Capital One Cafe
summary: The author shares their first experience visiting a Capital One Cafe, highlighting its unique blend of a coffee shop and bank. They found it to be a quiet place to work, offering 50% off beverages for Capital One cardholders, and noted the presence of "Cafe Ambassadors" for banking questions without sales pressure. The article concludes that these cafes present a pleasant alternative to traditional coffee shops like Starbucks, especially for Capital One customers.

title: JPMorgan Treasurer and Investment Chief Matt Cherwin Is Leaving Firm (JPM)
summary: Matt Cherwin, JPMorgan Chase & Co.'s Treasurer and Chief Investment Officer, is departing the firm. He has held the position since 2019 and plans to take time off before exploring new opportunities. JPMorgan has not yet named a successor, with the firm indicating that "next steps" will be considered in the coming weeks.

title: 10 Big Named Companies With Huge Free Cash Flows @Ycharts
