The article highlights built-in security features of commercial cards, such as chip technology and customizable spending limits, and educates on common fraud schemes like business email compromise, account takeover, skimming, data breaches, phishing, and internet safety. It also promotes virtual card solutions as an enhanced security measure, citing their near 0% fraud rate due to unique account numbers, secure vendor access, controlled credit limits, and custom expiration dates.

title: Schwab sets date to transition advisers, clients and assets from TD Ameritrade
summary: Charles Schwab Corp. has set Labor Day weekend 2023 as the official date for financial advisers to transition from the TD Ameritrade brokerage platform to Schwab Advisor Services. Schwab managing director Tom Bradley assured advisers there would be no repapering of clients and that service teams would largely remain intact, minimizing disruption. The company is actively preparing systems and conducting data migration simulations to ensure a smooth transition, aiming to complete the integration over two years after the acquisition closed.

title: “Red-Faced” Bank Robber Charged in Five Area Heists
summary: Kashiffe Beckford, 29, initially arrested after a dye pack exploded during a bank robbery, has now been charged with five bank robberies in the Bronx. Despite facing 11 felonies and 10 misdemeanors, he was released due to the crimes being non-violent and not bail eligible, as no weapon was used. Police are still investigating a more recent bank robbery that occurred after Beckford's arrest.

title: JPMorgan Chase Plans to Raise the Bar at New Manhattan Headquarters, Bet on Return to Office
summary: JPMorgan Chase is investing nearly $3 billion in a new, state-of-the-art headquarters in midtown Manhattan, signaling its strong belief in the future of office work and urban centers. The 60-story, all-electric, carbon-neutral building is designed to enhance employee well-being and productivity through features like advanced air quality monitoring, diverse workspaces, and a focus on hospitality, with input from experts like Deepak Chopra. CEO Jamie Dimon emphasizes a pragmatic approach to technology integration, ensuring commercial applicability for all new innovations.

title: Private Wealth Management: Next Generation
summary: This article from Morgan Stanley discusses Private Wealth Management for the next generation, highlighting the unique challenges faced by young individuals gaining significant wealth. It explains how Morgan Stanley advisors prepare clients for financial opportunities, leadership roles, and effective wealth preservation across generations. The piece also touches on tailored solutions including establishing independence, cultivating relationships, developing financial literacy, and making a personal mark in financial decisions.

title: Dólar hoy y dólar blue, EN VIVO: a cuánto cotizó y cuál fue su precio este 26 de octubre, minuto a minuto
summary: This article provides a minute-by-minute update on the parallel dollar (dólar blue) and official dollar exchange rates in Argentina for October 26, 2022. It covers the closing prices of various financial instruments, including the dólar blue, official dollar, financial dollars (CCL and MEP), and the performance of Argentine stocks and bonds. The report also touches on related economic news like Fitch's downgrade of Argentina's debt, declining supermarket sales, and changes to travel taxes and ANSeS benefits.

title: Vornado unduly influenced state in Penn Station redevelopment, lawsuit says
summary: A lawsuit filed by four community groups alleges that Vornado Realty Trust unduly influenced the Hochul administration's plan for the Penn Station redevelopment. The suit claims Empire State Development (ESD) yielded to Vornado's wishes regarding constructing 10 new towers to fund the transit hub's rebuilding, asserting the plan should be scrapped. Critics argue the proposed development, which includes 18 million square feet of office and residential space, will not generate sufficient revenue to fund the station's overhaul and primarily benefits Vornado through tax breaks and financial advantages.

title: How SMBC Group became a leader in transformation and digital perseverance
summary: SMBC Group, one of Japan's largest banks, is undergoing a significant digital transformation by partnering with Microsoft as its strategic cloud provider. This collaboration aims to modernize IT infrastructure, develop innovative products like Embedded Finance and digital supply chain solutions, and support customers in achieving their sustainability goals. The article highlights how SMBC's approach to digital transformation also involves a cultural shift, emphasizing talent empowerment and a customer-first mindset, positioning them for "digital perseverance" in a changing industry.

title: Follow the Money: ParkHub Acquires Parking Software Startup, UpSmith Raises $3.3M, Maverick Bancshares Seeks $17M for new Fort Worth Bank, and More
summary: This article details various financial activities and developments in North Texas, including ParkHub's acquisition of Smarking, UpSmith's $3.3 million pre-seed funding round to address the skilled worker shortage, and Maverick Bancshares' bid to raise $17 million for a new bank in Fort Worth. It also covers significant investments, acquisitions, and funding rounds for companies like Taysha Gene Therapies, RumbleOn, MAX, Zirtue, 4 Impact Data, NaturalShrimp, Crescent Real Estate, Dallas Venture Capital, Acqueon, Tyler Technologies, Integrity Marketing Group, and Centurion American Development Group.

title: Construction Starts for Centro Callan Apartments in San Leandro
summary: Construction has begun on the Centro Callan Apartments, a five-story mixed-use development at 100 Callan Street in San Leandro, Alameda County. The project will feature 196 residential units, a Sprouts grocery store, Union Bank, and other retail spaces, with completion expected by 2024. This joint venture by The Martin Group, Sansome Pacific Properties, and STARS REI aims to provide housing and revitalize the downtown area.

title: Fitch cambia a negativa la perspectiva de siete entidades financieras peruanas
summary: Fitch Ratings ha cambiado la perspectiva de siete entidades financieras peruanas de "estable" a "negativa", incluyendo BCP, Credicorp, Scotiabank, Interbank, Intercorp, BanBif y Cofide. Esta medida se debe a la revisión a la baja de la perspectiva de riesgo soberano de Perú, que pasó de estable a negativa el 20 de octubre, y al ajuste de la evaluación del entorno operativo para los bancos peruanos a negativo desde estable. La agencia citó el deterioro de la estabilidad política y la efectividad del gobierno como factores que aumentan los riesgos para las calificaciones de Perú.

title: Leaders in Trading 2022: Meet the nominees for… Outstanding Alternative Liquidity Provider
summary: The article announces the shortlisted nominees for the 2022 Editors’ Choice Outstanding Alternative Liquidity Provider Award: Citadel Securities, Flow Traders, Hudson River Trading, Jane Street, and XTX Markets. It then provides detailed overviews of each firm's activities, market presence, strategic investments, and contributions to liquidity provision across various asset classes, including their engagement in digital assets and DeFi.

title: Apollo holds crypto for clients as it expands in digital assets
summary: Apollo Global Management Inc. has partnered with Anchorage Digital to hold cryptocurrency for its clients, marking a significant step into digital assets despite the volatile crypto market. This move validates the long-term view of crypto for large institutions and follows Apollo's participation in Anchorage's Series D funding round in late 2021. Apollo also hired former JPMorgan executive Christine Moy to lead its digital asset strategy, reinforcing its commitment to blockchain and Web3 technologies.

title: JPMorgan Chase launches Story
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. has launched Story, a new multifamily rental management platform for property owners. The platform is currently being piloted with Chase customers and offered free for 12 months, allowing users to create leases and invoices, and collect rent payments online. Landlords not currently Chase customers will be able to sign up when it's released more broadly next year.

title: Amtrak and First National Bank of Omaha Launch Two New Amtrak Guest Rewards Mastercards
summary: Amtrak and First National Bank of Omaha (FNBO) have launched two new Amtrak Guest Rewards Mastercard Credit Cards. These co-branded cards offer enhanced benefits and rewards for Amtrak loyalty program members, allowing them to earn points for travel, upgrades, dining, and more. The new offerings include a Preferred Mastercard with an annual fee and a standard Mastercard with no annual fee, both designed to improve the customer travel experience.

title: Profile: David Levi, leader of the Brookfield Public Securities Group, and Brookfield Oaktree Wealth Solutions
summary: This profile details the career of David Levi, who leads both the Brookfield Public Securities Group and Brookfield Oaktree Wealth Solutions. The article highlights his leadership philosophy of trusting experts and setting a clear vision, which propelled him through successful roles at major financial organizations. It also discusses his current work in delivering alternative investment strategies to individual investors and his strong belief in the growing importance of alternatives in the investment landscape.

title: Predictions 2023: Banks Will Batten Down The Hatches But Prepare For The Upturn
summary: In 2023, banks are expected to brace for tougher economic conditions and potential global recession by focusing on cost control and operational efficiency. While cutting costs, smart firms will strategically invest in automation and process mining to prepare for a future economic upturn. Additionally, the global green finance market is predicted to recover significantly, with its value reaching $1.2 trillion, largely driven by green bonds and loans.

title: J.P. Morgan Launches New Life Sciences Private Capital Team Targeting Investments in Innovative Healthcare Companies
summary: J.P. Morgan Asset Management has launched a new life sciences private equity team called Life Sciences Private Capital, which will invest in early and growth-stage healthcare companies focusing on novel therapeutics and technologies. The team, led by industry experts Dr. Stephen Squinto, Dr. Gaurav Gupta, and Ms. Anya Schiess, will leverage JPMorgan Chase's resources to identify and support innovative companies. They aim to provide operational value beyond financial investment, with support from a group of strategic advisors comprising prominent life science experts.

title: Johnson & Johnson is paying $17.3 billion to buy a company that helps your heart pump blood
summary: Johnson & Johnson announced it will acquire Abiomed Inc., a maker of Impella heart pumps, for approximately $17.3 billion. This acquisition aims to expand J&J's medical device portfolio as it focuses on higher-return pharmaceutical and medical technology divisions following its planned consumer unit spinoff. The deal, which offers Abiomed shareholders a significant premium, is expected to be neutral or slightly negative for J&J's earnings in the first year but accretive starting in 2024.

title: The top five risks in 2023
summary: Barclays Private Bank identifies five main risks that could challenge its 2023 outlook: monetary and fiscal policies, wars, China’s economic momentum, COVID-19, and social unrest. These risks are interconnected and could compound if multiple materialize simultaneously, potentially adding significant volatility or disruption to the global economy. The report details how central banks are navigating inflation, the ongoing geopolitical tensions from the Ukraine war and potential flashpoints like Taiwan, China's struggle with zero-COVID and real estate, the continued threat of new COVID variants, and the rising global discontent fueled by inflation and climate change issues.

title: Why bonds may beat stocks in coming months, after ‘safe’ and ‘risky’ assets broadly moved in same direction in 2022, says Capital Economics
summary: Capital Economics predicts that bonds may outperform stocks in the coming months, diverging from their similar performance in 2022. This shift is attributed to increasing recession concerns and the belief that long-dated government bond yields have peaked and will decline further as inflation eases. John Higgins, chief markets economist at Capital Economics, suggests that while bond yields have peaked, risky assets may face more challenges until mid-next year.

title: Women of Influence honoree: Thelma Ferguson, JPMorgan Chase & Co.
summary: Thelma Ferguson, vice chair of commercial banking at JPMorgan Chase & Co., has been honored as a Woman of Influence. This article previews an interview with Ferguson, where she discusses offering advice to women in corporate leadership and the importance of supporting small businesses.

title: The Future of AI and Compliance in Finance – with Experts from UBS, HSBC, BMO and More
summary: The finance industry is grappling with evolving compliance challenges, including increased fines and the need to monitor employee communications more effectively. This article explores how AI, particularly machine learning and NLP, is being leveraged by financial institutions like UBS, HSBC, and BMO to enhance communications surveillance, improve legacy systems, and broaden market surveillance beyond traditional methods. These AI applications aim to streamline workflows, reduce false positives, and equip compliance teams to handle the increasing volume and complexity of regulatory requirements.

title: Wells Fargo mortgage staff brace for layoffs as U.S. loan volumes collapse
summary: Wells Fargo's mortgage division is facing significant layoffs due to a drastic 90% collapse in U.S. loan volumes compared to the previous year. The housing market slump, driven by rising interest rates, has left many mortgage staff idle and put employees on edge, with internal projections indicating more departures are likely. CEO Charlie Scharf has also stated the bank's intention to shrink its mortgage business and focus on existing customers.

title: Barclays builds up Asia business, sees growth in India and Australia
summary: Barclays Plc is actively expanding its footprint in Asia, with significant investments in India and Australia, and the establishment of a Taiwan subsidiary. Despite a cautious macroeconomic outlook, the bank's top regional executive, Jaideep Khanna, indicates that while they are currently focused on fortifying existing franchises, future expansion into new markets is not ruled out, though unlikely in 2023. Barclays aims to leverage robust growth opportunities in India and Australia, particularly within its corporate and institutional client base and investment banking activities.

title: CLIENT FIRST TAX & WEALTH ADVISORS ANNOUNCES NEW ADAPTIV™ SELECT ETF (TICKER: ADPV); A PROPRIETARY ACTIVELY MANAGED, LARGE CAP STOCK SELECTION ETF
summary: Client First Tax & Wealth Advisors has announced the Adaptiv™ Select ETF (ADPV), an actively managed, large-cap stock selection exchange-traded fund. This ETF aims to identify and own the top 25 U.S. Large Cap stocks in an uptrend, shifting to cash and short-term Treasury Bills during downtrends. The fund leverages proprietary rules-based calculations and weekly reconstitutions to manage risk and pursue returns.

title: Venetian ownership touts Strip success, expresses interest in additional casinos
summary: Apollo Global Management, owners of the Venetian resort-casino, are issuing a $620 million dividend after an "exceptional start" to their ownership, exceeding financial expectations since acquiring the property in February. Despite initial concerns from the Nevada Gaming Control Board about the quick dividend and potential recession preparedness, the board recommended approval, noting the Venetian's strong financial position and Apollo's interest in acquiring additional casinos in Las Vegas and other regions. Apollo plans to invest over $1 billion in the property over the next three to four years, and views the dividend as right-sizing their initial investment given the unexpected financial success.

title: Evertec reports $146M 3Q22 revenue, growth in ATH Móvil transactions
summary: Evertec Inc. announced $145.8 million in total revenue for the third quarter ended Sept. 30, 2022, holding relatively flat year-over-year despite negative impacts from a one-time credit to Popular Inc. and Hurricane Fiona. CEO Mac Schuessler highlighted strengthened relationships and extended contracts with Popular, alongside significant growth in Puerto Rico operations, including 6% year-over-year increase in point-of-sale transactions and 16% growth in ATH Móvil. The company also repurchased $37.3 million in common stock and anticipates consolidated revenue between $607 million and $615 million by year-end.

title: Procuración: AFIP debe admitir deducción de gastos de dividendos
summary: The Argentine General Attorney's Office (Procuración General) has issued a favorable opinion supporting companies' right to deduct expenses related to dividends for income tax purposes, contrary to AFIP's current stance. This comes as several companies, including Grupo Financiero Galicia and Telecom, are taking their cases to the Supreme Court. The opinion distinguishes between "exempt" or "non-taxable" income and "non-computable" income (like dividends), arguing that the law only prohibits expense deductions for the former.

title: Goldman Sachs seeks to impose order on expanding crypto universe with classification system
summary: Goldman Sachs, in partnership with MSCI and Coin Metrics, is launching "Datonomy," a data service to classify hundreds of digital coins and tokens for institutional investors. This system aims to standardize how the financial industry understands and invests in digital assets, providing a framework for performance tracking, risk management, and product creation in the crypto space. Datonomy will allow for more granular analysis of digital assets, similar to sector analysis in traditional equities.

title: ADPV Stock Fund Price and Chart — AMEX:ADPV
summary: This article provides a comprehensive overview of the Adaptiv Select ETF (ADPV), detailing its market price, key statistics like AUM and expense ratio, and its investment strategy. The fund aims to capture upside in the US equity market while taming downside risk by dynamically switching between large-cap equities and short-term US Treasurys based on market trends. It also includes technical analysis and answers frequently asked questions about the ETF.

title: LPL buying one of its own giant branches
summary: LPL Financial Holdings Inc. is acquiring Financial Resources Group Investment Services, one of its largest branch offices, for a base price of $140 million. This acquisition brings new management capabilities to banks and credit unions, according to LPL, and addresses Financial Resources Group's needs for capital and a succession plan. The deal highlights a trend of large broker-dealers actively participating in the mergers and acquisitions market for wealth management firms.

title: Voya Financial acquires benefits administration company
summary: Voya Financial Inc. announced its acquisition of Benefitfocus Inc., a cloud-based benefits administration company, for approximately $570 million. This acquisition will expand Voya's services to roughly 38 million individuals and accelerate its workplace-centered strategy, enhancing its ability to provide comprehensive benefits and savings solutions. Benefitfocus is expected to continue as a distinct business with its existing management team.

title: Atlanticus Launches Aspire® Banking Platform, New Debit
summary: Atlanticus Holdings Corporation launched the Aspire® Banking platform, a new debit product designed to provide a clear path to credit for the financially underserved. This program offers a bank account and debit card with no minimums or nuisance fees, and upon completing specific activities in as little as 90 days, customers are presented with an Aspire® Credit Card offer. The initiative aims to help the nearly 44 million unbanked or underbanked Americans establish positive financial habits and access credit.

title: Santander to block UK transfers to crypto exchanges in 2023
summary: Santander will block UK customers from making real-time payments to cryptocurrency exchanges in 2023 to protect them from scams. Starting November 15, the bank will also limit transfers to £1,000 per transaction and £3,000 within any 30-day period. This move follows an increase in crypto fraud victims and aligns with other UK banks' actions to mitigate risks in the largely unregulated crypto trading world.

title: UBS loses two advisor teams with $4.3B to Wells Fargo, RBC
summary: UBS recently lost two significant advisor teams, totaling $4.3 billion in assets under management, to Wells Fargo and RBC. The Margate Wealth Management Group, managing $2.6 billion, joined Wells Fargo, citing expanded services for ultra-high-net-worth clients. Separately, the Promus Wealth Management Group, with $1.7 billion in AUM, moved to RBC Wealth Management for its integrated technology platform and cultural fit.

title: Goldman launches digital asset classification system
summary: Goldman Sachs has launched Datonomy, a new digital asset classification system developed with MSCI and Coin Metrics, to provide institutional investors with a standardized way to analyze the crypto ecosystem. This subscription-based tool aims to bring transparency to the market by classifying digital assets based on investor usage and helping with portfolio performance review and risk management. This move signifies Goldman's continued strategic re-engagement with digital assets after previously halting and then relaunching its crypto trading desk.

title: How Can You Invest in the Great Transition to Clean Energy
summary: The article discusses investment opportunities in the global transition to clean energy, emphasizing the urgent need for action highlighted at the U.N. Climate Change Conference. It focuses on the roles of semiconductors and green buildings as key areas for investors. The authors detail how these sectors are crucial for achieving net-zero emissions and present significant market growth potential.

title: RCBC Receives US$460M Strategic Investment From SMBC
summary: Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation (SMBC) has significantly increased its stake in Rizal Commercial Banking Corporation (RCBC) to 20.0% through a US$460 million investment. This strategic move aims to support RCBC's long-term growth, technology investments, and human resources while expanding SMBC's presence in key Southeast Asian markets. The banks anticipate collaborations in corporate banking, sustainable finance, and digital services.

title: Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S. A. B. de C. V. Insider Trading & Ownership Structure
summary: This report details the ownership structure and recent insider trading activities for Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S. A. B. de C. V. Key insights include an ownership breakdown among general public, private companies, individual insiders, and institutions, indicating that individual insiders hold a significant portion. The report also lists the top 25 shareholders, with Fernando Chico Pardo being the largest individual shareholder, and notes insufficient data to determine recent insider buying vs. selling trends.

title: Exclusive | Goldman Sachs, Eager to Grow Cards Business, Courted Credit-Card Technology Firms
summary: Goldman Sachs is reportedly looking to expand its credit card business by acquiring a payments-technology firm. The bank has expressed interest in fintech credit-card platforms such as Deserve and Cardless, and payments company CoreCard Corp. Goldman Sachs already has close ties with Deserve and is exploring options to bolster its card capabilities.

title: Pending merger involving Tacoma-based bank leads to sell-off of branches across West
summary: Tacoma-based Columbia Banking System announced the sale of 10 bank branches across Washington, Oregon, and California as a condition for its pending merger with Portland-based Umpqua Holdings Corp. These divestitures, mandated by the U.S. Department of Justice, involve the sale of seven branches to 1st Security Bank of Washington and three to First Northern Bank, with all employees expected to be retained. The merger, which will keep the holding company in Tacoma and trade under Columbia's symbol (COLB), aims for closure in the first quarter of next year.

title: How XEMD Can Help With Emerging Markets Tax Loss Harvesting
summary: Emerging markets investing has seen negative headlines, with broad emerging market bond indexes performing poorly due to rising interest rates. However, intermediate-term emerging markets have shown outperformance. This article suggests that investors with taxable accounts could consider tax-loss harvesting using ETFs like the BondBloxx JP Morgan USD Emerging Markets 1-10 Year Bond ETF (XEMD), which tracks short- to intermediate-term U.S. dollar-denominated emerging market bonds and has shown relative performance advantages in a rising rate environment.

title: OceanFirst and Partners Bancorp call off merger, blaming regulatory delays
summary: OceanFirst Financial and Partners Bancorp have terminated their $186 million merger agreement, citing prolonged regulatory approval processes. Both companies stated that the decision was in their best interest due to the uncertainty surrounding the deal's conclusion, with no termination fees exchanged. This event reflects a broader trend of slowed bank M&A activity attributed to increased regulatory scrutiny and staffing shortages at agencies.

title: Growing Dividends Yield Stability
summary: This Morgan Stanley article discusses how investing in dividend-paying stocks, particularly those with consistent growth, can provide stability and outsized returns during turbulent market conditions. It highlights specific sectors poised for dividend growth, such as Energy, Packaged Food, Beverages and Household Products, Utilities, and Banks, while also cautioning investors to consider factors beyond just high yields, like debt load and earnings stability. The article emphasizes that while dividends offer income and a sign of earnings stability, investors should balance these benefits against the company's need to reinvest in its business.

title: News | Here's What JPMorgan's Head of Global Real Estate Sees As the Future of the Office
summary: David Arena, JPMorgan Chase's head of global real estate, believes the future of the office focuses on adaptable buildings and employee comfort, starting with ergonomic furniture. The bank's new New York headquarters will feature increased communal spaces, abundant plant life, advanced air cleaning, touchless technology, and circadian lighting, all designed for flexibility and employee well-being. Arena emphasizes that design choices must contribute to commercial outcomes by enhancing employee productivity and happiness, and the bank is exploring flexible lease terms and coworking models for its other properties.

title: BD says inflationary pressures persist; COVID-19 test sales plunge
summary: Becton Dickinson (BD) reported that revenue for its medical segment grew in the fourth quarter, partly due to the acquisition of pharmacy automation company Parata, despite facing continuous inflationary pressures, particularly in raw materials. The company’s CEO noted the impact of rising inflation and increased supply/transportation costs. Additionally, COVID-19 testing sales saw a significant decline from $316 million a year ago to $37 million in the recent quarter, affecting its life sciences segment.

title: BlackRock continues to top China ‘power ranking’
summary: BlackRock has once again secured the top position in Broadridge's half-yearly China "power ranking," maintaining its lead for the third consecutive time. This achievement is attributed to the strength and growth of both its wholly-owned fund management company and majority-controlled wealth management subsidiary. Broadridge's study highlights increasing interest among top global asset managers in establishing various entities in onshore China, despite market underperformance impacting overall assets under management.

title: Citigroup to purchase Deutsche Bank’s Mexico license
summary: Citigroup announced its plan to acquire Deutsche Bank's Mexican banking license to maintain its institutional operations in Mexico following the sale of its retail unit, Citibanamex, a move intended to simplify the firm's structure. The sale of Citibanamex is attracting significant bidders like Carlos Slim's Grupo Financiero Inbursa and Germán Larrea's Grupo México. The deal with Deutsche Bank is crucial for Citi to continue serving corporate and wealthy clients in Mexico after divesting its consumer banking arm.

title: ANNONSØRINNHOLD: Bør hun gå inn i boligmarkedet nå? Her er sjeføkonomens klare råd
summary: In uncertain economic times, Sara Sofie and Edvard are weighing whether to buy a home in Bergen or continue renting. Sara Sofie's father, chief economist Kyrre Knudsen, advises them to buy if they plan to stay in the city long-term, emphasizing the stability and long-term benefits of homeownership. Real estate agent Runar Aarekol echoes the importance of a solid plan and highlights that motivated buyers might find good opportunities now due to less competition.

title: New chair, directors appointed to Greater Louisville Foundation Board
summary: Greater Louisville Inc. (GLI) and the Greater Louisville Foundation (GLF) have announced new leadership appointments. Paul Costel of JPMorgan Chase was named chair of the GLF board, and Jill Horn of the Brown-Forman Foundation was appointed as a director. Joe Ventura of Humana joined GLI’s board of directors and executive committee, succeeding Alan Wheatley.

title: Meet the ETFs with the lowest tracking error
summary: This article identifies ETFs with the lowest tracking error across various categories as of October 2022, based on Cafemutual ETF Research. It highlights 10 large-cap ETFs with a tracking error of 0.03, including those from ICICI Prudential, Invesco India, Kotak, Mirae Asset, Nippon India, SBI, and UTI. The research also details top-performing ETFs in mid-cap, debt, factor, gold, international, sector, and thematic categories, providing a comprehensive overview of ETFs with minimal deviation from their underlying indices.

title: Berkshire Hathaway Cuts Stake in U.S. Bancorp By More Than Half. Buffett Has Been Selling Financials.
summary: Berkshire Hathaway, led by Warren Buffett, significantly reduced its stake in U.S. Bancorp by 56%, now holding 52.5 million shares valued at $2.4 billion. This move is consistent with Buffett's broader trend of selling off financial sector holdings. The reduction follows previous divestments in other financial companies.

title: The Rise of State Anti-ESG Legislation
summary: Across numerous states, there is a growing trend of anti-ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) legislation, with some states introducing "boycott bills" that prohibit governmental bodies from engaging with financial institutions perceived to be boycotting industries vital to the state economy. Other states restrict fund managers from considering ESG factors in investments. While proponents argue this prioritizes shareholder profits over ideology, critics contend that the anti-ESG movement misconstrues ESG policies, potentially costing taxpayers more, and serves as a political maneuver rather than protecting state interests.

title: 시장 방향성 좌우하는 금리…“금리 상승·하락 상관관계로 투자전략 수립”
summary: DB금융투자 연구원은 금리 방향성에 따른 투자 전략을 제시하며, 미국 ETF EQRR의 사례를 통해 금리 상승기에는 국채 금리와 상관관계가 높은 섹터에 투자하고, 금리 하락기에는 상관관계가 낮은 섹터에 투자하는 것이 유효하다고 분석했습니다. 국내 시장에도 이 전략을 적용한 결과, 금리 인하 시 상관관계가 낮은 섹터에 투자하는 것이 시장 대비 높은 성과를 보였습니다. 이는 금리 변동에 따른 적절한 투자 종목 선정이 중요함을 시사합니다.

title: Wex readies for acquisitions
summary: Wex, a payment software services provider, is actively seeking acquisitions, leveraging the current economic downturn to acquire targets at more favorable prices. CEO Melissa Smith aims for consistent annual revenue growth, with a portion expected from strategic acquisitions in energy, health benefits, and corporate payments. Despite strong revenue and transaction volume growth in Q3, the company reported a net loss and is focused on cost savings to strengthen its financial position for future purchases.

title: Acrivon Therapeutics Announces Pricing of Initial Public Offering
summary: Acrivon Therapeutics, a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company, announced the pricing of its initial public offering of 7,550,000 shares of common stock at $12.50 per share, expecting to raise approximately $99.4 million. The company also concurrently sold 400,000 shares to an existing stockholder in a private placement. Acrivon's shares are anticipated to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Market under the ticker symbol "ACRV" on November 15, 2022.

title: Barrick Announces Tender Offer for Any and All of Its 5.250% Notes Due 2042
summary: Barrick Gold Corporation has announced a cash tender offer to purchase any and all of its 5.250% Notes due 2042. The offer is subject to conditions outlined in the Offer to Purchase document, with an expiration date of November 18, 2022. Holders whose notes are accepted will receive a Total Consideration in cash, plus accrued and unpaid interest.

title: How Governments can Improve Cybersecurity | JPMorgan Chase
summary: This article by Rosa Ramos-Kwok, Managing Director and Head of Cybersecurity for Commercial Banking at JPMorgan Chase, outlines four key components for government entities to improve their cybersecurity posture. It emphasizes prioritizing cybersecurity at the highest levels, securing the weakest link (employees) through regular training, building a culture of cyber preparedness using frameworks like NIST CSF, and enlisting third-party expertise to supplement in-house resources. The piece highlights the increasing targeting of government agencies by cyberthreats and the significant financial impact of successful attacks.

title: PIMCO's ETF Transfer to NYSE Floor Trading Is a Key Milestone
summary: PIMCO's Active Bond ETF (BOND) has become the first active ETF to be traded from a booth on the NYSE floor, marking a significant milestone for the industry. This move is expected to enhance liquidity, improve price discovery, and reduce transaction costs for investors by adding human oversight from a Designated Market Maker. PIMCO launched its first active fixed income ETF in 2009 and continues to expand its lineup, with actively managed ETFs seeing accelerated adoption due to market volatility.

title: Broker-Dealer ETF Gets $211 Million Mystery Inflow, Most Since 2008
summary: The iShares U.S. Broker-Dealers & Securities Exchanges ETF (IAI) experienced a $211 million inflow on Monday, marking its largest single influx since February 2008 and the second-best since its 2006 launch. This unusual capital injection, likely from a single investor via an over-the-counter transaction, occurred despite the fund's year-to-date losses. While the source remains unknown, theories suggest it could be a tax trade or new interest in traditional Wall Street due to crypto market instability.

title: Prudential Launches FlexGuard Life, A Next-Generation Life Insurance Product That Goes Beyond Death Benefits
summary: Prudential Financial, Inc. has introduced FlexGuard Life, an innovative Indexed Variable Universal Life product designed to offer a flexible combination of protection, growth, and access for evolving life insurance needs. Inspired by the success of Prudential's FlexGuard Indexed Variable Annuity products, this new solution aims to help consumers achieve financial security by providing potential for strong cash value accumulation, downside protection, and customizable benefits for chronic or terminal illness.

title: JPMorgan Chase chief Jamie Dimon bullish on Austin despite economic uncertainty
summary: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon visited Austin, reasserting the bank's commitment to expansion in the city and Texas despite economic uncertainties and a projected recession. JPMorgan Chase is growing its Austin workforce by 10% and leasing additional office space, contrasting with other tech firms that are retrenching. Dimon expressed concern about global geopolitical factors but indicated he is not worried about a housing market crash similar to 2008.

title: Peter Marrone has few regrets as he prepares to exit Yamana Gold after a nearly 20-year run
summary: Peter Marrone, founder of Yamana Gold, is preparing to exit the company after its sale to Agnico Eagle Mines Ltd. and Pan American Silver Corp. for US$4.8-billion. This deal comes after an earlier, unpopular bid from Gold Fields Ltd. was abandoned. Marrone reflects on his nearly 20-year tenure, acknowledging past struggles but expressing pride in Yamana's recent turnaround, and hints at future ventures in the gold mining industry.

title: How to Navigate the Current Market Environment With Active Fixed Income ETFs
summary: This article discusses how active fixed income ETFs can help investors navigate the current market environment by providing reliable, yield-generating investments. It highlights two specific JPMorgan ETFs, JCPB and JPIE, detailing their investment strategies and potential benefits like diversification, income generation, and adaptability to market changes. The piece also promotes an upcoming webcast focusing on inflation, Fed monetary policy, and core fixed income investments.

title: Morgan Stanley rep goes RIA with $5 billion book of business
summary: Jim Martin, a former Morgan Stanley representative with nearly 40 years in the wirehouse channel, has transitioned to independence, launching Nordwand Capital, a multifamily office and investment firm. He moved a $5 billion book of business to Fidelity and Dynasty Financial Partners, specifically targeting ultra-high-net-worth families with a net worth of at least $100 million, after strategically reducing his client base by $4 billion. Industry experts view this as a significant move in the RIA space, highlighting a growing trend of large breakaways from wirehouses to independent models due to enhanced services and technology supporting RIAs.

title: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon backs spending on energy infrastructure during stop in San Antonio
summary: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon, during a stop in San Antonio, advocated for increased investment in energy infrastructure, stating that under-investment in oil and gas globally is causing shortages. He also commented on the recent U.S. elections, expressing hope that a divided Congress could lead to progress on issues like immigration and tax reform, and discussed the labor shortage in the San Antonio market. Dimon also reiterated his earlier warning about an impending economic "hurricane" and highlighted the war in Ukraine as the biggest geopolitical risk since World War II.

title: Grayscale Investments Reaffirms Safety of Holdings
summary: Grayscale Investments reaffirmed that the safety and security of its digital asset products are unaffected by recent market events, despite its affiliate Genesis Global Capital temporarily suspending redemptions and new loan originations. Grayscale emphasized that Genesis Global Capital is not a counterparty for its products and that all assets are held in segregated cold storage by Coinbase Custody Trust Company, LLC. Grayscale CEO Michael Sonnenshein expressed confidence in the crypto industry's future and advocated for greater regulatory clarity.

title: Brookfield expands into Saudi Arabia to target kingdom’s riches
summary: Brookfield Asset Management Inc plans to expand into Saudi Arabia, joining BlackRock Inc and global banks to capitalize on investment opportunities in the Gulf economy. The move follows wide-ranging economic reforms in the kingdom and targets areas such as infrastructure, renewables, private equity, and real estate. Other major firms like Blackstone Inc and KKR & Co are also increasing their presence and efforts in the region, aiming for high-net-worth clients and exploring significant projects.

title: JPMorgan (JPM) Gives All New Parents 16 Weeks of Leave as Perks Boosted
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. has significantly enhanced its employee benefits, offering 16 weeks of parental leave to all new parents for birth or adoption, irrespective of primary caregiver status. These improvements also include increased sick leave and expanded bereavement time. The update aligns JPMorgan's benefits more closely with those offered by competitors like Goldman Sachs and Bank of America.

title: Bitwise Launches Crypto ETF Despite SEC’s ETF Cold Feet
summary: Bitwise has launched the Crypto Industry Innovators ETF (BITQ), which invests in 30 companies deriving at least 75% of their income or net assets from cryptocurrency. This ETF offers investors exposure to the crypto economy through a familiar format, circumventing some complexities of direct digital asset ownership. While similar to other funds, BITQ is notable for being the first SEC-approved ETF to include "crypto" in its name, addressing investor comfort levels and advisor workflow challenges.

title: Citizens Financial Group CEO Bruce Van Saun on why banks aren't slowing down despite loss predictions
summary: Bruce Van Saun, CEO of Citizens Financial Group, discusses the current strength of the banking sector despite market predictions of losses. He highlights that consumers have high savings and employment, and businesses have improved their financial positions during the pandemic. Van Saun explains Citizens' defensive strategy with tighter credit risk and acknowledges the weakening housing market, but dismisses significant threats from crypto implosions or the need to acquire fintech firms.

title: JPMorgan Chase increasing employee benefits
summary: JPMorgan Chase is set to expand its employee time off policies starting in 2023. This move by the financial giant, which has a growing presence in Pittsburgh, aims to enhance benefits for its workforce. The article mentions this expansion in the context of other financial news, including bank M&A trends and branch closures by PNC.

title: Cost of living: Lloyds Bank introduces gambling limits for customers
summary: Lloyds Bank is introducing a new feature allowing customers to set personalized monthly limits on their gambling spending via its mobile app. This initiative aims to help customers manage their budgets amid the cost of living crisis, complementing the existing option to completely freeze gambling transactions. The trial seeks to understand the feature's helpfulness and provide greater control over spending habits, as inflation has significantly impacted consumer purchasing power.

title: Financial firms, lobbying organizations urge Congress to vote on SECURE 2.0
summary: Over 60 financial firms and lobbying organizations are urging Congress to pass the SECURE 2.0 retirement savings bill during the lame-duck session. The legislation, which includes provisions like raising the RMD age, increasing catch-up contributions, and expanding workplace retirement coverage, has bipartisan support and is being compiled from measures passed by the House and advanced by Senate committees. These groups stress the importance of enacting the bill before Congress adjourns to avoid reintroduction in the new year.

title: Deutsche Bank CEO warns of 'danger' of European reliance on foreign banks
summary: Deutsche Bank CEO Christian Sewing warned against Europe's increasing reliance on foreign banks, comparing it to the region's energy dependence on external suppliers, which has caused a crisis. He stated that Europe urgently needs to strengthen its own banking sector to avoid relying on foreign institutions to finance its future, criticizing current regulatory frameworks for not adequately supporting European banks. While acknowledging the past benefits of stronger supervision, Sewing argued that the regulatory pendulum might have swung too far, particularly in areas like leveraged finance, hindering economic recovery.

title: JPMorgan Chase bumps up parental leave to 16 weeks
summary: JPMorgan Chase is increasing its parental leave to 16 weeks for either parent, effective January 1, alongside expanded bereavement leave and up to four weeks of paid time off to care for seriously ill family members. The bank is also raising its full-time employee sick days from six to ten. These benefit enhancements aim to make JPMorgan competitive with other major banks in attracting and retaining talent.

title: Así es Galicia Ventures, el nuevo programa de innovación para escalar startups de América Latina
summary: Grupo Financiero Galicia launched Galicia Ventures, an open innovation and corporate venturing program aimed at accelerating business transformation by investing in and forming alliances with Latin American startups. The program will focus on Fintech, Agtech, and Insurtech industries, both B2C and B2B, leveraging cross-cutting technologies like Web3, DeFi, Big Data, Blockchain, AI, and Cybersecurity. Galicia Ventures plans to contact 350 regional startups in 2023, aiming for 2-3 investments with an average ticket of US$250,000, and five business alliances.

title: Peek inside JPMorgan's new downtown Seattle tech center
summary: JPMorgan has opened a new tech center in downtown Seattle, located in the 1201 Third tower. This center, which features collaborative work areas, is one of 11 such facilities the company operates across the U.S.

title: India's HDFC Bank, Canara Bank get approval for rupee trade with Russia - report
summary: India's HDFC Bank and Canara Bank have received approval from the central bank to open special "vostro accounts" for trading in rupees with Russia, according to a report. This move facilitates international trade settlements in rupees, a mechanism introduced by the Reserve Bank of India in July to boost exports and imports. The measure is also seen as supporting business ties with Russia amidst Western sanctions.

title: Medical debt dropped from credit scores: Here's how you can make sure it's removed from your report
summary: Billions of dollars of medical debt are being removed from credit reports due to recent changes by the three major credit reporting agencies. Previously, medical debt was problematic as it often resulted from unexpected health issues rather than reckless spending. Consumers are advised to check their credit reports at AnnualCreditReport.com to ensure that any eligible medical debt has been removed.

title: Leader of Walmart health business leaves for JPMorgan Chase
summary: Dr. Cheryl Pegus, head of Walmart's health and wellness business, is departing her role to join Morgan Health, a business unit of JPMorgan Chase. Morgan Health focuses on employer-sponsored health care.

title: JPMorgan American - Nov 2022
summary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of JPMorgan American (JAM) as of November 2022, highlighting its distinctive approach to US equity investing by blending growth and value styles. It discusses the fund's historical outperformance against its benchmark and peers since a strategic change in mid-2019, its low ongoing charge, and its resilient share price rating. The analysis also covers management changes, portfolio construction, and key investment characteristics.

title: New chief investment strategist at PNC Asset Management Group
summary: PNC Asset Management Group has appointed Marc Dizard as its new chief investment strategist. Dizard brings significant experience to the role within PNC Financial Services Group Inc. The Pittsburgh Business Times piece highlights this key personnel change.

title: Manulife takes control of China unit as foreign ownership barriers fall
summary: Manulife Investment Management has received approval from Beijing to take full control of its mainland Chinese joint venture, Manulife TEDA Fund Management, by acquiring the remaining 51% stake for 1.7 billion yuan (US$237.22 million). This move makes Manulife the first foreign asset manager to convert its joint venture into a wholly-owned fund management company in China, reflecting Beijing's increased willingness to open up its financial markets since foreign ownership restrictions were scrapped in April 2020. The full acquisition will grant Manulife direct access to China's large and rapidly growing retail fund market.

title: Private Patient Financing: A Sleek Term for a Questionable Business Model
summary: Hospitals are increasingly partnering with private lenders to offer financing options to patients, often involving interest-bearing payment plans. While hospitals traditionally offered interest-free plans, these new arrangements with companies like AccessOne and Synchrony allow third parties to profit from interest charged on medical debt. This trend, similar to Buy Now, Pay Later schemes, raises concerns as millions of Americans are paying interest on medical bills, and this industry boasts high profit margins, often at the expense of patients already struggling financially.

title: PIMCO ETF hits NYSE trading floor
summary: PIMCO has listed its PIMCO Active Bond ETF (BOND) on the NYSE trading floor, marking the exchange's first ETF listing in 15 years and the first actively-managed ETF in the open outcry arena. The firm is employing a digital and human hybrid system, including a designated market maker, to enhance liquidity, reduce volatility, and improve price determination. This move follows recent SEC rule changes permitting a wider range of ETFs to list on the NYSE floor, and PIMCO is considering further ETF listings there.

title: WSJ News Exclusive | Jeffrey Epstein Accusers Sue Deutsche Bank, JPMorgan
summary: Women who have accused Jeffrey Epstein of sexual abuse are suing Deutsche Bank AG and JPMorgan Chase & Co., alleging that the banks facilitated Epstein’s sex-trafficking operation. The lawsuits claim the banks ignored red flags about their client. Both lawsuits seek class-action status and unspecified financial damages, and were filed in federal court in New York.

title: Kosciusko County Court News
summary: This article provides a detailed list of recent court judgments in Kosciusko County, Indiana, covering various legal categories. It includes small claims, civil collections, evictions, plenaries, mortgage foreclosures, civil torts, and an extensive list of infractions from Superior Court III. The cases involve individuals and companies, with specific financial awards and penalties noted for each.

title: Linhas de crédito para a cafeicultura são oferecidas através de 37 agentes financeiros
summary: Brazilian coffee growers now have access to R$6.058 billion in credit lines from the Coffee Economy Defense Fund (Funcafé) for the 2022/2023 harvest. These funds are available through 37 financial institutions, including banks and cooperatives, and are intended for financing production, storage, commercialization, and the recovery of coffee plantations damaged by adverse weather. The credit is distributed across five main lines, with an interest rate capped at 11% for this harvest.

title: BDCs Sport Lofty Yields, But the Risks Are Growing. Time to Steer Clear.
summary: Business development companies (BDCs) have offered attractive dividend yields, around 10%, appealing to retail investors. However, there is a growing concern about the associated risks, suggesting a need for caution despite their popularity and increased assets.

title: Merger with HDFC to take 8-10 months more: HDFC Bank
summary: HDFC Bank expects to complete its merger with parent company HDFC by September of the following year, which is 8-10 months from the announced date. This timeline is shorter than the initial 12-18 months projected when the merger was announced on April 4. Both entities have sought shareholder approvals for this significant merger, which is valued at over USD 40 billion.

title: Banks explore reimbursing customers who send money to scam Zelle accounts
summary: Banks are beginning to explore options for reimbursing customers who have been scammed through Zelle, particularly in cases where scammers mimic bank customer service lines. This shift comes amidst increasing pressure from consumers and politicians, as banks have historically been slow to offer refunds for "authorized transactions" even if they were fraudulent. The changes would involve revising current refund procedures within their banking networks.

title: M&T Bank Corp. stock outperforms competitors despite losses on the day
summary: M&T Bank Corp. (MTB) stock fell 1.52% to $169.52 on a generally negative trading day for the stock market, breaking a three-day winning streak. Despite its own losses, the stock outperformed several key competitors including JPMorgan Chase & Co. (JPM), Bank of America Corp. (BAC), and Wells Fargo & Co. (WFC), which experienced larger percentage drops. The stock closed $23.90 below its 52-week high, with trading volume significantly below its 50-day average.

title: Blakes assists in RBC’s 13.5-billion-dollar acquisition of HSBC Canadian unit
summary: Blake, Cassels & Graydon acted as Canadian legal counsel for HSBC in its $13.5 billion sale of its Canadian assets to the Royal Bank of Canada. RBC's acquisition of HSBC's Canadian unit is expected to expand its presence by adding approximately 130 branches. The article also covers CPP Investments' $635-million acquisition of a stake in Brazilian network provider V.Tal and Iconic Minerals' deal to option 50 percent of its Smith Creek project.

title: How strategic alliances are reshaping supply chain finance solutions
summary: This article discusses how strategic alliances between banks and fintechs are reshaping supply chain finance solutions, offering a "best of both worlds" approach to address challenges like complex onboarding and the need for liquidity. Experts from J.P. Morgan, Taulia, and Flex highlight the importance of intuitive technology, robust data, and dedicated support teams for effective SCF programs, especially given the increased demand for early payments accelerated by the pandemic. They emphasize ongoing collaboration between financial institutions and technology providers to innovate and create scalable, flexible solutions for a diverse supplier base.

title: RBC to buy HSBC’s Canada unit for $10B
summary: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) has agreed to acquire HSBC’s Canada unit in an all-cash deal valued at C$13.5 billion ($10 billion). This acquisition, expected to close in late 2023, will add $99.6 billion in assets and 130 branches to RBC, further solidifying its position as Canada's largest bank. The deal may also alleviate pressure on HSBC from its largest shareholder, Ping An, which has been pushing for a split of its Western and Asian operations.

title: The lines between Food & Grocery delivery continue to blur
summary: The article discusses the blurring lines between food and grocery delivery services as major third-party delivery platforms expand their offerings. It highlights DoorDash's significant growth in attracting new digital visitors and its effective use of influencers, as well as the strategic partnerships between credit card issuers like Chase and Mastercard with Instacart and DoorDash to incentivize market growth.

title: HSBC to sell Canadian business to Royal Bank of Canada for US$10 billion
summary: HSBC will sell its Canadian operations to Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) for C$13.5 billion (US$10 billion) in cash, as HSBC focuses on its Asia strategy. The sale follows a strategic review of the Canadian business and comes amidst pressure from HSBC's largest shareholder, Ping An Insurance, to spin off its Asian business. The transaction is expected to close in late 2023, pending regulatory approvals.

title: Raft of top firms called in as Royal Bank of Canada buys HSBC Canada in ‘once in a generation’ $13.5bn cash deal
summary: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) is acquiring HSBC Bank Canada for C$13.5bn in an all-cash deal, described by RBC's CEO as a "once in a generation opportunity." This acquisition will significantly increase RBC's market share and client base, particularly among commercial clients with international needs and affluent clients. Top law firms Allen & Overy, Wachtell Lipton Rosen & Katz, and Linklaters are advising on the transaction.

title: HSBC to Axe More Than 100 UK Branches in Move to Mobile Banking
summary: HSBC announced it will close 114 bank branches across the UK starting next April due to declining customer footfall. After these closures, the bank will retain a network of 327 branches, with investments planned for their improvement. The move reflects a broader shift towards mobile banking services.

title: State Street pulls plug on $3.5 billion Brown Brothers Harriman acquisition
summary: State Street and Brown Brothers Harriman have mutually agreed to terminate their $3.5 billion acquisition deal after more than a year of regulatory uncertainty and scrutiny from the Biden administration. The deal, intended to make State Street the number one provider of asset services globally, faced increasing delays and complexities, ultimately leading to its cancellation without a breakup fee. Investors reacted positively to the news, with State Street's stock rising 5 percent.

title: BlackRock CEO Says ‘Next Generation for Markets’ Is Tokenization
summary: BlackRock CEO Larry Fink stated that the future of markets lies in the tokenization of securities, highlighting benefits like instantaneous settlement and reduced fees. While he believes blockchain technology will be crucial, he anticipates that most cryptocurrency companies will not survive. Fink also clarified BlackRock's minor exposure to the FTX scandal, noting their investment was in a subsidiary "fund of funds."

title: Banca de Inversiones Bancolombia amplía su participación en AFP Protección a 9,98%
summary: Banca de Inversiones Bancolombia has increased its stake in AFP Protección to 9.98% following a transfer of shares from Bancolombia S.A. The Superfianciera de Colombia has verified this change. Additionally, AFP Protección's shareholders recently approved a spin-off plan to create an insurance company for life annuities and provisional insurance, transferring assets worth $785.009 million.

title: Banks prepare for economic turbulence after mixed annual results
summary: Canadian banks concluded their fiscal year on an uncertain note, with benefits from rising interest rates offset by higher costs and increasing loan losses. Five out of six major lenders reported flat or lower profits, with some missing analyst estimates, while TD Bank bucked the trend due to strong deposit growth and loan margins. Looking ahead to fiscal year 2023, banks anticipate a challenging economic environment characterized by high inflation, slower growth, and geopolitical tensions, prompting a focus on managing lending margins and controlling expenses.

title: JPMorgan Chase Launches ‘Digital Money Coach,’ With Link to Human Advisors
summary: JPMorgan Chase has introduced a "Digital Money Coach" tool designed to help customers manage their finances. This new tool also serves as a pathway for clients to potentially connect and work with a J.P. Morgan advisor. This initiative provides J.P. Morgan Wealth Management advisors with a new avenue for client engagement.

title: Canadian banks gird for loan loss threat as economic outlook sours
summary: Canadian banks, including CIBC, Bank of Montreal, and Toronto-Dominion Bank, are increasing provisions for potential loan defaults due to inflation-hit customers and a souring economic outlook. While TD Bank exceeded estimates thanks to its U.S. retail business, CIBC and BMO fell short, with both reporting significant increases in credit loss provisions. The central bank's interest rate hikes have boosted lending profits but are also contributing to concerns over asset quality deterioration.

title: NexPoint Residential Trust, Inc. Completes Refinancings of 18-Properties With 1 Additional Refinancing Expected to Close on December 1st; "De-risks" the Balance Sheet through Improved Cost of Capital/Extends Weighted Average Maturity to 6.3 years
summary: NexPoint Residential Trust, Inc. (NXRT) announced the completion of refinancings for 18 properties, with one more expected to close on December 1st, totaling $807.6 million. This strategic move improves the company's cost of capital, extends its weighted average debt maturity to 6.34 years, and reduces the weighted average interest rate on total debt. The refinancing significantly "de-risks" the balance sheet by postponing meaningful debt maturities until 2025 and increasing liquidity.

title: One quarter of TD mortgages now have an amortization of 35+ years
summary: Over a quarter of TD Bank's residential mortgage portfolio now has an effective amortization of 35 years or longer, up from none a year ago. This increase is largely due to rising interest rates impacting variable-rate borrowers. While clients will need to increase payments at renewal, TD maintains its asset quality is strong and expects an unwind of some housing gains without a crisis.

title: New York Community Bancorp Completes Acquisition of Flagstar Bancorp
summary: New York Community Bancorp, Inc. (NYCB) announced the completion of its acquisition of Flagstar Bancorp, Inc., creating a regional banking franchise among the top 25 in the U.S. The combined entity will have $88.4 billion in assets, $66.0 billion in loans, and $58.3 billion in deposits on a proforma basis as of September 30, 2022. This merger aims to diversify revenue, improve funding mix, and enhance the interest-rate risk profile, while also expanding the retail banking network and national lending businesses.

title: Manulife Launches Forest Climate Fund to Raise $500 Million
summary: Manulife Investment Management has launched its Forest Climate Fund (FCF) with the goal of raising $500 million to acquire sustainably managed forests that sequester carbon. This initiative aims to generate high-integrity carbon credits for investors by prioritizing carbon capture over logging, and will also offer financial returns through various strategies. The fund is open to institutional investors globally, including pensions and endowments, and seeks to align with Manulife's broader sustainability and responsible investing goals.

title: Shoals Technologies Group, Inc. Announces Pricing of
summary: Shoals Technologies Group, Inc. announced the pricing of an upsized underwritten public offering of 26,000,000 shares of its Class A common stock at $22.25 per share. The company will offer 2,000,000 shares, and certain selling stockholders will offer 24,000,000 shares. The company plans to use its proceeds to fund a portion of a $58.1 million termination consideration for its Tax Receivable Agreement.

title: Latino-Owned Businesses May Be the U.S. Economy’s Best Bet
summary: Latino-owned businesses (LOBs) are rapidly expanding and could significantly boost the U.S. economy, potentially adding $1.46 trillion if their growth matched the national average. Despite their potential, LOBs often face challenges accessing capital, with 70% of funding coming from personal savings and only 6% from commercial loans. Nonprofits like Accion, supported by organizations such as JPMorgan Chase, help these entrepreneurs secure funding, build credit, and navigate the business landscape to unlock their full economic impact.

title: RIA Quick Takes: Orion deepens DFA embrace by using it as portfolio manager-inside-ETF ~ Hardship withdrawals surge at Vanguard and Fidelity ~ Schwab hires 400 ~ Fidelity flips six funds into ETFs ~ Kitces makes list before Christmas ~ Amit Dogra has $1
summary: This article provides a quick summary of several significant developments in the RIA industry. Key topics include Orion's expanded use of Dimensional Fund Advisors (DFA) in its ETFs, a notable increase in hardship withdrawals at Vanguard and Fidelity, Schwab's hiring of 400 new employees, and Fidelity's conversion of six mutual funds into ETFs. Additionally, it mentions Michael Kitces making a list and Amit Dogra's successful new venture in Portland.

title: AFTX IPO News - Gene therapy biotech Affinia Therapeutics withdraws $100 million IPO
summary: Affinia Therapeutics, a preclinical biotech focused on gene therapies for rare diseases and cancer, has withdrawn its plans for a $100 million initial public offering. The company, which originally filed in January 2022, had not updated its prospectus since. It had planned to list on the Nasdaq under the symbol AFTX.

title: Biden signs bill to block U.S. railroad strike
summary: President Biden signed legislation to avert a national railroad strike, which could have severely impacted the U.S. economy. The bill imposes a tentative contract agreement, but without a provision for paid sick leave, drawing criticism from some labor leaders. Despite the controversy, Biden stated the action was necessary to protect jobs, families, and supply chains from economic catastrophe.

title: Kakao Pay seeks to acquire Loca Mobility up for sale by MBK Partners
summary: Kakao Pay is looking to acquire Loca Mobility from MBK Partners, a move that could expand its business scope and create synergy with Kakao Mobility. The acquisition is part of MBK Partners' strategy to divest its investment in Lotte Card. Loca Mobility, the second-largest public transportation card operator in Korea, is set to open a preliminary bid on December 6, with MBK and Lotte Card hoping to fetch around 300 billion won ($231 million) from the sale.

title: News | New Headquarters of World's Largest Brokerage Stalls Amid Financing, Office Demand Concerns
summary: CBRE's planned 27-story headquarters in Dallas is stalled due to rising interest rates, inflation, and concerns about office demand. This delay jeopardizes millions in incentives from the city and state, as the project is unlikely to meet its construction timeline. The situation highlights broader challenges in the commercial real estate market, with CBRE undergoing cost-cutting measures and other companies renegotiating incentive agreements due to work-from-home trends.

title: How HSBC is executing a global overhaul
summary: HSBC is undergoing a global overhaul, marked by its recent agreement to sell its Canadian business to RBC for approximately US$10.1 billion. This move is part of the bank's broader strategy to cut costs and rationalize its operations, following similar sales of its US retail business and its French business, as well as branch closures in the UK. The CEO stated that the sale of the Canadian business makes strategic sense, freeing up capital for investment in core businesses and returns to shareholders.

title: Bank of Hope data breach class action settlement
summary: Bank of Hope agreed to a class action settlement to resolve claims that a 2018 data breach exposed Californians’ sensitive information. The settlement provides reimbursement for out-of-pocket expenses up to $500, two years of free identity-theft protection through Experian, and mandates cybersecurity improvements by Bank of Hope. The deadline for claims and exclusion was February 7, 2023.

title: Delaware District Court: Using Contract Rights to Strategic Advantage Not Grounds for Equitable Subordination in Bankruptcy
summary: The U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware affirmed that using contractual rights to strategic advantage is not grounds for equitable subordination in bankruptcy, a ruling welcomed by lenders. The case, *Tilton v. MBIA Inc. (In re Zohar III, Corp.)*, reinforces that courts require a high bar for misconduct, especially for non-insiders, to justify equitable subordination. This decision provides comfort to lenders looking to enforce their contractual rights without undue exposure to broad lender liability claims.

title: J.P. Morgan looks to offer active ETF focused on China
summary: J.P. Morgan is planning to launch an actively managed Exchange Traded Fund (ETF) that will focus its investments on China. This initiative by J.P. Morgan indicates a strategic move to offer investors specialized exposure to the Chinese market through an ETF structure. The announcement was made by Kathie O'Donnell on December 5, 2022.

title: Economic Outlooks: The Year Ahead
summary: RBC Capital Markets provides economic outlooks for the US, Canada, Europe, and Australia for the coming year, 2023. While many regions anticipate challenges such as recessions, persistent inflation, and tightening monetary policies, Australia is uniquely positioned to potentially avoid a recession due to strong resilience, high terms of trade, and robust labor market conditions. The report highlights country-specific factors, including central bank actions, energy crises, and consumer spending, that will shape economic performance.

title: Entergy New Orleans replenishes storm recovery coffers with $209.3 million issuance
summary: Entergy New Orleans (ENO) is issuing approximately $209.3 million in storm recovery bonds to replenish funds depleted by Hurricanes Zeta and Ida. These bonds, secured by storm recovery property, will be repaid through storm recovery charges on ENO's retail electric customers, with the charges adjusted semiannually. Both Moody's and S&P Global Ratings are assigning high ratings to the single tranche issuance, citing ENO's stability and experience as a servicer.

title: Morgan Stanley Cuts 2% of Global Work Force as Deal-Making Slows (Published 2022)
summary: Morgan Stanley is laying off approximately 2% of its global workforce, impacting around 1,600 employees across all divisions, due to a significant slowdown in deal-making activity. This move comes after the firm had paused layoffs during the pandemic and reflects broader economic jitters and rising interest rates impacting the investment banking sector. Other major banks like Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase have also seen their stock shares decline over the past year.

title: Wells Fargo Archives
summary: This archive of Finovate articles details Wells Fargo's digital transformation efforts, including the launch of its Vantage digital banking platform for commercial clients and the Flex Loan small dollar financing solution. It also covers Wells Fargo's participation in the Akoya Data Access Network for API-based data aggregation and historical analyses of its website design and mobile banking strategies. The collection highlights the bank's initiatives to enhance customer experience, manage short-term cash needs, and improve digital engagement.

title: Vietnam's EV maker Vinfast files for U.S. IPO to fuel global expansion
summary: Vietnam's electric-vehicle maker VinFast has filed for an initial public offering (IPO) in the United States to list on the Nasdaq under ticker symbol "VFS", aiming to fund its global expansion including a planned plant in North Carolina. The company will convert to a Singapore public limited company named VinFast Auto Ltd for the IPO, with Citigroup, Morgan Stanley, Credit Suisse, and JP Morgan leading a nine-bank syndicate. This move follows an earlier confidential submission and plans to raise $2 billion with a valuation of around $60 billion, although market conditions have cooled for EV startups.

title: Is Corporate America on a Path to Gender Equality?
summary: A discussion hosted by JPMorgan Chase and The Partnership for New York City brought together 50 women leaders to address gender equality in the workplace. The event highlighted research from McKinsey & Company indicating it could take a century to reach CEO-level gender parity, despite the potential for a $2.1 trillion boost to the US economy by narrowing the gender gap. While companies have programs for gender equality, cultural change and senior-level mentorship are crucial to achieving significant progress.

title: NRG Energy Acquires Smart Grid Solutions Company Vivint for $2.8 Billion
summary: NRG Energy has agreed to acquire Vivint Smart Home in an all-cash transaction valued at $2.8 billion, assuming an additional $2.4 billion in debt, bringing the total transaction value to $5.2 billion. Vivint, a smart grid solutions company serving 1.9 million customers, offers an intelligent home platform with products from security systems to smart home devices capable of integrating solar production data. This acquisition is expected to accelerate NRG's growth strategy, diversify its financial profile, and create a leading home solutions provider with 7.4 million customers across North America.

title: IMM, Lotte to inject another $76 mn in Hanssem at default risk
summary: South Korea's IMM Private Equity and Lotte Group are planning to inject an additional 100 billion won ($75.6 million) into Hanssem Co., the country's largest furniture maker, due to the company's loan-to-value (LTV) exceeding 85%. This supplementary investment aims to stabilize Hanssem's financial situation, as the company recorded an operating loss in the third quarter amid a real estate market downturn. IMM PE is also considering selling Hanssem's headquarters to enhance corporate value, and the new investment will exempt Hanssem from LTV testing until June 2024.

title: Small Business Owners Most Like AmEx, Closely Followed by Chase and BofA
summary: A J.D. Power report indicates that American Express cards are the most favored among small business owners for the second consecutive year, with Chase and Bank of America following. The study highlights that small businesses rely heavily on credit cards to manage inflation and supply-chain challenges, yet satisfaction with rewards programs has declined. Card companies are encouraged to see this as an opportunity to become a more valuable resource for these businesses, despite an expected decrease in credit card spending by SMBs in the coming year.

title: January 8, 2019 - EX-99.1 - 8-K: Current report filing | The Coca-Cola Company (KO)
summary: The Coca-Cola Company announced the completion of its $4.9 billion acquisition of Costa Limited from Whitbread PLC, following regulatory approvals. This acquisition provides Coca-Cola with a significant entry into the global coffee business, which is growing at 6% annually, offering a scalable platform for future expansion and new product introductions. The move is part of Coca-Cola's strategy to expand its portfolio in the growing coffee category and leverage Costa's capabilities with Coca-Cola's global reach.

title: Coca-Cola Takes Its Obesity Philanthropy to China
summary: New research reveals that Coca-Cola deliberately undermined China's efforts to address its growing obesity epidemic by shifting the direction of obesity research in its favor. Through financial support of organizations like the International Life Sciences Institute (ILSI), Coca-Cola promoted exercise as the primary solution to obesity, rather than dietary changes. This influence has significantly impacted China's public health policy, entrenching the idea that physical activity is the main solution.

title: Will Monster Reign with its new performance energy drink?
summary: Monster Beverage Corp. is launching a new performance energy drink called Reign in March, targeting both traditional energy drink consumers and the pre-/post-workout market with zero-sugar, zero-calorie options containing caffeine, BCAAs, and CoQ10. This move attempts to expand Monster's customer base to health-conscious consumers, despite competitive market challenges and recent struggles with international sales and gross margins. Alongside Reign, Monster plans further innovations in tea and coffee to drive growth and leadership in the energy drink sector.

title: Coca-Cola CEO: More uncertainty is the ‘biggest issue’
summary: Coca-Cola CEO James Quincey discussed the company's growth in 2019 and the soft drink sector during an interview on "Squawk Box" in Davos. He identified "more uncertainty" as the biggest issue facing the business. The article highlights his perspective on these challenges.

title: Coca-Cola Femsa y el Estado de México anuncian una alianza contra la inseguridad
summary: Coca-Cola Femsa and the State of Mexico have announced an alliance to combat insecurity. This partnership involves sharing video surveillance from Femsa's plants and Oxxo stores with the state's C5 centers, and integrating company trucks into the state's monitoring system for immediate response to incidents. Additionally, Femsa will contribute to crime prevention by developing recreational spaces in areas where the state is investing in lighting infrastructure.

title: Crónica: Visita a la planta más grande de Coca Cola Femsa
summary: This article details a visit to Coca-Cola Femsa's Toluca plant, which celebrates its 20th anniversary. It highlights the plant's growth from one production line to 12, producing 700,000 cases daily, and its position as the third-largest Coca-Cola bottler globally and the largest for Femsa. The piece also covers its sustainable practices, including achieving "zero waste" certification and utilizing renewable energy and water recycling.

title: Delta Air Lines, Coca-Cola Apologize For Offensive In-flight Napkins
summary: Delta Air Lines and Coca-Cola have issued apologies for in-flight napkins that were deemed "creepy" by passengers. The napkins, advertising Diet Coke, encouraged passengers to write down their name and number to give to their "plane crush." Both companies stated they are removing the offending napkins and replacing them with other designs.

title: Hershey Bans Animal Tests After Working With PETA
summary: The Hershey Company has re-committed to banning animal testing for marketing health claims after PETA identified a violation of a previous pledge. This recommitment follows an incident where Hershey provided cocoa ingredients for an experiment involving mice, which the company confirmed as an "anomaly" and has now formalized its no-animal-testing policy publicly. Hershey joins a growing list of companies that have ended animal experiments for health marketing claims after discussions with PETA.

title: Coke Sales Suffer in Southern California Under New Distribution System; Survey Says
summary: The Teamsters Union announced a conference call for Coca-Cola Co. investors and analysts to discuss declining sales and service in Southern California due to Reyes Coca-Cola Bottling's new "static routing" delivery program. A Teamster survey of retailers in metro Los Angeles and San Diego revealed significant disruption, raising questions for investors and impacting Teamster jobs ahead of contract negotiations.

title: Coke stock heads for worst day since 2008, Nvidia looks to capitalize on ‘positive set up’
summary: Coca-Cola Co. (Coke) stock is experiencing a significant downturn, heading for its worst day since 2008, largely due to "softness" in its North America business, a revenue miss, and a disappointing outlook for the year. The company is facing challenges in regions like Argentina and Turkey and plans to increase marketing expenses in 2019, despite some encouraging trends in North America and China.
