The initiative helps provide essential services, academic support, and a safe environment during these challenging times.

title: How Coca-Cola Is Using an Authentic Voice to Make a Difference
summary: This article highlights how Coca-Cola is leveraging an authentic voice to drive change and connect with consumers, especially through its sustainability efforts and social justice initiatives. Bea Perez, Coca-Cola's chief public affairs, communications, sustainability and marketing assets officer, discusses the company's evolution in communicating sustainability as a growth story and its commitment to values like transparency and action regarding social issues. The piece emphasizes the ongoing journey for brands in these areas, advocating for industry-wide collaboration.

title: Will Pepsi’s Driftwell ‘ScaleWell’?
summary: The article analyzes the market viability of PepsiCo's new sleep aid beverage, Driftwell, examining its pricing, placement, product attributes, and promotional strategy. It contrasts Driftwell's approach with Pepsi's traditional mass-market successes like Bubly, highlighting the challenges of scaling a niche functional beverage. The author suggests that for Driftwell to succeed, Pepsi will need patience, effective consumer learning, and a focus on building credibility for its active ingredients to eventually target the broader market of OTC sleeping pills.

title: Optimizing Liquidity for a Top Soft Drink Company
summary: This article details how J.P. Morgan helped a major flavored carbonated soft drink company optimize its liquidity and gain greater control over its cash flow. Through a comprehensive cash management solution, including a Host-to-Host system for centralized payments and an Intercompany Report module, J.P. Morgan enabled the company to streamline its treasury operations, improve visibility, and enhance liquidity through preferential overnight investment rates. The solution standardized operations in Mexico, integrating them into the North America shared service center.

title: Coca-Cola will launch its first alcoholic beverage in 2021
summary: Coca-Cola is set to launch its first alcoholic beverage, Topo Chico Hard Seltzer, in the U.S. in early 2021 through an agreement with Molson Coors Beverage Company. The new hard seltzer, inspired by Topo Chico sparkling mineral water, will come in four flavors and contain 4.7% alcohol by volume, entering a rapidly growing market segment already popular with brands like White Claw. This move is part of Molson Coors' strategy to expand its premium portfolio and compete in the hard seltzer market.

title: Molson Coors Strikes Deal with Coca-Cola to Manufacture, Market, Distribute Topo Chico Hard Seltzer in US
summary: Molson Coors has partnered with The Coca-Cola Company to manufacture, market, and distribute Topo Chico Hard Seltzer in the U.S., with a launch planned for the first half of 2021. This move is part of Molson Coors' strategy to expand its above-premium portfolio and strengthen its position in the rapidly growing hard seltzer market. The new hard seltzer will feature four flavors and aims to compete with dominant brands like White Claw and Truly Hard Seltzer.

title: PepsiCo (PEP) Locks Distribution Deal for evian in Canada
summary: PepsiCo's subsidiary, PepsiCo Beverages Canada, has signed an exclusive distribution agreement with Danone Waters of America to distribute evian natural spring water across Canada starting January 2021. This partnership aligns with PepsiCo's hydration strategy and is expected to expand evian's reach and accelerate its growth. The deal comes as beverage companies like PepsiCo, Coca-Cola, Molson Coors, and Boston Beer are revamping their product portfolios to meet altered consumer preferences, particularly focusing on health and wellness offerings.

title: La Colombe Coffee Roasters Signs 10-Year Distribution Pact with Molson Coors
summary: La Colombe Coffee Roasters has signed a 10-year exclusive distribution agreement with Molson Coors Beverage Company for its ready-to-drink coffee products, initially targeting drug and convenience channels with plans for broader expansion. This partnership aims to significantly boost La Colombe's market presence, particularly in retail sectors where it currently has limited reach, building on its strong sales growth that has outpaced the RTD coffee category. Molson Coors benefits by adding an "above-premium" non-alcoholic offering to its expanding portfolio, marking another step in its strategy beyond traditional alcoholic beverages.

title: Coca-Cola is discontinuing Zico, its coconut water brand
summary: Coca-Cola is discontinuing its Zico coconut water brand as part of a broader strategy to streamline its beverage lineup and focus on best-selling products. This move follows an earlier decision to discontinue the Odwalla juice and smoothie brand, and is part of an ongoing effort to eliminate "zombie brands" that are not growing. The company aims to cut costs and ease strain on supply chains amid declining beverage sales during the pandemic.

title: Coca-Cola to discontinue Zico coconut water and consider other cuts
summary: Coca-Cola is discontinuing its Zico coconut water brand and considering cutting other less-popular versions of Coke and Diet Coke as part of an effort to streamline its portfolio. This move follows ongoing efforts by the beverage giant to focus on offerings with large-scale potential and improve operational efficiency during the pandemic. Brands like Diet Coke Feisty Cherry, Coke Life, and Hubert's Lemonade are under review, while the company also plans buyouts for 4,000 employees as part of a broader restructuring.

title: Coca-Cola PH just modernized its fleet with 200 brand-new Toyotas
summary: Coca-Cola Beverages Philippines, Inc. (CCBPI) has acquired 200 new Toyota vehicles, including Wigo, Vios, and Hilux models, to enhance the safety and transportation of its sales personnel, especially amidst the COVID-19 pandemic. These new vehicles will replace decommissioned units and aim to protect employees serving micro, small, and medium enterprises. Toyota Motor Philippines will maintain these vehicles through its leasing partner, Orix Rental Corporation, emphasizing both companies' commitment to mobility and safety.

title: Kevin Smith
summary: This article profiles Kevin Smith, Chief Marketing Officer at Rollins Inc., highlighting his circuitous career path through global brands like Coca-Cola and the NFL before joining Rollins. It details how his diverse experiences prepared him for his current role, particularly in managing the 120-year-old Orkin brand and adapting it to modern times. The piece also emphasizes Smith's commitment to family, his data-driven marketing approach, and Rollins' focus on talent acquisition as keys to success.

title: Contact-Free Mobile Pouring Comes to Wendy's
summary: Wendy's has introduced a new contact-free mobile pouring option for Coca-Cola Freestyle machines at its restaurants nationwide. This innovation allows customers to select and pour beverages directly from their smartphones by scanning a QR code, eliminating the need for physical interaction with the dispenser. The initiative aims to enhance safety and hygiene in response to the ongoing coronavirus pandemic, offering a convenient solution for customers.

title: ARKO / GPM Expands to Almost 3,000 Combined Company Operated and Wholesale Sites Across 33 States
summary: ARKO Holdings, Ltd. / GPM Investments, LLC announced the closing of its acquisition of Empire Petroleum Partners' fuel distribution business and retail locations, expanding its network to nearly 3,000 sites across 33 states and doubling its annual fuel distribution to over 2 billion gallons. This strategic acquisition is a significant milestone for Arko, especially as it moves forward with its business combination with Haymaker Acquisition Corp. II, which is expected to result in the combined company being publicly listed on NASDAQ under the ticker ARKO. The deal enhances GPM's scale, diversifies its business mix, and significantly increases its cash flow with the addition of approximately 1,500 independently operated fueling stations and 85 company-operated convenience stores.

title: OXIGEN Beverages Inc. Announces $15 Million Series B Funding With Marquee Investors
summary: OXIGEN Beverages Inc. has secured $15 million in Series B funding, attracting a diverse group of celebrity and business leaders as investors, including Stephen Curry, Brett Eldredge, and Kevin Love. The company, which has seen 300-400% year-over-year growth, plans to use the capital to boost brand awareness through marketing and scale national distribution. OXIGEN is known for its pH-balanced, oxygen-boosted water made from 100% recycled plastic and has launched a "Recover + Rise" campaign supporting frontline workers.

title: Can’t find your favorite soda at the store? Here’s why
summary: A shortage of aluminum cans, coupled with increased demand for canned beverages due to people staying home, is making it difficult to find certain sodas and canned drinks. Beverage companies like Coca-Cola and Pepsi are focusing on their most popular brands, leading to reduced availability of less common varieties. The largest U.S. can manufacturer, Ball Corp, plans to open two new plants in 2021 to address the supply issues.

title: Campaign Spotlight: Private Sector launches "Ingat Angat Tayong Lahat" campaign for consumer confidence and economic recovery
summary: The private sector in the Philippines has launched the "Ingat Angat Tayong Lahat" campaign to restore consumer confidence and aid economic recovery amidst the COVID-19 pandemic. This initiative encourages businesses to maintain strict safety standards while increasing operations and urges Filipinos to safely resume activities outside their homes. The campaign, supported by numerous major corporations and media partners, emphasizes public-private sector cooperation and adherence to minimum health protocols to protect both lives and livelihoods.

title: Loop Industries (LOOP) stock: Tapping into infinite plastic recycling
summary: Loop Industries aims to overcome the limitations of mechanical recycling through its patented chemical recycling technology, which allows for unlimited plastic recycling and substitutes virgin plastics. The company, which is pre-revenue, has already secured packaging deals with major consumer brands like PepsiCo and Coca-Cola, aligning with global sustainability targets. Loop Industries plans to expand its operations globally through partnerships and eventually license its technology as a key growth driver.

title: Sempra Energy Named to Forbes JUST 100 List
summary: Sempra Energy was named to the Forbes JUST 100 list, ranking 96th among U.S. publicly traded corporations for its performance on issues important to the American public. The list evaluates companies based on factors such as fair wages, human rights, worker training, ethics, diversity, and worker health and safety. Lisa Alexander, Sempra's senior vice president of corporate affairs, expressed honor at the recognition for creating long-term sustainable value.

title: Coca-Cola eliminating Tab, its original diet soft drink
summary: Coca-Cola announced it is discontinuing Tab, its original diet soft drink launched in 1963, as part of an effort to drop underperforming products. Despite its nostalgic pop culture status, Tab's sales have been declining significantly, leading to its elimination alongside other brands. The decision reflects Coca-Cola's broader strategy to streamline its portfolio amidst pandemic-related financial pressures and shifting consumer preferences away from artificially sweetened drinks.

title: Coke Retiring Tab, ZICO Beverages
summary: The Coca-Cola Company is retiring several underperforming products, including TaB diet soda and ZICO coconut water, by December 31, 2020. This move is part of a global portfolio refresh aimed at prioritizing category-leading brands with the greatest potential for growth and scale, and allowing resources to be reallocated to promising innovations like Topo Chico Hard Seltzer and AHA flavored sparkling water. The decision was accelerated by ongoing COVID-19 supply chain challenges and shifting consumer behaviors, enabling the company to streamline its offerings more quickly.

title: Coca-Cola is discontinuing Tab after nearly 60 years
summary: Coca-Cola is discontinuing Tab, its first-ever diet soda, after nearly 60 years, as part of a broader effort to streamline its product lineup and focus on bestsellers. The decision, though hastened by the pandemic, was already underway to allow the company to invest more in powerhouse brands like Diet Coke and Coke Zero. Tab had maintained a small but devoted following despite its growth being largely cannibalized by Diet Coke's introduction in 1982.

title: Coca-Cola to retire Tab, its first diet soda, as it trims its portfolio
summary: Coca-Cola is retiring Tab, its first diet soda, and several other less popular beverages by the end of the year to streamline its portfolio. This move is accelerated by the coronavirus pandemic, allowing the company to focus on larger brands and products with higher growth potential. Tab, introduced in 1963, saw its popularity decline after the launch of Diet Coke in 1982.

title: Coca-Cola will stop making Tab diet soda, company announces
summary: The Coca-Cola Company announced it will retire Tab diet soda and other "underperforming products" by the end of the year as part of a portfolio rationalization. Tab, Coke's first diet soda launched in 1963, has seen declining sales, accounting for less than 0.03% of Coca-Cola's sales by 2017. The company plans to reallocate resources from these discontinued brands to growing brands like Diet Coke and Coca-Cola Zero Sugar, and to fund promising innovations.

title: Coca-Cola to end production of Tab soda
summary: Coca-Cola announced it will discontinue its iconic Tab soda, originally introduced in 1963 as the company's first diet cola. This move is part of the beverage maker's broader strategy to streamline its brand portfolio, focusing on products with significant growth potential, and follows the closures of other brands like Odwalla and Zico. The company plans to cut more than half of its 500 brands, reinvesting saved R&D and marketing dollars into growing brands like Aha sparkling water and Topo Chico.

title: Coca-Cola discontinues TaB diet soda in the US
summary: Coca-Cola is discontinuing TaB, its first-ever diet soft drink launched in 1963, in the US as part of a larger plan to streamline its SKUs and prioritize brands with greater growth potential. The company is retiring underperforming products, including Odwalla, Zico coconut water, and Coca-Cola Life, to focus resources on stronger brands like Diet Coke and Coke Zero Sugar. This move, accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic, aims to free up investments for burgeoning categories such as hard seltzer.

title: Coca-Cola retiring Tab, Zico brands
summary: The Coca-Cola Co. is discontinuing Tab diet soda and Zico coconut water, among other brands, as part of a portfolio refresh aimed at focusing on products with higher growth potential. This move, which was accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic, seeks to free up resources for more scalable brands and streamline their offerings due to changing consumer behaviors and supply chain challenges. The company plans to invest more in brands like Minute Maid, Simply, and Topo Chico.

title: Keurig is a machine: How the beverage giant is leveraging A.I. to fuel growth
summary: Keurig Dr Pepper (KDP) has shown impressive market share growth in the beverage industry, leveraging a broad product portfolio and strategic use of AI to adapt to changing consumer habits during COVID-19. CEO Bob Gamgort's vision of combining hot and cold beverage segments and utilizing data from connected Keurig brewers allowed KDP to rapidly identify and respond to shifts in demand, such as increased at-home coffee consumption and preferences for large packs of canned soft drinks. This strategy has resulted in strong revenue and profit growth, positioning KDP for future acquisitions and continued expansion.

title: Can shortage affects Milwaukee's brewers unevenly
summary: The pandemic, combined with the summer beer boom, has led to a significant aluminum can shortage in the U.S., affecting beverage sectors nationwide. Milwaukee brewers are experiencing this shortage unevenly, with some facing higher prices and limited supply, while others are less impacted due to their size or proactive measures. The article highlights how larger companies often receive preferential treatment from suppliers during shortages, leaving smaller craft breweries to bear the brunt of the issue, though some hope for future improvements in production.

title: Ecolab Partners With Water.org to Improve Access to Clean, Safe, Sustainable Water
summary: Ecolab has partnered with Water.org to improve access to clean, safe, and sustainable water for 100,000 people in at-risk watersheds in India. This collaboration aims to provide equitable access to water, sanitation, and hygiene solutions while contributing to positive recurring water benefits in high-stress river basins. The partnership aligns with Ecolab's 2030 Impact Goals and its involvement in the Water Resilience Coalition, emphasizing social responsibility and community well-being.

title: Coca-Cola Expects Growth in China Even as Global Sales Slide
summary: Coca-Cola anticipates growth in China this year, despite a continued decline in global sales due to various venue closures worldwide. The company's finance chief noted that Chinese consumers have largely returned to pre-pandemic habits, allowing for a faster recovery compared to other regions. While global third-quarter revenue decreased 9% year-over-year, it marked an improvement from the second quarter's 28% drop.

title: Coke is canceling 200 drink brands
summary: Coca-Cola is eliminating 200 brands, or half of its portfolio, to focus on more profitable offerings and higher-growth drinks. This move includes discontinuing beloved brands like Tab, Zico, and Odwalla, with further cuts expected in the "hydration" category. The company aims to reallocate resources to better-performing products, especially after a challenging period during the pandemic which saw net revenues decline by 9% in the third quarter.

title: Coca-Cola emerges from lockdown blues as out-of-home demand recovers
summary: Coca-Cola reported better-than-expected revenue and profit in the third quarter as the reopening of theaters and restaurants boosted "away-from-home" demand, which had significantly declined during earlier lockdowns. Despite concerns about potential regional lockdowns due to rising COVID-19 cases, the company is streamlining its product portfolio and noted increased consumer purchases of sparkling soft drinks and juices from grocery stores.

title: Coke bids adieu to 200 drink brands, slashing portfolio in half
summary: The Coca-Cola Company is cutting its beverage portfolio in half by discontinuing at least 200 brands by the end of the year to focus on more profitable products and emerge stronger from the pandemic. This move follows the discontinuation of Tab and includes other underperforming brands like Odwalla and ZICO, allowing Coke to streamline its offerings and invest in promising new ventures like Topo Chico Hard Seltzer.

title: 'Our world needs more Black attorneys': New program aims to shake up lack up diversity
summary: Ford Motor Co., through its charitable arm and in collaboration with the Henry Ford Learning Institute, is launching the Ford Law Career Academy to address the lack of diversity in the legal profession. This four-year program will start in high schools, exposing students from working-class backgrounds to various aspects of law and encouraging more Black students to pursue legal careers. The initiative is a response to the static 5% representation of Black attorneys in the U.S. over the past decade, despite the strong interest in social justice among today's youth.

title: The Black Women's Agenda is America's Agenda, As Stacey Abrams Has Reminded Us
summary: Stacey Abrams emphasized that the Black women's agenda is America's agenda, focusing on education and healthcare accessibility. She made these remarks while accepting the "Women on the Rise" Award at the Black Women’s Agenda, Inc. Awards Luncheon, where other influential Black women were also honored. Abrams urged people to elect candidates who reflect these values, highlighting the importance of local and state elections for impactful change.

title: Coca-Cola saying goodbye to half its drink brands
summary: Coca-Cola announced plans to eliminate 200 drink brands, roughly half of its portfolio, to recover from the impact of the coronavirus pandemic. The company aims to prioritize profitable, scalable brands, with reductions expected mainly in the "hydration space." This strategic move will also involve retiring underperforming products like Tab diet soda and ZICO coconut water, while exploring new categories such as alcohol-based seltzers.

title: Coca-Cola to Cut 200 Beverage Brands
summary: The Coca-Cola Co. is cutting more than half of its beverage brands, reducing its portfolio to about 200 products to focus on those with the greatest growth potential. This move includes retiring brands like Tab soda and Zico coconut water, freeing up resources to invest in stronger brands and new product launches. The decision, partly accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic, aims to streamline the company's offerings and enhance profitability despite a recent decline in net revenues.

title: Coca-Cola Europe Bottler in Talks for Record Australian Deal
summary: Coca-Cola European Partners Plc, the world's largest independent bottler, is reportedly in discussions to acquire Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd. The potential acquisition would significantly expand Coca-Cola European Partners' presence in the Asia Pacific region. An announcement regarding the deal could be made in the coming days.

title: Coca-Cola European Partners announces it has made a non-binding proposal to acquire Coca-Cola Amatil Limited
summary: Coca-Cola European Partners (CCEP) has made a non-binding proposal to acquire Coca-Cola Amatil Limited (CCL). This proposal involves acquiring 69.2% of CCL's shares from independent shareholders and conditionally acquiring The Coca-Cola Company's (KO) 30.8% interest. The acquisition aims to broaden CCEP's footprint, double its consumer reach, and drive sustainable growth through geographic diversification.

title: Coca-Cola European Goes Global With $6.6 Billion Deal
summary: Coca-Cola European Partners Plc has agreed to acquire Australian bottler Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd. for A$9.23 billion ($6.6 billion). This acquisition aims to create a global producer of packaged beverages, enabling the company to better navigate the industry's slowdown and the growing consumer preference away from sugary drinks. The deal represents a 19% premium on Coca-Cola Amatil's share price from last week, and its board plans to recommend the offer.

title: Bayer HLB Project Extended
summary: Bayer's multi-year project to find solutions for Huanglongbing (HLB) in citrus has been extended with a two-year, $10 million grant from the USDA’s National Institute of Food and Agriculture (NIFA). The project, which involves CRDF, California Citrus Research Board, PepsiCo, and Coca-Cola, aims to develop high-throughput testing for antimicrobial compounds, create a plant defense inducer (PDI), and identify antimicrobials to kill liberibacter. Researchers are currently conducting field trials in Florida and hope to identify a top PDI candidate soon, with the ultimate goal of product registration.

title: Say goodbye to San Francisco's iconic Coca-Cola sign
summary: San Francisco's iconic Coca-Cola billboard, a fixture in the South of Market area since 1937, is slated for removal by the Coca-Cola company. The removal, estimated to cost $100,000, is reportedly due to soaring rents. The sign was one of the longest actively operated commercial signs in the city.

title: Coca-Cola works with bottlers to convert operations as it cuts 200 product lines
summary: Coca-Cola is cutting approximately 200 product lines, halving its brand portfolio, as part of a new operating plan accelerated by the coronavirus pandemic. The company will consolidate 17 operating units into nine and work with bottlers to convert operations, focusing on bigger, more scalable bets and a "fail fast" approach to innovation. This move aims to streamline its supply chain and enhance efficiency, with decisions on product lines largely finalized.

title: Coca-Cola and AWS reimagine the future of contactless experiences
summary: Coca-Cola Freestyle partnered with Amazon Web Services (AWS) to develop a "pour by phone" contactless experience for its beverage dispensers in response to evolving consumer behaviors during the pandemic. This innovation allows users to operate the machines via their smartphones by scanning a QR code, eliminating the need for physical contact. The solution was rapidly developed and deployed, and over 30,000 machines now have this touchless capability, with a full U.S. rollout planned by the end of 2020.

title: Is PepsiCo Stock a Good Buy at These Prices?
summary: This article analyzes whether PepsiCo stock is a good investment, particularly comparing its performance against Coca-Cola. It highlights Frito-Lay's significant contribution to PepsiCo's operating profits and overall outperformance, addressing valuation, dividend yield, and analyst ratings. The article also discusses potential risks related to changing consumer preferences for healthier options and PepsiCo's efforts to adapt.

title: Louisville's KFC Yum Center awards PepsiCo Inc. pouring rights in 10-year contract
summary: PepsiCo Inc. has secured a 10-year contract for pouring rights at Louisville's KFC Yum Center, replacing The Coca-Cola Co. The agreement also includes exclusive marketing rights and the transformation of the arena’s outdoor plaza into Pepsi Plaza. The partnership will also involve community programs through Pepsi's "Pepsi Stronger Together" initiative, focusing on education and youth in Louisville.

title: Workers strike at Toledo, Ohio, Coca-Cola plant
summary: Workers represented by Teamsters Local 20 at a Coca-Cola Bottling Co. plant in north Toledo have gone on strike starting November 2, 2020, due to unresolved contract negotiations. The union stated that healthcare is the primary sticking point and accused the company of not negotiating in good faith. Coca-Cola Consolidated expressed disappointment, maintaining their offer was fair, and implemented plans to prevent business interruptions.

title: Amatil Enters into Scheme Implementation Deed With CCEP
summary: Coca-Cola Amatil Limited (Amatil) has announced that it has entered into a Scheme Implementation Deed with Coca-Cola European Partners plc (CCEP). This agreement is for the acquisition of all issued shares held by independent shareholders of Amatil, to be conducted via a Scheme of Arrangement. The company released an exchange document detailing the terms of this acquisition.

title: Our agreement to acquire Coca-Cola Amatil
summary: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners (CCEP) announced a binding agreement on February 14, 2021, for a best and final offer to acquire Coca-Cola Amatil Limited (CCL). This acquisition is described as a strategic opportunity to combine two major bottlers, driving faster and more sustainable growth and solidifying CCEP’s position as the largest Coca-Cola bottler by revenue. The transaction aims to unlock enhanced value for shareholders and strengthen CCEP's partnership with The Coca-Cola Company.

title: Coca-Cola buys coffee kiosk startup powered by mobile
summary: Coca-Cola's Costa Coffee unit acquired Briggo, a startup that operates automated coffee kiosks and rebranded it as Costa Coffee BaristaBot. This acquisition signifies Coca-Cola's interest in automated foodservice technologies integrated with mobile devices, expanding its distribution flexibility, especially in high-traffic areas. The move also intensifies Coca-Cola's competition with coffee chains like Starbucks and Dunkin', building on its previous acquisition of Costa Coffee.

title: Every good sign has its time
summary: The removal of San Francisco's iconic, 83-year-old Coca-Cola sign has sparked nostalgia and debate among residents. While some mourn the loss of a historic landmark, others question grieving a corporate sign and point to practical reasons like new construction. The article also explores the environmental impact of LED over traditional neon and suggests replacing such commercial billboards with community-focused art installations reflects a changing city.

title: What Does Wendy's Put on Their Hamburgers?
summary: This article features an interview with John Li, Wendy's VP of Culinary Innovation, who discusses the ingredients and philosophy behind Wendy's hamburgers, particularly the classic Dave's Single. He highlights the use of fresh, never-frozen beef and the brand's commitment to quality from ingredients to innovation in their menu items. Li also shares insights into the market research process for new hamburger creations and his personal favorites.

title: Coca-Cola Company Becomes Sole Owner of fairlife
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has acquired the remaining stake in fairlife LLC from its joint venture partner Select Milk Producers, making Coca-Cola the sole owner. fairlife will continue to operate independently from Chicago, and the terms of the deal were not disclosed. This acquisition allows Coca-Cola to further expand its beverage portfolio and build on fairlife's innovative dairy products and growth in the market.

title: Coke terminates agreement with recycling technology firm Loop Industries
summary: Coca-Cola has terminated its agreement with recycling technology firm Loop Industries. Despite the termination, Coke indicated openness to exploring a new framework agreement with Loop for North America and/or Europe. The article was published by Don Loepp on November 13, 2020.

title: Coca-Cola joins kombucha market with Mojo brand acquisition
summary: Coca-Cola has acquired Organic & Raw Trading Co., the Australia-based maker of the Mojo brand of organic kombucha drinks. This acquisition marks Coca-Cola's first full ownership of a kombucha brand, entering the rapidly growing probiotic beverage market. Mojo's cofounder and CEO, Anthony Crabb, and sales and market director, Andrew Buttery, will retain their positions.

title: Are Energy Drinks the New Tobacco?
summary: This article analyzes the regulatory scrutiny faced by the energy drink industry, drawing parallels to the Joe Camel tobacco advertising case of the late 1990s. Despite concerns from legislators and health authorities regarding the marketing of energy drinks to children and potential health effects, the author suggests that a legal challenge to restrict their advertising would face significant hurdles. The high burden of proof required to demonstrate direct causation between advertising and harm, coupled with the widespread social acceptance of caffeine, makes a unilateral ban unlikely.

title: Coke terminates agreement with recycling technology firm Loop Industries
summary: Coca-Cola Co. has terminated its agreement with Loop Industries Inc., a recycling technology firm, due to Loop's failure to meet a production milestone at a joint venture facility. This termination follows a report from Hindenburg Research questioning Loop's technology and a subsequent SEC subpoena, leading to a significant drop in Loop's stock price. Despite the termination, Coke expressed interest in exploring a new framework agreement with Loop.

title: Pepsi unveils first 2-liter bottle redesign in nearly 30 years
summary: PepsiCo is rolling out the first redesign of its 2-liter plastic bottles in nearly 30 years, featuring a slimmer profile and an enhanced grip point. This new design aims to make the bottles easier to pour and is part of PepsiCo's broader initiative to make its packaging 100% recyclable, compostable, or biodegradable within the next five years. The refreshed bottles will be introduced for various PepsiCo beverages, starting in select US cities with a nationwide launch planned for the near future.

title: San Diego firm Realty Income buys Coca-Cola building in Apopka for big price
summary: San Diego-based Realty Income has purchased the Coca-Cola building in Apopka, Florida, for a significant price. The acquisition is part of Apopka's Mid-Florida Logistics Park, which is currently the largest industrial development under construction in Central Florida, with potential for further expansion. This purchase highlights the growing real estate activity in the region, particularly driven by e-commerce.

title: National businesses that got their start in Wilmington. Recognize any of these names?
summary: This article highlights several successful national businesses that originated in Wilmington, North Carolina, demonstrating the city's impact across various industries. Featured companies include Freaker USA (beverage insulators), Live Oak Bank (small business lending), KWIPPED (online equipment marketplace), PPD (pharmaceutical research), and Fuzzy Peach (frozen yogurt franchise). These businesses showcase Wilmington's entrepreneurial spirit, from a unique product on Shark Tank to a global pharmaceutical giant contributing to COVID-19 research.

title: Pepsi debuts redesigned 2-liter bottles, teases new 'Apple Pie'-flavored variety
summary: PepsiCo is introducing a redesigned, slimmer 2-liter bottle, the first change in nearly 30 years, aiming to make it easier for consumers to grip and pour. This redesign will extend to other PepsiCo beverage brands. Additionally, Pepsi is launching a new, limited-edition "Apple Pie" flavored cola for the holidays, which consumers can win by sharing baking "fails" on social media.

title: Former Hershey exec Mary-Ann Somers joins Alter Eco board
summary: Mary-Ann Somers, a former Hershey executive with over 30 years of experience in consumer products and technology, has been appointed as an independent director to Alter Eco's Board. This makes her the first woman to join the board, a result of a collaboration with the Women On Boards (WOB) Project. Somers is expected to contribute significantly to Alter Eco's strategic growth, particularly leveraging her chocolate industry knowledge and digital expertise to scale the mission-driven brand and its sustainability initiatives.

title: Teamsters Local 20 reaches agreement with Coca-Cola, ends Toledo strike
summary: Teamsters Local 20 workers in Toledo, Ohio, reached an agreement with Coca-Cola Consolidated, ending a two-week strike. The union ratified a new contract on Wednesday morning, November 18th, and workers returned to their jobs on Thursday, November 19th. The revised deal includes higher wages to offset increased health care coverage rates for the workers.

title: Coca Cola Brings Marketing Muscle to the Dairy Case
summary: Coca-Cola is partnering with Select Milk Producers to launch fairlife fluid milk nationally, aiming to revitalize the declining fluid milk category. This initiative is part of Dairy Management, Inc.'s $500 million effort with seven major companies to boost fluid milk sales through innovation and marketing. Fairlife milk offers increased protein and calcium, reduced sugar, and is lactose-free, showing promising results in test markets.

title: Coca-Cola Is Open to Inorganic Growth in Still Beverages
summary: Coca-Cola is looking towards inorganic growth, specifically acquisitions, to expand its presence in the high-growth still beverages market. This strategy is in response to the continued underperformance of carbonated soft drinks compared to categories like bottled water, ready-to-drink coffee, and energy drinks. The company has already made strategic moves, including the acquisition of Innocent Drinks and a stake in Suja Juice and Monster Beverage.

title: Coca-Cola Ruling Sends Warning on Facebook, Medtronic Tax Fights
summary: A U.S. Tax Court ruling against Coca-Cola Co. in a $3.4 billion transfer pricing dispute with the IRS could have significant implications for other multinational companies, including Facebook Inc. and Medtronic Inc. The court upheld the IRS’s method for reallocating profits between Coca-Cola and its foreign affiliates for 2007-2009. This decision sends a warning to companies engaged in similar tax fights with the IRS regarding profit shifting to foreign entities.

title: Coca-Cola commits $500 million in additional spending with Black-owned suppliers
summary: The Coca-Cola Company announced a commitment to increase spending with Black-owned suppliers by an additional $500 million over the next five years. This initiative aims to support Black entrepreneurs who have been significantly impacted by the coronavirus pandemic and systemic racial injustice. The company also expanded its Supplier Development training program and partnered with organizations like the National Minority Supplier Development Council to foster growth and economic empowerment for minority-owned businesses.

title: The rise and fall of Tab | after surviving the sweetener scares, the iconic diet soda gets canned
summary: Tab, Coca-Cola's original diet soda, is being discontinued after 57 years. Despite surviving low sales, sweetener scares, and corporate ambivalence, its market share dwindled significantly after the introduction of Diet Coke. The company's decision is part of an effort to cut underperforming brands, ending the run for this beloved soda and prompting loyal "Tab-aholics" to stock up.

title: Apple Pie Pepsi is here so you don't have to bake one
summary: Pepsi has released a limited-edition Apple Pie flavored cola for the holiday season, designed to offer comfort and the taste of the classic dessert without the hassle of baking. This special cola, described as having notes of cinnamon, buttery crust, and crisp apple, is not sold in stores. Instead, it can only be won by participants of a social media contest on Twitter or TikTok, where they share photos or videos of their baking fails using #PepsiApplePieChallenge.

title: Toledo Teamsters Ratify New Contract with Coca Cola
summary: Members of Teamsters Local 20 in Toledo, Ohio, have ratified a new contract with Coca Cola Consolidated, ending a weeks-long strike that began on November 2nd. The new agreement includes improved wages to offset higher health care co-pays and a new classification for transport workers. The union emphasized its pride in supporting essential workers who continued working through the pandemic.

title: Coca-Cola CFO Helps Company Make Cuts, Operational Changes
summary: Coca-Cola's CFO, John Murphy, is leading a restructuring effort to cut costs and respond to the impact of the coronavirus pandemic. This includes reducing the number of brands, laying off or buying out thousands of employees, and revising the company's marketing strategy. The beverage giant has experienced significant revenue declines, with a 9% drop in the third quarter and a 28% decline in the second quarter compared to the prior year.

title: Coca-Cola CFO prefers ‘scenario management’ to ‘scenario planning’
summary: John Murphy, CFO of The Coca-Cola Company, emphasizes "scenario management" over "scenario planning," advocating for adaptable strategies with multiple contingency plans rather than fixed projections. He highlights the evolving role of the CFO as a strategic business partner and the importance of understanding consumer trends, building a broad beverage portfolio, and maintaining a competitive edge through global reach and local ownership. Murphy also notes the pandemic as a catalyst for rapid change and stresses the company's commitment to social responsibility through the Coca-Cola Scholars Program.

title: The Coca-Cola Company, PepsiCo and Nestlé named top plastic polluters for the third year in a row
summary: For the third consecutive year, The Coca-Cola Company, PepsiCo, and Nestlé have been identified as the world's leading plastic polluters, according to the "BRANDED Vol III" report by Break Free From Plastic. This report, based on an audit of 346,494 pieces of plastic waste from 55 countries, criticizes these corporations for failing to address the plastic crisis and for continuing to promote single-use plastic, which negatively impacts both the environment and the livelihoods of informal waste pickers, particularly in the Global South. Activists and organizations are urging these companies to shift away from single-use plastics and invest in robust reuse systems.

title: Coca-Cola funded public health conferences in effort to shift blame for obesity: New study
summary: A new study reveals that The Coca-Cola Company sponsored international public health conferences to divert blame for the obesity epidemic from its products, focusing instead on physical activity and individual choice. Documents obtained by U.S. Right to Know show Coca-Cola collaborated with sponsored researchers to promote its messaging at these conferences, fostering relationships with public health leaders. The study argues for stronger protection of scientific knowledge dissemination from corporate influence, suggesting a model similar to the tobacco industry sponsorship ban.

title: The Coca-Cola Company, PepsiCo, and Nestlé Named Top Plastic Polluters for Third Year
summary: For the third consecutive year, The Coca-Cola Company, PepsiCo, and Nestlé have been identified as the world's top plastic polluters, according to a report by Break Free From Plastic. The report, "BRANDED Vol III: Demanding Corporate Accountability for Plastic Pollution," highlights the continued reliance of these corporations on single-use plastics and the detrimental impact on communities, particularly in the Global South, despite their claims to address the plastic crisis. Activists are calling for these companies to end their addiction to single-use plastics and prioritize robust reuse systems.

title: coca-cola, PepsiCo and nestlé named top plastic polluters for third consecutive year
summary: Coca-Cola, PepsiCo, and Nestlé have been identified as the world's leading plastic polluters for the third year in a row, according to a report by Break Free From Plastic. The organization's annual brand audit collected plastic waste from 55 countries, highlighting the significant contribution of these corporations to global plastic pollution. Despite claims of working towards solutions, these companies continue to produce harmful single-use plastic packaging, prompting calls for them to adopt robust reuse systems and reduce plastic production.

title: Coca-Cola uses pandemic as ‘catalyst for change,’ excuse to ‘spring clean’ innovation pipeline
summary: Coca-Cola is leveraging the pandemic as an opportunity to streamline its operations and innovation pipeline, according to CFO John Murphy. The company is refocusing on local opportunities, reducing bureaucracy, and culling non-performing brands to achieve long-term sales and profit growth. Despite a significant drop in revenue during 2020 due to venue closures, Coca-Cola is optimistic about reaching its pre-pandemic growth targets by implementing these strategic changes.

title: Siddhartha s wife Malavika Hegde appointed as Coffee Day CEO a year after founder s suicide
summary: Malavika Hegde, wife of the late Cafe Coffee Day founder VG Siddhartha, has been appointed as the CEO of the coffee chain, over a year after Siddhartha's death by suicide. Siddhartha's death followed reports of immense financial strain and allegations of harassment from Income Tax officials. Coffee Day Enterprises had previously named SV Ranganath as interim chairman, and now Malavika Hegde, daughter of former Karnataka chief minister SM Krishna, will lead the company.

title: Coca-Cola sells its Centre County production facility for $5.6 million
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has sold its Centre County water bottling plant to Milesburg Properties, LLC, which is affiliated with Niagara Bottling, for $5.593 million. The sale's impact on the estimated 100 employees at the facility is unclear, as neither company responded to requests for comment. Local commissioners hope Niagara Bottling will continue to be a good community resource and employer.

title: Coca-Cola Sells Centre County Bottling Facility for $5.59 Million
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has sold its water bottling facility in Centre County, PA, to Milesburg Properties LLC for $5.59 million. Milesburg Properties LLC is associated with Niagara Bottling, a family-owned bottled water and soft drink manufacturer. The facility was originally owned by AquaPenn, then Danone, before Coca-Cola acquired majority interest.

title: Coca-Cola throws every media and creative account up for grabs in global agency review
summary: Coca-Cola has initiated a global agency review for all of its media and creative accounts, putting its entire advertising business up for grabs. This move will determine which agencies will handle the beverage giant's marketing efforts worldwide. The review was announced by E.J. Schultz and Bloomberg, indicating a significant shake-up in Coca-Cola's advertising strategy.

title: Coca-Cola sells bottling plant to Niagara Bottling
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has sold its water bottling facility in Centre County, Pennsylvania, to Niagara Bottling. The facility was sold to Milesburg Properties LLC, which shares a corporate office address with Niagara Bottling. A local commissioner expressed hope that Niagara Bottling will continue to be a positive community resource and employer.

title: Public relations agency Ogilvy Africa bags 11 wins at SABRE awards
summary: Ogilvy Africa and its clients secured 11 wins at the 2019 African SABRE Awards for their public relations campaigns. The awards recognized campaigns for clients like Safaricom, Coca-Cola, and Kenya Airways across various categories, highlighting the firm's integrated communications approach and ability to achieve earned media for clients. The awards will be presented in Kigali, Rwanda in May.

title: Companies Can Address the Impact of Single-Use Plastics in the Era of COVID-19
summary: Despite a temporary surge in single-use plastic consumption due to the COVID-19 pandemic, companies like Kimberly-Clark are continuing to push forward with long-term commitments to reduce plastic waste. The article highlights the significant environmental and economic costs of marine plastic pollution and details the strategies companies are employing, including product innovation, partnerships, and maintaining a long-term sustainability vision. It emphasizes the urgent need for collaboration between industry leaders, NGOs, and consumers to address the global plastic crisis.

title: Coca-Cola kicks off massive agency review to 'fundamentally transform' its marketing
summary: Coca-Cola has launched a comprehensive global review of its media and creative planning and buying practices, along with its agency appointments. This initiative aims to enhance effectiveness and efficiency across various marketing investments, including media, creative, and production, as part of the company's digital transformation. While expected to generate cost savings, the primary goal is a fundamental redesign of its marketing model and consolidation of third-party agencies.

title: Coca-Cola tops list of 10 corporate plastic polluters of 2020
summary: For the third consecutive year, Coca-Cola has been identified as the leading global plastic polluter among major brands, according to the "Branded Volume III" report by the Break Free From Plastic movement. The report lists Coca-Cola, PepsiCo, Nestlé, and seven other corporations as the biggest contributors to plastic waste, urging them to reduce single-use plastics and reinvent their delivery systems. Despite some companies joining initiatives like the New Plastics Economy Global Commitment, their reduction in virgin plastic use has been minimal.

title: Coca-Cola European Partners invests in countertop dispensing machines company Lavit
summary: Coca-Cola European Partners (CCEP) has invested in Lavit, a US-based company that produces compact countertop beverage systems. This investment, made through CCEP Ventures, aims to reduce packaging waste and carbon footprints by exploring new dispensed delivery solutions. Lavit's technology allows consumers to create customizable drinks on demand using aluminum EcoCaps, and the investment will support its growth and product development.

title: Coca-Cola Failed to Charge Arm’s-Length Royalties to Affiliates
summary: The U.S. Tax Court ruled that Coca-Cola owes over $3.3 billion in taxes for failing to charge "arm's-length" royalties to its affiliated bottlers, which increased the company's taxable income by more than $9 billion. The Internal Revenue Service (IRS) successfully argued that Coca-Cola's "10-50-50" method for calculating royalties over-compensated the supply points and under-compensated Coca-Cola for the use of its intangible property. The court largely upheld the IRS's adjustments, confirming that the supply points were operating as routine manufacturers and did not own significant marketing intangibles.

title: Coca-Cola Bottling Company United dispenses streamlined order management with RPA in Microsoft Power Automate
summary: Coca-Cola Bottling Company United implemented robotic process automation (RPA) using Microsoft Power Automate to streamline order and invoicing processes for its Freestyle vending machines. This solution, developed with Happiest Minds, automates an 11-step manual process, freeing up CRM agents and allowing the company to scale its Freestyle initiative more effectively. The RPA solution, dubbed "Asa," handles order entry, PO creation, supplier interaction, invoice processing, and data storage, significantly reducing labor costs and potential errors.

title: Coronavirus: Coca-Cola restructuring cuts 2,200 jobs worldwide
summary: Coca-Cola is cutting approximately 2,200 jobs globally, with 1,200 in the US, as part of a restructuring plan accelerated by the coronavirus pandemic. The company expects these job cuts to generate annual savings between $350 million and $550 million. Additionally, Coca-Cola plans to slim down its product portfolio by more than half, focusing on 200 key brands and discontinuing others like Tab soda and Zico coconut water.

title: Coca-Cola to cut 2,200 jobs globally, including 1,200 in U.S.
summary: Coca-Cola Co announced it will cut 2,200 jobs globally, including 1,200 in the United States, as the COVID-19 pandemic accelerates its business restructuring efforts. The company had previously offered voluntary separation packages and stated that the pandemic acted as a catalyst to speed up planned changes. Approximately 500 job cuts will impact its metro Atlanta headquarters.

title: Coca-Cola will cut 2,200 jobs worldwide as part of restructuring plan
summary: Coca-Cola announced cuts of approximately 2,200 jobs globally as part of a restructuring plan accelerated by the coronavirus pandemic. The beverage giant expects to incur $350 million to $550 million in severance costs from these job reductions. This move follows a strategic shift to slim down its portfolio and build new regional operating units, after seeing a 9% slide in net sales in the third quarter due to declining away-from-home consumption.

title: Coca-Cola is cutting 2,200 jobs
summary: Coca-Cola is cutting 2,200 jobs globally, including 1,200 in the United States, due to declining sales during the pandemic. The company expects severance packages to cost between $350 million and $550 million. Coca-Cola is also streamlining its operating units and canceling 200 brands as it focuses on its most popular beverages.

title: Coca-Cola to Cut 2,200 Jobs Worldwide Amid Covid Challenges
summary: Coca-Cola Co. is implementing widespread job cuts, affecting 2,200 employees globally and 1,200 in the U.S., as part of deeper restructuring efforts. These reductions, representing 2.5% of the total workforce, are a response to the ongoing challenges posed by venue shutdowns impacting soft-drink sales amid the Covid-19 pandemic. The company aims to navigate a tough business environment through a combination of voluntary buyouts and layoffs.

title: Coca Cola to cut 2,200 jobs worldwide in restructuring
summary: Coca-Cola announced plans to cut 2,200 jobs globally as part of a restructuring effort accelerated by the coronavirus pandemic. The job cuts, affecting about 1,200 roles in the U.S. (with 500 in metro Atlanta), will come through voluntary buyouts and involuntary layoffs, costing the company between $350 million and $550 million. This move is coupled with reducing its drink brands by half to 200, investing savings in growing brands, and streamlining its business segments from 17 to nine.

title: Why Kraft Heinz leaders say their new strategy will drive growth beyond the pandemic
summary: Kraft Heinz leaders are confident their new business strategy, rolled out in September 2020, will drive growth beyond the pandemic, despite initial delays and shifts in consumer behavior. The strategy focuses on reinvesting in brands, using a platform-based approach, and prioritizing consumer needs, which executives believe will lead to sustained success. This approach has already seen positive results in sales growth and consumer rediscovery of trusted brands during the pandemic.

title: The Story of Taylor California Cellars, Coca-Cola’s Forgotten Foray Into the Wine Industry
summary: This article details Coca-Cola's ambitious but ultimately short-lived venture into the wine industry with Taylor California Cellars in the late 1970s and early 1980s. It covers how Coca-Cola acquired the established Taylor Wine Company, leveraged aggressive marketing tactics and innovative packaging to rapidly grow Taylor California Cellars, and the reasons behind its eventual divestment due to low profit margins and fierce competition from E. & J. Gallo. The article also explains how subsequent ownership changes and poor management led to the decline and near disappearance of the Taylor brand in American winemaking.

title: Coca-Cola to cut 2,200 jobs globally
summary: Coca-Cola announced it will cut approximately 2,200 jobs globally, including 1,200 in the U.S. and 500 in Atlanta, as part of a company reorganization plan. While the pandemic was a catalyst for accelerating the changes, it was not the sole cause. The company expects severance programs to incur expenses between $350 million and $550 million.

title: Chocolate Pepsi? Brand Announces ‘Cocoa' Cola Flavor
summary: Pepsi has announced a new "Cocoa" Cola flavor that blends the taste of cola with cocoa and a hint of marshmallow, available as a limited edition. To unlock the flavor's release, Pepsi requires its announcement tweet to reach 2,021 retweets. This innovative flavor aims to bring unexpected joy during an atypical year.

title: Coca-Cola to Lay Off 2,200 Workers as it Pares Brands
summary: Coca-Cola announced layoffs for 2,200 workers, or 17% of its global workforce, as part of a restructuring effort to streamline its business units and brands. The pandemic accelerated these changes, with the company aiming to reduce its brand portfolio by half to 200, shedding slow-selling products and investing in growing brands and new launches. This move is expected to save the company money, with severance programs costing between $350 million and $550 million.

title: Coca-Cola to cut 2,200 jobs globally
summary: Coca-Cola announced a global reduction of approximately 2,200 jobs as part of a reorganization effort, with 1,200 cuts in the U.S. and 500 in Atlanta. The company cited the pandemic as a "catalyst" for accelerating these organizational changes, which include an estimated $350 million to $550 million in severance expenses. This reorganization also involves cutting several brands like Odwalla juices and Zico coconut water.

title: Coca-Cola cutting 2,200 jobs as coronavirus pandemic hurts sales
summary: Coca-Cola is laying off 2,200 workers globally, accounting for 17% of its workforce, as part of a restructuring accelerated by the coronavirus pandemic. The layoffs, costing $350 million to $550 million in severance, aim to streamline operations by reducing business units and brands, including ditching slow-selling products like Tab and Zico. The company plans to reinvest savings into growing brands and new product launches like Topo Chico Hard Seltzer.

title: Coca-Cola to cut 2,200 jobs — most in the US — as part of restructuring
summary: Coca-Cola is cutting 2,200 jobs globally, with 1,200 in the U.S., through buyouts and layoffs as part of a restructuring plan accelerated by the pandemic. The company expects severance costs to range from $350 million to $550 million. This move is part of a larger strategy initiated by CEO James Quincey to streamline operations, focus on faster-growing brands, and adapt to evolving consumer tastes, including reducing its business units and discontinuing about 200 brands.

title: What advertising can do, markets can see, hear and consume
summary: Colgate-Palmolive dominates the Kenyan toothpaste market with a 59 percent share, largely due to increased advertising spend and effective marketing strategies that have driven brand awareness and consumer advocacy. The company's success is also attributed to its global strategy of adapting to local tastes, strong in-store execution in emerging markets, and early adoption of online shopping trends. These efforts have earned Colgate a high global penetration rate and a strong position among the world's top brands.

title: Private-label Food and Beverage Market in US 2020-2024 - Featuring Albertsons Companies Inc., Amazon.Com Inc., Costco Wholesale Corp., Among Others to Contribute to the Market Growth
summary: The private-label food and beverage market in the US is projected to grow by USD 30.68 billion between 2020 and 2024, with a CAGR of almost 4%. This growth is primarily driven by product line extensions from private-label vendors and the premiumization of these products. Key companies contributing to this market include Albertsons Companies Inc., Amazon.com Inc., Costco Wholesale Corp., and Walmart Inc.

title: Coca-Cola UNITED manages rapid growth with Microsoft Power Platform
summary: Coca-Cola UNITED successfully leveraged Microsoft Power Platform to manage rapid growth, expanding operations and sales significantly. The low-code platform enabled quick development of applications for order processing and event management, streamlining operations and improving customer satisfaction. This adoption allowed Coca-Cola UNITED to move away from time-consuming custom coding and innovate faster.

title: These Are The World's Top 7 Most Impressive Competitive Eaters
summary: This article lists the top seven most impressive competitive eaters in the world, based on records broken, impact on the sport, and overall impressiveness. It highlights well-known figures such as Joey Chestnut, Miki Sudo, and Takeru Kobayashi, detailing their significant achievements and contributions to competitive eating. The piece acknowledges the debate over the "best" eater but ultimately crowns Joey Chestnut as the greatest of all time due to his numerous records.

title: Agribusiness giants ADM, Bunge trading in ‘conflict’ palm oil, report says
summary: A report by Global Witness alleges that agribusiness giants ADM and Bunge are sourcing palm oil from Indonesian mills linked to land and human rights violations and environmental destruction. The report claims that these companies are not adequately addressing these allegations through their grievance processes, thereby passing "conflict" palm oil to major consumer brands. Both ADM and Bunge have denied failing to police suppliers but have pledged to investigate the claims.

title: McCormick buys natural flavorings company FONA International for $710M
summary: McCormick & Co. has acquired natural flavorings provider FONA International for $710 million, significantly expanding its reach into growing categories like performance nutrition and health and wellness. This acquisition follows McCormick's purchase of Cholula hot sauce for $800 million in November, showcasing its strategy to broaden its portfolio of flavors, spices, seasonings, and condiments. FONA, with annual sales of about $114 million, is expected to see mid-to-high-single-digit growth and will play a role in McCormick's focus on health and wellness ingredients.

title: Coca-Cola Revisits Subscription Model; Latest CPG Company To Embrace The Digital D2C Future
summary: Coca-Cola has relaunched its subscription box program, "Coca-Cola Insiders Club," after pausing it due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The move positions Coke among other major brands adopting direct-to-consumer (D2C) models, driven by the digital shift and the appeal of selling directly to loyal customers. The article highlights that while D2C subscriptions offer significant potential, successful implementation requires a deep focus on customer value and continuous iteration.

title: The story behind Starbucks’ newest latte
summary: Starbucks introduced its new Pistachio Latte in 2021, a spin-off of the Starbucks Reserve Pistachio Latte first developed in 2019. The beverage, which features pistachio flavor with Starbucks espresso and steamed milk, was brought to market despite pandemic-related challenges during its development. Starbucks also launched other new items, including a Honey Almondmilk Cold Brew and Kale and Portabella Mushroom Sous Vide Egg Bites, and brought back seasonal favorites.

title: Why Coca Cola is reviving its subscription service
summary: Coca-Cola is relaunching its direct-to-consumer subscription program, Coke Insider, after abandoning it in early 2020 due to the pandemic. The program, which offers exclusive products and virtual perks for $45 per order, aims to boost customer engagement and gather data, especially after the company experienced significant revenue drops. This move aligns with a growing trend among large CPG companies like Mondelez and Heinz to explore DTC channels, despite their limitations in terms of sales volume.

title: Here are the 800-plus Atlanta jobs Coca-Cola is eliminating
summary: The Coca-Cola Company is in the process of a major reorganization that will lead to the elimination of over 800 jobs in Atlanta. These layoffs are scheduled to take effect in February and March as part of the company's global restructuring efforts. This article follows previous reports detailing initial job cuts and aspects of the severance packages offered.

title: Allergy-friendly cookie company Partake Foods gets $4.8M to fuel expansion
summary: Partake Foods, an allergy-friendly cookie company founded by Denise Woodard, secured $4.8 million in Series A funding. The investment round included participation from CircleUp Growth Partners, Jay-Z's Marcy Venture Partners, Lotus Bakeries’ fund FF2032, and celebrities like Rihanna and Bobby Wagner. The company plans to expand from 2,700 to 5,500 stores by the end of Q1 2021, capitalizing on the growing market for allergy-friendly and plant-based food options.

title: The Coca-Cola Co. acquiring BodyArmor for $5.6 billion
summary: The Coca-Cola Co. is acquiring full ownership of the sports nutrition company BodyArmor for $5.6 billion, adding to its previous 30% stake. BodyArmor will operate as a separate business unit within Coca-Cola North America, with its co-founder and president remaining involved. This acquisition aims to further Coca-Cola's innovation in hydration and health-and-wellness products.

title: Get High Dividend Exposure with the HDEF ETF
summary: The article discusses the Xtrackers MSCI EAFE High Dividend Yield Equity ETF (HDEF) as an option for investors seeking high dividend exposure with international diversification. HDEF offers exposure to developed markets outside the U.S., focusing on high-dividend stocks while hedging against currency risk. This strategy aims to provide stable dividend payments, exemplified by its top holding, Unilever PLC.

title: Coca-Cola, Tyson Foods and ADM among companies to suspend political donations
summary: Following the violent protests at the U.S. Capitol, major companies like Coca-Cola, Tyson Foods, and Archer Daniels Midland have announced the temporary suspension of political donations. This decision aligns with a broader corporate trend across various industries, prompted by the events and a growing consumer expectation for companies to reflect certain values. Companies are re-evaluating their political action committee activities and future contribution decisions in light of recent events.

title: Molson Coors enters American CBD beverage market with Veryvell
summary: Molson Coors, through its joint venture Truss CBD USA with HEXO Corp, has launched a new line of non-alcoholic, sparkling CBD beverages called Veryvell in Colorado. These hemp-derived, adaptogenic CBD waters are available in three flavors—Focus, Mind & Body, and Unwind—each containing 20mg of CBD. This move signifies Molson Coors' strategic expansion beyond traditional beer products into the wellness beverage market.

title: Founder of ZICO Coconut Water Re-Acquires Brand from The Coca-Cola Company
summary: PowerPlant Ventures, co-founded by ZICO founder Mark Rampolla, has re-acquired ZICO coconut water from The Coca-Cola Company. Rampolla originally founded ZICO in 2004 and sold it to Coca-Cola in 2013. The brand will now operate under a new entity called ZICO Rising, with Thomas Hicks and Alan George leading it as CEO and CFO.

title: Exclusive Interview: Alfredo Rivera, the First Hispanic Named President of Coca-Cola North America
summary: Alfredo Rivera, the first Hispanic president of Coca-Cola North America, shares his journey from Honduras to leading a major corporation. He discusses his early life, education, and career challenges, emphasizing lessons learned about leadership and being a "change-agent." Rivera also touches on balancing work and family, his hobbies, and his optimistic outlook for 2021 amidst the pandemic.

title: Unilever says global consumption will remain depressed in first half of year
summary: Unilever expects global consumption to remain suppressed in the first half of the year, with a recovery anticipated in the second half and into next year. CEO Alan Jope noted that while East Asia's business has returned to normal and Africa and Latin America show resilience, the company is still cautious about future predictions due to the pandemic's fluidity. Despite challenges, Unilever expects to grow ahead of the market and does not foresee significant margin setbacks.

title: Valero, USAA among San Antonio companies that donated to Republicans who voted to overturn presidential election results
summary: Two major San Antonio employers, Valero and USAA, are re-evaluating their political spending after the Jan. 6 Capitol assault, having donated significant sums to Republicans who voted to overturn the 2020 presidential election results. Valero has halted all political contributions, while USAA is re-evaluating its criteria. Other local companies like NuStar Energy and iHeartMedia also made substantial donations to these Republicans.

title: Coca-Cola HBC widens portfolio: ‘A beverage for every occasion around the clock’
summary: Coca-Cola Hellenic Bottling Company (CCHBC) is expanding its beverage portfolio to offer "a beverage for every occasion around the clock," moving beyond traditional soft drinks into categories like coffee, hard seltzers, and spirits. This diversification strategy includes recent launches like Topo Chico Hard Seltzer in Europe and leveraging Coca-Cola's acquisition of Costa coffee to enter new occasions. CCHBC aims to meet evolving consumer needs, from morning coffee to evening cocktails, across its 28 markets.

title: Monster Unveils 2021 Product Slate But No Hard Seltzer Yet
summary: Monster Beverage Corporation did not announce a hard seltzer product during its 2021 Virtual Investors Meeting, despite rising speculation and previous reports of trademark filings. Instead, the company announced new products including slim cans of existing SKUs, line extensions, and redesigns, along with a co-CEO appointment. Monster also reported strong sales growth for the first nine months of 2020 but acknowledged being outpaced by some competitors in dollar sales growth.

title: Coke will sit out Super Bowl as Big Game cola marketing goes flat
summary: Coca-Cola announced it will not advertise during the upcoming Super Bowl, marking a significant shift in its marketing strategy. This decision comes as Big Game cola marketing is reportedly losing its impact. The article highlights this as a notable industry development.

title: LeBron James parts ways with Coca-Cola, poised to back PepsiCo brands
summary: LeBron James has ended his long-standing endorsement deal with Coca-Cola. He is now expected to partner with PepsiCo, signaling a significant shift in his brand endorsements within the beverage industry.

title: PepsiCo Inc. stock underperforms Wednesday when compared to competitors
summary: PepsiCo Inc. stock (PEP) declined by 0.51% on Wednesday, closing at $141.33, despite a strong performance by the broader stock market, with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average both rising. The company's stock underperformed compared to competitors like Nestle S.A. ADR (NSRGY), Coca-Cola Co. (KO), and Unilever PLC ADR (UL), all of which saw gains on the same day. Trading volume for PepsiCo exceeded its 50-day average.

title: Coca-Cola releases breakthrough innovation: Coca-Cola with Coffee | 2021-01-25
summary: Coca-Cola has launched Coca-Cola with Coffee in the U.S., entering a new "refreshment coffee" category. This innovative beverage, designed to "sip like a Coke and finish like a coffee," comes in Dark Blend, Vanilla, and Caramel flavors, with zero-sugar options available. The launch marks the 50th market for this product, initially piloted in Japan in 2018, and is supported by a comprehensive marketing campaign.

title: Coca-Cola with Coffee launches nationwide with 2 options
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has launched Coca-Cola with Coffee nationwide in two versions: regular and zero sugar. Both varieties are infused with Brazilian coffee and come in 12-ounce cans, containing 69 milligrams of caffeine per can. The regular version offers dark blend, vanilla, and caramel flavors, while the zero sugar option comes in dark blend and vanilla.

title: Beyond Meat shares soar 26% as company teams up with PepsiCo to make plant-based snacks and drinks
summary: Beyond Meat and PepsiCo have formed a joint venture, "The PLANeT Partnership," to develop and market plant-based snacks and drinks. This collaboration sent Beyond Meat's shares up by as much as 31% in morning trading, reflecting the market's positive reaction to the partnership. While analysts see it as an incremental positive, questions remain about the ultimate market size for these new plant-based products from a company with Pepsi's reach.

title: Coca-Cola with Coffee is a New Product - So is Drone Delivery. DroneUp, Walmart, and Coke Team Up for Launch
summary: Coca-Cola, in collaboration with DroneUp and Walmart, is launching its new "Coca-Cola with Coffee" product, and simultaneously introducing drone delivery for product samples to residents in Coffee County, GA. This initiative leverages DroneUp's FAA waiver for flight over people and vehicles, aiming to bring drone delivery into mainstream consumer awareness. The new beverage, first introduced in Japan, is now available nationwide in the U.S. with several flavors and a zero-sugar option, containing 69 mg of caffeine per 12-oz can.

title: Top Takeaways From Packaged Beverage Retailer Survey
summary: A Goldman Sachs survey of nearly 35,000 convenience store locations revealed that beverage sales accelerated 7% year-over-year in Q4 2020. Retailers anticipate continued momentum in energy drinks and hard seltzers for 2021, with Monster Energy and Truly Hard Seltzer expected to perform strongly. Coca-Cola's decision to streamline its beverage portfolio was largely applauded by retailers, while Keurig Dr Pepper's focus on low-sugar options and PepsiCo's new flavors also generated excitement.

title: Coca-Cola launches new coffee-infused Cokes in Coffee County
summary: Coca-Cola has launched its new coffee-infused Coca-Cola with Coffee beverage nationwide in the U.S., following an initial offering to its Insiders Club. Available in three flavors and a zero-sugar variety, the drink aims to provide a mid-afternoon pick-me-up that combines the taste of Coke with the finish of coffee. This launch marks Coca-Cola's renewed attempt in the coffee-flavored soda market after an earlier product, Coca-Cola Blak, was discontinued.

title: Keurig Dr Pepper permanently closes Green Mountain Coffee Roasters Café, lays off employees
summary: Keurig Dr Pepper has permanently closed its Green Mountain Coffee Roasters Café in Waterbury, Vermont, which had been shut since March, leading to employee layoffs. The company stated that affected employees had been paid since March and would receive ongoing support, including severance packages. The number of layoffs is expected to be fewer than 50, representing less than 1% of the company's 26,000-person workforce, and the company is looking to fill 30 positions at other facilities.

title: Coca-Cola UNITED consolidates Valdosta and Sylvester operations
summary: Coca-Cola Bottling Company United is consolidating its Valdosta and Sylvester operations into a new, state-of-the-art facility in Tifton, Georgia. This move aims to improve efficiency, reduce delivery times, and expand distribution capacity, serving a wider range of locations including Tallahassee and Panama City. The company has assured all 145 affected employees from Valdosta and Sylvester that they will retain their jobs at the new facility, and the expansion is also expected to create new employment opportunities in the area.

title: Coca-Cola, Walmart team up to deliver coffee-flavored soda via drone
summary: Coca-Cola, Walmart, and DroneUp collaborated on a stunt campaign to deliver Coca-Cola with Coffee via drone in Coffee County, Georgia. This initiative promoted the new coffee-flavored soda and highlighted renewed interest in drone delivery for its potential to reduce costs, despite past regulatory hurdles. The move follows Walmart's earlier drone delivery tests and coincides with recent FAA approvals making commercial drone flights without on-site pilots more feasible, suggesting a wider adoption of this technology beyond promotional stunts.

title: Super Bowl Still Means Big Q1 Beer Volumes, But Full Year Impact Lessens
summary: The Super Bowl continues to drive significant beer sales volumes in Q1, topping $1.2 billion in traditional beer sales in 2020, along with substantial hard seltzer and FMB sales. However, its overall impact on annual beer sales volume has been declining since 2016, with Super Bowl week falling to 39th in sales volume ranking in 2020. Despite this, major beer companies like Anheuser-Busch InBev, Molson Coors, Constellation Brands, Heineken USA, and Diageo are investing heavily in regional advertising and marketing campaigns during the game to capture consumer attention.

title: Keurig Commercial introduces touchless brewing
summary: Keurig Commercial, the away-from-home coffee division of Keurig Dr Pepper, has launched touchless brewing capabilities for its office coffee makers. This feature allows consumers to operate the machines via the Keurig Remote Brew app by scanning a QR code and making beverage selections on their phone. This innovation aims to provide a safe and hygienic coffee solution for employees returning to offices.

title: Beer Run: As Budweiser Leaves Super Bowl, Rival Brews Battle For Attention
summary: As Budweiser opts out of a national Super Bowl ad for the first time in 37 years, rival brewers like Diageo, Boston Beer, and MolsonCoors are seizing the opportunity to market their brands. They are utilizing local ad inventory, digital campaigns, and social media to circumvent Anheuser-Busch InBev's long-standing national ad exclusivity during the game. This shift reflects a broader trend of advertisers seeking more cost-effective and targeted ways to reach consumers beyond expensive national Super Bowl spots.

title: Refreshing: Coca-Cola introduces 100% recycled bottles in the US
summary: Coca-Cola is launching 100% recycled plastic bottles in the US, a significant shift in its sustainability strategy aimed at reducing new plastic use by over 20% compared to 2018. The company, previously a proponent of plant-based bottles, is now focusing on recycled PET (rPET) to combat plastic waste. This move is expected to cut the carbon footprint of bottles by more than half and could signal a major change for the beverage industry's approach to circular economy practices.

title: The Coca-Cola Company Introduces Bottles Made from 100% Recycled Materials* in the United States
summary: The Coca-Cola Company announced the introduction of new 13.2oz bottles made from 100% recycled plastic material (rPET) in the United States, starting with its Coca-Cola brand, and expanding to DASANI and smartwater. This move is a significant step towards addressing plastic waste, aiming to reduce new plastic use by over 20% in North America compared to 2018 and supporting the company's World Without Waste goals. The company will also implement extensive on-package messaging to encourage consumers to recycle these new bottles.

title: Coca-Cola Shares Recycled Bottle Redesign
summary: The Coca-Cola Company is transitioning to 100% recycled PET plastic bottles across several brands, including Coke, Coke Zero Sugar, Diet Coke, and Fanta, starting February 2021. This move is part of the company's "World Without Waste" initiative, aiming for 100% recyclable packaging by 2025 and 50% recycled content by 2030. The shift is expected to reduce new plastic use by over 20% across its North America portfolio and cut GHG emissions by 10,000 metric tons annually.

title: UPDATE: Coca-Cola in 2020 posted sharpest volume drop since 1940s
summary: Coca-Cola experienced its sharpest annual decline in beverage volume since just after World War II in 2020, primarily due to the global pandemic's impact on sales in restaurants and public venues. The company's net revenue fell 11% to $33 billion, and net income dropped 9% to $7.7 billion, though its financial performance has shown some improvement since the early days of the coronavirus crisis. Additionally, Coca-Cola is facing a potential $12 billion tax bill from the IRS related to its method of allocating profits between its U.S. and international operations.

title: ‘Aunt Jemima’ becomes ‘Pearl Milling Company,’ Salesforce announces permanent remote workforce, and Heineken to lay off 8,000
summary: This article covers several major corporate news items: the rebranding of "Aunt Jemima" to "Pearl Milling Company" amidst broader DEI initiatives, Salesforce's announcement of a permanent "work-from-anywhere" policy, and Heineken's plans to lay off 8,000 employees as part of its "EverGreen" strategy. It also touches on a viral Zoom court incident, a survey of catchy brand jingles, and Coca-Cola's new 100% recycled plastic bottles.
