title: Coca-Cola Transitions Brands to 100% rPET, Unveils New ‘Sip-Size’ Bottle
summary: Coca-Cola is transitioning several of its U.S. beverage brands to 100% recycled PET (rPET) bottles, excluding caps and labels, and introducing a new 13.2-oz "sip-size" bottle. These innovations aim to reduce new plastic use by over 20% compared to 2018, cutting greenhouse gas emissions. The company is also switching Sprite's packaging from green to clear plastic to improve recyclability and moving away from bioplastics for its Dasani brand in favor of 100% rPET.

title: All Market’s Vita Coco Boosted caffeinated coconut water – Product Launch
summary: All Market has launched Vita Coco Boosted, a caffeinated version of its coconut water, in the US. This new product contains 40mg of caffeine from tea and MCTs, packaged in three flavors. It is positioned as an energizing drink without the jitters, available through Amazon, Walmart, and Wholefoods.

title: Coke plans data-driven, ‘always-on’ experiential campaigns as sales dip
summary: Coca-Cola's profits and revenue declined in Q4 as the pandemic impacted out-of-home sales more than expected, leading the company to focus on data-driven, "always-on" experiential marketing campaigns to boost efficiency. The beverage giant is also undertaking a global review of its advertising and media agencies, aiming for increased digital marketing efforts and greater flexibility across different markets. Despite market share gains at home, a significant sales recovery is not anticipated until vaccines are more widely available.

title: Lockdown living helps PepsiCo through pandemic, vaccine paves path to growth
summary: PepsiCo Inc. is predicting revenue growth in 2021, expecting pre-pandemic lifestyles to resume as economies reopen and COVID-19 vaccines are rolled out. The company navigated the health crisis better than Coca-Cola due to its reliance on grocery and retail channels, reporting an 8.8% rise in fourth-quarter revenue to $22.46 billion. PepsiCo anticipates a mid-single digit rise in annual organic revenue and a high-single digit increase in adjusted earnings, with some pandemic-driven changes like increased online shopping likely to persist.

title: IFF gives activist investor seat on board
summary: International Flavors & Fragrances (IFF) has offered Sachem Head Capital Management's Scott Ferguson a seat on its board, expanding it to 14 directors. This decision follows Sachem Head's reported $1 billion stake in IFF, with the activist investor aiming to improve financial performance and integrate DuPont Nutrition & Biosciences successfully. The move comes after concerns about IFF's integration challenges from previous acquisitions and its stock performance lagging competitors.

title: Coca-Cola estimates $12 billion tax liability if it loses US TP case
summary: Coca-Cola could face a potential tax liability exceeding $12 billion if it loses its ongoing transfer pricing dispute with the US Internal Revenue Service. The article highlights the significant financial risk for the company despite the specifics of the case being behind a subscriber paywall. Anjana Haines, managing editor at ITR, covers this development among other corporate tax matters.

title: Coke’s newest bottle is made from paper
summary: Coca-Cola is testing a new paper bottle in Europe as part of its efforts to reduce plastic waste. Developed by Danish startup Paboco, the bottle is made from a single sheet of paper fiber with a thin plastic liner, aiming to be fully recyclable and eventually use plant-based materials. This initiative seeks to replace some of the millions of tons of plastic packaging Coca-Cola uses annually.

title: Leftovers: Topo Chico twists on the tangerine; Tillamook shows vintage cheese is in
summary: This article highlights new product developments from three food and beverage companies. Topo Chico is introducing a Twist of Tangerine sparkling water, expanding its citrus line within the growing sparkling water market. Tillamook is releasing vintage cheeses from 2011 and 2018, emphasizing its heritage and quality in the dairy industry. SweetPea is launching a chickpea-based non-dairy frozen dessert, capitalizing on the increasing demand for plant-based and healthier alternatives.

title: Dollar Tree and Family Dollar Donated $2.7 Million to Charitable Partners in 2020
summary: Dollar Tree, Inc. and its Family Dollar brand, along with associate contributions, donated $2.7 million in 2020 to Boys & Girls Clubs of America, Operation Homefront, and United Way of South Hampton Roads. Vendor partners and customers also contributed millions, including a $1 million gift from The Coca-Cola Company. These funds supported youth programs, military families, and COVID-19 relief efforts in local communities.

title: Coca-Cola’s try at paper bottles starts with a trickle
summary: Coca-Cola is launching a limited trial of paper bottles for its plant-based AdeZ drink in Hungary, aiming to find alternatives to plastic. This online trial involves 2,000 bottles sold through a specific grocer. The company has a goal to make 100% of its packaging recyclable or out of recycled materials by 2030, though the paper bottles still contain a plastic lining.

title: Exclusive interview with "A Game-Changing Marketing Leader" - Chioma Afe, Group Head, Retail Marketing and Analytics, Access Bank Plc.
summary: This article features an exclusive interview with Chioma Afe, Group Head of Retail Marketing and Analytics at Access Bank Plc, recognized as a "Game-Changing Marketing Leader." She discusses her career journey, marketing insights, strategies for leveraging customer feedback, and advice for aspiring CMOs, emphasizing adaptation and digital marketing. The interview highlights her diverse experience across FMCG, media, and financial services, shaping her expertise in brand building and customer engagement.

Origin Materials, a startup creating sustainable plastic from sawdust, is going public through a SPAC merger with Artius Acquisition in a $1.8 billion deal. The company aims to replace petroleum-based plastics with carbon-negative materials, having already secured partnerships with major brands like Danone, Nestle, and PepsiCo. This transaction is expected to fully fund Origin Materials until it achieves EBITDA and free cash flow positive status by 2025, enabling the construction of its first full-scale commercial plant.

title: AB InBev files lawsuit against Constellation over use of Corona brand name
summary: AB InBev's Mexican arm, Grupo Modelo, has filed a lawsuit against Constellation Brands, alleging a violation of a brand licensing agreement regarding the use of the Corona name for hard seltzer. Grupo Modelo claims Constellation was only permitted to use the Corona brand for beer in the U.S., while Constellation maintains it has fully complied with the agreement. This legal dispute highlights the increasing competition and product category expansion within the alcohol sector, particularly in the rapidly growing hard seltzer market.

title: Board of Directors of The Coca-Cola Company Announces 59th Consecutive Annual Dividend Increase
summary: The Coca-Cola Company's Board of Directors approved its 59th consecutive annual dividend increase, raising the quarterly dividend from 41 cents to 42 cents per common share. The board also elected Stacy Apter as vice president and treasurer, making her the first female treasurer of the company. In 2020, the company returned $7 billion in dividends to shareowners.

title: Board of Directors of The Coca-Cola Company Announces 59th Consecutive Annual Dividend Increase
summary: The Coca-Cola Company's Board of Directors has approved its 59th consecutive annual dividend increase, raising the quarterly dividend by 2.4% from 41 cents to 42 cents per common share. This brings the annual dividend to $1.68 per share. The company also announced the election of Stacy Apter as vice president and treasurer, making her the first female to hold this position for Coca-Cola.

title: The Coca-Cola Company announces 59th consecutive annual dividend increase
summary: The Coca-Cola Company's Board of Directors has approved its 59th consecutive annual dividend increase, raising the quarterly dividend from 41 cents to 42 cents per common share. This results in an annual dividend of $1.68 per share. The company also announced the election of Stacy Apter as vice president and treasurer, making her the first female treasurer of the company.

title: Coca-Cola Zero Sugar will be the company's biggest source of growth in 2021, CEO says
summary: Coca-Cola CEO James Quincey announced that Coca-Cola Zero Sugar is projected to be the company's primary driver of growth in 2021 and for the next few years. The drink, launched in 2017 as an updated version of Coke Zero, has successfully boosted sales even amidst the coronavirus pandemic. While other new products like Topo Chico Hard Seltzer and AHA sparkling water are performing well, Coke Energy faced challenges due to lockdowns.

title: PepsiCo Halted From Selling Electrolyte Drink Amid TM Claim
summary: A Texas federal judge has issued a temporary restraining order preventing PepsiCo Inc. from launching its new Gatorade product, Gatorlyte, on February 21st. The halt comes after a Mexican sports drink manufacturer claimed that Gatorlyte is a clone of its own electrolyte beverage. This legal action targets PepsiCo and specifically its Quaker Oats Company and The Gatorade Company subsidiaries.

title: Coca-Cola Co. shifts innovation in 2021 to favor ‘big bets,’ while saving space for experimentation
summary: Coca-Cola Co. is revamping its innovation strategy for 2021, shifting focus from extensive experimentation to "big bets" that promise significant financial impact and scale. Despite this emphasis on larger projects, the company still plans to allocate resources for "thoughtful and intelligent experiments," which are expected to grow in number and value in the future. The company is also rebooting its Coke Energy product, which faced challenges in 2020, with optimism for better progress this year.

title: Covid-19 afecta ventas de Coca Cola FEMSA, caen 5.6% en 2020
summary: Coca Cola FEMSA (KOF) reported a 5.6% decrease in sales in 2020, reaching 183,615 million pesos, primarily due to the impact of the Covid-19 pandemic's lockdown and social distancing measures. Despite the challenges, the company's CEO, John Santa Maria, highlighted resilience and operational excellence, resulting in an increase in operating flow by 5% to 37,345 million pesos, though net profit decreased by 17.9%. KOF aims to continue its strategic and digital advancements to become a total beverage platform.

title: Coca-Cola Co. reduces virgin plastic use by 20 percent in North America
summary: Coca-Cola Co. has announced a 20 percent reduction in virgin plastic use across its North America portfolio compared to 2018, driven by its recycled-content initiatives. The company is actively introducing 100-percent recycled PET bottles for several brands in select markets and plans to transition Sprite to clear plastic bottles nationwide by 2022 to improve recyclability. These efforts are part of Coca-Cola's World Without Waste goals, emphasizing the importance of consumer recycling and infrastructure investment.

title: The Coca-Cola Co. eliminates its Office of Latin Affairs
summary: The Coca-Cola Co. has eliminated its Office of Latin Affairs, an office originally created by former CEO Roberto Goizueta to foster dialogue with Hispanic shareholders and build partnerships with Hispanic organizations. Despite the elimination of the office, Coca-Cola stated that its commitment to Hispanic consumers and communities remains strong. This move comes amidst other company changes, including executive bonuses and job eliminations.

title: Smucker to cut 80 jobs closing Virginia coffee plant in 2022
summary: J.M. Smucker will cut 80 jobs by closing its liquid coffee plant in Suffolk, Virginia, in spring 2022. This closure is part of a broader corporate restructuring and follows an announcement of a partnership with JDE Peet's for its liquid coffee business. While the company reported strong overall sales growth, particularly in coffee and retail consumer foods, it is seeking a leaner organization and focusing its portfolio.

title: Heineken, The Coca-Cola Company and the Coca-Cola System in Brazil Announce Redesigned Distribution Partnership
summary: Heineken N.V., The Coca-Cola Company, and the Coca-Cola System in Brazil have agreed to redesign their distribution partnership in Brazil. This agreement will transition Heineken® and Amstel brands to HEINEKEN Brazil's distribution network, while Coca-Cola System in Brazil will focus on Kaiser, Bavaria, Sol, Eisenbahn, and other international brands, with an initial term until December 31, 2026. The new partnership offers both companies more flexibility and allows for exploration into non-alcoholic and alcoholic segments respectively, benefiting Brazilian consumers with wider options.

title: Hershey unveils new goals to address climate change
summary: Hershey has announced new environmental and carbon emission goals, aiming to reduce direct and indirect emissions by over 50% by 2030 compared to 2018. The company also plans to make all its plastic packaging recyclable, reusable, or compostable by 2030 and invest in energy efficiency. These initiatives align Hershey with a growing trend among food and beverage companies to enhance sustainability and address consumer demand for eco-friendly practices.

title: The Parent of All Parents: Here's What Berkshire Hathaway Actually Does
summary: Berkshire Hathaway is a holding company led by Warren Buffett that owns about 70 private companies and minority stakes in 41 public stocks across various sectors. While it doesn't engage in manufacturing, it controls company shares and investment interests. Buffett is the top shareholder, and notable holdings include significant stakes in Apple and Coca-Cola, with a clear disinterest in investing in Tesla.

title: Kimberly-Clark Names Robert Long as Chief Research and Development Officer
summary: Kimberly-Clark Corporation announced the appointment of Robert Long as its new Chief Research and Development Officer, effective March 15, 2021. In this newly created role, Long will oversee global research, development, innovation, and quality functions, reporting directly to CEO Mike Hsu and serving on the executive leadership team. Long brings over four decades of experience from companies like The Coca-Cola Company and Procter & Gamble, where he held senior R&D and innovation leadership positions.

title: Kimberly-Clark Names Coca-Cola Vet Robert Long Its 1st Chief R&D Officer
summary: Kimberly-Clark has appointed Robert Long, a veteran from The Coca-Cola Company and Procter & Gamble, as its first chief research and development officer, effective March 15. In this new global role, Long will oversee research, development, innovation, and quality functions, reporting to chairman and CEO Mike Hsu. Hsu anticipates Long will drive growth by enhancing brands and expanding markets, leveraging his extensive experience in R&D within the consumer goods sector, including Coca-Cola's innovation and P&G's various product categories.

title: Transfer Pricing in Food & Beverage Multinationals
summary: This article discusses the critical issue of transfer pricing for U.S. Food & Beverage multinationals, highlighted by the U.S. Tax Court's ruling against Coca-Cola, which resulted in a $3.3 billion tax bill. It explains how transfer pricing impacts profit allocation between U.S. parent companies and their foreign affiliates, potentially leading to double taxation if not properly managed. The piece emphasizes the importance of developing sound transfer pricing policies, methodologies, and comprehensive documentation to prepare for IRS audits and avoid significant penalties.

title: Hispanic businesses threaten Coca-Cola with boycott after closing Office of Latin Affairs
summary: Hispanic business owners and supermarkets are threatening to boycott Coca-Cola following the closure of its Office of Latin Affairs. This action comes as a direct response to the company's decision, sparking concerns within the Hispanic business community. The boycott threat highlights potential negative impacts on Coca-Cola's market presence among this demographic.

title: Industria del reciclaje ve como señal positiva el fin de acuerdo entre embotelladoras para construir una planta bottle to bottle
summary: The Chilean recycling industry views the termination of the agreement between Embotelladora Andina, Coca-Cola Embonor, and CCU to jointly build a "bottle to bottle" PET recycling plant as a positive development. While such a plant is considered necessary, ANIR had concerns about potential market monopolization and scarcity of used bottles for other recyclers. The National Economic Prosecutor's Office (FNE) deemed the proposed joint venture unviable as an independent entity, leading to its dissolution and a new commitment from the Coca-Cola system to pursue a plant independently.

title: Conagra may sell Hebrew National, other brands to JBS for $700M, WSJ reports
summary: Conagra Brands is reportedly in discussions to sell its Hebrew National hotdog brand and potentially other brands like Egg Beaters and Odom's Tennessee Pride to JBS for approximately $700 million. This divestiture aligns with Conagra's strategy to streamline its portfolio, emphasizing frozen offerings and snacks, following its acquisition of Pinnacle Foods. For JBS, acquiring these established brands would expand its retail presence beyond its traditional processing operations, offering higher profit margins.

title: Auntie Anne's® and Coca-Cola® are Bringing the Action Home with Ways to Win Pretzels All Tournament Long
summary: Auntie Anne's and Coca-Cola are partnering to celebrate the return of the basketball tournament with promotions for pretzel fans. These include a "Buckets for Buckets" sweepstakes offering up to 5,000 free pretzel buckets, a mobile game called "Basketball Buckets Challenge" with instant win prizes, and special pretzel deals throughout the tournament. The initiatives aim to provide fans with tasty snacks and engaging activities to enjoy the tournament from home.

title: Board of Directors of Coca-Cola Bottlers’ Sales & Services Company, LLC Elects Bill O’Brien as Chairman During Q1 2021 Meeting
summary: Coca-Cola Bottlers’ Sales & Services Company (CCBSS) announced the election of Bill O’Brien, CEO of Reyes Coca-Cola Bottling (RCCB), as the new chairman of its board of directors. O'Brien succeeds Mark Schortman and brings over three decades of experience within the Coca-Cola System and beverage industry. CCBSS President and CEO Brandi Shortt highlighted O'Brien's extensive expertise as invaluable for the company's future strategic decisions.

title: PepsiCo signs up Lebron James as Mtn Dew Rise Energy launches
summary: PepsiCo has launched Mtn Dew Rise Energy, a new functional energy drink line, and announced professional basketball player LeBron James as its brand ambassador. The new line features six flavors, contains Citicoline and 180mg of caffeine, and is available in US retail stores. This partnership follows James's previous sponsorship with The Coca-Cola Co and marks his continued involvement with major beverage brands and other ventures.

title: Coca-Cola UNITED announces $48 million expansion at Mobile facility
summary: Coca-Cola Bottling Co. UNITED is investing $48 million in its Mobile, Alabama facility to expand its warehouse, optimize distribution, and install a state-of-the-art warehousing system. This expansion aims to enhance the working environment for associates, improve customer service along the Gulf Coast, and is expected to create new jobs. The project demonstrates the company's long-term commitment to the Mobile community and Alabama's economy.

title: Vita Coco Won the Coconut Water Wars, but an Old Rival Is Planning a New Battle
summary: Mark Rampolla, founder of Zico coconut water, reacquired the brand from Coca-Cola after its discontinuation, aiming to revive it and challenge longtime rival Vita Coco. The article details Rampolla's determination to rebuild Zico Rising into a leading coconut water company, revisiting his fierce rivalry with Vita Coco's co-founder Michael Kirban, which characterized the early growth of the coconut water market in the U.S.

title: Who will replace Procter & Gamble's CEO David Taylor?
summary: This article discusses the potential succession planning for Procter & Gamble's CEO David Taylor, who is nearing retirement age. While there's no immediate pressure for a change given P&G's strong performance, the article identifies Jon Moeller, the current COO, as a frontrunner and also highlights several other key executives, including three women and two Asia-born leaders, who are being groomed for top positions. It also details the recent financial performance of various P&G business units and touches on Taylor's tenure and the company's past challenges and successes.

title: New Water Coalition Launched to Invest in Conservation Efforts for the Upper Trinity River
summary: A coalition of industry, nonprofit, and governmental organizations has formed the Texas Water Action Collaborative (TxWAC) to improve the quality and quantity of the Trinity River. This initiative, launched on World Water Day, aims to address pollution and ensure a clean water future for the millions of people who depend on the river in Texas, from Dallas-Fort Worth to Houston. TxWAC will invest in the Upper Trinity River, developing best practices and models for conservation that could eventually be extended statewide.

title: The Coca Cola Co. adds to Simply Almond line
summary: The Coca Cola Co., under its Simply brand, has expanded its Simply Almond line with a new unsweetened vanilla almond beverage. This move brings Simply's focus on simple, delicious flavors to the dairy alternative market, offering a dairy- and gluten-free option with zero added sugar. The new product, along with existing Simply Almond varieties, is available nationwide in 46-ounce carafes.

title: Snapple is getting a huge makeover, owner Keurig Dr. Pepper CEO reveals
summary: Keurig Dr. Pepper CEO Bob Gamgort announced a complete makeover for the iconic Snapple brand, focusing on new sustainable packaging made from 100% post-consumer recycled plastic. The company is refreshing its existing brands as part of a broader strategy following a strong financial year, which included market share gains and reduced financial obligations. This redesign will also save on shipping costs and reduce its carbon footprint, while maintaining the brand's great taste.

title: Coca-Cola Research Finds Five Major Pandemic-Era Consumer Trends
summary: Coca-Cola's "Refreshing Insights" report identifies five key consumer trends shaped by the pandemic: a heightened focus on health, an increase in at-home activities, a greater desire for comfort and indulgence, accelerated e-commerce adoption, and a redefinition of value. These trends highlight lasting shifts in consumer behavior regarding purchasing, daily routines, emotional needs, and spending priorities.

title: Charting market cross currents: S&P 500 pulls in from record close
summary: U.S. stocks are lower on Monday, with the S&P 500 and Dow Industrials pulling back from record closes. The decline is partly attributed to concerns over a hedge fund's forced liquidation. The Nasdaq Composite is striving to maintain support at its 2020 peak.

title: Black executives call out Barra as GM pushes to be 'most inclusive' company
summary: Black media executives, led by Byron Allen, publicly criticized General Motors CEO Mary Barra in a full-page ad, accusing her of refusing to meet with them despite GM's claims of inclusivity and emphasis on Black Lives Matter. The executives argue that GM's advertising spending with Black-owned media is inadequate and represents systemic racism. GM defended its record, stating it intends to double its marketing investment with diverse media and has formed an Inclusion Advisory Board to promote diversity and inclusion.

title: The Coca Cola Co’s Vitaminwater Look & Gutsy – Product Launch
summary: The Coca-Cola Co has launched two new zero-sugar variants, "Look" (Blueberry Hibiscus) and "Gutsy" (Watermelon & Peach), under its Vitaminwater brand in the US. "Look" supports eye health with vitamin A and lutein, while "Gutsy" aids gut function with prebiotic fiber. These additions expand Vitaminwater's zero-sugar functional range, and Coca-Cola has also increased vitamin and electrolyte content across its Vitaminwater lines.

title: CNBC Exclusive: CNBC Transcript: Coca-Cola Chairman & CEO James Quincey Speaks with CNBC’s “Power Lunch” Today
summary: Coca-Cola Chairman & CEO James Quincey clarifies the company's "unequivocal" opposition to Georgia's new voting legislation, calling it "unacceptable" and a "step backwards." He explains that while the company initially worked privately to influence the bill, its passage led to a more public and forceful stance. Quincey reiterates Coca-Cola's long-standing commitment to broad access to voting and outlines plans to advocate for changes to the legislation, emphasizing the importance of diversity and inclusion for the company.

title: After calls to boycott Coca-Cola, CEO says the company has always opposed new Georgia voting law
summary: Coca-Cola CEO James Quincey stated the company has always opposed Georgia's new voting law, choosing to speak publicly after its passage. Critics have called for boycotts due to the law's perceived disenfranchisement of people of color, despite Coke's private lobbying efforts. Quincey used stronger language against the law, calling it "wrong" and needing change, after earlier expressions of disappointment from other company executives.

title: Delta, Coca-Cola blast home state Georgia's voting restrictions as 'unacceptable'
summary: Coca-Cola Co and Delta Air Lines, along with Microsoft Corp and Citi, have publicly criticized Georgia's new voting restrictions, calling them "unacceptable" and saying they unfairly restrict voting rights. The Republican-backed law, which has been slammed by President Biden and faces legal challenges, strengthens identification requirements and shortens early voting periods. This move comes after activists called for boycotts against companies for not opposing the law earlier, with Delta's criticism marking a reversal from an earlier statement.

title: Delta and Coca-Cola face backlash from Republicans after opposing Georgia voting law. (Published 2021)
summary: Delta Air Lines and Coca-Cola are facing strong backlash from Republicans after publicly opposing a new voting law in Georgia, which critics argue makes it harder for people to vote. Following the companies' statements, Georgia's governor accused Delta's chief executive of spreading false attacks, and state Republicans suggested increasing taxes on Delta as retribution. This situation highlights the contentious nature of corporate involvement in partisan politics, with other major Georgia companies, like UPS, opting for more neutral statements.

title: The Coca-Cola Co. launches 100 percent rPET bottle in various brands, markets
summary: The Coca-Cola Co. has launched 100 percent recycled PET (rPET) bottles for several of its brands, including Coca-Cola, Diet Coke, Coke Zero Sugar, Sprite, DASANI, and smartwater, as part of its "World Without Waste" initiative. This move, which began with regional rollouts in early 2021 and will expand nationwide, aims to increase recycled material use, reduce carbon emissions, and promote a circular economy for plastic packaging. The company is investing in recycling infrastructure and consumer education to boost recycling rates and ensure a sufficient supply of quality rPET.

title: GURU Organic Energy is a buy, Echelon says
summary: Echelon Capital Markets initiated coverage of GURU Organic Energy with a "Buy" rating and a $23.50 target price, citing strong management and explosive sales growth. Analyst Amr Ezzat projects a 42.4% return over 12 months for the company, highlighting its aggressive expansion in Canada and the US, and its use of natural ingredients in a competitive energy drink market. GURU aims for significant sales growth, targeting 1.3% market share in North America within ten years.

title: A look at origin, trade secrets and owner of soft drink company Dr Pepper dubbed better than Coca-Cola
summary: This article delves into the origins, trade secrets, and ownership of the soft drink company Dr Pepper, following a tweet by Ann Coulter claiming it to be superior to Coca-Cola. It explores the drink's creation by Charles Alderton in 1885, the various theories behind its name, and the legal battles that helped it achieve national distribution. The article also discusses the closely guarded secret formula of Dr Pepper and its current ownership by Keurig Dr Pepper.

title: Taste the Transformation: How Coca Cola is Building a Digital-First Business
summary: Coca-Cola is undergoing a significant digital transformation to reverse declining revenues, focusing on experience, operational, business, and cultural changes. Key initiatives include AI-powered vending machines that personalize experiences and organizational shifts to increase agility and leverage data during the COVID-19 pandemic. The company aims to become a digital-first business by integrating technology into all aspects of its operations and customer engagement.

title: Three Philadelphians make Forbes' 2021 billionaire's list: Victoria Mars, Brian Roberts and Richard Hayne
summary: Forbes has released its 2021 World's Billionaires List, revealing that despite global economic turmoil caused by the pandemic, the world's wealthiest individuals have become 86% richer. Three Philadelphians, Victoria Mars, Brian Roberts, and Richard Hayne, made the list, representing major companies like Mars Inc., Comcast, and Urban Outfitters. The list grew significantly this year, adding 660 new billionaires, including a record number of women.

title: Biden niece worked in Coca-Cola government relations as company lobbied against Uyghur forced labor bill
summary: Missy Owens, President Biden's niece, previously worked in Coca-Cola's government relations division for nearly a decade, departing in November of the prior year. During her tenure and after, Coca-Cola actively lobbied against the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act, a bill aimed at banning imports made with forced labor from China's Xinjiang region. The company has a significant market presence in China and is a sponsor of the 2022 Beijing Winter Olympic Games, drawing criticism for its stance on human rights issues in China while speaking out on domestic political matters like Georgia's voting law.

title: The Coca-Cola Co. unveils oat milk line
summary: The Coca-Cola Co. is expanding its plant-based dairy alternatives portfolio with the introduction of Simply Oat milk under its Simply brand. This new line includes original, vanilla, and creamy varieties, all of which are lactose-free, vegan, gluten-free, and non-GMO. The launch of Simply Oat follows the brand's previous introduction of Simply Almond in February, marking its second milk alternative offering.

title: Conagra incurs $15M in supply chain costs to keep up with demand
summary: Conagra spent $15 million in Q3 to adjust its supply chain and meet high consumer demand, bypassing its usual distribution network and shipping directly from plants. This investment was deemed necessary to keep products on shelves, as the company saw net sales increase by nearly 10% year-over-year. Conagra plans to rebuild inventory and may use price adjustments to offset these increased costs, which align with broader market trends of input cost inflation.

title: Delta Air Lines CEO skims Georgia election law controversy in earnings call
summary: Delta Air Lines CEO Ed Bastian addressed the controversy surrounding the company's stance on Georgia's new election law during a quarterly earnings call, stating that the airline has not experienced any significant business impact from the discussions. Delta had faced criticism from both liberals and conservatives for its position on the law, which mandates new identification requirements for absentee ballots. Despite the controversy and a $1.2 billion loss in Q1, Delta expects to break even by June due to improving bookings.

title: Pepsico boosts sales, earnings for Q1 2021
summary: Pepsico Inc. reported a significant increase in net revenue and net income for Q1 2021, with net revenue rising 6.8% to $14.8 billion and net income growing from $1.3 billion to $1.7 billion. The company surpassed analyst expectations for both revenue and earnings per share. CEO Ramon Laguarta cited overcoming challenges like difficult year-over-year comparisons and uneven international recoveries for the strong performance, and Pepsico maintains its positive outlook for 2021.

title: Heres Why Keurig Dr Pepper Stocks 80% Rally Is Not Surprising
summary: Keurig Dr Pepper (KDP) stock has seen an 80% rally since March 2020 lows, reaching almost $36 per share. This surge is attributed to the company's resilience during the pandemic, driven by its revenue mix focused on bottled beverages and coffee brewing systems, which benefited from increased at-home consumption. Despite the stock being 40% above its 2018 level, its valuation is considered fair, and continued revenue and earnings growth are expected to maintain its current price.

title: The Coca-Cola Company and Coca-Cola Beverages Africa Announce Plans for Initial Public Offering for Bottler
summary: The Coca-Cola Company and Coca-Cola Beverages Africa (CCBA) announced plans for an initial public offering (IPO) of CCBA, intending to list it as a publicly traded company specializing in African markets. The IPO, expected within the next 18 months, will see shares listed in Amsterdam (primary exchange) and Johannesburg. This move aims to allow CCBA to operate independently and secure capital for its growth, demonstrating Coca-Cola's continued commitment to the African continent.

title: Coca-Cola CEO says company will raise prices to offset higher commodity costs
summary: Coca-Cola announced it will raise prices on its beverages to counteract increasing commodity costs, following similar moves by other consumer goods companies. CEO James Quincey indicated that while the company is hedged for 2021, price increases will be necessary for 2022. The company plans to implement these changes intelligently, considering package sizes and optimizing price points for consumers, having last raised prices in 2018 due to aluminum tariffs.

title: How The Mastermind Behind LaCroix Puts The Fizz In Business
summary: The article profiles Nick Caporella, the CEO of National Beverage, detailing his unconventional approach to business that led to the success of LaCroix sparkling water. Despite competing with industry giants like Coca-Cola and PepsiCo, Caporella's unique marketing, innovative products, and strong leadership have driven significant growth and shareholder value for National Beverage. It also touches upon his personal journey from humble beginnings to becoming a successful entrepreneur.

title: Georgia’s Voting Laws and Coca-Cola’s Complicated History
summary: This article examines Coca-Cola's complicated history with social and political issues, particularly in Georgia, its home state. It delves into the company's past dealings with racial justice movements and compares them to its recent, belated statement on Georgia's "Election Integrity Act." The piece explores the reactions from politicians, both Republican and Democrat, and discusses the challenges Coca-Cola faces in navigating these controversies while preserving its brand image.

title: Coca-Cola beats on earnings, says demand in March hit pre-pandemic levels
summary: Coca-Cola reported better-than-expected first-quarter earnings, with demand in March returning to pre-pandemic levels despite slower recovery in North America and Western Europe. The company reiterated its full-year financial forecast and announced plans for a public listing of Coca-Cola Beverages Africa. CEO James Quincey acknowledged lingering uncertainties due to new COVID-19 case spikes globally.

title: McCormick CEO: 'We've been hard-pressed to keep up with' Old Bay Seasoning demand
summary: McCormick & Company's CEO, Lawrence Kurzius, revealed that demand for Old Bay Seasoning has been "extraordinary" during the COVID-19 pandemic, making it difficult for the company to keep shelves stocked. McCormick hired 1,400 additional people and adjusted supply chains to meet this surging consumer demand, particularly for top-selling items. While consumer solutions thrived, the flavor solutions segment, which supplies restaurants, saw more modest growth.

title: Former Coca-Cola CEO, Neville Isdell On Courage, Conviction, And Respect
summary: This article highlights three key leadership lessons from former Coca-Cola CEO Neville Isdell: courage, conviction, and respect. It details how Isdell exemplified these traits through inspiring others, building alignment for growth, and deeply respecting traditions and individuals. The piece uses examples from his career, including the Coca-Cola turnaround, to illustrate these principles.

title: Procter & Gamble Will Raise Prices On Baby And Feminine Care Products In September
summary: Procter & Gamble announced it will raise prices on baby care, feminine care, and adult incontinence products starting in September to offset rising commodity prices. This move follows similar announcements from competitors Kimberly-Clark and Coca-Cola, as companies expect a short-term bump in inflation as the economy recovers. The price increases will be mid-to-high single-digit percentages and will vary by brand.

title: Georgia religious leaders call for boycott of Home Depot over silence on voting laws
summary: A group of prominent Georgia clergy members is calling for a nationwide boycott of Home Depot. They criticize the company for its silence on the state's new voting restrictions and its refusal to meet with activists, contrasting its stance with other Georgia-based companies like Delta and Coca-Cola. The religious leaders are urging Home Depot to speak out against the new voting laws and meet with them to discuss changes.

title: Home Depot to face boycott over Georgia voting curbs
summary: Religious leaders in Georgia are calling for a boycott of Home Depot due to the company's silence on the state's new voting restrictions. Activists argue that the new laws make it harder for Black people and other racial minorities to vote, and Home Depot has not joined other corporations in opposing the measures. Home Depot stated its belief that "all elections should be accessible, fair and secure and support broad voter participation."

title: Coca-Cola sees progress toward recovery | 2021-04-20
summary: Coca-Cola reported positive signs in the first quarter of 2021, with volume trends improving, though recovery remains uneven globally due to the pandemic. The company saw a return to March 2019 volume levels by March 2021, but warned of challenges from rising COVID-19 cases impacting away-from-home business. Coca-Cola introduced new products and initiatives, including smartwater+, Coca-Cola with Coffee, and Topo Chico Hard Seltzer, while maintaining its full-year guidance for organic revenue and EPS growth.

title: Church leaders call for Home Depot boycott over Georgia voting curbs
summary: Black religious leaders in Georgia are calling for a boycott of Home Depot, accusing the company of not taking a strong stance against the state's new restrictive voting law. While other Georgia-based corporations like Delta and Coca-Cola have engaged with activists and opposed the law, Home Depot has stated it supports accessible, fair, and secure elections but has not denounced the legislation. The leaders warn that the boycott will escalate if Home Depot does not forcefully speak out against the law.

title: Monica Howard Douglas Elected Senior Vice President and General Counsel of The Coca-Cola Company
summary: The Coca-Cola Company announced the election of Monica Howard Douglas as Senior Vice President and General Counsel, effective immediately. Douglas, a 17-year veteran of the company, will oversee global legal functions and report to Chairman and CEO James Quincey. Additionally, the board elected two other officers, Jeffrey Gilbert and Lucy Reid, and declared a regular quarterly dividend of 42 cents per common share.

title: CEO Alison Watkins to exit Coca-Cola Amatil after Coca-Cola European Partners takeover
summary: Coca-Cola Amatil CEO Alison Watkins will depart the company following its acquisition by Coca-Cola European Partners, expected on May 10th. Watkins led CCA for nine years, overseeing significant operational changes and the negotiation of the CCEP takeover. Coca-Cola European Partners will also change its name to Coca-Cola Europacific Partners to reflect its expanded geographic footprint.

title: Monica Howard Douglas Elected Senior Vice President and General Counsel of The Coca-Cola Company
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has announced the election of Monica Howard Douglas as Senior Vice President and General Counsel, effective immediately. Douglas, a 17-year company veteran, will lead the global legal function and report to Chairman and CEO James Quincey. Additionally, the board elected Jeffrey Gilbert as Vice President and Chief Security Officer, Lucy Reid as Vice President of Strategic Ingredient Supply, and declared a quarterly dividend of 42 cents per common share.

title: AB InBev 100+ Accelerator partners with The Coca-Cola
summary: The AB InBev 100+ Accelerator has partnered with The Coca-Cola Company, Colgate-Palmolive, and Unilever to fund and pilot sustainable innovations specifically within supply chains. This collaboration aims to accelerate solutions in areas like water stewardship, circular economy, sustainable agriculture, and climate action, leveraging the combined global reach of these major corporations. The program provides funding and "hands-on" support to startups, with a strong focus on addressing both environmental and social challenges.

title: Why some food and drink companies lost sales during the COVID-19 pandemic
summary: During the COVID-19 pandemic, some food and drink companies experienced sales declines due to factors like reliance on already struggling categories (e.g., soda, meat), dependence on "on-the-go" consumption, and failure to adapt to changing consumer preferences for premium or value products. Companies with diversified portfolios or those that innovated into growing segments like plant-based foods and sparkling water fared better. The article highlights that while some sales may rebound post-pandemic, companies need to focus on innovation and relevance to maintain growth.

title: Coca-Cola, Unilever and Colgate-Palmolive join AB InBev’s sustainability accelerator
summary: The Coca-Cola Company, Colgate-Palmolive Company, and Unilever have joined AB InBev's 100+ Accelerator, an initiative launched in 2018 to fund and pilot sustainable innovation within supply chains. This collaboration aims to supercharge the adoption of sustainable solutions by supporting startups tackling challenges in water stewardship, circular packaging, upcycling, sustainable agriculture, and climate action. The new partners will help expand the program's reach and further its mission towards a more sustainable future.

title: Monica Howard Douglas elected Senior VP of The Coca-Cola Company
summary: The Coca-Cola Company announced the election of Monica Howard Douglas as senior vice president and general counsel. Douglas, a 17-year veteran of the company, will oversee the global legal function and report to Chairman and CEO James Quincey. The board also elected Jeffrey Gilbert as vice president and Chief Security Officer, and Lucy Reid as vice president of Strategic Ingredient Supply, and declared a quarterly dividend of 42 cents per common share.

title: Chemist convicted of stealing BPA-free can liner trade secrets for a Chinese firm
summary: Xiaorong (Shannon) You, a former R&D chemist, was convicted of stealing trade secrets related to BPA-free can liners from Coca-Cola and seven chemical companies. Prosecutors alleged she intended to sell the intellectual property, valued at $120 million, to a Chinese firm supported by government programs including the Thousand Talents Plan. You was found guilty on 11 charges, including trade secret theft, conspiracy, wire fraud, and economic espionage, with sentencing scheduled for November 1.

title: Ventas por WhatsApp y nuevas rutas: Coca-Cola Femsa apuesta por la omnicanalidad
summary: Coca-Cola Femsa is expanding its omnichannel strategy by leveraging WhatsApp for sales and improving delivery routes, particularly in Colombia, Brazil, and Mexico. The company aims to add more customers to its digital channels and plans to launch a digital payment system in Brazil and Mexico later this year. This move comes as the embottler reported positive results from its WhatsApp sales in Mexico and Brazil, indicating a strong focus on digital growth and efficiency.

title: Coca-Cola FEMSA Announces First Quarter 2021 Results
summary: Coca-Cola FEMSA announced its first-quarter 2021 results, reporting a 0.9% increase in consolidated volumes, driven by growth in several Latin American countries, although offset by declines in Mexico and Uruguay. Total revenues saw a 1.5% decrease due to unfavorable currency translation, despite comparable revenues growing by 5.4%. The company also reported an increase in operating income and a significant 23.7% rise in majority net income, largely due to reduced interest expenses.

title: AB InBev 100+ Accelerator Partners With The Coca-Cola Company, Colgate-Palmolive, and Unilever For Sustainable Start-Up Innovation
summary: AB InBev's 100+ Accelerator has partnered with The Coca-Cola Company, Colgate-Palmolive, and Unilever to fund and pilot sustainable innovation in supply chains. This collaboration aims to accelerate the adoption of sustainable solutions globally by supporting start-ups focused on challenges like water stewardship, circular economy, sustainable agriculture, and climate action. The initiative combines the global reach and resources of these major corporations to drive environmental and social progress.

title: Coca-Cola Launches ‘Simply Oat’ As Oat Milk Records Triple-Digit Sales Growth
summary: Coca-Cola is expanding its plant-based offerings by launching "Simply Oat" milk, available in original, vanilla, and creamy varieties, under its Simply brand. This move capitalizes on the triple-digit sales growth in the oat milk market, reflecting a broader consumer shift towards plant-based alternatives that is rapidly outpacing the traditional animal-based food industry. The company is entering a market where leading players like Oatly are experiencing significant growth and even pursuing IPOs, highlighting the booming popularity of oat milk globally.

title: Plastic pollution is a global problem – Starbucks needs to take global action
summary: Starbucks Coffee Korea announced a plan to phase out disposable cups by 2025, which Greenpeace International considers a significant step towards reducing plastic pollution. The move is attributed to pressure from the Korean government, which has enacted policies to reduce disposable waste. Greenpeace calls on Starbucks to implement similar global actions, including accepting reusable cups, launching returnable cup programs worldwide, and committing to eliminating disposable cups globally by 2025.

title: Saadia Madsbjerg to be Named President of The Coca-Cola Foundation
summary: The Coca-Cola Company announced that Saadia Madsbjerg will be named Vice President of Global Community Affairs for The Coca-Cola Company and President of The Coca-Cola Foundation, effective June 1. Madsbjerg, formerly of The Rockefeller Foundation and McKinsey & Co., brings extensive experience in corporate strategy, philanthropy, and impact investing. She will manage the Foundation's operations, including grant making and regulatory compliance, and succeeds Helen Price.

title: Coca-Cola appoints new general counsel
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has appointed Monica Howard Douglas as senior vice president and general counsel. She has been with the company for 17 years and will oversee Coca-Cola’s global legal function. Douglas succeeds Bradley Gayton, who is transitioning to a strategic consultant role, focusing on diversity initiatives within the company's legal framework.

title: AB InBev, Coca-Cola, Colgate-Palmolive, Unilever Join Forces for Sustainable Startup Innovation
summary: AB InBev, Coca-Cola, Colgate-Palmolive, and Unilever have teamed up with AB InBev's 100+ Accelerator program to fund and pilot sustainable innovation within supply chains. The 100+ Accelerator, launched in 2018, aims to address challenges in water stewardship, circular economy, sustainable agriculture, and climate action by scaling innovative solutions from startups. This collaboration seeks to accelerate the development and implementation of sustainable practices across various global supply chains.

title: Monster Beverage Corp continues to shine in Q1 but aluminium shortages threaten growth - results data
summary: Monster Beverage Corp reported record first-quarter net sales and profits, with sales climbing 17.1% to US$1.24bn, driven by strong performance in its energy drinks segment, particularly internationally. However, the company flagged concerns over aluminium can supply shortages in North America and Europe, requiring them to source from South America and Asia, which could lead to logistical issues. The Coca-Cola Co, a significant shareholder, continues its involvement with MBC.

title: Promo Coca Cola 2L Retornables
summary: Coca-Cola Andina launched a digital promotion in Argentina to encourage the use of 2L returnable bottles. Customers can exchange two empty 2L returnable bottles plus a small fee for a new Coca-Cola and another beverage (Sprite, Fanta, or Schweppes) in 2.0L returnable packaging. The promotion is valid until May 15th or while supplies last in specific regions of Argentina.

title: Burger King tests green packaging at 51 Miami-area units
summary: Burger King is conducting a pilot program in 51 Miami-area units to test new green packaging for eight of its most-used "guest-facing" items, including forks, straws, and Whopper wrappers. The initiative aims to gather customer feedback and inform a nationwide sustainable packaging rollout. Burger King is also expanding its partnership with Loop for reusable containers and collaborating with Coca-Cola and Kraft Heinz on sustainability efforts.

title: Unilever, Coca-Cola and Colgate-Palmolive join AB InBev’s sustainability accelerator
summary: Unilever, Coca-Cola, and Colgate-Palmolive have joined AB InBev's 100+ Accelerator to fund and pilot sustainable supply chain innovations. This collaboration aims to scale existing projects and broaden the accelerator's reach through financial backing and real-world testing of technologies in their own supply chains. The initiative seeks to supercharge the adoption of sustainable solutions for a more sustainable future.

title: Pepsi Apple Pie and Candy Kraft Mac & Cheese: Why food giants are designing extreme new flavors
summary: Food and beverage giants like PepsiCo and Kraft Heinz are increasingly launching novel, extreme flavors, which are often remixes of familiar tastes. This trend, dubbed "new nostalgia," has been amplified by the COVID-19 pandemic as consumers seek both comfort and adventure while spending more time at home. These limited-time offerings often serve as marketing tools to generate social media buzz, even if they don't always result in direct sales, while others aim to drive sales through a blend of familiarity and novelty.

title: Monster sees record sales; warns of aluminum can shortage
summary: Monster Beverage Corp. reported record sales in the first quarter of 2021, with net income up 11.5% to $315 million and quarterly sales growing 14.5% to $1.24 billion. Despite this, the company faced supply chain issues, particularly an aluminum can shortage, which impacted gross margins. Monster is seeking to source cans from South America and Asia and is evaluating pricing strategies to maintain market share without disturbing its successful business.

title: Melinda Gates divorce stocks: AutoNation to Mexican Coca-Cola
summary: Following her split from Bill Gates, Melinda Gates has acquired a diverse stock portfolio, revealed through SEC filings. This portfolio includes significant stakes in Mexican bellwethers like Coca-Cola Femsa and Grupo Televisa SA, as well as shares in Canadian National Railway and AutoNation. The total value of these transfers to Melinda Gates over the week amounts to nearly $2.4 billion.

title: General Mills CMO departs and company will not seek a replacement
summary: General Mills' global marketing chief, Ivan Pollard, has departed the company as part of an organizational restructuring, and the company confirmed it will not seek a replacement for the global CMO role. This move is aligned with General Mills' "Accelerate growth strategy" formulated last year, intended to better align its structure with strategic initiatives. Pollard, who joined in 2017, focused on revitalizing legacy brands and balancing technology-driven mandates with brand building, a departure that raises questions given recent trends of other large companies resurrecting the CMO position.

title: Coca-Cola Asks Its Workers to Be 'Less White' to Fight Racism
summary: Coca-Cola is facing backlash after it emerged that the company encouraged its employees to participate in an anti-racism course titled 'Facing Racism' by Robin DiAngelo, which instructed them to be "less white." The seminar's content, which included slides suggesting being "less white" means being "less oppressive" and "less arrogant," was leaked online, sparking a significant controversy and calls for a boycott. While Coca-Cola clarified that the course was not mandatory and was part of a broader diversity initiative, the program has been criticized for being racially divisive.

title: Burger King U.S. Launches Green Packaging Pilot Program, Expands Loop Reusables Test
summary: Burger King U.S. is launching a green packaging pilot program to test sustainable alternatives for various items like cutlery, straws, and Whopper wrappers in 51 Miami restaurants. This initiative, which includes paper and plant-based straws, aims to significantly reduce single-use plastic and paper waste. The company is also expanding its Loop reusables testing program with partners like The Coca-Cola Company and Kraft Heinz, extending it to Paris and London following initial trials in New York City, Portland, and Tokyo.

title: Former Coca-Cola Employee Convicted of Stealing Trade Secrets for the Chinese Government
summary: A former Coca-Cola employee, Dr. Xiaorong (Shannon) You, was convicted of stealing trade secrets related to BPA-free coatings for beverage cans, intending to benefit the Chinese government. The trade secrets, valued at almost $120 million, were taken from Coca-Cola and Eastman Chemical Company. This case highlights the importance of strong trade secret protection practices and the risks associated with certain foreign government-backed programs.

title: Cadence CEO says merger with BancorpSouth is 'all about growth'
summary: Cadence Bancorporation's CEO, Paul Murphy Jr., stated that the merger with BancorpSouth is driven by the goal of growth. The aim is to achieve greater scale, enabling the combined entity to compete for business from larger borrowers and enhance customer service and technology offerings.

title: How Does the Coca-Cola Company Plan to Support its Hispanic Partners?
summary: Coca-Cola's Vice President, Alba Castillo Baylin, is leading an initiative to reaffirm the company's commitment to Hispanic community partners following a restructuring that integrated the Office of Latino Affairs into a larger department. This move, initially met with concern, aims to strengthen ties and support the Hispanic community through increased resources, marketing integration, and supplier diversity. The company emphasizes its dedication to diversity and inclusion within its workforce and supply chain, and continues to engage with Hispanic organizations to address their needs.

title: Coke Discontinues Underperforming Energy Drink in North America
summary: Coca-Cola Co. is ceasing the sale of its Coca-Cola Energy drink in North America, little over a year after its launch. This decision is part of a broader strategy by the beverage giant to streamline its product portfolio. This follows earlier announcements regarding the discontinuation of Tab and Zico drink brands.

title: Coca-Cola discontinues energy drink in N.America
summary: Coca-Cola Co announced it would discontinue its energy drink in North America, a product launched last year, as part of a strategy to streamline its portfolio and focus on faster-moving beverages. The decision comes as consumers return to traditional sodas and flavored sparkling waters post-pandemic, though Coca-Cola Energy will remain available in other global markets. The company emphasized a disciplined approach to investment, scaling successful innovations while divesting from products that lack traction.

title: Coca-Cola to discontinue sales of Coca-Cola Energy
summary: Coca-Cola is discontinuing sales of Coca-Cola Energy in North America to streamline its portfolio and focus on better-performing brands. This decision comes after a short run for the beverage in the U.S., launched in 2020 following an initial debut in Europe, despite winning an arbitration claim against Monster Energy. Coca-Cola will continue to participate in the energy drink market through its partnership with Monster and focus on other promising brands like Aha and Coca-Cola with Coffee.

title: Coca-Cola y sus embotelladoras invertirán 11,000 mdp en sustentabilidad
summary: Coca-Cola México, along with its bottlers Arca Continental and Coca-Cola Femsa, will invest 11,000 million pesos over the next three years to boost sustainable development. This investment will focus on infrastructure for recycling plants, collection, and recycling efforts, strengthening their commitment as the primary recycler of food-grade PET in the country. The initiative aims to create direct and indirect jobs and recover 100% of their sold packaging by 2030.

title: Coca-Cola pulls plug on energy drink
summary: Coca-Cola has decided to discontinue its Coca-Cola Energy product in North America, little over a year after its launch. The company stated the decision is part of its strategy to focus on scaling successful innovations and being disciplined with products that do not gain sufficient traction. Coca-Cola Energy was initially launched in 25 countries and aimed to attract new consumers to the energy drink category.

title: Coca-Cola to discontinue Coca-Cola Energy in North America: a case of poor timing or clashing brand identities?
summary: Coca-Cola has announced it will discontinue Coca-Cola Energy in North America, little over a year after its launch, due to poor sales performance. Despite the overall energy drink market thriving, Coca-Cola Energy only captured 0.7% of US sales, struggling against established brands like Red Bull and Monster Energy. Experts suggest the failure might be attributed to poor timing, launching during the pandemic, and a brand identity clash between Coke's refreshment image and the functional energy drink proposition.

title: Coca-Cola is turning to hard seltzer and sports drinks in a bid to stay on top
summary: Coca-Cola, one of the world's largest beverage companies, is adapting to declining soda consumption by diversifying its product offerings. The company has entered the alcoholic beverage market with Topo Chico Hard Seltzer and invested in sports performance drinks like BodyArmor. Despite disruptions from the pandemic, Coca-Cola reported a 5% revenue increase in Q1 2021, and its CEO, James Quincey, highlighted strategic improvements in marketing and innovation.

title: Coca-Cola HBC enables real-time delivery tracking for customers by partnering with Shippeo
summary: Coca-Cola HBC has partnered with Shippeo, a leading real-time transportation visibility solution provider, to enable real-time delivery tracking for its customers. This collaboration aims to streamline logistics operations, improve on-time deliveries, and enhance efficiency by leveraging Shippeo's platform to provide accurate ETAs and reduce administrative tasks. The project's initial rollout has been completed in several countries, with further expansion planned throughout 2021 and 2022.

title: Keep America Beautiful litter study ignores corporate blame for plastic pollution
summary: Greenpeace USA criticizes a new Keep America Beautiful (KAB) report, arguing that while it notes a decrease in overall litter, KAB's focus on individual responsibility distracts from corporate accountability for plastic pollution. Greenpeace highlights the increasing proportion of plastic litter and calls out KAB's corporate partners, like Coca-Cola and PepsiCo, for their reliance on single-use plastics as the root cause of the environmental problem. John Hocevar, Greenpeace USA Oceans Campaign Director, states that solving the plastic crisis requires holding corporations accountable for their plastic production, which is projected to triple by 2050.

title: PepsiCo: a company profile 1898 - 2021
summary: This article provides a company profile of PepsiCo from its founding in 1898 up to 2021, detailing its history, mergers, and product acquisitions. It highlights significant advertising campaigns, both successful and controversial, and discusses the company's commitment to ESG values and sustainability efforts, such as the PepsiCo BottleLoop recycling initiative.

title: Coca-Cola Bottling Company Streamlines Operations with RPA
summary: Coca-Cola Bottling Company United partnered with Happiest Minds to implement Robotic Process Automation (RPA) using Microsoft Power Automate, streamlining its order management processes. This digital transformation addressed challenges with legacy applications and third-party websites, leading to significant cost savings and increased efficiency. The "Asa" master automated service agent, built on Microsoft Azure, allowed the company to avoid hiring 10 full-time employees and enabled existing CRM agents to focus on other projects.

title: ‘Woke’ Values Boomerang on Coca-Cola
summary: This article from the National Review argues that Coca-Cola is facing negative repercussions due to its embrace of "woke" values. The piece suggests that the company's progressive stances are alienating consumers and impacting its business negatively. It implies a backlash against corporate activism.

title: Coca-Cola faces competition probe as retailers call foul over unfair trading practices
summary: The European Commission has launched an investigation into Coca-Cola's sales policies, specifically its discounting system, over potential violations of competition rules. Retailers allege that Coca-Cola abuses its market power by leveraging "must-have" brands to limit competition and impose unfavorable conditions. This probe echoes a 2005 ruling against Coca-Cola for similar practices, and if found in breach, the company could face significant fines.

title: Coke, Pepsi campaigns differ on reopening as anticipation grows for sunny summer
summary: Coca-Cola and PepsiCo have launched differing marketing campaigns to capitalize on the anticipation of post-pandemic reopening for summer. While Coca-Cola's "Open for Summer" campaign takes a more cautious and poetic approach with new packaging, Pepsi's "The Mess We Miss" ad boldly depicts germ-spreading activities, risking backlash but aiming for memorability. Experts debate whether Pepsi's aggressive approach is suitable given lingering pandemic uncertainties and shifts in hygiene habits.

title: Coca-Cola HBC to Digitally Transform its End-to-End Planning with Blue Yonder
summary: Coca-Cola HBC is partnering with Blue Yonder to digitally transform its end-to-end supply chain planning using Blue Yonder's SaaS-based Luminate Planning solutions. This initiative aims to improve demand forecasting, optimize production and resource allocation, enhance sustainability efforts, and enable faster decision-making across its 28 operating countries. The new cloud-based system will integrate data from multiple sources to create an efficient and agile supply chain.

title: Eli Lilly kicks off global media review
summary: Global pharmaceutical giant Eli Lilly and Company has initiated a review of its media agency requirements. OMD, the incumbent for nearly two decades, is defending the pitch, which is expected to involve at least four major holding companies and is estimated to be worth between $600 million and $800 million. This review follows other significant media pitches this year, as healthcare has emerged as a growth area for agencies, and Eli Lilly experienced a 10% revenue increase in 2020.

title: Eddie Harris says he hopes the Coke boycott will spread across NC.
summary: Surry County Commissioner Eddie Harris initiated a boycott of Coca-Cola machines in county buildings due to the company's criticism of Georgia's new voting laws. Harris hopes this boycott will expand across North Carolina, arguing that the 2020 presidential election was unfair and that stronger election security is needed. He believes it is time to speak out against perceived "left-wing politics."

title: Coca-Cola Cuts Its Energy Drink
summary: The Coca-Cola Co. is discontinuing the sale of Coca-Cola Energy in North America. This decision is part of a broader strategy to streamline its portfolio and focus on products showing greater traction, such as AHA and Coca-Cola with Coffee. Coca-Cola Energy was launched in the U.S. in January 2020 and featured 114 milligrams of caffeine, guarana extract, and B vitamins.

title: Krispy Kreme reveals its plans for an initial public offering trading as DNUT. (Published 2021)
summary: Krispy Kreme, owned by JAB Holding, announced its plans for an initial public offering, with shares set to trade on the Nasdaq under the symbol DNUT. The company reported a 17 percent increase in sales to $1.1 billion in its last fiscal year, but also saw losses nearly double to $60 million as it invested in transformation efforts. This IPO marks Krispy Kreme's second public listing, having previously gone public in 2000 before being acquired by JAB in 2016.

title: 'We are trying to cancel Coca-Cola': NC county bans Coke machines in office buildings
summary: Surry County, North Carolina commissioners voted 3-2 to ban Coca-Cola vending machines from county office buildings. Commissioner Eddie Harris stated the move was to "cancel Coca-Cola" effectively using the company's own tactics against perceived liberal leanings. This action was taken in response to Coca-Cola's criticism of new restrictive voting laws passed by Georgia Republicans, which some argue target minority voters.

title: The Coca-Cola Company And The Ocean Cleanup Join Forces To Clean Up 15 Of The World’s Most Polluting Rivers Of Plastic Waste
summary: The Coca-Cola Company and The Ocean Cleanup have partnered to clean up 15 of the world's most polluting rivers of plastic waste by the end of 2022. This collaboration involves deploying The Ocean Cleanup's Interceptor technology and utilizing Coca-Cola's global network and waste management expertise to collect and recycle plastics, contributing to a circular economy and Coca-Cola's "World Without Waste" strategy. The initiative aims to tackle rivers primarily in Southeast Asia and Central America, with collected plastic being recycled to make new bottles.

title: Coca-Cola Becomes First Global Implementation Partner to Help Accelerate Cleanup
summary: The Ocean Cleanup and Coca-Cola have partnered to deploy Interceptors in 15 rivers worldwide by the end of 2022, aiming to accelerate plastic cleanup efforts. This partnership leverages Coca-Cola's global network to support deployment logistics, funding, and waste handling, while The Ocean Cleanup provides its technology and data solutions. Both organizations emphasize the importance of industry collaboration to address the global crisis of ocean plastic pollution.

title: How Coca-Cola United Streamlined Freestyle Order Management
summary: Coca-Cola Bottling Company United partnered with Happiest Minds Technologies to streamline its Freestyle order management process using Microsoft Power Automate RPA bots. This digital transformation, built on Microsoft Azure and Power Platform, allowed the company to avoid hiring additional full-time employees and freed up existing CRM agents for other projects. The automated system orchestrates the entire order process from purchase order to reconciliation in SAP, securely accessing internal and external systems.

title: North Carolina county bans Coca-Cola machines over ‘left-wing’ politics
summary: Surry County, North Carolina, has voted to ban all Coca-Cola vending machines from its office buildings. The decision by the all-Republican county commissioners is a protest against Coca-Cola's criticism of Georgia's restrictive new voting laws, which one commissioner labeled as "left-wing" politics. The machines, however, had yet to be removed at the time of the article's publication.

title: Anheuser-Busch US Beers Now Brewed With 100% Wind And Solar Power
summary: Anheuser-Busch announced that it has achieved its goal of brewing all its US beers with 100% renewable electricity from solar and wind power, four years ahead of its 2025 target. This achievement is marked by the official online launch of the Anheuser-Busch Solar Farm in Pecos County, Texas, the largest solar project for the beverage industry in the United States. The company's commitment to sustainability also includes water stewardship, recyclable packaging, smarter agricultural practices, and aims for a zero-emission truck fleet by 2025.

title: Coca-Cola: Brands with heavy or perishable items can still leverage e-commerce
summary: The CEO of The Coca-Cola Company, James Quincey, explained that brands with heavy, bulky, or perishable products can still effectively use e-commerce by adopting a broad definition of the term. He identified four key areas for e-commerce engagement: e-B2B platforms, food delivery for immediate consumption, online grocery retail, and direct-to-consumer (D2C) for consumer engagement. Quincey emphasized that while some e-commerce channels, like D2C for heavy items, may not be financially dominant, they still offer significant value for building consumer loyalty and improving retailer relationships.

title: 10 Coca-Cola Products You Can’t Buy Anymore
summary: This article lists 10 Coca-Cola products that are no longer available for purchase, highlighting the company's continuous efforts to streamline its portfolio by discontinuing underperforming brands. It explains that while the pandemic fast-tracked some decisions, the strategy to retire certain products was already in motion. The piece delves into the history and reasons behind the discontinuation of various beverages, including TaB, Odwalla, Zico Coconut Water, Coca-Cola Life, Coca-Cola Blak, Coca-Cola C2, OK Soda, Diet Coke Lime, Diet Coke Feisty Cherry, and New Coke.

title: El parque eólico Los Teros, de YPF, ya tiene en operaciones sus 175 MW de capacidad instalada
summary: YPF Luz has fully commissioned its Los Teros II wind farm, adding 52 MW to the existing 123 MW at Los Teros I, bringing the total capacity to 175 MW. This project, located in Azul, Buenos Aires, involved an investment of $235 million and consists of 45 General Electric wind turbines. The park can produce 838 GWh per year, equivalent to supplying 215,000 homes, and boasts a high capacity factor of 55%.

title: ICEE® Debuts THREE New Products to Kick-Off the Summer Season
summary: The ICEE Company, a subsidiary of J&J Snack Foods Corp., announced the launch of three new frozen novelty products: ICEE Red Cherry Ice Cream Float Tubes, ICEE Blue Raspberry Ice Cream Float Tubes, and mystery flavored ICEE Mermaid & Baby Narwhal Tubes. These new gluten-free, low-calorie treats are available nationwide to kick off the summer season. The expansion aims to offer more fun, frozen options for the whole family, building on ICEE's existing product lines.

title: Coca-Cola Sued for False Advertising Over Sustainability Claims
summary: Earth Island Institute has filed a lawsuit against Coca-Cola, alleging false advertising and greenwashing due to the company's sustainability claims, despite being the world's leading plastic waste generator. The suit, filed in District of Columbia Superior Court, does not seek damages but aims to halt Coca-Cola's deceptive marketing practices and encourage transparency regarding its plastic use. This action highlights a broader issue of corporations, including those in the fossil fuel industry, facing legal challenges over misleading environmental representations.

title: Earth Island Sues Coca-Cola Over Greenwashing Claims & False Advertisement
summary: Earth Island Institute has filed a lawsuit against Coca-Cola, alleging the beverage giant is greenwashing its image despite being the world's largest plastic polluter. The lawsuit, filed on World Oceans Day, seeks to hold Coca-Cola accountable for misleading consumers about its sustainability practices, which the environmental organization claims cause significant damage to marine life and coastal communities. Earth Island is represented by Richman Law & Policy and argues Coca-Cola is in violation of the District of Columbia’s Consumer Protection Procedures Act.

title: LDC’s “Mastergold” Cooking Oil E-store Live on JD.com
summary: Louis Dreyfus Company (LDC) has launched its first-ever e-store on JD.com, a major Chinese B2C online retailer, to sell its Mastergold cooking oils to Chinese consumers. This strategic move aims to leverage China's booming e-commerce market, which presents significant growth opportunities for food brands. The online store will initially offer peanut and sunflower cooking oils, with plans to expand to a wider range including non-GMO soybean, corn flaxseed, rice bran, olive, and linseed oils.

title: Coke market value falls $4bn after Ronaldo snub
summary: Coca-Cola's market value dropped by $4 billion after Cristiano Ronaldo removed two of their bottles from a Euro 2020 news conference, advocating for water instead. The incident, followed by a share price drop, prompted a response from Coca-Cola and Euro 2020 organizers acknowledging diverse drink preferences and the importance of sponsorship. This occurred days before Ronaldo became the leading scorer in European Championship history.

title: Coca-Cola loses $4 billion in market value after Cristiano Ronaldo shuns Coke
summary: Coca-Cola's market value dropped by $4 billion after soccer star Cristiano Ronaldo removed its bottles during a Euro 2020 press conference, instead advocating for water. Following his actions, the company's share price fell and its market capitalization decreased from $242 billion to $238 billion. Coca-Cola, an official sponsor of the tournament, stated that everyone is entitled to their drink preferences.

title: Staples CEO Is Stepping Down
summary: Staples Inc. CEO J. Alexander (Sandy) Douglas is stepping down after three years, with John A. Lederer, executive chairman of the board, appointed as interim CEO. Douglas's departure comes as Staples recently made another offer to acquire competitor Office Depot. Staples Promotional Products, a subsidiary, was ranked third on Counselor’s list of largest distributors in the industry.

title: Staples CEO steps down
summary: J. Alexander (Sandy) Douglas is resigning as CEO of Staples, effective June 18, and will be succeeded on an interim basis by executive chairman John A. Lederer. Staples, owned by Sycamore Partners, has begun a search for a permanent CEO. The departure, stated to be by mutual agreement, comes amid Staples' third attempt to acquire the consumer business of Office Depot.

title: Coca-Cola, Monster win appeal of $9.6 million verdict over ‘Hansen’s’ rights
summary: A California appellate court has overturned a $9.5 million jury verdict against Coca-Cola Co and Monster Beverage Co related to the alleged misuse of Hubert Hansen's publicity rights for their "Hansen's" brand drinks. The court ruled that the trial judge improperly interpreted evidence that should have been weighed by the jury, leading to a prejudiced outcome for the defendants. The case has been remanded for a new trial, with the appellate court emphasizing that the interpretation of asset transfer agreements regarding intellectual property should have been left to the jury.

title: Coca-Cola North America Steps up Spending With Minority-Owned Media Companies
summary: Coca-Cola North America announced its plan to nearly double its spending with minority-owned media companies over the next three years, allocating 8% of its annual media budget by 2024 to Black, Hispanic, and AAPI-owned media. This initiative includes a significant boost in 2021 spending and the launch of a pilot certification assistance program to support the growth of these businesses. The commitment aligns with Coca-Cola's broader efforts to foster diversity, equity, and inclusion, and to support diverse suppliers across its supply chain.

title: Coke and Pepsi eye new sustainability goals after years of failed promises
summary: Coca-Cola and PepsiCo are under increasing pressure from investors and customers to adopt more ambitious sustainability goals, particularly regarding reusable and refillable packaging, after decades of focusing on plastic recycling with limited success. Both companies have a history of setting and missing recycling targets, leading environmentalists to question the effectiveness of their new commitments. Despite past failures, the pandemic and growing demand for corporate responsibility are pushing these beverage giants to genuinely integrate sustainability into their core operations, beyond just recycling initiatives.

title: Profile: Beverage giant The Coca-Cola Company
summary: This article profiles The Coca-Cola Company, highlighting its history, global presence, and strategic approach to procurement, particularly in supplier diversity and sustainability. It details Coca-Cola's efforts in increasing spending with minority-owned businesses and implementing sustainable agricultural practices, emphasizing their commitment to strengthening local communities and fostering innovation. The company's unique supply chain management through Coca-Cola Bottlers’ Sales & Service (CCBSS) and various awards are also noted.

title: Procter & Gamble, PepsiCo, Unilever Are Developing 'False' Solutions To Plastic Pollution, Reveals Report
summary: A report by the non-profit Break Free From Plastic movement reveals that major FMCG companies like Procter & Gamble, PepsiCo, and Unilever are largely investing in "false solutions" to plastic pollution.
