Out of 265 corporate projects analyzed from 2018 to April 2021, only 15% focused on proven methods like reuse, refill, and alternative delivery systems, with the vast majority being ineffective or even damaging. Environmental advocates urge these companies to end their reliance on single-use plastics and scale up genuine reuse-based systems instead of promoting misleading initiatives.

title: CEOs from The Coca-Cola Company and Alibaba Group to Lead The Consumer Goods Forum Board of Directors
summary: The Consumer Goods Forum (CGF) announced the election of Daniel Zhang, Chairman & CEO of Alibaba Group, and James Quincey, Chairman & CEO of The Coca-Cola Company, as its new Co-Chairs for a two-year term. They succeed Özgür Tort and Emmanuel Faber and will lead the CGF in accelerating actions on sustainability, health, and safety challenges, building on the strategic shift with the creation of eight Coalitions of Action. Frans Muller and Alan Jope were also appointed Vice Co-Chairs.

title: Coca-Cola HBC strengthens its coffee portfolio
summary: Coca-Cola HBC has announced a strategic move to boost its coffee portfolio by acquiring a 30% equity stake in Casa Del Caffè Vergnano S.p.A., a premium Italian coffee company. This investment is coupled with an exclusive, long-term distribution agreement for Caffè Vergnano products in Coca-Cola HBC's territories outside Italy. The partnership aims to broaden Coca-Cola HBC's coffee offerings beyond its existing Costa Coffee brand, catering to a wider range of consumer preferences and leveraging its extensive distribution network for Caffè Vergnano's expansion.

title: Here’s Why Keurig Dr Pepper Stock Is Beating Coke and Pepsi
summary: Keurig Dr Pepper's (KDP) stock is outperforming Coca-Cola and PepsiCo this year, despite sodas not being the trendiest beverages. The article attributes this success to sodas being a long-term winner for the company.

title: Coca-Cola Great Britain to use fully recycled plastic for 500ml bottles
summary: Coca-Cola Great Britain is transitioning all its 500ml or smaller "on-the-go" plastic bottles to fully recycled plastic content, a move expected to save 29,000 tonnes of virgin plastic annually. This initiative, supported by UK Environment Minister Rebecca Pow, is part of Coca-Cola's global ambition to collect and recycle a bottle or can for each one sold by 2025 and follows similar moves in North America. The company also advocates for a Deposit Return Scheme in the UK to increase the availability of food-grade recycled plastic.

title: 2021 State of the Beverage Industry: Bottled water bubbling over with growth
summary: This article details the continued growth of the bottled water industry in 2021, highlighting its expansion even during the COVID-19 pandemic. It emphasizes the role of health and wellness attributes, convenience, and the increasing popularity of sparkling and enhanced waters in driving this growth. The report includes sales figures and insights from industry experts on market trends and innovation within the water category.

title: ¿Por qué Oxxo ya vende cervezas de Grupo Modelo?
summary: Oxxo, a convenience store chain owned by FEMSA, has started selling Grupo Modelo beers like Corona and Victoria following the termination of an exclusivity agreement with Cuauhtémoc Moctezuma (Heineken). This new alliance, established in 2019, allows Modelo products to be sold in Oxxo stores, gradually expanding its presence across Mexico, benefiting both companies by increasing Grupo Modelo's sales and leveraging Oxxo's extensive reach.

title: Coca-Cola FEMSA publicó su primer informe de bono verde
summary: Coca-Cola FEMSA has published its first green bond report, detailing the use of US$235.48 million, or 33.4%, of the US$705 million raised in September 2020. These funds have been allocated to projects promoting a circular economy, water conservation, and climate change initiatives, aligning with the company's environmental objectives and the UN Sustainable Development Goals. The report highlights progress in using recycled PET, reducing water usage in production, and advancing towards 100% renewable energy in operations.

title: Descartes continues customer-driven acquisition strategy with GreenMile purchase
summary: Descartes Systems Group acquired GreenMile, a cloud-based mobile routing solution specializing in food and beverage, for $30 million upfront plus a potential $10 million earn-out. This acquisition is part of Descartes' customer-driven strategy to enhance its global logistics network and improve customer offerings, particularly in last-mile delivery and supply chain operations. GreenMile's platform provides driver visibility, route optimization, and delivery performance management tools, benefiting clients like Coca-Cola and PepsiCo.

title: John Tonnison Joins US Foods As EVP, Chief Information & Digital Officer
summary: US Foods Holding Corp. has appointed John Tonnison as its new Executive VP, Chief Information and Digital Officer, where he will oversee the company's technology vision, strategy, and all IT functions. Tonnison brings over three decades of experience, including nearly two decades at Tech Data Corporation, and replaces former CIO Keith Rohland. He will report to Chairman and CEO Pietro Satriano and focus on driving best-in-class digital commerce solutions for US Foods' customers.

title: Coca-Cola Zero Sugar gets a recipe refresh
summary: Coca-Cola Co. is launching a new recipe and packaging for Coca-Cola Zero Sugar, aiming for an "even more iconic Coke taste" by optimizing the flavors while keeping the same ingredients and nutritional information. This refresh comes with a new look for the product, following historical lessons for the beverage maker.

title: Coca-Cola Updates Zero Sugar Drink
summary: Coca-Cola is launching an updated Coca-Cola Zero Sugar with an improved flavor blend and new packaging, set to achieve full U.S. distribution by August. The company partnered with model Emily Ratajkowski for the launch event in New York City. The new CSD aims to deliver the classic Coke taste without added sugar.

title: PepsiCo Q2 2021 sales jump 20.5%, will raise prices
summary: PepsiCo announced a 20.5% jump in Q2 2021 sales, reaching $19.22 billion, and an increase in net income, prompting an upward revision of its full-year earnings forecast. The company plans to raise product prices after Labor Day to offset increased raw material, advertising, and marketing costs, driven by supply chain disruptions and rising consumer demand as the U.S. economy reopens. Despite these challenges, PepsiCo expects 6% organic revenue growth and 11% core constant currency EPS growth for fiscal year 2021.

title: Coca-Cola Is Changing the Flavor of a Soda. Again. (Published 2021)
summary: Coca-Cola is changing the flavor and look of Coke Zero Sugar, aiming for an "even more iconic Coke taste," a move that has already sparked consumer anxiety and comparisons to the 1985 "New Coke" debacle. This change to one of its popular diet spinoffs risks a backlash from consumers who remember the company's past controversial flavor alterations. The company is seeking to deliver a taste that more closely resembles "classic" Coke.

title: Coca-Cola is reformulating one of its beverages to ‘refresh’ its taste and packaging
summary: Coca-Cola is once again reformulating its Coca-Cola Zero Sugar beverage, aiming for a "more delicious and refreshing" taste and updated packaging. This change, which includes a simplified design and retention of the same sweetening ingredients, follows a previous reformulation in 2017. The new version is rolling out in select markets and will be nationwide by September.

title: Why is Tesla incorporated in Delaware?
summary: This article explains why a disproportionate number of companies, including Tesla, Amazon, and Google, are incorporated in Delaware despite not being headquartered there. Key reasons include flexible corporate law, the efficient Court of Chancery, favorable tax treatment for out-of-state income, and a long-standing state focus on business formation. The article also touches on the challenges this presents for regional data and business coverage.

title: Artificial Intelligence at Coca-Cola – Two Current Use-Cases
summary: Coca-Cola leverages AI in two main areas: understanding customer preferences for product development and enhancing its customer rewards program. The Coca-Cola Freestyle machines use data to inform decisions for new product launches, while a TensorFlow-based OCR solution simplifies code entry for loyalty program participants, boosting engagement and improving character recognition accuracy over time. These AI applications help Coca-Cola better relate to its customers, optimize marketing, and drive sales.

title: North Carolina General Assembly appoints 2 members to App State Board of Trustees
summary: The North Carolina General Assembly appointed James "Jamie" E. Harris and Steven D. Wyatt to Appalachian State University's Board of Trustees. Both are App State alumni and bring extensive professional experience to their four-year terms, which began on July 1. Harris has a background in finance as a CFO for SPX Corporation and other companies, while Wyatt has nearly 40 years of city and county management experience.

title: Soft drinks are big business in Alabama
summary: The soft drink industry, particularly Coca-Cola Bottling Company United and Buffalo Rock, has a significant economic impact in Alabama, generating billions in sales and thousands of jobs. Both companies, with histories spanning over a century, are major privately-held bottlers for Coca-Cola and PepsiCo respectively, and continue to make substantial investments in the state despite evolving consumer preferences.

title: Energy market thrives during pandemic
summary: The energy drink and shot market experienced significant growth during the pandemic, with total energy drink sales up 9.2% in 2020 to approximately $14.3 billion. This growth is attributed to consumers relying on these products for energy to cope with increased workloads and challenges brought on by the pandemic. The market is also seeing innovation in flavors, functionality, and performance energy variations, although energy shots have experienced a decline due to reduced convenience store traffic and limited innovation.

title: Coca-Cola leans on early pandemic lessons to prepare for Delta variant hit
summary: Coca-Cola plans to combat the potential impact of the Delta variant by focusing on bigger brands and strengthening its supply chain, a strategy learned from the early pandemic. Despite new restrictions in some regions, the beverage giant exceeded second-quarter expectations and increased its full-year sales forecast, though sales in some Asian markets were affected. The company's vulnerability to venue closures makes it riskier than PepsiCo, according to analysts.

title: Coca-Cola sees strong results as away-from-home channels recover
summary: Coca-Cola reported strong Q2 2021 results, with concentrate sales up 26% and net income soaring 48%, driven by the recovery of away-from-home channels and robust at-home demand. The company raised its full-year guidance for earnings per share growth to 13-15% and organic sales growth to 12-14%, despite challenges in the supply chain and commodity costs. Management expects to retain some of the at-home gains made during the pandemic while benefiting from the continued recovery of out-of-home consumption.

title: Coca-Cola spurs 42% revenue growth after returning to pre-pandemic marketing spend
summary: Coca-Cola reported a 42% increase in net revenues to $10.1 billion in Q2 2021, largely attributed to a return to pre-pandemic marketing spend levels. The company doubled its marketing investment year-over-year, focusing on innovation, effectiveness, and efficiency. This strategy led to significant growth, outpacing Q2 2019 revenues and earnings, with notable success in new product launches, targeted campaigns, and e-commerce.

title: Sparkling beverages soar in popularity among young Chinese
summary: Sparkling beverages are rapidly gaining popularity among young Chinese consumers, driven by health consciousness and a preference for low or no-sugar, calorie-free options. Brands like Genki Forest have successfully capitalized on this trend with innovative marketing and product development, leading to significant market growth. Despite challenges, such as a recent setback for Nongfu Spring, the carbonated water market in China is projected to continue its expansion, attracting major beverage companies.

title: Coca-Cola Expanding Wabi Digital Ecosystem
summary: Coca-Cola is expanding its Wabi digital ecosystem to improve relationships with retailers and bottling partners, as well as gather valuable consumer insights. The platform, which enables direct-to-consumer and B2B sales, is being used in regions with high densities of mom-and-pop shops and is accelerating the digitization of relationships with bottlers and independent retailers. Coca-Cola is also experimenting with multi-category approaches and leveraging its sales force for account development and in-store activations.

title: Coca-Cola Successfully Petitions to Cancel Trademark Registrations Based on Misrepresentation of Source
summary: Coca-Cola successfully petitioned the Trademark Trial and Appeal Board (TTAB) to cancel U.S. trademark registrations for "THUMS UP" and "LIMCA" held by Meenaxi Enterprise, Inc. The TTAB found that Meenaxi misrepresented the source of the goods, deliberately trading on the goodwill of Coca-Cola's well-known Indian beverage brands. This decision highlights that trademark owners do not need to sell products under a mark in the U.S. to seek cancellation if another party misrepresents the source, especially when capitalizing on international brand recognition.

title: Coca-Cola Femsa fortalecerá la distribución de marcas de Heineken en Brasil
summary: Coca-Cola Femsa, el principal embotellador de Coca-Cola en América Latina, ha llegado a un acuerdo con Heineken para rediseñar el sistema de distribución en Brasil, fortaleciendo la presencia de las marcas de cerveza de Heineken en el portafolio de Femsa. Este acuerdo permitirá a Coca-Cola Femsa integrar nuevas marcas como Tiger y expandir su oferta más allá de los productos Coca-Cola. La renovación del acuerdo, que dura hasta 2026 con posibilidad de extensión, también establece que Coca-Cola podrá producir y distribuir bebidas alcohólicas y otras cervezas, complementando el portafolio de Heineken.

title: Coca-Cola to Auction Its First-Ever NFT Collectibles on International Friendship Day
summary: Coca-Cola is launching its first-ever NFT collectibles on International Friendship Day, with all proceeds from the four-day auction on OpenSea going to Special Olympics International. The collection includes a "Friendship Box" containing a custom Coca-Cola Bubble Jacket Wearable, a Sound Visualizer, and a Friendship Card, all inspired by shared moments of friendship and reinterpreted for the metaverse. These multi-sensory NFTs celebrate Coca-Cola's heritage and aim to connect with new audiences in virtual worlds.

title: United Natural Foods, Inc. Names Sandy Douglas as Chief Executive Officer and Jack Stahl as Independent Chair of the Board; Company Leaders Comment
summary: United Natural Foods, Inc. (UNFI) has appointed J. Alexander (Sandy) Miller Douglas as its new Chief Executive Officer and a member of its Board of Directors, effective August 9, following the retirement of former CEO Steven Spinner. Concurrently, Jack Stahl has been elected as the Independent Chair of the Board. Douglas brings extensive leadership experience from Staples and Coca-Cola, while Stahl has served on UNFI's board since 2019 and will now lead as Independent Chair, with Peter Roy stepping down as Lead Director but remaining on the board.

title: UNFI Announces Appointments of Sandy Douglas as Chief Executive Officer and Jack Stahl as Independent Chair of the Board
summary: United Natural Foods, Inc. (UNFI) announced the appointment of J. Alexander (Sandy) Miller Douglas as its new Chief Executive Officer and a member of its Board of Directors, effective August 9, 2021. Douglas, formerly CEO of Staples, Inc. and President of Coca-Cola North America, succeeds Steven Spinner. Concurrently, Jack Stahl was elected as the Independent Chair of the Board, also effective August 9, 2021.

title: Ex-Staples chief Sandy Douglas to become new UNFI CEO
summary: J. Alexander (Sandy) Miller Douglas, former chief executive officer of Staples Inc., is set to become the new CEO of United Natural Foods Inc. (UNFI), succeeding the retiring Steven Spinner. Douglas will begin his role on August 9, with Spinner transitioning to an advisory position. This appointment follows a ten-month search to find a replacement for Spinner, who has led UNFI since 2008 and oversaw the significant acquisition of Supervalu Inc.

title: Former Coca-Cola Exec Appointed as New UNFI CEO
summary: United Natural Foods, Inc. (UNFI) has appointed J. Alexander (Sandy) Miller Douglas, former CEO of Staples and President of Coca-Cola North America, as its new Chief Executive Officer, effective August 9, 2021. Douglas replaces retiring CEO Steven Spinner. Jack Stahl has also been elected Independent Chair of the Board.

title: José Said Saffie: De los textiles a la banca, a la Coca Cola y a los negocios inmobiliarios
summary: This article details the vast and varied business empire of José Said Saffie, tracing his family's origin from textile manufacturing to their current dominance in banking, beverage bottling (Coca-Cola), and real estate through companies like Embotelladora Andina and Parque Arauco. It highlights the Said group's expansion into Latin America, particularly Argentina, and their strategic alliances and investments over several decades, including their involvement with BBVA-BHIF. The article also touches upon the family's historical trajectory, navigating political changes in Chile and adapting their business model to achieve significant financial success.

title: Coca-Cola Beverages Africa and Genpact Partner to Transform Operations to Drive Competitive Growth
summary: Coca-Cola Beverages Africa (CCBA) has partnered with Genpact, a global professional services firm, to streamline its operations and accelerate competitive growth. Genpact will establish a multi-function, digitally enabled shared services organization to centralize and automate CCBA's finance, procurement, and data management, initially focusing on South Africa with plans for expansion. This collaboration aims to improve customer service, enable real-time business decisions, and offer new career opportunities for CCBA employees transferring to Genpact.

title: PepsiCo to sell Tropicana, other juice brands for $3.3 billion
summary: PepsiCo announced the sale of its Tropicana and other North American juice brands to French private equity firm PAI Partners for $3.3 billion. The move aims to simplify PepsiCo's product range, reduce focus on high-sugar drinks, and provide funds for investment in health-focused snacks and zero-calorie beverages. PepsiCo will retain a 39% stake in the new joint venture and exclusive U.S. distribution rights for the brands.

title: PepsiCo exiting juice business
summary: PepsiCo is selling a majority stake in its Tropicana, Naked, and other juice businesses to private equity firm PAI Partners for approximately $3.3 billion, retaining a 39% ownership in a joint venture. This divestment allows PepsiCo to focus on healthier snacks, zero-calorie beverages, and products like SodaStream, aligning with a broader industry trend of major beverage companies streamlining portfolios. The sale also reflects the long-term decline in fruit juice consumption and the evolving role of juice in consumer diets.

title: PepsiCo to sell Tropicana, other juice brands for $3.3B
summary: PepsiCo is selling its Tropicana, Naked, and other juice brands in North America and Europe to private-equity firm PAI Partners for $3.3 billion in pre-tax proceeds. PepsiCo will retain a 39% noncontrolling stake and exclusive distribution rights for chilled direct store delivery. This divestment aims to strengthen PepsiCo's balance sheet and allow it to focus on its core businesses, healthier snacks, and zero-calorie beverages amidst declining juice sales over recent years.

title: Refresco to acquire three production facilities in the US from The Coca-Cola Company
summary: Refresco, the world's largest independent bottler, announced an agreement to acquire three production facilities in the United States from The Coca-Cola Company. This acquisition is subject to regulatory approval and will expand Refresco's manufacturing footprint and technological capabilities in North America. Refresco will also enter into long-term agreements for contract manufacturing activities with Coca-Cola.

title: Inflation is ‘bad for America,’ says Scotts Miracle-Gro CEO
summary: Scotts Miracle-Gro CEO Jim Hagedorn voiced strong frustration over inflation, calling it "bad for America" and highlighting that some commodity pricing is "irresponsible" as companies raise prices simply "because they can." The company's shares dropped to a nine-month low despite beating earnings expectations, as inflationary pressures are expected to negatively impact future profits. Hagedorn warned that these cost pressures, which feel "unrelenting," are detrimental not only to profit margins but also to the broader economy.

title: Refresco Acquires U.S. Bottling Plants from Coca-Cola
summary: Refresco, a Dutch bottling conglomerate, has acquired three U.S. manufacturing facilities from The Coca-Cola Company, including plants in Truesdale, Missouri; Waco, Texas; and Paw Paw, Michigan. These facilities will continue to produce Coca-Cola products under a long-term co-packing agreement. This acquisition expands Refresco's North American presence and aligns with its strategy to grow its branded customer business while maintaining its private label services, serving clients like Pepsi and Monster.

title: Coca-Cola plans to close Northampton plant in 2023; city to lose major employer and revenue source
summary: Coca-Cola announced its plan to close its Northampton bottling facility in late spring 2023, impacting 320 employees and significantly affecting the city's economy. The closure is part of a national restructuring and a deal with manufacturer Refresco. Northampton Mayor David Narkewicz expressed disappointment over the loss of a major employer, taxpayer, and water revenue source.

title: Coca-Cola to shutter bottling plant in 2023; 319 to lose jobs
summary: Coca-Cola announced it would close its bottling plant in Northampton, Massachusetts, in summer 2023, affecting 319 employees. The decision is part of a corporate restructuring linked to expanding into new markets and sustainable packaging. This closure represents a significant economic loss for Northampton, which had invested in and provided tax incentives for the plant over the years.

title: Coca-Cola to close Massachusetts bottling plant in 2023, leaving hundreds jobless
summary: Coca-Cola announced its plans to close a Massachusetts bottling plant in Northampton by summer 2023, impacting 319 employees. This closure is part of a larger corporate restructuring and will result in a significant economic loss for the city, as the plant is its largest manufacturer, water customer, and taxpayer, contributing $306,000 in annual property taxes. The company also plans to sell facilities in Michigan, Missouri, and Texas.

title: Latham Advises Coca-Cola İçecek in US$250 Million Privatization of Uzbek Bottling Business
summary: Latham & Watkins advised Coca-Cola İçecek (CCI) in its successful US$250 million bid to acquire a 57.118% stake in Coca-Cola Bottlers Uzbekistan, Ltd (CCBU) from the State Assets Management Agency of Uzbekistan. The acquisition values 100% of CCBU at US$430 million and is expected to close within two months, pending government and regulatory approvals. CCI is a major multinational beverage company and one of the key bottlers for The Coca-Cola Company.

title: Coca-Cola asks if new Zero Sugar is 'Best Coke Ever?' in multichannel push
summary: Coca-Cola has launched an integrated "Best Coke Ever?" campaign to promote its new Zero Sugar product in the U.S. This multichannel effort spans TV, streaming audio, OOH, digital, social media, and sports sponsorships, inviting consumers to taste and decide if it lives up to the tagline. The campaign follows strong Q2 2021 revenue growth for Coca-Cola and aims to support the new recipe, which has already seen success internationally.

title: PepsiCo to launch Mountain Dew-branded alcoholic drinks in 2022
summary: PepsiCo is set to release an alcoholic Mountain Dew beverage called "Hard Mtn Dew" in the U.S. early next year, following Coca-Cola's entry into the alcoholic drinks market. Boston Beer Co, known for Truly hard seltzer, will produce the citrus-flavored malt beverage, which will have a 5% alcohol by volume. This move comes as adult drinkers' preferences are evolving, despite a recent slowdown in hard seltzer demand.

title: Mountain Dew goes hard as PepsiCo, Boston Beer partner on a boozy version
summary: PepsiCo and Boston Beer Co. are partnering to launch Hard Mtn Dew, an alcoholic version of the popular soft drink, in early 2022. This collaboration aims to tap into evolving consumer tastes for low-calorie alcoholic beverages. The new drink will contain 5% alcohol by volume, feature flavors like black cherry and watermelon, and will be caffeine and sugar-free.

title: Coca-Cola closing pair of bottling plants affecting nearly 500 workers
summary: Coca-Cola plans to close two bottling plants in California and Massachusetts by 2023, impacting nearly 500 workers. These closures are part of the company's "asset right" strategy to streamline operations and focus on growing brands as consumer tastes evolve, building on earlier efforts to cut jobs and divest underperforming brands. The move highlights Coca-Cola's ongoing restructuring amidst evolving consumer habits and a broader labor shortage.

title: Coca-Cola Femsa adquiere la cerveza brasileña Therezópolis
summary: Coca-Cola Femsa is acquiring the Brazilian craft beer brand Therezópolis to complement its beer portfolio in the Brazilian market. The acquisition, made in conjunction with its subsidiary Coca-Cola Andina, is awaiting regulatory approval and is part of a strategy to expand its beverage offerings without becoming a beer producer. This move also aligns with their renewed distribution agreement with Heineken in Brazil.

title: Detroit Coca-Cola plant closing in October, moving to Grand Rapids
summary: The Coca-Cola plant in Detroit is scheduled to close in October 2021, resulting in approximately 135 job losses as operations move to Grand Rapids. Great Lakes Coca-Cola cited the Detroit facililty's age and issues, alongside the Grand Rapids facility's readiness, as reasons for the consolidation. Teamsters Local 337 is actively opposing the move, noting that the city of Detroit has offered incentives for the company to stay.

title: Aluminum can shortage holds back Monster
summary: Monster Beverage Corp. experienced a decrease in net income during the third quarter of 2021, reporting $337.21 million, down 3.1% from the previous year, despite a 13% increase in net sales to $1.41 billion. The company attributed these financial results primarily to an ongoing aluminum can shortage, compounded by freight inefficiencies, shipping container shortages, and port congestion. Monster also noted a favorable impact from foreign currency exchange rates on its net sales and successfully launched its True North Pure Energy Seltzer line.

title: Coca Cola HBC seals Egypt deal after first-half profit jump
summary: Coca Cola HBC agreed to acquire a majority stake in Coca-Cola Bottling Company of Egypt for $427 million following a significant rise in its first-half comparable operating profit. Despite expecting lower operating profit margins in the second half of the year due to rising cost inflation, the company anticipates overall annual margin expansion. Analysts, however, expressed concerns about upside risk to FY22 margin expectations given continued high raw material costs.

title: Vita Coco parent enters new functional beverage segment with Pwr Lift protein water
summary: Vita Coco's parent company, All Market, has launched Pwr Lift, a new line of protein-infused waters, expanding its presence in the functional beverage market. The drinks, available in four flavors on Amazon, contain 10 grams of whey protein, B vitamins, and electrolytes, and are marketed as post-workout recovery beverages. This move comes as All Market prepares for a potential IPO, aiming to compete in a growing but competitive functional beverage sector.

title: Beer Sectoral Group (BSG) names Baker Magunda as Chairman
summary: The Beer Sectoral Group (BSG) of the Manufacturers Association of Nigeria (MAN) has appointed Baker Magunda as its new Chairman, effective August 1, 2021. Magunda, who is currently the Managing Director/CEO of Guinness Nigeria Plc, replaces Jordi Borrut Bel. The BSG includes major Nigerian beer manufacturers such as Nigerian Breweries Plc, Guinness Nigeria Plc, and International Breweries Plc.

title: Procter & Gamble regains its title as top global advertiser
summary: Procter & Gamble has reclaimed its position as the world's top advertiser, surpassing Amazon, with a marketing expenditure of $11.5 billion in its last fiscal year. This resurgence highlights the CPG giant's strategy of maintaining ad spending even during difficult economic times, a move that brand consultants argue has consistently benefited the company. While Amazon has the capacity to increase its ad spending significantly, P&G's continued investment in marketing has proven effective in sustaining its brand presence and sales growth.

title: PepsiCo Announces "Net Water Positive" Commitment
summary: PepsiCo has announced its ambition to become "Net Water Positive" by 2030, aiming to replenish more water than it uses, particularly in high-risk watersheds. This commitment includes reducing water usage in its operations and expanding The PepsiCo Foundation's safe water access program with a $1 million investment in Sub-Saharan Africa. The initiative, in partnership with WaterAid, seeks to provide safe water to 100 million people by 2030 and addresses critical needs exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Los Angeles Lakers Sign BioSteel as Sports Drink Sponsor
summary: The Los Angeles Lakers have signed a multi-year partnership with hydration brand BioSteel, making it the official sports drink of the team. This deal marks BioSteel as the fifth NBA team sponsor since 2020, as the company aims to become a top-tier sports drink brand in the U.S. Their strategy involves leveraging NBA team and player sponsorships, supported by a majority stake from Canopy Growth and a distribution network from Constellation Brands.

title: Keurig Dr Pepper launches Pepper Perks loyalty program
summary: Keurig Dr Pepper launched the Pepper Perks loyalty program for its Dr Pepper brand, allowing fans to earn points by scanning receipts of purchases for rewards like limited-edition flavors and merchandise. This initiative aims to strengthen brand loyalty and provides an opportunity to test new flavors, following similar successful strategies by competitors like Coca-Cola and Pepsi. The move capitalizes on the growing preference for loyalty programs among consumers and the soda category's young core customer base.

title: Embotelladoras de Coca-Cola en Chile suscriben contrato para distribuir marcas de Viña Santa Rita
summary: Coca-Cola Embonor S.A., its subsidiary Embotelladora Iquique S.A., and Embotelladora Andina S.A. have signed a five-year distribution agreement with Viña Santa Rita in Chile. This contract, effective November 2nd, will cover the sale, commercialization, and distribution of Viña Santa Rita's wines, sparkling wines, and wine cocktails, including brands like Casa Real, Medalla Real, Carmen, Santa Rita, 120, and Terra Andina. The agreement strengthens Coca-Cola Embonor's alcohol beverage portfolio and enhances Viña Santa Rita's market access and product availability.

title: Always Coca-Cola: Coca-Cola tops soft drinks brand rankings
summary: Coca-Cola maintains its position as the world's most valuable and strongest soft drink brand despite a 13% decline in brand value, according to Brand Finance. While Coca-Cola and most soft drink brands saw an overall decline in value due to COVID-19 impacts, Dr Pepper and Red Bull emerged as the fastest-growing brands. The report highlights that the soft drinks sector was the most severely affected among food and drink categories, though recovery is expected for strong brands.

title: Refresqueras y cerveceras: ¿en alerta por la sequía en México?
summary: Mexico's upcoming severe drought, as declared by Conagua, poses a significant threat to beverage companies like Coca-Cola Femsa, Arca Continental, Grupo Modelo, and Heineken. These companies rely heavily on water for production and sanitation, and while they have water management programs, Moody's predicts increased capital expenditure will be necessary. Analysts suggest that bottlers, especially Coca-Cola Femsa, might face production cuts and distribution challenges, though beer companies could be less affected due to strategic plant locations and existing water conservation efforts.

title: The Difference Between LaCroix and Topo Chico, Explained
summary: This article explains the key differences between two popular sparkling water brands, LaCroix and Topo Chico. It covers their origins, production methods, flavor offerings, and how they are used in cocktails, highlighting what makes each brand unique and contribute to their market success.

title: The 2021 Top 100 Food and Beverage Companies
summary: Food Engineering's 2021 Top 100 Food and Beverage Companies report shows a significant reshuffling, with PepsiCo claiming the top spot from Nestlé due to substantial revenue growth. The impact of the 2020 pandemic, including supply chain challenges and shifts in consumer demand, heavily influenced the rankings, causing movements within the top 10 and highlighting strong performances in dairy and energy drink sectors. The article details adjustments made by major companies like JBS, Anheuser-Busch InBev, ADM, and Coca-Cola, while also recognizing infrastructure investments and sustainability efforts made by companies like Keurig Dr Pepper and The JM Smucker Company.

title: Top 100 Food and Beverage Company Highlights: #8 The Coca-Cola Company
summary: The Coca-Cola Company saw significant net revenue acceleration by 42% in Q2, driven by pandemic recovery, posting $10.1 billion with 26% growth in concentrate sales. The company is undergoing a global restructuring effort, including job cuts and streamlined operations into nine units and five global categories. Recent activities include the sale of US production facilities, intent to acquire Bodyarmor, increased takeover offers for Coca-Cola Amatil, and investments in cultured milk products, alongside product launches and discontinuation.

title: Energy Traders See Big Money in Carbon-Emissions Markets
summary: Large energy trading firms, including Vitol and Glencore, are expanding their carbon-emissions trading operations, following the lead of major oil companies like Shell and BP. This shift is driven by global governmental efforts to grow the market for trading carbon emissions. Companies that exceed their emission allowances can purchase more, while those below their limits can sell their excess credits.

title: Coca-Cola Sets the Course for Multicultural Marketing and Supplier Diversity
summary: Coca-Cola is enhancing its multicultural marketing and supplier diversity strategies in response to the growing diversity of the U.S. population. The company appointed Henry Hendrix as VP of Multicultural Marketing Strategy and Engagement and Fernando Henriquez as VP of Supplier Diversity, aiming to almost double marketing spending in minority-owned media over the next three years. This initiative also includes expanding supplier diversity programs globally and fostering partnerships with organizations like the U.S. Hispanic Chamber of Commerce to support minority businesses.

title: Brexit driver crisis leaves Coca-Cola with aluminium cans shortage
summary: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners (CCEP) is experiencing a shortage of aluminium cans due to the UK's HGV driver crisis, a problem exacerbated by Brexit and the pandemic. Despite these logistics challenges, the company reports high service levels and increased profits, while other businesses like Wetherspoon also face supply issues. The Road Haulage Association estimates a shortage of over 100,000 drivers.

title: EXCLUSIVE Amazon considers more proactive approach to determining what belongs on its cloud service
summary: Amazon is reportedly planning to adopt a more proactive strategy to identify and remove content on its Amazon Web Services (AWS) cloud platform that violates its policies, such as those against promoting violence. This initiative involves expanding the Trust & Safety team and hiring specialists to monitor for emerging threats. While an AWS spokesperson initially denied changes and stated the existing team already handles abusive content, the move suggests a potential shift towards greater content arbitration by the leading cloud provider, raising free speech debates.

title: Nippon Paper and Coca-Cola Japan Sign Memorandum of Understanding on Collaboration for Building a Sustainable Society
summary: Nippon Paper Industries Co., Ltd. and Coca-Cola (Japan) Co., Ltd. have signed a memorandum of understanding to collaborate on building a sustainable society. This expanded agreement, following a previous one from 2013-2021, will focus on three key areas: Resources (resource recycling and conservation), Communities (community development), and Inclusion (respect for diversity) over the next decade. The collaboration aims to leverage both companies' expertise to address social challenges related to sustainability.

title: PNC Announces Amanda Rosseter As Chief Communications Officer
summary: PNC Financial Services Group, Inc. announced Amanda Rosseter has joined the company as chief communications officer, bringing nearly three decades of experience from roles at Equifax and The Coca-Cola Company. In her new role, Rosseter will lead strategic external and internal communications, overseeing media relations, corporate responsibility, and executive communications, as PNC executes its national expansion strategy. Kristen Baird Adams, who previously served as interim chief communications officer, will return as chief of staff to PNC's Office of Regional Presidents.

title: BlackRock Partners With the Thurgood Marshall College Fund to Benefit Students at Historically Black Colleges and Universities
summary: BlackRock has partnered with the Thurgood Marshall College Fund (TMCF) to support students at Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs) and Predominantly Black Institutions (PBIs). BlackRock will make an annual contribution to TMCF, derived from a portion of the net revenue from its BlackRock Liquid Federal Trust Fund (BLFT), a socially aware government money market fund. This initiative aims to provide financial support, leadership guidance, and career development opportunities, particularly through partnerships with diverse broker-dealers, to enhance socioeconomic mobility for minority students and strengthen minority-owned businesses.

title: Topo Chico Is Well Sourced to Win the Seltzer Wars
summary: Topo Chico, a sparkling water brand originating from Monterrey, Mexico, has seen significant growth in popularity across the U.S. This rapid expansion is largely due to its acquisition by The Coca-Cola Company in 2017, which broadened its distribution. Sales have surged, with a 39 percent increase in one 12-month period, demonstrating Coca-Cola's strategic investment in trending beverage brands.

title: Coca-Cola takes flexible approach to navigate COVID-19
summary: The Coca-Cola Co. is adopting a flexible and adaptive strategy to navigate the ongoing impacts of COVID-19, leveraging its strong brands and balance sheet. This approach involves scaling operations selectively in regional markets and aligning marketing agendas with local conditions, while also streamlining internal functions for greater agility. The company is focusing on maintaining relevance to consumers and customers globally by balancing scale with intimacy in local markets.

title: Noticia CCB | Ruta tenderos: Formación a 1.000 pequeños comerciantes en Bogotá para fortalecer sus negocios
summary: The Coca-Cola System and the Bogotá Chamber of Commerce have launched "Ruta Tenderos," an initiative to strengthen traditional small shops in Bogotá. The project will provide training and digital integration support to 1,000 small business owners, focusing on areas like accounting, customer service, inventory management, and electronic payments. This effort aims to foster economic and social sustainability by helping these businesses innovate and contribute to the country's economic reactivation post-pandemic.

title: 7 US stocks to buy on a dip
summary: This article identifies seven U.S. stocks with "wide economic moats" and "low uncertainty ratings" that Morningstar analysts recommend adding to a watchlist for potential dips, despite being fairly valued at the time of writing. The article highlights Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) and PepsiCo (PEP) as examples, detailing their diverse revenue bases, strong cash flow generation, and strategic initiatives that contribute to their competitive advantages. The author encourages investors to use this list to be "prepared" for market pullbacks, aligning with the "Be Prepared" motto.

title: 5 ways The Coca-Cola Company is reimagining its marketing strategies
summary: The Coca-Cola Company is revamping its marketing strategies focusing on five key areas to improve efficiency and effectiveness. These strategies include prioritizing the attraction of new consumers, implementing rigorous measurement of campaign results, and identifying and eliminating underperforming campaigns. Additionally, the company aims to align distribution capabilities with marketing ambitions and enforce strict discipline in its marketing practices across global brands.

title: Paris Nikolopoulos, General Manager of Coca-Cola Romania
summary: Paris Nikolopoulos, General Manager of Coca-Cola Romania, emphasizes continuous learning ("weiterbildung") as a key to his success, particularly in adapting to new cultures during his international career with Coca-Cola. He focuses on a five-pillar strategy for Coca-Cola Romania, including prioritizing brands, disciplined innovation, boosting market reach, enhancing marketing, and evolving supplier partnerships, all while promoting sustainability and highlighting the importance of the local team. Nikolopoulos asserts that the real "secret formula" for Coca-Cola Romania lies in its passionate and connected people, rather than just the well-known brand.

title: Pepsi pledges to halve unrecycled plastic in packaging by 2030
summary: PepsiCo has announced new sustainability goals under its "pep+" initiative, aiming to halve its use of "virgin" plastic and increase recycled content in its packaging by 2030. This move responds to growing consumer demand for sustainable products, particularly from younger generations. The initiative faces challenges related to recycling infrastructure and cost, which Pepsi must balance against the risk of losing environmentally conscious customers.

title: Lawyer Limelight: Michael Holmes
summary: This article profiles Michael Holmes, a prominent trial lawyer at Vinson & Elkins, detailing his journey from a summer associate inspired by the courtroom to co-head of the firm's Complex Commercial Litigation practice and Vice-Chair Elect. It highlights his significant legal victories, including the Huntsman/Hexion merger and the Energy Transfer acquisition of Williams, and touches on his upcoming role in the firm's new leadership structure. Holmes's dedication to his craft, his mentors, and the collaborative team environment at Vinson & Elkins are emphasized throughout the piece.

title: PepsiCo to reduce plastic use, launch plant-based snacks in green push
summary: PepsiCo is launching a new initiative called "pep+" to reduce its virgin plastic use by half by 2030 and incorporate 50% recycled content in all plastic packaging. The company also plans to introduce plant-based protein snacks in partnership with Beyond Meat, with initial products expected in early 2022. These moves come amidst increasing pressure from environmental groups regarding the food and beverage giant's plastic waste generation, although some activists argue PepsiCo still needs to do more.

title: Coffee Holding purchases $2.5M investment in plant-based protein drink
summary: Coffee Holding Co. Inc. has invested $2.5 million in OWYN (Only What You Need), a manufacturer of plant-based protein drinks. This investment aims to capitalize on OWYN's significant growth in the ready-to-drink and plant-based beverage markets, as stated by Coffee Holding President and CEO Andrew Gordon. OWYN products are currently sold in approximately 20,000 locations.

title: Danone’s Evian partners with Loop on water bottle made with recycled plastic
summary: Danone's Evian brand is rolling out a new prototype water bottle made from 100% recycled PET using technology from Loop Industries. This initiative is a major step towards Evian's goal of using all recycled plastic in its bottles by 2025 and aims to repurpose PET waste that would otherwise be discarded. The technology allows diverse plastic waste to be transformed into food-grade plastic, with commercial rollout starting in South Korea in 2022.

title: Judge tosses Greenpeace suit over Walmart recyclable labeling
summary: A federal judge in San Francisco dismissed Greenpeace's lawsuit against Walmart Inc. over its labeling of house-brand plastic products as "recyclable." The judge ruled that Greenpeace lacked the necessary standing to bring the claims under California's Unfair Competition Law, but gave the environmental group until October 15 to file an amended complaint. This case is part of a broader trend of lawsuits alleging deceptive recyclable labeling on single-use plastic products.

title: Coca-Cola Femsa emite 4,900 mdp en bonos de sustentabilidad
summary: Coca-Cola FEMSA (KOF) has issued 9,400 million pesos (approximately $470 million) in sustainability-linked bonds in the local market to refinance debt. The company commits to reducing its water usage in beverage production from 1.49 liters per liter of beverage to 1.36 liters by 2024 and 1.26 liters by 2026. Failure to meet these sustainability targets will result in a 25 basis point increase in interest rates on the bonds.

title: U.S. BANK STADIUM PREVIEWS NEW FOOD AND BEVERAGE OFFERINGS AHEAD OF THE 2021 VIKINGS SEASON
summary: U.S. Bank Stadium is rolling out a completely re-imagined food and beverage program for the 2021 Vikings season, featuring new menu items, various beverage options, and partnerships with numerous local Twin Cities vendors. The upgrade focuses on elevating core food offerings while introducing new technology elements like self-checkout markets and a cashless payment system. Additionally, new partnerships with Pothole Pizza, Vizzy Hard Seltzer, Miller Lite, Absolut, and Crown Royal will enhance the fan experience.

title: PepsiCo (PEP) vs. Coca-Cola (KO): Which soft drink giant is a better investment?
summary: This article compares PepsiCo (PEP) and Coca-Cola (KO) as investment options, highlighting their similarities in broad product portfolios and high-yield dividends. It discusses how both companies navigated the COVID-19 pandemic, their entry into alcoholic beverages, and their dividend policies. The analysis also covers their Q2 2021 financial performance and stock market trajectory, concluding that PepsiCo might offer better value due to its stronger position.

title: An unprecedented supply chain disruption forces food and beverage manufacturers to pivot
summary: The food and beverage manufacturing sector faced significant supply chain disruptions during the pandemic, forcing companies like Smucker Foods, Maple Leaf Foods, and Coca-Cola Canada Bottling to adapt. These companies pivoted by sourcing alternative materials, leveraging strong supplier relationships, implementing new safety protocols, and adjusting product offerings to mitigate shortages and meet surging consumer demand. Legal departments played a crucial role in supporting these changes through contract negotiations, risk mitigation, and strategic planning for future challenges.

title: Yum! Brands appoints Sabir Sami as global division CEO of KFC
summary: Yum! Brands has appointed Sabir Sami as the global division chief executive officer of KFC, effective January 1, 2022. Sami, previously KFC Asia managing director, will be responsible for driving KFC's global brand strategy and performance, succeeding Tony Lowings. His experience in leading KFC Asia's high-growth region, particularly India, positions him well for this new role at Yum!'s largest brand.

title: Ball Corp. plans $290M factory investment amid increasing can demand
summary: Ball Corp. announced a $290 million investment in a new beverage can factory, driven by booming demand for aluminum cans. This move is part of the company's continuous expansion efforts over the past year, establishing new manufacturing locations to meet market needs.

title: Ball Corporation investing $290M in new aluminum can plant in Nevada
summary: Ball Corporation is investing $290 million in a new aluminum beverage packaging plant in Las Vegas to address the ongoing shortage of aluminum cans. This facility, scheduled to begin production in late 2022, will create 180 jobs and help meet the increasing demand from beverage companies transitioning to aluminum packaging. The company anticipates that demand will continue to outstrip supply well into 2023, and this new plant, along with other production increases, aims to alleviate the supply chain pressure.

title: Vita Coco Is Moving Toward a $100 Million IPO, Date and Price to Come
summary: Vita Coco, owned by All Market Brands, has filed for a $100 million IPO on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol "COCO." The company, known as the top coconut-water supplier, is converting to a Public Benefit Corporation and reported $334 million in sales for the 12 months ending June 30, 2021. The IPO aims to capitalize on the growing plant-based beverage market.

title: What domains Coca-Cola and other end users bought
summary: This article details recent domain name sales to end-users on Sedo, highlighting Coca-Cola's purchase of LemonDou.com for a hard seltzer beverage. It also notes a continued trend of NFT and blockchain-related businesses acquiring domain names, with NFTchain.com selling for $88,000 as the top sale. The piece lists several other companies and their domain acquisitions, covering various industries from solar power to healthcare.

title: El Pollo Loco Hears the Call for the Crunch and Celebrates National Taco Day with the Return of the Crunchy Taco
summary: El Pollo Loco is bringing back its popular Crunchy Taco as a digital-only menu item from October 4 through November 1, in anticipation of National Taco Day. To celebrate, every Crunchy Taco order on National Taco Day will include a free Mexican Coke, and Loco Rewards members will receive a buy-one-get-one-free offer. This return is a response to customer demand and marks the company's first digital-exclusive menu offering.

title: Rethinking Sustainable Packaging and Innovation in the Beverage Industry
summary: This article discusses the Coca-Cola Company's sustainable packaging initiative, "World Without Waste," and its efforts to reduce plastic waste in the beverage industry. Raoni Lotar, Frontline Marketing Director, details goals to make packaging 100% recyclable by 2025 and use 50% recycled material by 2030, alongside efforts in collection and partnerships. The company highlights innovations like label-less bottles and the importance of collaborative events like ReThink in achieving sustainability targets.

title: The Coca-Cola Company Unveils New Global Brand Platform for Coca-Cola Trademark
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has launched "Real Magic," a new global brand philosophy and platform, refreshing its trademark promise to unite and uplift people. This marks the first new global platform since 2016 and introduces a refreshed visual identity, including the "Hug" logo. The platform kicks off with the "One Coke Away From Each Other" campaign, blending real and virtual worlds and featuring collaborations with gamers and artists.

title: Cola-Cola hopes ‘Real Magic’ campaign casts right spell for a global turnaround
summary: Coca-Cola has launched its first global campaign in five years, "Real Magic," aiming to boost sales and reverse its fortunes after a challenging period and major restructuring. The campaign targets Gen Z with a tech-focused approach, prominently featuring gaming and partnerships with influencers like Twitch. This initiative comes as the company navigates an agency consolidation review and seeks to regain market share from competitors like PepsiCo.

title: Coca-Cola scores highest on sustainable packaging, but most CPGs fall short, report says
summary: A report by nonprofit As You Sow graded 50 consumer-facing companies on their packaging sustainability, with Coca-Cola receiving the highest score of "B" for its transparency, recycling commitments, and support for producer responsibility. Many other food and beverage companies, including Keurig Dr Pepper and Nestlé, scored lower, with eight receiving an "F." While companies have made increased pledges for 100% recyclable, compostable, or reusable packaging by 2025, the report highlights the need for more significant action and financial investment in recycling infrastructure.

title: ‘Real magic’: Coca-Cola launches new global brand philosophy
summary: Coca-Cola has launched a new global brand platform called 'Real Magic', replacing its previous platform from 2016. This initiative aims to refresh the brand's commitment to uniting and uplifting people by acknowledging the unexpected moments that create magic in a "virtual and divided world." The launch includes a new visual identity, a new "hug" logo, and a campaign titled "One Coke Away From Each Other," developed with BETC London, Daniel Wolfe, and Mathematic.

title: Embotelladoras de Coca-Cola en Chile distribuirán bebidas alcohólicas
summary: Coca-Cola Embonor and Embotelladora Andina have signed a distribution agreement with Viña Santa Rita to sell and distribute wines, sparkling wines, and wine cocktails in Chile. This move is part of Coca-Cola Embonor's diversification strategy to include alcoholic beverages, with an anticipated increase in sales of 28 million liters, equivalent to $32.3 million. The agreement is also expected to enhance their competitiveness against Compañía Cerveceras Unidas (CCU) in the Chilean market.

title: Where AB-InBev, Molson Coors, Diageo rank in the Corporate Plastic Pollution Scorecard
summary: As You Sow released its "Corporate Plastic Pollution Scorecard 2021," evaluating 50 major U.S. consumer companies on their efforts to reduce plastic pollution. The report highlights progress in virgin plastic reduction commitments but notes that no companies have sufficiently robust policies given the urgency of the crisis. Coca-Cola received the highest grade with transparency and strong recycling commitments, while adult beverage companies like Diageo, Molson Coors, and AB InBev received lower scores, indicating significant room for improvement, particularly in recycling support and packaging design.

title: id2021finalwebversion101.htm
summary: Keurig Dr Pepper (KDP) held its 2021 Investor Day to highlight its transformation into a modern beverage company, emphasizing its strong financial model, sustainable growth, and significant M&A capacity. The company aims for mid-single digit net sales growth and high-single digit adjusted EPS growth in the long term, supported by industry-leading cash conversion and a scalable business model. KDP also detailed its strong ESG commitments, robust go-to-market strategy, and an expanded capital allocation plan that now includes inorganic options like share buybacks.

title: The Coca-Cola Company Unveils New Global Brand Platform for Coca-Cola Trademark
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has launched a new global brand philosophy and platform called "Real Magic," refreshing its trademark promise to unite and uplift people. This platform, the first since 2016, introduces a refreshed visual identity, including the "Hug" logo, and launches with the "One Coke Away From Each Other" campaign, blending real and virtual worlds. The campaign involves collaborations with artists, gamers like DJ Alan Walker, and partners like Twitch, seeking to engage audiences through unique and ownable experiences.

title: Coca-Cola Global Brand Refresh Focuses on Consumer Experience
summary: Coca-Cola has launched a new 'Real Magic' brand platform, including a refreshed visual identity and global campaign, to celebrate humanity and create a movement towards a more human way of doing things. This marks the first update to its global platform for the Coke Trademark in five years and aims to significantly increase the consumer base through an ecosystem of experiences tied to consumption occasions and consumer passion points like gaming. The campaign features a new "Hug" logo and an integrated approach blending real and virtual worlds, exemplified by the "One Coke Away From Each Other" campaign that includes celebrity gamers and a code hunt for prizes.

title: Press Clips: A-B Considers $1.2 Billion Sale of German Brands; Molson Coors Rolls Out Topo Chico Margarita Hard Seltzer Variety Pack
summary: Anheuser-Busch InBev is reportedly exploring a $1.2 billion sale of some of its German beer brands as it shifts focus to "beyond beer" products. Concurrently, Molson Coors is launching a Topo Chico Margarita Hard Seltzer variety pack and aims for a 10% share of the hard seltzer market by the end of 2021. The article also touches on a decline in hard seltzer purchasing contracts and new partnerships in the beverage industry.

title: Coca-Cola thinks ‘outside the box,’ books bulk vessels to ship supplies
summary: Coca-Cola is utilizing bulk vessels to transport materials, a non-traditional approach to navigate limited vessel space and keep production lines running globally. This strategy, adopted by other retailers facing supply chain congestion, involves carrying over 60,000 tons of material to non-congested ports to avoid delays and high demurrage fees. While individual company actions may not shift market dynamics, this move highlights the significant impact and overstretched state of current logistics.

title: Top Women in Convenience Awards Gala Honors Change Champions
summary: The 2021 Top Women in Convenience (TWIC) Awards Gala celebrated 74 outstanding women from the convenience store industry, including five Women of the Year. Held in Chicago, the event highlighted themes of resilience, leadership, and the importance of mentorship, particularly for women in historically male-dominated fields. Honorees shared personal reflections on their careers, the impact of COVID-19 on women, and the ongoing progress and challenges in achieving gender equality within the industry.

title: The Coca-Cola Company unveils fresh brand platform for Coca-Cola trademark
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has launched a new global brand platform called "Real Magic" with a refreshed visual identity and logo. This platform aims to celebrate humanity and unite people, building on lessons from the past 18 months, and will be supported by a new campaign blending real and virtual worlds, featuring gamers and interactive elements. The initiative marks the first new global brand platform for Coca-Cola since 2016.

title: Coca-Cola Is Launching This for the First Time in Half a Decade
summary: Coca-Cola is launching a new brand campaign called "Real Magic," featuring a new logo and tagline, for the first time in five years. This rebrand comes amidst declining sales for Classic Coke and the discontinuation of underperforming brands as the company adapts to changing consumer preferences and addresses past criticisms. The campaign aims to connect with a younger, more health-conscious demographic that demands new approaches from the beverage giant.

title: The Coca-Cola Company Announces ESG Presentation for Investors
summary: The Coca-Cola Company announced an upcoming webcast for investors on November 3 at 11 a.m. ET to discuss its environmental, social, and governance (ESG) priorities. Bea Perez and Henrique Braun, along with other company leaders, will lead the discussion and a moderated Q&A session. Investors are invited to join the webcast and can review the company's latest Business & ESG Report in advance.

title: Net Zero by 2040
summary: Coca-Cola HBC aims to achieve Net Zero emissions across its entire value chain by 2040, having already reduced direct emissions by 58% and total value chain emissions by a third since 2010. The company's strategy involves significant reductions in direct emissions and collaborative efforts with suppliers to address indirect scope 3 emissions. This commitment is supported by science-based targets validated by SBTi, including renewed climate targets for 2030 and 2040, and targets for Forest, Land and Agriculture (FLAG) emissions.

title: Innovation and Trust: Imperatives in the Emerging Relationship Between Banks & VASPs
summary: The article discusses the growing collaboration between traditional banks and Virtual Asset Service Providers (VASPs) due to the booming cryptocurrency market. It highlights the opportunities for banks to offer new financial products and services while emphasizing the need for thorough due diligence when partnering with VASPs, given the evolving regulatory landscape. The author advises banks to assess a VASP's risk assessment, regulatory compliance, and governance to ensure a successful and secure partnership in the digital asset space.

title: Irish businessman and TV presenter Sir Gerry Robinson dies aged 72
summary: Sir Gerry Robinson, the Donegal-born businessman and television presenter known for his work with Matchbox Toys, Coca-Cola, and Granada Television, has died at the age of 72. He gained public recognition for fronting BBC shows like 'I'll Show Them Who's Boss' and 'Can Gerry Robinson Fix the NHS?', where he advised struggling businesses and hospitals. Knighted in 2004, he had returned to his home county of Donegal in 1996.

title: Coca-Cola FEMSA alerta sobre nueva estafa en supuestas ofertas laborales
summary: Coca-Cola FEMSA has issued a warning regarding a new scam involving fake job offers that solicit banking information from unsuspecting individuals. The company clarifies that all recruitment processes are conducted solely through official channels and that sensitive financial data is never requested via phone calls or unofficial means. Interested applicants are directed to the official careers website, careers.femsa.com/KOF, to apply for positions and receive employment information.

title: Coca-Cola and PepsiCo wade into booze amid an uncertain future
summary: Coca-Cola and PepsiCo are cautiously entering the alcohol market through partnerships, aiming to learn about the category before fully committing. This move is driven by the search for new growth avenues and higher profit margins, leveraging partners' expertise in the complex alcohol distribution system. Both companies are also subtly exploring potential future ventures into the cannabis market if regulations permit.

title: Birmingham’s Coca-Cola Bottling Company United’s production team wins coveted President’s Award for Quality Excellence
summary: The New Orleans Coca-Cola Production Center, a facility of Birmingham's Coca-Cola Bottling Company United, Inc., has won the prestigious President's Award for Quality Excellence from The Coca-Cola Company. The facility was recognized for its best-in-class performance in reducing consumer complaints and its commitment to quality, even amidst challenges like Hurricane Ida. This achievement highlights the team's resilience and dedication to the company's core values.

title: Pricier shipping containers and port delays haven't slowed Vita Coco's growth, co-CEO says
summary: Vita Coco, despite supply chain challenges and port delays, has continued to grow its business substantially, according to co-founder and co-CEO Mike Kirban. The company went public on Nasdaq under the symbol "COCO," raising $173 million with an initial offering price of $15 per share, although shares fell nearly 4% in afternoon trading. Vita Coco's strong long-term contracts with coconut manufacturers have helped it avoid higher commodity costs, a key differentiator from competitors.

title: Exclusive: Coca-Cola unveils prototype bottle made from 100% plant-based sources
summary: Coca-Cola has revealed a prototype bottle made entirely from 100% plant-based plastic (bPET), a significant step towards reducing dependence on oil-based PET. This innovation leverages commercially scalable technologies and is part of Coca-Cola's broader ambition to achieve net-zero carbon emissions by 2050, aiming to use three million tonnes less virgin plastic from oil sources by 2025. The company plans to eliminate oil-based virgin PET from plastic bottles in Europe and Japan by 2030, relying on recycled and renewable materials.

title: The Coca-Cola Company and PepsiCo named top plastic polluters for the fourth year in a row
summary: For the fourth consecutive year, The Coca-Cola Company and PepsiCo have been identified as the world's leading plastic polluters by Break Free From Plastic's annual Brand Audit. The report also highlights Unilever rising to become the third-worst polluter, drawing criticism given its role as a principal partner for COP26. The audit, based on global volunteer cleanups, underscores that these corporations' voluntary commitments are having minimal impact and calls for governments to implement policies to reduce plastic production and hold producers accountable.

title: Kraft Heinz CEO: Miguel Patricio Biography
summary: This article provides a biography of Miguel Patricio, the CEO of Kraft Heinz, detailing his career progression from various global CPG companies, through his significant tenure at AB InBev where he focused on marketing and growing the Asia Pacific region, to his current role leading Kraft Heinz's transformation. It highlights his strategies for premiumization, marketing innovation, and fostering creativity to drive growth, along with recent financial performance and strategic asset divestitures under his leadership.

title: Coca-Cola CEO expects to see sporadic product shortages through 2022
summary: Coca-Cola CEO James Quincey anticipates sporadic product shortages to continue through 2022 due to ongoing supply chain challenges and higher inflation. Despite these issues, Coke's earnings and revenue surpassed Wall Street estimates, leading to a 2% rise in share price and an updated fiscal 2021 forecast. Quincey likened the situation to an earthquake with diminishing aftershocks, acknowledging some persistent structural issues.

title: Coca-Cola raises profit forecast as strong soda sales counter cost pressures
summary: Coca-Cola Co raised its full-year profit forecast, driven by higher prices and strong global demand for its sodas. Despite anticipating continued strong demand, CFO John Murphy acknowledged that the company is not immune to cost inflation in 2022 or potential business impacts from new COVID-19 lockdowns. Coca-Cola plans to increase marketing expenditure and prices to navigate these potential challenges.

title: These 10 Stocks Make Up 87% of Warren Buffett's Portfolio
summary: This article details the top 10 stock holdings in Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway portfolio, which collectively account for 87% of its $329.7 billion valuation. It highlights Buffett's belief that diversification isn't essential if one knows their investments well. The individual stocks, including Apple, Bank of America, and Coca-Cola, are discussed with brief explanations for their inclusion and performance.

title: Despite higher prices, McDonald’s, Kraft Heinz and Coca-Cola post solid earnings.
summary: Despite consumers facing higher prices due to supply chain delays and labor shortages, McDonald's, Kraft Heinz, and Coca-Cola all reported better-than-expected quarterly earnings. Their large scale and ability to pass on cost increases to consumers helped them maintain profitability. While some businesses like Kraft Heinz saw a slight decrease in net sales, all three companies demonstrated resilience in a challenging economic environment.

title: Big brands are world’s top plastic polluters for the fourth time
summary: A new study by Break Free from Plastic revealed that major brands like Coca-Cola, PepsiCo, Unilever, Nestlé, and P&G are the world's top corporate plastic polluters for the fourth consecutive year. The report, based on audits conducted by volunteers in 45 countries, highlights the continued failure of these companies to adopt sustainable practices despite the climate crisis and the pandemic. Environmental groups are urging lawmakers to pass single-use plastic bans and hold these corporations accountable for their environmental impact.

title: Coca-Cola nearly doubled its advertising this year
summary: Coca-Cola significantly increased its advertising budget this year, nearly doubling it from a year ago. Experts suggest this is a strategic move to maintain "top of mind" awareness among consumers, even for established brands, especially after cutting costs at the pandemic's outset. This advertising also helps combat inflation by allowing price increases while retaining loyal customers.

title: New York pension fund joins exit from Unilever over Israel restrictions
summary: New York's $268 billion state pension fund has restricted its holdings in Unilever Plc due to sales limits imposed by its Ben & Jerry's brand in Israeli-occupied Palestinian territories. The fund's comptroller stated that a review found Unilever and its subsidiary "engaged in BDS activities." Other U.S. states have taken similar actions following Ben & Jerry's July decision, which Unilever said was made independently and did not signify support for the BDS movement.

title: Coca-Cola Co. offers optimistic outlook
summary: The Coca-Cola Co. reported a strong third quarter with net income rising 42% to $2.5 billion and sales up 16% to $10 billion, leading to an optimistic outlook and raised fiscal 2021 guidance. Despite challenges like uneven global recovery and commodity inflation, the company's chairman and CEO is confident in meeting the goal of emerging stronger from the pandemic. Management expects organic revenue growth of 13% to 14% and comparable EPS growth of 15% to 17% for 2021, and is proactively managing increased costs for 2022.

title: The Coca-Cola Company Acquires Remaining Stake in BODYARMOR
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has acquired full ownership of BODYARMOR, a sports performance and hydration beverage line, for $5.6 billion in cash. This acquisition follows an initial 15% stake purchased in 2018. BODYARMOR will operate as a separate business within Coca-Cola’s North America unit, continuing its strong growth trajectory in the U.S. sports drink category.

title: Coca-Cola is buying sports drink maker BodyArmor
summary: Coca-Cola has acquired sports-drink maker BodyArmor for $5.6 billion, marking its largest brand acquisition to date. This move aims to challenge PepsiCo-owned Gatorade's market dominance and leverage BodyArmor's growing market share. Coca-Cola plans to use both Powerade and BodyArmor to compete more effectively in the expanding sports and performance drinks market.

title: Coca-Cola to fully acquire Gatorade rival BodyArmor for $5.6 bln
summary: Coca-Cola announced it will acquire the remaining stake in BodyArmor for $5.6 billion, intensifying its competition with PepsiCo's Gatorade in the sports drink market. This acquisition is Coca-Cola's largest for a single brand and reflects a strategic shift to bolster its presence in the rapidly growing sports hydration category. BodyArmor, valued at $6.59 billion by the deal, currently boasts $1.4 billion in annual retail sales and a 50% growth rate.

title: Coca-Cola Acquires Full Ownership of BodyArmor
summary: The Coca-Cola Co. has completed its acquisition of full ownership of BodyArmor, a sports performance drink, for $5.6 billion in cash. Coca-Cola initially held a 15% stake and will now manage BodyArmor as a separate business unit within its North America operations, retaining BodyArmor's executive leadership. BodyArmor experienced significant growth, with a 25% increase in dollar sales in convenience stores over the past year.

title: Coca-Cola Takes Full Ownership Of Bodyarmor For USD$5.6 Billion
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has acquired full ownership of sports drink company BodyArmor for USD$5.6 billion, following an initial 15% stake purchase in 2018. BodyArmor will operate as a separate business within Coca-Cola's U.S. operations, with its co-founder Mike Repole and president Brent Hastie remaining with the company. The acquisition marks Coca-Cola's largest brand purchase to date and comes as BodyArmor has surpassed Powerade in market share.

title: Meet The Markets: Introducing Germany
summary: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners (CCEP) introduces Germany as part of its "Meet the Markets" series, highlighting its long history, operations, and key figures in the country. The article details CCEP's product portfolio, customer reach, sustainability initiatives, and local community investments in Germany. It also shares interesting facts about Fanta and Mezzo Mix, both of which originated in Germany.

title: Splash Beverage Group’s TapouT Performance Drink Gets Rebrand: Enhanced Ergonomic Bottle & Clean Ingredients
summary: Splash Beverage Group is rebranding its TapouT performance hydration-recovery drink, set to launch in January 2022, to broaden its consumer appeal and secure larger distribution networks. The rebrand emphasizes clean ingredients like zero sugar and no artificial sweeteners, and features an ergonomic bottle and dual-language (English and Spanish) labeling. This strategic move aims to leverage the growing performance drink market, following the significant valuation seen in the Body Armor acquisition by Coca-Cola.

title: The Coca-Cola Company Names WPP as Global Marketing Network Partner; Also Appoints Complementary Media Partner
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has named WPP as its Global Marketing Network Partner to drive long-term growth across its brands in over 200 countries. This new integrated agency model aims to transform and modernize marketing and innovation, focusing on consumer-centric, data-driven experiences. Additionally, Dentsu has been appointed as a Complementary Media Partner in select markets, and a Strategic Roster of approved agencies will provide access to creative minds globally.

title: WPP wins Coca-Cola’s massive agency review
summary: WPP has won Coca-Cola's extensive agency review, securing a major account. The decision follows a competitive pitch process for one of the largest marketing accounts in the industry.

title: Coca-Cola company names WPP as global marketing network partner
summary: WPP, the world's largest advertising company, has been named the global marketing network partner for The Coca-Cola Company, a significant win for WPP. This deal includes handling media in eight of Coca-Cola's nine operating units and the majority of its creative work. Coca-Cola also named Dentsu as a complementary media partner and will include Publicis Groupe and IPG in a strategic roster for an open-source creative model.

title: P&G ‘will grind to a halt': Anti-vax group claims to be employees in YouTube video
summary: An anti-vaccination group claiming to be Procter & Gamble employees released a YouTube video protesting the company's vaccine mandate and warning of production shutdowns. P&G announced in September that its 26,000 U.S. employees must provide proof of vaccination, get an exemption, or submit to weekly testing. P&G stated that the video distorts its policy, noting that roughly 75% of its workforce is vaccinated, and is proceeding with compliance with the federal mandate.

title: WPP wins majority of $4 billion Coca-Cola business
summary: WPP has secured the majority of Coca-Cola's $4 billion global marketing business, creating a bespoke unit called OpenX to handle creative, media, data, and marketing technology. Dentsu will act as a complementary media partner in specific geographies like Japan and Korea, while Coca-Cola will also leverage an open-source creative model to tap diverse talent. This major win consolidates Coca-Cola's marketing efforts and represents a significant shift for the involved holding companies.

title: WPP Named Global Marketing Network Partner for Coca-Cola
summary: WPP has been selected as the global marketing network partner for Coca-Cola, winning a significant pitch against rivals such as IPG, Dentsu, and Publicis Groupe. This appointment tasks WPP with driving growth for Coca-Cola's brand portfolio across over 200 countries and territories, as part of Coca-Cola's strategy to modernize its marketing and boost revenue. Coca-Cola's advertising spend was $2.78 billion in 2020, down from previous years.

title: Your guide to Veterans Day free gifts, discounts and events in the Springfield area
summary: This article provides a comprehensive guide to Veterans Day discounts, free gifts, and events in the Springfield, Missouri area. It lists various businesses offering deals to active military members and veterans, including free food, drinks, discounts on retail, and free haircuts. Additionally, it details several ceremonies and events being held by colleges, universities, and other organizations to honor veterans.

title: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners makes US$15m switch to battery power at UK sites
summary: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners (CCEP) is investing US$15 million to switch to lithium-ion batteries for its equipment, such as forklift trucks, at its UK sites. This move is part of the company's broader goal to achieve net-zero carbon emissions. CCEP aims to reduce its carbon footprint and enhance sustainability in its operations.

title: MediaCom Becomes The Coca-Cola Company’s Global Media Agency As Part Of WPP’s OpenX Team
summary: WPP has been chosen as The Coca-Cola Company's Global Marketing Network Partner, with MediaCom serving as the global media agency for the bespoke OpenX team across most markets. This partnership, spanning over 200 markets, aims to transform Coca-Cola’s marketing effectiveness and efficiency starting January 1, 2022. The agreement highlights WPP's integrated capabilities across content, media, data, production, and technology.

title: Walmart asks judge to trash lawsuit over recyclable labeling
