title: Coca-Cola UNITED Celebrates Opening of $10M Panama City Sales Center
summary: Coca-Cola Bottling Company United, Inc. (UNITED) celebrated the grand opening of its new $10 million facility in Panama City, Florida, which will serve as a sales and distribution center, warehouse, and administrative office space. This new facility, replacing one heavily damaged by Hurricane Michael, represents a significant investment in the community, creating local jobs and improving service capacity for customers across Northwest Florida. Company executives highlighted the resilience of the community and the commitment to long-term growth in the region.

title: Graphic Packaging expands paperboard topper range with minimal material solution
summary: Graphic Packaging has introduced EnviroClip, a new paperboard topper for multipack beverage cans, designed as a minimal material alternative to plastic rings and shrink film. This solution complements their existing KeelClip range, offering a recyclable and renewable option made from sustainably managed forests without adhesives or plastic lamination. EnviroClip is available for various can sizes and configurations, expanding accessibility for beverage companies seeking sustainable packaging.

title: Making a Difference Through the Energize Learning Project: An Interview with AIM-Progress Africa Hub
summary: This article details The Hershey Company's "Energize Learning" project in Côte d’Ivoire and Ghana, which provides vitamin-fortified peanut butter snacks ("ViVi") to schoolchildren. The initiative aims to improve nutrition, combat child labor by incentivizing school attendance, and strengthen local agri-food systems by sourcing ingredients locally. The project, in partnership with Project Peanut Butter and local governments, currently reaches over 45,000 children daily.

title: Coca-Cola CMO on Building Consumer Loyalty, Trust
summary: Melanie Boulden, CMO of Coca-Cola North America, discusses her strategies for building consumer loyalty and trust. Her priorities include recruiting the next generation of consumers with evolving preferences, embracing shifts to online purchasing, and developing a more efficient marketing organization. Boulden emphasizes listening to consumers, delivering on promises, ensuring transparency, and investing in purpose-driven initiatives like sustainable packaging and diversity.

title: Finance at the Center of Data and Analysis at Coca-Cola
summary: Coca-Cola CFO John Murphy discusses how data and analytics are central to the company's new business model and finance transformation. He emphasizes finance's critical role in data governance, collaboration, and ensuring alignment across departments like marketing and supply chain. Murphy also details the organizational changes made, including centralizing finance functions, and the importance of motivating employees and maintaining clear communication during the transformation process.

title: Coca-Cola CMO on Building Consumer Loyalty, Trust
summary: Melanie Boulden, CMO of Coca-Cola North America, discusses strategies for building consumer loyalty and trust in a competitive and evolving market. She highlights three key priorities: recruiting the next generation of consumers, adapting to shifts in marketplace dynamics like online purchasing, and establishing a new marketing organization following a major company reorganization. The article emphasizes the importance of listening to consumers, delivering on promises, and evolving marketing efforts to stay culturally relevant and transparent.

title: Coca-Cola FEMSA lanzó su Informe Anual Integrado
summary: Coca-Cola FEMSA (KOF) released its 2021 Integrated Annual Report, "Re-Evolución," highlighting its operational, financial, and non-financial achievements driven by its strategic framework and purpose. The report emphasizes the company's resilience, adaptability, and agility, showcasing positive results across strategic fronts, from portfolio management and digital transformation to sustainable development. Key achievements include significant financial growth, expansion of its omni-channel platform, sustainable financing for green projects, and notable progress in circular economy, water management, and climate action initiatives.

title: Facing production constraints, Hershey turns to SKU rationalization
summary: Hershey is addressing omicron-induced production challenges by rationalizing SKUs, focusing on its most popular products to free up capacity and reduce complexity. This strategy, previously used by other food and beverage makers during the pandemic, helps maintain operational efficiency amidst rising inflation, labor shortages, and supply chain constraints. Despite offering less variety, the company has seen increased shelf space and minimal negative impact from these choices.

title: Creating a World Without Waste: The Coca-Cola Company Teams Up with Bill Nye to Demystify Recycling in Striking Animation
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has partnered with Bill Nye to release an animated, stop-motion short film that explains the plastic recycling process. This initiative is part of Coca-Cola's "World Without Waste" goal to collect and recycle a bottle or can for every one it sells by 2030, and to use at least 50% recycled material in its packaging by the same year. The film aims to demystify recycling and inspire action towards a circular economy for plastic bottles.

title: Keurig Dr Pepper CEO to step down in July
summary: Keurig Dr Pepper CEO and Chairman Bob Gamgort will step down on July 29, to be succeeded by CFO and international division president Ozan Dokmecioglu. Gamgort will transition to executive chairman for two years, working closely with Dokmecioglu who will lead the company's operational strategy. This leadership change comes after Gamgort successfully integrated the merged companies and grew sales, while Dokmecioglu is an insider familiar with the company's finances and strategy.

title: Williams Sonoma Partners with the Kentucky Derby® to Inspire At-Home Race Day Celebrations
summary: Williams Sonoma has partnered with the Kentucky Derby and Woodford Reserve to inspire at-home race day celebrations for the 148th Kentucky Derby. This partnership includes a curated line of merchandise, co-branded cocktail mixes, special recipes from Chef Kelsey Barnard Clark, and virtual and in-person cooking events. The collaboration aims to bring the authentic charm of the Derby into homes and offers a sweepstakes for a trip to the 149th Kentucky Derby in 2023.

title: The Coca-Cola Co Performance Trends 2017-21 – results data
summary: This article analyzes The Coca-Cola Co's performance trends from 2017 to 2021, examining how the company's results during this period prepared it for future challenges. It highlights a 16% increase in year-on-year sales for 2021 and discusses broader trends affecting the global soft drinks category. The report aims to provide insights into the company's trajectory and the key factors shaping its industry presence.

title: Constellation Brands buys remaining stake in RTD drink Austin Cocktails
summary: Constellation Brands has acquired the remaining stake in Austin Cocktails, a female-founded ready-to-drink (RTD) cocktail company, after initially investing in 2018. This acquisition aligns with Constellation's strategy to expand into fast-growing RTD categories and promote diversity, as the RTD segment, including hard seltzers, is projected for significant growth. The move follows other industry players' investments in RTD cocktails and reinforces Constellation's commitment to innovation and growth in the evolving alcohol market.

title: Functional Energy Drink Market to See Booming Growth | Red Bull, Coca Cola, Pepsi
summary: A new study by HTF Market Intelligence Consulting Pvt. Ltd. forecasts significant growth in the Functional Energy Drink market from 2021-2027. The report covers revenue size, CAGR, consumption, and key market players such as Red Bull, Coca Cola, and PepsiCo Inc. It examines market segments by product type (Isotonic, Hypertonic, Hypotonic) and application (Store Based, Non-Store Based), alongside regional analysis across APAC, Europe, North America, South America, and MEA.

title: Ambev unveils new approach for growth
summary: Ambev, known for beer brands like Brahma, Skol, and Antarctica, is shifting its strategy to become a broader "platform" encompassing food and services beyond beverages. This new approach involves digital transformation, alliances, and acquisitions focused on technology and logistics, including offering credit to customers through its Bees platform and Bees Bank. The company's CEO, Jean Jereissati, highlights how increased digitalization during the pandemic helped achieve record sales and revenue in 2021, positioning Ambev as countercyclical to market conditions.

title: Femsa firma acuerdo para comprar Sigma Supply en Estados Unidos
summary: Femsa, through its subsidiary Envoy Solutions, has agreed to acquire Sigma Supply of North America to strengthen its distribution business in the United States. This acquisition will expand Envoy's presence into Texas and bolster its reach in the South and Mid-Atlantic regions, adding significant capabilities in packaging materials, solutions, and services. The deal, which enhances Femsa's national distribution platform strategy, is expected to close in the second quarter of 2022 and adds to the over $1.7 billion in annual revenue from previously acquired companies in this sector.

title: Coca-Cola, Kraft-Heinz, Unilever: CPG Companies Embracing the Data Revolution
summary: This article highlights how major Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG) companies like Coca-Cola, Kraft-Heinz, and Unilever are leveraging data and artificial intelligence across their business operations. They are using technology for supply chain planning, demand forecasting, marketing campaigns, and enhancing consumer experiences. The article provides specific examples of how each company is implementing data-driven strategies for innovation and efficiency.

title: LinkedIn releases 25 best workplaces to work in Nigeria ranking
summary: LinkedIn has released its 2022 list of the 25 best workplaces to grow careers in Nigeria, with financial services companies dominating the top positions, including Access Bank, GTB, Stanbic IBTC, and Zenith Bank. The ranking is based on unique LinkedIn data across seven pillars of career progression, including company stability, skills growth, and gender diversity. The report aims to encourage Nigerian organizations to prioritize organizational culture and talent retention in an evolving work environment.

title: Hasbro plans to further hike prices of toys, warns of $100 million Russia hit
summary: Hasbro Inc. announced plans to increase toy prices further to offset soaring costs and projected a potential $100 million revenue hit this year due to pausing shipments to Russia. The company also lifted its fiscal 2022 operating profit growth forecast and reported a 4% rise in net revenue, though adjusted first-quarter earnings per share missed estimates. These measures are intended to mitigate supply issues and improve product availability for the holiday season.

title: Mars invites Mondelēz International, Nestlé and General Mills into key climate action group
summary: Mars, in partnership with Guidehouse, PepsiCo, and McCormick & Company, has invited nine major global brands, including Mondelēz International, Nestlé, and General Mills, to join the Supplier Leadership on Climate Transition (Supplier LoCT) consortium. This initiative aims to drive action towards achieving net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050, focusing on engaging and mobilizing suppliers to reduce Scope 3 emissions. The consortium offers instructional seminars and direct mentoring to help suppliers build internal capacity for climate action.

title: Energy drink A Shoc raises $29M from investors including Keurig Dr Pepper
summary: A Shoc, an energy drink distributed by Keurig Dr Pepper, raised $29 million in a Series B funding round with investors including Keurig Dr Pepper, Aaron Judge, Freddie Freeman, and Michael Strahan. The company, founded by Lance Collins, is positioned in the fast-growing U.S. energy drink market and has a "path to ownership deal" with Keurig Dr Pepper. Given Collins' track record of building and selling successful brands to large corporations like Coca-Cola and Keurig Dr Pepper, a full acquisition by Keurig Dr Pepper is a strong possibility as it seeks to compete with Monster and Rockstar.

title: The Coca-Cola Company donates $1 million to get more Georgia commercial truck drivers on the road
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has donated $1 million to the Technical College System of Georgia (TCSG) Foundation to support its Commercial Truck Driving Program. This investment aims to create 11 new full-time and two part-time instructor roles, improving training capabilities and doubling enrollment of commercial drivers in Georgia by 2023. The initiative also includes a "Delivering the Future" truck tour to raise awareness about career opportunities in the trucking industry.

title: The Untold Truth Of Yum Brands
summary: Yum Brands, parent company of KFC, Pizza Hut, and Taco Bell, originated from PepsiCo's restaurant division before becoming an independent entity in 1997. The company has a history of acquiring and divesting various restaurant chains, expanding significantly in China, and has faced past controversies regarding food safety. Despite challenges, Yum Brands is a major global restaurant company, known for its philanthropic efforts and commitment to sustainability.

title: Jim McGreevy to Join Coca-Cola PACS Following Beer Institute Departure
summary: Jim McGreevy, the outgoing president and CEO of the Beer Institute, will join Coca-Cola's North America Political Action Committees (PACS) as VP of public policy, federal government relations, and political engagement. He will start his new role on May 16, leading the company's strategic engagement on various public policies. During his eight-year tenure at the Beer Institute, McGreevy achieved significant milestones, including permanent federal excise tax relief for brewers and importers and lobbying for brewers to be considered essential workers during the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Coca-Cola Company pledges $1M to train truck drivers in Georgia
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has donated $1 million to the Technical Colleges System of Georgia’s (TCSG) Commercial Truck Driving Program to address the critical shortage of truck drivers. This investment will create 13 new instructor roles, aiming to double the enrollment of commercial drivers in Georgia by 2023. The initiative also includes a "Delivering the Future" truck tour to raise awareness about career opportunities with Coca-Cola UNITED and the TCSG program.

title: Coca-Cola sales surge as crowds return to music, sports venues
summary: Coca-Cola reported a 16% surge in first-quarter sales, driven by increased attendance at entertainment venues despite the company's exit from Russia and rising operational costs. The beverage giant exceeded Wall Street expectations, posting $2.78 billion in net income. It maintained its full-year revenue and per-share growth projections, indicating continued confidence in its performance.

title: Coca-Cola turns to refillable glass bottles in fight against inflation
summary: Coca-Cola is expanding the use of more affordable, refillable glass bottles in markets severely affected by inflation, as the company anticipates a potential slowdown in consumer demand despite current strong sales. CEO James Quincey expects consumer "elasticity" to increase, signaling an eventual weakening of demand in response to continued price hikes. The company reported a 16% rise in net revenue in the first quarter, but also noted that suspending operations in Russia would impact its annual profit and net revenue.

title: PepsiCo Boosts Its Sales Outlook; CFO Sees ‘Big Momentum’
summary: PepsiCo has increased its full-year sales growth estimate to 8% from 6%, attributing the stronger outlook to easing pandemic restrictions and increased consumer activity. The company's first-quarter revenue of $16.2 billion surpassed analyst expectations, with CFO Hugh Johnston noting significant business momentum. Despite anticipating higher input costs, PepsiCo expects its North American food and beverage units, as well as international markets, to perform well.

title: Coca-Cola’s recovery from COVID varies by region
summary: Coca-Cola reported increased net income and operating revenues in the first quarter of 2022, driven by recovery in away-from-home channels and increased consumer mobility in most regions. However, market recovery was uneven, with strong growth in North America and Latin America, but declines in China due to strict COVID lockdowns. The company also announced the suspension of its business in Russia and expects commodity price inflation for the fiscal year.

title: PepsiCo says revenues jumped after it raised prices. (Published 2022)
summary: PepsiCo reported strong first-quarter revenues primarily driven by price increases across its snack and beverage brands, despite modest volume growth. The company saw revenues rise 9.3 percent to $16.2 billion, with its Frito-Lay North American division experiencing a 12 percent pricing soar. Executives acknowledged consumers facing inflation and aim to monitor behavior closely for future pricing decisions while emphasizing the company's historical resilience during inflationary periods.

title: National Museum of the American Latino Receives $2 Million Gift From The Coca-Cola Company
summary: The Smithsonian's National Museum of the American Latino announced a $2 million gift from The Coca-Cola Company to support the new museum and its Molina Family Latino Gallery. This donation establishes Coca-Cola as a Corporate Founder of the gallery and a Founding Donor of the museum, aiming to showcase the diverse stories and contributions of Latinos in the United States. The gift will enable dynamic exhibitions and programming, including the inaugural "¡Presente! A Latino History of the United States" exhibition, which will open in the summer at the National Museum of American History.

title: Nike Inc. hires new Jordan brand CMO Shannon Watkins, from Aflac, Coca Cola - Bizwomen
summary: Nike Inc. has appointed Shannon Watkins, formerly of Aflac and Coca-Cola, as the new Chief Marketing Officer for its Jordan brand. Her hiring is part of Nike's broader strategy to enhance its direct-to-consumer and digital sales efforts, coinciding with other recent executive hires and changes to the company's return-to-office policy. Watkins received an AdWeek award in 2021 for her work on a collaboration focusing on inequities in HBCUs.

title: Delta Air Lines adds gray uniforms after problems with 'passport plum' version
summary: Delta Air Lines is introducing new gray uniforms, alongside their existing purple ones, after the "passport plum" version, debuted in 2018, drew complaints from workers. The new uniforms, like the purple ones, will carry the OEKO-TEX certification, ensuring they are free of harmful substances. This move addresses employee concerns while maintaining the airline's commitment to quality textiles.

title: Conagra Brands Names Lucy Brady President of Grocery and Snacks
summary: Conagra Brands has appointed Lucy Brady as President of Grocery and Snacks, effective June 15. Brady will be responsible for modernizing the company and growing its grocery and snack portfolio, which includes brands like Slim Jim and Duncan Hines. She brings extensive experience from previous roles at McDonald’s and Boston Consulting Group, where she focused on digital customer engagement, strategy, and business development.

title: These Atlanta CEOs make 1,000 times their typical employees
summary: CEOs at major Atlanta companies like Coca-Cola, Carter's, and Fleetcor Technologies earn salaries that are 1,000 times higher than their typical employees. The article highlights the CEO-to-worker pay ratio at 40 of Georgia's largest public companies, including UPS, Aflac, and Delta Air Lines. This report was published by the Atlanta Business Chronicle.

title: Industrial Sugar Market to Reach USD 46.56 Billion by 2029
summary: The global industrial sugar market is projected to reach USD 46.56 billion by 2029, growing at a CAGR of 2.72% from USD 38.58 billion in 2022. The market, which was valued at USD 37.62 billion in 2021, saw a decline in demand during the COVID-19 pandemic. Key drivers include increasing utilization in processed foods and beverages, and strong demand for sugar confectioneries, particularly in the Asia Pacific region.

title: Coca-Cola aims to use 50 percent recycled glass by 2030
summary: Coca-Cola Bottling Co. United has set a goal to incorporate 50 percent recycled material into its glass bottles by 2030. This initiative is supported by an expanded partnership with O-I Glass, which will remanufacture Coca-Cola's recycled glass into new bottles. The collaboration aims to recycle over 700,000 out-of-date and damaged bottles annually, highlighting glass's role in a sustainable, circular economy.

title: Kraft Heinz wants to solve its supply chain problems — in the metaverse
summary: Kraft Heinz is leveraging the metaverse and a partnership with Microsoft to enhance its supply chain efficiency. By creating "digital twins" of its facilities, the company aims to resolve logistical issues virtually, speed up operations, and ensure products like Lunchables and Velveeta reach shelves faster. This technological investment seeks to improve dependability and responsiveness to shifting consumer demands.

title: Coca-Cola Beverages Florida Recognized as a US Best Managed Company
summary: Coca-Cola Beverages Florida (Coke Florida) has been recognized as a 2022 US Best Managed Company, an award sponsored by Deloitte Private and The Wall Street Journal. This honor acknowledges the company's excellence in strategic planning, commitment to its employees, resilient culture, and strong financial performance. Coke Florida, the third-largest privately held and sixth-largest Coca-Cola bottler in the U.S., highlighted this recognition as validation of its associates' diligence and resilience through unprecedented business challenges.

title: Taste the 'metaverse' in Coca-Cola's new pixel-flavored soda
summary: Coca-Cola has launched a new limited-edition soda flavor called Coca-Cola Zero Sugar Byte, which it describes as the first Coca-Cola flavor "born in the metaverse." Inspired by gaming, the drink aims to bring the "flavor of pixels to life" and is accompanied by immersive digital experiences, including an island in Fortnite Creative and an augmented reality game. This release follows Coca-Cola's earlier "Starlight" flavor, which was advertised as a taste of outer space.

title: Molson Coors to Release Simply Spiked Lemonade in June
summary: Molson Coors Beverage Company announced that its new Simply Spiked Lemonade line, inspired by The Coca-Cola Company's Simply juice brand, will launch in June. This product marks the latest collaboration between the two companies, following the success of Topo Chico Hard Seltzer. Simply Spiked Lemonade will be available in four distinct flavors and is expected to capitalize on significant consumer hype.

title: Chemist sentenced to 14 years for stealing Eastman, other companies’ trade secrets
summary: A chemist, Xiaorong You (aka Shannon You), has been sentenced to 14 years in prison for stealing trade secrets from Eastman Chemical Company and several other companies. These trade secrets, valued at nearly $120 million, were related to BPA-free can coatings, which You intended to use for a can-coating manufacturer in China, supported by Chinese government grants. She was convicted of multiple charges including conspiracy to commit trade secret theft and economic espionage after gaining access to the information while working at Coca-Cola and Eastman.

title: US jails ex-Coca-Cola engineer Xiaorong You in China trade secrets case
summary: A former Coca-Cola engineer, Xiaorong "Shannon" You, has been sentenced to 14 years in a US prison for stealing trade secrets related to BPA-free internal coatings for drink cans. Prosecutors stated that You intended to use the stolen information, which cost companies nearly $120 million to develop, to establish a company in China backed by millions in Chinese government grants. Her actions were found to benefit the Chinese government, province of Shandong, city of Weihai, and the Chinese Communist Party.

title: How will Coca-Cola meet its pledge to make 25% of its beverage packaging refillable or returnable?
summary: Coca-Cola plans to make 25% of its beverage packaging refillable or returnable by 2030, focusing on emerging markets in Latin America and Africa where inflation is a major concern. The company is expanding initiatives like its "Universal Bottle" scheme and reusable PET bottles, driven by sustainability imperatives, growing consumer demand for eco-friendly options, and the need to mitigate rising operational costs. Challenges include securing a steady supply of food-grade recycled PET, the higher cost of bio-based alternatives, and addressing consumer convenience and financial barriers associated with refillable solutions.

title: US Sentences Chemist for Theft of Coca-Cola Secrets Worth $120 Million
summary: A former Coca-Cola chemist, Xiaorong You, has been sentenced to 14 years in prison for stealing trade secrets related to BPA-free coatings for soda cans, valued at nearly $120 million. She stole these secrets to benefit a Chinese company, Weihai Jinhong Group, and the Chinese government. The judgment also includes three years of supervised release and $200,000 in damages.

title: Vita Coco co-founder: 'The overall coconut water category continues to show robust growth'
summary: Vita Coco, which went public in October 2021, reported a 28% year-over-year increase in net sales for Q1 2022, reaching $96 million. The company's co-founder and executive chairman, Mike Kirban, highlighted Vita Coco's 50% market share in the coconut water category and its growing household penetration, attributing much of the category's robust growth to consumer demand from multicultural groups. Despite supply chain challenges and rising costs, Vita Coco plans further price increases in 2022 and anticipates a return to historical gross margins as pricing takes effect and costs normalize.

title: Kraft Heinz Explores Potential of Paper-Based Ketchup Bottle
summary: Kraft Heinz is collaborating with Pulpex to develop a recyclable, paper-based bottle for its Heinz Tomato Ketchup, aiming to be the first sauce brand to adopt this technology. This initiative supports Kraft Heinz's sustainability goals to make all packaging recyclable, reusable, or compostable by 2025 and achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050. The Pulpex bottles, made from sustainably sourced pulp and featuring food-grade coatings, offer a lower carbon footprint compared to traditional packaging and are curbside-recyclable.

title: FIFA World Cup™ Trophy Tour by Coca-Cola Kicks Off Global Journey in Dubai
summary: The FIFA World Cup™ Trophy Tour by Coca-Cola has commenced its global journey in Dubai, featuring former FIFA World Cup™ winners Iker Casillas and Kaká. For the first time, the tour will visit all 32 qualifying countries, stopping in 51 countries and territories to offer fans exclusive experiences and support sustainability efforts. This initiative continues Coca-Cola's long-standing partnership with FIFA, aiming to bring the excitement of the FIFA World Cup to fans worldwide.

title: Rhodes College to Award Honorary Degree to Retired Coca-Cola Enterprises Executive Vicki R. Palmer
summary: Rhodes College will award an honorary Doctor of Humanities degree to Vicki R. Palmer ’75, a retired executive from Coca-Cola Enterprises Inc., at its 173rd Commencement. Palmer, a financial expert and community leader, had a distinguished career including roles at First Tennessee Bank, FedEx, and Coca-Cola, and has been a significant benefactor and alumna of Rhodes College. She will be honored for her accomplishments and contributions during the ceremony on May 14.

title: Coca-Cola Company
summary: This article provides a brief overview of The Coca-Cola Company. It highlights the company's global presence and its primary business as a beverage company focusing on the manufacture, retail, and marketing of non-alcoholic beverage concentrates and syrups.

title: Coke Headed Back to UA Is the Real Thing
summary: The University of Arkansas is finalizing a 10-year deal to make Coca-Cola the official beverage sponsor, returning after a switch to Pepsi in 2012. This partnership will bring a variety of Coke products to campus and athletic events, offering scholarships and internship opportunities for students, and supporting campus sustainability efforts. The agreement marks a significant return for Coca-Cola to the Razorbacks.

title: University and Coca-Cola in Final Stages of New Campus Beverages Contract
summary: The University of Arkansas is nearing a 10-year agreement to make Coca-Cola its exclusive non-alcoholic cold beverage sponsor and provider, effective July 1, 2022. This partnership follows a competitive selection process and will replace the current contract with PepsiCo. The deal includes internship and scholarship funding for students, support for sustainability efforts, and will make various Coca-Cola, Dr Pepper, and Monster brands available across campus and at athletic venues, while Gatorade remains the official Isotonic Drink Sponsor for Razorback Athletics.

title: University of Arkansas nears deal for return of Coca-Cola
summary: The University of Arkansas is finalizing a 10-year deal to bring Coca-Cola back as its exclusive beverage provider, replacing PepsiCo whose $19 million contract expires on June 30. This new agreement, effective July 1, will offer diverse Coca-Cola products on campus and at events, alongside providing internship opportunities and scholarship funding for students. The total financial value of the new contract will be disclosed after final negotiations are complete.

title: The Coca-Cola Co, Coca-Cola Europacific Partners roll out tethered bottle cap in UK
summary: The Coca-Cola Co and Coca-Cola Europacific Partners have begun rolling out tethered bottle caps across the UK, starting with an initial launch in Scotland. This redesign aims to keep the cap attached to plastic bottles after opening. The move is part of an initiative to improve recycling and reduce litter.

title: Dippin' Dots to be acquired by Icee owner J&J Snack Foods for $222M
summary: J&J Snack Foods, known for brands like Icee and Superpretzel, is set to acquire Dippin' Dots for $222 million by the end of June. This acquisition will add a well-known frozen novelty brand to J&J Snack Foods' portfolio, complementing its existing frozen beverage and novelty businesses. The deal is expected to accelerate growth and be accretive to J&J Snack Foods' earnings per share, leveraging its expertise in integrating new brands and expanding distribution.

title: Beer Insights Conference: A-B Focuses Beyond Beer on Hard Seltzer, RTDs; Mergers and Acquisitions Expected to Ramp Up
summary: Anheuser-Busch InBev is prioritizing hard seltzers, Cutwater Spirits, Nütrl Vodka Seltzer, and Ghost Energy in its beyond beer division, even as Bud Light Seltzer sales decline. The company is adapting to the consumer shift from sugar/malt-based seltzers to spirits-based RTDs, with Cutwater being a strong performer. The article also anticipates an increase in mergers and acquisitions in the beverage industry, driven by market maturation and premiumization, and highlights DEI initiatives by Constellation Brands and Diageo.

title: Jumia releases reports of 2022 first quarter
summary: Jumia Technologies AG announced strong financial results for the first quarter of 2022, showcasing significant growth in GMV, orders, and revenue, reaching nine-quarter highs. The company emphasized its path to profitability through accelerated usage growth, improved marketing efficiency, and continued execution of its growth strategy. Jumia also highlighted its progress in monetizing logistics services for third parties and strong growth in its advertising campaigns, securing its position as a leading brand in the Egyptian market.

title: Conagra Brands Showcases Stellar Snacks Line-up at 2022 Sweets & Snacks Expo
summary: Conagra Brands showcased its $2.9 billion snacking portfolio, featuring iconic and emerging brands, at the 2022 Sweets & Snacks Expo in Chicago. The company highlighted new innovations from brands like Slim Jim, DAVID and BiGS Sunflower Seeds, ACT II, Angie's BOOMCHICKAPOP, Andy Capp's, and Snack Pack, along with merchandising solutions. This presentation aimed to connect with customers and emphasize the strength and variety of their snack offerings across various categories.

title: Onur Dedeköylü appointed as CCO of Pegasus Airlines
summary: Onur Dedeköylü, who served as Senior Vice President for Marketing at Pegasus Airlines since 2010, has been promoted to Chief Commercial Officer (CCO). In his new role, effective May 13, 2022, Dedeköylü will oversee the Commercial division, including sales, network planning, marketing, revenue management, guest experience, and cargo departments. He is recognized for his significant contributions to ancillary product management, digital transformation, and brand building at Pegasus Airlines.

title: Boston Beer Co. Launches TeaPot, Cannabis-Infused Iced Tea
summary: Boston Beer Company, known for Samuel Adams, is entering the cannabis market with "TeaPot," a THC-infused iced tea, launching in Canada in July. This move marks one of the first major alcohol companies to launch its own THC brand, with plans for eventual U.S. market entry despite federal marijuana prohibition. The company aims to attract new consumers with cannabis beverages, seeing it as a more socially acceptable form of consumption than other cannabis products.

title: Colgate-Palmolive: Stability Amid Volatility
summary: This article argues that Colgate-Palmolive (CL) offers favorable risk/reward for investors due to its strong global brand, distribution network, and consistent free cash flow, despite recent underperformance. The analysis highlights the company's profitability compared to competitors and growth in its pet nutrition segment, projecting a significant upside for the stock. While acknowledging challenges like lagging sales in North America and Europe, falling margins, and private label growth, the article concludes that the stock is undervalued based on its discounted cash flow model.

title: EBG Acquires Sparkfly Perks to Support Expansion of Corporate Client Base
summary: EBG, a prominent e-commerce solutions provider specializing in travel and entertainment, has acquired Sparkfly Perks, a national discount platform for employee benefits. This acquisition will allow EBG to broaden its corporate client base, including major organizations like The Coca-Cola Company, and integrate new products into its extensive offerings through the Working Advantage platform. This move solidifies EBG's position for continued growth, building on previous strategic acquisitions and investment partnerships.

title: Why Coca-Cola is Discontinuing Honest Tea
summary: Coca-Cola is discontinuing its Honest Tea brand by the end of the year to streamline its beverage portfolio and focus on more profitable and scalable brands like Gold Peak and Peace Tea. The company aims to consolidate its ready-to-drink tea strategy around these two brands, which have seen increased sales and are better positioned to meet consumer preferences and supply chain demands. Honest Kids will remain part of the business, and Coca-Cola intends to explore licensing opportunities for the Honest brand in other categories.

title: RPET Trends: Will Refillable Bottles Go Mainstream?
summary: Refillable PET bottles are gaining popularity in Latin America and other developing regions due to cost-effectiveness and wider consumer appeal, while developed markets like Europe and the US are seeing a resurgence driven by consumer concerns over plastic waste. Initiatives from major brands and supermarkets are driving this comeback, focusing on high RPET content bottles and circularity. Despite challenges like consumer perception, these efforts aim to re-establish refillables as a mainstream option, significantly reducing environmental impact.

title: Legg Mason Low Volatility High Dividend ETF (LVHD) Pays Off
summary: The Legg Mason Low Volatility High Dividend ETF (LVHD) has demonstrated resilience amidst market turbulence, outperforming the S&P 500 Index with a 2.2% loss year-to-date compared to the S&P 500's 13.1% decline. The fund focuses on high-quality companies with strong dividend yields, steady profits, and low share-price volatility, favoring sectors like utilities, consumer staples, and real estate, and boasts a 3.06% dividend yield. While it lagged the S&P 500 in 2020 due to its focus on established companies over high-growth stocks, it proved 5% less volatile over a three-year period.

title: Nobody Likes Index Funds, Except Investors
summary: The article discusses the criticisms leveled against index funds, despite their success with investors. It highlights a "three-pronged attack" from the political left, the political right, and active fund managers, each with different motivations for their objections. Ultimately, the author argues that index funds remain excellent investments, and the real issue may be the size of major money-management firms, regardless of their investment strategy.

title: Last Call: Ball Partners with Manna Capital for Aluminum Mill in NM; Instacart Calls Spirit-Based RTDs ‘Drink of Summer’
summary: Ball Corp., the world's largest aluminum beverage can manufacturer, has partnered with Manna Capital Partners to build and operate an aluminum can sheet rolling mill and recycling center in Los Lunas, New Mexico, expected to be operational by 2026. Instacart predicts ready-to-drink (RTD) canned cocktails will be the "drink of the summer" for 2022, as over a third of legal-drinking-age consumers reported being "officially over" hard seltzers. Other news includes the return of the Oregon Brewers Festival, the BA's guide to cultural observances for craft brewers, Athletic Brewing's young and diverse consumer base, Heineken USA transitioning import rights for three brands, and High Noon's ad campaign against malt-based seltzers.

title: Accenture joins the TOUR Championship as a Proud Partner
summary: Accenture has joined the TOUR Championship as a Proud Partner, an agreement extending through 2027. This partnership aims to elevate the FedExCup Playoffs finale at East Lake Golf Club and enhance its positive impact on the Atlanta community. Accenture will also make an annual contribution to First Tee, supporting youth development.

title: Coca Cola Consolidated settles 401(k) lawsuit
summary: Coca-Cola Consolidated has settled a class-action lawsuit filed under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA) concerning its 401(k) plan. The settlement amounts to $3.5 million, to be distributed among the participants. The lawsuit alleged that the plan utilized "high risk" and expensive actively managed Fidelity Freedom Funds target-date funds instead of index funds and that recordkeeping and administrative costs were excessive.

title: Bimbo, Femsa, Bachoco y otras empresas de consumo enfrentan el reto de contener los precios a 100 días de la invasión a Ucrania
summary: Mexican consumer goods companies like Bimbo, Femsa, and Bachoco are struggling to contain price increases 100 days after the invasion of Ukraine. Rising commodity prices, especially for wheat and corn, due to the conflict, are forcing these companies to adjust product prices and seek efficiencies. Strategies include leveraging technology, pre-purchasing raw materials, introducing new products, and offering smaller product presentations to mitigate the impact on consumers and maintain profitability amidst persistent inflation.

title: How Target Conquered the World in the 2000s
summary: This article chronicles Target's transformation from a local discounter to a national trendsetter in the 2000s, as recounted by former chief marketing officer Michael Francis. It highlights the company's "Expect More, Pay Less" philosophy, strategic designer collaborations like Michael Graves and Isaac Mizrahi, and its innovative marketing campaigns that built a strong brand presence and fostered community engagement. Francis also discusses Target's commitment to urban vitality and its internal culture of relentless innovation.

title: Coca-Cola sube de precio en 2022, pero no bajará su consumo
summary: Coca-Cola Femsa ha incrementado los precios de sus productos en México, incluyendo Coca-Cola, jugos Del Valle, y leche Santa Clara, citing inflationary pressures on raw materials. Despite these price hikes, effective June 6, 2022, experts and small business owners do not anticipate a significant drop in consumption, noting that demand often recovers after an initial dip and is currently boosted by hot weather. Other bottlers like Arca Continental are also facing similar challenges and exploring strategies like smaller, more affordable packaging and a return to returnable bottles to mitigate costs and maintain sales.

title: We are customer centric only when our customers tell us we are
summary: Coca-Cola HBC has transformed its approach to customer centricity, moving from annual surveys of a small sample to real-time digital feedback from all customers. This shift, in partnership with Customer Gauge since 2021, aims to enable faster responses to customer needs and better experiences. The company's sales teams have rapidly adopted the new system, earning an award for user engagement, demonstrating a strong commitment to continuous improvement based on comprehensive customer feedback.

title: Urban Outfitters trims low-profit SKUs to boost margins
summary: Urban Outfitters is cutting down on low-profit SKUs to improve its margins and mitigate high freight costs. This strategy is part of a three-year plan that also includes larger, earlier orders, and aims for a 500 basis point initial markup improvement, with results expected to materialize in Q4. Other tactics involve product distortion, fabric positioning, 3-D product design technology, raising retail prices, and increased reliance on ocean transportation.

title: Russian-owned successor of McDonald’s opens in Moscow
summary: After McDonald's exited Russia due to the conflict in Ukraine, its former restaurants reopened under Russian ownership and a new name, Vkusno-i Tochka (Tasty-period), in Moscow. The new chain aims to fill the void left by McDonald's, retaining staff and mimicking the original restaurant's layout, though potentially seeking new suppliers for certain products like soft drinks. The reopening drew crowds, albeit smaller than McDonald's initial 1990 debut, and resonated with a sense of nostalgia for Western consumerism.

title: A Deeper Look at Coca‑Cola’s Emerging Business in Alcohol
summary: Coca-Cola is expanding its presence in the alcohol beverage market, which began with Lemon-Dou in Japan in 2018. The company is strategically experimenting with flavored alcohol beverages (FABs), including hard seltzers, hard alternatives, and pre-mixed cocktails, using a disciplined and responsible approach. Coca-Cola emphasizes consumer focus, offering more choices in this rapidly expanding segment, and is committed to promoting responsible consumption through a comprehensive Policy on Alcohol Responsibility.

title: PepsiCo commits to new sustainable packaging goal
summary: PepsiCo, Inc. has announced a new goal to increase the percentage of its beverages sold through reusable models from 10% to 20% by 2030, reinforcing its prior commitment to reduce single-use virgin plastic. This initiative, part of its pep+ sustainability program, will be supported by a four-pronged approach including expanding its SodaStream business, increasing refillable bottle offerings, investing in concentrates, and developing fountain drink options. The company's efforts align with a broader industry trend toward sustainable packaging, moving towards a circular economy model.

title: Canned Jack & Coke to hit stores as part of Coca-Cola and Brown-Forman deal
summary: Coca-Cola and Brown-Forman have partnered to release a ready-to-drink canned Jack Daniel's & Coca-Cola. The beverage will be made with Jack Daniel's Tennessee Whiskey and Coca-Cola, bringing the classic bar cocktail to stores. This collaboration marks a significant move for both companies into the pre-mixed cocktail market.

title: Jack-and-Coke in a can: Coca-Cola and Brown-Forman team up for new drink
summary: Coca-Cola and Brown-Forman are collaborating to launch a canned Jack-and-Coke cocktail, marking Coke's fourth new alcoholic beverage in under two years and its first for its namesake soda. The drink will debut in Mexico later this year before expanding globally, with a zero-sugar option available. This move aligns with a broader trend of soda companies entering the alcoholic beverage market through partnerships as ready-to-drink options gain popularity.

title: Jack & Coke: Jack Daniel’s, Coca-Cola Set to Launch RTD Cocktail
summary: Coca-Cola and Jack Daniel's Tennessee Whiskey are partnering to launch a ready-to-drink (RTD) "Jack Daniel's & Coca-Cola" cocktail, starting in Mexico in late 2022. This product marks Coca-Cola's first alcoholic drink to carry its official branding and packaging, accelerating its push into the beverage alcohol segment. The RTD beverage will contain 5% ABV and also be available in a zero-sugar version, building on both companies' existing presence in the RTD market.

title: Jack Daniel’s and Coca-Cola Are Launching A New RTD Cocktail
summary: Jack Daniel's and Coca-Cola announced a collaboration to launch a canned, ready-to-drink (RTD) version of the classic Jack & Coke cocktail. The RTD beverage, which will be 5–9 percent ABV and also available in a zero-sugar format, was first released in Mexico in late 2022 and became available in the United States in May at a suggested price of $12.99 per 4-pack. This partnership marks the first time these two major beverage companies have collaborated on such a product, following a trend of "boozification" in the soft drink industry.

title: Jack Daniel’s Tennessee Whiskey launches new ready-to-drink cocktail with Coke
summary: Jack Daniel’s and Coca-Cola have partnered to release a new ready-to-drink pre-mixed cocktail combining Jack Daniel’s Old No. 7 Brand Tennessee Whiskey with Coca-Cola. The canned drink, which will be 5 percent ABV and also available in a zero-sugar version, is slated to launch initially in Mexico in late 2022, with no specific U.S. release date yet announced. This collaboration brings together two iconic American brands to offer consumers a convenient and portable cocktail option.

title: Jun 2022: No bartender required: Premixed Jack and Coke going on sale
summary: Coca-Cola Co. is partnering with Brown-Forman Corp., maker of Jack Daniel's Tennessee Whiskey, to launch a premixed, canned Jack and Coke. This new ready-to-drink cocktail, which will also have a zero-sugar option, is set to debut globally after first launching in Mexico later this year. The move capitalizes on the strong growth in the ready-to-drink alcoholic beverage market.

title: Brown-Forman and The Coca-Cola Company Announce Plans to Debut Jack Daniel’s® Tennessee Whiskey and Coca-Cola®™ Ready-to-Drink Cocktail
summary: Brown-Forman and The Coca-Cola Company announced a global partnership to launch a ready-to-drink (RTD) Jack & Coke cocktail, made with Jack Daniel’s Tennessee Whiskey and Coca-Cola. The pre-mixed beverage will debut in Mexico in late 2022 and will be available globally, with a zero-sugar option also planned. This collaboration brings together two iconic American brands to offer consumers a convenient and portable version of the classic bar drink.

title: Casey’s® and MTN DEW® Team up to Charge Your Outdoor Adventures This Summer With the Release of Exclusive New Flavor: MTN DEW OVERDRIVE
summary: Casey's and MTN DEW have collaborated to launch an exclusive new flavor called MTN DEW OVERDRIVE, available only at Casey's convenience stores starting in June. This new drink features a blend of mango, raspberry, and lime flavors, designed to fuel outdoor adventures. The partnership also introduces a new character, Benny the Bearalope, and integrates Casey's-themed elements into the beverage's label.

title: The Coca-Cola Company Announces Plans to Delay Listing of Coca-Cola Beverages Africa as a Publicly Traded Company
summary: The Coca-Cola Company announced it is delaying plans to list Coca-Cola Beverages Africa (CCBA) as a publicly traded company. This decision aligns with Coca-Cola's strategy to focus resources on its core brands and innovation, with the exact timing of a potential future IPO in 2023 dependent on macroeconomic conditions. Despite the delay, the company's intention to have an Africa-focused bottler trade as an independent public entity remains unchanged.

title: Mistaken Identity? Drink Maker Celsius Falls 10% On Monday
summary: Shares of Celsius Holdings, Inc. fell by 10% on Monday, likely due to mistaken identity by investors. The beverage company, which sells calorie-burning drinks, shares a name with cryptocurrency lending firm Celsius, which paused withdrawals and transfers on the same day. Celsius Holdings had not released any news or earnings, and its peers in the beverage sector saw only small movements.

title: PepsiCo to open Oklahoma distribution center
summary: PepsiCo Inc. is set to open a new distribution center in Lawton, Oklahoma, this month. The facility was constructed at the Lawton Airport Industrial Park to enhance product distribution efforts. This move aims to improve the company's logistical operations in the region.

title: Some Publicly Traded Bourbon Companies, in Honor of National Bourbon Day
summary: This article discusses publicly traded companies that offer exposure to the bourbon and broader alcohol market, despite most bourbon companies being privately owned. It highlights Brown-Forman (BF.B) as a key player with major bourbon brands and mentions other alcohol companies and ETFs like Invesco Dynamic Food and Beverage ETF (PBJ) for investment consideration. The piece also touches on general alcohol industry investments beyond bourbon.

title: CIO 100 Index 2022 in association with Equinix — Part 3
summary: The Business & Finance CIO 100 Index 2022, in association with Equinix, recognizes the top 100 Chief Information Officers in Ireland. This article, part three of a four-part series, highlights several key CIOs and IT leaders across various innovative companies in Ireland, detailing their experience, roles, and contributions. The index was officially launched at the Dublin Tech Summit with a breakfast reception and keynote address from Harry Moseley, Co-CIO of Zoom.

title: Why have Brown-Forman and Coca-Cola chosen Mexico for their RTD collaboration debut?
summary: Brown-Forman and Coca-Cola announced their plan to launch a Jack Daniel’s and Coca-Cola canned cocktail in Mexico, following prior RTD expansions in Brazil. This article analyzes why Mexico and Brazil are attractive markets for Ready-to-Drink (RTD) alcoholic beverages, citing their large beverage alcohol markets, established distribution networks, and sizable young, legal-drinking-age populations. Both countries show strong growth potential for RTDs, despite beer dominating their overall alcohol markets, driven by consumer interest in new flavors and convenience.

title: Why the Jack Daniel’s Coca-Cola tie-up could be a game-changer
summary: The collaboration between Brown-Forman and The Coca-Cola Co. to launch a co-branded Jack Daniel’s and Coca-Cola premixed drink is anticipated to be a significant market disruptor. This venture, starting in Mexico, represents a major step for Coca-Cola into alcoholic beverages and offers substantial benefits to both companies, particularly in expanding Jack Daniel's market penetration and leveraging Coca-Cola's global distribution. The article also prompts the broader spirits industry, especially Scotch brands, to consider similar RTD innovations to remain relevant with younger consumers.

title: Leftovers: PepsiCo brings Bubly into RTD mocktails; Minute Maid gives juice a Gen Z refresh
summary: PepsiCo's Bubly brand is launching a Bellini-inspired, nonalcoholic canned mocktail for the summer to capitalize on the growing demand for both RTD cocktails and nonalcoholic beverages. Concurrently, Minute Maid, owned by Coca-Cola, is introducing "Minute Maid Aguas Frescas" with a "Refreshing AF" marketing campaign aimed at Gen Z consumers to revitalize the struggling juice category. Additionally, Einstein Bros. Bagels and B&G Foods are collaborating to release an "Everything Bagel Seasoning" for grocery stores, encouraging its versatile use beyond breakfast foods.

title: smartwater Announces Zendaya as Newest Global Brand Ambassador
summary: smartwater has announced Zendaya as its newest global brand ambassador to launch a campaign that celebrates defining 'smart' on one's own terms. As part of this partnership, Zendaya will also collaborate with smartwater and the Global Water Challenge to support community water quality and access improvements, starting with her hometown of Oakland, California. This initiative builds on The Coca-Cola Company's long-standing investments in clean water access globally.

title: Coca-Cola has an ambitious plan to double its number of customers in the next few years
summary: Coca-Cola's global chief marketing officer, Manuel Arroyo, aims to double the company's consumer base by implementing QR codes on all packaging within three years to gather data and enhance marketing efficiency. This goal is supported by a new partnership with WPP, dubbed OpenX, which seeks to create a single, consistent global marketing strategy, moving away from fragmented approaches. The partnership emphasizes shared metrics with WPP, linking compensation to the growth of Coca-Cola's consumer base.

title: Coca-Cola wants to fill the space between beer and soft drinks
summary: Coca-Cola is strategically entering the flavored alcoholic beverage market to bridge the gap between beer and soft drinks, leveraging products like Topo Chico Hard Seltzer, Simply Mixed, and the newly launched ready-to-drink Jack Daniel’s & Coca-Cola. The company sees significant potential in at-home consumption for these offerings, including a zero-sugar option for the Jack and Coke line, and is also accelerating efforts around health and wellness, ESG, convenience, and functionality trends. Manuel Arroyo Prieto, Coca-Cola's chief marketing officer, highlighted the early success and potential of the Jack and Coke product, with global rollout plans beginning in Mexico.

title: Alcoholic Beverages Market Forecast Report 2022: USD 393.96 Billion Market Growth Opportunity by 2026| Technavio
summary: The global alcoholic beverages market is projected to grow by USD 393.26 billion from 2021 to 2026, advancing at a CAGR of 3.23%, according to Technavio. This growth is driven by the increasing popularity of craft beverages, mergers and acquisitions, and extensive marketing efforts, though challenges like counterfeit products and high taxation persist. Key players include Anheuser Busch InBev SA, Diageo Plc, and Heineken NV, with APAC expected to contribute significantly to market revenue.

title: Keurig Dr Pepper Expands RTD Portfolio With Atypique Addition
summary: Keurig Dr Pepper is set to acquire the rights to Atypique, a non-alcoholic, ready-to-drink cocktail brand, from Station Agro-Biotech. This strategic move aims to expand KDP's RTD portfolio and leverage Station Agro-Biotech's R&D capabilities with KDP’s sales and distribution network. The acquisition highlights the growing global RTD cocktails market, a sector that has seen significant growth and M&A activity.

title: Coca-Cola Co. leverages ‘intelligent experimentation’ to land ‘epic’ innovation
summary: Coca-Cola Co. is evolving its innovation strategy to focus on "intelligent experimentation," allowing it to test and scale new products and marketing strategies more efficiently. This approach involves running hundreds of controlled experiments to measure impact and systematically scaling successful initiatives globally. The company aims to foster fewer but more "epic" innovations and significantly improve its innovation success rate, which was previously only 3%.

title: Dr Pepper Maker Opens 300,000 sq ft Newbridge Manufacturing Plant
summary: Keurig Dr Pepper (KDP) Ireland has opened a 300,000 sq ft international operations hub in Newbridge, Co Kildare, marking its second manufacturing plant for beverage concentrate and its first outside North America. The facility plans to add 20 jobs by year-end, bringing the total to 100, and will serve as a 'centre of excellence' for concentrate production and global sourcing. This expansion underscores Ireland's reputation as a manufacturing and supply chain hub, as acknowledged by IDA Ireland CEO Martin Shanahan.

title: Coca-Cola among brands greenwashing over packaging, report says
summary: A report by the Changing Markets Foundation accuses major brands like Coca-Cola and Unilever of "greenwashing" by making misleading claims about the eco-friendliness of their plastic packaging. The report highlights examples of companies promoting packaging as recyclable or made from ocean plastic, while obscuring the true environmental impact or difficulties in actual recycling. It calls for regulators to take these claims seriously and advocates for systemic solutions like deposit return systems and plastic reduction.

title: Coke teams up with Marshmello for limited-edition flavor
summary: Coca-Cola is launching a limited-edition flavor in collaboration with Grammy-nominated artist Marshmello, marking the first time the company has co-created a beverage with an artist. The new strawberry and watermelon flavor will be available in regular and zero-sugar options with distinctive black-and-white cans, supported by a Twitch activation featuring "metamerch." This initiative is part of the Coca-Cola Creations platform, which aims to create unique flavors and position Coca-Cola as a lifestyle brand through merchandise and virtual experiences, while also promoting Marshmello's new song "Numb."

title: What's the Impact of the Strong Dollar on My Portfolio?
summary: The strong U.S. dollar, experiencing its biggest rally in 20 years, negatively impacts non-U.S. fund returns and profitability for American companies operating overseas. While it offers advantages for consumers traveling abroad, investors in international stocks and bonds face challenges due to unfavorable exchange rates and increased repayment costs for dollar-denominated debt. Despite the difficulties, some Morningstar analysts suggest currency hedging can minimize volatility, and others view the current currency weakness as an attractive buying opportunity for international funds.

title: Coca-Cola Continues Digital Experience Drive With Marshmello Tie-up
summary: Coca-Cola is launching a new collaboration with Grammy-nominated music producer Marshmello as part of its Coca-Cola Creations platform. This limited-edition drink will combine Marshmello's favorite flavors, strawberry and watermelon, with the taste of Coca-Cola, and will be packaged in distinct black and white cans. This initiative follows the successful first release, "Intergalactic," and aims to drive digital experiences through collaboration, creativity, and cultural connections.

title: The Cheesecake Factory Brings Basque Cheesecake to Its Menu for the First Time Ever
summary: The Cheesecake Factory is introducing a new Classic Basque Cheesecake to its menu, coinciding with National Cheesecake Day on July 30. This crustless cheesecake, originating from San Sebastian, Spain, is known for its burnt top and ultra-creamy center, and will be served with fresh berries and whipped cream. The company will also continue its long-standing support for Feeding America, donating a portion of cheesecake sales to the hunger-relief organization.

title: 2022 State of the Beverage Industry | Sports, protein drinks adapt to the market alongside functional beverages
summary: The sports and protein drinks category is rapidly adapting to the evolving beverage market, driven by consumer demand for functional and hybrid beverages, as well as low- and no-calorie options. Sales in this sector are showing strong growth, with sports drinks achieving $9.9 billion in dollar sales, a 17.8% year-over-year increase. The market is also seeing a significant trend towards plant-based ingredients and products offering additional health benefits like immunity, digestive health, and sustainability.

title: Diageo partners with Vita Coco on canned cocktail beverage
summary: Diageo is collaborating with The Vita Coco Company to launch a new line of premium canned cocktails called Vita Coco Spiked with Captain Morgan. These rum-based cocktails, available in three flavors, will hit the market in early 2023, capitalizing on the rapid growth of the ready-to-drink cocktail category. The partnership leverages both companies' market leadership in their respective sectors to expand their brand reach and offer a differentiated product.

title: Keurig Dr Pepper achieves 11% PCR use
summary: Keurig Dr Pepper increased its post-consumer resin (PCR) use in plastic packaging to 11% in 2021, up from 2% the previous year, primarily by utilizing 100% recycled PET bottles for several brands. This progress keeps the company on track for its goal of 25% PCR use by 2025 and eliminated 57 million pounds of virgin plastic last year. The shift also contributed to a 9% reduction in Scope 1 and 2 greenhouse gas emissions compared to its 2018 baseline.

title: E.l.f. appeals to gamers with themed line of beauty, skincare products
summary: E.l.f. Cosmetics has launched "Game Up," a limited-edition line of eight beauty and skincare products specifically targeting the gaming community. This collection will be available on E.l.f.'s website, Target, and Shoppers Drug Mart, featuring gamified names and hidden codes for loyalty rewards. E.l.f. is promoting the line through a live, retro-themed arcade event in Los Angeles, livestreamed on its Twitch channel, leveraging its existing strategy of engaging with gaming influencers and communities since 2020.

title: Coca-Cola Beverages Florida Breaks Ground On New Distribution Center At U.S. 301 & Causeway Blvd.
summary: Coca-Cola Beverages Florida, the largest minority-owned business in Florida, has broken ground on an 800,000 sq. ft. complex in Tampa, located at U.S. Highway 301 and Causeway Boulevard. This state-of-the-art facility represents a $250 million investment and will serve as a fully automated fulfillment center and corporate offices. The groundbreaking ceremony was attended by local officials and partners, highlighting the company's significant economic impact and community involvement.

title: Ofertas laborales en Coca-Cola Andina: Conoce las vacantes disponibles y cómo postular
summary: Coca-Cola Andina, one of the largest Coca-Cola bottlers globally, has numerous job openings, primarily in the Metropolitana region of Chile. These roles range from administrative positions to sales, including specific opportunities for route salespeople, mechanical technicians, quality inspectors, and logistics assistants. Interested candidates can apply through the trabajando.cl website by creating an account, filling out a form, and submitting their CV.

title: Vita Coco launches its first packaged coconut juice in sustainable aluminium cans
summary: Vita Coco has launched its first ready-to-drink coconut juice, packaged in sustainable 16.9-ounce aluminium cans. This new product extends the shelf-life of the juice and leverages aluminium's infinite recyclability for a circular economy. The juice comes in mango and original with pulp flavors, is gluten-free, and non-GMO, marking Vita Coco's entry into the refreshing drinks category.

title: Former Coca-Cola exec joins Lemon Perfect
summary: Former Coca-Cola Co. executive Jim Brennan has joined Lemon Perfect, a flavored lemon water brand, as president and chief revenue officer. Mr. Brennan, who previously served as a board member and strategic adviser, is tasked with scaling the company, which quadrupled its business in 2021 and aims for significant distribution growth. He plans to leverage his three decades of experience to make Lemon Perfect the leading brand in the enhanced water category.

title: A Warren Buffett Protégée Strikes Out on Her Own (Published 2022)
summary: Tracy Britt Cool, a former top lieutenant to Warren Buffett at Berkshire Hathaway, has launched her own investment firm, Kanbrick, applying the investment principles she learned from him. After a decade working closely with Buffett, Ms. Britt Cool, 37, left Berkshire in early 2020 to build her own firm, focusing on finding companies with strong, defensible business models. She aims to apply Buffett's investment philosophy, emphasizing "moats," understanding businesses, and a "margin of safety."

title: HK's Swire Pacific buys Coca-Cola bottling operations in Vietnam, Cambodia
summary: Hong Kong-based conglomerate Swire Pacific Ltd announced on Monday its acquisition of Coca-Cola's packaging and distribution operations in Vietnam and Cambodia. This $1.02 billion cash deal marks Swire Pacific's expansion into the Southeast Asian beverages market, purchasing Coca-Cola Indochina through its Swire Beverages and Swire Coca-Cola units.

title: Hong Kong's Swire Pacific Acquires Coca-Cola Bottling Operations In Vietnam & Cambodia
summary: Hong Kong-based Swire Pacific Ltd, through its subsidiary Swire Coca-Cola Limited, is set to acquire Coca-Cola's packaging and distribution operations in Vietnam and Cambodia for $1.02 billion in cash. This acquisition marks Swire Coca-Cola's first investment in Southeast Asia, expanding its franchise population by 15% to 876 million people. The move aligns with Swire Coca-Cola's strategy to increase its bottling business's global scale, volume, and revenues.

title: PepsiCo CEO: Consumers continuing to bet on health
summary: PepsiCo CEO Ramon Laguarta discussed how consumer preferences are driving the company's strategy in snacks and beverages. He highlighted the significant and "unstoppable" trend toward non-sugar options in beverages, citing Gatorade Zero's success, and noted a strong consumer focus on "permissible snacks" and portion control. Laguarta emphasized that health remains a key long-term vector for consumer choices, influencing PepsiCo's innovation and commercial strategies.

title: Carolyn Everson Elected to Board of Directors of The Coca-Cola Company
summary: The Coca-Cola Company announced the election of Carolyn Everson to its Board of Directors. Everson brings extensive experience from leadership roles at Instacart, Facebook (now Meta), Microsoft, and Viacom, where she was involved in global business and sales. Her appointment is expected to provide valuable knowledge and perspective to the company given her background in media and consumer-facing businesses.

title: Carolyn Everson Re-Emerges With a Seat on Coca-Cola Board
summary: Carolyn Everson, a former executive at Facebook, Microsoft, and Instacart, has been elected to The Coca-Cola Company's Board of Directors. Everson, who left Instacart at the end of last year, already serves on the board of talent agency CAA and has been working as an advisor and agency investor. Her appointment adds significant digital and tech experience to Coca-Cola's board.

title: Swire Coca-Cola to acquire Coca-Cola bottling businesses in Vietnam and Cambodia
summary: Swire Coca-Cola Limited, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Swire Pacific Limited, is set to acquire Coca-Cola bottling businesses in Vietnam and Cambodia. This acquisition marks Swire Coca-Cola's first investment in Southeast Asia, significantly expanding its operating footprint and franchise population to approximately 876 million people. The move capitalizes on the region's dynamic non-alcoholic beverage market, valued at over $6 billion and projected to grow at a CAGR of over 6% until 2036.

title: GALLERY: Coca-Cola mural returns to downtown Panama City
summary: The Panama City Coca-Cola Bottling Company hosted a grand unveiling ceremony for a restored Coca-Cola mural in downtown Panama City on Wednesday, July 20, 2022. Artist Logan Flint, who helped paint the mural, and local personalities like Wes Morgan of Coca-Cola and Pam Armstrong of TomÕs Hot Dogs were present. Jayson Kretzer, Executive Director of the Bay Arts Alliance, was also acknowledged for his support of downtown murals.

title: Coca-Cola Bottling Company celebrating 123 years in Chattanooga
summary: Coca-Cola Bottling Company United is celebrating 123 years of bottling in Chattanooga, marking the city as home to the first bottled Coca-Cola. The company is partnering with local businesses like Rock City, Ruby Falls, the Tennessee Aquarium, and Chattanooga Airport to give away free Cokes and encourage community celebration using #CocaColaOurTown. Chattanooga is recognized as a "Coke town" given its significant history with the company.

title: Coca-Cola’s Globally Experienced CFO Named as New President
summary: Coca-Cola's chief financial officer, John Murphy, who has extensive international experience, has been named the company's new president, effective October 1. He will retain his CFO responsibilities while taking on the presidency, succeeding Brian Smith. Murphy's past roles include leading the Asia Pacific group and significant time working in Japan, where he contributed to the development of Georgia Coffee.

title: Market saturation prompts hard seltzers to differentiate through key attributes
summary: The hard seltzer market, once a rapidly growing segment, is experiencing saturation and deceleration. Experts note that while beer-centric seltzers have slowed, spirits-based seltzers, largely driven by brands like High Noon, are showing significant growth. To maintain relevance, hard seltzer brands are focusing on differentiation through attributes like low calories, low ABV, natural flavors, and targeting specific consumer demographics like Gen X and millennials, as well as incorporating trends from the spirits market such as tequila-based RTDs.

title: The Coca-Cola Company Q2 Profit Decreases, but beats estimates
summary: The Coca-Cola Company reported a decrease in Q2 profit to $1.91 billion, or $0.44 per share, compared to $2.64 billion last year. However, adjusted earnings of $0.70 per share beat analysts' estimates of $0.67 per share. The company's revenue increased by 9.7% to $11.33 billion for the quarter.

title: From burgers to hi-tech gadgets, stressed consumers buy cheap
summary: Global consumers are showing mixed signals due to record inflation, with lower-income households sticking to essential goods and cheaper options, while wealthier consumers continue to splurge on luxury items and travel. Companies like Walmart, McDonald's, Coca-Cola, and Unilever are seeing varying impacts, with some raising prices successfully and others considering more discount options to cater to stressed consumers. The market reflects a divide, highlighting economic strain on some segments while others remain resilient in their spending habits.

title: Coca-Cola Tops Estimates on Higher Prices, Raises Guidance
summary: Coca-Cola's second-quarter sales surpassed expectations, leading the company to raise its full-year guidance. Despite decades-high inflation and a 12% average increase in product prices, consumers continued to pay more for its beverages. The company attributed some of the price increase to product mix changes, while still gaining market share globally.

title: Walmart's slashed profit outlook sends warning about state of the American consumer
summary: Walmart significantly cut its profit forecast due to inflation causing consumers to spend more on necessities and less on discretionary items like clothing. This shift in spending habits is impacting other major retailers, leading to increased discounts and potential inventory issues across the industry. While discounters like Walmart might see more foot traffic for groceries, their lower profit margins on essential goods are affecting overall profitability, signaling a challenging environment for the American consumer and retail sector.

title: Coca-Cola raises revenue forecast as soda demand defies price hikes
summary: Coca-Cola Co raised its full-year revenue forecast due to strong demand for its sugary sodas, despite increased prices intended to offset higher costs. Global sales volumes grew 8% in the second quarter, and the company plans further price hikes in response to rising costs. Net revenue for the quarter exceeded analyst expectations, although operating margins were impacted by higher expenses.

title: Coca-Cola sees strong consumer demand despite rising prices
summary: Coca-Cola reported strong financial results for its second quarter, with a 12% rise in net revenue and an 8% increase in global unit case volume, despite rising prices due to inflation. The company raised its top-line guidance for the second half of the year, expecting 12-13% organic revenue growth and 5-6% comparable earnings per share growth, while closely monitoring consumer behavior as costs continue to climb. CFO John Murphy will also assume the role of president in September.

title: Coca-Cola Posts Higher Quarterly Sales Despite Price Increases
summary: Coca-Cola reported strong second-quarter sales and increased its revenue outlook for the year, largely due to consumers returning to events and travel destinations despite rising prices. The beverage company's success comes as inflation continues to climb, pushing consumer price indices to their highest levels in decades. Consumers are demonstrating a willingness to pay more for soda, contributing to Coca-Cola's higher quarterly sales.

title: Constellation Brands debuts Woodbridge wine and soda mashup
summary: Constellation Brands' Woodbridge is launching a new wine soda that blends white wine with classic soda flavors like lemon-lime, orange, and grapefruit, available in 250-milliliter cans with 7% ABV. This move reflects a broader trend of beverage companies blurring the lines between alcoholic and non-alcoholic categories, offering consumers more convenient and less intimidating options. The introduction aims to attract drinkers seeking alternatives to traditional wines and could provide a boost to the wine category, which has seen stagnant consumption in recent years.

title: Coca-Cola eliminating green PET in North America
summary: Coca-Cola is phasing out green PET plastic bottles from its North American operations, affecting brands like Sprite. This change is part of a broader move to simplify recycling processes. The article highlights this development within the plastics industry.

title: Coca-Cola increased marketing spend to create brand value amid price hikes
summary: The Coca-Cola Company reported a 12% increase in net revenues to $11.3 billion in Q2 2022, exceeding analyst expectations due to pricing increases and global sales volume growth. To justify price hikes and create brand value, the company increased its marketing spend, focusing on experiential campaigns linking consumption with consumer passions like music and gaming, and leveraging digital-first strategies and cultural activations. Coca-Cola also raised its full-year organic revenue guidance, preparing for a challenging consumer environment by stepping up investments and utilizing data for better consumer reach.

title: Coca-Cola to keep passing through costs
summary: Coca-Cola Co. plans to continue increasing prices on its products to offset rising commodity and operating costs, expecting organic revenue growth of 12% to 13% for the fiscal year. Executives are monitoring a potential recession but believe the company has lead time before it impacts their strong brands and grocery categories. Despite a decrease in net income for the second quarter, net operating revenues increased, driven by higher prices and concentrate sales, and unit case volume grew across categories.

title: Jacksonville Jaguars Announce Partnership with Coca-Cola Beverages Florida
summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars announced a multi-year partnership with Coca-Cola Beverages Florida, LLC (Coke Florida), making it the team's official soft drink and water partner. This agreement grants Coke Florida exclusive rights to provide beverages like Coca-Cola brands and smartwater at TIAA Bank Field for Jaguars games and other events. Both organizations anticipate growth and new audience reach in the Jacksonville market through this collaboration.

title: Sprite shifting from green to clear bottles to boost recycling
summary: Coca-Cola is transitioning Sprite bottles from green to clear PET plastic in North America, starting in August, to enhance their recyclability into new beverage bottles. This move, along with similar changes for other brands and the use of 100% recycled plastic for Dasani, aims to increase the availability of food-grade recycled PET (rPET). The company expects these changes to save over 20 million pounds of virgin plastic and cut more than 25,000 metric tons of greenhouse gas emissions in 2023, supporting a circular plastic packaging economy.

title: SEE IT: The Coca-Cola Company is making a big change to its Sprite bottles
summary: The Coca-Cola Company is changing its Sprite bottles from green plastic to clear plastic to improve recyclability and promote a "circular economy" for plastics. This move aims to increase the amount of recycled PET used in new beverage containers, addressing a demand that currently outpaces supply. Other Coca-Cola brands like Fresca, Seagram’s, Mello Yello, and Dasani are also transitioning to clear or 100% recycled bottles.

title: Sprite is ditching its iconic green bottle — and that’s good for the environment
summary: Coca-Cola is transitioning Sprite from its iconic green plastic bottles to clear plastic bottles starting August 1 in North America. This change aims to improve the recyclability of the bottles, as clear plastic can be recycled into new bottles more times than colored plastic. Other Coca-Cola brands like Fresca, Seagram's, and Mello Yello will also adopt clear bottles, and Dasani bottled water will use bottles made entirely from recycled plastic, saving millions of pounds of new plastic.

title: Coca-Cola prioritizes core brands and focuses on digital strategy
summary: Coca-Cola's business in China improved in June 2022 due to a focus on core branded products and a shift to digital engagement as consumers moved to at-home consumption. The company's Q2 2022 global revenue rose 12 percent year-on-year to $11.33 billion, exceeding market expectations, and it saw strong unit case volume growth globally and in Asia Pacific, particularly in China. This growth was supported by new product launches and strong e-commerce performance during the "June 18" festival.
