title: Coca-Cola to transition green plastic portfolio to clear PET bottles in North America
summary: The Coca-Cola Company is transitioning its green plastic beverage bottles, starting with Sprite in North America, to clear PET to improve recyclability into new beverage bottles. This move aims to increase the availability of food-grade recycled PET (rPET) and drive a circular economy for plastic. Additionally, DASANI will roll out bottles made from 100% recycled PET, and Coca-Cola has pledged to increase refillable/returnable packaging options globally by 2030.

title: Coca-Cola to eliminate green PET in North America
summary: The Coca-Cola Co. is transitioning all of its green PET plastic bottles to clear PET in North America to improve bottle-to-bottle recycling. This change, which began with Sprite on August 1st, will include other brands like Fresca, Seagram’s, and Mello Yello in the coming months. The company is also producing DASANI bottles made from 100% recycled PET.

title: The Glimpse Group Completes Its Previously Announced Brightline Interactive Transaction, Making It One Of The Largest Independent Immersive Technology Software and Services Companies
summary: The Glimpse Group, Inc. announced the completion of its merger with Brightline Interactive (BLI), significantly expanding its footprint in the immersive technology market. This transaction brings Glimpse's combined annual revenue run rate to approximately $15 million and grows its team to over 200 immersive technology professionals. The merger also adds new Tier 1 customers, two patents from BLI, and strengthens Glimpse's executive team, positioning it as a leading enterprise-focused immersive technology software and services company.

title: Coca-Cola Consolidated to terminate primary U.S. pension plan through lump sum, group annuity
summary: Coca-Cola Consolidated announced its intention to terminate its primary U.S. pension plan. This termination will be executed through a combination of lump-sum payments and a group annuity. This move affects the company's pension funds.

title: Spirits-Based Seltzers Reach 9.1% Share of Segment; Truly Sheds Most Share; White Claw Stabilizes; Topo Chico Largest Share Gainer
summary: Spirits-based hard seltzers now comprise 9.1% of the total hard seltzer market, which has seen overall declines. While brands like Truly and several Anheuser-Busch InBev seltzers are losing significant market share, spirits-based High Noon and Molson Coors' Topo Chico Hard Seltzer are experiencing triple-digit growth and gaining share. The report from Jefferies highlights a shift in consumer preference and increased competition in the evolving hard seltzer segment.

title: An Update on our Russian operations
summary: Coca-Cola HBC has announced significant changes to its Russian operations, ceasing all production and sales of The Coca-Cola Company brands in Russia with no plans to reintroduce them. The company will establish a smaller, locally managed entity called Multon Partners, focusing on existing local brands like Dobry, Rich, and Moya Semya, with raw materials sourced domestically. This move responds to the ongoing geopolitical crisis, while Coca-Cola HBC continues to support its employees and communities in Ukraine and neighboring countries.

title: Houston Texans unveil Fan First Deals to elevate gameday experience for fans
summary: The Houston Texans, in partnership with Aramark, have announced "Fan First Deals" for the 2022 season, significantly lowering prices on four popular concession items at home games. This initiative aims to enhance the gameday experience by making food and drinks more affordable. Prices for items like hot dogs, chicken tender baskets, soda, and beer will see an average decrease of 20%, building on existing low-price offerings for water and beer outside the stadium.

title: Mexico Should Stop Making Beer in Drought-Plagued North, AMLO Says
summary: Mexican President Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador has suggested that beer production should cease in the drought-stricken northern region of Mexico, the world's largest beer exporter. He noted that areas like Monterrey, home to major beermakers, have faced severe water scarcity. Lopez Obrador stated that the government would support companies willing to relocate their production to the south or southeast of the country.

title: Coca-Cola distributor of the triangle announces plans to move operations to Chatham County, Apex
summary: The Durham Coca-Cola Bottling Company announced plans to relocate its operations to Chatham County, specifically at the intersection of Highway 751 and US 64, with an Apex address. The move involves constructing a 175,000-square-foot facility, bringing 180-200 employees, and aims for enhanced sustainable building specifications. The new location will centralize its service area, covering multiple counties in the Triangle region.

title: Coca-Cola HBC agrees to acquire Three Cents
summary: Coca-Cola HBC AG announced its agreement to acquire ESM Effervescent Sodas Management Limited ("Three Cents") for an enterprise value of €45 million. Three Cents is a fast-growing, super-premium adult sparkling beverage and mixer business. This acquisition strengthens Coca-Cola HBC's 24/7 beverage partner strategy and expands its portfolio in the super-premium segment.

title: Durham Coca-Cola leaving headquarters for new Apex location
summary: Durham Coca-Cola Bottling Company, established in 1905, is relocating its headquarters from Hillsborough Street to a new 170,000-square-foot facility in Apex, North Carolina. The groundbreaking for the new facility is set for the first quarter of 2023, with completion expected by 2024. The new headquarters, which will be dedicated to the current president's grandfather and father, will be built in partnership with Beacon Partners and is designed to feature sustainable building specifications and be a more efficient working environment.

title: KeelClip, a fiber-based can packaging solution, coming to U.S. shelves soon
summary: Graphic Packaging International has launched its KeelClip fiber-based can packaging solution in the United States, with the first installation at Liberty Coca-Cola Beverages' facility in Elmsford, NY. This sustainable technology replaces plastic rings and shrink wrap for can multipacks, having already saved over 3 million pounds of plastic in 2021 globally. Liberty Coca-Cola Beverages expects this transition to remove 75,000 pounds of plastic packaging annually from its supply chain in the Northeastern U.S. markets.

title: P&G, Coca-Cola, and McCormick Develop Innovative Recycling Practices
summary: Procter & Gamble, Coca-Cola, and McCormick are implementing various innovative recycling practices to enhance sustainability. P&G is transitioning to recyclable paperboard packaging for its laundry pods, aiming to reduce plastic waste significantly. Coca-Cola is deploying reverse vending machines in the U.K. to encourage bottle return and recycling, offering incentives to consumers. McCormick is adopting 100% post-consumer recycled PET bottles for its food dyes, which will substantially decrease its carbon footprint.

title: Coke bottles taste of dreams for latest experimental flavor
summary: Coca-Cola has launched "Dreamworld," the fourth and final product from its Creations platform for 2022, aiming to capture the taste of dreams and target Gen Z consumers. The launch includes digital and experiential activations like an AR music experience with Tomorrowland and a digital fashion collection for the metaverse. This strategy follows previous Creations flavors, which have contributed to Coca-Cola's reported 12% year-on-year growth in net revenue to $11.3 billion.

title: Coca-Cola bottler to detail costs of exiting Russia
summary: Coca-Cola HBC AG, the bottler for Coca-Cola Co, is set to detail the costs associated with exiting Russia after five months of winding down operations. The bottler has stopped producing and selling Coke-branded products in Russia, renaming its local business Multon Partners and focusing on local brands. This full exit is critical for Coca-Cola Co's legal efforts in Russia to protect its brand and prevent unauthorized imports of its products.

title: Coca-Cola HBC flags one-time $195 mln hit from Russian operations
summary: Coca-Cola HBC, a bottler for Coca-Cola Co, announced a one-time charge of 190 million euros ($195.4 million) in the first half of the year due to costs associated with halting sales and production of Coca-Cola products in Russia. Despite this hit, the company reinstated its annual comparable operating profit forecast to between 740 million and 820 million euros, exceeding market expectations. Its shares rose 6% following the announcement, as strong emerging markets boosted net sales revenue, though net profit was affected by the Russian charge.

title: Coca-Cola bottler removes plastic with launch of fiber-based multi-pack in the US
summary: Liberty Coca-Cola Beverages, a US Coca-Cola bottler, is the first in the country to adopt Graphic Packaging International's fiber-based KeelClip solution for multi-pack packaging, eliminating plastic rings and shrink wrap. This transition is expected to remove 75,000 pounds of plastic packaging annually from the supply chain across its northeastern US territories. The KeelClip technology, already successful in Europe, also offers hygiene benefits by protecting can tops and ergonomic carrying features.

title: New Coca-Cola distribution facility coming to Apex
summary: Durham Coca-Cola Bottling Company announced plans to build a new 170,000-square-foot distribution facility in Apex, N.C. The facility, expected to break ground in Q1 2023 and open in 2024, will be located at US 64 and NC 751. It is designed to be a zero-landfill waste facility and will distribute Coca-Cola, Dr Pepper, and Monster products.

title: Coca-Cola's new flavor 'Dreamworld' supposedly tastes like dreams
summary: Coca-Cola is releasing "Dreamworld," its fourth and final limited-edition flavor in the Coca-Cola Creations series, which claims to taste like dreams. This abstract flavor is part of a marketing campaign targeting Gen Z, known for its unique flavors and multimedia collaborations, and is intended to provoke discovery and debate among consumers. The release is accompanied by an augmented reality music experience and a digital fashion collection, continuing the trend of conceptual flavors despite some criticism aimed at the company's "innovation."

title: Monster Beverage Corp. stock outperforms competitors despite losses on the day
summary: Monster Beverage Corp. (MNST) stock declined by 0.58% on Thursday, closing at $89.30, yet still outperformed competitors Coca-Cola Co. and PepsiCo Inc. despite the market's mixed trading session. The stock closed $10.51 short of its 52-week high, with trading volume below its 50-day average. This performance highlights Monster Beverage's relative strength against its peers in a challenging market.

title: Florida Citrus Commissioners Reappointed
summary: Governor Ron DeSantis announced the reappointment of all nine members to the Florida Citrus Commission on August 5. The commission members, who include leaders from various citrus-related businesses and organizations, will continue their roles, pending confirmation by the Florida Senate. This article lists each reappointed commissioner along with their professional backgrounds and affiliations.

title: Watch the newest commercials from T-Mobile, Acorns, Cîroc and more
summary: This article highlights new commercials from various brands, including T-Mobile, Acorns (featuring Christopher Walken), Cîroc, Subway, and Principal Financial Group. It briefly mentions other topics covered by Ad Age, such as AI in campaigns and marketing winners and losers.

title: Ball shutters beverage can plants as alcohol demand declines
summary: Ball Corporation is permanently closing two beverage can facilities in Phoenix and St. Paul, Minnesota, due to softening consumer demand for alcohol and a need to optimize capacity. These closures, and the delay of a new plant in Nevada, are part of the company's efforts to increase operating efficiencies and save approximately $30 million in fixed costs per facility. The decision follows a period of record demand for aluminum cans in 2020 and a net loss of $174 million in Q2 amidst slower demand and higher cost inflation.

title: Graphic Packaging to launch KeelClip paperboard technology in US market
summary: Graphic Packaging International is partnering with Liberty Coca-Cola Beverages to launch its KeelClip paperboard packaging technology in the United States, starting with an installation in Elmsford, New York. This sustainable solution replaces plastic rings and shrink wrap for multipacks of cans with fiber-based packaging, aiming to remove 75,000 pounds of plastic annually from the supply chain. The technology has already seen significant success in Europe, contributing to a more sustainable future by reducing reliance on plastics.

title: PepsiCo Inc. stock rises Thursday, still underperforms market
summary: On Thursday, PepsiCo Inc. (PEP) stock saw a modest increase of 0.10% to $180.40, despite an overall positive trading day for the broader market. The stock remained just under its 52-week high, and its performance was mixed compared to competitors like Nestle S.A. ADR (NSRGY), Coca-Cola Co. (KO), and Unilever PLC ADR (UL). Trading volume for PepsiCo was below its 50-day average.

title: Keurig Dr Pepper denies reported talks to buy Bang Energy drink owner
summary: Keurig Dr Pepper denied reports that it is in talks to acquire Bang Energy drink owner, though it confirmed that M&A and brand partnerships are key to its growth strategy. The negotiations, reported by Bloomberg, suggested a potential valuation of over $2 billion for Bang. An acquisition would significantly bolster Keurig Dr Pepper's presence in the growing energy drink market, following Bang's recent exit from a distribution deal with PepsiCo.

title: Dippin' Dots debuts Times Square location
summary: Dippin' Dots has opened a new co-branded store in Times Square with its sister company, Doc Popcorn. The location is managed by multi-unit franchisee Neil Hershman and follows his successful openings in the Flatiron District and Downtown Brooklyn. This expansion aims to capture the high traffic of Times Square, a key tourist destination.

title: Southern Company renews as Proud Partner of the TOUR Championship
summary: Southern Company has renewed its partnership as a Proud Partner of the TOUR Championship through the 2027 tournament, continuing its long-standing support for the PGA TOUR's season finale. This agreement solidifies its role alongside The Coca-Cola Company and Accenture, with Southern Company remaining an Official Marketing Partner of the PGA TOUR. The company's involvement has significantly contributed to the tournament's charitable efforts, including the East Lake Foundation, Drew Charter School, First Tee – Metro Atlanta, and the annual Payne Stewart Award.

title: Conagra Brands names Tracy Schaefer SVP/CIO
summary: Conagra Brands Inc. has appointed Tracy Schaefer as Senior Vice President and Chief Information Officer, effective August 22, 2022. Schaefer has been with Conagra Brands since 2001 and has held various leadership roles in finance, IT, and global business services. CFO Dave Marberger highlighted her strong track record, deep business understanding, and strategic mindset as critical assets for the company's strategic plans.

title: Coca-Cola names new president for its largest operating unit
summary: Coca-Cola has appointed a new president for its largest operating unit. The new president previously served as chief people officer and chief of staff to the chairman and CEO of The Coca-Cola Company. This announcement was made by The Business Journals.

title: Coca-Cola names new president of North America operations
summary: Coca-Cola has appointed Jennifer Mann as the new president of its North America operating unit, effective January 1, 2023. Mann, who joined Coca-Cola in 1997, currently leads Global Ventures, overseeing acquisitions like Costa Coffee and the investment in Monster Beverage Corp. She replaces Alfredo Rivera, who will step down on December 31.

title: Coca-Cola Taps Jennifer Mann as President of Its North America Operating Unit
summary: Jennifer Mann has been appointed as the corporate senior vice president and president of Coca-Cola's North America operating unit, effective January 1, 2023. Mann, who previously led Global Ventures, has a 25-year career with the company and is recognized for scaling global acquisitions like Costa Coffee and Monster Beverage Corp. She will be replacing Alfredo Rivera, who is stepping down at the end of the year.

title: The Coca-Cola Company Appoints Jennifer Mann as President of the North America Operating Unit
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has appointed Jennifer Mann as the new president of its North America Operating Unit, effective January 1, 2023. She will succeed Alfredo Rivera, who will step down on December 31, 2022, and remain as a senior advisor until March 2023. Mann, who has been with Coca-Cola for 25 years, previously served as corporate senior vice president and president of Global Ventures, responsible for scaling acquisitions and brands such as Costa Coffee and Monster Beverage Corp.

title: Coca‑Cola supporting community access to clean and safe water through new 2030 Water Strategy
summary: Coca-Cola Philippines is strengthening its commitment to water stewardship with a new 2030 Water Strategy, focusing on increasing water use efficiency and addressing community water resource challenges. The company, through its Coca-Cola Foundation Philippines, has implemented initiatives like the Agos Program, which has made safe water accessible to underserved communities and enhanced water management practices. Coca-Cola Beverages Philippines, Inc. (CCBPI) was also recognized for its industry-leading water resource management, demonstrating a 31% decrease in absolute water consumption in 2020 and achieving a 132% water replenishment rate in the Philippines.

title: Coca-Cola appoints Jennifer Mann as president of North America operating unit
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has appointed Jennifer Mann as the new president of its North America operating unit, effective January 1, 2023. She will succeed Alfredo Rivera, who is stepping down after 38 years with the company. Mann, who joined Coca-Cola in 1997, currently serves as corporate senior vice president and president of Global Ventures.

title: Live Nation bets millions on high-tech reusable cups to combat plastic waste
summary: Live Nation is investing $5 million in Turn Systems to implement reusable cup programs at its venues and festivals, aiming to significantly reduce plastic waste. The system provides reusable cups and collection bins, with return rates varying from 58% to over 90% in trials at events like Lollapalooza and Sueños. This initiative is part of Live Nation's broader environmental efforts, which include a partnership with canned water company Liquid Death, with a goal to displace over 1 million single-use cups this year.

title: Starbucks taps PepsiCo veteran Laxman Narasimhan as CEO
summary: Starbucks Coffee Co. has appointed Laxman Narasimhan as its new CEO, effective October 1, 2022, succeeding interim CEO Howard Schultz. Narasimhan brings nearly 30 years of experience from global consumer-facing brands, including PepsiCo Inc., and will join the board of directors on April 1, 2023. During a transition period, he will immerse himself in the company's brand, culture, and "Reinvention" plan.

title: ¿Quieres reciclar? Coca-Cola se alía con Rappi para recolectar el PET de los consumidores
summary: Coca-Cola México y Rappi han lanzado un proyecto piloto para recolectar envases de PET y otros materiales reciclables directamente de los hogares de los consumidores en tres alcaldías de la Ciudad de México. Esta alianza busca incrementar las tasas de reciclaje en el país y acercar a las empresas a su meta de recolectar y reciclar el 100% de sus envases para 2030, en un contexto de altos costos de materias primas. El programa incentivará a los usuarios de Rappi a participar, contribuyendo a la economía circular.

title: Workday Rising: The Importance of Community and Connection
summary: This article highlights the upcoming Workday Rising conference, emphasizing the importance of community and connection among customers in a constantly changing world. Sheri Rhodes, Chief Customer Officer, expresses her excitement for the event, where attendees will learn from each other and Workday innovations to enhance their businesses and lives. The conference will feature customer stories on embracing change, preparing for the future of work, and adapting to industry-specific challenges.

title: Will there be an end to the soda price increase? Not likely. Here's why.
summary: The cost of soda has increased by over 45% in less than four years, with a 12-pack now retailing for upwards of $7. Consumers like Rachel Hatfield and Rebecca Dunn find these prices "ridiculous" and "stupid money," forcing them to cut back on purchases despite inflation. The rise in prices is attributed to inflation, increased aluminum costs, and the lack of significant competition between beverage giants PepsiCo and Coca-Cola, suggesting that these price hikes are likely to continue.

title: Barry Simpson to Step Down as Chief Platform Services Officer of The Coca-Cola Company
summary: The Coca-Cola Company announced that Barry Simpson will step down from his role as chief Platform Services officer, effective September 30, 2022, and will remain a senior advisor until February 2023. Simpson, who led the Platform Services organization since its creation in 2021, will see his responsibilities restructured under two new leaders, Neeraj Tolmare as CIO and another yet-to-be-named executive, both reporting to John Murphy. The article also provides details about Simpson's 14-year career history within the Coca-Cola system and a brief overview of The Coca-Cola Company.

title: Coca-Cola Restructures Platform Services
summary: The Coca-Cola Company is restructuring its platform services organization by splitting leadership responsibilities. Barry Simpson will step down, and the group will be led by Neeraj Tolmare as global CIO for digital and technology services, and a second executive for other services, both reporting to John Murphy. This restructuring is part of a larger initiative to build a networked global organization, which the company CEO states is a work in progress with ongoing improvements.

title: The Best Beauty Looks Of The 2022 Emmys
summary: This article showcases the best hair and makeup looks from the 74th Primetime Emmy Awards red carpet in 2022. It highlights various celebrities, detailing their hair and makeup artists and the products they used. The piece emphasizes the importance of red carpet glamour as a spectacle alongside the awards themselves.

title: Keurig Dr Pepper acquires equity stake in C4 Energy maker
summary: Keurig Dr Pepper is acquiring an approximately 30% ownership stake in Nutrabolt, the maker of C4 Energy, for $863 million. This investment also includes a long-term sales and distribution agreement to significantly expand C4 Energy's market presence. The move strengthens Keurig Dr Pepper's position in the rapidly growing performance energy drink market, making it Nutrabolt's largest investor behind its founder.

title: COCA-COLA PARTNERS WITH ATLANTA ARTISTS TO CELEBRATE ITS GEORGIA-BORN HERITAGE
summary: The Coca-Cola Company is partnering with eight local artists in Metro Atlanta to commission murals celebrating its Georgia-born heritage and the city's diverse culture. This initiative aims to feature Coca-Cola brands within the social tapestry of Atlanta's neighborhoods. One such mural by Fabian Williams is prominently displayed at the newly opened Black Art In America Gallery and Sculpture Garden in East Point, sponsored by Coca-Cola as part of this ongoing partnership.

title: Clorox Leans Into Scenario Planning for Never-Normal Supply Chain Future
summary: Clorox is investing significantly in ERP and supply chain improvements to navigate a volatile environment, upgrading its 20-year-old ERP to a cloud-based system and implementing new supply chain capabilities as part of a $500 million digital transformation. The company is focusing on more frequent forecasting and scenario planning, recognizing that while supply chain stability is improving, it will not return to pre-pandemic conditions. Clorox aims to automate manual processes and leverage data for better visibility, cost reduction, and optimized inventory levels.

title: Meet Dave & Buster’s New, Futuristic Revenue Stream
summary: Dave & Buster's is piloting a new "Game & Go" micro-market, developed in partnership with Coca-Cola and powered by Zippin's checkout-free technology, to address issues with food and beverage attachment among gamers. This automated store, located in Hollywood, Florida, offers snacks and drinks, including alcohol with ID monitoring, and aims to increase revenue without cannibalizing existing sales. The initiative reflects Dave & Buster's broader strategy to diversify revenue streams beyond traditional restaurant offerings, following significant financial growth and the acquisition of Main Event.

title: Me & My Team: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners, East Kilbride
summary: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners' East Kilbride factory is implementing a major vision for digitalization and automation, supported by significant investments in sustainability and efficiency. The site has reduced its carbon footprint by 47% since 2010, invested £32m in the past five years, and is pioneering initiatives like attached bottle caps and advanced monitoring systems. The article highlights their focus on continuous improvement, talent development, and preparing for future regulatory changes like Scotland's deposit return scheme.

title: Ogilvy Appoints Guillermo Vega Global Creative Lead for The Coca-Cola Company
summary: Ogilvy has appointed Guillermo Vega as the global creative network lead for The Coca-Cola Company, where he will be responsible for defining and driving the creative vision for TCCC's brand portfolio. Vega will be based in New York and join the leadership team of OpenX from WPP, the bespoke agency offering created for TCCC. His extensive experience includes leading Saatchi & Saatchi London and co-founding Wieden+Kennedy São Paulo, demonstrating a strong track record in growing creative agencies and working with significant brands.

title: Arca Continental announces new agreement with Coca-Cola
summary: Mexican bottling company Arca Continental has announced a new long-term collaboration agreement with Coca-Cola, covering markets in Mexico, Ecuador, Peru, and Argentina. This agreement aims to improve customer service, drive profitable growth, and implement better digital initiatives across Latin America. The collaboration underscores a long-standing commitment and seeks to align economic aspects, investments, and long-term business strategies for shared value creation.

title: Inside ASU's contract with Coca-Cola
summary: Arizona State University has a decade-long contract with Coca-Cola valued at $30 million, which includes stipulations for marketing Coke products and limits on competing beverages. Health experts and studies raise concerns about such contracts promoting sugar-sweetened beverages on university campuses, despite the financial benefits for ASU which go towards student engagement programs. The contract also involves extensive marketing requirements and raises questions about its impact on sustainability goals and student health choices.

title: Exclusive: PepsiCo ends Pepsi, 7UP production in Russia months after promising halt over Ukraine
summary: PepsiCo has stopped producing Pepsi, 7UP, and Mountain Dew in Russia, nearly six months after initially announcing a suspension of sales and production following the invasion of Ukraine. This decision came after Reuters found these products with recent production dates still widely available in Russia. The action aligns with PepsiCo's March 2022 pledge, though the company continues to sell essential goods like milk and baby food in the country.

title: Fries shortage resolved, successor to McDonald's in Russia eyes full reopening
summary: Vkusno & tochka, the successor to McDonald's in Russia, has resolved its potato supply issues and expects to have all 850 restaurants open by the end of the year. CEO Oleg Paroev reported positive results since opening on June 12, with sales occasionally exceeding those under the McDonald's brand, despite initial challenges. The company is also replacing imported ingredients with local products and is in talks with the last remaining former franchisee to join the brand.

title: How a Top Fidelity Growth Fund Is Navigating This Market
summary: Fidelity Growth Discovery FDSVX, co-managed by Jason Weiner and Asher Anolic, has navigated 2022's challenging market for growth stocks better than many peers by focusing on "growth quality" rather than simply high-growth potential. The fund emphasizes companies with strong gross margins and predictable earnings growth, incorporating names like Microsoft, Coca-Cola, and UnitedHealth Group, which are not typically associated with aggressive growth funds. This strategy has helped the fund outperform its category over various timeframes despite the overall market downturn.

title: The Coca-Cola Company Announces New Leaders in Operations
summary: The Coca-Cola Company announced new leadership appointments in its operations. Evguenia "Jeny" Stoichkova will become the president of Global Ventures, focusing on scaling acquisitions like Costa Coffee and Monster Beverage Corp. Sedef Salingan Sahin will succeed Stoichkova as president of the Eurasia & Middle East operating unit, both effective January 1, 2023.

title: What Kroger, Walmart, Target learned from China's Alibaba about grocery's future
summary: Kroger, Walmart, and Target have adopted an "Omnichannel Retail" strategy, a concept pioneered by Alibaba's Jack Ma in China with his "New Retail" model of high-tech Freshippo supermarkets. This strategy integrates brick-and-mortar stores with online orders, logistics, and data analytics to enhance efficiency and customer experience. Kroger, in particular, has seen significant digital growth, aiming to double its digital revenues by the end of 2023, and investing heavily in automation and supply chain management.

title: Evguenia Stoichkova Named President Of Coca-Cola Global Ventures
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has appointed Evguenia Stoichkova as the new president of its Global Ventures unit, effective January 1, 2023. In this role, she will be responsible for scaling the company's acquisitions and brands, including Costa Coffee and Monster Beverage Corp. Stoichkova previously served as president of Coca-Cola's Eurasia and Middle East operating unit, and will be succeeded by Sedef Salingan Sahin.

title: Diageo to leave US spirits trade body DISCUS
summary: Diageo has announced its decision not to renew its membership with the Distilled Spirits Council of the United States (DISCUS), the largest advocate for the US spirits industry. The company stated this is part of a review of its industry organization memberships, aiming to focus resources on key strategic priorities while remaining an active participant in the industry. Despite leaving, Diageo will continue to be involved in certain DISCUS-affiliated initiatives.

title: MOLSON COORS EXPANDS EXCLUSIVE AGREEMENT WITH THE COCA-COLA COMPANY TO LAUNCH TOPO CHICO SPIRITED LINE OF CANNED COCKTAILS
summary: Molson Coors Beverage Company has expanded its exclusive agreement with The Coca-Cola Company to launch Topo Chico Spirited, a new line of spirit-based, ready-to-drink canned cocktails. This move builds on the success of Topo Chico Hard Seltzer and Simply Spiked Lemonade, further expanding Molson Coors' premium beverage portfolio. Topo Chico Spirited will be available in over 20 markets in 2023, featuring cocktails made with 100% real spirits, including premium tequila.

title: Coca-Cola and WWF team up for nature
summary: The Coca-Cola Company and World Wildlife Fund (WWF) have renewed their partnership, focusing on climate resilience, agriculture, freshwater, and plastic waste. This collaboration builds on over a decade of work on water security and aims to address the critical challenges of climate change and biodiversity loss through a more holistic approach. They report progress in sustainable ingredient sourcing, plastic waste reduction, and advancing climate targets, planning to leverage their partnership for global, locally relevant solutions.

title: The Walt Disney Company Appoints Veteran Media and Technology Executive Carolyn Everson to Its Board of Directors
summary: The Walt Disney Company announced the appointment of Carolyn Everson, a seasoned media and technology executive, to its Board of Directors, effective November 21. This decision reinforces Disney's commitment to a strong, independent board and has the support of Third Point LLC, an investment firm. Everson's extensive experience from companies like Facebook (Meta) and Instacart is expected to bring valuable perspective to Disney's global brand expansion and long-term growth strategies.

title: Coca-Cola Teams Up With Bill Nye to Demystify Recycling
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has partnered with science personality Bill Nye to create an animated film that demystifies the plastic recycling process. The stop-motion film, created by Mackinnon & Saunders, features an animated Bill Nye explaining the end-to-end recycling journey. This initiative aims to educate consumers on recycling and highlights Coca-Cola's efforts in sustainable development and partnerships with organizations like WWF and The Ellen MacArthur Foundation.

title: Biggest Plastic Polluter named Sponsor for COP27 – Greenpeace Reaction
summary: Greenpeace reacted to the announcement that Coca-Cola, identified as the world's biggest plastic polluter, will sponsor COP27. Greenpeace criticizes Coca-Cola for producing 120 billion throwaway plastic bottles annually, primarily from fossil fuels, which exacerbates both plastic and climate crises. They argue that this sponsorship undermines COP27's goals and urge Coca-Cola to end its reliance on single-use plastics to truly address climate change.

title: Coca-Cola bottler makes major change to aluminum can packaging: ‘First of its kind’
summary: Liberty Coca-Cola Beverages is implementing a significant environmental change by replacing plastic rings on its aluminum can packaging with fiber-based paper packaging. This initiative, described as "first of its kind" in the U.S., aims to eliminate 75,000 pounds of plastic annually and mitigate harm to marine life. The new packaging will be distributed in Pennsylvania, New Jersey, and New York.

title: Coca-Cola Opens West Coast HQ at Spectrum Terrace
summary: The Coca-Cola Co. has opened its new West Coast operations facility at the Spectrum Terrace office campus in Irvine, California. This nearly 10,000-square-foot office will serve as the headquarters for the company's West Zone operations, overseeing over a dozen states and territories. The new space is designed for "connection, collaboration and coaching" for its 125 employees and positions Coca-Cola closer to key markets and customers, including potential partnerships with companies like Amazon, which is also moving into the campus.

title: Award-winning Valleys pub named one of the best in the UK
summary: The Lion Hotel in Treorchy, Rhondda, has been recognized as one of the best pubs in the UK, winning the Community Hero award at the 2022 Great British Pub Awards. It was the only Welsh establishment to receive an award this year among four Welsh nominees. The pub is known for its strong community involvement, including acting as a shop during the pandemic and collaborating with local schools.

title: Seth Goldman Goes 'Back Into The Iced Tea World' With New Brand Just Ice Tea - Exclusive Interview
summary: Seth Goldman, founder of the discontinued Honest Tea, has launched a new tea brand called Just Ice Tea, with much of his original team. The new brand, which debuted in September 2022, emphasizes fair trade and organic ingredients, using honey or agave instead of cane sugar, aligning with his company Eat the Change's focus on planet-friendly food. Just Ice Tea launched with six flavors, aiming to fill the void left by Honest Tea and support its former suppliers, with plans for expanded distribution and future innovation.

title: WPP acquires branding agency Passport to expand creative and design offerings
summary: WPP has acquired Passport Brand Design, a Southern California-based branding agency founded in 2004. This acquisition aims to expand WPP's creative and design offerings, integrating Passport into VMLY&R's global network. The move aligns with WPP's strategy to enhance core creative capabilities and deliver integrated solutions to clients across various consumer categories and global markets.

title: Constellation Brands Q2 Profit Tops Estimates; Beer Business Net Sales Up 15%
summary: Constellation Brands reported strong Q2 performance, with profit topping estimates and Beer Business net sales growing 15%. The company also increased its full-year net sales outlook for the Beer Business and declared a quarterly dividend. Additionally, Constellation Brands reached an agreement to divest a portion of its mainstream and premium wine portfolio.

title: Heartland Coca-Cola unveils plan to build production facility in southern Olathe
summary: Heartland Coca-Cola Bottling Company plans to build a new $250 million production facility in southern Olathe, projected to open in late 2024. The 600,000 square foot campus will replace their Lenexa plant operations, with all 175 production employees offered positions at the new site. The Olathe City Council approved a conditional development agreement and a benefit district to support the project, including potential tax abatements and funding for infrastructure improvements like a new road.

title: How Coca-Cola’s sustainable supply chain finance programme works
summary: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners (CCEP) has launched a €600m sustainability-linked supply chain finance program with Rabobank to incentivize its suppliers to reduce emissions, use renewable electricity, and share carbon data. This initiative aims to address the 90% of CCEP's emissions that come from its supply chain and supports the company's net-zero targets. Suppliers meeting specific KPIs receive a discount on early payments, with the program rolling out globally by the end of the year.

title: PEP Stock: Is PepsiCo a safe investment in the bear market?
summary: PepsiCo (NASDAQ: PEP) is considered a safe investment due to its strong fundamentals, brand loyalty, and consistent financial performance, even amidst economic challenges. While its valuation appears high after recent gains, its attractiveness as a dividend stock and long-term investment remains, though short-term market volatility might be a concern. The company is set to release its Q3 2022 results on October 12, with analysts expecting continued growth in earnings and revenues.

title: BBVA México es intermediario colocador en la primera emisión de un bono social emitido por un corporativo en México, Coca-Cola FEMSA
summary: BBVA México acted as the placement agent and social structuring agent for Coca-Cola FEMSA's successful issuance of MXN 6 billion in sustainable and social bonds. This marks the first social bond issuance by a corporate in the consumer sector in the Americas and for the Coca-Cola System, with funds dedicated to social and sustainability projects. The bond issuance reinforces Coca-Cola FEMSA's commitment to community development and environmental goals, as well as BBVA México's role in promoting sustainable finance.

title: Constellation Brands divests wine brands to The Wine Group
summary: Constellation Brands has divested several mainstream and premium wine brands, including Cooper & Thief and The Dreaming Tree, to The Wine Group. This strategic move aligns with its broader strategy to reposition its portfolio towards higher-end wine and craft spirits, following an earlier divestiture of most of its popular and mainstream wine and spirits portfolio in 2021. The divestment aims to focus the company's efforts on leading premium brands like Meiomi, Kim Crawford, and The Prisoner Wine Company, enhancing its growth and shareholder value in a premiumized market.

title: WPP acquires Passport to boost integrated programs for brands
summary: WPP has acquired Southern California-based brand design agency Passport Brand Design to enhance VMLY&R's global network and design capabilities. The acquisition aims to help brands create connected consumer experiences by providing integrated programs, aligning with WPP CEO Mark Read's strategy to expand creative capabilities through M&A. Financial terms were not disclosed, and Passport will join VMLY&R.

title: Wedbush Securities Equity Research Welcomes Veteran Consumer Analyst Gerald Pascarelli, CFA® as Senior Vice President, Equity Research, Beverages; Initiates Coverage on CELH, KDP, MNST, PEP, KO, SAM, BFB, STZ, MGPI, TAP, and NAPA
summary: Wedbush Securities has announced the appointment of Gerald Pascarelli, CFA® as Senior Vice President, Equity Research, Beverages. Pascarelli initiates coverage on 11 beverage stocks, marking the firm's entry into the beverages equity research sector. He brings extensive experience from Cowen, Inc. and Kingdon Capital Management, specializing in data-driven consumer analysis.

title: Coca-Cola FEMSA recompra 299.8 millones de dólares en bonos
summary: Coca-Cola FEMSA conducted a public offer to repurchase $299.8 million of its outstanding senior bonds due in 2043 and 2030. HSBC and J.P. Morgan acted as dealer managers for the offer, which initially had a cap of $250 million but was increased due to high demand. The company was advised by Cleary Gottlieb Steen & Hamilton, while the banks received legal support from Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom and Galicia Abogados.

title: PepsiCo’s Higher Prices for Soda and Snacks Test Consumers’ Resolve
summary: PepsiCo has increased prices on its snacks and drinks by an average of 17% over the last year, leading to a rise in third-quarter sales. This move tests consumer willingness to continue purchasing at higher costs amidst record food inflation in the U.S. Companies are closely monitoring consumer reactions to these price hikes, as food inflation hit 13.5% in August compared to the previous year.

title: Coke or Pepsi? Cross-Basket Insights Reveal Buying Patterns, Shopping Behavior
summary: A study by Veryfi, which analyzes consumer shopping habits using AI, found that Coca-Cola buyers are loyal to Coca-Cola beverages but frequently purchase PepsiCo snacks. The research suggests opportunities for both companies to expand their market share by understanding these cross-basket buying patterns. Veryfi derives its insights from hundreds of millions of receipts, offering a detailed look into brand affinities.

title: Relevos en Coca Cola Femsa: Ian Craig sustituye a John Santa María en la dirección general
summary: Coca-Cola Femsa announced leadership changes, with Ian Craig set to replace John Santa María as CEO starting January 1, 2023. This succession is part of the company's anticipated planning processes. Additionally, Alfonso Garza Garza will retire from his role as CEO of Femsa Strategic Businesses, with Constantino Spas Montesinos taking over that position.

title: PepsiCo Boosted by Higher Prices
summary: PepsiCo reported stronger-than-expected third-quarter sales, prompting the company to raise its full-year revenue and earnings forecast. While sales volumes were down slightly, a significant 17% surge in pricing drove the positive results, with higher prices not deterring customers. Despite increased costs and marketing spend, PepsiCo's net income rose 21% to $2.7 billion, exceeding Wall Street's forecasts.

title: Indorama Ventures, Coca-Cola open PET recycling plant
summary: Indorama Ventures and Coca-Cola have opened PETValue Philippines, the country's first food-grade, bottle-to-bottle recycling facility in Cavite province. This plant, a partnership with Coca-Cola Beverages Philippines, will recycle approximately 2 billion used PET bottles annually and supports Coca-Cola's "World Without Waste" initiative. Indorama Ventures is also expanding its global recycling capacity to meet its 2025 and 2030 sustainability targets.

title: Big CPGs have not been making food and drink healthier, study finds
summary: A study by the Access to Nutrition Initiative (ATNI) found that the 11 largest food companies in the U.S. have made inadequate progress in making their products healthier, more affordable, and accessible, despite public commitments. The average score for companies in ATNI's 2022 U.S. Index was only 4.2 out of 10, indicating poor performance, with 70% of products being "less healthy." The report emphasizes the need for more concrete actions from these companies to align with national goals for improving public health and reducing diet-related diseases.

title: VMLY&R Bolsters Global Agency Leadership for Coca-Cola Company Business
summary: VMLY&R has announced key leadership appointments for its Coca-Cola Company business, promoting Stephanie DeCelles to global client lead and naming Chase Cornett as global chief strategy officer. Both will join the OpenX from WPP team, a bespoke agency servicing Coca-Cola, to drive strategic focus and breakthrough work for the global brand. These appointments highlight VMLY&R's commitment to strengthening its partnership with The Coca-Cola Company.

title: An activist investor has a garbage plan for Coca-Cola
summary: Activist investor Engine No. 1, known for its win against Exxon, is now targeting Coca-Cola with a plan to address plastic waste. The fund, which holds a small stake in Coca-Cola, suggests the beverage giant invest in or partner with a waste-management company, specifically mentioning Republic Services, to enhance recycling infrastructure and meet its 2030 recycling goals. This move aims to tackle Coca-Cola's significant plastic pollution footprint and push for greater corporate responsibility in environmental sustainability.

title: The Coca‑Cola Company in South Africa continues to offer consumers choice
summary: The Coca-Cola Company (TCCC) in South Africa continues to prioritize consumer choice by offering seven low-calorie/low-kilojoule carbonated cold drinks, despite a global portfolio refresh that included discontinuing TaB. This strategy, according to Silke Bucker, Senior Marketing Director, is consumer-centric, aiming to satisfy evolving consumer needs and provide diverse options, including new products like Coca-Cola No Sugar No Caffeine. TCCC's focus remains on listening to and responding to consumer demand to accelerate its transformation into a total beverage company.

title: FDA to Redefine ‘Healthy’ As Leading CPG Brands Fail to Deliver Better Food
summary: The FDA is updating its definition of 'healthy' for food labeling to better reflect modern nutritional science, focusing on limiting added sugars, sodium, and saturated fats, and requiring a minimum serving of beneficial ingredients. This move comes as major CPG brands have largely failed to make their products healthier, despite pledges, with recent research showing little progress from the largest food companies in the U.S. toward improving the nutritional quality of their offerings. The new guidelines aim to help consumers make more informed choices, particularly regarding highly processed foods.

title: Coca-Cola Femsa crece a doble digito en ingresos y utilidades
summary: Coca-Cola Femsa reported double-digit growth in both revenues and utilities during the third quarter of the year, driven by increased sales volume and price adjustments. The company's total revenues rose by 18.2% to 57,093 million pesos, and net utility increased by 27.9%. John Santa Maria, CEO of Coca-Cola FEMSA, highlighted the company's strong momentum and strategic progress.

title: UN’s Coke sponsorship leaves bad taste with environmentally conscious groups
summary: Coca-Cola's sponsorship of the COP27 U.N. climate summit has sparked outrage among environmental groups and activists, who accuse the company of "greenwash" due to its significant contribution to plastic pollution. Critics argue that corporate involvement, especially from major polluters, undermines the integrity of climate negotiations and provides a marketing platform rather than genuine commitment to environmental solutions. The controversy highlights broader concerns about corporate lobbying and influence at critical international climate conferences.

title: Coca-Cola raises full-year outlook as earnings beat expectations
summary: Coca-Cola (KO) raised its full-year outlook for adjusted earnings per share and organic revenue growth after beating Wall Street's expectations for its third-quarter earnings. The company's organic revenue grew 16%, driven by price hikes, while unit case volume rose 4%. Coca-Cola expects commodity prices to remain volatile and anticipates further price hikes and challenges from foreign currency in 2023, while also focusing on offering more affordable options to consumers.

title: Coke Sponsoring COP27 Is the Definition of ‘Greenwashing,’ Activists Say
summary: Activists are criticizing the United Nations' decision to accept Coca-Cola as a sponsor for COP27, labeling the partnership as "pure greenwash." They point to Coca-Cola's significant contribution to global plastic waste and its historical lobbying against environmental regulations, despite the company's claims of working towards emission reductions and plastic cleanup. Environmental groups argue that corporations deeply implicated in climate issues should not be allowed to sponsor critical climate summits.

title: Shrinkflation is boosting Coca-Cola’s bottom line
summary: Coca-Cola is leveraging "shrinkflation" by offering smaller product packs to appeal to budget-conscious consumers amidst rising inflation. This strategy contributed to a 10% year-over-year net revenue rise to $11.1 billion in Q3, with unit case volume growing by 4%. The company has raised its full-year organic revenue and adjusted earnings per share guidance, despite anticipating continued volatility in commodity prices and competitive pressures.

title: Coca-Cola lifts forecasts as demand keeps pace with pricier sodas
summary: Coca-Cola Co (KO.N) raised its annual forecasts after strong Q3 results, mirroring rival PepsiCo, as multiple price increases for its sodas did not deter consumer demand. Despite concerns about inflation's impact on consumer spending in some regions, the company plans to introduce smaller capacity bottles to stabilize prices, and beat analyst expectations for both revenue and profit.

title: Coca-Cola prioritizes offering more value to consumers: ‘We're not chasing the competitors. We're chasing the consumers and the retailers,’ says CEO
summary: Coca-Cola is focusing on delivering increased value to consumers by introducing products at more affordable price points, amid a challenging global economic environment. Chairman and CEO James Quincey emphasized that the company is "chasing the consumers and the retailers," rather than competitors, to drive growth. This strategy includes investments in sports drinks like BODYARMOR and Powerade, along with offering affordable options like smaller multi-packs to address consumer pressures.

title: Coca-Cola builds Metaverse marketing trove with TMELAND
summary: Coca-Cola has partnered with Tencent Music Entertainment's TMELAND, China's first virtual social music platform, to launch a metaverse zone for its Fan Festival. This initiative allows users to create avatars, shop, play games, and interact with celebrity avatars, targeting a Gen Z audience. The venture highlights the growing potential for brands to engage consumers through immersive digital experiences in China, following similar moves by Pepsi and Adidas Originals on TMELAND.

title: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners has pulled its signature mixers range
summary: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners (CCEP) has discontinued its Signature Mixers range in the UK, citing a strategy focused on prioritizing best-performing brands. CCEP aims to streamline its portfolio and concentrate on widely appealing "hero products" in the competitive soft drinks market.

title: Negocio de logística de FEMSA reporta un robusto tercer trimetre de 2022
summary: FEMSA's Logistics and Distribution division reported a robust third quarter in 2022, achieving 19,986 million pesos, a 70.3% growth over the same period last year. This growth was significantly boosted by Envoy Solutions' strong performance, an American diversified distribution company. The company's OXXO Gas business also had a solid quarter, with a 33.6% increase in quarterly revenues and a return to pre-pandemic mobility levels.

title: Femsa planea abrir más quioscos de Valora y lanzar una fintech B2B en Europa
summary: Mexican bottler and retailer Femsa plans to expand its Swiss kiosk operator Valora in Europe, opening new stores and affiliating independent businesses in Germany. Additionally, Femsa intends to launch a B2B fintech service in Europe. This move follows Femsa's acquisition of Valora and comes after its consumer-facing fintech Spin by Oxxo received a license in Mexico, aiming for 10 million users by 2023.

title: Flows Into Consumer Staples ETFs Rebound on Economic Uncertainty
summary: Investors are increasingly moving back into consumer staples ETFs, a defensive strategy during economic uncertainty. The Invesco S&P 500® Equal Weight Consumer Staples ETF (RHS) has seen significant net inflows, indicating a preference for equal-weighted approaches to mitigate company-specific risks that are common in market-cap weighted funds dominated by a few large companies. This shift reflects advisors' search for downside protection while still participating in market upside in the current economic climate.

title: Greens push to oust Coke from COP 27 sponsorship
summary: Two environmental groups, Just Zero and Beyond Plastics, are calling for the removal of Coca-Cola Co. as a sponsor from COP 27, arguing that the company's role as a major plastics polluter undermines the climate conference's goals. They assert that plastics have become "the new coal" in terms of environmental impact and accuse Coca-Cola of greenwashing its image through sponsorship while continuing to contribute significantly to plastic waste. Critics cite reports highlighting Coca-Cola as the world's top plastic polluter and its lobbyists' efforts against real recycling improvements.

title: The anti-ESG funds exploiting the US political divide
summary: The article discusses the rise of anti-ESG funds in the US, which are exploiting the political divide by offering investments that prioritize shareholder value over socially responsible agendas. These funds, such as Strive Asset Management and ACVF, cater to investors who believe ESG investing is politically motivated and detrimental to financial returns. Despite their growing media attention, experts question their overall impact on corporate behavior and capital movement compared to traditional large asset managers.

title: Monster: Price Increases Tempering Costs
summary: Monster Beverage Company reported a 15.2% year-over-year sales growth in Q3, despite increased expenses and cost of goods impacting margins. The company implemented a 6% price increase in the U.S. and plans further international pricing actions to mitigate costs, while also defending its strategy of prioritizing product availability. Monster is focused on innovation with planned launches of Monster Energy Zero Sugar, its first alcoholic beverage "The Beast Unleashed," and Monster Tour Water, alongside an expanded alcoholic beverage pipeline and a new performance drink line, Rainstorm.

title: Coca-Cola plastic packaging up by 8.8% in one year
summary: Oceana reports that The Coca-Cola Company's plastic packaging increased by 8.8% in one year, amounting to over 579 million pounds. This increase occurred despite pledges to boost recycled content and decrease virgin plastic use, which the company failed to significantly advance. Oceana urges Coca-Cola to focus on increasing refillable bottle systems, which are more effective in reducing plastic pollution and carbon footprint than recycling efforts alone.

title: Why Apple raised the price of the iPhone, but not in the U.S. and China
summary: Apple increased the price of its iPhone 14 series for many international buyers due to the strong U.S. dollar and currency headwinds, which significantly impacted the company's revenue growth. CEO Tim Cook noted that foreign exchange headwinds were over 600 basis points last quarter, preventing double-digit revenue growth. While the U.S. and China avoided price hikes, consumers in markets like the U.K., Japan, Germany, and Australia saw significant increases, a strategy Apple previous reversed in 2019 due to declining sales, though they report no such drop-off this time.

title: Greece Fines Coca-Cola-Bottler Over Price-Fixing
summary: Greece has imposed a 10.34 million euro fine on Coca-Cola 3E, the largest bottler for The Coca Cola Company in the country, for price-fixing violations. The fine stems from a 2016 complaint alleging the bottler tried to block competitors in the soft drink market on Rhodes and the Dodecanese islands. This action occurs amidst global economic turbulence and increased scrutiny of corporate practices regarding price-fixing and abuses.

title: Wolverine Worldwide names Nicholas Long as lead independent director
summary: Wolverine World Wide, Inc. has appointed Nicholas T. Long as its lead independent director, effective November 4, 2022. Long, who has been a director since 2011 and chairs the compensation committee, succeeds Dr. David T. Kollat. CEO Brendan Hoffman highlighted Long's extensive experience in global brand-building and consumer-focused businesses as crucial for the company's strategic objectives.

title: B&B Theatres Signs 10-year Contract with The Coca-Cola Company
summary: B&B Theatres has announced a new 10-year partnership with The Coca-Cola Company, which will include the installment of Coca-Cola Freestyle machines across B&B's cinemas by holiday season 2022. This collaboration emphasizes shared values, an enhanced guest experience, and a mutual passion for cinema innovation. B&B Theatres is ranked #6 on Boxoffice PRO’s Giants of Exhibition 2022 list, operating 513 screens at 56 locations.

title: Coke Is a Sponsor of the Climate Summit in Egypt. Some Activists Aren’t Happy. (Published 2022)
summary: Coca-Cola's sponsorship of the COP27 climate summit in Egypt has drawn strong criticism from climate activists, who point to the company's increasing plastic production as detailed in a recent report. Activists argue that Coca-Cola, named the world's leading plastic polluter in 2021, is greenwashing its image while its plastic use, largely derived from fossil fuels, continues to rise. Despite Coca-Cola's claims of environmental commitments, a report from the Ellen MacArthur Foundation indicates that the company will likely miss its target for recyclable or compostable packaging by 2025.

title: Coca-Cola to restructure North American workforce with voluntary buyouts
summary: Coca-Cola is implementing a "voluntary separation program" including employee buyouts to restructure its North American workforce of approximately 6,000 people. This move follows previous restructurings and job cuts aimed at streamlining operations and focusing on growing brands, though the company states this current initiative is not primarily for cost-cutting. Employees have a short window, November 14-18, to decide on accepting the buyout offer.

title: Coca-Cola Supplies Alcorn Athletics with Gift
summary: Coca-Cola has gifted Alcorn State University Athletics with a new, fully-branded 35-foot equipment truck, capable of carrying over 6,000 pounds of gear. This donation is the result of a partnership between Alcorn President Dr. Felecia Nave and Coca-Cola representatives Russ Hendley and Mario Lee, providing a mobile billboard and essential transport for the Braves. The truck was presented on November 9, 2022, outside Jack Spinks – Marino Casem Stadium, and also came filled with Coca-Cola beverages.

title: Keurig Dr Pepper invests $50M in Athletic Brewing
summary: Keurig Dr Pepper has invested $50 million in Athletic Brewing, a nonalcoholic craft beer maker, acquiring a minority stake and a board seat. This investment is part of Athletic Brewing's $75 million fundraising round and reflects Keurig Dr Pepper's strategy to expand into the rapidly growing nonalcoholic beverage category. The move contrasts with competitors who are entering the ready-to-drink alcoholic beverage market.

title: Keurig Dr Pepper CEO pushed out after 3 months over personal conduct ‘violations’
summary: Keurig Dr Pepper CEO Ozan Dokmecioglu resigned after less than four months in the role due to unspecified violations of the company's Code of Conduct related to personal behavior, not strategy or financial reporting. Former CEO Bob Gamgort will return to the top position. The company emphasized its commitment to ethics and integrity for all employees.

title: How Droughts in Mexico Could Shape the Future of the Beer Industry (Published 2022)
summary: Mexico's severe droughts are intensifying the conflict between major beer corporations and local communities over water access. While brewers like Heineken continue to consume vast quantities of water, residents face shortages and health issues, sparking protests and a national debate on resource allocation. This situation is forcing the government and industry to confront the growing disparity in water access amid climate change, putting pressure on major global brands.

title: It’s not just Coca-Cola: Corporations have co-opted the UN climate talks
summary: This article criticizes the growing corporate influence at UN climate talks, specifically highlighting Coca-Cola's sponsorship of COP27 given its status as the world's largest plastic producer. Despite widespread criticism and a petition signed by nearly 240,000 people, corporations like Coca-Cola, Microsoft, IBM, and Bloomberg Philanthropies continue to play significant roles in these conferences. The piece suggests that this corporate involvement undermines the environmental goals of the climate talks.

title: Coca-Cola Seeing 'Encouraging Results' From Alcoholic Beverages Launches
summary: The Coca-Cola Company is reporting encouraging early results from its alcoholic beverage partnerships with Molson Coors and Constellation Brands for Simply Spiked Lemonade and Fresca Mixed. This follows their initial foray into the ready-to-drink alcoholic market with Lemon-Dou in 2018 in Japan. These initiatives support Coca-Cola's strategy to become a "total beverage company" with options for all occasions and need states.

title: Kraft Heinz Bets (Even) Bigger On Supply Chain Visibility
summary: Kraft Heinz is deepening its partnership with Microsoft, adopting the new Supply Chain Center to enhance supply chain visibility through AI-backed capabilities. This initiative is part of a larger transformation to integrate and centralize data, allowing for more agile risk assessment and improved product delivery across North America. The platform leverages AI models for demand and supply insights, order management automation, and Teams integration to streamline operations and decision-making.

title: COP27 Sponsor The Coca-Cola Company named worst plastic polluter for five years in a row according to 2022 Brand Audit
summary: The Coca-Cola Company, PepsiCo, and Nestlé have been identified as the world's top plastic polluters for the fifth consecutive year, according to the 2022 Brand Audit by Break Free From Plastic. This report highlights the ineffectiveness of corporate voluntary commitments in reducing environmental impact, with plastic packaging use actually increasing for many companies. Activists are advocating for a legally-binding Global Plastics Treaty to enforce reductions in plastic production and promote reuse-based alternatives, especially as Coca-Cola sponsors COP27 despite its significant plastic footprint.

title: Break Free From Plastic names Coca-Cola the world’s worst plastic polluter for fifth consecutive year
summary: For the fifth consecutive year, Break Free From Plastic has identified Coca-Cola as the world’s worst plastic polluter through its global brand audit report. Coca-Cola, PepsiCo, and Nestlé consistently rank as top polluters, highlighting that voluntary corporate commitments are insufficient to reduce environmental footprints. Activists are advocating for a legally binding Global Plastics Treaty to significantly cut plastic production, hold corporations accountable, and promote reuse models for packaging.

title: Coca-Cola Co.’s Mojo Kombucha shuts factory, warns products to disappear from shelves
summary: Coca-Cola Co.'s Mojo Beverages brand, known for Mojo Kombucha, is closing its kombucha factory. As a result, its products will no longer be available on shelves in the near future. The company stated this was a difficult decision.

title: Molson Coors to End La Colombe, HEXO Partnerships
summary: Molson Coors announced it is ending its partnerships with coffee roaster La Colombe and cannabis producer Hexo Corp. Effective March 31, 2023, the La Colombe partnership will conclude due to logistical challenges for distributors, while the Truss CBD beverage joint venture with Hexo will dissolve at the end of 2022 due to regulatory hurdles. Molson Coors plans to reallocate resources to other non-beer ventures like ZOA energy drink and Topo Chico Spirited.

title: Coca Cola Christmas Truck confirms its return for 2022
summary: Coca-Cola has confirmed the return of its Christmas Truck Tour for 2022, featuring a winter market theme and supporting FareShare by donating up to 100,000 meals to those in need. The tour will offer interactive activities, personalized Coca-Cola products, and will see the beloved "Holidays Are Coming" advert return to TV. For the first time, Coca-Cola is also collaborating with RNIB and NaviLens to make its packaging accessible for blind and partially sighted people.

title: Popular Coca-Cola Christmas Truck tour returns for 2022
summary: The Coca-Cola Christmas Truck tour is returning for 2022, featuring a Christmas market theme, interactive activities, and food huts. This year, the tour supports FareShare, a charity fighting hunger and food waste, with Coca-Cola donating the equivalent of one meal for every attendee. The company is also collaborating with RNIB to implement NaviLens technology on promotional multipacks, making packaging accessible for blind and partially sighted people.

title: Coca-Cola Rethinks Hybrid Work to Tell a Better Workplace Story
summary: Coca-Cola is rethinking its hybrid work strategy to create a more compelling workplace story for its employees, focusing on connection, social capital, and flexible office design. This initiative, highlighted at the CoreNet Global Summit, involved redesigning their Singapore headquarters to reflect local culture and provide varied work areas to support hybrid work. The article emphasizes that a successful hybrid model requires more than just technology, integrating aesthetic design, amenities, and HR policies to enhance the employee experience and attract workers back to the office.

title: Cabarrus County joins Concord in approving more incentives for Red Bull, Rauch at $1B-plus beverage hub
summary: Cabarrus County has approved additional incentives for Red Bull and Rauch North America, who, along with Ball Corp., plan a an expanded $1 billion-plus beverage hub at The Grounds at Concord. This move follows Concord's earlier consideration of incentives for increased investment in the project. The companies are set to break ground on the facility next year.

title: Coca-Cola will now make local deliveries in Belgium with 30 electric Renault Trucks vehicles
summary: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners (CCEP) is deploying 30 electric Renault Trucks vehicles for "last mile" deliveries in Belgium, starting with five in the Antwerp area. This initiative, part of a €7 million investment, aims to electrify one-fifth of CCEP's Belgian fleet, reduce CO2 emissions by 75% compared to diesel trucks, and contribute to the company's goal of cutting overall CO2 emissions by 30% by 2030 and achieving climate neutrality by 2040. The trucks will cover average routes of 150 km per day, charged overnight with 100% green energy.

title: LG Household & Health Care appoints first female CEO
summary: LG Household & Health Care has appointed Lee Jung-ae as its first female CEO, effective December 1. Lee, a veteran marketer, has a strong background in the company's cosmetics, beverage, and household goods divisions. This appointment is part of broader personnel changes across LG affiliates, including new CEOs for LG CNS and promotions within LG Electronics and LG Chem.

title: Meet The Markets: Introducing Spain
summary: This article introduces Coca-Cola Europacific Partners (CCEP) in Spain, highlighting its history, economic contribution, and commitment to sustainability and community programs. It details CCEP Spain's innovation in product offerings, significant job creation, and environmental efforts like emissions reduction, plastic recycling, and waste collection. Key facts and figures demonstrate CCEP's substantial presence and impact on the Spanish economy and environment.

title: Coca-Cola Femsa aumenta los precios de refrescos, agua y leche
summary: Coca-Cola Femsa announced a third price increase for its products, including soft drinks, water, and milk, effective November 28th. The price hike, ranging from 1 to 2 pesos, is attributed to rising raw material costs and inflation. Specific price adjustments are detailed for various Coca-Cola, flavored soft drinks, Santa Clara milk, Ades products, and Ciel water presentations.

title: What Can Brands Learn from Coca-Cola’s Greenwashing Lawsuit Win?
summary: Coca-Cola successfully defended itself against a greenwashing lawsuit filed by Earth Island Institute, which accused the company of false advertising regarding its sustainability claims. The court dismissed the case primarily because Coca-Cola's statements were deemed aspirational, not actionable, and not directly tied to product labeling. This ruling suggests a potential challenge for future greenwashing claims against companies, especially regarding general corporate ethos statements.

title: The Coca-Cola Company Names Henrique Braun to Newly Created Role of President, International Development
summary: The Coca-Cola Company announced the creation of a new role, President, International Development, and named Henrique Braun to fill it, effective January 1, 2023. Braun will oversee seven operating units, including Latin America, Japan and South Korea, Africa, and others. John Murphy, President and CFO, will also take on oversight of the Bottling Investments Group.

title: Coca-Cola creates new role of president, International Development
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has appointed Henrique Braun to the newly created role of President, International Development, effective January 1, 2023. Braun will oversee seven operating units covering dozens of countries and territories, reporting directly to CEO James Quincey. This new role expands his responsibilities beyond his current position as president of the Latin America operating unit, which he has held since 2020.

title: Coke’s sustainably chief throws down a marker on regulations for reporting supplier emissions
summary: Coca-Cola's chief sustainability officer, Bea Perez, announced the company's support for the SEC's proposed regulations on supplier emissions, or Scope 3 emissions, despite previous quibbles regarding implementation details for smaller suppliers. Perez emphasized the need for fairness and consistency in reporting, while Kristina Wyatt, formerly of the SEC, clarified that the proposed rules allow for flexibility, including using industry benchmarks for smaller entities during a phase-in period. The article highlights Coca-Cola's existing voluntary climate targets to reduce total greenhouse gas emissions by 25% by 2030 and its ambition for net-zero carbon emissions by 2050.

title: Coca-Cola announces Christmas truck is coming to Bristol
summary: Coca-Cola's famous Christmas truck is returning to Cribbs Causeway in Bristol on December 3rd as part of its 'Magic of Giving’ Christmas campaign. This year, the event will feature a winter market, festive food, and interactive games, with Coca-Cola donating the equivalent of a meal to FareShare for every visitor. The initiative aims to support FareShare's efforts in tackling food poverty, with a goal of funding 200,000 meals.

title: How Coca-Cola’s new marketing leader will approach the job
summary: Shakir Moin has been promoted to lead Coca-Cola Co.'s North American marketing. Moin previously headed the company’s Costa coffee business and is known for working in Costa stores to gain business insights. The article will detail his approach to his new role.

title: Coca-Cola's Plastic Pollution Problem
summary: The Sierra Club criticizes Coca-Cola for its significant plastic pollution, highlighting the company's annual production of 3 million tons of plastic packaging and its alleged misleading recycling claims. The article discusses Coca-Cola's history of prioritizing plastic over more recyclable materials like aluminum and details a lawsuit filed by the Sierra Club against Coca-Cola regarding false advertising of its bottles' recyclability.

title: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners Australia inaugurates US$43.7m Moorabbin can line
summary: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners (CCEP) Australia has opened a new US$43.7 million can line at its Moorabbin site in Victoria, designed to meet rising consumer demand for canned beverages and increase local production. The facility is CCEP Australia's most sustainable production line, boasting significant water and energy efficiencies, including a yearly saving equivalent to six Olympic-sized swimming pools of water. The new line can produce up to 1700 cans per minute and, alongside a new distribution center in Mentone, is expected to reduce inter-state freight and carbon emissions.

title: The Coca-Cola Company names Henrique Braun as president, international development
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has appointed Henrique Braun as president of international development, a new role overseeing seven operating units across many countries. Braun, who previously led the Latin America operating unit, will begin his new duties on January 1, 2023, reporting to CEO James Quincey. John Murphy, president and CFO, will also take on oversight of the company’s Bottling Investments Group.

title: Executives from eBay and Golden State Foods Join GS1 US Board of Governors
summary: GS1 US has elected Scott Gaffney from eBay and Brian Dick from Golden State Foods to its Board of Governors. These industry leaders will help guide GS1 US's strategy to enhance supply chain efficiency and visibility across various sectors, supporting members with digital transformation and demand planning. Their expertise is expected to be instrumental in optimizing supply chains to meet consumer needs.

title: Layoffs in food industry mount as PepsiCo joins Coca-Cola, General Mills, Walmart and others in cost-savings and restructuring efforts
summary: Major food industry players like PepsiCo, Coca-Cola, and General Mills are implementing layoffs and restructuring efforts to combat inflationary pressures and manage rising commodity costs. This trend extends to food tech companies, foodservice providers, and retailers like Walmart and Amazon, all seeking cost savings. Despite these workforce reductions, the consumer packaged goods industry still faces a significant number of job openings, indicating a complex labor market influenced by increased wage demands.

title: PepsiCo sets global packaging goals following shareholder scrutiny
summary: PepsiCo has set an ambitious global packaging goal for 2030, aiming to deliver up to 20% of its beverage servings through reusable models, doubling its current rate. This move is part of the PepsiCo Positive (pep+) sustainability programme and is accelerated by shareholder pressure, particularly from "As You Sow." The company plans to expand its SodaStream business and work with bottlers to increase reusable plastic and glass bottle offerings to achieve this target.

title: Kraft Heinz Co. stock outperforms competitors on strong trading day
summary: Kraft Heinz Co. (KHC) stock advanced 1.19% on Wednesday, closing at $39.89, despite a generally grim trading session for the broader stock market. The company's stock outperformed competitors like Coca-Cola Co. (KO), PepsiCo Inc. (PEP), and Mondelez International Inc. Cl A (MDLZ) and ended a two-day losing streak. The stock is currently $4.98 below its 52-week high, reached on May 10th.

title: Say We Care Programme
summary: The Coca-Cola Foundation is funding the 'Say We Care' initiative to provide essential relief packs to 6,000 vulnerable families across nine districts in Sri Lanka. This effort responds to the severe economic crisis and high food insecurity in the country. The initiative specifically targets pregnant mothers, children, persons with disabilities, and low-income households, building on TCCF's history of supporting communities during challenging times.

title: From Nostalgic to Cheeky: 12+ Christmas Commercials and What They Teach Us About Storytelling
summary: This article analyzes over 12 Christmas commercials, ranging from nostalgic classics to modern, cheeky campaigns, to extract lessons in effective storytelling for marketers. It explores how brands use emotion, creativity, and unique narratives to create memorable holiday advertisements that resonate with audiences. The piece highlights various storytelling takeaways, emphasizing the importance of relatable characters, emotional impact, and innovative approaches in holiday marketing.

title: Keurig Dr Pepper spends $863M for stake in C4 Energy maker
summary: Keurig Dr Pepper is acquiring a 30% stake in Nutrabolt, the maker of C4 Energy and Xtend Energy drinks, for $863 million. This deal includes a long-term sales and distribution agreement, giving Keurig Dr Pepper a significant entry into the rapidly growing performance energy drink market. The investment strategically positions Keurig Dr Pepper to adapt to changing consumer trends in the beverage industry.

title: Coke CMO Melanie Boulden Moves to Tyson Foods
summary: Melanie Boulden, formerly North America CMO for Coca-Cola, is moving to Tyson Foods as EVP, Chief Growth Officer, a newly created role, effective February 6. She will oversee global brand marketing, innovation, R&D, and communications for Tyson's portfolio.
