summary: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners (CCEP) has sold its Australian producer Feral Brewing Co. to a joint venture involving Nail Brewing and an undisclosed consortium of investors. This move allows CCEP to focus on its core non-alcoholic ready-to-drink (NARTD) products. Feral Brewing's production assets have been sold to Beerfarm, which will continue to produce Feral-branded products.

title: Coca-Cola Bottling Company United To Invest $330M In New Alabama Facility
summary: Coca-Cola Bottling Company United is investing $330 million in a new state-of-the-art facility in Birmingham, Alabama, creating up to 50 new jobs and retaining over 750 existing positions. The new complex, located on the former Stockham Valves and Fittings site, will include a multi-floor office complex and a large warehouse with advanced order fulfillment technology. This investment signifies the company's continued commitment to the Birmingham community and its future growth.

title: Costa Coffee Expands Iced Coffee Latte Line in U.S. This Summer
summary: Costa Coffee is expanding its iced coffee latte line nationwide in the U.S. this summer, offering Mocha, Caramel, and Signature Blend flavors with real cane sugar and 100% Arabica beans. To promote this launch, Costa Coffee is partnering with Y7 Studio to offer "Sip and Flow" yoga experiences, including free digital memberships and in-studio classes in select cities, along with free Costa Iced Coffee Lattes. The new line, developed by The Coca-Cola Company, aims to invigorate the coffee category and cater to active lifestyles, with products available at major retailers across the country.

title: Restaurant Brands International Inc. Appoints Patrick Siewert as Senior Advisor in Asia-Pacific Region
summary: Restaurant Brands International Inc. has appointed Patrick Siewert as its Senior Advisor in the Asia-Pacific region to help drive growth and expansion. Siewert brings extensive experience in food, beverage, and consumer products in Asia, including 16 years with the Carlyle Group and a prior role as COO for Coca-Cola in Asia. His appointment supports RBI's goal of opening 7,000 new international restaurants by 2028, particularly enhancing master franchise partnerships and talent acquisition in the APAC region.

title: Beyond the Game: The Coca-Cola Company Helps Boys & Girls Club Teens Score Big in the Business of Sports at the 2024 NCAA Final Fours
summary: The Coca-Cola Company partnered with Boys & Girls Clubs of America to provide teens with a hands-on sports marketing experience at the 2024 NCAA Women's Final Four. Teens from Boys & Girls Clubs of Northeast Ohio gained insights into careers in sports business, participated in a virtual learning session with industry experts, and even saw their own in-game entertainment idea come to life during the championship practice. This initiative highlights the diverse career opportunities within the sports industry beyond being an athlete and reinforces Coca-Cola's long-standing partnership with the Boys & Girls Clubs.

title: Why Investing Guru Jeremy Grantham’s New ETF Shuns Nvidia and Tesla Stock
summary: Legendary investor Jeremy Grantham's new ETF, GMO’s U.S. Quality ETF, is outperforming the stock market despite intentionally excluding high-momentum stocks like Nvidia and Tesla. The ETF instead focuses on defensive stocks such as Coca-Cola, alongside five of the "Magnificent Seven" tech stocks. This strategy highlights a preference for quality and value over pure momentum plays.

title: Why Investing Guru Jeremy Grantham’s New ETF Shuns Nvidia and Tesla Stock
summary: Legendary value investor Jeremy Grantham's new GMO’s U.S. Quality ETF is outperforming the stock market despite shunning high-momentum stocks like Nvidia and Tesla. The ETF opts for more defensive stocks such as Coca-Cola, while still holding five of the "Magnificent Seven" tech stocks. This strategy highlights a focus on quality and value over pure momentum plays.

title: Keurig Dr Pepper Expands DSD Operations With Kalil Bottling Acquisition
summary: Keurig Dr Pepper (KDP) is expanding its direct-store delivery (DSD) reach through the acquisition of Kalil Bottling Co. and its Arizona operations. This strategic move aims to strengthen national DSD capabilities, enhance scale, and build brands in a fast-growing beverage market, adding approximately 425 employees and extending KDP's system reach and local consumer insights. The acquisition is part of KDP's broader strategy to consolidate distribution and optimize its route to market for its portfolio of leading brands.

title: Food co-ops aren't known for price-conscious customers. That's changing
summary: Natural food co-ops are traditionally known for organic and fair-trade products, but are now shifting focus towards affordability due to changing consumer values and economic pressures. This includes increasing offerings of cheaper organic brands and even conventional products like Coca-Cola. This strategic move aims to attract a broader customer base and has led to a rise in sales for many co-ops.

title: Quality Assurance at Coca Cola with CO2 Purity Monitoring
summary: This article highlights how Coca-Cola Beverages Northeast utilizes the Thermo Scientific MAX-Bev system for CO2 purity monitoring. Sarah Heald, Quality Supervisor, explains the system's role in ensuring beverage-grade CO2 purity, reducing human error, and significantly streamlining the quality control process. The MAX-Bev system allows for accurate and precise testing, crucial for maintaining product taste and meeting industry standards, ultimately contributing to "the perfect sip" for consumers.

title: Clorox Is Accelerating Innovation With Generative AI Investment
summary: Clorox is accelerating its innovation strategy by investing in a generative AI tool to identify global trends and rapidly develop digital prototypes. This initiative is part of the company's digital transformation following a cyber attack and aims to enhance customer relationships and operational efficiency. The first AI-driven innovation launched in 90 days, significantly faster than previous timelines.

title: Coca-Cola ad in Bangladesh sparks backlash for ‘denying ties with Israel’
summary: A Coca-Cola advertisement in Bangladesh has caused significant backlash for attempting to distance the brand from Israel amidst the war in Gaza and a widespread boycott. The commercial, which claims Coca-Cola is not an Israeli product and mentions a Coke factory in "Palestine," has been criticized for insensitivity and factual inaccuracies, as the factory is located in an Israeli settlement in the occupied West Bank. Despite being briefly withdrawn, the ad reappeared with comments disabled, failing to curb public outrage and boycott efforts.

title: Spin-off da UFMG é adquirida pelo Grupo Bradesco
summary: The UFMG spin-off Kunumi, co-founded by professor Nívio Ziviani and CEO Alberto Colares, has been acquired by Bradesco Holding de Investimentos S.A. Kunumi, established in 2016, specializes in artificial intelligence, developing a platform that mimics brain function to analyze large datasets and solve complex problems. This acquisition highlights an innovative legal model where UFMG, as a co-founder, benefits from the company's success through an usufruct of shares agreement.

title: Coca-Cola United celebrates start of $330 million Alabama growth project
summary: Coca-Cola Bottling Company United Inc. has begun a $330 million growth project in Birmingham, Alabama, marking an investment that will create 50 new jobs and retain 750 existing ones. The new facility, located in the Kingston community, will house various Coca-Cola operations and act as a gateway to the city. Gov. Kay Ivey and company leadership celebrated the project, emphasizing Coca-Cola United's long-standing commitment to Alabama.

title: Coca-Cola operates in Russia despite exit claims, PepsiCo adds new factory
summary: Despite official claims of exiting the Russian market, Coca-Cola products remain widely available in Russia, with its subsidiary Coca-Cola HBC continuing to profit and even increase market share through the "Dobry Cola" brand. Simultaneously, PepsiCo is expanding its business in Russia, having opened a new snack factory in April, despite previously announcing a cessation of investments and sales. These actions have drawn criticism, with advocacy groups like the Ukrainian Congress Committee of America urging global corporations to fully withdraw from the Russian market.

title: PepsiCo anticipates missing certain 2025 packaging sustainability goals
summary: PepsiCo has stated in its 2023 ESG report that it expects to miss some of its 2025 packaging sustainability goals, including the target to design 100% of its packaging to be recyclable, compostable, biodegradable, or reusable. The company projects reaching 98% by 2025 for this goal and also reported a 6% increase in virgin plastic use, despite aiming for a 20% reduction by 2030. Despite the shortfalls, PepsiCo highlighted progress in areas like switching to fiber carriers for beverage multipacks and increasing recycled PET content in some products.

title: Governor Gianforte Welcomes $100 Million Coca-Cola High Country Investment in Montana
summary: Governor Greg Gianforte celebrated the opening of a new $100 million Coca-Cola High Country facility in Billings, Montana, which will create over 100 jobs. This investment marks Coca-Cola High Country's largest facility in the state and supports manufacturing, sales, and distribution across the region. The move highlights the Gianforte administration's efforts to attract job-creating businesses to Montana through tax code reforms and fostering a pro-business environment.

title: The Coca-Cola Company Launches Olympic and Paralympic Games Campaign for North America Featuring Versatile Roster of Athletes and Brands
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has launched its Olympic and Paralympic Games campaign for North America, featuring a diverse roster of Team USA and Team Canada athletes. The campaign builds on the global theme "Celebrate Everyday Greatness" and includes new commercials, digital experiences with prize opportunities via QR codes on packaging, and media partnerships. It highlights several Coca-Cola brands and athletes such as Alex Morgan, Simone Biles, and Katie Ledecky, celebrating Coca-Cola's long-standing partnership with the Olympic Games.

title: Emporia Coca-Cola transitions to new ownership
summary: The Emporia Coca-Cola Bottling Company, a long-standing local business, has been acquired by Heartland Coca-Cola Bottling Company. This sale marks the end of the DeBauge family's extensive involvement in the local beverage industry. Heartland Coca-Cola, led by former NBA professional Junior Bridgeman, acquires Emporia Coca-Cola and Classic Vending as part of its strategic expansion in the Midwest.

title: The Coca-Cola Company Announces Timing of Second Quarter 2024 Earnings Release
summary: The Coca-Cola Company announced it will release its second quarter 2024 financial results on July 23 before the New York Stock Exchange opens. An investor conference call will follow at 8:30 a.m. ET to discuss the results, with a webcast available for investors. Downloadable files and a transcript will be provided on the company's website after the call.

title: Coca-Cola and POWERADE Kick Off New Worldwide Partnership with CONMEBOL For Copa América 2024™
summary: Coca-Cola and POWERADE have announced a new worldwide partnership with CONMEBOL for Copa América 2024™, building on Coca-Cola's extensive legacy in global football. This sponsorship provides both brands with significant visibility across digital, in-venue, and TV platforms throughout the tournament. The collaboration aims to deepen fan connection and promote the sport's positive values, especially in Latin America where football is deeply embedded in culture.

title: How Did Dr Pepper Catch Up to Pepsi?
summary: Dr Pepper has recently tied Pepsi as the second-most-popular soda in the U.S. by sales volume, a remarkable achievement given its long history as a niche drink. This success is attributed to its unique "sweet and spicy" flavor, a landmark 1960s lawsuit allowing it on both Coke and Pepsi soda fountains, innovative marketing campaigns targeting younger generations, and recent expansions into new flavors and digital advertising. Pepsi's declining market share and strategic shift towards sugar-free options and energy drinks also contributed to Dr Pepper's ascendance.

title: PepsiCo, Coca-Cola sued by Baltimore for cleanup costs
summary: The City of Baltimore has sued PepsiCo, Coca-Cola, and other companies to recover costs associated with plastic pollution cleanup. The lawsuit alleges false claims, design defects, and deceptive practices by the companies, which Baltimore states have increased plastic production while externalizing cleanup costs. This marks PepsiCo's second plastics-related lawsuit in less than a year.

title: Keurig Dr Pepper: Selling Calls Can Yield 7% With Room For Upside (NASDAQ:KDP)
summary: The article highlights Keurig Dr Pepper's strong market share gains, particularly Dr Pepper surpassing Pepsi, and its rapid top and bottom-line growth since 2018. It suggests that KDP shares are attractively valued and recommends a covered call position to potentially yield 16% over a year with minimal risk, rating KDP as a 'Buy'.

title: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners chooses Systal Technology Solutions for network transformation
summary: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners (CCEP) has partnered with Systal Technology Solutions for a network transformation across Europe, involving support for over 6,500 devices in 300 locations across 11 countries. This expanded partnership builds on a six-year relationship and aims to enhance CCEP's operational efficiency and ensure business continuity. Separately, CCEP part-owner The Coca-Cola Company recently signed a significant cloud and AI services contract with Microsoft.

title: ‘It’s Magic When the World Comes Together’: Olympic Athletes and Fans Alike Embrace in Global Coca-Cola Campaign for Paris 2024
summary: Coca-Cola has launched a new global campaign for the Paris 2024 Olympic and Paralympic Games, centered around the theme "it’s magic when the world comes together." The multi-channel campaign, which includes a powerful brand film and distinctive can designs, uses the gesture of a hug to symbolize unity, inclusion, and the power of sport to foster connections. Coca-Cola aims to refresh athletes, officials, and fans as a Worldwide Partner of the Games and Presenting Partner of the Paris 2024 Olympic Torch Relay.

title: SA gas users plan venture to secure supply before 2026
summary: South Africa's industrial gas users are forming a joint venture to secure gas supply after Sasol announced it would halt supply from Mozambique in 2026. The Industrial Gas Users Association of Southern Africa (IGUA-SA) is spearheading this effort, planning an externally funded, private company based on a cost-pass-through model. This initiative aims to avert a major crisis that could jeopardize hundreds of thousands of jobs and force industrial users to switch to more expensive and environmentally damaging fuels.

title: C-Store People News for July 2024
summary: This article details significant personnel changes across the convenience-store industry in July 2024, including new hires, promotions, and retirements at retailers, suppliers, and associations. Key appointments include Maryann Mannen as CEO of Marathon Petroleum Corp., Nate Brazier as President and CEO of Stinker Stores, and Caitlyn Carr as President and CEO of Coca-Cola Bottlers’ Sales & Services Co. The article highlights the ongoing evolution within the industry and its leadership.

title: The Fascinating Evolution of Coca-Cola: From Cocaine Tonic to Tech-Savvy Giant
summary: This article details the historical evolution of Coca-Cola, starting from its origins in 1886 as a tonic containing coca leaf extract, which included cocaine. It describes how the company transitioned away from cocaine by 1904, though it continues to use decocainized coca leaves for flavoring, with the extracted cocaine sold to pharmaceutical companies. The article also highlights Coca-Cola's modern initiatives, including sustainable coca farming and a strategic partnership with Microsoft for digital transformation.

title: Jack Daniel’s® and Coca‑Cola ARTD Debuts in South Africa
summary: Brown-Forman Corporation and The Coca-Cola Company have launched the Jack Daniel’s and Coca-Cola Alcoholic Ready-To-Drink (ARTD) spirit cooler in South Africa, following its success in over 25 global markets. This new offering, available in original and Zero Sugar variants, combines Jack Daniel’s Tennessee Whiskey with Coca-Cola in a convenient 300 ml slim can with 5% ABV. The companies emphasize responsible drinking and will implement a phased rollout in select liquor stores.

title: The history of and ties Coca-Cola has to Columbia
summary: This article explores the historical connections between Coca-Cola and Columbia, SC, explaining how the city earned its "Soda City" nickname due to the bottling company's presence. It highlights the former location of the Columbia Coca-Cola Bottling Company and mentions that Coca-Cola Bottling Company Consolidated is now located in Blythewood. A notable historical anecdote includes Michael Jordan judging a Coca-Cola-sponsored slam dunk contest in Columbia in 1988, won by former Gamecock Stephen "Jo Jo" English.

title: Alta demanda provoca desabasto de algunos productos de Coca-Cola
summary: Coca-Cola FEMSA confirmed a shortage of some of its products in Mexico due to exceptionally high demand, especially during a period of high temperatures in May. This surge in demand has led the company to prioritize the production of its most profitable product, Coca-Cola, over other flavored soft drinks, impacting availability and leading to price increases. Despite health warnings, Coca-Cola remains deeply ingrained in Mexican family culture, with Chiapas showing the highest consumption rates.

title: WPP brings back data hotshot Brian Lesser to lead GroupM
summary: WPP has appointed Brian Lesser as Global CEO of GroupM, its media investment arm. Lesser, who previously held a CEO role at GroupM North America and Infosum, is known for his expertise in data and technology-driven marketing. He replaces Christian Juhl, who will transition to president of corporate development within WPP.

title: Esta es la razón por la que hay desabasto de productos Coca Cola en México
summary: FEMSA has acknowledged a shortage of some Coca-Cola products in Mexico because the high demand has exceeded its production capacity. Despite record production levels, the company is struggling to meet demand, especially for non-Coca-Cola flavored beverages, leading them to prioritize the traditional Coca-Cola. To address this, FEMSA is adding two new production lines and has relocated another to the southeastern region to boost capacity.

title: Coca-Cola raises full-year sales guidance after stronger-than-expected second quarter
summary: Coca-Cola has raised its full-year sales guidance after a stronger-than-expected second quarter, driven by continued price increases. The company anticipates organic sales to grow between 9% and 10% this year, up from previous projections. Revenue for the April-June period rose 3% to $12.4 billion, surpassing Wall Street expectations, despite signs of softening demand among lower-income consumers due to price hikes.

title: Coca-Cola boosts full-year outlook thanks to higher prices
summary: Coca-Cola has raised its full-year outlook due to strong performance in the second quarter, primarily driven by higher pricing. The company's strategy of increasing prices has positively impacted its financial projections for the year.

title: Coca-Cola raises forecasts, bets on price hikes and ad blitz
summary: Coca-Cola has increased its annual sales and profit forecasts, expecting to benefit from strategic price hikes and an extensive advertising campaign, particularly in international markets where demand remains robust. The company's shares rose nearly 2% after it reported a surprising increase in second-quarter revenue. This strategy includes marketing new products and sponsoring major global events to appeal to a younger demographic, while also promoting budget-friendly options.

title: Coca-Cola leverages AI, technology to drive sales, volume in difficult economic climate
summary: Coca-Cola is using AI and digital technologies like its Studio X to boost sales and volumes, particularly for new products, in a challenging economic environment. The company exceeded Q2 expectations with a 3% revenue growth to $12.4 billion, despite a global average price increase of 9%, by enhancing marketing, innovation, and price-pack architecture through technology, including AI-driven personalized messaging to retailers. This strategy contrasts with its rival PepsiCo, which reported lower-than-expected revenue due to volume declines.

title: Hello World: The Coca-Cola Company Teams Up with the International Olympic Committee to Debut All-New Soundtrack of the Olympic Games Featuring Global Music Superstars
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has partnered with the International Olympic Committee to release an all-new soundtrack for the Olympic Games, titled "Hello World (Song of the Olympics TM )." Created by Ryan Tedder and performed by Gwen Stefani and Anderson .Paak, the song aims to celebrate togetherness, positivity, and the spirit of the Olympic and Paralympic Games Paris 2024. The collaboration marks a significant moment in Coca-Cola's 96-year relationship with the Olympic movement, with the song set to debut on July 25th alongside a music video.

title: Keurig Dr Pepper earnings meet estimates as higher prices fuel U.S. soda sales
summary: Keurig Dr Pepper (KDP) reported Q2 2024 earnings and revenue that met Wall Street expectations, driven by higher prices in its U.S. refreshment beverages division. The company's U.S. coffee division saw sales decline, while its international division experienced strong growth. KDP reiterated its full-year financial outlook.

title: Coca-Cola Southwest Beverages prioritizes company culture and employee engagement
summary: Coca-Cola Southwest Beverages (CCSWB) prioritizes company culture and employee engagement through its Market Investment Days (MIDs) program. This initiative involves executive and office-based teams visiting frontline staff to gather feedback and foster transparency, communication, and trust, leading to significant improvements and doubled sales since 2017. The program also led to the revival of the annual "truck rodeo" and system-wide adoption of effective practices, reinforcing CCSWB's commitment to its employees and community.

title: Mondelēz International taps Nestlé, P&G veteran as tech chief
summary: Mondelēz International has appointed Filippo Catalano as its new chief information and digital officer. Catalano, who previously held senior technology roles at Nestlé, Reckitt, and Procter & Gamble, will report directly to CEO Dirk Van de Put. This appointment reflects a broader trend of companies enhancing their tech leadership, with Catalano tasked with driving digital transformation for the global snack company.

title: Recipe for Magic: WPP and NVIDIA Omniverse Help The Coca-Cola Company Scale Generative AI Content That Pops With Brand Authenticity
summary: WPP and NVIDIA are partnering with The Coca-Cola Company to scale generative AI content for global marketing campaigns. Utilizing NVIDIA Omniverse and NIM microservices, particularly USD Search and USD Code, Coca-Cola can rapidly personalize and localize marketing assets across over 100 markets. This collaboration allows for quicker iteration on creative campaigns and the production of brand-authentic, culturally relevant 3D advertising content.

title: Mexico, Canada and beyond: Keurig Dr Pepper’s international growth strategy
summary: Keurig Dr Pepper is focusing on Mexico and Canada as key markets for its international growth strategy, driven by a "buy, build and partner model." The company reported a 15% increase in international sales in the latest quarter, with a strong performance in both Latin American and Canadian markets, and plans to expand into new areas like low and no-alcohol beverages. KDP sees its international portfolio, currently representing about $2 billion in sales annually, as an increasingly significant growth driver.

title: Embotelladora Andina duplica sus ganancias en el segundo trimestre
summary: Embotelladora Andina reported a significant increase in its second-quarter profits, attributing the growth to strong operational results and the absence of a non-operational loss recorded in 2023. The company's attributed profits reached $24.601 million (US$26 million), doubling the previous year's figures for the same period. This growth was driven by increased income in Brazil and Paraguay, although sales in Argentina and Chile saw a reduction.

title: Ganancias. Coca-Cola Andina aumentó sus beneficios casi 77%
summary: Coca-Cola Andina, an embottler for Coca-Cola products in South America, reported a 76.8% increase in net profits during the first half of the year, reaching over U$S 93 million. Consolidated net sales rose by 12% to over U$S 1.5 billion, although sales in Argentina decreased by 19.5%, marking it as the only market with negative growth. The company's adjusted EBITDA grew by 18.5%, driven by increased sales volumes in Brazil and Paraguay and higher sugar prices, despite a decrease in sales in Argentina.

title: Coca-Cola Consolidated Partners with ISN to Improve Contractor Safety and Compliance
summary: Coca-Cola Consolidated, the largest Coca-Cola bottler in the U.S., has selected ISNetworld as its primary contractor management system. This partnership with ISN aims to enhance contractor safety and compliance by assisting with site orientations, compliance reviews, documentation, and insurance. The company plans to implement the system across all manufacturing facilities and integrate compliance requirements within the first year.

title: FANTA® AND WARNER BROS. PICTURES ANNOUNCE GLOBAL PARTNERSHIP WITH THE HIGHLY ANTICIPATED NEW MOVIE BEETLEJUICE BEETLEJUICE WITH LIMITED-EDITION FLAVOUR
summary: Fanta and Warner Bros. Pictures have announced a global partnership to celebrate the release of the new movie Beetlejuice Beetlejuice, debuting in cinemas on September 6, 2024. This collaboration includes a limited-edition Fanta Beetlejuice flavor, character-themed packaging for the full Fanta range, and exclusive physical and digital experiences accessible via QR codes. The partnership aims to encourage consumers to "Summon What You Wanta" this Halloween season with unique activations throughout September and October.

title: Investors - Governance - Board of Directors - Person Details
summary: This page introduces Keith Credendino as the Chief Information Officer of Macy's, Inc., a role he assumed in August 2024. It details his responsibilities, which include overseeing information technology applications, infrastructure, and operations that support Macy's' data-first modernization strategy. The article also highlights his previous experience at Macy's as Senior Vice President, Technology Product Development, Customer Experience, and prior roles at Inspire Brands, The Home Depot, InterContinental Hotels Group, and Cox Enterprises, emphasizing his expertise in large-scale e-commerce, loyalty systems, and cloud-native infrastructure.

title: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners invests $105.5m in Australian manufacturing
summary: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners (CCEP) is investing $105.5 million to expand its manufacturing capabilities in Australia, funding a new Warmfill Line at its Moorabbin plant in Victoria. This investment will boost the production of Powerade and Fuze Tea, addressing rising demand for sports drinks and no-sugar variants. The project, including a new 4,200m² manufacturing hall and high-speed production line, is expected to reduce transportation by 2.9 million kilometers annually and will be operational by Q1 2026.

title: vitaminwater® Introduces Paint Your Rent: A Chance to Transform Your Living Space in Full vitaminwater Color This Summer
summary: vitaminwater is launching its "Paint Your Rent" campaign, inviting fans to creatively incorporate vitaminwater colors and flavors into their living spaces for a chance to win free rent for a year and custom design services from Havenly. The campaign aims to bring vibrancy into homes, offering five winners custom design inspiration and a color-coordinated mini-fridge stocked with vitaminwater flavors. Mood boards created with Havenly's lead designer, Kelsey Fischer, showcase how different vitaminwater flavors can inspire unique interior design aesthetics.

title: CCEP GB launches PMPs for Jack Daniel’s and Coca-Cola ARTD range
summary: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners Great Britain (CCEP GB) has introduced price-marked packs (PMPs) for its Jack Daniel’s and Coca-Cola alcohol ready-to-drink (ARTD) range to offer clear value to customers and boost sales in convenience stores. The 330ml cans, priced at £2.39, include Jack Daniel’s and Coca-Cola Original Taste and Zero Sugar variants, which CCEP GB considers essential stock for retailers. This initiative is supported by POS materials and forms part of a broader promotional campaign with consumer giveaways and retailer incentives.

title: Coca-Cola® Zero Sugar Kicks Off Fan-Focused Fall Sports Campaign with Exclusive Partnership with EA SPORTS™ College Football 25
summary: Coca-Cola Zero Sugar is launching a fall sports campaign, partnering with EA SPORTS™ College Football 25 as its exclusive CPG sponsor. The campaign includes in-game rewards like College Ultimate Team™ packs for scanning Coke Zero Sugar, a "Fan Work is Thirsty Work Tour" visiting college campuses, and opportunities to win merchandise and trips. This initiative extends the "Best Coke Ever?" platform, aiming to connect with sports fans through refreshing taste and engaging experiences.

title: Ball Corporation collaborates with global beverage brands to champion sustainable aluminium packaging
summary: Ball Corporation is partnering with major beverage brands like Coca-Cola and PepsiCo to advance sustainability in aluminum packaging. This collaboration aims to meet the rising demand for aluminum, driven by its recyclability and lower carbon footprint, while addressing the challenge of enhancing recyclability for mixed aluminum packaging. The company's initiatives include developing lightweight designs, boosting recycled content, and incorporating renewable energy to achieve decarbonization within the aluminum industry.

title: Coca-Cola Andina y Coca-Cola Embonor, inauguran planta que permitirá producir las primeras botellas de bebida con plástico reciclado en Chile
summary: Coca-Cola Andina and Coca-Cola Embonor have inaugurated Re-Ciclar, a state-of-the-art recycling plant in Chile, which will produce the country's first beverage bottles made with food-grade recycled plastic. This $35 million investment aims to reduce new plastic circulation and strengthen the circular economy, with a capacity to recycle over 350 million bottles annually. Starting in 2025, 15% of all Coca-Cola bottles in Chile will contain recycled PET resin, with plans for gradual increases towards 100% recycled packaging.

title: Swire Coca-Cola to Build 570,000 SF Bottling Plant Near Denver International Airport Campus
summary: Swire Coca-Cola USA plans to invest $350 million to $500 million in a new 570,000-square-foot bottling plant near Denver International Airport. This facility will replace two existing centers in Denver and is expected to break ground in Q3 2025, with operations starting in Q1 2027. The project, located on 97 acres, will employ approximately 200 people and will bottle both plastic bottles and aluminum cans.

title: Coca-Cola must face greenwashing lawsuit: D.C. Appeals Court
summary: The D.C. Court of Appeals has ruled that Coca-Cola must face a greenwashing lawsuit brought by the environmental nonprofit Earth Island Institute. The lawsuit alleges that Coca-Cola deceptively markets its sustainability efforts, overturning a prior dismissal by a lower court. The case will now proceed to determine if Coca-Cola's statements on sustainability constitute deceptive marketing practices under D.C. law, given its continued reliance on single-use plastics.

title: Former Chipotle boss Brian Niccol takes over Starbucks with long to-do list of problems
summary: Brian Niccol, formerly CEO of Chipotle Mexican Group, is taking over as Starbucks CEO with a challenging agenda, including declining sales and long order times. Despite his success at Chipotle, Wall Street remains cautious due to Starbucks' global footprint and complex issues like union negotiations and activist investor pressure. Niccol is expected to focus on high-impact projects, justify Starbucks' premium prices, streamline operations, and navigate the struggling China market, all while managing employee morale and the lingering influence of former CEO Howard Schultz.

title: Campbell Soup is changing its name to reflect a broader portfolio
summary: Campbell Soup plans to change its name to The Campbell's Company to better reflect its diversified product portfolio beyond soup. While soup remains a billion-dollar business, acquisitions like Snyder's-Lance and Sovos Brands, along with growth in other brands like Goldfish and Pepperidge Farm, mean snacks now account for roughly half of its sales. Shareholders are expected to vote on the name change at the annual meeting in November.

title: Carlsberg to become new PepsiCo bottler in Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan
summary: Carlsberg and PepsiCo are expanding their strategic partnership, with Carlsberg set to become the PepsiCo bottler in Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan from January 1, 2026. Carlsberg plans to invest over EUR 100 million in a new production facility in Kazakhstan, expecting a double-digit return on invested capital from the first year. This agreement strengthens Carlsberg's market presence and builds on their existing bottling agreements in other markets.

title: Coca-Cola commits to ‘critical’ open web advertising through curation
summary: Coca-Cola views the open web as critical for its advertising strategy, despite common industry perceptions of it being fraught with low-quality inventory and fraud. The company is actively investing in the open web outside of "walled gardens" by implementing curation strategies to ensure ad quality and mitigate risks. This approach allows Coca-Cola to build bespoke, localized marketplaces, leveraging SSPs for precise inventory targeting and aiming to restore confidence in programmatic buying.

title: D.C. Appellate Court Revives Case Against Coca-Cola, Placing "Sustainability" Claims Under Scrutiny
summary: The D.C. Court of Appeals has revived a "greenwashing" lawsuit against Coca-Cola, ruling that even aspirational statements about sustainability can be considered misleading under the D.C. Consumer Protection Procedures Act. This decision overturns a lower court’s dismissal, indicating that companies must ensure their sustainability claims, especially regarding mass-produced single-use plastics and recycling goals, are not deceptive. The ruling suggests that businesses can no longer insulate themselves from legal action by simply making vague or aspirational environmental commitments.

title: Coca-Cola Chairman and CEO James Quincey Recognized with the Yale Legend in Leadership Award
summary: James Quincey, Chairman and CEO of The Coca-Cola Company, is set to receive the Yale Legend in Leadership Award at the Yale CEO Caucus for his successful stewardship of the iconic brand. Under his leadership since 2017, Coca-Cola's stock is trading at near all-time highs, with increased revenues and an improved margin profile, driven by relentless product innovation and a reorientation towards a diverse beverage portfolio. He also significantly advanced the company's social responsibility initiatives, including water stewardship and philanthropic giving.

title: Chinese-born U.S. citizen gets 14 years for stealing trade secrets from Eastman, Coca-Cola
summary: Xiaorong You, a Chinese-born U.S. citizen, has been sentenced to 14 years in prison for stealing trade secrets from American companies, including Eastman and Coca-Cola, with the intent to establish a competing business in China. Her conviction was upheld on appeal, though the victim companies' loss figures were recalculated for resentencing. Judge Ronnie Greer reinstated the previous sentence and a $200,000 fine, highlighting her lack of responsibility and the threat posed to U.S. economic security.

title: The Coca-Cola Company and Bacardi Limited announce plans to debut BACARDÍ & Coca-Cola ready-to-drink cocktail
summary: The Coca-Cola Company and Bacardi Limited announced an agreement to launch a ready-to-drink (RTD) pre-mixed cocktail, BACARDÍ Mixed with Coca-Cola RTD. This product will first be available in select European markets and Mexico in 2025. The collaboration builds on the historical creation of the Cuba Libre cocktail, which combined BACARDÍ rum and Coca-Cola.

title: The Coca-Cola Company and Bacardi Limited Announce Plans to Debut BACARDÍ & Coca-Cola Ready-To-Drink Cocktail
summary: The Coca-Cola Company and Bacardi Limited announced a partnership to launch a ready-to-drink (RTD) BACARDÍ rum and Coca-Cola pre-mixed cocktail. This new product will debut in select European markets and Mexico in 2025, expanding both companies' presence in the growing alcohol RTD market. The collaboration highlights the historical connection between BACARDÍ rum and Coca-Cola, famously used in the Cuba Libre cocktail.

title: Cracker Barrel Celebrates 55th Birthday with Special Promotions
summary: Cracker Barrel Old Country Store is celebrating its 55th birthday with special promotions for guests, including free slices of its Double Chocolate Fudge Coca-Cola Cake and free beverages from its original 1969 menu for Cracker Barrel Rewards members with a minimum dine-in purchase. These offers are available from September 19th to September 22nd, honoring the brand's heritage and loyal customers. The celebration highlights Cracker Barrel's commitment to authentic country-inspired experiences and homestyle cooking.

title: Coca-Cola Is Doing Away With One Of Its Sodas
summary: Coca-Cola is discontinuing its Spiced Coke flavor in 2025 due to a lack of consumer adoption. This decision follows a history of Coca-Cola adding and removing products, with the company learning a significant lesson from the "New Coke" incident in 1985. Coca-Cola plans to introduce a new flavor in 2025, which may be announced during the Super Bowl.

title: Coca-Cola discontinues Spiced flavor months after debut
summary: Coca-Cola has announced the discontinuation of its Spiced flavor, just months after its debut in February. The company plans to replace it with an "exciting new flavor" in 2025. Spiced was the first permanent new flavor introduced by Coca-Cola in over three years.

title: Coca-Cola phasing out ‘permanent’ flavor less than a year after debut
summary: Coca-Cola is discontinuing its "permanent" Coca-Cola Spiced flavor less than a year after its North American debut. The company stated this is part of a strategy to adjust its product range and introduce an exciting new flavor in 2025. Coca-Cola Spiced was intended to be a permanent addition alongside Classic, Cherry, Vanilla, and Cherry Vanilla flavors.

title: Coca-Cola & Bacardi to launch RTD cocktail as innovation heats up in the space
summary: Coca-Cola and Bacardi are partnering to launch a ready-to-drink (RTD) pre-mixed cocktail, "Bacardi Mixed with Coca-Cola RTD," set for release in 2025 in select European markets and Mexico. This collaboration highlights a growing trend of major soft drink and alcohol companies partnering to tap into the expanding RTD market. The article also details similar ventures by other big brands like PepsiCo, Monster, and other Coca-Cola partnerships, showcasing the rapid innovation and category blurring within the beverage industry.

title: Coca-Cola Consolidated Unveils $25M in Upgrades to West Memphis Production Facility
summary: Coca-Cola Consolidated has invested $25 million into upgrading its West Memphis production facility, including a new state-of-the-art bottling line to increase production from 26 million to 29 million cases annually. The upgrades also introduce new lighter-weight bottles made from 100% recycled plastic for 20-ounce Coca-Cola products and will create 19 new jobs. This expansion highlights the company's continued commitment to the community and economy, alongside a $1.2 million contribution to Arkansas community programs.

title: Carlos Arenas deja dirección de Oxxo México; Carlos Arroyo asume nuevo rol
summary: Carlos Arenas will retire from his role as General Director of Oxxo Mexico after 40 years with Femsa. Carlos Arroyo Rico will succeed him, taking the position on November 19, 2024. Arroyo, with extensive experience in retail and Quick Service Restaurants, will report to José Antonio Fernández Garza, General Director of Femsa Proximity and Health.

title: Why Ambev Stock Remains Unattractive Despite Solid Q2 Results (NYSE:ABEV)
summary: Ambev's Q2 results showed margin recovery and stable volumes, but the article argues that slow growth in the mature Brazilian beer market and currency risks make the stock unattractive, despite its reasonable valuation. The author suggests Ambev's growth prospects and returns are less compelling compared to other Brazilian stocks and high-yield treasuries, presenting a high opportunity cost for investors.

title: FEMSA, Delek US Close Sale of Retail Network
summary: FEMSA has finalized its acquisition of Delek US Holdings Inc.'s retail operations, including 249 convenience stores primarily in Texas, for approximately $385 million. This move marks a significant expansion for the Mexican beverage and convenience-store giant into the U.S. market, leveraging its expertise gained from operating the OXXO chain. The acquisition is seen as a strategic fit for FEMSA to build a scalable platform in the fragmented U.S. market, with potential for future expansion.

title: U.S. Soft Drinks Market Size, Share & Trends Analysis
summary: The U.S. soft drinks market is projected to reach USD 467.18 billion by 2030, growing at a CAGR of 7.5% from 2024. This growth is driven by the increasing population and easy availability of soft drinks, though health concerns and counterfeit products pose challenges. Key players dominating the market include Coca-Cola, PepsiCo, and Dr Pepper Snapple.

title: Beer’s Hot Brands –
summary: The article highlights the "Hot Brands" in the beer and FMB (flavored malt beverage) sectors for 2023, showcasing brands that achieved impressive volume gains despite a sluggish overall industry. It details that 31 brands made the list, including a mix of domestic, imported, FMBs, craft beers, and non-alcoholic options, with Constellation Brands and Molson Coors Beverage having multiple entries. The success is attributed to various factors such as strategic marketing, new product innovation, and capitalizing on consumer trends and distribution.

title: Florence manufacturing plant closes, resulting in layoffs for 108 workers
summary: Multinational manufacturing company Jabil is closing one of its facilities on Ted Bushelman Drive in Florence, Kentucky, resulting in the layoff of 108 plant workers. The closure is due to one of Jabil's customers moving out of state, and the layoffs are projected to be completed by December 6. Jabil, a Fortune 150 company headquartered in St. Petersburg, Florida, manufactures electronic circuit boards and systems for major companies including Apple, Coca-Cola, and Alphabet.

title: Innovation Beverage Group Through Sysco, the Global Leader in Foodservice Distribution, Announces Australian Bitters Now Available Nationwide in the U.S.
summary: Innovation Beverage Group (IBG) announced that its award-winning Australian Bitters are now available nationwide in the U.S. through Sysco, the global leader in foodservice distribution. This expansion marks IBG's entry into the foodservice category beyond traditional alcohol distributors, targeting the U.S. which is the largest bitters market globally. The partnership aims to make Australian Bitters more accessible to restaurants, bars, and consumers across the United States.

title: Coca-Cola and The Coca-Cola Foundation Support Hurricane Relief
summary: The Coca-Cola Company and The Coca-Cola Foundation are providing immediate assistance to areas affected by Hurricanes Helene and Milton, including Florida, Georgia, and the Carolinas. Their relief efforts include substantial grants to the American Red Cross totaling $1.75 million, donations of nearly 50,000 cases of water, and a $75,000 donation to Team Rubicon. The company is also collaborating with other disaster relief agencies to support long-term recovery and rebuilding in the hard-hit regions.

title: Nuevo: BBDO Chile, Banco de Chile y Teletón buscan inspirar a las nuevas generaciones a donar
summary: BBDO Chile, Banco de Chile, and Teletón launched an animated campaign titled "Solidaridad: el orgullo de Chile" to encourage donations and inspire younger generations. The campaign highlights the beauty of Chile's landscapes and the pride the country feels for its people's solidarity during the Teletón. Produced by Believe, the initiative aims to boost participation in the charitable cause.

title: The Coca-Cola Co. spotlights innovation, insights at NACS Show
summary: The Coca-Cola Co. showcased new beverage innovations, sustainable initiatives, and retail insights at the 2024 NACS Show. Upcoming products for 2025 include Coca-Cola Orange Cream, Sprite + Tea, and POWERADE Xtra Sour. The company also highlighted partnerships for sustainability and new platforms like Coca-Cola Lens to help retailers drive traffic and increase basket size.

title: Coca-Cola Consolidated recalls ‘zero sugar’ drinks that contain sugar
summary: Coca-Cola Consolidated has recalled 13,152 cartons of Minute Maid Zero Sugar Lemonade in Indiana, Kentucky, and Ohio because they mistakenly contained regular Minute Maid Lemonade. The error, classified as a Class II recall by the FDA, means consumers received sugary drinks instead of the advertised zero-sugar product, which can have health implications for individuals managing sugar intake, such as diabetics. The company initiated the voluntary recall in September and states that all affected products are now off the market.

title: Netflix Executive Bela Bajaria Elected to Board of Directors of The Coca-Cola Company
summary: Bela Bajaria, Chief Content Officer for Netflix Inc., has been elected to the Board of Directors of The Coca-Cola Company, effective immediately, bringing the board to 12 directors. Bajaria oversees all television and film content for Netflix globally with an annual budget of approximately $17 billion. The Coca-Cola Company also declared a regular quarterly dividend of 48.5 cents per common share.

title: Coca-Cola CEO says McDonald's E. coli outbreak won't hurt beverage company's sales
summary: Coca-Cola CEO James Quincey does not expect the E. coli outbreak linked to McDonald's Quarter Pounder burgers to significantly impact Coca-Cola's sales, despite McDonald's being its largest restaurant customer. The CDC has linked the outbreak to McDonald's Quarter Pounder burgers, causing temporary unavailability in some regions and prompting the removal of certain onions. Coca-Cola aims to support McDonald's through the situation, even as both companies face challenges from sluggish consumer spending.

title: Coca-Cola recalls 28 million bottles in Austria
summary: Coca-Cola is recalling 28 million half-liter plastic bottles of its products in Austria due to a potential risk of small metal pieces being present from a factory mishap. This "precautionary measure" applies to Coke, Fanta, Sprite, and MezzoMix beverages with best-before dates between February 4, 2025, and April 12, 2025. Consumers can return affected bottles for a refund, and Austrian authorities are monitoring the recall process.

title: Monster and Celsius Energized: Which Stock Offers More Upside?
summary: This article compares two leading energy drink companies, Monster Beverage (MNST) and Celsius Holdings (CELH), analyzing their market positions, financial performance, and future upside potential. While Monster is a larger, established brand targeting adrenaline junkies, Celsius caters to fitness enthusiasts and shows greater upside according to analyst price targets, despite both facing challenges from health concerns and consumer spending habits. The piece details their respective Q2 2024 earnings, distribution partnerships with Coca-Cola and PepsiCo, and analyst ratings, concluding that Celsius offers significantly more growth potential.

title: Keurig Dr Pepper raises its bets on energy drinks with $990 million deal for Ghost
summary: Keurig Dr Pepper is acquiring a 60% stake in energy-drink maker Ghost for $990 million, with plans to purchase the remaining stake in 2028, to strengthen its refreshment beverages portfolio. This move comes as the energy drink market continues to grow, attracting deals from other major beverage companies like PepsiCo. The acquisition is expected to close in late 2024 or early 2025 and modestly aid Keurig's adjusted profit starting in 2025.

title: A Trick-or-Treat Favorite, Tootsie Rolls Have Been Made in America for 128 Years
summary: This article highlights the 128-year history of Tootsie Rolls, a beloved American candy, and its continued production in Chicago. It details the company's manufacturing process, its significant daily output of 65 million Tootsie Rolls, and its considerable share in the annual Halloween candy market. The article also touches upon the candy's cultural impact, its simple ingredients making it allergen-friendly, and mentions other Made in America candy companies for Halloween.

title: Coca-Cola FEMSA: Impressive Growth Amid Headwinds
summary: Coca-Cola FEMSA (KOF) reported robust Q3 results with significant revenue and EBITDA growth, driven by digital transformation and efficiency improvements. The company's strategic initiatives and geographic expansions are set to support continued medium-term growth. With a forward P/E of 15.3x, KOF shows a potential upside of 16%–25% by 2025, leading to a reaffirmed Buy rating.

title: The World Is My Yard: Platform Gives HBCU Students Access to Campus Experiences, Career Prep Resources and More
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has launched "The World Is My Yard," a digital platform on the +one mobile app, offering Historically Black Colleges and University (HBCU) students access to campus experiences, career preparation, and wellness resources. This initiative expands Coca-Cola's long-standing support for HBCUs, providing tools for academic success and post-graduate career readiness. The platform includes event information, career prep resources like internships and skill-building courses, and perks such as premium subscriptions and discounts.

title: Build-A-Bear Workshop Appoints Kim Utlaut as Senior Vice President, Chief Brand Officer
summary: Build-A-Bear Workshop has appointed Kim Utlaut as its new Senior Vice President and Chief Brand Officer. Utlaut, previously with The Coca-Cola Company, will be responsible for evolving Build-A-Bear's brand and communications strategy, focusing on strengthening customer relationships across its global offerings. This appointment comes after three consecutive record-setting years for Build-A-Bear, as the company continues to expand its retail presence and advance its digital transformation.

title: LA County sues Coke, Pepsi over ‘deception' in plastics recycling
summary: Los Angeles County has filed a lawsuit against Coca-Cola and Pepsi, alleging deceptive practices related to their plastic packaging recycling claims. The lawsuit highlights plastic pollution in the Los Angeles River as a key area of concern, suggesting that the companies' recycling assertions are misleading consumers and contributing to environmental issues. This legal action targets the marketing and environmental impact of plastic use by major beverage companies.

title: THE COCA-COLA COMPANY RELAUNCHES BARRILITOS IN CALIFORNIA & TEXAS
summary: The Coca-Cola Company is relaunching Barrilitos, a Mexican soft drink brand established in 1938, in California and Texas. The authentic soft drink, bottled and produced in México, will be available in four fruit flavors and two sizes, aiming to connect with multicultural Gen Z, Millennials, and families. This regional relaunch introduces a refreshed brand identity while preserving its classic flavors and tradition to meet the growing demand for nostalgic soft drinks with cultural heritage.

title: The Coca-Cola Company Announces New Reporting Lines for Costa Coffee and innocent Businesses to Europe Operating Unit
summary: The Coca-Cola Company announced that innocent Drinks and Costa Coffee will report to its Europe operating unit, effective January 1, 2025, to streamline their organizational structure. This change will also sunset the Global Ventures group, with oversight of the Monster Beverage Corp. investment moving to CFO John Murphy and financials for 2022-2024 to be reissued to reflect these adjustments. The reclassification aims to integrate these businesses more directly with operating units for future growth.

title: EXCLUSIVE: CCEP & Britvic boycotts hit sales at some shops
summary: Some convenience stores and wholesalers are experiencing localized sales drops for Coca-Cola and Britvic products due to Palestine-related boycotts, despite broader data showing no widespread impact. Alternative brands like AG Barr and Salaam Cola are seeing increased sales in affected areas. Retailers in heavily impacted regions report customer criticism and are adapting by either not stocking boycotted items or donating profits to related causes.

title: Soda is making a comeback with higher sales for Coke, Pepsi
summary: Soda sales, particularly for Coca-Cola and Dr Pepper, are experiencing a surprising comeback after two decades of decline. Consumers are opting for sodas as an affordable treat over more expensive alternatives, despite health concerns. The growth is also fueled by new marketing strategies, zero-sugar options like Coke Zero, and social media trends such as "dirty soda."

title: PepsiCo beats New York state's lawsuit over plastics pollution
summary: A New York court dismissed the state's lawsuit against PepsiCo over plastics pollution, with the judge criticizing Attorney General Letitia James for bringing the case. The judge stated that James failed to prove PepsiCo created a public nuisance, arguing that littering was a public issue, not a corporate one. Both James and PepsiCo have reacted to the decision, with James expressing disappointment and PepsiCo reiterating its commitment to plastics reduction.

title: PepsiCo Wins Plastics Pollution Lawsuit
summary: PepsiCo has won a lawsuit brought by New York's Attorney General, Letitia James, accusing the company of polluting the environment with single-use plastic packaging. A state Supreme Court Justice dismissed the case, stating that James failed to prove PepsiCo created a public nuisance and criticized the lawsuit as "predatory." PepsiCo expressed satisfaction with the decision and reiterated its commitment to plastics reduction and recycling.

title: Coca-Cola and PepsiCo sued (again) over recycling claims. What brands should know
summary: Los Angeles County has filed a civil lawsuit against Coca-Cola and PepsiCo, accusing them of deceptive marketing regarding the recyclability of single-use plastic bottles and deeming plastic a "public nuisance." This action follows a similar, though dismissed, lawsuit in New York against PepsiCo, highlighting a growing trend of jurisdictions challenging corporate claims about plastics. Experts suggest companies should reduce rhetoric about recycling, focus on alternative packaging, and support uniform standards for sustainability claims to avoid similar legal challenges.

title: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners cuts annual sales forecast on weak Europe demand
summary: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners (CCEP) has lowered its annual sales forecast due to reduced demand in Europe and weakness in Indonesia, the latter linked to the Middle East conflict. Although soda demand remains resilient, lower-income consumers are cutting back on dining out, affecting CCEP's volumes. The company now expects annual comparable revenue to rise about 3.5%, down from a prior forecast of 4%.

title: How Creativity Powers Coca-Cola
summary: During Advertising Week LATAM, Rafael Pitanguy of VML and Luciana Mendes of The Coca-Cola Company discussed how creativity rooted in Latin American culture powers Coca-Cola's global brand strategy. They highlighted the importance of balancing originality with familiarity and constant reinvention to keep the iconic brand relevant across generations. Several award-winning VML campaigns for Coca-Cola were showcased as examples of this successful creative approach.

title: Wheels of Change: the Story of NIO (Part 1)
summary: The article "Wheels of Change: the Story of NIO (Part 1)" details the evolution of NIO Inc. from its founding in 2014 by Li Bin, highlighting its rapid ascent in the high-end EV market, its significant investments in R&D, and the development of its unique battery swapping ecosystem. It covers strategic financial injections, key product launches like the ES8 and ES6, and the company's commitment to in-house technology development even through periods of financial struggle. The story emphasizes how NIO has transformed from a struggling startup to a major player in the intelligent electric vehicle industry, with a focus on user experience and technological innovation.

title: Top 100 Consumer Goods Companies of 2024
summary: The article ranks the top 100 consumer goods companies of 2024 based on fiscal year 2023 revenue, highlighting the top 10. It details how these companies navigated challenges like inflation and supply chain issues by balancing cost savings with investments in technology, operational efficiency, and consumer engagement strategies. The report emphasizes the increasing adoption of digital tools, AI, and C-suite changes to drive growth and maintain competitive advantage in a dynamic market.

title: Cheers! Coca-Cola Beverages Florida unveils new sales and distribution center in NW Ocala
summary: Coca-Cola Beverages Florida has opened a new $10 million sales and distribution center in northwest Ocala, creating 120 jobs and demonstrating a significant investment in the local community. The 28,000-square-foot facility will serve Marion and Sumter counties, distributing a wide range of Coca-Cola products. Company officials emphasized their commitment to community engagement, environmental action, and economic empowerment, including partnerships with local organizations like Habitat for Humanity and the Boys & Girls Club of Marion County.

title: Pepsi, Coca-Cola untruthful about about single-use plastic waste, lawsuit claims
summary: Los Angeles County has filed a lawsuit against PepsiCo and Coca-Cola, alleging the beverage giants misled consumers about the effectiveness of recycling in reducing single-use plastic waste. The county claims both companies promote false information about their environmental efforts, despite contributing significantly to plastic pollution and the presence of microplastics in their products. The lawsuit seeks to end these alleged deceptive practices, demanding financial restitution and civil penalties.

title: Primo Brands completes merger with BlueTriton affiliate
summary: Primo Brands has completed its merger with BlueTriton Brands, leading to the closure of BlueTriton's Aberfoyle, Ont. water bottling facility by January 2025. This merger brings together an iconic brand portfolio, including Poland Spring and Pure Life, aiming for sustainable shareholder value through operational efficiencies and synergy goals. The Aberfoyle facility was previously owned by Nestlé Waters Canada before its acquisition by One Rock Capital Partners in partnership with Metropolous & Co.

title: Are Wall Street Analysts Bullish on Coca-Cola Stock?
summary: Wall Street analysts maintain a "Strong Buy" consensus rating for Coca-Cola (KO) stock, with a mean price target suggesting a 16.6% upside from current levels. This optimism follows KO's Q3 earnings beat and expected 6% EPS growth for the current fiscal year. Despite challenges in the European market, the company's outperformance against broad market indices and sector-specific ETFs in the past year indicates a robust financial outlook.

title: Top 10 Soft Drink Brands in the World in 2026
summary: This article lists the top 10 soft drink brands globally in 2026 based on market revenues, highlighting the beverage industry's growth despite health concerns. It details key financial data and popular product offerings for each brand, including PepsiCo, Unilever, Coca-Cola, and others. The article also notes the industry's shift towards healthier alternatives to attract health-conscious consumers.

title: Victory! Coca-Cola, PepsiCo, and Others Cut Funding for Barbaric Animal Tests After Push From PETA
summary: Following advocacy from PETA, five major food and beverage companies, including PepsiCo, Coca-Cola, Campbell Soup Company, Sensient Technologies, and Fresh Innovations, have ceased funding cruel animal experiments at the University of Wisconsin–Madison Food Research Institute. These companies intervened after learning their donations were being used for horrific tests such as force-feeding mice parasite-infested feces and poisoning pregnant monkeys. As a result, the Food Research Institute has changed its policy to allow corporations to restrict their donations from being used for animal experimentation.

title: Victory! Sensient Technologies Stops Funding Deadly Animal Tests After PETA Appeal
summary: Sensient Technologies has announced it will stop funding animal experiments at the University of Wisconsin–Madison Food Research Institute after an appeal from PETA. This decision follows similar withdrawals of support from other major companies like PepsiCo, Coca-Cola, Campbell Soup Company, and Fresh Innovations. The Food Research Institute has since changed its policy to allow sponsors to restrict their donations from being used for animal experimentation.

title: New York’s plastic lawsuit against PepsiCo has been dismissed. What’s next?
summary: A New York state Supreme Court judge dismissed a plastic pollution lawsuit against PepsiCo, labeling it "predatory." This decision raises questions about similar pending lawsuits nationwide, though environmental attorneys express confidence that analogous litigation can still succeed elsewhere, citing potential appeals and the legal merits of public nuisance and consumer protection claims related to plastic waste.

title: Coke Florida Names Industry Veteran Andy Hill as Chief Customer Officer
summary: Coca-Cola Beverages Florida, LLC (Coke Florida) has appointed Andy Hill as its Senior Vice President, Chief Customer Officer. Hill, an industry veteran with over 30 years of experience, will lead various customer-facing functions and provide strategic oversight to the executive leadership team. CEO Troy Taylor highlighted Hill's experience across consumer and retail industries and his role in integrating sales and marketing to enhance customer experience.

title: Coca-Cola causes controversy with AI-made ad
summary: Coca-Cola is facing online backlash for an AI-made Christmas promotional video, which critics are calling "soulless" and "devoid of any actual creativity." The video, intended to homage a 1995 commercial, has sparked controversy among creatives who argue against using AI to replace human artists. Despite the criticism, some experts believe that the cost savings and improving technology will lead to continued corporate adoption of AI in advertising.

title: Más de 80 mujeres se graduaron del Programa Mujeres ON de Coca-Cola FEMSA Costa Rica
summary: Over 80 women graduated from the third edition of the "Mujeres ON" program by Coca-Cola FEMSA Costa Rica, aimed at empowering women micro-entrepreneurs. Since its inception in 2022, the program has trained over 250 women, providing them with essential business skills, legal guidance, financial knowledge, and commercial support. The initiative, a collaboration with several key organizations, seeks to strengthen women's businesses in the food, beverage, and commerce sectors, fostering economic development and equality.

title: Coca-Cola Faces Furious Backlash Over New AI Advert That's "Ruined Christmas"
summary: The Coca-Cola Company is facing backlash for its new AI-generated Christmas advert, which marks the second year of using the technology in its festive campaigns. Despite criticism from the public who feel it lacks the "essence of Christmas" and argue for human animators, Coca-Cola is defending its use of AI, calling it the future of creativity and storytelling. The company highlighted AI's ability to control cinematic details and create immersive stories as a "transformational leap" in content creation.

title: Investors urge Coca-Cola, Kraft Heinz, others to provide transparency on products’ health impact
summary: Over 30 investors and asset managers, managing over $3 trillion in assets, have urged leading food and beverage companies like Coca-Cola, Kraft Heinz, and PepsiCo to annually disclose the "healthiness" of their products. This coalition, spearheaded by ShareAction, asked the companies to adopt an internationally accepted nutrition rating system and disclose healthiness metrics, including sales-weighted average scores, to address the systemic risk posed by poor health and obesity. The investors believe greater transparency will promote healthier product portfolios and long-term financial and social value.

title: Coca-Cola: Quenching Israel’s genocidal soldiers’ thirst
summary: The BDS Movement has endorsed a #BoycottCoke campaign due to Coca-Cola's alleged complicity in Israeli war crimes through its operations in Israeli settlements, deemed illegal under international law. The timing of this endorsement is influenced by images of Israeli soldiers with Coke cans during the ongoing conflict and calls from Palestinian activists, leading the Palestinian BDS National Committee to prioritize the boycott to pressure the company to end its involvement.

title: Coca Cola reactivó su planta en Mendoza con dos ejes: innovación y sostenibilidad
summary: Coca-Cola has reactivated its bottling plant in Mendoza, Argentina, introducing a new line for returnable PET bottles (2L, 2.5L) and glass bottles (1.25L). This initiative emphasizes sustainability and circular economy principles, aiming to reduce plastic waste by promoting reuse and offering consumers a more economical option. The plant is equipped with advanced technology capable of processing 48,000 liters per hour, aligning with environmental responsibility and community demand for sustainable practices.

title: Sorbitol Market to Reach USD 3,387.8 Mn by 2033
summary: The global sorbitol market is projected to reach USD 3,387.8 million by 2033, growing at a CAGR of 6.7% from USD 1,771.2 million in 2023. This growth is driven by increasing demand for sugar-free products in food, beverages, pharmaceuticals, and personal care, despite challenges like raw material price volatility and potential gastrointestinal issues. Key players like ADM and Cargill are expanding their sorbitol offerings to capitalize on rising health and wellness trends.

title: Designated Driver
summary: Coca-Cola is bringing back its "Designated Driver" initiative for the 21st year across the island of Ireland. This campaign rewards designated drivers during the Christmas season with two free soft drinks or water from participating venues throughout December. The aim is to promote safe Christmas travel for friends and family.

title: 2 no-brainer Warren Buffett stocks to buy into 2025
summary: As 2024 concludes, investors are looking to Warren Buffett's philosophy for guidance. This article highlights two "forever stocks" from Buffett's portfolio, Pool Corporation (NASDAQ: POOL) and Coca-Cola (NYSE: KO), as compelling long-term opportunities for 2025. It examines their recent performance, financial stability, and potential for growth.

title: Up 21% in 2024, Is This Vanguard ETF the Best Way to Invest in Warren Buffett Value Stocks Like Berkshire Hathaway, Coca-Cola, Bank of America, and Chevron?
summary: This article examines whether the Vanguard Mega Cap Value ETF (MGV) is a good way to invest in Warren Buffett's value stocks, given its 21% gain in 2024. It compares the ETF's diversified holdings, including Berkshire Hathaway, Coca-Cola, Bank of America, and Chevron, with Buffett's concentrated investment strategy. The article also discusses the option of directly investing in Berkshire Hathaway or its top holdings for investors seeking a more direct approach or dividend income.

title: Coca-Cola and Women’s Foodservice Forum Inspire Brilliance at Leadership Development Workshop
summary: The Coca-Cola Company hosted over 200 leaders at its global headquarters for a Women’s Foodservice Forum (WFF) Leadership Development Workshop, aimed at inspiring action, fostering growth, and facilitating connections for women in the industry. This event, part of an eight-city tour, reinforced Coca-Cola’s commitment to its 2030 aspiration of having 50% women in leadership globally, through partnerships that support impactful programming. Speakers focused on topics such as broadening one's career perspective, managing fear, and leveraging personal "superpowers."

title: The Coca-Cola Company Evolves Voluntary Environmental Goals
summary: The Coca-Cola Company announced updated voluntary environmental goals, building on decades of sustainability work to improve water security in high-risk locations, reduce packaging waste, and decrease emissions. These revised goals aim to enhance long-term business resilience and positively impact local communities. Achieving these objectives will necessitate ongoing investment in innovation, infrastructure, enabling legislation, and collaboration with partners.

title: Water, Packaging & Emission Goals: Coca-Cola's 2035 Vision
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has updated its environmental goals with a 2035 vision centered on circularity and waste reduction. Key objectives include securing water in 200 high-risk areas, increasing recycled material content in packaging to 35-40% and a 70-75% collection rate, and aligning Scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions reductions with the Paris Agreement's 1.5°C goal. The company emphasizes collaboration, investment, and transparent reporting to achieve these ambitious sustainability targets.

title: Coca-Cola 'evolves' sustainability goals, timelines
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has revised its sustainability goals, extending timelines and reducing targets for recycled content and packaging collection, while eliminating previous goals related to reusable packaging and virgin plastic reduction. The company cites learnings, innovation needs, and infrastructure challenges for this evolution, aligning with other major brands that are adjusting ambitious 2025 or 2030 targets. Notably, virgin plastic use increased between 2020 and 2023 due to business growth, despite efforts to lightweight packaging and use rPET.

title: Reportan 13 de las 35 empresas del IPC en la BMV ganancias en 2024
summary: Only 13 of the 35 companies listed on the Mexican Stock Exchange's S&P/BMV IPC index have reported positive returns in 2024, with the overall index declining by 9.8%. Genomma Lab, Chedraui, and Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacífico (GAP) lead the companies with gains, attributed to strong quarterly results, rising metal prices, and favorable exchange rates. Conversely, 22 companies have seen negative performance, with Orbia, Grupo Carso, and Grupo Bimbo experiencing the worst drops due to profit-taking and market reactions to government policies and international uncertainty.

title: Coca-Cola vs. Procter & Gamble: Which Is the Better Dow Dividend King Stock to Buy Before the End of the Year?
summary: This article compares Coca-Cola and Procter & Gamble, both Dow Dividend Kings, to determine which is a better investment by the end of the year. While both face challenges with sales volume, Coca-Cola is highlighted for its better valuation and higher dividend yield. Procter & Gamble, despite its strong capital return program and operating margins, trades above its historical P/E average, whereas Coke is below.

title: Greenpeace USA slams Coca-Cola’s abandoned environmental promises
summary: Greenpeace USA criticizes The Coca-Cola Company for abandoning its 2022 commitment to offer 25% of its beverage volume globally in reusable packaging by 2030. Coca-Cola, identified as the world's worst plastic polluter for six consecutive years, continues to increase its plastic bottle production despite joining voluntary environmental initiatives. Greenpeace USA calls for governments to hold corporations accountable and ban single-use plastic packaging.

title: Coca-Cola rolls back sustainability goals, timelines
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has scaled back and eliminated several of its voluntary sustainability goals, including those related to reusable packaging and virgin plastic reduction, and extended its timeframe to 2035. The company's new targets include aiming for 35% to 40% recycled material in primary packaging by 2035 and collecting 70% to 75% of bottles and cans introduced into the market annually. This adjustment follows a trend of large brands not meeting ambitious environmental targets, with Coca-Cola citing business growth as a reason for not reducing virgin plastic use in previous years.

title: The Coca-Cola Company Names Henrique Braun Executive Vice President and Chief Operating Officer
summary: The Coca-Cola Company announced Henrique Braun has been named Executive Vice President and Chief Operating Officer, effective January 1, 2025. In this expanded role, Braun will oversee all of the company’s operating units worldwide, reporting directly to Chairman and CEO James Quincey. He previously served as EVP and President, International Development, and held various leadership positions across North America, Europe, Asia, and Latin America since joining the company in 1996.

title: WPP and Universal Music Group to create dynamic music and entertainment solutions for global brands
summary: WPP and Universal Music Group have announced a strategic partnership to create dynamic music and entertainment solutions for global brands. This collaboration will leverage UMG's artists, labels, and data insights with WPP's creative scale to develop music-focused campaigns and responsibly explore AI's role in connecting brands and artists. The initiative builds on previous successful collaborations, aiming to enhance brand engagement through music.

title: Universal Music Group inks strategic partnership with advertising giant WPP
summary: Universal Music Group (UMG) has announced a strategic partnership with WPP, a large multinational advertising and public relations company. The collaboration aims to provide clients' brands with advanced audience engagement strategies by leveraging music and UMG's artist network. Additionally, the partnership will explore how AI can enhance connections between brands and artists, building on past successful collaborations like the Coke Studio and Sprite Limelight platforms.

title: Kraft Heinz and Mondelēz International among companies targeted by UPF lawsuit
summary: A lawsuit filed in Pennsylvania alleges that major food companies, including Mondelēz International and Kraft Heinz, deliberately engineer ultra-processed foods (UPFs) to be addictive, particularly targeting children. The lawsuit claims these practices contribute to chronic diseases and mimics tactics used by tobacco companies. The food industry, however, has vehemently denied these accusations, asserting its commitment to food safety and lawful operations.

title: Coca-Cola Co. promotes Henrique Braun to COO role
summary: The Coca-Cola Co. has promoted long-time veteran Henrique Braun to the position of chief operating officer, effective January 1st. Braun, who joined the company in 1996, will continue to oversee international development units and report directly to chairman and CEO James Quincey. This expanded role recognizes Braun's impressive track record in driving growth and operational accomplishments within the company.

title: Dollar General Releases Holiday Deals for December 16-24 - Final Days of DG’s 24 Days of Savings
summary: Dollar General has announced its final holiday deals for December 16-24 as part of its "24 Days of Savings" promotion, featuring daily discounted items. These offers include deals on holiday tins, beverages, paper towels, pizzas, a stand mixer, and a mini-fridge. The promotions are available in-store while supplies last, supplementing other holiday savings.

title: Kraft Heinz, Nestle, others market unhealthy, addictive foods on kids, lawsuit claims
summary: A lawsuit has been filed against major food companies including Kraft Heinz, Nestle, and General Mills, alleging they market unhealthy and addictive ultra-processed foods to children. The plaintiff, Bryce Martinez, claims these marketing practices have led to an "explosion" of chronic diseases since the 1980s and that the companies have knowingly inflicted harm in pursuit of profits. The lawsuit seeks compensatory, economic, statutory, treble, punitive, and exemplary damages.

title: Coca-Cola’s confusing emissions claims draw fire
summary: Coca-Cola's updated emissions targets are drawing criticism for appearing to lower ambition and introduce confusing changes to baselines and included subsidiaries. While the company claims an "evolution" towards a more aggressive 1.5-degree pathway, the removal of plastic reduction goals and shifting reporting metrics make it difficult to assess their true climate commitment. This inconsistency makes it challenging for external observers like media and sustainability researchers to accurately evaluate the company's progress and intentions.

title: From Tide Pods to Coach bags, how Fortune 500 companies use museums of their hits and misses to drive success
summary: Fortune 500 companies are increasingly utilizing in-house museums and archives to drive success by learning from past product hits and misses. These collections, like P&G's "Wall of Failures" and Coach's handbag archive, serve practical purposes beyond nostalgia, guiding product development, C-suite decision-making, and culture-building among employees. The article highlights how brands like Delta, Walmart, Lego, Reckitt, and Coca-Cola leverage their histories to inspire innovation, foster a sense of purpose, and navigate challenges.

title: ‘Forgotten’: How one Mexican city struggles against big industry for water
summary: The Mexican city of San Cristóbal de las Casas faces severe water stress due to excessive extraction by multinational corporations like Coca-Cola, impacting its 200,000 residents.
