The author highlights why QQQM was chosen over the more common QQQ and discusses its appeal after significant price declines in quality tech stocks like Apple, Amazon, and Microsoft. The author also mentions a collaboration with Hoya Capital for an income-focused investing service.

title: Poly Delivers Extensive Portfolio of Devices Certified for Microsoft Teams to Achieve Greater Meeting Collaboration
summary: Poly has announced an expanded portfolio of Microsoft Teams certified solutions aimed at enhancing meeting equity and collaboration. These new and updated devices, ranging from video conferencing systems to phones, are designed for various meeting spaces and work styles, offering features like Poly DirectorAI technology for improved remote user experience and NoiseBlockAI for clearer audio. This initiative builds on Poly's long-standing partnership with Microsoft to provide comprehensive communication solutions for hybrid work environments.

title: Making sense of the shoebox: How H&R Block uses Azure AI to transform tax returns
summary: H&R Block is leveraging Microsoft Azure AI services, including Azure Form Recognizer and Azure Cognitive Search, to modernize its tax preparation process. This transformation allows tax professionals to spend less time on data entry and more time on personalized client interactions. By digitizing documents and streamlining client history retrieval, H&R Block aims to reduce client anxiety, enhance efficiency, and provide richer financial conversations, aligning with evolving client needs for digital and hybrid tax solutions.

title: Mercedes-Benz and Microsoft collaborate to boost efficiency, resilience and sustainability in car production
summary: Mercedes-Benz and Microsoft are partnering to enhance the efficiency, resilience, and sustainability of car production through the new MO360 Data Platform. This platform will connect Mercedes-Benz's global passenger car plants to the Microsoft Cloud, enabling faster identification of supply chain bottlenecks, dynamic resource allocation for electric and Top-End Luxury vehicles, and data-driven decisions on the shop floor. The collaboration aims for a 20% improvement in passenger car production efficiency by 2025 and will help reduce the ecological footprint by monitoring and forecasting carbon emissions, energy, water usage, and waste management.

title: Microsoft debuts new Surface devices with chip and design upgrades
summary: Microsoft unveiled three new Surface devices: the Surface Pro 9, Surface Studio 2+, and Surface Pro 5 Laptop, all featuring updated processors and design enhancements. The Surface Pro 9, a two-in-one device, offers both Intel Alder Lake and Arm-based SQ3 chip options. The Surface Studio 2+ workstation was updated with an Intel Core i7-11370H chip and Nvidia RTX 3060 graphics, while the Surface Pro 5 Laptop is available in two screen sizes with Intel Alder Lake processors.

title: WEF recognises Dr. Reddy’s Hyd factory as part of its Global Lighthouse Network
summary: Dr. Reddy’s Laboratories' manufacturing facility in Bachupally, Hyderabad, has been recognized by the World Economic Forum (WEF) as part of its Global Lighthouse Network for leadership in applying Fourth Industrial Revolution technologies. This recognition highlights the factory's success in leveraging digital advancements to enhance productivity, workforce engagement, sustainability, and supply chain resilience. Cipla's Oral Solid Dosage plant in Indore also received similar recognition, showcasing the growing adoption of Industry 4.0 technologies in the Indian pharmaceutical sector.

title: Cisco partners with Microsoft to add Teams to its meeting devices
summary: Cisco Systems Inc. will integrate Microsoft Corp.'s Teams messaging app into its meeting devices, offering users an alternative to its Webex video conferencing software. Cisco aims to be a hardware platform for various conferencing software, including Microsoft Teams, Zoom, and Google, believing this strategy will enhance customer experience and benefit the company. This move comes as Webex faces stiff competition from newer platforms like Zoom.

title: Cisco partners with Microsoft to add Teams to its meeting devices
summary: Cisco Systems Inc. announced a partnership with Microsoft Corp. to integrate the Teams messaging app into its meeting devices. This move offers an alternative to Cisco's Webex and allows users to access various conferencing platforms on Cisco hardware, reflecting a strategy to become a versatile hardware platform for multiple software providers. Microsoft Teams will be available on Cisco devices starting in the first quarter of next year.

title: Microsoft uses strategically located subsidiaries to lower taxes more than previously known, new analysis finds
summary: A new report by the Centre for International Corporate Tax Accountability and Research (CICTAR) alleges that Microsoft uses a network of subsidiaries, particularly in Ireland and Bermuda, to significantly minimize its tax liabilities globally. While not suggesting illegal activity, the analysis raises concerns about profit shifting and its impact on tax revenues in countries where Microsoft conducts substantial business. The report points out that despite high profit margins, some Microsoft subsidiaries report much lower margins, reducing taxable income.

title: |‘Short-form video has changed the way music is performed, shared, and enjoyed. Competition for eyeballs is fierce.’
summary: |The article features an interview with Sherry Tan, Managing Director of Warner Music China, discussing the rapid growth of China's music market, now the world's sixth-largest. Tan highlights the significant impact of short-form video platforms like Douyin on music consumption and promotion, as well as Warner Music China's strategy to localize and foster international careers for Chinese artists. She also addresses opportunities in gaming, Web3, and the challenges of fierce competition for audience attention in a constantly evolving digital landscape.

title: Haleon to improve accessibility for visually impaired customers
summary: Haleon has partnered with Microsoft to enhance accessibility for blind and partially sighted customers using the Seeing AI app. The app allows users to scan barcodes of over 1,500 Haleon products, including Sensodyne and Centrum, to hear information like product names, ingredients, and instructions. This initiative aims to promote health inclusivity and greater independence for visually impaired individuals, with plans for global expansion and Android availability.

title: Microsoft - Gaming Global Taxes, Winning Government Contracts
summary: A new report by CICTAR alleges that Microsoft uses a complex network of shell companies in various tax havens, such as Bermuda, to significantly reduce its global tax obligations while simultaneously securing lucrative government contracts. The report highlights instances where Microsoft subsidiaries, despite reporting billions in profits, pay little to no tax, leading to public funds being diverted from essential services like healthcare and education. Public Services International calls for transparency in corporate taxation and suggests that governments should mandate global tax standards for companies seeking public contracts.

title: N-able’s Cove Data Protection aims to compete with Veeam, Datto and Commvault Metallic
summary: N-able is rebranding its backup solution to Cove Data Protection, positioning it as a core offering to directly compete with major players like Veeam, Datto, Acronis, and Commvault Metallic. The multi-tenant cloud solution (SaaS) focuses on efficient file-level backups for endpoints and Microsoft 365, stored across N-able's global data centers, with an emphasis on competitive pricing for MSPs. While currently prioritizing Microsoft 365 support, N-able aims to differentiate itself through efficiency and cost-effectiveness, bringing enterprise-level technology to SMEs via MSPs.

title: How much Netflix’s new ad-supported plan will cost and what you get (and don’t)
summary: Netflix is launching a cheaper, ad-supported plan for $6.99 a month starting November 3rd in the U.S., which will include 4 to 5 minutes of commercials per hour. While this plan offers a discount, some shows and movies will be unavailable due to licensing, and downloads won't be permitted. This move comes as Netflix faces increased competition and investor pressure to grow its subscriber base and revenue.

title: 5 Minutes with… Erica Roberts
summary: Erica Roberts, the newly appointed CCO at BBH USA, discusses her move from Publicis New York and her long-standing admiration for BBH's unique approach to advertising. She highlights the agency's distinct culture and leadership, emphasizing its "zag" mentality in a "zigging" industry. Roberts also touches on her previous impactful work for The J.M. Smucker Company and the "Power of One" model within Publicis Groupe.

title: LaLiga and Globant agree to create global technology company
summary: LaLiga has announced a joint venture with Globant, a software development company, to establish a global technology company focused on sports and entertainment. This partnership aims to advance LaLiga Tech's products and services, incorporating new technologies like Web 3.0, metaverse, and gaming, while expanding its global reach. Both parties anticipate this collaboration will enhance fan engagement and drive digital transformation in the sports industry.

title: 3M’s Post-It Partners With Microsoft on Brainstorming App Venture
summary: 3M's Post-It brand has partnered with Microsoft to launch a new app designed to digitize brainstorming. The app, available to Microsoft Teams users, provides a virtual whiteboard and sticky notes for collaborative idea sharing in hybrid environments. It allows users to upload photos of physical Post-Its, sort and organize ideas, and includes features like "Search & Stack" and "Zen Mode."

title: Microsoft Office suite becomes Microsoft 365 app
summary: Microsoft Corporation announced that its productivity suite, including Office.com, the Office mobile app, and the Office app for Windows, will merge into a single "Microsoft 365 app." This change, featuring a new icon and more features, will roll out gradually starting November 2022. Existing accounts, subscriptions, and files will be automatically updated without disruption, and users can continue to access core applications like Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook.

title: Solving customer problems in real-time with at NetApp Cloud Field Day Exclusive
summary: This article discusses the second part of NetApp's Cloud Field Day Exclusive, focusing on real-world solutions for hybrid and multicloud challenges. It highlights how NetApp addresses customer pain points like skill gaps, complexity, cost optimization, and consistency in diverse cloud environments. The day also included a Q&A session with Google Cloud executives, discussing the partnership and the future of cloud file storage.

title: The female venture capitalist creating billions in a new world of work beyond the office
summary: Brianne Kimmel's Worklife Ventures has invested in 50 startups since 2019, with nine valued over $1 billion, focusing on the changing work/life balance and the future of remote work. Kimmel, whose venture is backed by Marc Andreessen and Zoom CEO Eric Yuan, plans to continue scaling businesses for freelancers and creators. Despite economic challenges, Worklife Ventures aims to support companies enabling productive work outside traditional office settings, a thesis Kimmel developed before the pandemic.

title: Microsoft Teams SIP Gateway to support analog phones via Analog...
summary: Microsoft announced at Ignite that its Teams SIP Gateway will support analog phones starting in early 2023, allowing existing analog endpoints like door access systems and elevator phones to connect to Teams. It will support specific Analog Telephone Adaptors (ATAs) from AudioCodes, Cisco, and Poly. Additionally, SIP Gateway will support Algo overhead paging devices, ringers, and speakers, also coming in 2023.

title: Mercedes-Benz strikes Dolby Atmos partnership with Apple Music and Universal
summary: Mercedes-Benz has partnered with Universal Music Group and Apple Music to integrate Spatial Audio with Dolby Atmos into its vehicles, making them the first non-Apple devices to offer this feature natively in a car. This collaboration aims to set a new standard for in-car music quality, with UMG encouraging artists to mix music in Dolby Atmos and using Mercedes-Benz vehicles for song approval and quality assurance. Drivers with Apple Music subscriptions can now access Spatial Audio content in compatible Mercedes-Benz models.

title: Microsoft to drive sustainability through the Microsoft Cloud
summary: Microsoft is expanding its Cloud for Sustainability platform with new ESG capabilities to help organizations track and reduce their environmental footprint. The updates include enhanced calculation methodologies for Scope 3 emissions, improved usability and security features in Microsoft Sustainability Manager, and an expanded data model for water and carbon data. Additionally, Microsoft has updated the Emissions Impact Dashboard for Azure and introduced Environmental Credit Service to streamline the voluntary environmental markets.

title: Exploring the Metaverse
summary: Nigel Pereira explores the metaverse, describing it as a three-dimensional internet populated with live people, tracing its origins to Neal Stephenson's 1992 novel "Snow Crash." The article discusses the current state of disconnected metaverses, similar to the early internet, and highlights real-world applications in simulation for surgery, science, and training, as well as virtual tourism and collaboration with NASA.

title: Gartner Top 10 Strategic Technology Trends for 2023
summary: Gartner has identified the Top 10 Strategic Technology Trends for 2023, which are categorized into four key priorities: Optimize, Scale, Pioneer, and Sustainable Technology. These trends aim to help organizations enhance resilience, improve productivity, engage customers, and pursue sustainable solutions. The article details each of the ten trends and their potential impact on business strategies over the next three years.

title: Morgan Stanley CEO James Gorman: “I'm perfectly happy to see our tech spend go up”
summary: Morgan Stanley CEO James Gorman expressed satisfaction with increased tech spending, viewing it as crucial for efficiency and innovation, despite a 22% drop in bank revenues. He highlighted the importance of cloud technology, robo-advisors, and cybersecurity, while also reflecting on market recalibrations due to past "ridiculous" valuations and the return to fundamental economic principles. The bank's wealth management and fixed income sectors performed well, offsetting a decline in investment banking.

title: What’s Changed: 2022 Magic Quadrant for Security Information and Event Management
summary: This article analyzes Gartner's 2022 Magic Quadrant for Security Information and Event Management (SIEM), highlighting significant changes since the 2021 report. It details vendor movements within the Leaders, Challengers, and Visionaries quadrants, noting company-specific developments and new entrants. The report focuses on shifts including Microsoft's rise, IBM's stability, and the repositioning of several other key SIEM providers.

title: Announcing the 2022 CyberScoop 50 award winners
summary: Scoop News Group has announced the winners of the 2022 CyberScoop 50 Awards, celebrating cybersecurity leaders in both public and private sectors. These individuals are recognized for their work in protecting vital networks, information, and critical infrastructure through hard work, ingenuity, and creativity. The awards highlight a diverse group from the information security community, ranging from newcomers to seasoned policy and strategy officials.

title: Gartner Top 10 Tech Trends For 2023: Metaverse, AI, Cloud
summary: Gartner has released its top 10 technology trends for 2023, focusing on themes like optimizing resilience, scaling solutions, and pioneering new opportunities amidst economic uncertainty. The trends include the metaverse, super apps, adaptive AI, industry cloud platforms, and sustainability, emphasizing technology's role in addressing global challenges and driving business value beyond just cost savings. Each trend is accompanied by an example of its real-world application.

title: M&A List: Identity and Access Management (IAM) Security Mergers and Acquisitions -
summary: This article compiles a list of mergers and acquisitions in the Identity and Access Management (IAM) security market, highlighting the robust M&A activity driven by market fragmentation and strong demand from MSSPs, MSPs, and end-customers. The global IAM market is projected to reach $34.52 billion by 2028, growing at a 14.5% CAGR from 2021. The list details specific acquisitions and mergers from 2017 to 2022 involving key players and private equity firms in the cybersecurity space.

title: Zillow Sued For Alleged Wiretapping
summary: Zillow is facing multiple class-action lawsuits in Pennsylvania, Washington, and Missouri, alleging violations of state wiretapping laws. These lawsuits, similar to prior cases against Facebook and Carrier IQ, claim that Zillow and its third-party vendors (like Microsoft) record users' mouse movements, clicks, keystrokes, and other interactions to create "session replays" without explicit consent. The article highlights the ongoing debate about consumer privacy versus the need for website analytics, and the implications of applying older wiretapping laws to modern web technologies.

title: Opinion: AMD’s Lisa Su takes center stage at CES, taking aim at Intel and Nvidia
Opinion: AMD’s Lisa Su takes center stage at CES, taking aim at Intel and Nvidia
summary: AMD CEO Lisa Su used her CES keynote to confidently declare that the company expects to challenge and potentially surpass bigger rivals like Intel and Nvidia. She detailed AMD’s 2019 plans for computers, servers, and videogames, featuring new high-end graphics cards and a second-generation server chip. Su showcased the performance of early versions of AMD's 7-nanometer hardware against offerings from its competitors.

title: Ambarella's CV25 camera SoC with CVflow computer vision processing | Security News
summary: Ambarella has unveiled the CV25 camera System-on-Chip (SoC), part of its CVflow family, designed for next-generation intelligent solutions. This SoC integrates advanced image processing, high-resolution video encoding, and CVflow computer vision processing into a low-power design. The CV25 enables AI at the edge for applications like home monitoring, surveillance, and automotive solutions, supporting features such as facial recognition and driver monitoring.

title: NVIDIA Resets The Self-Driving Bar Again With AutoPilot Supporting 'Level 2+'
summary: NVIDIA announced its DRIVE AutoPilot system at CES 2019, which it describes as the "world's first commercially available Level 2+ automated driving system" that will enable supervised self-driving vehicles by 2020. The company also revealed that Mercedes-Benz has chosen NVIDIA as its AI partner for developing next-generation vehicles. Additionally, NVIDIA launched the new GeForce RTX 2060 GPU and announced over 40 new gaming laptops featuring GeForce RTX GPUs.

title: Corsair Vengeance 5180 gaming PC review: "A beautiful machine with performance to match"
summary: This article reviews the Corsair Vengeance 5180 gaming PC, highlighting its powerful components, excellent dual-chamber design, and brilliant RGB lighting. While acknowledging its large size and non-overclockable CPU, the review praises its performance at 1080p and 1440p and its overall value for gamers seeking a pre-built machine.

title: Amazon Stock Rises as the 'Scout' Delivery Robot Is Unveiled
summary: Amazon announced the launch of its new delivery robot, "Scout," a cooler-sized ground unit designed for autonomous package delivery, initially accompanied by an Amazon employee. This announcement led to a 0.91 percent rise in Amazon's stock prices. The article also mentions other strong performers in the Entrepreneur Index™, including NVIDIA Corp. and Analog Devices, while J.M. Smucker Company, OReilly Auto Parts, and Brown-Forman Corp saw declines.

title: Caterpillar, Nvidia Warnings Send Wall Street Tumbling
summary: U.S. stocks tumbled following warnings from Caterpillar and Nvidia, which highlighted concerns about a slowing Chinese economy and the impact of tariffs on corporate profits. Caterpillar missed profit estimates due to softening demand in China and rising costs, while Nvidia cut its revenue forecast due to weak demand and lower data center sales. This sent major indexes like the Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq Composite lower, despite overall positive earnings reports.

title: China weakness spreads far and wide, from Caterpillar to Nvidia
summary: Major US and European companies like Caterpillar, Nvidia, and Intel are reporting significant impacts from the slowing demand in China across various sectors, from industrial machinery and technology to automotive parts. While many industries are feeling the pinch, luxury goods and some consumer brands like Tiffany & Co. and Starbucks are, for now, experiencing continued growth, creating a mixed economic picture. The emerging trend suggests a broadening slowdown in China is affecting a diverse range of goods and services.

title: Will Top-Down Hardware/Software Co-Design Ever Happen?
summary: This article discusses the long-standing challenge and evolution of hardware/software co-design in the EDA industry over the past two decades. Author Frank Schirrmeister reflects on past predictions and notes the significant progress made in verification, virtual prototyping, and the "shift left" methodology, even if not exactly as anticipated. He concludes that new abstraction layers and tools, like those for iOS and Android, and middleware like OpenGL, are enabling a new level of hardware/software optimization.

title: Opinion: AMD has won Wall Street’s trust, and its stock is showing the results
summary: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) has gained significant credibility on Wall Street, a trust it previously lacked. Despite reporting slightly below-expectation fourth-quarter revenue and a first-quarter outlook due to excess graphics chip inventories, the stock did not face a typical decline. This indicates Wall Street's growing faith in CEO Lisa Su's ability to deliver, especially with a forecast heavily weighted to the second half of the year.

title: NVIDIA Responds to TRC Capital’s ‘Mini-Tender’ Offer
summary: NVIDIA has issued a response to an unsolicited "mini-tender" offer from TRC Capital Corporation to purchase up to 1,000,000 shares of NVIDIA's common stock at $149.88 per share. NVIDIA is not affiliated with TRC, expresses no opinion on the offer, and advises shareholders to consult with their brokers or financial advisors and exercise caution. The company also clarified that a mini-tender offer is an offer for less than 5 percent of a company’s shares and is not subject to the same disclosure requirements as larger tender offers.

title: Aehr launches FOX-CP wafer-level test & reliability screening system
summary: Aehr Test Systems has launched the FOX-CP, a new low-cost single-wafer test and reliability verification system designed for logic, memory, and photonic devices. This system, part of the FOX-P product family, is optimized for shorter test times, multiple touchdowns, and includes features like 2048 Universal Channels, making it suitable for silicon photonics and VCSEL arrays. The FOX-CP helps reduce test costs by identifying failing die before packaging and is available for order and shipment.

title: SoftBank Sells Entire Nvidia Stake
summary: SoftBank's nearly $100 billion Vision Fund sold its entire 4.9% stake in Nvidia Corp. in January, realizing a $3.3 billion return. This move comes as Nvidia's shares have been affected by trade war fears and projected lower-than-expected revenue, leading to a nearly 50% loss in value since October 2018.

title: Make Your Data Pipeline Super-Efficient by Unifying Machine Learning and Deep Learning
summary: This article discusses how NetApp and NVIDIA technologies can unify and accelerate data pipelines for machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL). It highlights the inefficiencies of traditional approaches that separate data preparation, ML, and DL stages, and proposes a combined solution using NVIDIA RAPIDS and NetApp's Data Fabric and ONTAP AI to create a seamless, end-to-end AI pipeline from edge to core to cloud. The integration aims to reduce data sprawl, improve processing efficiency, and solve specific data science challenges with features like FabricPool, FlexCache, and FlexClone.

title: Coke stock heads for worst day since 2008, Nvidia looks to capitalize on ‘positive set up’
summary: Coca-Cola Co. (Coke) stock is experiencing a significant downturn, heading for its worst day since 2008, largely due to "softness" in its North America business, a revenue miss, and a disappointing outlook for the year. The company is facing challenges in regions like Argentina and Turkey and plans to increase marketing expenses in 2019, despite some encouraging trends in North America and China. The article also mentions Nvidia looking to capitalize on a positive setup, alongside other earnings watch updates for Six Flags, Avon, and Yeti.

title: Machine learning is the biggest disruptive tech: AMD CTO Mark Papermaster
summary: AMD CTO Mark Papermaster discusses the significance of the company's new 7nm chips in meeting the insatiable demand for computational power, especially in data centers and mobile devices. He highlights machine learning as the biggest disruptive technology, noting its potential to leverage data and predict results, while also addressing concerns about AI and robotics replacing human jobs. Papermaster also touches on GPU usage in the crypto space, indicating AMD's focus on broader GPU markets in gaming, servers, and blockchain.

title: Nvidia to Acquire Mellanox, Its Biggest Deal Ever at Roughly $7 Billion
summary: Nvidia has agreed to acquire networking firm Mellanox Technologies Ltd. for approximately $6.9 billion, marking its largest acquisition to date. This move is aimed at strengthening Nvidia's position in cloud computing, following a downturn in its core graphics-chips business. The deal signifies Nvidia's continued expansion beyond its traditional graphics processing unit market into new technology areas.

title: NVIDIA to pay $6.9 billion for Israeli company Mellanox
summary: NVIDIA is set to acquire Israeli company Mellanox for $6.9 billion. This acquisition highlights a significant investment in Israeli technology and business, as ISRAEL21c is now part of the Unpacked family, focusing on smart, engaging, and inspiring content about Israel, Judaism, and the Jewish experience.

title: Nvidia to make largest acquisition in its history with $6.9 billion deal for Mellanox
US gaming firm Nvidia to buy Israeli chip maker Mellanox for $6.9 billion
summary: US gaming and computer graphics giant Nvidia Corp. is set to acquire Israeli chip maker Mellanox Technologies Ltd. for $6.9 billion in cash. This deal marks the second-largest tech acquisition in Israel's history and will enhance Nvidia's capabilities in high-speed data center solutions. Mellanox, founded in 1999, specializes in servers and storage switching solutions and has seen significant demand for its products.

title: Nvidia to buy Mellanox for $6.9 billion as it pushes into data centers
summary: Nvidia has agreed to acquire chipmaker Mellanox Technologies Ltd. for $6.9 billion, a move aimed at bolstering its presence in the expanding data center market. The acquisition is Nvidia's largest ever and seeks to accelerate its successful initiatives in providing graphics chips for artificial intelligence work in data centers. The deal signals a potential resumption of consolidation within the semiconductor industry, despite concerns about regulatory approvals amid the U.S.-China trade war.

title: ‘Happy and sad day,’ Mellanox founder says of $6.9 billion sale to Nvidia
summary: Mellanox Technologies founder and CEO Eyal Waldman expressed mixed feelings about Nvidia's $6.9 billion acquisition of his company, calling it a "happy and sad day." The deal, Israel’s second-largest tech acquisition, will see Nvidia acquire Mellanox for $125 a share, aiming to strengthen its position in the data center components market. Waldman, who founded Mellanox in 1999, indicated that while the sale was the right move for shareholders and employees, his own future at the firm remains undecided.

title: Nearly Half of Israel's Largest Exporters Are Foreign-Owned

This trend was underscored by Nvidia's $6.9 billion acquisition of Israeli chipmaker Mellanox Technologies Ltd.

title: Global Computer Companies Announce NVIDIA-Powered Enterprise Servers Optimized for Data Science

The platform supports various NVIDIA Jetson platforms, including the new low-cost Jetson Nano, and offers open-source hardware reference designs.

This acquisition marks Nvidia's largest to date, aimed at expanding its reach into data centers crucial for AI and machine learning.

title: Intel dumps its Nervana neural network processors for Habana’s AI chips
summary: Intel Corp. has decided to discontinue development of its Nervana neural network processors, opting instead to focus on the AI chip technology acquired with Habana Labs Ltd. for $2 billion. This decision comes as Habana's chips, such as the Gaudi and Goya, have demonstrated superior performance compared to Nervana's NNP-T and NNP-I processors. The move could have implications for Intel's AI Platforms Group, led by a Nervana co-founder, raising questions about potential mergers with Habana.

title: MRCY Stock Price | Analyst Target 75.14 & Moderate Buy Consensus
summary: This article provides an overview of Mercury Systems Inc (MRCY) stock, detailing its current price, analyst consensus of "Moderate Buy" with a target of $75.14, and company information. It covers key metrics, recent news, and instructs on how to buy MRCY stock on eToro. The company is a technology firm serving the aerospace and defense industry with mission-critical products.

title: How analog in-memory computing can solve power challenges of edge AI inference
summary: This article explores how analog in-memory computing can address the significant power consumption and latency issues of edge AI inference, which are prevalent with cloud-based AI solutions. It highlights the memory bottleneck in traditional digital computing and introduces a multi-level memory architecture, like Microchip Technology's memBrain, that integrates computation directly into memory, dramatically reducing power usage. The technology utilizes SuperFlash memory cells to perform Multiply-Accumulate operations efficiently at the edge, offering extreme low power, smaller footprint, and lower development costs for AI applications.

title: An A+ ETF For AV and AI Tech
summary: This article highlights the ARK Autonomous Technology & Robotics ETF (ARKQ) as a prime investment vehicle for artificial intelligence (AI) and autonomous vehicles (AV) technologies. ARKQ is noted for its significant allocation to Tesla and its strategic positioning to benefit from the growth in these disruptive technologies. The article delves into how AI, particularly machine learning and deep learning, is crucial for AV development due to the massive data processing requirements from vehicle sensors.

title: Are video games a worthwhile investment?
summary: Raj Lala, CEO of Evolve ETFs, discusses the investment potential of the video game industry, explaining why he launched the HERO ETF to provide exposure to major gaming companies. He highlights the significant evolution of the industry's revenue model beyond simple sales, citing in-app purchases, subscriptions, and esports as key drivers. Lala emphasizes that gaming fits into Evolve's strategy of investing in disruptive technologies that will shape the future and advises financial advisors to understand the full ecosystem of the market.

title: Nvidia forecast tops expectations on cloud sales despite coronavirus hit
summary: Nvidia Corp exceeded Wall Street's first-quarter revenue expectations, driven by strong sales of its chips to cloud computing vendors, despite projecting a $100 million hit due to the coronavirus outbreak. This forecast signals a rebound in chip demand, particularly in the data center business, which helped offset a slight miss in gaming revenue and increased Nvidia's shares. The company expects current-quarter revenue of $3 billion, plus or minus 2%.

title: Nvidia stock closes at record as data-center sales inspire analyst love fest
summary: Nvidia's stock soared to a new record high on Friday, driven by robust data-center sales that exceeded expectations after a challenging year. Analysts responded positively by raising price targets, as the company's shares closed up 7% at $289.79, marking its first record close in nearly a year and a half. This surge highlights investor confidence in Nvidia's performance in the data-center market.

title: Samsung wins 5-nanometer modem chip contract from Qualcomm
summary: Samsung Electronics has secured a contract to manufacture Qualcomm's new 5G X60 modem chips using its advanced 5-nanometer process technology, marking a significant win for Samsung in its competition with TSMC. This deal is crucial for Samsung's efforts to expand its non-memory chip business and regain market share in the foundry sector. The X60 modem chips are expected to be widely used in 5G mobile devices, potentially boosting Samsung's market presence.

title: Nvidia stock rockets past $300 to third straight record close as holdout analyst turns bullish
summary: Nvidia stock surpassed $300 for the first time, reaching a third consecutive record close due to an analyst's increased bullishness. Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon upgraded Nvidia's rating from market perform to outperform and raised his price target to $360 from $300. This shift marks a significant positive turn for the stock as a previously holdout analyst acknowledges an "error" in not being more positive sooner.

title: AI Helps Doctors Diagnose the Coronavirus | NVIDIA Technical Blog
summary: Physicians in Wuhan, China, are utilizing AI software accelerated by NVIDIA GPUs to detect visual signs of Covid-19, aiding in patient screening and prioritizing those likely to have the virus. The AI software, developed by Infervision, was fine-tuned with over 2,000 CT images from early coronavirus patients and trained on NVIDIA V100 GPUs. This solution has been deployed in 34 hospitals across China, reviewing over 32,000 cases, and is being evaluated in Europe and the United States.

title: Humanoid Robot Market Demand, Current Outlook, Future Growth,
summary: The humanoid robot market is experiencing significant growth driven by increasing adoption in retail, education, research, and caregiving, as well as technological advancements. Software is expected to dominate the market due to the integration of AI algorithms, while biped motion types also hold a significant share. North America currently leads the market, but the Asia-Pacific region is projected to show the fastest growth.

title: Nvidia Moves Conference To Online-Only Amid COVID-19 Concerns
summary: Nvidia Corp has canceled the in-person component of its annual user conference scheduled for March 22-26 due to COVID-19 concerns, opting instead for an online-only format. CEO Jensen Huang will still deliver a keynote address via livestream, and attendees who paid for passes will receive full refunds. The move comes as analysts anticipated Nvidia to announce new products with advanced chipmaking processes.

title: Nvidia acquires data storage and management platform SwiftStack
summary: Nvidia has acquired SwiftStack, a software-centric data storage and management platform, to enhance its AI, high-performance computing, and accelerated computing workloads. SwiftStack's co-founder Joe Arnold expressed excitement about joining Nvidia to contribute to its AI supercomputing efforts. While the acquisition price was not disclosed, SwiftStack had previously raised $23.6 million in funding.

title: Nvidia secures SwiftStack technology -by buying the company
summary: Nvidia has acquired SwiftStack, an object storage software company, to enhance its internal data centers and provide its AI Stack solutions to customers. Nvidia will integrate SwiftStack's 1space technology to ensure GPUs are constantly fed with data, but does not intend to become a storage vendor. The acquisition highlights a trend of object storage companies becoming instrumental for end-to-end vertical solutions.

title: Rambus' HBM2E Memory Controller & PHY Offer Chipmakers Cost-Effective Designs
summary: Rambus has unveiled its HBM2E memory controller and PHY designs, offering chipmakers a cost-effective alternative to in-house R&D. These designs align with the JEDEC HBM2E standard, supporting up to 12-layer 3D stacked DRAM with capacities up to 36GB and an aggregate memory bandwidth of 410 GBps. HBM2E is expected to primarily impact AI and high-performance computing applications where high bandwidth and limited board space are crucial.

title: Nvidia tweeted then deleted a video of a blinking eye, what does it mean?
summary: Nvidia tweeted then deleted a mysterious video featuring a blinking eye, leading to speculation about an upcoming announcement on March 19, 2020. The video, which showed an eyeball tracking two points of light, is thought to be related to either Nvidia's next-generation Ampere GPU or foveated rendering technology for virtual reality. This tease comes ahead of Nvidia's annual GPU Technology Conference, which will be an all-digital event.

title: BOTZ: The Robotics/Artificial Intelligence ETF Is Not A Bargain Buy Even After Recent Crash (NASDAQ:BOTZ)
summary: The Global X Robotics & A.I. ETF (BOTZ) has underperformed broader markets, tumbling over 20% year-to-date due to the coronavirus pandemic. Despite the significant drop, the article argues that BOTZ is not a bargain buy, citing subpar earnings growth and profitability among its top holdings. The ETF's heavy exposure to Japan and negative earnings trends in 2019 suggest continued underperformance compared to the broader technology sector and S&P 500.

title: Apple’s App Store Rules Limit Rival Gaming Services While Arcade Runs Free
summary: Apple's App Store rules are preventing rival gaming services like Google Stadia, Nvidia GeForce, and Microsoft XCloud from reaching iPhone and iPad users. The guidelines ban services that rely on streaming from the cloud, a restriction Apple's own Arcade service bypasses by being integrated as a feature within the App Store. Critics view these rules as arbitrary, favoring Apple's own offerings over those from outside developers.

title: New Solutions from NetApp Power Enterprise AI Needs
summary: NetApp introduced new AI solutions at the NVIDIA GPU Technology Conference (GTC) Digital event, including a unique AI control plane designed to simplify data-pipeline and provisioning tasks for data scientists and engineers. These solutions, developed in partnership with NVIDIA, aim to accelerate AI adoption and improve the management of AI projects from pilot to production across various industries. NetApp also highlighted enterprise-scale solutions like ONTAP AI and DGX SuperPOD, as well as a new medical imaging solution for healthcare.

title: AXS Esoterica NextG Economy ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (BATS:WUGI)
summary: The AXS Esoterica NextG Economy ETF (WUGI) is an actively-managed ETF focusing on global companies involved in the 5G-enabled digital economy, launched on March 31, 2020. As of March 3, 2026, its stock was trading at $67.83, down 6.5% since the beginning of the year, with $28.10 million in assets under management and a 4.38% dividend yield. The ETF's top holdings include major technology companies like NVIDIA, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, and Meta Platforms.

title: GTC Thursdays: Building Out an AI Center of Excellence
summary: This article discusses the importance of establishing an AI Center of Excellence (CoE) to overcome challenges in enterprise AI adoption and accelerate project success. It outlines key considerations for building a CoE, including executive sponsorship, strategic goal setting, data cataloging, infrastructure design, data science strategy, and operational planning with milestones and metrics. The author emphasizes the benefits of centralizing talent and democratizing AI technology access to drive efficiency and higher quality AI outcomes.

title: Top 10 Processors for AI Acceleration at the Endpoint
summary: This article reviews various processors designed for AI acceleration at the endpoint, highlighting offerings from major companies and startups. It covers application processors like Intel Movidius Myriad X, NXP i.MX 8M Plus, and XMOS xcore.ai, as well as automotive SoCs like Texas Instruments TDA4VM and GPUs such as Nvidia Jetson Nano, detailing their specifications and target applications. The piece provides a snapshot of the current market for AI and machine learning accelerators.

title: Nvidia completes acquisition of Israel’s Mellanox for $7 billion
summary: Nvidia has completed its $7 billion acquisition of Israel-based Mellanox Technologies, uniting two leaders in high-performance and data center computing. This acquisition aims to enhance Nvidia's offerings from AI computing to networking, allowing for higher performance and lower operating costs in next-generation data centers. The deal, initially valued at $6.9 billion, received final approval from Chinese antitrust authorities, paving the way for its completion.

title: Nvidia plans to continue to invest in Israel with Mellanox as base, CEO says
summary: Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang announced the company's intention to continue investing in Israel, leveraging its $7 billion acquisition of Mellanox Technologies Ltd. Mellanox will serve as Nvidia's base in the country, maintaining its operations as a separate entity. The firm highlighted Israel's significant talent pool and its strategic importance as one of Nvidia's largest tech centers globally, with no layoffs planned despite the coronavirus pandemic.

title: NVIDIA Completes Acquisition of Mellanox, Creating Major Force Driving Next-Gen Data Centers
summary: NVIDIA announced the completion of its $7 billion acquisition of Mellanox Technologies, uniting two leaders in high-performance and data center computing. This strategic move combines NVIDIA's computing expertise with Mellanox's networking technology to enhance performance, resource utilization, and reduce operating costs for customers. The acquisition is expected to immediately benefit NVIDIA's non-GAAP gross margin, non-GAAP EPS, and free cash flow.

title: AMD (NASDAQ:AMD) Reports 41% Year-Over-Year Revenue Growth, Record Notebook Sales
summary: AMD reported Q1 FY2020 earnings with $1.79 billion in revenue, marking a 41% year-over-year growth, despite missing Wall Street analyst expectations and its own previous guidance. The company saw strong performance in Ryzen and EPYC processors and record notebook sales, although overall sequential revenue dropped. AMD remains optimistic about Q2 FY2020, forecasting 21% year-over-year revenue growth.

title: NVIDIA buys Israeli company Mellanox for $7 billion
summary: This article states that NVIDIA bought the Israeli company Mellanox for $7 billion. It appears to be an outdated article reused as part of an announcement about ISRAEL21c becoming part of Unpacked, an OpenDor Media brand. The current content focuses on this transition and what it means for ISRAEL21c's content and community.

title: Nvidia to acquire Sequoia-backed networking startup Cumulus Networks
summary: Nvidia Corp. announced its agreement to acquire Cumulus Networks Inc., a data center networking startup backed by $129 million in funding. This acquisition follows Nvidia's $6.9 billion acquisition of Mellanox Technologies Ltd., as Cumulus software is a key component for some Mellanox products. The deal aims to give Nvidia control over a critical software component and align Cumulus' feature development roadmap with its own goals, optimizing the integration of software and hardware.

title: Micro but mighty: Semiconductors remain the key to technology leadership
summary: The article emphasizes the critical role of semiconductors in the 21st-century information economy, likening data to "oil" but stressing that semiconductors translate data into usable information. It highlights the United States' historical dominance in this field and its efforts to defend against challenges from countries like Japan in the 1980s and more recently China. The author argues that the U.S. needs a broader strategy beyond export restrictions, involving close collaboration with allies, especially Japan, to maintain its technological leadership.

title: Nvidia shares heading for first record close since coronavirus pandemic
summary: Nvidia shares are on track for a record close, recovering from a COVID-19 related drop, after an analyst boosted the price target ahead of earnings. The analyst cited Nvidia's acquisition of Mellanox Technologies and increased demand for gaming chips and data-center spending as reasons for the upgrade. The company's stock has risen significantly year-to-date, outperforming semiconductor and S&P 500 indexes.

title: COVID-19 Impact and Recovery Analysis | Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) Market 2020-2024 | Demand for High Memory GPU to Boost Growth | Technavio
summary: Technavio projects the Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) market to grow by USD 38.28 billion between 2020 and 2024, with a CAGR exceeding 29%. This growth is primarily driven by the increasing demand for high-memory GPUs, coupled with the expansion of the PC gaming and gaming console markets. The report provides an in-depth analysis of market trends, vendor landscapes, and the impact of COVID-19, segmenting the market by device type and geography.

title: Nvidia Unveils New Data Center Chips to Speed Pace of AI
summary: Nvidia Corp. announced new Ampere graphics chips and computers for AI processing in data centers, claiming a 20x performance increase over predecessors. These new chips are designed to handle both AI training and inference tasks, a capability that will bolster Nvidia's leadership in the growing AI market. The company is selling Ampere-based computers called DGX for $199,000 each, touting their superior performance compared to traditional Intel-based server arrays.

title: Nvidia confirms Ampere will power next-gen GeForce graphics cards
summary: Nvidia has confirmed that its new Ampere GPU architecture will power next-gen GeForce graphics cards, unifying its entire GPU range from gaming to data centers. CEO Jen-Hsun Huang announced that Ampere will replace both Turing and Volta chips, with the architecture also being used in supercomputers to aid in COVID-19 research. While a specific release date for gaming cards wasn't given, an August/September announcement is anticipated.

title: Kensho Collaborates with NVIDIA to Advance Automatic Speech Recognition
summary: Kensho, an S&P Global company, announced Scribe, a new end-to-end speech recognition solution optimized for finance and business. Leveraging NVIDIA NeMo on NVIDIA GPUs, Scribe improves accuracy and expands coverage for earnings calls and other financial audio. Kensho and NVIDIA are continuing to explore further collaboration opportunities to advance automatic speech recognition.

title: Taiwanese Chipmaker Plans to Build $12 Billion Factory in Arizona
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) plans to invest $12 billion in building a new chip plant in Arizona, with construction expected to begin in 2021 and completion by 2024. This move is intended to address U.S. national security concerns and shift high-tech manufacturing to the U.S., while also balancing TSMC's relationships with both American clients and China. The facility will create 1,600 jobs and utilize 5-nanometer process technology, though the scale is relatively small compared to TSMC's overall operations.

title: TSMC’s Announcement Of A New U.S. Semiconductor Fab Is Big News
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) announced plans to build a new semiconductor fabrication facility (fab) in Arizona, a move deemed significant despite its initial limited scale. This investment, estimated at $12 billion for a 5 nm technology fab, highlights the challenges and costs of advanced semiconductor manufacturing. While a welcome development for the U.S. supply chain, it represents only a small step towards securing domestic semiconductor production, as the U.S. will still rely heavily on Asian facilities for capacity and specialized processes like packaging.

title: TSMC Announces Intention to Build and Operate an Advanced Semiconductor Fab in the United States
summary: TSMC announced its plan to build and operate an advanced semiconductor fab in the U.S. state of Arizona. This facility will use 5nm technology, have a capacity of 20,000 wafers per month, create over 1,600 high-tech jobs directly, and involves a total investment of approximately US$12 billion from 2021 to 2029. The project is strategically important for the U.S. semiconductor ecosystem and relies on continued U.S. federal government and Arizona state support.

title: What Is a DPU?
summary: This article explains what a Data Processing Unit (DPU) is and how it differs from CPUs and GPUs, positioning it as the third pillar of computing. It details the key components of a DPU, including a multi-core CPU, high-performance network interface, and acceleration engines, emphasizing its role in modern data centers and SmartNICs. The article also outlines ten critical capabilities for network data path acceleration engines within a DPU.

title: Nvidia should dodge massive coronavirus effects thanks to data centers and videogames
summary: Nvidia is expected to largely avoid significant negative impacts from the coronavirus pandemic due to strong demand in its data center and videogame segments. The article anticipates data-center sales exceeding $1 billion for the first time and gaming chip growth of 25%. This analysis is part of a series tracking COVID-19's effects on major businesses.

title: Opinion: It’s official: Nvidia is not just a gaming company anymore
summary: Nvidia's first-quarter earnings report indicates a significant shift from being primarily a gaming company to a major player in the data-center market. Data-center chip sales surpassed $1 billion for the first time, demonstrating its growing importance. This transformation is further highlighted by Nvidia's new business segment reporting, emphasizing both computing and graphics divisions.

title: AMD Stock Pushes Lisa Su to Top of CEO Compensation List
summary: Lisa Su, CEO of Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), topped the annual CEO compensation survey by the Associated Press in 2019 with a $58.5 million pay package, largely due to AMD's strong stock performance. She is the first woman to achieve this No. 1 ranking. Her leadership is credited with turning around AMD, focusing the company on high-growth areas like high-performance computing, computer graphics, and graphics processing units.

title: AMD CEO Lisa Su Tops Earnings as Highest Paid CEO in The S&P 500
summary: AMD CEO Lisa Su has become the highest-paid CEO in the S&P 500, with a pay package valued at $58.5 million. This compensation is attributed to AMD's impressive performance over the past five years, driven by the success of EPYC, Ryzen, and Radeon products. Lisa Su is also the first woman to hold this distinction, being one of only 20 women on the list compared to 309 men.

title: Intel stock slips as new lines of AI chips released
summary: Intel stock experienced a decline after the company launched new artificial intelligence and data analytics chips. The company's shares fell by 1.2%, underperforming the broader market. This occurred despite new product introductions aimed at supporting AI and data analytics.

title: Mercedes-Benz cars to be built on Nvidia autonomous driving platform from 2024
summary: Nvidia announced a deal with Daimler Mercedes-Benz to supply a chip and software platform for autonomous driving functions in cars produced from 2024. This partnership will see Nvidia's high-end Drive AGX Orin Platform become standard in Mercedes-Benz vehicles, allowing for over-the-air software updates similar to smartphones. The agreement follows Daimler's decision to pause its autonomous driving alliance with BMW.

title: Mercedes-Benz, Nvidia deepen autonomous driving alliance
summary: Semiconductor maker Nvidia Corp has partnered with Daimler to develop a next-generation chip and software platform for Mercedes-Benz cars, enabling advanced autonomous driving functions by 2024. This alliance allows Mercedes to accelerate its development of automated driving capabilities and software applications, with both companies committing significant resources to bringing this technology to market. The platform will enable continuous software updates for Mercedes-Benz vehicles, similar to smartphone updates.

title: Mercedes-Benz and NVIDIA to Build Software-Defined Computing Architecture for Automated Driving Across Future Fleet
summary: Mercedes-Benz and NVIDIA are collaborating to create a revolutionary in-vehicle computing system and AI computing infrastructure for automated driving functions. This software-defined architecture, built on the NVIDIA DRIVE platform, will be rolled out across the next-generation Mercedes-Benz fleet starting in 2024, enabling upgradable automated driving, safety, and convenience features through over-the-air updates. The partnership aims to continually enhance the car ownership experience with a team of AI and software engineers.

title: Nvidia on Cusp of Topping Intel in Market Cap After 70% Gain
summary: Nvidia (NVDA) is nearing Intel (INTC) in market capitalization for the first time, buoyed by a more than 70% stock gain in 2020. This surge is attributed to investor confidence that the COVID-19 pandemic is accelerating the shift towards cloud-based digital services, for which Nvidia's technology is crucial. The graphics chipmaker's rapid growth positions it to potentially overtake the long-standing chip giant.

title: Nvidia Valuation Soars Past Intel on Graphics Chip Boom
summary: Nvidia's market valuation has surpassed Intel's for the first time, driven by high demand for its graphics chips in data centers and other growing tech sectors. Nvidia (NVDA) gained 2.4% on Wednesday, reaching a market value exceeding $248 billion, with its shares up 72% this year, while Intel (INTC) shares have fallen 2%. This surge reflects investor confidence that the pandemic is accelerating a shift to cloud-based digital services utilizing Nvidia's technology.

title: Nvidia surpasses Intel as largest U.S. chip maker by market cap
summary: Nvidia Corp. has surpassed Intel Corp. to become the largest U.S. chip maker by market capitalization for the first time. This milestone was achieved on Wednesday, July 8, 2020, with Nvidia's market cap reaching $251.31 billion compared to Intel's $248.16 billion. While other companies like Texas Instruments and Qualcomm have previously and temporarily held the top spot over Intel, this marks a significant achievement for Nvidia.

title: The 10 Biggest Networking Company Acquisitions Of 2020 (So Far)
summary: This article details the 10 biggest networking company acquisitions of 2020 to date, highlighting significant deals made by tech giants like Nvidia, Cisco, and F5 Networks. It covers purchases ranging from billion-dollar agreements to more strategic acquisitions aimed at expanding portfolios in areas like 5G, cloud security, and software-defined networking, despite the economic downturn caused by the global pandemic. The acquisitions underscore the dynamic nature of the networking market and companies' efforts to enhance their services and product offerings.

title: Nvidia market value closes in on Intel
summary: Nvidia is nearing Intel in market capitalization for the first time, fueled by a 70% stock surge this year due to the accelerated shift to cloud-based digital services. Nvidia's market cap has reached approximately $245 billion, just shy of Intel's $249 billion. This milestone would position Nvidia as the third-largest chipmaker globally by market cap, trailing only Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. and Samsung Electronics Co.

title: NVIDIA Now Most Valuable US Chipmaker, Intel Falls Behind
summary: NVIDIA has overtaken Intel to become the most valuable U.S. chipmaker, with its market capitalization reaching $251.3 billion compared to Intel's $248.2 billion. This surge is attributed to NVIDIA's strong financial performance, its dominance in gaming and data center markets, rapid adoption of its GPUs in AI, efficient cost management, and robust cash flow. The company's stock has shown exceptional growth, rallying 73.7% year-to-date and over twenty-fold in the last five years.

title: Switzerland’s Logitech partners with India’s Gamer, Streamer Shagufta ‘Xyaa’ Iqbal
summary: Logitech, a Swiss and American computer peripheral manufacturer, has partnered with Indian gamer and streamer Shagufta Iqbal, known as Xyaa. This partnership comes as gaming companies increase online promotions. Xyaa, who has garnered over 200,000 YouTube subscribers and 80,000 Instagram followers, has a long-standing career in competitive gaming and previously worked as a Software Developer.

title: SoftBank Explores Sale or IPO for Chip Designer Arm Holdings
summary: SoftBank Group Corp. is reportedly exploring options for its British chip designer Arm Holdings, including a full or partial sale or a public offering. The Japanese conglomerate acquired Arm four years ago for $32 billion. Goldman Sachs Group Inc. is advising on the early-stage review.

title: Gartner’s 2020 Magic Quadrant for Data Center and Cloud Networking: Key Takeaways
summary: Gartner's 2020 Magic Quadrant for Data Center and Cloud Networking identifies 11 vendors, categorizing them into Leaders, Challengers, Visionaries, and Niche Players based on their vision and execution. Cisco, Arista Networks, and Juniper Networks were named Leaders, recognized for their investments in analytics, product portfolios, and automation capabilities. The report also highlights the strengths and market positions of Challengers like Huawei, Visionaries including VMware and Dell EMC, and Niche Players such as NVIDIA-Mellanox Technologies.

title: Lenovo Legion™ Offers More Ways to Raise Your Game
summary: Lenovo has expanded its Legion gaming PC lineup, integrating AMD Ryzen mobile and desktop processors into five new models. This expansion provides gamers with more choices and aims to deliver immersive experiences with improved performance, graphics, and display technology. The new offerings include Lenovo Legion laptops (17-inch Legion 5, Legion 5P, IdeaPad Gaming 3) and desktops (Legion Tower 5, IdeaCentre Gaming 5), all featuring advanced thermal solutions and high refresh rate displays.

title: New in July 2020: Playback Improvements for H.264 and HEVC on Windows
summary: Adobe has released updates for Premiere Pro and After Effects, significantly improving H.264 and HEVC playback performance on Windows Intel systems, offering up to a 2X speed increase due to collaboration with Intel. The update also introduces ProRes 4444 XQ export for macOS, previously Windows-only, and features the Roto Brush 2 in After Effects Beta, which uses Adobe Sensei for faster rotoscoping. These enhancements are part of Adobe's ongoing efforts to boost application quality and performance through strategic partnerships.

title: University of Florida and Nvidia partner to build academia’s fastest supercomputer yet
summary: The University of Florida and Nvidia Corp. are partnering to build what they claim will be the fastest artificial intelligence supercomputer in academia. This machine, an upgrade to UF's existing HiPerGator, will tackle issues like COVID-19 research, rising seas, and personalized medicine, and is made possible by a $25 million donation from Nvidia founder Chris Malachowsky and an additional $25 million in hardware and services from Nvidia. UF also plans to invest $20 million and aims to become a leading AI university, producing 30,000 "AI-enabled graduates" by 2030.

title: Intel's 7nm is Broken, Company Announces Delay Until 2022, 2023
summary: Intel announced a significant delay in the rollout of its 7nm CPUs, pushing their debut to late 2022 or early 2023. This delay is attributed to a "defect mode" causing yield degradation, putting Intel approximately twelve months behind its internal targets for 7nm process. The company is now exploring contingency plans, including the use of third-party foundries for some components and entire chip designs, and plans to increase shipments of 10nm chips by 20%.

title: Banking on AI: RBC Builds a DGX-Powered Private Cloud
summary: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) has built an NVIDIA DGX-powered private cloud to enhance its AI capabilities and transform client experiences, leveraging a strategic investment in AI through its research institute, Borealis AI. This new infrastructure allows RBC to run thousands of simulations and analyze millions of data points rapidly, enabling the development of smart applications and significant savings in total cost of ownership. The initiative showcases RBC's commitment to innovation and its early adoption of emerging technologies to maintain its competitive edge in the financial services industry.

title: Nvidia sets 16 new performance records in latest MLPerf AI benchmarks
summary: Nvidia's latest A100 GPU and its DGX SuperPOD system achieved 16 new performance records in the third annual MLPerf benchmark tests, showcasing significant advancements in AI training. The company's hardware excelled in new recommendation systems tests, Natural Language Processing, and reinforcement learning. This performance highlights a four-times improvement over Nvidia's previous DGX system, reinforcing its position in the AI hardware market alongside other strong contenders like Google.

title: Arista, Juniper, Nvidia Switch Vendor ‘Leaders,’ Says Forrester
summary: A Forrester Research report on programmable switch vendors names Arista Networks, Huawei, Juniper Networks, and Nvidia as "leaders." Arista particularly stood out due to its flexible EOS operating system, while Cisco, despite its significant market presence, was placed in the "strong performers" and "contenders" categories for its IOS-XE and NX-OS platforms, respectively. Nvidia also had a dual presence, with its Cumulus Networks operations named a leader and its Mellanox acquisition a contender.

title: Hermann Hauser: ARM sale to Nvidia would be a disaster
summary: Hermann Hauser, co-founder of ARM, stated that a potential sale of the British chip designer to US firm Nvidia would be "disastrous." He argues that Nvidia, being a competitor to many of ARM's licensees, would compromise ARM's crucial neutrality, leading current licensees to seek alternatives. Hauser believes the UK government should intervene to help ARM become an independent British company once again, possibly through a public listing.

title: CHT, partners kick off self-driving bus services
summary: Chunghwa Telecom (CHT), Kingwaytek Technology, and Tamsui Bus have launched autonomous passenger transport services in New Taipei. The service utilizes an autonomous driving platform integrating C-V2X communication, self-driving buses built by Kingwaytek, roadside sensors, and a cloud monitoring system. CHT has also established a monitoring center to manage real-time data for smart transportation applications.

title: Fleet Dreams Are Made of These: TuSimple and Navistar to Build Autonomous Trucks Powered by NVIDIA DRIVE
summary: TuSimple and Navistar are partnering to build dedicated self-driving semi-trucks, with production slated to begin in 2024. These autonomous trucks will be powered by the NVIDIA DRIVE AGX platform, moving beyond retrofitted vehicles to custom-built designs optimized for self-driving systems. This collaboration signifies a major step towards widespread deployment of autonomous freight, supported by Navistar's infrastructure and TuSimple's HD map network.

title: How RBC Built Its Own GPU Farm for an Artificial Intelligence-Powered Banking Platform
summary: The Royal Bank of Canada (RBC), working with Red Hat and Nvidia, has developed an AI computing platform powered by a custom-built Nvidia GPU farm to enhance its banking services. This platform allows for extremely fast processing of client records and real-time analysis of market data, significantly improving efficiency compared to CPU-based systems. The collaborative effort not only benefits RBC but is also expected to provide valuable insights and technologies for the broader fintech industry and other sectors, as the partners gained considerable expertise in AI and cloud technologies.

title: Startup Lunit Uses AI to Help Doctors Prioritize Patients with COVID-19 Symptoms
summary: Lunit, a South Korean medical imaging startup, has developed an AI-based system called Lunit INSIGHT CXR to quickly detect pneumonia and other radiological findings on chest X-rays. This system is crucial for triaging COVID-19 patients by providing near-instant evaluations. The company has partnered with GE Healthcare and utilizes NVIDIA technology to commercialize its AI solutions, aiming to enhance medical diagnosis and treatment efficiency.

title: Blaize Takes On Nvidia, Intel With Xplorer Edge AI Chips
summary: Blaize, an AI chip startup, is launching its Xplorer Accelerator cards and Pathfinder P1600 embedded modules to compete with Intel and Nvidia. These new products are based on a Graph Streaming Processors architecture that reportedly offers up to 60 times better system-level efficiency for edge AI applications compared to traditional CPU and GPU solutions. Blaize plans to target the market through OEMs, system integrators, VARs, and ISVs, leveraging its proprietary AI software suite.

title: The geopolitical implications of the microchip race
summary: The semiconductor industry has become a critical geopolitical battleground between the United States and China. Both nations recognize that winning the microchip race will confer a significant advantage in the ongoing great power competition. While China's domestic microchip production lags behind Western technology, the country could potentially close the gap by leveraging political power and securing foreign expertise, though U.S. efforts are aimed at thwarting these advancements.

title: Nvidia Expands Partner Program With New Incentives, Training
summary: Nvidia has enhanced its Partner Network with new incentives, industry-specific training, and improved sales tracking for its growing channel of over 1,500 members. Key additions include a fixed back-end rebate for Elite partners, dedicated market development funds, and an expanded "AI Champions Club." The company is also planning future expansions, such as integrating Mellanox and Cumulus Networks' partner programs and introducing a cloud service provider program.

title: Swing Trading Semiconductors The IBD Way
summary: This article details Investor's Business Daily's (IBD) swing trading strategy for semiconductor stocks, emphasizing a shift from a semiconductor ETF to individual sector leaders like AMD and Nvidia. It highlights how the strategy adapted to the coronavirus market rally, initially gaining broad exposure through an ETF and later refining positions to focus on outperforming individual stocks. The piece explains IBD's method of identifying and investing in strong leaders for optimal swing trading results.

title: SoftBank builds $1.2 billion Amazon stake; invests in Netflix, Tesla
summary: SoftBank Group Corp has built a $1.2 billion stake in Amazon and also invested in Netflix, Tesla, Microsoft, and Alphabet, marking a strategic shift towards liquid stocks. This move comes as the company expands its investment activities beyond unlisted startups and its Vision Fund, which has recently seen its holdings fall below acquisition prices. The group is leveraging a massive asset sale program to buy shares in these tech giants, whose values are currently rising amidst a tech stock rally.

title: Nvidia hurdles $300 billion market cap, which Intel hasn’t topped since the dot-com bust
summary: Nvidia Corp. has surpassed a $300 billion market capitalization for the first time, establishing itself as the largest U.S. chip company. This milestone comes as Nvidia's stock has risen over 100% this year, while Intel's has declined by nearly 20%. Nvidia is set to report its second-quarter earnings soon after achieving this record valuation.

title: Gold Diggers; Nvidia ARMed; TSLA’s Chinese Bevy; Sorry Chevy
summary: This article discusses the current market trends in gold, Nvidia, Tesla, and General Motors. It highlights gold's rallying price despite being considered a "boring" investment, Nvidia's potential acquisition of ARM Holdings, Tesla's fluctuating registration numbers in China despite a rising stock price, and General Motors' reluctance to fully embrace the EV market. The article also provides a rundown of upcoming earnings reports in the retail and semiconductor sectors.

title: August NVIDIA Studio Driver Now Ready for Download — Brings Support for Adobe Premiere Rush, Premiere Pro and More Creative App Updates
summary: NVIDIA has released its August Studio Driver, which offers support for new updates across a range of creative applications including Adobe Premiere Rush, Premiere Pro, Blender, V-Ray 5 for Maya, Flicker Free, and BorisFX Optics. Key features include AI-powered tools in Adobe apps like Auto Reframe and Scene Edit Detection, OptiX acceleration for all NVIDIA GPUs in Blender, and performance enhancements in V-Ray 5 and Flicker Free. The update aims to improve productivity for creators, especially those working remotely, with increased speed and new functionalities.

title: Intel's next-gen Xe-HPG gaming GPU will be made by TSMC on 6nm in 2021
summary: Intel's forthcoming Xe-HPG gaming-focused graphics card, expected in 2021, will be manufactured by Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) using their 6nm process node. This move positions Intel to compete directly with AMD and NVIDIA, as the Xe-HPG is rumored to include hardware ray tracing and GDDR6 memory. While Intel's Xe-LP and Xe-HP designs will be produced in-house on their 10nm SuperFin process, the strategic decision to utilize TSMC's 6nm node for the gaming GPU aims to provide a competitive edge against 7nm and 8nm offerings from rivals.

title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang: Our Future Is About ‘Data Center-Scale Computing’
summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang emphasized that the company's future hinges on "data center-scale computing" rather than just chip-level optimization. This strategy is highlighted by the recent acquisition of Mellanox and the success of its data center division, which for the first time surpassed gaming revenue. Huang stressed that innovation must encompass communication between chips and system-level solutions, including the DGX deep learning systems, to achieve holistic data center performance.

title: Intel plans big stock buyback after shares plummet, boosting prices in after-hours trading
summary: Intel announced a plan to buy back $10 billion of its stock by the end of the year, following a nearly 19% drop in its shares over the past month. This decision resulted in a nearly 4% gain in after-hours trading. The company views these repurchases as prudent given that its shares are trading below intrinsic valuation, amidst struggles with new chip engineering and increased competition from rivals like AMD and Nvidia.

title: Apple worth $1 trillion more since COVID-19 crashed the NASDAQ 100
summary: This article highlights how certain tech companies, particularly Apple and Tesla, have seen significant market value increases since the NASDAQ 100's low point in March 2020 following the COVID-19 crash. Apple's market capitalization grew by over $1 trillion to surpass $2 trillion, while Tesla also experienced a remarkable recovery. The article also notes other companies like Mercadolibre, PayPal, NVIDIA, eBay, Align Technology, and Lululemon that showed strong rebounds, contrasting these with a couple of pharma stocks that had not fully recovered.

title: Reliance Industries Successfully Became The Second Largest Brand In The World After Apple In 2020
summary: Reliance Industries, led by Mukesh Ambani, was ranked the second-largest brand globally after Apple in the FutureBrand Index 2020. The company was recognized for its ethical behavior, growth, innovative products, and excellent customer service due to its transformation into an advanced conglomerate catering to diverse consumer needs, spanning petrochemicals, telecommunications, and more. FutureBrand highlighted that Reliance's success is partly due to its expansion and investments from Google and Facebook, positioning it for potential future growth in the rankings.

title: Pixel Perfect: V7 Labs Automates Image Annotation for Deep Learning Models
summary: V7 Labs, a U.K. startup, has developed an AI-powered web platform called V7 Darwin that automates image annotation for deep learning models. This platform is trained to detect and label almost any object, accelerating the training process by up to 50x compared to human annotation. V7 Darwin is optimized on NVIDIA GPUs and is being applied across various industries, including healthcare, manufacturing, and agriculture, to improve efficiency and reduce costs associated with AI model development.

title: City's technology chief Louis Stewart hired away by Nvidia Corp.
summary: Louis Stewart, Sacramento's chief innovation officer, is leaving his municipal role to join Nvidia Corp., a Santa Clara-based technology company. He is expected to start his new position in mid-September.

title: Nvidia says its new 28B-transistor flagship graphics chip is fastest ever built
summary: Nvidia has launched its new RTX 30 series, a flagship line of consumer graphics cards. The top-tier RTX 3090 features 28 billion transistors and is considered the "fastest GPU ever built for gaming and creative types," capable of running 8K resolution games at 60 frames per second. This series, based on Nvidia's Ampere architecture, promises a significant generational leap in performance and power efficiency.

title: NVIDIA Delivers Greatest-Ever Generational Leap with GeForce RTX 30 Series GPUs
summary: NVIDIA has unveiled its GeForce RTX 30 Series GPUs, powered by the NVIDIA Ampere architecture, delivering the most significant generational performance leap in GeForce history with up to 2x the performance and 1.9x the power efficiency of the previous generation. These new GPUs, including the RTX 3090, 3080, and 3070, offer unprecedented real-time ray tracing and AI gaming capabilities, along with new tools like NVIDIA Reflex, Omniverse Machinima, and Broadcast. Fortnite is also integrating RTX real-time ray tracing, enhancing the gaming experience with advanced graphical features.

title: Taiwan Semiconductor Is the Most Important Company in the World
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM) is highlighted as the world's most important company due to its dominant lead in advanced chip manufacturing technology, particularly in 7nm and 5nm processes. Despite its strategic importance and lead over competitors like Intel and Samsung, the stock's valuation is influenced by geopolitical risks related to its location in Taiwan and the ongoing tensions between the U.S. and China. The company is, however, exploring building a plant in Arizona to mitigate some of these risks.

title: Micron Announces GDDR6X Memory, Powering the World's Fastest Graphics Cards
summary: Micron Technology announced GDDR6X, the world's fastest discrete graphics memory solution, capable of reaching system bandwidths up to 1 terabyte per second. This new memory, developed in collaboration with NVIDIA, powers the new NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 and GeForce RTX 3080 GPUs, enabling advanced gaming experiences with high resolutions and real-time ray tracing. GDDR6X achieves its speed through innovative four-level pulse amplitude modulation (PAM4) signaling, significantly increasing memory bandwidth and offering lower power consumption per transaction.

title: ‘Fortnite’ Is RTX On! Real-Time Ray Tracing Comes to One of Most Popular Games on the Planet
summary: NVIDIA and Epic Games announced that Fortnite is integrating real-time ray tracing, AI-powered NVIDIA DLSS, and NVIDIA Reflex technology, significantly enhancing the game's visuals and responsiveness. These advancements will be available across all Fortnite modes, including a new "RTX Treasure Run" creative map designed to showcase the ray tracing effects. The collaboration highlights how NVIDIA's GeForce RTX 30 Series GPUs are improving competitive gaming with next-level graphics and performance.

title: Micron Unveils GDDR6X Memory For NVIDIA GeForce RTX 30 Series – The Next Chapter In Graphics Memory
summary: Micron has introduced its new GDDR6X memory, designed for NVIDIA's GeForce RTX 30 series graphics cards, specifically the RTX 3090 and RTX 3080. This memory features PAM4 multi-level signaling, doubling the I/O data rate and achieving bandwidths up to 1 TB/s for high-fidelity gaming. GDDR6X also offers improved power efficiency, consuming 15% less power per transferred bit compared to GDDR6, and is expected to reach speeds higher than 21 Gbps in the future.

title: Samsung Electronics lands order to produce next-generation chips for U.S. Nvidia
summary: Samsung Electronics has secured a significant foundry order to produce next-generation graphics processing units (GPUs) for Nvidia, specifically the GeForce RTX 30 Series. This marks a strategic win for Samsung, as Nvidia previously relied on TSMC for its GPU production. The deal leverages Samsung's 8-nano fabrication process, aiming to double GPU performance and challenging TSMC's dominance in the foundry market.

title: NVIDIA sued over 401(k) plan fees
summary: NVIDIA has been sued over fees associated with its 401(k) plan. This news is reported by Pensions & Investments, specializing in lawsuits and legal matters concerning retirement plans.

title: The new 2021 Mercedes S-Class goes tech-tastic
summary: The 2021 Mercedes S-Class is revealed as a technological marvel, featuring advanced infotainment, driver assistance systems, and luxurious interior amenities. Despite a familiar exterior, the car is lighter, more aerodynamic, and includes features like Level 3 autonomy, fingerprint recognition, and extensive customization options. Mercedes also emphasizes the car's environmental consciousness with its production plant and use of recycled materials.

title: China semiconductor-related shares open higher Friday
