summary: Pfizer Inc and BioNTech SE announced that two of their experimental coronavirus vaccine candidates were granted "fast track" status by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, accelerating the regulatory review process. This news caused their stock prices to rise significantly, boosting market sentiment regarding COVID-19 vaccine development. While the fast track designation helps speed up review for drugs addressing unmet medical needs, analysts noted that such a designation doesn't necessarily indicate a candidate's potential and is likely to be granted to most COVID-19 treatments.

title: BNTX Stock Jumped 5% in Pre-market, BioNTech Vaccine Receives Fast Track Status from FDA
summary: BioNTech (BNTX) stock surged in pre-market trading after its experimental coronavirus vaccines, developed with Pfizer, received "Fast Track" designation from the FDA. This regulatory endorsement is seen as a significant milestone in the development of a safe and effective vaccine against SARS-CoV-2. The companies aim to produce millions of doses by the end of 2020 and over a billion by the end of 2021, leading to increased investor attention and a substantial rise in BioNTech's share price.

title: Pfizer, BioNTech Get $1.95 Billion Covid-19 Vaccine Order From U.S. Government
summary: The U.S. government has placed a $1.95 billion order with Pfizer and BioNTech for 100 million doses of their experimental COVID-19 vaccine, with an option to acquire another 500 million doses. The vaccine, which has shown promising early results, will be provided to Americans free of charge if it receives regulatory clearance. This agreement signifies the government's preparations to distribute a vaccine, once proven safe and effective.

title: Pfizer and US government reach $1.95 billion deal to produce millions of Covid-19 vaccine doses
summary: The US government announced a $1.95 billion deal with Pfizer to secure 100 million doses of a Covid-19 vaccine, with an option to acquire an additional 500 million doses. The vaccine, developed by Pfizer and BioNTech, would be delivered nationwide in Q4 2020 if it receives emergency use authorization and proves effective in trials, and would be available to Americans at no cost. This agreement is part of the Operation Warp Speed program aimed at making an effective Covid-19 vaccine readily available.

title: U.S. signs contract with Pfizer for COVID-19 vaccine doses
summary: The Trump administration has signed a contract with Pfizer to pay nearly $2 billion for 100 million doses of a COVID-19 vaccine, with an option to purchase an additional 500 million doses. This agreement is part of Operation Warp Speed, aiming to deliver 300 million vaccine doses by January 2021, contingent on FDA approval for safety and effectiveness. Americans are expected to receive the vaccine for free once authorized.

title: Pfizer Vaccine Deal, Microsoft's Strong Performance
summary: Pfizer announced a $1.95 billion deal with the U.S. government to deliver a coronavirus vaccine in 2021, causing its shares and BioNTech's shares to surge. Microsoft also reported strong fourth-quarter results, surpassing estimates with a 13% revenue increase, though net income decreased due to physical store closures. Tesla also beat Wall Street expectations for its second-quarter profits, with significant increases in cash and vehicle deliveries, and its stock continues to perform well.

title: US govt spends US$1.95 bil to secure Covid-19 vaccine
summary: The US government has agreed to pay Pfizer Inc and German biotech firm BioNTech SE $1.95 billion for 100 million doses of their Covid-19 vaccine candidate. This agreement includes an option for the US to acquire an additional 500 million doses and is part of the Trump administration's "Operation Warp Speed" to accelerate vaccine development. The vaccine candidate is currently undergoing testing, with regulatory approval expected as early as October if trials are successful.

title: Arcturus and Duke-NUS announce approval of clinical trials for COVID-19 vaccine candidate
summary: Arcturus Therapeutics Holdings Inc. and Duke-NUS Medical School have received approval for clinical trials of their COVID-19 vaccine candidate, LUNAR-COV19, from the Singapore Health Sciences Authority. This vaccine utilizes Arcturus' STARR™ technology and Duke-NUS's rapid screening platform, aiming for a single, low-dose administration. Human dosing is expected to begin soon in a study evaluating safety, tolerability, and immune response in up to 108 adults.

title: Glaucoma drug delivery devices enter new frontier
summary: This article discusses new developments in glaucoma drug delivery devices presented at the annual Glaucoma 360 meeting. Various companies are developing innovative solutions, including bioresorbable implants, micro-fluidic delivery systems, biodegradable implants, subconjunctival devices, and hand-held precise micro-dose applicators, all aimed at improving patient adherence and treatment efficacy for glaucoma. These advancements focus on long-term, sustained, and more convenient drug delivery compared to traditional eye drops.

title: U.S. to pay Pfizer, BioNTech $1.95 billion for COVID-19 vaccine
summary: The U.S. government has agreed to pay Pfizer Inc and BioNTech SE nearly $2 billion for 100 million doses of their COVID-19 vaccine, enough to inoculate 50 million people, pending safety and efficacy approval. The agreement includes an option for an additional 500 million doses, with the vaccine to be made available to Americans at no cost. Pfizer aims to begin late-stage trials soon and expects to manufacture up to 100 million doses globally by the end of 2020.

title: Mattel Appoints Diana Ferguson to Its Board of Directors
summary: Mattel Inc. has appointed Diana S. Ferguson, CFO of Cleveland Avenue LLC, to its board of directors, effective July 21, 2020. Ferguson, who brings extensive experience in corporate financial management and strategic planning, will serve on the board’s audit committee and become its chair on September 1. This appointment supports Mattel's strategy to transform into an IP-driven, high-performing toy company and drive shareholder value.

title: An Easier Way to Understand the Pharma Industry
summary: This article provides an overview of the global pharmaceutical industry, detailing its subfields, regulatory bodies, and growth drivers. It covers publicly traded stocks and ETFs, the industry's supply chain, and critical regulations, highlighting why the pharma sector is unique due to its high regulation and capital intensity. The piece also explores factors contributing to the industry's growth, such as an aging population, changing lifestyles, increased income, chronic diseases, and globalization.

title: Moderna gets further $472 million U.S. award for coronavirus vaccine development
summary: Moderna has received an additional $472 million from the U.S. government's BARDA to support the late-stage clinical development of its coronavirus vaccine candidate, bringing the total funding to approximately $955 million. The additional funding will support the expanded Phase 3 study planned to begin on July 27 with 30,000 participants. Moderna aims to deliver 500 million to 1 billion doses per year starting in 2021.

title: Global Phase 2/3 Clinical Trial for COVID-19 Vaccine Starts at NYU Langone Health
summary: NYU Langone Health announced the commencement of a global Phase 2/3 clinical trial for a lead mRNA COVID-19 vaccine candidate, with NYU Grossman School of Medicine participating as one of 120 centers. This phase follows successful initial safety trials and aims to enroll up to 30,000 healthy participants globally to assess the vaccine's ability to prevent SARS-CoV-2 infection. The trial is a collaboration between Pfizer Inc. and BioNTech SE, testing the BNT162b2 vaccine candidate, which has already shown promising immune responses in earlier phases.

title: Final test of Moderna’s COVID-19 vaccine trial begins
summary: The final stage of Moderna's COVID-19 vaccine study has commenced, with 30,000 US participants testing the experimental immunization. This trial, co-developed by the National Institutes of Health and Moderna, Inc., is the first of several large-scale studies planned for leading vaccine candidates through the fall. Researchers will monitor participants for infections to assess the vaccine's efficacy and safety.

title: Robust Growth Visible for Inhalation Anesthesia Market
summary: The Global Inhalation Anesthesia Market is projected to experience robust growth between 2020 and 2025, driven by an increase in emergency cases, accidents, and the aging population suffering from various diseases. Key players in this market include Baxter, AbbVie, Piramal Enterprises, Halocarbon Products, Hikma Pharmaceuticals, Lunan Pharmaceutical Group, Jiangsu Hengrui Medicine, and Fresenius Kabi. The market is segmented by type (Sevoflurane, Desflurane, Isoflurane), application (Induction, Maintenance), and region, with North America expected to show the highest CAGR.

title: Moderna and Pfizer Begin Late-Stage Vaccine Trials (Published 2020)
summary: Moderna and Pfizer have both initiated late-stage clinical trials for their respective coronavirus vaccines, each aiming to enroll 30,000 participants to assess safety and effectiveness. Moderna's trial began with volunteers receiving shots, while Pfizer, in partnership with BioNTech, also started its study after securing a $1.95 billion deal with the U.S. government for vaccine doses. Both studies will monitor for side effects and evaluate the vaccines' ability to prevent Covid-19 infection and severe illness.

title: Trump Administration Selects Five Coronavirus Vaccine Candidates as Finalists (Published 2020)
summary: The Trump administration has selected five companies as finalists to develop a coronavirus vaccine, aiming for widespread inoculation by the end of the year. The chosen companies are Moderna, Oxford University/AstraZeneca, Johnson & Johnson, Merck, and Pfizer. While seen by the White House as a critical step in progress, many scientists view the goal of early availability as optimistic due to the complex nature of vaccine development.

title: Sonoco ThermoSafe Creating Industrywide PharmaPortal™
summary: Sonoco ThermoSafe is developing PharmaPortal™, a vendor-neutral blockchain platform built on IBM Blockchain Transparent Supply, to enhance transparency and traceability in the temperature-controlled pharmaceutical supply chain. This initiative aims to address inefficiencies contributing to an estimated $35 billion in losses within the $230 billion cold chain pharmaceutical distribution market. The platform will initially focus on traceability of temperature-controlled drugs like vaccines, ensuring an audit trail of environmental conditions, and will invite industry leaders to collaborate on its development.

title: AGILE: Phase III, Double-Blind, Randomised, Placebo-Controlled Study of Ivosidenib in Combination with Azacitidine in Adults with Newly Diagnosed Acute Myeloid Leukaemia and an IDH1 Mutation
summary: This article details the AGILE Phase III clinical trial, a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled study evaluating ivosidenib in combination with azacitidine for newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukaemia (AML) patients with an IDH1 mutation who are ineligible for intensive chemotherapy. The study builds on promising Phase Ib results, including a 78.3% overall response rate and 60.9% complete remission rate with a manageable safety profile. Key changes to the Phase III protocol include event-free survival as the primary endpoint and specified criteria for induction chemotherapy ineligibility.

title: U.S. Reaches $2.1 Billion Deal With Sanofi, GlaxoSmithKline For COVID-19 Vaccine Push
summary: The U.S. government announced a $2.1 billion deal with Sanofi and GlaxoSmithKline for COVID-19 vaccine development, including the purchase of 100 million doses. This agreement is part of Operation Warp Speed and marks the sixth vaccine candidate to join the portfolio and the largest vaccine deal to date. The companies have committed to making the vaccine affordable and accessible, with 100 million doses to be available to Americans at no cost if approved.

title: US to Pay $2.1 Billion to Sanofi, GSK in COVID-19 Vaccine Deal
summary: The US government has agreed to pay Sanofi SA and GlaxoSmithKline Plc $2.1 billion for COVID-19 vaccines sufficient to inoculate 50 million people, marking the largest deal yet under "Operation Warp Speed." This agreement also covers testing and manufacturing costs for the experimental vaccine, with options for the US to purchase an additional 500 million doses. Sanofi and GSK are also in talks to supply up to 300 million doses to the European Union.

title: Award-Winning Television Host Meredith Vieira Joins Pfizer's Find Your MBC Voice to Help Empower People Living with Metastatic Breast Cancer to Speak Up
summary: Meredith Vieira has partnered with Pfizer for the "Find Your MBC Voice" initiative, aiming to empower individuals with metastatic breast cancer (mBC) to actively engage in discussions about their treatment options with their doctors. The program provides a Treatment Discussion Guide and launches WMBC Radio, a streaming station offering resources and stories. This initiative seeks to improve communication and shared decision-making for those living with mBC, a condition for which there is no cure.

title: Pfizer reups PPD deal in a contract research pact spree
summary: Pfizer has expanded its contract research organization (CRO) partnerships by signing a new three-year agreement with PPD for drug development services, with an option to extend for two more years. This move follows similar extended pacts with Syneos Health and Icon, reinforcing Pfizer's strategy of utilizing preferred CROs. The financial terms of the deal were not disclosed.

title: PPD Signs New Service Agreement With Pfizer
summary: Wilmington-headquartered PPD Inc. (Nasdaq: PPD) has signed a new three-year agreement with Pfizer Inc. to provide drug development services, with optional two-year extensions. This agreement builds on their existing relationship, where PPD supports Pfizer's drug development initiatives across multiple therapeutic areas. Financial details were not disclosed, but PPD expressed commitment to innovative solutions and quality execution for Pfizer.

title: Regeneron and BioNTech Partner on Immunotherapy Combo for Melanoma
summary: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals and BioNTech have formed a strategic collaboration to develop an immunotherapy combination for melanoma. The partnership will combine BioNTech’s BNT111 FixVac product with Regeneron and Sanofi’s checkpoint inhibitor Libtayo (cemiplimab) and plans to initiate a randomized Phase II trial in patients with anti-PD1-refractory/relapsed, unresectable Stage III or IV cutaneous melanoma. The companies will equally share development costs and retain full commercial rights to their respective products.

title: FDA rejects a peanut allergy treatment, sinking a small biotech’s shares
summary: The FDA rejected DBV Technologies' peanut allergy treatment, Viaskin Peanut, citing design issues and requesting more clinical data and manufacturing information. This setback significantly impacted DBV's shares and financial outlook, while a rival treatment from Aimmune Therapeutics, Palforzia, saw a temporary stock increase despite initial sales challenges due to the coronavirus pandemic. Analysts believe the rejection could force DBV to raise more capital due to the costly new requirements.

title: Moderna sets high price in early coronavirus vaccine supply deals
summary: Moderna has set a high price of $32 to $37 per dose for its experimental coronavirus vaccine in early preorder deals, which is significantly more expensive than competitors. While these initial agreements are for small quantities, future larger supply deals might involve a lower price. This pricing strategy from Moderna is likely to generate controversy, especially when compared to the lower prices implied by deals made by Pfizer and Johnson & Johnson.

title: Pfizer, Amgen will rake in billions during 'golden age' for biosimilars: analyst
summary: An analyst report suggests that Pfizer and Amgen are entering a "golden age" for biosimilars, with Pfizer's biosimilar sales growing significantly and Amgen's biosimilar business also robust. Despite potential future pricing pressures, the U.S. market offers strong commercial prospects for biosimilars compared to Europe due to higher achievable prices. Both companies are expected to generate billions annually from their biosimilar portfolios in the coming years.

title: Johnson & Johnson pledges 100M coronavirus vaccine doses to U.S. for $10 each
summary: Johnson & Johnson has secured a deal with the U.S. government to supply 100 million doses of its COVID-19 vaccine candidate, Ad26.COV2.S, for just over $1 billion, pricing each dose at approximately $10. This agreement, which includes manufacturing in the U.S., allows for an additional purchase of 200 million doses. While still in early human trials, J&J anticipates initial results in September and could begin phase 3 efficacy testing next month.

title: With Court Win, BMS and Pfizer Stave Off Eliquis Generic Challengers – For Now
summary: Bristol Myers Squibb (BMS) and Pfizer secured a federal court victory, upholding patents for their anticoagulant drug Eliquis. This ruling prevents generic competitors Sigmapharm, Sunshine Lake, and Unichem from entering the market until at least 2026, and potentially until 2031 for some manufacturers, protecting a significant revenue stream for both companies. The decision follows previous settlements with Micro Labs Limited and Mylan Pharmaceuticals Inc., further solidifying BMS and Pfizer's market position for Eliquis.

title: Trump signs ‘Buy American’ executive order for essential drugs
summary: President Trump signed an executive order requiring federal agencies to purchase essential drugs and medical supplies from U.S. manufacturers. This initiative aims to reduce reliance on foreign supply chains and prevent shortages, a concern highlighted by the coronavirus pandemic. The order also directs the FDA to determine which drugs qualify, with exemptions for cost and availability, and seeks to streamline regulatory processes for domestic manufacturing.

title: Icelandic Biopharmaceutical Company Alvotech Signs Huge Contract with Teva
summary: Alvotech, an Icelandic biopharmaceutical company, has signed a significant collaboration agreement with Teva Pharmaceuticals. This partnership, one of the largest business contracts ever for an Icelandic company, focuses on commercializing five biosimilar product candidates in the US market. The agreement is expected to generate hundreds of billions of ISK for Alvotech over the next decade and will lead to an increase in staff at its Reykjavík headquarters.

title: Bausch + Lomb to be spun off. Rochester impact out of focus for now
summary: Bausch Health announced plans to spin off its Bausch + Lomb eye care division into a separate publicly traded entity. The immediate impact on Rochester, where Bausch + Lomb has over 1,100 employees and manufactures key eye products, is currently unclear though the Rochester facility is expected to be part of the new eye care business. This move follows Valeant's acquisition of Bausch + Lomb in 2013 and recent expansions at the Rochester site for contact lens production.

title: Bristol Myers, Pfizer fend off a key challenge to their top-selling heart drug
summary: A Delaware district court judge has upheld two key patents for Bristol Myers Squibb and Pfizer's blockbuster blood-thinner Eliquis, protecting it from generic competition from Sigmapharm, Sunshine Lake, and Unichem until 2031. This ruling is a significant victory for both companies, especially for Bristol Myers, as Eliquis is a critical revenue driver and helps offset debt from its acquisition of Celgene. While other generic versions might launch as early as 2026 due to prior settlements, the upholding of these patents secures Eliquis' market position for a longer period.

title: Pfizer agrees to manufacture Gilead's coronavirus drug remdesivir
summary: Pfizer has committed to manufacturing and supplying Gilead Sciences' antiviral drug remdesivir through a multiyear agreement. This collaboration aims to significantly increase the availability of the intravenous drug, which has been shown to reduce recovery times for some hospitalized coronavirus patients. Pfizer will produce the drug at its facility in McPherson, Kansas, contributing to global efforts to combat the COVID-19 crisis.

title: Pfizer to make Gilead's COVID-19 treatment remdesivir
summary: Pfizer Inc. announced a multiyear agreement to manufacture Gilead Sciences Inc.'s COVID-19 treatment, remdesivir. This deal comes as Gilead faces pressure to increase the supply of the antiviral drug, which has been difficult to access despite its proven efficacy for hospitalized COVID-19 patients. Pfizer will produce remdesivir at its McPherson, Kansas plant, aiming to boost global availability of the treatment.

title: WilmerHale Achieves Significant Victory for Bristol-Myers Squibb and Pfizer in Patent Suit
summary: WilmerHale secured a decisive trial victory for Bristol-Myers Squibb Company and Pfizer Inc. in a Hatch-Waxman litigation concerning patents for their blockbuster drug Eliquis®. The District of Delaware court found that proposed generic products from three defendants infringed on patents expiring in 2026 and 2031, following a case that initially involved 25 generic companies.

title: Japan plans to buy AstraZeneca’s COVID-19 vaccine
summary: Japan plans to acquire AstraZeneca's experimental COVID-19 vaccine and support local manufacturing of Novavax's candidate to bolster its vaccine stockpile amidst rising infections. The country will order 120 million doses from AstraZeneca and has a separate deal to buy 120 million doses of Pfizer and BioNTech's vaccine candidate. Japan is also developing its own vaccines while procuring supplies from international pharmaceutical companies.

title: Kansas plant will produce Covid-19 drug that is in short supply
summary: Gilead Sciences Inc. has partnered with Pfizer Inc. to increase the production of its Covid-19 treatment, remdesivir. A Pfizer plant in Kansas will be involved in manufacturing the drug, which is currently in short supply. This initiative aims to address the urgent demand for remdesivir among hospitals and state attorneys general for treating Covid-19 patients.

title: Dr.Reddy’s launches generic version of Ciprodex
summary: Dr. Reddy's Laboratories has launched a generic version of Ciprodex (Ciprofloxacin 0.3% and Dexamethasone 0.1%) Otic Suspension, USP, in the U.S. market. This product, indicated for treating ear infections, is the first-to-market generic and follows USFDA approval. Ciprodex had U.S. sales of approximately $453 million MAT for the twelve months ending June 2020.

title: US Makes Deal with Biotech Company for 100 Million Doses of Potential COVID-19 Vaccine
summary: The U.S. government has announced a deal with biotech company Moderna to acquire 100 million doses of a potential COVID-19 vaccine. This comes as three vaccine candidates in the U.S. are in final human trials, while Russia has controversially registered its own vaccine, Sputnik V, before completing Phase 3 trials. Other countries like China and Mexico are also advancing their vaccine development and trial efforts.

title: US government strikes $1.525 billion deal with Moderna for 100 million doses of its Covid-19 vaccine
summary: The US government has finalized a $1.525 billion deal with Moderna Inc. to secure 100 million doses of its Covid-19 vaccine, mRNA-1273, once approved. The contract allows for an additional 400 million doses and aims to provide vaccines to Americans at no cost as part of Operation Warp Speed. This agreement follows similar deals with Pfizer and Janssen, emphasizing the Trump administration's efforts to create a diverse vaccine portfolio.

title: U.S. inks $1.5 billion deal with Moderna for 100 million doses of COVID-19 vaccine
summary: The United States has finalized a $1.5 billion agreement with Moderna Inc. to secure 100 million doses of its potential COVID-19 vaccine, mRNA-1273. This deal is part of the U.S. government's Operation Warp Speed, aiming to deliver a vaccine by year-end, and follows other advanced purchase agreements with various pharmaceutical companies to ensure a substantial vaccine supply for the nation. Moderna's vaccine candidate is currently in its final testing stage, with results expected in September.

title: Bristol Myers Squibb takes on racial inequality with $300M pledge to up diversity, improve healthcare access
summary: Bristol Myers Squibb has pledged $300 million over the next five years to combat racial inequality by increasing diversity within its workforce, enhancing clinical trial diversity, and improving healthcare access for underserved populations globally. This initiative, spurred by recent discussions around racism, includes specific goals such as doubling executive roles for Black and Latinx staff in the U.S. by 2022 and training 250 diverse clinical investigators. The company also aims to address issues like inadequate minority patient inclusion in clinical trials and will spend $1 billion with diverse-owned suppliers by 2025.

title: 4 innovative ways Johnson & Johnson has helped protect the public's health during outbreaks since the late 1800s
summary: Johnson & Johnson has a long history of contributing to public health during outbreaks, dating back to the late 1800s. The company's efforts include educating the public about hygiene, being one of the first to vaccinate employees during a smallpox outbreak, mass-producing epidemic masks during the Spanish flu, and actively working on treatments and vaccines for current global health threats like COVID-19, tuberculosis, and Ebola. These initiatives demonstrate Johnson & Johnson's sustained commitment to safeguarding global public health.

title: Phase I/II study of COVID-19 RNA vaccine BNT162b1 in adults
summary: This study reports available safety, tolerability, and immunogenicity data from an ongoing placebo-controlled, observer-blinded dose-escalation study of the COVID-19 RNA vaccine BNT162b1 in 45 healthy adults. The vaccine demonstrated dose-dependent local reactions and systemic events that were generally mild to moderate and transient, with a 30-μg dose showing robust immunogenicity comparable or superior to convalescent sera. These promising results support further evaluation and accelerated clinical development of this mRNA vaccine candidate.

title: Pfizer's COVID vaccine shows 'robust' results in early trial
summary: Pfizer's experimental COVID-19 vaccine, BNT162b1, demonstrated a robust immune response in an early-stage trial involving 45 healthy adults. The RNA-based vaccine elicited significantly higher levels of neutralizing antibodies compared to those recovering from SARS-CoV-2, with responses increasing with dose and a second shot. While generally well-tolerated, phase 3 trials are necessary to confirm its safety, strength, and duration of protection.

title: US eyes controversial human challenge trials for COVID-19 vaccine
summary: US government scientists are beginning to manufacture a synthetic strain of the novel coronavirus for potential use in human challenge trials, where volunteers would be intentionally infected after vaccination. These controversial trials, advocated by groups like 1 Day Sooner, would aim to accelerate vaccine testing but raise significant ethical concerns due to the lack of "rescue therapies" for COVID-19. While the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) considers such studies for future vaccine generations, many scientists emphasize prioritizing current field trials and question the ethical and practical implications of challenging healthy, young individuals when there's no treatment and the pandemic is widespread.

title: Genentech’s New NMOSD Drug Offers At-Home Treatment, Lower Cost
summary: Genentech has introduced a new NMOSD drug, Enspryng, which provides at-home treatment options for patients. The drug is priced lower than its competitors from Alexion and Viela Bio. Enspryng had already received approvals in Canada, Japan, and Switzerland before its announcement for US availability.

title: Yale and Yale New Haven Hospital begin Phase 3 trial of COVID-19 vaccine
summary: Yale School of Medicine and Yale New Haven Hospital have commenced Phase 3 of the Pfizer COVID-19 vaccine trial. This trial utilizes a novel modified RNA approach to generate immunity, moving from successful initial phases that confirmed safety and immune response to this phase which aims to prove its effectiveness in preventing infection. The study emphasizes diverse participation, facilitated by the YCCI Cultural Ambassadors program, and aims to ensure rapid yet safe vaccine development.

title: FDA Rejects Gilead’s Rheumatoid Arthritis Drug, Filgotinib, Over Safety Concerns
summary: The FDA issued a Complete Response Letter for Gilead Sciences' New Drug Application for filgotinib, a rheumatoid arthritis drug, due to safety concerns. The agency requested additional data from the MANTA and MANTA-Ray trials, which evaluate the drug's impact on sperm parameters, and expressed concerns about the overall benefit/risk profile of the 200 mg dose. This rejection positions Gilead behind competitors in the JAK inhibitor market and raises questions about future development timelines for filgotinib.

title: [ARCHIVED] COVID-19 Update - 8/19/20
summary: This archived update from August 19, 2020, reports 9 new positive COVID-19 cases in Cape May County residents and 2 new out-of-county cases, with zero new deaths. It also details an agreement between the U.S. government and Pfizer Inc. for the large-scale production and delivery of 100 million doses of a COVID-19 vaccine, with an option for an additional 500 million doses, to be available at no cost to the American people. The vaccine delivery was slated to begin in the fourth quarter of 2020 pending FDA authorization and successful clinical trials.

title: Moderna: More than 40% of participants enrolled for trial
summary: Moderna announced that over 13,000 participants have been enrolled in its late-stage COVID-19 vaccine trial, representing more than 40% of the 30,000-volunteer target. The company highlighted that 18% of these participants are from Black, Latino, American Indian, or Alaska Native communities, groups disproportionately affected by COVID-19 and historically underrepresented in clinical trials. Moderna expects to complete enrollment for the trial in September, with the vaccine candidate mRNA-1273 being part of a U.S. government initiative to accelerate vaccine development.

title: Salesforce, Amgen, and Honeywell Int’l will join Dow Jones Industrial Average
summary: Salesforce, Amgen, and Honeywell International are set to join the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) before trading opens on August 31, 2020. These companies will replace ExxonMobil, Pfizer, and Raytheon Technologies. The changes are a response to Apple's 4:1 stock split, which would have reduced the index's information technology weighting, and are intended to maintain the index's level.

title: Salesforce to replace Exxon in Dow Jones Industrial Average index next week
summary: Salesforce.com Inc, Amgen Inc, and Honeywell International Inc are set to replace Exxon Mobil Corp, Pfizer Inc, and Raytheon Technologies Corp in the Dow Jones Industrial Average index starting August 31. This change follows Apple Inc's stock split, which would have reduced the index's weight in the information technology sector.

title: Salesforce to replace Exxon in Dow Jones Industrial Average index next week
summary: Salesforce.com Inc, Amgen Inc, and Honeywell International Inc are set to join the Dow Jones Industrial Average index on August 31, replacing Exxon Mobil Corp, Pfizer Inc, and Raytheon Technologies Corp. This change follows Apple Inc's stock split, which prompted a rebalancing of the index's representation in the information technology sector.

title: How Syracuse researchers are using cows to fight coronavirus
summary: Researchers at Upstate Medical University are participating in a clinical trial using genetically-engineered cows from SAB Biotherapeutics to produce human antibodies against Covid-19. The experimental treatment, known as SAB-185, involves infusing patients with these cow-derived antibodies, which are believed to be more potent and longer-lasting than those from convalescent plasma. SAB Biotherapeutics has received significant federal funding for this research, aiming to provide both treatment and short-term immunity for high-risk populations.

title: Exxon kicked out of Dow Industrials
summary: Exxon Mobil, Pfizer, and Raytheon Technologies were removed from the Dow Jones Industrial Average, making way for Salesforce.com, Amgen, and Honeywell International. This reshuffling, the biggest in seven years, reflects the increasing dominance of technology companies and the declining influence of commodity firms in the American economy, a trend amplified by the 2020 pandemic. The changes were prompted by Apple's stock split, which reduced tech's sway in the price-weighted index, leading the Dow's handlers to seek greater technology representation.

title: Ex-pharmaceutical company boss faces insider trading charges
summary: A former pharmaceutical company head, Sepehr Sarshar, has been arrested on insider trading charges. He is accused of illegally sharing information about a $3.2 billion buyout offer with friends and family, allowing them to gain over $700,000 from trading securities in Auspex Pharmaceuticals, a company he founded. Sarshar faces charges including securities fraud and wire fraud.

title: Exxon Mobil dropped from the Dow after nearly a century, replaced by Salesforce
summary: Exxon Mobil, a Dow Jones Industrial Average member since 1928, is being removed from the blue-chip index and replaced by Salesforce.com. Drug company Pfizer and Raytheon Technologies are also being replaced by Amgen and Honeywell respectively. These changes, effective August 31, were prompted by Apple's stock split and aim to better reflect the American economy.

title: Exxon yanked from Dow after nearly a century
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. was removed from the Dow Jones Industrial Average after more than 90 years, a symbolic move reflecting the oil industry's recent struggles, including falling oil prices and climate concerns. This change saw SalesForce.com Inc., Amgen Inc., and Honeywell International Inc. replace Exxon, Pfizer Inc., and Raytheon Technologies Corp. While Exxon maintains its focus on shareholder value, critics argue the company is failing to adapt to a changing energy market.

title: Exxon Mobil replaced by a software stock after 92 years in the Dow is a 'sign of the times'
summary: Exxon Mobil, a Dow component for 92 years, has been replaced by software company Salesforce, marking a significant shift in the index. This change, alongside Amgen and Honeywell International replacing Pfizer and Raytheon Technologies, reflects the declining prominence of the energy sector and the corresponding rise of technology stocks. The move is seen as a "sign of the times," highlighting the faltering energy industry against a backdrop of strong tech growth.

title: Teva Pharmaceutical’s U.S. Unit Indicted on Price-Fixing Charges - WSJ
summary: Teva Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd.'s U.S. unit has been indicted on price-fixing charges by the Justice Department. The generic drugmaker is accused of participating in three different conspiracies, leading to at least $350 million in overcharges for consumers on cholesterol medication and other drugs. This indictment marks the highest-profile action in an ongoing investigation into the generic-drug industry.

title: GSK presents promising phase 2a data for chronic hepatitis B treatment
summary: GSK announced promising Phase 2a data for its investigational antisense oligonucleotide, GSK3228836, for chronic hepatitis B. The data showed significant reductions in hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and hepatitis B virus DNA after four weeks of treatment in both NA-treated and NA-naïve patients. This marks a potential step towards achieving a functional cure for the 260 million people globally affected by chronic hepatitis B, with a Phase 2b program expected to start by the end of 2020.

title: China approves Sinovac's COVID-19 vaccine candidate for emergency use | Daily Sabah
summary: China has approved Sinovac Biotech Ltd.'s coronavirus vaccine candidate, CoronaVac, for emergency use as part of a program to vaccinate high-risk groups. Another state-owned pharmaceutical giant, China National Biotec Group (CNBG), also secured emergency use approval for one of its vaccine candidates. These approvals are part of China's strategy to prevent possible outbreaks during autumn and winter, although specifics on deployment remain scarce.

title: What Dow Changes Mean For ETF Investors
summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) is undergoing a significant shakeup, with Exxon, Pfizer, and Raytheon Technologies being replaced by Salesforce, Amgen, and Honeywell. These changes are designed to diversify the index and better reflect the American economy, particularly after Apple's stock split impacted the technology sector's weighting. For ETF investors tracking the DJIA, such as through DIA, these adjustments will inevitably alter portfolio returns and exposure.

title: Amgen Joins Dow Jones Industrial Average as the Benchmark Index Revamps to ‘Better Reflect’ the U.S. Economy
summary: Amgen, Salesforce, and Honeywell have been added to the Dow Jones Industrial Average, replacing Pfizer, Exxon Mobil, and Raytheon Technologies. This revamp aims to better reflect the U.S. economy's shift towards innovative technologies. Amgen's inclusion marks the first biotech stock in the index, highlighting the growing significance of the biotech industry.

title: ANALYSIS - WPP's path out of the pandemic
summary: WPP, the world's largest advertising company, has outlined a strategy for prosperity after what it believes was the economic low point of the pandemic. Despite an 11.5% fall in first-half revenue, WPP announced a dividend to shareholders, signaling confidence in its performance. CEO Mark Read highlighted accelerated digital transformation, the rise of e-commerce, and increased focus on ESG issues as key trends shaping the industry and WPP's future approach.

title: Novo launches type 2 diabetes pill in UK after NICE waives review
summary: Novo Nordisk has launched Rybelsus (semaglutide), its oral type 2 diabetes treatment, in the UK after NICE waived a review, allowing direct negotiations for its inclusion in NHS formularies. The drug offers an alternative to injectable GLP-1 therapies, with clinical data demonstrating superior blood sugar reduction and consistent weight loss compared to existing treatments. This move addresses issues of patient adherence and injection-related barriers reported by UK GPs, potentially easing prescription and adoption.

title: Oak Grove Technologies Awarded Role-Player Training Contract at U.S. Special Operations Command
summary: Oak Grove Technologies LLC received a $10.5 million ceiling increase modification to a contract for role-player training support to the U.S. Special Operations Command (USSOCOM) Army component. This modification raises the contract ceiling to over $24.8 million and extends the performance period by six months, with work expected to be completed by February 2021 at Fort Bragg, North Carolina. The article also details numerous other significant defense contracts awarded to various companies by the Navy, Army, Defense Logistics Agency, U.S. Transportation Command, Air Force, and Missile Defense Agency.

title: Bridgewest Australia Holdings LLC Acquires Pfizer manufacturing facility in Adelaide, Australia
summary: The Bridgewest Group, through its subsidiary Bridgewest Australia Holdings LLC, has acquired Pfizer's biologics manufacturing facility in Adelaide, Australia. Pfizer will operate the facility under a leaseback arrangement until Q3 2021 before Bridgewest assumes full operational control. Bridgewest plans to invest in expanding the facility's capabilities to become a full-service Contract Development and Manufacturing Organization (CDMO), including mammalian cell production, cell and gene therapy, and microbial/vaccine production.

title: CDC tells states: Be ready to distribute vaccines on Nov. 1
summary: The CDC has instructed states to prepare for coronavirus vaccine distribution by November 1st, raising concerns among public health experts about potential political influence on vaccine approval before the presidential election. McKesson Corp. is contracted to distribute vaccines, and states are asked to expedite facility applications and consider waiving requirements to meet the aggressive timeline. Many experts doubt adequate safety and efficacy data will be available by then, highlighting a "credibility gap" despite the urgent need for a safe and effective vaccine.

title: Fighting a war on two fronts: ImmunityBio targets cancer and COVID-19
summary: ImmunityBio is employing its second-generation human adenovirus 5 vaccine platform, initially developed for advanced cancer treatment, to also combat COVID-19. The company's hAd5 platform overcomes limitations of earlier adenovirus vaccines, allowing for effective vaccination even with pre-existing immunity and enabling the expression of multiple antigens. ImmunityBio has developed two hAd5–SARS-CoV-2 vaccine constructs, with an investigational new drug application submitted for phase 1 trials expected to begin in June 2020.

title: Dr Reddys unveils Methylphenidate Hydrochloride ER Tablets in US
summary: Dr. Reddy's Laboratories Ltd. has launched Methylphenidate Hydrochloride Extended-Release Tablets USP, a generic version of Concerta, in the U.S. market. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (USFDA) approved the drug, which is indicated for the treatment of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). The market for Concerta and its generics had U.S. sales of approximately USD 1.159 billion in the twelve months ending June 2020.

title: Covid-19 Vaccine Race Turns Deep Freezers Into a Hot Commodity
summary: The distribution of Covid-19 vaccines depends heavily on the availability of specialized deep freezers capable of maintaining extremely low temperatures, as some experimental vaccines require storage at minus 80 degrees Celsius. This need is creating a supply chain challenge for drug, logistics, and public-health officials.

title: Top 10 Cord Blood Banking Companies Worldwide
summary: This article identifies and describes the top 10 cord blood banking companies globally, based on criteria such as units stored, company size and age, and technological innovation. It provides detailed profiles of each company, highlighting their key achievements, market position, and unique characteristics. The list serves as a guide for understanding the leaders and standards within the cord blood industry.

title: Commodity of Doom | Andrew Marzoni
summary: This article explores the complex cultural, political, and social history of smoking, moving beyond a simple public health narrative. It delves into the symbolism of the cigarette in literature and film, the motivations behind quitting, and how the anti-smoking movement intertwined with broader political and economic shifts. The piece ultimately frames smoking as a profound human condition, reflecting various facets of modern society, from agriculture and labor to capitalism and individual identity.

title: Merck takes aim at Pfizer with pneumonia vaccine data
summary: Merck announced that its experimental pneumonia vaccine, V114, showed an immune response comparable to Pfizer's Prevnar 13, and even outperformed it on certain strains. This puts Merck in direct competition with Pfizer in the lucrative pneumococcal vaccine market. Both companies are developing next-generation vaccines to cover more bacterial strains not addressed by current market offerings.

title: AstraZeneca Vaccine Tests Face Delay After Patient Gets Ill
summary: AstraZeneca has paused its experimental coronavirus vaccine trial after a participant developed an unexplained illness. This halt is part of a standard review process to ensure safety and maintain trial integrity. The incident led to a temporary dip in AstraZeneca's shares, though investors largely viewed it as a common occurrence in drug testing.

title: -EU enters final talks for BioNTech-Pfizer vaccine
summary: The European Commission has entered final talks with BioNTech-Pfizer to purchase up to 300 million doses of a potential COVID-19 vaccine. This agreement would be the sixth advance purchase agreement for the EU and the largest initial order for Pfizer and BioNTech, with initial deliveries expected by the end of 2020. The vaccine, based on messenger RNA (mRNA) technology, aims to prompt an immune response against the virus.

title: Pfizer and BioNTech may supply EU with 200 million doses of COVID-119 vaccine
summary: Pfizer and BioNTech have concluded exploratory talks with the European Commission to supply 200 million doses of their investigational BNT162 mRNA-based COVID-19 vaccine candidate to EU Member States, with an option for an additional 100 million doses. Deliveries could begin before the end of 2020, pending clinical success and regulatory authorization. The vaccine would be produced in BioNTech's German sites and Pfizer's Belgian site, and the companies are also interested in supplying the COVAX Facility.

title: Discovery of PF-06835919: A Potent Inhibitor of Ketohexokinase (KHK) for the Treatment of Metabolic Disorders Driven by the Overconsumption of Fructose | Journal of Medicinal Chemistry
summary: This article reports the discovery of PF-06835919, a potent, first-in-class inhibitor of Ketohexokinase (KHK), currently in Phase 2 clinical trials. The inhibitor aims to treat metabolic disorders like nonalcoholic fatty liver disease and insulin resistance, which are driven by excessive fructose consumption. Its development leveraged a fragment-derived lead and an optimized binding mode targeting the Arg-108 residue.

title: Pfizer CEO: Company refused taxpayer money for COVID-19 vaccine development to 'liberate our scientists'
summary: Pfizer CEO Albert Bourla explained his company's decision to refuse U.S. taxpayer money for its COVID-19 vaccine development. He stated this choice was made to "liberate our scientists from any bureaucracy" and political influence, emphasizing the goal to focus solely on scientific challenges. Bourla also mentioned the possibility of federal approval for their vaccine candidate before the end of the year.

title: Pfizer says coronavirus vaccine study still on track for October readout
summary: Pfizer announced that its late-stage coronavirus vaccine study is still expected to yield initial results by the end of October, despite a slowing infection rate in the U.S. The company has enrolled over 29,000 participants, with 12,000 having received the second dose, and has requested to expand the trial to 44,000 participants. Pfizer also disclosed that reported side effects have been generally mild to moderate, and an independent study committee has not recommended pausing the trial, unlike AstraZeneca's vaccine study which was temporarily halted due to an unexplained illness.

title: Our Ultimate Stock Pickers' Top 10 Dividend-Yielding Stocks
summary: This article identifies the top 10 dividend-yielding stocks from Morningstar's Ultimate Stock Pickers, emphasizing undervalued companies with strong competitive advantages and sustainable dividends. It highlights companies like Pfizer, Cisco Systems, PepsiCo, and BNY Mellon, detailing their financial health, market position, and reasons for inclusion. The analysis aims to help investors find quality businesses trading at attractive prices amidst market recovery.

title: Experimental COVID-19 Drug Shows Promise in Preliminary Cell Research
summary: A preliminary study on human cells by NYU Grossman School of Medicine and Pfizer suggests that the antiviral drug candidate PF-00835231 may be as effective as, or more potent than, remdesivir in blocking SARS-CoV-2 reproduction. The drug targets the viral enzyme 3CL pro, a different mechanism from remdesivir, suggesting potential for combined therapy. This early research, while promising, requires confirmation through human clinical studies.

title: Lebrikizumab rapidly improves quality of life
summary: Lebrikizumab, an IL-13 inhibitor, demonstrated rapid and dose-dependent improvements in atopic dermatitis (AD) symptoms and quality of life in phase 2b trials. Patients experienced significant reductions in Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) scores and pruritus, with improvements seen as early as day two. The drug, developed by Eli Lilly and Company, specifically targets IL-13, suggesting its central role in AD pathophysiology.

title: Injectable Drugs: CDMOs/CMOs and Suppliers Expand
summary: The demand for injectable drugs is increasing due to the rise of biologic-based drug development and complex APIs, making injectable delivery a preferred method. In response, Contract Development and Manufacturing Organizations (CDMOs), Contract Manufacturing Organizations (CMOs), and other suppliers are expanding manufacturing capacities and advancing technologies. This article details numerous expansions and technology advancements by key players in the industry throughout 2020.

title: Dr Reddy's ties up for Russian vaccine
summary: Dr. Reddy's Laboratories has partnered with the Russian Direct Investment Fund (RDIF) to conduct clinical trials for the Sputnik V vaccine in India and distribute 100 million doses once approved. This collaboration comes as India faces a rapidly rising number of COVID-19 cases. While Dr. Reddy's will handle distribution, RDIF is also seeking an Indian manufacturing partner for the vaccine.

title: After win at patent office, Bristol Myers inks Revlimid deal with Dr. Reddy's
summary: Bristol Myers Squibb has reached a patent settlement with Dr. Reddy's Laboratories regarding its top-selling cancer drug, Revlimid. This agreement allows Dr. Reddy's to launch a "volume-limited" generic version sometime after March 2022, with an unlimited license starting January 31, 2026. This deal follows similar agreements with Natco Pharma and Alvogen, as BMS continues to manage the looming generics assault on Revlimid.

title: Bristol Myers' Opdivo with Exelixis drug cuts kidney cancer death risk -study
summary: A late-stage study reveals that Bristol Myers Squibb's Opdivo, in combination with Exelixis's Cabometyx, reduced the risk of death by 40% in previously untreated patients with advanced kidney cancer. The drug combination also doubled patients' median progression-free survival compared to traditional chemotherapy. This promising data could significantly boost Opdivo's sales, which have lagged behind competitors in recent years.

title: With Eli Lilly data, another drug emerges to stop breast cancers from returning
summary: Eli Lilly's drug Verzenio, in combination with standard hormone therapy, has shown promising results in a Phase 3 trial for preventing the recurrence of early-stage, hormone-positive breast cancer. The MONARCHe trial found that patients on Verzenio were 25% less likely to see their cancers return, significantly impacting a patient population where recurrence remains a challenge. Despite potential side effects and high cost, the drug's effectiveness, especially in high-risk patients, marks a significant advance in adjuvant breast cancer treatment.

title: EPO destroys Teva copaxone patent after appeal
summary: The European Patent Office (EPO) has destroyed a patent licensed to Teva for its multiple sclerosis drug, Copaxone, due to a lack of inventive step after an appeal by generics manufacturers. This reversal of an earlier EPO decision means that Mylan is now free to release its generic product Clift to market once listed by the IFA. Three related divisional patents remain active and are subject to ongoing opposition proceedings.

title: Vivet Therapeutics and Pfizer Inc. Enter into Manufacturing Agreement for Vivet’s Investigational Gene Therapy for Wilson Disease
summary: Vivet Therapeutics and Pfizer Inc. have announced a manufacturing agreement for Vivet’s investigational gene therapy, VTX-801, for Wilson disease. Pfizer will supply VTX-801 for a Phase 1/2 clinical trial expected to begin in early 2021. This agreement follows Pfizer's 2019 minority equity investment in Vivet and an option to acquire the company, further solidifying their collaboration on gene therapy development.

title: As Johnson & Johnson kick-starts phase 3 COVID-19 test, early data show up its promise
summary: Johnson & Johnson has revealed promising phase 1/2 trial data for its COVID-19 vaccine candidate, Ad26.COV2.S, which has now entered late-stage testing. The data suggest a single dose can elicit strong immune responses and neutralizing antibodies. This early success supports J&J's strategy for a single-shot vaccine, potentially simplifying logistics and accelerating global vaccination efforts against the pandemic.

title: Operation Warp Speed’s Big Vaccine Contracts Could Stay Secret
summary: Operation Warp Speed has routed over $6 billion in vaccine funding through Advanced Technologies International, Inc., a defense contract management firm, instead of directly contracting with vaccine makers. This use of a third party means that the contracts between ATI and pharmaceutical companies like Novavax, Pfizer, Sanofi, and Johnson & Johnson may not be accessible through public records requests, and detailed documents could remain secret for five years. This opaque contracting method has drawn scrutiny from the Senate, with senators expressing concerns about accountability, selection criteria for vaccine candidates, and potential conflicts of interest.

title: Thessaloniki Native, Pfizer CEO Albert Bourlas Says Coronavirus Vaccine Progressing
summary: Pfizer CEO Albert Bourlas, a Thessaloniki native, is leading the company's efforts to develop a coronavirus vaccine. He emphasized that Pfizer is prioritizing scientific rigor over speed, stating that "the only rival here is the virus." Bourlas believes there is a 60% chance of determining the vaccine's safety and effectiveness by the end of October and stressed that vaccine skepticism could endanger others.

title: Biopharma Firm Zai Lab Raises $825 Million in Hong Kong IPO
summary: Chinese biopharmaceutical company Zai Lab Ltd. raised $825 million in a secondary listing on the Hong Kong stock exchange, with shares rising after their debut. The company aims to focus on patients in China and attract Asian investors, in addition to considering a listing on Shanghai's STAR Market. This move is part of a trend of U.S.-listed Chinese companies seeking listings closer to home amid rising U.S.-China tensions and increased scrutiny.

title: LifeSci Acquisition Corp. Announces Merger Agreement with Vincera Pharma, Inc. to Create New Publicly Listed Oncology Company
summary: LifeSci Acquisition Corp. (LSAC) announced a definitive merger agreement with Vincera Pharma, Inc., a biopharmaceutical company focused on oncology therapeutics. The combined company, to be renamed Vincera Pharma, Inc., is expected to have approximately $60 million in cash at closing and will be listed on The Nasdaq Capital Market under the ticker symbol "VINC." This merger aims to accelerate Vincera's pipeline growth, which includes a clinical-stage PTEFb/CDK9 inhibitor licensed from Bayer, and strengthen its position as a publicly listed company.

title: EMERGENT BioSolutions Inc.: A Lodestone Amongst Pebbles—Addressing Public Health Through Vaccines
summary: Emergent BioSolutions Inc. has built a 20-year reputation on enhancing and protecting public health through the delivery of solutions for public health threats, evolving into a leader in specialty vaccine and therapeutic technology and development. They partner with the U.S. Government on medical countermeasures and have expanded into addressing the opioid crisis and travel health. Emergent BioSolutions leverages its expertise in vaccine development and hyperimmune platforms with the goal of protecting and enhancing one billion lives by 2030.

title: 9 Drug Companies Pledge to ‘Stand With Science’ on Coronavirus Vaccines (Published 2020)
summary: Nine pharmaceutical companies issued a joint pledge to "stand with science" regarding coronavirus vaccines, promising thorough vetting for safety and efficacy before release. This move aims to restore public trust amid concerns that President Trump is politicizing the vaccine development process by suggesting a vaccine could be available before Election Day. The companies vowed to base decisions on large, high-quality clinical trials and adhere to regulatory guidance.

title: Moderna, Regeneron COVID-19 Candidates Show Early Positive Data
summary: Moderna and Regeneron Pharmaceuticals both reported positive preliminary results for their COVID-19 therapeutic candidates. Moderna's mRNA-1273 vaccine candidate showed dose-dependent binding antibody responses in older adults, while Regeneron's REGN-COV2 antibody cocktail rapidly reduced viral load and alleviated symptoms in non-hospitalized COVID-19 patients, particularly those who had not mounted their own immune response. Both companies are continuing with advanced clinical trials for their respective treatments.

title: Healthcare Roundup – Aptorum Group raises $9M in public offering, Pfizer inks deal with CStone
summary: This healthcare roundup covers several key developments: Aptorum Group's $9M public offering, Pfizer's $200M equity investment in CStone Pharmaceuticals for oncology assets in China, and Moderna's COVID-19 vaccine showing a strong immune response in older adults. Additionally, it notes Inovio's stock decline due to a clinical hold, and Novacyt securing a new contract for COVID-19 testing gear in the U.K.

title: for clinical monitoring of treatment response in migalastat-treated patients with Fabry disease
summary: This article assesses the utility of plasma globotriaosylsphingosine (lyso-Gb3) for monitoring treatment response in Fabry disease patients treated with migalastat. The study found no significant correlations between changes in lyso-Gb3 and clinical measures of disease progression like left ventricular mass index (LVMi), estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), or pain, nor did lyso-Gb3 levels predict Fabry-associated clinical events (FACEs). While lyso-Gb3 serves as a pharmacodynamic biomarker, the findings suggest it may not be a suitable prognostic biomarker for clinical monitoring in migalastat-treated patients.

title: COVID-19 Vaccine Timeline Is Caught In “Crucible” Of US Presidential Election - Pfizer CEO Protests
summary: Pfizer CEO Albert Bourla has criticized the politicization of the COVID-19 vaccine approval timeline by US President Donald Trump, asserting that Pfizer is operating "at the speed of science" and will not yield to political pressure. He emphasized that the amplified political rhetoric undermines public confidence in the vaccine, which is crucial for its acceptance. Separately, a new global laboratory network is being established to rigorously compare various COVID-19 vaccine candidates, and the European Medicines Agency is investigating reports of acute kidney injuries in patients treated with Gilead's Remdesivir.

title: Gilead Sciences Settles Medicare Kickbacks Claims with DOJ for $97M
summary: Gilead Sciences has agreed to pay $97 million to settle allegations from the U.S. Department of Justice that the company violated the False Claims Act by receiving Medicare kickbacks. The settlement addresses claims that Gilead used a 501(c)(3) foundation, Caring Voice Coalition (CVC), to unlawfully cover co-pays for its pulmonary arterial hypertension drug, Letairis. This action allegedly induced patients to purchase the drug and undermined Medicare's co-pay structure, which is designed to guard against inflated drug prices.

title: Trump COVID-19 treatment: President had stakes in Regeneron and Gilead, makers of antibody cocktail, Remdesivir
summary: President Trump previously held capital gains in Regeneron Pharmaceuticals and Gilead Sciences Inc., the manufacturers of two medicines used in his COVID-19 treatment. A 2017 financial disclosure form showed capital gains from both companies, though subsequent forms did not list these holdings. The article also touches on the experimental nature of Regeneron's treatment and Trump's continued stake in the maker of hydroxychloroquine.

title: With a sweetened offer, BridgeBio plans to reel in a subsidiary
summary: BridgeBio Pharma is making a second attempt to fully acquire its former subsidiary, Eidos Therapeutics, with a sweetened offer. The deal would give BridgeBio control over acoramidis, a drug for transthyretin amyloidosis which could compete with Pfizer and Alnylam. This acquisition would integrate a late-stage program into BridgeBio's pipeline and streamline the development and commercialization of acoramidis, a potential best-in-class drug for both ATTR-related nerve damage and cardiomyopathy.

title: Regeneron antibody cocktail used by Trump faces patent suit
summary: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals is being sued by Allele Biotechnology and Pharmaceuticals for alleged unauthorized use of Allele’s patented fluorescent protein, mNeonGreen, in developing its COVID-19 antibody cocktail. Allele is seeking royalties, claiming their technology was crucial for the rapid development and testing of the treatment and other vaccine candidates. A similar lawsuit has been filed against Pfizer and BioNTech.

title: CollPlant and United Therapeutics accelerate kidney bioprinting
summary: CollPlant Biotechnologies and United Therapeutics Corporation have expanded their partnership to accelerate human kidney bioprinting using CollPlant's rhCollagen-based bioink. United Therapeutics invested $3 million to advance the development of this bioink, which offers superior properties for bioprinting due to its human collagen content derived from genetically modified tobacco plants, avoiding animal or cadaver sources. This collaboration is part of a broader effort to address the critical shortage of organs for transplant by enabling the 3D printing of functional organs.

title: Pfizer preps Kalamazoo plant for COVID-19 vaccine approval
summary: Pfizer is preparing its Kalamazoo manufacturing facility for potential federal approval of its COVID-19 vaccine, with clinical trial data expected by late October. The company has invested $87 million to reconfigure the plant for vaccine production and anticipates making millions of doses by year-end if approved. The article also discusses the mRNA technology used by Pfizer and Moderna, and challenges including potential virus mutations and the scientific community's call for more extensive safety monitoring.

title: Regeneron, Pfizer and BioNTech Accused of Infringing Allele Patent in Connection with COVID-19 Technologies
summary: Allele Biotechnology and Pharmaceuticals, Inc. has filed patent infringement lawsuits against Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc., Pfizer, Inc., and BioNTech SE, alleging unauthorized use of its mNeonGreen fluorescent protein technology. The lawsuits claim that mNeonGreen, protected by U.S. Patent No. 10,221,221, was used by these companies in the development and testing of COVID-19 related technologies, including Regeneron's antibody cocktail and Pfizer and BioNTech's BNT162 vaccine candidate. Allele is seeking judgments of willful infringement, damages, and trebled damages for the alleged unauthorized use of its patented technology.

title: Trump’s endorsement sends Regeneron and Eli Lilly stocks rising
summary: Shares of Regeneron and Eli Lilly rose after President Trump publicly praised their experimental antibody treatments for COVID-19 and expressed a desire for their emergency approval and free distribution. Trump attributed his rapid recovery from coronavirus to Regeneron's drug, though his claims about it being a "cure" were misleading as it is a therapeutic, not a cure, and is still experimental. Both companies are seeking emergency authorization for their treatments, and Eli Lilly is also collaborating with the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation to make its treatments accessible globally.

title: Moderna Makes Milestone Pledge To "Not Enforce Our Patents" On COVID-19 Vaccine Technologies During Pandemic & Issue Open Licenses Afterward
summary: Moderna announced it would not enforce its COVID-19-related patents against other companies during the pandemic and would license its intellectual property for the post-pandemic period. This move was praised by some advocates as a model for other pharmaceutical companies but also drew skepticism, with critics suggesting it was influenced by legal challenges and consumer pressure. The company plans to submit its vaccine candidate to the FDA by November 25, 2020, for emergency use authorization.

title: Pfizer's breast cancer drug Ibrance fails late-stage study
summary: Pfizer's cancer drug Ibrance failed to meet its main goal in a late-stage trial for early-stage breast cancer, marking a setback for the company's efforts to expand the drug's use. This positions Eli Lilly's Verzenio as the leading treatment in the adjuvant space for early breast cancer, as Verzenio successfully met its trial goals for reducing recurrence risk. Pfizer's stock remained flat, while Lilly's shares rose after the news.

title: Once-Weekly Somatrogon Reduces Treatment Burden in Children With GHD
summary: A phase 3 study conducted by Pfizer and OPKO Health demonstrated that once-weekly somatrogon significantly reduces treatment burden for children aged 3 to 17 years with growth hormone deficiency (GHD) compared to daily somatropin injections. The study, C0311002, showed a favorable reduction in Life Interference total scores and overall improved treatment experience, with a comparable safety profile. These findings suggest somatrogon has the potential to improve adherence and patient preference if approved.

title: Bristol Myers Squibb's Zeposia boosts remission rates over placebo in ulcerative colitis patients
summary: Bristol Myers Squibb's Zeposia showed promising results in a Phase 3 study for ulcerative colitis, achieving clinical remission in 18.4% of patients at 10 weeks compared to placebo, and maintaining remission in 37% at one year. While effective, its benefit was less pronounced in patients previously treated with anti-TNF inhibitors. Bristol Myers Squibb is considering a filing for ulcerative colitis and is also pursuing an indication for Crohn's disease, with Zeposia already approved for multiple sclerosis.

title: Johnson & Johnson suspends trial of potential coronavirus vaccine after participant becomes ill
summary: Johnson & Johnson has temporarily halted its advanced clinical trial for a potential coronavirus vaccine after a participant experienced an "unexplained illness." This announcement comes as two Bay Area health-care providers were preparing to enroll local participants and highlights the inherent risks in large-scale clinical studies. The company did not disclose details about the illness, citing privacy concerns, and noted that such adverse events are an expected part of clinical trials.

title: Johnson & Johnson pauses clinical trials for a Covid-19 vaccine over participant's illness
summary: Johnson & Johnson has temporarily halted its Covid-19 vaccine clinical trials after a participant developed an "unexplained" illness. This pause, in accordance with regulatory standards, is not uncommon in vaccine development and has been seen in other trials like AstraZeneca's. The company is currently investigating the participant's condition to determine if it's related to the experimental vaccine or the placebo.

title: Trial Set to Evaluate Palbociclib for Patients with Advanced Breast Cancer Using Signatera MRD Test
summary: Natera announced that its Signatera molecular residual disease (MRD) test will be used in the DARE study, a randomized, multicenter, phase 2 clinical trial evaluating palbociclib (Ibrance) for patients with HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer. The trial aims to enroll 100 MRD-positive patients to assess ctDNA-guided second-line adjuvant therapy and determine if early intervention based on Signatera's detection of molecular relapse can delay or avert clinical relapse. Signatera will be critical for patient enrollment eligibility and monitoring therapy effectiveness.

title: Precision BioSciences Appoints Alex Kelly as Chief Corporate Affairs Officer
summary: Precision BioSciences has appointed Alex Kelly as its new Chief Corporate Affairs Officer. In this role, Kelly will oversee investor relations and corporate communications, reporting directly to CEO Matt Kane. Kelly brings extensive experience from previous roles at Allergan and Actavis, where he managed corporate affairs and integration efforts for major mergers.

title: Dr Reddy’s potential cancer drug shows promise against Covid, gets nod for phase 3 trial
summary: Dr Reddy's Laboratories has been asked to conduct phase 3 clinical trials for its potential cancer drug, 2-Deoxy-D-Glucose oral powder (2-DG), after it showed efficacy against Covid-19 in phase 2 trials. Although the expert panel found the phase 2 sample size "inadequate" for market approval, it acknowledged the positive results. The drug works by inhibiting glucose supply to cells and was tested on 40 patients.

title: Sanofi reports positive animal test results for potential COVID-19 vaccine
summary: Sanofi and Translate Bio announced positive preclinical results for their experimental COVID-19 mRNA vaccine, MRT5500, showing a favorable immune response in mice and monkeys. Human clinical trials (Phase 1/2) are expected to begin in the fourth quarter to assess safety and dosage. This vaccine candidate utilizes messenger RNA technology, similar to others in development by companies like Moderna and Pfizer.

title: Pfizer CEO says 3rd week of November earliest it can seek coronavirus vaccine OK
summary: Pfizer Inc.'s CEO Albert Bourla announced that the company cannot seek emergency authorization for its COVID-19 vaccine before the third week of November, assuming all goes well. This timeline is due to the need for the vaccine to demonstrate both effectiveness and safety, specifically tracking participants for two months after their second dose to monitor for side effects. Moderna Inc., another leading contender, also projected a similar timeline, with initial limited doses expected to be available by year-end for healthcare workers.

title: Pfizer may seek US green light to use COVID vaccine in late Nov
summary: Pfizer announced that it may file for US authorization of its COVID-19 vaccine in late November, which would make it unlikely for a vaccine to be available before the US election. The company stated that while efficacy data might be available this month, safety data will not be ready until November at the earliest. This timeline has implications for controlling the pandemic and has sparked political commentary regarding the vaccine's availability.

title: Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma Market : Analysis By Product Type, Usage,
summary: This report from Data Bridge Market Research analyzes the global Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma market, forecasting significant growth between 2020 and 2027. It highlights market drivers, restraints, opportunities, and the competitive landscape, including key players like Merck & Co. Inc., Bristol-Myers Squibb Company, and Novartis AG. The report also addresses the impact of COVID-19 and provides geographical coverage.

title: Earliest US filing for COVID vaccine would be late November: Pfizer
summary: Pfizer announced that it expects to file for US authorization of its COVID-19 vaccine in late November, potentially making a vaccine available in the US by the end of the year. This timeline suggests a vaccine would not be available before the US election, contrary to President Trump's statements. The company awaits safety data from its 44,000-person clinical trial, which should be available next month, and will apply for Emergency Use Authorization soon after reaching the safety milestone in the third week of November.

title: Indian-American teen wins $25,000 for work on potential Covid-19 treatment
summary: A 14-year-old Indian-American girl, Anika Chebrolu, has won a $25,000 young scientist challenge for her discovery of a potential Covid-19 treatment. Her work involves using in-silico methodology to find a molecule that can selectively bind to the SARS-CoV-2 virus's Spike protein. Chebrolu hopes to further develop her findings with the help of scientists to create an actual cure for the virus.

title: Moderna Nears Finish Line For Enrollment In Phase 3 Coronavirus Vaccine Study
summary: Moderna is close to completing enrollment for its Phase 3 COVE study for a coronavirus vaccine, with 98.4% of the targeted 30,000 participants already enrolled. The company has seen an uptick in enrollment pace and expects the first interim analysis results to be available in November. Moderna is also pursuing regulatory submissions in the EU and Canada, with further updates expected during its Q3 earnings call on October 29.

title: Newport Hospitality Group, Inc. Selected to Manage Three Additional Hotels
summary: Newport Hospitality Group Inc. (Newport) has been chosen by Apple Hospitality REIT, Inc. to manage three additional hotels: the Courtyard by Marriott Philadelphia Great Valley/Malvern, the Courtyard by Marriott Philadelphia Valley Forge/Collegeville, and the Hampton Inn & Suites Jackson, TN. These new additions expand Newport's portfolio, with President Wayne West expressing confidence in their ability to excel under Newport's management. Newport Hospitality Group, based in Williamsburg, Virginia, specializes in managing select and full-service hotels across the Eastern United States.

title: Novartis Canada inaugure un centre d’innovation Biome à Montréal
summary: Novartis Pharmaceuticals Canada Inc. has launched the Novartis Canada Biome, an innovation hub in Montréal aimed at fostering disruption in healthcare through data and digital technologies. This hub, joining a global network, will collaborate with emerging tech companies and individuals, operating out of Mila, a prominent AI research institute. The initiative seeks to bridge digital technology with patient needs by converging data science, technology, and AI to develop innovative healthcare solutions.

title: Rectal Vaginal Fistula Treatment Market is Predicted to Register Highest Growth Value during 2020-2025 | J&J, GSK, Pfizer, Allergan, AbbVie, Novartis, Bayer, Roche, Eli Lilly, Sanofi
summary: A new report forecasts significant growth for the Global Rectal Vaginal Fistula Treatment Market between 2020 and 2025, driven by factors like increasing prevalence of pelvic cancer and Crohn’s disease. The study provides a SWOT analysis and profiles key industry players including Johnson & Johnson, GSK, Pfizer, and Novartis. North America is expected to lead this market's growth.

title: Anatomy of a deal: How MyoKardia got BMS to bump up its buyout to $13B
summary: This article details how MyoKardia negotiated with Bristol Myers Squibb to increase its acquisition price to $13.1 billion. Initially, MyoKardia was not seeking a buyout, but after BMS made an offer for $185 per share, MyoKardia's executives repeatedly pressed for a higher valuation, citing the company's standalone potential, eventually reaching $225 per share. The deal resulted in a significant premium for MyoKardia's shareholders and its leadership team.

title: Next in hunt for coronavirus vaccine: Testing shots in kids
summary: The global search for a COVID-19 vaccine for children is just beginning, raising concerns among U.S. pediatricians about the availability of a vaccine for young children by the next school year. While adults are more vulnerable, vaccinating children is crucial to ending the pandemic. Pfizer has started testing its vaccine in adolescents, with other companies like Moderna, Johnson & Johnson, and Novavax planning pediatric research later in the year, highlighting the need for age-specific trials to ensure safety and effectiveness.

title: Pfizer Sets Up Its ‘Biggest Ever’ Vaccination Distribution Campaign
summary: Pfizer Inc. is preparing for its largest-ever vaccine distribution effort to ship billions of Covid-19 vaccine doses globally. The company plans to use frozen boxes, cargo planes, and trucks as part of this mega logistics operation. In Kalamazoo, Mich., a major hub equipped with 350 large freezers has been established to handle millions of doses, with aims to deliver 100 million doses this year and 1.3 billion in 2021.

title: How Pfizer Partner BioNTech Became a Leader in Coronavirus Vaccine Race
summary: The article details how BioNTech, led by CEO Ugur Sahin, quickly pivoted from cancer research to developing a COVID-19 vaccine in early 2020, anticipating the global pandemic. Despite initial resistance from his board, Sahin and CMO Özlem Türeci pushed ahead, leading to a partnership with Pfizer. Nine months later, their vaccine candidate is nearing the end of clinical trials, positioning BioNTech as a front-runner in the race and significantly increasing its stock value.

title: Arixa Pharmaceuticals Announces Acquisition by Pfizer’s Hospital Business
summary: Arixa Pharmaceuticals announced its acquisition by Pfizer's Hospital Business. Pfizer will further develop Arixa's lead compound, ARX-1796, an oral prodrug of avibactam, which has the potential to be a novel oral beta-lactamase inhibitor + antibiotic combination for drug-resistant Gram-negative infections. This acquisition aims to provide an oral treatment option for conditions like complicated urinary tract infections, potentially reducing hospital stays.

title: Trump Sets Up Pharma Billionaires for Coronavirus Payday
summary: The article details how the Trump administration's funding for Regeneron's Covid-19 antibody treatment, used by Donald Trump, lacked affordability guarantees, potentially leading to high costs and limited access for most patients. It highlights that Regeneron received hundreds of millions in public funds, and executives profited from stock sales following positive news about the treatment, while concerns about transparency and public access remain. Critics argue that the government's contracting methods may have been designed to avoid oversight and public interest safeguards.

title: Pfizer not yet ready to release Covid-19 vaccine data from late-stage trial
summary: Pfizer Inc. announced on October 27, 2020, that it was not yet ready to release data from the late-stage trial of its Covid-19 vaccine candidate, despite earlier indications from its CEO that data could be available that month. The independent data monitoring board had not yet conducted interim efficacy analyses. The company also reported a 4.3% drop in third-quarter sales, attributed to increased competition for its pain drug Lyrica and reduced demand for other treatments during the pandemic.
