title: Pfizer Says Covid-19 Vaccine Late-Stage Trial Almost Fully Enrolled - WSJ
summary: Pfizer Inc. announced that its late-stage global trial for a Covid-19 vaccine is nearing full enrollment, with its CEO urging patience as researchers gather trial results. The drugmaker has not yet performed the initial review to determine the vaccine's safety and efficacy. This news comes as the pandemic has also impacted Pfizer's third-quarter sales.

title: Peripheral Neuropathy Treatment Market | Scope, Drivers, Trends and Challenges 2020-2024| Technavio
summary: The global peripheral neuropathy treatment market is projected to grow by $241.99 million between 2020 and 2024, driven by recent drug approvals and rising awareness of the condition. Asia was the largest market in 2019, with diabetic peripheral neuropathy being the leading type segment. Key vendors include Daiichi Sankyo, Eli Lilly, and Grunenthal GmbH.

title: 'It could really benefit the world': Teens and tweens volunteer for Covid-19 vaccine trials
summary: The article highlights the participation of teens and tweens in Covid-19 vaccine trials, emphasizing their motivation to contribute to science despite some initial nervousness. It features individuals like 12-year-old Abhinav and 16-year-old Katelyn Evans, who volunteered for Pfizer's trial, and discusses the safety protocols and the rationale behind including younger age groups in vaccine research. The piece also addresses skepticism from some parents about testing vaccines on children developed quickly, while experts assert the safety and necessity of these trials for understanding vaccine efficacy across all ages.

title: Eliquis partners BMS and Pfizer join the pharma crowd urging doctor visits during COVID-19
summary: Bristol Myers Squibb and Pfizer have launched a new campaign called "No Time to Wait" to encourage people to seek prompt medical attention for conditions like atrial fibrillation, deep vein thrombosis, and pulmonary embolism during the COVID-19 pandemic. The campaign, which includes TV ads featuring real doctors, aims to raise awareness of symptoms and address the significant drop in primary care visits observed during the pandemic. This initiative promotes their co-marketed anticoagulant, Eliquis, which saw sales of $4.8 billion in the first half of 2020.

title: Regeneron named top biopharma company to work for
summary: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc. has been named the top company to work for by Science magazine in its annual Top Employers Survey of the global biotech and pharmaceutical industry. The company has consistently ranked in the top two for the past decade, earning high marks for innovation, social responsibility, and employee loyalty. Regeneron's leadership highlighted the company's science-driven culture and rapid response to the COVID-19 pandemic as key factors in its success.

title: Bristol Myers bet pays off as psoriasis drug beats Amgen rival in study
summary: Bristol Myers Squibb's experimental psoriasis drug, deucravacitinib, demonstrated superior efficacy over Amgen's approved treatment Otezla and placebo in a late-stage study, causing Bristol Myers' shares to rise. Both deucravacitinib and Otezla are oral treatments, offering an advantage in a market dominated by injectable medicines. While detailed safety data are still pending, analysts project deucravacitinib could achieve peak sales of $2 billion by 2027, potentially challenging Otezla's market position.

title: Prevail and Alector Both Declare Victory in Year-Long Legal Battle
summary: Prevail Therapeutics and Alector both claimed victory following a year-long arbitration over Prevail CEO Asa Abeliovich's alleged breach of contract from his time with Alector. Prevail highlighted the rejection of claims that Abeliovich stole trade secrets, while Alector focused on the arbitrator's finding that Abeliovich destroyed documents. Despite both companies claiming a win, the arbitration concluded with Abeliovich ordered to pay damages for breach of contract and document destruction, though the financial impact is expected to be minor for both companies.

title: Hepatitis B Vaccines Market Will Showcase Neutral Impact During 2020-2024 | High Prevalence of Hepatitis B Globally to Boost Market Growth | Technavio
summary: The global Hepatitis B Vaccines Market is projected to grow by USD 524.00 million between 2020 and 2024, at a CAGR of over 4%, driven by the high prevalence of hepatitis B worldwide. Technavio's report provides a holistic market update, including size, forecast, trends, growth drivers, challenges, and vendor analysis, considering the impact of COVID-19. The study identifies rising awareness initiatives as a key driver for market growth in the coming years.

title: Report: Oxford chief says there’s ‘small chance’ COVID-19 vaccine is ready by Christmas
summary: The director of Oxford University's COVID-19 vaccine trial, Andrew Pollard, stated there's a "small chance" their vaccine, developed with AstraZeneca, could be ready for deployment by Christmas 2020. Pollard is optimistic about presenting trial results by year-end, despite a previous pause in the U.S. trial due to an unexplained illness. The Oxford-AstraZeneca candidate is considered a frontrunner among global vaccine efforts.

title: China quickly moving up the pharma innovation ladder
summary: China is rapidly advancing in pharmaceutical innovation, particularly in cancer therapeutics, evidenced by Chinese biopharmaceutical companies receiving FDA approvals and making significant R&D breakthroughs. This growth is driven by substantial investments, regulatory reforms, and an evolving innovation ecosystem that makes drug approvals faster and more efficient. Despite these advancements, a gap still exists between the domestic pharmaceutical industry and global leaders, indicating a need for continued reforms and optimization.

title: AstraZeneca chief says COVID vaccine on track for year end
summary: AstraZeneca's CEO, Pascal Soriot, stated that the company's COVID-19 vaccine is on track for large-scale vaccinations by year-end, possibly as early as December. He dismissed reports of delays, noting that recent infection surges have helped gather necessary clinical data. While test results are expected by year-end, Soriot emphasized that the efficacy and longevity of the vaccine still need to be confirmed.

title: COVID vaccine candidate is 90% effective, makers claim
summary: A COVID-19 vaccine jointly developed by German company BioNTech and US firm Pfizer has demonstrated 90% effectiveness in preventing infections during Phase III trials, marking a significant breakthrough. While experts and political leaders welcomed the news, caution was urged as the vaccine is not yet available and ongoing monitoring for safety and efficacy will be crucial. Production has already begun, with plans to deliver millions of doses globally by 2021.

title: FedEx readies COVID-19 vaccine delivery pipeline
summary: FedEx is preparing its global network to deliver millions of COVID-19 vaccine doses once they become available. Building on its experience with the H1N1 vaccine, the company has invested in cold-chain infrastructure and new tracking technology like SenseAware ID to ensure safe and timely delivery, especially considering the ultra-cold temperature requirements of some vaccines. FedEx anticipates that administration centers, rather than cold-chain logistics, will be the primary "pinch point" in the distribution process.

title: Zoom and other ‘stay-at-home’ stocks got crushed on the positive vaccine news
summary: Shares of "stay-at-home" stocks like Zoom, Amazon, and Netflix dropped significantly after positive news regarding a COVID-19 vaccine from Pfizer and BioNTech. Investors rotated out of these pandemic-benefiting companies and into those expected to gain from an economic reopening, such as banks and cruise lines.

title: Pfizer Says Experimental COVID-19 Vaccine Is More Than 90% Effective
summary: Pfizer announced that its experimental COVID-19 vaccine is more than 90% effective based on interim analysis of a study involving over 43,000 volunteers. This marks the first COVID-19 vaccine to exceed the FDA's minimum effectiveness threshold of 50%. While promising, more follow-up data is required before Pfizer can seek emergency use authorization from the FDA.

title: Pfizer says COVID-19 vaccine is looking 90 percent effective
summary: Pfizer announced that an early analysis of its COVID-19 vaccine data suggests it is 90% effective, putting the company on track for emergency-use approval from the FDA. This news was met with significant optimism in markets and by health experts like Dr. Anthony Fauci, though officials noted that further data is needed and initial supplies will be limited. The company funded its own testing and manufacturing, distinguishing it from other vaccine developers involved in Operation Warp Speed.

title: How Pfizer's St. Louis site is playing a key role developing Covid-19 vaccine candidate
summary: Pfizer's Chesterfield facility in St. Louis is a crucial U.S. manufacturing center for the Covid-19 vaccine and plays a key role in the early development steps. The site is one of three identified by Pfizer for vaccine production within the U.S.

title: Pfizer vaccine news 'as good as you could hope for'
summary: Pfizer announced that its COVID-19 vaccine appears to be at least 90% effective in an early analysis, a result widely celebrated by doctors and scientists as "extraordinary." While this early data is promising, experts caution that more safety data is needed, and the efficacy rate could change as the trial continues. The article also highlights Pfizer's independence from Operation Warp Speed funding for its research, which CEO Albert Bourla believes allowed the company to remain agile.

title: 'Great day for humanity': Pfizer says COVID-19 vaccine over 90% effective
summary: Pfizer announced that its experimental COVID-19 vaccine, developed with BioNTech, is over 90% effective, marking a significant milestone in the fight against the pandemic. This news caused world markets to surge, with particular gains for Pfizer and BioNTech stocks, and raised optimism for a return to normalcy, though questions remain about duration of protection and distribution. The companies plan to seek U.S. emergency authorization and project producing 1.3 billion doses in 2021.

title: Gold slides amid Pfizer’s hopeful COVID-19 vaccine news
summary: Gold prices plummeted below $1,900 an ounce following the announcement of Pfizer's COVID-19 vaccine showing over 90% effectiveness, sparking hopes for economic recovery and dimming prospects for further stimulus. This led to gold's biggest slide since August, as investors reacted to reduced needs for economic stimulus and a potential reopening of economies. Industrial metals, equities, and oil prices concurrently saw jumps, indicating a shift in investor sentiment.

title: Novavax on track to begin U.S. trial of COVID-19 vaccine this month
summary: Novavax announced it is on track to begin a delayed U.S.-based, late-stage study of its experimental COVID-19 vaccine, NVX-CoV2373, later this month, having received "fast-track" status from the FDA. The company expects data from this trial to support U.S. authorization and approval, even as other vaccine developers like Pfizer Inc. report positive initial data from their own trials. Novavax also updated on its Phase II trials in South Africa and the UK.

title: Hurra!! Bundesgericht in Kalifornien erklärt gentechnisch veränderten Lachs für rechtswidrig - VICTORY: Court blocks genetically engineered salmon
summary: A U.S. District Court in California ruled that the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) violated environmental laws in its approval of genetically engineered salmon, noting that the FDA failed to adequately analyze the environmental risks, including potential harm to endangered wild salmon populations. This decision is a significant victory for environmental and consumer organizations that have long opposed the "Frankenfish." The article highlights the controversy surrounding genetically modified salmon, the attempts by companies like AquaBounty to commercialize it, and the public's widespread opposition to unlabeled GMO food despite sales in places like Canada.

title: Coronavirus: Turkish Germans raise new Covid vaccine hopes
summary: A Turkish-German husband-and-wife team, founders of the German biotech firm BioNTech, have emerged as frontrunners in developing a Covid-19 vaccine. Their company, in partnership with Pfizer, announced that their vaccine is over 90% effective based on early Phase 3 trial results. This marks a significant achievement in rapid vaccine development, leveraging their expertise in mRNA technology previously used for cancer treatments.

title: CPPIB and partner TPG Capital double down on cruise industry
summary: The Canada Pension Plan Investment Board (CPPIB) and TPG Capital LP have invested an additional US$500-million into Viking Cruises Ltd., marking a doubling down on their previous 2016 investment. This capital injection aims to help the cruise operator recover and rebuild after the devastating impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, which forced Viking to suspend operations and incurred significant debt. Despite the industry's challenges and the specialized market of older customers, CPPIB expressed confidence in Viking's long-term value, especially following positive vaccine news.

title: Arcturus expects its COVID-19 vaccine to be ready by Q1 2021
summary: U.S. biotech firm Arcturus Therapeutics announced that it expects to begin distributing its COVID-19 vaccine candidate in the first quarter of next year, following promising early-stage trial results. The company has secured supply deals with Israel and Singapore and is rapidly preparing for later-stage trials. This announcement comes as Pfizer also reported high efficacy for its own vaccine, causing a sharp drop in Arcturus' shares despite positive analyst ratings for its candidate.

title: Eli Lilly's coronavirus antibody treatment will be needed even if there is a vaccine, CEO says
summary: Eli Lilly's CEO Dave Ricks stated that coronavirus antibody treatments will remain necessary even with the availability of a vaccine, due to some patients potentially not responding to vaccines or challenges in global vaccine distribution. The company's Covid-19 antibody treatment received emergency use authorization from the FDA, aiming to help non-hospitalized, high-risk patients. Ricks highlighted the importance of these therapies, especially in developing countries where vaccine storage and deployment may be difficult, and mentioned a successful study showing reduced hospitalizations for patients receiving Lilly's treatment.

title: Why Pfizer’s Covid-19 Vaccine Is Unlikely To Move The Needle For The Stock
summary: This article argues that Pfizer's highly effective Covid-19 vaccine is unlikely to significantly boost the company's stock due to factors like lower profitability compared to prescription drugs, shared profits with BioNTech, anticipated competition, and logistical challenges with storage. It also reviews other vaccine stock performance and development.

title: Pfizer COVID-19 vaccine "very promising" but has cold chain issues -WHO
summary: The WHO chief stated that Pfizer's COVID-19 vaccine is "very promising" and a vaccine is hoped for by year-end. However, the vaccine's requirement for ultra-cold storage at minus 70 degrees Celsius poses significant distribution challenges, particularly for regions with warmer climates and less developed infrastructure like Africa. Equitable distribution of vaccine doses remains a key concern for the United Nations agency.

title: Pfizer vaccine trial success signals breakthrough in pandemic battle
summary: Pfizer Inc. announced its experimental COVID-19 vaccine is over 90% effective based on initial trial results, marking a significant development in the fight against the pandemic. While regulatory approval and mass rollouts are not expected this year, the news sent global markets surging. The companies plan to seek U.S. emergency use authorization this month and hope to produce up to 50 million doses in 2020 and 1.3 billion in 2021.

title: Pfizer, BioNTech’s strong results give lift to other coronavirus vaccines
summary: The successful interim results from Pfizer and BioNTech's coronavirus vaccine trial, showing over 90% effectiveness, are boosting confidence in other vaccine candidates. This success validates the common strategy of targeting the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein. While Moderna is expected to be next with results, the article highlights the importance of T-cell response and ongoing trials from AstraZeneca and Johnson & Johnson in determining the broader success of other vaccine platforms.

title: What we know about Pfizer’s coronavirus vaccine distribution plan
summary: Pfizer and BioNTech are preparing their COVID-19 vaccine distribution plan, which will involve approximately 12 trucks and 20 planes daily, once regulatory approval is granted. They will work directly with DHL, FedEx, and UPS to ship frozen vials requiring dry ice directly to vaccination points, bypassing McKesson due to strict cold chain requirements. Pfizer plans to produce up to 50 million doses in 2020 and 1.3 billion in 2021, while managing raw material supply and manufacturing capacity.

title: Pfizer's COVID-19 vaccine looks impressive, but Sanofi, J&J and Novavax shots eye a logistics edge
summary: Pfizer's COVID-19 vaccine, while highly efficacious, faces significant distribution challenges due to its ultra-cold storage requirements and two-dose regimen. Competitors like Sanofi, Johnson & Johnson, and Novavax are developing vaccines that could offer a logistical advantage with more standard refrigeration needs and potentially single-dose options. The article highlights that these "later-to-market" vaccines might be better suited for a global vaccination effort, especially in regions with limited cold chain infrastructure.

title: Yelp CEO is encouraged by antitrust case against Google
summary: Yelp CEO Jeremy Stoppelman expressed encouragement regarding the U.S. antitrust case against Google, stating that it validates his long-held belief in Google's monopoly in internet search. Stoppelman alleges that Google abuses its dominant position by prioritizing its own content, harming competition and consumers. Despite initial pandemic-related challenges, Yelp reported better-than-expected sales in the third quarter and anticipates further improvement with a vaccine rollout.

title: These Penn scientists paved the way for the Pfizer COVID-19 vaccine
summary: The Pfizer and Moderna COVID-19 vaccines are based on messenger RNA technology developed by University of Pennsylvania scientists Drew Weissman and Katalin Karikó. Their breakthrough 15 years ago involved modifying mRNA to prevent harmful inflammatory responses, a crucial step for the successful development of RNA-based vaccines. This foundational research has been lauded as Nobel Prize-worthy and promises broader applications in treating various diseases beyond vaccines.

title: Novavax Posts Coronavirus Vaccine Contract That Government Didn't Disclose
summary: Novavax publicly released its $1.6 billion Operation Warp Speed contract for COVID-19 vaccine development, manufacturing, and supply, a deal the government had not previously disclosed. This contract, issued through a third party (Advanced Technology International), reveals terms not previously known and highlights concerns about transparency and taxpayer safeguards in federal vaccine agreements. Experts argue for greater public access to contract details and stronger protections regarding pricing and patent rights.

title: Pfizer CEO Sold Millions In Stock After Coronavirus Vaccine News, Raising Questions
summary: Pfizer CEO Albert Bourla sold $5.6 million worth of company stock on the same day Pfizer announced its coronavirus vaccine was over 90% effective, raising questions about the timing of his stock-trading plan. NPR found irregularities regarding when the CEO entered into this preset plan, specifically its adoption the day before a press release about vaccine progress. This incident brings to light broader concerns about executives using 10b5-1 plans around significant company announcements.

title: The COVID-19 vaccine challenge you might not have known about
summary: Pfizer's newly developed COVID-19 vaccine, shown to be 90% effective, presents a significant distribution challenge due to its requirement for ultra-cold storage at -70 to -80 degrees Celsius. Most hospitals lack this capacity, leading to concerns about spoilage and equitable access, especially in rural or less wealthy areas. While Pfizer is working on logistics, and some facilities are expanding cold storage, the issue highlights a major hurdle for widespread vaccine deployment.

title: Pfizer CEO made $5.6 million stock sale on same day as COVID-19 vaccine update: filing
summary: Pfizer CEO Albert Bourla sold $5.56 million worth of company shares on the same day the company announced its COVID-19 vaccine was 90% effective. The sale was part of a pre-established 10b5-1 plan authorized in August, allowing insiders to trade a predetermined number of shares at a predetermined time. Pfizer's stock saw a significant rise following the vaccine update.

title: Metagenomi closes USD 65 million Series A financing led by Leaps by Bayer and Humboldt Fund
summary: Metagenomi, a genomic medicines company, successfully closed a USD 65 million Series A financing round led by Leaps by Bayer and Humboldt Fund. The company, which specializes in precision gene editing systems, emerged from stealth mode and plans to use the capital to expand its gene editing systems for therapeutic use and advance its own pipeline. Metagenomi aims to improve patient access to gene editing technologies by developing safe and accurate modalities for therapeutic development.

title: Feds will partner with pharmacy chains to distribute future Covid-19 vaccines
summary: The U.S. government announced a partnership with pharmacy chains, including Safeway, to distribute future Covid-19 vaccines. This program aims to ensure widespread availability of vaccines, covering about 60% of pharmacies nationwide. Patients will not be charged for their doses.

title: Topgolf Acquisition Makes Sense, But Callaway Overpaid For a Company Over a Barrel
summary: Callaway Golf Co. (ELY) is acquiring the remaining 86% of Topgolf Entertainment Group at a valuation over $2 billion. While the acquisition offers significant synergies, particularly in custom fitting and apparel sales, analysts like Casey Alexander of Compass Point Research & Trading believe Callaway overpaid for a company in a compromised financial position due to COVID-19. Despite the high price, Alexander sees long-term potential for Callaway in the combined entity, especially after its share price drop made the deal more attractive.

title: Israel signs deal with Pfizer for potential COVID-19 vaccine
summary: Israel has signed a deal with Pfizer Inc. for 8 million doses of its potential COVID-19 vaccine, enough to inoculate close to half of Israel's population. The agreement is contingent on approval from the U.S. FDA and Israel's health ministry, with Pfizer expecting to apply for approval by the end of November. This deal follows Pfizer's announcement that its experimental vaccine is over 90% effective and complements Israel's existing agreement with Moderna Inc. for its vaccine candidate.

title: Focus: U.S. states race to buy ultra cold vaccine freezers, fueling supply worries
summary: U.S. states, cities, and hospitals are urgently acquiring ultra-cold freezers to store Pfizer's COVID-19 vaccine, despite CDC advice to hold off, revealing a significant infrastructure gap for a super cold vaccine campaign. This scramble is causing months-long waits for specialty freezers and highlights a lack of coordinated federal response, forcing states to compete for essential equipment. The situation is further complicated by the high cost of these freezers and the differing temperature requirements of other vaccine candidates like Moderna's.

title: Early Data Show Moderna’s Coronavirus Vaccine Is 94.5% Effective (Published 2020)
summary: Moderna announced its coronavirus vaccine is 94.5% effective based on early data, making it the second company, after Pfizer, to report promising results. Both companies plan to seek emergency authorization from the FDA soon, with initial vaccine doses expected by December for high-risk individuals. However, widespread public availability is still several months away, despite the urgent and escalating pandemic.

title: Pfizer and Moderna Give Investors a Shot of Hope
summary: Moderna announced its coronavirus vaccine is 94.5% effective, following Pfizer's earlier announcement of 90% effectiveness, leading to a rally in travel and hospitality stocks. Despite Pfizer's vaccine requiring ultra-cold storage, Moderna's can be stored in standard refrigerators. The news also positively impacted luxury stocks, with Bernard Arnault joining the centibillionaire club, and highlighted China's growing middle class and the ongoing home improvement boom.

title: Moderna’s COVID-19 vaccine is 94.5 percent effective, according to interim analysis
summary: Moderna announced that an interim analysis of its COVID-19 vaccine candidate, mRNA-1273, showed 94.5 percent efficacy in preventing COVID-19 in its Phase III COVE trial. The analysis, based on 95 cases, also indicated the vaccine was generally well tolerated with mostly mild to moderate adverse events. Moderna plans to seek Emergency Use Authorization from the US FDA and submit applications to global regulatory agencies soon.

title: Moderna says preliminary trial data shows its coronavirus vaccine is more than 94% effective, shares soar
summary: Moderna announced preliminary Phase 3 trial data indicating its coronavirus vaccine is over 94% effective in preventing Covid-19, leading to a significant jump in the company's shares. This news follows similar positive results from Pfizer's vaccine candidate, intensifying the global race for a Covid-19 vaccine. The company plans to apply for emergency use authorization from the FDA in the coming weeks and expects to have 20 million doses ready by year-end.

title: Moderna says its vaccine is 94.5% effective in preventing COVID-19
summary: Moderna announced its experimental COVID-19 vaccine is 94.5% effective based on interim clinical trial data, making it the second U.S. company with highly effective vaccine results. This development means the U.S. could have two authorized vaccines by December, with a key advantage for Moderna's being its less stringent cold storage requirements compared to Pfizer's vaccine. The trial data also showed Moderna's vaccine prevented severe COVID-19 cases, and the company expects to produce 20 million doses this year for the U.S.

title: Moderna says its COVID-19 vaccine is nearly 95 percent effective
summary: Moderna announced its COVID-19 vaccine is nearly 95 percent effective in preventing illness, including severe cases, based on preliminary results from its Phase III clinical trial. This news follows similar positive results from Pfizer and BioNTech, with both companies planning to seek emergency use authorization. The article highlights the mRNA technology used by both vaccines and discusses Moderna's vaccine stability at refrigerated temperatures.

title: Moderna’s Covid Vaccine Found 94.5% Effective in Early Analysis
summary: Moderna Inc. announced that its Covid-19 vaccine demonstrated 94.5% effectiveness in a preliminary analysis of its late-stage clinical trial. This positive development follows a similar announcement from Pfizer and BioNTech, indicating that new messenger RNA vaccine technology could soon help control the pandemic. Both vaccines show promise in preventing severe illness, offering hope to millions worldwide.

title: Early data on Moderna COVID-19 vaccine candidate shows 94.5% efficacy
summary: Moderna Inc. announced that early data shows its mRNA-1273 vaccine candidate for COVID-19 is 94.5% effective. A key advantage over the Pfizer candidate is its stability at standard refrigerator temperatures for up to 30 days. Moderna plans to produce 20 million doses by the end of 2020, with significantly more in 2021, and the U.S. has already purchased 100 million doses pending FDA approval.

title: VIEW Moderna says its vaccine is 94.5% effective in preventing COVID-19
summary: Moderna announced its experimental COVID-19 vaccine is 94.5% effective, making it the second U.S. company to report highly positive interim results. Experts praised the effectiveness and easier storage requirements compared to Pfizer's vaccine, emphasizing the need for multiple effective vaccines globally. Political and market reactions were largely positive, highlighting the significance of these developments in the fight against the pandemic.

title: Moderna’s top medical officer says Israel will be among first to get vaccine
summary: Moderna's chief medical officer, Israeli Dr. Tal Zaks, announced that Israel would be among the first countries to receive its coronavirus vaccine, with initial doses expected early next year. This follows the company's announcement of a 94.5% efficacy rate for its vaccine. Israel has reportedly purchased 1-2 million doses, and the government is working to secure vaccines from multiple sources.

title: Early data show Moderna's COVID vaccine 94.5% effective
summary: Moderna Inc. announced early data from a late-stage clinical trial showing its COVID-19 vaccine candidate is 94.5% effective, including preventing all severe cases in the vaccine group. This news follows Pfizer and BioNTech's announcement of their vaccine's 90% efficacy; both require two doses and cold storage. While promising, experts caution that widespread vaccination capable of significantly impacting the pandemic is still months away.

title: Moderna and Pfizer Reveal Secret Blueprints for Coronavirus Vaccine Trials (Published 2020)
summary: Moderna and Pfizer, two leading contenders in the race for a coronavirus vaccine, have released detailed blueprints of their vaccine trials. This rare move aims to build public trust amidst concerns that a vaccine could be rushed for political reasons. The disclosures outline how participants are selected, trial monitoring, conditions for early stoppage, and the criteria for determining vaccine effectiveness, with timelines suggesting results may extend into next year.

title: Berkshire Hathaway Invests in Four Large Drugmakers
summary: Berkshire Hathaway announced a significant investment of $5.7 billion into the pharmaceutical sector, acquiring stakes in four major drugmakers: Abbvie Inc., Bristol-Myers Squibb Co., Merck & Co., and Pfizer Inc. This move, disclosed in a regulatory filing, reflects a strategic shift towards healthcare, potentially influenced by the COVID-19 pandemic. Concurrently, Berkshire Hathaway also invested in T-Mobile US Inc. and divested holdings in Costco Wholesale Corp. and several banks.

title: GlaxoSmithKline Most Heavily Fined Drug Company
summary: A new study published in JAMA reveals that pharmaceutical companies paid over $30 billion in financial penalties for illegal activities between 2003 and 2016 in the United States. GlaxoSmithKline (GSK) was identified as the most heavily fined, paying nearly $9.8 billion across 27 cases for issues including bribery, improper marketing, and pricing violations. The study highlights that such fines often represent a small percentage of company revenues and that drug company executives rarely face prison time, raising questions about their deterrent effect.

title: Buffett's Berkshire bets big on AbbVie, Bristol Myers, Merck, Pfizer as COVID-19 drives healthcare investment
summary: Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway has significantly increased its investment in the biopharma sector, pouring over $5.66 billion into AbbVie, Bristol Myers Squibb, Merck & Co., and Pfizer during the third quarter. This move reflects the growing interest in healthcare investments driven by the COVID-19 pandemic, with global healthcare funding to private firms reaching record highs. Berkshire Hathaway also holds stakes in Biogen and Teva, though the latter's stock has been impacted by legal challenges and business performance issues.

title: After nearly 60 years, Mylan makes way for Viatris
summary: Mylan NV has officially transformed into Viatris (Nasdaq: VTRS) following its merger with Pfizer Inc.'s Upjohn division, a deal announced in July 2019. The new company is headquartered in the U.S. with major facilities in Canonsburg, Shanghai, and Hyderabad, and will no longer trade under Mylan's ticker symbol (Nasdaq: MYL). Viatris plans a restructuring program to save $1 billion, affecting its 45,000 employees.

title: Warren Buffett is going all in on the vaccine rally, piling into these stocks
summary: Warren Buffett’s Berkshire Hathaway Inc. has significantly invested in the pharmaceutical sector, including new stakes in Merck & Co., Pfizer Inc., AbbVie Inc., and Bristol-Myers Squibb Co., ahead of anticipated COVID-19 vaccine developments. Concurrently, Berkshire Hathaway has continued to reduce its investments in financial companies like Wells Fargo & Co. and JPMorgan Chase & Co. These strategic shifts indicate a strong bet on the potential of the vaccine rally while divesting from traditional financial holdings.

title: Viatris: A new kind of global healthcare company
summary: Viatris, a new global healthcare company formed by the combination of Mylan and Pfizer's Upjohn division, launched on November 17, 2020. The company aims to improve patient outcomes with a global portfolio of over 1,400 molecules, including branded medicines, generics, biosimilars, and OTC treatments. Viatris emphasizes access to high-quality medicines, sustainable operations, and strategic partnerships, focusing on major therapeutic areas and contributing to the WHO Essential Medicines List.

title: Pfizer and Moderna Covid vaccines 95% effective in clinical trials
summary: Pfizer and Moderna announced their experimental COVID-19 vaccines are approximately 95% effective, according to final analyses of their clinical trials. Both mRNA-based vaccines demonstrated strong efficacy across various demographics and are seeking emergency use authorization from the FDA. The article also discusses the storage challenges for these vaccines and the potential need for multiple vaccine options.

title: Novo Nordisk reports positive data from type 2 diabetes medicine trial
summary: Novo Nordisk has announced positive headline results from its Phase IIIb SUSTAIN FORTE trial for once-weekly semaglutide in type 2 diabetes patients. The trial showed that semaglutide 2mg achieved a statistically significant and superior reduction in HbA1c and body weight compared to the 1mg dose. Both doses were found to be safe and well-tolerated.

title: Pfizer Upjohn concludes merger with Mylan to create Viatris
summary: Pfizer Inc. has completed the transaction to spin off its Upjohn Business and combine it with Mylan N.V. to form Viatris Inc. This all-stock Reverse Morris Trust deal resulted in Pfizer stockholders owning approximately 57% and Mylan shareholders owning approximately 43% of the outstanding shares of Viatris common stock. Pfizer will issue its initial 2021 financial guidance in conjunction with its Q4 2020 earnings release.

title: Pfizer offers Brazil deal for millions of vaccine doses
summary: Pfizer has offered Brazil millions of COVID-19 vaccine doses for the first half of 2021, awaiting regulatory approval. This comes as Brazil experiences an accelerating rate of coronavirus infection. Brazil's Health Ministry met with Pfizer and plans to meet with other vaccine developers, while the country's health regulator, Anvisa, has streamlined its approval process for COVID-19 vaccines.

title: New Pfizer Results: Coronavirus Vaccine Is Safe and 95% Effective (Published 2020)
summary: Pfizer announced that its coronavirus vaccine is 95% effective and safe, with no serious side effects, based on complete late-stage trial results. The company, in partnership with BioNTech, plans to seek emergency authorization from the FDA "within days." This development offers significant hope for controlling the pandemic, with Pfizer aiming to produce up to 50 million doses by year-end and 1.3 billion by the end of next year if authorized.

title: ETF of the Week: iShares Russell 2000 ETF (IWM)
summary: The iShares Russell 2000 ETF (IWM) offers exposure to small-cap U.S. stocks and has seen increased interest due to vaccine prospects and potential economic recovery. Its recent performance outstripped large-cap counterparts, ending a long drought for the Russell 2000 index. The article highlights how IWM could benefit from a post-pandemic economic rebound, especially with increased fiscal spending and a potential shift towards cyclical companies.

title: Viatris Inc. Launches as a New Kind of Healthcare Company, Positioned to Meet the World’s Evolving Healthcare Needs
summary: Viatris Inc., formed from the combination of Mylan N.V. and Pfizer’s Upjohn business, officially launched to become a new global healthcare company. It aims to broaden access to high-quality medicines across more than 165 countries, leveraging its scientific, manufacturing, and distribution expertise. With a commitment to financial returns for shareholders and a focus on responsible operations, Viatris seeks to empower people worldwide to live healthier lives by connecting them to essential products and services.

title: New FMD Vaccine Enhances Safety and Accessibility
summary: The Pirbright Institute and its research partners have granted MSD Animal Health an exclusive commercial license for a new, effective, and affordable vaccine against foot-and-mouth disease (FMDV). This innovative vaccine, made of 'virus-like particles' (VLPs), is more stable than existing FMD vaccines, less reliant on a cold-chain for distribution, and can differentiate between vaccinated and infected animals, making it revolutionary for controlling the disease in endemic regions and preventing mass culling during outbreaks. The development promises significant economic and welfare benefits for livestock farmers globally.

title: SR One Completes GSK Spinout, Closes $500 Million Fund
summary: Venture capital firm SR One, formerly the venture capital arm of GlaxoSmithKline, has completed its spinout from the pharma giant and successfully closed its first independent fund at $500 million. This fund will be used to invest in elite biotechnology companies developing innovative medicines, with GSK remaining the largest contributor. The spinout enables SR One to scale its investment strategy and expand its team.

title: Moderna has never distributed a product before. A Swiss company is here to help
summary: Swiss company Lonza Group AG is assisting Moderna Inc. with the production and distribution of its COVID-19 vaccine candidate, as Moderna has no prior experience distributing products. Lonza has begun commercial batch production of the vaccine's main ingredient in the U.S. and plans to start European production soon, aiming for a capacity of 400 million doses annually. This partnership is crucial for the vaccine's rollout, given Moderna's new mRNA technology and lack of established distribution channels.

title: First Atlantic FCU chooses CEO; OceanFirst Bank names senior VP
summary: Ann Goldinak has been promoted to CEO of First Atlantic Federal Credit Union in Eatontown, having served as senior vice president and CFO for six years. Eric K. Mason has been appointed Senior Vice President and Commercial Lending Team Leader for OceanFirst Bank in northern New Jersey. Nicole E. French has been promoted to Regional Manager of Southern New Jersey for Preferred Home Health Care & Nursing Services.

title: Pfizer and BioNTech submit for EUA of COVID-19 vaccine with FDA
summary: Pfizer Inc. and BioNTech SE have applied to the US FDA for Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) for their mRNA COVID-19 vaccine candidate, BNT162b2. The submission is based on Phase III trial data showing 95% efficacy and good tolerability. If approved, high-risk individuals in the US could receive the vaccine by December 2020.

title: Lilly, Precision Biosciences team up on Duchenne gene therapy in $135M deal
summary: Eli Lilly is expanding its focus into gene therapy development, partnering with Precision BioSciences for in vivo gene therapies, starting with Duchenne muscular dystrophy. The deal includes $100 million upfront, a $35 million investment, and potential milestones up to $420 million per product, with a total potential value exceeding $2.6 billion if additional targets are pursued. This collaboration leverages Precision's ARCUS genome editing platform and marks a shift for Lilly, which previously expressed reservations about gene therapy for ultra-rare conditions.

title: Sinovac’s CoronaVac Trials Show Favorable Results
summary: Early clinical trials for Sinovac's COVID-19 vaccine candidate, CoronaVac, have shown promising results, indicating it safely induces an immune response in healthy volunteers within a month of vaccination. The inactivated virus vaccine exhibited mild side effects and a robust antibody response, particularly with a 28-day dosing interval. While antibody levels were lower than in recovered COVID-19 patients, CoronaVac offers an advantage in easy storage at standard refrigerator temperatures.

title: Biosimilars: US FDA Developing Guidance For First Interchangeable Exclusivity
summary: The US FDA is currently developing guidance for the first interchangeable biosimilar exclusivity. The first approved interchangeable biosimilar is entitled to one year of exclusivity. This guidance is one of several the FDA is working on related to interchangeability.

title: Israel nears deal for AstraZeneca's COVID-19 vaccine
summary: Israel is finalizing a deal with AstraZeneca for approximately 10 million doses of its experimental COVID-19 vaccine, with initial supplies expected in the first half of 2021 pending regulatory approvals. This agreement, along with existing deals with Pfizer and Moderna and talks with Russia, is part of Israel's broad strategy to secure coronavirus vaccines for its population. The AstraZeneca vaccine, developed with Oxford University, is likely a two-dose course, meaning 10 million doses would cover over half of Israel's 9 million citizens.

title: Worst-Case Scenario for Regeneron: What If Eylea Sales Slow Down by 2018?
summary: This article examines Regeneron Pharmaceuticals' heavy reliance on its key drug, Eylea, which recorded global sales of $4.1 billion in fiscal 2015. It discusses Eylea's approval history and sales growth expectations, with analysts projecting moderate growth after 2016 as the drug approaches its peak sales potential of $6 billion. The article also touches upon Eylea's competition and suggests investing in ETFs like SPDR S&P 500 ETF for diversified exposure.

title: Pfizer seeks US FDA approval for COVID-19 vaccine’s emergency use
summary: Pfizer has requested emergency use authorization from the US FDA for its COVID-19 vaccine, following trial results showing it to be 95 percent effective. This step could lead to limited vaccine distribution as early as next month, pending FDA review and subsequent decisions on allocation. The company and its German partner BioNTech are also pursuing similar applications in Europe and the UK.

title: FDA authorizes emergency use of the antibody cocktail given to Trump to treat Covid-19
summary: The US Food and Drug Administration issued an emergency use authorization for Regeneron’s antibody cocktail, REGEN-COV2, to treat Covid-19 in high-risk patients with mild to moderate disease. This treatment, previously given to President Donald Trump, aims to reduce Covid-19-related hospitalizations and emergency room visits. Regeneron anticipates an initial demand exceeding supply, making equitable distribution crucial, and expects to have doses for approximately 300,000 patients by the end of January 2021.

title: The Role of Nanoparticles in Drug Delivery
summary: This article discusses the crucial role of nanoparticles in advanced drug delivery systems, highlighting their ability to enhance bioavailability, targeting, and circulation time. It details various types of nanoparticles used in drug delivery, such as nanocrystals, polymeric micelles, and liposomes, and explains how instruments like the Nicomp DLS system are utilized for their characterization, particularly for size and zeta potential analysis. The content also covers process monitoring of nanoparticle manufacturing using online DLS systems to ensure quality and specification adherence.

title: COVID-19: FDA authorises Regeneron antibody drug given to Trump
summary: The US FDA has granted emergency-use authorisation for Regeneron Pharmaceuticals Inc’s COVID-19 antibody therapy, similar to the treatment given to President Donald Trump. This treatment, casirivimab and imdevimab, is intended for mild to moderate COVID-19 in adults and pediatric patients at risk of severe disease, but not for hospitalised patients or those requiring oxygen. Regeneron received over $500m from the US government for development, and the first 300,000 doses will be provided free, though administration costs may apply.

title: Moderna Chief Sells More Shares Ahead of Key Vaccine Filing
summary: Moderna CEO Stephane Bancel sold an additional $1.74 million in company shares last week ahead of the anticipated emergency use filing for their Covid-19 vaccine in the U.S. This sale comes as Moderna's stock reached new highs and follows Pfizer and BioNTech's vaccine submission. Analysts expect Moderna to file its vaccine for emergency use the following week.

title: Chinese-Made Covid-19 Vaccine May Be Available in Indonesia by January
summary: Indonesian authorities may grant emergency use authorization for Sinovac Biotech Ltd.'s Covid-19 vaccine candidate by late January, provided complete data on quality, safety, and efficacy is submitted. The head of Indonesia's Food and Drug Monitoring Agency noted that final stage trial data from Indonesia is expected in January 2021, and an efficacy rate of at least 50% is required. The initial plan for a November vaccination program was delayed due to insufficient data from phase three trials.

title: Omaha’s AMC Oakview Plaza 24 closes permanently
summary: AMC's Oakview Plaza 24 movie theater in Omaha has permanently closed its doors on November 8, after nearly 23 years of operation. The closure is a result of financial strains exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic, leading landlords to terminate leases with AMC. This specific theater is one of six nationwide affected by an agreement with landlord EPR Properties, though other AMC locations in the Omaha-Council Bluffs area remain open.

title: Former CEO of Norwalk’s Priceline checking out at Booking.com
summary: Jeff Boyd, the former CEO of Priceline and Booking Holdings, is retiring as chairman of Booking Holdings' board of directors. Boyd played a crucial role in transforming Priceline into the online travel giant it is today, notably through the $135 million acquisition of Booking.com and overseeing a 50-fold increase in company stock value. Under his leadership, Booking Holdings became Connecticut's most valuable dot-com company, with a market capitalization exceeding $82 billion.

title: TSX Extends Gains To 4th Straight Session, Ends More Than 1% Up
summary: The Canadian stock market's S&P/TSX Composite Index ended over 1% up, extending gains for the fourth straight session, driven by news of President-elect Joe Biden's transition in the U.S. and positive vaccine updates. Energy stocks, healthcare, consumer discretionary, and financials were among the top performers, while oil prices surged and gold prices fell. U.S. stocks also saw significant gains with the Dow closing above 30,000 for the first time.

title: Bintai Kinden eyes vaccine foray to cushion M&E volatility
summary: Bintai Kinden Corp Bhd is venturing into the healthcare sector, specifically the distribution of a Covid-19 vaccine, to diversify its income away from the volatile mechanical and electrical (M&E) engineering business. The company has secured exclusive distribution rights for a US-developed Covid-19 vaccine in Southeast Asia, with an option for other regions. This new segment is expected to contribute significantly to its future profits, despite the vaccine still being in pre-clinical trials.

title: Ford snaps up freezers to store COVID-19 vaccine for autoworkers
summary: Ford Motor Co. has ordered a dozen ultra-cold freezers to store Pfizer Inc.'s COVID-19 vaccine for its employees, mirroring efforts by states and cities to prepare for national vaccine rollout. These specialized freezers are necessary given the stringent temperature requirements of certain COVID-19 vaccines. While autoworkers are considered essential, they are not prioritized for early vaccine distribution, prompting Ford to take its own measures.

title: Novartis Snags Exclusive Rights from Mesoblast for MSC Therapy Against COVID-Induced ARDS
summary: Novartis has secured exclusive worldwide rights from Mesoblast to develop, commercialize, and manufacture remestemcel-L, a mesenchymal stromal cell (MSC) therapy, for acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), including that associated with COVID-19. The deal includes a $50 million upfront payment, comprising $25 million cash and $25 million in equity, plus future performance-based milestones and royalties. Remestemcel-L is currently in a Phase III study for COVID-19-related ARDS and has shown promising results in a compassionate use program with an 83% survival rate.

title: DGRO: This Dividend Growth Strategy Will Play Well In An Economic Recovery
summary: The iShares Core Dividend Growth ETF (DGRO) is poised to benefit from an economic recovery due to its value-oriented portfolio and overweighting in cyclical sectors like financials and industrials. Despite a modest 2% dividend yield, DGRO's strategy targets companies with sustainable dividend growth, making it a compelling long-term core holding. The article suggests that a post-COVID recovery could lead to outperformance for DGRO, especially with rising optimism around potential vaccines.

title: IGC Starts Phase 1 Alzheimer's Trial Testing Low-dose Cannabinoid
summary: India Globalization Capital (IGC) Pharma has initiated a Phase 1 clinical trial for IGC-AD1, an investigational cannabis-based treatment for mild to severe Alzheimer's dementia. The study, involving 12 participants, will assess the safety and pharmacokinetics of the low-dose cannabinoid formulation, which is based on research showing THC's ability to bind to and prevent amyloid plaque aggregation. The company expects to complete this phase during the first half of 2021, with secondary goals including monitoring dementia-related behavioral aspects.

title: Moderna's COVID-19 Vaccine Candidate Gets More Good News : Shots - Health News
summary: Moderna announced new data showing its COVID-19 vaccine candidate is 94% effective and provides strong protection against serious illness, leading the company to apply for emergency use authorization with the FDA. Similar to the Pfizer vaccine, it appears to be 100% effective at preventing severe COVID-19 cases, though supplies will initially be limited. Researchers are still investigating if the vaccine prevents asymptomatic infections and advise continued mask-wearing post-vaccination.

title: Moderna Asking FDA To Approve COVID-19 Vaccine After Trial "Already Saved Lives"
summary: Moderna Inc. announced its intention to request emergency use authorization for its COVID-19 vaccine from U.S. and European regulators following new study results confirming its strong protection. The move intensifies the effort to initiate limited vaccinations as the coronavirus pandemic continues to worsen globally. This request marks a significant step in the race to combat the ongoing health crisis.

title: Why ExxonMobil and Chevron Should Merge
summary: ExxonMobil and Chevron have both endured difficult business conditions in 2020 due to weak oil prices and the pandemic. Analyst Paul Sankey suggests a merger between ExxonMobil and Chevron could create a more resilient and efficient "mega-major" oil company, potentially named Chevron, allowing for cost reductions and stability for ExxonMobil's dividend. This comes as Chevron recently surpassed ExxonMobil in market capitalization for the first time.

title: Osteoarthritis Therapeutics Market 2020-2024- Featuring Abbott Laboratories, Bayer AG, Among Others to Contribute to the Market Growth | Industry Analysis, Market Trends, Opportunities, and Forecast 2024
summary: The osteoarthritis therapeutics market is projected to grow by USD 2.99 billion between 2020 and 2024, with a CAGR of almost 9%, driven by the increasing incidence of osteoarthritis. Technavio's latest report provides a detailed analysis of market size, trends, drivers, challenges, and vendor landscape, including key players like Abbott Laboratories and Bayer AG. The report also addresses the impact of COVID-19 on the market.

title: 'It's Like Star Trek': Moderna's Coronavirus Vaccine Moves Toward Approval
summary: Moderna announced its coronavirus vaccine demonstrated a 94.1% efficacy rate with no significant safety concerns in phase three clinical trials, leading to an emergency use application with the FDA. Following Pfizer, Moderna is the second company to seek approval, with vaccine distribution potentially starting before the end of 2020. The article highlights the vaccine's novel mRNA technology, described as "Star Trek technology," which holds vast potential beyond COVID-19 for other medical treatments.

title: Novel Tubulin-Targeting Therapies Make Headway
summary: Clinical findings have been reported for emerging tubulin-targeting agents VERU-111 and plinabulin, showing promise in cancer treatment. Both agents target microtubules, which are critical for cell function, and aim to provide increased efficacy with less toxicity compared to older microtubule-targeting agents. VERU-111 demonstrated anti-tumor activity in preclinical models and early clinical trials for prostate cancer, while plinabulin showed positive results in preventing chemotherapy-induced neutropenia.

title: From Idea To Mass Production, Moderna's COVID Vaccine Will Come From Massachusetts
summary: Moderna's COVID-19 vaccine, developed and produced in Massachusetts, has received emergency use authorization from the FDA. The company, founded by Flagship Pioneering, utilized messenger RNA technology to achieve 94% efficacy in trials. Despite potential distribution bottlenecks and public perception challenges, the vaccine's less stringent cold storage requirements are seen as an advantage.

title: EU criticises ‘hasty’ UK approval of COVID-19 vaccine
summary: European regulators, particularly the European Medicines Agency (EMA), have criticized the UK's rapid approval of the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine, suggesting their longer, more evidence-based process is safer. A German politician called the UK's move "problematic," while UK officials defended their approval stating all strict tests were met. The UK is now preparing for a large-scale rollout of the vaccine, prioritizing care home residents and staff.

title: UK approves new Covid-19 jab, with rollout starting next week
summary: The UK has become the first country to approve the Pfizer and BioNTech Covid-19 vaccine, with rollout expected to begin next week. While care home residents and staff are prioritized, logistical challenges due to the vaccine's ultra-cold storage requirements mean NHS staff might receive it first, especially given the difficulties in distributing it to smaller care homes. The UK has ordered 40 million doses, enough to vaccinate 20 million people, and expects 800,000 doses next week.

title: Pfizer and BioNTech Achieve First Authorization in the World for a Vaccine to Combat COVID-19
summary: Pfizer and BioNTech announced that the U.K. has granted a temporary authorization for emergency use for their COVID-19 mRNA vaccine (BNT162b2), marking the first such authorization globally. The companies are ready to deliver initial doses to the U.K. immediately, with further regulatory decisions expected worldwide. This authorization follows a successful Phase 3 clinical study demonstrating 95% efficacy and represents a significant step in combating the pandemic.

title: Pfizer says supply chain challenges contributed to slashed target for COVID-19 vaccine doses in 2020
summary: Pfizer reduced its 2020 production target for its COVID-19 vaccine from 100 million to 50 million doses due to challenges in its raw material supply chain. The company also cited later-than-expected clinical trial results as a contributing factor. Despite the initial delays, Pfizer states that production line modifications are complete and doses are now being made rapidly.

title: IBM warns hackers targeting COVID vaccine 'cold chain' supply process
summary: IBM has issued a warning about hackers targeting the COVID-19 vaccine "cold chain" supply process, which is crucial for maintaining vaccine temperatures during distribution. The cybersecurity unit detected an advanced phishing campaign attempting to gather information on various aspects of the cold chain, specifically mimicking an executive from Chinese cold chain provider Haier Biomedical. While the perpetrators remain unknown, IBM emphasized the significant effort put into the attacks, suggesting involvement from entities deeply aware of the vaccine supply chain.

title: BioCryst Announces FDA Approval of ORLADEYO™
summary: BioCryst Pharmaceuticals announced FDA approval for ORLADEYO™ (berotralstat), the first oral, once-daily therapy to prevent hereditary angioedema (HAE) attacks in adults and pediatric patients 12 years and older. Clinical trials demonstrated a significant and sustained reduction in HAE attacks, improving quality of life for patients. BioCryst is launching a patient support program, EMPOWER Patient Services, to help ensure access to the new medication.

title: US Startup Ignites Consumer Health Portfolio Build With North American Rights To ThermaCare
summary: A US startup is building its consumer health portfolio by acquiring North American rights to ThermaCare. This move comes after several past transactions involving ThermaCare by companies such as GSK, Pfizer, and Angelini, highlighting the product's M&A activity within the OTC market. The acquisition reflects strategic moves in the consumer health sector to expand product offerings and market presence.

title: Supply-Chain Obstacles Led to Last Month’s Cut to Pfizer’s Covid-19 Vaccine-Rollout Target
summary: Pfizer Inc. reduced its Covid-19 vaccine rollout target for this year due to unexpected challenges in scaling up raw material supply chains. The pharma giant found that raw materials in early production did not meet its standards, further complicated by the clinical trial outcome arriving later than initially projected. This situation highlights the difficulties drug makers face in quickly establishing complex supply chains to meet high demand for new vaccines.

title: Fauci slams UK regulator for pushing Pfizer shot’s review
summary: Anthony Fauci criticized the UK's drug regulator for what he called a rushed approval of the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine, suggesting they did not scrutinize the data carefully enough. This decision meant the UK would deploy the vaccine before the US and EU. Fauci later clarified his comments, stating he didn't intend to imply sloppiness, while the MHRA defended its "rolling review" process as thorough despite being fast.

title: Pfizer scaled back vaccine output targets earlier this year
summary: Pfizer Inc. scaled back its Covid-19 vaccine production targets earlier this year due to difficulties in securing raw materials for large-scale manufacturing. The company initially aimed for 100 million doses by year-end but revised that to 50 million, though it is now confident in supplying 1.3 billion doses by the end of 2021. This news led to a dip in Pfizer shares and the wider stock market, highlighting the global reliance on rapid vaccine production to end the pandemic.

title: Pfizer has sought emergency approval for COVID-19 vaccine in India -govt adviser
summary: Pfizer Inc. has applied for emergency use authorization of its COVID-19 vaccine in India, making it the first company to do so in the country with the world's second-highest number of infections. A top government health adviser stated that Indian authorities received the application on Saturday, and a decision is expected sooner than the typical 90-day review period. However, logistical challenges remain, as the vaccine requires ultra-cold storage, which is difficult for many Indian facilities to maintain.

title: Pfizer, BioNTech near 2020 vaccine target, easing output concern
summary: BioNTech SE announced it is on track to produce 50 million doses of its Covid-19 vaccine with partner Pfizer Inc. by the end of 2020, alleviating previous concerns about missing production targets. The companies are also exploring ways to increase their capacity beyond the promised 1.3 billion doses for next year. This update comes as their vaccine has received initial marketing approval in the U.K., with potential approvals in the U.S. and Europe soon.

title: Vaginal Fungi Infections Treatment Market Develop Rapidly
summary: The global vaginal fungi infections treatment market is expected to grow, with North America holding a dominant position due to the burden of recurrent vulvovaginal candidiasis. The COVID-19 pandemic, however, is anticipated to limit market growth by impacting the development, production, and supply of drugs. Key players in this market include Pfizer Inc., Bausch Health Companies Inc., and ANI Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

title: SK injects $200 mn into Roivant partnership for new drug development
summary: SK Holdings is investing $200 million into Roivant Sciences to develop new drugs using Roivant's targeted protein degradation platform, marking a significant entry into this promising market for a Korean company. The partnership aims to accelerate drug development and strengthen SK Holdings' global footprint through its pharma arm SK Biopharmaceuticals and contract manufacturing organization arm SK Pharmteco.

title: Valneva expands development for potential Lyme vaccine
summary: Valneva and Pfizer are accelerating the pediatric development of their Lyme vaccine candidate, VLA15, with plans to initiate the VLA15-221 study in Q1 2021. This study will be the first to enroll pediatric populations aged 5-17 and will compare a three-dose schedule with a reduced two-dose schedule. The collaboration aims for a Phase 3 pivotal efficacy trial in 2022 to target all major populations for the vaccine.

title: U.S. agency behind Kodak's beefy drug manufacturing loan played by the books, investigation finds: report
summary: An investigation by the Office of the Inspector General of the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) found that DFC officials acted appropriately in planning to award Kodak a $765 million loan for drug manufacturing. Despite the finding of no misconduct or conflicts of interest, the report suggested the DFC needs to reassess how it announces market-sensitive transactions. Separately, Kodak's own review cleared its executives of insider trading accusations related to the loan.

title: UK begins rollout of Pfizer's coronavirus vaccine: Here's what you need to know
summary: The UK commenced its coronavirus vaccine rollout on Tuesday, becoming the first country to administer the Pfizer-BioNTech jab outside of trial conditions. Many questions surround the historic program, including how the UK became the first to approve it, who manufactured it, and how long its protection lasts. The initial phase of the rollout targets front-line health workers, care home workers, and individuals over 80 across 50 hospital hubs.

title: Florida's Top Public Health Official Says 'Pfizer 5' Will Have COVID Vaccine Next Week
summary: Florida's top public health official announced that five Florida hospitals, dubbed the "Pfizer 5," are expected to receive COVID-19 vaccinations as early as next week, pending emergency use authorization from the federal government. These initial doses will prioritize front-line health-care workers, with plans to expand distribution to more hospitals and potentially include Moderna's vaccine in subsequent waves. The announcement comes as Governor Ron DeSantis traveled to Washington D.C. for a White House summit on vaccine rollout.

title: Israel receives initial shipment of Pfizer coronavirus vaccine
summary: Israel has received its first shipment of Pfizer coronavirus vaccines, with a distributor predicting enough doses for about a quarter of the population by year-end. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated his intention to be the first Israeli vaccinated, as the country prepares to begin administration on December 20. Israel has also ordered vaccines from Moderna and AstraZeneca, aiming to vaccinate high-risk populations first.

title: COVID-19 vaccine from China likely first to arrive in Philippines — vaccine czar
summary: The first COVID-19 vaccine to arrive in the Philippines is likely to be from China's Sinovac Biotech, with a potential arrival by March if a contract is signed this month. Vaccine czar Carlito Galvez also stated that Russia's Gamaleya Institute vaccine might arrive in the first quarter of 2021, but expressed more confidence in Sinovac due to its use in Brazil and Indonesia and its deemed safety by vaccine experts. The Philippines plans to inoculate around 24.7 million Filipinos, prioritizing health workers, senior citizens, and indigent individuals.

title: Focus: Crimped U.S. dry ice supply complicates rural U.S. vaccine release
summary: Rural U.S. areas face difficulties in securing sufficient dry ice for the storage and distribution of Pfizer's COVID-19 vaccine, which requires ultra-cold temperatures. Many states are rushing to obtain dry ice for suitcase-sized shipping containers, while dry ice suppliers acknowledge potential vulnerabilities in the supply chain due to unknown demand and reduced carbon dioxide production from ethanol plants. The logistical challenges are heightened by the vaccine's short shelf life once opened, especially for communities with limited resources.

title: Thermo Fisher’s ‘ultra-low’ temperature freezers in high demand to preserve Pfizer’s COVID-19 vaccine
summary: Thermo Fisher Scientific is experiencing unprecedented demand for its ultra-low-temperature (ULT) freezers, essential for storing Pfizer's COVID-19 vaccine at extremely cold temperatures. The company has ramped up production significantly, investing in increased capacity and hiring, to meet this global need. While freezer sales contribute to revenue, a larger surge comes from its diagnostics business, and Thermo Fisher is also venturing into vaccine manufacturing.

title: While FDA advisory panel backs Pfizer’s COVID-19 vaccine, patient advocates urge caution
summary: An FDA advisory panel has recommended emergency use authorization for Pfizer and BioNTech's COVID-19 vaccine candidate. While this marks a significant step towards combating the pandemic, patient advocates have voiced concerns, citing insufficient long-term safety and efficacy data, and a lack of diversity in clinical trials. Experts also emphasized the need for more serological data to ensure effective vaccine distribution, especially given initial limited supplies.

title: Airlines Gear Up to Transport Vaccines That Could Revive Travel
summary: Airlines like American, Delta, and United have been preparing for months to transport billions of coronavirus vaccine doses worldwide. This critical operation involves readying planes and crews for urgent shipments, with the hope that successful distribution will revive air travel. A major challenge is maintaining the ultra-cold temperatures required for some vaccines, such as Pfizer's, while also circulating a vaccine that could help restore airline passenger numbers.

title: NEJM releases ‘impressive’ peer-reviewed data for Pfizer COVID-19 vaccine candidate
summary: The New England Journal of Medicine (NEJM) has published peer-reviewed data for Pfizer Inc.'s BNT162b2 mRNA COVID-19 vaccine candidate, confirming its safety and 95% efficacy against COVID-19 in individuals aged 16 or older. NEJM editors described the data as "impressive," highlighting a "remarkable level of safety and efficacy" and presenting a pathway to saving lives and overcoming the global pandemic.

title: Moderna begins study of COVID-19 vaccine in adolescents
summary: Moderna has initiated a mid-to-late stage study for its COVID-19 vaccine candidate in adolescents aged 12 to less than 18, aiming for data ahead of the 2021 school year. The trial will enroll 3,000 healthy participants in the U.S. to assess the safety and effectiveness of its mRNA-1273 vaccine. This move follows Moderna's submission for emergency use authorization in adults, with rival Pfizer also studying its vaccine in younger age groups.

title: Pfizer’s COVID-19 vaccine gets nod from scientists, paving way for FDA authorization
summary: An independent panel of scientists has endorsed Pfizer and BioNTech's COVID-19 vaccine, recommending its emergency use to the FDA. If authorized, which is widely expected soon, the vaccine could be administered to healthcare workers and nursing home residents within days, marking a crucial step in combating the pandemic. The vaccine demonstrated 95% efficacy in trials and was well-tolerated, though questions remain about its effect on transmission and its use in younger age groups.

title: Pfizer Applies for Emergency F.D.A. Approval for Covid-19 Vaccine (Published 2020)
summary: Pfizer announced it submitted an application to the F.D.A. for emergency use authorization of its Covid-19 vaccine, which it developed with BioNTech. The vaccine was found to be 95 percent effective, setting in motion a process that could see the first Americans vaccinated by mid-December if approved. Moderna also expects to apply for emergency authorization for its similar vaccine, which showed 94.5 percent effectiveness.

title: Pfizer plans to file for full FDA approval of COVID-19 vaccine in April 2021
summary: Pfizer announced its intention to file for full U.S. FDA approval for its COVID-19 vaccine by April 2021, even as the vaccine awaited emergency use authorization. This announcement was made during a meeting with independent FDA advisers who were evaluating the emergency authorization of the vaccine developed with BioNTech SE.

title: ViiV Healthcare announces positive CHMP opinion for Rukobia (fostemsavir), a first-in-class attachment inhibitor for the treatment of adults with multidrug-resistant HIV with few treatment options available
summary: ViiV Healthcare announced that the European Medicines Agency's CHMP issued a positive opinion recommending approval for Rukobia (fostemsavir) for adults with multidrug-resistant HIV-1 infection. This first-in-class attachment inhibitor addresses a significant unmet need for patients with limited treatment options, with findings from the BRIGHTE study showing 60% of heavily treatment-experienced adults achieved and maintained viral suppression at 96 weeks. This move brings a crucial new treatment closer to patients who are at risk of progressing to AIDS due to their resistance to current therapies.

title: The FDA has authorized the first Covid-19 vaccine in the US
summary: The FDA has granted emergency use authorization (EUA) to the Pfizer/BioNTech Covid-19 vaccine, marking the first vaccine approved for distribution in the US outside of clinical trials. The initial 6.4 million doses are expected to ship soon, prioritizing health workers and long-term care facility residents. Challenges for the rollout include maintaining the vaccine's ultra-cold storage requirements, ensuring recipients return for a second dose, and the ethical dilemma of managing placebo participants in ongoing clinical trials.

title: GlaxoSmithKline and Sanofi COVID-19 vaccine delayed until late 2021
summary: GlaxoSmithKline and Sanofi announced a delay in their COVID-19 vaccine program until late 2021, aiming to improve its immune response in older adults. This setback is a blow to hopes for widespread vaccine availability by early 2021 and affects the Trump administration's Operation Warp Speed, which had invested $2.1 billion. The companies plan a new study in February and, if successful, Phase 3 trials could begin in the second quarter, pushing potential availability to the third or fourth quarter of next year.

title: GSK/Sanofi Covid vaccine delayed until end of next year
summary: The GlaxoSmithKline and Sanofi COVID-19 vaccine has been delayed until the end of 2021 after trials revealed it failed to produce a strong immune response in older people. The companies will reformulate the vaccine and launch a phase 2 trial in February, aiming for approval in the last quarter of 2021. This setback highlights the complexities of vaccine development despite other successful candidates, and GSK emphasizes the need for multiple vaccines to combat the pandemic.

title: Viatris Inc. Announces Additional Details of Previously Disclosed Global Restructuring Initiative
summary: Viatris Inc. announced further details of its global restructuring initiative, targeting at least $1 billion in cost synergies by the end of 2024 and impacting up to 20% of its global workforce. The restructuring involves optimizing commercial capabilities, enabling functions, and closing, downsizing, or divesting up to 15 manufacturing facilities, including specific sites in West Virginia, Ireland, Puerto Rico, and India. The company anticipates incurring pre-tax charges between $500 million and $600 million for committed restructuring actions, with expected annual savings of $250 million to $300 million once fully implemented.

title: FDA OKs Pfizer vaccine, opening new front against COVID-19; shots to begin within days
summary: The FDA has authorized the emergency use of Pfizer Inc. and BioNTech's COVID-19 vaccine, allowing widespread immunizations to begin. The two-dose vaccine, which was 95% effective in clinical trials, clears the way for states to order and distribute doses, with healthcare workers and priority groups receiving the first shots. While marking a significant step in ending the pandemic, officials caution that herd immunity will be a long process requiring widespread vaccination efforts.

title: FedEx to Ship First Wave of COVID-19 Vaccines Across the United States
summary: FedEx Express announced operations are in motion to transport its first shipments of COVID-19 vaccines across the United States following FDA approval for the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine. The company will use its FedEx Priority Overnight service with advanced monitoring and temperature-controlled solutions. FedEx has also committed $4 million in cash and in-kind transportation support to nonprofits to help reach underserved communities.

title: GP2/GM-CSF Combo Elicits 100% DFS Rate in HER2 3+ Breast Cancer at 5 Years
summary: A phase 2b trial demonstrated a 100% disease-free survival rate at 5 years for patients with HER2/neu 3-positive breast cancer treated with GP2 immunotherapy plus granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) following adjuvant trastuzumab. This significant finding, presented at the 2020 San Antonio Breast Cancer Symposium, supports the initiation of a pivotal phase 3 trial for this combination. The treatment was also well-tolerated with no serious adverse effects reported, highlighting its potential to address an unmet need in recurring breast cancer.

title: AstraZeneca to buy Boston biotech Alexion for $39 billion in rare-disease push
summary: AstraZeneca is set to acquire Boston-based Alexion Pharmaceuticals for $39 billion in a cash and stock deal, marking its largest acquisition since 1999. This move will significantly expand AstraZeneca's presence in rare diseases and immunology, complementing its existing focus on cancer treatments. The acquisition is expected to close in the third quarter of 2021, and Alexion's shareholders will own 15% of the combined company.

title: Drugmaker Viatris to cut up to 20% of workforce
summary: Viatris Inc., a newly formed pharmaceutical spinoff, announced plans to cut up to 20% of its global workforce, affecting as many as 9,000 employees. The company also intends to close, cut, or sell up to 15 manufacturing sites worldwide as part of an effort to reduce costs by at least $1 billion over the next few years. Initial sites affected by these cuts will include locations in Morgantown, West Virginia, Ireland, Puerto Rico, and India.

title: The FDA didn’t ‘approve’ Pfizer’s COVID-19 vaccine. Here’s why
summary: This article explains why the FDA issued an Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) for Pfizer's COVID-19 vaccine rather than a full approval. It details the stringent conditions for an EUA during a public health emergency, emphasizing the rapid development needed for new medicines while still ensuring safety and efficacy through rigorous clinical trials. The article also clarifies that an EUA is temporary and manufacturers will need to pursue full FDA approval by continuing their trials.

title: With U.S. now in hand, BioNTech CEO looks for more vaccine production
summary: BioNTech CEO Ugur Sahin is focused on scaling up vaccine manufacturing to meet the massive demand for their COVID-19 vaccine, especially after its authorization in the U.S. and expected conditional approval in Europe. The company plans to produce up to 1.3 billion doses next year and is working to expedite the activation of a new production plant in Marburg, Germany. Sahin also noted the vaccine's early efficacy and mentioned discussions with Pfizer about potentially evaluating a single-dose version.

title: WRAPUP 3 U.S. FDA authorizes Pfizer COVID-19 vaccine for emergency use
summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted emergency use authorization for Pfizer's COVID-19 vaccine, with the first inoculations expected within days. The vaccine, developed with BioNTech, showed 95% effectiveness and will initially be administered to healthcare workers and elderly individuals. This authorization marks a significant step in combating the pandemic in the U.S., where cases are surging and hospitals are nearing capacity, though a meaningful impact on spread is still some time away.

title: US to buy 100m more doses of Moderna COVID-19 vaccine
summary: The United States government will purchase an additional 100 million doses of Moderna Inc's COVID-19 vaccine, bringing its total order to 200 million doses. This acquisition comes as the US prepares for a mass vaccine roll-out, with officials hoping to bring the surging pandemic under control amidst a high number of cases and deaths. Federal and state authorities are coordinating distribution plans, prioritizing healthcare workers and vulnerable populations, while facing significant logistical challenges.

title: AstraZeneca acquires rare-disease specialist Alexion in $39 billion deal
