summary: AstraZeneca Plc is acquiring rare-disease specialist Alexion Pharmaceuticals Inc. in a $39 billion cash-and-stock deal, marking AstraZeneca's largest acquisition to date. This move aims to expand AstraZeneca's portfolio into treatments for uncommon blood and immunological disorders, bolstering its growth strategy beyond its focus on cancer and the COVID-19 vaccine. The acquisition, which provides Alexion shareholders with a 45% premium, is expected to close in the third quarter of 2021, and will establish AstraZeneca's rare disease headquarters in Boston, promising significant financial synergies.

title: Kuwait Approves Pfizer-BioNTech, Bahrain Registers Sinopharm
summary: Bahrain has approved Sinopharm Group Co.'s vaccine for widespread use after previously authorizing its emergency use for frontline workers. Meanwhile, neighboring Kuwait has authorized the use of Pfizer Inc. and BioNTech SE’s vaccine. The Sinopharm vaccine has already been administered to hundreds of thousands in China under emergency authorization but awaits public use approval from drug regulators.

title: The Mass Distribution of Covid-19 Vaccines Is Under Way. ‘Everything Has to Come Together.’ - WSJ
summary: The mass distribution of Covid-19 vaccines has begun, involving a complex logistical operation across the United States. This effort, comparable to a wartime mobilization, requires the coordination of various professionals and specialized equipment like ultracold freezers and sensors to ensure safe and efficient delivery of the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine.

title: Pfizer-BioNTech Covid-19 Vaccines Begin Shipping
summary: Pfizer and BioNTech have begun shipping their Covid-19 vaccines across the U.S. following FDA approval. Trucks from UPS and FedEx are dispatching doses from a Michigan plant to health departments and hospitals nationwide. This rollout marks a significant step in the effort to combat the surging pandemic.

title: FedEx to ship first set of Pfizer COVID-19 vaccines to United States
summary: FedEx Express has begun shipping the first batches of Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccines across the United States following FDA emergency use approval. The company is utilizing its Priority Overnight® service with advanced monitoring to ensure safe transport. This effort is part of a broader commitment by FedEx to combat the pandemic, including substantial donations for vaccine distribution to underserved populations globally.

title: With vaccine distribution underway, it's 'game on' for FedEx
summary: FedEx Corp. has begun the distribution of Pfizer's COVID vaccine, which requires storage at -94 degrees Fahrenheit. This marks a significant logistical undertaking for the company. The article references related news about FedEx and UPS's unified efforts in vaccine distribution, highlighting the critical role these companies play.

title: Rollout of Pfizer-BioNTech Covid-19 Vaccine Slows in U.K. Due to Allergic-Reaction Monitoring
summary: The rollout of the Pfizer-BioNTech Covid-19 vaccine in the U.K. is experiencing delays. This is due to logistical challenges and new monitoring requirements for patients after two severe allergic reactions occurred on the first day of the vaccination campaign. Doctors are now required to monitor each patient for 15 minutes post-injection, impacting the anticipated speed of vaccine distribution beyond hospitals.

title: 3 cases that changed the patent disclosure landscape of proteins
summary: This article examines three key U.S. Federal Circuit court cases—Centocor Ortho Biotech, Inc. versus Abbott Laboratories (2010), AbbVie Deutschland GMBH & Co. v. Janssen Biotech, Inc. & Centocor (2013), and Amgen Inc. versus Sanofi, Aventisub, LLC (2017)—that significantly reshaped patent disclosure requirements for protein-based claims, particularly antibodies. It highlights the shift from simply disclosing an antigen to needing comprehensive structural and functional details or representative species to support broad claims. The author advises life science innovators to consider these precedents for developing robust patent portfolios.

title: FDA Finds Moderna Covid-19 Vaccine Highly Effective - WSJ
summary: The FDA announced that the Covid-19 vaccine developed by Moderna Inc. is "highly effective," paving the way for an emergency authorization this week. This would make it the second vaccine available in the U.S. against the pandemic. Moderna's data also suggests the first dose may reduce asymptomatic infections, potentially curbing virus transmission.

title: Oman Approves Pfizer-Biontech Vaccine for Covid-19
summary: Oman has approved the import and use of Pfizer Inc. and BioNTech SE's Covid-19 vaccine for individuals aged 16 and above. This decision makes Oman the latest country in the region, following Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, and Bahrain, to allow the use of this vaccine, which boasts a 95% effectiveness rate. The announcement was made by the sultanate's state-run agency.

title: Kroger To Provide COVID-19 Vaccines At Smith’s Stores
summary: Kroger, parent company of Smith's Food & Drug, announced plans to offer COVID-19 vaccines nationwide through its stores. Vaccinations will be deployed in collaboration with state health departments and the federal government, following CDC rollout plans. Smith's has previously been involved in COVID-19 response efforts, including offering free drive-through testing and rapid antibody tests.

title: U.S. and Pfizer Are Negotiating Deal for More Vaccine Doses Next Year (Published 2020)
summary: The Trump administration is negotiating a deal with Pfizer to secure tens of millions of additional Covid-19 vaccine doses for Americans in the first half of next year. This agreement would involve the administration helping Pfizer obtain the necessary raw materials to increase production. The move aims to address an anticipated vaccine shortage, as current pre-orders cover less than half of the U.S. population.

title: Hospitals Discover a Surprise in Their Vaccine Deliveries: Extra Doses (Published 2020)
summary: Hospital pharmacists have discovered that vials of the Pfizer vaccine, intended to hold five doses, often contain enough for a sixth or even seventh dose. The FDA has since issued guidance allowing the use of these extra, full doses from individual vials, which could significantly increase the number of people vaccinated. This discovery initially caused confusion among hospitals regarding whether to use or discard the additional vaccine.

title: Westlake Village venture capital firm announces $500M to invest in biotech companies
summary: Westlake Village BioPartners has launched two new funds totaling $500 million to invest in promising biotech companies, particularly in the greater Los Angeles area and Thousand Oaks. This investment supports the growing biotech hub in Thousand Oaks, which is anchored by Amgen and includes new incubator spaces for early-stage life sciences companies. The initiative aims to foster innovation in therapeutic technologies and create high-paying jobs, repurposing industrial spaces for state-of-the-art research facilities.

title: US medical industry urged to reassess paid events amid doctor kickback concerns
summary: The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services has issued a rare "fraud alert," urging the medical industry to re-evaluate paid events for doctors due to concerns over kickbacks. This alert comes after federal investigations revealed that such payments often induce the prescribing of specific drugs or devices, sometimes for off-label uses. The move signals increased scrutiny on industry-funded speaker programs and serves as a warning to both companies and physicians about violating anti-kickback statutes.

title: Novartis announces positive FDA Advisory Committee recommendation for use of Entresto® to treat patients with HFpEF
summary: Novartis announced that the FDA Cardiovascular and Renal Drugs Advisory Committee voted 12 to 1 in favor of Entresto (sacubitril/valsartan) for treating heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). This recommendation is based on data from the PARAGON-HF study, supporting Entresto's benefit in reducing worsening heart failure events in HFpEF patients, a condition with no currently approved treatments. If approved, Entresto would be the first therapy indicated for both major types of chronic heart failure: HFpEF and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF).

title: Fosun Pharma to import 100 mln doses of BioNTech's COVID-19 vaccine to China
summary: Shanghai Fosun Pharmaceutical Group announced it would import at least 100 million doses of BioNTech's COVID-19 vaccine to mainland China in the coming year, pending approval. This deal marks a significant move as China has not yet publicly announced supply agreements with Western drugmakers. Fosun Pharma is making an initial payment of 125 million euros for 50 million doses and is currently conducting Phase 2 clinical trials for the vaccine candidate BNT162b2 in China.

title: Leon County Set To Receive 2,500 Doses Of Moderna COVID-19 Vaccine
summary: Leon County is preparing to receive 2,500 doses of Moderna's COVID-19 vaccine, with distribution expected to begin as early as next week. This makes Leon County one of Florida's pilot sites for vaccination, prioritizing staff and residents of skilled nursing facilities. Governor Ron DeSantis anticipates emergency use authorization for the Moderna vaccine by the end of the week, with the state initially receiving 370,000 doses.

title: US says Pfizer vaccine production may face challenges
summary: US officials are collaborating with Pfizer Inc. to address potential production challenges for its COVID-19 vaccine, as indicated by the US Secretary of Health and Human Services. Pfizer's CEO had previously requested the government's aid under the Defense Production Act to alleviate critical supply limitations for vaccine components. The US plans to secure hundreds of millions of vaccine doses from Pfizer and other drugmakers, with Moderna's vaccine authorization also anticipated soon.

title: Operation Warp Speed chief showers praise on FedEx, UPS
summary: General Gus Perna, COO of Operation Warp Speed, expressed profound satisfaction with FedEx and UPS's performance in distributing Pfizer's COVID-19 vaccine. Despite his extensive background in military logistics, Perna was particularly impressed by the express carriers' professional execution, high standards, and proactive mitigating strategies, especially concerning weather challenges. He lauded the dedication of both companies' leadership and front-line workers in ensuring the safe and timely delivery of critical vaccine supplies across the nation.

title: U.S. expert panel endorses Moderna COVID-19 vaccine, paving way for emergency use approval
summary: A U.S. expert panel has endorsed Moderna's COVID-19 vaccine, clearing the path for its emergency use approval. This makes it the second vaccine option for the U.S., with initial doses expected to go to healthcare workers and vulnerable nursing home residents. Canada also anticipates receiving 168,000 doses of Moderna's vaccine by year-end, pending Health Canada approval, and its storage requirements make it more suitable for remote areas compared to the Pfizer vaccine.

title: How Will Moderna Meet The Demand For Its COVID-19 Vaccine?
summary: Moderna, an upstart biotech company with no products previously on the market, is relying heavily on outsourcing to meet the demand for its COVID-19 vaccine. The article details the roles of contract manufacturers like Catalent and Lonza in producing and packaging the vaccine, while also highlighting past FDA inspection issues at some of these facilities. Despite these challenges, Moderna is projected to deliver millions of doses by mid-2021, supported by significant federal funding.

title: FDA Approves Amgen's RIABNI™ (rituximab-arrx), A Biosimilar To Rituxan® (rituximab)
summary: The FDA has approved Amgen's RIABNI™ (rituximab-arrx), a biosimilar to Rituxan®, for adult patients with Non-Hodgkin's Lymphoma, Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia, Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis, and Microscopic Polyangiitis. RIABNI will be available in the U.S. in January 2021 at a Wholesale Acquisition Cost 23.7% lower than Rituxan. This approval marks Amgen's fifth biosimilar approval, reinforcing its commitment to providing affordable and effective treatment options.

title: W&M alumna leads groundbreaking research platform at Moderna
summary: Melissa J. Moore '84, Chief Scientific Officer of platform research at Moderna Inc., is a key figure in the development of Moderna's COVID-19 vaccine, mRNA-1273. Her decades of research into messenger RNA (mRNA) technology have been instrumental in enabling Moderna to rapidly develop and produce the vaccine. Moore emphasizes the public good aspect of scientific research and the broader applications of mRNA technology for other diseases and conditions.

title: F.D.A. Authorizes Moderna Vaccine, Adding Millions of Doses to U.S. Supply (Published 2020)
summary: The FDA authorized Moderna's coronavirus vaccine for emergency use, making it the second vaccine available to the American public after Pfizer's. This authorization allows millions more doses to be shipped across the U.S., with initial doses expected to be administered within days. The decision intensifies discussions about which groups, such as essential workers or the elderly, will receive the next round of vaccinations.

title: Hope is here: COVID-19 vaccine arrives at HCA Healthcare facilities
summary: HCA Healthcare facilities began receiving and administering the COVID-19 vaccine to frontline workers in mid-December 2020, marking a significant turning point in the pandemic. Key personnel across various locations, including South Carolina, Virginia, and Tennessee, were among the first to receive the Pfizer/BioNTech vaccine, expressing hope and gratitude for the scientific achievement. The article also provides a Q&A section addressing common concerns about vaccine types, safety, development speed, and distribution plans.

title: Covid: US approves Moderna as second vaccine
summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Moderna as the country's second Covid-19 vaccine, clearing the way for millions of doses to be distributed. This authorization follows the recent approval and distribution of the Pfizer/BioNTech vaccine. The US has pre-ordered 200 million doses of Moderna, with six million ready for immediate shipment, as the country continues to battle the world's highest numbers of Covid-19 deaths and cases.

title: The Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices’ Interim Recommendation for Use of Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine — United States, December 2020
summary: The Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) issued an interim recommendation for the use of the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine in individuals aged 16 years and older, following its Emergency Use Authorization by the FDA on December 11, 2020. This recommendation is based on an evidence-based review, including a large clinical trial showing 95.0% efficacy in preventing symptomatic COVID-19, with generally mild to moderate reactogenicity. The committee emphasized the vaccine's high certainty for preventing symptomatic COVID-19 and its role in addressing a major public health problem, while also noting the need for ongoing safety and effectiveness studies.

title: How the Covid-19 Vaccine Will Be Delivered to Millions, From Factory to Front Line
summary: This article details the complex ultracold supply chain established to distribute Covid-19 vaccines from Pfizer and Moderna across the U.S. It explains the manufacturing and packaging processes, specific temperature requirements for each vaccine, and the logistics partnerships involved in getting doses from factories to hospitals, pharmacies, and long-term care facilities. The distribution plan addresses the challenges of maintaining vaccine efficacy and equitable access based on storage capabilities.

title: US FDA approves Moderna vaccine on emergency basis: Report
summary: The US FDA has decided to approve Moderna Inc's coronavirus vaccine on an emergency basis after a panel of doctors overwhelmingly recommended it. This approval provides a second COVID-19 vaccine for the US, following Pfizer-BioNTech's, offering hope despite the rapidly spreading pandemic. Moderna's vaccine has a logistical advantage as it does not require specialised ultra-cold refrigeration, unlike the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine.

title: Covid: Moderna vaccine moves closer to US approval
summary: The Moderna vaccine is nearing emergency approval in the US after being endorsed by an expert panel, with the FDA expected to authorize it quickly, allowing millions of doses to ship. The US has agreed to purchase 200 million doses of the vaccine, which was found to be 94% effective and easier to store than the Pfizer/BioNTech vaccine. This development follows the US's earlier approval and rollout of the Pfizer/BioNTech vaccine, with the vaccination program aiming to reach 100 million people by April.

title: Moderna’s Covid-19 Vaccine Is Cleared for American Use
summary: U.S. health regulators have authorized Moderna Inc.'s Covid-19 vaccine for use in Americans aged 18 and older, marking it as the second such shot to receive FDA permission. Vaccinations are expected to begin as early as Monday, with federal officials anticipating shipments within 24 hours of authorization. The vaccine, developed with the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, was found to be safe and effective in trials, although some side effects were noted.

title: XPO Logistics provides truck transport for Pfizer vaccine
summary: XPO Logistics announced it is transporting Pfizer's COVID-19 vaccine using refrigerated trucks, supporting the U.S. government's distribution efforts, primarily on behalf of UPS. The company is also preparing to transport other vaccine candidates, such as Moderna's, and cautions that the intense focus on vaccine logistics may impact general cargo capacity. XPO is leveraging its temperature-controlled equipment and digital transportation platform to ensure secure and efficient delivery of vaccines and related medical supplies.

title: Inside one of the new, quick-build factories making the Moderna vaccine
summary: Swiss manufacturer Lonza rapidly constructed factories to produce Moderna's COVID-19 vaccine by using adaptable building shells, significantly reducing the typical construction time from years to months. This innovative approach allowed for the quick setup of manufacturing lines, with Lonza producing key vaccine ingredients in both Switzerland and New Hampshire to meet global demand for hundreds of millions of doses. The article highlights the efficiency of this method and the collaboration that enabled rapid vaccine production following the development of mRNA technology.

title: Pfizer-BioNTech Covid-19 Vaccine Is Cleared for Use by EU Drug Agency
summary: The European Medicines Agency has cleared the Pfizer-BioNTech Covid-19 vaccine for use, recommending its authorization. This decision paves the way for formal approval by EU authorities this week and potential distribution across 27 member states as early as next week. The approval comes as Europe faces a deadly winter surge of the virus and deals with a new mutation found in Britain.

title: iShares Global Healthcare ETF IXJ
summary: The iShares Global Healthcare ETF (IXJ) tracks the performance of healthcare companies worldwide. Established in 2001, it mirrors the S&P Global 1200 Healthcare Sector Index and invests at least 80% of its assets in stocks comprising this index. As of April 2022, IXJ had $3.49 billion in net assets across 116 holdings, including major players like UnitedHealth Group, Johnson & Johnson, and Pfizer.

title: Farmworker Health Clinic Gets Precious Gift In Battling COVID-19
summary: AgroFresh Solutions, Inc. has donated the use of three ultra-cold freezers to the Yakima Valley Farm Workers Clinic to assist in storing COVID-19 vaccines. These freezers, capable of maintaining temperatures between -97° F and -112° F, are crucial for the Pfizer vaccine and are in high demand. The donation will help the clinic better serve farmworker clients in the Yakima Valley, an area disproportionately affected by COVID-19.

title: Vaccinations move to nursing homes as pandemic rages in California
summary: The U.S. government and major pharmacy chains, Walgreens and CVS, began vaccinating nursing home residents against COVID-19, following vaccinations for healthcare workers. This effort comes as the pandemic continues to strain healthcare systems, particularly in California where ICU beds are scarce. The rollout includes about 7.9 million doses of Pfizer/BioNTech and Moderna vaccines, with President-elect Joe Biden also receiving his shot to boost public confidence.

title: Biotech Surge – COVID-19 Cure is Just the Start
summary: The article discusses the surge in the biotech sector, particularly driven by COVID-19 vaccine developments, and highlights the performance of the NASDAQ Biotechnology Index and related ETFs like VanEck Vectors Biotech ETF (BBH). It emphasizes that beyond the immediate vaccine urgency, strong fundamentals, increased R&D spending, and growing investor funding suggest sustained long-term growth for the biotech industry. The article also points out that while immediate earnings potential from vaccines is enticing, the sector's innovation and investment trends indicate continued expansion well into the future.

title: Eli Lilly’s Antibody Treatment Gets Emergency F.D.A. Approval (Published 2020)
summary: The FDA has granted emergency authorization for Eli Lilly's COVID-19 antibody treatment, bamlanivimab, which is similar to the therapy given to former President Trump. The treatment is authorized for newly infected individuals aged 12 and older who are at high risk for severe COVID-19 but not for hospitalized patients. This approval comes at a critical time as the pandemic rages, and the company has already secured a $375 million deal with the U.S. government for 300,000 doses.

title: Merck signs $356M deal to supply US with experimental coronavirus drug
summary: Merck has secured a $356 million deal with the U.S. government to supply 60,000 to 100,000 doses of its experimental COVID-19 drug, MK-7110. This drug, acquired through the $425 million buyout of OncoImmune, is designed to mitigate the inflammatory response in severely ill hospitalized patients. Initial Phase 3 trial results showed that MK-7110 improved recovery rates, and the agreement includes expanding production capacity by June 2021, highlighting the government's continued focus on treatments despite vaccine rollouts.

title: The US FDA’s Nifty Fifty
summary: The article titled "The US FDA’s Nifty Fifty" was published on December 23, 2020, and was authored by Michael McCaughan. The specific content of the article is not provided in this snippet, but its title suggests a focus on 50 key aspects or developments related to the US FDA.

title: Chinese pharmaceutical firm Sinovac says its COVID-19 vaccine is more than 50 percent effective, but data withheld
summary: Chinese pharmaceutical firm Sinovac Biotech Ltd.'s COVID-19 vaccine was found to be more than 50 percent effective in a Brazilian clinical trial, meeting the minimum standard set by US regulators. However, researchers delayed releasing more detailed data at the company's request, raising transparency concerns among experts. This delay is impacting vaccination plans in Sao Paulo, which has already received millions of doses of the CoronaVac vaccine.

title: Boston Doctor Reports Serious Allergic Reaction After Getting Moderna’s Covid Vaccine (Published 2020)
summary: A Boston physician experienced a severe allergic reaction minutes after receiving Moderna's Covid-19 vaccine, marking the first reported adverse event linked to that vaccine. The doctor, who has a shellfish allergy, recovered quickly after self-administering an EpiPen and receiving hospital treatment. This incident follows previous reports of anaphylaxis linked to the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine.

title: Restoring immune balance: Targeting CD6 to treat autoimmune and inflammatory disease
summary: This article discusses Equillium's itolizumab, an anti-CD6 antibody product candidate, being developed to treat autoimmune and inflammatory diseases. Itolizumab selectively downregulates T effector cells, which are believed to drive autoimmunity, while sparing regulatory T cells, helping to restore immune balance. The drug is currently in clinical trials for acute graft-vs-host disease (aGVHD), lupus nephritis, and uncontrolled asthma, showing promising interim results in aGVHD and having received Fast Track and Orphan status designations.

title: Novavax begins U.S. phase 3 trial of coronavirus vaccine
summary: Novavax Inc. has initiated a final-stage Phase 3 trial for its coronavirus vaccine, NVX-CoV2373, in the U.S. and Mexico, enrolling 30,000 participants. This trial, supported by Operation Warp Speed, aims to evaluate the vaccine's efficacy and broaden the available vaccine options alongside those from Pfizer and Moderna. Initial results from a separate U.K. trial are expected early next year, as the company ramps up global manufacturing capacity.

title: Novavax starts late-stage trial of COVID-19 vaccine in United States
summary: Novavax Inc. has officially started a large late-stage clinical trial for its experimental COVID-19 vaccine in the United States, following two previous delays related to manufacturing scale-up. The trial aims to enroll up to 30,000 volunteers across North America. Although lagging behind other authorized vaccines, experts emphasize the need for multiple vaccines to combat the global pandemic.

title: Targeting BCL-2 with venetoclax and dexamethasone in patients with relapsed/refractory t(11;14) multiple myeloma
summary: This study evaluated the safety and efficacy of venetoclax (Ven) and dexamethasone (Dex) combination therapy in patients with t(11;14) positive relapsed/refractory (R/R) multiple myeloma (MM). The VenDex combination demonstrated efficacy and manageable safety in heavily pre-treated patients, with objective response rates of 60% and 48% in distinct study phases. The findings support further investigation of Ven combinations in this patient population, especially given the positive outcomes for those with high-risk cytogenetic abnormalities.

title: Aprea Therapeutics Closes Out 2020 with Phase III Flop
summary: Aprea Therapeutics' shares plunged over 77% after its late-stage cancer treatment, a combination of eprenetapopt and azacitidine for TP53 mutant myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS), failed to meet its primary endpoint of complete remission rate with statistical significance. While the combination showed a higher complete remission rate compared to azacitidine alone, the results did not reach statistical significance, despite the company's belief in eprenetapopt's clinical benefit for patients with TP53 mutant malignancies. Aprea plans to continue analyzing data and pursuing its clinical development programs for its sole asset.

title: Pfizer, AstraZeneca chosen for lab to foster Israel biotech startups
summary: Pharma giants Pfizer, AstraZeneca, Merck, Teva, along with Amazon Web Services and Israel Biotech Fund, have been selected by the Israel Innovation Authority to establish an innovation lab. The lab will focus on developing AI-based computational technologies for personalized drugs and treatments, supporting new startups in the biotech sector. This initiative aligns with Israel's "Bio-convergence Strategy" to integrate biology and engineering, fostering local entrepreneurship and leveraging expertise from global partners.

title: Delta Air Lines, Airbnb, Peloton: Stocks That Defined the Week
summary: This article highlights major companies whose stocks were influenced by recent news events. Delta Air Lines announced a $200 monthly surcharge for unvaccinated employees, while Pfizer's Covid-19 vaccine received full FDA approval, boosting its shares. Walmart introduced "Walmart GoLocal," expanding its Spark Driver delivery platform for other businesses.

title: Under pandemic pressure, drugmakers raise prices in US: Report
summary: Major drugmakers like Pfizer, Sanofi, and GlaxoSmithKline planned to raise prices on over 300 medications in the US on January 1, 2021, mostly under 10 percent. These increases come as pharmaceutical companies face reduced demand due to the COVID-19 pandemic and new drug-pricing rules, seeking to offset lost revenue. Despite political pressure from both the Trump and Biden administrations to lower drug costs, companies argue the "modest increases" are necessary for continued investment in new medicines.

title: Exclusive: Drugmakers to hike prices for 2021 as pandemic, political pressure put revenues at risk
summary: Major drugmakers like Pfizer, Sanofi, and GlaxoSmithKline are set to increase prices on over 300 drugs in the U.S. starting January 1, 2021. These increases, generally kept at or below 10%, are intended to offset revenue losses due to the COVID-19 pandemic's impact on doctor visits and new prescriptions, and to counter new drug price-cutting regulations. Despite political pressure from both the Trump administration and President-elect Biden to lower drug costs, pharmaceutical companies argue that these modest adjustments are necessary to fund research and development.

title: Minimal Efficacy Observed With Eprenetapopt Plus Azacitidine in TP53-Mutant MDS
summary: A phase 3 clinical trial investigating the combination of eprenetapopt and azacitidine for patients with TP53-mutant myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) did not meet its primary endpoint of improving complete responses compared to azacitidine alone. Although the combination showed a numerically higher complete response rate (33.3% vs 22.4%), the difference was not statistically significant. Aprea Therapeutics, Inc. noted that patients still showed a slight improvement with the added eprenetapopt, and further analysis of maturing data and secondary endpoints is ongoing.

title: Jeff Bezos, Jamie Dimon and Warren Buffett tried to solve health care. 3 years later, their company has shut down
summary: Haven, the joint healthcare venture founded by Amazon, Berkshire Hathaway, and JPMorgan Chase, is shutting down after three years. The company aimed to provide better healthcare services at lower costs for its employees but struggled to expand beyond its founding partners. The three companies will continue to collaborate informally to address their individual employee healthcare needs.

title: Impact of COVID-19 on Vaginal Fungi Infections Treatment Market
summary: This article details the "Impact of COVID-19 on Vaginal Fungi Infections Treatment Market" report by Coherent Market Insights. The report covers a SWOT analysis by 2027, featuring key players like Pfizer Inc. and Bausch Health Companies Inc. It highlights the rising incidence of vaginal fungi infections, with significant outpatient visits and high lifetime prevalence among women, driving market growth.

title: Peruvian minister raises 'controversy' over Pfizer vaccine liability clause
summary: Peru's health minister, Pilar Mazzetti, revealed a "controversy" in negotiations with Pfizer Inc. for COVID-19 vaccines, specifically concerning a liability waiver and jurisdictional immunity. Mazzetti stated that while vaccines are needed, Peru must protect its sovereignty and future generations, echoing similar concerns raised by other countries like Brazil and Argentina. The World Bank is reportedly working with countries to address these liability waiver issues, which have become a significant obstacle in vaccine supply deals.

title: Big drugmakers just raised their prices on 500 prescription drugs
summary: Major pharmaceutical companies, including AbbVie, Bristol Myers Squibb, GlaxoSmithKline, and Pfizer, have increased prices on over 500 prescription drugs by a median of 4.6% at the start of the new year, according to 46brooklyn Research. This move continues a trend of annual price hikes in the U.S., where drug prices are higher than in other developed countries due to a lack of negotiation with manufacturers. Both former President Trump and then President-elect Biden had plans to address rising drug costs, while drugmakers like Pfizer justified increases to cover investment in new medicines.

title: IconOVir Bio Raises $77 Million in Series A Financing to Develop Next-Generation Oncolytic Viruses to Treat Solid Tumors
summary: IconOVir Bio has successfully raised $77 million in Series A funding to advance its next-generation oncolytic virus therapy for solid tumors. The financing was co-led by Nextech and Vida Ventures, with participation from other significant investors. The company, formed by the team behind Kite Pharma and Allogene Therapeutics, also announced the appointment of Mark McCamish, M.D., Ph.D., as CEO and plans to submit an IND for its lead candidate, IOV-1042, in the first half of 2022.

title: Philippines to allow emergency use of Pfizer COVID-19 vaccine ‘within a week’
summary: The Philippines' Food and Drug Administration announced it would issue an emergency use authorization for the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine within a week. While the approval would expedite the process, vaccine availability for the populace depends on securing supply deals and establishing ultra-low temperature storage facilities, which the country currently lacks. Other pharmaceutical companies like AstraZeneca, Sinovac Biotech, and Gamaleya have also either applied for or inquired about emergency use authorization in the Philippines, with the government pursuing various procurement strategies.

title: Pfizer Bids Farewell To Blue Pill With New Double Helix Logo
summary: Pfizer has unveiled a new brand identity, replacing its traditional blue pill logo with a double helix design. This rebrand signifies the company's shift towards being a science-focused firm, emphasizing the "DNA at the heart" of its operations. The new logo and imagery are part of a broader marketing strategy.

title: Sound Income ETFs Bring Active Approach to Creating Retirement Income
summary: Sound Income Strategies launched two actively managed income-based ETFs, SDEI and SDEF, designed to make income-generating strategies more accessible, especially for retirees. The Sound Equity Income ETF (SDEI) focuses on current income and long-term capital appreciation from dividend-paying companies, targeting a dividend yield double that of the S&P 500. The Sound Enhanced Fixed Income ETF (SDEF) seeks current income and capital appreciation from a mix of investment-grade and high-yield fixed income securities.

title: Pfizer study suggests vaccine works against virus variant
summary: A new study by Pfizer and researchers from the University of Texas Medical Branch in Galveston suggests that the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine is effective against the N501Y mutation found in the highly contagious coronavirus variants from Britain and South Africa. The preliminary lab tests, though not yet peer-reviewed, showed that antibodies from vaccinated individuals successfully fended off the virus with this mutation. While the vaccine also appeared effective against 15 other potential mutations, the E484K mutation found in the South African variant was not tested but is next on their research agenda.

title: Kuehne + Nagel lands global logistics deal for Moderna COVID-19 vaccine
summary: Kuehne + Nagel has secured a global logistics deal to manage the warehousing and distribution of Moderna Inc.'s COVID-19 vaccine outside of the U.S. This agreement follows the vaccine's approval in Europe and the U.K., with initial deliveries to European countries expected imminently. The logistics giant will leverage its extensive network and specialized pharmaceutical infrastructure to maintain the vaccine's critical cold chain requirements across Europe, Asia, the Middle East, Africa, and parts of the Americas.

title: Sanofi Ups Immunology Game With $1.4 Billion Acquisition of Kymab
summary: Sanofi is acquiring UK-based Kymab for $1.4 billion to strengthen its immunology pipeline, focusing on the human monoclonal antibody KY1005. KY1005 targets the immune system regulator OX40L and has shown promise in treating immune-mediated diseases and inflammatory disorders like atopic dermatitis. This acquisition is part of Sanofi's strategic expansion in core therapeutic areas, following previous deals for immuno-oncology and autoimmune disease assets.

title: Anche la famiglia miliardaria Stevanato investe in PatchAi, startup healthcare di un under 30
summary: PatchAi, an Italian digital health startup, has successfully closed a €1.7 million funding round, with the billionaire Stevanato family's investment vehicle, Sfem Italia, leading one of the tranches. This funding will enable PatchAi to expand its business into new therapeutic areas and scale internationally. The startup, which uses an AI-powered empathetic virtual assistant to improve patient engagement and clinical research, has already seen significant success with adherence rates up to 95% and partnerships with leading pharma companies like Novartis and Roche.

title: Can Global X's GNOM Become the Next Big ETF?
summary: The article discusses the potential of the Global X Genomics & Biotechnology ETF (GNOM) to become a major player in the biotechnology space, highlighting its strong performance and the high growth potential of the genomics industry. GNOM offers targeted exposure to emerging areas within healthcare, focusing on companies benefiting from advances in genomic science and biotechnology. The genomics field, which studies an organism's complete DNA, is poised for significant growth, with applications aimed at improving human health and longevity.

title: Pfizer Invests $120 Million In Four Clinical-stage Biotech Companies In H2 2020 - Quick Facts
summary: Pfizer Inc. announced investments totaling $120 million in four clinical-stage biotech companies during the second half of 2020 through its Pfizer Breakthrough Growth Initiative (PBGI). This program aims to provide funding and scientific expertise to promising clinical development programs in areas like oncology, rare disease, and inflammation & immunology. The investments include ESSA Pharma, Trillium Therapeutics, Vedanta Biosciences, and Homology Medicines, with Vedanta Biosciences planning to use its proceeds for a Phase 2 study in inflammatory bowel disease.

title: Israel’s Biond Biologics to get $125 million from Sanofi to develop cancer drug
summary: Israeli immunotherapy company Biond Biologics has secured a worldwide license agreement with French drugmaker Sanofi for the development and commercialization of its anti-tumor drug, BND-22. The deal includes an upfront payment of $125 million, with potential milestone payments reaching $1 billion, plus royalties. Biond will conduct the initial phase 1a clinical trial, while Sanofi will handle subsequent clinical development and commercialization.

title: Alum leads legal team for Pfizer's COVID-19 vaccine
summary: Douglas Lankler, J.D. ’90, executive vice president and general counsel at Pfizer, led the legal team for Pfizer's COVID-19 vaccine development and distribution. He discusses the intense public pressure, the unique legal challenges, and the efforts to rally employees during this unprecedented time. Lankler also touches on the management challenges faced by his remote legal team and the future of work post-pandemic.

title: Philippines approves Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine for emergency use
summary: The Philippines' Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted emergency use authorization (EUA) for the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine, effective immediately. FDA head Enrique Domingo stated that the known and potential benefits of the vaccine outweigh its risks. This approval follows Pfizer's EUA application submitted on December 23 last year, while other applications from Sinovac Biotech, AstraZeneca, and Gamaleya are still under review or awaiting approval.

title: Viatris to focus on partnerships, integration in the near term
summary: Viatris CEO Michael Goettler announced that the company's near-term strategy will heavily involve partnerships and licensing agreements to leverage its existing platform. This announcement comes as Viatris, formed from the merger of Mylan NV and Pfizer's Upjohn unit, has been undergoing significant strategic changes, including job reductions and factory closures, particularly its Morgantown plant. The focus on partnerships is a key part of shaping how the company moves forward.

title: Sinovac official defends vaccine’s effectiveness
summary: A senior official from Sinovac Biotech Ltd. defended the company's COVID-19 vaccine after trials in Brazil showed a lower efficacy rate than initially suggested, explaining that the Brazilian trials were conducted on high-risk health workers. In contrast, trials in Turkey indicated a higher effectiveness rate of 91.5%. The official highlighted that participants in vaccine trials with higher reported effectiveness, like BioNTech-Pfizer, were mostly ordinary citizens with lower infection risk.

title: Norway raises concern about Pfizer Covid-19 vaccine safety after 29 deaths
summary: Norway has raised concerns regarding the safety of Pfizer's Covid-19 vaccine after 29 elderly individuals with serious underlying health conditions died following vaccination. The Norwegian Medicines Agency is currently assessing these deaths, emphasizing that all reported fatalities were linked to elderly people with severe pre-existing disorders, as Pfizer's vaccine was the only one available in Norway at the time. This development led Australia, which had an agreement to acquire ten million doses, to await critical information from Pfizer and health authorities.

title: Global Orphan Drugs Market Research During 2021-2025 | Market Planning Structure | Technavio
summary: The global orphan drugs market is projected to grow by USD 138.70 billion between 2021 and 2025, driven by the increasing incidence of rare diseases and the emergence of combination therapies. Technavio's latest report provides a comprehensive analysis of market size, trends, growth drivers, challenges, and vendor landscape, including the impact of COVID-19. Key players such as AbbVie Inc., Novartis AG, and Pfizer Inc. are profiled in the report.

title: Nearly 12,000 doses of Moderna COVID-19 vaccines spoiled en route to Michigan
summary: Nearly 12,000 doses of Moderna COVID-19 vaccines spoiled due to temperature control issues during their delivery to Michigan. The 21 shipments, containing 11,900 doses, were being transported by McKesson Corp., a federal contractor for vaccine distribution. This incident occurred on January 17th.

title: Cabozantinib and Panitumumab for RAS Wild‐Type Metastatic Colorectal Cancer - Strickler - 2021
summary: This clinical trial investigates the combination of cabozantinib and panitumumab for treating RAS wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC), especially in patients who have developed resistance to anti-EGFR therapies due to MET amplification. The study established the maximum tolerated dose and recommended phase II dose, observing antitumor activity and improved tolerability with cabozantinib dose modifications. The findings suggest potential clinical benefit, warranting further research into biomarker identification and optimal dosing strategies.

title: Gene Therapy Comparability
summary: The inaugural Gene Therapy Comparability Summit aims to bring together large pharmaceutical companies and innovative biotechs to focus on effective and comparable manufacturing processes for gene therapies. The summit, featuring companies like Pfizer and Takeda, will address challenges in maintaining safety, quality, consistency, and efficacy during scale-up from clinical to commercial manufacturing, as well as satisfying regulatory demands. Experts will share insights on topics such as changing facilities and cell lines, developing bioassays, and handling limited gene therapy lots.

title: ViiV Healthcare announces FDA approval of Cabenuva (cabotegravir, rilpivirine), the first and only complete long-acting regimen for HIV treatment
summary: ViiV Healthcare announced that the FDA has approved Cabenuva, the first and only complete long-acting injectable regimen for HIV-1 treatment in adults. This innovative co-pack combines ViiV Healthcare’s cabotegravir and Janssen’s rilpivirine, enabling virologically suppressed adults to reduce their treatment dosing from 365 days to just 12 days per year. The approval is based on phase III ATLAS and FLAIR studies, demonstrating Cabenuva's effectiveness and patient preference over daily oral therapy.

title: The global fight- how close are Pfizer competitors to producing a vaccine of their own?
summary: As the COVID-19 pandemic continues, this article explores the progress of Pfizer's competitors in developing their own vaccines and treatment therapies. It highlights companies like Johnson & Johnson, Emergent BioSolutions Inc., and Merck, detailing their approaches, from single-dose vaccines and hyperimmune therapies to oral antiviral candidates and unique vaccine delivery methods. The piece also questions the long-term efficacy of rapidly developed first-generation vaccines and discusses the significant financial profits pharmaceutical companies stand to gain.

title: Here are MSCI’s five ESG trends to watch in 2021
summary: MSCI's report highlights five key ESG trends for 2021, including increased investor demand for decarbonization and Paris Agreement-aligned investments, a more nuanced understanding of ESG's financial benefits, growing concerns over biodiversity, a surge in ESG disclosure requirements, and a focus on financial innovation to address social inequality. The report emphasizes that climate change demands serious action, and investors will need to address complex issues ranging from environmental impact to social justice.

title: CDC quietly changes Covid vaccine guidance to OK mixing Pfizer and Moderna shots in 'exceptional situations'
summary: The CDC updated its Covid-19 vaccine guidance to allow for mixing Pfizer and Moderna shots in "exceptional situations," and to permit a delay of up to six weeks for the second dose. While not recommending routine mixing, the agency acknowledged the two mRNA vaccines are similar enough that it's unlikely to cause harm or reduce efficacy in rare cases where the original vaccine or record isn't available. This change aims to provide flexibility for clinicians during unusual circumstances, echoing similar guidance from the UK.

title: Pfizer To Supply 40 Million COVID-19 Shots For Poor Countries
summary: Pfizer has committed to supply up to 40 million doses of its COVID-19 vaccine to the WHO-backed COVAX program this year. This deal aims to provide affordable vaccines to 92 poor and middle-income countries, marking a significant step towards equitable global vaccine distribution. The companies will provide the vaccine at a "not-for-profit price" and help with the ultracold storage requirements.

title: Dubai: First doses of Pfizer vaccine to be rescheduled
summary: The Dubai Health Authority (DHA) announced that first-dose appointments for the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine will be rescheduled due to the manufacturer's production expansion impacting global supplies. While second-dose appointments remain unchanged, the DHA will notify recipients of new first-dose schedules via SMS. Dubai's free vaccination campaign began in December following the vaccine's approval.

title: Merck Shuts Down Covid Vaccine Program After Lackluster Data
summary: Merck & Co. is discontinuing the development of its two experimental Covid-19 vaccines after early trial data showed they failed to generate immune responses comparable to natural infection or existing vaccines. The company, which historically has had success with vaccines, will re-purpose its resources to focus on Covid-19 therapies instead. This decision follows a different strategy taken by Merck compared to rivals Pfizer Inc., Moderna Inc., and Johnson & Johnson, as Merck opted for a more traditional approach using weakened viruses.

title: COVAX to purchase up to 40 million COVID-19 vaccine doses from Pfizer and BioNTech
summary: COVAX has finalized an agreement to purchase up to 40 million doses of the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine. These doses, intended for 92 low- and lower-middle-income countries at a not-for-profit price, are expected to begin delivery in the first quarter of 2021. This initiative aims to ensure equitable global access to vaccines, with Pfizer and BioNTech also committing to support healthcare systems in developing countries for vaccine deployment.

title: Wayne State Seeks Volunteers for COVID-19 Vaccine Trial
summary: Wayne State University's School of Medicine is seeking volunteers for the Phase 3 clinical trial of a COVID-19 vaccine developed by Novavax, Inc. Initially targeting older, higher-risk individuals, the trial is now also recruiting younger adults, particularly those not yet eligible for Pfizer or Moderna vaccines. Dr. Elizabeth Secord, who is leading the trial at WSU, emphasizes the Novavax vaccine's safety and effectiveness, noting it does not use messenger RNA technology.

title: Pfizer to Deliver U.S. Vaccine Doses Faster Than Expected
summary: Pfizer Inc. announced plans to deliver 200 million Covid-19 vaccine doses to the U.S. by the end of May, which is two months ahead of their original schedule. This accelerated delivery is due to a labeling change, and the company is also developing a booster shot to combat emerging variants of the virus.

title: Sanofi, after R&D setback, lends a hand to vaccine rival Pfizer for coronavirus shot production
summary: Following a setback in its own vaccine development, Sanofi is partnering with Pfizer and BioNTech to produce 100 million doses of their rival COVID-19 vaccine for Europe in 2021. Sanofi will utilize its Frankfurt site, with first batches expected by August, demonstrating industry solidarity and leveraging its manufacturing capabilities. This move comes as Pfizer and BioNTech work to scale up production and as other vaccine producers face manufacturing challenges.

title: Sanofi to bottle BioNTech/Pfizer vaccine
summary: French pharmaceutical company Sanofi has signed a contract with Pfizer and BioNTech to bottle their coronavirus vaccine, aiming to provide 100 million doses for the EU by the end of the year. This initiative comes as Sanofi's own vaccine efforts faced setbacks, leading them to contribute to the collective vaccination effort by utilizing their Frankfurt factory. CEO Paul Hudson stated that while bottling is complex, the company remains committed to its own research and development.

title: Biden administration aims to have enough vaccine for most Americans by summertime
summary: President Biden announced plans to acquire an additional 200 million doses of COVID-19 vaccines from Pfizer/BioNTech and Moderna, bringing the total to 600 million, aiming to inoculate most Americans by summer. He also committed to increasing vaccine allocation to local governments. Despite these efforts, challenges like new virus variants and supply shortages remain as the administration pushes for a $1.9 trillion relief package.

title: Sanofi to Make Millions of BioNTech-Pfizer Vaccine Doses
summary: Sanofi has announced an agreement to produce millions of doses of the BioNTech-Pfizer coronavirus vaccine, an unusual collaboration aimed at accelerating vaccination efforts. The French drugmaker will make its production facility in Frankfurt available to BioNTech, with deliveries expected to begin this summer. This deal is projected to produce over 125 million doses of the mRNA vaccine for the European Union.

title: EU and AstraZeneca fight over vaccine delays while death toll mounts
summary: A dispute has escalated between the European Union and AstraZeneca over delays in COVID-19 vaccine deliveries. The EU criticizes AstraZeneca for not upholding its "moral, societal and contractual responsibilities," while AstraZeneca CEO Pascal Soriot states the company only agreed to a "best effort" to deliver doses, not a guaranteed schedule, attributing delays partly to the UK finalizing orders earlier. The spat threatens to sour relations and has led to EU threats of tightening controls on vaccine exports.

title: Pfizer Covid-19 Vaccine Works Against Mutations Found in U.K, South Africa Variants, Lab Study Finds
summary: A preliminary laboratory study by Pfizer found that its Covid-19 vaccine is effective against coronavirus mutations identified in the U.K. and South Africa. While antibodies were slightly less effective against the South Africa variant, the overall impact on vaccine effectiveness was small. These findings, though not yet peer-reviewed, suggest that current vaccines may offer protection against new strains.

title: Lilly strikes deal to acquire drug for chronic pain
summary: Eli Lilly has announced a deal to acquire the rights to an experimental chronic pain drug, AK1780, from Japan's Asahi Kahei Pharma. The initial payment is $20 million, with potential milestone payments up to $210 million for development and $180 million for sales achievements. This acquisition further expands Lilly's pain treatment pipeline, which already includes migraine drugs Emgality and Reyvow, and a non-opioid pain drug, tanezumab, developed with Pfizer.

title: Eli Lilly CEO David Ricks on treating coronavirus amid threat of new strains
summary: Eli Lilly CEO David Ricks discusses the company's antibody treatments for COVID-19 and the challenges posed by new strains of the virus. He emphasizes the importance of vaccination, robust genomic testing, and international surveillance to combat the evolving pandemic. Ricks also touches on the administration of antibody therapies, the need for enhanced public health infrastructure, and the potential impact of corporate tax rate changes on pharmaceutical manufacturing.

title: $ 1,299 Billion Growth in Global Health and Wellness Market During 2020-2024 | Featuring Key Vendors Including Bayer AG, Brunswick Corp., and Core Health & Fitness LLC | Technavio
summary: Technavio projects the global health and wellness market to grow by USD 1,299.84 billion at over 6% CAGR from 2020-2024, with 32% of this growth originating from the APAC region. The market's expansion is driven by increasing emphasis on health and well-being, rising disposable incomes, and a growing middle-class population, despite a negative impact from COVID-19. Key vendors highlighted include Bayer AG, Brunswick Corp., and Core Health & Fitness LLC, all contributing to various aspects of health and wellness products and services.

title: Novavax says its Covid-19 vaccine is 90% effective, but far less so against one variant
summary: Novavax announced that its Covid-19 vaccine demonstrated nearly 90% effectiveness in a UK trial, but showed significantly reduced efficacy, only 49%, against a new variant in South Africa. Despite the lower efficacy against the South African variant, experts emphasize the vaccine's overall potential and the ongoing work to develop booster shots and ensure a diverse range of vaccine technologies. Novavax, a company new to market its own product, received $1.6 billion from Operation Warp Speed and expects to produce 2 billion doses in 2021.

title: Johnson & Johnson' single-shot vaccine is 66 percent effective against COVID-19
summary: Johnson & Johnson's single-shot COVID-19 vaccine demonstrated 66% effectiveness against moderate to severe illness in a global study. While this is less than two-shot rivals, its single-dose nature and refrigerator storage requirements make it a valuable option for accelerating global vaccination efforts, especially in regions with logistical challenges. The company plans to seek emergency use authorization soon and aims to supply 100 million doses to the U.S. by June.

title: Novartis signs initial agreement to provide manufacturing capacity for Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine
summary: Novartis has signed an initial agreement with BioNTech to support the production of the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine. Novartis will use its aseptic manufacturing facilities in Stein, Switzerland, to fill bulk mRNA active ingredient into vials. Production is expected to begin in the second quarter of 2021, with initial shipments anticipated in the third quarter.

title: FTC Approves Merger of Pfizer’s Upjohn and Mylan N.V., with Caveats
summary: The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has approved the merger of Pfizer's Upjohn division and Mylan N.V. to form Viatris Inc., following resolution of antitrust concerns. The approval requires the divestiture of rights and assets in seven generic drug markets and conditional permission from the FTC for future involvement in three other specified markets. The FTC's final order was approved by a 3-2 vote.

title: Novartis joins Sanofi in aiding manufacture of coronavirus vaccines
summary: Novartis announced it will assist Pfizer and BioNTech in manufacturing their coronavirus vaccine by filling vials at its Swiss facility, following a similar agreement made by Sanofi. This highlights a growing trend of pharmaceutical companies collaborating to ramp up global vaccine supply amid the ongoing pandemic and the emergence of new, more transmissible variants. Novartis is also in discussions with other companies to produce raw materials for various COVID-19 treatments and vaccines.

title: Novartis Signs Pact to Help Produce Pfizer-BioNTech Vaccine
summary: Novartis AG has announced an agreement to assist in the production of the Pfizer-BioNTech Covid-19 vaccine. This collaboration aims to alleviate supply concerns and increase vaccine availability. Production is slated to begin in the second quarter, with delivery expected in the third quarter from Novartis's Swiss manufacturing facilities.

title: Protalix BioTherapeutics Announces Presentations at the 17th Annual WORLDSymposium™ 2021
summary: Protalix BioTherapeutics announced it would deliver an oral and a poster presentation at the 17th Annual WORLDSymposium™ 2021, an event focused on lysosomal diseases. The presentations will highlight data from its BRIDGE Phase III open-label study evaluating pegunigalsidase alfa for Fabry disease. The oral presentation is scheduled for February 10, 2021, at 1:24 PM EST, and the poster presentation will be from 2:30 to 3:30 PM EST on the same day.

title: Moderna Increases COVID-19 Vaccine Shipments While Pfizer Lags Behind
summary: Moderna significantly increased its COVID-19 vaccine shipments to states, while Pfizer's increase was minimal. Both companies need to boost production to meet contractual goals of 100 million doses each by the end of March. The article also highlights the need for greater transparency from vaccine manufacturers regarding their supply numbers.

title: BPX Energy is bringing drilling rigs back to Texas
summary: BPX Energy, the U.S. shale oil business of BP plc, is reinstating drilling rigs in Texas. The CEO stated that the Denver-based division's Texas holdings have exceeded expectations. This move signals a renewed focus on drilling operations in the region.

title: Moderna Vaccine Distributor McKesson Has Shipped 25 Million Doses in U.S.
summary: McKesson Corp., the federal distributor for Moderna's Covid-19 vaccine, announced it had shipped over 25 million doses across the U.S. by the end of January. The company, which also distributes vaccination supply kits, has significant capacity for more distributions and expects this work to boost its earnings. Pfizer and BioNTech operate a separate distribution network for their vaccine.

title: Amgen Reports Fourth Quarter And Full Year 2020 Financial Results
summary: Amgen reported strong financial results for the fourth quarter and full year 2020, with total revenues increasing 7% and 9% respectively, driven by higher volume growth of key products like Otezla, MVASI, KANJINTI, and Repatha. Despite the ongoing impact of COVID-19, the company advanced its pipeline and provided 2021 revenue guidance between $25.8 billion and $26.6 billion, alongside EPS guidance. The report also detailed product sales performance by geographic region and product, along with updates on its clinical pipeline, including sotorasib and tezepelumab.

title: Comparing the Covid-19 vaccines developed by Pfizer, Moderna, and Johnson & Johnson
summary: This article provides a detailed comparison of the Covid-19 vaccines developed by Pfizer, Moderna, and Johnson & Johnson, covering their types, target populations, efficacy, number of doses, durability of protection, booster status, mix-and-match booster options, vaccine uptake, side-effect profiles, safety during pregnancy, and storage requirements. It highlights the differences in mRNA and viral vector technology, varying efficacy rates, and the evolving challenges each vaccine has faced since its introduction. The article was last updated on January 31, 2022, reflecting ongoing developments in vaccine science and policy.

title: Everything we know about Johnson & Johnson’s single-dose Covid-19 vaccine
summary: Johnson & Johnson's single-dose Covid-19 vaccine, developed by its subsidiary Janssen, showed promising results in phase 3 clinical trials, preventing 66% of Covid-19 cases overall, 85% of moderate-to-severe cases, and 100% of deaths. Its single-dose format and refrigeration requirements could significantly ease global distribution compared to other two-dose vaccines. The company plans to submit its data to the FDA for emergency use authorization, potentially making it the third vaccine available in the US.

title: Charlie Scharf’s no-nonsense style could create a more stable Wells Fargo
summary: This article discusses Wells Fargo CEO Charlie Scharf's no-nonsense management style, honed during his time with Jamie Dimon, as he works to stabilize the scandal-ridden bank. It also touches on NASDAQ CEO Adena Friedman's defense of new board diversity requirements and news of Jeff Bezos stepping down as Amazon CEO, with Andy Jassy taking over. Other topics include the effectiveness of Russia's Sputnik V vaccine, AstraZeneca's vaccine data, and the GameStop stock plunge.

title: Johnson & Johnson asks US to approve single-dose COVID jab
summary: Johnson & Johnson has requested emergency use authorization from the US FDA for its single-dose COVID-19 vaccine. This vaccine, which demonstrated 66% efficacy in trials, offers advantages over existing options as it does not require a second shot or freezing for storage, simplifying distribution. The US has already secured 100 million doses of J&J's vaccine, with an option for 200 million more, aiming to boost the country's immunization efforts.

title: Johnson & Johnson asks U.S. regulators to approve its one-shot COVID-19 vaccine
summary: Johnson & Johnson has requested U.S. regulatory approval for its single-dose COVID-19 vaccine, which showed strong protection against moderate to severe illness in trials. This easier-to-use option could boost vaccine supplies, although its efficacy appeared slightly lower than two-dose vaccines from Pfizer and Moderna. The FDA will review the data before deciding on authorization.

title: Pfizer withdraws vaccine application in India
summary: Pfizer has withdrawn its application for emergency use authorization of its BioNTech-Pfizer coronavirus vaccine in India after the Indian health regulator requested local trials and expressed concerns about a lack of immunogenicity data. The company plans to submit a new application with additional information. Key challenges include the need for local trials and the ultra-cold storage requirements of the vaccine, which are difficult to meet in India.

title: Pfizer withdraws application for emergency use of its Covid-19 vaccine in India
summary: Pfizer has withdrawn its application for emergency-use authorization of its Covid-19 vaccine in India, developed with Germany's BioNTech. The company's decision came after discussions with India's drugs regulator, which sought additional information and indicated a need for local trials. Pfizer plans to re-submit its application in the future once more information becomes available.

title: Pfizer drops India vaccine application after regulator seeks local trial
summary: Pfizer has withdrawn its application for emergency-use authorization of its COVID-19 vaccine in India. This decision came after the Indian drug regulator, CDSCO, requested a local safety and immunogenicity study, which Pfizer was unwilling to undertake given prior approvals elsewhere. Consequently, the vaccine will not be immediately available in India, one of the world's most populous countries.

title: Pfizer drops India vaccine application after regulator seeks local trial
summary: Pfizer Inc. withdrew its application for emergency-use authorization of its COVID-19 vaccine in India after the regulator demanded a local safety and immunogenicity study. This decision means the vaccine will not be available in India and China in the near future. Pfizer intends to re-engage with the Indian authorities and resubmit its request with additional information.

title: Malin-backed Immunocore files for $258m Nasdaq IPO
summary: Immunocore, a UK biotech company partially owned by Dublin-listed Malin, has filed for a $258 million IPO on the Nasdaq. The company plans to use the proceeds to advance its lead product, an eye cancer therapy, through its phase-three clinical trial and prepare for its commercial launch, as well as fund other product candidates. Malin retains a 6 percent stake in Immunocore, valued at approximately €51 million, and will not participate in the IPO.

title: South Africa pauses rollout of AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine
summary: South Africa has halted its planned rollout of the AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine after a small study indicated it offered little to no protection against the dominant B.1.351 variant circulating in the country. The nation will instead use vaccines from Johnson & Johnson and Pfizer. This decision follows research from Oxford University and the University of the Witwatersrand, which found the AstraZeneca vaccine ineffective against mild-to-moderate infection from the variant, although no severe cases were reported in the trial.

title: Private Equity Health Care Acquisitions – January 2021
summary: This article by the Private Equity Stakeholder Project (PESP) tracks private equity-backed healthcare acquisitions in January 2021, highlighting the growing investor interest and associated risks. It details acquisitions by firms like Levine Leichtman Capital Partners and Audax Group, noting past legal issues faced by some of their portfolio companies, including alleged billing fraud. The report provides a comprehensive list of add-on acquisitions and new PE investments/buyouts from the specified month.

title: ViiV Healthcare receives Marketing Authorisation for Rukobia (fostemsavir), a first-in-class attachment inhibitor in combination with other antiretrovirals for the treatment of adults with multidrug-resistant HIV
summary: ViiV Healthcare, a global specialist HIV company, has received European Marketing Authorisation for Rukobia (fostemsavir) for adults with multidrug-resistant HIV-1 infection who have limited treatment options. Fostemsavir is a first-in-class attachment inhibitor that blocks HIV from attaching to host cells and has demonstrated sustained virologic suppression and clinically significant CD4+ T-cell recovery in trials. This approval addresses a critical unmet need for heavily treatment-experienced patients.

title: Understanding the pharmaceutical lifecycle and the benefits of a menu-driven approach
summary: This article discusses the evolution of the biopharmaceutical industry towards full-service contract development and manufacturing organizations (CDMOs) and highlights Avid Bioservices' menu-driven approach. Avid Bioservices, a clinical and commercial CDMO, offers flexible services that support projects of various sizes and stages, helping clients avoid the pitfalls of all-or-nothing contracts. The company emphasizes its extensive regulatory compliance, manufacturing capabilities, and analytical services designed to meet diverse client needs throughout the pharmaceutical lifecycle.

title: The list of Montreal's top employers for 2021 has been released
summary: The 2021 list of Montreal's Top Employers has been announced, recognizing 60 companies that provide exceptional work environments. Organized by Canada's Top 100 Employers, the competition evaluates criteria such as physical workplace, benefits, training, and community involvement. Employers are compared within their industries, with winners ranging from large corporations to local businesses across various sectors.

title: BioNTech starts vaccine production at new site in Germany
summary: BioNTech has started production of its COVID-19 vaccine at a new facility in Marburg, Germany, aiming to significantly boost the EU's vaccine supply. The company plans to produce 250 million doses in Marburg in the first half of 2021 and expects annual capacity to reach 750 million doses. This move comes as the EU faced delays in vaccine shipments, and BioNTech aims to meet its contractual commitments and increase deliveries.

title: Walmart, Sam's Club pharmacies to begin COVID-19 vaccines Friday
summary: Walmart and Sam's Club pharmacies are set to begin administering COVID-19 vaccines on Friday across more than 1,000 locations in 22 states, focusing on underserved communities. This initiative is part of the Federal Retail Pharmacy Program, with Walmart aiming to deliver up to 13 million doses per month when supplies allow. The company emphasizes its commitment to providing vaccine access, particularly in rural and underserved areas, likening it to receiving a flu shot.

title: Target offering employees incentives to get COVID-19 vaccines
summary: Target is providing incentives to its employees to encourage COVID-19 vaccination, including up to four hours of pay for hourly staff and free Lyft rides to vaccine appointments. This initiative aligns with similar efforts from other essential businesses like Trader Joe's and Instacart, aiming to ensure ease of access to the vaccine for its workforce. However, Target will not mandate the vaccine for employment.

title: TDM and T2T – Perfect Partners?
summary: This article explores the relationship between therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) and treat-to-target (T2T) strategies in managing Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD). It discusses the development and effectiveness of TDM for anti-TNF monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) and evaluates clinical trials that have investigated whether combining TDM with T2T regimens improves patient outcomes. The authors conclude that while TDM has value, especially for higher-risk patients or when used proactively, its overall benefit in improving long-term remission in IBD across a general population remains unclear.

title: Bristol Myers Takes $470 Million Write-off and Scraps Orva-Cel CAR-T Program
summary: Bristol Myers Squibb has decided to abandon its orva-cel CAR-T therapy, taking a $470 million write-off, despite recent FDA approval for another CAR-T therapy, Breyanzi (liso-cel), and an upcoming PDUFA date for ide-cel. The company's head of drug development explained this decision by stating ide-cel is considered the frontrunner in the crowded BCMA field, and the orva-cel platform will be utilized for next-generation CAR cell development rather than the current medicine itself. This move follows a period where a $6.4 billion Contingent Value Rights payout, tied to the approval of liso-cel, ide-cel, and Zeposia, was terminated due to delays, partly caused by the COVID-19 pandemic affecting FDA inspections.

title: Amicus drug for Pompe disease falls short in key clinical trial, but company will push for approval
summary: Amicus Therapeutics announced that its Pompe disease drug did not prove superior to the current standard treatment in a large clinical trial. Despite this, the company believes the results, combined with other patient benefit data, are sufficient for regulatory approvals and plans to submit to the FDA in Q2, with other global filings to follow. CEO John Crowley expressed confidence in the drug's profound effect and its potential to become a new standard of care.

title: Here’s how the Johnson and Johnson vaccine compares to others
summary: A new single-dose COVID-19 vaccine from Johnson & Johnson is under FDA review. While its overall efficacy at 66% is lower than Moderna and Pfizer, it is 85% effective against severe cases and doesn't require ultracold storage, making it easier to distribute globally. The vaccine also showed efficacy against new variants during its trials, a critical advantage for mass immunization.

title: Teva CEO Sees Risks in Relying on China for Drug Ingredients
summary: Teva CEO Kåre Schultz expressed concerns about the global reliance on China for essential drug ingredients, specifically highlighting the risks observed during the early stages of the Covid-19 pandemic. The outbreak raised fears that disruptions in the supply of pharmaceutical components from China could severely impact the world's drug supply. Schultz's testimony to a House committee touched on these supply chain vulnerabilities.

title: VERU-111 Elicits Early Efficacy Signals in Pretreated mCRPC
summary: A phase 1b study of VERU-111, a novel tubulin inhibitor, demonstrated early antitumor activity and a well-tolerated safety profile in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) who had previously failed androgen receptor-targeting agents. The drug showed PSA declines in a significant number of patients, with some achieving partial responses and prolonged treatment without progression. A phase 2 trial is ongoing, and a pivotal phase 3 VERACITY trial is set to launch based on positive discussions with the FDA.

title: The factory that's racing to make Johnson & Johnson's COVID-19 vaccine
summary: Emergent BioSolutions, a U.S. drug maker, is working to accelerate the production of Johnson & Johnson's COVID-19 vaccine. The company, which has a history of government contracts for biodefense medicines, was selected by the Obama administration to build a facility designed to quickly ramp up vaccine production during pandemics. Despite challenges and concerns about delays, Emergent is confident in its ability to fulfill the order, benefiting from aggressive contracting measures like the Defense Production Act.

title: Japanese government committee approves Pfizer's COVID-19 vaccine - NHK
summary: A Japanese government health panel has approved Pfizer Inc.'s COVID-19 vaccine for use, marking the first such approval in Japan. Vaccinations are slated to begin in the middle of next week, initially targeting 10,000 health workers. The government aims to secure sufficient supplies to vaccinate the entire population by mid-year.

title: Laurent Levy and Tanguy Lim-Seiwert, MD, on the Potential of NBTXR3 to Treat Patients With Head and Neck Cancers
summary: Laurent Levy, CEO of Nanobiotix, and Tanguy Lim-Seiwert, MD, of John Hopkins Medicine, discussed the potential of NBTXR3, a radio enhancer designed to destroy tumors using physics when activated by radiotherapy. NBTXR3 has shown positive results in trials, including a phase 3 soft tissue sarcoma trial in Europe. This approach aims to benefit millions of cancer patients by introducing physics into cell treatment.

title: Japan approves its first COVID-19 vaccine
summary: Japan officially approved its first COVID-19 vaccine, co-developed by Pfizer Inc., for nationwide inoculations. While marking a significant step, the rollout is months behind many other countries due to Japan's requirement for local clinical testing, despite a fast-track approval process. The country plans to vaccinate front-line medical workers first, followed by others, with concerns remaining over reliance on imports and the pace of vaccination before the Tokyo Olympics.

title: What you need to know about severe reactions to COVID vaccines
summary: This article addresses common concerns about COVID-19 vaccine side effects, focusing on serious allergic reactions (anaphylaxis) and reported deaths. It clarifies that while some deaths occurred shortly after vaccination, medical specialists found no direct connection to the vaccines, particularly among the elderly and frail. The piece also details the rarity and management of anaphylaxis, noting that the risk from COVID-19 infection far outweighs the vaccine's risks.

title: Warren Buffett’s Berkshire Hathaway Bought Verizon and Chevron. Here’s What Else It Traded.
summary: Warren Buffett’s Berkshire Hathaway made notable changes to its investment portfolio during the fourth quarter. Beyond the acquisitions of Verizon Communications and Chevron, the company also bought Merck, Bristol-Myers, and AbbVie. Concurrently, Berkshire Hathaway divested its holdings in Pfizer and trimmed some of its Apple stock.

title: Waste employers prep COVID-19 vaccine plans as most workers still await shots
summary: Waste management companies and associations are preparing vaccination plans and encouraging workers to get shots, despite most waste and recycling employees still awaiting vaccine access in early state rollouts. While some advocacy to prioritize these essential workers has occurred, organizations like SWANA and NWRA are focusing on educating members and sharing information from health agencies. Companies such as Waste Management, Casella Waste Systems, and Republic Services are offering incentives like paid time off for vaccinations, though none are mandating them.

title: N. Korean hackers tried to steal Pfizer vaccine know-how, lawmaker says
summary: South Korea's intelligence agency reported that North Korea attempted to hack Pfizer Inc to steal information on coronavirus vaccines and treatments. This incident is part of a broader trend of state-backed hacking groups targeting health and pharmaceutical entities during the COVID-19 pandemic. North Korea, facing international sanctions, is suspected of seeking to sell stolen data rather than develop its own vaccine, despite being slated to receive AstraZeneca-Oxford vaccines through COVAX.

title: Bristol Myers Squibb, Sanofi to pay $834m in Plavix case
summary: A US judge in Hawaii ordered Bristol Myers Squibb Co and Sanofi SA to pay over $834 million for failing to properly warn non-white patients about health risks associated with their jointly-created blood thinner, Plavix. The companies engaged in deceptive practices by not changing the drug's label to reflect risks, particularly for patients of color who may not metabolize the drug effectively. Both companies have vowed to appeal the ruling, stating the decision is "unsupported by the law and at odds with the evidence at trial."

title: 10 biotechs become 1: Centessa launches with $250M to prove unorthodox R&D model
summary: Centessa Pharmaceuticals has launched with $250 million in funding, formed from the merger of 10 startups backed by Medicxi. The company aims to scale Medicxi's "asset-centric" R&D model by providing centralized resources while allowing subsidiaries to operate autonomously.
