summary: The global Apixaban (Eliquis) market is projected to grow at a CAGR of 7.5% through 2030, driven by the increasing prevalence of venous thromboembolism-related illnesses and more therapeutic indications for the drug. Key market segments include tablets and capsules, various distribution channels like hospitals and online pharmacies, and oral or injectable administration. North America is expected to lead this market, with major players including Abbott, Bristol-Myers Squibb, and Pfizer.

title: In venue fit for head of state, Suga seeks vaccine from Pfizer CEO
summary: Japanese Prime Minister Yoshihide Suga met with Pfizer CEO Albert Bourla in a high-profile setting to secure vaccine deliveries amid concerns about supply and a growing outbreak in Japan. Suga requested Bourla to accelerate the delivery of 20 million doses planned for October, thanking him for vaccine donations for Olympic participants. Japan is facing a resurgence of COVID-19 cases and a lagging vaccination rate, especially among younger people, despite criticism for prioritizing the Olympics.

title: Arvinas and Pfizer enter up to $2.4bn deal to develop breast cancer drug
summary: Arvinas and Pfizer have formed a global partnership to develop and commercialize ARV-471, an investigational breast cancer therapy. The deal includes an upfront payment of $650 million from Pfizer, a $350 million equity investment, and up to $1.4 billion in milestone payments for Arvinas. The companies will equally share development costs and profits for ARV-471, which is an oral PROTAC estrogen receptor protein degrader currently in Phase II trials.

title: As Olympics begin, Japan rolls out red carpet for Pfizer CEO
summary: Japan's Prime Minister Yoshihide Suga met with Pfizer CEO Albert Bourla to secure COVID-19 vaccine deliveries amid concerns over dwindling supply and a surging outbreak, coinciding with the start of the Olympics. Japan's vaccination rate lags, with only 23% of its population fully vaccinated, prompting Suga to request accelerated delivery of 20 million doses. Bourla, in Tokyo for the Olympics opening, also discussed with Suga the donation of Pfizer vaccines for Olympic participants.

title: Pfizer, Johnson & Johnson settle high-profile Remicade biosim lawsuit on undisclosed terms
summary: Pfizer and Johnson & Johnson have settled their nearly four-year legal battle over the competitive practices surrounding J&J's immunology blockbuster Remicade and Pfizer's biosimilar, Inflectra. The terms of the settlement, which ended a groundbreaking case that was expected to be a bellwether for the biosimilar industry, remain undisclosed. Pfizer had accused J&J of using "exclusionary contracts" to stifle competition for Inflectra, though both companies released statements affirming their commitment to patient access and a competitive market.

title: Pfizer Inks Second Collaboration with Arvinas, Makes Billion-Dollar Investment on a Novel Agent for Breast Cancer Therapy
summary: Pfizer and Arvinas have entered a second collaboration, with Pfizer investing over a billion dollars in Arvinas' lead immuno-oncology candidate, ARV-471, for breast cancer therapy. The deal includes a $650 million upfront payment and a $350 million equity investment from Pfizer. This partnership aims to accelerate the development and commercialization of ARV-471, a targeted protein degrader for ER-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer, building on a previous 2018 collaboration.

title: WORLD – Covid vaccine maker BioNTech attempts shot for malaria next
summary: BioNTech, the company behind a successful Covid-19 vaccine, is now venturing into developing a malaria vaccine using mRNA technology. This initiative marks BioNTech's first solo project and new infectious disease effort since the pandemic, aiming to start patient trials by late next year. The project also focuses on building manufacturing infrastructure in Africa for future mRNA vaccines, addressing the significant global health burden of malaria.

title: Pfizer says 2021 COVID-19 vaccine sales to top $33.5 bln, sees need for boosters
summary: Pfizer has increased its 2021 sales forecast for its COVID-19 vaccine to $33.5 billion and believes a third booster dose will be necessary to maintain high protection against the virus, especially the Delta variant. The company also suggested filing for emergency use authorization for a booster as early as August, citing data showing significantly increased antibody levels after a third dose. This comes amidst declining vaccine efficacy over time and ongoing discussions with regulators about booster shots for certain populations, while billions globally still await their first dose.

title: Driven by Profits from Antibiotics, Animal Health Industry Is Feeding Risks of ‘Superbugs’ & Next Pandemic
summary: A new report by the FAIRR Initiative warns that the animal health industry's uncontrolled use of antibiotics in intensively farmed livestock is fueling a global "superbug" crisis and increasing the risk of the next pandemic. The report criticizes 10 major animal health companies for marketing critical drugs as growth promoters and preventative medications, contributing to misuse and overuse in livestock. It highlights that 70% of global antibiotics are given to animals and calls for better stewardship, alternative treatments like vaccines and probiotics, and clearer labeling to prevent antibiotic resistance.

title: GSK and Vir Biotechnology announce Joint Procurement Agreement with European Commission for COVID-19 treatment, sotrovimab
summary: GSK and Vir Biotechnology have signed a Joint Procurement Agreement with the European Commission to supply up to 220,000 doses of sotrovimab, an investigational single-dose COVID-19 treatment. This agreement will allow participating EU Member States to purchase sotrovimab for high-risk patients following local or EU-level emergency authorization. Sotrovimab demonstrated a 79% reduction in hospitalizations or death in the Phase 3 COMET-ICE trial and has shown activity against circulating variants, including Delta and Lambda.

title: Sanofi raises profit forecast after second quarter beat
summary: Sanofi has increased its 2021 profit forecast after exceeding second-quarter expectations, driven by strong sales of its vaccines and eczema treatment, Dupixent. The French drugmaker now targets an earnings per share growth of approximately 12% and remains confident in its COVID-19 vaccine project with GlaxoSmithKline, expecting regulatory approval by year-end. Despite its vaccine coming later than competitors, Sanofi believes it will play a significant role globally and as a potential booster shot.

title: Pfizer backs protein degrader drugs with Arvinas deal
summary: Pfizer is investing $1 billion in Arvinas, a Yale University spin-out, to commercialize ARV-471, a protein degrader drug for breast cancer. This significant investment comprises a $350 million equity investment and $650 million cash upfront, building on a previous licensing deal from 2018. ARV-471, a proteolysis targeting chimera (Protac), targets the oestrogen receptor and is currently in Phase 2 clinical trials, with Phase 3 studies planned for metastatic breast cancer.

title: 1.5 Million Pfizer Vaccine Doses, Donated by the United States, Arrive in Thailand
summary: The United States donated 1.5 million doses of Pfizer COVID-19 vaccine to Thailand, with an additional one million doses committed, reaffirming U.S. support and partnership in fighting the pandemic. This donation is part of President Biden's commitment to provide safe and effective vaccinations globally and help accelerate vaccination campaigns in the region. The Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine, developed by American and German companies, is 95 percent effective and was the first to receive WHO emergency use authorization.

title: New Harvard-MIT Biotech Center Appoints CEO, Begins Construction on Facility
summary: The newly named Landmark Bio, a Harvard-MIT biotech center, has appointed Ran Zheng as its inaugural CEO and begun construction on a 40,000 square-foot facility in Watertown, Mass. This public-private partnership aims to accelerate the production and delivery of new treatment technologies through collaborations between academics, biopharma, and medical leaders. The facility will focus on cell and gene therapy, gene editing, and messenger RNA products, partnering with several Harvard Medical School affiliates and the Massachusetts Life Science Center.

title: Pfizer and Moderna raise prices for COVID-19 vaccines in EU- FT
summary: Pfizer and Moderna have increased the prices of their COVID-19 vaccines for new supply contracts with the European Union, according to the Financial Times. Pfizer's shot rose to 19.50 euros from 15.50 euros, while Moderna's vaccine is now priced at $25.50, up from about 19 euros previously, though this is lower than an earlier agreed $28.50 due to a larger order volume. Both companies declined to comment on the confidential contract details.

title: Forecast: Analysts Think Pfizer Inc.'s (NYSE:PFE) Business Prospects Have Improved Drastically
summary: Analysts have significantly upgraded Pfizer Inc.'s revenue and earnings per share forecasts for 2021, indicating a drastic improvement in business fundamentals. Despite these optimistic revisions, the consensus price target remains largely unchanged, suggesting that the long-term impact on the stock's valuation is still uncertain. Pfizer is projected to grow much faster than in the past and outperform its industry competitors in revenue growth, although some warning flags related to its balance sheet have been identified.

title: Sanofi bets $3.2B on mRNA with deal to buy Translate Bio
summary: Sanofi is acquiring its research partner Translate Bio for $3.2 billion, signaling a major commitment to messenger RNA (mRNA) technology. This acquisition leverages the success of mRNA in COVID-19 vaccines and aims to expand its application to other vaccines, immunology, oncology, and rare diseases. The deal is expected to close in the third quarter of the year, with Sanofi already owning a 6.5% stake in Translate Bio.

title: Pfizer to require U.S. workers receive COVID-19 vaccine or regular tests
summary: Pfizer will require all its U.S. employees and contractors to either get vaccinated against COVID-19 or undergo weekly testing. This policy aims to protect the health and safety of their staff and the community. Employees with medical or religious objections can seek accommodations, while international staff are strongly encouraged to get vaccinated where possible.

title: Moderna COVID-19 vaccine remains 93% effective after six months
summary: Moderna announced that its COVID-19 vaccine maintains 93% effectiveness six months after the second dose, generating over $4 billion in second-quarter sales and driving the company to a significant profit. The company is also developing other vaccines and a potential COVID-19 booster shot, with second-quarter earnings surpassing Wall Street expectations.

title: Moderna's Covid vaccine 93 percent effective six months after second dose, company says
summary: Moderna announced its Covid-19 vaccine maintained 93% effectiveness six months after the second dose, comparable to its initial clinical trial results. However, the company stated that a booster shot would likely be necessary before winter due to waning antibody levels, especially in light of the Delta variant. Moderna also confirmed robust antibody responses from its booster candidates against several variants and detailed significant vaccine contract sales for 2021 and 2022.

title: Gemcitabine and APG-1252, a novel small molecule inhibitor of BCL-2/BCL-XL, display a synergistic antitumor effect in nasopharyngeal carcinoma through the JAK-2/STAT3/MCL-1 signaling pathway
summary: This study investigates the synergistic antitumor effect of gemcitabine and APG-1252, a novel BCL-2/BCL-XL inhibitor, in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). The combination therapy demonstrated enhanced anti-proliferation, apoptosis induction, and suppression of invasion and migration in NPC cells both in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, this synergistic effect is attributed to the activation of caspase-dependent pathways and the blocking of the JAK-2/STAT3/MCL-1 signaling pathway.

title: Novavax’s Vaccine Works Well — Except on Variant First Found in South Africa (Published 2021)
summary: Novavax announced that its COVID-19 vaccine is highly effective, showing nearly 90% efficacy in a large trial in Britain. However, the vaccine's efficacy dropped significantly to just under 50% in a smaller South African trial, where the B.1.351 variant was prevalent. This finding highlights the challenge of mutating viruses and prompted Novavax to develop a new vaccine specifically targeting the South African variant.

title: Israeli survey finds 3rd Pfizer vaccine dose has similar side effects to 2nd
summary: An initial Israeli survey found that most people who received a third dose of Pfizer's COVID-19 vaccine experienced similar or fewer side effects compared to their second dose. The survey by Clalit, Israel's largest healthcare provider, involved about 4,500 people over 60 who received booster shots. The findings suggest the booster is well-tolerated, with soreness at the injection site being the most common side effect.

title: WSJ News Exclusive | RNA Tech Firm GreenLight Biosciences to Go Public in $1.5 Billion SPAC Deal
summary: GreenLight Biosciences Inc., an RNA-technology firm, is set to go public through a $1.5 billion SPAC deal, combining with Environmental Impact Acquisition Corp. The company is developing mRNA vaccines for Covid-19 and other diseases, including a seasonal flu shot and a treatment for sickle-cell disease. Additionally, GreenLight Biosciences is working on RNA-based sustainable alternatives to pesticides and herbicides.

title: Pfizer, BioNTech seek US COVID-19 vaccine clearance for children 5-11
summary: Pfizer Inc and BioNTech SE have requested emergency use authorization from US regulators for their COVID-19 vaccine for children aged 5 to 11. This age group currently has no approved COVID-19 vaccine. The FDA's advisory panel is scheduled to meet on October 26 to discuss the application, potentially paving the way for around 28 million children to receive the two-dose vaccine.

title: Sanofi, eyeing impurity concerns, pulls hypertension meds in Korea and the U.K. Could the next big 'sartan' recall be on the horizon?
summary: Sanofi has pulled several hypertension medications containing irbesartan in Korea and the U.K. due to concerns about azido impurities. This action follows similar sartan drug recalls triggered by regulatory bodies in Canada and Europe. The impurity, a potential mutagen, raises cancer risk concerns, and Sanofi's proactive recall in Korea is a precautionary measure while testing for azido impurities in older batches is ongoing.

title: Pfizer shares hit record high with COVID-19 vaccine stocks on a tear
summary: Shares of Pfizer Inc. reached a new record high on Tuesday, the first time in over 20 years, as investor interest in COVID-19 vaccine makers surged amidst rising coronavirus cases in the United States. Analysts suggest that investors are finally giving Pfizer credit for its vaccine, viewing it not just as a one-time cash infusion but as a durable business due to the ongoing pandemic and potential for vaccine technology in other diseases. This rally also coincides with strong performances from other vaccine companies like Moderna and BioNTech, with Pfizer forecasting $33.5 billion in COVID-19 vaccine sales for 2021.

title: India in talks to buy 50 million doses of Pfizer vaccine - WSJ
summary: India is reportedly in talks to acquire 50 million doses of the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine, as confirmed by the Wall Street Journal and a Pfizer spokesperson. This move aims to bolster India's vaccination efforts, which have primarily relied on the AstraZeneca vaccine and a home-grown shot, as the country seeks to vaccinate its entire adult population by December amidst concerns over the Delta variant. India has also approved other vaccines, including Johnson & Johnson's one-shot vaccine, and is engaging in advanced negotiations for its local manufacture.

title: Merck’s Best Seller Racks Up Another Regulatory Win
summary: Merck's Keytruda, in combination with Eisai’s Lemvima, received FDA approval as a first-line treatment for advanced renal cell carcinoma. This approval was based on Phase III study data showing significant improvements in progression-free survival, overall survival, and objective response rates compared to Pfizer’s Sutent. The decision highlights the potential of this combination therapy despite a high rate of serious adverse events.

title: Xywav Approved for Idiopathic Hypersomnia
summary: The FDA has approved Jazz Pharmaceuticals' Xywav (calcium, magnesium, potassium, and sodium oxybates) oral solution for the treatment of idiopathic hypersomnia in adults. This makes Xywav the first and only medicine indicated for this condition. The approval was based on a phase 3 study demonstrating Xywav's significant improvements in sleepiness and disease severity compared to placebo.

title: Focus: Pfizer, Moderna seen reaping billions from COVID-19 vaccine booster market
summary: Pfizer, BioNTech, and Moderna are poised to generate billions of dollars from COVID-19 vaccine booster shots, creating a market comparable to annual flu vaccine sales. Analysts predict substantial revenue for these companies in 2023, primarily from boosters, with the annual market potentially settling at $5 billion or higher as more drugmakers join. The need for boosters is supported by waning antibody levels and increased breakthrough infections due to the Delta variant, though the frequency and necessity are still being researched and debated by some scientists and the WHO.

title: China's Sinovac to invest $60 mln in vaccine facility in Chile
summary: Chinese pharmaceutical company Sinovac Biotech Ltd announced an investment of $60 million to build a fill-and-finish vaccine plant in Chile. This move aims to solidify Sinovac's presence in Latin America, particularly in Chile, which has extensively utilized its COVID-19 vaccine, CoronaVac. Chile has achieved one of the world's fastest vaccination campaigns, with over 60% of its population fully vaccinated using substantial doses from Sinovac.

title: Pfizer expands recall of anti-smoking drug over carcinogen presence
summary: Pfizer Inc. has expanded its recall of the anti-smoking drug Chantix, adding four more lots due to elevated levels of cancer-causing nitrosamines. This latest recall brings the total to 16 lots impacted, which were distributed across the U.S. and Puerto Rico. While no adverse events have been reported, Pfizer advises patients to consult their doctors for alternative treatment options if they have received an affected lot.

title: Explainer: Who is eligible for a third COVID-19 vaccine dose in the U.S.?
summary: U.S. health officials have authorized a third dose of COVID-19 vaccines from Pfizer and Moderna for individuals with compromised immune systems. This decision is based on evidence that the standard two doses offer less protection for these populations, which health officials estimate to be less than 3% of American adults. The article details who is considered immunocompromised, clarifies that a prescription is not needed, and outlines what other countries are doing regarding booster shots.

title: More venues, music acts move forward with COVID-19 requirements to attend shows
summary: In response to the Delta variant surge, many music venues and artists are implementing COVID-19 requirements for attendees and employees. Venues like The Pour House and Motorco, along with Live Nation, will require proof of vaccination or a negative COVID-19 test to attend shows. This measure aims to protect businesses, customers, and artists from potential industry-wide lockdowns.

title: Pfizer submits initial data for COVID-19 vaccine booster authorization
summary: Pfizer and BioNTech have submitted initial data to U.S. regulators for authorization of a COVID-19 vaccine booster dose, showing high neutralizing antibodies against various variants. The companies expect late-stage trial results soon, while the World Health Organization has called for a moratorium on booster shots in favor of equitable distribution. Last week, U.S. regulators authorized a third dose for immunocompromised individuals.

title: 5 years after Pfizer buyout, SEC charges Medivation's former deal-making lead with insider trading
summary: The SEC has charged Matthew Panuwat, Medivation's former head of business development, with insider trading. Panuwat allegedly bought stock options in Incyte Corporation just days before the announcement of Pfizer's $14 billion acquisition of Medivation, profiting over $107,000. This case follows previous insider trading charges related to the 2016 Pfizer-Medivation deal.

title: GSK receives FDA accelerated approval for JEMPERLI (dostarlimab-gxly) for adult patients with mismatch repair-deficient (dMMR) recurrent or advanced solid tumors
summary: GSK has received accelerated FDA approval for JEMPERLI (dostarlimab-gxly) to treat adult patients with mismatch repair-deficient (dMMR) recurrent or advanced solid tumors. This marks the second FDA approval for dostarlimab in 2021 and offers a new treatment option for patients who have progressed on prior therapies and lack other alternatives. The approval is based on results from the GARNET study, which showed an objective response rate of 41.6% across dMMR solid tumors, with 95% of responders maintaining their response for at least six months.

title: Moderna to Launch Clinical Trials for mRNA-Based HIV Vaccine
summary: Moderna is set to begin human clinical trials for its mRNA-based HIV vaccine, seeking 56 HIV-negative individuals aged 18 to 50. The Phase I study, involving two vaccine candidates (mRNA-1644 and mRNA-1644v2-Core), will assess safety and is expected to launch on August 19, concluding in spring 2023. This initiative leverages the mRNA technology successfully used in COVID-19 vaccines, offering a potentially modifiable approach to combat the mutating HIV virus.

title: Pharma Market Update: H1 2021 in Review
summary: The pharmaceutical industry experienced both challenges and opportunities in the first half of 2021, largely driven by the COVID-19 pandemic. While vaccine development proved victorious, discussions around patent removal impacted investor sentiment, and financial institutions reported mixed fund performances for pharma ETFs. Despite some setbacks, analysts believe in the sector's long-term recovery and potential for attractive stock valuations.

title: As Covid-19 Boosters Loom, Pfizer and Moderna Expected to See Billions More in Sales
summary: Pfizer and Moderna are projected to earn billions more in sales due to increased demand for Covid-19 boosters and mRNA vaccines, driven by the Delta variant. The Biden administration is recommending booster shots for fully vaccinated Americans eight months after their second dose. The companies are also raising prices for their vaccines.

title: The TAC universe grows beyond PROTACs
summary: The therapeutic targeting chimera (TAC) field is expanding beyond PROTACs by leveraging autophagy for protein degradation. This strategy aims to destroy a wider range of disease-driving substrates compared to the proteasome-based approach used by PROTACs. A growing number of companies are exploring autophagy-inducing compounds for therapeutic purposes.

title: AP: Top Donor Of Gov. Ron DeSantis Is Regeneron Investor
summary: Florida Governor Ron DeSantis is facing criticism because one of his top donors, Citadel CEO Ken Griffin, is an investor in Regeneron Pharmaceuticals. DeSantis has been actively promoting and opening monoclonal antibody treatment centers using Regeneron's COVID-19 treatment. While Citadel's investment in Regeneron is a small portion of its overall portfolio, and the company has larger stakes in vaccine manufacturers Moderna and Pfizer, the link has drawn attention and questions from Democrats.

title: SHAREHOLDER ALERT: WeissLaw LLP Investigates Trillium Therapeutics Inc.
summary: WeissLaw LLP is investigating Trillium Therapeutics Inc. (NASDAQ: TRIL) regarding potential breaches of fiduciary duty by its board of directors concerning Pfizer Inc.'s proposed acquisition of the company for $18.50 per share, totaling $2.26 billion. The investigation questions whether the board acted in shareholders' best interests and if the $18.50 offer adequately compensates shareholders, especially given analyst price targets above the merger consideration. WeissLaw LLP, known for its extensive litigation in stockholder class and derivative actions, encourages affected shareholders to contact them for more information.

title: Pfizer Agrees to Buy Cancer Biotech Trillium Therapeutics at a 200% Premium
summary: Pfizer announced its agreement to acquire Trillium Therapeutics for $2.3 billion in cash, or $18.50 per share. This represents a 208.8% premium over Trillium's Friday closing price, valuing the cancer biotech's treatments with "blockbuster potential."

title: Trillium Therapeutics' stock nearly triples after buyout deal with Pfizer valued at $2.26 billion
summary: Trillium Therapeutics' stock surged by 189.3% in premarket trading after Pfizer announced an agreement to acquire the immuno-oncology company for $2.26 billion in cash. Pfizer will pay $18.50 per Trillium share, a 203.8% premium over its Friday closing price. This acquisition aims to enhance Pfizer's hematology portfolio within its oncology division.

title: Trillium Therapeutics shares soar on Pfizer’s $2.26B deal
summary: Pfizer is acquiring cancer company Trillium Therapeutics in a deal valued at $2.26 billion, causing Trillium's stock to surge. Pfizer will pay $18.50 per share for shares it does not already own, representing a 118% premium. This acquisition aims to enhance Pfizer's hematology portfolio and improve outcomes for people living with blood cancers, a disease that affected over one million people globally in 2020.

title: Pfizer Agrees $2.26 Billion Takeover of Cancer Specialists Trillium Therapeutics
summary: Pfizer (PFE) has announced it will acquire Trillium Therapeutics (TRIL), an immuno-oncology specialist, for approximately $2.3 billion in cash. The acquisition, priced at $18.50 per share, represents a significant premium and aims to bolster Pfizer's hematology portfolio with Trillium's biologics treatments that enhance the immune system's ability to combat cancer cells. This move reinforces Pfizer's commitment to oncology and its search for scientific breakthroughs in the treatment of blood cancers.

title: Pfizer Bets $2.26 Billion on Trillium’s Checkpoint Inhibitors
summary: Pfizer is acquiring Trillium Therapeutics for $2.26 billion, purchasing all outstanding shares not already owned at $18.50 per share, a 118% premium. This acquisition strengthens Pfizer's oncology pipeline, particularly in hematology, by adding Trillium's lead biologics, TTI-622 and TTI-621, which are novel SIRP alpha-Fc fusion proteins targeting the SIRP alpha-CD47 axis in various blood cancers. Trillium's drugs are currently in Phase Ib/II studies and have shown promising activity as monotherapies against lymphoid malignancies.

title: Pfizer to Acquire Trillium Therapeutics for $2.3B
summary: Pfizer is set to acquire Trillium Therapeutics for $2.26 billion, significantly bolstering its oncology pipeline with next-generation immuno-therapeutics designed to treat hematological malignancies. Trillium's lead molecules, TTI-622 and TTI-621, are SIRPα–CD47 targeting molecules that have shown promising activity as monotherapy in clinical studies for various lymphoid malignancies. This acquisition builds on Pfizer's prior investment in Trillium through its Breakthrough Growth Initiative and aims to advance these potential medicines to patients suffering from blood cancers globally.

title: Pfizer signs deal to buy Trillium Therapeutics for US$2.26 billion
summary: Pfizer Inc. has signed a deal to acquire Trillium Therapeutics Inc. for US$2.26 billion, paying US$18.50 per share in cash. This acquisition follows Pfizer's previous US$25 million investment in Trillium in September 2020. Trillium, a biotechnology company, focuses on developing treatments to enhance the immune system's ability to combat cancer cells.

title: Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine Gets Full Approval from FDA
summary: The FDA has granted full approval to the Pfizer/BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine for individuals aged 16 and older, marketing it as Comirnaty. This marks the first COVID-19 vaccine to receive full FDA approval, previously operating under Emergency Use Authorization. The approval is expected to increase public confidence and potentially lead to more vaccine mandates, with evaluations highlighting its 91% effectiveness and ongoing safety monitoring for side effects like myocarditis.

title: Belgium agrees to buy 10,000 courses each of Pfizer, Merck COVID-19 pills
summary: Belgium has agreed to purchase 10,000 courses each of the COVID-19 antiviral oral treatments from Pfizer and Merck. This decision comes as governments worldwide scramble for these treatments and despite Merck's drug facing setbacks due to disappointing trial data. The EU drug regulator has not yet authorized either treatment but has issued advice for emergency use amidst a rise in Omicron variant cases.

title: Vet Med alumnus a key player in Pfizer vaccine development
summary: Fred Angulo, a UC Davis School of Veterinary Medicine alumnus, played a crucial role in the development of Pfizer's COVID-19 vaccine as an epidemiologist for vaccine development. After a 26-year career at the CDC, Angulo joined Pfizer and utilized his public health expertise, honed by influential mentors like Dr. Calvin Schwabe, to expedite vaccine development. He emphasizes the critical role of science and collective trust in overcoming pandemics, drawing on his extensive experience with national and international outbreaks.

title: Pfizer, GSK and Teva lead 2022's round of January drug price hikes: GoodRx
summary: As of early January 2022, drugmakers have increased the U.S. list prices of over 400 brand-name medications, with an average hike of 5.2%, according to GoodRx. Pfizer leads with the largest number and steepest increases, including a 16.8% jump on Solu-Cortef. GlaxoSmithKline and Teva Pharmaceuticals also raised prices on numerous products, while BioMarin's price increases were noted as "more aggressive than years past" by analysts.

title: An Under the Radar High Quality ETF
summary: The Fidelity Quality Factor ETF (FQAL) received a five-star rating from CFRA, outperforming its peers and the S&P 500 in 2021 despite its smaller asset size. The fund focuses on free cash flow and return on invested capital with a sector-neutral approach, and CFRA expects it to continue outperforming. Eight of its top-10 holdings are considered undervalued by CFRA analysts.

title: Biohaven and Pfizer Complete Collaboration Transaction for Commercialization of Rimegepant and Zavegepant Outside United States
summary: Biohaven Pharmaceutical Holding Company Ltd. and Pfizer Inc. have finalized a collaboration agreement for the commercialization of migraine treatments rimegepant and zavegepant outside the U.S. This transaction includes an upfront payment of $500 million to Biohaven, comprising cash and an equity purchase, and eligibility for up to $740 million in future milestones. Biohaven retains global R&D rights and U.S. market rights for the therapies, which are designed to address the significant unmet needs of migraine sufferers worldwide.

title: Pfizer, BioNTech to develop shingles shot, after COVID-19 vaccine success
summary: Pfizer and BioNTech are partnering for the third time to develop an mRNA-based vaccine for shingles, following the success of their COVID-19 vaccine. Pfizer is making a $150 million equity investment and will pay BioNTech an additional $225 million upfront. Clinical trials are expected to begin in the second half of 2022, and if successful, their vaccine will compete with GlaxoSmithKline's Shingrix in a market addressing an estimated one million shingles cases annually in the United States.

title: Document
summary: Biohaven Pharmaceutical Holding Company Ltd. and Pfizer Inc. have completed their collaboration transaction for the commercialization of rimegepant and zavegepant outside the United States. This agreement includes an upfront payment of $500 million to Biohaven, consisting of cash and Pfizer equity, with Biohaven potentially receiving up to $740 million in future milestones. The collaboration aims to expand the availability of these migraine treatments globally, while Biohaven retains U.S. market rights and global R&D leadership.

title: Pfizer and BioNTech set their sights on developing mRNA-based shingles vaccine
summary: Pfizer Inc. (NYSE:PFE) and BioNTech SE (NSDQ:BNTX) are collaborating to develop an mRNA-based vaccine for herpes zoster (shingles), building on their previous successful partnership for a COVID-19 vaccine. The companies will share development costs and profits, with BioNTech receiving $225 million upfront and potential additional payments of $200 million. Clinical trials are expected to begin in the second half of 2022.

title: Tie pharma CEO pay to fair global COVID-19 vaccine access, investors say
summary: A group of institutional investors managing $3.5 trillion in assets is urging pharmaceutical companies to link executive compensation to equitable global access to COVID-19 vaccines. They sent a letter to Pfizer, Johnson & Johnson, Moderna, and AstraZeneca, advocating for them to adopt a WHO roadmap for vaccine equity. The investors highlight the disparity in vaccination rates between wealthy nations and countries in Africa, stressing the economic and moral imperative for broader distribution.

title: J&J says its single dose protects against breakthrough COVID-19 for up to 6 months
summary: Johnson & Johnson announced that a real-world study showed its single-shot COVID-19 vaccine is effective against breakthrough infections and hospitalizations for up to six months. The study, conducted before the Omicron variant emerged, indicated J&J's vaccine protection wanes later than two-dose vaccines from Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna. No waning of protection was observed for ICU admissions across all three vaccines.

title: Pfizer/BioNTech vaccine protects children against rare COVID-19 complication - CDC
summary: A CDC report indicated that two doses of the Pfizer/BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine are highly effective in protecting children aged 12-18 against Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C). The vaccine was found to be 91% effective in preventing MIS-C, a serious condition causing organ inflammation weeks after COVID-19 infection. The study, however, had limitations regarding its effectiveness against the Omicron variant and did not include children aged 5-11, who are at the highest risk for MIS-C.

title: Mexico grants emergency use approval for Merck's COVID-19 pill
summary: Mexico's health regulator has granted emergency use authorization for Merck's COVID-19 pill, Molnupiravir. President Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador also indicated that Pfizer's Paxlovid pill is expected to be approved soon. Both medications, already approved in the United States, will be made available in public hospitals in Mexico.

title: Italy to receive 40,000 Merck antiviral drug doses next week - official
summary: Italy is set to receive approximately 40,000 doses of Merck & Co's experimental COVID-19 antiviral drug, molnupiravir, next week, adding to the nearly 12,000 doses already distributed. These doses are intended for patients at risk of severe outcomes from the disease. Additionally, Italy will receive 200,000 courses of Pfizer's COVID-19 drug in February, with an option to purchase an extra 400,000 doses.

title: Pfizer, Bayer each strike up deals to add in-vivo gene editing to pipeline mix
summary: Pfizer and Bayer have both announced new collaborations to advance in-vivo gene editing technologies. Pfizer is partnering with Beam Therapeutics for base-editing therapies, potentially worth up to $1.35 billion in milestones. Bayer is working with Mammoth Biosciences on in-vivo CRISPR gene editing, with an upfront payment of $40 million and over $1 billion in potential milestones.

title: Pfizer, Beam Therapeutics Partner to Develop Treatments for 3 Genetic Diseases
summary: Pfizer has announced a $1.3 billion partnership with Beam Therapeutics to develop three treatments for genetic diseases within the next four years. The collaboration will leverage Beam's "base editing" technology, which allows for precise corrections of genetic errors. This initiative marks a significant advancement in the field of genetic medicine.

title: Pfizer CEO says Omicron variant targeted vaccine is most likely outcome
summary: Pfizer CEO Albert Bourla stated that a redesigned COVID-19 vaccine specifically targeting the Omicron variant is the most probable outcome. Pfizer and BioNTech are developing both an Omicron-specific vaccine and a bivalent shot. Bourla indicated that Pfizer could be ready to seek approval and start production of a redesigned vaccine as early as March.

title: Novartis and Molecular Partners report positive topline data from Phase 2 study for ensovibep (MP0420), a DARPin antiviral therapeutic for COVID-19
summary: Novartis and Molecular Partners have released positive topline data from their Phase 2 EMPATHY study for ensovibep, a DARPin antiviral therapeutic for COVID-19. The study met its primary endpoint of viral load reduction and showed a 78% reduction in the risk of hospitalization, ER visits, or death. Novartis will exercise its option to in-license ensovibep, accelerate manufacturing, and seek expedited regulatory authorizations globally, starting with the FDA’s Emergency Use Authorization.

title: MRNA Shares Up 9% as Moderna Starts Working on Booster Targeting Omicron Variant
summary: Moderna Inc. (MRNA) shares rose by over 9% following the announcement that the company is developing a booster shot specifically targeting the Omicron variant of COVID-19. CEO Stephane Bancel stated the Omicron-specific booster is expected to be available in Fall 2022 and will soon enter clinical trials. Additionally, Moderna has updated its advanced purchase agreements for 2022 product sales to $18.5 billion and is also exploring a universal flu vaccine using mRNA technology.

title: BD, Pfizer, Wellcome Collaborate to Improve Global Hospital Antimicrobial Stewardship Practices
summary: BD, Pfizer, and Wellcome have announced a collaboration to enhance global hospital antimicrobial stewardship practices by examining the role of diagnostics in combating antimicrobial resistance (AMR). This initiative aims to identify both benefits and gaps in diagnostic testing within AMR stewardship to improve patient care, clinical practice, and healthcare economics. The collaboration will also raise awareness of the critical role diagnostics play in addressing the rising threat of AMR, which is exacerbated by improper antimicrobial use and the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: S.Korea authorises Novavax COVID-19 vaccine, imports Pfizer pills
summary: South Korea has authorized Novavax Inc.'s COVID-19 vaccine and is preparing to distribute Pfizer's antiviral pills to combat a potential surge in Omicron infections. The first batch of Pfizer's Paxlovid antiviral pills is set to arrive, with treatments starting for high-risk patients. The Novavax vaccine joins several other approved vaccines, and SK Bioscience Co Ltd will produce it locally.

title: Pfizer study shows COVID-19 booster can be given along with pneumonia shot
summary: A Pfizer study has found that its COVID-19 vaccine booster dose can be safely administered alongside its next-generation pneumonia vaccine, PREVNAR 20, in individuals aged 65 and above. The study showed strong safety and immune responses, suggesting that co-administration could reduce the number of visits patients need to make for recommended immunizations. PREVNAR 20 was approved by the U.S. FDA last year to protect adults against severe pneumococcal diseases.

title: Gene Editing Stocks Might Be Building Some Momentum
summary: The gene editing sector, particularly companies presenting at the virtual JPMorgan healthcare conference, shows signs of gaining positive momentum after a challenging 2021. This renewed interest could benefit ETFs like the ARK Genomic Revolution Multi-Sector Fund (ARKG), which holds key gene-editing firms such as Intellia Therapeutics and Editas Medicine. Partnerships with larger pharmaceutical companies like Regeneron and Pfizer are driving new developments and potential catalysts for these innovative biotechnology firms.

title: Ana Maria Rodriguez gains $30K for re-election bid with help from health care, unions, charter schools
summary: Republican Sen. Ana Maria Rodriguez raised $30,000 in her last month of fundraising before the 2022 Legislative Session, bringing her total to $582,000 for her re-election bid. Nearly half of the new funds came from health care and pharmaceutical companies, trade groups, unions, and charter schools, with Independent Living Systems contributing the largest single donation of $3,000. She spent over $24,000, primarily on consulting, as no one has yet filed to challenge her in Senate District 39.

title: Intellia To Take On Pfizer Blockbuster With Gene-Editing Therapy
summary: Intellia is developing NTLA-2001, a gene-editing therapy, to compete with Pfizer's blockbuster drug Vyndaqel. While the therapy is still in early stages, Intellia is accelerating its efforts. The company aims to challenge the established market with its innovative gene-editing approach.

title: Pfizer says it applied for Japan gov't approval for oral COVID-19 drug
summary: Pfizer Inc. has applied for Japanese government approval for its oral COVID-19 treatment, building on global Phase II/III trials that included Japan. This move comes as Japan faces a surge in COVID-19 cases driven by the Omicron variant, with the government actively seeking oral treatments to control serious infections. Prime Minister Fumio Kishida aims to distribute Pfizer's pills next month, having already secured 2 million doses.

title: Consumer Healthcare Market SWOT Analysis by Size, Status and Forecast to 2022-2028 | Merck, Herbalife, Nestle
summary: This article provides a detailed SWOT analysis of the Consumer Healthcare market, evaluating its future growth potential and providing insights for decision-makers. The report covers market breakdowns by applications and types, revenue and sales estimation, competitive analysis of key players like GlaxoSmithKline, Merck, Herbalife, and Nestle, and regulatory analysis. It also includes FIVE FORCES & PESTLE ANALYSIS and geographical investigations across major regions such as APAC, Europe, North America, South America, and MEA.

title: Update - GSK Consumer Healthcare
summary: GSK confirmed it rejected three unsolicited, conditional, and non-binding proposals from Unilever plc to acquire its Consumer Healthcare business, with the latest offer being £50 billion. GSK's board deemed these proposals to fundamentally undervalue the business and its future prospects. The company remains focused on executing its proposed demerger of the Consumer Healthcare business in mid-2022 to create an independent global company.

title: GSK rejects Unilever’s $68.4bn offer for Consumer Healthcare business
summary: GSK has rejected three unsolicited bids from Unilever for its Consumer Healthcare business, which is a joint venture with Pfizer. The latest offer, valued at nearly $68.4bn, was deemed to "fundamentally undervalue" the business and its future prospects. GSK plans to proceed with a demerger of the consumer healthcare unit into a new, independent company this year.

title: Sema4 to Acquire GeneDx, Strengthening its Market-Leading AI-Driven Genomic and Clinical Data Platform
summary: Sema4 announced the acquisition of GeneDx, a leader in genomic testing, from OPKO Health, Inc. This strategic move is expected to create one of the largest genomic clinical testing providers in the U.S., with projected pro forma 2022 revenue of $350 million. The acquisition will be supported by a $200 million private placement, including investment from Pfizer, and will integrate GeneDx's extensive genomic data with Sema4's AI-driven health intelligence platform to enhance precision medicine solutions.

title: FDA approves AbbVie, Pfizer drugs for eczema, creating competition for Sanofi
summary: The FDA has approved AbbVie's Rinvoq and Pfizer's Cibinqo for the treatment of moderate to severe eczema, introducing significant competition for Sanofi's top-selling drug, Dupixent. Both newly approved drugs are oral JAK inhibitors, offering a convenience advantage over injectable treatments like Dupixent. These approvals are crucial for AbbVie and Pfizer, with Rinvoq projected to generate substantial sales in eczema treatment, and Cibinqo aiming to expand Pfizer's immunology business.

title: Sema4 secures a deal to acquire GeneDx, capturing $200M in private investment
summary: Sema4 is acquiring GeneDx, a move expected to enhance data-driven insights and improve its market position in women’s health and rare disease diagnostics. The deal, which includes a $200 million private investment from life science investors including Pfizer, aims to make the combined company one of the largest genomic clinical testing providers in the U.S. with projected $350 million in pro forma 2022 revenue. Katherine Stueland, CEO of GeneDx, will become co-CEO of Sema4.

title: The tiny Boston startup helping Pfizer with Covid-19 antivirals
summary: PostEra, a small Boston startup, has been collaborating with Pfizer Inc. since late 2020 to aid in the development of small-molecule drugs for Covid-19, leveraging machine learning. The company plans to establish its primary workforce in the Greater Boston area. This partnership highlights the increasing role of AI and machine learning in pharmaceutical research and development.

title: Vet Med Alumnus Aids Pfizer Vaccine Development
summary: Dr. Fred Angulo, a UC Davis School of Veterinary Medicine alumnus, played a crucial role as an epidemiologist at Pfizer Inc., contributing to the rapid development of the COVID-19 vaccine. His career trajectory from veterinary medicine to public health, including a long tenure at the CDC, highlights his dedication to addressing widespread health crises. Angulo emphasizes the importance of science and interdisciplinary collaboration, inspired by his UC Davis education, in tackling global health challenges.

title: Teva ponies up $420M to settle with investors who said company hid price-fixing scheme
summary: Teva Pharmaceutical will pay $420 million to settle a lawsuit with shareholders who accused the company of concealing a price-fixing scheme that led to inflated drug prices and share values. Teva denies wrongdoing, stating the settlement reflects its general interest and commitment to patients. The legal action dates back to 2016, with the Department of Justice also indicting Teva in 2020 on criminal conspiracy charges related to price-fixing.

title: Telemedicine and Ulcerative Colitis: An HCP Perspective
summary: Dr. Marla Dubinsky, a gastroenterologist, discusses the role of telemedicine in managing ulcerative colitis (UC) during the COVID-19 pandemic. She highlights how virtual appointments allow for continuous disease management, address patient concerns about COVID-19, and facilitate connections with various healthcare team members beyond gastroenterologists. Dr. Dubinsky also touches on overcoming technological challenges and ensuring patients continue to receive necessary care and medications.

title: No Time to Wait Educates About Potentially Serious Conditions
summary: This article highlights the "No Time to Wait" campaign, an initiative by the Bristol Myers Squibb–Pfizer Alliance, aimed at raising awareness about Deep Vein Thrombosis (DVT) and Pulmonary Embolism (PE). It describes the symptoms and risks associated with these potentially serious conditions and urges individuals to seek timely medical attention for diagnosis and treatment. The campaign emphasizes the importance of not delaying visits to healthcare providers even when symptoms might seem minor.

title: Efficacy of sacubitril/valsartan versus olmesartan in Japanese patients with essential hypertension: a randomized, double-blind, multicenter study
summary: This phase III, randomized, double-blind study evaluated the efficacy and safety of sacubitril/valsartan compared to olmesartan in Japanese patients with mild to moderate essential hypertension. The study found that sacubitril/valsartan (200 mg and 400 mg) provided superior reductions in mean sitting systolic blood pressure (msSBP), mean sitting diastolic blood pressure (msDBP), and mean sitting pulse pressure (msPP) compared to olmesartan 20 mg. Sacubitril/valsartan was also generally well-tolerated with comparable safety profiles to olmesartan, suggesting it is an effective treatment option for this patient population.

title: Use of the Janssen (Johnson & Johnson) COVID-19 Vaccine ...
summary: This report from the CDC's Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) updates recommendations for the Janssen COVID-19 vaccine, preferentially recommending mRNA vaccines (Pfizer-BioNTech or Moderna) for all persons aged ≥18 years in the United States. The decision follows a review of updated vaccine effectiveness and safety data, including continued reports of thrombosis with thrombocytopenia syndrome (TTS) and Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) associated with the Janssen vaccine. While the benefits of the Janssen vaccine still outweigh the risks of being unvaccinated, the benefit-risk balance is more favorable for mRNA vaccines due to higher effectiveness and less severe rare adverse events.

title: Pfizer CEO sees annual COVID vaccine rather than frequent boosters
summary: Pfizer CEO Albert Bourla stated that an annual COVID-19 vaccine would be preferable to frequent booster shots to combat the pandemic effectively. He hopes for a single annual vaccine that covers the Omicron variant and other strains, making it easier for public health campaigns. Pfizer is working on a redesigned vaccine for Omicron and could seek approval as early as March.

title: Pfizer’s growth hormone deficiency drug comes up short at the FDA
summary: The FDA has rejected Pfizer's long-acting human growth hormone drug, somatrogon, which was developed for once-weekly dosing in children with growth hormone deficiency. This setback delays Pfizer and Opko Health's entry into a market where Ascendis Pharma recently gained approval for a similar once-weekly treatment. Pfizer is evaluating the FDA's comments to determine the next steps for somatrogon, which is already approved in other countries like Japan, Canada, and Australia.

title: CCI approves acquisition of three GlaxoSmithKline group entities
summary: India's Competition Commission of India (CCI) has approved the acquisition of GlaxoSmithKline Asia Pvt Ltd by two other GlaxoSmithKline group entities, GlaxoSmithKline Consumer Healthcare Overseas and GlaxoSmithKline Consumer Healthcare UK Trading. This internal restructuring involves the transfer of GlaxoSmithKline Asia's products and GSK Consumer Brands to GSK CH HoldCo, which is 68% owned by GSK and 32% by Pfizer. Before the deal, GlaxoSmithKline Asia Pvt Ltd will acquire trademarks for 'Iodex' and 'Ostocalcium' brands in India from GlaxoSmithKline Pharmaceuticals Ltd.

title: San Diego-Based Company Signs Deal With Pfizer to Speed Up Vaccine Production
summary: Codex DNA, a San Diego-based company, has signed a licensing deal with Pfizer to accelerate vaccine production. The company's unique "biological printer" technology aims to produce DNA and mRNA materials for vaccines quickly, especially during global health crises. This expanded agreement is expected to help combat emerging variants and potentially revolutionize the approach to future pandemics.

title: Will Abbott Stock Rise After Its Q4 Results?
summary: Abbott is set to report its Q4 2021 results, with expectations slightly below consensus estimates due to mixed impacts from the Omicron variant – boosting diagnostics but potentially hurting medical devices. Despite this, Trefis estimates Abbott's stock valuation at $141 per share, suggesting a 12% upside from its current market price, even though near-term macroeconomic risks could cause a temporary dip after the earnings report. The company's revenues and EPS are predicted to be slightly under consensus, a trend that is expected to continue into 2022 due to anticipated declines in Covid-19 testing sales.

title: Pfizer pushes to intervene in lawsuit seeking COVID vaccine information from FDA
summary: Pfizer Inc. is seeking to intervene in a Texas federal lawsuit that demands the FDA release information used in licensing the company's COVID-19 vaccine. Pfizer argues its intervention is necessary to protect trade secrets and accelerate document release, while plaintiffs contend the move is premature. A judge has ordered a fast-track release of hundreds of thousands of documents, acknowledging the case's "paramount public importance."

title: New Advances in the Treatment of Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy and Spinal Muscular Atrophy
summary: This article summarizes a symposium from the World Muscle Society 2021 Virtual Congress, discussing new advances in treating Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA) and Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD). It highlights the strong efficacy of disease-modifying treatments for SMA, especially when administered pre-symptomatically, and the critical need for global newborn screening programs. For DMD, the discussion focuses on gene therapy clinical trials and the importance of early diagnosis and tailored treatment goals given the disease's progressive and variable nature.

title: Touting a new way to drug an all-important family of proteins, a startup launches with $100M
summary: Septerna, a new biotechnology company, has launched with $100 million in funding to develop drugs targeting G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs). The company, co-founded by Nobel laureate Robert Lefkowitz, aims to overcome historical difficulties in GPCR drug discovery by utilizing a novel approach to purify and study these crucial proteins. Septerna plans to advance five drug discovery programs, with three potentially reaching human testing within a few years, focusing on endocrine disorders, metabolism, inflammation, and central nervous system diseases.

title: Eli Lilly says FDA could deny expanded use of arthritis drug for eczema
summary: Eli Lilly announced it expects the U.S. FDA to deny expanded approval for its rheumatoid arthritis drug, Olumiant, as an eczema treatment due to lack of alignment on the indicated population. The drug, a JAK inhibitor, has faced regulatory scrutiny after competitors showed increased risks. Lilly is discontinuing its lupus program for Olumiant but still seeks approval for COVID-19 and alopecia areata uses.

title: Pfizer signs up to promote Alex Therapeutics' smoking cessation app in Germany
summary: Pfizer's German division has partnered with Alex Therapeutics to clinically validate and promote its smoking cessation app, Elia, within Germany. The goal is to develop a prescription app reimbursable under German digital healthcare regulations, leveraging Alex Therapeutics' AI-powered platform and evidence-based psychology methods. This collaboration builds on a long-standing relationship between the two companies in the field of smoking cessation.

title: Insight: Merck's COVID pill is last choice for U.S. patients, global use varies
summary: Merck & Co's new antiviral pill, molnupiravir, is largely the last choice for treating COVID-19 in the U.S. due to its lower efficacy and potential safety concerns compared to other available treatments like Pfizer's Paxlovid. While demand is low in the U.S. and some European countries, its use varies globally, with some low-income countries utilizing generic versions due to affordability. Doctors and healthcare systems prioritize more effective options, leading to significant stockpiles of molnupiravir in the U.S.

title: Explainer: How does Merck's COVID-19 pill compare to Pfizer's?
summary: This article explains the differences between Merck's and Pfizer's COVID-19 antiviral pills, molnupiravir and Paxlovid, respectively. It compares their efficacy, mechanisms of action, safety profiles, and supply availability, noting Pfizer's pill showed higher efficacy in trials. The piece also discusses their importance as treatment options, especially given limitations of other therapies against new variants.

title: Pfizer and Ionis halt vupanorsen program after meeting primary endpoint in dyslipidemia study
summary: Pfizer is discontinuing the development of vupanorsen, an investigational antisense therapy for cardiovascular indications and severe hypertriglyceridemia, despite the drug meeting its primary endpoint in a Phase 2b trial. The decision was made because the degree of improvement was not deemed sufficient for further development, and higher doses were associated with liver enzyme elevations. Pfizer is returning the development rights to Ionis Pharmaceuticals.

title: U.S. gives full approval to Moderna’s COVID-19 vaccine
summary: U.S. health regulators have granted full approval to Moderna’s COVID-19 vaccine, officially branded Spikevax, more than a year after its initial emergency authorization. This decision signifies that the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has completed a rigorous review process, similar to other long-established vaccines, using data from over 200 million doses administered in the U.S. While previous full approval for Pfizer's vaccine did not significantly boost vaccination rates, regulators hope this extra endorsement will encourage more people to get vaccinated.

title: Novavax finally submits its COVID-19 vaccine to the FDA. Is it too late?
summary: Novavax has finally submitted its COVID-19 vaccine, NVX-CoV2373, for Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) to the FDA after multiple delays. The protein-based shot demonstrated 90% efficacy against symptomatic disease in trials. Despite approvals in other regions, its prospects in the U.S. market are uncertain given the dominance of mRNA vaccines and the timing of its submission.

title: Pfizer Ends Development of Vupanorsen Over Disappointing Results, Safety Issues
summary: Pfizer and Ionis Pharmaceuticals have discontinued the clinical development of vupanorsen, an investigational therapy for cardiovascular risk reduction and severe hypertriglyceridemia. This decision follows phase 2b study results which, despite showing statistically significant reductions in non-HDL-C and triglycerides, did not yield sufficient efficacy to continue the program and also revealed dose-dependent elevations in liver fat and enzymes. The companies hope the scientific knowledge gained will contribute to a better understanding of these conditions.

title: U.S. grants full approval to Moderna's COVID vaccine in adults
summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted full approval to Moderna's COVID-19 vaccine, now branded Spikevax, for individuals aged 18 and older, making it the second fully approved COVID-19 vaccine in the U.S. The vaccine had previously been under emergency use authorization since December 2020. While the vaccine is approved in over 70 countries, the FDA is still reviewing its use for adolescents and has noted a potential link to rare cases of heart inflammation.

title: Bill Sessa is Ready to Deliver Breakthroughs for Common Diseases
summary: Bill Sessa has joined Pfizer as Senior Vice President and Chief Scientific Officer for the Internal Medicine Research Unit (IMRU) in February 2022. He aims to advance novel treatments for cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, leveraging his 30 years of research at Yale University. Sessa plans to refine existing pipelines and expand Pfizer's cardiometabolic strategy, with a focus on tackling widespread conditions like obesity, Type 2 diabetes, non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), heart failure, and chronic renal disease.

title: First patients to receive immunotherapy treatment are still cancer-free a decade later
summary: Two patients treated with CAR-T cell therapy for a form of blood cancer are still cancer-free a decade later, demonstrating the potential long-term efficacy of this promising but costly immunotherapy. This milestone suggests that CAR-T cells can potentially cure leukemia, with the modified immune cells remaining active and surveilling for cancer cells for years. Researchers are now focused on adapting this therapy to treat solid cancers.

title: Merck’s Covid Pill Fumble Gives Pfizer Potential $17 Billion Win
summary: Merck's decision to shelve a 10-year-old drug, boceprevir, has inadvertently given Pfizer a significant advantage in the Covid-19 treatment market. Boceprevir, originally for hepatitis C, provides a key component to Pfizer's Paxlovid antiviral, accounting for a substantial portion of its effectiveness against the coronavirus. This pharmaceutical oversight is poised to result in a potential $17 billion win for Pfizer.

title: HARTE HANKS LAUNCHES EXPANDED HEALTHCARE PRACTICE
summary: Harte Hanks, Inc. announced the launch of an expanded healthcare practice to be led by Janel Harris, an executive with extensive experience in the healthcare agency world. The company aims to provide fully integrated services including patient insights, data analytics, customer care, creative execution, fulfillment, and logistics, leveraging its global reach and technology stack. Harte Hanks already works with major healthcare companies like GSK, Abbott, Blue Cross/Blue Shield, and Pfizer and recently opened a new state-of-the-art e-commerce and distribution facility in Kansas City to support its healthcare services.

title: In world first, South Africa's Afrigen makes mRNA COVID vaccine using Moderna data
summary: South Africa's Afrigen Biologics has successfully created its own mRNA COVID-19 vaccine based on Moderna's publicly available sequence, marking the first time such a vaccine has been produced without the developer's direct assistance. This initiative is part of a WHO-backed project to improve vaccine access in lower and middle-income countries, especially in Africa, where vaccine imports are high. The company aims to begin human trials for its vaccine candidate by late 2022 and is also developing a next-generation mRNA vaccine that does not require freezing temperatures for storage.

title: The Secret is Out About Tampa: It’s the New Miami
summary: Tampa is emerging as a major economic and real estate hub, drawing comparisons to Miami due to its booming population, diversified economy, and attractive lifestyle. Spearheaded by groups like RPH Multifamily Group, the city is experiencing significant investment, job growth, and soaring property values, alongside recent sports championships, making it a highly desirable location for both individuals and businesses.

title: The people of the world vs Pfizer Inc.
summary: During the COVID-19 pandemic, Pfizer maximized profits from its vaccine and treatment, Paxlovid, leading to concerns about accessibility, especially in lower-income countries. Public Citizen highlighted that Pfizer's contracts with governments include clauses that undermine national sovereignty, grant immunity to the company, and keep pricing and terms secret. Activists are demanding greater transparency, technology transfer for mRNA vaccines, and global access to life-saving medications.

title: Sanofi's simplified brand opens a fresh chapter as new strategy, pandemic help turn the page
summary: Sanofi has undergone a significant corporate rebranding, simplifying its identity by culling the Genzyme and Pasteur names and introducing a new logo. This effort, initiated in mid-2020 and driven by a new CEO and "Play to Win" strategy, aims to unify the company's image after a history of complex mergers and acquisitions. The pandemic also highlighted the increasing importance of a strong corporate brand over individual product brands in the pharmaceutical sector.

title: P2X3 Receptor Antagonist Field Murkier as Bayer Abandons Program
summary: Bayer has decided to abandon the Phase II development of its P2X3 receptor antagonist, eliapixant, citing an unfavorable benefit-risk profile across four indications. This decision follows Merck's receipt of a Complete Response Letter from the FDA for its P2X3 receptor antagonist, gefapixant, for chronic cough, further complicating the P2X3 receptor antagonist landscape. Despite these setbacks, other companies like BELLUS Health and Shionogi continue to develop their respective P2X3 receptor antagonists for conditions such as chronic cough and neuropathic pain.

title: Johnson & Johnson plant pauses Covid vaccine production, report says
summary: A Johnson & Johnson facility in the Netherlands, the sole producer of usable batches of its single-shot Covid-19 vaccine, has reportedly halted production since late last year. The plant is now focusing on a vaccine for a different, potentially more profitable, non-Covid virus. This pause could reduce the supply of J&J's Covid vaccine by hundreds of millions of doses, though J&J stated it is still fulfilling obligations and has millions of doses in inventory, with plans to restart Covid vaccine production in March.

title: AI for Pharma
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic has accelerated the adoption of AI in the pharmaceutical industry, with a majority of healthcare organizations planning to invest in the technology. AI and machine learning are significantly improving drug discovery, clinical trials, and manufacturing processes, potentially generating nearly $100 billion annually in the U.S. healthcare system. Major pharmaceutical companies are collaborating with AI vendors to enhance efficiency, reduce R&D costs, and accelerate the development of new treatments and diagnostic tools.

title: Pfizer Forecasts $54 Billion in 2022 Sales From Its Covid-19 Vaccine, Treatment
summary: Pfizer Inc. is forecasting $54 billion in sales for 2022 from its Covid-19 vaccine and treatment, driven by surging demand and the antiviral pill Paxlovid. The drugmaker expects its total revenue to reach around $100 billion this year and is actively seeking deals to expand its pipeline of experimental products. This comes amidst ongoing efforts to combat the pandemic, including the distribution of booster shots in some countries.

title: Lander held on to vaccine maker stock months into tenure
summary: Eric Lander, Biden's former top science adviser, maintained significant financial investment in vaccine maker BioNTech SE for months after his Senate confirmation, nearly at the end of his allotted 90-day divestment period. Although deemed legally compliant by an OSTP spokesperson, watchdog groups argue it raises conflict of interest concerns, especially given his public advocacy for vaccination efforts during that time. This situation mirrors similar instances with other Cabinet members, highlighting potential issues with current ethics pledges.

title: Chemical Engineering Alumnus Paul Mensah Elected to the National Academy of Engineering
summary: Paul Mensah, a University of Virginia chemical engineering alumnus and Vice President of Biotherapeutics Pharmaceutical Sciences at Pfizer Inc., has been elected to the National Academy of Engineering. This prestigious recognition highlights his significant contributions to accelerating biotherapeutic development, including key components for the first approved COVID-19 vaccine. Mensah's election is a testament to his prolific career, leadership at Pfizer, and continued involvement with UVA's chemical engineering department as an advisor and mentor.

title: Pfizer’s COVID sales to top $50bn this year, investors want more
summary: Pfizer anticipates its 2022 sales from its COVID-19 vaccine and antiviral pill, Paxlovid, to exceed $54 billion, yet this forecast fell short of Wall Street's higher expectations, causing a slight dip in share prices. CEO Albert Bourla indicated that final sales for Paxlovid could be considerably higher as current outlooks only include signed or nearly signed contracts. The company is also exploring aggressive acquisition strategies to fuel future growth and working on an improved version of Paxlovid, as competition in the antiviral market is expected to intensify.

title: U.S. plans to roll out COVID-19 shots for children under 5 years in February
summary: The U.S. government plans to start rolling out COVID-19 vaccines for children under 5 years old as early as February 21, pending authorization from the FDA. The FDA is considering the Pfizer/BioNTech vaccine for this age group, even after it did not meet a key target in clinical trials for two-to-four-year-olds. An initial 10 million doses of a lower concentration vaccine are expected to be shipped to states, with additional supply to follow.

title: Drugmaker Teva may pay as much as $3.6 billion in U.S. opioid settlement
summary: Teva Pharmaceutical Industries announced it expects to pay between $2.7 billion and $3.6 billion in cash and medicine to settle thousands of U.S. opioid lawsuits. This estimate is based on a recent $225 million settlement with Texas and a proposed nationwide settlement involving other drug distributors and Johnson & Johnson. The company CEO is confident a national deal can be reached within the next year, utilizing the Texas settlement model which combines cash payments with product donations for substance abuse treatment.

title: Eli Lilly talks up 'long-term' game plan for tirzepatide launch, but don't expect major sales early on
summary: Eli Lilly is prioritizing a long-term strategy for the launch of its diabetes drug tirzepatide, focusing on patient access and foundational marketing rather than immediate high sales. The company acknowledges the competitive market, particularly with Novo Nordisk's GLP-1 blockbusters, but anticipates significant peak sales, potentially reaching $4.9 billion. Lilly is also exploring tirzepatide's use for obesity and considering separate branding for different indications.

title: Biohaven and Pfizer Announce Positive Topline Results of Pivotal Trial of Rimegepant for the Acute Treatment of Migraine in China and South Korea
summary: Biohaven and Pfizer announced positive top-line results from a Phase 3 clinical trial of rimegepant for the acute treatment of migraine in China and South Korea. The study met its co-primary endpoints of freedom from pain and freedom from the most bothersome migraine-associated symptom at 2 hours post-dose, with sustained efficacy up to 48 hours and a favorable safety profile. This marks the fourth positive Phase 3 study for rimegepant, and Pfizer holds commercialization rights outside the U.S., while Biohaven retains U.S. market rights.

title: China’s Approval of Pfizer Pill Opens Door to Ending COVID Zero
summary: China has conditionally approved Pfizer's COVID-19 antiviral pill, Paxlovid, marking the first foreign pharmaceutical product endorsed for COVID-19 in the country. This decision signals a potential shift away from China's strict COVID Zero strategy, which has relied heavily on domestically developed vaccines and therapeutics. Experts suggest that having an effective antiviral could help mitigate the lower efficacy of China's homegrown vaccines and prepare the country for a more flexible approach to the pandemic.

title: Pfizer and Regeneron led pharma's sales growth in Q4 while Teva, Biogen and Gilead lagged
summary: Pfizer and Regeneron significantly boosted pharma's Q4 sales, with growth exceeding 100% due to successful COVID-19 vaccines and antibodies. AstraZeneca also saw substantial growth at 63%, driven by pipeline delivery and the Alexion acquisition. In contrast, companies like Teva, Biogen, and Gilead faced declining sales due to issues such as generic competition and the underperformance of new treatments like Aduhelm.

title: Money Calls the Shots
summary: Amnesty International published "Money Calls the Shots" on February 14, 2022, updating its assessment of pharmaceutical companies' restrictions on access to Covid-19 vaccines. The report evaluates five leading vaccine manufacturers (AstraZeneca plc, BioNTech SE, Johnson & Johnson, Moderna Inc., and Pfizer Inc.) and, for the first time, includes Chinese producers Sinopharm and Sinovac Biotech Ltd.

title: Karim Mikhail, President and CEO of Amarin Corporation
summary: Amarin Corporation's President and CEO, Karim Mikhail, discusses the company's commitment to tackling cardiovascular diseases, which remain the leading cause of death globally despite COVID-19's dominance. He highlights their flagship product, icosapent ethyl (VASCEPA/VAZKEPA), proven to reduce cardiovascular risk and its global expansion efforts. Mikhail also details Amarin's adaptation of its go-to-market strategy to an omnichannel approach in response to pandemic-induced changes in healthcare access, emphasizing the importance of a diverse workforce and the significant public health impact their work has.

title: BioNTech Unveils Mobile Covid-19 Vaccine Factories for Developing World
summary: BioNTech SE, in collaboration with Pfizer Inc., has introduced mobile vaccine production units designed to bring Covid-19 vaccine manufacturing to developing countries, particularly in Africa. These modular factories, housed in shipping containers, will produce mRNA vaccines on a not-for-profit basis, with each unit capable of producing approximately 50 million doses annually. The initiative aims to address the limited access to vaccine supplies in these regions.

title: Vaccines and Monoclonal Antibodies in Immunization
summary: This article discusses how monoclonal antibodies can complement traditional vaccines to provide rapid immunity against infectious diseases, including COVID-19, influenza, and RSV. It explains that while vaccines train the body to produce its own antibodies over time, monoclonal antibodies offer direct, immediate protection, which can be crucial for vulnerable populations like infants who may be too young for vaccination or when no vaccine is available. Scientists are working to extend the duration of protection offered by these antibodies.

title: Natalie Holles lands at freshly funded biotech startup focused initially on hives
summary: Natalie Holles has been appointed CEO of Third Harmonic Bio, a biotech startup that has secured $105 million in funding. The company, initially focused on treating hives, marks Holles' return to a CEO role after her previous position with a late-stage gene therapy company. This move signifies a new chapter for Holles, leading a smaller company targeting a significant disease.

title: Lawsuit over Pfizer's disclosures before Chantix recall is dismissed
summary: A federal judge has dismissed a proposed class-action lawsuit against Pfizer Inc. concerning its Chantix anti-smoking drug. The lawsuit, brought by consumers, alleged that Pfizer failed to disclose cancer-causing agents in the drug before its recall. The judge found no plausible evidence that Pfizer had a duty to disclose nitrosamine contamination or that its labels were misleading, especially since full rebates were offered for unused Chantix.

title: Pyrukynd Approved for Hemolytic Anemia Due to Pyruvate Kinase Deficiency
summary: The FDA has approved Pyrukynd (mitapivat) for the treatment of hemolytic anemia in adults with pyruvate kinase deficiency, a rare inherited disease. This approval is based on two Phase 3 studies, ACTIVATE and ACTIVATE-T, which demonstrated the drug's effectiveness in increasing hemoglobin levels and reducing transfusion burden in patients. Pyrukynd is a first-in-class oral selective PK activator and represents the first disease-modifying medication for this condition.

title: GSK to name consumer healthcare unit 'Haleon' after spin-off
summary: GlaxoSmithKline announced that its consumer healthcare joint venture with Pfizer will be named Haleon and confirmed plans for a mid-2022 spin-off. This move follows GSK's rejection of Unilever's acquisition bid, as the drugmaker aims to focus on its prescription drugs and vaccines business. Shareholders are expected to receive at least 80% of GSK's current 68% stake in the new consumer health group.

title: Sanofi and GSK plan to ask regulators to authorize their COVID-19 vaccine
summary: Sanofi and GlaxoSmithKline (GSK) are seeking regulatory authorization for their COVID-19 vaccine candidate, which showed 100% effectiveness against hospitalization and severe disease in trials. Their protein-based vaccine can serve as a primary vaccine or a booster shot, significantly raising antibody levels. This development offers a conventional alternative to existing mRNA and viral vector vaccines.

title: New Sanofi and GSK vaccine demonstrates strong protection against severe Covid-19 in clinical trials
summary: Sanofi and GSK have announced positive late-stage clinical trial results for their new protein subunit Covid-19 vaccine, Vidprevtyn. The vaccine demonstrated 100% effectiveness against severe Covid-19 disease, including hospitalizations, and 75% effectiveness against moderate or severe cases. The companies plan to seek authorization in the US and Europe, positioning Vidprevtyn as a potential booster option given its traditional vaccine technology and refrigeration storage capabilities.

title: Japan to accept Johnson & Johnson COVID vaccine for border entry next month
summary: Japan announced it would accept the Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 vaccine for international travelers starting next month, allowing those vaccinated to enter the country and qualify for shorter quarantine periods. This adds the J&J shot to a list that already includes Pfizer, Moderna, and AstraZeneca vaccines, although the J&J vaccine has not been domestically approved in Japan. Effective March 1, Japan will also increase its daily entry cap and ease quarantine rules for students, workers, and other visa holders, but not for tourists.

title: Moderna Projects COVID-19 Vaccine Sales at $19 Billion for 2022
summary: Moderna announced robust financial results for Q4 2021 and full-year 2021, with revenues of $7.2 billion and $18.5 billion respectively, largely driven by its COVID-19 vaccine, Spikevax. The company projects $19 billion in COVID-19 vaccine sales for 2022 from signed advance purchase deals. Moderna is also expanding its mRNA pipeline with 44 programs in development, including vaccines for other infectious diseases and cancer, as it prepares for a potential endemic phase of COVID-19.

title: Biohaven and Pfizer Receive Positive CHMP Opinion for Migraine Treatment
summary: Biohaven Pharmaceutical Holding Company Ltd. and Pfizer Inc. announced that the Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use (CHMP) of the European Medicines Agency (EMA) adopted a positive opinion for rimegepant, a calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) receptor antagonist, for both acute and preventive treatment of migraine in adults.
