title: U.S. doctors reconsider Pfizer's Paxlovid for lower-risk COVID patients
summary: U.S. doctors are re-evaluating the use of Pfizer's COVID-19 antiviral Paxlovid for lower-risk patients due to concerns about symptom recurrence and the need for a second isolation period. While Paxlovid use has surged, driven by government promotion, reports of rebound symptoms have led the CDC to advise renewed isolation. Despite Pfizer stating that rebound is uncommon and not uniquely associated with Paxlovid, some doctors are now reserving it for high-risk individuals, especially those unvaccinated, boosted, or with significant health conditions, questioning its broad utility in a vaccinated and previously infected population.

title: Net Zero by 2040: How Pfizer is Fighting Climate Change with Ambitious Science Based Goals
summary: Pfizer announced its commitment to achieve Net Zero by 2040, a decade ahead of the standard's expectations, building on its earlier goal to be carbon neutral by 2030. The company emphasizes environmental sustainability due to its impact on public health and aims to reduce emissions throughout its value chain, including urging suppliers to adopt science-aligned reduction targets. Pfizer is also working towards 100% renewable electricity by 2030, with a significant virtual power purchase agreement already in place for North America.

title: How the next generation of immuno-oncology could help us get ahead of cancer
summary: This article discusses the potential of next-generation immuno-oncology to transform cancer treatment. It highlights how manipulating the immune system, specifically T and NK cells and their checkpoints, can improve outcomes for various cancer types. The article also introduces GSK's research into the CD226 axis and its portfolio of antibodies targeting specific checkpoints, aiming to enable the immune system to fight cancer more effectively.

title: Paxlovid Becomes Household Name for Covid-19 Patients
summary: Pfizer's antiviral drug, Paxlovid, has become the leading Covid-19 treatment in the U.S., with over 412,000 prescriptions. It has surpassed Merck's molnupiravir, which had around 110,000 prescriptions. Both drugs were approved by the FDA for high-risk individuals to prevent hospitalization, but Paxlovid demonstrated higher efficacy and improved supply.

title: BMS, Novartis and Roche Score New Approvals for Key Drugs
summary: Bristol Myers Squibb's Opdivo (nivolumab), Novartis's Kymriah (tisagenlecleucel), and Roche's Evrysdi (risdiplam) each received new FDA approvals for expanded indications. Opdivo was approved as a first-line therapy for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, Kymriah for relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma, and Evrysdi's label was extended to include pre-symptomatic infants with spinal muscular atrophy. These approvals provide new treatment options for patients across various serious conditions, demonstrating continued advancements in pharmaceutical development.

title: GSK to acquire clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company Affinivax, Inc.
summary: GSK has announced its definitive agreement to acquire Affinivax, a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company, for an upfront payment of $2.1 billion and up to $1.2 billion in potential development milestones. This acquisition aims to strengthen GSK's vaccines R&D pipeline by incorporating Affinivax's novel Multiple Antigen Presenting System (MAPS) technology, particularly its next-generation 24-valent pneumococcal vaccine candidate which is in phase II development and has received Breakthrough Therapy designation. The deal is expected to close in the third quarter of 2022, supporting GSK's medium-term outlook.

title: Pfizer to exit GSK consumer health joint venture after spinoff
summary: Pfizer plans to sell its 32% stake in the consumer health joint venture with GlaxoSmithKline after it spins off into a new standalone corporation called Haleon. GSK will contribute at least 80% of its 68% holding to Haleon, which is set to begin trading on the London Stock Exchange on July 18. Both companies aim to focus on vaccines and new medicine development, with Pfizer exiting in a "disciplined manner" to maximize shareholder value.

title: Pfizer to Sell Stake in Haleon
summary: Pfizer Inc. announced its intention to sell its 32% stake in Haleon PLC, a consumer healthcare joint venture with GSK plc, once Haleon lists on the London Stock Exchange in July. The sale will be executed in a "disciplined manner" to maximize shareholder value for Pfizer while avoiding destabilizing Haleon's shares. This move reflects Pfizer's strategic shift towards innovative medicines and vaccines, with vaccines contributing significantly to its Q1 2022 revenue.

title: Regulus Appoints Amin Kamel, Ph.D., as Vice President, DMPK
summary: Regulus Therapeutics Inc. has appointed Amin Kamel, Ph.D., as Vice President, DMPK. Dr. Kamel will support the clinical development of the company's lead candidate, RGLS8429, for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD). His appointment includes an option to purchase 200,000 shares of Regulus' common stock, vesting over four years.

title: Moderna delays COVID vaccine deliveries to EU by several months
summary: Moderna Inc. has agreed to delay some COVID-19 vaccine deliveries to the European Union by several months, pushing them to late 2022 or early 2023. This decision comes as the EU is experiencing a drop in demand for COVID-19 vaccines and has also made similar arrangements with Pfizer and BioNTech. Despite the delay, Moderna maintains its $21 billion vaccine sales forecast for 2022, and the amended agreement will give EU countries access to a next-generation vaccine if approved.

title: Pfizer's Paxlovid reduces COVID risk in seniors regardless of vaccine status -study
summary: A new Israeli study found that Pfizer's antiviral treatment Paxlovid significantly reduces COVID-19 hospitalization and death rates in vaccinated and unvaccinated patients aged 65 and older, even during the Omicron variant's rise. However, the treatment did not show significant benefits in preventing severe illness or reducing mortality among younger adults aged 40-64. The study highlights Paxlovid's effectiveness in vulnerable older populations, regardless of their prior immunity status.

title: Novavax COVID Vaccine Efficacy In Omicron, Delta Variants Among Unknowns Ahead Of Advisory Cmte
summary: Ahead of the FDA's Vaccines and Related Biological Products Advisory Committee meeting on June 7, there are uncertainties regarding the efficacy of the Novavax COVID-19 vaccine against the Omicron and Delta variants. The committee will discuss Novavax's Emergency Use Authorization request. This article highlights the key issues and related content concerning COVID-19 vaccines and their approval process.

title: GSK to form consumer healthcare business ‘Haleon’
summary: GSK plc announced its intention to separate its consumer healthcare business to form an independent listed company, Haleon plc, through a demerger of at least 80% of GSK's 68% holding in the joint venture with Pfizer. This separation, expected to complete by July 18, 2022, will allow GSK to focus solely on biopharmaceuticals while Haleon becomes a world leader in consumer healthcare. The move is conditional on GSK shareholder and regulatory approvals, representing the most significant corporate change for GSK in 20 years.

title: Early Promise in Treating MS Seen With FibroBiologic's Fibroblast Therapy
summary: FibroBiologics' investigational cell therapy, CYMS101, showed early promise in treating multiple sclerosis (MS) by inhibiting disease activity in a mouse model and appearing safe in initial clinical trials. The therapy, which uses human dermal fibroblasts, is designed to be a more accessible and cost-effective alternative to stem cell treatments. Future studies, including a Phase 1/2 clinical trial, are planned to further evaluate its efficacy and safety.

title: ASCO22: J&J, Pfizer trade BCMA bispecific data in myeloma
summary: Johnson & Johnson and Pfizer presented new data for their BCMA-targeting bispecific antibodies, teclistamab and elranatamab, respectively, for relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma at ASCO. J&J's teclistamab showed an improved overall response rate of 63% and 39% complete responses with a median follow-up of 14 months, while Pfizer's elranatamab achieved a 60.6% ORR in preliminary phase 2 data. Both drugs are vying for market entry in an increasingly competitive landscape of BCMA-directed therapies, with teclistamab likely to reach the market sooner.

title: Pfizer to invest $120M at Kalamazoo area site to boost Paxlovid output, create 250 jobs
summary: Pfizer is investing $120 million at its Kalamazoo County facility, creating 250 jobs, to boost production of its COVID-19 oral treatment, Paxlovid. This investment will make the site one of the world's largest producers of active pharmaceutical ingredient for Paxlovid, with a capacity of 1,200 metric tons annually. Governor Gretchen Whitmer and U.S. Rep. Fred Upton praised the move for its economic impact and its contribution to fighting COVID-19.

title: Future Packaging to redefine India Pharm industry growth: InnoPack Pharma
summary: The 11th Annual InnoPack Pharma Confex, presented by West Pharma and CPhI Conferences India, aimed to showcase the latest packaging, labeling, and drug delivery device advancements for the Indian pharmaceutical industry. With India's pharmaceutical packaging market projected to reach $3.027 billion by 2030, the event provided a crucial platform for industry stakeholders to address challenges and foster growth, supported by government initiatives like the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme. The confex emphasized the role of innovative packaging in meeting healthcare demands and contributing to an "Atmanirbhar Bharat" (self-reliant India).

title: Pfizer to Invest $120 Million in Paxlovid Manufacturing
summary: Pfizer Inc. is investing $120 million in its Portage, Michigan facility to significantly increase the production of its COVID-19 antiviral treatment, Paxlovid. This investment aims to meet global demand, with the facility expected to become one of the world's largest producers of the active pharmaceutical ingredient for Paxlovid, creating 250 new jobs. The move highlights Pfizer's commitment to battling the pandemic and expanding manufacturing innovation in the U.S.

title: FDA advisers back Novavax COVID-19 shots as 4th US option
summary: FDA advisers have recommended Novavax's COVID-19 vaccine as a fourth option in the U.S., particularly for adults who have yet to be vaccinated. The protein-based vaccine uses a more traditional technology compared to mRNA vaccines and is already available in several other countries. While the panel noted its potential benefits and role in addressing vaccine hesitancy, questions remain regarding its efficacy against newer variants like Omicron and the long-term data on potential side effects like heart inflammation.

title: FDA advisers vote to recommend Novavax Covid-19 vaccine
summary: FDA advisers have recommended the Novavax Covid-19 vaccine for emergency use in adults, with a 21-0 vote and one abstention. This protein-based vaccine offers an alternative to mRNA shots, potentially appealing to vaccine-hesitant individuals. The committee acknowledged concerns about a possible link between the vaccine and heart inflammation, recommending further evaluation.

title: FDA committee OKs Novavax's late-to-the-game COVID-19 vaccine
summary: An independent FDA committee has voted to recommend Novavax's COVID-19 vaccine for emergency use authorization in the U.S. This vaccine, a protein-based shot, has already been approved in 41 other countries and could become the fourth FDA-approved coronavirus vaccine on the U.S. market. The decision aims to increase vaccine uptake, especially among those hesitant about mRNA technology.

title: Moderna says updated COVID shot boosts omicron protection
summary: Moderna announced that its experimental COVID-19 vaccine, which combines the original shot with protection against the omicron variant, appears to be effective. Preliminary study results indicate that individuals who received this combination shot experienced a higher boost in omicron-fighting antibodies compared to those who only received a fourth dose of the original vaccine. This development is significant as vaccine makers consider updating booster recipes to combat future coronavirus surges and new variants.

title: Dupilumab FDA Approved for AD Patients 6 months to 5 years
summary: The FDA has approved dupilumab (Dupixent) for children aged 6 months to 5 years with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis, marking it as the first biologic medicine for this age group. This approval is supported by data from the LIBERTY AD trial, which showed significant improvement in skin condition, itch, and quality of life for patients treated with dupilumab. The drug offers a new targeted treatment option for young children, addressing a significant unmet need.

title: Millions of COVID-19 shots ordered for nation's youngest, officials say
summary: White House officials have indicated that millions of COVID-19 vaccine doses have been ordered for young children ahead of potential federal authorization. Approximately 1.45 million Pfizer doses and 850,000 Moderna doses have been ordered from the initial 5 million available. This group of children under 5 is the last to become eligible for vaccination, though uptake among older children has been low, raising questions about demand for these new doses.

title: Alnylam follows rivals with new study results for kidney disease drug
summary: Alnylam Pharmaceuticals announced positive Phase 2 trial results for its genetic medicine, cemdisiran, for IgA nephropathy, showing a 37% reduction in urinary protein. While this positions Alnylam to enter a competitive market with other drugs already approved or in late-stage development, the company's investors are more focused on the upcoming APOLLO-B trial results for Onpattro, which could significantly expand its market. Alnylam, despite its product launches, continues to operate at a loss, but sees cemdisiran and the potential Onpattro expansion as keys to future profitability.

title: Big Tobacco Is Funding Opposition to Global Covid Vaccine Access
summary: Major tobacco companies, including British American Tobacco and Japan Tobacco International, are funding the Consumer Choice Center (CCC), an organization actively opposing a World Trade Organization proposal to suspend intellectual property rules for COVID-19 vaccines and treatments. Critics argue that the tobacco industry is undermining global public health efforts, driven by its reliance on intellectual property rules for profit, past use of these rules against public health measures, and even its own foray into COVID-19 vaccine development. This opposition highlights the industry's broader interest in protecting intellectual property, which it has historically used to fight regulations and secure its financial interests.

title: HPLC market to grow by $1.26bn in five years
summary: The high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) market is projected to grow by $1.26 billion, reaching a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 5.33 percent between 2022 and 2026. This growth is primarily driven by increasing uses of HPLC and rising healthcare investments. North America, particularly the US and Canada, is expected to lead this expansion, contributing a third of the market growth, despite the high cost of HPLC instruments acting as a restraint.

title: Regenxbio debuts $65M gene therapy manufacturing facility at its Maryland HQ
summary: Regenxbio has launched a new $65 million gene therapy manufacturing facility in Rockville, Maryland, enhancing its capacity for adeno-associated virus vector production up to 2,000 liters. This facility is part of a larger $100 million investment to establish end-to-end gene therapy capabilities. The company also joined a U.S. initiative for rare disease gene therapies and recently received $370 million from AbbVie for its eye disease gene therapy RGX-314.

title: Decoding Disease
summary: Amgen subsidiary deCODE genetics is celebrating its 25th anniversary, focusing on using population-scale genomic research to understand human diversity and disease. By studying large populations rather than preclinical models like mice, deCODE aims to improve drug discovery and development, with a substantial portion of Amgen’s R&D pipeline now supported by deCODE’s genetic insights. The company utilizes advanced techniques like Whole Genome Sequencing, Genome Wide Association Studies, and multi-omics data analysis to identify disease-associated variants and pathways, particularly benefiting from Iceland's unique population structure for extensive data collection.

title: FDA approves Lilly, Incyte drug for alopecia, but includes safety warning
summary: The FDA has approved Olumiant, developed by Eli Lilly and Incyte, as the first systemic therapy for severe alopecia areata, despite including a black box safety warning. The drug, a JAK inhibitor, is associated with serious side effects including heart attacks, strokes, and cancer, which could complicate its launch given its high cost. Olumiant's approval follows successful Phase 3 trials and aims to address a significant unmet need for over 300,000 Americans suffering from severe alopecia.

title: Pfizer stops enrollment in Paxlovid trial in standard-risk population
summary: Pfizer has stopped enrollment in a clinical trial for its COVID-19 antiviral drug, Paxlovid, for standard-risk patients. A study indicated that the treatment was not effective in significantly reducing symptoms in this group, although it has emergency use authorization and has been effective for high-risk individuals. The new data will be included in Pfizer's application to the FDA for full approval of Paxlovid's use in high-risk populations.

title: U.S. FDA advisers overwhelmingly back Moderna COVID vaccine for ages 6-17
summary: Advisers to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration unanimously recommended Moderna's COVID-19 vaccine for children and teens aged 6 to 17. The FDA is expected to authorize the vaccine soon, followed by a recommendation from the CDC. Despite potential concerns regarding heart inflammation, U.S. regulators found the risks were not statistically significant and data was inconsistent across safety databases.

title: Boehringer To Acquire Trutino Under Aggressive Cancer R&D Strategy
summary: Boehringer is set to acquire Trutino Biosciences as part of its aggressive cancer R&D strategy, focusing on precision cancer medicines. While the financial details of the acquisition remain undisclosed, this move follows other recent deals by Boehringer aimed at strengthening its oncology pipeline.

title: CIO 100 Index 2022 in association with Equinix — Part 3
summary: The Business & Finance CIO 100 Index 2022, in association with Equinix, recognizes the top 100 Chief Information Officers in Ireland. This article, part three of a four-part series, highlights several key CIOs and IT leaders across various innovative companies in Ireland, detailing their experience, roles, and contributions. The index was officially launched at the Dublin Tech Summit with a breakfast reception and keynote address from Harry Moseley, Co-CIO of Zoom.

title: Adcom says yes to two vaccines, two approaches for US tots
summary: The FDA's Vaccines and Related Biologic Products Advisory Committee unanimously voted to support emergency use authorizations for both Moderna and Pfizer-BioNTech's COVID-19 mRNA vaccines for children aged 6 months and older. This decision brings the U.S. closer to having two vaccine options available for nearly all Americans, marking a significant milestone in the vaccination effort.

title: Paxlovid Doesn’t Work For Healthier Patients, Pfizer Says
summary: Pfizer announced it would stop enrolling healthier patients in a study for its COVID-19 drug, Paxlovid, because the pill did not alleviate symptoms or significantly reduce hospitalization and death in low-risk individuals. This is a setback for expanding the drug's use, though Pfizer will continue to focus on studying Paxlovid in vulnerable populations and expects no impact on its full-year revenue forecast due to existing contracts. The company plans to submit these trial results to the FDA as part of its application for full approval of Paxlovid, which currently holds emergency-use authorization for high-risk adults.

title: AGP to acquire select portfolio of products from Viatris Inc
summary: AGP Limited's board has approved the acquisition of a selected portfolio of products from Viatris Inc. through a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) named OBS Pakistan (Private) Limited. This strategic move aims to increase AGP's market share, enhance its product portfolio, and is expected to add over Rs4 billion to the company's consolidated topline within 12 months. The acquisition will be financed through an optimal capital structure of 25% equity and 75% debt, with AGP owning up to 85% shareholding in the SPV.

title: Suzanne Nora Johnson elected new USC Board of Trustees chair
summary: Suzanne Nora Johnson, a USC alumna and former vice chair of Goldman Sachs, has been elected the new chair of the USC Board of Trustees. She brings extensive experience from various corporate and nonprofit boards and is committed to unifying the Trojan Family to achieve President Carol L. Folt's ambitious goals. Johnson succeeds Rick Caruso, who stepped down to run for mayor of Los Angeles.

title: Pro-lifers question Novavax’s fetal tissue claim
summary: Pro-life advocates are questioning Novavax's claim that its COVID-19 vaccine is free from any links to aborted fetal tissue. While Novavax states no human fetal-derived cell lines were used in its development or production, a prominent pro-life research group, the Charlotte Lozier Institute, argues that some confirmatory lab tests for the vaccine did involve cells derived from abortions. This raises concerns for vaccine holdouts who object to the use of fetal cell lines due to religious or ethical reasons.

title: Pfizer chisels off stake in Akero with $25M equity investment to support NASH dreams
summary: Pfizer has made a $25 million equity investment in Akero Therapeutics to support its two mid-phase trials for efruxifermin (EFX) in nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH). This investment, part of Pfizer’s Breakthrough Growth Initiative, gives Pfizer a 6.7% ownership stake in Akero and will contribute to funding the company's operations until Q3 2024. Akero also secured a $100 million term loan facility from Hercules Capital Inc., providing a longer runway for its clinical programs.

title: JATT Acquisition Corp. and Zura Bio Limited Announce Definitive Business Combination Agreement to Create NYSE Listed Biotechnology Company
summary: JATT Acquisition Corp. and Zura Bio Limited have announced a definitive business combination agreement, valuing the combined entity at $215 million pro forma enterprise value. The merger will create a NYSE-listed biotechnology company focused on advancing Zura Bio's lead candidate, ZB-168, an anti-IL7Rα monoclonal antibody, into Phase 2 clinical trials for alopecia areata and other immune disorders. The transaction is expected to close in Q4 2022 and will provide up to $189 million in gross proceeds to fund ZB-168's development.

title: 6 Month to 5th Birthday Vaccine: Frequently Asked Questions
summary: The article addresses frequently asked questions about the COVID-19 vaccine for children aged 6 months to 5 years, following its CDC authorization. It emphasizes the vaccine's safety and effectiveness in preventing severe illness and MIS-C, details the rigorous testing process with lower dosages for this age group, and clarifies misconceptions about mRNA vaccines. The piece highlights that vaccination is crucial for protecting young children against COVID-19 and its variants.

title: June 17 Quick Takes: Skyrizi gains first IBD approval
summary: AbbVie's Skyrizi received FDA approval for moderate-to-severe Crohn’s disease, its first approval for an inflammatory bowel disease, with AbbVie projecting significant sales from this and other indications. Meanwhile, Acadia Pharmaceuticals faced a setback as an FDA advisory committee did not recommend approval for Nuplazid in Alzheimer's disease psychosis due to efficacy concerns. The article also touches on other company updates from Cytokinetics, Scholar Rock, Moderna, and Pfizer-BioNTech.

title: USC taps Suzanne Nora Johnson to replace Rick Caruso as head of Board of Trustees
summary: Suzanne Nora Johnson has been appointed as the new chair of the University of Southern California's Board of Trustees, replacing Rick Caruso, who is running for mayor of Los Angeles. An alumna of USC, Johnson has served on the board since 1998 and previously held positions at Goldman Sachs, Intuit, and Pfizer. She emphasized her commitment to unifying the "Trojan Family" and working collaboratively with students, faculty, staff, and the broader Los Angeles community.

title: Glycosylated Peptide Market: Analysis of Prevailing Trends
summary: A new research report from Coherent Market Insights analyzes the Glycosylated Peptide Market, providing a comprehensive evaluation of factors impacting global business introduction and forecasts through 2028. The report highlights recent trends in major regions and includes valuable information on market size, market share, revenue predictions, and growth capabilities. Key companies to watch in this market include Pfizer Inc., Teva Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd., Bachem Holding AG, GlyTech, Inc., Sussex Research Laboratories Inc., Samsung Bioepis, and Celltrion Inc.

title: Can Olema Oncology Prevail Where Other SERDs have Recently Failed?
summary: Olema Oncology is developing OP-1250, a selective ER degrader (SERD) and complete estrogen receptor (ER) antagonist, to treat advanced breast cancer. Despite past failures of other SERDs from companies like Sanofi and Roche, Olema's CEO Sean Bohen is confident in OP-1250's potential, citing promising early data and the drug's dual mechanism of action. The company is progressing quickly towards Phase II trials, believing its approach will advance treatment for ER+, HER2- breast cancer.

title: 7 Stocks to buy that will make you rich by 2030
summary: This article identifies seven stocks across various sectors that could lead to significant wealth by 2030, assuming current revenue growth rates continue. The selected companies—Applied Materials, Coinbase Global, Intel, Altria Group, Novartis, Pfizer, and StoneCo—are analyzed for their market positions, growth prospects, and potential challenges. The author emphasizes long-term investing over short-term speculation.

title: US to roll out COVID vaccines for youngest children next week
summary: The US CDC has approved COVID-19 vaccines for children as young as six months, allowing a nationwide rollout to begin next week. This decision follows FDA authorization of Moderna's shot for children aged six months to five years and Pfizer-BioNTech's for those six months to four years. President Biden hailed the decision as a "monumental step," with appointments for eligible children expected to start scheduling next week.

title: Is COVID-19 seasonal? A time series modeling approach
summary: This study investigates whether COVID-19 exhibits seasonal patterns similar to other respiratory viruses, using time series modeling of case rates in the United States and Europe from March 2020 to April 2022. The findings suggest that COVID-19 activity peaks between November and March, aligning with the traditional winter viral respiratory season, although the US Southern Census Region also experienced an anomalous second peak in late summer 2021. The authors conclude that annual protective measures, such as seasonal booster vaccines, should be implemented in a similar timeframe to influenza prevention strategies.

title: AbbVie files sNDA with FDA to expand atogepant label
summary: AbbVie has submitted a supplemental New Drug Application (sNDA) to the FDA for atogepant (Qulipta) to expand its use as a preventive treatment for both episodic and chronic migraine. The drug was initially approved in September 2021 for episodic migraine. The sNDA includes data from the pivotal Phase 3 PROGRESS study, which demonstrated a statistically significant reduction in mean monthly migraine days for chronic migraine patients.

title: BMS, Pfizer and Merck face steep patent cliffs but all have the financial flexibility for M&A: Moody's
summary: Moody's Investors Service analysis reveals that Bristol Myers Squibb, Pfizer, and Merck are highly exposed to patent cliffs between 2026 and 2029, potentially impacting significant revenues. However, these companies possess substantial financial flexibility, including high cash levels and strong free cash flow, enabling them to pursue mergers and acquisitions to counter these losses. Conversely, AbbVie and Sanofi are identified as having the least patent cliff exposure during the same period.

title: Pfizer to acquire 8.1% share in French firm Valneva
summary: Pfizer is investing $95 million (€90.5 million) to acquire an 8.1% share in French firm Valneva to further support their Lyme partnership. This investment will fund the Phase III development of their Lyme disease vaccine candidate, VLA15, with Pfizer planning to commence the trial in Q3 2022 and file a Biologics License Application in 2025.

title: Phase 2 Data Show Vidofludimus Calcium Suppresses MRI Lesions in Relapsing MS With Good Tolerability
summary: Phase 2 data from the EMPhASIS trial indicate that vidofludimus calcium significantly reduced new MRI lesions in patients with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (MS) and showed a favorable safety profile. This investigational selective DHODH inhibitor is designed as a better-tolerated alternative to existing treatments like teriflunomide. The positive results support its progression to phase 3 testing for relapsing-remitting MS.

title: COVID vaccines in Jackson and Klamath Counties for children 6 months to 5 years
summary: Jackson and Klamath Counties are now offering COVID-19 vaccines for children aged 6 months to 5 years, with the Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna vaccines approved for this age group. Public health officials emphasize that vaccination significantly reduces the risk of hospitalization and death from COVID-19, and parents are encouraged to consult their healthcare providers for more information. The article also provides details on how to find vaccination sites and notes the upcoming closure of the Jackson County Expo vaccination site.

title: COVID vaccine for kids ages 6 months to 5 years now available but parents divided
summary: The COVID-19 vaccine is now available for children aged 6 months to 5 years, with the FDA and CDC affirming its benefits outweighing risks. Despite medical professionals, like Dr. Stephen Turkovich, advocating for its safety and effectiveness, parents remain divided due to concerns over long-term studies and potential side effects versus the vaccine's protective benefits. The article highlights both hesitant and supportive parental views on vaccinating young children.

title: Cast your eyes over these 15 weird and wonderful biotech stocks we found on the ASX
summary: This article highlights 15 unique and interesting biotech companies listed on the ASX, detailing their specific technologies, market capitalization, and recent developments. It covers a range of innovations from spray-on skin and concussion technology to pain assessment apps and sperm separation systems, providing a snapshot of the diverse biotech landscape in Australia.

title: Jazz drug fails in late-stage study for multiple sclerosis
summary: Jazz Pharmaceuticals announced that its drug, Sativex, failed a late-stage clinical trial for treating muscle spasticity caused by multiple sclerosis, as it did not meet its primary endpoint. This is a setback for Jazz, which acquired Sativex through its $7 billion acquisition of GW Pharmaceuticals, though two larger trials for the drug are still ongoing. Despite the disappointment, analysts noted that expectations for this initial trial were modest, and the drug remains a smaller product compared to Jazz's other major therapies.

title: Roivant and Pfizer Unveil Priovant Therapeutics and Ongoing Registrational Studies for Oral Brepocitinib in Dermatomyositis and Lupus
summary: Roivant Sciences and Pfizer have announced the launch of Priovant Therapeutics, a new company focused on developing therapies for autoimmune diseases. Priovant will advance brepocitinib, a potential first-in-class dual inhibitor of TYK2 and JAK1, with ongoing registrational studies for dermatomyositis (Phase 3 VALOR study) and systemic lupus erythematosus (Phase 2b study). Pfizer holds a 25% equity ownership in Priovant and has licensed the global development rights for brepocitinib to the new entity.

title: Roivant Reduces Pipeline by Several Programs Across Vants
summary: Roivant Sciences has discontinued several development programs across its Vant subsidiaries to reprioritize its pipeline and focus capital on its most promising opportunities. The discontinued programs include gene therapies and treatments for dermatological conditions, allowing the company to concentrate on new initiatives like Priovant Therapeutics and advance multiple pivotal clinical trials. Roivant maintains significant financial flexibility with $2.1 billion in cash and cash equivalents, projecting a cash runway of over two years.

title: Pfizer and BioNTech forge new COVID-19 vaccine deal with U.S. government
summary: Pfizer and BioNTech have secured a new $3.2 billion agreement with the U.S. government to supply 105 million additional doses of their COVID-19 vaccine. This deal may include an omicron-adapted vaccine, pending FDA authorization, and has an option for the U.S. government to purchase up to 195 million more doses. This aims to bolster the U.S. response to potential future COVID-19 waves.

title: The scientist's struggle: Lessons from the journey of mRNA pioneers Katalin Karikó and Drew Weissman
summary: This article details the challenging journey of mRNA pioneers Katalin Karikó and Drew Weissman, whose decades of tireless work led to the mRNA vaccines used during the COVID-19 pandemic. Despite numerous setbacks, grant rejections, and intellectual property disputes, their research on packaging mRNA into lipid nanoparticles proved foundational. The piece highlights their struggle to gain recognition and funding for early-stage science and their current perspectives on the pharmaceutical industry's role in advancing innovation.

title: Promotional Products Case Study: Rewarding Pets & Vets
summary: This case study details how Zoetis, a global animal-health company, partnered with Stran & Co. to create the Zoetis Petcare Rewards program. The program incentivizes pet owners to purchase Zoetis pharmaceuticals by earning points redeemable for future vet services, and rewards veterinarians with branded merchandise for prescribing their products. The initiative has significantly grown, demonstrating an effective marketing strategy for the animal health industry.

title: [Special] ‘BeiGene to offer affordable innovative drugs’
summary: BeiGene, a Chinese multinational pharmaceutical company, has established a Korean offshoot with the goal of providing innovative drugs at reasonable prices. General Manager Yang Ji-hye, formerly of Pfizer and Novartis, emphasizes BeiGene's heavy investment in R&D and its philosophy of ensuring no patient is marginalized due to drug costs. The company's first drug, Brukinsa, is undergoing reimbursement review in Korea, and they plan to bring other key drugs like Tislelizumab to the market.

title: Major boost for research on the interaction between inflammatory bowel diseases, the immune system and gut bacteria
summary: The Novo Nordisk Foundation has granted DKK 60 million to Professor William Winston Agace for research into inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD). This project aims to map the mechanisms behind immune tolerance in the gut and how chronic IBD, such as ulcerative colitis and Crohn’s disease, disrupt these processes. The research will focus on the role of stromal cells in maintaining immune balance and aims to identify new treatment targets and biomarkers for IBD.

title: Pfizer signs new $3.2 billion COVID vaccine deal with U.S. government
summary: Pfizer and BioNTech have secured a new $3.2 billion deal with the U.S. government for 105 million doses of their COVID-19 vaccine, including an Omicron-adapted version. The price per dose has increased by over 50% compared to the initial contract. The agreement also includes an option for the U.S. government to purchase an additional 195 million doses, boosting Pfizer's projected vaccine sales for 2022.

title: Sirana Pharma and Pfizer to work on treatment for brittle bone disease
summary: German biotech company Sirana Pharma has partnered with Pfizer to research and validate a novel treatment for osteogenesis imperfecta (OI), also known as brittle bone disease, a condition currently without approved drugs. Sirana Pharma will contribute its microRNA-targeting approach, while Pfizer will provide its expertise in musculoskeletal disorders and drug development, aiming to identify potential drug candidates for this rare genetic disorder. The collaboration focuses on addressing the unmet medical need in bone diseases, leveraging both companies' strengths to advance new therapeutic options.

title: Podcast avec Caroline DELANGLE
summary: This article announces a podcast featuring Caroline DELANGLE, Head of Cross Asset Solutions at Federal Finance Gestion. The podcast will discuss Federal Indiciel US, a fund created in 2002 to track the performance of the S&P 500. The article also provides extensive financial data for numerous funds across various risk profiles.

title: Lepore is new HINJ chair
summary: Chris Lepore, a senior executive at Johnson & Johnson, has been appointed as the new chairman of the HealthCare Institute of New Jersey (HINJ). He succeeds Jack Cox in this role, advocating for the life science industry in the state. The article also mentions other key appointments, including Elizabeth Woody as vice president and Chuck Leitgeb as treasurer.

title: Sanofi launches Impact® brand of medicines for low-income countries
summary: Sanofi Global Health, a nonprofit unit, has launched Impact®, a new brand of 30 standard of care medicines for nonprofit distribution in 40 lower-income countries, covering therapeutic areas like diabetes, cardiovascular disease, tuberculosis, malaria, and cancer. Additionally, Sanofi has established an Impact fund to support innovative startups providing scalable healthcare solutions in underserved regions. This initiative aims to improve access to essential medicines and strengthen local healthcare systems through partnerships and investment.

title: CureVac files lawsuit against BioNTech over patent infringement
summary: CureVac N.V. has filed a lawsuit in Germany against BioNTech SE, alleging infringement of CureVac’s patents in the manufacture of BioNTech and Pfizer's Comirnaty COVID-19 vaccine. CureVac is seeking compensation, not an injunction to halt vaccine production or distribution. BioNTech stated its intention to vigorously defend its intellectual property rights against the claims.

title: How Pfizer Won the Pandemic, Reaping Outsize Profit and Influence
summary: Pfizer achieved immense profits and influence during the pandemic through its COVID-19 vaccine and antiviral Paxlovid. The company's financial success allowed it to shape U.S. health policy, often announcing recommendations before government officials, and generated significant revenue projections for its COVID-19 products. Critics worry about Pfizer's growing power in public health decision-making, arguing that pharmaceutical companies are taking on roles traditionally held by independent experts.

title: U.S. FDA allows pharmacists to prescribe Pfizer's COVID-19 pill
summary: The U.S. FDA has authorized state-licensed pharmacists to prescribe Pfizer's Paxlovid COVID-19 pill to expand access to timely treatment for eligible patients. This decision comes despite the American Medical Association's preference for doctor-prescribed decisions due to the drug's complexities and need for patient history review. Pharmacists are instructed to assess patients' health records for kidney and liver issues and refer them to a doctor if insufficient information is available.

title: Charles Schott, Rollins: Upfitting your vehicles in unpredictable times
summary: Charles "Charlie" Schott, Fleet Director for Rollins Inc., discusses the complexities of vehicle upfitting for different business needs, including pest control, and how to manage fleet operations in unpredictable times. He emphasizes the importance of a "Tried & True Process" for vehicle ordering and building "Brand Loyalty" with automakers to navigate current supply chain challenges. Schott highlights Rollins' shift towards electric-powered equipment and cautious adoption of EVs while dealing with the unique requirements of hazardous material transport.

title: Africa CDC signs memorandum with Pfizer for COVID-19 pill
summary: The African Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) has signed a memorandum of understanding with Pfizer to provide African nations with access to Paxlovid, Pfizer's COVID-19 antiviral treatment, at cost. The World Health Organization has recommended Paxlovid for mild to moderate COVID-19 cases in high-risk patients, citing an 85% reduction in hospitalization risk. This agreement aims to expand access to the pill in low- and middle-income countries, with distribution logistics within Africa yet to be determined by the African Union.

title: Pfizer Receives Approval for COVID Treatment Paxlovid
summary: Pfizer submitted a New Drug Application (NDA) for its oral COVID-19 treatment Paxlovid, moving towards full approval after receiving emergency use authorization. The drug has demonstrated an 88% reduction in hospitalization or death risk in high-risk patients. Despite some hindrances due to symptom recurrence, Pfizer projects significant sales potential for Paxlovid for FY 2022.

title: Africa CDC says it has signed MOU with Pfizer for COVID pill
summary: The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) announced on Thursday that it has signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with Pfizer for the supply of its COVID-19 antiviral pill, Paxlovid, to African countries. This agreement will allow African nations to access the treatment at cost. Paxlovid has shown nearly 90% effectiveness in preventing hospitalizations and deaths in high-risk adults.

title: EU drugs regulator open to COVID boosters that target older Omicron offshoots
summary: The European Medicines Agency (EMA) is considering COVID-19 booster vaccines that target older Omicron offshoots for the fall, amid rising cases from new subvariants. This approach differs from the U.S. FDA, which specifically seeks inclusion of newer BA.4 and BA.5 strains. The EMA emphasizes keeping options open due to the unpredictability of future circulating variants and the difficulty of perfectly matching vaccine composition to evolving viruses.

title: Millions of COVID-19 Shots Discarded, while Intermittent Fasting Could Curb Serious Disease
summary: Millions of COVID-19 vaccine doses are being discarded due to dropping vaccination rates and expiration dates, with Moderna alone throwing out 30 million doses. The risk of contracting COVID-19 outdoors, while lower than indoors, is not zero and depends on variant transmissibility. Meanwhile, a study suggests that long-term intermittent fasting may reduce the risk of severe COVID-19 hospitalization or death by decreasing inflammation and potentially interfering with the virus's ability to attach to cells, though it is not a substitute for vaccination.

title: Dr. Reddy's launched Fesoterodine Fumarate Extended-Release Tablets in the US market
summary: Dr. Reddy's Laboratories Ltd. announced the launch of Fesoterodine Fumarate extended-release tablets in the U.S. market, a generic equivalent to Toviaz. This launch follows USFDA approval, targeting the overactive bladder market which had US sales of approximately $211 million. The tablets are available in 4 mg and 8 mg strengths.

title: Mayor Adams, Mayor's Fund, and Pfizer Announce $1.5 Million Grant to Boost City's Stem Education Efforts for Middle and High School Students
summary: Mayor Eric Adams announced a $1.5 million grant from Pfizer Inc. to the Mayor's Fund to Advance New York City, dedicated to bolstering STEM educational programs for middle and high school students. The grant will support initiatives like "Exploring Futures," expanding career exploration for middle schoolers, and "College Now for Careers," enabling high school students to earn college credits in STEM fields. This funding aims to create career pathways and ensure young New Yorkers are prepared for future high-demand industries.

title: Happify Health Weaves a New Path as Twill, the Intelligent Healing Company™
summary: Happify Health has rebranded as Twill, establishing itself as "The Intelligent Healing Company™" to signify its evolution from wellness apps to a clinical-grade platform. Twill offers "Sequences™," configurable digital-first solutions that combine evidence-based digital therapeutics, well-being products, care communities, and coaching to provide personalized care for specific medical conditions. The company has already partnered with major healthcare entities like Elevance Health, Biogen, and Almirall to address conditions such as mental health, MS, pregnancy, and psoriasis.

title: Moderna mRNA Portfolio on Track to Hit 2025 Goal with Nipah Virus Trial Launch
summary: Moderna has initiated a Phase I clinical trial for mRNA-1215, a vaccine targeting the Nipah virus, a highly lethal zoonotic disease. This effort is part of Moderna's broader strategy to expand its mRNA vaccine portfolio, having already advanced several other candidates, including for Zika virus, and is on track to meet its goal of developing 15 priority vaccine programs by 2025. The company is also actively involved in developing mRNA vaccines for influenza and various oncology indications, alongside other pharmaceutical companies in the competitive mRNA space.

title: FDA Removes Clinical Hold on FLAMINGO-01 Trial in High-Risk HER2/Neu-Positive Breast Cancer
summary: The FDA has removed the clinical hold on the phase 3 FLAMINGO-01 trial for GLSI-100, a HER2/neu-peptide, designed for patients with high-risk HER2/neu-positive breast cancer. This allows the study to continue evaluating the activity and safety of GLSI-100 following discussions between Greenwich Life Sciences and the FDA regarding manufacturing and pharmacy process issues. The trial, NCT05232916, expects to enroll approximately 598 patients and will assess invasive breast cancer–free survival as its primary endpoint.

title: Hospira Issues A Voluntary Nationwide Recall For One Lot of Propofol Injectable Emulsion, USP (containing benzyl alcohol), Due To The Potential Presence of Visible Particulate.
summary: Hospira, Inc., a Pfizer company, has issued a voluntary nationwide recall for one lot of Propofol Injectable Emulsion, USP (containing benzyl alcohol) due to the potential presence of visible particulate matter. This recall, impacting lot DX9067, carries a risk of life-threatening adverse clinical effects such as blood vessel blockage, heart attack, and tissue necrosis, though no adverse events have been reported for this specific lot to date. The product was distributed to wholesalers, hospitals, and the Department of Defense in the U.S. from June 10 to June 26, 2020.

title: Eli Lilly and Co and Novo Nordisk AS Among Leading Companies in the Type 2 Diabetes Pipeline Market | GlobalData Plc
summary: Eli Lilly and Co and Novo Nordisk AS are identified as leading companies in the Type 2 Diabetes pipeline market, with Eli Lilly having the highest number of drugs in development. A report by GlobalData Plc details comprehensive information on therapeutics under development, including analysis by stage, target, mechanism of action, route of administration, and molecule type. The report also highlights key players and provides insights into R&D strategies for the Type 2 Diabetes market.

title: Agomab extenses Series B with USD40m Bringing Total Amount to USD114m
summary: Agomab Therapeutics NV has extended its Series B financing round by an additional $40.5 million, bringing the total raised to $114 million. Pfizer led this extension and has also partnered with Agomab to support the development of its lead compound for fibrostenotic Crohn's Disease. The funding will advance Agomab's pipeline of growth-factor-targeting antibodies and small molecules aimed at resolving fibrosis, repairing tissue, and restoring organ function.

title: Sanofi, Pfizer and More Use Upskilling to Solve the Life Science Talent Shortage
summary: Life science companies like Sanofi, Certara, Pfizer, and Thermo Fisher are utilizing upskilling programs to address talent shortages and skill gaps within the industry. These programs focus on training existing employees to fill open roles, foster a culture of continuous learning, and improve employee retention and attraction amidst a competitive labor market. The initiatives include digital academies, specialized pharmacometrics training in underserved regions, and comprehensive learning and development frameworks.

title: FDA Authorizes Novavax’s Covid-19 Vaccine
summary: The FDA has authorized Novavax Inc.'s Covid-19 vaccine for adults aged 18 and older, offering a new vaccination option that utilizes traditional protein-based technology. This authorization comes at a time when demand for Covid-19 vaccines and boosters is generally low. The company hopes this older technology will appeal to individuals hesitant about mRNA vaccines.

title: Want to Short TSLA Stock? Check Out the New TSLQ ETF.
summary: The AXS TSLA Bear Daily ETF (TSLQ) has launched, offering investors 1x inverse exposure to Tesla (TSLA) stock. This new leveraged single-stock ETF, which carries a 1.15% expense ratio, is designed for experienced investors seeking to bet against TSLA, which has declined over 40% year-to-date. Both the SEC and Federal Reserve Chair Gary Gensler have warned of the significant risks associated with single-stock ETFs.

title: If You Are Shorting Tesla via the AXS TSLA Bear Daily ETF (TSLQ), You Are in for Chronic Underperformance and Years of Toil
summary: AXS Investments has launched single-stock ETFs, including the AXS TSLA Bear Daily ETF (TSLQ), which allows investors to short Tesla. However, the article highlights that these ETFs are a "mind-numbingly dumb" and "very risky" investment due to exorbitant expense ratios (1.15%), daily resets leading to chronic underperformance, and a lack of diversification. The author warns that shorting Tesla via TSLQ is likely to result in chronic underperformance and significant losses over time despite its intended purpose.

title: AXS Launches Single-Stock Leveraged ETFs. They Aren’t for Long-Term Investors.
summary: AXS Investments has introduced a new suite of single-stock leveraged and inverse exchange-traded funds (ETFs) on the Nasdaq. These eight new funds are designed for active traders to amplify short-term bets on individual companies, rather than for long-term investors or retirement savers. Experts warn that these products are not suitable for passive investment strategies due to their inherent risks.

title: Canada clears Moderna's COVID vaccine for children under 5
summary: Canada has approved Moderna Inc.'s COVID-19 vaccine, Spikevax, for children aged 6 months to under 5 years, making it the first vaccine available for this age group in the country. This authorization allows approximately 1.7 million more children to be eligible for vaccination. Health Canada recommended that doses for this age group be one-quarter the size given to individuals over 12 years old.

title: Finally, a weight-loss drug that really works – but there’s a catch
summary: Novo Nordisk's Wegovy, a drug that regulates hunger using a hormone, has shown significant effectiveness in treating obesity. This article explores the impact of this new medication through the personal story of Lisa Robillard, who has struggled with weight loss for 40 years. While Wegovy is highly effective, the piece questions if it is the ultimate solution to the ongoing obesity crisis.

title: 경기 방어주로 부각…증시 침체에도 '탄탄'
summary: 글로벌 증시 침체 우려 속에서도 헬스케어 상장지수펀드(ETF)가 경기 방어주로 부각되며 반등하고 있다. 대표적인 미국 헬스케어 ETF인 XLV는 최근 1개월간 주가가 상승했으며, 장기적으로도 안정적인 수익률을 보여주고 있다. 금융투자 업계는 헬스케어 업종의 M&A 모멘텀이 하반기에도 시장 수익률을 넘어설 것으로 전망하고 있다.

title: Haleon makes market debut as GSK and Pfizer complete consumer health spin-off
summary: Haleon PLC has made its stock market debut as the largest company to list in London in over a decade, following its spin-out from GSK PLC and Pfizer. Existing GSK investors received shares in Haleon, with GSK retaining a 13.5% stake and Pfizer holding 32%. The consumer health company, known for brands like Sensodyne and Panadol, generated £9.5bn in sales last year and is expected to have an enterprise valuation of £40bn to £45bn, placing it in the top quarter of the FTSE 100.

title: Moderna Stock vs. Pfizer Stock: Which Is the Better Buy Now?
summary: This article analyzes whether Moderna or Pfizer stock is the better buy based on Morningstar's proprietary metrics as of July 2022. It compares the two companies on price/fair value, uncertainty, economic moat, and capital allocation ratings. Ultimately, Morningstar concluded that Moderna was the better buy at the time due to its undervaluation, despite Pfizer having stronger competitive advantages and lower uncertainty.

title: Incyte Announces U.S. FDA Approval of Opzelura™ (ruxolitinib) Cream for the Treatment of Vitiligo
summary: Incyte announced the U.S. FDA approval of Opzelura™ (ruxolitinib) cream 1.5% for the topical treatment of nonsegmental vitiligo in adult and pediatric patients 12 years and older, making it the first and only FDA-approved repigmentation treatment for vitiligo. The approval is supported by positive Phase 3 clinical trial data showing significant improvements in facial and total body repigmentation. Incyte will host an investor conference call on July 19, 2022, to discuss this milestone.

title: Psychedelic therapeutics market to have steady growth: InsightAce
summary: InsightAce Analytic projects the global psychedelic therapeutics market to reach US$8.31 billion by 2028, growing from US$3.61 billion in 2021 at a CAGR of 13.2 percent. This growth is attributed to renewed interest in psychedelics for mental health, increasing awareness of conventional drug inefficiencies, and rising stress levels. North America is expected to remain the dominant market.

title: Haleon has painful London debut following GSK demerger
summary: Haleon, the consumer healthcare company spun off from GSK, experienced a challenging debut on the London Stock Exchange, with its share price falling 6.6% on the first day, valuing the company at £30.5bn. This valuation was significantly lower than the £50bn offer Unilever made for the division in late 2021, leading to questions about GSK's judgment and leaving shareholders aggrieved. Despite the shaky start, Haleon is now the world's largest standalone consumer pharmaceutical business, while GSK plans to focus on vaccines and specialty medicines.

title: Amgen exec describes generative biology’s promise to unveil sequence, structure and function
summary: Amgen is heavily investing in generative biology, an emerging field that combines AI, machine learning, and high-throughput automation to accelerate protein drug discovery. Alan Russell, VP of biologics at Amgen, leads the Digital Biologics Discovery Group and emphasizes the importance of integrating wet lab and dry lab approaches to understand the links between protein sequence, structure, and function. The company's strategy involves leveraging decades of data generation, strategic investments in AI-ready infrastructure, and partnerships like the Teneobio acquisition and collaboration with Generate Biomedicines to overcome the challenges and timelines associated with traditional drug discovery.

title: Novavax COVID-19 vaccine approved by FDA and CDC, with UI Health Care’s help
summary: The FDA and CDC have approved Novavax Inc.'s COVID-19 vaccine for individuals 18 and older, making it the fourth authorized vaccine. UI Health Care played a crucial role by hosting one of the Phase 3 trials, with 150 Iowans participating. This vaccine utilizes traditional vaccine technology, similar to flu shots, which may appeal to those hesitant about mRNA vaccines, and can be stored at refrigerator temperatures for easier distribution.

title: Agonistic anti‐CD27 antibody ameliorates EAE by suppressing IL‐17 production
summary: This study investigates the role of CD27 costimulation in Experimental Autoimmune Encephalomyelitis (EAE), an animal model for multiple sclerosis, focusing on its impact on IL-17 production. The research demonstrates that agonistic anti-CD27 antibody treatment significantly reduces EAE severity and suppresses IL-17 and GM-CSF production by activated CD4+ T cells. These findings suggest CD27 costimulation as a potential therapeutic target for autoimmune diseases characterized by excessive IL-17 responses.

title: When will Novavax's vaccine be available, and how can I get it?
summary: The Biden administration has warned states to expect a limited supply of Novavax's COVID-19 vaccine, with the first shipments likely unavailable until the week of July 25, potentially delaying availability until August. This rollout differs from previous vaccines which were deployed quickly. Approximately three million doses will be available, primarily directed towards unvaccinated patients, though actual distribution to accessible locations like pharmacies remains uncertain.

title: The trispecific DARPin ensovibep inhibits diverse SARS-CoV-2 variants
summary: The trispecific DARPin ensovibep effectively inhibits a diverse range of SARS-CoV-2 variants, including Omicron sublineages BA.1 and BA.2, by co-operatively binding to the spike protein trimer and preventing ACE2 binding. Cryo-electron microscopy confirmed its mechanism of action. In a Roborovski dwarf hamster model, ensovibep reduced fatality and viral load comparably to a standard-of-care monoclonal antibody cocktail, supporting its potential as a broad-variant therapeutic for COVID-19.

title: FDA Fast Tracks OP-1250 for HR+, HER2- Metastatic Breast Cancer Treatment
summary: The FDA has granted Fast Track designation to OP-1250 for the treatment of HR+, HER2- metastatic breast cancer that has progressed after prior endocrine therapy and a CDK 4/6 inhibitor. This designation will expedite the development of OP-1250, a novel oral complete estrogen receptor antagonist and selective ER degrader. Two clinical trials are currently underway to further evaluate the efficacy and safety of OP-1250 as a monotherapy and in combination with palbociclib.

title: Clinical Catch-Up: Prometheus, Algernon, Seelos, Inozyme and Takeda
summary: This article provides a brief overview of recent clinical trial advancements from several biopharmaceutical companies. Prometheus Biosciences completed enrollment for a Phase II trial in ulcerative colitis, Algernon Pharmaceuticals reported positive Phase II data for ifenprodil in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, and Seelos Therapeutics dosed the first patient in a study for SLS-005 in ALS. Additionally, Inozyme Pharma, Kowa Pharmaceuticals, ADC Therapeutics, Synaptogenix, Celldex Therapeutics, and Takeda announced progress or results from their respective clinical programs, while VistaGen Therapeutics reported that its Phase III trial for social anxiety disorder failed to meet its primary endpoint.

title: Pfizer's retiring CFO mentored more than 20 future C-suite execs during his career. Here's what he's learned
summary: Frank D'Amelio, Pfizer's retiring CFO, mentored over 20 future C-suite executives during his 20-year career as a CFO, including 15 years at Pfizer. He emphasizes that business success hinges on talented people and the importance of mentoring, even informally, by providing honest feedback and opportunities for growth. D'Amelio highlights specific former mentees who achieved high-level positions, sharing insights into his mentoring philosophy.

title: Celcuity secures FDA 'breakthrough therapy designation' for breast cancer drug
summary: Celcuity received FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation for its experimental breast cancer drug, gedatolisib, for patients with ER+/HER- advanced metastatic breast cancer. This designation expedites development and signals confidence in early data showing a 75% clinical benefit rate. The Plymouth-based company plans to begin a global Phase 3 clinical trial soon.

title: A closer look at the X-ray equipment market
summary: The X-ray equipment market is experiencing significant growth, driven by technological advancements like AI integration and increased demand for early disease diagnosis. The COVID-19 pandemic further accelerated the adoption of digital radiography (DR) and mobile X-ray systems due to their efficiency and speed. The global market, valued at $6.7 billion in 2021, is projected to grow with a CAGR of 2.3% through 2030, with increasing adoption in developing countries and the rise of teleradiology and cloud computing contributing to market evolution.

title: Shares of HCA Healthcare Rise on Earnings Report
summary: HCA Healthcare Inc. reported second-quarter earnings that surpassed analyst expectations, leading to a significant rise in its stock price. Despite the quarterly earnings beat, the company's shares are down year-to-date and over the last 52 weeks. For investors seeking diversified healthcare exposure beyond market-cap weighted ETFs, the Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight Health Care ETF (RYH) offers an alternative with equal weighting for all holdings.

title: Pfizer, BMS vet hits Replay with $55M seed financing, 'Big DNA' ambitions
summary: Replay, a new biotech led by former Pfizer and Bristol Myers Squibb executive Adrian Woolfson, has launched with $55 million in seed financing. The company aims to reprogram biology and develop next-generation genomic products to target complex conditions like solid tumors and polygenic diseases. The funding was led by KKR and OMX Ventures, with participation from Artis Ventures, Lansdowne Partners, SALT, DeciBio Ventures, and Axial.

title: Behind Pfizer’s new quest to target a ‘transformation’ in pharma
summary: Pfizer and Roivant Sciences formed Priovant Therapeutics to target the growing autoimmune disease market with brepocitinib, a dual JAK1/TYK2 inhibitor. Priovant is focusing brepocitinib on systemic lupus erythematosus and dermatomyositis, conditions with high unmet needs, and aims for regulatory approval by late 2026 for dermatomyositis. The company hopes to revolutionize autoimmune disease therapy similar to how oncology treatments have advanced.

title: Pfizer loses U.S. appeal over co-pays for heart failure patients
summary: A federal appeals court in New York has denied Pfizer's challenge to a U.S. anti-kickback law, preventing the drugmaker from directly covering co-pays for low-income heart failure patients using its expensive drugs, Vyndaqel and Vyndamax. The court ruled that Pfizer's Direct Copay Assistance Program violated the ban on providing financial support to induce federally reimbursable drug purchases, siding with the government's argument against Medicare being burdened by "astronomical" drug prices. Pfizer expressed disappointment, asserting that co-pay assistance would enhance access to its critical medicine for patients.

title: White House says more money needed to develop additional COVID-19 vaccines
summary: The White House indicates that additional funding is likely required to develop and launch its fall COVID-19 vaccination campaign, particularly for new variant-adapted vaccines. While HHS stated that a recent 105 million dose order from Pfizer would be funded through reallocated funds, COVID-19 Response Coordinator Ashish Jha suggested more money from Congress would be needed. The Biden administration's request for $22.5 million for coronavirus efforts remains stalled in Congress.

title: Correction to: Real-world characteristics, treatment experiences and corticosteroid utilisation of patients treated with tofacitinib for moderate to severe ulcerative colitis
summary: This article is a correction to a previously published article in BMC Gastroenterology concerning the real-world characteristics, treatment experiences, and corticosteroid utilization of patients with moderate to severe ulcerative colitis treated with tofacitinib. The correction addresses an error in the copyright holder information, specifying that it should have been "Pfizer Inc. and The Author(s)" instead of just "The Author(s)". The original article has been updated to reflect this change.

title: 10 Big Named Companies With Huge Free Cash Flows @Ycharts
summary: This article identifies ten large-cap companies that exhibit high free cash flow relative to their market capitalization, using the Price to Free Cash Flow (P/FCF) metric. It explains that P/FCF is a robust valuation tool as it considers free cash flow, which accounts for capital expenditures, providing a more accurate view of a company's available cash. The list includes companies like JPMorgan Chase, Pfizer, and Apple, detailing their market cap, free cash flow, and P/FCF ratios.

title: Pfizer and BioNTech tease next-gen COVID-19 vaccine strategy
summary: Pfizer and BioNTech are developing a next-generation COVID-19 vaccine, BNT162b5, which features a modified spike protein to improve immunogenicity and durability of immune response. This vaccine candidate, blending RNAs for the ancestral strain and the Omicron BA.2 sub-lineage, is entering a Phase 2 study with 200 participants. The initiative aims to provide broader and more lasting protection againstSARS-CoV-2.

title: Regulatory warning letters in pharma: What can we learn post-COVID?
summary: This article examines the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on FDA inspections and the resulting trends in regulatory warning letters issued to pharmaceutical manufacturers. Authors Mirna Vazquez and Jessica Rayser from Charles River Laboratories discuss how decreased inspection numbers did not equate to reduced focus on quality, with certain citations increasing, particularly concerning investigations and equipment. The piece also highlights the FDA's continued emphasis on data integrity despite pandemic-related challenges, stressing that patient safety and product quality remain paramount.

title: Monoclonal antibody pairs "zipper" to target cancer
summary: Researchers have developed a new cancer treatment technology called Hexelect, which uses pairs of monoclonal antibodies (MAbs) that "zipper" together to form heterohexamers on cancer cells. This approach increases the specificity of the drug, activating complement-dependent cytotoxicity only when both MAbs bind to two specific antigens on the target cell, thereby reducing side effects on healthy cells. The technology, developed by Genmab and Leiden University in collaboration with the University of New Mexico, was published in Nature Biotechnology and shows promise for highly specific cancer therapies.

title: Pharma Stocks, ETFs Can Deal With Drug Pricing Legislation
summary: The reappearance of drug pricing legislation in a mid-term election year might seem challenging for the healthcare sector, but analysts believe blue-chip pharmaceutical companies, including those in the VanEck Vectors Pharmaceutical ETF (PPH), can manage potential lower drug prices. A proposed Senate plan would allow Medicare to negotiate reduced pharmaceutical prices, targeting 10 drugs initially and potentially more later, with discounts based on how long a drug has been on the market. Despite these developments, PPH holdings are not necessarily facing immediate downside as the proposal applies only to Medicare recipients, and companies may already be adjusting pricing in anticipation.

title: Biden Administration Plans to Offer Updated Booster Shots in September (Published 2022)
summary: The Biden administration plans to roll out a new Covid-19 booster campaign in September featuring retooled vaccines from Pfizer and Moderna, which are expected to be more effective against the Omicron subvariant BA.5. Federal officials decided to wait for these updated shots rather than expand eligibility for second boosters of existing vaccines to younger Americans now. This decision aims to strengthen immunity more effectively for everyone ahead of a potential winter surge.

title: U.S. sets $1.74 billion deal with Moderna for updated COVID vaccine
summary: The U.S. government has agreed to a $1.74 billion deal with Moderna for 66 million doses of an updated COVID vaccine targeting the Omicron subvariant, intended for a fall and winter booster campaign. This deal, combined with a previous agreement with Pfizer and BioNTech, brings the U.S. booster supply to about 171 million shots. The updated vaccines aim to combat the BA.4 and BA.5 Omicron subvariants that are currently dominant in U.S. infections.

title: U.S. sets $1.74 billion deal with Moderna for updated COVID vaccine
summary: The U.S. government has announced a $1.74 billion deal with Moderna for 66 million doses of an updated COVID vaccine targeting the Omicron subvariant. This agreement, combined with a previous deal with Pfizer and BioNTech, aims to provide approximately 171 million booster shots for a fall and winter campaign. The updated vaccines are crucial as the BA.4 and BA.5 Omicron subvariants, which have significant mutations, are causing a rise in U.S. infections.

title: With ‘bold experiment’ in drug pricing, Arcutis aims to stand out in plaque psoriasis
summary: Arcutis Biotherapeutics has set a lower wholesale price of $825 for its new plaque psoriasis drug, Zoryve, compared to competitors, a strategy the company calls a "bold experiment." CEO Frank Watanabe believes this pricing will accelerate insurance coverage and patient adoption by reducing out-of-pocket costs and avoiding prior authorizations. The company hopes this approach will differentiate Zoryve in a crowded market for inflammatory skin treatments.

title: As pharma's NASH failures pile up, Regeneron thinks it found the target that matters
summary: Regeneron researchers have identified a promising new target for nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) called the CIDEB gene, which showed a 53% risk reduction for NASH in individuals with specific loss-of-function mutations. This discovery, based on a large genetic analysis of over 540,000 people, could inform new therapeutic approaches for the notoriously hard-to-treat liver disease, where many other pharmaceutical companies have met clinical failure. Regeneron is optimistic that this genetic insight will lead to an approved treatment, distinguishing its efforts from previous industry setbacks.

title: Biosimilars: An Important Tool in Cigna’s Efforts To Lower Drug Prices and Support Innovation
summary: Cigna advocates for biosimilars to reduce drug spending and increase market competition, estimating potential savings of $225 billion to $375 billion over the next decade. While biologics are essential for various conditions, they are costly, and manufacturers often employ tactics to extend patent protection. Cigna has actively promoted biosimilar adoption, exemplified by moving Avsola and Inflectra to preferred status and incentivizing switches to biosimilar alternatives.

title: Rigel bets $230M that Forma's leukemia drug gets in formation with FDA
summary: Rigel Pharmaceuticals has acquired exclusive licensing rights to Forma Therapeutics’ oncology treatment, olutasidenib, for $2 million upfront. The agreement includes potential milestone payments totaling up to $233 million, tied to regulatory approval, commercial sales, and future development. Olutasidenib, currently awaiting an FDA decision by February 2023, is for relapsed/refractory acute myeloid leukemia and would be Rigel's second commercial product in hematology-oncology if approved.

title: Poseida Therapeutics Announces Strategic Global Collaboration with Roche Focused on Allogeneic CAR-T Cell Therapies for Hematologic Malignancies
summary: Poseida Therapeutics announced a strategic global collaboration with Roche to develop allogeneic CAR-T cell therapies for hematologic malignancies. Poseida will receive $110 million upfront, potentially up to $110 million in near-term milestones, and could earn up to $6 billion in aggregate value plus tiered royalties. The collaboration leverages Poseida's cell therapy approach and Roche's expertise to advance existing and next-generation CAR-T programs.

title: Novavax available at public health district vaccine clinics
summary: The Novavax COVID-19 vaccine is now available at all Corpus Christi-Nueces County Health District clinics, becoming the fourth vaccine authorized in the U.S. It is a two-dose series, administered three to eight weeks apart, and is available at no cost to residents. Three clinic locations are open for appointments in Nueces County.

title: Global TNF Alpha Inhibitors Market Report 2022-2026 & 2031
summary: The global TNF Alpha Inhibitors market is projected to grow from $38.56 billion in 2021 to $40.73 billion in 2022, reaching $43.83 billion by 2026. This growth is primarily driven by the increasing prevalence of inflammatory diseases like inflammatory bowel disease and psoriasis. Key players in this market include AbbVie, Amgen, and Johnson & Johnson, though the market faces limitations due to the adverse side effects of TNF alpha inhibitors.

title: Chairman Of World’s Hottest Stock AMTD Now Worth Nearly $37 Billion, More Than Li Ka-Shing
summary: Calvin Choi, chairman of AMTD Digital, has seen his stake in the company surge to nearly $37 billion, making him Asia's sixth-richest person on paper. This valuation, driven by a 14,000% stock increase, is largely unexplainable by the company's financial performance or small employee base. Despite concerns about the stock's stability and comparisons to meme stocks, Choi continues to expand AMTD Group's ventures, including into the metaverse, while facing scrutiny over past financial practices.

title: Merck & Co.'s $40B Acquisition of Pharmaceutical Company Seagen
summary: Merck & Co. is pursuing a $40 billion acquisition of Seattle-based biotech firm Seagen, which would be the largest pharmaceutical acquisition since 2020. This move is crucial for Merck's oncology business as its key drug, Keytruda, will lose patent exclusivity by 2028. Seagen, a cancer-focused company with four patented drugs and a strong development pipeline, could provide Merck with a powerful set of treatments, though the deal is expected to face significant scrutiny from the Federal Trade Commission due to potential anti-competitive concerns.

title: Pneumococcal 24-Valent Conjugate Vaccine Gets Fast Track Designation
summary: The FDA has granted Fast Track designation to VAX-24, an investigational 24-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine, for the prevention of invasive pneumococcal disease in adults 18 years and older. Vaxcyte is currently comparing VAX-24 to Prevnar 20 in phase 1/2 clinical studies, with topline safety results anticipated later this year. This designation is expected to expedite the delivery of VAX-24 to both adults and children, offering broader protection against the serious disease.

title: Biohaven Reports Second Quarter 2022 Financial Results and Reports Recent Business Developments
summary: Biohaven Pharmaceutical Holding Company Ltd. announced its second quarter 2022 financial results, highlighted by a 57% sequential increase in NURTEC ODT net product revenue to $194 million. The company reported a net loss of $6.21 per share, primarily due to derivative losses related to the pending acquisition by Pfizer. Biohaven also shared progress on its pipeline, including the FDA's acceptance of the zavegepant nasal spray New Drug Application and commencement of a Phase 3 trial for taldefgrobep alfa in Spinal Muscular Atrophy.

title: WSJ News Exclusive | Pfizer in Advanced Talks to Buy Global Blood Therapeutics for About $5 Billion
summary: Pfizer Inc. is reportedly in advanced talks to acquire Global Blood Therapeutics Inc. for approximately $5 billion. This potential deal would allow Pfizer to bolster its pharmaceutical portfolio and pipeline, specifically in the area of sickle-cell disease with GBT's recently approved drug. Pfizer aims to finalize the agreement in the coming days, although other suitors may still be involved.

title: Biotech ETFs Rally as Global Blood Therapeutics Surges on Potential Pfizer Deal
summary: Biotechnology-related exchange-traded funds (ETFs) saw a rally after reports emerged of Pfizer Inc. (NYSE: PFE) potentially acquiring Global Blood Therapeutics (NasdaqGS: GBT) for $5 billion. This potential acquisition would allow Pfizer to expand its drug portfolio with long-term commercial treatments beyond its COVID-19 vaccine. Global Blood Therapeutics' FDA-approved drug, Oxbryta, for sickle cell disease, is a key asset driving this interest.

title: Pfizer to buy Global Blood Therapeutics in $5.4 billion deal
summary: Pfizer announced a $5.4 billion agreement to acquire Global Blood Therapeutics, a blood disorder drugmaker. This acquisition boosts Pfizer's rare disease treatment portfolio with Oxbryta, a drug for sickle cell disease, and is part of Pfizer's strategy to acquire new assets and diversify its sales beyond its COVID-19 products. The deal comes as Pfizer, flush with cash from vaccine sales, seeks to expand its pipeline to ensure strong earnings visibility as key patents approach expiration.

title: Pfizer continues pandemic-revenue buying spree with $5.4 billion hematology deal
summary: Pfizer is acquiring Global Blood Therapeutics for $5.4 billion to bolster its rare hematology capabilities, utilizing the significant revenue generated during the COVID-19 pandemic. This acquisition, which includes the sickle cell disease drug Oxybryta, is part of Pfizer's strategy to expand its portfolio and achieve $25 billion in sales from new business developments by 2030, following several other recent acquisitions. The deal is expected to close in the fourth quarter, pending regulatory and shareholder approval.

title: These Stocks are Buzzing Thanks to the US Senate Passing $430B Climate Bill
summary: The US Senate passed the $430 billion Inflation Reduction Act, allocating about $370 billion to climate and energy programs, causing clean energy stocks and related ETFs to rally. Electric vehicle companies like Tesla, Rivian, and Lucid Group saw gains, while pharmaceutical giants Pfizer, Sanofi, and Eli Lilly experienced slight declines due to Medicare drug price negotiation provisions. The bill's passage into law is expected to benefit the clean energy sector, despite earlier volatility influenced by Senator Manchin's stance.

title: Watkins Advises on Global Blood Therapeutics’ US$5.4 Billion Sale to Pfizer
