summary: Latham & Watkins LLP advised J.P. Morgan Securities LLC and Centerview Partners LLC, financial advisors to Global Blood Therapeutics (GBT), on its US$5.4 billion sale to Pfizer Inc. The acquisition aims to enhance Pfizer's rare hematology offerings and reinforce its commitment to addressing critical needs in the underserved sickle cell disease community with GBT's pipeline.

title: Pfizer to Acquire Global Blood Therapeutics for $5.4 Billion to Enhance Presence in Rare Hematology
summary: Pfizer announced its definitive agreement to acquire Global Blood Therapeutics (GBT) for approximately $5.4 billion. This acquisition aims to enhance Pfizer's presence in rare hematology and reinforce its commitment to sickle cell disease (SCD) by integrating GBT's expertise and leading portfolio, including Oxbryta and promising pipeline candidates. The deal is expected to create an SCD franchise with potential combined worldwide peak sales exceeding $3 billion.

title: Positive trial results for schizophrenia drug, KarTX, from PureTech's founded entity, Karuna Therapeutics
summary: Karuna Therapeutics announced positive topline results from its Phase 3 EMERGENT-2 trial for KarXT (xanomeline-trospium), a schizophrenia drug. The trial met its primary endpoint, showing a statistically significant reduction in symptoms. PureTech Health plc, a founder of Karuna, stands to benefit from royalty and milestone payments from the commercialization of KarXT.

title: Flush with cash, Pfizer buys Global Blood Therapeutics in $5.4 billion deal
summary: Pfizer has agreed to acquire Global Blood Therapeutics (GBT) for $5.4 billion in cash, aiming to bolster its portfolio as COVID-19 vaccine and treatment sales are expected to decline. This acquisition adds GBT's sickle cell disease treatment, Oxbryta, and two pipeline assets, which Pfizer projects could generate over $3 billion in annual sales. The deal reflects Pfizer's strategy of diversifying its M&A deals to improve growth in the latter half of the decade.

title: Novavax tumbles 31% as waning COVID-19 vaccine demand hits revenue forecast
summary: Novavax's shares fell by 31% after the company significantly cut its annual revenue forecast due to decreased demand for its COVID-19 vaccine. The company's vaccine, which was launched late in the U.S., has seen low administration rates, leading to a reduction in its 2022 revenue expectation from $4-$5 billion to $2-$2.3 billion, impacting investor confidence. Despite current challenges, analysts believe Novavax could still play a role in the future COVID re-vaccination market.

title: Novavax tumbles 30% as waning COVID-19 vaccine demand hits outlook
summary: Novavax shares dropped significantly after the company drastically cut its annual revenue forecast due to weaker-than-expected demand for its COVID-19 vaccine. Reduced demand from low- and middle-income nations and a slow uptake in the U.S. market contributed to the revised outlook, despite hopes for its vaccine among mRNA skeptics. The company remains optimistic about next year, anticipating a more competitive market with updated vaccine versions.

title: Pfizer Inc. stock rises Wednesday, still underperforms market
summary: Pfizer Inc. (PFE) stock increased 0.34% on Wednesday, closing at $49.95, marking its third consecutive day of gains. Despite the rise, the stock significantly underperformed the broader market indices like the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average. Pfizer also lagged behind some of its competitors while outperforming others on the day.

title: A lightspeed approach to pandemic drug development
summary: Pfizer successfully developed COVID-19 vaccines and treatments at "lightspeed" by streamlining decisions, running parallel processes, and fostering a purpose-driven culture. This approach, which significantly shortened development timelines from years to months, can serve as a model for future drug development in other therapeutic areas. Key factors included external partnerships, internal R&D investments, and expedited clinical programs in consultation with regulatory agencies.

title: Pfizer’s new pneumococcal vaccine meets study goal in children
summary: Pfizer's new pneumococcal vaccine, Prevnar 20, met its primary study goal in a Phase 3 trial for children, showing immune responses comparable to Prevnar 13. The company plans to seek expanded FDA approval for Prevnar 20 in children later this year, intensifying its competition with Merck in the pneumococcal vaccine market.

title: Great Greeks of international biotechnology
summary: This article highlights the significant contributions of Greek scientists and entrepreneurs in the international biotechnology sector and explores Greece's potential to become a key player in the field. It discusses the challenges, such as bureaucracy and lack of a unified strategy, that Greece faces in attracting investments and retaining talent, and outlines proposals made to the Prime Minister by a working group of prominent Greek biotech figures to establish a favorable ecosystem. The piece features interviews with successful Greek professionals like Dr. Simos Simeonidis, Dr. Vangelis Vergetis, and Dr. Stelios Papadopoulos, chairman of Biogen, emphasizing their commitment to innovation and collaboration.

title: Sanofi trial failure halts work on breast cancer treatment amcenestrant
summary: Sanofi has halted development of its breast cancer treatment, amcenestrant, after a second trial failed to show any benefit, impacting the company's shares. This failure puts more pressure on Sanofi to develop new drugs, as it increasingly relies on its successful eczema treatment, Dupixent. The news also comes amidst ongoing concerns and a recent drop in share price due to litigation surrounding the heartburn drug Zantac, which Sanofi previously sold.

title: Next-gen Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine candidates fare well in Phase 2/3 study
summary: Pfizer and BioNTech have released positive Phase 2/3 study data for two omicron-specific COVID-19 vaccine candidates, a monovalent and a bivalent option. Both next-generation vaccines demonstrated a significantly higher immune response against omicron BA.1 compared to their original vaccine. The companies plan to share this data with health authorities to accelerate the potential introduction of an omicron-adapted booster.

title: Quest Diagnostics introduces new HCV obstetrics test panel
summary: Quest Diagnostics has launched a new obstetrics laboratory test panel designed to screen eligible pregnant individuals for hepatitis C (HCV), based on findings from their Health Trends study. The study revealed that less than 41% of pregnant individuals were screened for HCV last year, with lower rates among those with Medicaid. This new panel integrates HCV antibody testing into standard obstetric tests to improve screening rates and promote better outcomes, aligning with recent guidelines from health organizations.

title: Canada OKs Pfizer COVID booster for kids 5-11, sees monkeypox cases slow
summary: Canada's health ministry has authorized Pfizer's COVID-19 vaccine as a booster for children aged five to 11, six months after their initial two doses. Concurrently, Canada is also observing a decline in COVID-19 cases, though health officials stress preparedness for new variants, and a slowing trend in new monkeypox cases, with the majority reported among men who have sex with men.

title: FDA asks Pfizer to test second Paxlovid course in patients with COVID rebound
summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has requested Pfizer Inc. to conduct a study on the efficacy of a second course of its antiviral drug, Paxlovid, for patients who experience a rebound of COVID-19 symptoms after initial treatment. This directive comes after reports of recurrent infections, including in high-profile figures like President Joe Biden and Dr. Anthony Fauci, prompting the FDA to ask Pfizer to finalize a trial protocol by September 30 of next year. Pfizer is currently collaborating with the FDA to iron out the details of this study to address the need for retreatment in some patients.

title: The Efficacy of Anti-TNFs in Immune-Mediated Disease
summary: This mini-review article discusses the efficacy of anti-TNF therapies in the treatment of various immune-mediated inflammatory diseases (IMIDs) such as rheumatoid arthritis, Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis, and psoriasis. It highlights how these therapies have revolutionized IMID management, summarizing data from meta-analyses of clinical trials and real-world studies. The article also touches on the challenges of treatment, including loss of response, and current strategies to optimize anti-TNF therapy.

title: Pfizer and BioNTech Submit Application to U.S. FDA for Emergency Use Authorization of Omicron BA.4/BA.5-Adapted Bivalent COVID-19 Vaccine
summary: Pfizer and BioNTech have submitted an application to the U.S. FDA for Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) of their Omicron BA.4/BA.5-adapted bivalent COVID-19 vaccine as a booster dose for individuals 12 years and older. This follows FDA guidance, and if authorized, the companies are prepared for immediate distribution to address potential surges in fall and winter. A conditional marketing authorization application has also been initiated with the European Medicines Agency.

title: Hospira Issues A Voluntary Nationwide Recall For One Lot of Propofol Injectable Emulsion (containing benzyl alcohol), Due To The Potential Presence of Visible Particulates
summary: Hospira, Inc., a Pfizer company, is voluntarily recalling one lot of Propofol Injectable Emulsion (containing benzyl alcohol), 100mL Single Patient Use Glass Fliptop Vial, due to the potential presence of visible particulates. The recalled lot EA7470 was distributed nationwide in the U.S. from July 16, 2020, through July 24, 2020. Patients receiving the impacted product could face adverse events such as vessel blockage, heart attack, or hypersensitivity reactions, though no adverse events have been reported to date for this specific lot.

title: Pfizer's COVID vaccine 73.2% effective in kids under 5, new data shows
summary: New data from Pfizer and BioNTech indicates their COVID-19 vaccine is 73.2% effective in preventing the disease among children aged 6 months to 4 years. This updated efficacy figure, based on a study conducted when the Omicron BA.2 variant was dominant, follows the U.S. rollout of the shots for this age group in June. The companies are also preparing an application for a bivalent vaccine targeting BA.4/BA.5 subvariants for children under 12, and an adult booster application is already submitted.

title: VitaCholine®: The DHA Booster
summary: This article promotes a webcast discussing the synergistic effect of VitaCholine and DHA on brain health, particularly during pregnancy. Recent research from Cornell University suggests that VitaCholine supplementation significantly improves DHA status in pregnant women compared to DHA alone. The webcast aims to educate product developers and marketers on leveraging this nutrient synergy for new products and claims across the lifespan.

title: Johnson & Johnson lost to Pfizer in bidding war for Global Blood Therapeutics: Bloomberg
summary: Johnson & Johnson was the mysterious "company A" that battled Pfizer for Global Blood Therapeutics (GBT), initially offering $55 per share and raising it multiple times before losing out to Pfizer's final $67.50 bid. This would have been J&J's largest acquisition in two years and the first under new CEO Joaquin Duato. For Pfizer, the acquisition brings an FDA-approved sickle cell disease drug, Oxbryta, and pipeline candidates, with SVB Securities analysts projecting GBT's SCD franchise sales to reach $2.7 billion by 2030.

title: Cemiplimab plus chemotherapy versus chemotherapy alone in non-small cell lung cancer: a randomized, controlled, double-blind phase 3 trial
summary: The EMPOWER-Lung 3 phase 3 study investigated cemiplimab plus platinum-doublet chemotherapy as a first-line treatment for advanced non-small cell lung cancer (aNSCLC), regardless of PD-L1 expression or histology. The trial was stopped early due to meeting preset overall survival (OS) efficacy criteria, showing a median OS of 21.9 months for the cemiplimab group versus 13.0 months for the placebo group. Cemiplimab proved to be the second anti-PD-1/PD-L1 agent effective in aNSCLC as both monotherapy and in combination with chemotherapy for both squamous and non-squamous histologies.

title: Rare Diseases Treatment Market Size, Share, Growth, Trends | Report 2022-2030
summary: The rare diseases treatment market, valued at USD 119.71 billion in 2021, is projected to reach USD 335.99 billion by 2030, growing at a CAGR of 12.15%. Key growth drivers include the increasing prevalence of rare diseases, supportive government regulations like the Orphan Drug Act, and strategic collaborations in product development. North America currently dominates the market, with the Asia Pacific expected to be the fastest-growing region.

title: Moderna sues Pfizer, BioNTech over COVID-19 vaccine patents
summary: Moderna has filed lawsuits against Pfizer and BioNTech in U.S. federal and German courts, alleging patent infringement related to their COVID-19 vaccine, Comirnaty. Moderna claims the companies copied its mRNA technology, which it developed over a decade, for their vaccine. While Moderna is not seeking to remove Comirnaty from the market or prevent future sales, it expects intellectual property respect and a commercially reasonable license for ex-low/middle-income markets.

title: Abbott Update On Powder Formula Recall | Abbott Newsroom
summary: Abbott is restarting Similac infant formula production at its Sturgis, Michigan facility, expecting products to reach shelves in about six weeks. The company has taken steps to increase formula supply nationwide, including importing from Ireland and Spain, and prioritizing production at other U.S. facilities. Abbott reaffirms its commitment to quality and safety, detailing enhanced testing and facility upgrades, while also addressing investigations into previous Cronobacter concerns.

title: Moderna suing Pfizer, BioNTech for patent infringement in development of COVID-19 vaccine
summary: Moderna is suing Pfizer and BioNTech for patent infringement related to the development of their COVID-19 vaccine, alleging they copied mRNA technology Moderna pioneered. The lawsuit seeks unspecified monetary damages and was filed in the U.S. and Germany. Moderna states it is protecting its intellectual property, which it invested billions in creating over a decade before the pandemic.

title: Moderna Sues Pfizer and BioNTech Over Covid Vaccine Technology (Published 2022)
summary: Moderna has filed lawsuits against Pfizer and BioNTech in the U.S. and Germany, alleging that their COVID-19 vaccine infringes on Moderna's mRNA technology patents. Moderna claims the patents were filed between 2011 and 2016, preceding the pandemic. Pfizer and BioNTech have expressed surprise and stated they will vigorously defend against the allegations, asserting the originality of their work.

title: Moderna Sues Pfizer, BioNTech Over COVID-19 mRNA Vaccine Patents
summary: Moderna has filed patent infringement lawsuits against Pfizer and BioNTech in both the U.S. and Germany, alleging that their COVID-19 vaccine, Comirnaty®, infringes on Moderna's mRNA technology patents filed between 2010 and 2016. Moderna claims this foundational work was critical to developing its own vaccine, Spikevax®. While not seeking to remove Comirnaty® from the market or block future sales, Moderna is seeking compensation for the use of its patented technologies in markets outside the AMC 92 low- and middle-income countries.

title: Pfizer Inc. stock falls Friday, still outperforms market
summary: Pfizer Inc. (PFE) stock fell on Friday, August 26, 2022, by 2.25% to $46.82, despite an overall dismal trading session for the market where the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average saw larger declines. The stock underperformed some competitors like Johnson & Johnson, Merck & Co., and Novartis AG ADR. Pfizer Inc. closed $14.89 below its 52-week high reached in December 2020.

title: Moderna to sue BioNTech/Pfizer over COVID vaccine
summary: Moderna is suing Pfizer and BioNTech, alleging that their COVID-19 vaccine, Comirnaty, infringes on patents related to Moderna's mRNA technology platform. Moderna claims to have pioneered this technology and invested billions in its development prior to the pandemic. While Moderna previously vowed not to enforce COVID-related patents, it states that the pandemic has entered a new phase where vaccine supply is no longer a barrier, expecting competitors to respect intellectual property rights in most markets.

title: Moderna sues Pfizer/BioNTech for patent infringement over COVID vaccine
summary: Moderna has sued Pfizer and BioNTech for patent infringement, alleging they copied Moderna's mRNA technology for their COVID-19 vaccine. The lawsuit, filed in the U.S. and Germany, seeks unspecified monetary damages. Pfizer and BioNTech have expressed surprise and stated they will vigorously defend against the allegations, asserting their vaccine was based on BioNTech's proprietary technology.

title: Covid-19 vaccine: Moderna sues Pfizer/BioNTech for patent infringement
summary: Moderna has filed lawsuits against Pfizer and its German partner BioNTech, alleging patent infringement in the development of their COVID-19 vaccine. Moderna claims Pfizer/BioNTech copied its innovative mRNA technology, which Moderna pioneered and patented between 2010 and 2016. While Moderna previously stated it would not enforce its patents early in the pandemic, it seeks undetermined monetary damages for activities after March 8, 2022.

title: Moderna sues Pfizer and BioNTech with Freshfields in Europe
summary: Moderna has filed patent infringement lawsuits against Pfizer and BioNTech in Germany and the US, seeking damages related to their mRNA COVID-19 vaccines. Moderna claims the companies unlawfully copied key features of its patented mRNA technology, which it developed between 2010 and 2016. The lawsuits specifically exclude damages for sales to AMC 92 countries and do not seek injunctive relief to remove the vaccines from the market, focusing instead on compensation for alleged past infringements.

title: Novartis Scemblix®, with novel mechanism of action, approved by the European Commission for adult patients with chronic myeloid leukemia
summary: The European Commission has approved Novartis's Scemblix (asciminib) for adult patients with Philadelphia chromosome-positive chronic myeloid leukemia in chronic phase (Ph+ CML-CP) who have been previously treated with two or more tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs). Scemblix, a first-of-its-kind STAMP inhibitor, offers a new treatment option for patients experiencing intolerance or resistance to existing TKI therapies. This approval is based on results from the pivotal Phase III ASCEMBL trial, which demonstrated a significantly higher major molecular response rate and lower discontinuation rate due to adverse reactions compared to bosutinib.

title: Scientists question Moderna invention claim in COVID-19 vaccine dispute
summary: Moderna is engaged in a patent dispute with Pfizer and BioNTech over their COVID-19 mRNA vaccines, accusing them of infringing on its patented inventions. However, scientists Drew Weissman and Katalin Karikó claim a key invention cited by Moderna, the 1-methylpseudouridine modification, was patented by them years earlier. This legal battle arises as both companies anticipate new markets for updated vaccine formulations and increased profits.

title: Role of kappa‐opioid and mu‐opioid receptors in pruritus: Peripheral and central itch circuits
summary: This research article explores the roles of kappa-opioid receptors (KORs) and mu-opioid receptors (MORs) in regulating pruritus (itch) within both peripheral and central nervous systems. It highlights how KORs generally suppress itch while MORs can promote it, and discusses promising therapeutic strategies targeting these receptors for chronic pruritic conditions like atopic dermatitis and uremic pruritus. The article also reviews opioid receptor modulators currently in clinical development and emphasizes the need for further research into their precise mechanisms and optimal delivery methods.

title: Arcturus Awarded $63.2M to Advance Self-amplifying mRNA Vaccine for Pandemic Influenza Response
summary: Arcturus Therapeutics Holdings, Inc. has been awarded $63.2 million by BARDA to advance its self-amplifying mRNA vaccine for pandemic influenza response. This funding will support preclinical development through Phase 1 clinical studies over a three-year period. The vaccine utilizes Arcturus' STARR™ platform, which offers advantages like lower doses, freeze-dried formulation for stable cold chain, and rapid scalability, aligning with U.S. government pandemic preparedness goals.

title: Are Fibroblasts Overlooked?
summary: This article discusses the overlooked potential of fibroblasts in regenerative medicine, contrasting them with more commonly researched stem cells. FibroBiologics Regenerative Medicine, led by Pete O'Heeron and Dr. Hamid Khoja, is developing fibroblast-based therapies for conditions like degenerative disc disease, Multiple Sclerosis, and cancer immunology, highlighting their ease of sourcing, culturing, and immune modulation capabilities. The company is also investigating the specific mechanisms by which fibroblasts function in various clinical applications.

title: CDC recommends new booster shots to fight omicron
summary: The CDC has endorsed updated COVID-19 booster shots from Moderna and Pfizer-BioNTech, which target both the original coronavirus strain and the omicron BA.4 and BA.5 subvariants. The decision, based on a 13-1 advisory vote, aims to better protect against currently circulating variants, with some experts recommending a longer waiting period between shots for optimal effectiveness. While some advisers expressed concerns about the lack of human trial data for these specific reformulated boosters, others argued that the approach is similar to annual flu vaccine updates and crucial for staying ahead of the evolving virus.

title: Inflation act has slashed value of small molecules: Lilly’s Ricks
summary: Eli Lilly CEO David Ricks states that the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) has significantly reduced the economic value of small molecule therapies, effectively halving their worth. He warns that this will lead companies like Eli Lilly and Co. (NYSE:LLY) to abandon development programs that would have previously been considered viable, creating incentives misaligned with science and patient needs.

title: COVID-19 mRNA Vaccine Safety Among Children Aged 6 months to...
summary: This report details the initial safety findings of mRNA COVID-19 vaccines (Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna) among children aged 6 months to 5 years in the U.S. from June 18 to August 21, 2022. Data from v-safe and VAERS indicate that local and systemic reactions are expected but generally mild to moderate, with serious adverse events being rare. No cases of myocarditis were reported in this age group, consistent with preauthorization clinical trials.

title: Taiwan approves Omicron-targeted Moderna COVID vaccine
summary: Taiwan has approved Moderna Inc's Omicron-targeted COVID-19 vaccine for use as a booster shot for individuals aged 18 and over. The approval by the Taiwan Food and Drug Administration came after evaluating the vaccine's effectiveness and safety, considering the urgent public health needs. This follows a similar authorization by the U.S. FDA for updated Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna booster shots designed to target the BA.4 and BA.5 Omicron subvariants.

title: Explainer: Updated COVID vaccines are coming to U.S. Should you get one?
summary: Updated COVID-19 booster shots targeting the BA.4 and BA.5 Omicron subvariants have been approved in the U.S. for individuals aged 12 and older, with Pfizer/BioNTech and Moderna vaccines rolling out. Health officials recommend these boosters due to waning immunity and for preventing serious illness and long COVID, though some experts advise caution against overstating benefits. Those who recently had a booster or COVID should wait at least two to three months before getting the updated shot to ensure a better immune response.

title: Amazon discriminating against Asians, whites in grant program, class action lawsuit says
summary: A class action lawsuit alleges that Amazon discriminates against Asian and white applicants in its "Diversity Grant" program, which offers stipends to Black, Latinx, and Native American entrepreneurs. The lawsuit, filed by Crystal Bolduc, claims the program violates the Civil Rights Act of 1866 by forcing Asian and white hopefuls to cover their own startup costs. Bolduc seeks to end the program and obtain damages for those who have experienced racial discrimination due to it.

title: Innovators: Dr. Judith Klimovsky
summary: Dr. Judith Klimovsky, EVP and Chief Development Officer at Genmab, leverages her extensive oncology R&D background to advance antibody-drug conjugates, guided by a patient-first philosophy. She played a key role in the FDA approval of Tivdak for cervical cancer and champions a leadership style that fosters empathy and deep connections within her team, especially through virtual interactions. Klimovsky emphasizes active listening, critical thinking, and inclusivity to drive innovation and breakthroughs in cancer treatment.

title: Heritage Global Partners Awarded New Global Vendor Contract With Pfizer
summary: Heritage Global Partners (HGP) has been re-selected by Pfizer as its global vendor for laboratory equipment asset disposition services through a new multi-year contract starting January 1, 2023. This extended partnership, built on a decade of collaboration, will see HGP manage the sales and redeployment of Pfizer's surplus lab assets worldwide, aiming for approximately 5,000 asset sales annually. The agreement emphasizes HGP's role in helping Pfizer achieve financial asset recovery and contribute to the circular economy by extending the lifecycle of assets.

title: 퇴행성 뇌질환 '헌팅턴병' 치료제 방향성은?
summary: KAIST 송지준 교수 연구팀이 헌팅턴병 치료를 위한 새로운 방법론을 제시했습니다. 이 연구는 질병을 유발하는 돌연변이 헌팅틴 단백질의 기능을 유지하면서 질병을 막는 형태로 전환하는 방법을 제안하며, 헌팅턴병 치료제 개발에 새로운 방향을 제시할 것으로 기대됩니다. 이 연구 결과는 국제 학술지 '임상연구저널(Journal of Clinical Investigation Insights)'에 게재되었습니다.

title: Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) Clinical Trial Analysis Featuring 60+ Companies | DelveInsight
summary: DelveInsight's report highlights that over 60 companies are actively developing more than 75 treatment therapies for Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD). The report provides comprehensive insights into the pipeline, including various stages of clinical development, key companies involved, and promising therapies like Vamorolone and Delandistrogene moxeparvovec. Recent clinical trial advancements for treatments such as CAP-1002, pamrevlumab, elamipretide, and RGX-202 are also detailed.

title: FDA rejects Alvotech’s Humira copycat on manufacturing issues
summary: The FDA rejected Alvotech’s application for its Humira biosimilar (AVT02) due to manufacturing issues found during an inspection of its Reykjavik plant. This rejection comes despite AVT02 being approved in several other countries. Alvotech aims to address the deficiencies and expects to be ready for a July 1, 2023 U.S. launch, joining other companies preparing to introduce interchangeable Humira biosimilars.

title: Insula deep rTMS and varenicline for smoking cessation: A randomized control trial study protocol
summary: This study protocol outlines a randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled clinical trial investigating the efficacy of combining insula deep repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) with varenicline for smoking cessation. The trial will enroll 50 nicotine-dependent smokers, aiming to determine if this combined approach leads to improved abstinence rates compared to varenicline treatment alone. The primary outcome will be 7-day point prevalence abstinence at 12 weeks, with several secondary outcomes including nicotine dependence, withdrawal symptoms, and long-term abstinence.

title: Unfractionated Heparin Market to Continue Impressive Measured
summary: A market research report predicts the Unfractionated Heparin Market will experience impressive growth through 2028. The comprehensive study, by Coherent Market Insights, offers in-depth analysis of market structure, key players, growth strategies, and future prospects, segmented by product type, application, end-user, and geography. Major companies identified include B. Braun Melsungen AG, Pfizer, Inc., and Baxter International Inc.

title: How AI Could Speed Drug Discovery
summary: Artificial intelligence and machine learning are revolutionizing drug discovery by speeding up the development process and identifying viable drug targets more efficiently. Morgan Stanley Research believes these advancements could lead to 50 additional novel therapies and a $50 billion market opportunity over the next decade. The technology offers significant cost savings and improved outcomes for patients, while analysts anticipate an inflection point for the sector as investors gain confidence in AI-enabled drug development through strong data readouts and biopharma partnerships.

title: Bristol Myers gets FDA approval for new type of psoriasis drug
summary: Bristol Myers Squibb received FDA approval for Sotyktu, a new type of psoriasis pill that targets the TYK2 protein. This drug is notable as it doesn't require patients to try biologic drugs first and does not carry the cardiovascular and cancer warnings associated with other JAK inhibitors, despite TYK2 being from the same family. Bristol Myers expects Sotyktu to achieve $4 billion in peak sales and plans to expand its use to other autoimmune disorders.

title: FAMU COVID-19 vaccination site now offering new Moderna, Pfizer boosters
summary: Florida A&M University's COVID-19 vaccination site is now providing the updated Moderna and Pfizer boosters. These boosters are available for individuals aged 12 and older who have completed their primary vaccination series with Pfizer, Moderna, or Novavax, and are at least two months past their last booster or vaccination. The site is open Monday through Saturday from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

title: GSK Eases Cervarix Out Of India, Eyes On Trajectory Of Synflorix
summary: GSK is withdrawing its HPV vaccine Cervarix from the Indian market, reflecting changing dynamics for HPV vaccines in the country. The company's focus will now shift to the trajectory of its pneumococcal vaccine, Synflorix. This move comes amidst increased competition and evolving market conditions for vaccines in India.

title: From the ‘go-go days’ to a bubble crunch — the biotech sector faces its next challenge
summary: The biotech sector experienced a significant downturn from its early 2021 highs, with the XBI index falling from over $160 to under $70 by June 2022, before a slight recovery. This "bubble crunch" is attributed to factors like inflation and oversupply of companies, rather than a full crash. Industry experts believe the sector will rebound, likely through consolidation and M&A, with financially stable companies and those with clear data catalysts best positioned for future growth.

title: Novartis and BeiGene announce positive phase 3 trial results for hepatocellular carcinoma treatment
summary: Novartis and BeiGene have announced positive results from a phase 3 trial (RATIONALE 301) for tislelizumab in patients with previously untreated, unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The study demonstrated non-inferior overall survival compared to sorafenib, along with a higher objective response rate and more durable responses, although superiority for OS was not met. Novartis plans to discuss this data with regulatory authorities, highlighting tislelizumab's potential as a new treatment option for this aggressive disease.

title: mRNA vaccines expressing homo-prototype/Omicron and hetero-chimeric RBD-dimers against SARS-CoV-2
summary: This letter to the editor reports on the development and evaluation of mRNA vaccines expressing homo-prototype/Omicron and hetero-chimeric RBD-dimers against SARS-CoV-2. Building on prior success with a protein subunit vaccine (ZF2001) based on dimeric RBD, the researchers applied this immunogen design to an mRNA platform. The study demonstrates the immunogenicity and efficacy of the RBD-dimer mRNA vaccine in mice and highlights the mRNA platform's flexibility for rapid adaptation to SARS-CoV-2 variants like Delta and Omicron.

title: An HIV vaccine is ‘more than five years away,’ former AIDS Society head warns
summary: Linda-Gail Bekker, former president of the International AIDS Society, estimates that an HIV vaccine is "more than five years away" despite the potential of mRNA technology. Though five mRNA-based HIV vaccine trials are in early human testing, it will take years to reach final stages. Bekker highlighted the contrast between rapid COVID-19 vaccine development due to massive funding and the slower progress for HIV and tuberculosis, emphasizing the need for sustained global attention and investment.

title: Pfizer starts late-stage trial of mRNA-based flu vaccine
summary: Pfizer Inc. has initiated a late-stage U.S. trial for an mRNA-based influenza vaccine, enrolling 25,000 patients. This vaccine utilizes the same mRNA technology as their COVID-19 shot, offering potential for faster adaptation to evolving flu strains. The company anticipates that this flexibility and rapid manufacturing could lead to better strain matches for future flu seasons.

title: Merck & Co. Inc. stock underperforms Wednesday when compared to competitors despite daily gains
summary: Merck & Co. Inc. (MRK) stock gained 1.59% on Wednesday, closing at $86.95, amidst a generally favorable trading day for the broader market. Despite these gains, the stock underperformed some competitors like Johnson & Johnson (JNJ), which rose 2.06%, though it fared better than Roche Holding AG (RHHVF) and Pfizer Inc. (PFE), which both saw slight declines. Merck's closing price was still $8.77 below its 52-week high.

title: Chantix class action alleges Pfizer sold medicine with known carcinogen
summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Pfizer, Inc. alleging that the company sold its Chantix medication with a known human carcinogen, n-nitroso varenicline. Plaintiff Teresa Baptiste claims Pfizer failed to adhere to current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP) and knowingly manufactured, sold, and distributed adulterated drugs. The lawsuit seeks declaratory and injunctive relief, along with exemplary or punitive damages for a nationwide class of consumers.

title: FDA Warns Monkeypox Could Mutate and Resist Treatment If Antiviral Drug Is Overused
summary: The FDA has warned against the overuse of Tpoxx, the only drug available for monkeypox, due to concerns that the virus could mutate and develop resistance. This guidance comes as new monkeypox cases have fallen by about 50% since August, attributed to vaccinations and educational outreach. The agency highlighted that Tpoxx targets a single protein, making the virus susceptible to resistance through mutation, despite calls from patient groups for wider access to the drug.

title: FDA: TPOXX use should be restricted to ensure drug’s efficacy against monkeypox
summary: The FDA is warning that TPOXX, the only drug available for monkeypox, should be used sparingly to prevent the virus from developing resistance, as its efficacy is not fully known. Despite being approved for smallpox based on animal studies, human data for monkeypox treatment is lacking. The CDC advises against prescribing TPOXX for mild cases to preserve its effectiveness amidst ongoing clinical trials to assess its true efficacy.

title: Lawsuit claims Pfizer fellowship program is biased against whites, Asian-Americans
summary: A group called Do No Harm has sued Pfizer Inc., alleging that the drugmaker's Breakthrough Fellowship Program is discriminatory by exclusively accepting Black, Latino, and Native American applicants. The lawsuit, filed in Manhattan federal court, claims the program violates civil rights laws and seeks an injunction to prevent Pfizer from using race as a factor in its fellowship selections. Pfizer stated it had not yet reviewed the lawsuit but expressed confidence that its program complies with all U.S. employment laws, aiming to boost minority representation.

title: Weis Markets in-store pharmacies now offering bivalent COVID-19 boosters
summary: Weis Markets announced that its in-store pharmacies are now providing the Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna bivalent COVID-19 vaccine boosters. These boosters are available following FDA authorization and CDC recommendation for eligible individuals, with pharmacist immunizers administering them at no charge. Customers can schedule appointments online or utilize walk-in options, and rapid at-home COVID-19 antigen tests are also available.

title: U.S. warns MPX could mutate to resist antiviral drug Tpoxx
summary: U.S. health officials caution against the overuse of Tpoxx, the only drug available to treat MPX, due to the risk of the virus mutating and rendering the medication ineffective. The FDA updated its guidance, emphasizing that even a small molecular change could significantly impact Tpoxx's antiviral activity, while the CDC advised against prescribing it to healthy adults without severe symptoms. This guidance comes as new MPX cases have fallen and officials express optimism about the outbreak's trajectory.

title: Canadian biotech venture capital firm Lumira starts hedge fund to target oversold public companies
summary: Lumira Ventures, a prominent Canadian biotech venture capital firm, is launching a new hedge fund, Lumira Ventures Opportunity Fund 1, to invest in publicly traded health sciences companies it believes are oversold. This move diversifies its investment strategy beyond private startups, following a trend seen among U.S. biotech investors. The fund will primarily target established biotherapeutics and medical technology firms, seeking to capitalize on a recent deep sell-off in the biotech market, despite strong underlying industry fundamentals.

title: Biohaven Announces Record Date for Anticipated Spin-Off
summary: Biohaven Pharmaceutical Holding Company Ltd. has set September 26, 2022, as the record date for the anticipated spin-off of its subsidiary, Biohaven Ltd. Shareholders will receive one common share of SpinCo for every two Biohaven common shares held. The spin-off is contingent on shareholder approval at a special meeting on September 29, 2022.

title: FASN inhibition targets multiple drivers of NASH by reducing steatosis, inflammation and fibrosis in preclinical models
summary: This study investigates the pharmacological inhibition of Fatty Acid Synthase (FASN) as a therapeutic strategy for non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH). Researchers tested FASN inhibitors in human cell cultures and three preclinical mouse models, demonstrating that FASN inhibition reduces steatosis, inflammation, and fibrosis. The findings support the development of FASN inhibitors, such as TVB-2640 (denifanstat), for clinical use against NASH.

title: Haleon believes it is not liable for any potential Zantac liabilities
summary: Haleon, a consumer healthcare company, states it is not liable for any claims related to the heartburn drug Zantac, despite investor concerns and litigation alleging the drug contains a probable carcinogen. The company maintains it never marketed Zantac in the U.S. and has rejected indemnification requests from GSK and Pfizer, though GSK disagrees with Haleon's stance. Uncertainty surrounding Zantac litigation has impacted the market value of several pharmaceutical companies.

title: Haleon Shares Rise as GSK, Pfizer Indeminification Requests Rejected
summary: Haleon's shares rose after the company rejected indemnity requests from GSK and Pfizer regarding Zantac litigation in the US, where over 2,000 personal injury cases connect the heartburn drug to cancer. Haleon stated that its joint venture agreement's indemnities only cover consumer healthcare businesses as conducted in 2018 when neither GSK nor Pfizer marketed OTC Zantac in the US or Canada. The company also posted a 22.1% jump in first-half adjusted operating profit, though it anticipates challenges from rising inflation impacting consumer spending.

title: MeiraGTx opens first commercial-scale gene therapy plant in Ireland
summary: MeiraGTx has opened a 150,000 square-foot commercial-scale gene therapy manufacturing facility in Shannon, Ireland, which it claims is the first of its kind in the country. The plant consolidates gene therapy development, testing, and manufacturing in-house, aiming to significantly shorten time to patient for advanced therapeutic products. This move by MeiraGTx, which includes facilities for viral vector manufacturing, plasmid DNA production, and a quality control hub, is expected to create at least 100 jobs and contributes to Ireland's growing presence in cell and gene therapy biomanufacturing.

title: Pfizer to supply up to 6 mln COVID pill courses for lower income countries
summary: Pfizer Inc. announced a deal to supply up to 6 million courses of its COVID-19 antiviral treatment, Paxlovid, to the NGO Global Fund for low- and middle-income countries. This initiative aims to address disparities in COVID response and make the treatment available in 132 nations, pending local regulatory clearances. The agreement is part of Pfizer's broader strategy to ensure equitable access to oral COVID treatments, including collaborations with generic drugmakers for lower-priced production.

title: Catalyst Pharmaceuticals Inc. stock falls Thursday, underperforms market
summary: Catalyst Pharmaceuticals Inc.'s stock (CPRX) fell by 2.09% on Thursday, closing at $12.20, underperforming the broader market as both the NASDAQ Composite and Dow Jones Industrial Average also declined. This marked the sixth consecutive day of losses for the company, and its shares closed $5.02 below its 52-week high. Competitors like Johnson & Johnson, Pfizer Inc., and Abbott Laboratories, however, saw gains.

title: Spero (SPRO) Skyrockets 168% on Licensing Deal With GSK
summary: Spero Therapeutics (SPRO) saw its shares surge 168% after announcing an exclusive licensing agreement with GSK for its antibiotic candidate, tebipenem HBr, designed to treat complicated urinary tract infections. Under the deal, Spero will receive an upfront payment of $66 million and potential milestone payments and royalties, with GSK also investing $9 million in Spero's common stock. This partnership provides Spero with significant funding and commercial expertise, extending its cash runway beyond 2024 and advancing the development of tebipenem HBr, for which the FDA has outlined a clear regulatory path toward potential approval.

title: Pfizer, Sangamo set to resume gene therapy study after safety delay
summary: Pfizer and Sangamo Therapeutics are preparing to resume a Phase 3 trial for their hemophilia A gene therapy, giroctocogene fitelparvovec, after a safety-related suspension due to blood clotting concerns. The companies plan to restart patient recruitment this month and dosing in October, following adjustments to their study protocol and the FDA lifting a clinical hold. This delay pushes trial data expectations to early 2024, potentially placing their therapy behind competitors like BioMarin Pharmaceutical.

title: Pfizer vs. Moderna: What are the new bivalent boosters’ differences?
summary: Both Moderna and Pfizer have new FDA-authorized bivalent COVID-19 vaccines targeting the original strain and the omicron variant. The primary difference lies in eligibility: Moderna's booster is for adults 18 and over, while Pfizer's is cleared for anyone 12 and older. Both are mRNA shots with similar side effects to previous vaccines, and adults are allowed to mix and match brands.

title: Pfizer CEO Albert Bourla tests positive for COVID-19 for second time in less than 2 months
summary: Pfizer CEO Albert Bourla announced he tested positive for COVID-19 for the second time in less than two months but is experiencing no symptoms. He stated that he had not yet received the new bivalent booster due to CDC guidelines recommending a three-month waiting period after a previous infection. Bourla emphasized that despite progress, the virus remains a concern, and encouraged eligible individuals to get boosted as updated shots targeting the Omicron variant have been authorized by the FDA.

title: Transthyretin Amyloidosis Treatment Market Size, Trends, Share, Growth | Report 2022-2030
summary: The global transthyretin amyloidosis treatment market, valued at approximately USD 4.87 billion in 2021, is projected to reach USD 9.35 billion by 2030, exhibiting a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 7.52%. Key market drivers include supportive reimbursement programs, a growing African American population susceptible to ATTR amyloidosis, increased research into diagnostic techniques, and strategic initiatives by major pharmaceutical companies to raise awareness and provide patient assistance. North America dominated the market in 2021, while the MEA region is anticipated to show the fastest growth due to unmet treatment needs and rising disease awareness.

title: Johnson & Johnson taps Scottish inspiration in branding its consumer spinoff
summary: Johnson & Johnson has named its consumer health spinoff Kenvue, drawing inspiration from Scottish etymology where "ken" means knowledge. This new entity, which generated $14.6 billion in revenue in 2021 from brands like Tylenol and Band-Aid, will focus on everyday care products. The move follows a trend among pharmaceutical companies to separate consumer divisions to concentrate on more profitable drug businesses.

title: J&J’s consumer health spinout to be named Kenvue
summary: Johnson & Johnson has announced Kenvue as the name for its consumer health spinout, which is expected to be separated next year. Kenvue will sell well-known products like Band-Aids, Tylenol, and Listerine, and the split is intended to boost the value of both the consumer health company and J&J's pharmaceutical and medical device businesses. J&J has already appointed key leadership for Kenvue, including former CVS Health CEO Larry Merlo as chair-designate.

title: J&J says new Band-Aid and Tylenol company to be named Kenvue | Company Business News
summary: Johnson & Johnson announced that its new consumer-health products company, which will house brands like Band-Aid and Tylenol, will be named Kenvue. This separation of the consumer unit, with $15 billion in annual revenue, from J&J's prescription-drug and medical-device business, is expected to be completed next year. Kenvue is a portmanteau of "ken" (knowledge) and "vue" (sight), signifying its focus on consumer insights and health solutions.

title: Biohaven’s ALS drug comes up short in Mass General trial
summary: Biohaven Pharmaceuticals announced that its experimental amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) drug, verdiperstat, failed to show benefit over a placebo in a late-stage clinical trial conducted by Massachusetts General Hospital. This marks the second clinical setback for verdiperstat, following an earlier failure in treating multiple system atrophy. Despite the disappointment, Biohaven, which Pfizer plans to acquire, stated it would continue research into neurodegenerative diseases, while the platform study design was highlighted for its efficiency in providing a definitive answer.

title: Teva settles price-fixing claims with Georgia for a 'modest' $3.3M
summary: Teva Pharmaceuticals has settled price-fixing claims with Georgia for $3.346 million, bringing its total state settlements for such allegations to three. The company continues to deny the allegations, characterizing the settlement amounts as "modest," especially when compared to a $420 million agreement with investors over similar claims or the larger settlements paid by other generics companies like Sandoz and Taro Pharmaceuticals. This state-by-state approach is similar to how Teva initially handled opioid claims before pursuing a nationwide settlement.

title: Solid Bio yields to Sarepta on Duchenne with plans for merger, R&D shakeup
summary: Solid Biosciences is merging with AavantiBio and combining management, shifting its strategic focus for developing a Duchenne muscular dystrophy gene therapy. The combined company will retain Solid's name and pursue a newer Duchenne gene therapy, SGT-003, alongside treatments for other neuromuscular and heart diseases, financed by a $75 million private stock offering. This move represents a strategic pivot for Solid Biosciences after previous setbacks and the success of Sarepta Therapeutics in Duchenne gene therapy development.

title: Moderna turns down China request for vaccine technology: report
summary: Moderna has reportedly rejected China's request for the core intellectual property of its COVID-19 vaccine, leading to a collapse in negotiations for its sale in the country. The pharmaceutical company cited commercial and safety concerns related to the vaccine's recipe. Despite this, Moderna is still interested in selling its product in China and has recently shown interest in restarting talks.

title: Amid scrutiny around Europe's vaccine purchase, Pfizer CEO Albert Bourla pulls out of committee hearing
summary: Pfizer CEO Albert Bourla has withdrawn from a European Parliament committee hearing scheduled for October 10, where he was expected to address scrutiny over the EU's COVID-19 vaccine procurement strategy, particularly Pfizer's third contract. The European Court of Auditors raised concerns about the negotiation process for this contract. Janine Small, president of international development markets at Pfizer, will attend in his place to discuss the company's vaccine development.

title: Capitol fountain turns pink for Breast Cancer Awareness Month
summary: The Capitol fountain in Harrisburg, Pennsylvania, was turned pink to mark Breast Cancer Awareness Month, continuing an annual tradition. This act serves as a reminder for women to get mammograms, a place of reflection for those lost to the disease, and a symbol of hope for survivors. During the event, a $150,000 check was presented to the Pennsylvania Breast Cancer Coalition by Mid Penn Bank, and pink strawberry milkshakes were distributed.

title: Biohaven Relaunches As Biohaven Ltd. After Pfizer Buyout Closes
summary: Biohaven has relaunched as Biohaven Ltd. following its buyout by Pfizer. The newly formed company will concentrate its research and development efforts on therapies for epilepsy, obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), and spinal muscular atrophy (SMA). This move comes after Pfizer's acquisition of their migraine portfolio.

title: Pfizer Teams Up with UF to Offer Graduate Scholarship in Statistics
summary: Pfizer Inc. has partnered with the University of Florida's College of Liberal Arts and Sciences to fund a graduate scholarship in the Department of Statistics. This initiative aims to support a student in biostatistics, with the inaugural recipient being Steven Goodman, a second-year PhD candidate focusing on spatial statistics. The collaboration seeks to attract diverse talent to quantitative sciences, provide students with direct industry experience, and strengthen the pipeline of skilled statisticians for the pharmaceutical sector.

title: Upcoming Opportunities in Genomics and Precision Medicine
summary: This article announces a research report on the "Global Genomics and Precision Medicine Market" by Stratagem Market Insights, forecasting growth dynamics and revenue generation from 2022 to 2029. The report details top manufacturing strategies, industry share, and prime opportunities, highlighting key players such as Pfizer Inc., Qiagen Inc., and Quest Diagnostics Inc. It also segments the market by product types (Genomics, Transcriptomics, Epigenomics) and applications (Oncology, CNS, Immunology, Respiratory Medicine, Infections, Others).

title: More former Bristol Myers employees sue over COVID-19 vaccination brouhaha
summary: Four former Bristol Myers Squibb employees have filed a lawsuit against the drug giant, alleging wrongful termination due to the company's COVID-19 vaccination policy. They claim BMS violated Title VII of the Civil Rights Act by denying religious exemptions. This lawsuit follows similar actions by other former employees who also challenged BMS's vaccine mandate.

title: Money on the Move: EnPlusOne, Cellarity, Voyager and More
summary: This article details several significant financial activities in the biopharmaceutical sector, including funding rounds for innovative drug discovery and delivery platforms, cancer imaging, and RNA synthesis. Key developments include EnPlusOne Biosciences securing $12 million for its ezRNA platform, Cellarity raising $121 million in Series C financing for its unique drug discovery approach, and Voyager Therapeutics receiving $10 million from Pfizer for an AAV capsid license option. Additionally, Pfizer completed its $11.6 billion acquisition of Biohaven Pharmaceuticals, and Alloy Therapeutics garnered $42 million in Series D funding to expand its drug discovery technologies.

title: German COVID vaccine developer BioNTech signs research deal with Australia
summary: BioNTech SE, the German biotech firm behind a widely used COVID-19 vaccine, will establish research and manufacturing centers in Australia, utilizing its mRNA technology. This partnership with Australia's Victoria state aims to conduct clinical research for experimental mRNA vaccines and therapies and set up manufacturing facilities in Melbourne. This initiative marks Australia's second mRNA deal, aiming to enhance domestic vaccine manufacturing capabilities after initial reliance on foreign imports led to political challenges.

title: Eli Lilly gets FDA's speedy review for obesity drug
summary: Eli Lilly's diabetes drug Mounjaro has received "fast track" status from the FDA for its obesity treatment application, allowing for an expedited review. A study showed Mounjaro helped patients lose over 20% of their weight, positioning it to compete with Novo Nordisk's Wegovy as a blockbuster obesity drug. This development is significant as obesity affects over 40% of the U.S. population and incurs substantial annual costs.

title: COVID rebound after Pfizer treatment likely due to robust immune response, study finds
summary: A U.S. government study suggests that the rebound of COVID-19 symptoms in some patients after taking Pfizer's antiviral Paxlovid is linked to a robust immune response, rather than a weakened one. The research indicates that a longer course of the drug is not necessary to prevent recurrence and that the drug does not impede the immune system. Further detailed studies are needed to fully understand this phenomenon, but the current findings support patient isolation during rebound.

title: Provention and Sanofi enter deal to launch teplizumab for type 1 diabetes
summary: Provention Bio and Sanofi US have partnered to co-promote teplizumab, an investigational drug for delaying the onset of clinical type 1 diabetes (T1D). This agreement allows Provention to leverage Sanofi's commercial resources for the launch, with an FDA decision on teplizumab's approval anticipated on November 17. Sanofi will also acquire $35 million of Provention's common stock upon FDA approval and has an exclusive right of first negotiation for international marketing rights for teplizumab.

title: Canada authorises Pfizer's Omicron retooled booster By Reuters
summary: Canada has authorized an updated COVID-19 booster shot by Pfizer Inc and BioNTech SE, targeting the Omicron BA.4 and BA.5 subvariants, for individuals aged 12 and older. This marks the second such bivalent vaccine approval in Canada, following Moderna's booster last month. Pfizer is also seeking approval for its Omicron-tailored shot for children aged 5-11.

title: Pfizer exec denies CEO negotiated EU COVID vaccine contract via text message
summary: A Pfizer executive has categorically denied that the company's CEO negotiated a COVID-19 vaccine supply agreement with the European Commission via text messages, stating such complex deals involve too many people and take too long. This comes after the European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen revealed exchanging texts with Pfizer CEO Albert Bourla during contract negotiations, and the Commission later stated the texts no longer existed. The contract was the largest ever sealed for COVID-19 vaccines, committing the EU to buy 900 million Pfizer-BioNTech shots, with an option for another 900 million.

title: Takeda Pharmaceutical 2022: Back to business
summary: Takeda Pharmaceutical is shifting its focus to brand growth after years of acquisitions and divestitures. The company reported strong performance for its growth products in fiscal year 2021, with significant revenue increases despite a decline in net income. Takeda is also actively developing new therapies through acquisitions and partnerships, and expanding the indications and geographic reach of its key products.

title: AbbVie 2022: Still immune
summary: Despite the Allergan acquisition, AbbVie's revenue and growth drivers remain heavily concentrated in immunology, with Humira, Skyrizi, and Rinvoq accounting for nearly half of its top-line revenue. The company reported strong financial performance in 2021 and the first half of 2022, driven by increased sales of its key products and strategic partnerships. AbbVie also expanded its pipeline with acquisitions and collaborations, focusing on neuroscience, autoimmune diseases, glaucoma, and oncology.

title: New TYK2 inhibitors: a growing race to top Bristol Myers
summary: The article discusses the burgeoning competition in the development of TYK2 inhibitors, following the FDA approval of Bristol Myers Squibb's Sotyktu for psoriasis, which lacked the safety warnings associated with older JAK inhibitors. Several startups are racing to develop their own TYK2-targeting drugs, aiming to offer safer and more convenient oral treatments for autoimmune diseases, with potential annual sales for these drugs estimated to reach billions. The article details how these inhibitors work, their advantages over conventional treatments, and lists key companies and their clinical development progress.

title: Viatris weighs sale of consumer health assets in Europe – Bloomberg News
summary: Viatris Inc. is reportedly considering selling its European consumer health assets in a deal potentially worth over 3 billion euros ($2.9 billion). The drugmaker is working with Jefferies Financial Group Inc to find suitors, including private equity groups. This move aligns with a broader trend of drugmakers separating consumer health businesses to focus on pharmaceuticals.

title: Top 50 Pharma Companies 2022: Notes & Methodology
summary: This article details the methodology and criteria used by Med Ad News to rank the world's top 50 pharmaceutical companies for its 36th annual special report in 2022. It outlines how companies are selected, the financial metrics used for ranking (such as revenue, earnings, R&D, market capitalization), and the process for converting foreign currencies. The report also includes significant industry developments like new entrants to the top 50 list and the criteria for selecting the "Company of the Year."

title: Envisioning a healthier every day, for every woman
summary: Organon & Co, a spin-off from MSD, is dedicated to improving health outcomes for women globally by focusing on unmet needs and addressing historical healthcare disparities. The company emphasizes a commitment to its female-majority leadership, progressive workplace policies around menopause and pregnancy loss, and integrating ESG principles into its business model. Organon also invests in innovations, such as acquisitions of Alydia Health and Forendo Pharma, and collaborations with Henlius Biotech, to develop new treatments across various therapy areas for women.

title: Walmart to compete with Walgreens, CVS in recruiting clinical trial subjects
summary: Walmart announced its entry into clinical trial recruitment through its new service, Walmart Healthcare Research Institute, directly competing with Walgreens and CVS Health Group. The initiative aims to leverage Walmart's diverse customer base across its clinics and pharmacies to help drug companies find participants for clinical trials, addressing a common challenge in medical research. This move is part of Walmart's broader strategy to expand into high-margin businesses like healthcare, following similar ventures by its rivals.

title: Age 5-11 COVID Vaccine: Everything You Need to Know on Safety, Efficacy, and Distribution
summary: The article discusses the safety, efficacy, and distribution of the COVID-19 vaccine for children aged 5-11, following its authorization by the CDC and FDA. It addresses common concerns, including why younger children need vaccination, vaccine safety and effectiveness, long-term effects, and administration details like dosage. The information is based on insights from URMC infectious disease expert Jennifer Nayak, M.D., and pediatrician Stephen Cook, M.D., M.P.H.

title: Eli Lilly Bets Nearly $500M on Metabolic Disease Pact with Nimbus (Updated)
summary: Eli Lilly has entered into a collaboration and licensing deal with Nimbus Therapeutics worth up to $496 million to develop novel targeted therapies for metabolic diseases. The partnership focuses on identifying isoform-selective small molecule activators of AMPK heterotrimers, a high-value target known for its role in glucose, lipid metabolism, and inflammation. Nimbus believes its computational drug discovery engine and understanding of AMPK subunits can overcome past challenges in targeting AMPK for conditions like obesity-related diseases and diabetes.

title: Merck and Moderna Move Forward with Personalized Cancer Vaccine (Updated)
summary: Merck has exercised its option to co-develop and commercialize Moderna's personalized cancer vaccine, mRNA-4157/V940, based on an existing agreement. The vaccine is currently in a Phase II trial in combination with Merck's Keytruda for high-risk melanoma patients. The collaboration aims to leverage mRNA technology for a personalized approach to cancer treatment, with Merck paying Moderna $250 million and the companies splitting costs and profits equally.

title: Moderna pops 17% after Merck exercises option to jointly develop a personalized cancer vaccine
summary: Moderna's stock surged by as much as 17% after Merck exercised an option to jointly develop and commercialize personalized cancer vaccines, an agreement initially established in 2016. Merck will pay Moderna $250 million, and data from a phase 2 trial evaluating Moderna's vaccine combined with Merck's Keytruda for high-risk melanoma is expected in the fourth quarter. This collaboration is seen as a significant move for Moderna to diversify its revenue beyond its COVID-19 vaccines and validates mRNA technology for broader therapeutic applications.

title: Moderna to stay ahead in mRNA technology: CSO Melissa Moore
summary: Moderna's Chief Scientific Officer, Melissa Moore, states that the company, despite being the leader in mRNA technology, faces increasing pressure from rivals and plans to expand its drug pipeline to over 100 next year. Moore acknowledged criticisms regarding the stability and cost of mRNA vaccines but anticipates that these issues will improve over time as the technology matures. The article highlights Moderna's significant role in developing the COVID-19 vaccine and its ongoing efforts in R&D for various other diseases.

title: Worldwide Repeat Expansion Disorders Treatment Industry to 2030 - North America Remains as the Global Leader and APAC to Present the Largest Opportunity - ResearchAndMarkets.com
summary: The repeat expansion disorders treatment market is projected to grow at a CAGR of 13.5% from 2022 to 2030, with North America holding the dominant market share in 2021 and Asia Pacific presenting the largest future opportunity. This growth is driven by increasing research into therapies for these inherited conditions, which are caused by expansions in DNA repeats and are linked to over 40 different illnesses. Key market players include Pfizer Inc., CRISPR Therapeutics, and Merck & Co. Inc., among others, as advancements uncover complexities in disease mechanisms.

title: What 35 Years In Biotech Has Taught Me
summary: Dinesh Patel, CEO of Protagonist Therapeutics, shares lessons learned from 35 years in the biotech industry, including the importance of consistent fundraising, replicating success, building strong teams and culture, and effectively navigating inevitable setbacks. He emphasizes that companies fail from depleting reserves rather than drug program failures, and highlights the need for leaders to evolve and maintain commitment to their core principles and patients.

title: Stevanato Group and IL Group Partner to Improve Safe Processing & Handling of Hazardous Injectables
summary: Stevanato Group and IL Group have partnered to develop an integrated and automated solution for the safe processing and handling of hazardous injectable drugs. This collaboration aims to enhance inspection capabilities and containment for sensitive drugs, improving safety for healthcare professionals and patients. The solution combines Stevanato Group's Vision Robot Unit (VRU) with IL Group’s labeling technology and their Vial Protect Pack.

title: Self-Administered Etripamil Nasal Spray for PSVT Beneficial in Phase 3 RAPID Trial
summary: The Phase 3 RAPID trial demonstrated positive efficacy and safety for self-administered etripamil nasal spray in patients with paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia (PSVT). A significant portion of patients (64.3%) converted to sinus rhythm within 30 minutes compared to placebo (31.2%), with mild to moderate nasal administration site adverse events. These results, combined with previous trials, support a New Drug Application submission, potentially shifting PSVT treatment from emergency departments to unsupervised settings.

title: DC now offering updated COVID boosters for kids between 5 and 11
summary: DC Health announced that updated bivalent COVID-19 booster vaccines are now available for children aged 5 to 11 in the District. Both Pfizer and Moderna bivalent boosters will be offered at various District vaccination sites. This decision follows the FDA's approval for elementary school-aged children to receive these boosters, with health officials recommending them for anyone aged 5 or older if at least two months have passed since their last primary series or booster shot.

title: Johnson & Johnson Isn’t Rushing Into M&A
summary: Johnson & Johnson, despite being cash-rich with $34 billion and facing patent expiration for its top-selling drug Stelara, is not rushing into mergers and acquisitions. While other big pharma companies are actively pursuing deals to replenish their pipelines, J&J's focus on growth and a consumer split means it is proceeding more slowly with M&A. This measured approach comes as J&J reported strong third-quarter profits but cut its full-year sales guidance.

title: U.S. Eye Drops and Lubricants Market Projected to Reach $22,625
summary: The U.S. Eye Drops and Lubricants Market is projected to reach $22,625 million, driven by evolving market trends and the discovery of advanced treatments. Key players include Johnson & Johnson and Pfizer Inc., with North America holding the largest market share due to a high prevalence of eye diseases. Artificial tears are a significant segment, and the market is expected to see continued growth, especially in the hormones segment and the eye diseases application area.

title: Acute Myeloid Leukemia Market Size to Surpass US$ 4.31 Billion by 2030 - Growth Plus Reports
summary: The global acute myeloid leukemia market is projected to reach US$ 4.31 billion by 2030, growing at a CAGR of 10.2%, driven by rising incidence rates, an aging population, and advancements in drug discovery. Antineoplastics currently hold the largest market share due to their high demand as a common and effective cancer treatment. North America dominates the market, attributed to the high prevalence of AML and significant R&D investments in the region.

title: Johnson & Johnson signals job cuts amid consumer health separation, inflation pressure
summary: Johnson & Johnson is considering potential job cuts and restructuring to "rightsize its infrastructure" as it separates its consumer health business into a new standalone company, Kenvue. The move is also driven by macroeconomic pressures, a strong U.S. dollar, and inflation impacting the company's profit margins. While the extent of the layoffs is unclear, it is not expected to be a major restructuring for the company, which employs 141,700 full-time staff globally.

title: Recombinant Vaccines Market Size & Share | Analysis By 2031
summary: The global recombinant vaccines market, valued at $8.1 billion in 2021, is projected to reach $24.7 billion by 2031, growing at an 11.4% CAGR. This growth is fueled by increasing R&D activities, a rise in infectious and zoonotic diseases, and higher vaccination rates, with the COVID-19 pandemic positively impacting its development. Key segments include human papillomavirus and adult end-users, with North America currently dominating and Asia-Pacific expected to show the highest growth.

title: Pfizer Targets Covid Vaccine Price of at Least $110 a Dose
summary: Pfizer plans to sell its Covid-19 vaccine on the commercial market in the U.S., targeting a price of $110 to $130 per dose for adults. The drugmaker is currently in negotiations with health insurers regarding this pricing. This move comes as Pfizer prepares to transition from government contracts to commercial sales, potentially early next year.

title: Catalyst Pharmaceuticals Inc. stock outperforms competitors on strong trading day
summary: Catalyst Pharmaceuticals Inc. (CPRX) stock rose 0.87% to $12.76 on Thursday, despite a down day for the broader market. This gain snapped a two-day losing streak for the company, which closed $4.46 below its 52-week high. CPRX also outperformed competitors such as Johnson & Johnson, Pfizer Inc., and Abbott Laboratories.

title: Walmart to pay $215 mln to settle Florida opioid claims
summary: Walmart Inc. has agreed to pay $215 million to resolve claims from Florida that its pharmacies contributed to the opioid epidemic in the state. As part of the settlement, Walmart will also provide 672,000 naloxone treatment kits to first responders in Florida. This agreement is part of Florida's broader effort to combat the opioid crisis, which has so far secured $3.2 billion through legal actions against various companies.

title: Pfizer expects to hike U.S. COVID vaccine price to $110-$130 per dose
summary: Pfizer announced its intention to significantly increase the price of its COVID-19 vaccine to between $110 and $130 per dose once the U.S. government's current purchasing program concludes. This price hike is in anticipation of the market shifting to private insurance in 2023, with Pfizer expecting the vaccine market to mirror the annual flu shot market size for adults. The company expressed confidence that the new price would reflect the vaccine's cost-effectiveness and not be a barrier to access for insured patients, though access for uninsured individuals remains unclear.

title: Pfizer to charge you $110-$130 per COVID vaccine dose
summary: Pfizer announced it will charge between $110 and $130 per dose for its COVID-19 vaccine once the U.S. government stops purchasing the shots, which could happen early next year. Despite the commercial pricing, the company expects most people with private insurance or public programs like Medicare and Medicaid will still receive the vaccine for free. This new price point reflects increased costs for single-dose vials and commercial distribution, making it more expensive for cash-paying customers than typical flu shots.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Parathyroid Hormone Replacement With TransCon PTH in Hypoparathyroidism: 26-Week Results From the Phase 3 PaTHway Trial
summary: This study evaluated the efficacy and safety of TransCon PTH in treating hypoparathyroidism, comparing it to a placebo over 26 weeks. The results showed that 79% of participants treated with TransCon PTH achieved the primary composite endpoint, including independence from conventional therapy and maintained normal calcium levels, compared to only 5% in the placebo group. The treatment also significantly improved patient-reported outcomes related to quality of life and reduced urine calcium excretion, indicating its potential as an effective physiological replacement therapy for hypoparathyroidism.

title: Pfizer says it's eyeing a $110 to $130 list price for COVID-19 vaccine in U.S.
summary: Pfizer is considering a list price of $110 to $130 per single-dose vial for its COVID-19 vaccine in the U.S. commercial market. This price reflects increased costs for commercial distribution and the vaccine's societal value. The transition from government purchasing to a commercial model is anticipated no sooner than early 2023, with Pfizer aiming for continued equitable access and affordability.

title: The world's first Phase 3 psilocybin clinical trial is about to commence
summary: Compass Pathways is set to begin the world's first Phase 3 clinical trial for psilocybin therapy, aiming for FDA approval by late 2025. The trial will involve nearly 1,000 participants with treatment-resistant depression across two main studies, Pivotal 1 and Pivotal 2. These trials will evaluate the efficacy and safety of single and double doses of psilocybin with psychological support, comparing them to a placebo.

title: Psychedelic Bulletin #120: Beckley Psytech Acquires Eleusis; A Look at COMPASS’ Phase 3 Design; New Psychedelic Drug Dev Scoops $22m Series A
summary: This bulletin covers significant developments in the psychedelic industry, including Beckley Psytech's acquisition of Eleusis, which brings ELE-101 into its pipeline, and Empyrean Neuroscience securing $22 million Series A funding for genetically engineered psychedelic therapeutics. It also details COMPASS Pathways' heavily anticipated Phase 3 trial designs for COMP360 psilocybin therapy, highlighting the complexities and expectations surrounding its efficacy and safety. Additionally, the bulletin notes increased DEA production quotas for psychedelics, Alberta's move to regulate psychedelic therapy, and other company updates and policy changes.

title: Astellas and Taysha Gene Therapies Announce Strategic Investment to Support Development of Taysha's AAV-based Gene Therapy Programs
summary: Astellas and Taysha Gene Therapies announced a strategic investment of $50 million by Astellas to acquire 15% of Taysha's common stock. This investment supports the advancement of Taysha's AAV gene therapy development programs for Rett syndrome (TSHA-102) and giant axonal neuropathy (TSHA-120). Astellas also gains an exclusive option to license these two clinical stage programs and a Board observer seat on Taysha's Board of Directors.

title: Pfizer, facing lawsuit, says minority fellowship program serves public interest
summary: Pfizer is defending its minority fellowship program against a lawsuit claiming it illegally excludes white and Asian-Americans, arguing the program serves the public interest by addressing historical discrimination and boosting minority representation. The drugmaker stated that the program is a form of voluntary affirmative action, which helps to recruit, retain, and promote minorities, and aims to enroll 100 fellows by 2025 as part of a nine-year commitment. This legal battle comes as the Supreme Court is set to consider the future of affirmative action in higher education.

title: Pfizer defends fellowships challenged by law firm working to end affirmative action
summary: Pfizer is defending its Breakthrough Fellowship program against a lawsuit filed by Consovoy McCarthy, a law firm also challenging affirmative action in college admissions. The lawsuit, on behalf of the nonprofit Do No Harm, alleges Pfizer's program for minority candidates discriminates against white and Asian applicants. Pfizer argues its program is a lawful attempt to boost workforce diversity and address historical discrimination, citing long-standing Supreme Court precedent.

title: GE Healthcare adds Danielle Halstrom as chief comms, corporate marketing officer
summary: GE Healthcare has appointed Danielle Halstrom as its new chief communications and corporate marketing officer, effective October 24, 2022. Halstrom, formerly of Pfizer and Bristol Myers Squibb, will oversee all internal, external, executive, and digital communications, as well as corporate brand reputation. Her appointment precedes GE's plan to separate into three independent public companies, with GE Healthcare expected to launch officially in January 2023.

title: Merck reveals chairman succession as earnings beat forecasts
summary: Merck announced that CEO Robert Davis will succeed Ken Frazier as chairman of the company's board, effective December 1, solidifying Davis's leadership. This follows Frazier's decade-long tenure as CEO, during which he championed Keytruda, an immunotherapy that has become a major revenue driver for Merck. The transition means Davis will hold both CEO and chairman roles, a common structure among large U.S. drugmakers, and he faces the challenge of developing new medicines to sustain revenue as Keytruda's patents approach expiration in 2028.

title: |How Johnson & Johnson Innovation lasted 5 decades -
summary: |Johnson & Johnson Innovation (JJDC), the world's oldest CVC, attributes its five-decade longevity to unwavering management support, disciplined investment strategy, and adaptability. Debi Watson, VP of venture investments, highlights the unit's consistent vision, long-term investment horizon, and willingness to evolve business models. Despite challenges in balancing strategic focus with disruptive innovation, JJDC remains committed to its core strategy even amidst shifting economic conditions.

title: EU regulator recommends adding heavy periods to side effects of mRNA COVID shots
summary: The European Medicines Agency (EMA) has recommended listing heavy menstrual bleeding as a side effect for Moderna and Pfizer-BioNTech's mRNA COVID-19 vaccines. This decision follows reports observed in clinical trials, real-world cases, and medical literature, though cases are generally non-serious and temporary. The EMA emphasizes that the benefits of the vaccines still outweigh the risks, and there's no evidence suggesting impact on reproduction or fertility.

title: Amid COVID-19 Global Pandemic, The Pfizer Foundation Helps IRC Pursue Urgent Expansion of Health Access in Humanitarian Settings
summary: The Pfizer Foundation has partnered with the International Rescue Committee (IRC) to expand health access in humanitarian settings, especially crucial amidst the COVID-19 pandemic which exacerbated vulnerabilities for displaced populations.
