summary: Erasca is reprioritizing its pipeline following underwhelming early-phase cancer data, leading to the discontinuation of several ERAS-007 applications and shelving a KRAS inhibitor. While some ERAS-007 trials in combination with other drugs disappointed, the company saw promising partial responses in metastatic BRAF V600E-mutated colorectal cancer patients. The biotech attributes some of these decisions to an increasingly competitive landscape.

title: Intellia Therapeutics Announces New Positive Clinical Data from Phase 1 Study of NTLA-2002, an Investigational In Vivo CRISPR Genome Editing Treatment for Hereditary Angioedema (HAE)
summary: Intellia Therapeutics announced positive new clinical data from its Phase 1 study of NTLA-2002, an investigational in vivo CRISPR genome editing treatment for Hereditary Angioedema (HAE). The data showed a 95% mean reduction in monthly HAE attack rates across all patients, with many remaining attack-free for extended periods. NTLA-2002 was well tolerated, reinforcing its potential as a functional cure and addressing the significant treatment burden associated with current HAE therapies.

title: Novartis to buy Seattle biotech firm Chinook Therapeutics in $3.2B deal
summary: Novartis announced its plan to acquire Seattle-based Chinook Therapeutics for $3.2 billion, with the deal potentially reaching $3.5 billion if regulatory milestones are met. Chinook, founded in 2019, specializes in therapies for chronic kidney disorders, including IgA Nephropathy, with lead experimental drugs atrasentan and zigakibart in advanced clinical trials. This acquisition highlights a continuing trend of major biotech deals in the Seattle region, following Pfizer's acquisition of Seagen and Sobi's deal to buy CTI BioPharma.

title: Spero Therapeutics Appoints Sath Shukla as CEO
summary: Spero Therapeutics announced the appointment of Satyavrat “Sath” Shukla as its new President, CEO, and a member of the Board of Directors, effective August 1, 2023. Shukla, currently the CFO and Treasurer, will succeed Ankit Mahadevia, M.D., who will become Chairman of the Board. This leadership transition aims to build upon Spero's foundation in anti-infectives and rare diseases, furthering the development of key drug candidates like tebipenem HBr and SPR720.

title: Bristol Myers sues US government over Medicare drug price negotiation plan
summary: Bristol Myers Squibb Co has sued the U.S. government over its Medicare drug price negotiation plan, arguing it violates the Fifth and First Amendments. This is the third lawsuit challenging the Inflation Reduction Act's provision, which the pharmaceutical industry claims will cut profits and hinder new drug development. Analysts expect Bristol Myers' blood thinner Eliquis to be among the first ten drugs chosen for price negotiation.

title: Bullish or Bearish? Vetting Animal Health Care Stocks
summary: The article discusses the resurgence of pet care stocks, particularly focusing on animal health care companies, driven by increased pet owner spending on health and wellness. It vets two specific companies, Zoetis, Inc. (NYSE: ZTS) and Elanco Animal Health, Inc. (NYSE: ELAN), examining their growth drivers, financial performance, and future prospects within the expanding U.S. pet care market. The piece highlights key developments like new drug approvals and financial guidance updates for both companies.

title: Eli Lilly's migraine drug fails to prove superiority to Pfizer's
summary: Eli Lilly announced that its migraine prevention drug, Emgality, did not demonstrate superiority over Pfizer's rival drug, Nurtec, in a recent post-approval study. The three-month study, involving 580 patients, was the first head-to-head comparison of the two drugs. Despite not proving superiority, Emgality still showed "clinically meaningful" efficacy and safety results.

title: Apogee Therapeutics Strengthens Team with Appointments of Industry Leaders to Board of Directors and Management
summary: Apogee Therapeutics announced the appointments of Jennifer Fox and William “BJ” Jones to its board of directors, with Ms. Fox also chairing the audit committee. The company also appointed Rebecca Dabora, Ph.D., as chief technology officer. These additions bring extensive experience in healthcare investment banking, commercial strategy, and chemistry, manufacturing, and controls (CMC) to support Apogee's advancement of biologics for atopic dermatitis and COPD.

title: Lilly's phase 2 results published in the New England Journal of Medicine show orforglipron, a once-daily oral nonpeptide GLP-1 receptor agonist, achieved up to 14.7% mean weight reduction at 36 weeks in adults with obesity or overweight
summary: Eli Lilly and Company announced positive Phase 2 results for orforglipron, a once-daily oral nonpeptide GLP-1 receptor agonist, demonstrating significant weight reduction and improved A1C levels. Published in the New England Journal of Medicine, the study showed up to 14.7% mean weight reduction at 36 weeks in adults with obesity or overweight, and in The Lancet, up to 2.1% reduction in A1C for adults with type 2 diabetes. These findings support the progression of orforglipron into Phase 3 clinical programs for chronic weight management and type 2 diabetes.

title: RNA Based Therapeutic Market Trend 2023: Anticipated Growth to Reach $25.12 Billion by 2030 | 17.6%
summary: The RNA-based therapeutic market is projected to reach $25.12 billion by 2030, growing at a CAGR of 17.6% from its 2021 valuation of $4.93 billion. This growth is driven by increasing R&D investments, technological advancements like mRNA and RNAi therapeutics, and the rising demand for targeted and personalized medicine. Key players like Moderna, BioNTech, and Alnylam Pharmaceuticals are actively involved, with North America leading the market and Asia-Pacific showing the fastest growth.

title: ACTIVELY INVESTING IN GLOBAL HEALTH: Real-world approaches to healthcare make a difference
summary: The article highlights the partnership between Pfizer, The Pfizer Foundation, and World Vision to combat communicable and infectious diseases, which are leading causes of child mortality, particularly in marginalized communities. Their collaboration focuses on strengthening healthcare systems and implementing community-based programs. An example is the Expanding Access to Immunization and Treatment program in Uganda, which has screened over 129,000 children and trained over 1,000 community health workers, aiming to reduce child mortality.

title: FDA approves somatrogon-ghla to treat pediatric growth hormone deficiency
summary: The FDA has approved somatrogon-ghla (NGENLA; Pfizer Inc and OPKO Health Inc) for children aged 3 and older with growth failure due to insufficient growth hormone secretion. This new once-weekly injection aims to reduce the burden of daily treatments and improve adherence for pediatric patients with growth hormone deficiency (GHD). The approval is based on phase 3 study data showing its non-inferiority to somatropin in annual height velocity at 12 months.

title: FDA Approves Pfizer, OPKO’s Once Weekly Ngenla for Human Growth Deficiency in Pediatric Patients
summary: The FDA has approved somatrogon-ghla (Ngenla) from Pfizer and OPKO Health for pediatric patients aged 3 and older with growth failure due to inadequate growth hormone secretion. This once-weekly subcutaneous injection offers a significant reduction in treatment burden compared to daily injections. Clinical trials demonstrated its non-inferiority to daily somatropin and a comparable safety profile, with potential availability in the US market by August 2023.

title: FDA approval of BioMarin’s Roctavian to test gene therapy pricing model
summary: The FDA has approved BioMarin's Roctavian for severe hemophilia A, marking an important gene therapy milestone for 2023. The launch of Roctavian, priced at $2.9 million, will be a crucial test for the marketability and pricing models of gene therapies, especially considering its outcomes-based warranty. This warranty promises up to 100% reimbursement if the patient does not respond to the treatment.

title: FDA rejects Alvotech’s Humira biosimilar for the third time
summary: The FDA has rejected Alvotech's Humira biosimilar, AVT02, for the third time due to deficiencies at a manufacturing facility in Reykjavik, Iceland. This rejection further delays the drug's US launch, despite its prior approval in Australia, Canada, and the EU. Alvotech plans to resubmit the biologics license application (BLA) with additional data for interchangeability designation and is exploring capital raising options.

title: FDA Approves BioMarin’s Hemophilia A Gene Therapy Roctavian
summary: The FDA has approved BioMarin’s valoctocogene roxaparvovec (Roctavian) for adults with severe hemophilia A, making it the first gene therapy for this condition in the US. The approval was based on positive data from the phase 3 GENEr8-1 clinical trial, showing significant reductions in annualized bleeding rates and FVIII utilization. BioMarin plans to price the one-time treatment at $2.9 million and offer an outcomes-based warranty.

title: New Humira rivals likely to hit US market with small discounts in July
summary: Multiple biosimilar versions of AbbVie's top-selling drug Humira are expected to launch in the U.S. in July, adding to the competition started by Amgen in January. Despite increased generic competition, industry experts anticipate only small price discounts for these new versions due to pharmacy benefit managers' negotiation strategies. This pricing dynamic means that while health plans might secure some savings, patients paying co-insurance based on list prices may not see significant relief.

title: Samsung Bioepis, Celltrion Healthcare launch Humira biosimilar in US
summary: Samsung Bioepis and Celltrion Healthcare have launched their respective Humira biosimilars, Hadlima and Yuflyma, in the U.S. market. Hadlima offers an 85% discount compared to Humira's list price and includes patient support programs, while Yuflyma provides a 5% discount, with actual selling prices variable due to rebates. The article highlights the significant role of Pharmacy Benefit Managers (PBMs) in drug formulary inclusion and pricing in the U.S. market.

title: First Trust Exchange-Traded Fund III - First Trust Morningstar Dividend Leaders Index Fund (FDL) News, Articles, Events & Latest Updates
summary: This article provides recent news and updates for the First Trust Morningstar Dividend Leaders Index Fund (FDL). It highlights several financial articles discussing FDL and other dividend ETFs outperforming the S&P 500, offering current income, and gaining investor interest amid market volatility and sector rotations. The feed includes news from Zacks and Stocktwits discussing various dividend-focused investment strategies and company-specific financial reports impacting dividend stocks.

title: Settlement checks in the mail from Roundup, EpiPen, Zoom, others
summary: Readers of Top Class Actions are reporting the receipt of settlement checks from seven different class action lawsuits. These settlements address various claims including false advertising for Roundup, spam calls from Bath Saver, privacy issues related to Yahoo data breaches, antitrust violations by EpiPen manufacturers, price-fixing for lithium-ion batteries, Apple iCloud storing data on third-party servers, and security failures by Zoom that led to "Zoom bombing." Claimants are receiving payments ranging from small amounts to several thousands of dollars depending on the settlement terms and individual claims.

title: The Commercial Market for Legal Psychedelics: Spravato
summary: This article examines the commercial market for legal psychedelics, focusing on Spravato (esketamine), the first FDA-approved psychedelic. It highlights Spravato's impressive sales growth, showing the potential for psychedelics in mainstream pharma. The piece also discusses the future outlook for upcoming psychedelic drugs like those from MAPS and Compass Pathways.

title: Pfizer backs CRISPR biotech Caribou in latest cell therapy investment
summary: Pfizer has invested $25 million in Caribou Biosciences by purchasing 4.69 million shares, specifically to advance Caribou's experimental multiple myeloma treatment, CB-011. This investment gives Pfizer a right of first negotiation for CB-011 and includes Pfizer's Sriram Krishnaswami joining Caribou's board. The move signals Pfizer's continued strategic involvement in cell therapy, even as it pares back some of its internal gene therapy work.

title: Pfizer makes equity investment in Caribou Biosciences
summary: Pfizer has invested $25 million to acquire a minority stake in Caribou Biosciences, a move that significantly boosted Caribou's shares. This investment, representing nearly 4.7 million shares at a premium, highlights Pfizer's ongoing strategy of investing in smaller biotechnology firms, especially those developing cell therapies using CRISPR genome editing. Caribou plans to use the proceeds to advance its experimental CAR-T cell therapy, CB-011, for blood cancer.

title: APVO436 Triplet Shows Promise in Treatment-Naïve AML
summary: The combination of APVO436, venetoclax, and azacitidine has shown promising duration of remission results in a phase 1b trial for treatment-naïve acute myeloid leukemia (AML) patients, with an 82% high response rate. The triplet therapy was generally safe and well-tolerated, with most cytokine release syndrome cases being mild or moderate. This data supports further development in phase 2 trials for both frontline and relapsed/refractory AML populations.

title: Pfizer Inc. stock underperforms Thursday when compared to competitors despite daily gains
summary: Pfizer Inc. (PFE) shares rose by 0.91% on Thursday, closing at $36.77, marking its third consecutive day of gains. However, the stock underperformed compared to the broader market, as the Dow Jones Industrial Average increased by 0.47% while the S&P 500 Index fell by 0.68%.

title: Pfizer Tornado Damage Threatens Tenuous US Drug Supply Chain
summary: A tornado strike at a major Pfizer manufacturing facility in Rocky Mount, North Carolina, has prompted hospital drug buyers and healthcare service providers to assess the potential impact on the already fragile US drug supply chain. Premier Inc. and Vizient Inc. are collaborating with other drugmakers to increase production and manage inventory, as hundreds of medicines were already in short supply before the incident. This damage threatens to exacerbate existing drug shortages across the country.

title: Tornado at Pfizer Plant Exposes Fragility of Drug Supply Chain
summary: A recent EF-3 tornado strike at a Pfizer facility in North Carolina has highlighted the critical fragility of the US drug supply chain. This event underscores the urgent need for solutions to drug shortages, which have reached nearly a decade-high level this year. The article proposes establishing a government-funded strategic reserve of vital medicines to ensure equitable distribution during unexpected disruptions.

title: Lilly's obesity drug leads to about 26% weight loss in new studies
summary: Eli Lilly announced that its experimental obesity drug, Mounjaro (tirzepatide), helped patients achieve an average weight loss of 26.6% in two late-stage studies. The drug demonstrated significant weight reduction in obese or overweight individuals without type 2 diabetes, reinforcing its potential as a blockbuster treatment and strengthening Lilly's position in the competitive obesity market. These results build on previous findings and align with the drug's earlier success in patients with type 2 diabetes also experiencing obesity or overweight.

title: Bristol Myers sales fall, cuts 2023 forecast as drugs face competition
summary: Bristol Myers Squibb reported lower-than-expected second-quarter sales and cut its full-year 2023 forecasts due to generic competition for its key drugs Revlimid and Eliquis. The company now anticipates revenue to fall by low-single-digit percentages for 2023 and has also lowered its earnings forecast. Despite challenges, BMS plans a $4 billion share buyback in the third quarter and is preparing for a leadership transition.

title: What Is The Real Value Of Pfizer Inc (PFE) Using A Simple DCF
summary: This article analyzes Pfizer Inc. (PFE) using a Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) model to determine its intrinsic value. Based on the model's assumptions, Pfizer is significantly undervalued, with a calculated DCF value of $72.54 per share compared to its current market price of $35.64, indicating a margin of safety of over 50%. The valuation highlights the company's strong projected free cash flows and a substantial terminal value, though it advises investors to consider multiple valuation methods.

title: Merck beats on revenue boosted by Keytruda sales, but posts quarterly loss due to Prometheus deal
summary: Merck reported stronger-than-expected second-quarter revenue, primarily driven by robust sales of its cancer drug Keytruda and HPV vaccine Gardasil. However, the company posted a net loss of $5.98 billion for the quarter, largely due to a $10.2 billion charge associated with its acquisition of Prometheus Biosciences. Despite the loss, Merck raised its 2023 sales forecast, citing strong underlying growth in oncology and vaccines.

title: Glaucoma Market Size, Share, Growth, Industry Analysis 2023 to 2032
summary: The global glaucoma market was valued at USD 8.06 billion in 2022 and is projected to reach USD 12.69 billion by 2032, growing at a CAGR of 4.64%. North America held the largest revenue share in 2022, while open-angle glaucoma and prostaglandin analogs dominated disease type and drug class segments, respectively. The market growth is driven by pipeline drugs, product launches, and the increasing prevalence of age-associated eye disorders.

title: FDA Approves ZURZUVAE™ (zuranolone), the First and Only Oral Treatment Approved for Women with Postpartum Depression, and Issues a Complete Response Letter for Major Depressive Disorder
summary: The FDA has approved ZURZUVAE™ (zuranolone) 50 mg as the first and only oral, once-daily, 14-day treatment for adults with postpartum depression (PPD), with an expected commercial launch in Q4 2023. However, the FDA issued a Complete Response Letter for zuranolone in Major Depressive Disorder (MDD), stating insufficient evidence of effectiveness and requiring additional studies. Biogen and Sage Therapeutics highlight the significance of this approval for women with PPD, while expressing disappointment regarding the MDD decision.

title: GSK will close its factory in Nigeria and move to third party direct distribution
summary: GlaxoSmithKline (GSK) Consumer Nigeria is shutting down its manufacturing operations and moving to a third-party distribution model, impacting 290 employees. While Nigerian media link this to foreign exchange shortages, the article suggests GSK's decision is more influenced by its corporate demerger with Haleon and a strategic review of African operations, exemplified by similar moves in Kenya. This transition follows a trend of multinational companies restructuring their presence in Nigeria due to economic challenges and strategic shifts.

title: Gates, CIFF, Pfizer, BD expand commitment for contraceptives
summary: The Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, Children’s Investment Fund Foundation (CIFF), Pfizer, and Becton, Dickinson & Company (BD) have expanded their partnership to increase access to injectable contraceptives for women in low- and lower-middle-income countries. This agreement, extending through 2030, aims to deliver over 320 million doses with a guaranteed price of $0.85 per unit, and will increase manufacturing capacity by 65 percent while expanding coverage to 92 countries. The initiative seeks to address barriers to family planning and promote gender equality.

title: ANL - Adlai Nortye Ltd. ADR Stock Price and Quote
summary: This article provides detailed stock information for Adlai Nortye Ltd. (ANL), including its current price, historical performance metrics, and key financial data. It also lists recent news, analyst ratings, and company developments, such as participation in investor conferences and clinical trial updates.

title: Have Effective Antidepressants Finally Arrived? Developments in Major Depressive Disorder Therapy
summary: This article explores recent developments in the treatment of Major Depressive Disorder (MDD), focusing on new pharmacotherapies after decades of limited progress. It highlights the potential of NMDA receptor antagonists like ketamine and esketamine, orally administered NMDA antagonists such as bupropion/dextromethorphan, neurosteroids like brexanolone and zuranolone, and the re-emerging interest in psychedelic drugs like psilocybin. The author discusses how these novel approaches offer hope for patients who do not respond to traditional antidepressants and address unmet needs like faster onset of action and better management of severe symptoms.

title: A short-lived hold for Arcellx & Gilead | ApexOnco - Clinical Trials news and analysis
summary: The FDA has lifted a clinical hold on Arcellx and Gilead's CART-ddBCMA multiple myeloma trial, less than two months after it was imposed due to a patient death. This is positive news for both companies, especially Gilead, which has seen several oncology setbacks. The trial protocol has been modified to allow expanded bridging therapies and retraining of clinical sites, with preliminary data expected in the second half of 2024.

title: Clinical trial to evaluate onvansertib as first-line mCRC treatment
summary: Cardiff Oncology announced plans for a phase-two clinical trial to evaluate onvansertib as a first-line treatment for RAS-mutated metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC). This follows promising results from a previous study where onvansertib showed significant tumor shrinkage and extended progression-free survival as a second-line treatment. The trial, supported by Pfizer Ignite, aims for accelerated FDA approval if successful.

title: Zavzpret From Pfizer
summary: The FDA has approved Pfizer's Zavegepant nasal spray (Zavzpret) for the acute treatment of migraine with or without aura in adults, excluding preventative use. This calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) receptor antagonist, administered as a single 10-mg intranasal spray, proved statistically superior to placebo in clinical trials for immediate pain relief and freedom from most bothersome symptoms. While effective, its use is contraindicated in patients with hypersensitivity to its components, severe hepatic impairment, or low creatinine clearance.

title: Is Pfizer Inc (PFE) Stock Significantly Undervalued?
summary: This article analyzes whether Pfizer Inc. (PFE) stock is significantly undervalued based on GuruFocus metrics. Despite recent gains, Pfizer appears undervalued compared to its GF Value of $52.84, with strong profitability and growth metrics. The analysis suggests a potential for higher long-term returns given its current valuation.

title: Artiva Biotherapeutics’ NK Cell Therapy AlloNK Cleared for Trial in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
summary: Artiva Biotherapeutics' investigational allogeneic natural killer (NK) cell therapy, AlloNK (AB-101), has received FDA clearance to begin a clinical trial. The trial will evaluate AlloNK in combination with rituximab for patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and active lupus nephritis (LN). This marks the first IND clearance for an allogeneic NK or CAR-T therapy for an autoimmune disease, with AlloNK having already shown promising safety data in lymphoma trials.

title: Alzheimer’s drug lecanemab set to soon be approved for use in Japan
summary: The Alzheimer's drug lecanemab, developed by Eisai Co. and Biogen Inc., is expected to be approved for manufacturing and sales in Japan after being endorsed by a health ministry expert panel. This medication targets early-stage Alzheimer's and mild cognitive impairment by removing amyloid beta, aiming to slow the disease's progression. It is anticipated to be commercially available by year-end, pending final approval, though concerns exist regarding its cost and potential side effects like cerebral edemas.

title: THE DERMATOLOGY FOUNDATION AND SKIN OF COLOR SOCIETY PARTNER TO DELIVER NEW DEI RESEARCH SUPPORT FOR 2024 WITH $1M GRANT FROM SANOFI-REGENERON
summary: The Dermatology Foundation (DF) and the Skin of Color Society (SOCS) have partnered to launch the Sanofi-Regeneron Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Mid-Career Award, backed by a $1 million grant. This initiative aims to support three established investigators in dermatology, expanding understanding of dermatological issues affecting underrepresented or underserved groups. Applications begin in September 2023 for research projects focused on health equity, with each award providing $100,000 annually for up to three years.

title: An Inside Look into the CDC and FNIH
summary: Julie Louise Gerberding, prior CDC director and current president and CEO of the Foundation for the National Institutes of Health (FNIH), discusses her experiences at both organizations in a Q&A. She provides insights on the CDC's focus during her tenure, the pharma industry's role, and the challenges and opportunities facing the biopharmaceutical sector today.

title: Pantera enters the Smackover- Next to $435BN “lithium hopeful” … uhhh Exxon Mobil?
summary: Pantera Minerals (ASX:PFE) has acquired a 35% interest in Daytona Lithium, a private company that holds leased acreage in the lithium-rich Smackover Formation in Arkansas, strategically located next to Exxon Mobil's recent acquisitions. This move places PFE among major players like Exxon, Albemarle, and Standard Lithium in a rapidly developing lithium land rush. The article highlights the potential of the Smackover Formation for lithium extraction from brines using Direct Lithium Extraction (DLE) technology, despite associated risks, and positions PFE for potential re-valuation as it progresses its project.

title: REGAL Trial Examining Galinpepimut-S in AML to Continue Without Modifications
summary: The phase 3 REGAL trial, evaluating galinpepimut-S for acute myeloid leukemia (AML) patients, has been recommended to continue without modifications by an independent data monitoring committee. This decision follows a prespecified risk-benefit assessment of unblinded data, with an interim analysis anticipated later this year or early next. The study is nearing completion of enrollment in the fourth quarter, marking significant milestones for SELLAS Life Sciences Group, Inc.'s development program for galinpepimut-S.

title: Pfizer and BioNTech Get Positive EU Opinion for Updated COVID-19 Vaccine
summary: The European Medicines Agency's CHMP has recommended marketing authorization for Pfizer Inc. and BioNTech SE’s Omicron XBB.1.5-adapted monovalent COVID-19 vaccine for individuals 6 months and older. The updated vaccine is designed to offer improved protection against current subvariants and is ready for shipment to EU member states pending a final decision from the European Commission. Pfizer and BioNTech have also filed an application with the US FDA for approval of this vaccine.

title: Psychedelic Bulletin #144: Otsuka to Buy Mindset; Responses to FDA Draft Guidance; Cybin to Acquire Small Pharma; Usona Publishes Phase 2 Study
summary: This Psychedelic Bulletin covers significant news in the psychedelic space, including Otsuka Pharmaceutical's acquisition of Mindset Pharma for CAD $80M, Cybin's all-share acquisition of Small Pharma, and COMPASS Pathways raising $125M. The article also details industry responses to the FDA's draft guidance on psychedelic clinical trials, focusing on issues like therapist roles, psychotherapy justification, adverse event reporting, and monitor ratios. Finally, it highlights Usona Institute's published Phase 2 study for psilocybin in Major Depressive Disorder and a UK cross-party committee's recommendation to reschedule psychedelics.

title: Sanofi appoints a venture investor to R&D head as executive team expands
summary: Sanofi has appointed Houman Ashrafian, a scientific advisor at SV Health Investors and a cardiologist, as its new head of research and development, effective September 11. This fills the position left by John Reed earlier this year. The company also announced a broader expansion of its executive team with new appointments for head of business operations and chief digital officer, aiming to strengthen its R&D transformation and digital strategy.

title: Pfizer says updated COVID shot generated strong reaction vs new variant in mice
summary: Pfizer announced that its updated COVID-19 vaccine, intended for use this fall, generated a strong antibody response against the highly mutated BA.2.86 subvariant in a preclinical study involving mice. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention had previously suggested that BA.2.86 might be more effective at causing infections in individuals who have had COVID-19 or were vaccinated with earlier versions of the shot. This news follows Moderna's earlier announcement that its updated shot also showed likely effectiveness against the BA.2.86 variant in human clinical trials.

title: Biotech execs vie for a share of obesity drug boom: ‘It’s the early innings’
summary: Biotech executives believe that while Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly have led the way in the new era of obesity drugs, the market is too vast for them to dominate it alone. Companies like Kallyope, Structure Therapeutics, and Aardvark Therapeutics are developing new treatments, including oral drugs and therapies targeting new neural pathways, to offer alternatives or complementary options beyond the current GLP-1 based injectables. The market is seen as "early innings" with significant opportunities for innovation in addressing obesity and related conditions like cardiovascular disease and NASH.

title: GSK spends big on new RSV vax commercials, but it's an AbbVie clean sweep as August's top pharma drug ad spender
summary: AbbVie dominated pharmaceutical drug advertising spending in August, securing the top three spots with Skyrizi, Rinvoq, and surprisingly, Vraylar. While GSK made a significant push for its new RSV vaccine Arexvy, overall spending for the top 10 drugs increased from July but remained below June's figures. The article details the spending for each of the top 10 drugs, highlighting new entries and shifts in rankings.

title: Seagen partners Nurix on 'degrader-antibody conjugates'
summary: Seagen has partnered with Nurix Therapeutics in a deal worth up to $3.46 billion to develop "degrader-antibody conjugates" (DACs) for cancer therapy. This new class of drugs combines Seagen's expertise in antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) with Nurix's protein degrader technology, aiming to target and break down cancer-driving proteins. The collaboration seeks to advance cancer treatment, with Seagen responsible for development and commercialization using Nurix's DELigase platform.

title: Best Practices for Conquering the Enablement Requirement After Amgen
summary: This article discusses the implications of the Supreme Court's decision in Amgen Inc. v. Sanofi regarding the enablement requirement for patent claims, particularly in biotechnology. It explores the challenges of functional genus claims and offers best practices for patent applicants seeking broader coverage, including detailed species claims and exploring alternative claim types. The article also touches on enforcement aspects and the importance of written description post-Amgen.

title: FDA Greenlights Updated COVID-19 Vaccines; Bivalent Vaccines No Longer Authorized
summary: The FDA has approved and authorized updated monovalent COVID-19 vaccines from Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna, which target the XBB.1.5 sublineage of SARS-CoV-2. Consequently, bivalent COVID-19 vaccines are no longer authorized for use in the US. These new vaccines are expected to be effective against currently circulating variants like EG.5 and BA.2.86 and will be available soon, with the CDC's Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices set to discuss recommendations for their use.

title: Exelixis links up with AI drug finder Insilico, LIB offloads China rights for PCSK9 inhibitor
summary: Exelixis has licensed a phase 1 cancer treatment, ISM3091, from Insilico Medicine for $80 million upfront and undisclosed milestones, marking its entry into AI-driven drug discovery. Simultaneously, LIB Therapeutics has sold the greater China licensing rights for its late-stage PCSK9 inhibitor, lerodalcibep, to Hasten Biopharmaceutical Company for $20 million upfront and $305 million in potential biobucks. This move comes after LIB's recent phase 3 success with lerodalcibep.

title: Bausch + Lomb seeks funding for eye drug acquisition from Novartis
summary: Bausch + Lomb is seeking nearly $2 billion to finance its acquisition of Xiidra eye drops and other assets from Novartis, a deal valued at $1.75 billion. Fitch Ratings views the acquisition as "strategically sound" despite increased leverage, anticipating it will boost Bausch + Lomb's ophthalmic pharmaceutical market presence. The company plans to raise funds through new senior notes and an incremental term loan facility.

title: ICON to partner with US government agency to test COVID vaccine candidates
summary: Contract research firm ICON Plc is partnering with the Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority to conduct a mid-stage clinical trial for next generation COVID-19 vaccine candidates. This collaboration is part of the U.S. government's "Project NextGen," a $5 billion initiative aimed at developing better protection against coronaviruses. The trial will assess the efficacy of new vaccine candidates compared to currently available shots.

title: US pharmacy chains gear up to administer updated COVID shots
summary: U.S. drugstore chains CVS Health and Walgreens Boots Alliance announced that updated COVID-19 vaccines would be available at their stores as soon as this week, following approval from regulators. The CDC director signed off on broad use of these updated shots, which are designed to target the circulating variant of the virus. While the government ended the public health emergency, the vaccines will remain free for most insured Americans, with a program planned for the uninsured.

title: Case Report: ASCENIV use in three young children with immune abnormalities and acute respiratory failure secondary to RSV infection
summary: This case report details the use of ASCENIV, an FDA-approved IVIG product with high antibody titers against respiratory pathogens, in three young children with immune abnormalities and severe RSV infection. Despite prior conventional therapies, these patients in an intensive care setting received ASCENIV and subsequently recovered without observed adverse effects. The study suggests ASCENIV may offer potential benefits as an adjunct treatment for severe RSV in immunodeficient pediatric patients and calls for further randomized controlled trials.

title: Bristol Myers plans to double experimental treatments to expand research pipeline
summary: Bristol Myers Squibb plans to double its experimental treatments in clinical trials over the next 18 months, focusing on cell therapies, to combat increasing generic competition for its top-selling drugs. The company aims to advance six new candidates, including three cell therapies for immune system disorders and various cancers while expanding its manufacturing capacity and continuing development for other diseases. This strategy comes as two of its key drugs, Revlimid and Eliquis, face declining demand and price negotiations by the U.S. Medicare health program.

title: Empowering Patient Advocates Across the Globe
summary: Bristol Myers Squibb (BMS) partners with patient advocacy programs and influencers globally to support patients beyond medication. Initiatives like "Look for the Spot" train tattoo artists to check for melanoma, while the HEROES program trains hair stylists to spot skin conditions, demonstrating innovative approaches to health awareness. These efforts, celebrated during Global Patient Week, underscore BMS's commitment to patient-centered care and addressing unmet needs worldwide.

title: BioNTech and CEPI Announce Partnership to Advance mRNA Mpox Vaccine Development and Support CEPI's 100 Days Mission
summary: BioNTech and CEPI have partnered to accelerate the development of an mRNA-based mpox vaccine, BNT166, with CEPI committing up to $90 million in funding. This collaboration supports CEPI's 100 Days Mission to rapidly develop vaccines against future pandemic threats. BioNTech is initiating a phase 1/2 clinical trial for BNT166, aiming to develop a safe, effective, and scalable vaccine that can be equitably accessed globally.

title: (oral decitabine and cedazuridine) for the treatment of adults with newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukaemia
summary: Otsuka and Astex announced that the European Commission has approved INAQOVI® (oral decitabine and cedazuridine) for the treatment of adults with newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukaemia who are ineligible for standard induction chemotherapy. This approval makes INAQOVI® the first and only oral hypomethylating agent licensed in the European Economic Area for this patient population, offering a new oral treatment option. The decision is based on positive results from the Phase 3 ASCERTAIN clinical trial, which demonstrated pharmacokinetic exposure equivalence to intravenous decitabine.

title: Biden administration announces $600 million to produce COVID tests and will reopen website to order them
summary: The Biden administration is allocating $600 million to boost domestic production of at-home COVID-19 tests and will reopen its website for Americans to order free tests. This initiative aims to prevent potential shortages during an anticipated rise in coronavirus cases in colder months. The funding will support 12 manufacturers and produce 200 million tests for federal stockpiles and online orders.

title: FDA updates Nuplazid label to clarify its safe use in Parkinson's
summary: The FDA has updated the prescribing information for Nuplazid (pimavanserin), a treatment for Parkinson's disease-related hallucinations and delusions, to clarify its safe use in patients both with and without dementia. The update to the "black box warning" specifies that Nuplazid should not be used in dementia patients with psychosis unless the psychosis is related to Parkinson's, aiming to help healthcare providers identify appropriate candidates. This change ensures that the therapy remains available for Parkinson's patients experiencing psychosis, regardless of their dementia status.

title: Pfizer Restarts Production Plant in North Carolina Following Tornado Damage in July
summary: Pfizer has restarted its Rocky Mount, N.C., production plant, 10 weeks after it sustained severe tornado damage in July. The plant, which produces about 25% of Pfizer's sterile injectables used in U.S. hospitals, aims for full production across its three manufacturing suites by the end of 2023. While some medicines may not be in full supply until next year, the expedited restart prioritized critical drugs based on patient need and inventory levels.

title: About 250,000 courses of COVID pill Paxlovid being administered per week - Pfizer CEO
summary: Pfizer's CEO Albert Bourla announced that approximately 250,000 courses of its oral antiviral COVID-19 treatment, Paxlovid, are being administered weekly due to a surge in U.S. cases. The company is, however, still awaiting approval for Paxlovid to be sold on the U.S. commercial market, though Pfizer is prepared for a smooth transition for its COVID-19 vaccines to commercial sale. There have been initial challenges with the rollout of updated COVID-19 vaccines, despite Pfizer having supplied a significant number of Paxlovid courses to the U.S. government.

title: Aurobindo Reverses Roles With Pfizer As It Drops Pin On Indonesia: What’s The Draw?
summary: Aurobindo Pharma has acquired 15 brands from Pfizer and Viatris, marking its entry into Indonesia and highlighting the growing potential of Southeast Asia's pharmaceutical market. This move represents a strategic shift for the Indian pharmaceutical company, expanding its global footprint. The article explores the motivations behind Aurobindo's focus on Indonesia and the broader implications for the pharmaceutical landscape in the region.

title: AbbVie Terminates Caribou CAR-T Contract in Culling of Cancer Pipeline
summary: AbbVie has terminated its collaboration and license agreement with Caribou Biosciences, focusing on allogeneic CAR-T therapeutics, as part of a strategic move to cull its cancer pipeline. This follows similar terminations with I-Mab and Harpoon Therapeutics, indicating a broader restructuring of AbbVie's oncology portfolio. Caribou noted that AbbVie's decision was strategic and unrelated to Caribou's performance or data generated.

title: Caribou hires chief people officer shortly after AbbVie drops CAR-T deal
summary: Caribou Biosciences hired Reigin Zawadzki as its first chief people officer following AbbVie's decision to terminate their CAR-T therapy development partnership. AbbVie is ending the February 2021 deal, which included $350 million in milestones per program, due to strategic focus rather than Caribou's performance. Despite this, Caribou CEO Rachel Haurwitz emphasized Zawadzki's role in maintaining company culture and supporting teams as they advance their CAR-T and CAR-NK cell therapy pipeline, building on a recent $25 million investment from Pfizer.

title: Pfizer and BioNTech Receive Health Canada Authorization for XBB.1.5-Adapted Monovalent COVID-19 Vaccine
summary: Pfizer Canada ULC and BioNTech SE announced that Health Canada has authorized their Omicron XBB.1.5-adapted monovalent COVID-19 vaccine (COMIRNATY® Omicron XBB.1.5) for individuals 6 months of age and older. This updated vaccine will be administered as a single dose for those 5 years and older, and as a three-dose series (or single dose depending on prior vaccination) for children 6 months through 4 years. The companies expect the vaccine to be available in Canada in the coming weeks, aiming to protect against current dominant XBB sublineages ahead of the fall/winter respiratory virus season.

title: Structure Raises $300M as Oral GLP-1 Drug’s Data Keep Up With Pfizer, Eli Lilly
summary: Structure Therapeutics successfully raised $300 million through a private placement of securities after announcing encouraging preliminary Phase 1b data for its oral GLP-1 drug candidate, GSBR-1290. The data showed significant weight loss in overweight and obese participants, positioning the drug competitively against rivals from Pfizer and Eli Lilly, despite a delay in its mid-stage study. The funding is expected to extend the company's cash runway through 2026 for upcoming pivotal trials.

title: Preclinical CRO Market Size, Share | CAGR Of 7.5%
summary: The global Preclinical CRO (Contract Research Organization) market is projected to reach USD 10.5 billion by 2032, growing at a CAGR of 7.5% from USD 5.2 billion in 2022. This growth is driven by the increased outsourcing of preclinical services by pharmaceutical and biopharmaceutical companies, medical device manufacturers, and academic organizations, aiming to reduce costs and leverage specialized expertise. Toxicology testing and patient-derived organoid models are key contributing segments, with North America currently dominating the market share and Asia Pacific expected to show the fastest growth.

title: Boeing PAC joins fleet of corporate givers to Kentucky Republican Party building fund
summary: Aerospace giant Boeing's PAC donated $100,000 to the Kentucky Republican Party's building fund, bringing the total corporate donations for the renovation and expansion of the Mitch McConnell Building to $2.75 million. This fund, allowed by a 2017 Kentucky law, accepts unlimited corporate contributions, unlike other political committees. The Republican building fund reported having over $2.7 million cash on hand, significantly more than the Kentucky Democratic Party's building fund.

title: Lilly to enter radiopharmaceutical drug field with $1.4B Point buyout
summary: Eli Lilly is acquiring Point Biopharma for approximately $1.4 billion, marking its entry into the radiopharmaceutical drug field for cancer treatment. This acquisition includes three clinical-stage drugs and gives Lilly manufacturing and R&D facilities, expanding its oncology unit. The deal highlights a growing interest among large pharmaceutical companies in radiopharmaceuticals due to recent advancements in their development and commercial success seen with drugs like Novartis' Pluvicto.

title: Need for innovative treatment options for insomnia as Z-drugs show limitations: GlobalData
summary: GlobalData highlights the critical need for new insomnia treatments due to the limitations of traditional Z-drugs, which are associated with significant side effects and dependence. While Z-drugs have dominated the market, emerging dual orexin receptor antagonists (DORAs) offer a superior safety profile, despite perceived lower efficacy compared to Z-drugs. The market is largely genericized, and few late-stage pipeline products offer novel mechanisms of action, underscoring the demand for innovative therapies with both improved efficacy and safety.

title: ALX Oncology Announces Proposed Public Offering
summary: ALX Oncology Holdings Inc. announced a proposed underwritten public offering of its common stock and pre-funded warrants. The company intends to use the net proceeds to fund the ongoing development of evorpacept, including clinical trials for market expansion, and for general corporate purposes. Piper Sandler and Cantor are acting as joint book-running managers for the offering.

title: Pfizer resolves Promosome patent lawsuit over COVID-19 vaccine
summary: Pfizer, BioNTech, and biotech firm Promosome have agreed to resolve Promosome's patent infringement lawsuit concerning messenger RNA technology used in COVID-19 vaccines. Promosome will dismiss its case with prejudice and has agreed not to bring future claims over the patent against Pfizer and BioNTech. This agreement follows Promosome abandoning a related lawsuit against Moderna and comes after Promosome had sought a share of royalties from vaccine sales, which generated billions for Pfizer and Moderna.

title: Inherited retinal diseases and gene therapies: A pharmaceutical overview
summary: This article provides an overview of gene therapy's transformative impact on previously "untreatable" inherited retinal diseases (IRDs). It details the two main categories of gene repair—replacement and suppression—and delivery methods (subretinal and intravitreal injections). The piece then highlights ongoing clinical trials for specific IRDs like Retinitis Pigmentosa, Choroidermia, Leber Congenital Amaurosis, Stargardt disease, and Achromatopsia.

title: Lilly bets on radiopharmaceuticals
summary: Eli Lilly and Company is entering the radiopharmaceutical market with the acquisition of POINT Biopharma Global for $1.4 billion. This deal includes two drugs in advanced clinical trials and a specialized manufacturing facility, as Lilly aims to invest in developing radioligand medicines for hard-to-treat cancers. The move positions Lilly alongside other big pharma companies like Novartis and Bayer that have already invested in this growing therapeutic area.

title: Blood Plasma Derivatives Market: A Comprehensive Analysis |
summary: Allied Market Research has released a comprehensive study on the "Blood Plasma Derivatives Market - Global Outlook and Forecast 2023-2030." The report analyzes market risks, opportunities, and provides strategic decision support, segmenting the market by key regions and covering growth drivers and the investment landscape. The global market, valued at $36.471 billion in 2020, is projected to reach $89.767 billion by 2030, growing at a CAGR of 9.4%.

title: Bristol-Myers Squibb to acquire Mirati in up to $5.8 billion deal
summary: Bristol-Myers Squibb announced its acquisition of cancer drugmaker Mirati Therapeutics for up to $5.8 billion, aiming to diversify its oncology portfolio and offset future revenue losses from patent expirations. The deal includes Mirati's lung cancer drug Krazati and another promising compound, MRTX1719. Bristol will acquire Mirati for $58 per share in cash, totaling around $4.8 billion, with an additional contingent value right potentially adding $1 billion.

title: FDA rejects Alnylam’s request to expand approval of one of its drugs to include heart patients
summary: The FDA rejected Alnylam Pharmaceuticals' request to expand the approval of its gene-silencing medicine, Onpattro, to treat ATTR-CM, a rare progressive heart disease. The FDA concluded that the benefits were not "clinically meaningful," a decision that surprised Alnylam's CEO. Despite the setback for Onpattro, Alnylam is pursuing a similar expansion for another of its drugs, Amvuttra, which is currently in late-stage clinical trials for the same heart condition.

title: Why Shares of Ventyx Biosciences Are Dropping Tuesday
summary: Shares of Ventyx Biosciences dropped significantly after the company released unimpressive Phase 2 trial results for its ulcerative colitis therapy, VTX002. While the drug showed some efficacy and a strong safety profile, investors were concerned it didn't distinguish itself sufficiently from existing S1P1 receptor modulators on the market from Pfizer and Bristol Myers Squibb. Despite the setback for VTX002, Ventyx has other programs in its pipeline, including VTX958 for psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis, and Crohn's disease, and maintains a solid cash position to fund operations.

title: First U.S. patients undergo innovative brain cancer treatment in new clinical trial at HCA Healthcare’s Johnston-Willis Hospital
summary: HCA Healthcare’s Johnston-Willis Hospital is the first in the U.S. to enroll patients in a new clinical trial for brain metastases from lung cancer. The trial combines noninvasive focused ultrasound with systemic immunotherapy, using Insightec's technology to temporarily open the blood-brain barrier to deliver critical medications. This groundbreaking research aims to improve treatment outcomes for brain tumors, potentially impacting lung cancer, breast cancer, and melanoma patients.

title: Biogen Lays Off 113 Reata Employees Weeks After Completing $7B Acquisition
summary: Biogen is laying off 113 employees from Reata Pharmaceuticals' Plano, Texas site, weeks after completing its $7.3 billion acquisition of Reata in July 2023. These layoffs, primarily affecting general, administrative, and some development roles, are part of Biogen's broader cost-reduction program aimed at saving $1 billion by 2025. This workforce reduction will impact about a third of Reata's 321 employees, while Biogen retains staff essential for the launch of Skyclarys, Reata's FDA-approved treatment for Friedrich's Ataxia.

title: Pfizer stock sinks as pharma giant cuts earnings outlook on weaker COVID demand
summary: Pfizer Inc. slashed its full-year sales outlook by $9 billion due to declining demand for its COVID-19 vaccine and Paxlovid treatment, causing its stock and shares of other vaccine makers to fall. The company now expects earnings between $1.45 to $1.65 per share on revenue of $58 billion to $61 billion, including a $5.5 billion charge for inventory write-offs. This reduction primarily stems from a $7 billion drop in Paxlovid revenue and a $2 billion reduction for its Comirnaty vaccine.

title: Top 15 Labcorp Competitors and Alternatives
summary: This article analyzes the top 15 competitors and alternatives to Labcorp, a major healthcare company specializing in clinical laboratory services. It provides detailed information on each competitor, including their founding year, headquarters, key services, and recent activities, highlighting the competitive landscape in the medical diagnostics and pharmaceutical services industry.

title: Why You Should Invest In Healthcare Stocks
summary: The article advocates for investing in healthcare stocks, highlighting their stability due to constant demand regardless of economic conditions, and the sector's significant economic contribution. It suggests avoiding pharmaceutical stocks due to regulatory risks and recommends alternative investments like over-the-counter medicine companies (Kenvue), medical device manufacturers (Stryker), hospital networks (HCA Healthcare), health insurers (UnitedHealth Group, Cigna Group), and innovative genetic detection or diagnostics firms (Illumina, Danaher, Augmedix, West Pharmaceutical Services, Intuitive Surgical). The author also suggests an equal-weight healthcare ETF (Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight Health Care) to diversify away from large drugmakers.

title: Pfizer Inc. agrees to pay $2M to resolve alleged compensation discrimination at New York City location
summary: Pfizer Inc. has agreed to pay $2 million in back wages and interest to female employees at its New York City headquarters to resolve alleged compensation discrimination. The agreement with the U.S. Department of Labor’s Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs (OFCCP) also requires Pfizer to set aside $500,000 for future salary adjustments, review its compensation system, and provide enhanced training to managers. This action stems from a compliance review covering 2015-2016, which found discrimination against 86 female professional employees.

title: Takeda ponies up €130M to settle tax linked to distant AbbVie-Shire breakup fee
summary: Takeda has agreed to pay 130 million euros to settle a tax assessment from Irish authorities related to a breakup fee from AbbVie's abandoned takeover bid for Shire in 2014. Despite initially challenging the charge, which arose before Takeda acquired Shire, the company will pay the settlement by December 31, 2023, and will revise its 2023 fiscal year revenue forecast accordingly. The original $1.64 billion breakup fee was paid to Shire after AbbVie's $55 billion merger proposal failed due to U.S. regulations deterring tax inversion deals.

title: GSK enters exclusive license agreement with Hansoh for HS-20089
summary: GSK has entered into an exclusive license agreement with Hansoh Pharma for HS-20089, a B7-H4 targeted antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) in phase I clinical trials. This agreement grants GSK exclusive worldwide rights (excluding Greater China) to develop and commercialize HS-20089, which targets gynaecologic cancers, with an upfront payment of $85 million and potential milestones up to $1.485 billion. The deal strengthens GSK's oncology portfolio, particularly in gynaecologic cancers, and leverages Hansoh's innovative R&D capabilities.

title: Rajiv Malik to retire as President of Viatris effective April 1, 2024
summary: Rajiv Malik, President of Viatris Inc., a global healthcare company, announced his retirement effective April 1, 2024. Malik, a nearly 40-year pharmaceutical industry veteran, played a crucial role in integrating Viatris' legacy companies, Mylan and Upjohn. He will continue to serve on the Viatris Board of Directors, ensuring continuity and contributing his experience and insight to the company's future strategic plans.

title: Abivax Adds $236M to Show Its Anti-Inflammatory Med Can Stand Apart in Crowded Field
summary: Abivax, a Paris-based biotech, raised nearly $236 million through a U.S. stock market debut and a private placement to fund late-stage clinical development of obefazimod, an orally administered drug for ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease. The company aims to differentiate its anti-inflammatory small molecule from existing biologic therapies by modulating multiple inflammatory pathways with a potentially better safety profile. Despite a 30% drop in stock price from its IPO, Abivax plans to release preliminary Phase 3 data for ulcerative colitis in early 2025 and 2026, and for Crohn's disease in late 2025.

title: Phase 3 OAKS and DERBY studies show clinically meaningful reduction in GA lesion growth
summary: The 24-month results from the Phase 3 OAKS and DERBY studies for pegcetacoplan injection (SYFOVRE) in geographic atrophy (GA) secondary to age-related macular degeneration (AMD) have shown a clinically meaningful reduction in GA lesion growth, with increasing effects over time. These results, published in The Lancet, also demonstrate a well-tolerated safety profile across more than 1,200 patients. Experts highlight the significance of these findings for treating this progressive disease and bringing the treatment to patients globally.

title: Pfizer to pay $2M to resolve allegations that the company underpaid women
summary: Pfizer will pay $2 million to resolve allegations of pay discrimination against 86 women, stemming from a U.S. Department of Labor review covering 2015-2016. The Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs (OFCCP) alleged that Pfizer violated Executive Order 11246 by paying these women less than comparable male employees. While Pfizer agreed to the settlement, stating the discrepancies were minor and from seven years ago, the company denied revising its compensation system as stated by the DOL, asserting its commitment to equitable pay practices.

title: Zenith Epigenetics Ltd. Announces Collaboration with Cencora on ZEN-3694
summary: Zenith Epigenetics Ltd. announced a collaboration with Cencora to accelerate the commercialization of its ZEN-3694 program, an advanced epigenetic approach for cancer treatment. Cencora will provide various services, including regulatory and market access insights, to strategize ZEN-3694's market introduction and ensure successful patient access. ZEN-3694 is currently in clinical development for multiple oncologic indications with numerous partners and collaborators.

title: Bristol Myers' incoming CEO plots turnaround for struggling new launches
summary: Bristol Myers Squibb's incoming CEO, Chris Boerner, plans to reinvigorate underperforming new drug launches like Abecma and Zeposia, emphasizing that their struggles are a matter of "when" not "if" they meet expectations. Despite current challenges, BMS expects its new products to generate over $10 billion in sales by 2026, slightly delayed from an earlier 2025 target. The company is actively addressing issues, including expanding manufacturing for Abecma and focusing on market access for Zeposia, while also leveraging recent acquisitions to drive future growth.

title: US shifting COVID antivirals to commercial market on Nov. 1
summary: Effective November 1st, the U.S. government will transition the distribution of Pfizer's Paxlovid and Merck's Lagevrio COVID-19 antiviral treatments to the commercial market. Despite this change, health officials state that most patients will still be able to access these treatments at little to no cost. The government will continue to supply existing doses for a transition period, and an agreement with Pfizer will maintain free Paxlovid for Medicare, Medicaid, and uninsured patients through 2024 and 2028, respectively.

title: Sanofi Plans Spin-Off of Consumer Business, Lowers Profit Outlook
summary: Sanofi announced plans to spin off its consumer health business by late 2024 and abandoned its 2025 operating profit margin goal of 32%, instead focusing on long-term profitability. This decision led to a more than 15% drop in shares and follows a trend among other major drugmakers like Johnson & Johnson and GlaxoSmithKline. The French drugmaker aims to concentrate on transformative medicines, particularly in immunology and inflammation, and anticipates a decline in low-single digits for 2024 due to increased R&D investment, with a strong rebound predicted for 2025.

title: A brain-focused biotech raises $225M to develop drugs for schizophrenia, Parkinson’s
summary: MapLight Therapeutics, a San Francisco-based biotechnology company, has successfully raised $225 million in Series C funding to advance its drug development programs for neurological disorders like schizophrenia, Alzheimer’s psychosis, and Parkinson's. The round was led by Novo Holdings, with participation from new investors such as 5AM Ventures and Cowen Healthcare Investments. The fresh capital will enable the company to push its most advanced candidates into mid-stage clinical trials next year and continue progress on its other pipeline programs.

title: Pfizer to shutter North Jersey campus; nearly 800 jobs affected
summary: Pfizer plans to close its Peapack, New Jersey campus by February 2024, affecting nearly 800 jobs due to slumping sales of its COVID-19 vaccine and treatment. Many employees will be relocated to the NYC headquarters or Parsippany, NJ site. The closure will significantly impact the local tax base, as Pfizer currently contributes 9% of the local taxes.

title: Lilly buys out Beam in heart drug alliance with Verve
summary: Eli Lilly is expanding its involvement in gene editing by acquiring option rights to several of Verve Therapeutics' drug programs from Beam Therapeutics. This deal, valued at $200 million upfront with an additional $50 million equity investment in Beam and potential milestone payments of $350 million, strengthens Lilly's position in developing gene-edited medicines for heart disease. The collaboration includes programs targeting PCSK9 and ANGPTL3 genes, with Lilly taking on a share of future development expenses and U.S. profits.

title: Cellectis gets another bailout | ApexOnco - Clinical Trials news and analysis
summary: Cellectis has secured a new bailout deal with AstraZeneca, nine years after a previous agreement with Pfizer. AstraZeneca will invest $25 million upfront and an $80 million equity investment in Cellectis, with potential for further investment and milestone payments, focusing on novel cell and gene therapy candidates. This comes as a significant boost for Cellectis, whose market cap had substantially declined, marking the third time the company has been rescued by a major pharmaceutical partner.

title: AstraZeneca and Cellectis enter gene therapy partnership worth over $2.2bn
summary: AstraZeneca has formed a collaboration and investment agreement with Cellectis, valued at over $2.2 billion, to accelerate the development of gene therapies for oncology, immunology, and rare diseases. This partnership grants AZ access to Cellectis's gene editing technologies and manufacturing capabilities, with exclusive rights to 25 genetic targets for up to ten potential products. AstraZeneca will make an initial payment of $105 million in 2023, followed by a $140 million equity investment in early 2024, leading to approximately 44% ownership of Cellectis, in addition to potential milestone payments and royalties.

title: A Family Affair
summary: This article explores the unique leadership dynamic of Krystal Biotech, a gene therapy company founded and led by husband-and-wife team Krish and Suma Krishnan. It highlights their decision to work together, beginning with a personal sacrifice by Suma to unite their family, and how their complementary expertise has driven the company's success. The piece underscores their shared commitment to helping patients, which transcends personal considerations in their professional collaboration.

title: Pharma CEOs ‘find their voice’ on Israel-Hamas conflict
summary: In the wake of the October 7th Hamas attack on Israel, several prominent biopharma CEOs, including those from Pfizer, Merck, Eli Lilly, Bayer, and Regeneron, have publicly condemned the violence. This marks a shift where business leaders are increasingly expected to weigh in on social issues, despite potential risks of alienating customer groups. The article highlights how this stance reflects a growing trend for corporate social responsibility, influenced by figures like former Merck CEO Ken Frazier who took a stand on social issues in the past.

title: Historic Collaborative Effort: Pharma Giants Rethink the Future of Life Sciences Transacting at MediLedger Face-to-Face Meeting, Hosted by Cencora
summary: Major pharmaceutical companies convened at Cencora's headquarters for the MediLedger Face-to-Face Meeting to discuss transforming the healthcare supply chain through efficiency, transparency, and innovation. Key topics included the financial impact of MediLedger, data alignment, claims processing, scalability, business intelligence, and AI integration. The meeting aimed to translate discussions into actionable strategies for the benefit of providers and patients.

title: How French pharma giant Sanofi is betting big on AI
summary: Sanofi, the French pharmaceutical giant, has been heavily investing in artificial intelligence (AI) over the past two years, forging multiple partnerships and deals with AI companies to transform its drug discovery and development processes. The company aims to become the first AI-powered pharmaceutical company at scale, utilizing AI to enhance research, optimize clinical trials, and streamline manufacturing. This trend of big pharma investing in AI is growing, as companies seek to leverage advanced technologies to develop innovative therapeutics and improve efficiency.

title: Zoetis Earnings: U.S. Commercialization of Librela Is Off to a Good Start and Bolsters the Wide Moat
summary: Zoetis posted strong third-quarter results, driven by companion animal segment growth and livestock stabilization, reaffirming its full-year expectations and fair value estimate. The successful U.S. commercialization of Librela for canine osteoarthritis reinforces the firm's wide economic moat, despite impending competitive pressures from rival products in 2024 and 2025. Zoetis also saw significant growth in diagnostics revenue, especially in the U.S., strategically expanding into an attractive market.

title: Arbutus Biopharma CEO to retire as company cuts workforce by 24%
summary: Arbutus Biopharma's CEO, William Collier, is set to retire at the end of the year. The company is also implementing a 24% workforce reduction. These changes follow Arbutus's decision in September to narrow its research focus to conserve cash.

title: FDA approves Eli Lilly's tirzepatide for weight loss, paving way for wider use of blockbuster drug
summary: The FDA has approved Eli Lilly's tirzepatide for weight loss, to be marketed as Zepbound, a significant development for individuals with obesity or who are overweight with related conditions. This approval expands the use of the drug, previously known as Mounjaro for Type 2 diabetes, and positions Eli Lilly as a major competitor in the growing obesity drug market. The drug works by activating GLP-1 and GIP hormones, with clinical trials showing substantial weight loss.

title: AI helps fight muscle loss and unhealthy aging
summary: BioAge Labs is utilizing AI and genetic data to develop drug therapies aimed at combating muscle loss and unhealthy aging. The company successfully repurposed an existing drug, BGE-105, which showed promising results in preventing muscular atrophy in a phase 1 clinical trial. This approach highlights how AI can accelerate drug discovery by identifying key molecular pathways linked to healthy longevity and disease prevention.

title: World’s First Approved Chikungunya Vaccine
summary: Valneva SE announced that the U.S. FDA approved IXCHIQ®, the world's first single-dose, live-attenuated vaccine for preventing chikungunya virus disease in individuals aged 18 and older at increased risk of exposure. This approval addresses an unmet medical need for a potentially debilitating disease with limited treatment options. The vaccine demonstrated a 98.9% seroresponse rate at 28 days in pivotal Phase 3 trials and sustained 96.3% at six months post-vaccination.

title: FDA Accepts sBLA for Interchangeability Designation for Latest Humira Biosimilar
summary: The FDA has accepted a Supplemental Biologics License Application (sBLA) for adalimumab-bwwd (Hadlima), a Humira biosimilar from Samsung Bioepis and Organon, seeking interchangeability designation. If approved, Hadlima would be the third Humira biosimilar to achieve this status, allowing pharmacists to substitute it for the reference product without physician permission, thereby improving patient access and affordability. The sBLA is supported by clinical data from a Phase 4 study demonstrating pharmacokinetic similarity and comparable outcomes for patients switching between Humira and Hadlima.

title: Novo Nordisk wants to be a cardiovascular company, too, with sights set on inflammation
summary: Novo Nordisk, already a leader in diabetes and obesity, is strategically expanding into the cardiovascular disease market. This move is bolstered by the successful Select trial of its drug Wegovy, which demonstrated significant reductions in heart complications. The company is actively developing new heart disease treatments and acquiring related medications to establish itself as a major player in this field.

title: Pfizer to cut 500 jobs at UK site as part of wider cost cuts
summary: Pfizer announced it would cut 500 jobs at its Sandwich, Kent site in the U.K. as part of a larger $3.5 billion cost-cutting initiative. This move follows a reduction in its full-year revenue forecast and a quarterly loss, primarily due to lower-than-expected sales of its COVID-19 vaccine and treatment. Pfizer's shares were up 2% on the day of the announcement but had lost about 42% of their value year-to-date due to concerns over COVID product demand.

title: FDA approves new Bristol Myers drug for lung cancer
summary: The FDA has approved Bristol Myers Squibb's new lung cancer medication, Augtyro, which was acquired through a $4 billion buyout of Turning Point Therapeutics. The drug targets lung tumors with ROS1 gene alterations and is expected to outperform rivals, potentially doubling the market size for this specific treatment. Augtyro is part of Bristol Myers Squibb's strategy to offset patent expirations of its top-selling drugs.

title: AiBtl signs $667m licensing deal for ABVC’s CNS drug
summary: ABVC BioPharma has signed a definitive global licensing agreement with AiBtl for its central nervous system (CNS) drugs, a deal potentially valued at $667 million. Under the agreement, ABVC will receive 46 million shares from AiBtl worth $460 million, $7 million in milestone cash payments, and 5% royalties on net sales up to $200 million. The licensed drugs include ABV-1504 for major depressive disorder (MDD) and ABV-1505 for attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), both of which are plant-based norepinephrine transporter inhibitors.

title: What's Going On With Penny Stock AgeX Therapeutics?
summary: Serina Therapeutics Inc., a privately held clinical-stage biotechnology company, has entered into a non-exclusive license agreement with Pfizer Inc., allowing Pfizer to utilize Serina's POZ polymer technology. This development follows Serina Therapeutics' August announcement of a merger agreement with AgeX Therapeutics Inc., with the combined entity retaining the Serina Therapeutics name and focusing on CNS indications. Amidst these corporate activities, AgeX Therapeutics (AGE) stock experienced a significant decline on heavy trading volume.

title: Pfizer's CEO Sends a Warning to Eli Lilly. Is the Stock a Buy?
summary: Pfizer's CEO, Albert Bourla, believes the company will become a major player in the weight loss market, challenging current leader Eli Lilly, following its $7 billion acquisition of Metsera. While Eli Lilly has a significant lead with existing products and a strong pipeline, Pfizer aims to launch its first anti-obesity drug by late 2028 and expects a turnaround due to its pipeline and new products, making its stock potentially attractive.

title: Dr Reddy's Labs unveils USFDA-approved drug-free non-invasive migraine management device Nerivio in India
summary: Dr. Reddy's Laboratories has launched Nerivio in India, an USFDA-approved, drug-free, non-invasive wearable device for managing migraines. This device utilizes Remote Electrical Neuromodulation (REN) to stimulate nerve endings, activating the body's natural pain-relieving processes. Nerivio is intended for both acute and preventive migraine treatment in adults and adolescents, and marks Dr. Reddy's entry into digital therapeutics.

title: Sickle Cell Disease Treatment Market Size to Garner Around USD 50.45 Billion by 2032
summary: The global sickle cell disease treatment market is projected to reach approximately USD 50.45 billion by 2032, expanding at a CAGR of 35.1% from 2023. Key growth drivers include market expansion in developing regions, a robust pipeline of innovative therapies, and global health initiatives. North America currently leads the market, while Asia-Pacific is anticipated to exhibit the fastest growth.

title: Texas AG sues Pfizer over quality-control lapses in kids' ADHD drug
summary: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton has sued Pfizer and its supplier Tris Pharma, alleging they knowingly provided ineffective children's ADHD medication, Quillivant XR, to the state's Medicaid program. The lawsuit claims the companies manipulated quality-control testing between 2012 and 2018, and that independent tests frequently showed the drug failed to dissolve properly. Pfizer denies the allegations, stating their product's safety was not impacted, while Tris Pharma intends to rigorously defend against the claims.

title: EPO revokes Moderna patent in vaccine dispute with BioNTech
summary: The European Patent Office (EPO) has revoked one of Moderna's mRNA patents, EP 3 718 565 B1, in its dispute with BioNTech, Pfizer, Sanofi, and other pharmaceutical companies. Moderna, which had sued BioNTech for patent infringement in several European countries, confirmed it would appeal the EPO's decision. The case revolves around two Moderna patents for mRNA technology, with Moderna seeking damages for sales made by competitors after March 8, 2022.

title: Xenon drug misses main goal of depression study
summary: Xenon Pharmaceuticals announced that its experimental drug, XEN1101, did not meet its primary goal in a mid-stage clinical trial for major depressive disorder. Despite missing the main endpoint, the company highlighted several positive findings and supportive data, leading to a rise in stock price as analysts viewed the results as a "net win" given low expectations for antidepressant activity. Xenon plans to continue exploring the drug's development for depression and other indications, including ongoing late-stage trials for seizures.

title: U.S. Sickle Cell Disease Treatment Market Analysis [2030]
summary: The U.S. sickle cell disease treatment market, valued at USD 1.44 billion in 2022, is projected to grow at a CAGR of 17.3% by 2030, driven by the increasing prevalence of the disease and a focus on novel drug development. Pharmacotherapy is expected to be the fastest-growing segment, with new drug approvals and pipeline products contributing to market expansion. Key players are intensifying R&D efforts and forming partnerships to enhance product accessibility.

title: Drug Discovery Services Market Size To Hold USD 75.68 Bn By 2032
summary: The global drug discovery services market is projected to grow from USD 19.37 billion in 2022 to USD 75.68 billion by 2032, exhibiting a CAGR of 14.6%. This growth is attributed to increasing R&D investments, technological advancements, and the growing trend of outsourcing by pharmaceutical companies. North America is expected to hold the largest market share due to its well-established pharmaceutical industry and significant R&D expenditures.

title: AbbVie to Acquire ImmunoGen With its Platinum-Resistant Ovarian Cancer Drug Elahere
summary: AbbVie announced its acquisition of ImmunoGen for approximately $10.1 billion, primarily for ImmunoGen's FDA-approved platinum-resistant ovarian cancer drug, Elahere. This acquisition is expected to bolster AbbVie's oncology pipeline in solid tumors and is anticipated to be accretive to diluted earnings per share starting in 2027. The deal includes ImmunoGen's full oncology portfolio, which AbbVie believes could drive long-term revenue growth and expand Elahere's market presence.

title: AbbVie seeks lift from 'guided missile' cancer drug with $10 bln ImmunoGen deal
summary: AbbVie will acquire ImmunoGen for $10.1 billion in cash to bolster its cancer drug portfolio with ImmunoGen's "guided missile" cancer therapies. This acquisition aims to offset the impending loss of exclusivity for AbbVie's top-selling drug Humira and address competition for its cancer drug Imbruvica. ImmunoGen's Elahere, an antibody-drug conjugate (ADC), is projected to become a blockbuster drug by 2030.

title: Biotech Announces New Responder in Breast Cancer Trail
summary: BriaCell Therapeutics Corp. (BCTX:NASDAQ;BCT:TSX.V) has announced a new exceptional responder in its Phase 2 study for Bria-IMT, a personalized immunotherapy for advanced breast cancer, as highlighted by H.C. Wainwright analyst Emily Bodnar. The patient exhibited significant tumor reduction and pain relief, demonstrating the therapy's systemic efficacy and ability to cross the blood-brain barrier. H.C. Wainwright maintains a Buy rating and a US$18 price target for BriaCell, projecting substantial commercial potential.

title: AbbVie (ABBV) to Acquire ImmunoGen (IMGN) for $10.1 Billion
summary: AbbVie (ABBV) announced its definitive agreement to acquire cancer biotech ImmunoGen (IMGN) for $10.1 billion, primarily for ImmunoGen's ovarian cancer drug, Elahere. This acquisition is expected to diversify AbbVie's oncology pipeline and highlights a trend of increased M&A activity in the biotech sector for innovative cancer treatments. The deal, which offers a significant premium to ImmunoGen shareholders, is anticipated to close in mid-2024.

title: Drug development trends: insight from Thermo Fisher’s Anil Kane
summary: Anil Kane of Thermo Fisher Scientific discusses current drug development trends, including the continued interest in small molecules, the rise of biologics and advanced therapies, and the emerging focus on oral delivery for large molecules. He also highlights the growing popularity of prefilled syringes for patient convenience and the industry's shift towards developing globally approvable drug substances and products, often supported by continuous manufacturing and digital technologies.

title: Pfizer and Valneva Complete Recruitment for Phase 3 VALOR Trial for Lyme Disease Vaccine Candidate, VLA15
summary: Pfizer Inc. (NYSE: PFE) and Valneva SE (Nasdaq: VALN; Euronext Paris: VLA) have completed recruitment for the Phase 3 VALOR trial for their Lyme disease vaccine candidate, VLA15. The trial enrolled 9,437 participants across the U.S., Europe, and Canada, aiming to confirm efficacy, safety, lot consistency, and immunogenicity. Regulatory filings in the U.S. and Europe are anticipated in 2026, subject to positive data.

title: Blackstone explores sale of Anthos Therapeutics -sources
summary: Private equity firm Blackstone is reportedly exploring the sale of Anthos Therapeutics, a developer of blood thinners it founded four years ago with Novartis' backing. Despite having no approved products or revenue, Anthos could fetch several billion dollars due to its anticoagulants progressing to late-stage clinical trials, significantly increasing its value from Blackstone's initial $250 million investment.
