This move comes as patents for leading blood thinners are set to expire, creating a potential opening for new treatments like Anthos's abelacimab.

title: Pfizer plans to depart BIO | STAT
summary: Pfizer has decided to leave the Biotechnology Innovation Organization (BIO), a major biotechnology industry trade association. This departure is seen as a blow to BIO, which represents a wide range of companies from small startups to large pharmaceutical firms. BIO acknowledged the difficult economic situation for the industry, expressing disappointment but hoping for Pfizer's return when conditions improve.

title: Eli Lilly obesity drug now available in US pharmacies
summary: Eli Lilly's newly approved obesity treatment, Zepbound, is now available in U.S. pharmacies, with a potential cost of $550 per month for those without insurance coverage, which is half its list price. The drug enters a rapidly growing market, with Wall Street analysts projecting Zepbound sales to reach approximately $2 billion in 2024. Zepbound has already been added to the preferred medicines list by at least one major pharmacy benefit manager, Cigna's Express Scripts.

title: An end to breast cancer? California company develops groundbreaking vaccine with promising future
summary: A California company, Anixa Biosciences, has developed a groundbreaking vaccine targeting triple-negative breast cancer, with initial trials showing promising results. The vaccine, created through decades of research at the Cleveland Clinic, aims to prevent breast cancer recurrence and potentially eliminate the disease. A second, larger trial with 600 women is set to begin in 2024, with hopes for FDA approval within five years.

title: Sanofi’s Sarclisa gets one up on Darzalex | ApexOnco - Clinical Trials news and analysis
summary: Sanofi's Sarclisa has achieved a significant win with its phase 3 Imroz trial, meeting the primary endpoint of progression-free survival in first-line multiple myeloma patients ineligible for transplant. This advancement positions Sarclisa favorably against Genmab and Johnson & Johnson’s Darzalex, particularly as an analogous Darzalex study, Cepheus, has seen delays. Despite Sarclisa's lower sales compared to Darzalex, this clinical success provides a crucial boost for Sanofi's drug.

title: Life Sciences & Quantum: A Faster, Safer Way to Develop Drugs
summary: Quantum computing has the potential to revolutionize drug discovery and development by significantly reducing the time and cost involved in bringing new medicines to market. By leveraging the unique properties of quantum mechanics, these computers can model complex molecular interactions far beyond the capabilities of classical supercomputers, leading to faster identification of promising drug candidates. Major pharmaceutical companies and tech giants are already investing in this technology, aiming to create more effective and safer drugs, including personalized medicines tailored to individual genetic makeups.

title: Troubled Evofem, marketer of contraceptive gel Phexxi, sells itself to Aditxt in $100M deal
summary: Evofem, the company behind the contraceptive gel Phexxi, has agreed to sell itself to biotech Aditxt for approximately $100 million. Despite initial FDA approval, Evofem has faced financial difficulties, with its share price plummeting over 99% in recent years. The deal includes Aditxt assuming Evofem's senior secured debt and exchanging Evofem's shares for Aditxt stock, aiming to close in the first half of 2024.

title: Pfizer Loses $12.93 Billion as COVID Vaccines Stall
summary: Pfizer's market value dropped by $12.93 billion after the company revised its 2024 revenue forecast downwards due to waning demand for its COVID-19 vaccines and related products. This downturn is supported by a Kaiser Family Foundation survey showing diminishing public interest in COVID-19 vaccinations. To counter this, Pfizer is looking to diversify its portfolio with the $43 billion acquisition of biotech cancer specialist Seagen and aims for significant cost savings.

title: Pfizer shares sink after it resets 2024 COVID expectations
summary: Pfizer's shares fell to a 10-year low after the company forecast 2024 sales significantly below Wall Street expectations, primarily due to revised COVID-19 vaccine and treatment revenue projections. The drugmaker also lowered its adjusted profit forecast for 2024 and is undertaking cost-cutting measures, while struggling with a disappointing RSV vaccine launch and declining COVID-19 vaccination rates.

title: Hyperlipidemia Drugs Market To Attain Revenue USD 31.23 Bn By 2032
summary: The global hyperlipidemia drugs market, valued at USD 21.2 billion in 2022, is projected to reach USD 31.23 billion by 2032, growing at a CAGR of 4%. This growth is driven by inactive lifestyles, rising healthcare expenditure, an aging population, and increasing R&D activities and drug approvals. North America is expected to hold the largest market share due to its advanced healthcare infrastructure and high prevalence of hypercholesterolemia.

title: Hospira, Inc. Issues A Voluntary Nationwide Recall For 4.2% Sodium Bicarbonate Injection, 8.4% Sodium Bicarbonate Injection, and Atropine Sulfate Injection Due to the Potential Presence of Glass Particulate Matter
summary: Hospira, Inc., a Pfizer company, is voluntarily recalling specific lots of 4.2% Sodium Bicarbonate Injection, 8.4% Sodium Bicarbonate Injection, and Atropine Sulfate Injection nationwide due to the potential presence of glass particulate matter. The presence of such particulates could lead to serious adverse events in patients, including inflammation, granuloma, and blood vessel blockage or life-threatening blood clots. Although no adverse events have been reported to date, the company emphasizes patient safety and has instructed wholesalers and hospitals to quarantine and return the affected products.

title: Bristol Myers Squibb acquires Karuna Therapeutics for $14 billion, boosting neuroscience portfolio
summary: Bristol Myers Squibb is acquiring Karuna Therapeutics for $14 billion to significantly boost its neuroscience pipeline, specifically with KarXT, a promising antipsychotic under FDA review for schizophrenia and in trials for Alzheimer's psychosis. This acquisition, approved by both companies' boards, is expected to enhance Bristol Myers Squibb's growth and reach for patients with these conditions. Analysts are optimistic about KarXT's potential sales, projecting up to $6.8 billion with multiple uses.

title: Pfizer Accelerates Climate Action through Pan-European Virtual Power Purchase Power Agreements
summary: Pfizer has signed pan-European virtual power purchase agreements (VPPAs) for solar power in southern Spain to accelerate its climate action and achieve its Net-Zero Standard goal by 2040. These agreements, brokered by Schneider Electric and with Bruc, secure 124MW from four new solar projects to cover all of Pfizer's purchased electricity for its EU sites. This move is a significant step towards Pfizer's goal of using 100% renewable energy by 2030 and reducing its carbon footprint.

title: Ionis, Astrazeneca win FDA approval of competitor to Alnylam drug
summary: The FDA has approved Wainua, a new drug from AstraZeneca and Ionis Pharmaceuticals, for transthyretin amyloidosis polyneuropathy. This approval intensifies the rivalry between Ionis and Alnylam, as Wainua directly competes with Alnylam's existing drugs Onpattro and Amvuttra. Analysts believe Wainua, developed with newer LICA technology, could capture a significant market share despite Alnylam's current lead, particularly as both companies pursue trials for a more common form of the disease affecting the heart.

title: AstraZeneca buys Chinese CAR-T biotech Gracell in a $1.2bn deal
summary: AstraZeneca has signed a definitive agreement to acquire Gracell Biotechnologies, a China-based CAR T-cell therapy biotech, for approximately $1.2 billion in combined upfront and potential contingent value payments. This acquisition aims to expand AstraZeneca's portfolio in chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapies, with the deal expected to close in Q1 2024. Gracell's lead asset, GC01F, is a dual BCMA and CD19 targeting CAR-T cell therapy being investigated for multiple myeloma and systemic lupus erythematosus.

title: Global Complicated Urinary Tract Infections Treatment Industry size is set to experience a 5.76% CAGR by 2033, according to FMI’s projections
summary: The global complicated urinary tract infections (cUTI) treatment industry is projected to grow at a CAGR of 5.76% to reach US$16.1 billion by 2033, up from US$9.2 billion in 2023. This growth is driven by advancements in diagnosis such as biosensors and new assays, the increasing prevalence of diabetes and kidney stones, and the launch of more efficient combination drugs. North America is expected to lead the market, while Penicillin and combinations are predicted to see the fastest growth among drug classes.

title: Here are the 20 worst-performing stocks among the S&P 500 in 2023
summary: The article identifies the 20 worst-performing stocks within the S&P 500 for the year 2023, despite a general market rally. It notes that 178 stocks in the index were still down for the year, highlighting companies like Pfizer, Dollar General, Enphase Energy, and Walgreens as significant underperformers. Dollar General is specifically mentioned with a 45% stock price decline.

title: Life-Sciences Property Sector Cools After Multiyear Winning Streak - WSJ
summary: The life-sciences property sector, once a hot commercial-property market favored by investors during the pandemic, is now facing stress. Vacancies in lab buildings are rising due to increased supply and a decline in available funding. Unlike traditional office spaces, life-sciences buildings are less affected by remote work because lab work requires specialized, on-site equipment.

title: Layoffs At Pearl River’s Pfizer Campus And Elsewhere Signal A Reset For COVID Vaccine Maker
summary: Pfizer is implementing significant layoffs across several facilities, including a nearly 30% reduction at its Pearl River campus, impacting a total of 285 workers. These workforce adjustments are attributed to an “enterprise-wide cost realignment program” stemming from decreased demand for its COVID-19 vaccine and antiviral drug, and substantial lost revenue related to Paxlovid. Despite the layoffs, Pfizer is also investing $470 million in renovations and expansion at its Pearl River site, alongside recent acquisitions like Seagen, signaling a strategic reset for the pharmaceutical giant.

title: Canada approves Pfizer's gene therapy for bleeding disorder
summary: Canada's health regulator has approved Pfizer's gene therapy for hemophilia B, a rare inherited bleeding disorder, based on trials showing a single dose was superior to current treatments. This approval precedes a U.S. decision and makes Pfizer's Beqvez the second gene therapy for hemophilia B, following CSL's Hemgenix approved by the FDA in November 2022. Pfizer is also seeking U.S. approval for an experimental antibody treatment for both hemophilia A and B.

title: CVS will remove AbbVie's Humira from some drug reimbursement lists in April
summary: CVS Health announced it will remove AbbVie's blockbuster drug Humira from some of its preferred drug lists for reimbursement starting April 1, favoring biosimilar versions instead. This move is aimed at lowering drug costs for customers by promoting biosimilars with significantly lower list prices. CVS will also offer a co-branded version of Humira through its company Cordavis in the second quarter of the year.

title: AgroFresh Solutions' Clinton Lewis, Jr. On Taking The Public Company Private
summary: AgroFresh Solutions, after struggling as a public company due to its SPAC origins, significant debt, and lack of liquidity, decided to go private. CEO Clinton Lewis Jr. explains that this move, facilitated by private equity firm Paine Schwartz Partners, allows the company to pursue both organic and inorganic growth opportunities more effectively. The private structure provides fresh equity and financial resources, enabling strategic acquisitions like Tessara.

title: FDA Grants Priority Review to Pfizer and Genmab's Tivdak for Cervical Cancer Treatment
summary: The FDA has granted Priority Review to Pfizer and Genmab's supplemental Biologics License Application (sBLA) for Tivdak (tisotumab vedotin-tftv), aiming to convert its accelerated approval to full approval for recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer. This decision is based on positive results from the Phase III innovaTV 301 trial, which showed improved overall survival, progression-free survival, and objective response rate compared to chemotherapy. Tivdak, an antibody-drug conjugate, targets tissue factor on tumor cells and represents an important treatment option for patients with limited choices.

title: Pfizer’s PDE4 inhibitor shows early efficacy in psoriasis, atopic dermatitis
summary: Pfizer's topical PDE4 inhibitor, PF-07038124, has shown early efficacy in a phase 2a study for treating atopic dermatitis and plaque psoriasis. Patients treated with the drug exhibited significant improvements in IGA and EASI scores compared to a vehicle group, with the drug being well-tolerated and devoid of treatment-related adverse events. This suggests a potential therapeutic benefit for these dermatological conditions.

title: Valneva Vaccinates First Participant in Pediatric Trial of Single-Shot Chikungunya Vaccine
summary: Valneva has vaccinated the first participant in its Phase 2 clinical trial for a single-shot chikungunya vaccine in children. This trial aims to evaluate the vaccine's safety and immunogenicity in children aged one to eleven, following positive Phase 3 data in adolescents and regulatory approval for adults in the U.S. The goal is to extend the vaccine's label to include younger age groups, addressing the significant public health threat of chikungunya globally.

title: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) Market
summary: The Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) market is projected to experience impressive growth between 2023 and 2032, driven by increasing prevalence and awareness of the disorder, along with the launch of new pipeline products. Key companies and therapies are identified, and the report from DelveInsight provides an in-depth understanding of market trends, epidemiology, and treatment scenarios across major global regions.

title: Global Medicine Spending to Reach $2.3 Trillion by 2028 as More Patients Get Access to Better Therapies, Says IQVIA Institute Report
summary: A new IQVIA Institute report projects global medicine spending to hit $2.3 trillion by 2028, driven by increased patient access to novel therapies, especially in immunology, endocrinology, and oncology. This updated outlook raises the growth forecast despite lower expectations for COVID-19 vaccines and therapeutics, indicating that global use and spending are surpassing pre-pandemic rates. The report highlights significant growth drivers including innovative oncology drugs and GLP-1 agonists for obesity, while noting the impact of biosimilars on immunology spending.

title: The Largest Announced M&A Deals of 2023
summary: The article provides an overview of the largest M&A deals announced in 2023, highlighting significant consolidations across various sectors. Key acquisitions include ExxonMobil and Chevron in energy, Pfizer and Cisco in pharmaceuticals and technology, and major movements in telecommunications, electric vehicles, and mining. These deals reflect strategic growth, diversification, and expansion in a dynamic economic environment.

title: Kyverna sets plans for IPO in test of biotech enthusiasm
summary: Kyverna Therapeutics announced plans for an Initial Public Offering (IPO) to fund the development of its lead cell therapy, KYV-101, for lupus. This move signals a potential resurgence in the biotech IPO market, which has been slow since 2021. Kyverna's treatment, licensed from the NIH, targets autoimmune diseases and has multiple trials underway, including for lupus nephritis, systemic sclerosis, myasthenia gravis, and multiple sclerosis.

title: More patients are getting their meds online. Big Pharma wants in on the action
summary: Driven by the pandemic, patients are increasingly comfortable with online medication access, prompting major pharmaceutical companies like Eli Lilly to enter the direct-to-consumer telehealth market. Eli Lilly recently launched LillyDirect, a platform routing patients to telehealth services for prescriptions of its drugs, such as the obesity medication Zepbound, with fulfillment through an online pharmacy. This move signals Big Pharma's intent to capitalize on the growing online prescription trend, and the full article, exclusive to STAT+ subscribers, delves deeper into this development.

title: Head and Neck Cancer (HNC) Pipeline Analysis Covering Clinical
summary: A new report by DelveInsight titled "Head and Neck Cancer (HNC) Pipeline Insight" provides a comprehensive analysis of over 120 pipeline drugs from 100+ pharma and biotech companies. The report details ongoing clinical development activities, growth prospects in the Head and Neck Cancer Therapeutics Market, and profiles emerging therapies and companies. It covers drugs from pre-clinical to marketed stages, including their mechanism of action, type, route of administration, and regulatory approvals.

title: Pfizer Inc. stock rises Monday, still underperforms market
summary: Pfizer Inc. (PFE) shares rose 0.11% on Monday to $28.31, marking its second consecutive day of gains. Despite this rise, the stock underperformed the broader market, as both the S&P 500 Index and the Dow Jones Industrial Average saw larger percentage increases.

title: Decoding Economic Trends: Insights from Our Speaker’s Presentation
summary: This article summarizes a presentation from the New England Life Science & Biotech Summit, where experts discussed the economic outlook and fundraising environment for life science companies. Speakers Mark Luschini and David Reed provided an optimistic view, highlighting the U.S. economy's resilience and anticipated growth in R&D spending due to an upcoming "patent cliff." The article also advises companies on preparing for a potential reopening of the IPO window in 2024, emphasizing a shift towards more conservative deal economics and a focus on profitability.

title: Ionis’ long-term HAE drug lowered attack rates, topline Phase 3 results show
summary: Ionis Pharmaceuticals announced positive topline Phase 3 results for its RNA-targeted treatment, donidalorsen, showing a statistically significant reduction in hereditary angioedema (HAE) attack rates when administered monthly or bimonthly. The drug also demonstrated a favorable safety profile, paving the way for a potential regulatory filing later this year. While the prophylactic HAE market is competitive, Ionis hopes to carve out a niche with its long-term dosing efficacy.

title: Karuna, Cerevel might be just the start of psychiatry drug M&A
summary: The acquisitions of Karuna Therapeutics by Bristol Myers Squibb and Cerevel Therapeutics by AbbVie signal a renewed interest in psychiatry drug development, particularly for schizophrenia treatments. Deal documents reveal that multiple major pharmaceutical companies were vying for these biotechs, suggesting a potential wave of further mergers and acquisitions in the neuropsychiatry space. Analysts believe the success of a new class of muscarinic receptor agonist drugs could unlock significant market opportunities and attract more dealmakers.

title: Sanofi to buy Inhibrx in deal worth up to $2.2B
summary: Sanofi has announced its acquisition of Inhibrx in a complex deal potentially worth up to $2.2 billion. The acquisition's primary focus is Inhibrx's experimental drug INBRX-101 for alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, while other Inhibrx assets will be spun out into a new publicly traded company. Sanofi will pay $1.7 billion upfront for Inhibrx equity, with additional funds tied to a contingent value right.

title: Former Pfizer Director Alleged Wrongful Termination
summary: A former Pfizer Analytics Director, Frank Han, has filed a wrongful termination and whistleblower retaliation lawsuit against Pfizer. Han claims he was fired after attempting to expose alleged Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (FCPA) violations within the company, specifically concerning $168 million in payments to potentially influential government officials in China. The lawsuit, originally filed in California state court and later moved to federal court, seeks various damages including lost wages and emotional distress.

title: Exosome-based SARS-CoV-2 vaccine selected for Project Nextgen
summary: Capricor Therapeutics Inc.'s Stealthx exosome-based multivalent vaccine for SARS-CoV-2 has been chosen for the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services' Project Nextgen initiative. This project aims to develop COVID-19 vaccines that offer broader and more durable protection against the virus.

title: Indian-American Ex-Pfizer Employee Charged With Insider Trading On Covid Pill
summary: An Indian-American former Pfizer employee, Amit Dagar, has been convicted of insider trading and conspiracy to commit insider trading. Dagar was found guilty by a jury in New York for using confidential information about Pfizer's COVID-19 pill, Paxlovid, to illegally profit in the stock market. He traded Pfizer call options and tipped off a friend based on early positive clinical trial results before they were publicly released.

title: RayzeBio drew other pharma interest before Bristol Myers deal
summary: Radiopharmaceutical drugmaker RayzeBio attracted bids from two other major pharmaceutical companies before ultimately agreeing to a $4.1 billion buyout by Bristol Myers Squibb. Documents reveal that Bristol Myers engaged in aggressive negotiations, outbidding competitors with a final offer of $62.50 per share, significantly higher than initial proposals, highlighting the growing interest in the radiopharmaceutical market.

title: Pfizer Inc. stock remains steady Friday, still outperforms market
summary: Pfizer Inc. (PFE) shares closed unchanged on Friday, even as the broader stock market saw mixed results. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose, while the S&P 500 Index experienced a slight decline. Pfizer Inc. closed significantly below its 52-week high.

title: Pfizer’s First-Launched Vyndamax Patent Case Is Down to Validity
summary: Pfizer's legal battle to safeguard its heart drug Vyndamax against generic competition has progressed, as Dexcel Pharma Technologies Ltd. conceded that its proposed generic version infringes three key patents. This concession narrows the case to focus solely on the validity of Pfizer's patents. The development is significant for Pfizer, given the increasing importance of Vyndamax sales to the company's revenue.

title: Gilead Sets Sights on Hepatitis C Elimination as it Marks 10 Years of Curative Therapies
summary: Gilead is marking 10 years since the FDA approved its first curative therapy for Hepatitis C (HCV), which has transformed the lives of over 4 million people treated with Gilead's medicines globally. The company is now focusing on the ambitious goal of eliminating HCV worldwide by 2030, building on the success of its highly effective therapies that boast cure rates of 95% or more. This milestone highlights the remarkable progress from HCV once being considered a virtual death sentence to a curable disease.

title: COUR Pharmaceuticals Secures $105 Million in Series A
summary: COUR Pharmaceuticals has secured $105 million in Series A financing, co-led by Lumira Ventures and Alpha Wave Ventures, with participation from major pharmaceutical companies and investment funds. These funds will advance COUR's Myasthenia Gravis and Type 1 Diabetes product candidates into Phase 2a clinical trials and support other pipeline opportunities. The investment highlights confidence in COUR's proprietary antigen-specific immune tolerance platform for treating autoimmune and inflammatory diseases.

title: US Syphilis Cases Rise to Highest Level in More Than 70 Years
summary: Syphilis cases in the U.S. have reached their highest level in over 70 years, with a 17% increase in 2022 to 207,000 cases. This surge represents a seven-fold increase compared to two decades ago. The rise in infections is compounded by a shortage of Pfizer's treatment for the disease.

title: Roche, Pfizer, Bristol Myers back immune disease firm Cour Pharmaceuticals
summary: Cour Pharmaceuticals, an immune disease firm, has successfully raised $105 million in Series A funding from major pharmaceutical companies including Roche, Pfizer, and Bristol Myers Squibb. This investment will support the advancement of two clinical-stage drugs targeting myasthenia gravis and type 1 diabetes. The company's platform utilizes polymer nanoparticles to reprogram the immune system and induce tolerance to disease-specific antigens.

title: The US uses endangered monkeys to test drugs. This law could free them.
summary: The US biomedical industry heavily relies on long-tailed macaques for drug testing, leading to a significant decline in their wild populations and their classification as endangered. Animal rights groups are leveraging the Endangered Species Act (ESA) to protect these captive monkeys, arguing that the law's "take" prohibition extends to preventing harm in research settings, potentially ending their use in experiments. This effort faces industry opposition and regulatory hurdles but could set a precedent for other endangered species used in scientific research.

title: Some Great Blue Chips Found in MOAT
summary: The article highlights the VanEck Morningstar Wide Moat ETF (MOAT) as a good option for investors seeking blue-chip exposure. It explains that MOAT's methodology, which focuses on companies with sustainable competitive advantages, results in holdings that are large- and mega-cap firms suitable for long-term growth. The ETF's sector diversification and specific blue-chip holdings like Pfizer, Bristol-Myers Squibb, and Comcast are discussed as examples of its investment strategy.

title: Vaxcyte Looks to Raise $750M in Latest Public Offering
summary: Vaxcyte, a California-based vaccine biotech, is undertaking another public offering to raise approximately $750 million by selling over 10.9 million shares at $64 each. This offering follows a similar sale in 2023 that aimed to net $500 million. The company recently completed enrollment for a Phase I/II clinical study for its VAX-31 pneumococcal conjugate vaccine candidate and plans to release topline data in Q3 2024, despite facing strong competition from major pharmaceutical companies like Pfizer, Merck, and Sanofi in the pneumococcal vaccine market.

title: Why a former BMS exec calls her new CEO role ‘unfinished business’ in cancer care
summary: Caroline Loew, former Bristol-Myers Squibb executive, is the new CEO of Mural Oncology, an Alkermes spinoff. She views her new role as "unfinished business" in cancer care, focusing on building a new culture and advancing next-generation immuno-oncology therapies like nemvaleukin. Loew emphasizes strategic thinking, patient-first principles, collaboration, and inclusivity as pillars of her leadership at Mural.

title: How Dr. Ted Love Went From Studying Molecular Biology To Becoming The Former CEO Of A Company Acquired By Pfizer For $5.4B
summary: Dr. Ted Love transitioned from molecular biology and medicine to a successful career in biotechnology, culminating in his role as CEO of Global Blood Therapeutics (GBT). Under his leadership, GBT developed Oxbryta® for sickle cell disease and was later acquired by Pfizer for $5.4 billion. Following the acquisition, Dr. Love retired but remains active in the sickle cell community and serves on several boards.

title: Liver Disease Biotechs’ Stocks Crash on Eli Lilly’s Mounjaro Data
summary: Stocks of biotech companies developing treatments for MASH (Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatohepatitis) crashed after Eli Lilly's latest earnings report included clinical trial data related to Mounjaro. This news significantly impacted the sector.

title: Pfizer’s Nurtec could become first blockbuster CGRP inhibitor
summary: Pfizer's Nurtec is on track to become the first blockbuster CGRP inhibitor, leading sales in a competitive migraine treatment market. The CGRP class collectively generated $3.8 billion in revenue in 2023, representing a 21% increase from 2022. Nurtec outperformed other oral migraine therapies like Ubrelvy and Lilly’s Emgality.

title: Pfizer Inc. stock underperforms Friday when compared to competitors
summary: Pfizer Inc. (PFE) shares fell 0.04% on Friday, closing at $27.56, despite a mixed trading session for the broader market. This drop ended a three-day winning streak for the company's stock. The S&P 500 Index rose, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average experienced a slight decline.

title: UT Southwestern collaborates with Pfizer to develop improved RNA delivery technologies: Newsroom
summary: UT Southwestern Medical Center is partnering with Pfizer Inc. to advance RNA-enhanced delivery technologies for genetic medicine therapies through its Program in Genetic Drug Engineering. This collaboration aims to improve the fundamental understanding and development of new delivery technologies for RNA-based therapies, leveraging AI design methodologies and both organizations' expertise. The joint effort seeks to accelerate Pfizer's RNA medicines portfolio and explore new therapeutic applications, particularly building on Dr. Daniel Siegwart's pioneering work in lipid nanoparticles for genetic drug delivery.

title: Does Government Disclosure of a Company’s Trade Secrets Amount to an Unlawful Taking Under the Fifth Amendment?
summary: The article discusses a Court of Federal Claims decision in *Vanda Pharmaceuticals, Inc. v. United States*, addressing whether government disclosure of a company's trade secrets constitutes an unlawful taking or breach of contract. While the court dismissed the breach of contract claim and some claims as time-barred, it allowed a Fifth Amendment takings claim to proceed, raising questions about what information shared with the FDA can be considered proprietary trade secrets.

title: Better Choice acquires Aimia in pursuit of a pet weight loss supplement
summary: Better Choice, a pet health and wellness company, has acquired its former R&D partner, Aimia Pet Healthco Inc., to develop treats and toppers for pet weight loss. This acquisition aims to better manage internal clinical trials for a supplement to combat pet obesity, mirroring successful human and domestic animal weight loss medications like Slentrol, Wegovy, Ozempic, and Mounjaro. The initiative seeks to integrate protein and nutrients from Halo products to promote lean muscle and overall pet health.

title: Scrip Asks…What Does 2024 Hold For Biopharma? Part 6: Therapeutic Area Advances
summary: This article - Part 6 of the "Scrip Asks…What Does 2024 Hold For Biopharma?" series - focuses on anticipated therapeutic area advances in 2024. It highlights high hopes for the fields of metabolism, neurology, and oncology within the biopharmaceutical industry. The piece suggests significant developments are expected in these key areas.

title: rprx-20231231rpplcpressx.htm
summary: Royalty Pharma plc reported strong financial results for Q4 and full year 2023, with Portfolio Receipts of $3,049 million for the full year and net cash provided by operating activities of $2,988 million. The company announced significant transaction activity totaling up to $4.0 billion in 2023, adding eight potentially transformative therapies to its portfolio, and provided 2024 guidance for Portfolio Receipts of $2,600 to $2,700 million. Positive updates were noted across its development-stage royalty portfolio, including key clinical trial successes and corporate acquisitions relevant to its royalty interests.

title: Ocrevus continues steady growth trajectory in 2023
summary: Roche's multiple sclerosis drug Ocrevus generated over $7 billion in revenue in 2023, marking a 12% increase from the previous year. Despite other therapies entering the market, Ocrevus has maintained a steady growth trajectory since its launch in 2017, with a significant fourth-quarter sales bump contributing to its strong performance. The article also notes the uncertain future of late-stage BTK inhibitors in the MS market.

title: Olezarsen receives Orphan Drug designation from U.S. FDA for familial chylomicronemia syndrome
summary: Ionis Pharmaceuticals announced that its investigational medicine, olezarsen, has received Orphan Drug designation from the U.S. FDA for familial chylomicronemia syndrome (FCS). This rare genetic disease leads to extremely high triglyceride levels and recurrent acute pancreatitis. The designation provides incentives for development and highlights the critical need for effective treatments for FCS, a condition for which there are currently no FDA-approved therapies.

title: “顶流”并购投行总裁预测：2024是药企并购大年
summary: Eric Tokat, Co-President of top investment bank Centerview Partners, predicts 2024 will be a strong year for pharmaceutical mergers and acquisitions. This trend is driven by the biotech industry's shift towards strategic collaborations, large pharmaceutical companies' need to address the "patent cliff," and the significant market potential in areas like ADC, AI in medicine, and cell and gene therapies. This creates a promising outlook for the biopharmaceutical sector.

title: Lilly Edges Out J&J to Top 20 BioPharma Market Cap List for 2023
summary: Eli Lilly surpassed Johnson & Johnson to claim the top spot in GlobalData's 2023 biopharma market cap list, with its market capitalization growing by 59.2% to $553.4 billion, driven by surging demand for its GLP-1 drugs for diabetes and obesity. Novo Nordisk secured third place with a 51.5% growth rate, also fueled by GLP-1 drug sales. While some companies like Vertex and Regeneron showed significant growth, others like Moderna and Pfizer experienced considerable market cap declines due to factors such as decreased COVID-19 sales and generic competition.

title: Procter & Gamble inks toothpaste licensing deal with Burt’s Bees
summary: Procter & Gamble has signed a licensing deal with Burt's Bees to begin manufacturing Burt's Bees toothpaste products. This move by P&G follows extensive research into consumer demand for natural products, with 35% of U.S. consumers interested in simple and effective toothpaste formulas. While toothpaste is the initial focus, other products may be considered for the future.

title: Why Global Baby Care Products Market is demanding globally with
summary: The global baby care products market is experiencing significant demand, driven by increasing parental awareness of child safety, rising disposable incomes, and the growth of the working women population. Key players like Procter & Gamble, Kimberly Clark, and Johnson & Johnson are leading this market, which is projected to grow to over $110 billion by 2025 with a CAGR of 6%. North America currently holds the largest share due to high expenditure and progressive technology, though high costs and a lack of regulatory guidelines pose challenges to market growth.

title: Procter & Gamble Amps Up Beauty Tech at CES
summary: Procter & Gamble showcased its advancements in beauty technology at CES, featuring connected products across its beauty, health, and skincare portfolios. The company unveiled innovations like SK-II's Future X Smart Store, an updated AI-based Olay Skin Advisor, the Opté Precision Skincare System, and the AIRIA smart home fragrance system. P&G also highlighted the Oral-B Genius X toothbrush and a new Heated Razor by GilletteLabs, emphasizing its commitment to combining technology with consumer understanding.

title: We're techy, too! Deere, Tide maker head to CES gadget show
summary: Traditional companies like John Deere and Procter & Gamble are exhibiting at CES for the first time, demonstrating that "every company today is a technology company." They are showcasing innovations ranging from self-driving tractors and AI-powered combine harvesters to smart toothbrushes and heated razors, reflecting a broader economic shift where consumers expect digital experiences. These companies aim to attract investors, partners, and skilled employees by highlighting their tech-forward initiatives.

title: Procter & Gamble offshoot brand Opté launches high tech beauty wand
summary: P&G Ventures' offshoot brand Opté has launched the Opté Precision Skincare System, a smart-beauty wand that uses advanced technology to scan, detect, and correct hyperpigmentation. Unveiled at CES 2019, the device combines blue LED scan lights, a digital camera, a Minicomputer Precise Color Algorithm, and a Micro Serum Jet Printer with a Precision Serum. This innovation allows for precise application to only affected areas, offering a new category of digital skincare for Procter & Gamble.

title: US based toothpaste firm suffers $11 million loss in Vietnam
summary: Colgate-Palmolive Vietnam is struggling in the competitive oral care market, facing fierce competition from global rivals like Unilever (P/S, Close-up) and local brands. Despite market potential, Colgate's revenue growth has been slow while costs increased, leading to accumulated losses of nearly $11 million by the end of 2017, exceeding its charter capital.

title: I Worked for Gillette's Parent Company for More Than 20 Years. Here's What I Think About Their Crazy Controversial Ad
summary: A former Procter & Gamble marketing executive offers an inside, yet unbiased, perspective on Gillette's controversial "The Best Men Can Be" ad. He argues that while polarizing, the ad successfully evokes emotion and makes a social statement, which he believes is crucial for brand relevance in today's landscape. The author reflects on the ad's impact from both an advertising and social standpoint, concluding that it sparks necessary debate and encourages self-reflection.

title: Dentsu's Carat takes majority of P&G media business
summary: Procter & Gamble has significantly shifted its media business to Dentsu's Carat following a bidding process, though Omnicom's Hearts & Science retains some of the business. P&G is moving more work in-house and providing brands with greater flexibility in media planning and buying while exploring a new media model. The company aims to optimize its media buy and pursue further cost reductions by 2021.

title: What that Gillette ad says about the trend in woke advertising
summary: Procter & Gamble's Gillette released a new ad addressing "toxic masculinity" and the #MeToo movement, following a trend of companies taking stances on social issues. The article explores how this "woke" advertising strategy can be successful, citing examples like Nike's Colin Kaepernick campaign, while also warning about failures like Pepsi's and Ram Trucks' ads that were perceived as artificial. Ultimately, the success of such campaigns hinges on authenticity and consistent follow-through.

title: Turnaround traction? P&G reports stronger sales - again, stock soars
summary: Procter & Gamble reported another strong quarter of growth, prompting an increase in its annual sales forecast. Organic sales rose 4 percent for the second consecutive quarter, leading to a 4.9 percent increase in stock price. Despite overall positive results, the grooming unit experienced a dip, and the company is facing challenges with raw material costs.

title: P&G releases refillable packaging
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) announced a partnership with TerraCycle's Loop platform to introduce "collect and recycle" solutions for its brands, aiming to eliminate packaging waste. As part of this initiative, P&G is also launching reusable, refillable packaging for several of its popular products, to reduce reliance on single-use packaging. The program will be validated through in-market learning experiments in New York and Paris starting mid-2019.

title: P&G releases refillable packaging
summary: Procter & Gamble has partnered with Loop, a circular e-commerce platform by TerraCycle, to introduce refillable packaging and "collect and recycle" solutions for many of its global brands. This initiative aims to eliminate packaging waste and is part of P&G's Ambition 2030 sustainability goals, with initial testing beginning in mid-2019 in New York and Paris. The collaboration focuses on durable, reusable packaging for popular products like Pantene, Tide, Cascade, and Crest, along with circular solutions for hygiene products and grooming items.

title: Colgate predicts lower profits in 2019 as strong dollar bites
summary: Colgate-Palmolive forecasts a decline in 2019 profits due to the strong dollar, which exacerbates emerging market sales issues and rising input costs. The company expects earnings per share to fall by "low-single-digit" levels, contradicting analyst expectations for a rise, and anticipates flat to modestly higher net sales. This outlook led to a 3.2 percent drop in Colgate shares in pre-market trading, as the strong dollar makes products more expensive overseas and diminishes repatriated revenues.

title: Colgate-Palmolive expects profit to decline in 2019
summary: Colgate-Palmolive forecasts a surprise drop in 2019 profit, blaming higher raw material costs and a stronger dollar, impacting its shares. Despite beating revenue estimates with $3.81 billion, the company anticipates a mid-single-digit decline in earnings per share for the year due to increased advertising spending and fluctuating exchange rates. This comes as the company faces stiff competition and challenges in key markets like Latin America, despite strong sales in North America.

title: Employment approaches 800 at P&G plant; shampoo production underway
summary: Procter & Gamble's new plant in Berkeley County, W.Va., is nearing completion, with exterior construction 90% done and shampoo production already underway. The company currently employs 785 workers and plans to hire an additional 300-plus within the next 18 months. This $500 million investment is part of a North American supply chain transformation, involving the transfer of production from other P&G facilities that are closing or downsizing.

title: P&G strikes licensing deal for Febreze product
summary: Procter & Gamble has entered into a licensing agreement with Helen of Troy, allowing Helen of Troy to use the Febreze brand name on its OdorGrab Air Cleaner product. This deal enables brand expansion for Febreze into the air purifier market. The agreement was updated on January 30, 2019.

title: P&G buys purpose-driven feminine care marketer This Is L.
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) has acquired This Is L., a purpose-driven feminine care products maker known for its L. brand made with organic cotton. The acquisition aligns with P&G's strategy to center its business around purpose and tap into the disruptor market for organic materials in feminine care. This move complements P&G's existing feminine care portfolio and reflects a broader CPG trend of acquiring startup brands.

title: FIVE QUESTIONS: P&G president touts L. acquisition's 'great growth potential'
summary: Jennifer Davis, president of Procter & Gamble Co.'s Global Feminine Care division, discussed the "great growth potential" of a recent acquisition. She stated that the acquisition would help P&G appeal to younger consumers. The article is framed as "FIVE QUESTIONS," implying an interview format, though the full questions and answers are not provided in this snippet.

title: Procter & Gamble job fair set for Feb. 27 in Hagerstown
summary: Procter & Gamble will host an open house and job fair on Feb. 27 from 5:30 to 7:30 p.m. at the Fletcher Branch of the Washington County Free Library in Hagerstown, seeking to hire additional plant technicians for its Tabler Station manufacturing facility near Martinsburg, W.Va. The company aims to hire over 450 people in the next 18 months, particularly for shampoo and conditioner production, and plans to produce a variety of hand dishwashing products, body washes, and other consumer goods at the site.

title: Will P&G stock split again soon?
summary: Procter & Gamble's stock is approaching all-time highs, prompting speculation about a potential stock split, a question not asked by investors in 15 years. Historically, P&G has split its stock two-for-one when shares trade above $100 for an extended period, leading to anticipation among investors. The article explores past precedents for splits and delves into why one might not have happened in other instances where the stock briefly crossed the $100 mark.

title: Procter & Gamble face Israeli class-action lawsuit regarding Oral B mouthwash labelling
summary: Procter & Gamble is facing an Israeli class-action lawsuit seeking $8.3 million over the labeling of its Oral B and Pro Expert mouthwashes. The lawsuit alleges that the Hebrew instructions encourage excessive use compared to the English instructions, leading to higher repeat purchases. The Tel Aviv District Court approved the class-action status, stating P&G failed to adequately inform consumers of both usage options.

title: Denver Company Pays $4.2M for Former Procter & Gamble Plant
summary: A Denver-based real estate investment company, IPT Avenel DC Urban Renewal, LLC (registered out of the same address as Black Creek Group), purchased a former Procter & Gamble plant in Woodbridge, Middlesex County for over $4.2 million in November. The P&G facility, which manufactured fragrances and chemicals for Tide detergent, had been shuttered the previous year, leading to the transfer of production to an Ohio plant. The new owner's plans for the property, located at 100 Essex Avenue East, are currently unknown.

title: Update: P&G moving around employees to take bite from 500 employee cut in 2020
summary: Procter & Gamble is moving employees around to mitigate job losses from a previously announced cut of 500 positions as production shifts from Iowa City to West Virginia by 2020. The company is working with the factory's union, hiring locally for other positions, and moving some employees to different facilities to lessen the impact. While hair care and body wash production are moving, oral rinse manufacturing will remain, and toothbrush employees will not be affected.

title: How To Land A Full-Time Gig At P&G
summary: This article details Payton Lang's journey from intern to full-time employee at Procter & Gamble, highlighting her application process, internship experience, and advice for students. Lang, a Washington University in St. Louis Olin Business School graduate, shares insights on securing a position with the global company, emphasizing preparation, networking, and authenticity.

title: P&G sets world record for longest TV commercial
summary: Procter & Gamble Co. set a Guinness World Record for the longest TV commercial ever by airing a 14-hour version of an Old Spice ad. The commercial was composed of hundreds of short clips edited together. This achievement was officially recognized by Guinness World Records.

title: Former P&G executive joins C-suite of pharma firm
summary: Dr. Andreas Grauer, a former Procter & Gamble Co. executive, has been appointed as the chief medical officer of Corcept Therapeutics Inc. Corcept Therapeutics is a pharmaceutical company focused on discovering and developing drugs for metabolic, oncologic, and psychiatric disorders. This move strengthens Corcept Therapeutics' leadership team with Grauer's extensive experience.

title: FTI Consulting adds Rodolfo Araujo as senior managing director in Washington, DC
summary: FTI Consulting has appointed Rodolfo Araujo as a senior managing director in its strategic communications segment in Washington, D.C. Araujo, an expert in corporate governance, proxy contests, and M&A, will lead the Americas corporate governance and activism offering and join the firm's activism and M&A solutions practice. He brings nearly a decade of experience from Institutional Shareholder Solutions (ISS) and Sands Capital, where he specialized in analyzing equity markets and advising on high-profile corporate events for major clients.

title: P&G social media post featuring plus-size model makes waves
summary: A social media post by Procter & Gamble featuring a plus-size model for its Venus razors sparked thousands of responses, including critical ones. Although the model, Anna O’Brien, was not paid for the endorsement, P&G requested to share her photo on the brand's Twitter account. The post generated significant engagement and discussion online.

title: Big Firms Can't Innovate: How P&G Ventures Is Dispelling The Myth
summary: This article discusses how P&G Ventures, a new division within Procter and Gamble, is challenging the notion that large corporations cannot innovate. Leigh Radford, VP and GM of P&G Ventures, explains how the initiative operates like a startup studio to create new brands and businesses, focusing on direct-to-consumer models and fostering a lean, agile environment within the large company structure. The division aims to solve consumer problems in categories new to P&G and adapt to the changing landscape of brand discovery.

title: Why Coty Stock Lost 67% Last Year
summary: Coty's stock dropped 67% last year due to struggles absorbing the Cover Girl acquisition, executive upheaval, and weaker-than-expected guidance from supply-chain disruptions. Despite some short-lived gains and new leadership appointments, investors lost faith in the company's turnaround potential. The company hopes new CEO Pierre Laubies can execute a turnaround to recoup some losses, with new leadership aiming to shore up pain points.

title: Wisconsin carrier recognized by Procter & Gamble
summary: Contract Transport Services (CTS), a Green Bay, Wisconsin-based carrier, received two "Carrier of the Year" awards from Procter & Gamble for Best Customer Service On-Time and Best Tender Service. This recognition highlights CTS's exceptional service, innovation, responsiveness, and strong partnership with P&G, marking the first time the company has earned such honors. CTS President Curt Reitz attributed the awards to the dedication of their drivers and staff who consistently go above and beyond.

title: Procter & Gamble plant in Albany named Manufacturer of Year
summary: The Procter & Gamble plant in Albany was named Georgia's 2019 Manufacturer of the Year in the large manufacturer category by Gov. Brian Kemp. The plant, which employs over 500 people and has been in the community for more than 45 years, was recognized for its economic impact, community involvement, corporate responsibility, and commitment to workforce development. P&G's Albany plant produces paper towels and tissue paper, contributes significantly to the local and state economy, and actively participates in community organizations.

title: P&G veteran tapped as president of Ulta Beauty
summary: Dave Kimbell, a former brand manager at Procter & Gamble, has been appointed president of Ulta Beauty Inc., the largest U.S. beauty retailer. This move brings a P&G veteran into a top leadership role at a major beauty company.

title: What Makes A CSR Message Resonate With Millennials And Generation-Z?
summary: This article explores how Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) messages resonate with Millennial and Generation-Z consumers. It highlights that while young consumers expect companies to be socially responsible, authenticity, commitment, and alignment between the company and the cause are crucial for effective CSR campaigns. The piece also notes that many young consumers are price-conscious and may not pay a premium for CSR efforts, though such initiatives can influence brand preference at similar price points.

title: P&G renames Merck Limited as Procter & Gamble Health Ltd
summary: Procter & Gamble has renamed Merck Ltd in India as Procter & Gamble Health Limited, following its global acquisition of Merck KGaA's consumer health business. The name change was approved by the Registrar of Companies, effective May 6th. This move signifies P&G's strategy to leverage its combined expertise and strong brand portfolio in India's growing consumer health market.

title: Misconduct at Kraft Heinz puts spotlight on employee pressure to meet bonus targets
summary: Kraft Heinz announced it will restate its financial statements for 2016 and 2017 by $181 million due to employee misconduct in procurement, resulting in reprimands for about a dozen employees. This incident has raised questions about the company's internal controls and its bonus structure, which heavily ties employee compensation to annual targets. Critics suggest that aggressive cost-cutting targets and rapid promotions of inexperienced staff may have contributed to a culture susceptible to such misconduct.

title: Procter & Gamble Strength is Feeding Gains for 'XLP' ETF
summary: The article discusses how Procter & Gamble's strong performance is significantly contributing to the gains of the Consumer Staples Select SPDR (XLP) ETF. Despite the stock being largely established, its recent growth, including a 40% rise over the past year, has buoyed the ETF, which has a 15% allocation to P&G. Analysts suggest P&G's stock is breaking out above a long-term trendline, indicating a higher trajectory.

title: Living Legacies Series: Meet Paul Sagel, Co-Creator of Crest Whitestrips
summary: Paul Sagel, co-creator of Crest Whitestrips, shares his 26-year journey at P&G, detailing the product's innovative development and profound impact on consumers. He discusses the early challenges, the pivotal moment of pitching the idea to the CTO, and his continued passion for innovation at P&G today. Sagel emphasizes the importance of improving lives through superior products and highlights the rapid pace of modern innovation.

title: Shaving Start-Up Harry’s Will Be Sold to Owner of Schick for $1.37 Billion (Published 2019)
summary: Harry's, a shaving start-up, is being acquired by Edgewell Personal Care, the owner of Schick and Wilkinson razor brands, for approximately $1.37 billion in stock and cash. This deal highlights a trend of established companies purchasing younger, internet-born competitors, similar to Unilever's acquisition of Dollar Shave Club. Post-acquisition, Harry's founders, Andy Katz-Mayfield and Jeff Raider, will manage Edgewell's U.S. operations, aiming to strengthen their position as a distant second to Procter & Gamble's Gillette in the men's shaving market.

title: Shaving upstart Harry's is selling for $1.37 billion to the company that owns Schick razors
summary: Edgewell Personal Care, owner of Schick and Wilkinson razor brands, announced its plan to acquire U.S.-based shaving startup Harry's for $1.37 billion in a cash-and-stock deal. This acquisition aims to expand Edgewell's presence in the rapidly growing U.S. grooming market, with Harry's founders Andy Katz-Mayfield and Jeff Raider joining Edgewell's executive team. The deal makes Harry's the latest shaving startup bought by a larger rival, highlighting the increasing focus on the men's grooming industry.

title: Razor startup Harry’s will be acquired by Edgewell Personal Care for $1.37B
summary: Edgewell Personal Care is set to acquire razor startup Harry's for $1.37 billion, expanding its portfolio of direct-to-consumer brands. Harry's co-founders will become co-presidents of U.S. operations for Edgewell following the acquisition. The deal, which involves 79% cash and 21% stock, is expected to close by the end of the first quarter of 2020.

title: P&G Union center near Dayton airport sold for $93 million
summary: The Procter & Gamble distribution center in Union, Ohio, near the Dayton airport, was sold for over $93 million to ILPT Properties LLC. P&G, which operates as a tenant, stated that the sale will not impact its business operations, lease, or employee numbers. The facility, strategically located for logistics, was acquired from ARCP ID Union OH, with ILPT Properties focusing on e-commerce-driven industrial and logistics real estate.

title: Morgan Stanley upgrades Coca-Cola to overweight: 'Coke is now our top mega-cap staples pick'
summary: Morgan Stanley upgraded Coca-Cola shares to overweight from equal weight, setting a new 12-month price target of $55. The firm believes Coca-Cola is trading at an "unfair discount to peers" given its superior growth outlook, pricing power, and rebounding emerging market trends. Coca-Cola is now Morgan Stanley's top mega-cap staples pick, with analysts raising future EPS estimates.

title: P&G unveils its largest R&D center in the world. It's in Mason, Ohio.
summary: Procter & Gamble has unveiled its new and expanded Mason Business Center, which is now the company's largest research & development center globally. P&G invested $400 million in the expansion, bringing the facility to 2 million square feet and accommodating 2,800 workers, including those from its consolidated Sharon Woods innovation center. This move aims to boost efficiency after years of corporate restructuring and divestitures.

title: What the Harry’s acquisition means for retailers
summary: The acquisition of direct-to-consumer brand Harry's by Edgewell Personal Care highlights a broader trend of consumer product giants buying startups to gain direct customer connections and data. This shift presents both challenges and opportunities for traditional retailers, who must adapt by partnering with niche brands or developing their own private labels to remain competitive against CPGs that are now building their own direct marketing capabilities. While some see this as a defensive move by CPGs, others believe it could streamline operations for retailers by consolidating brand management.

title: Colgate-Palmolive tops Gartner’s 2019 Supply Chain rankings
summary: Colgate-Palmolive has secured the top position in Gartner’s 2019 Supply Chain Top 25 rankings, moving up from fourth place in 2018 due to strong financial performance and focus on corporate social responsibility. Alibaba and Akzo Nobel also made their debut on the shortlist. Unilever joined the "Masters" category after consistently ranking in the top five for seven consecutive years, recognized for its advanced digital supply chain processes and use of emerging technologies.

title: Loop’s ‘waste-free’ e-commerce platform launches with P&G, Kroger, Walgreens on board
summary: Loop, TerraCycle's "circular shopping platform," has launched its e-commerce site with Kroger and Walgreens as founding retail partners. The platform offers multi-use packaging for products from brands like Unilever, Mars, Nestle, PepsiCo, Colgate-Palmolive, and Procter & Gamble, aimed at significantly reducing waste. The pilot program, currently available in limited U.S. and Paris locations, requires a deposit for packaging that is returned, cleaned, refilled, and resold, emphasizing the companies' commitment to testing and scaling sustainable consumer solutions.

title: Intuit Acquires Data Analytics Startup Origami Logic
summary: Intuit Inc. has announced its agreement to acquire Silicon Valley-based data analytics startup Origami Logic Inc. for an undisclosed amount, expected to close in Q4 2019. Founded in 2011, Origami Logic provides market performance analytics to major brands and has raised $64.5 million in total funding. This acquisition aims to enhance Intuit's ability to deliver personalized insights to its customers.

title: How P&G created a ‘ready for anything’ supply chain
summary: Procter & Gamble has transformed its disaster response from reactive to proactive over the last decade by centralizing decision-making and implementing advanced technology. The company now uses Kinaxis's Rapid Response software, which integrates P&G's supply chain data with external information like weather forecasts, allowing for quick scenario planning and pre-emptive adjustments to avoid disruptions. This strategic shift enabled P&G to maintain consistent supply during events like Hurricane Harvey, when competitors struggled.

title: Building a Simple, Low Cost Indexed ETF Portfolio in USD
summary: This article discusses the advantages of building a low-cost, indexed ETF portfolio using USD-denominated ETFs, primarily to reduce withholding taxes in registered accounts like RRSPs. It explains the concept of withholding taxes on ETFs, strategies to efficiently convert CAD to USD using Norbert's Gambit, and outlines several USD ETF portfolio options with significantly lower total MERs compared to their CAD counterparts. The author emphasizes the potential savings, especially for larger portfolios, despite the initial effort involved in currency conversion and managing US-listed ETFs.

title: Former P&G vice president tapped as managing partner by private equity firm
summary: Luigi Feola, a 21-year veteran and former general manager for global luxury brands at Procter & Gamble, has been appointed as a managing partner for the world's largest consumer-focused private equity firm. This move signifies a significant career transition for Feola from a major consumer goods corporation to a leadership role in private equity.

title: 3M Deconsolidates Venezuelan Subsidiary
summary: 3M has deconsolidated its Venezuelan subsidiary, citing an "unstable environment and heightened unrest" and expecting a $160 million charge in the second quarter, although the move is not expected to cause economic impact to 3M. This follows similar actions by other Minnesota companies like Ecolab and major corporations such as Colgate-Palmolive and PepsiCo due to Venezuela's unstable economic conditions.

title: Vans Owner VF Corp. Taps Tmall to Bolster China Offering
summary: VF Corp., parent company of brands like Vans, The North Face, and Timberland, is expanding its collaboration with Alibaba's Tmall to enhance its reach and sales to Chinese consumers. Tmall will utilize data-driven initiatives to help VF Corp. target buyers, identify growth opportunities, and tailor products for the Chinese market. This partnership builds on previous successful collaborations, including product launches informed by the Tmall Innovation Center.

title: P&G and Tokyo 2020 create first-ever medal podiums made entirely of recycled plastic for upcoming Olympic Games
summary: P&G and Tokyo 2020 are collaborating to create the first-ever Olympic medal podiums made entirely from recycled plastic for the upcoming Olympic Games. This initiative involves collecting plastic from the public and oceans, contributing to sustainability goals and raising awareness about plastic waste. The project aligns with broader Olympic Movement efforts to embed sustainability principles and highlights how the Games can inspire environmental action.

title: Former PepsiCo CIO Robert Dixon Named To The Okta Board of Directors
summary: Okta, Inc. has announced the appointment of Robert Dixon, former Senior Vice President and Global CIO of PepsiCo, Inc., to its board of directors, effective June 14. Dixon brings extensive experience from PepsiCo and Procter & Gamble, as well as current board positions with Anthem, Inc. and Build-A-Bear Workshop, Inc. His expertise in digital transformation and IT infrastructure is expected to provide invaluable insight for Okta's vision of enabling organizations to leverage technology effectively.

title: Alibaba and JD.Com to Combine Facial Recognition With Data in Bid for Merchant Loyalty
summary: Alibaba and JD.com are integrating facial recognition and deep customer data to enhance merchant loyalty and diversify revenue streams amidst slowing e-commerce growth in China. This "new retail" approach offers personalized marketing and operational efficiencies, benefiting brands like Bestore and Nestle, while raising questions about data management and retailer dependency.

title: Estée Lauder CEO Fabrizio Freda on Makeup Trends and Chinese Millennials
summary: Estée Lauder CEO Fabrizio Freda discusses the company's strategy for growth in emerging markets, particularly China, and how they navigate trade conflicts. He highlights the differences in spending habits and attitudes between Chinese and U.S. millennials, emphasizing the importance of "glocal" strategies and continuous transformation to capture opportunities in a volatile market. Freda also touches on the company's acquisition strategy and the emerging trend of personalization in the beauty industry.

title: Howard Hughes Corp hires Centerview Partners to explore alternatives, including a sale: Sources
summary: Howard Hughes Corp. has hired Centerview Partners to explore strategic alternatives, including a potential sale of the company, due to its struggling stock performance over the past three years. Chairman Bill Ackman supports the review, which also includes exploring joint ventures or spinoffs, with the goal of completion by the end of summer. The company later confirmed the strategic review, leading to a significant jump in its shares.

title: Goldman upgrades Procter & Gamble, predicting a 'double-digit' return
summary: Goldman Sachs upgraded Procter & Gamble to "buy" from "neutral," predicting a potential "double-digit return" for shareholders. The firm raised its target price to $125 from $114, citing P&G's benefit from accelerated end-market growth and an expected increase in organic volume and profit dollar growth. Despite past concerns about growth and trade war effects, P&G shares were up, continuing a yearly trend of over 20% growth.

title: Procter & Gamble launches hair care line for black women
summary: Procter & Gamble's My Black is Beautiful platform has launched a new hair care line specifically for Black women, available exclusively at Sally Beauty stores and online. The line, inspired by an online community of 2.6 million women, was developed in partnership with Sally Beauty and P&G's technical expertise in textured hair. It includes shampoo, conditioner, conditioning creams, and an intense recovery treatment designed to nourish, moisturize, and renew curly hair.

title: Milacron acquired by another local public company for $2B
summary: Milacron Holdings Corp., a Cincinnati-based public company, announced its acquisition for $2 billion by another Greater Cincinnati public company. Tom Goeke is the CEO of Milacron, which is a plastics processing company based in Blue Ash. This significant transaction involves two local public entities.

title: Donald Knauss, Richard Smucker Honored by Grocery Manufacturers Assoc.
summary: Donald Knauss and Richard Smucker are being honored with the 2019 Hall of Achievement Award by the Grocery Manufacturers Association (GMA) for their significant contributions to the consumer packaged goods industry. Knauss previously served as chair and CEO of The Clorox Company, while Smucker was the CEO and co-CEO of The J.M. Smucker Company. The award will be presented at GMA’s annual Leadership Forum on August 15th.

title: The potential of polypropylene
summary: The article explores the growing potential for recycling polypropylene (PP), driven by technological advancements, increased demand from global brands for recycled materials, and heightened consumer awareness of plastic waste. Companies like Envision Plastics, St. Joseph Plastics, and PureCycle Technologies are spearheading efforts to innovate PP recycling processes and expand the market for postconsumer recycled (PCR) PP. Despite challenges in collection, standardization, and pricing, reprocessors see significant future growth, with PureCycle Technologies notably preselling its recycled PP output for the next two decades.

title: Procter & Gamble Class Action Says Costco Rebates Aren’t Delivered
summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Procter & Gamble (P&G) alleging that the company failed to deliver $25 rebates promised to consumers who purchased $100 worth of P&G products at Costco. The plaintiff claims P&G did not fulfill its obligations, stating the program ended and directing inquiries to Costco, despite consumers meeting the promotion's terms. The lawsuit alleges breach of contract, violation of consumer sales practices acts, and unjust enrichment, seeking redress for all U.S. persons who participated and did not receive their rebate.

title: P&G up to 1,100 employees — and growing
summary: Procter & Gamble's Tabler Station plant in Berkeley County, W.Va., now employs about 1,100 people and aims to fill 275 more positions. The plant, which produces products like Dawn and Swiffer, expects all operations to be functional by the end of 2020. This expansion is part of P&G's broader North American supply chain transformation, involving over $500 million in investment.

title: Procter & Gamble continues growth streak with year-end results
summary: Procter & Gamble reported strong year-end results, exceeding analyst expectations with its best sales-growth numbers in over a decade. Despite an $8 billion accounting charge related to the Gillette brand's declining value, the company reported core earnings per share of $1.10 and 7 percent organic sales growth. P&G attributes its resurgence to a 2014 strategy of divesting brands and investing in premium products.

title: P&G Posts Strong Sales Even as It Raises Prices
summary: Procter & Gamble reported its highest quarterly sales growth in over a decade, driven by strong consumer spending on household staples despite price increases. However, the company also incurred an $8 billion charge to write down the value of its Gillette razor business, highlighting challenges faced by big brands from changing consumer habits and new online competitors. P&G's shares rose following the strong sales report.

title: P&G posts strong sales, takes $8 billion Gillette writedown
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) reported strong quarterly revenue and adjusted profit, beating Wall Street expectations, despite taking an $8 billion non-cash writedown on its Gillette shaving business. The writedown is attributed to currency fluctuations, increased competition, and a shrinking market for razors as consumers shave less frequently. P&G's shares rose significantly after the strong earnings report, driven by organic sales growth across its beauty and fabric/home care units.

title: Procter & Gamble shares jump on earnings beat, optimistic 2020 outlook despite Gillette write-down
summary: Procter & Gamble reported stronger-than-expected fourth-quarter earnings and revenue, leading to a jump in share price, despite an $8 billion write-down of its Gillette brand. The company offered an optimistic forecast for fiscal 2020, projecting revenue growth of 3% to 4% and adjusted EPS growth of 4% to 9%. This performance was driven by strong organic sales growth, particularly in health care and fabric/home care segments, and strategic price increases.

title: P&G posts strong sales, takes $8 bln Gillette writedown
summary: Procter & Gamble Co. reported strong quarterly revenue and adjusted profit, beating Wall Street expectations and sending shares to a record high. Despite the positive performance, the company took an $8 billion non-cash writedown on its Gillette shaving business due to currency fluctuations, increased competition, and a shrinking market for razors as consumers shave less frequently. The writedown primarily reflects challenges in the grooming segment, while other categories like beauty and home care showed significant organic sales growth.

title: Report: Chipotle, Sweetgreen bowls contain cancer-linked ‘forever chemicals’
summary: A report from The New Food Economy found that molded fiber bowls from restaurants like Chipotle and Sweetgreen contain cancer-linked "forever chemicals" called PFAS. While the levels don't exceed FDA thresholds and no immediate health threat is suggested for consumers, these chemicals do not biodegrade and can accumulate in the environment and potentially migrate into food. This raises concerns for environmental sustainability and long-term health, despite these bowls often being advertised as compostable.

title: 'Icon' Procter & Gamble celebrates 50 years in Cenla
summary: Procter & Gamble's Pineville plant is celebrating 50 years of operation, evolving from 150 employees making dry laundry detergent to approximately 600 employees producing a diverse range of products with a payroll of over $60 million. The plant is considered an economic icon in Central Louisiana, not only for its direct employment and payroll but also for its ripple effect on local infrastructure, supporting ancillary businesses, and community involvement. Local leaders credit P&G with driving significant economic growth and providing stable, well-paying jobs, making it a critical fixture in the region.

title: Hasbro will phase out plastics from packaging — but not toys
summary: Hasbro Inc. announced plans to phase out plastic from its product packaging, including elastic bands and shrink wrap, starting in 2020 with a goal to virtually eliminate plastic from new product packaging by the end of 2022. While this initiative addresses consumer backlash against single-use plastics in packaging, the company has not yet committed to reducing plastic usage in the toys themselves. Chief Operating Officer John Frascotti indicated that plans for more sustainable materials in toys would be announced soon, though some packaging, like for Easy Bake Oven ingredients, will retain plastic due to health and regulatory requirements.

title: P&G executives: Best still to come at Alexandria plant
summary: Procter & Gamble executives, including CEO David Taylor, visited their Pineville plant to celebrate its 50th anniversary. They expressed strong optimism for the plant's future growth and its critical role in the company's North American fabric care business, despite its already significant achievements. The facility, which started producing dry laundry detergent in 1969, now employs about 600 people and has expanded its product offerings to include Tide Pods.

title: Procter & Gamble celebrates 50 years at Alexandria plant
summary: The Procter & Gamble plant in Alexandria, Louisiana, celebrated its 50th anniversary, recognized by CEO David Taylor as a "world-class manufacturing facility." The plant plays a vital role in producing laundry products for a third of the U.S. and is an economic engine and community pillar, according to Pineville Mayor Clarence Fields. The company has invested millions into the facility, promising future growth.

title: Procter & Gamble Stock: What’s behind Its Solid Return?
summary: The article discusses Procter & Gamble's strong stock performance, highlighting a 29.7% year-to-date return driven by robust organic sales, share buybacks, and a healthy dividend yield. It attributes this success to consistent growth in organic sales, impressive profit margins, and a focus on premium innovation, even as other consumer staples like Kimberly-Clark, Colgate-Palmolive, and Church & Dwight also show solid returns. The outlook for P&G remains positive, with continued organic sales growth and margin expansion expected to support the stock.

title: 3M’s chief sustainability officer, Gayle Schueller, on how her company is embracing the circular economy
summary: Gayle Schueller, 3M’s chief sustainability officer, discusses the company's commitment to waste prevention, recycling, and overall environmental sustainability. 3M aims to integrate sustainability into its product development to reduce environmental impact and avoid past mistakes related to chemical persistence. The company's efforts include using recycled materials in products like Scotch-Brite sponges and Thinsulate insulation, and developing smog-reducing roofing granules.

title: Oral Care: Comparative Market Share Analysis, Know Who’s
summary: This press release announces a new research study by HTF MI providing a comprehensive analysis of the Global and China Oral Care Market. The study covers historical progress, ongoing market scenarios, future prospects, and detailed data on leading companies, products, strategies, and market shares. It also examines market dynamics, key growth drivers, challenges, and regional segmentation with a forecast up to 2025.

title: Church & Dwight: An Example of the American Valuation Premium
summary: This article examines the high valuation of U.S. consumer staple stocks, using Church & Dwight (CHD) as a prime example, and compares them to their European counterparts like Unilever, noting an "S&P 500 index premium" in the U.S. Despite Church & Dwight's strong brand portfolio and historical outperformance, the author expresses caution due to its current elevated valuation metrics relative to historical averages and discusses potential forward return scenarios. The article suggests that while consumer staples are defensive, their current valuations are stretched, leading the author to keep CHD on a watchlist rather than investing new money.

title: PureCycle, Aptar partner to produce recycled polypropylene resin
summary: AptarGroup has partnered with PureCycle Technologies LLC to introduce PureCycle's Ultra-Pure Recycled Polypropylene (UPRP) into dispensing applications. PureCycle's process transforms plastic feedstock into UPRP resin with virgin-like properties, closing the loop in plastics reuse and making recycled plastics more accessible. Aptar will collaborate with PureCycle on the transformation process and prepare for food-grade requirements in Europe, while PureCycle plans to build its first plant in Ohio to produce 100 million pounds of UPRP per year starting in 2021.

title: P&G: Consumer giant's ads are getting political. Will that draw backlash?
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) has increasingly incorporated socially-conscious messages into its advertising, a strategy some critics argue politicizes its products. While P&G states this approach aligns with evolving consumer expectations for brands to "stand for something," it has also faced backlash, particularly for ads like Gillette's "toxic masculinity" campaign, raising questions about whether such marketing risks alienating consumers. The company, however, maintains that its focus on "equality" is a winning formula, with executives noting increased brand affinity and long-term loyalty among consumers who appreciate a company's values.

title: 79 jobs expected to shift at P&G facilities under new subcontractor
summary: 79 jobs associated with facilities support at Procter & Gamble (P&G) locations in Southwest Ohio are expected to shift as Eurest Services' contract with Jones Lang LaSalle (JLL) ends. While local entities were informed of a "plant closing," Eurest clarifies it is not closing facilities or eliminating jobs, but rather transitioning contracts. Personnel will either be retained by Eurest and repositioned or transitioned to the new support services contractor.

title: Going Beyond the Tampon, Big Brands Try New Ideas
summary: Major feminine-care brands like Kimberly-Clark and P&G are investing in innovative alternatives to traditional tampons and pads, driven by consumer demand for sustainable and chemical-minimizing products. Kimberly-Clark has invested $25 million in Thinx, a maker of reusable "period proof underwear," while P&G launched a Tampax menstrual cup. This signals a shift in a market that has seen little change for over half a century, addressing a growing interest in new feminine hygiene solutions.

title: Former P&G executive to help guide big data firm
