This recognition highlights companies that voluntarily participate in the Safer Choice program, investing in research and reformulation to ensure their products meet stringent safety and environmental criteria. The program evaluates ingredients, product performance, packaging, pH, and VOCs to identify products safer for human health and the environment.

title: Orlando Magic Advance Sustainability Efforts with PureCycle's PureZero™ Program
summary: The Orlando Magic is partnering with PureCycle Technologies to launch the PureZero™ waste program, becoming the first NBA team to implement this initiative. The program aims to divert thousands of pieces of plastic waste from landfills and waterways by using PureCycle's technology to recycle No. 5 plastic (polypropylene) from stadium concessions into ultra-pure recycled plastic. This partnership underscores the Magic's commitment to sustainability and circular recycling within their home arena, the Amway Center.

title: Popular Dry Shampoos Found to Have Cancer-CausinTg Chemical
summary: An independent study by Valisure found that 70% of 148 batches from 34 brands of spray-on dry shampoo contained high levels of benzene, a known carcinogen. Brands like Not Your Mother's, Batiste, Sun Bum, and John Paul Mitchell Systems were identified, some with significantly higher benzene levels than previously found in other personal-care products. Valisure has filed a petition with the FDA requesting a recall of these products, highlighting concerns about the complexity of the supply chain and the regulation of cosmetics.

title: P&G to offset rising costs with price increases, productivity initiatives
summary: Procter & Gamble plans to counter rising freight and commodity costs with price increases and new productivity initiatives. The company has already implemented a second round of price hikes and is focusing on optimizing its supply chain through its "Supply Chain 3.0" initiative, which will likely involve enhanced automation and digital capabilities. P&G expects a $3.9 billion after-tax headwind from commodities and logistics in fiscal year 2023.

title: Aspen Aerogels Appoints Katie Kool to Board
summary: Aspen Aerogels, Inc. (NYSE: ASPN), a technology leader in sustainability and electrification solutions, announced the appointment of Katie Kool to its Board of Directors, where she will also serve on the Audit Committee and the Nominating, Governance and Sustainability Committee. Kool previously served as CEO of Tide Cleaners and held various executive leadership roles at Procter & Gamble. Her appointment is expected to bring significant business and financial acumen to Aspen Aerogels, as the company also announced the departure of Robert M. Gervis from the Board.

title: Why Apple raised the price of the iPhone, but not in the U.S. and China
summary: Apple increased the price of its iPhone 14 series for many international buyers due to the strong U.S. dollar and currency headwinds, which significantly impacted the company's revenue growth. CEO Tim Cook noted that foreign exchange headwinds were over 600 basis points last quarter, preventing double-digit revenue growth. While the U.S. and China avoided price hikes, consumers in markets like the U.K., Japan, Germany, and Australia saw significant increases, a strategy Apple previous reversed in 2019 due to declining sales, though they report no such drop-off this time.

title: CCP Dismisses Colgate Palmolive’s Complaint Against P&G’s Safeguard TV Commercial
summary: The Competition Commission of Pakistan (CCP) has dismissed a complaint filed by Colgate Palmolive (CP) against Procter & Gamble (P&G) regarding a Safeguard TV commercial. CP alleged that P&G's advertisement was deceptive, claiming Safeguard Liquid Hand Soap offered superior germ protection compared to ordinary soap, which CP argued was misleading as handwashing with any soap is effective. The CCP inquiry found that P&G had a reasonable basis for its claims about Safeguard's unique germ-inhibiting properties.

title: Better Buy: Procter & Gamble vs. Kimberly-Clark
summary: This article compares Procter & Gamble (PG) and Kimberly-Clark (KMB) stocks, highlighting their sales momentum, profitability, and valuation. P&G demonstrates stronger sales growth and higher operating margins, while Kimberly-Clark offers a higher dividend yield and lower valuation. The author concludes that P&G is the better buy due to its superior performance and ability to weather economic downturns.

title: Jennifer Garner Has The Best-Kept Secret For Getting Kids To Eat Their Veggies
summary: Jennifer Garner shares her secrets for encouraging kids to eat vegetables, emphasizing gardening, making fresh produce available for snacking, and introducing diverse flavors early in life. She also discusses her children's food brand, Once Upon A Farm, which provides organic, non-GMO baby food and snacks, and its partnership with Save The Children to combat food insecurity. Garner highlights the importance of providing proper nutrition to children across the nation.

title: P&G execs earned $87 million from stock in fiscal year 2022 - Cincinnati Business Courier
summary: Procter & Gamble's top executives collectively earned over $87 million from stock sales in the fiscal year that recently concluded. This total includes profits derived from both stock options and direct stock sales. The article is a brief overview from the Cincinnati Business Courier.

title: Eastman to provide PepsiCo with recycled PET
summary: Eastman has secured an offtake agreement with PepsiCo to supply processed PET from its third planned chemical recycling facility in the U.S. This facility, expected to be operational by the end of 2026, will have an input capacity of 160,000 tonnes/year of hard-to-recycle PET waste. The agreement is a significant step for Eastman's circular economy initiatives, with other similar facilities in Tennessee and France also underway.

title: Procter & Gamble, Airbnb, other larger advertisers, see marketing opportunity amid inflation pricing
summary: Amid economic instability and inflation, major advertisers like Procter & Gamble, Airbnb, and PepsiCo are viewing marketing as a strategic investment rather than a cost. They are shifting ad spending towards more targeted digital platforms and brand advertising to justify price increases to consumers and drive growth, rather than cutting budgets. This approach aims to maintain brand recognition and capitalize on consumers' expectation of higher prices to achieve long-term margin uplift and efficient growth.

title: Procter & Gamble unveils plans for $500 million manufacturing facility in Arizona
summary: Procter & Gamble Co. (PG) plans to invest $500 million in building a new manufacturing facility in Arizona. The plant will be located on more than 400 acres, approximately an hour from Phoenix. This move comes after a year-long search for a suitable site for the consumer goods giant.

title: Colgate-Palmolive Co. stock underperforms Friday when compared to competitors
summary: Colgate-Palmolive Co. (CL) stock underperformed on Friday, November 11, 2022, slipping 0.53% to $74.57 despite an overall positive day for the stock market. The company closed significantly below its 52-week high and showed mixed performance compared to competitors like Procter & Gamble Co. (PG), Unilever PLC ADR (UL), and Reckitt Benckiser Group PLC (RBGPF). Trading volume was also below its 50-day average.

title: Procter & Gamble unveils plans for $500 million manufacturing facility in Arizona
summary: Procter & Gamble Co. (PG) has announced plans to construct a new $500 million manufacturing facility in Arizona. This development was reported by the Cincinnati Business Courier and the Phoenix Business Journal. The Cincinnati-based consumer goods giant is making a significant investment in expanding its manufacturing capabilities.

title: Procter & Gamble picks site to build $500 million manufacturing facility
summary: Procter & Gamble plans to invest $500 million in a new fabric care manufacturing plant in Coolidge, Arizona, spanning over 400 acres. The 2 million square-foot facility will be located within the Inland Port Arizona industrial park and will support P&G's fabric care portfolio, including products like Tide Pods and Downy Unstopables. This investment aims to expand the company's manufacturing capabilities in the region.

title: Procter & Gamble to build $500 million factory for fabric care products in Arizona
summary: Procter & Gamble plans to invest $500 million in building a new factory in Coolidge, Arizona, set to open by 2025. This facility will employ 500 new workers and produce fabric care products like Tide pods, Downy Unstopables, and Bounce dryer sheets. The project aims to serve consumers and customers across the region and bolster Arizona's manufacturing industry.

title: Arizona city gives green light to Procter & Gamble manufacturing plant
summary: The city of Coolidge, Arizona, has approved an initial development agreement for Procter & Gamble's new 2 million-square-foot manufacturing plant. This decision follows an extensive search by P&G across 500 sites in multiple states. The facility is expected to be a significant addition to the area's industrial landscape.

title: [Latest] Global Mosquito Repellent Market Size/Share Worth USD 10.3 Billion by 2030 at a 7% CAGR: Custom Market Insights (Analysis, Outlook, Leaders, Report, Trends, Forecast, Segmentation, Growth, Growth Rate, Value, Analysis, Outlook)
summary: The global mosquito repellent market, valued at USD 5.1 billion in 2021, is projected to reach USD 10.3 billion by 2030, growing at a CAGR of 7%. This growth is driven by factors like increased urbanization, rising e-commerce penetration, and growing awareness of mosquito-borne diseases, particularly in the Asia-Pacific region, which is expected to hold the largest market share. Sprays and offline distribution channels currently dominate, though online sales are rapidly expanding.

title: [Latest] Global Mosquito Repellent Market Size/Share Worth USD 10.3 Billion by 2030 at a 7% CAGR: Custom Market Insights (Analysis, Outlook, Leaders, Report, Trends, Forecast, Segmentation, Growth, Growth Rate, Value, Analysis, Outlook)
summary: The global mosquito repellent market is projected to reach USD 10.3 billion by 2030, growing at a CAGR of 7% from its 2021 valuation of USD 5.1 billion. This growth is driven by increased urbanization, e-commerce adoption, rising awareness of natural products, and outdoor activities. The Asia-Pacific region is expected to dominate the market due to its large population, increasing disposable income, and government initiatives against mosquito-borne diseases.

title: The Tom Ford acquisition is all about fragrance
summary: The article details Estée Lauder's acquisition of Tom Ford for $2.3 billion, highlighting that the primary driver for the deal is Tom Ford's highly successful fragrance business, which makes up a significant portion of its beauty sales. Estée Lauder plans to outsource Tom Ford's fashion and accessories lines while focusing on expanding the beauty segment, particularly in emerging markets like China and the Middle East, despite recent sales dips in Asia for Estée Lauder. The acquisition is seen as a strategic move to secure a fast-growing brand and save on royalties.

title: P&G Holds 2022 Investor Day
summary: P&G held its 2022 Investor Day on November 17, where executives reviewed the company's integrated business strategy and its strengthening through four focus areas. Chairman, President, and CEO Jon Moeller outlined how strategic choices drive balanced growth and value creation, focusing on a robust portfolio, superiority in products, productivity, constructive disruption, and an efficient organizational structure. The company also announced four areas of increased intentionality: supply chain excellence, environmental sustainability, digital acumen, and a superior employee value equation.

title: Procter and Gamble fined nearly $35K after worker death at North Carolina facility
summary: Procter and Gamble (P&G) has been fined $34,502 by the North Carolina Department of Labor for three serious safety violations following the death of an employee at its Guilford County facility in May. The worker was fatally struck and pinned by equipment which is alleged to have been unsecured. P&G has 15 working days to respond to the citations.

title: Worker crushed to death by 3,000-pound container, NC officials say. Now company cited
summary: Procter & Gamble is facing a $34,000 fine for "serious" safety violations after a 49-year-old worker, Montrell Rudd, was crushed to death by a 3,000-pound container in their Browns Summit facility. The North Carolina Department of Labor cited the manufacturer for three violations, including failing to secure the container and operating the lift truck unsafely. P&G has requested an informal conference regarding the citations.

title: Coty Inc. Cl A stock rises Tuesday, still underperforms market
summary: Coty Inc. Cl A (COTY) stock increased by 1.20% on Tuesday, closing at $7.59, yet it still underperformed the broader market, which saw the S&P 500 Index and Dow Jones Industrial Average rise by 1.36% and 1.18% respectively. The stock remained $3.23 below its 52-week high. Competitor stocks such as Procter & Gamble Co., Estee Lauder Cos. Cl A, and Inter Parfums Inc. also saw gains on the same day.

title: Innovation Series: Behind P&G’s Bounty
summary: This article details the innovation behind Procter & Gamble's Bounty paper towels, focusing on Senior Inventor Paul Trokhan. Trokhan developed a secret technology in 1982 that gave Bounty its superior absorbency, strength, and softness, and his work resulted in nearly 250 patents. He retired in 2022, 40 years after his key Bounty invention, and believes the technology will continue to be successful for many more years.

title: Church & Dwight Co. stock rises Wednesday, outperforms market
summary: Church & Dwight Co. (CHD) stock increased by 0.61% to $78.57 on Wednesday, outperforming the broader market indexes like the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average. This marked the stock's fourth consecutive day of gains, although it remained below its 52-week high. The company's performance was mixed when compared to competitors like Johnson & Johnson, Procter & Gamble Co., and Reckitt Benckiser Group PLC.

title: P&G Says They Will Not Rely on Acquisitions to Drive Growth
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) CEO Jon Moeller stated the company will not rely on acquisitions for growth, prioritizing organic growth due to high financing costs and seller expectations. However, P&G remains open to substantive acquisitions in the beauty and personal care sector, where it currently lacks dominance. This strategy follows previous portfolio downsizing and recent targeted acquisitions in prestige beauty, focusing on daily use and efficacy.

title: Clorox Co. stock underperforms Tuesday when compared to competitors
summary: Shares of Clorox Co. (CLX) fell 1.07% on Tuesday, closing at $147.43, marking its second consecutive day of losses. This underperformance occurred on a mixed trading day, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average rising slightly and the S&P 500 Index decreasing. The stock also lagged behind competitor Procter & Gamble Co. (PG) and closed significantly below its 52-week high.

title: Kimberly-Clark Corp. stock falls Tuesday, still outperforms market
summary: Kimberly-Clark Corp. (KMB) stock fell 0.11% on Tuesday, closing at $133.16, marking its second consecutive day of losses. Despite the decline, the stock still outperformed the broader market, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average rising slightly and the S&P 500 Index falling. Kimberly-Clark also outperformed competitors Johnson & Johnson and Procter & Gamble Co., which saw larger percentage drops.

title: P&G’s Forest Degradation Claim Warrants SEC Scrutiny
summary: The NRDC has filed a complaint with the SEC regarding Procter & Gamble's claims about forest degradation in its supply chains, arguing that P&G's statements are misleading to investors. Despite a 2020 shareholder vote urging P&G to address deforestation, the company's disclosures indicate continued sourcing from primary forests and reliance on inadequate third-party certifications. The NRDC recommends the SEC investigate these claims, require corrections, and consider enforcement action to protect investors and uphold sustainability standards.

title: Environmentalists ask SEC to examine P&G's wood pulp supply chain claims
summary: An international environment advocacy group, the Natural Resources Defense Council (NRDC), has asked the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to investigate Procter & Gamble Co.'s claims about its wood pulp supply chain. The NRDC alleges that P&G's statements regarding forest preservation are misleading to investors, as the company sources from pristine forests and caribou habitats to produce products like Charmin and Bounty. The group is pushing for SEC enforcement action or updated statements from P&G, citing concerns about investor perceptions and the company's reliance on third-party certifications.

title: Yusen Logistics Receives "Best Business Partner Award" from Procter & Gamble at 2022 Logistics Award
summary: Yusen Logistics Brazil has been honored with the "Best Business Partner Award" by Procter & Gamble at the 2022 Logistics Award. This recognition highlights Yusen Logistics' collaboration and understanding of P&G's needs, particularly for their operations in Manaus, Brazil, and their expansion into new international road routes. The award acknowledges their services in storage, production, and international freight forwarding for P&G since 2014.

title: Procter & Gamble elevates Bala Purushothaman to Global CHRO
summary: Procter & Gamble has appointed Bala Purushothaman as its Chief Human Resource Officer (CHRO), effective January 1, 2023. He will succeed Tracey Grabowski, who is retiring after over three decades with the company. Purushothaman, who started his career with P&G India in 1992, becomes the fourth Indian to join the company's global leadership team in recent years.

title: Huge Demand for Women's Razor Globally. Annual Sales to Reach $5 Billion by 2028. Gillette, BIC, Edgewell and Harry's Well Positioned to Capitalize a Billion Dollar Opportunity - Arizton
summary: The global women's razor market is projected to reach $5.28 billion by 2028, growing at a CAGR of 4.85% from 2023-2028, driven by product innovations, the rise of facial razors, and the genderless movement. Key players like Gillette, Edgewell, BIC, and Harry's are well-positioned to capitalize on this growth, which is also influenced by increasing online distribution and the development of eco-friendly and gender-neutral products. Cartridge razors currently hold the largest market share, and vendors are focusing on unique designs with improved functionality and sustainability.

title: P&G to pay $8 million to settle class-action lawsuit over benzene in Old Spice, Secret deodorant products
summary: Procter & Gamble has agreed to pay up to $8 million to settle a class-action lawsuit regarding the presence of benzene in some of its Old Spice and Secret deodorant products. The Cincinnati-based company is resolving claims stemming from concerns over the chemical contaminant found in these personal care items. This settlement marks a significant development in the legal proceedings against the consumer goods giant.

title: Executives from eBay and Golden State Foods Join GS1 US Board of Governors
summary: GS1 US has elected Scott Gaffney from eBay and Brian Dick from Golden State Foods to its Board of Governors. These industry leaders will help guide GS1 US's strategy to enhance supply chain efficiency and visibility across various sectors, supporting members with digital transformation and demand planning. Their expertise is expected to be instrumental in optimizing supply chains to meet consumer needs.

title: P&G Pays Out $8 M in Benzene Settlement
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) will pay $8 million to settle claims that its aerosol products contained benzene, a known carcinogen. This settlement follows a November 2021 recall and several class-action lawsuits, benefiting consumers who purchased specific P&G aerosol antiperspirant, deodorant, body spray, dry shampoo, or dry conditioner products between November 4, 2015, and December 31, 2021. The FDA classifies benzene as a human carcinogen, with exposure potentially leading to increased risks of cancers and blood disorders.

title: Doing the Right Thing: A Business Built on Trust
summary: P&G employees celebrate their heritage and commitment to their Purpose, Values, and Principles (PVPs) during their annual "Do the Right Thing Celebration." This tradition dates back to 1887, when the company gained a reputation for quality products and ethical practices. The PVPs serve as the foundation for P&G's culture, guiding daily decisions and ensuring the company's enduring values are passed down through generations.

title: The 2022 Beauty Inc Awards: Retailers of the Year
summary: The 2022 Beauty Inc Awards recognized Walmart as Retailer of the Year for Mass and Ulta Beauty as Retailer of the Year for Specialty. Walmart was lauded for its strategic initiatives, including a partnership with Space NK and new brand launches targeting Gen Z. Ulta Beauty continued its strong growth, driven by its appeal to Gen Z consumers and successful launch of popular beauty brands.

title: Teamsters Protest at Procter & Gamble Headquarters, Call on Company to Demand Supplier Monosol End Forced Labor
summary: Members of Teamsters Local 135 protested outside Procter & Gamble (P&G) headquarters, urging the company to compel its supplier MonoSol to cease forced overtime for workers and negotiate a fair contract. MonoSol, which supplies water-soluble packaging to P&G, recently locked out nearly 200 Teamsters after they rejected a contract offer and authorized a strike. The Teamsters are highlighting P&G's Responsible Sourcing Policy and MonoSol's commitment to the UN Global Compact, both of which prohibit forced labor and uphold workers' rights.

title: American Express Elects Deborah P. Majoras to its Board of Directors
summary: American Express Company announced that Deborah Platt Majoras has been elected to its Board of Directors, effective December 7, 2022. Ms. Majoras previously served as Chief Legal Officer and Corporate Secretary of Procter & Gamble Co. for 12 years and was Chair of the Federal Trade Commission from 2004 to 2008. Stephen J. Squeri, Chairman and CEO of American Express, highlighted her extensive legal, regulatory, and public policy experience as a significant asset to the Board.

title: Sandler receives P&G award
summary: For the second consecutive year, nonwovens producer Sandler has been honored with Procter & Gamble’s External Partner of the Year Award, specifically in the feminine hygiene products division. Sandler was one of just 11 companies chosen from approximately 50,000 P&G suppliers. The company also received the External Business Partner Excellence Award in the baby care category, reinforcing its reputation for new products, quality, and flexible service.

title: P&G Doubles Down on Digital Capacity and Shelf Orchestration With Supply Chain 3.0
summary: Procter & Gamble is heavily investing in its Supply Chain 3.0 strategy, leveraging emerging technologies and advanced algorithms to drive productivity, cost effectiveness, and market growth. This digital transformation includes partnerships with companies like Microsoft for a digital platform utilizing IoT, AI, machine learning, and edge computing to enhance visibility and real-time decision-making across its manufacturing sites globally. P&G is also applying these advancements to optimize shelf orchestration based on point-of-sale data and shopper behavior, aiming to improve on-shelf availability and the overall shopping experience.

title: Kathi Seifert
summary: Kathi Seifert, a retired executive vice president from Kimberly-Clark Corp., continues to be a significant influencer in and out of Wisconsin. She has held numerous board positions across various companies and nonprofits, and prior to her 2004 retirement, led global branding, product positioning, R&D, and capital investment for Kimberly-Clark's personal care products. Seifert has been recognized by Fortune and Forbes magazines as a top woman executive.

title: Del Monte Foods Appoints Jim Caltabiano as Chief Financial Officer
summary: Del Monte Foods, Inc. has announced the appointment of Jim Caltabiano as its new Chief Financial Officer (CFO). Caltabiano brings nearly 30 years of experience from major consumer packaged goods companies, including Ajinomoto Foods and Campbell Soup Company. He will be responsible for overseeing Del Monte Foods' financial organization and will report to Chief Operations Officer, Parag Sachdeva.

title: Newell nabs new CFO, shuffles C-suite
summary: Newell Brands announced that Mark Erceg will become its new CFO, succeeding Chris Peterson, who will transition to president. Erceg, a Procter & Gamble alum, brings extensive financial experience from previous CFO roles at several major companies. This leadership change comes as Newell Brands faces slumping sales and economic uncertainty, with the company focused on aligning its cost structure.

title: Citizenship Report 2022 – Environmental Sustainability
summary: Procter & Gamble's 2022 Citizenship Report details its environmental sustainability efforts under "Ambition 2030," focusing on climate, waste, water, and nature. Key goals include achieving net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2040, designing 100% recyclable or reusable packaging by 2030, restoring more water than consumed in stressed areas, and protecting natural ecosystems. The report outlines progress, significant partnerships, and innovative solutions across its global operations and supply chains.

title: Deborah Majoras, formerly of P&G, joins American Express board of directors
summary: Deborah Majoras, former chief legal officer of Procter & Gamble, has been appointed to the board of directors for American Express. The announcement was made by Meg Erpenbeck of the Cincinnati Business Courier. This marks a new role for Majoras after her long tenure at P&G.

title: Scented candles market 2023-2027, A descriptive analysis of parent market, five forces model, market dynamics, & segmentation- Technavio
summary: The global scented candles market is projected to grow by USD 758.83 million between 2022 and 2027, at a CAGR of 3.46%, according to Technavio. Europe is expected to hold the largest market share, contributing 30% of global growth due to demand during festive seasons and increasing consumer awareness of ingredients. Key drivers include rising investments in household interiors and the expansion of e-commerce, while intense competition from the unorganized sector poses a significant challenge.

title: 3M to stop making hazardous ‘forever chemicals’ starting in 2025
summary: 3M announced it will cease manufacturing all PFAS, known as "forever chemicals," by the end of 2025 due to evolving regulatory and business landscapes, expecting a financial loss of $1.3 billion to $2.3 billion. These chemicals are common in household products and linked to health issues, prompting regulatory efforts and studies on their widespread presence in the environment, food, and human bodies. The decision reflects 3M's move towards sustainable growth and reducing environmental impact.

title: P&G and Cincinnati: How John Smale's legacy lifted both to great heights
summary: John Smale, former CEO of Procter & Gamble, significantly impacted both the company and the city of Cincinnati through his leadership from 1981 to 1990. During his tenure, P&G saw tremendous growth and strategic acquisitions, while Smale also championed the company's community involvement, most notably through the Smale Commission which addressed the city's crumbling infrastructure. His legacy of character, vision, and corporate responsibility continues to be recognized in Cincinnati, symbolized by the John G. and Phyllis W. Smale Riverfront Park.

title: Innovators Series: Meet the Innovator Making Laundry Day Easier
summary: This article introduces Jack English, a P&G Laundry Scientist, who has dedicated 25 years to perfecting laundry product technology. It highlights his work on the new Downy RINSE & REFRESH product, explaining how it enhances odor removal, stain cleaning, and keeps laundry fresh for an extended period. English expresses his passion for his work and helping consumers, while also being involved in community service.

title: Procter & Gamble continues sponsoring Russia’s war with two giant factories
summary: Procter & Gamble continues to operate two large factories in Russia, contributing significantly to the Russian budget through taxes and facilitating employee mobilization for military service, despite international condemnation of Russia's actions in Ukraine. This business activity contradicts P&G's stated ethical policies and supports the Russian economy, which in turn funds the invasion of Ukraine. The article highlights how P&G and other companies' continued presence in Russia undermines efforts to isolate the aggressor state and details the financial contributions made by P&G's operations in Russia.

title: Hasbro toy company taps Chris Cocks as CEO
summary: Hasbro has appointed Chris Cocks, head of its digital gaming division and Wizards of the Coast, as its new CEO, effective February 25. He succeeds interim CEO Rich Stoddart, who will become board chairman. Under Cocks's leadership, Wizards of the Coast's revenue more than doubled, surpassing $1 billion in 2021.

title: Toothbrush Market was Valued USD 6.85 Billion in 2021 and will Reach USD 9.76 Billion by 2029, & it will Grow at CAGR of 4.8%
summary: The global toothbrush market was valued at USD 6.85 billion in 2021 and is projected to reach USD 9.76 billion by 2029, growing at a CAGR of 4.8%. Key drivers include increased oral hygiene awareness, frequent replacement due to whitening focus, and health consciousness, with electric toothbrushes and soft-bristled brushes showing significant growth. Asia-Pacific is a major market due to its large population and demographic trends, while North America also shows considerable growth.

title: What 2023 holds for consumers and household goods
summary: This article by Oksana Sobol of The Clorox Company discusses key consumer trends influencing the household goods market in 2023, following the economic challenges of 2022. It highlights continued consumer caution due to inflation, the elevated role of the home, an expanded definition of health beyond just absence of illness, and sustained momentum for sustainability. The author explains how Clorox's diverse portfolio is well-positioned to meet these evolving consumer needs.

title: Procter & Gamble Acquires Black-Founded, Woman-Led Hair Brand Mielle Organics
summary: Procter & Gamble has announced its acquisition of Mielle Organics, a Black-founded, woman-led hair company, which will join P&G Beauty pending regulatory approval. This acquisition highlights P&G's commitment to economic empowerment for Black and women-owned businesses, a move celebrated by Mielle Organics founder Monique Rodriguez as a significant step for Black entrepreneurs. Alongside the acquisition, P&G has pledged $10 million to Mielle Cares, Mielle Organics' non-profit, to support economic and educational resources in Black and Brown communities.

title: P&G acquires haircare brand Mielle Organics
summary: Procter & Gamble is acquiring textured haircare brand Mielle Organics, pending regulatory approval, to expand access to its products for Black women globally. Mielle will operate as an independent subsidiary of P&G Beauty, retaining its founders, Monique Rodriguez and Melvin Rodriguez, in their leadership roles, and has committed $10 million with P&G to the non-profit Mielle Cares. This acquisition follows P&G's strategy of investing in beauty brands, having spent $1.4 billion on acquisitions in 2022 primarily for skincare and haircare companies.

title: Corium Pharma Solutions Appoints Mark Sirgo as Chief Executive Officer
summary: Corium Pharma Solutions has appointed Dr. Mark Sirgo as its new Chief Executive Officer and a member of its Board of Directors. Dr. Sirgo brings over 35 years of pharmaceutical industry experience, including founding BioDelivery Sciences International and overseeing the development and commercialization of three products. His appointment is expected to drive the company's next phase of growth in transdermal contract development and manufacturing.

title: Male grooming products market: APAC is estimated to account for 30% of the market's growth from 2022 to 2027 - Technavio
summary: The male grooming products market is projected to grow by USD 35.64 billion between 2022 and 2027, with an accelerating CAGR of 8.78%. The Asia-Pacific (APAC) region is expected to contribute 30% to this growth, driven by an increasing number of fashion-conscious consumers. The shave care segment currently holds the largest market share and is anticipated to see significant expansion.

title: President GWR Ron Fleming appointed to Board of Directors of NAWC
summary: Ron Fleming, President and CEO of Global Water Resources, has been elected to the board of directors of the National Association of Water Companies (NAWC). Fleming expressed honor in joining the board to help prioritize high-quality service, rate structures, and public access to safe, reliable water. Global Water Resources has been a NAWC member since July 2020, and Fleming believes his appointment will strengthen the company's efforts in environmental stewardship, water quality improvements, and infrastructure investments.

title: Ulta Beauty Appoints Michelle Crossan-Matos as Chief Marketing Officer
summary: Ulta Beauty has appointed Michelle Crossan-Matos as its new chief marketing officer. In this role, she will be responsible for overseeing various marketing functions including integrated marketing, creative, loyalty programs, and public relations. Crossan-Matos previously held leadership positions at Samsung Electronics America and Procter & Gamble, bringing extensive experience in beauty and personal care to Ulta Beauty.

title: Procter & Gamble revenue and profit fall as company looks to higher prices to offset declining sales
summary: Procter & Gamble (PG) saw its revenue and profit decline in the fiscal second quarter of 2023, as increased prices were not enough to fully offset falling sales volumes and foreign exchange headwinds. All divisions experienced declining sales volume, but organic revenue still rose by 5% due to higher pricing. Despite these challenges, the company slightly increased its sales growth outlook for 2023 to between 4% and 5%, while remaining cautious about the macroeconomic environment.

title: P&G raises sales forecast on price hikes, sees volumes fall
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) increased its full-year sales forecast despite experiencing a 6% drop in sales volumes in its second quarter, primarily due to price hikes. The company plans to continue raising prices to offset high commodity, transportation, and labor costs. While P&G maintains confidence in the U.S. consumer market, it notes slower recovery in China and increased competition from private label brands in Europe.

title: Procter & Gamble Earnings Show Resiliency but Stock Overvalued
summary: Procter & Gamble's fiscal second-quarter 2023 earnings report indicates the company is successfully navigating macroeconomic and competitive challenges, with results largely meeting market expectations. Despite this resiliency and an increase in organic sales growth guidance, Morningstar analysts consider the stock overvalued at its current price compared to their fair value estimate. Investors are advised to await a more attractive entry point, even as P&G demonstrates strength in consumer loyalty amid price increases.

title: P&G looks to replicate $65M success after taking media planning, buying in-house in fabric care
summary: Procter & Gamble's U.S. fabric care brands saved approximately $65 million in advertising costs over a year by bringing media planning and buying in-house. This move involved developing proprietary algorithms for ad placement, increasing ad frequency, and is part of P&G's multi-year strategy to enhance in-house capabilities. The company plans further investment in this approach, aiming for continued productivity gains, despite recent sales declines and increased commodity prices.

title: P&G touts big savings from fabric care in-housing strategy
summary: Procter & Gamble has significantly increased its marketing efficiency by in-housing media functions for some business units, with its fabric care team saving $65 million annually through this strategy. This move allows for more frequent ad placements and the development of proprietary algorithms for better TV commercial placement. While P&G emphasizes "sufficiency" over mere spending, other product categories are building their own approaches, demonstrating the company's varied strategies to optimize efficiency and cut costs amidst inflationary pressures.

title: Proctor & Gamble to Build $500M Plant in Phoenix-Area Town
summary: Procter & Gamble has acquired 430 acres in Coolidge, Arizona, to build a new 2 million-square-foot manufacturing facility for its fabric care products, representing a $500 million investment. The project is expected to create 500 new jobs. The site, valued at approximately $53.4 million, is located within the Inland Port Arizona industrial park, and development is slated to begin later in 2023.

title: Former Clorox executive joins IFF board
summary: Dawn Willoughby, former executive vice president and chief operating officer of The Clorox Co., has been appointed as an independent director to the board of IFF, effective Feb. 1. Willoughby previously held roles at Procter & Gamble and currently serves on the boards of The J.M. Smucker Co. and TE Connectivity. IFF's chair, Dale Morrison, highlighted Willoughby's relevant skills and experience in supporting the company's growth and transformation.

title: Procter & Gamble CIO: ‘Everybody Must Own the Digital Story’
summary: Procter & Gamble CIO Vittorio Cretella emphasizes the importance of digital transformation across the entire CPG ecosystem to improve customer experiences, build loyalty, and drive growth. He details how P&G leverages technologies like AI, IoT, and cloud computing for everything from product formulation and manufacturing efficiency to consumer engagement and privacy. Cretella also addresses challenges in scaling AI, highlighting the need for integrating data, developing talent, and fostering a culture that embraces automation while prioritizing consumer trust and data privacy.

title: The most bought and sold multi-asset funds over the past year
summary: This article analyzes the multi-asset fund flows in 2022, revealing that investors favored higher-equity allocation funds and shunned lower-risk options. It identifies specific funds that attracted significant inflows or experienced substantial withdrawals across different Investment Association multi-asset sectors, highlighting the impact of market performance and investor preferences. Vanguard's LifeStrategy funds were prominent among both bought and sold lists, reflecting diverse investor strategies.

title: Banana Boat sunscreen recall expanded over benzene concerns
summary: Edgewell Personal Care Company has expanded its recall of Banana Boat Hair & Scalp Sunscreen Spray SPF 30 to include an additional batch, bringing the total to four batches, due to the presence of the cancer-causing chemical benzene. The benzene is linked to the product's propellant, not an ingredient in the sunscreen itself. Although no adverse events have been reported, the company has notified retailers and is offering reimbursements to consumers.

title: William Leo Kiely III
summary: William Leo Kiely III, 75, passed away on January 6, 2023. He was a distinguished business leader, serving as President of Coors Brewing Company and CEO of MillerCoors, and held degrees from Harvard and Wharton. Kiely was also deeply involved in philanthropic activities, including supporting his wife's foundation for women's empowerment, and cherished time with his family.

title: Procter & Gamble is recognized as an international sponsor of the war
summary: The National Agency on Corruption Prevention (NACP) has added Procter & Gamble (P&G) to its list of international war sponsors. This decision stems from P&G's continued operations in Russia, where it pays taxes to the state budget and contributes to mobilization efforts despite an earlier promise to reduce its presence. The NACP highlights that P&G's sustained business in Russia, including key production plants, allows it to profit from the Russian market and indirectly support the aggressor country's military actions.

title: BlackRock — the world’s largest asset manager — says central banks are 'deliberately' causing recessions and warns of a downturn unlike any other. 3 shockproof assets for your protection
summary: BlackRock, the world's largest asset manager, predicts a unique recession caused by central banks deliberately overtightening policy to combat inflation, warning that central banks may not intervene to rescue the economy. The firm suggests investors consider "shockproof" assets like consumer staples, fine wine, and real estate as hedges against this impending downturn.

title: Colgate-Palmolive Co. stock outperforms market on strong trading day
summary: Colgate-Palmolive Co. (CL) shares increased by 0.76% to $74.29 on Friday, outperforming the broader market which saw the S&P 500 Index and Dow Jones Industrial Average decline. The stock closed $9.52 below its 52-week high and also outperformed a key competitor, Procter & Gamble Co.

title: Tristan Walker, MBA ’10,“Values Are Universal”
summary: Tristan Walker, MBA '10, founder and CEO of Walker & Company, discussed his entrepreneurial journey and the importance of personal values in his career. He shared insights on his persistence in securing early opportunities, the challenges of raising capital for a niche market, and the significance of selling his company to Procter & Gamble, becoming their first Black CEO. Walker emphasized how his values and lived experiences guided his business decisions and leadership style.

title: Unilever plc Final Results 2022 February 9, 2023
summary: Unilever reported strong 2022 full-year results with 9.0% underlying sales growth, driven by price increases across all business groups, reaching €60.1 billion in turnover. Despite high input costs, underlying operating profit improved slightly, and the company plans for continued growth and margin improvement in 2023. Unilever also highlighted its new operating model, share buyback program, and dividend payments.

title: Unilever Sees Consumer Backlash Worsening on Inflation
summary: Unilever anticipates a decline in product volumes this year as consumers react negatively to price increases on popular items like Dove soap and Hellmann’s mayonnaise. The company expects sales growth to slow from last year's 9% pace and reported its weakest operating margin in at least seven years. This indicates a worsening consumer backlash against inflation.

title: Germaine Hunter, V.P. and DEI leader at Marathon Petroleum Corp., to be ONU Black History Month keynote speaker
summary: Ohio Northern University will host Germaine Hunter, Vice President of Talent Acquisition and Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion at Marathon Petroleum Corporation, as its Black History Month keynote speaker on February 27. Hunter will speak on "Building Inclusive Communities – Supporting Today, Building for Tomorrow" and engage with various student groups, faculty, and staff. He is known for his work in developing diversity action plans and leading recruiting efforts, and previously served as the first chief diversity officer at The Clorox Company.

title: Navigate 2023 With Recession-Resistant ETF ZECP
summary: The Zacks Earnings Consistent Portfolio ETF (ZECP) is presented as a recession-resistant strategy for investors concerned about a potential economic downturn in 2023. ZECP, Zacks Investment Management's first ETF, identifies companies with strong balance sheets and consistent earnings, having demonstrated resilience through past recessions. The fund seeks to offer an active approach to navigate market volatility, focusing on quality companies with stable historic and forecasted earnings per share.

title: Newell Brands CEO Saligram to retire; forecasts 2023 results below estimates
summary: Newell Brands CEO Ravi Saligram is set to retire on May 16, with Chris Peterson named as his successor. The company also projected 2023 annual results, including net sales and profit per share, below analysts' estimates, which led to an 11% drop in premarket trading. Newell has been affected by rising costs and a slowdown in consumer spending, leading to job cuts and a tough operating environment.

title: Coty Inc. Cl A stock outperforms market on strong trading day
summary: Coty Inc. Cl A (COTY) stock rose 0.90% to $11.27 on a down day for the broader market, hitting a new 52-week high. The stock extended its four-day winning streak and outperformed competitors like Estee Lauder, Inter Parfums, and Procter & Gamble. Trading volume for COTY significantly exceeded its 50-day average.

title: Ecolab Inc. stock rises Tuesday, outperforms market
summary: Ecolab Inc. (ECL) stock rose 7.11% on Tuesday to $158.40, outperforming the broader market which saw the S&P 500 Index and Dow Jones Industrial Average fall. This marked the stock's third consecutive day of gains, and it also outperformed key competitors like Procter & Gamble Co., Waste Management Inc., and Colgate-Palmolive Co. The trading volume for Ecolab Inc. also exceeded its 50-day average.

title: Will Walmart open wallets? Prices in focus as retailer reports earnings
summary: Walmart's upcoming earnings report will provide insight into American shopper behavior amidst rising grocery prices. Analysts are keen to see how Walmart plans to counteract supplier price hikes and maintain its dominant position in the grocery market, possibly through price investments and private-label offerings. The retailer is expected to show a rise in Q4 sales, driven by higher-income shoppers attracted to its "Everyday Low Price" strategy.

title: How Procter & Gamble's media strategy changes the role of agencies
summary: This article discusses how Procter & Gamble's evolving media strategy is transforming the traditional role of advertising agencies. It features insights from Marc Pritchard's speech at the 2023 ANA Media Conference, highlighting the significant shifts occurring in the brand marketing landscape due to these strategic changes. The piece also includes other related articles on AI in advertising and marketing winners and losers.

title: P&G’s Pritchard says AI, algorithms are improving ad effectiveness
summary: P&G's brand chief Marc Pritchard states that artificial intelligence and algorithms are crucial for improving advertising efficiency and effectiveness, moving away from simply being the largest media spender. The company has invested in in-housing marketing functions and developing proprietary algorithms to leverage vast consumer data. This shift allows P&G to optimize ad performance, leading to increased sales and significant cost savings.

title: Why Procter & Gamble's in-house media strategy may be difficult for other marketers to follow
summary: Procter & Gamble's in-house media strategy might be challenging for other marketers to adopt, a point highlighted at the 2023 ANA Media Conference. The article features insights from industry leaders, including Jill Kelly, CEO of EssenceMediacom. This discussion suggests that while P&G's approach may be effective for them, it may not be easily scalable or replicable for other companies.

title: This Pharmaceuticals Company Looks To Be A Better Pick Over Procter & Gamble Stock
summary: This article argues that AbbVie stock (ABBV) is a better investment than Procter & Gamble (PG), despite both trading at similar valuations. The comparison highlights AbbVie's stronger past revenue growth, higher profitability, and better future revenue growth forecast driven by new drugs, even with the impending biosimilar competition for Humira.

title: Work Is Changing; Workspaces Are, Too
summary: P&G is redesigning its workspaces globally to adapt to the rise of hybrid work, focusing on collaboration, productivity, and employee well-being. These new spaces integrate advanced technology to facilitate remote and in-person engagement, incorporate sustainable design principles, and embrace local culture and universal accessibility. The goal is to create engaging environments that attract and retain talent and foster innovation.

title: Hand Wash Global Market Report 2023
summary: The global hand wash market grew from $12.22 billion in 2022 to $13.23 billion in 2023, with an expected growth to $19.02 billion by 2027 due to rising infectious diseases and product innovation. Asia-Pacific was the largest market in 2022, and North America is projected to be the fastest-growing region. Major players include Unilever, Procter & Gamble, and Reckitt Benckiser.

title: Should You Buy This Households & Personal Products Company Over Colgate-Palmolive Stock?
summary: This article analyzes whether Procter & Gamble (P&G) or Colgate-Palmolive (CL) is a better investment in the consumer-defensive sector. While both stocks are compared on revenue growth, profitability, and financial position, P&G is deemed the better choice due to superior metrics, despite trading at a higher valuation. The analysis suggests P&G stock will offer better returns than CL stock in the next three years.

title: Women’s History Month: Meet the P&G Innovators Behind the Innovation
summary: Procter & Gamble is celebrating Women's History Month by highlighting five women innovators: Laura Goodman (Scientific Communications Director), Daniela Rios (Government Relations & Public Policy Director), Basak Aydin (Senior Director, Product Supply, Gebze Plant Manager), Lucy Yuan (Senior Director, Tianjin Plant Manager, Global Bar Platform Leaders), and Vicki Jung (Director Surface Care Packaging). These women discuss their impactful work, from developing products that improve consumer lives to influencing public policy and fostering team growth. Their stories emphasize P&G's commitment to innovation, community betterment, and employee development.

title: Four P&G Brands Raise the Bar with Accessible and Sustainable Packaging
summary: Procter & Gamble highlights how four of its brands—Ariel, Gillette, Herbal Essences, and Lenor—are setting new industry standards by integrating accessible and sustainable packaging designs. The company emphasizes that inclusive design not only benefits consumers with disabilities but also aligns with environmental goals, addressing customer feedback on plastic use and difficulty in opening products. Initiatives include tactile indicators, recycled plastics, NaviLens QR codes, and child-safe ergonomic opening systems, all recognized by industry awards.

title: Like a boss: Spider women offer views on leadership
summary: This article highlights three University of Richmond alumnae in leadership roles to celebrate International Women's Day. It features Amber Nichols, General Manager of the Capital City Go-Go; Heidi Petz, President and COO of Sherwin-Williams; and Stephanie Headley, Senior Vice President for North American skin care with P&G, leading the Olay brand. Each woman shares insights from their careers and their paths to success.

title: How Procter & Gamble is re-investing in radio to find TV audiences
summary: Procter & Gamble increased its radio spending by 43% last year to $235 million as a strategy to reach TV audiences. This reinvestment highlights a media spending shift to find consumers through different channels.

title: Time For Procter & Gamble (Or A CPG) To Buy The Honest Company (NASDAQ:HNST)
summary: The article suggests that The Honest Company (HNST) should be acquired by a larger Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG) company like Procter & Gamble due to its recent poor financial performance and a perceived lack of urgency from management. The author highlights the company's missed Q4 FY 2022 Adj. EBITDA and awful FY 2023 guidance as reasons for this recommendation, aiming to benefit long-suffering shareholders.

title: Cyber thieves swipe worker information at Cincinnati-based Procter and Gamble
summary: Cyber thieves have stolen worker information from Cincinnati-based Procter and Gamble by exploiting a bug in an external file transfer tool called GoAnywhere. P&G confirmed that personal data of employees was compromised, but stated that sensitive information like social security numbers or banking details were not included, and no customer data was taken. A cybersecurity expert noted that a Russian group selling "ransomware as a service" was likely responsible for the attack, highlighting the difficulty of maintaining 100% security against sophisticated threats.

title: Procter & Gamble confirm breach
summary: Procter & Gamble confirmed that one of its companies was affected by the Fortra GoAnywhere vulnerability, leading to a breach where attackers obtained some employee information. The company stated that no sensitive data like social security numbers, credit card details, or customer data was compromised, and business operations continue normally. The Russia-linked Cl0p ransomware syndicate, which claimed responsibility, has victimized numerous organizations using this zero-day flaw.

title: Polycoated paper packaging can’t be recycled everywhere. A new group is trying to change that.
summary: A newly formed Poly Coated Paper Alliance aims to achieve widespread recycling of polycoated paper packaging. The alliance, including members like Sonoco, Procter & Gamble, and General Mills, will focus on universal product design guidelines, upgraded mill specifications, and closing data gaps. They will embark on a two-year research and data-gathering process to advance end-market acceptance for these materials.

title: Attackers start leaking Procter & Gamble data
summary: Russia-linked ransomware syndicate Cl0p has begun leaking what they claim is commercial data belonging to Procter & Gamble (P&G). This leak stems from a vulnerability in Fortra's GoAnywhere managed file transfer software, which Cl0p has exploited to breach numerous companies. P&G confirmed that one of its entities was affected but maintains that no sensitive customer data like Social Security numbers or credit card details were exposed, with the leaked samples primarily showing commercial client purchase information.

title: Top 10 Procter & Gamble Competitors & Alternatives
summary: This article lists the top 10 competitors and alternatives to Procter & Gamble, a leading consumer goods company. It provides details on each competitor, including their founding year, headquarters, key products, and historical background. The list highlights the diverse range of companies vying for market share in the consumer goods sector against P&G.

title: P&G Unwinds ‘Precision’ Makeup Brand Opte Four Years After Launch
summary: Procter & Gamble Co. is phasing out its "precision" makeup brand Opte, an inkjet wand for targeted makeup application, four years after its launch. The decision was made as part of P&G Ventures' strategy to focus on products with the biggest impact, despite Opte being touted for several years and receiving an innovation award. P&G will continue to offer technical and warranty support though new product and refill orders have ceased.

title: Procter & Gamble's earnings boosted by higher prices for Pampers diapers and Bounty kitchen paper
summary: Procter & Gamble's fiscal third-quarter earnings exceeded Wall Street expectations due to price increases on household products like Tide, Bounty, and Pampers. The company raised prices by approximately 10% across its brands, indicating that consumers are not switching to cheaper private-label alternatives. This led to a 3.5% rise in P&G's stock on Friday.

title: Double-Digit Price Increases Bolster Profits at Procter & Gamble (Published 2023)
summary: Procter & Gamble reported bolstered profits in the first quarter of 2023 due to a 10 percent price increase across its brands, marking the second consecutive quarter of double-digit hikes. This strategy allowed the company's profit margin to expand, offsetting increased raw material costs, even as sales volumes declined slightly. P&G also raised its revenue forecast for the fiscal year and announced plans for a significant stock buyback program.

title: P&G Says Consumer Demand Is Stabilising Despite Higher Prices
summary: Procter & Gamble Co. raised its sales projection for the fiscal year ending in June, citing higher prices and a slight increase in demand for some products, with shares rising the most in three years. Despite a decline in total unit sales, the company noted that volumes are starting to stabilise, particularly in the US, and that while some costs are easing, bottom-line forecasts remain cautious due to ongoing high labour and commodity costs. The gains were primarily driven by a 10 percent jump in prices, with specific volume increases seen in beauty and healthcare segments, offsetting declines in other divisions.

title: Procter & Gamble rakes in profits after 10% price hike amid inflation
summary: Procter & Gamble reported strong quarterly sales and profits, driven by a 10% price hike across its brands, particularly in fabric and home care. Despite inflation-weary consumers buying fewer products, the company exceeded Wall Street expectations for sales and earnings and raised its outlook for fiscal 2023. Sales volume declines were moderated by the economic reopening in China, P&G's second-biggest market.

title: Margin care: Consumer giant Procter & Gamble is navigating inflation with ease
summary: Procter & Gamble reported strong quarterly earnings and revenue growth, exceeding Wall Street expectations and raising its 2023 outlook, despite accusations of "greedflation" due to price hikes. The consumer goods giant, with over 65 brands, demonstrated healthy profit margins across its diverse divisions, particularly in Fabric & Home Care, Grooming, and Beauty. Sales volume decreased, but a 10% average price increase resulted in a 4% overall sales rise.

title: P&G expects $2.2B hit from supply costs in 2023
summary: Procter & Gamble anticipates a $2.2 billion hit to earnings in 2023 due to inflation in commodity and material costs, despite price hikes and productivity savings. The company is leveraging its "Supply Chain 3.0" initiative and digital investments to achieve $1.5 billion in savings and enhance its competitive advantage against rising costs and private label brands. While price increases have significantly boosted gross margins, P&G faces growing retailer resistance to further hikes, leading it to focus on improving its offerings and sustained investment in innovation.

title: Kimberly-Clark CEO again promises big developments in the ‘poop’ category
summary: Kimberly-Clark's stock jumped after the company reported better-than-expected quarterly earnings and raised its full-year guidance. The company, known for Kleenex, Huggies, and Cottonelle, announced a 10% price increase for the second consecutive quarter, significantly expanding gross margins. The CEO also hinted at exciting upcoming innovations in bathroom tissue, referring to it as "a better clean" in the "poop" category.

title: Kimberly-Clark lifts 2023 profit forecast on higher prices
summary: Kimberly-Clark Corp raised its full-year profit forecast for 2023, driven by consistent price hikes that led to better-than-expected first-quarter sales despite weak volumes. The company's gross margin increased to 33.2% as it raised prices across all categories by 10%, mirroring a trend seen with peer Procter & Gamble, which also benefited from price increases. Kimberly-Clark now expects 2023 profit growth between 6% and 10%.

title: El Paso's Helen of Troy getting first female CEO as Julien Mininberg sets retirement date
summary: Helen of Troy, an El Paso-based consumer products company, will appoint Noel Geoffroy as its first female CEO, effective March 1, 2024, succeeding Julien Mininberg. Geoffroy, currently the COO, will lead the company's restructuring efforts and future strategic plans. Mininberg, who led the company for a decade, will retire.

title: The latest innovations to help people be well and thrive
summary: The Clorox Company highlights recent innovations across its brands, focusing on products designed to meet consumer needs and support well-being. These innovations include Clorox Free & Clear cleaning products, Fresh Step Crystals Health Monitoring Litter, and new portable collagen and magnesium supplements. The article also showcases sustainable packaging from Burt's Bees and new flavor offerings from Hidden Valley Ranch and more durable Glad trash bags.

title: Colgate-Palmolive’s stock pops after earnings beat as company raises prices by double-digit percentage
summary: Colgate-Palmolive's stock rose 3.6% after reporting better-than-expected first-quarter earnings, driven by significant price increases, including a 10.5% hike in North America. This trend reflects the pricing power demonstrated by several consumer-goods companies this earnings season, such as Procter & Gamble, Kimberly-Clark, PepsiCo, Nestlé, and Unilever, who also implemented double-digit price increases with minimal impact on sales volumes.

title: Dividend-Paying Cleaning Stocks to Buy Now
summary: This article identifies several dividend-paying cleaning stocks, including Clorox, Ecolab, Cintas, Procter & Gamble, and Reckitt Benckiser, as strong investment opportunities. The demand for cleaning products and services has surged due to the COVID-19 pandemic, leading to a "long-lasting and transformative" emphasis on hygiene. The featured companies either specialize in cleaning or have significantly expanded their hygiene-related offerings to capitalize on this trend.

title: P&G subsidiary iMFLUX in Hamilton to close, lay off 122
summary: Procter & Gamble's Hamilton-based subsidiary, iMFLUX, is set to close its plant and lay off 122 employees by June 30, 2023. The closure is part of P&G's transition to a new model for iMFLUX's injection molding technology, which will involve third-party sales, licensing, and a smaller internal team. P&G is assisting affected employees with potential internal placements, severance packages, and job search support.

title: P&G to shutter Hamilton subsidiary iMFLUX, laying off 122 workers
summary: Procter & Gamble Co. is closing its Hamilton-based plastic molding subsidiary, iMFLUX, resulting in 122 layoffs. The company notified Ohio officials of the layoffs, which will take effect on June 30, and will not renew iMFLUX's lease. P&G plans to transition iMFLUX into a smaller research and development operation, seeking to reassign affected employees or provide severance packages.

title: Bleach maker Clorox raises annual forecasts on higher prices
summary: Clorox Co. raised its annual sales and profit forecasts due to higher product prices, which helped the company overcome a slowdown in demand. Despite a drop in volume for some segments, price hikes increased gross margins and led to a 6% rise in net sales for the third quarter. The company now expects fiscal 2023 net sales to increase between 1% to 2% and projects annual adjusted earnings between $4.35 and $4.50 per share.

title: Procter & Gamble commits to new actions and shares strong progress on commitments to promote Equality and Inclusion across the Asia Pacific, the Middle East, and Africa
summary: Procter & Gamble has announced new commitments and shared progress on its Equality & Inclusion (E&I) initiatives across the Asia Pacific, Middle East, and Africa (AMA) regions. New commitments include educating over 35 million adolescent girls on puberty and menstrual hygiene and establishing a task force of certified "Mental Health First Aiders" for its 19,000 employees. P&G is also making significant strides in its existing programs, such as the ReLaunch program for STEM careers, investing $175 million in women-owned and women-led businesses, improving advertising accessibility, and increasing female representation among brand advertisement directors.

title: How Procter & Gamble supports employees’ dual role as caregivers
summary: Procter & Gamble has implemented a two-pronged approach to support its employees in their caregiving roles, recognizing that caregiving extends beyond just childcare to include a wide range of family and non-family members. Following an employee focus group, P&G hired a concierge service, Cariloop, to help employees find resources and financial aid for caregiving, and also developed strategies to help managers and teams discuss caregiving issues openly. This initiative aims to reduce employee stress, increase productivity, and aid in retaining diverse talent, although some employees still face skepticism or guilt regarding the use of such services.

title: India's P&G Hygiene and Health Care posts drop in Q3 sales on muted demand
summary: Procter & Gamble Hygiene and Health Care Ltd (PROC.NS) reported a 1% dip in Q3 sales to 8.81 billion rupees ($107.73 million) due to waning pandemic-driven demand for healthcare products and elevated inflation. Despite the sales drop, the company's profit rose to 1.65 billion rupees, benefiting from a 575 million rupees gain from tax adjustments. The company's shares have fallen about 6% this year, amidst a challenging operating environment.

title: Gerry D’Angelo, Procter & Gamble’s No. 1 Media Executive, to Retire.
summary: Gerry D’Angelo, Procter & Gamble's top global media executive, is retiring after seven years with the company. He is credited with leading P&G's extensive in-housing of media planning and buying, increasing the use of programmatic trading, and bolstering brand reach. D'Angelo will remain active in the industry as an advisor and mentor.

title: Colgate-Palmolive beats Q4 profit estimates helped by price hikes
summary: Colgate-Palmolive (India) Ltd's fourth-quarter profit fell less than expected, helped by price hikes implemented to combat surging costs. The company reported a 2.3% fall in net profit to 3.16 billion rupees, while sales rose nearly 4% to 13.42 billion rupees due to price increases. Its better-than-feared earnings follow previous drops in profit and come as other consumer goods makers also report mixed earnings for the March quarter.

title: FSTA Top Holdings List & Exposure (Fidelity MSCI Consumer Staples Index ETF)
summary: This article details the top holdings and exposure of the Fidelity MSCI Consumer Staples Index ETF (FSTA). It lists the top 25 stocks held by the ETF, ranked by weight, which collectively make up 81.38% of the fund. Key holdings include Walmart, Costco Wholesale, and Procter & Gamble, providing a snapshot of FSTA's investment strategy in the consumer staples sector.

title: P&G buys back Kansas City plant it planned to shut down; here's why
summary: Procter & Gamble Co. (NYSE: PG) re-acquired its 118-year-old Kansas City, Kansas, soap plant in late April 2023. The company had initially planned to close the facility and relocate operations, but surging demand for its products during the pandemic led to its continued operation. Financial terms of the buy-back were not disclosed.

title: P&G’s stock leads Dow decliners after downgrade by analyst, who says investors may have shown it ‘too much love’
summary: Procter & Gamble Co.'s stock declined after Truist analyst Bill Chappell downgraded it to "hold" from "buy," citing that the company's success is already priced into the stock. Chappell also reduced his price target for P&G shares from $165 to $155. He indicated that there are no foreseeable catalysts to justify new investments in P&G's stock, despite the company's strong performance over the past two decades.

title: How McDonald’s, P&G, Coca-Cola, GM and other big brands are spending on Black-owned media
summary: This article by Ad Age investigates how major brands such as McDonald's, P&G, Coca-Cola, and GM are allocating their advertising budgets towards Black-owned media companies. The content is based on a survey conducted by Ad Age focusing on the spending patterns of these large brands.

title: Always®, International Paper, and Period Heroes Join Forces to Advocate for Federal Action to Help #EndPeriodPoverty in the U.S.
summary: Always, International Paper, and Period Heroes convened in Washington D.C. to support Congresswoman Grace Meng's Menstrual Equity for All Act, aiming to end period poverty by ensuring access to free period products in federal buildings and schools. The initiative highlights that 1 in 5 girls miss school due to lack of period products and advocates for systemic change beyond product donations. This effort stresses the importance of legislative action to address the widespread issue of period poverty and its impact on education and confidence.

title: Unilever posts 20% increase in revenue
summary: Unilever Ghana PLC reported a 20% increase in revenue, reaching GH¢632 million in 2022, up from GH¢530 million in 2021. The company's profit surged significantly to GH¢15 million from GH¢0.4 million the previous year, despite global economic challenges. This growth is attributed to strategic price increases, continuous innovation, and the resilience of its workforce.

title: 2022’s Top Advertisers: P&G, Comcast Join Radio’s $200 Million Club.
summary: Procter & Gamble and Comcast Corp. both surpassed $200 million in radio ad spending in 2022, securing their positions as top advertisers. P&G increased its radio allocation by 48% and Comcast by 35%, while other significant spenders included Deutsche Telekom, the U.S. Government, Berkshire Hathaway, and Pfizer, with Pfizer showing the fastest growth among major advertisers. The article also highlights shifts in ad spending across different media, with AVOD and local radio seeing significant increases.

title: A Discussion With P&G's Chief Sustainability Officer
summary: This article features an interview with Virginie Helias, P&G's Chief Sustainability Officer, discussing the evolution of sustainability at P&G and their strategies to tackle the plastic waste crisis. Helias highlights P&G's shift from regulatory compliance to embedding sustainability across all business functions and emphasizes the importance of partnerships and collaboration to achieve circularity goals, particularly in developing markets. She details P&G's progress towards reducing virgin plastic and increasing recyclable packaging, and outlines their efforts to create a more sustainable and equitable plastics value chain through responsible sourcing and community engagement.

title: Perrigo Appoints Patrick Lockwood-Taylor as President and CEO
summary: Perrigo Company plc has appointed Patrick Lockwood-Taylor as its new President, Chief Executive Officer, and Board member, effective June 30, 2023. Mr. Lockwood-Taylor brings over 25 years of experience in global consumer product leadership, previously serving in a dual role at Bayer AG as President of Bayer U.S. and Regional President of Consumer Health North America, where he achieved significant growth and market share recovery. The company's Chairman, Orlando D. Ashford, highlighted Lockwood-Taylor's experience and proven track record as ideal for executing Perrigo's "Optimize & Accelerate" strategy.

title: Procter & Gamble's Jeff Kent Discusses AI and Machine Learning
summary: Jeff Kent, VP of Smart Platforms Technology & Innovation at Procter & Gamble, detailed the company's application of AI and machine learning to cut manufacturing costs and improve operations. P&G aims for significant efficiency gains and cost reductions using its "WISE" initiative, including the SmartBox edge device, and is implementing thousands of machine learning algorithms across its global sites. The company is strategically moving beyond the traditional Purdue model to achieve more direct and agnostic communication in its push for digitalization and Industry 4.0.

title: Candle Market Size to Grow by $2.8 Billion from 2022 to 2027: Technavio
summary: The global candle market is projected to grow by $2.8 billion from 2022 to 2027, driven by evolving lifestyles, increased home decor demand, and a CAGR of 5.79%. North America is expected to contribute 28% to this growth, fueled by festive demand, natural essential oil candles, and eco-friendly attributes like wooden wicks. Key market players are implementing various growth strategies in this fragmented market.

title: VF Taps Gaming Tech Exec to Be CEO
summary: VF Corp. has appointed Bracken Darrell, former CEO of Logitech, as its new president and CEO, effective July 17. Darrell is known for his history of successful turnarounds, including doubling Logitech’s revenue and increasing its market cap tenfold during his 10-year tenure. He takes over a company where some brands like Vans and Dickies have struggled, though the Vans turnaround is reportedly on track.

title: VF Corporation Appoints Bracken Darrell as President and CEO
summary: VF Corporation (NYSE: VFC) has appointed Bracken Darrell as its new President and CEO, effective July 17, 2023. Darrell previously served as President and CEO of Logitech International for 10 years, where he significantly expanded revenue and market capitalization. Richard Carucci has been named Chair of the Board, and interim CEO Benno Dorer will remain a Board member.

title: Better Buy: Procter & Gamble vs. Clorox
summary: This article compares Procter & Gamble (PG) and Clorox (CLX), concluding that P&G is the better buy primarily due to its significantly larger marketing budget and ability to dominate competitive markets. While Clorox leads in niche categories, P&G's financial muscle allows it to consistently out-promote competitors and maintain an "unfair advantage" in consumer staples. The article emphasizes that P&G's size allows it to better navigate consumer price sensitivity and market competition.

title: P&G’s Vanished Forest Degradation Commitment
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) has removed its commitment to prohibit forest degradation from its latest forest sourcing policy, despite previous investor pressure. This move suggests a backtracking on responsible sourcing claims, leaving P&G as a continued driver of degradation in Canada's boreal forests, which has significant climate and biodiversity impacts. The NRDC highlights that P&G's previous claims were misleading and calls for a genuine commitment to eliminate forest degradation.

title: Toothpaste Market size to grow by USD 3.99 billion from 2021 to 2026| Rising dental issues in the children and elderly population to drive the market - Technavio
summary: The global toothpaste market is projected to grow by USD 3.99 billion from 2021 to 2026, driven by an increase in dental issues among children and the elderly and rising awareness of oral hygiene. APAC is expected to contribute 60% to this growth. The market is fragmented with vendors competing on technological advancements and product pricing, while the growth of e-commerce is identified as a key trend.

title: SAP SE Appoints Pinar Dolen as Vice President, Chief Analytics Officer
summary: SAP SE has appointed Pinar Dolen as Vice President, Chief Analytics Officer to lead its global analytics organization and support its transformation into an intelligent, sustainable enterprise. Dolen brings extensive experience in digital transformation from her previous roles at Procter & Gamble and Louis Dreyfus Company. She will leverage advanced analytics to drive SAP's strategic objectives.

title: Despite a decade of effort, P&G can’t please activists on deforestation
summary: Procter & Gamble has struggled for a decade to satisfy environmental activists regarding its deforestation policies, despite implementing sustainable sourcing targets and grievance trackers. Activists criticize P&G's continued sourcing from areas tied to deforestation and forest degradation, particularly in the Canadian boreal forest and its palm oil supply chain. Descendants of P&G's founders are also engaging with the company and activists to advocate for more responsible environmental practices, highlighting the complexity of balancing business needs with ecological concerns.

title: Focus: P&G drops forest pledge, drawing ire of green groups, investors
summary: Procter & Gamble has removed a prior pledge from its corporate policy to not purchase wood pulp from degraded forests, a move that has drawn strong criticism from environmental groups and some investors. P&G stated this change was made because a widely applied definition of forest degradation is unavailable, and affirmed it will comply with an upcoming EU deforestation law. However, environmental NGOs and investors argue there is a broad understanding of forest degradation and are pushing back against the policy change.

title: Unilever appoints chairman of Compass Group Meakins as chair designate
summary: Unilever announced the appointment of Ian Meakins, chairman of Compass Group, as its chair designate, set to replace Nils Andersen. Meakins will join the board on September 1 and become chairman on December 1, while Andersen will step down at the company's Annual General Meeting in May 2024 after nine years of service. Meakins brings a strong background from executive and non-executive roles in various industries, including prior positions at Diageo, Bain & Company, and Procter & Gamble.

title: P&G Beats Profit and Sales Estimates on Higher Prices
summary: Procter & Gamble (PG) surpassed profit and sales estimates for its fiscal 2023 fourth quarter, driven by higher prices for its products, even while facing increased costs. Shares rose over 3% following the announcement. However, the company's outlook for fiscal 2024 fell below forecasts due to anticipated macroeconomic challenges.

title: Will inflation make consumers abandon their favorite brands?
summary: Procter & Gamble is being cautious about its 2024 outlook despite better-than-expected quarterly earnings, driven by concerns that inflation may cause consumers to abandon their favorite brands for cheaper alternatives. While brand loyalty is strong due to habit, P&G mitigates this risk by offering a range of brands at different price points, allowing consumers to trade down within its own product portfolio.

title: P&G Trimming SKUs As Part of Collaborative Commerce Strategy
summary: Procter & Gamble is reducing its SKU count, leveraging POS data and proprietary algorithms to optimize product offerings and improve service levels. This initiative is part of a larger collaborative commerce strategy with retail partners, aiming to drive efficiencies, productivity, and maximize overall sales throughput, as other CPG companies like Mondelez and Unilever have also done. The company views SKU rationalization as both a cost-saving and top-line growth opportunity, enhancing its evolving omnichannel strategy.

title: Procter & Gamble sales rise slightly, fueled by higher prices
