While insiders own less than 1% of the large company, board members collectively hold $97 million in shares.

title: Trump in Schwab tie-up for $250m financial services offering
summary: Donald Trump's media venture, Truth Social, is expanding into financial services with Truth.Fi, a platform planning to invest up to $250 million in cryptocurrency and traditional assets. This initiative, supported by Charles Schwab for asset custody and advisory services, aims to back American economic growth and the "Patriot Economy." The announcement led to a 10% surge in TMTG's stock, aligning with Trump's ongoing advocacy for digital assets and following Elon Musk's similar financial services announcement for X.

title: ZK International to launch xSigma crypto wallet with Visa card
summary: ZK International's subsidiary, xSigma Corp., is launching the xSigma Wallet, a new cryptocurrency banking wallet supporting purchases with various payment methods and featuring an xSigma-branded Visa card for crypto-asset top-ups. This initiative addresses memecoin interest and aligns with the company's focus on DeFi, despite ZK International experiencing financial volatility and significant cash burn, as highlighted by InvestingPro. The parent company, specializing in steel pipe products, recently reported a 405% increase in gross profits and secured a $4.47 million contract.

title: Moov Lands Trump Media Processing Deal And Supports Jack Henry’s Visa Direct Push
summary: Payment processor Moov Financial Inc. has secured a deal to process payments for Trump Media and Technology Group Corp.'s Truth Social platform and Truth+ streaming service, encompassing credit, debit, and ACH acceptance. In related news, Moov is also collaborating with Jack Henry & Associates Inc. on its new Visa Direct service, which enables financial institutions to offer enhanced digital payment services to small and mid-sized businesses. This partnership aims to strengthen relationships with businesses by providing integrated digital payment and deposit solutions.

title: Visa leans into A2A payments
summary: Visa is expanding its services to include account-to-account (A2A) payments, starting in the UK in early 2025 before a wider European rollout. This move allows Visa to grow beyond its traditional card-based transactions, offering "pay-by-bank" options, initially for bill-pay services. The strategy aims to capture new payment flows and leverage Visa's existing capabilities, while the company also reported a 5% increase in net income for its fiscal first quarter.

title: Visa’s general counsel Julie Rottenberg sells $874,480 in stock
summary: Visa’s general counsel, Julie Rottenberg, recently sold 2,572 shares of Visa Class A Common Stock for $874,480 through a pre-established trading plan. Concurrently, she exercised stock options to acquire an equal number of shares for $207,869, resulting in her holding 11,925 shares. The stock sale occurred while Visa's shares were trading near their 52-week high, and the company has a market capitalization of $674.5 billion.

title: Turning Point Brands, Inc.'s (NYSE:TPB) high institutional ownership speaks for itself as stock continues to impress, up 6.6% over last week
summary: Turning Point Brands, Inc. (NYSE:TPB) is largely owned by institutional investors, holding 82% of the company, which indicates their significant influence on the stock price. The stock has seen a 6.6% increase over the last week and a 195% return over the past year. Top institutional shareholders include BlackRock, The Vanguard Group, and Morgan Stanley, with the top 14 shareholders collectively owning 50% of the company.

title: Charles Schwab Asset Management Increases Stake in Tesla in Q4
summary: Charles Schwab Asset Management increased its stake in Tesla during the fourth quarter of 2024, acquiring nearly 800,000 additional shares to hold over 17.32 million shares valued at almost $7 billion. This continued investment highlights institutional confidence in Tesla, despite a reported 23% drop in net income in 2024 and declining vehicle registrations in key markets like the U.S., Germany, France, the Netherlands, UK, and China. Tesla's shares have risen 92% over the last twelve months, trading at $360.50 at the time of writing.

title: PayPal Stock Price Forecast - PYPL Shares Poised for Major Comeback as $20B Buyback Drive Value
summary: PayPal Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ:PYPL) is trading at $63.04, significantly below its 2021 highs, but analysts predict a major comeback driven by strong Q3 2025 results, a new dividend policy, and a $20 billion share buyback program. The company delivered solid financial performance with $8.42 billion in revenue and $1.97 billion in operating cash flow, along with a strategic pivot towards AI-driven commerce through a partnership with OpenAI. Despite competitive pressures, PayPal's valuation gap, robust capital return program, and focus on profitability make it a compelling value opportunity with a target range of $90-$100 in the next 12 months.

title: MUFG buy-in deal jacks up Gcash valuation to $5B
summary: MUFG Bank Ltd. has completed the acquisition of an 8-percent stake in Ayala-led Mynt, the operator of GCash, boosting its valuation to $5 billion. This transaction follows an initial announcement last August, with the Japanese bank injecting $393 million into the e-wallet brand. Ayala Group’s AC Ventures Holdings Inc. also increased its ownership in GCash by acquiring an additional 8 percent interest for P22.9 billion, bringing its stake to 13 percent.

title: Trio of firms hope to make paying for an EV charge simpler
summary: EFTCorp, Rubicon, Visa, and Verifone have introduced a new open-loop payment system for electric vehicle charging, aiming to simplify the process for EV owners. This solution allows users to pay with a credit card directly at charging stations, eliminating the need for third-party payment accounts. The initiative is expected to increase the accessibility of EV charging and promote greater adoption of electric vehicles in South Africa, with potential for scaling to other regions and services.

title: Payments players mull new approaches to fraud
summary: Companies in the payments industry, including Google, Nacha, Early Warning Services, and Truist, are actively seeking new strategies to combat push-payment fraud, which cost the Americas $102.6 billion in 2023. These organizations are advocating for increased data sharing, greater involvement from law enforcement, and improved digital identity tracking to better protect consumers and corporate customers from sophisticated scam operations. The challenge lies in balancing fraud prevention with maintaining frictionless payment experiences and managing the vast scale of transactions under constant attack from criminal groups.

title: What drove this Vanguard fund to just top the U.S.’s oldest and largest ETF by $1.5 billion
summary: The Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO) has surpassed the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY) in assets under management, becoming the world's largest exchange-traded fund. VOO now holds almost $632 billion, about $1.5 billion more than SPY, which was previously the oldest and largest U.S. ETF. This shift is attributed to VOO's lower cost in tracking the S&P 500 index.

title: How Capital One and Discover Forged US$33.5bn Merger
summary: Capital One and Discover Financial Services shareholders have approved a US$33.5 billion merger, aiming to create a payments and banking powerhouse to challenge Visa and Mastercard. The acquisition leverages Discover's payment network and Capital One's technology prowess, but faces regulatory hurdles and antitrust concerns despite shareholder support. The combined entity would control over US$630 billion in assets and aims for a finalization in early 2025.

title: Worried about U.S. stocks? You can diversify in a market loaded with potential
summary: An investment strategy that has worked for years might eventually make up a large portion of a portfolio, increasing overall risk. The S&P 500 has performed well but has also become concentrated in a small number of stocks. To diversify and mitigate this risk, Shuntaro Takeuchi of Matthews Asia recommends U.S. investors consider adding exposure to the Japanese market.

title: Institutions own 43% of Invesco Mortgage Capital Inc. (NYSE:IVR) shares but individual investors control 57% of the company
summary: Individual investors hold a significant majority of 57% in Invesco Mortgage Capital Inc. (NYSE:IVR), while institutions own 43% of the company's shares. This distribution suggests that individual investors have substantial influence over management decisions. BlackRock, Inc. is the largest institutional shareholder with 9.2% of shares outstanding.

title: Managing Cash With Money Market Funds vs. ETFs
summary: This article examines the growing trend of money market ETFs as an alternative to traditional money market mutual funds for cash management. It highlights key differences, including tradability, floating NAVs, and accessibility, while noting their similar regulatory frameworks and investment goals. The piece also discusses the impact of interest rates and market uncertainty on the appeal of these cash management tools.

title: Ally Financial: Planned Credit Card Business Sale Shows Renewed Focus On Core Business
summary: Ally Financial is selling its credit card business to concentrate on its core operations, primarily car loans, in an effort to recover from past difficulties. This sale is expected to be income-neutral while increasing tangible book value by $1 per share. With a low price/book ratio and a Forward P/E of 10.46, the company shows potential value, especially with planned share repurchases and a renewed focus on profitable segments despite retaining exposure to interest rate and market risks.

title: Amex, Alipay target fast-growing China market
summary: American Express has partnered with Chinese digital payment giant Alipay to expand its presence in China, the world's fastest-growing card market. Amex customers can now add their credit cards to Alipay digital wallets, leveraging Amex's 2020 license to clear local currency transactions in China. This move positions Amex to benefit from the projected 46.8% increase in card use in the Asia-Pacific region by 2029.

title: Mastercard taps State Dept official for top role
summary: Mastercard has announced that its former legal boss, Richard Verma, will rejoin the company as chief administrative officer after serving two years at the State Department. Concurrently, Tim Murphy, the current CAO, has been promoted to vice chairman. Verma's return is notable as Mastercard faces various litigations, including a 20-year dispute over merchant interchange fees and a civil probe by the Justice Department regarding its debit card practices.

title: Condenan al BBVA y a Prisma a pagar una multa por daño punitivo a un cliente a quien no le atendieron su reclamo para desconocer un consumo que no había hecho
summary: The Commercial Chamber's "Sala E" condemned BBVA and Prisma Medios de Pago to pay a fine for punitive damages to a client due to their negligent handling of his claim regarding an unauthorized credit card charge. The companies failed to properly respond to the client's dispute concerning a $543.83 transaction made in Mexico, violating consumer protection laws. This decision reinforces the obligation of financial institutions to adhere to established procedures for credit card disputes and to provide dignified treatment to consumers.

title: Visa CEO Ryan McInerney sells $3.13 million in shares
summary: Visa CEO Ryan McInerney sold 8,620 shares of Visa Class A common stock for approximately $3.13 million, as part of a pre-established trading plan. Concurrently, he exercised stock options to acquire the same number of shares for about $696,668. The transactions occurred while Visa's stock was trading near its 52-week high, and the company maintains a strong financial health score according to InvestingPro.

title: DIA vs. SDY: Which State Street ETF Is the Better Dividend Stock?
summary: This article compares two State Street ETFs, SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) and SPDR S&P Dividend ETF (SDY), for investors seeking dividend income. While DIA offers better growth and overall returns due to its exposure to Dow Jones stocks and even some Magnificent 7 components like Microsoft, SDY provides a higher dividend yield and lower beta, making it suitable for income-oriented investors prioritizing stability. The choice depends on an investor's preference for growth with some income or pure income with stability.

title: Growth & Electronification Could Enhance MBS Opportunities
summary: The U.S. mortgage-backed securities (MBS) market is expanding and becoming more efficient due to electronification, making it a promising area for fixed income investors. Despite past illiquidity issues, new technological advancements are making MBS more accessible, with a significant increase in issuance to $1.1 trillion by Q3 of last year. ETFs like the Vanguard Mortgage-Backed Securities Index Fund ETF Shares (VMBS) offer an all-inclusive and cost-effective option for retail investors to gain exposure to this evolving market.

title: Earnings call transcript: Descartes Systems Q2 2025 revenue hits record high
summary: Descartes Systems Group reported record Q2 2025 revenues of $179.8 million, a 10% increase year-over-year, and record net income of $38 million. The company's adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 44.6%, driven by strong services revenue and strategic acquisitions like PackageRoute and Finale Inventory. Descartes remains debt-free with significant cash reserves and is focusing on AI and technology investments to navigate a complex global trade environment.

title: Visa and Access Bank introduce revolutionary ‘Tap to Phone’ payment solution in Nigeria
summary: Visa, a leader in digital payments, has partnered with Access Bank in Nigeria to launch 'Tap to Phone', an innovative payment solution. This service transforms NFC-enabled Android smartphones into payment terminals, allowing merchants to accept Visa payments by tapping a card to the phone. The initiative aims to enhance financial inclusion, empower small businesses, and drive Nigeria towards a more digital and inclusive financial future, building on Visa’s global efforts to support small and micro-sized businesses.

title: Live Nation Loses Bid to Narrow DOJ Ticketmaster Case
summary: A federal judge in New York denied Live Nation Entertainment Inc.'s attempt to narrow the Justice Department’s antitrust case against it, which seeks to break off Ticketmaster. The DOJ and some 30 states allege Live Nation has illegally monopolized the live events industry, controlling a significant portion of concert venues and ticketing. A trial is scheduled for March 2026.

title: Cartel Crackdown Could Hit Remitly and Western Union
summary: Remittance companies Remitly and Western Union are facing increased scrutiny and risk due to a trifecta of challenges: slowing growth in key markets, growing competition from more affordable payment options like peer-to-peer apps and cryptocurrency, and a federal crackdown on cross-border transfers linked to cartels. The Trump administration has designated cartels as terrorist groups, leading to new FinCEN restrictions and potential legal ramifications for financial institutions processing cartel-linked transactions. This heightened regulatory environment, coupled with existing competition and scrutiny over companies' pricing practices, could significantly impact the profitability and operations of these remittance providers, putting a strain on immigrants sending money home.

title: The Compound and Friends: Big Market Delusion
summary: This article announces a new episode of "The Compound and Friends" podcast, titled "Big Market Delusion." The episode, sponsored by VanEck, discusses topics including TSLA performance, U.S. equity valuations, the S&P 500 selloff, bullish European stocks, and making a case for small caps. The article also promotes the Morningstar Investment Conference.

title: Visa’s chief risk officer Paul Fabara sells $12.9 million in stock
summary: Paul Fabara, Visa's Chief Risk and Client Services Officer, sold 39,350 shares of Visa's Class A common stock for approximately $12.9 million after exercising stock options. Following these transactions, Fabara now directly holds 26,413 shares. The company has also been actively fighting fraud, preventing over $350 million in scam attempts with analyst ratings remaining largely positive.

title: Lawsuit Against Lockheed Martin Criticizes Firm for Using In-House TDFs
summary: A lawsuit has been filed against Lockheed Martin, alleging that the company violated its fiduciary duties by using underperforming, high-fee in-house target-date funds (TDFs) in its 401(k) plans for its own benefit. The plaintiffs claim that Lockheed Martin Investment Management Co. (LMIMCo), Lockheed's subsidiary, offered TDFs that were two to five times more expensive and performed worse than TDFs from independent providers like Vanguard, while also marketing them as the sole investment needed for retirement. The lawsuit seeks a declaration of breach of duties under ERISA and disgorgement of sums derived from the alleged improper transactions.

title: Galileo Is Tops Among Digital Debit Issuers, Javelin Says
summary: A Javelin Strategy & Research report ranks Galileo Financial Technologies LLC's Digital First product as the leader among digital debit card issuers, citing its flexibility, security, and scalability. The product allows consumers to use a digital card immediately while a physical card with the same details is mailed. Thales and FIS also earned strong recognition as overall leaders in the digital issuance scorecard.

title: Shark Tank’s Anupam Mittal to NPCI: Time to disrupt companies like Visa and MasterCard with UPI
summary: Anupam Mittal, judge on Shark Tank India, advocates for leveraging India's UPI system to challenge global payment giants like Visa and Mastercard, citing its costless transactions. He urges the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) to push UPI's global expansion. Meanwhile, NPCI is working to mitigate fraud by restricting the 'Collect Payments' feature.

title: Company speaks on establishing data center in Nigeria, FG react
summary: Visa Inc. plans to establish a data center infrastructure in Nigeria, reiterating its commitment to the Nigerian market with over $1 billion in investments, including $200 million in Interswitch. Vice President Kashim Shettima praised Visa's investment and assured continued government support, highlighting Nigeria's growing digital economy and fintech landscape. The move aims to introduce new technologies and bolster mobile payment services in the country.

title: Grazzy, U.S. Bank Debit Card Program Simplifies the Way Tipped Employees Earn and Receive Digital Tips
summary: Grazzy and U.S. Bank have partnered to launch a prepaid debit card program designed to simplify digital tip access for hourly employees. This initiative allows employers to issue physical debit cards, enabling employees to receive tips and wages at the end of each shift, even without traditional bank accounts. The program aims to improve financial wellness, offer flexible pay options for employees, and potentially help businesses with employee retention and cost savings.

title: In a world of flux, fundamentals (and active stock-picking) matter.
summary: This article by Justin P. White, CFA, discusses the importance of investing in high-quality, "durable compounder" companies in a world of economic and geopolitical uncertainty. These companies exhibit consistent double-digit earnings growth, pricing power, and sustainable competitive advantages, enabling them to navigate market volatility and generate superior shareholder returns over time. The author highlights examples like Hilton Hotels, Chubb, and Visa as companies possessing these key characteristics.

title: ETFs Around the World: iShares MSCI Emerging Markets ETF (IEM) vs Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets Shares ETF (VGE)
summary: This article compares two prominent Emerging Markets ETFs: the iShares MSCI Emerging Markets ETF (IEM) and the Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets Shares ETF (VGE). It examines their fund objectives, profiles, holdings, performance, distributions, and fees, highlighting that while both offer diversified exposure to emerging markets, they exhibit differences in management fees and historical returns over various timeframes. The analysis aims to help investors navigate these options for potential growth opportunities.

title: OLB Group Announces Support for Mastercard Cryptocurrency Processing
summary: The OLB Group, Inc. has announced its readiness to process Mastercard Bitcoin payments through its OmniSoft business management platform and SecurePay Payment Gateway Platform. This move follows Mastercard's support for cryptocurrency, aiming to accelerate public acceptance of Bitcoin and other digital currencies for everyday transactions. OLB's platforms support multiple cryptocurrencies and offer comprehensive payment options, including conversion to fiat currencies and direct transactions with various crypto wallets.

title: WEX SPARK Health & Benefits 2025 Gathers Industry Leaders to Drive Innovation, Business Growth
summary: WEX is hosting its SPARK Health & Benefits 2025 event in San Diego from March 31 to April 3, bringing together industry leaders to discuss innovation in the health and benefits sector. The event will focus on topics such as AI-driven insights for benefits decisions, simplifying reimbursement processes, enhancing fraud detection, and understanding policy objectives. Key features include the WEX Innovation Experience and the WEX Community Awards, recognizing industry achievements.

title: Matt McGowan Appointed Senior Vice-President, Business Solutions, Bell Media
summary: Bell Media has appointed Matt McGowan as its new Senior Vice-President, Business Solutions. In this role, McGowan, formerly of Snapchat Canada, will lead the advertising sales and partnerships strategy for Canada’s largest media and entertainment company. His extensive experience in media and technology is expected to drive Bell Media's transformation into a digital media and content leader.

title: DJD ETF Holdings List — AMEX:DJD
summary: This article provides a detailed list of the top holdings for the Invesco Dow Jones Industrial Average Dividend ETF (DJD) as of February 26, 2026. It includes the weight percentage, shares, and market value for each company held within the ETF, such as Verizon, Merck, Chevron, and Johnson & Johnson. The information offers insights into the fund's composition and its major investments.

title: Top 10: Women in Fintech
summary: This article highlights the top 10 influential women in the Fintech industry, recognizing their leadership and significant contributions. It profiles executives from major companies like Visa, PayPal, Klarna, Nasdaq, and JPMorgan Chase, detailing their roles in digital transformation, technological innovation, and financial inclusion. The piece emphasizes their impact on shaping the future of finance and technology.

title: XLF ETF Holdings List — AMEX:XLF
summary: This article provides a list of the top holdings for the State Street Financial Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLF) as of February 25, 2026. Key holdings include Berkshire Hathaway Inc. Class B, JPMorgan Chase & Co., and Visa Inc. Class A, detailing their weight percentage, shares, and market value within the ETF.

title: Why I Believe JEPI and JEPQ ETFs Are Still Strong Investments Despite a Weak Stock Market
summary: This article argues that JPMorgan's JEPI and JEPQ ETFs remain strong investment options even in a volatile stock market. These actively managed funds offer high-yield and portfolio diversification by investing in S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 stocks, respectively, and generating income through covered call strategies. While JEPI focuses on blue-chip stocks for steady income, JEPQ is more tech-focused but both aim to provide robust returns despite market downturns.

title: Why Europe is yet to see a non-AAA CLO ETF
summary: Europe has not yet seen a non-AAA CLO ETF due to restrictive regulatory challenges, despite success in the US with products like VanEck's $1bn non-AAA CLO ETF (CLOI). European regulations, particularly from the Central Bank of Ireland, require publicly listed CLO ETFs to maintain at least 80% exposure to AAA-rated tranches, making it difficult to replicate US strategies that include lower-rated securities. This regulatory environment, combined with a perceived saturation in the AAA CLO ETF space, hinders the launch of more diverse CLO ETF offerings in Europe.

title: Visa CEO Ryan McInerney sells $3 million in stock
summary: Visa CEO Ryan McInerney sold 8,620 shares of Class A Common Stock for approximately $3.02 million. This transaction occurred under a Rule 10b5-1 trading plan and near Visa's 52-week high. The article also highlights Visa's strong performance, its bid to replace Mastercard for Apple's credit card, and efforts to integrate with cryptocurrency wallets and combat scams.

title: Affirm director Keith Rabois sells $730,520 in stock
summary: Keith Rabois, a director at Affirm Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ: AFRM), recently sold 16,088 shares of company stock for approximately $730,520. Following this transaction, conducted under a Rule 10b5-1 trading plan, Rabois retains 45,432 shares. The sale occurred as Affirm's stock has declined year-to-date, despite recent positive news regarding a partnership with Stride Bank and continued optimistic analyst ratings.

title: Consumers Plan to Use Tax Refunds To Pay Down Debt, ACI Finds
summary: A survey by ACI Worldwide Inc. reveals that 39% of consumers plan to use their 2025 tax refunds to pay down credit card debt and other loans, indicating a continued focus on financial stability amidst inflation. The survey, conducted with YouGov Plc, also highlights that 44% intend to deposit refunds into savings, and a growing number of respondents prefer digital payment methods for taxes, though awareness of tax-related scams remains low.

title: VOO, SPY, IVV Shed Assets as Market Rout Continues
summary: The three largest S&P 500 ETFs—VOO, SPY, and IVV—have collectively shed billions in assets, dropping about 7% since a recent market rout began. This decline occurred despite significant inflows from investors "buying the dip," betting on a market turnaround following an initial market slump after President Trump's inauguration and subsequent tariffs. The asset managers have seen their total AUM fall from over $1.7 trillion last week to $1.6 trillion as of Wednesday, with VOO and SPY still attracting billions in new money while IVV experienced outflows.

title: Goldman Sachs Earnings: Strong Start to 2025 as Uncertainty Breeds Heightened Trading Activity
summary: Goldman Sachs Group reported a strong start to the year, driven by exceptional trading revenue due to market volatility, which offset a tepid dealmaking environment. Despite strong quarterly results, shares remain modestly overvalued, and Morningstar maintains a fair value estimate of $490 per share. The global banking and markets segment saw significant net revenue gains, while the asset and wealth management segment experienced mixed results but continued positive net inflows.

title: Europe Real-Time Payments Market Size, & Growth Report, 2033
summary: The Europe real-time payments market, valued at USD 6.52 billion in 2024, is projected to reach USD 17.45 billion by 2033, growing annually at 11.56%. This growth is driven by increasing demand for instantaneous transactions and regulatory support, despite challenges like high implementation costs and cybersecurity risks. Key market opportunities include expanding cross-border payments and integrating emerging technologies like AI and blockchain.

title: Investing in JPMorgan Equity Premium Income ETF (JEPI): A High-Yield Income Opportunity
summary: The article discusses the JPMorgan Equity Premium Income ETF (JEPI) as a high-yield income opportunity for investors. It highlights JEPI's covered-call strategy, diversified portfolio, and strong performance during market volatility, noting its current 8% forward dividend yield. While acknowledging JEPI's tax inefficiency compared to some alternatives, the article concludes that its consistent dividends and downside protection make it an attractive option for income-focused investors, especially given current market conditions.

title: Better Dividend Growth Stock: Costco vs. Visa
summary: This article analyzes Costco (COST) and Visa (V) as dividend growth stocks, highlighting their robust business models and commitment to shareholder returns. While both offer double-digit dividend growth, Visa is presented as the more compelling option due to its higher historical growth rate, lower payout ratio, and asset-light business model. However, the author suggests that including both in a diversified portfolio could be ideal for many dividend growth investors.

title: With The Final OKs, the Capital One-Discover Combo Sets a May 18 Closing
summary: Capital One Financial Corp.'s $35-billion acquisition of Discover Financial Services received its final federal regulatory approvals from the Federal Reserve and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, clearing the way for a May 18 closing. The merger, announced in February 2024, aims to increase competition in banking and payments, create a more powerful rival to Visa and Mastercard, and leverage Discover's network and credit card portfolio. However, integrating the two companies will present challenges due to their differing corporate cultures and business operations, such as customer service centers.

title: Europe Smart Card Market Size, Share,Trends & Analysis, 2033
summary: The Europe smart card market was valued at USD 3.08 billion in 2024 and is projected to reach USD 4.15 billion by 2033, growing at a CAGR of 3.35% from 2025 to 2033. Key drivers include rising demand for contactless payment solutions and government initiatives for secure identity verification, with Germany dominating the market and Spain showing the fastest growth. Challenges such as high implementation costs, cybersecurity concerns, and interoperability issues need to be addressed for continued expansion.

title: Watch Launch of New Elm Market Navigator ETF | Bloomberg ETF IQ 04/21/2025
summary: This Bloomberg ETF IQ segment discusses current market volatility, ETF flows, and asset allocation strategies, featuring Victor Haghani, CIO of Elm Wealth, and Rebecca Venter, Fixed Income Product Manager at Vanguard. Haghani introduces the new Elm Market Navigator ETF, emphasizing its tax efficiency and dynamic asset allocation approach, while Venter highlights Vanguard's active short-duration bond ETF and its role in managing portfolio duration. The discussion also touches on the concept of "safe haven" assets amidst market uncertainty and the increasing trend of fixed income ETF launches.

title: La audaz estrategia de los bancos para competir con la digitalización y las fintech
summary: Banks are reinventing themselves to compete with fintechs by developing new digital payment solutions. Banco Galicia's Nave, a payment solution initially offering QR codes for account-to-account payments, has evolved to include card payments and integrated e-commerce solutions, demonstrating how traditional financial institutions are adapting. This strategy focuses on providing comprehensive financial platforms, competitive commissions, and personalized services, especially for SMEs, and emphasizes the increasing shift towards secure digital payments over traditional methods.

title: Visa (V) Announces New $30 Billion Share Buyback Program | V Sto
summary: Visa (V) has announced a new $30 billion share buyback program, approved by its board of directors, following a previous repurchase of $4.5 billion in Q1. The company also declared a quarterly cash dividend of 59 cents per share. Wall Street analysts maintain an "Outperform" rating for Visa, with an average target price suggesting a 10.40% upside from its current price.

title: Shift4 Payments Q1 Earnings: Capitalizing On Payment Tech Growth (NYSE:FOUR)
summary: Shift4 Payments is positioned for substantial growth within the rapidly evolving payments industry, fueled by recent leadership changes and robust earnings, including a 35% year-over-year increase in Q1 payment volume. The company expects 20% organic revenue growth in 2025, driven by innovations like SkyTab, and will expand globally through the $2.5 billion acquisition of Global Blue. Despite competition, Shift4, with a $5 billion market cap, is projected to double in value over five years through both organic and inorganic growth.

title: Analysts Offer Insights on Financial Companies: OneMain Holdings (OMF) and Visa (V)
summary: Analysts have issued bullish sentiments on financial companies OneMain Holdings (OMF) and Visa (V). John Rowan of Janney Montgomery maintained a Buy rating on OneMain Holdings with a $63.00 price target, while Trevor Williams from Jefferies maintained a Buy rating on Visa with a $400.00 price target. Both companies received "Buy" or "Strong Buy" consensus ratings from analysts.

title: Why the Capital One/Discover Deal Is About Much More Than Payments
summary: The Capital One and Discover deal, recently approved by regulators, is poised to reshape not just the payments landscape but also the broader banking industry. Experts anticipate significant impacts on deposit generation, small business finance, and even a potential bid for the Apple Card portfolio. The integration of Discover's debit network, exempt from Durbin amendment restrictions, is seen as a key asset that could significantly boost Capital One's national digital banking strategy and competitive edge.

title: Sam Altman’s World Officially Launches in the U.S., Inks Partnerships with Visa, Stripe, and Match Group
summary: Sam Altman's company, Tools for Humanity, officially launched World in the U.S. with the goal of creating a "human-first identity and financial network" that verifies users as human online, especially in an age of pervasive AI. The service, which provides 16 Worldcoin (WLD) to new users in exchange for an iris scan, has secured partnerships with Visa, Stripe, and Match Group for various financial and verification services. Despite regulatory hurdles and privacy concerns, the company is focusing on expanding its network and plans to monetize through app charges, transaction fees, and mini-apps within the World platform.

title: Green Dot, Crypto.com partner for banking services
summary: Green Dot has partnered with Crypto.com to offer banking services, allowing Crypto.com customers to convert digital assets to fiat currency and access funds at Green Dot locations nationwide. This collaboration, leveraging Green Dot’s embedded finance platform Arc, also introduces an interest-earning savings account for Crypto.com users. The move further integrates Crypto.com with traditional finance, following previous partnerships with Visa and FIS.

title: Two JPMorgan ETFs that are providing a destination for risk-averse investors
summary: JPMorgan's Equity Premium Income ETF (JEPI) and Ultra-Short Income ETF (JPST) are attracting risk-averse investors by offering downside protection and income generation. JEPI aims to provide income by selling out-of-the-money options, while JPST focuses on fixed income to provide portfolio stability. These ETFs are highlighted as popular choices for investors seeking to weather market volatility.

title: Visa Q2 Earnings Top Forecasts, Adds $30B Buyback Plan
summary: Visa (NYSE: V) reported strong fiscal second-quarter 2025 earnings, surpassing analyst expectations with a 9.3% year-over-year increase in net revenue and a 10% rise in non-GAAP EPS. The company's Board of Directors also authorized a new $30 billion multi-year share repurchase program, demonstrating a significant commitment to returning capital to shareholders. Texas Pacific Land reported mixed Q2 earnings, missing EPS estimates but exceeding revenue forecasts, while announcing a $1.60 quarterly dividend.

title: Alphabet Inc. $GOOG Shares Acquired by Vestmark Advisory Solutions Inc.
summary: Vestmark Advisory Solutions Inc. significantly increased its stake in Alphabet Inc. ($GOOG) by 90.1% in Q2, acquiring an additional 21,533 shares to own a total of 45,422 shares valued at $8.06 million. Other major institutional investors like Kingstone Capital, Vanguard, and JPMorgan Chase also expanded their positions in Alphabet, with institutional investors and hedge funds now owning approximately 27.26% of the stock. Alphabet recently reported strong quarterly earnings, beating analyst estimates, and announced a quarterly dividend, while analysts maintain a "Moderate Buy" rating with an average target price of $324.81.

title: Who Owns Dave & Buster’s?
summary: Dave & Buster's Entertainment, Inc. is a publicly traded company on NASDAQ under the ticker symbol PLAY. No single entity owns the company outright; instead, ownership is distributed among institutional investors, individual shareholders, and company executives. Hill Path Capital holds the largest stake at 17.67%, with other major institutional investors like BlackRock and Vanguard also holding significant positions.

title: Apple Inc. $AAPL Shares Bought by Almanack Investment Partners LLC.
summary: Almanack Investment Partners LLC significantly increased its stake in Apple Inc. ($AAPL) by 176.3% in Q2, acquiring 38,213 additional shares and making Apple its 12th largest holding. This move comes as institutional ownership in Apple stands at 67.73%, and analysts have raised price targets for the stock, with a consensus of "Moderate Buy." Meanwhile, several company insiders have been net sellers of their shares in recent months.

title: CSM Advisors LLC Buys New Stake in NetApp, Inc. $NTAP
summary: CSM Advisors LLC acquired a new position in NetApp, Inc. (NASDAQ:NTAP) during the second quarter, purchasing 63,280 shares valued at approximately $6.74 million. Other institutional investors like Vanguard Group Inc., Ameriprise Financial Inc., UBS AM, Invesco Ltd., and Amundi also adjusted their holdings in NetApp. The article also provides details on analyst ratings, NetApp's stock performance, recent earnings, dividend announcements, and insider trading activity.

title: DowDuPont Is Splitting Into 3 Companies. Here’s Everything You Need to Know.
summary: DowDuPont is splitting into three independent companies: Dow, DuPont, and Corteva, each focusing on different chemical sectors. Dow will handle commodity chemicals, DuPont specialty chemicals, and Corteva agricultural products. The article explains the rationale behind the split, details what each new company will produce, and provides insights for investors regarding stock trading, dividends, and valuations of the individual entities post-split.

title: CES 2019: Why IBM CEO Ginni Rometty's Opening Address Delivers
summary: IBM CEO Ginni Rometty's CES 2019 keynote address effectively dissected the future of technology and business opportunities, highlighting deep data, Broad AI, and IBM's new Q System One. She emphasized the importance of ethics, transparency, and preparing society for the future through "new collar jobs" and apprenticeship programs. Rometty demonstrated IBM's commitment to inclusive growth and practical innovation in the tech space.

title: State Of American Energy 2019
summary: The "State of American Energy 2019" report, "America’s Generation Energy," highlights the crucial role of natural gas and oil in driving U.S. economic health, global security, and individual prosperity. API President and CEO Mike Sommers emphasized how this "Generation Energy" is reshaping the global energy balance, fueling manufacturing, and leading environmental progress. The report also detailed polling results showing strong American support for natural gas and oil, and panel discussions addressed infrastructure needs and the Renewable Fuel Standard.

title: Ex-Halliburton chairman Dave Lesar to start new oil-services company
summary: Former Halliburton chairman Dave Lesar is launching a new oilfield services company with funding from private equity firm CSL Capital Management. Lesar, who retired from Halliburton at the end of 2018, confirmed that his new venture will not compete with his previous company, despite having a non-compete clause. This move follows his previous remarks about wanting to remain involved in the oilfield services sector.

title: Inside Imperial Oil Limited’s 20-Acre Campus in Quarry Park
summary: Imperial Oil Limited relocated its headquarters from downtown Calgary to a 20-acre campus in Quarry Park, focusing on a community-centric corporate culture and enhanced staff interaction. The LEED Gold certified campus features five office buildings, a 750-foot "Pipeline" corridor, and amenities such as a cafeteria, wellness center, and historical displays. The design prioritizes flexibility and collaboration with wireless phones, portable laptops, and unassigned desks.

title: It's official: Chevron to buy Petrobras refinery
summary: Chevron officially announced its acquisition of Petrobras' refinery in Pasadena, marking it as Chevron's sole refinery in Texas. This move follows previous reports and coincides with expansion efforts in Chevron's Permian operations. The acquisition is a significant development for Chevron's presence in the Houston area.

title: Enterprise Products Partners closes 2018 with $4.1 billion profit amid record shipments
summary: Enterprise Products Partners closed 2018 with a $4.2 billion profit, driven by record shipments of crude oil, natural gas, and natural gas liquids. The company exceeded analyst expectations for earnings per share in Q4 but missed revenue estimates. CEO Jim Teague highlighted 23 new operational and financial records set in 2018 due to increased volumes and higher marketing margins.

title: Exxon's Darren Woods is about to do something its CEO hasn't done in 15 years
summary: ExxonMobil CEO Darren Woods is set to speak on an earnings conference call, breaking a 15-year company tradition previously held by his predecessor, Rex Tillerson. This change reflects increased pressure on Exxon after a significant stock drop and underperformance relative to peers. Woods will address fourth-quarter results, with analysts keenly watching for improvements in production, profit, refining performance, Permian basin output, and capital expenditure plans.

title: Exxon Reorganizing Exploration Units
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp announced a major reorganization of its global exploration businesses to counter years of weak oil and gas output. The restructuring will consolidate seven companies into three new entities, aiming to double profits by 2025 and better integrate upstream, downstream, and chemical segments. This move comes as CEO Darren Woods seeks to reset the company's trajectory after costly misfires under his predecessor.

title: Sempra Energy begins startup process for Cameron LNG
summary: Sempra Energy has begun the startup process for its Cameron LNG project in Hackberry, Louisiana, marking a significant step in bringing the Gulf Coast's third liquefied natural gas complex into operation. Over 8,000 workers are involved in the effort to activate the first of three production units, with the goal of shipping the first cargo within weeks or months. This venture is a collaboration between Sempra and companies from Japan and France, aiming to meet growing global demand for LNG.

title: Texas Shale Forces Big Oil Cost Revolution, Chevron CEO Says
summary: Chevron CEO Mike Wirth states that the low break-even costs in the Permian Basin are forcing Chevron, and the oil industry at large, to become significantly more efficient across all operations. He emphasizes a strategy of continuous cost discipline and preparing for lower energy prices, rather than betting on high prices. This approach allows Chevron to focus investment on high-return areas like the Permian, even as other projects are abandoned.

title: The refining top 40: Marathon moves up
summary: The merger of Marathon and Andeavor has created a new number-one independent refiner in the US, Marathon Petroleum, with over three million barrels per day of refining capacity. This makes Marathon the first North American independent refiner to join the global top 5, displacing Rosneft and pushing Valero down in rankings. The article categorizes global refiners and predicts continued growth for global NOCs, a shrinking downstream portfolio for global majors, and a potential slowdown for regional independents.

title: Canada operations
summary: ExxonMobil, through its Canadian affiliates Imperial Oil Limited and ExxonMobil Canada (EMC), conducts integrated oil and gas activities across Canada. Imperial Oil is Canada’s largest petroleum refiner and a major producer of crude oil, natural gas, and petrochemicals, while EMC focuses on offshore oil and gas projects in Atlantic Canada and holds petroleum assets in Western and Northern Canada. The company emphasizes its commitment to operational excellence, advanced technology, innovation, and career development for its employees in Canada.

title: San Patricio County approves tax incentives for Steel Dynamics mill
summary: San Patricio County officials have approved a 10-year tax abatement agreement to attract a proposed $1.8 billion Steel Dynamics flat roll steel mill. The incentives include 100% tax abatement for the first three years, dropping to 70% for years 4-10, contingent on the company meeting employment benchmarks such as creating 500 full-time jobs with health benefits. Although Steel Dynamics has not yet made a final decision on the mill's location, local leaders are actively competing to secure the project for the county.

title: Activist-shareholders-push-TransDigm-on-greenhouse-gas
summary: Activist shareholders, including representatives of the New York City comptroller and five city retirement systems, are pressuring Cleveland-based aerospace component maker TransDigm Group Inc. to adopt a policy to reduce its greenhouse gas emissions in line with the Paris Agreement. While TransDigm's board is asking shareholders to vote against the proposal, arguing their decentralized business model makes a top-down approach impractical, experts note a growing trend of investors pushing for more specific environmental, social, and governance (ESG) initiatives. Companies in energy and transportation are particularly targeted, and law firms advise proactive goal-setting to avoid shareholder-driven policies.

title: Exxon Resumes Seismic Survey in Guyana
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp has resumed seismic exploration for oil and gas off the coast of Guyana after a December incident with the Venezuelan navy. Guyana says vessels have traveled unimpeded since the incident and is promoting its oil and gas opportunities, while Exxon explores the southeast portion of the Stabroek block. The restart of operations comes amid an ongoing territorial dispute with Venezuela and discussions around a potential environmental permit for Exxon's Liza oil field development and future contracts with the Guyanese government.

title: Exxon's Cyprus gas discovery adds another giant to East Med collection
summary: ExxonMobil has made a significant gas discovery, Glaucus-1, offshore Cyprus, estimated at 5 to 8 trillion cubic feet, adding to the East Mediterranean's growing gas resources. While this solidifies the region's position as an exploration hotspot, infrastructure bottlenecks, geopolitical disputes with Turkey, and the lack of sufficient local markets complicate the commercialization and export plans for this and other regional finds. Exxon may need to collaborate with other developers like Eni and Total to support a greenfield LNG development for export.

title: Is LNG the New Oil?
summary: The global LNG market is rapidly growing, impacting international relations and geopolitical strategies due to its role in energy transformation and security. The U.S. has emerged as a significant player, influencing global LNG trade dynamics with its market-based approach and flexible contracts, leading to intense competition and shifting energy policies worldwide. This transformation has positioned LNG in international political discourse, drawing parallels to how oil has historically influenced global affairs.

title: CrossAmerica Partners Closes Out 2018 With Flurry of Activity
summary: CrossAmerica Partners LP finalized plans for 192 convenience stores acquired from Circle K's parent company, Alimentation Couche-Tard Inc., making significant progress on the dealerization process. The company also secured a new supply contract for former Jet-Pep sites and achieved $9.5 million in cost savings through synergies with Couche-Tard. CrossAmerica plans to continue growth initiatives in 2019 without requiring additional capital, focusing on fuel strategic reviews, rebranding efforts, and evaluating third-party acquisitions.

title: SASREF partners with Aon to create Leadership Development Program (QAED) to nurture Saudi talent
summary: SASREF, a joint venture of Saudi Aramco and Shell International, has collaborated with Aon to launch a specialized Leadership Development Program (QAED). This initiative aims to enhance the skills and competencies of over 90 SASREF professionals to support strategic business growth and align with Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 goal of nurturing Saudi talent. The program utilized Aon's assessment tools and executive coaching to develop leaders for long-term organizational impact.

title: Larry Prince Obituary - Sandy Springs, GA
summary: Larry L. Prince, born October 4, 1938, passed away peacefully on March 5, 2019, in Atlanta. He had a distinguished nearly 47-year career at Genuine Parts Company, including 15 years as Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, and served on numerous corporate and community boards. He is survived by his wife Sandra, son Larry L. Prince, Jr., sister Susie P. Haines, and nephew Tyrone Shelton.

title: Venezuela must pay Conoco over $8 billion - World Bank
summary: The World Bank ruled that Venezuela must pay ConocoPhillips over $8 billion as compensation for the 2007 expropriation of its oil assets by Hugo Chavez's government. This makes ConocoPhillips the largest beneficiary in claims stemming from nationalizations in Venezuela, although the company may face challenges in collecting the payment given Venezuela's history with arbitration cases and its current economic crisis.

title: Citgo, Valero try to return Venezuelan oil following sanctions
summary: Top U.S. buyers of Venezuelan oil, including Citgo and Valero, are attempting to return millions of barrels of crude due to U.S. sanctions imposed on Venezuela and its state-run oil company, PDVSA. Over 6 million barrels of Venezuelan crude are in limbo, as U.S. firms cannot pay PDVSA, and the Guaido administration lacks bank accounts to receive funds. This situation has led to stranded tankers, accumulating demurrage fees, and a scramble by PDVSA to avoid further export shortfalls amid declining oil shipments.

title: Crude by rail volumes fall as Calgary-based Imperial Oil cuts Alberta shipments
summary: Crude-by-rail shipments from Western Canada significantly dropped in February, reaching their lowest level since May of the previous year. This decline was largely attributed to Imperial Oil Ltd.'s decision to cut its rail shipments to near zero in response to the Alberta government's crude production curtailment program, which narrowed price differentials between Alberta and U.S. crude, making rail transport less economical. Imperial Oil had moved approximately 168,000 barrels per day by rail in December, nearly half of Canada's total crude-by-rail exports at that time.

title: Baker Hughes eyes LNG market for growth in 2019
summary: Baker Hughes is targeting the liquefied natural gas (LNG) market as a significant area for growth in 2019, securing high-profile contracts for turbines and equipment for new export terminals globally. The company's Turbomachinery & Process Solutions Division, which contributed over a fourth of its 2018 revenue, is focused on providing technology that enables efficient and lower-emission LNG production. Recent projects in Siberia, British Columbia, and Texas highlight the momentum in the LNG industry, with Baker Hughes anticipating substantial revenue from these ventures.

title: Aspen Oil Sands Project, Alberta- Solvent-assisted SAGD technology
summary: The Aspen Oil Sands Project in Alberta is an Imperial Oil-developed steam-assisted gravity drainage (SAGD) oil sands project employing solvent-assisted SAGD technology to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and water usage. The C$2.6bn phase one development, expected to start production in 2022, will produce 75,000 barrels of bitumen per day, with plans for a phase two expansion to 150,000 bpd. Key contractors include Babcock & Wilcox Enterprises and Acden Lakeshore Contracting.

title: ExxonMobil weighs operating in Israel, looking for off-shore oil and gas blocks
summary: ExxonMobil is considering operating in Israel, potentially becoming the first major oil company to do so. Executives from Exxon reportedly met with Israeli Energy Minister Yuval Steinitz to discuss bidding in an upcoming auction for offshore oil and gas exploration rights. The firm has already secured a $50,000 data deal from Israel's energy ministry ahead of the June auction.

title: Andrew Clyde’s Salary Hits $5.94M at Murphy USA
summary: Murphy USA CEO Andrew Clyde earned $5.94 million in total compensation in 2018, an increase from the previous year. Other top executives, including Mindy K. West and John A. Moore, also received significant compensation, as did members of the company's board of directors. The details were disclosed in a proxy statement filed with the SEC, ahead of the company's annual stockholders meeting where re-election of some board members and a non-binding vote on executive compensation are on the agenda.

title: BP already hit its methane targets. Or did it?
summary: BP announced it met its ambitious methane emissions target of 0.2 percent of total production by the end of 2018, just a year after setting it. This rapid achievement raises questions among environmental groups about the methodologies used and the transparency of the data, as they advocate for clearer demonstration and validation of such claims in the industry. The company's actions are set against a backdrop of increasing scrutiny on natural gas's climate impact and ongoing efforts to roll back federal methane regulations.

title: Exxon hires ex-BP crude oil trader in Singapore
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp has hired former BP crude oil trader Ruddin Dhilawala to enhance its trading capabilities in Singapore. This marks the company's second external hire for its Singapore crude oil trading desk since July, as part of Exxon's broader strategy to expand into energy trading by building an experienced global team and strengthening risk-management systems to boost profits.

title: Celanese names Lori Ryerkerk as new CEO
summary: Celanese Corp. announced that Lori Ryerkerk will succeed Mark Rohr as CEO, effective May 1, 2019. Rohr will transition to Executive Chairman, focusing on shareholder value and the company's 2020 growth strategy, while Ryerkerk brings 35 years of experience in petrochemicals and refining, including leadership roles at Royal Dutch Shell and ExxonMobil. Both expressed excitement about the transition and the company's future growth and performance.

title: Second Large Plastics Manufacturer — Chevron Phillips Chemical — Agrees to Report on Plastic Pollution Pellet Spills
summary: Chevron Phillips Chemical Co. has agreed to publically report on spills of pre-production plastic pellets, known as nurdles, following engagement with the Plastic Pollution Coalition member As You Sow. This agreement comes after similar action by ExxonMobil and mandates reporting on pellet loss, recovery, best practices, and supply chain engagement, with third-party auditing to verify data. The move aims to increase transparency regarding plastic pellet pollution, which is a significant source of ocean microplastic and harmful to marine life.

title: Brownsville: Three LNG Facility Projects on Track to Commence Exports in 2023-2024
summary: Three major LNG facility projects in Brownsville, including Rio Grande LNG, Texas LNG, and Annova LNG, are moving forward to begin exports in 2023-2024. These projects, located at the Port of Brownsville, involve significant investment, job creation, and environmental considerations. Regulatory approvals are progressing, with Final Investment Decisions and construction anticipated in the near future.

title: Chevron, Anadarko Beyond 'Just a Shale Deal,' as Global Options Expand
summary: Chevron announced a $33 billion merger with Anadarko Petroleum Corp., creating the No. 1 U.S. producer with expanded global natural gas and oil opportunities. The deal, valued at $50 billion including debt, significantly strengthens Chevron's position in the Permian Basin, deepwater Gulf of Mexico, and LNG export business while aiming for $2 billion in annual synergies. Analysts view this as a strategic move beyond just shale, propelling Chevron into the top echelon of global oil and gas producers.

title: Chevron Buys Anadarko
summary: Chevron Corp. has agreed to acquire Anadarko Petroleum Corp. for $33 billion, a move that significantly boosts Chevron's footprint in Permian shale oil and liquefied natural gas. The deal, valued at $50 billion including debt, is expected to enhance free cash flow and earnings per share for Chevron within a year of closing, and generate $1 billion in cost synergies.

title: Chevron vaults into new league with $33B acquisition of Anadarko, one of Colorado's largest oil and gas operators
summary: Chevron announced its acquisition of Anadarko Petroleum for $33 billion in a cash-and-stock deal, significantly expanding its operations in deepwater exploration and particularly in the Permian Basin and Delaware Basin. This move vaults Chevron from the fourth to the second-largest producer among major drillers, making it an "UltraMajor" and enhancing its LNG business and presence in Colorado. The deal, which includes a bump in stock buybacks and asset divestitures, is pending shareholder and regulatory approval and reflects a strategic move amidst volatile oil prices.

title: Chevron vaults into new league by buying Anadarko for $33 billion
summary: Chevron announced a $33 billion cash-and-stock deal to acquire Anadarko Petroleum, significantly boosting its position in the Permian Basin, Gulf of Mexico, and LNG business in Mozambique. This acquisition transforms Chevron from the fourth largest producer among major drillers to the second, creating what analysts are calling an "UltraMajor." The deal is expected to close in the second half of the year, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals, and includes plans for increased stock buybacks and asset divestitures.

title: Chevron Leaps to `Ultramajor' Oil Status With Anadarko Deal
summary: Chevron Corp. has agreed to acquire Anadarko Petroleum Corp. in a $33 billion cash-stock deal, significantly expanding its U.S. shale oil and African liquefied natural gas assets. This acquisition propels Chevron into the top tier of global energy companies, putting it on par with the production levels of Exxon Mobil Corp. and Royal Dutch Shell Plc. The combined entity's cash flow in the prior year would have surpassed Exxon's.

title: Chevron buying Anadarko, will likely take over operations of Roraima Block
summary: Chevron Corp. announced a $33-billion acquisition of Anadarko Petroleum Corp., a deal that will significantly expand Chevron's presence in U.S. shale oil and African liquefied natural gas, positioning it among the top global energy companies. This acquisition means Chevron will likely take over Anadarko's operations on the Roraima Block offshore Guyana, where Anadarko's exploration was previously halted by a Venezuelan Navy interception. The deal is expected to create a formidable competitor to ExxonMobil and Royal Dutch Shell, with Chevron planning to divest $15 billion to $20 billion in assets to reduce debt and return cash to investors.

title: Exxon Mobil makes new oil discovery offshore Guyana
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp announced a new oil discovery offshore Guyana in the Turbot area of the Stabroek Block, bringing the total estimated oil-equivalent barrels to over 5.5 billion. This marks the thirteenth discovery in the block, considered one of the largest in the world over the last decade, with partners Hess Corp and China National Offshore Oil Corporation.

title: Robots in the Permian? Climate concerns drive innovation
summary: Oil supermajors like Chevron and Exxon Mobil are heavily investing in the Permian Basin, using advanced automation, cloud computing, and AI to maximize oil extraction. This strategy is seen as a hedge against future climate change regulations and potential drops in oil demand, allowing for quick returns and flexibility. However, environmentalists criticize the focus on fossil fuels, and some experts question the feasibility of the desired automation and the long-term sustainability of shale production.

title: Allstate Insurance to create 1,300 new jobs in major expansion of Irving operations
summary: Allstate Insurance Co. plans a significant expansion of its Irving operations, creating 1,300 new jobs and investing $11 million over the next five years. The company will receive a $2.6 million grant from the Texas Enterprise Fund and up to $2.8 million from the city of Irving, contingent on job creation milestones. This expansion will make Allstate the second-largest employer in Irving.

title: Occidental Petroleum outbids Chevron for Anadarko Petroleum
summary: Occidental Petroleum has outbid Chevron for Anadarko Petroleum with a cash-and-stock offer valued at approximately $57 billion, a 20 percent premium over Chevron's $33 billion deal. This move intensifies the competition for Anadarko's assets, especially its lucrative Permian Basin position, Gulf of Mexico presence, and a natural gas project in Mozambique, amid rising U.S. crude prices. The takeover would significantly boost Occidental's position in the Permian Basin, with the company aiming to complete the combination by the end of the year.

title: New Orleans Sues Oil and Gas Companies to Preserve Wetlands, But Is That Enough?
summary: New Orleans has filed a lawsuit against 11 oil and gas companies, accusing them of destroying surrounding wetlands, similar to other suits filed by Louisiana parishes. Mayor LaToya Cantrell stated the city and its people have been harmed, with their way of life threatened by the loss of coastal wetlands. The suit alleges violations of the state's Coastal Zone Management Act of 1978, by failing to restore damage or clean up hazardous waste, contributing to the rapid land loss that exacerbated the impact of Hurricane Katrina.

title: Asphalt | bp Products and services | bp America
summary: BP America provides asphalt products and solutions for roadway construction and maintenance, operating one of the largest asphalt-producing refineries in Whiting, IN, and state-of-the-art terminals in Chicago and Bartlett, IL. They offer a range of performance-graded asphalt binders suitable for paving and industrial applications, serving customers across the Midwest, US, and Canada. The company emphasizes its expertise and customer support through an experienced sales, marketing, and technical team.

title: IEEFA Argentina: Vaca Muerta development stalled?
summary: The provincial government controlling Argentina's Vaca Muerta oil and gas reserves faces challenges in spurring serious development from concession holders, with many companies not announcing plans for increased investment as their pilot phases end. Of 13 concessions ending pilot periods soon, eight have not declared development plans, leading the government to demand action. This inaction raises concerns about Argentina's ability to meet its ambitious energy production goals and suggests some companies may be engaging in "real estate speculation" rather than active development.

title: Top 2019 GOM Equity Producers
summary: A combined Chevron and Anadarko entity would top the list of 2019 Gulf of Mexico equity producers, according to Rystad Energy, yielding over 400,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. BP plc and Royal Dutch Shell plc secured second and third positions, respectively, while Equinor ASA and Fieldwood Energy LLC rounded out the top five. The article also mentions recent acquisition activities impacting the GOM production landscape, including Chevron's bid for Anadarko and Murphy Oil Corporation's acquisition of deepwater GOM assets.

title: DowDuPont Is Splitting Into 3 Companies. Here’s Everything You Need to Know.
summary: DowDuPont, the world's largest chemical conglomerate with $86 billion in 2018 sales, is splitting into three independent companies: Dow, DuPont, and Corteva. Dow will focus on commodity chemicals, DuPont on specialty chemicals, and Corteva on agricultural chemicals and seeds. This article explains the rationale behind the split, details what each new company will produce, and offers advice for investors on understanding the upcoming changes and investment opportunities.

title: Exxon OKs $2B Baytown chemical expansion project
summary: Exxon has approved a $2 billion chemical expansion project in Baytown, Texas, which is part of its larger $20 billion "Growing the Gulf" initiative. This expansion signifies a continued investment in the region and follows several other significant projects by Exxon, as highlighted by related articles mentioning refinery expansions and LNG export projects.

title: Exxon Mobil sues Cuba for $280 million over expropriated property
summary: Exxon Mobil sued Cuba's state-owned Cuba-Petroleo and CIMEX Corp for $280 million over assets seized after Fidel Castro's revolution, becoming the first corporation to sue Cuba since the Trump administration allowed a long-dormant section of the 1996 Helms-Burton Act to take effect. The lawsuit targets a refinery, gasoline stations, and other properties, aligning Exxon Mobil with other large claimants and potentially increasing international pressure on Cuba. Cuba maintains its nationalization of property was legal and that the lawsuit violates international law.

title: Jordan Cove LNG slows spending, delays project to wait for permits
summary: Pembina Pipeline Corp., the backer of the Jordan Cove LNG project, is cutting its projected spending by half and delaying the project's startup by a year as it awaits key state and federal permits. The company plans to spend $50 million this year on the $10 billion project, down from a previous forecast of $100 million, while facing a challenging market with plummeted LNG prices in Asia and competition from other export facilities. Analysts like Robert McCullough suggest the project faces a significant cost disadvantage and question its viability given current market conditions and stronger competitors.

title: Occidental CEO Battles Oil-Field Giant to Rule the Permian Basin
Where Does the United States Export Oil?
summary: The United States' crude oil exports in 2018 were primarily directed to Canada (19%), Korea (12%), and China (11%), with the top five countries accounting for 57% of total exports. When petroleum products are included, Mexico becomes the top destination. The industry is also developing infrastructure, such as Enterprise Products Partners' new export terminal, to support increasing crude oil exports.

title: Four 3X Leveraged Oil ETFs to Get Slick With Trading
summary: Despite U.S.-China trade tensions, oil and gas operators remain optimistic about commodity prices for the rest of 2019, anticipating a price range of $65-$75 per barrel. This optimism is driving continued capital spending and potential growth. For ETF traders looking to capitalize on this outlook, the article highlights four 3X leveraged oil ETFs: United States 3x Oil (USOU), UBS ETRACS ProShares Dly 3x Lng Crud ETN (WTIU), VelocityShares 3x Lng Crude Oil ETN New (UWT), and ProShares UltraPro 3x Crude Oil ETF (OILU).

title: When fairness matters, more disclosure is key
summary: This article discusses the evolving role and scrutiny of fairness opinions in Canadian mergers and acquisitions. It highlights how courts and regulators are increasingly demanding greater disclosure, transparency regarding fee arrangements, and detailed analysis to support these opinions, moving beyond just stating independence or flat fees. The piece suggests that issuers should provide more comprehensive disclosure, methodology, and analysis to ensure their fairness opinions are robust and accepted in legal challenges.

title: Imperial Oil Resources Ltd.: 2019 Harmattan Offering
summary: Imperial Oil Resources Limited, on behalf of ExxonMobil Canada Energy, has initiated a process for the disposition of its Harmattan asset in central Alberta. The offering includes over 85,000 gross/49,000 net hectares with 2018 average production of 4,500 BOE per day, 54% liquids, primarily from Cardium, Viking, and Mississippian formations. Interested parties can access a virtual data room starting May 23, 2019, with non-binding proposals due by June 27, 2019.

title: Saudi oil giant Aramco strikes deal to buy US natural gas from Sempra Energy
summary: Saudi Aramco has signed an agreement with Sempra Energy to buy 5 million tons of liquefied natural gas (LNG) per year for 20 years from Sempra's proposed Port Arthur, Texas export terminal. This deal signifies Aramco's push to become a major player in the global gas market and provides a significant boost for Sempra in financing the multi-billion dollar facility. If finalized, it would be one of the largest LNG deals ever signed, enabling Aramco to nearly double its total gas production and compete more directly with global energy companies.

title: Suncor’s hydrogen-cyanide emissions exceeded permit last year; Colorado now weighing refinery’s request to increase limit
summary: Suncor Energy's Commerce City refinery exceeded its permit limit for hydrogen cyanide emissions in 2018, releasing 14.1 tons against a 12.8-ton limit. Colorado health officials have not penalized Suncor and are currently considering the refinery's request to increase its permit limit for hydrogen cyanide to 19.9 tons annually, raising concerns among residents and environmental advocates about air quality and regulatory oversight. The article highlights the ongoing debate between environmental concerns, community health impacts, and the state's regulatory approach to industrial pollution.

title: Plains All American enters joint venture to expand Red River Pipeline
summary: Plains All American Pipeline has formed a joint venture with Delek US to expand the capacity of its Red River Pipeline. This $128 million deal will boost the pipeline's capacity from 150,000 to approximately 235,000 barrels per day by the first half of 2020. The expansion aligns with Plains' strategy to optimize existing systems and allows Delek, an existing customer, to significantly increase its committed capacity on the pipeline.

title: Canadian Natural buys assets for $3.8-billion as Devon Energy exits Canada’s oil patch
summary: Canadian Natural Resources Ltd. is acquiring the Alberta assets of Devon Energy Corp. for $3.8-billion, marking another foreign company's exit from Western Canada's oil fields. The acquisition is expected to boost CNRL's earnings per share and free cash flow, making it Canada's largest crude producer. The deal highlights ongoing challenges for Alberta's oil industry, including limited export capacity and regulatory concerns.

title: Devon Energy Announces Strategic Exit of Canadian Business for CAD $3.8 Billion
summary: Devon Energy announced its strategic exit from its Canadian business, agreeing to sell its assets to Canadian Natural Resources Limited for CAD $3.8 billion (USD $2.8 billion). This sale is a key step in Devon's transformation into a U.S. oil growth business, with proceeds earmarked for debt reduction. The company also plans to divest its Barnett Shale gas assets by the end of 2019 to complete its focus on high-return U.S. oil plays.

title: Exxon Mobil to pay $1M to settle oil spill in Yellowstone River
summary: A judge has approved an agreement for Exxon Mobil Corp. to pay $1.05 million to settle federal pollution violations stemming from a 2011 pipeline break that released 63,000 gallons of crude oil into Montana's Yellowstone River. This settlement resolves the final federal enforcement case against Exxon regarding the incident. Exxon had previously paid $12 million for natural resource damage, $2.6 million for pipeline safety and state pollution violations, and spent an estimated $135 million on cleanup and repairs.

title: Plug and Play Announces Partnership with Phillips 66
summary: Plug and Play, a global innovation platform, announced a partnership with Phillips 66, a diversified energy manufacturing and logistics company. Phillips 66 will join Plug and Play's Energy & Sustainability platform to connect with innovative startups focusing on areas like workforce safety, operational efficiency, and supply chain. This collaboration aims to bridge Houston's energy industry with Silicon Valley's technological advancements.

title: Eni enters into cooperation pact with KazMunayGas
summary: Kazakhstan’s state-owned oil and gas company KazMunayGas (KMG) and Eni’s affiliate, Agip Caspian Sea B.V., signed a memorandum of cooperation to expand their relationship. The pact focuses on technological cooperation in hydrocarbon exploration and production, co-development opportunities, and staff training for KMG. This agreement strengthens their long-term partnership, particularly as partners in the giant Kashagan field.

title: Exxon-Sabic Texas Project to Create Nearly 7,000 Jobs
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. and Saudi Basic Industries Corp. (SABIC) are moving forward with the construction of a 1.8-million-metric-ton ethane steam cracker complex near Corpus Christi, Texas. This project is projected to create over 6,600 jobs, including 6,000 during construction and more than 600 permanent operational jobs with an average annual salary of $90,000. Construction is expected to begin in the third quarter of 2019, with startup slated for 2022, marking SABIC's first joint venture with ExxonMobil outside of Saudi Arabia.

title: Inside General Electric's moves to turn off the lights at its venture capital arm
summary: General Electric is looking to sell off its venture capital arm, GE Ventures, which has invested in hundreds of companies since its founding in 2013. The portfolio, valued at approximately $500 million, is considered to be of moderate strength and is subject to significant discounts in the secondary market. GE Ventures is effectively no longer making new investments as it seeks a buyer and evaluates strategic options.

title: Saudi’s Sabic, Exxon Mobil approve Texas chemical plant plan
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp and Saudi Basic Industries Corp (Sabic) have formally approved the construction of a new chemical complex in Texas. The project, located near Corpus Christi, will be the world’s largest steam cracker and is expected to generate $50 billion in "economic output" within its first six years. This joint venture marks Sabic's first outside Saudi Arabia and highlights the growing importance of petrochemicals as a driver for global oil and gas markets.

title: Putnam Focused Large Cap Value ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NYSEARCA:PVAL)
summary: This article provides details on the Putnam Focused Large Cap Value ETF (PVAL), an actively managed, non-transparent ETF investing in large-cap value companies in the US. It lists current price, key statistics, holdings such as Citigroup and Walmart, and recent news headlines related to the fund. The ETF launched on May 25, 2021, and is managed by Putnam.

title: Energy Investing Showdown: Midstream/MLPs vs. Majors vs. Broader Energy
summary: This article compares midstream/MLPs, integrated energy majors (like Exxon and Chevron), and broader energy investments, highlighting their defensive characteristics and performance. Midstream has outperformed this year due to its fee-based business model and resilience to commodity price volatility. The article also discusses tradeoffs in yield, oil price sensitivity, and diversification for investors considering these energy investment options.

title: 10 Things You Didn’t Know About WESCO International CEO John Engel
summary: This article details ten facts about John J. Engel, the CEO of WESCO International, highlighting his educational background, significant net worth, career milestones, and his roles in various influential business organizations. It covers his financial compensation, stock holdings, and leadership positions beyond WESCO, including directorships and memberships in prominent business councils. The article also touches upon the challenges he faced early in his CEO tenure during the Great Recession.

title: Have It All, Part 9 - Marathon Petroleum/Andeavor Logistics’ Permian Crude Gathering System
summary: This article, part of the "Have It All" series, examines Marathon Petroleum/Andeavor Logistics’ evolving crude gathering system in the Permian Basin. It discusses how the system, initially small, has grown to become a key integrated asset within its owners' larger value chain, connecting crude production to refineries or export terminals. The piece also details the complex mergers and acquisitions involving MPC, MPLX, and Andeavor Logistics that shaped the current infrastructure.

title: Anadarko approves $20 billion LNG export project in Mozambique
summary: U.S. energy firm Anadarko Petroleum Corp has approved a $20 billion gas liquefaction and export terminal in Mozambique, marking Africa's largest single LNG project. This decision was largely expected and is set to transform Mozambique's economy while positioning the project to meet growing Asian and European energy demands. The project secured long-term buyers despite a recent slump in LNG prices, demonstrating industry confidence in future demand.

title: Italian Energy Giant Rejects Suspected Iran Oil
summary: Italian oil company Eni SpA rejected a shipment of suspected Iranian crude oil, citing specifications that did not match its contract and properties consistent with Iranian crude. This incident highlights the challenges energy companies face in navigating US sanctions against Iran, due to the Iranian regime's deceptive shipping practices like ship-to-ship transfers and disabling tracking systems. The rejected cargo, originally believed to be Iraqi oil from Nigeria’s Oando PLC, had been transferred multiple times before reaching Eni.

title: Chevron Phillips Chemical in $15 billion bid to acquire Nova Chemicals
summary: Chevron Phillips Chemical (CPCHEM) has made a US$15 billion bid to acquire Nova Chemicals, a move that would make CPCHEM the third-largest polyethylene producer in North America and the largest producer of high-density polyethylene (HDPE) in the region.
