summary: Energy Transfer LP is joining other energy companies in the competitive race to construct a new pipeline that will transport natural gas from the Permian Basin to Gulf Coast export hubs. The company aims to complete its project within two years of a final investment decision, utilizing existing assets, and analysts consider their proposal to be a highly economic option for the region. Energy Transfer is also progressing with other major projects, including the Gulf Run pipeline in Louisiana and its own LNG export facility at Lake Charles.

title: Irving-based chemicals firm Celanese strikes $11 billion deal for DuPont business
summary: Irving-based chemicals company Celanese Corp. is acquiring the majority of DuPont de Nemours Inc.’s mobility and materials business for $11 billion in cash, marking one of the largest chemicals deals since 2020. This acquisition will significantly expand Celanese's engineered materials capabilities, particularly for future mobility, connectivity, and medical uses. Celanese expects the deal to add $4 or more per share to its earnings by 2026 and double its total free cash flow within five years.

title: Hubba Hubba: Appalachia Sees Continued Investment in Carbon Capture and Storage
summary: Appalachia is seeing continued investment in carbon capture and storage (CCS) with a new hydrogen and carbon capture hub planned for Ohio, Pennsylvania, and West Virginia by a coalition of major energy, petrochemical, and steel companies. This initiative aims to reduce emissions across various industries, create jobs, and drive innovation, modeling an integrated low-emission energy and production system. The region's abundant natural gas resources are key to producing blue hydrogen, a process that separates hydrogen from natural gas with the resulting carbon dioxide stored underground, showcasing Appalachia's role in a lower carbon future.

title: Skadden, Kirkland lead DuPont’s $11 bln sale of unit to Celanese
summary: DuPont has engaged Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom for its $11 billion sale of its mobility and materials business to Celanese Corp. Celanese, in turn, is being advised by Kirkland & Ellis and Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher for the acquisition and its financing. This deal marks DuPont's largest transaction since its separation from DowDuPont, as it continues to streamline its portfolio.

title: Roy Fuller Obituary - Dallas, TX
summary: Roy Lee Fuller, born March 25, 1927, passed away peacefully on February 20, 2022, at the age of 94. He had a notable career trajectory from Geophysical Services Inc. (GSI) to Texas Instruments, followed by an energetic retirement involving hardware store ownership, chamber of commerce leadership, and rural land investments. Fuller, a veteran of WWII and a gifted musician, is survived by his wife Pat, children, stepchildren, grandchildren, and great-grandchildren.

title: The Top Carbon ETF’s of 2022: Investing Ideas for Canadians
summary: This article identifies the top carbon ETFs for Canadian investors in 2022, highlighting newly available options on Canadian exchanges like Horizons Carbon Credits ETF (CARB) and Ninepoint Carbon Credit ETF (CBON). It also discusses the U.S.-based KraneShares Global Carbon Strategy ETF (KRBN) and Carbon Streaming Corporation (NETZ) as significant investments in the carbon market. The piece emphasizes the growing accessibility of carbon-related investments due to global decarbonization efforts.

title: ‘Clear signs of recovery’ – Sasol CEO
summary: Sasol reported strong operational results for the first half of its 2022 financial year, with adjusted Ebitda increasing 71% to R31.8 billion and cash flow up 60% to R27.9 billion. Despite these positive figures and "clear signs of recovery" to pre-pandemic levels, the company is retaining interim dividends due to high macroeconomic uncertainty. Sasol continues to prioritize debt reduction, aiming to repay R18.2 billion in outstanding debt by November 2022.

title: Alta do petróleo turbina arrecadação dos governos e lucros da Petrobras enquanto gasolina e diesel sobem no posto
summary: The article discusses how the rising price of oil has significantly boosted the revenue of the Brazilian federal, state, and municipal governments, as well as the profits of Petrobras, despite increasing fuel costs for consumers. In the last three years, the federal government alone accumulated at least R$123 billion from royalties, special participations, and Petrobras dividends. States and municipalities also saw substantial increases in their coffers from oil-related revenues, leading to discussions in Congress about using these extraordinary gains to mitigate the impact of higher fuel prices on consumers.

title: Marathon Petroleum Corp: What are oil workers fighting against?
summary: This article details the struggles of US oil refinery workers against Marathon Petroleum Corp. and the United Steelworkers union. It highlights Marathon's substantial profits, the impact of federal bailouts and layoffs on workers, and the demand for a nationwide refinery strike amidst stagnant wage offers and ongoing exploitation.

title: Exxon, PNG sign deal to clear way for P'nyang gas field
summary: Exxon Mobil and its partners have signed a deal with the Papua New Guinea (PNG) government to develop the P'nyang gas field, ending years of uncertainty. Gas from P'nyang will supply Exxon's LNG plant in PNG after current sources are depleted. This agreement, which secures a 63% government take, is considered a significant win for PNG and sets a new benchmark for future negotiations.

title: Texas oil refinery workers ratify Exxon labor contract offer
summary: Unionized workers at Exxon Mobil's Beaumont, Texas, refinery voted to accept a new labor contract, ending a nearly 10-month lockout. The new agreement grants Exxon the right to determine plant assignments, a key company demand, and adds Martin Luther King Jr. Day as a paid holiday. Despite the contract's approval, the United Steelworkers union plans to continue pursuing an unfair labor practices complaint against Exxon.

title: Newpark Resources settles conflict with activist investor, expands board
summary: Newpark Resources has settled a conflict with activist investor Brad Radoff, who had advocated for the company to sell off its fluid systems business. As part of the agreement, Newpark Resources will expand its board. Radoff's main concern was that the fluid systems business, which primarily serves the upstream oil and gas industry, did not turn a profit in 2021.

title: Opinion: As the stock market struggles, look at these ‘hard-asset’ commodity funds
summary: Amidst stock market struggles and escalating geopolitical tensions, "hard-asset" commodity funds are presented as a potential haven for investors. These assets, including metals, fossil fuels, and agricultural goods, are benefiting from inflationary pressures and offer a degree of stability compared to more volatile investments like small-cap growth stocks or cryptocurrencies. The article suggests that these funds could be a strategic investment during periods of market uncertainty.

title: Iraq to develop oil and gas in the Western Desert in collaboration with Halliburton Co., Saudi Aramco
summary: Iraq plans to collaborate with Halliburton Co. and Saudi Aramco to develop oil and gas reserves in its Western Desert, specifically in the Anbar province and the Akkas natural gas field. This initiative aims to reduce Iraq's dependence on oil for electricity and achieve gas self-sufficiency by 2025. The Iraqi government will cover development costs, with potential investment from Saudi Aramco.

title: El Gobierno autoriza ajustes para distribuidoras y transportadoras de gas a partir de marzo
summary: The Argentine government has authorized gas tariff adjustments for distributors and transporters, resulting in an average 20% increase for residential users and 15% for SMEs starting in March. This measure was implemented through Decree 91/2022 after public hearings and aims to reduce state subsidies that covered the difference caused by a three-year tariff freeze. The decree ratifies agreements between the Ministry of Economy, the Enargas, and gas companies, impacting factures with adjustments based on gas price, transport, distribution, and taxes.

title: Exxon's workforce falls by 9,000 in 2021 amid cost cuts
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp announced a reduction of 9,000 global employees in 2021 as a result of a comprehensive cost-cutting program initiated after the COVID-19 pandemic. This workforce reduction contributed to the company's best annual profit in seven years in 2021, following a historic loss in 2020. The company plans further restructuring, including combining refining and chemicals businesses and cutting $6 billion from operating costs by next year.

title: ExxonMobil Makes First Commercial Sale of Certified Circular Polymers
summary: ExxonMobil announced its first commercial sale of certified circular polymers, produced using its Exxtend™ advanced recycling technology, to Berry Global for food-grade packaging. The company's Baytown, Texas facility has processed over 4 million pounds of plastic waste and plans to significantly increase its global annual advanced recycling capacity to 1 billion pounds by 2026 to meet growing market demand for sustainable plastics. This move aims to expand the range of recyclable plastic materials and support a more circular economy.

title: Over the Hedge: The Best Commodities To Invest in
summary: This article explores the best commodities to invest in, including energy, metals, and agriculture, as a hedge against inflation and stock market volatility. It delves into the pros and cons of commodity investing, specific opportunities within each category like oil & gas, lithium, gold, copper, silver, palladium, hemp, and coffee, and various methods for gaining exposure to these markets. The author emphasizes diversification and understanding market factors, geopolitical risks, and extraneous events like weather.

title: Where are Houston’s Fortune 500 companies? Downtown still reigns.
summary: Downtown Houston remains the primary location for Fortune 500 companies, housing ten of the 25 located in the greater Houston area. North Houston has recently gained two major Fortune 500 headquarters with Exxon Mobil and Hewlett Packard Enterprise relocating there, while other concentrations of these companies are found in West Houston, Energy Corridor, Memorial City, Katy, and the Galleria area. The article details the specific companies and their locations, highlighting the diverse geographical distribution of Houston's top businesses.

title: Exxon, union reach tentative return-to-work deal for locked-out refinery workers -sources
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp and the United Steelworkers union (USW) have reached a tentative agreement for nearly 600 workers locked out of a Beaumont, Texas, refinery to return to work starting in March. The USW Local 13-243 is scheduled to vote on the agreement, which would end the lockout that began in May 2021. The agreement outlines the return of workers while an investigation by the U.S. National Labor Relations Board into alleged unfair labor practices continues.

title: Oil companies, union reach deal on U.S. refinery workers pact
summary: Oil companies, led by Marathon Petroleum, and the United Steelworkers union have reached a new national contract for 30,000 U.S. refinery, chemical plant, and pipeline workers. The four-year agreement includes a 12% pay increase and provisions for union health and safety representatives at each facility. Negotiations stalled earlier but resumed after union protests, leading to the new agreement.

title: bp to exit Rosneft shareholding | News and insights | Home
summary: BP announced its decision to exit its 19.75% shareholding in Rosneft due to Russia's aggression against Ukraine. Both BP-nominated directors, Bernard Looney and Bob Dudley, will resign from Rosneft's board, leading to a material non-cash charge in BP's Q1 2022 results. BP's financial framework and distribution guidance remain unchanged, but it will no longer report Rosneft's results.

title: Exxon Texas refinery lockout to end on March 7
summary: Exxon Mobil announced that a 10-month lockout of union workers at its southeast Texas refinery will end on March 7, following the United Steelworkers union's acceptance of a return-to-work agreement. The agreement allows nearly 600 locked-out workers to return, after a new six-year contract was ratified that gives Exxon control over job assignments. The union's long-term presence at the refinery remains subject to a pending NLRB investigation regarding the lockout and a vote to remove the union.

title: Shell Is Leaving Joint Ventures With Russia's Gazprom
summary: Shell announced its decision to withdraw from joint ventures with Russia's Gazprom and related entities. This move follows Russia's invasion of Ukraine and aligns with similar actions taken by other companies like BP. The departure signifies a significant response from the energy sector to the geopolitical conflict.

title: The Energy Sector: 6 Things To Know
summary: This article discusses the energy sector, highlighting its evolving nature beyond traditional oil and gas to include clean energy sources. It emphasizes the sector's continued ties to oil prices, especially in light of geopolitical events like the Russia-Ukraine crisis, and explores various investment avenues, including individual stocks, ETFs, and both traditional and renewable energy options.

title: Halliburton Opens Saudi Chemical Research Plant
summary: Halliburton has officially opened a new chemical reaction plant in Saudi Arabia. This facility will manufacture a wide range of chemicals for the oil and gas industry, as well as other sectors, and will expand Halliburton's research into specialty chemicals for oilfield stimulation and production. This investment reinforces Halliburton's commitment to Saudi Arabia and supports the local In-Kingdom Total Value Add program.

title: Exxon Mobil to exit major Russian venture, will not invest in new developments
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. announced it is halting operations of its Sakhalin-1 oil and gas venture in Russia and taking steps to exit the project. This decision comes in response to Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. Exxon Mobil stated its support for the people of Ukraine, deplored Russia’s military action, and affirmed compliance with all sanctions.

title: Exxon Mobil says it plans to leave its last remaining Russian project. (Published 2022)
summary: Exxon Mobil announced its withdrawal from its last Russian oil and gas project, Sakhalin-1, following Russia's invasion of Ukraine. This decision comes after similar moves by BP and Shell, marking the end of an era for Western oil companies in Russia. Exxon cited humanitarian reasons and safety obligations for its phased exit from the project, in which it holds a 30% stake.

title: Exxon to Shut Down Oil Production in Russia After Ukraine Attack
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. announced it is halting operations at a multibillion-dollar oil and gas project in Russia and will cease further investments in the country due to its invasion of Ukraine. The U.S. oil giant is preparing to shut down production from the Sakhalin Island development, where it holds a 30% stake alongside Russian, Japanese, and Indian partners, and plans to exit the consortium. This decision follows similar moves by other major energy companies like BP and Shell.

title: Chevron CEO points to 'difficult decisions' by competitors to leave Russia
summary: Chevron CEO Michael Wirth expressed concern over the situation in Ukraine, acknowledging the difficult decisions competitors made regarding operations in Russia. He highlighted Chevron's limited exposure to Russia and emphasized the importance of the Caspian Pipeline Consortium for world oil supply. Wirth also discussed increasing cybersecurity spending and plans for Chevron to boost oil output in the Permian shale basin and Kazakhstan.

title: Exxon Mobil to discontinue operations at Russia's Sakhalin-1
summary: Exxon Mobil announced it is beginning the process to discontinue operations and exit the Sakhalin-1 venture in Russia. The company also stated it would not be investing in any new developments in Russia. This decision follows escalating international pressure on companies to divest from Russia.

title: H2U Technologies Closes $11M in Series A Funding from Jericho Energy Ventures, Freeflow Ventures, VoLo Earth Ventures, and Hess Corporation
summary: H2U Technologies has successfully closed an oversubscribed $11 million Series A funding round, led by Jericho Energy Ventures, Freeflow Ventures, VoLo Earth Ventures, and Hess Corporation. The company plans to use the proceeds to advance its innovative electrolyzer designs and build its proprietary Catalyst Discovery Engine™, which utilizes AI to identify non-Platinum Group Metal (PGM) PEM catalysts for green hydrogen production. This development aims to significantly reduce the cost and reliance on rare earth metals for clean hydrogen, thereby accelerating the energy transition and decarbonization efforts.

title: Kinross Gold suspending Russian mining operations amid Ukraine invasion
summary: Kinross Gold Corp. has decided to suspend its mining operations and all development work in Russia due to the ongoing military invasion of Ukraine. Russia accounted for 23% of Kinross's production last year, with the Kupol mine being its most profitable operation. The company cited the safety of its 2,000+ employees and adherence to sanctions as reasons for the decision, which comes amidst broader corporate withdrawals from Russia and existing political risk concerns for Kinross's stock.

title: Alberto Fernández confirmó que el aumento del 20% en las tarifas es solo el comienzo
summary: President Alberto Fernández announced that the 20% increase in utility rates for electricity and gas is just the beginning of continuous price hikes, aligning with IMF demands. These increases, tied to salary indices, are criticized for disproportionately affecting informal workers and for not clarifying the real costs of production and distribution. The government's decision to prioritize capitalist profits and pass the burden of reduced energy subsidies onto the population is expected to lead to further mobilization from workers.

title: Exxon to exit Russia, leaving $4 bln in assets
summary: Exxon Mobil announced its decision to exit Russian oil and gas operations and halt new investments due to Moscow's invasion of Ukraine, impacting over $4 billion in assets and putting a proposed LNG facility on Sakhalin Island in doubt. This move follows similar actions by other Western companies, though Exxon's Russian business is considered relatively small within its wider enterprise. The company had been under pressure to sever ties and is now evacuating U.S. employees from the region.

title: Exxon Deplores Ukraine Attack, Begins Russia Exit, CEO Says
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. has started the process of exiting its Russian operations, including its stake in the Sakhalin-1 oil development, due to international sanctions and Russia's actions in Ukraine. CEO Darren Woods stated this would be a "complicated" process. The Sakhalin-1 asset is valued at approximately $4 billion and contributes 1% to 2% of Exxon's earnings.

title: Exxon Mobil plans to exit Russian operations following Ukraine invasion
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. announced its plan to exit operations in Russia, including its stake and operator position in the Sakhalin-1 oil field, and reverse future investments in the country. This decision comes in response to the Ukraine invasion, with the company's Russian assets valued at over $4 billion.

title: Oil Prices Drop as Iran Deal is Renegotiated
summary: Oil prices dropped to $110 per barrel after the prospect of Iranian crude returning to the market emerged amidst renegotiations of the 2015 Iran nuclear deal. The U.S. and other nations are in talks to restore the agreement, which could bring Iranian oil back, potentially offsetting Russian supply. This development has implications for funds like the Invesco DB Oil Fund (DBO), which tracks crude oil market value without direct commodity exposure.

title: Insurance giant AIG joins movement against financing Arctic oil development
summary: Insurance giant American International Group (AIG) announced it will no longer support new Arctic energy exploration, coal-fired plants, or coal mines as part of its commitment to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050. This decision has received mixed reactions in Alaska, with environmental groups like The Wilderness Society commending AIG for protecting Indigenous communities and addressing climate change, while industry alliances express disappointment, viewing the move as politically motivated and hindering responsible resource development. AIG joins other insurance companies and banks in taking similar stances against Arctic drilling.

title: Halliburton opens first-of-its-kind chemical plant in Saudi Arabia
summary: Halliburton has opened a new chemical plant in Jubail, Saudi Arabia, marking a significant investment in the country. This facility is part of the $1 billion Halliburton has invested in Saudi Arabia over the last decade. Executives from Aramco and Halliburton CEO Jeff Miller were present at the inauguration.

title: Canadian Natural Resources reports Q4 profit up, raises quarterly dividend
summary: Canadian Natural Resources Ltd. reported a significant increase in its fourth-quarter profit and raised its quarterly dividend by 28%, despite the volatile oil market exacerbated by global geopolitical events. The company emphasized a prudent, longer-term perspective on oil prices, highlighting its focus on sustainable dividend increases and strong debt reduction, with net debt decreasing by $1.9 billion. CNRL's revenue soared to $9.21 billion in Q4, and its full-year earnings reached $7.66 billion.

title: First U.S. refiner suspends purchases of Russian crude for Hawaii refinery
summary: Par Pacific Holdings Inc. has announced it will suspend purchases of Russian crude oil for its Hawaii refinery, becoming the first U.S. refiner to publicly do so after sanctions imposed due to Russia's invasion of Ukraine. The company plans to source crude from North and South America and was the fifth largest U.S. importer of Russian crude in 2021. This move comes as other Western companies halt Russian operations and the U.S. considers further sanctions on Russia's oil sector.

title: Exxon sues U.S. over taxes related to gas project in Qatar
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp has filed a lawsuit against the U.S. government seeking a partial refund of $2.1 billion in taxes and penalties. The taxes are related to a gas project in Qatar, with Exxon alleging overpayment of income taxes and misclassification of agreements. The company claims the U.S. erroneously collected taxes for tax years 2010 and 2011 and has not respected the partnership's decision to finance its venture with debt.

title: Commodity funds post hefty gains over the past week
summary: Commodity mutual funds and ETFs experienced significant gains over the last week due to rising crude oil and metal prices, intensified by the conflict between Russia and Ukraine. Key performers included ProShares Ultra Bloomberg Crude Oil, United States Oil Fund LP, and iShares S&P GSCI Commodity-Indexed Trust, with oil prices reaching 2008 highs and other commodity futures also soaring. This surge led to a net inflow of $7.9 billion into commodity funds in February, marking the largest influx since August 2020.

title: U.S. OKs 2,700,000 bbls of crude oil from SPR to ExxonMobil -statement
summary: The U.S. Department of Energy has approved the release of 2.7 million barrels of crude oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve to ExxonMobil Corp. This action is part of the Biden administration's broader initiative, authorized in November 2021, to enhance the U.S. fuel supply.

title: The Scale of Shell's Global AI Predictive Maintenance Program
summary: Shell has successfully scaled its AI-driven predictive maintenance program to monitor over 10,000 pieces of equipment globally, significantly reducing operating costs, preventing downtime, and improving safety and environmental outcomes. This achievement, made possible through a partnership with C3 AI and Microsoft Azure, involves ingesting 20 billion rows of data weekly and running over 10,000 machine learning models. Shell is now making its predictive maintenance solutions commercially available through the Open AI Energy Initiative to accelerate the energy transition across the industry.

title: How BlackRock, Vanguard, and UBS Are Screwing the World
summary: This article argues that major asset management firms like BlackRock, Vanguard, and UBS, despite controlling trillions in wealth, are hindering progress on climate change. They are heavily invested in fossil fuel and agribusiness companies, and also profit from unjust responses to crises through investments in private prisons and border security. The author contends that their business model prioritizes short-term returns and fee generation over genuine climate sustainability, necessitating comprehensive regulatory strategies and public investment to achieve climate justice.

title: GE Turbines Will Power New 2-GW Gas-Fired Plant in China
summary: GE Gas Power and Harbin Electric announced that Chinese utility Shenzhen Energy Group Corporation Co. has ordered three GE 9HA.01 gas turbines for its new 2-GW Guangming combined cycle power plant in China. This plant, expected to be operational by late 2023, will help replace the electricity output from the retiring Guangdong Shajiao coal-fired complex. The project highlights China's move towards gas-fired power generation to support its energy transition and emissions reduction goals.

title: Exxon Mobil CEO says oil companies were in tough position before Ukraine-Russia war
summary: Exxon Mobil CEO Darren Woods stated that oil companies were challenged to ramp up production to meet demand even before the Ukraine crisis due to underinvestment during the COVID-19 pandemic and reduced government support. Woods also highlighted the global energy security needs exposed by the conflict and Exxon's efforts to increase production despite also halting operations in Russia. The article touches on rising oil prices, the U.S. government's deliberation on banning Russian oil imports, and the interconnectedness of the energy industry.

title: Dow slides nearly 800 points as oil hits $120 a barrel while Russia conflict rattles investors
summary: Global stocks, including the Nasdaq, dropped significantly as oil prices surged to $120 a barrel. This market reaction was driven by investor concerns over potential sanctions on Russian crude oil and the broader economic implications of the conflict in Ukraine. The national average for gasoline also rose to $4 per gallon.

title: ANTHONY CAVANNA Obituary (2022) - Washington, DC - The Washington Post
summary: Anthony J. Cavanna, a key executive instrumental in taking Trex Company Inc. public in 1999, passed away on February 10, 2022, at the age of 82. He had a distinguished 35-year career at ExxonMobil before co-founding Trex and overseeing its financial success. Cavanna was also a dedicated alumnus of Villanova School of Engineering and was knighted for his contributions to the Belgian economy.

title: Petroleum reserve releases should double, quadruple to aid markets -Hess CEO
summary: Hess Corp CEO John Hess urged energy-consuming nations to significantly increase crude oil releases from strategic reserves to combat skyrocketing petroleum prices. He specifically called for the U.S. and IEA to release an initial 120 million barrels and commit to another 120 million barrels, stating that the previously announced 60 million barrel release was insufficient. Other energy executives, including Petronas CEO Tengku Muhammad Taufik Tengku Aziz and Exxon Mobil CEO Darren Woods, echoed concerns about high prices, supply shortages, and the need for increased investment and supportive policies in the oil and gas sector.

title: Hess CEO says oil is in the 'intensive care unit' — U.S., other nations need to act
summary: Hess Corporation CEO John Hess asserted that the oil market is in the "intensive care unit" and urged the U.S. and other nations to take immediate action to stabilize prices amidst the Russia-Ukraine war. He called on the International Energy Agency to release 240 million barrels from strategic petroleum reserves, arguing that last week's 60 million barrel release was insufficient to avert an economic recession.

title: Canada Oil Can Help Replace Russia Crude Imports to U.S.: Suncor
summary: Suncor Energy Inc. CEO Mark Little stated that Canada could supply the U.S. with a third of the oil imports the country typically receives from Russia, following the Biden administration's ban. Canadian oil executives criticized the blocking of the Keystone XL pipeline, arguing it could have helped ease prices, and questioned why the U.S. was seeking oil from OPEC countries instead of Canada. President Biden's ban targets approximately 700,000 barrels per day of Russian oil imports.

title: John Hess Built His Net Worth in the Oil and Gas Industry
summary: John Hess, CEO of Hess Corporation, has amassed a net worth of at least $440 million through his family's long-standing involvement in the oil and gas industry, founded by his father Leon Hess. He recently urged the U.S. and IEA to take more aggressive action to stabilize oil prices amidst the Russia-Ukraine war and rising petroleum costs, advocating for larger releases from strategic reserves. Hess believes these actions are crucial to prevent an economic recession.

title: ConocoPhillips CEO: Not much conversation between oil industry and Biden Administration
summary: ConocoPhillips CEO Ryan Lance stated that there was not much conversation between the oil industry and the Biden Administration before Russia invaded Ukraine, but that has since ramped up due to national and energy security concerns. Lance also cautioned that the Russia-Ukraine situation may not resolve quickly, requiring longer-term planning for energy security. While initially commenting on a potential ban on energy exports as "stupidest", the CEO and ConocoPhillips fully support President Biden's ban on Russian oil imports.

title: ConocoPhillips CEO says a decision to drill more today won't see oil flowing for up to a year
summary: ConocoPhillips CEO Ryan Lance stated that even if drilling for new oil started immediately today, it would take 8 to 12 months for the oil to begin flowing, offering no immediate relief to elevated prices. His comments followed the U.S. ban on Russian oil imports and highlighted challenges like inflation and supply chain issues impacting the oil industry's ability to ramp up production quickly. Lance also suggested that tapping into strategic petroleum reserves could provide short-term relief, but a longer-term strategy is needed for energy security given the potential for sustained high oil prices.

title: San Antonio’s Valero Energy was a big buyer of Russian oil; with new ban, it’s looking elsewhere
summary: San Antonio-based Valero Energy Corp., a major buyer of Russian crude oil, faces a new ban on imports from Russia imposed by President Biden in response to the invasion of Ukraine. The company, which purchased over 15 million barrels of Russian oil last year, will now have to seek alternative sources, likely contributing to higher gasoline prices. Analysts note the difficulty of replacing Russian crude quickly and the potential for a significant oil supply shortage.

title: McNeese LNG Center of Excellence Executive Director Named
summary: Jason French, a prominent leader and consultant in the liquid natural gas (LNG) industry, has been appointed as the executive director of the McNeese LNG Center of Excellence. This center aims to be a hub for research, workforce development, and safety in the LNG industry, partnering with the McNeese College of Science, Engineering and Mathematics. Funded by a $2.75 million grant from the U.S. Economic Development Administration, the center will provide education and training for students and industry employees.

title: 3M suspends 'all business operations' in Russia
summary: 3M announced on Wednesday its decision to suspend all business operations in Russia following the invasion of Ukraine, joining numerous other multinational companies. The Maplewood-based company has a corporate office in Moscow and two production plants in Russia, and its focus remains on the safety of its colleagues. This move aligns with U.S. sanctions and similar actions taken by rivals like Honeywell and other Minnesota-based companies.

title: Woodside and Santos soar as investors return to energy stocks
summary: Investors are re-evaluating their positions in energy stocks like Woodside Petroleum and Santos, leading to a significant increase in share prices, as global oil and natural gas prices soar due to structural underinvestment, heightened demand, and global sanctions against Russia. Analysts believe that years of underinvestment in supply, exacerbated by recent geopolitical events, point to sustained higher energy prices, despite long-term risks posed by increasing renewable energy adoption. The report also highlights the potential for further price increases unless a deal with Iran can alleviate supply pressures.

title: State Street Global Advisors CEO on ESG in the 2022 Proxy Voting Season
summary: State Street Global Advisors' CEO, Cyrus Taraporevala, and Global Head of Asset Stewardship, Benjamin Colton, discuss their 2022 proxy voting guidelines, emphasizing the long-term strategic importance of ESG factors despite global events like the Russia-Ukraine war. They highlight SSGA's "value, not values" principle, focusing on how ESG drives risk-adjusted returns, and detail increased expectations for climate transition plans and board diversity, particularly for female and underrepresented community members. The interview also touches on the evolving definition of the "S" in ESG, underscoring the significance of human capital management and the need for consistent data in ESG assessment.

title: Exxon Mobil’s lobbying report sets benchmark, ESG advocates say
summary: Exxon Mobil has released a report detailing its 2020 lobbying activities, providing investors insight into its advocacy on climate policies and establishing a new benchmark for corporate disclosure on political spending. This report, a response to a shareholder resolution, covers federal and state lobbying, as well as grassroots efforts. ESG advocates view this as a significant step towards greater transparency, though they hope for even more comprehensive disclosure in the future, including social media and election-related spending.

title: Tras la suba de YPF, Shell también aumentó los precios de los combustibles
summary: Following YPF's price hike, Shell also increased fuel prices in Argentina. This marks the second fuel price increase of 2022, with an average cumulative rise of 24.5%, directly attributed to the impact of the war in Ukraine on oil prices. Axion is expected to follow suit with its own price adjustments.

title: Celanese Corp. stock outperforms market on strong trading day
summary: Celanese Corp. (CE) shares rose 1.30% to $139.81 on Monday, outperforming the mixed stock market as the Dow Jones Industrial Average saw a slight rise and the S&P 500 Index declined. The company's stock broke a two-day losing streak but remained $36.69 below its 52-week high. Trading volume for Celanese Corp. also exceeded its 50-day average.

title: Fact check: Is the U.S. polluting the air more than ever?
summary: This article fact-checks a claim by U.S. Rep. Glenn Grothman that the U.S. has made significant strides in reducing carbon emissions compared to other countries. PolitiFact rated his claim as "True," citing data showing an 8.2 percent decrease in U.S. greenhouse gas emissions from 2010 to 2019, while countries like China and India saw increases. The article also touches on Grothman's concern that stricter U.S. environmental laws could push manufacturing jobs to countries with lower standards.

title: The Zacks Analyst Blog Highlights Chevron, Exxon Mobil, Tesla, Target Corp, and Marriott International
summary: This Zacks Analyst Blog highlights five U.S. corporate giants—Chevron, Exxon Mobil, Tesla, Target Corp, and Marriott International—as strong buy recommendations despite current market volatility, inflation, and geopolitical tensions. These companies are identified for their strong fundamentals, positive earnings estimate revisions, and solid growth potential. The article provides a detailed analysis of why each company is a compelling investment, citing their business models, market positioning, and financial outlook amidst challenging economic conditions.

title: YPF aumentó este lunes entre 9,5 y 11,5% el precio de los combustibles
summary: YPF increased the price of its basic fuels by an average of 9.5% and premium fuels by 11.5% starting this Monday. The company stated that this adjustment is due to the rise in international oil prices and demand levels exceeding those before the pandemic, which necessitate imports to supplement local supply. This marks the second fuel price hike in 2022, with the previous increase occurring in early February after an eight-month freeze.

title: Workers at Exxon Mobil refinery in Texas vote to retain USW union after lockout
summary: Workers at an Exxon Mobil Corp refinery in Beaumont, Texas, voted to keep the United Steelworkers (USW) union as their representative following a lockout. The vote count indicated that those opposing the union did not reach the majority needed for decertification, with 229 out of 495 ballots cast against the USW. This outcome allows the USW to continue representing employees at the refinery and oil packaging facility.

title: Energy ETFs Retreat as Crude Oil Dips Below $100
summary: Energy ETFs plunged as crude oil prices fell below $100, driven by waning supply fears and concerns over demand due to a spike in COVID-19 cases in China. The decline was also influenced by potential progress in the Iran nuclear deal, which could reintroduce Iranian oil to global markets, and ongoing Russia-Ukraine ceasefire talks. Additionally, China's decreased oil processing rates and the Federal Reserve's anticipated interest rate hike further weighed on the oil market.

title: Exxon Mobil loses appeal to stop climate change probes
summary: A federal appeals court has denied Exxon Mobil Corp's attempt to halt climate change investigations by Massachusetts and New York. The 2nd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals ruled that Exxon could not sue Massachusetts' Attorney General in federal court due to ongoing state-level litigation and that its case against the New York Attorney General was moot. These investigations aim to determine if Exxon misled investors and the public about its knowledge of climate change impacts.

title: When “Emperors” Preaching ESG Purport to Represent Millions of Us, a Lot Can Go Wrong
summary: This article criticizes BlackRock CEO Larry Fink's influence over corporate decisions through the voting of shares in index funds, particularly his promotion of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) investing. It argues that Fink, by advocating for ESG initiatives like reducing oil and gas investments, is misrepresenting the diverse interests of millions of mom-and-pop investors whose money BlackRock manages. The author contends that such actions can lead to unintended negative consequences, such as rising gasoline prices, which disproportionately affect low-income groups.

title: Companies like Shell and Valero are turning to Ecuador to secure oil barrels
summary: Following the U.S. ban on Russian crude imports, refiners like Valero Energy Corp., Marathon Petroleum Corp., and Shell Plc are actively seeking oil supplies from Ecuador. Ecuador's state oil company, EP Petroecuador, is holding meetings with these companies to secure mid- and long-term supply contracts, capitalizing on the high global oil prices and the urgent need to replace Russian barrels. Ecuador plans to significantly boost its oil production, with Petroecuador aiming to increase output by over 50% in four years.

title: EXCLUSIVE: Shell, Merck Animal Health back regenerative agtech Vence for carbon & traceability capabilities
summary: Vence, a US startup providing virtual fencing for ranchers using regenerative agriculture, has secured funding from Merck & Co and Shell Ventures. This investment, adding to Vence's $12 million Series A round, will facilitate partnerships to scale its offering, focusing on carbon sequestration for Shell and traceability applications with Merck Animal Health. Vence's technology supports rotational grazing and generates data for carbon credit generation and animal tracking.

title: News Content Hub - Rigs report: contracting activity jumps, Valaris drillship sustains minor damage
summary: Global offshore drilling activity significantly increased, with seven new contracts pushing the total to 351 contracted jack-ups and floaters. Maersk Drilling secured a 150-day contract for its Maersk Resolve rig, valued at US$16.9M. Concurrently, the Valaris DS-16 drillship and bulk carrier Akti sustained minor damage in a collision due to gale-force winds in Pascagoula, Mississippi, though Valaris expects no delays to its contract commencement.

title: Feeling Short on Energy? Give This Inverse ETF a Look
summary: The energy sector has seen a recent decline, with the S&P GSCI Energy index falling over 20% since March 8, creating an opportunity for bearish traders. An inverse ETF, the Direxion Daily Energy Bear 2X Shares (ERY), is presented as a way to capitalize on further weakness in the energy sector. The article notes that despite recent drops, energy has been a stellar performer and a hedge against inflation for much of the year, but ongoing negotiations regarding the Russia-Ukraine conflict could temper oil prices.

title: US oil giant Halliburton suspends operations in Russia
summary: Halliburton and Schlumberger, two major US oil field services companies, have announced the suspension of their operations in Russia due to sanctions imposed over the invasion of Ukraine. Halliburton halted future business, shipments of sanctioned parts, and has no active joint ventures, while Schlumberger ceased investment and technology deployment. This move follows similar actions by over 400 other multinational firms pressured to exit the Russian market.

title: A Saskatchewan family fights Imperial Oil over land rendered worthless by contamination
summary: A Saskatchewan family, the Browns, is embroiled in a legal battle with Imperial Oil after discovering groundwater contamination from a neighbouring fertilizer facility rendered their business property worthless. The contamination, which Imperial Oil was aware of since 2004, led to the closure of the Browns' third-generation business and a rejected line of credit application. The family is seeking to have Imperial Oil buy their land at its uncontaminated value, while the provincial government's "voluntary action" approach to contamination and slow legal process leave the Browns feeling abandoned and frustrated.

title: Baker Hughes joins Halliburton and Schlumberger in pausing Russian operations
summary: Baker Hughes announced it is suspending new investments for its Russia operations, following similar moves by rivals Halliburton Co. and Schlumberger, in response to U.S. sanctions over Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. This decision means these major oil field services companies are winding down or suspending activities in Russia, joining over 400 other multinational firms. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has urged remaining U.S. businesses to leave Russia, stating the market is "flooded with our blood."

title: Halliburton suspends future business in Russia
summary: Oilfield services company Halliburton Co has announced the suspension of its future business operations in Russia, including dealings with certain state-owned Russian customers. This decision aligns with U.S. sanctions amidst the ongoing conflict. The company also stated it has no active joint ventures in Russia and had previously halted shipments of specific sanctioned parts and products to the country.

title: Workers go on strike at California refinery owned by Chevron
summary: Over 500 workers at Chevron Corp.'s refinery in Richmond, California, initiated a strike after rejecting a contract offer the United Steelworkers union deemed unreasonable. Chevron stated that refinery operations would continue and that it does not anticipate supply chain issues, despite concerns that a prolonged strike could impact California's high gasoline prices. The dispute arose as local bargaining units negotiated specific issues beyond a national agreement for oil workers.

title: Steelworkers Walk Off Job at Chevron Richmond Refinery
summary: Over 500 workers at Chevron Corp.'s Richmond refinery went on strike due to safety concerns and demands for higher wages to combat inflation and high Bay Area living costs. The United Steelworkers union stated that the strike began after workers rejected Chevron's contract offer, which offered a 2.5% pay increase while the union sought 5%. The strike raises concerns about potential impacts on California's already high gasoline prices, though Chevron anticipates no issues in maintaining product supply with replacement workers.

title: Once the biggest importer of Russian oil, Valero looks to Latin America and elsewhere to replace it
summary: Valero, formerly the largest U.S. importer of Russian oil, is seeking new crude supplies from Latin America and other regions after voluntarily discontinuing Russian purchases due to the invasion of Ukraine. The company is actively pursuing supply contracts with countries like Ecuador to fill the void, despite market uncertainties and rising oil prices. Analysts offer mixed prospects for Valero, with some seeing potential benefits from market shifts, while others foresee a negative impact on profitability despite the company's efforts to adapt.

title: $1 billion land sale targets Permian Basin amid continued growth in oil and gas markets
summary: APA Corporation sold over $1 billion worth of Permian Basin properties and shares in its midstream company, Kinetik, last week. The Houston-based oil and gas firm cited continued growth in the U.S. market following Russia's invasion of Ukraine and the global decline in COVID-19 cases as the reason for the sale. The company plans to use the proceeds for debt reduction and investment in new drilling, while also partnering with LongPath Technologies for continuous methane monitoring in the Permian.

title: Halliburton stops new business in Russia and will wind down its operations
summary: Halliburton has announced it will stop new business in Russia and wind down its operations there, joining Schlumberger and Baker Hughes in cutting ties with Russian oil operations due to escalating sanctions and the war in Ukraine. This move by major oil field services companies is expected to significantly impact Russia's oil production, especially for more complex projects requiring Western technology. While Russia has increased its domestic service capabilities, the exit of these companies will likely hinder its ability to sustain or grow production levels.

title: Límites en la capacidad de transporte y transformaciones del downstream
summary: The article discusses the challenges and transformations in Argentina's midstream and downstream oil and gas sectors, focusing on the need to expand transport capacity for gas and crude from Vaca Muerta. Industry experts highlighted the importance of projects like the Néstor Kirchner Gas Pipeline to reduce imports, the role of underground gas storage for winter demand, and how refineries are adapting to lighter Vaca Muerta crude. The discussion also covered the increasing demand for fuel and the continued need for imports despite efforts to maximize domestic processing.

title: From electric AVs to oil: Ex-GM exec Ammann signs on at Exxon Mobil
summary: Former GM executive Dan Ammann, who previously led GM's autonomous vehicle unit Cruise, has been appointed president of Exxon Mobil Corp.'s Low Carbon Solutions business, effective May 1. Ammann's departure from Cruise in late 2021 was reportedly due to differing visions for the company's future with GM leadership. In his new role, Ammann will focus on commercializing ExxonMobil's low-emission portfolio to create shareholder value and support global emission-reduction efforts.

title: Suncor and TC Energy lobby to delay climate transparency rules
summary: Canadian oil and gas companies, including Suncor and TC Energy, are lobbying regulators to delay new climate transparency rules. These proposed regulations would mandate public companies to disclose detailed information on how climate change could impact their operations and finances. Regulators and financial experts warn that delaying these measures could lead to a "climate bubble" that destabilizes the economy, while companies cite concerns about the "burden" and complexity of such reporting.

title: Global High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE) Market to Boost in Coming Years – Projected to Reach 78.0 Million Tons by 2028 | BlueWeave Consulting
summary: The global High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE) market is projected to grow from 54.7 million tons in 2021 to 78.0 million tons by 2028, at a CAGR of 5.6%. This growth is driven by HDPE's diverse applications, including packaging, and the increasing demand for lightweight materials and developing construction sectors. The Asia-Pacific region is expected to dominate this market due to significant industrial and infrastructure development.

title: Strategy, Sustainability & Climate Presentation: TotalEnergies reports on the progress made in 2021 and expands its ambition towards Carbon Neutrality
summary: TotalEnergies presents its 2022 Progress Report on Sustainability & Climate, detailing advancements in its transformation strategy and an updated climate ambition, aligning with its commitment to reach net zero by 2050. The company made significant progress in 2021, including increased investments in renewables and a reduction in greenhouse gas emissions. TotalEnergies is expanding its ambition with new targets for reducing emissions from petroleum product sales and methane, supported by a disciplined investment policy focused on decarbonized energies and maintaining existing infrastructure.

title: Powerful clouds of methane spotted in Alabama coal country
summary: Satellite observations have revealed powerful clouds of methane near a coal-mining basin in Alabama, highlighting a significant, often overlooked, climate impact of coal. These plumes were detected near mines operated by Warrior Met Coal Inc., RJR Mining Co., and Southland Resources, with methane being a greenhouse gas far more potent than carbon dioxide in the short term. The discovery underscores the ongoing challenge of methane emissions from coal mining, which can persist even after mines are closed.

title: Exxon Mobil Powering Bitcoin Mining Pilot Using Excess Natural Gas: Report
summary: Exxon Mobil is reportedly using its pilot program to turn unspent natural gas into profit by powering a Bitcoin mining operation. This initiative, in agreement with Crusoe Energy Systems, utilizes gas from an oil well in the Bakken Formation to run mobile generators for crypto-mining servers. The oil giant is considering expanding similar projects to other locations globally to reduce waste from gas flaring.

title: KBR and ExxonMobil Catalyst to collaborate on next gen propane dehydrogenation technology
summary: KBR and ExxonMobil Catalysts and Licensing are collaborating to advance propane dehydrogenation (PDH) technology. This partnership will combine ExxonMobil's new catalyst with KBR's K-PRO Propane Dehydrogenation technology to efficiently convert propane into propylene. The collaboration aims to offer significant financial savings and reduced energy consumption for K-PRO customers, leveraging over 50 years of combined expertise in catalyst innovation and technology development.

title: No injuries reported after ExxonMobil Billings Refinery fire
summary: A fire broke out at the ExxonMobil Billings Refinery on Saturday night, March 26, and was extinguished by early Sunday morning. No injuries were reported, and all employees and contractors were accounted for. Officials are investigating the cause and assessing damages, with air monitoring showing no adverse readings in the area.

title: TGS ampliará el gasoducto Vaca Muerta Norte
summary: Transportadora Gas del Sur (TGS) will invest $60 million to expand the Vaca Muerta Norte gas pipeline, increasing its capacity by 17 million cubic meters daily. This project will connect Los Toldos and El Trapial to the Tratayén plant, addressing a key bottleneck in transporting gas from the Vaca Muerta formation. The expansion is crucial for supporting the growing natural gas production in the region, with operations expected to begin by June of the following year.

title: House Panels Have Mixed Success Getting Oil Execs to Appear
summary: Executives from several major oil companies are expected to testify at a House Energy and Commerce Committee hearing on skyrocketing gasoline prices. However, a separate hearing planned by the House Natural Resources Committee on the same issue was canceled after executives from Devon Energy Corp., EOG Resources Inc., and Occidental Petroleum Corp. declined to participate. Democrats are scrutinizing the oil industry amid rising prices and the Russia-Ukraine conflict, while the industry dismisses these concerns as "political grandstanding."

title: Trudeau Climate Plan Seeks 42% Cut in Oil and Gas Emissions
summary: Canada's Prime Minister Justin Trudeau's government aims for a 42% reduction in emissions from the oil and gas sector by 2030. This plan involves a tax credit for carbon-capture projects, details of which are expected in the upcoming federal budget. The blueprint does not yet include a specific emissions cap for the fossil-fuel industry.

title: Permian Basin land sought after by oil and gas companies Russia conflict grows fuel demand
summary: Oil and gas companies are actively acquiring land in the Permian Basin to increase production amid rising fuel demand spurred by the conflict in Russia. Orion Diversified Holdings recently purchased 320 acres in Ward County, Texas, to expand its oil and gas operations and wastewater disposal capabilities. The region is also seeing advancements in produced water recycling, driven by partnerships like Texas Pacific Land Corporation and Aris Water Solutions, to address environmental concerns and support increased drilling activity.

title: How Republic's investment in secondary plastics processing puts a 'different twist' on vertical integration
summary: Republic Services is investing in an integrated plastics recycling facility (PRF) in Las Vegas to produce over 100 million pounds of recycled plastic annually, including food-grade PET. This move represents a "different twist" on vertical integration for haulers and MRF operators, driven by growing demand for post-consumer recycled content and technological advancements conducive to more efficient plastics recovery. The initiative aims to capture more value within the recycling system and address market inefficiencies, though questions remain about its impact on existing processors and overall supply expansion.

title: Here's Where I'd Pump a Trade in Exxon
summary: The author suggests a trade opportunity in Exxon Mobil (XOM) due to the ongoing energy rally. The article recommends buying April 22, $85 calls for XOM, expecting the stock to approach $90 again in the next month. This trade is based on the belief that the energy market is still in the early stages of its rally.

title: Huge HPE Campus Acquired by Mexcor
summary: Mexcor International has acquired a 2 million-square-foot former Hewlett Packard Enterprise corporate campus in Northwest Houston, marking one of the largest transactions in the area in years. This acquisition significantly expands Mexcor's footprint, adding 66 acres and over 2 million square feet to its existing 28-acre facility, positioning the liquor and beverage distributor for continued growth and diversification into technology ventures. Meanwhile, Hewlett Packard Enterprise has relocated its global headquarters to a new facility at City Place, where Exxon Mobil is also establishing its headquarters.

title: Exxon to complete Baton Rouge, Louisiana, FCC work by April 5 -sources
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp is scheduled to complete an overhaul of a gasoline-producing fluidic catalytic cracker (FCC) at its Baton Rouge, Louisiana refinery by April 5. The 110,000-bpd PCLA 3 FCC was shut down on February 25 for planned maintenance. Additionally, the company plans to shut a 45,000-bpd diesel hydrotreater in April for work expected to last until mid-June.

title: Herschel Expansion Project, Gulf of Mexico, US
summary: The Herschel Expansion project in the deepwater Gulf of Mexico commenced operations in February 2022, with its first phase aiming to boost the Na Kika platform's production by 10,600 barrels of oil equivalent a day. BP operates the project with a 50% stake, partnered with Shell, and it involves subsea tieback of three deepwater oil wells to the existing Na Kika semi-submersible platform. The project is located in Mississippi Canyon block 520 and uses a shared infrastructure with the Manuel oil project for export to the Na Kika platform.

title: Exxon Mobil gets Guyana's approval for fourth offshore oil project
summary: Exxon Mobil has received approval from Guyana's Environmental Protection Agency to begin work on its fourth offshore oil project, Yellowtail, in the South American country. This approval allows for construction and operation, with production expected to start in 2025 and pump up to 250,000 barrels of oil and gas per day. The permit includes strict environmental conditions, such as prohibiting routine gas flaring and requiring insurance for environmental damages.

title: ‘The Future is Bleak, and the Future is Bright.’ What It’s Like to Be a Clean Energy CEO as Gas Prices Skyrocket
summary: This article interviews Jason Few, CEO of FuelCell Energy, about the challenges and opportunities for clean energy amidst rising gas prices. Few discusses the slow adoption of fuel-cell technology, the importance of government policies and cost reduction, and the role of carbon capture in achieving global climate goals. He also shares his personal clean energy commitments and thoughts on the broader energy transition.

title: Women Manufacturing Leaders Earn National Recognition
summary: Employees from nine CBIA member companies were recognized in the Manufacturing Institute’s 2022 STEP Ahead Awards, honoring 130 outstanding women in science, technology, engineering, and production fields. The awards also acknowledged emerging leaders, highlighting the industry's need to close both the 800,000 open job gap and the gender gap. This recognition aims to inspire the next generation of female leaders to pursue careers in manufacturing.

title: Exxon to invest $10 billion in massive Guyana offshore oil project
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp announced a $10 billion investment in its fourth oil production project, Yellowtail, off the coast of Guyana. This project is part of Exxon's strategy to produce up to 1.2 million barrels per day of oil and gas by 2027 from Guyana, with contributions from partners Hess Corp and CNOOC Ltd. Yellowtail is expected to produce about 250,000 barrels of oil per day starting in 2025 and will include six drill centers and up to 26 production and 25 injection wells.

title: Exxon signals record quarterly profit from oil and gas prices
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp announced that its first-quarter operating profits from oil and gas could reach up to $9.3 billion, potentially marking a seven-year quarterly record. This significant increase is attributed to the surge in oil and gas prices, particularly following Russia's invasion of Ukraine. However, potential impairments from its Russian operations could temper the final results, which are expected on April 29.

title: Executives due at gas price hearing gave $1 million to parties, candidates
summary: Six oil and gas executives scheduled to testify before a House Energy and Commerce subcommittee on gas price gouging have collectively contributed over $1 million to political candidates and parties since the 1990s, with a strong lean towards Republican causes. Pioneer Natural Resources CEO Scott Sheffield is the top donor among them, having given approximately $469,000. These personal contributions, primarily to Republican campaigns and committees, are under scrutiny as the executives prepare to discuss rising gasoline prices.

title: Canada to Approve Equinor’s $12 Billion Bay du Nord Offshore Oil Project
summary: Canada has approved Equinor ASA's $12 billion Bay du Nord offshore oil project, marking a significant win for the oil industry despite Prime Minister Justin Trudeau's climate goals. The project, located off the coast of Newfoundland, is expected to produce at least 300 million recoverable barrels of oil and create thousands of jobs, with initial production anticipated by the end of the decade. This decision comes as global energy security gains importance and amidst domestic political considerations for the Liberal Party.

title: Which Value Stocks Are Leading the Way Over Growth?
summary: Value stocks have significantly outperformed growth stocks, particularly during the first quarter of 2022, solidifying a trend that began in 2021. While surging oil prices and energy stocks contributed significantly to this rally, healthcare companies like AbbVie and consumer defensive stocks such as Costco also played major roles. Despite their strong performance, most value stocks, with the exception of oil and gas drilling companies, are not considered overvalued.

title: Exxon, Chevron paid their CEOs over $22 mln each last year -filings
summary: Exxon Mobil CEO Darren Woods and Chevron CEO Michael Wirth each received over $22 million in compensation last year, as detailed in recent securities filings. This news comes as U.S. lawmakers accuse oil companies of price gouging amidst high gasoline costs, with executives defending their actions and asserting that no single company controls fuel prices. The significant executive paychecks have drawn criticism from some Congressional members, who highlighted the disparity between CEO compensation and consumers struggling with rising expenses.

title: Royal Bank defends funding B.C.'s Coastal GasLink pipeline despite environmental concerns
summary: Royal Bank of Canada's CEO defended its funding of the Coastal GasLink pipeline amidst criticisms from investors, Indigenous groups, and environmentalists. CEO Dave McKay emphasized regulatory approvals and support from elected First Nations, while critics highlighted the pipeline's environmental impact and its challenge to B.C.'s emission reduction goals. The debate also touched on the differing views between elected and hereditary Wet'suwet'en leaders regarding land authority and the project's benefits.

title: ExxonMobil Introduces New Exceed™ S Performance Polyethylene, Enabling Converters to Rethink Film Design for Simpler Solutions
summary: ExxonMobil has launched its new Exceed™ S performance polyethylene (PE) resins, designed to simplify film formulations while enhancing performance, processing efficiency, and packaging durability. These innovative resins offer an industry-leading combination of stiffness and toughness, enabling converters to create more durable flexible packaging, increase production capacity, and facilitate solutions with sustainability benefits. The new platform addresses the complexity of modern film design, aiming to reduce scrap and improve overall customer satisfaction.

title: Delayed by Covid-19, Swanson School finally celebrates 2020 Distinguished Alumni in person, on campus
summary: The Swanson School of Engineering at the University of Pittsburgh finally celebrated its 2020 Distinguished Alumni class in person after a two-year delay due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Dean James Martin II welcomed the honorees, emphasizing that while the celebration was postponed, pride in their achievements remained strong. The event recognized a cohort of eight distinguished alumni, highlighting their leadership and contributions.

title: Sempra exec speaks of plans to expand LNG facility
summary: Sempra Infrastructure President Dan Brouillette announced plans to expand the Cameron LNG facility in Louisiana, proposing another train to export 6.75 million tons of LNG annually. The expansion is driven by global demand for natural gas and is expected to create 1,500 construction jobs and 69 permanent positions. Brouillette also highlighted the strategic importance of this expansion for European energy security and discussed a carbon storage facility in development.

title: Sin la estatización de YPF no habría ni un pozo en Vaca Muerta
summary: Axel Kicillof defends the 2012 nationalization of YPF, stating that without it, there would be no development in Vaca Muerta. He argues that the nationalization was crucial for Argentina's energy sovereignty, reversing a catastrophic decline in production under Repsol's management and making energy self-sufficiency possible. Kicillof also discusses the potential for offshore exploration and addresses criticisms regarding the nationalization, emphasizing its positive impact on the country's energy landscape.

title: BNY Mellon (BK) Infographic: Key financials and quarterly highlights
summary: The Bank of New York Mellon Corporation (NYSE: BK) reported its first-quarter 2022 earnings results. Total revenue increased by 2% to $3.9 billion, while net income applicable to common shareholders fell 19% to $699 million, and EPS dropped 11% to $0.86. Assets under management increased 2% to $2.3 trillion.

title: Chevron, other energy giants must face California climate change cases in state court
summary: A federal appeals court has ruled that lawsuits filed by six California cities and counties against ExxonMobil, Chevron Corp, and other energy companies over climate change must be heard in state court. This decision by the 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals is the third such ruling after the Supreme Court had previously allowed companies to argue for federal jurisdiction. The plaintiffs accuse the companies of creating a public nuisance and failing to warn about climate change risks, seeking compensation for related infrastructure costs.

title: U.S. Oil Economics Have Shifted. Here's Who Benefits.
summary: The article discusses how the U.S. oil industry's economics have shifted after the "drill, baby, drill" era, impacting companies like Halliburton. It suggests that while this period initially saw weak stock performance and job cuts for service providers, new beneficiaries are emerging from the changed landscape. The piece aims to explore who gains from these recent developments in the American oil sector.

title: Amid Soaring Prices, Eni Ships First Oil from Mexico Project
summary: Italy's Eni SpA, a leading private oil producer in Mexico, has begun shipping its first oil cargo from the Miamte FPSO platform offshore Tabasco, marking a significant milestone for international energy companies in Mexico. This development comes as oil prices exceed $100/bbl, with Eni aiming to ramp up its total country output to 65,000 boe/d in 2022 and 90,000 boe/d by 2025. The project highlights increasing private sector production in Mexico, even as state-owned Pemex faces declining output from mature fields.

title: Marathon Petroleum Corp. stock rises Tuesday, still underperforms market
summary: Marathon Petroleum Corp. (MPC) stock increased by 0.37% on Tuesday, closing at $90.44. Despite this gain, it underperformed the broader market, with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average both rising more significantly. The stock remained slightly below its 52-week high and showed mixed performance compared to competitors like Exxon Mobil and Chevron, which declined, while BP PLC ADR rose.

title: Exxon Mobil drilling offshore in Brazil's Sergipe/Alagoas basin with a potential of a billion barrels
summary: Exxon Mobil is drilling in Brazil's Sergipe-Alagoas basin, an area offshore that could hold up to a billion barrels of oil and gas equivalent, according to its partner Murphy Oil. This exploratory well, named Cutthroat-1, is part of nine blocks held by Exxon (50% stake), Enauta (30%), and Murphy Oil (20%). If successful, it would mark Exxon's first discovery as an operator in Brazil.

title: Amcor adds sustainable laminates to pharmaceutical packaging portfolio
summary: Amcor has expanded its pharmaceutical packaging range with new sustainable High Shield laminates. These recycle-ready options, available in paper-based and polyolefin-based materials, are designed for sachets, stickpacks, and strippacks, meeting the pharmaceutical industry's barrier and performance needs while supporting recyclability. The new laminates will initially launch in Europe to address growing sustainability requirements.

title: Manchados por el petróleo: un historial de derrames, impunidad y abusos en la Amazonía de Perú, Colombia, Ecuador y Bolivia
summary: This investigative report details over 200 sanctioning processes against 72 oil companies for environmental infractions in the Amazon regions of Peru and Colombia over the last decade, totaling more than $55 million in fines. It highlights the recurring problems of oil spills, lack of remediation, and the overlap of oil concessions with indigenous territories and protected areas. The report also notes the lack of transparency from governmental institutions in Ecuador and Bolivia regarding similar issues.

title: Oklahoma Shale Driller Chaparral Rebrands as Canvas Energy
summary: Chaparral Energy Inc. has rebranded as Canvas Energy Inc., completing a strategic transformation focused on ESG principles, efficient low-cost field operations, and sustainable free cash flow generation. The Oklahoma-based company, which emerged from Chapter 11 bankruptcy last October, aims to use its fresh assets and strong balance sheet to self-fund its new strategy. The rebranding includes a new name, logo, website, and updated corporate presentation.

title: In wild west of sustainable investing, which funds are the most responsible?
summary: The article discusses the growth and challenges of sustainable investing, noting that 2021 tested the optimism of the previous year. It highlights the increased scrutiny on ESG funds due to greenwashing concerns and the emerging standards for transparency and disclosure. Corporate Knights conducted research on over 1,000 ETFs and mutual funds to identify top performers in financial and sustainability metrics.

title: Chevron Corp. stock falls Thursday, underperforms market
summary: Shares of Chevron Corp. (CVX) fell by 4.61% on Thursday, closing at $164.58, significantly underperforming the broader market, as the S&P 500 Index and Dow Jones Industrial Average also experienced declines. The stock closed $10.18 below its 52-week high and also underperformed a competitor, Exxon Mobil Corp. (XOM). Trading volume was below its 50-day average.

title: Exxon sees carbon capture market at $4 trillion by 2050
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. projects the carbon capture and storage (CCS) market to reach $4 trillion by 2050, representing about 60% of its estimated oil and gas market for the same period. The company is investing in this technology as a key emissions reduction strategy amid public pressure, with Occidental Petroleum also seeing CCS as a significant future industry.

title: Gasoducto Néstor Kirchner: beneficios e impactos de largo plazo de la obra que transportará el gas de Vaca Muerta
summary: The article details the benefits and long-term impacts of the Néstor Kirchner Gas Pipeline, a crucial project for Argentina's energy development. This pipeline will transport gas from Vaca Muerta, aiming to improve domestic supply, reduce reliance on imported fuels, and enable gas exports to neighboring countries. The project is divided into three stages, designed to progressively increase transport capacity to 39 million cubic meters per day.

title: Woodside CEO Meg O’Neill on how a travel bug drew her to the oil and gas sector
summary: Woodside CEO Meg O'Neill has navigated a challenging period in her first eight months, dealing with a $63 billion merger, controversy over a $US12 billion gas project, a global energy crisis, and increasing ESG pressures. This article highlights her experience leading Australia's largest oil and gas producer through these significant events.

title: Gasolina brasileira é a 2ª mais cara entre os maiores produtores de petróleo; Governo Bolsonaro dolarizou preços dos combustíveis
summary: O Brasil, apesar de ser o nono maior produtor de petróleo, possui a segunda gasolina mais cara entre os principais produtores, ficando atrás apenas da Noruega. A dolarização dos preços dos combustíveis, implementada inicialmente no governo Temer e mantida por Bolsonaro, além do desmonte da Petrobras e a redução da capacidade de refino, são apontados como as principais causas para os preços recordes no país. Isso resulta em um impacto significativo na renda do trabalhador brasileiro, que gasta uma parcela muito maior de seu salário para abastecer o tanque em comparação com países como Noruega e Estados Unidos.

title: Global X launches Europe’s first uranium industry ETF
summary: Global X has launched Europe's first ETF providing exposure to the uranium industry, the Global X Uranium UCITS ETF, listed on the London Stock Exchange and Deutsche Börse Xetra. This launch comes as uranium prices have surged due to global climate initiatives and the ongoing war in Ukraine, which has highlighted nuclear power's role as a bridging fuel and created potential supply chain strains. The ETF tracks the Solactive Global Uranium & Nuclear Components v2 Index, investing in companies involved in uranium mining, exploration, and related technologies, reflecting strong interest in the sector seen in Global X's US-listed uranium ETF.

title: Republic Services landfill near Pearland houses one of nation's largest renewable natural gas plants
summary: Republic Services' Blue Ridge Landfill near Pearland is home to one of the nation's largest renewable natural gas (RNG) operations. This plant, developed with Morrow Energy, leverages landfill gas to produce renewable natural gas. The facility is a significant contributor to clean energy efforts, according to EPA data.

title: ExxonMobil Receives Top Certification for Methane Emissions Management for Natural Gas from Permian Basin
summary: ExxonMobil announced that natural gas from its Permian Basin facilities at Poker Lake, New Mexico, has received the highest "A" grade certification from MiQ for methane emissions management. This marks the first time a company has achieved this certification for natural gas produced alongside oil, helping ExxonMobil meet customer demand for energy with fewer emissions. The company plans to expand this certification process to other operating areas and is selling commercial volumes of this certified natural gas, with Xcel Energy as a key customer.

title: AIFC Green Finance Centre expresses its readiness to provide services to transnational companies
summary: The AIFC Green Finance Centre presented its services for sustainable financial instruments and ESG transformation to the Kazakhstan Association "Foreign Investors’ Council." The Centre is prepared to act as a single operator for external reviews of green and social projects for companies in Kazakhstan and will participate in the upcoming Plenary meeting focusing on decarbonization and the Astana Finance Days conference.

title: PEP Earnings: Key quarterly highlights from PepsiCo’s Q1 2022 financial results
summary: PepsiCo (NASDAQ: PEP) reported strong first-quarter 2022 earnings, with net revenues growing 9.3% to $16.2 billion and organic revenue up 13.7%. Net income attributable to PepsiCo more than doubled to $4.2 billion, or $3.06 per share, compared to the prior-year period. The company exceeded both top and bottom-line estimates and provided an optimistic outlook for fiscal year 2022, projecting 8% organic revenue growth and a 6% increase in core EPS to $6.63.

title: Exxon makes three new oil discoveries in Guyana and boosts reserves
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp announced three new oil discoveries off the coast of Guyana, increasing its recoverable oil and gas potential to nearly 11 billion barrels. These discoveries further solidify Guyana's role as a key source for Exxon's future production, with the company and its partners aiming to produce 1.2 million barrels per day from the Stabroek block by 2027. Guyana plans to utilize the oil proceeds for significant infrastructure and energy projects, highlighting the economic impact of these finds.

title: Documents show Spire scrambling for survival of St. Louis pipeline after court ruling
summary: This article details how Spire Inc. engaged in assertive marketing and political lobbying to ensure the survival of its 65-mile STL Pipeline after a court ruling questioned its necessity. The company warned of heat outages for 400,000 customers, obtained a temporary operating permit, and simultaneously worked to undermine the transition to renewable energy. The article also highlights Spire's legal battles with property owners and its broader fight against electrification, which it sees as an "existential threat" to its profits from residential gas sales.

title: Cenovus Energy triples dividend as profits soar with crude prices
summary: Cenovus Energy reported a significant increase in its quarterly profit, exceeding analyst expectations, and subsequently tripled its dividend. This surge in profitability is attributed to rising crude prices, exacerbated by global supply concerns following Russia's invasion of Ukraine. The company also announced plans to return a significant portion of its excess free funds flow to shareholders and raised its capital expenditure forecast for 2022 due to increased refinery rebuilding costs.

title: Qué pasa con el gasoducto Néstor Kirchner; la obra pública más importante de esta gestión
summary: The article discusses the status of the Néstor Kirchner gas pipeline, considered Argentina's most important public work of the current administration. It details the reasons for its importance, the delays in its construction, and the challenges regarding its financing. The pipeline is crucial for increasing gas transport capacity from Vaca Muerta and reducing reliance on imported LNG.

title: Walmart Boosts Fuel Discount for Premium Members
summary: Walmart is expanding its fuel discount program for Walmart+ members, offering up to 10 cents off per gallon at participating stations. The discount will now be available at 12,000 Exxon and Mobil stations, in addition to Walmart and Murphy's stations and Sam's Club locations.
