title: Reborn Coffee scales down IPO size. Here’s what you need to know
summary: Reborn Coffee has decided to scale down its IPO to $17 million, deviating from its original plan to offer units comprising one common share and one warrant. The company, headquartered in Brea, California, plans to list on the Nasdaq under the symbol REBN and intends to use the IPO proceeds primarily for expanding its store network and opening 20 company-operated outlets within a year. Despite experiencing significant growth in revenues in 2021, the company also incurred a higher loss, and its future prospects will depend on the evolving pandemic situation.

title: E3 Lithium Receives TSXV Approval and Closes Agreement with Imperial Oil
summary: E3 Lithium announced it received TSX Venture Exchange (TSXV) approval and closed its agreement with Imperial Oil. The company issued over 3.4 million prepaid warrants to Imperial Oil Limited for CAD $6.35 million and also issued common shares and paid a finder's fee for the transaction. This agreement will help advance E3 Lithium's Clearwater Lithium Project development.

title: Darren Aronofsky’s Climate Series “Black Gold” Exposes ExxonMobil Cover-Up
summary: Darren Aronofsky's climate series "Black Gold" investigates ExxonMobil's alleged three-decade-long cover-up regarding climate change. The docuseries features former ExxonMobil scientists and politicians, including Al Gore, who speak about the company's efforts to sow doubt about climate science for profit. It also delves into the history of the Global Climate Coalition and its role in opposing climate action, such as influencing the US withdrawal from the Kyoto Protocol.

title: CenterPoint's Lesar tops list of Houston's best-paid corporate executives in male-dominated lineup
summary: CenterPoint Energy CEO David Lesar was the highest-paid executive among Houston public companies in 2021, earning $37.8 million, largely due to a turnaround at the company. Eight of the top ten highest-paid executives were from the energy sector, reflecting the industry's rebound. The average compensation for these top executives rose 9.5 percent in 2021, and the list remained male-dominated.

title: How is the stock market doing? See which Houston companies are up and down the most in 2022
summary: The stock market saw rapid changes in the first half of 2022, with the S&P 500 down 21 percent, but energy stocks in Houston generally performed well. In contrast, consumer-focused companies faced declines due to inflation and rising interest rates. The article highlights the biggest gainers and losers among Houston-based companies, with NexTier Oilfield Solutions leading the gains and Conn's experiencing the largest decline.

title: “No nos reten”: el enojo de Gustavo Petro frente a Ecopetrol, ¿qué pasó?
summary: President-elect Gustavo Petro has expressed his intent to change Ecopetrol's direction, even suggesting modifying its statutes. His statements came after an article discussed Ecopetrol's corporate governance and protections for shareholders. This move is seen as a way for the new government to implement its agenda, including a shift towards cleaner energies and away from fossil fuel exploration, despite concerns from the finance minister-designate and market volatility affecting Ecopetrol's stock.

title: Hilcorp, Exxon and Conoco Top Greenhouse Gas Emitters, Environmental Groups Say
summary: A new report by environmental nonprofits Ceres and the Clean Air Task Force identifies Hilcorp Energy Co., Exxon Mobil Corp., ConocoPhillips, and Occidental Petroleum Corp. as the leading emitters of planet-warming greenhouse gases in the U.S. oil-and-gas industry. Based on federal data, the report also notes these companies are the top emitters of methane, a potent greenhouse gas of growing concern due to its heat-trapping capabilities.

title: Pioneer, Devon and ConocoPhillips Join OGMP 2.0, Commit to Leading Methane Performance and Increased Transparency in Emissions Reporting
summary: Pioneer Natural Resources Company, Devon Energy Corp., and ConocoPhillips have joined the Oil and Gas Methane Partnership (OGMP) 2.0 Initiative, committing to enhanced transparency in methane emissions reporting and reduction. This move aims to establish a global standard for methane performance and demonstrate their dedication to climate mitigation and responsible energy production. The companies express their commitment to leveraging this framework to advance their emissions reduction goals and encourage industry-wide improvements.

title: Hilcorp Energy, Exxon Mobil and ConocoPhillips release the most greenhouse gasses among U.S. oil and gas companies
summary: According to a new report based on U.S. government data, Hilcorp Energy, Exxon Mobil, and ConocoPhillips are the leading emitters of greenhouse gases among 303 U.S. oil and gas companies that report to the EPA. While these companies rank high in absolute emissions, they often emphasize emissions intensity, which measures emissions per unit of energy produced, as a more accurate reflection of their efforts to decarbonize. The report, commissioned by Clean Air Task Force and Ceres, highlights a significant divergence in emissions intensity among producers, underscoring the role of operational decisions in climate impact.

title: Hedge funds bet on Brazil oil and gas output surging 122%
summary: Hedge funds and investors are increasingly backing "junior producers" in Brazil's oil and gas sector, seeking alternatives to the turmoil-prone state-owned Petroleo Brasileiro SA. These junior companies are acquiring fields divested by Petrobras and are projected to significantly boost Brazil's oil and gas output, with ANP forecasting a 122% increase by 2025 from these assets. Despite risks like market volatility and past bankruptcies, investors see substantial profit potential due to anticipated production growth and attractive share prices.

title: Taiwan edge AI company Gorilla Technology IPO surges 123% on first day of Nasdaq trading
summary: Taiwanese edge AI company Gorilla Technology Group saw its IPO surge 123% on its first day of Nasdaq trading, closing at US$33.43 under the ticker "GRRR." The company plans to use the proceeds from its business combination with Global SPAC Partners for working capital and international expansion, aiming to form a "Smart City Diverse Industry Alliance" to expand global markets for edge AI analytics solutions. Gorilla Technology has developed its edge AI technology over 20 years, holding 31 patents, and provides comprehensive video-centric and content management solutions across various sectors with key partnerships including Softbank, Intel, and Dell.

title: Sasol Outage Means All South African Oil Refineries Are Now Shut
summary: Sasol Ltd. has declared force majeure on petroleum product supplies due to crude delivery delays at its Natref refinery, co-owned with TotalEnergies SE. This outage effectively shuts down almost all of South Africa's oil refining capacity, following a series of similar closures across the country. The temporary closure significantly impacts the nation's fuel production.

title: Oilsands companies exploring nuclear power to reduce emissions
summary: Oilsands companies are increasingly exploring small modular reactors (SMRs) as a means to reduce emissions and transition away from natural gas for heat generation. While SMR technology is not yet commercially available, its proponents suggest it could be a viable solution within the next decade, with the Pathways Alliance consortium actively investigating its potential. However, the economic viability and regulatory hurdles, including securing government financial support, remain key challenges for widespread adoption in the oilsands.

title: Halliburton Q2 Income Surges As Global Drilling Activity Rises
summary: Halliburton reported a significant surge in its second-quarter adjusted net income, increasing by 41% to $442 million. This growth was driven by rising drilling activity in both North America and international markets, with North American revenue specifically climbing 26%. The oilfield services provider anticipates multiple years of growth in international markets, and its CEO noted strong margin expansion due to increased activity and pricing gains across its service lines.

title: Brazil's Petrobras set to cut gasoline prices Wednesday
summary: Brazil's state-run oil company Petrobras announced it would cut gasoline prices at its refineries by about 5% on Wednesday, marking its first price reduction since late 2021. This decision, influenced by political pressure ahead of an upcoming election, will bring average prices down to 3.86 reais per liter and has led analysts, including JPMorgan, to revise down Brazil's inflation outlook for the year. Petrobras stated the cut aligns with its policy of pegging domestic fuel rates to international prices while allowing for variation during volatility.

title: Production at Brazil's Petrobras falls; refinery utilization nears 100%
summary: Petrobras's oil production decreased in the second quarter due to asset divestments and increased maintenance stoppages, with crude production falling by 5.2% quarterly and 5% annually. Despite the decline, the company maintained its 2022 production guidance and saw its refinery utilization rate reach 97% by the end of June. Petrobras warned of significant planned refinery stoppages in the second half of the year, particularly in Q4.

title: ConocoPhillips eyes U.S. Gulf of Mexico exit -sources
summary: ConocoPhillips is reportedly exploring a sale of its stake in the Ursa platform and Princess subsea well in the U.S. Gulf of Mexico, signaling its exit from deepwater energy production in the region. This move aligns with the company's strategy to divest assets, targeting $4 billion to $5 billion by the end of 2023, as it shifts focus to the Permian Basin. The divestment, potentially valued in the high hundreds of millions of dollars, would further solidify Conoco's presence as a major Permian operator.

title: Mountain Express Oil Grows in the Northeast
summary: Mountain Express Oil Inc. has expanded its presence in the Northeast by acquiring The Store brand from Team Schierl Cos., which includes 26 convenience stores in Wisconsin and Michigan. They also formed a strategic partnership with VM Petro, a New York-based wholesale petroleum product distributor, to further growth in the region. These moves align with Mountain Express Oil's vision for national expansion, leveraging new and existing relationships within the industry.

title: The Ethical Investor: ESG funds are quietly buying oil and gas stocks to chase return
summary: ESG funds, after years of avoiding the fossil fuel sector, are now reportedly investing in oil and gas stocks to capitalize on strong returns, especially given the energy sector's recent gains in the S&P 500. This shift is justified by some experts who argue that owning these stocks can facilitate engagement with management to improve environmental practices, rather than divesting entirely. However, Australian ESG funds have generally underperformed their benchmarks this year due to their allocation towards tech over energy stocks, though long-term performance for responsible investing remains promising.

title: Earnings: Schlumberger (SLB) Q2 profit rises as revenues grow 20%
summary: Schlumberger Limited reported strong Q2 2022 results with revenues up 20% year-over-year to $6.8 billion, and adjusted earnings increasing by 67% to $0.50 per share. All four operating segments experienced double-digit growth, driven by increased upstream activity and service pricing. The company expects full-year 2022 capital investment to rise by 18% to $2 billion, signaling continued momentum in the multi-year upcycle.

title: ConocoPhillips considers exit from US Gulf of Mexico
summary: ConocoPhillips is reportedly considering selling its minority stake in the Shell-operated Ursa platform and the Princess well in the US Gulf of Mexico, a move that would mark its exit from US offshore operations. This potential sale, valued in the high hundreds of millions of dollars, is driven by ConocoPhillips's recent focus on expanding its footprint in US shale basins, particularly the Permian. The company may retain the assets if a suitable offer is not received.

title: C&EN’s Global Top 50 chemical firms for 2022
summary: C&EN's 2022 Global Top 50 chemical firms survey reveals a significant recovery for the chemical industry in 2021, with combined sales jumping 38% to $1.1 trillion for the 50 largest companies. This surge was primarily driven by the world economy's rebound from the COVID-19 pandemic and rising commodity prices, especially in petrochemicals and fertilizers. The article highlights key corporate strategies, including investments in sustainability, specialized chemicals, and battery materials, while several firms adjust portfolios by divesting commodity businesses or expanding in Asia.

title: U.S. becomes top LNG exporter in first half of 2022 - EIA
summary: In the first half of 2022, the United States became the world's leading exporter of liquefied natural gas (LNG), increasing its supply to Europe amidst the ongoing conflict in Ukraine. U.S. LNG exports rose by 12%, driven by expanded export capacity, higher prices, and strong demand, particularly from European nations seeking to diversify their energy sources. Although a fire at the Freeport LNG facility temporarily reduced exports in June, the U.S. is expected to continue increasing its LNG export capacity in the coming years.

title: Cheniere and PTT Sign Long-Term LNG Sale and Purchase Agreement
summary: Cheniere Energy, Inc. has announced a 20-year Sale and Purchase Agreement (SPA) with PTT Global LNG Company Limited (PTTGL) for 1.0 million tonnes per annum (mtpa) of LNG, starting in 2026. This agreement signifies PTTGL's first direct LNG contract with a U.S. producer and highlights the growing global need for reliable long-term LNG supply. PTT aims to expand its LNG portfolio to 9 mtpa by 2030, reinforcing its commitment to energy security and sustainability.

title: Rig activity shows Scott Saxberg, former Crescent Point CEO, is back drilling in southeast Saskatchewan
summary: Scott Saxberg, former CEO of Crescent Point Energy, is actively drilling in southeast Saskatchewan with his new company, Cache Island Corp. Cache Island's strategy combines oil and gas resources with renewable assets to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 while maximizing profits. Saxberg, known for building Crescent Point into a major producer, left the company in 2018 and has since focused on this new hybrid energy model.

title: Exxon accelerates production in Guyana, makes two new discoveries
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp announced two new oil discoveries offshore Guyana and has surpassed its original year-end daily production target for the country, reaching 360,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. These efforts are part of Exxon's strategy to accelerate production and invest in long-term, lower-cost, and lower-carbon emission megaprojects. Guyana has become a key region globally for oil discoveries, with an estimated 11 billion barrels of recoverable oil found to date.

title: Equinor second quarter 2022
summary: Equinor reported strong second-quarter 2022 adjusted earnings of USD 17.6 billion and USD 5.00 billion after tax, driven by high production and elevated energy prices due to Russia's invasion of Ukraine. The company also announced a significant increase in capital distribution, including a higher extraordinary cash dividend and an expanded share buy-back programme. Equinor is progressing its energy transition strategy through investments in low-carbon initiatives and exited all joint ventures in Russia during the quarter.

title: ‘Not the same oil industry.’ Record profits don’t create jobs.
summary: Despite record profits, the oil industry's employment levels have not returned to pre-pandemic highs, indicating a structural change driven by technology adoption and consolidation. While the industry faces challenges in finding qualified workers, it is also embracing new technologies like remote drilling and drones, which are reducing the need for traditional oil field jobs and shifting demand towards a more diverse, high-tech workforce. Companies like Halliburton, Baker Hughes, and Schlumberger are prioritizing efficiency through technology and responding to investor pressure for returns, rather than focusing on job growth.

title: 10 Big Named Companies With Huge Free Cash Flows @Ycharts
summary: This article identifies ten large-cap companies that exhibit high free cash flow relative to their market capitalization, using the Price to Free Cash Flow (P/FCF) metric. It explains that P/FCF is a robust valuation tool as it considers free cash flow, which accounts for capital expenditures, providing a more accurate view of a company's available cash. The list includes companies like JPMorgan Chase, Pfizer, and Apple, detailing their market cap, free cash flow, and P/FCF ratios.

title: Indonesian ExxonMobil accusers get day in court after 21 years
summary: A US judge has ruled that a case alleging human rights abuses against ExxonMobil can proceed to trial, allowing 11 Indonesian villagers to finally have their day in court after more than two decades. The villagers accuse the oil giant of complicity in torture, sexual assault, and beatings by Indonesian military security guards at an ExxonMobil plant in Aceh Province in the late 1990s and early 2000s. ExxonMobil denies the claims, stating the company strongly condemns human rights violations in any form and is reviewing the decision.

title: Cheniere, NextDecade Each Clinch LNG Contracts for Asian Deliveries
summary: Cheniere Energy Inc. and NextDecade Corp. have secured new long-term LNG supply contracts with Asian partners. Cheniere signed a 20-year deal with Thailand's PTT Public Co. Ltd. for 1 million metric tons/year, with exports potentially starting in 2026. NextDecade executed a similar 20-year agreement for 1 mmty with ExxonMobil's Asian LNG marketing arm from its Rio Grande LNG project.

title: Exxon Accelerates Production in Guyana, Makes Two New Discoveries
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp announced two new oil discoveries offshore Guyana and that it has already exceeded its original year-end daily production target for the South American country. The U.S. major is now producing more than 340,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, with partner Hess reporting current production at 360,000 boepd. These discoveries, Seabob and Kiru-Kiru, bring the total to over 30 and reinforce Guyana's growing role as a global oil power.

title: NextDecade to supply LNG to Exxon Mobil from Texas Rio Grande plant
summary: NextDecade Corp announced a 20-year agreement to supply 1 million tonnes per annum (MTPA) of liquefied natural gas (LNG) to a unit of Exxon Mobil Corp from its proposed Rio Grande LNG export project in Texas. Commercial operations for the first liquefaction train are expected to begin as early as 2026. This deal comes amid increased global demand for alternative gas supplies following Russia's invasion of Ukraine, prompting NextDecade to anticipate a positive final investment decision on up to three trains in the second half of 2022.

title: Hess Upping Bakken Production as Global Oil Markets Seen Tightening to Year’s End
summary: Hess Corp. plans to significantly increase its Bakken Shale production in the second half of 2022, bringing 50 new wells online to capitalize on a tightening global oil market. The company anticipates global oil markets will become even tighter due to growing demand, lagging supply, and potential sanctions on Russian oil. Hess projects annual production growth of over 10% for the next five years, driven by its Bakken and Guyana assets.

title: Commodity markets: A short and long-term perspective
summary: This article provides an analysis of commodity markets from both short-term and long-term perspectives, noting a recent decline in broad-based commodity prices, particularly in energy and industrial metals. It suggests that while near-term volatility will persist due to global uncertainties, commodities could offer timely hedging opportunities for investors, especially given ongoing inflation and geopolitical risks. The article also highlights the role of precious metals as portfolio diversifiers.

title: Energy ETFs Surged as Chevron, Exxon Enjoyed Record Quarterly Profits on High Oil Prices
summary: Energy sector ETFs saw significant gains following record quarterly profits announced by Exxon Mobil (XOM) and Chevron (CVX). Both companies reported their highest-ever earnings, attributing success to high crude oil prices, strong supply/demand dynamics, and strategic investments. These results led to a surge in energy-related ETFs like XLE and VDE, with Chevron and Exxon shares also climbing.

title: Big oil's quarterly profits hit record $50 billion, with BP yet to come
summary: Major oil companies, including Exxon Mobil, Chevron, Shell, and TotalEnergies, reported a combined record profit of $51 billion in the second quarter, largely due to high fuel prices and a rebound in economic activity. Instead of significantly increasing oil and gas output, these companies are prioritizing shareholder returns through massive share buyback programs, despite criticism and calls from governments and consumers for increased investment in production to alleviate soaring energy costs. This strategy reflects a focus on capital discipline and a long-term shift towards low-carbon energy, while also facing government pressure regarding windfall taxes.

title: Petrobras y Ecopetrol anuncian descubrimiento de gas natural en aguas profundas de Colombia
summary: Petrobras and Ecopetrol have announced the discovery of natural gas in the Uchuva-1 exploratory well in Colombian Caribbean deep waters. This finding is significant for Colombia, as it reaffirms the Caribbean region as a major source of gas for the country, crucial for over 10 million Colombian families. The discovery comes as Colombia's proven gas reserves increased slightly from 7.7 to 8 years between 2020 and 2021.

title: Exxon and Chevron Report Record Profits on High Oil and Gas Prices
summary: Exxon Mobil and Chevron reported record profits in the second quarter of 2022, driven by soaring oil and gas prices resulting from geopolitical events and economic recovery. Exxon's income reached $17.9 billion, and Chevron's profit more than tripled to $11.6 billion. These robust earnings, which are expected across other major Western oil companies as well, are likely to intensify political pressure on the industry to increase production and help reduce consumer costs.

title: Exxon, Chevron post blowout earnings, oil majors bet on buybacks
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp and Chevron Corp reported record revenues bolstered by surging crude oil and natural gas prices, following similar results from European majors. Exxon posted a $17.9 billion quarterly profit, the highest for any international oil major in history, leading the U.S. pair, along with Shell and TotalEnergies, to combine for nearly $51 billion in the recent quarter. The companies are increasingly betting on share buybacks, with Exxon more than doubling its projected buyback program to $30 billion through 2022 and 2023.

title: U.S. Cities and States Are Suing Big Oil Over Climate Change. Here’s What the Claims Say and Where They Stand.
summary: At least 20 pending lawsuits have been filed by U.S. cities and states against major fossil fuel companies, alleging they misled the public about climate change. These lawsuits primarily focus on claims that companies failed to disclose their knowledge of fossil fuels' environmental impact, using legal tactics previously seen in tobacco and pharmaceutical litigation. While most cases are still in jurisdictional battles, some recent federal court decisions have supported state jurisdiction, potentially encouraging more states to file similar suits.

title: Exxon, Chevron Post Blowout Earnings, Oil Majors Bet on Buybacks
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp and Chevron Corp reported record revenues and profits due to surging crude oil and natural gas prices, with Exxon posting an all-time high quarterly profit for an international oil major. The major oil companies, including Shell and TotalEnergies, returned $23 billion to shareholders through buybacks, capitalizing on high margins, while facing criticism from politicians and consumer advocates over soaring profits amid high consumer fuel prices. Companies argue prices reflect global supply issues and underinvestment rather than gouging, resisting increased capital expenditure in favor of shareholder returns.

title: South Korea plans to expand renewable energy sources with nuclear
summary: South Korea aims to achieve its net-zero 2050 target by expanding both nuclear power generation and other renewable energies. The country plans to increase nuclear's share to 30% of power by 2030 and phase out coal-fired plants, despite a current high dependence on imported energy and a recent global rise in commodity prices. While reducing reliance on Russian oil and LNG, South Korea still faces challenges in fully diversifying its coal import portfolio amidst international competition.

title: ExxonMobil deal boosts Brownsville liquified natural gas project
summary: ExxonMobil's recent agreement to purchase 1 million tons of liquified natural gas annually for 20 years from NextDecade Corporation's Rio Grande LNG facility in Brownsville marks a significant step forward for the long-stalled project. This deal helps secure crucial financing despite years of market uncertainty and ongoing opposition from local environmental and human rights groups. The project aims to capitalize on abundant West Texas natural gas to meet global demand, exacerbated by recent geopolitical events impacting energy security, particularly in Europe.

title: Hafnia tanker involved in bunker oil spill in Mississippi River
summary: A Hafnia tanker, Hafnia Rhine, discharged an estimated 9,500 litres of bunker oil into the Mississippi River near Kenner, Louisiana, during a fuelling operation with a fuel barge. The US Coast Guard is overseeing the clean-up efforts with National Response Corp and Environmental Safety and Health Consulting Services, which have deployed containment and sorbent booms. Hafnia immediately activated its Vessel Response Plan and is cooperating with federal and state agencies, with the cause of the discharge still under investigation.

title: Executive Viewpoint: The solution to our energy crisis does exist
summary: Jeremy D. Thigpen of Transocean Ltd. argues that the solution to the current energy crisis, characterized by high prices and geopolitical risks, is to safely and responsibly produce more oil and gas. He highlights that years of underinvestment and pressure to transition away from hydrocarbons have led to supply exceeding demand, despite global consumption projections indicating continued reliance on these energy sources. Thigpen emphasizes the need for increased capital investment in traditional energy, regulatory support, and public advocacy to ensure energy security and meet global demand, while also urging the development of all energy sources to prevent future crises.

title: Eni plans second LNG platform offshore Mozambique as Europe seeks gas
summary: Eni SpA is planning a second liquefied natural gas (LNG) production vessel offshore Mozambique to help Europe diversify its gas supplies. This potential project could be built in less than four years and would complement Eni's existing Coral-Sul FLNG platform. European nations are seeking new energy sources due to Russia's invasion of Ukraine, making timely development crucial for both Europe and Mozambique.

title: TechnipFMC Wins Contract for Gas to Energy Project in Guyana
summary: TechnipFMC has been awarded a "significant" contract by ExxonMobil's affiliate in Guyana for the Gas to Energy Project. This project involves the engineering, procurement, construction, and installation of subsea risers and pipelines to connect offshore FPSOs to a gas-fired power plant on shore, with startup expected by the end of 2024. The pipeline will transport up to 50 million standard cubic feet per day of natural gas, supporting Guyana's energy needs.

title: Ohio-based Marathon Petroleum reports profits soar amid high fuel prices during second quarter
summary: Marathon Petroleum reported a significant increase in profits during the second quarter of 2022, with its per-barrel profit margin tripling amidst high fuel prices. The company's adjusted net income reached $5.7 billion, up from $437 million in the same period last year, and Marathon refined at 100% capacity to meet strong demand. CEO Michael Hennigan attributed high prices to outside factors and noted the company's efforts to drive down costs.

title: How a little-known stock soared 21,000% to overtake Costco
summary: AMTD Digital, a previously little-known Hong Kong-based financial services startup, saw its stock surge by 21,000% since its IPO less than a month ago, becoming the latest focus for Reddit traders on WallStreetBets. This dramatic rise, which saw its market cap surpass Shell and Costco, echoes the GameStop and AMC frenzies of January 2021. The company itself stated it was unaware of "material circumstances" driving the sudden increase.

title: ‘Grotesque greed’: UN chief Guterres slams oil and gas companies
summary: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has condemned the "grotesque greed" of oil and gas companies, urging governments to tax their excessive profits to aid vulnerable populations. He highlighted that it is immoral for these companies to make record profits during an energy crisis while impacting the poorest and the climate. Guterres stressed that the funds from such taxes should support those struggling with the global food, energy, and finance crises exacerbated by the war in Ukraine and climate breakdown.

title: Italy’s Eni plans second LNG platform off Mozambique as Europe seeks gas
summary: Italy's Eni is planning a second liquefied natural gas (LNG) production vessel off Mozambique to help Europe diversify its gas supplies. This new platform would complement the existing US$7-billion Coral-Sul FLNG platform, which is set to begin exporting fuel this year. The project's progression depends on agreement from partners including ExxonMobil and China National Petroleum.

title: News Content Hub - Rigs report: Transocean inks US$1.2Bn in deals; Valaris contract backlog passes US$500M
summary: Transocean secured over US$1.2 billion in new contracts for its ultra-deepwater drillships, including a 5.8-year deal with Petrobras for the Petrobras 10000 and a two-year contract for Deepwater Conqueror in the US Gulf of Mexico. Valaris also announced new contracts and extensions totaling approximately US$560 million, with a significant 540-day contract from Equinor for Valaris DS-17 working offshore Brazil. The article also highlights active rig counts remaining stable, along with other significant contracts awarded to Stena Drilling, Aker Solutions, TechnipFMC, and Saipem by various energy majors.

title: Mexican-American Advisor Managing $1.9 Billion Helps Clients At Morgan Stanley Diversify Away From Energy
summary: Arturo Karakowsky, a Mexican-American Managing Director at Morgan Stanley Wealth Management overseeing $1.9 billion in AUM, focuses on diversifying his Houston-based clients away from a heavy concentration in the energy sector. He emphasizes the importance of diversity within his 12-person team and his own background as an asset. Karakowsky is bullish on a long-term outlook for fixed income, equities, and alternatives, despite expecting short-term market volatility.

title: Top House Democrat probes oil company earnings
summary: House Energy and Commerce Chair Frank Pallone has launched an inquiry into the record profits of major oil companies, including Exxon Mobil, Chevron, Shell, and BP, demanding information on how they are utilizing these earnings. This comes as the UN Secretary-General criticized the industry's "grotesque greed" and called for governments to tax the profits. Oil companies defended their actions, citing investments in production and refining capacity, while also acknowledging consumer struggles with high energy costs.

title: Nauticus Robotics Announces Contract with Shell
summary: Nauticus Robotics has secured a contract with Shell to advance the qualification phase for a more efficient method of acquiring subsea integrity data using Nauticus' Aquanaut and Hydronaut robotic platforms. This collaboration aims to provide significant cost savings and improve subsea data collection through supervised autonomy and advanced robotic capabilities. The partnership will focus on remote operations and integration with leading inspection tooling service providers.

title: 2 reasons why I'd pick Woodside shares over Santos
summary: The author prefers Woodside Energy Group Ltd (ASX: WDS) shares over Santos Ltd (ASX: STO) due to two main reasons: a significantly larger expected dividend yield in the coming financial years and Woodside's substantial investment in green energy projects. Woodside is projected to offer grossed-up dividend yields of 15.8% for FY22 and 12% for FY23, compared to Santos's 6.8% and 7.3% respectively. Additionally, Woodside's $5 billion investment in green energy, including hydrogen and solar projects, is seen as a key aspect of future-proofing the company.

title: Producing zero-emission hydrogen with natural gas
summary: Williams recently invested in Aurora Hydrogen, a company focused on technology that converts natural gas to hydrogen without carbon dioxide emissions. This investment supports Williams' strategy to leverage natural gas for decarbonization and will help scale Aurora Hydrogen's production to a demonstration plant by 2023. The technology promises to reduce global CO2 emissions significantly while using less electricity and not requiring water.

title: Oklahoma City energy companies report quarterly profits topping $1 billion
summary: Oklahoma City's major energy companies, including Devon Energy, Continental Resources, and Chesapeake Energy, reported over $1 billion in quarterly profits, driven by high oil and gas prices. These companies have boosted shareholder payouts through increased dividends and share repurchases, while facing political pressure to increase supply and ongoing industry challenges like labor shortages. Despite recent drops in oil prices, the region's energy activity and state tax revenues from production remain strong.

title: Gaseous Helium Market SWOT Analysis by Key Players: Airgas, Buzwair, Exxon Mobil
summary: HTF Market Intelligence Consulting Pvt. Ltd. has released a new research study titled "Gaseous Helium Market - Global Trends, Insights to 2028." The report evaluates market risks, highlights opportunities, and provides strategic decision-making support, covering trends, growth drivers, technologies, and investment structures. Key players identified include Air Liquide SA, Air Products & Chemicals, Inc., Airgas, Buzwair, Exxon Mobil Corporation, Gazprom, Gulf Cryo, Iwatani Corporation, Linde AG, Messer Group GmbH, PGNiG (PL), Praxair Inc., Somatrach, and Weil Group Resources, LLC.

title: Imperial Oil continues to investigate pipeline spill in the Northwest Territories
summary: Imperial Oil is investigating a pipeline spill of approximately 55,000 litres of produced water in Norman Wells, N.W.T., which occurred on July 27. While the company states there is no risk to public health or wildlife, residents downstream in Fort Good Hope have removed their fish nets as a precautionary measure due to observed sheens on the water. The Canada Energy Regulator is following up on the incident and plans an environmental inspection.

title: Corporations Join the Nuclear Fusion Craze
summary: Major corporations like Google, Chevron, and Sumitomo are investing in nuclear fusion technology, indicating a growing belief in its potential as a viable source of clean energy. This corporate interest coincides with a broader resurgence of nuclear energy, as Europe considers green bonds for the power source and Germany rethinks its nuclear facility shutdown plans amidst an energy crisis. Silicon Valley, in particular, is embracing nuclear fusion as a future source of abundant, cheap, and clean energy.

title: Yum! Brands (YUM) has what it takes to satisfy investor appetite
summary: Yum! Brands (YUM) showed positive revenue performance in Q2, primarily driven by Taco Bell, despite weakness in KFC and Pizza Hut and challenges in Russia and China. Despite recent earnings misses and market volatility, observers suggest buying and holding the stock due to its competitive dividend, global scale, and digital capabilities. The company's Q2 revenue increased 2% to $1.63 billion, with adjusted earnings down 9% annually to $1.05 per share.

title: Exxon Mobil's Nigeria asset sale hits regulatory hurdle
summary: Nigeria's petroleum regulator has rejected Exxon Mobil's $1.28 billion sale of its Nigerian unit shares to Seplat, despite President Muhammadu Buhari's approval, citing regulatory matters. The Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) maintains that the petroleum minister's consent relies on the commission's recommendation, and they had previously declined the deal. This regulatory hurdle, further complicated by an objection from state firm NNPC Limited, underscores the challenges in implementing Nigeria's new petroleum law and oil majors' efforts to exit shallow water operations.

title: Strive Launches U.S. Energy Index Fund (DRLL) to Deliver a New Shareholder Mandate to U.S. Energy Companies
summary: Strive Asset Management has launched its U.S. Energy ETF (DRLL), aiming to refocus American energy companies on long-term profitability and increased oil and gas production, rather than ESG-driven political agendas. The firm plans to use its shareholder engagement to push for maximizing shareholder value by capitalizing on global energy demand. Strive anticipates significant appreciation in U.S. energy stocks due to factors like easing lockdown policies and supply shortages.

title: Meet the energy and climate bigwigs with White House access
summary: This article details the increased in-person meetings between Biden administration officials and energy executives, environmental leaders, and other stakeholders. Visitor logs reveal discussions between top White House advisers like Brian Deese and Gina McCarthy with CEOs from Chevron and Exxon Mobil, as well as various utility and environmental group representatives. These meetings provide insight into the efforts to shape the administration's energy and climate policies.

title: DHT Holdings assigns $25 mln for scrubber retrofits
summary: Crude oil tanker company DHT Holdings is investing $25 million to retrofit eight additional vessels with scrubbers, bringing their total scrubber-fitted fleet to 23 vessels. This investment is driven by the expectation of higher fuel price spreads and will be funded with existing liquidity. The company also reported a significant increase in net profit for Q2 2022, primarily due to higher tanker rates, and expressed optimism about the market outlook despite ongoing crew change difficulties.

title: Luque disertará sobre transición energética en Neuquén
summary: Comodoro Rivadavia's mayor, Juan Pablo Luque, will speak at the Expo Oil & Gas in Neuquén, an event that gathers key figures in the hydrocarbon industry. He will discuss energy transition, a topic he anticipates will be further explored at a forum in Comodoro in October. Luque aims to highlight the regional importance of hydrocarbons, propose a hydrogen law, and diversify energy production to align with global sustainability trends.

title: YPF acelerará construcción de planta de gas al avanzar megaducto en Vaca Muerta
summary: Argentina's largest hydrocarbon producer, YPF, plans to fast-track the construction of a gas processing plant due to increased transport capacity from the Vaca Muerta megaduct. The company has revised its 2022 capital expenditure projection upward by 10% to approximately US$4 billion, primarily for the gas plant, additional shale well drilling, and inflation adjustments. YPF aims to begin construction this semester, ahead of its original 2025 schedule, and is also advancing an oil pipeline project to connect its shale assets to refining facilities and an export pipeline to Chile.

title: Nigerian president withholds approval of Exxon Mobil's asset sale
summary: Nigeria's President Muhammadu Buhari has revoked his initial approval for Exxon Mobil's $1.28 billion sale of local offshore shallow water assets to Seplat. This reversal came after the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission expressed its opposition to the deal without providing a reason. The decision is being closely watched by other oil majors in Nigeria, who are also looking to divest from shallow water operations due to community disruptions and a desire to focus on deep-water drilling.

title: The Inflation Reduction Act Includes a Bonanza for the Carbon Capture Industry
summary: The Inflation Reduction Act significantly boosts the carbon capture industry by increasing tax credits for capturing CO2 from polluting sources to $85 per metric ton and for removing CO2 directly from the atmosphere to $180 per ton. This legislation, along with prior infrastructure investments, is expected to drive substantial growth in the sector, despite skepticism from environmentalists regarding the technology's effectiveness and its implications for fossil fuel companies. The new incentives are also likely to fuel local controversies, particularly concerning the construction of CO2 pipelines.

title: Antitrust rules, Petro-Canada profits may hinder Suncor from selling unit
summary: Suncor Energy is considering selling its Petro-Canada gas station business, which could yield over $8 billion and appease activist shareholders. However, Canadian antitrust regulations and the division's stable profits, which hedge against volatile oil prices, could complicate or deter such a sale, making it difficult to achieve an optimal price. Analysts and shareholders suggest that Suncor's public stress about the sale might also lead to lower offers.

title: Oil Outages In Gulf Of Mexico Are Straining An Already Tight Market
summary: Oil outages in the Gulf of Mexico, caused by a leak at a Louisiana booster station that halted Shell's Amberjack and Mars pipelines, are exacerbating an already tight global energy market. Shell has since completed repairs and is ramping up production at its Mars, Ursa, and Olympus fields, while Chevron and Equinor also saw disruptions. The incident underscores the fragility of oil supply at a time when global demand is accelerating and inventories remain below the five-year average.

title: Oil and gas exploration leads to new wells in Oklahoma
summary: Several energy companies have reported new successful oil and gas wells across Oklahoma, including significant production from Continental Resources, Ovintiv Mid-Continental, and Marathon Oil Company. These wells are located in counties such as Carter, Garvin, Kingfisher, Caddo, Ellis, McClain, and Custer, with impressive daily yields of oil and natural gas. The article details the specific production rates, depths, spud dates, and completion dates for many of these new wells.

title: Shell Makes Gas Discovery at Colombia's Deepest Offshore Well
summary: Shell has announced a gas discovery at the Gorgon-2 well in ultra-deep waters off the southern Colombian Caribbean coast. This well, drilled to a depth of approximately 2,400 meters, is the deepest in Colombian waters and confirms the extension of a 2017 discovery. Shell and Ecopetrol are 50/50 partners in the South Caribbean blocks, and this discovery is expected to boost Colombia's energy security and potential for future gas exports.

title: Colombia Enters Unchartered Waters
summary: In June 2022, Gustavo Petro became Colombia's first leftist president, leading to uncertainty among business communities due to his campaign promises of radical economic policy changes, particularly in the extractive sector. While Petro's proposed reforms for the energy, mining, and infrastructure sectors are ambitious, the article suggests that their full implementation will be challenging given the critical economic contributions of these industries and Petro's lack of a congressional majority. The piece highlights that Petro will likely need to moderate his proposals to govern effectively, with future cabinet appointments offering a clearer indication of his administration's trajectory.

title: 20 People to Know in Energy: Kyle Mork, president and CEO, Greylock Energy
summary: Kyle Mork, president and CEO of Greylock Energy, is featured as one of 20 People to Know in Energy by the Pittsburgh Business Times. Mork's career began at Halliburton as a technical professional, followed by a role as a drilling engineer at Energy Corporation of America, where he eventually became CEO in 2016. The article highlights his journey and leadership in the energy industry.

title: Tucker Carlson Gives the New Anti-ESG DRLL ETF a Big Boost
summary: The newly launched Strive U.S. Energy ETF (DRLL), an anti-ESG fund, has raised $100 million since August 10, with its founder Vivek Ramaswamy promoting conservative energy politics. The fund, backed by Peter Thiel and Bill Ackman, holds stakes primarily in large integrated oil companies like Exxon Mobil, Chevron, and ConocoPhillips. Its success hinges on the value of these assets, offering investors a way to express a political stance against ESG standards while playing the U.S. energy sector.

title: ONGC signs agreement with ExxonMobil for deepwater exploration in India
summary: Indian oil explorer ONGC signed a Heads of Agreement with ExxonMobil for deepwater exploration in India's East and West coasts. This collaboration aims to monetize India's oil and gas resources and reduce its reliance on costly imports, with ExxonMobil's expertise expected to facilitate efficient fast-track development.

title: U.S. oil refiners aim to run full bore, spurning recession fears
summary: U.S. crude oil refiners plan to operate at near full capacity in the current quarter, setting aside recession concerns and dropping retail prices. This high operating level is expected to keep gasoline prices below their spring peaks and provide strong earnings for refiners. Major companies like Marathon Petroleum and Valero Energy aim for high utilization rates, citing no indication of demand destruction despite the approaching autumn maintenance season and potential hurricane impacts.

title: As inflation batters, TRS eyes natural gas
summary: The Teacher Retirement System of Texas (TRS), a $200 billion pension fund, is turning its attention to natural gas investments as a hedge against inflation. While inflation negatively impacts most of its portfolio, TRS's 6% allocation to Energy, Natural Resources and Infrastructure (ENRI) has performed well. The fund is specifically eying opportunities in natural gas infrastructure and export facilities, particularly on the US east coast, to capitalize on increased global demand and record prices.

title: Peaking: Why Peaks Matter
summary: This report from RMI examines why demand peaks are critical for financial markets, particularly concerning the fossil fuel industry. It argues that a peak in demand signals a turning point from growth to decline, leading to falling volumes, prices, and profits, ultimately resulting in stranded assets and company bankruptcies. The report highlights the fossil fuel sector's vulnerability to these peaks due to low growth, high capital intensity, and the presence of cheaper renewable alternatives.

title: Why is the Woodside share price whizzing 5% higher on Friday?
summary: The Woodside Energy Group Ltd (ASX: WDS) share price surged nearly 5% on Friday, outperforming the broader ASX 200 index. This significant rise, also seen in other ASX 200 energy shares like Santos and Beach Energy, is attributed to an increase in crude oil prices. Higher oil prices make oil producers like Woodside more profitable, contributing to Woodside's 49% year-to-date gain.

title: The Big Four oilsands companies’ influence threatens Alberta democracy, argues political scientist
summary: A political scientist argues that the hyperconcentration of oilsands production in four major companies (Cenovus Energy, Canadian Natural Resources Limited, Imperial Oil, and Suncor Energy) poses a threat to Alberta's democracy. These "Big Four" control about 84% of Alberta’s bitumen production and significantly contribute to the provincial government's revenue through royalties and taxes. This financial dependency gives these companies substantial political influence, as demonstrated by their lobbying efforts through the Pathways Alliance.

title: YPF anunció un aumento de 7,5%, en promedio, para combustibles y gasoil
summary: YPF announced an average increase of 7.5% for fuels, specifically an 8.5% rise for gasoline and 6% for diesel, effective August 21, 2022. The company stated it would continue efforts to maintain supply amidst record demand and rising costs. This adjustment follows a 9% increase in May, bringing the total increment over 12 months to 41.7%, which is below the Consumer Price Index (IPC) and other relative economic prices.

title: GTNXP Statement
summary: The GTNXP Statement from TC Energy highlights the importance of natural gas in meeting North America's long-term energy needs and its role in greenhouse gas emission reduction. The Gas Transmission Northwest XPress Project (GTNXP) aims to upgrade existing systems to meet increased demand in the Western U.S., evidenced by securing long-term agreements for 100 percent of the project's capacity. TC Energy emphasizes the project's support from various stakeholders and its commitment to providing reliable energy while creating economic benefits.

title: Blockchain for Energy signs up new consortium member Devon Energy
summary: Blockchain for Energy (B4E) announced that Devon Energy, a major oil exploration and production firm with a market cap of $47 billion, has joined its consortium, bringing its total membership to nine. The group focuses on the oil and gas sector's extraction side and currently has five workstreams, including a commodity transport solution using blockchain and IoT sensors that is already in production. Other projects address ESG emission disclosures, joint venture exploration management, and a mineral royalty blockchain solution.

title: Oil bonanza hints at higher Petronas contributions — but not without cost
summary: The article discusses how the current oil bonanza is expected to lead to higher contributions from Petronas to the Malaysian government, helping to fill national coffers amidst inflation and rising living costs. However, it also highlights the costs associated with this dependence, such as Petronas's high dividend payout ratio and the need for significant capital expenditure, warning that the "oil party" may not last forever and that Malaysia needs to be more prudent given the volatility of oil prices.

title: Sasol delivers first dividend in three years after oil price surge
summary: South Africa's largest fuel producer, Sasol Ltd., has declared its first dividend in three years following a surge in oil and chemical prices and strong demand. The company more than quadrupled its full-year earnings and significantly reduced its debt, which neared $10 billion two years ago. This recovery is largely attributed to cost-cutting measures, asset divestment, and the skyrocketing energy prices after Russia's invasion of Ukraine, despite incurring hedging losses.

title: Exxon plans January coker, crude unit work at Louisiana refinery -sources
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp plans to shut down a coker and crude distillation units at its 520,000 barrel-per-day Baton Rouge, Louisiana, refinery for maintenance in January. The maintenance will begin with the 50,000-bpd Far East Coker, which will be shut for 68 days to replace all four of its coke drums. Subsequently, work will be performed on the refinery's four crude distillation units.

title: CrossAmerica Announces Pending Acquisition of Assets of Community Service Stations
summary: CrossAmerica Partners LP announced a definitive agreement to acquire assets from Community Service Stations, including wholesale fuel supply contracts for 39 dealer-owned locations, 34 subjobber accounts, and two commission locations, totaling approximately 75 million gallons of fuel annually. This acquisition is expected to expand CrossAmerica's fuels business in the New England market and is anticipated to close in Q4 2022, financed by cash on hand or undrawn credit. The partnership expects the acquisition to be immediately accretive to distributable cash flow.

title: Energy Transfer signs 20-year LNG supply deal with Shell
summary: U.S. pipeline operator Energy Transfer LP has secured a 20-year agreement with Shell Plc to supply 2.1 million tonnes of liquefied natural gas (LNG) per year from its proposed Lake Charles facility. This deal comes amid soaring global demand and prices for LNG, exacerbated by factors such as Russia's invasion of Ukraine. Shell, an original backer of the project, had withdrawn two years prior during the pandemic-driven market downturn.

title: Is Exxon Stock a Buy?
summary: Morningstar analyst Allen Good believes Exxon Mobil (XOM) is a strong buy, preferring it over Chevron despite its continued commitment to oil and gas over renewables. The company's strategy, which includes investing in low-carbon technologies while keeping oil and gas core, is seen as more successful and less risky given projected high commodity prices and strong refining margins. Morningstar has a fair value estimate of $102 per share for Exxon, noting its narrow economic moat and high uncertainty rating due to commodity price risks.

title: Chart Industries CEO Expects LNG Plants to Go Up Faster as Projects Utilize New Designs
summary: Chart Industries CEO Jillian Evanko anticipates a rapid acceleration in LNG plant construction due to a shift towards smaller, modular designs that reduce costs and construction times. This modular approach, first adopted in the US and now gaining international traction, is helping to meet the escalating global demand for LNG, especially in light of recent geopolitical events. Evanko also highlighted hydrogen and carbon capture as key long-term growth areas for the company.

title: Exxon, Shell, Chevron end lawsuits against Nigeria's state-owned oil company
summary: Four major oil companies, including Exxon, Shell, and Chevron, have agreed to end U.S. lawsuits seeking to enforce multi-billion dollar arbitration awards against Nigeria's state-owned oil company, NNPC. This decision follows new deepwater oil production sharing agreements between the companies and NNPC, with the lawsuits expected to be terminated after the agreements take effect. The disputes stemmed from accusations that NNPC drew more oil than permitted under previous contracts, with awards totaling nearly $4 billion.

title: The backlash against BlackRock, ESG investing intensifies
summary: Texas has barred 10 companies and 348 investment funds, including BlackRock and UBS, from doing business with the state because they "boycott energy companies" through their ESG investing strategies. This action follows a state law enacted last year and contributes to a growing trend among red states pushing back against "woke capitalism" and ESG funds. Despite the ban, companies like BlackRock assert their continued investment in the fossil fuel industry, and experts suggest the financial impact on Wall Street may be limited compared to actions by other large states.

title: Dow temporarily cutting PE production by 15 percent
summary: Dow Inc., one of the world's largest polyethylene resin makers, is temporarily reducing its global PE production capacity by approximately 15 percent due to global logistics constraints, including port and rail congestions. This move aims to balance elevated inventories and improve logistics resiliency, particularly ahead of the hurricane season in the U.S. Industry analysts suggest the cuts are a temporary solution to PE overcapacity and declining prices but may not be widely followed by competitors.

title: UN monitors thrust into debate over what to do with 1.4 trillion litres of oilsands wastewater
summary: UN monitors are investigating the impacts of oilsands tailings ponds on the Peace-Athabasca Delta and Wood Buffalo National Park, driven by concerns from the Mikisew Cree First Nation. This international scrutiny comes as Canada considers new regulations that could allow for the release of treated oilsands wastewater for the first time, a move opposed by many Indigenous and environmental groups due to concerns about water quality and inadequate regulatory oversight of environmental liabilities. The debate centers on how to manage the 1.4 trillion litres of accumulated wastewater, with industry advocating for safe treated release and environmentalists demanding stricter measures.

title: Imperial Oil finds source, but not cause of Mackenzie River leak
summary: Imperial Oil has identified the section of pipeline responsible for a 55,000-litre treated water leak at its Norman Wells facility last month. The leak occurred from an exposed section of pipeline under the Mackenzie River, confirming that produced water entered the river. While the company stated that water samples showed no immediate risk to public health or aquatic life, the cause of the leak is still under investigation.

title: Exxon to Sell Arkansas Shale Gas Assets to Flywheel Energy
summary: Exxon Mobil (XOM.N) has reached an agreement to sell its Fayetteville Shale natural gas properties in Arkansas to Flywheel Energy, a privately held U.S. oil and gas producer. This sale is part of Exxon's strategy to divest $15 billion in non-core assets to focus on more profitable ventures, especially as global natural gas prices and demand increase. The deal, which includes approximately 5,000 gas wells and related infrastructure, is expected to close by the end of October, though specific financial terms remain confidential.

title: Important step to decarbonise Europe
summary: Northern Lights, a joint venture of Equinor, Shell, and TotalEnergies, has signed the world's first commercial agreement for cross-border CO2 transportation and storage with Yara. This landmark deal involves capturing CO2 from Yara's plant in the Netherlands and storing it permanently under the seabed off Norway, marking a significant step towards decarbonizing heavy industries. The agreement fills the capacity for Phase 1 of the project, with plans underway to expand to Phase 2, aiming for an annual storage capacity of 5-6 million tonnes of CO2.

title: ExxonMobil (XOM) Enters Deal to Divest Fayetteville Assets
summary: ExxonMobil (XOM) has agreed to sell its Fayetteville Shale assets in Arkansas to Flywheel Energy. This divestment, which includes natural gas wells and related infrastructure across 381,000 acres, aligns with ExxonMobil's strategy to focus on more profitable assets and achieve its goal of raising $15 billion from asset sales to reduce debt. The deal is expected to close by the end of October, pending regulatory approvals.

title: WSJ News Exclusive | Exxon Escalates Dispute With Russia Over Barred Exit From Giant Oil Project
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. has notified Russian officials of its intent to sue the government if it is not allowed to exit the Sakhalin-1 oil-and-gas project. A Russian decree enacted in early August has prevented Exxon from transferring operatorship and selling its 30% stake in the venture, despite the company's prior plans to divest following Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

title: KNOT Takes Delivery of Dual-Fuel Shuttle Tanker. Charter Secured with Eni
summary: Knutsen NYK Offshore Tankers (KNOT) has taken delivery of "Sindre Knutsen," a new dual-fuel LNG shuttle tanker built by Daewoo Shipbuilding & Marine Engineering. This vessel, similar to its sister ship "Frida Knutsen," will be chartered to Eni Trade & Biofuels S.p.A. for oil transportation in the North Sea and Barents Sea, utilizing LNG fuel and a VOC recovery system to reduce emissions.

title: Why the time is right for North American LNG
summary: Global demand for liquefied natural gas (LNG) is surging, driven by energy security concerns and the transition towards lower-carbon economies. Enbridge Inc. is positioned to capitalize on this demand, especially with its infrastructure along the U.S. Gulf Coast and its investment in the Woodfibre LNG project in British Columbia, which aims to provide cleaner LNG to Asian markets. The company emphasizes its commitment to reducing carbon emissions throughout the natural gas value chain.

title: Imperial, Exxon complete $1.9-billion sale of XTO Energy Canada to Whitecap Resources
summary: Imperial Oil Ltd. and ExxonMobil Canada have finalized the sale of their oil and gas-producing assets in the Montney and Duvernay areas to Whitecap Resources Inc. for $1.9 billion. The assets were held by XTO Energy Canada, which was jointly owned by Imperial and ExxonMobil. This acquisition adds approximately 32,000 barrels per day of production and over 2,000 drilling locations for Whitecap Resources.

title: Imperial, Exxon completes $1.9B sale of XTO Energy Canada to Whitecap Resources
summary: Imperial Oil Ltd. and ExxonMobil Canada have finalized the $1.9 billion sale of their Montney and Duvernay oil and gas assets to Whitecap Resources Inc. The deal involves XTO Energy Canada's holdings, including almost 230,000 net hectares in Montney shale and 29,000 net hectares in Duvernay shale. Whitecap expects the acquisition to add approximately 32,000 barrels per day of production and over 2,000 drilling locations.

title: Shell, Exxon Mobil Sell California Oil and Gas Producer to German Asset Manager
summary: Exxon Mobil and Shell have agreed to sell their stakes in Aera Energy LLC, one of California's largest oil and gas producers, to German asset manager IKAV Capital Partners GmbH. Aera Energy, a joint venture of the two oil giants, is responsible for nearly a quarter of California's total oil and gas production.

title: Exxon, Shell sell California oil assets for $4 billion to IKAV
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp and Shell Plc have sold their California oil joint-venture Aera to German asset manager IKAV for $4 billion, marking the end of their 25-year partnership in one of California's largest oil producers. This divestment aligns with both companies' strategies to move away from mature energy properties and focus on new projects with high growth potential, like Exxon's ventures in Guyana and Brazil. The deal is expected to close in Q4 2022, with Shell anticipating an impairment charge of $300 million to $400 million from the sale.

title: Norwegian energy group Equinor completes Russia exit
summary: Norwegian energy group Equinor has finalized its complete withdrawal from Russia, fulfilling a commitment made after the invasion of Ukraine. This makes Equinor the first international oil and gas company to execute a full and orderly exit from Russia. Other major energy firms like TotalEnergies and ExxonMobil are still in the process of divesting or facing challenges in their attempts to leave.

title: Direxion Plans Energy-Focused Single-Stock ETFs
summary: Direxion has filed for eight new single-stock ETFs focused on major energy companies like Chevron, ConocoPhillips, ExxonMobil, and EOG Resources. These funds will offer leveraged and inverse exposure, allowing investors to bet on both the upside and downside of these key energy stocks. The move comes as the energy sector, while having strong year-to-date performance, has recently faced significant outflows from the largest energy ETF (XLE).

title: Blackstone and Carlyle take different sides on oil and gas investment
summary: Private equity giants Blackstone and Carlyle Group are taking differing approaches to oil and gas investments amidst pressure to divest from fossil fuels and invest in cleaner energy. Blackstone is largely pulling back from new oil and gas exploration and production investments, while Carlyle Group and Brookfield Asset Management Inc. advocate for transforming existing traditional energy producers into more climate-friendly businesses, emphasizing "invest, not divest" strategies. This divergence reflects the challenges of volatile returns, a fraught political climate, and difficulties in financing and exiting fossil fuel assets, contrasting with the growing investment in renewable energy.

title: Exxon Beaumont, Texas, chemical plant upset triggered flaring -sources
summary: A malfunction at Exxon Mobil Corp's Beaumont, Texas, chemical plant led to flaring on Friday, according to sources familiar with the plant's operations. The chemical plant utilized portions of the adjoining refinery's safety flare system, though the refinery's operations remained normal. Exxon issued community notices regarding the flaring, which is a safety measure used by plants when they cannot process hydrocarbons normally.

title: Golden Pass LNG beefs up trading team as it moves closer to startup
summary: Golden Pass LNG, a joint venture between Qatar Energy and Exxon Mobil, is expanding its trading team as its commercial operations draw nearer and as global demand for LNG rises due to the energy crisis in Europe. The facility, located near Sabine Pass, Texas, is targeting a 2024 startup and has recently hired several key personnel for its commercial LNG planning and analytics departments. This move comes as the company prepares to compete in a growing U.S. LNG export market.

title: Will Friday’s weak gain in crude oil prices grow this week?
summary: Crude oil prices saw a weak gain on Friday amidst investor nervousness about China's COVID-19 shutdowns and the global economy, ahead of an OPEC+ meeting. West Texas Intermediate and Brent crude futures rose marginally, while natural gas prices fell. Various Oklahoma and other energy stocks experienced gains, with some utility stocks declining.

title: Former Trump Energy Secretary Says EU Efforts to Control Energy Costs Are Like a Ponzi Scheme
summary: Former U.S. Energy Secretary Dan Brouillette stated that some of the measures European governments are taking to control electricity costs resemble a "Ponzi scheme," as they alleviate immediate pain without offering a long-term solution by simply circling money. He advocates for increased energy production and infrastructure development, particularly in the U.S. and Europe, to address the global energy scarcity. Brouillette also criticized the Biden administration's request for U.S. oil producers to limit exports, citing fiduciary responsibilities to shareholders and market conditions.

title: EPA deals blow to Phillips 66’s Bluewater, proposed deepwater terminal offshore Corpus Christi
summary: The EPA has dealt a blow to Phillips 66's proposed Bluewater deepwater terminal offshore Corpus Christi, stating that the project would not meet federal emissions standards. The agency requested that Bluewater withdraw its current application for Clean Air Act permits, revise its pollution control measures, and resubmit. This decision was celebrated by environmental groups, as it is expected to reduce pollution by 18,000 tons annually.

title: FLEETCOR® Signs ExxonMobil Relationship
summary: FLEETCOR Technologies, Inc. has signed network agreements with Exxon Mobil Corporation, enhancing the market position and product versatility of FLEETCOR’s North American commercial fleet card business, including its Comdata and Fuelman brands. The agreements provide brand-wide acceptance of Fuelman cards at over 12,000 Exxon and Mobil stations and will add acceptance of Comdata trucking cards at commercial fueling locations in 2023. This expansion offers cardholders benefits such as Exxon Mobil's Synergy Diesel Efficient™ fuel and the Exxon Mobil Rewards+™ loyalty program.

title: 5 Ways You Can Get Income From Your Investments Right Now |…
summary: This article outlines five easy ways investors can generate income from their investments, offering yields of up to 9%. It covers dividend-paying stocks and ETFs, bonds, REITs, Master Limited Partnerships (MLPs), and preferred shares. The author emphasizes the importance of diversifying an income portfolio to suit individual risk tolerance.

title: Why so many LNG terminals are adopting carbon capture
summary: Liquefied natural gas (LNG) companies are increasingly investing in carbon capture and storage (CCS) technology voluntarily to reduce their emissions and enhance their climate credentials. This proactive approach is driven by a desire to attract international customers, particularly from Europe and Asia, and to stay ahead of potential future regulations and reporting requirements. The Inflation Reduction Act's expanded 45Q tax incentive has also improved the economic viability of CCS for these companies.

title: Argentina is excited to export LNG: what are the three projects in the pipeline
summary: Argentina is enthusiastic about the prospect of exporting Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) from Vaca Muerta, identified as a key driver for economic development. The country, despite having the world's second-largest shale gas reserves, currently lacks the necessary infrastructure for large-scale LNG production and export. Three major projects are currently in the pipeline: a significant joint venture between YPF and Petronas, a modular plant by Excelerate and TGS in Bahía Blanca, and a potential Tecpetrol plant in Río Negro.

title: Oil ETFs: What You Should Know Before You Invest
summary: This article explains what oil ETFs are, differentiating between those investing in oil industry equities and those in oil futures. It provides an overview of various types of oil ETFs, their performance, and investment opportunities and risks, emphasizing the current overweight recommendation for the energy sector. The author also offers specific ETF recommendations like XLE and VDE, and discusses considerations for investing in crude oil and gas futures via ETFs.

title: Petronas announces oil discovery in Suriname
summary: Petronas Suriname E&P BV (PSEPBV) has announced its first oil discovery at the Baja-1 well in Block 53, offshore Suriname. The well, located about 189km offshore, successfully encountered light oil in the Campanian-aged sedimentary sequence. This discovery is a significant milestone for Petronas in unlocking deepwater hydrocarbon resources and growing its international portfolio, particularly in the Americas.

title: Slovakia's gas importer SPP signs LNG contract with ExxonMobil
summary: Slovakia's national gas importer SPP has signed a liquefied natural gas (LNG) supply deal with ExxonMobil to diversify its energy sources and reduce dependence on Russian gas. SPP has also secured transport arrangements from LNG terminals in Italy and Croatia, enabling it to cover over 65% of its customers' consumption from non-Russian sources. This move aims to ensure gas supply stability for Slovakia during the 2022/2023 winter season.

title: ConocoPhillips stock outperforms competitors on strong trading day
summary: Shares of ConocoPhillips (COP) rose 3.37% to $111.97 on Friday, outperforming competitors like Exxon Mobil Corp. (XOM) and Chevron Corp. (CVX) on a strong trading day for the broader market. The stock closed $12.11 below its 52-week high, marking its second consecutive day of gains. Trading volume for ConocoPhillips was slightly below its 50-day average.

title: ExxonMobil Expands Fleet Reach With New Partnership
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. has partnered with FLEETCOR Technologies Inc. to allow Fuelman and Comdata cards to be accepted at over 12,000 Exxon and Mobil stations across the U.S., expanding fleet reach and offering benefits like Synergy Diesel Efficient fuel and the Exxon Mobil Rewards+ loyalty program. Fuelman cardholders can immediately use their cards, while Comdata trucking cards will gain access starting in 2023. This collaboration aims to enhance the fueling experience for fleet customers by providing convenience, control, and savings.

title: Opinion: Are Oklahoma 401(k) Plans Helping to Destroy State’s Energy Business?
summary: This opinion piece argues that Oklahoma 401(k) plan participants might unknowingly be investing in funds that work against the state's vital energy industry. The author, Terry Morgan of Ok401k, highlights the trend of large mutual fund companies adopting ESG investing criteria, which he claims can force corporations to comply with "woke" agendas and potentially harm the profitability of energy companies. He urges Oklahomans to be aware of how their investments are being used and suggests alternative funds like those from STRIVE Asset Management.

title: Look to SPLV for Stability in Your Portfolio
summary: Investors are increasingly turning to the Invesco S&P 500 Low Volatility ETF (SPLV) for portfolio stability, with the fund attracting significant inflows in recent months. SPLV invests in the 100 least volatile securities from the S&P 500, focusing on established "blue-chip" companies known for their stability and dividends rather than high growth. The ETF is positioned as a defensive option that may outperform during bear markets and underperform in bull markets.

title: Brief Contract Extension for BW Offshore's FPSO in Gabon
summary: BW Offshore has secured a brief contract extension for its Petroleo Nautipa FPSO, operating in Vaalco's Etame field offshore Gabon, delaying demobilization until October 4, 2022. This FPSO is expected to be scrapped after demobilization, following an impairment charge in 2021 by BW Offshore on its older FPSO fleet. The Etame field's production will continue with a new FSO solution, the Cap Diamant, which is projected to significantly reduce operating costs and extend the field's economic life.

title: 3 Best Index Funds to Buy Now
summary: This article identifies three top index funds for investors looking for diversification, long-term gains, and low costs. The recommended funds are the iShares U.S. Energy ETF (IYE) for exposure to the energy sector, the Vanguard 500 Index Fund (VOO) for tracking the S&P 500, and the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) for investing in leading technology stocks. It explains the benefits of ETFs, such as lower fees compared to actively managed mutual funds.

title: Want gas under 3 dollars? Here are the lowest fuel prices in the area
summary: Some gas prices in the Triangle area have dropped below $3 a gallon, primarily in Wilson, North Carolina. While Raleigh metro area stations in Fuquay-Varina, Angier, and Garner offer gas at $3.15 per gallon, Wilson residents can find prices just under $3 at locations like Murphy USA, Walmart Neighborhood Market, and Circle K. Commuters express relief over the lower prices, hoping the trend continues.

title: 2022 Top 400 Sourcebook: Fluor Is EPC Contractor for Offshore Louisiana Gas Export Plant's Two Phases
summary: Fluor Corp. has been awarded two contracts for engineering, procurement, and fabrication management for New Fortress Energy's offshore natural gas export plant in the Gulf of Mexico, off Grand Isle, Louisiana. The project's two phases involve adding gas treatment and liquefaction units to fixed offshore platforms, with the first phase expected to operate in early 2023. Other major energy projects mentioned include Cheniere Energy's LNG plant expansion in Texas, Worley's petrochemical plant in Corpus Christi, and the Santos-Repsol Pikka oilfield development in Alaska.

title: Cover Story: OSV players hope for better charter rates
summary: The OSV industry, a key component of oil and gas exploration, is seeing an inflection point with rising charter rates and utilization, according to global operator Tidewater Inc. However, local Malaysian OSV players face challenges due to cabotage laws and legacy low charter rates, despite ongoing negotiations with Petronas for better terms and age limit extensions for vessels. The industry also grapples with high operating costs, funding difficulties, and a need for consolidation.

title: La movida de Ecopetrol que beneficia a palmeros y deja sin tierra a campesinos
summary: Ecopetrol secured a "special reserve" of over 9,000 hectares of baldío land in Puerto Gaitán, Meta, for the Campo Rubiales project, a process that took only three years. This decision, approved by then-President Iván Duque, has effectively blocked long-standing land claims by displaced farmers like Esneyder Lozano, who have occupied and made these lands productive for years. The article highlights inconsistencies and raises questions about private palm oil plantations on these lands and the swift approval for Ecopetrol compared to the lack of response for campesino land applications.

title: JX Nippon to buy NRG's stake in Petra Nova carbon capture plant near Houston
summary: JX Nippon, a co-developer of the Petra Nova carbon capture unit, is set to assume full ownership of the facility. The Petra Nova plant near Houston is described as the largest carbon capture unit of its kind globally, with an estimated development cost of $1 billion, partially funded by a $195 million grant from the Department of Energy.

title: Crude oil tanker floats new dividend policy
summary: Bermudian-based DHT Holdings Inc, a crude oil tanker company, has announced a new dividend policy to return 100 per cent of net income to shareholders quarterly, effective from Q3. Meanwhile, Bermuda-based offshore drilling services company Valaris Limited received a $40 million partial early repayment from its joint venture ARO Drilling and authorized a $100 million share repurchase program. Additionally, executives at Bermudian-based LNG shipping company Flex LNG Ltd exercised and sold share options.

title: TC Energy CEO François Poirier comments on global energy crisis and growing LNG demand
summary: TC Energy CEO François Poirier highlights North America's crucial role in addressing the global energy crisis through clean energy, emphasizing the growing demand for LNG. He notes that LNG can simultaneously improve energy security and reduce emissions, especially given the resurgence of coal in Europe. Poirier also points out challenges in expanding natural gas infrastructure due to regulatory delays, which hinder Canada's competitiveness and energy transition efforts.

title: Chevron's TCO to divert 200,000 t of oil to Batumi in October amid CPC maintenance - sources
summary: Tengizchevroil (TCO), operated by Chevron, plans to reroute 200,000 tonnes of oil via rail to Georgia's Batumi port in October. This diversion is a response to maintenance work at the Caspian Pipeline Consortium (CPC) terminal, which significantly reduces its loading capacity. TCO previously used this alternative route earlier in the year during unscheduled CPC maintenance.

title: Exclusive: Exxon boosts Guyana oil output, undecided on future auction bid
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp is uncertain about bidding for new offshore areas in Guyana, as it ramps up production faster than expected and Guyana grapples with new oil lease terms.
