title: Summit yields ‘historic win’ for climate payments
summary: The COP27 climate summit in Egypt concluded with a landmark agreement to create a global fund for climate damage payments from wealthy to developing nations. However, this triumph was somewhat muted by a last-minute addition to the final text, which tacitly endorsed natural gas as a "low-emission" energy source, sparking controversy among delegates and activists. The deal, while a win for climate payments, fell short on commitments for steeper carbon reductions and faced criticism for not bridging the gap between climate science and policy.

title: Russia’s War Rewires Global Crude Trade
summary: Russia's war in Ukraine has significantly rewired global crude trade routes, leading to a surge in revenue for oil tanker tycoons. European bans on Russian oil are diverting cargoes to Asia, forcing ships to travel thousands of miles further and increasing "ton miles," a key industry metric. This shift is expected to keep freight rates strong for years, exacerbated by an aging tanker fleet and low new order books, creating a "paradigm shift" in the shipping industry.

title: Exxon says Britain's Fawley oil refinery unaffected by strike
summary: Exxon Mobil announced that its 390,000 barrel per day Fawley oil refinery in southern England remains unaffected by strike action. The company stated that operations are continuing as normal and they do not anticipate any impact on fuel supplies. The strike, organized by the UK's GMB Union over pay, involves members employed by contracting companies rather than Exxon Mobil directly.

title: Petrobras eletrifica plataformas para frear avanço de emissões | InvestNews
summary: Petrobras plans to electrify its offshore production vessels (FPSOs) to reduce emissions by up to 30% compared to previous designs, while simultaneously increasing oil production. This "all electric" technology addresses scope 1 and 2 emissions from oil production, refining, and transportation. The company aims for a 25% reduction in operational emissions by 2030 and full neutralization through efficiency gains and offsets, aligning with the Paris Agreement.

title: Employees Start Strike at Biggest European BP Oil Refinery
summary: Dutch unions have initiated a partial strike at BP Plc's Rotterdam refinery, one of Europe's largest, following an outage that halted fuel production. Workers are refusing to cooperate on restarting production units after a fault is resolved, intensifying a pay dispute with BP. This action follows a previous work-to-rule and comes amidst broader concerns about refinery outages and fuel supply in Europe.

title: Seapeak unveils $1.1bn order for five LNG carriers linked to ExxonMobil business
summary: Seapeak has announced a $1.1 billion order for five new LNG carriers. The order was placed with Samsung Heavy Industries and is linked to ExxonMobil's business operations. These new vessels will expand Seapeak's fleet, supporting the growing demand for LNG transportation.

title: Report: Bob Simpson's MorningStar Partners Files for Proposed $100 Million Public Offering
summary: MorningStar Partners LP, an oil and gas company led by Bob Simpson, is pursuing a proposed $100 million initial public offering and plans to change its name to TXO Energy Partners. The company, focused on the Permian and San Juan basins, reported $15 million in net income on $204 million revenue for a nine-month period ending September and aims to list its shares on the NYSE under the symbol TXO. It was founded by Bob Simpson after the 2009 sale of XTO Energy.

title: How Canada’s Top 10 oil and gas producers are working to reduce emissions
summary: This article highlights how Canada's top 10 oil and gas producers are implementing various strategies to reduce emissions. Each company's approach, ranging from solar panel installations and CO2 capture to methane reduction and electrification, is detailed with specific examples and production figures from 2021. The article underscores the industry's commitment to providing reliable energy while minimizing its environmental footprint.

title: US Treasury authorizes Chevron to expand oil pumping in Venezuela
summary: The U.S. Treasury Department has authorized Chevron Corp. to expand its oil operations in Venezuela, following renewed talks between the socialist Maduro regime and Venezuelan opposition leaders. This decision aligns with the U.S. policy of targeted sanctions relief tied to steps that alleviate suffering and support democracy in Venezuela. The move also comes as the Biden administration seeks to address rising energy prices and global oil shortages.

title: Exxon Mobil Has a Potash Problem in the Permian Basin
summary: Exxon Mobil is facing a unique challenge in the Permian Basin due to shared land with potash mining companies. This situation is hindering the oil company's ability to access oil-rich reserves directly, unlike many of its competitors. The conflict arises because potash, a vital crop nutrient, lies underground near oil and natural-gas reserves, creating a drilling obstacle for Exxon Mobil.

title: WSJ News Exclusive | Exxon Mobil Has a Potash Problem in the Permian Basin
summary: Exxon Mobil is facing challenges in developing a key asset in the Permian Basin due to sharing land with potash mining companies. Unlike many rivals, Exxon's direct access to oil-soaked rocks is hindered by underground mines extracting potash, a vital crop nutrient. This situation complicates the drilling efforts of the Texas-based oil company in New Mexico.

title: Plan to cut statewide fuel emissions 20% starts Jan. 1
summary: Washington's new Clean Fuel Standard, adopted by the Department of Ecology, will begin on January 1, 2023, aiming to cut statewide transportation emissions by 20% by 2034. This program utilizes a market-based approach to incentivize fuel producers to reduce the carbon intensity of their products and is not expected to significantly impact gas prices, adding less than a tenth of a cent in 2023. The initiative seeks to promote cleaner transportation options and investments in low-carbon fuels and zero-emission vehicle infrastructure.

title: Biden Admin Authorizes Chevron to Resume Oil Pumping in Venezuela
summary: The Biden administration has authorized Chevron Corp. to resume limited natural resource extraction operations in Venezuela through its joint venture with PDVSA. This decision follows resumed talks between the Nicolás Maduro regime and the opposition Unitary Platform, aiming to alleviate suffering and support the restoration of democracy in Venezuela. The authorization allows oil sales to the U.S. and directs profits to pay down Chevron's debt, not to PDVSA, but has faced criticism from Republicans regarding U.S. oil policy.

title: Oil Industry Refuses to Answer Questions on Gas Price Hikes Amidst Record Profits, as Experts Stress Need for New Accountability Measures
summary: Five major oil refiners — Chevron, Marathon, Phillips 66, PBF Energy, and Valero — refused to attend a California Energy Commission hearing on record gas price spikes and their unprecedented profits. Governor Gavin Newsom and experts emphasized the need for new transparency and accountability measures, including a proposed price-gouging penalty, to protect consumers from excessive pricing by oil companies. This refusal comes despite significant profit increases for these companies while crude oil prices were declining.

title: Chevron vs. ExxonMobil: Which energy stock is a better buy?
summary: This article compares ExxonMobil (XOM) and Chevron (CVX) as investment opportunities in the energy sector, highlighting their recovery and growth despite macroeconomic uncertainties. It discusses their stock performance, dividend history, and financial strengths, ultimately favoring Chevron due to its strong project portfolio and stable production growth, particularly in the Permian basin.

title: ETF 360: Strive’s Cole Discusses Energy Sector’s Long-Term Potential
summary: In a recent "ETF 360" episode, Strive Asset Management's Matt Cole discussed the Strive U.S. Energy ETF (DRLL) with VettaFi's Todd Rosenbluth. Cole highlighted the energy sector's strong fundamentals and profitability, noting its potential for continued outperformance relative to the tech sector. He also suggested that factors like a potential end to China's zero-COVID policy could further boost oil prices and DRLL's value.

title: Montana Attorney General Questions ‘Woke’ Investments
summary: Montana Attorney General Austin Knudsen has joined other state attorneys general in questioning ESG (Environmental Social Governance) investments, arguing that these "liberal woke" interests are infiltrating businesses and trying to move societal goals through pressure in business. Knudsen specifically highlighted concerns about ESG's impact on energy investments in Montana, claiming that such firms, like Vanguard, aim to push utilities away from traditional fossil fuels, thus driving up heating costs. He believes these actions are detrimental to energy markets and the state's economy, and has urged the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) to prevent these authorizations.

title: Independentes vão investir US$ 10 bi em projetos vendidos pela Petrobras
summary: Independent oil and gas operators who acquired upstream assets from Petrobras are set to invest $10 billion in these projects by 2027. This investment aims to boost production to 485,000 barrels per day within five years, adding 980 million barrels of oil equivalent to reserves. The move signals a significant shift in Brazil's oil production landscape, with Petrobras's market share projected to decrease as independent operators grow.

title: State oil regulators sued for approving new oil well drilling projects in Southern California
summary: The Center for Biological Diversity has sued the California Geologic Energy Management Division (CalGEM) for approving new oil and gas wells in Southern California without adequate environmental and public health assessments. The lawsuit alleges CalGEM failed to comply with the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) by relying on outdated studies that do not account for residential proximity, climate change, or specific well impacts. Environmental advocates are seeking a writ of mandate to vacate the approvals and prevent future drilling until CalGEM fulfills its CEQA obligations.

title: Plans for increased gas extraction from Oseberg approved
summary: Equinor and its partners have received approval to invest NOK 10 billion in the Oseberg field to significantly increase gas extraction and reduce CO2 emissions. The upgrades include installing two new compressors and partially electrifying platforms, which will increase recoverable gas reserves by 54% after 2025 and cut CO2 emissions by about 320,000 tonnes annually. This project is set to transform Oseberg into Norway's third-largest gas field, with production extending to 2040 and a scheduled start-up in 2026.

title: ENFR Outperforms Broader Energy Sector in November
summary: The Alerian Energy Infrastructure ETF (ENFR) outperformed the broader energy sector in November due to the stable cash flows and lower commodity price exposure of midstream energy companies, even as crude oil prices declined. The ENFR's underlying index, AMEI, gained 4.25% in November and is up 27.04% year-to-date, significantly surpassing the S&P 500. Midstream companies are also showing positive dividend trends and share repurchases, indicating continued strong performance into 2023.

title: Tellurian chief Charif Souki is selling new style LNG business, but so far no one's buying it
summary: Charif Souki, chairman of Tellurian, is struggling to find major investors for the company's $13.6 billion Driftwood liquefied natural gas project in Louisiana. Souki is promoting a unique business model that exposes Tellurian to more price volatility in exchange for potentially higher profits, a departure from the traditional fixed-price, long-term contracts used by other LNG companies. Despite soaring demand for natural gas, investors and analysts are skeptical of this high-risk approach, especially with rising inflation and construction costs.

title: Hess to Buy $750 Million in Carbon Credits From Guyana
summary: Hess Corporation has agreed to purchase $750 million worth of carbon credits from Guyana over the next decade, aiming to help preserve the country's Amazonian rainforests. This deal marks the second major carbon credit agreement for Guyana, following a 2009 deal with Norway, and will allocate 30% of the funds to Indigenous Amerindian communities. Hess, a partner in Guyana’s offshore oil sector, praised Guyana's efforts in forest protection and combating climate change.

title: Coastal GasLink Pipeline Cost to Rise Again, TC Energy Warns
summary: TC Energy has announced a "material increase" in the cost of its Coastal GasLink pipeline project, citing labor costs, skilled labor shortages, contractor underperformance, and unexpected events like drought. This is the second time this year that the company has flagged rising costs for the project, which was previously estimated at C$11.2 billion. The company anticipates providing an updated capital cost estimate early next year and plans to pursue recoveries from contractors.

title: ExxonMobil CEO Gets Pay Raise
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp announced an increase in the annual salaries of its top executives, including CEO Darren Woods, whose salary will rise to $1.88 million from $1.70 million, effective January 1, 2023. This pay hike follows record quarterly profits for the oil major and comes amidst accusations of war profiteering from U.S. President Joe Biden. The company also raised the pay of its CFO and senior vice presidents.

title: Trading firm Trafigura helps Germany secure more natural gas
summary: Trafigura, a commodities trading firm, has brokered a $3 billion loan to help Germany secure long-term natural gas supplies. The company will use its existing gas and liquefied natural gas reserves, including U.S.-sourced LNG, to supply significant volumes to Europe and Germany over the next four years. This move aims to bolster Europe's energy security, particularly for Germany, which has seen its reliance on Russian gas decrease significantly since the war in Ukraine.

title: Hess Signs $750M REDD+ Carbon Credits Deal with Guyana
summary: Hess Corporation has signed a $750 million deal with Guyana to purchase REDD+ carbon credits over the next decade, supporting the South American nation's efforts to protect its Amazonian rainforests. This agreement, running from 2022 to 2032, involves Hess buying 37.5 million REDD+ jurisdictional carbon credits and aligns with Guyana's Low Carbon Development Strategy 2030 and Hess's net-zero emissions target by 2050. Approximately 30% of Hess's investment will be allocated to developing Indigenous Amerindian communities in Guyana.

title: Exxon starts new polypropylene unit at Baton Rouge, Louisiana complex
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp has launched a new polypropylene unit at its Baton Rouge, Louisiana complex, investing over half a billion dollars. This expansion doubles the plant's capacity by adding 450,000 metric tons of polypropylene production, which is used in manufacturing various products from food containers to medical supplies. The new unit creates 65 full-time jobs and employed over 650 people during its construction phase.

title: Strategy 2040
summary: Ecopetrol S.A. has unveiled its "Energy that Transforms" strategic vision for 2040, alongside operational and financial goals for 2022-2024. This strategy aims to address environmental, social, and governance challenges, focusing on sustainable value generation. Ecopetrol plans to diversify into new businesses to reduce its carbon footprint and achieve net-zero carbon emissions by 2050 (scopes 1 and 2).

title: Exxon Mobil gives employees massive pay raises
summary: Exxon Mobil is significantly raising employee salaries by an average of 9% and granting restricted stock options to 14,000 employees globally, marking its largest salary increase in 15 years. This comes amidst record-breaking profits for the oil giant in 2022. The article contrasts Exxon's good fortune with mass layoffs occurring in the tech, housing, and financial sectors at companies like Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs, PepsiCo, Intel, and BuzzFeed.

title: Exxon plans to raise spending in 2023, boost share buybacks
summary: Exxon Mobil announced plans to increase its capital spending in 2023 by approximately 10%, totaling between $23 billion and $25 billion, and boost its share buyback program. The company will average $17.5 billion annually for buybacks over the next two years, up from $15 billion this year, and aims to produce a record 4.2 million barrels of oil equivalent per day by the end of 2027, primarily from Guyana, the U.S., and Brazil. Exxon is also increasing investments in lower-carbon projects, focusing on curbing emissions from existing operations.

title: Exxon Lifts Share Buyback to $50 Billion After Record Profit
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. has increased its annual share buyback program to $50 billion through 2024, expanding its previous plan of $30 billion through 2023. This decision comes six weeks after the oil giant reported its highest profit in its 152-year history. The buyback will include $15 billion in share repurchases for the current year, marking the highest annual total since 2013.

title: Cleanup continues at oil spill site near Meadowbank Mine
summary: Cleanup efforts are ongoing at an oil spill site near Agnico Eagle Mines Ltd.'s Meadowbank Mine, following a tanker truck rollover on November 28. Approximately 29,000 litres of oil were spilled, though federal authorities confirm no freshwater bodies have been affected. Investigations into the cause of the incident are still underway, and the Kivalliq Inuit Association has noted that trenches have been dug to contain the spill.

title: Exxon, Chevron to spend billions more on oil projects next year
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp and Chevron Corp plan to increase their project investments next year, allocating more funds towards energy projects amidst high oil demand and prices. Despite increased spending, this will not immediately translate to higher oil production for Exxon, though Chevron anticipates a compound annual increase through 2026. Both companies expect significant cash generation, with a focus on shareholder returns and lower-carbon initiatives.

title: Technical Pulse: US Market Sector Analysis Which sectors could outperform in 2023?
summary: The article analyzes the performance of US market sectors in 2022, identifying Energy, Healthcare, and Aerospace & Defence as top performers, while Technology, Consumer Cyclicals, and Banks underperformed. It discusses sector rotation analysis based on the business and stock market cycles, suggesting that Utilities, Financials, and Real Estate sectors could outperform in 2023 as the market potentially enters a recessionary phase, especially if interest rates ease. The report concludes by highlighting the shift from value and defensive stocks in 2022 towards rate-sensitive sectors for the upcoming year.

title: Looking for Cheap Energy Stocks? Try Outside the U.S.
summary: While U.S. energy stocks have become expensive, non-U.S. energy companies remain undervalued, largely due to ESG concerns and more aggressive energy transition strategies outside the U.S. This disparity offers long-term investors an opportunity to find cheaper stocks in the energy sector abroad. The article highlights four specific undervalued non-U.S. energy stocks: Saipem, Beach Energy, Santos, and BP.

title: How Exxon Mobil’s CEO Views Energy Shortages and Increasing Profits
summary: Exxon Mobil's CEO, Darren Woods, discusses the company's historic profits and surging stock price, largely attributed to rising energy prices. He addresses the company's long-term future amidst the global shift away from fossil fuels, explaining why Exxon is focusing on carbon capture rather than renewables. The interview covers energy security and policy, highlighting the company's strategic direction.

title: Exxon completes sale of Chad, Cameroon operations for $407 million
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp completed the $407 million sale of its operations in Chad and Cameroon to London-listed Savannah Energy PLC. This move is part of Exxon's strategy to exit African operations with declining crude oil production, focusing instead on its Mozambique LNG project and more profitable ventures in the Americas. Savannah Energy acquired Exxon's 40% stake in the Doba oil project and its indirect interest in the Chad-Cameroon export transportation system.

title: Oil Companies Have Plundered Louisiana's Coast. They Owe Us Reparations.
summary: This article argues that oil and gas companies owe reparations to Indigenous and historically Black communities in southern Louisiana for the massive destruction of the state's coastal wetlands. It highlights how these communities disproportionately suffer from land loss and climate change, while the fossil fuel industry has profited immensely and influenced regulations. The author calls for financial reparations as a means to recover from past abuses and to fundamentally change the extractive system, advocating for the return of land to Indigenous people to protect ancestral territories.

title: Oil production plateaus in the Permian push producers to drill deeper
summary: Oil production in the Permian Basin, which has historically driven 90% of global oil output growth, is facing a plateau as premium land becomes depleted. Producers are now drilling deeper and seeing lower yields per foot, leading to a slowdown in U.S. shale growth and putting renewed power back into the hands of OPEC. The shift complicates efforts to manage oil prices and highlights the challenges of sustaining rapid growth in mature shale plays.

title: Takeaways from the Democrats’ Big Oil investigation
summary: House Oversight and Reform Committee Democrats released over 1,200 pages of internal oil and gas industry documents, revealing companies' climate change strategies, divisions over ESG investments, and efforts to maintain corporate secrecy. The investigation found that oil majors are concerned about their "license to operate" and aim to secure a future for oil and gas through public relations and specific policy advocacy. The documents also highlight BP's shift post-Trump election, Exxon's reputational challenges affecting collaborations, and Chevron's skepticism towards net-zero goals.

title: Pembina Pipeline Corporation announces 2023 guidance, business update and sale of KAPS interest
summary: Pembina Pipeline Corporation has released its 2023 financial guidance, projecting adjusted EBITDA of $3.5 to $3.8 billion and a $730 million capital investment program. The company also announced the sale of Pembina Gas Infrastructure’s interest in the Key Access Pipeline System (KAPS) for $662.5 million, with proceeds to repay credit facilities. Additionally, Pembina provided business updates including the reactivation of the Nipisi Pipeline, continued development for a Redwater Expansion, and plans to direct excess cash flow towards debt repayment in 2023.

title: PETRONAS, Eni And Euglena To Explore Biorefinery Opportunity In Malaysia
summary: PETRONAS, Eni, and Euglena are jointly exploring the development of a biorefinery in Malaysia's Pengerang Integrated Complex, with an investment decision expected by 2023 and completion by 2025. This facility aims to produce Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) and Hydrogenated Vegetable Oil (HVO) from non-food chain raw materials. The collaboration leverages PETRONAS' integrated value chain, Eni's biorefinery expertise, and Euglena's biotechnology for a sustainable energy future.

title: ExxonMobil Starts Operations at Large-Scale Advanced Recycling Facility
summary: ExxonMobil has successfully started operations at its large-scale advanced recycling facility in Baytown, Texas, capable of processing over 80 million pounds of hard-to-recycle plastic waste annually. The facility uses proprietary Exxtend™ technology to transform plastic waste into raw materials for new products, supporting a circular economy. The company aims to expand its global capacity to recycle 1 billion pounds of plastic annually by year-end 2026, with plans for additional facilities worldwide.

title: Exxon Mobil starts operations at first large-scale plastic recycling plant in Baytown
summary: Exxon Mobil has commenced operations at its first large-scale plastic recycling plant in Baytown, Texas. The facility is designed to process over 80 million pounds of plastic waste annually. This marks a significant move for the company into advanced recycling.

title: As state law for industry tax breaks nears end, Gregory-Portland ISD approves more agreements
summary: The Gregory-Portland ISD approved five tax incentive agreements, including with Cheniere Energy and solar farms, just before a state law allowing such breaks expires. The decision came amid a rush of last-minute applications statewide, with school districts leveraging potential financial benefits like supplemental payments of up to $100 per student per year. Despite environmental concerns and criticisms regarding the hurried process, the board ultimately prioritized the financial advantages these agreements provide, which have historically brought significant revenue to the district.

title: Regulator charges Suncor Energy after worker injured
summary: Suncor Energy Inc has been charged by the Canada-Newfoundland and Labrador Offshore Petroleum Board after a worker was injured on the Terra Nova offshore oil vessel. The worker fell from a ladder in December 2019 while conducting gas testing, and the regulator alleges Suncor failed to ensure the worker wore a safety harness and appropriate protective equipment, as well as failing to produce a compliant written report. This incident follows previous scrutiny of Suncor's safety record, which led to the former CEO's resignation and a reduction in the company's contractor workforce.

title: What could the consequences of the RBC greenwashing case be?
summary: Canada's Competition Bureau has launched an inquiry into the Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) over allegations of greenwashing, specifically concerning its continued financing of fossil fuel projects while claiming alignment with the Paris Agreement. This landmark case could set a precedent for courts globally in addressing greenwashing in the absence of specific legislation. The inquiry focuses on RBC's substantial fossil fuel investments and its commitments regarding indigenous communities and coal financing, potentially leading to significant repercussions for the bank and influencing broader industry regulations.

title: Unprecedented Price Caps Pit Australia’s Leader Against Big Gas
summary: Australia's political leaders and the resources industry are embroiled in a major dispute over new government powers to set natural gas market prices. The industry is threatening an investment freeze due to the domestic price cap, with accusations of "Soviet-era policy" being met with counter-accusations regarding excessive profits. This conflict highlights the tensions arising from government intervention in energy markets.

title: Exxon Is Avoiding Tankers That Previously Transported Russian Oil
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. (NYSE:XOM) is avoiding hiring oil tankers that have previously carried Russian crude, mimicking a similar move by Shell Plc. This policy, effective from December 5th, puts pressure on shipowners to choose between servicing Russian oil interests or maintaining contracts with major Western oil companies. Exxon's stance allows them to terminate charters if the tankers fail to meet this requirement.

title: Eni Plans Second Republic of Congo FLNG Unit in Bid to ‘Leverage Gas Equity’
summary: Eni SpA is expanding its natural gas export capabilities from the Republic of Congo by commissioning a second floating LNG (FLNG) unit from Wison Heavy Industry Co. Ltd. This 2.4 million metric tons/year capacity unit, expected online next year, will complement the existing Tango FLNG unit, aiming for a total production of 3 mmty of LNG from the Marine XII block by 2025. This initiative is part of Eni's strategy to leverage its gas equity and mirrors similar projects in Mozambique and new gas discoveries in Cyprus.

title: Refiner Par Pacific Holdings promotes CFO to president, names next CFO
summary: Par Pacific Holdings is promoting its CFO, Will Monteleone, to president, effective January 1, 2023. Monteleone will oversee the company's refining, retail, logistics, and renewable fuels operations.

title: 'Good Year' for Offshore Exploration in Malaysia with 10 Discoveries Made
summary: Malaysia recorded 10 oil and gas discoveries in 2022, primarily offshore Sarawak, Sabah, and Peninsular Malaysia, indicating a successful year for exploration. Petronas and its partners saw increased exploration activities, with 16 wells completed and a 60% success ratio. The company plans to drill up to 30 exploration wells in the coming year to boost hydrocarbon resources.

title: Italy's LNG Import Capacity And New Terminals
summary: Italy is aiming to significantly increase its liquefied natural gas (LNG) import capacity from nearly 17 billion cubic meters (bcm) to 27 bcm to fully replace Russian gas supplies. This involves deploying two new floating storage and regasification units (FSRUs) in Piombino and offshore Ravenna, adding 5 bcm capacity each. The article also details the three existing LNG terminals in Rovigo, Livorno, and Panigaglia, outlining their current capacities and ownership structures.

title: Colombia's oil theft soars, leaving trail of environmental harm
summary: Oil theft in Colombia has surged, increasing more than threefold since 2018, contributing significantly to environmental devastation and fueling the country's booming cocaine and illegal mining industries. The stolen crude is refined into "pategrillo," a bootleg fuel used in cocaine production and illegal mining operations. The spills from pipeline tapping and waste from clandestine refineries leave vast areas contaminated, severely damaging ecosystems and posing long-term ecological threats, with authorities struggling to quantify and address the full extent of the environmental impact.

title: BP secures 20-year extension for Tangguh PSC in Indonesia
summary: BP and its partners have been granted a 20-year extension for their Tangguh Production Sharing Contract (PSC) in Indonesia, allowing them to operate the Tangguh gas field until 2055. This extension supports the continued operation of the Tangguh LNG facility, which will see increased capacity with a third production train becoming operational in 2023, and future development projects like Tangguh UCC and a CCUS initiative. The move reinforces BP's long-term commitment to Indonesia's natural gas supply.

title: Drill Pipe Market Size, Share, Global Report, By Solution, By End User, By Vertical, By Region, Analysis Till 2030
summary: This report by Stratagem Market Insights provides a comprehensive analysis of the global Drill Pipe Market from 2022 to 2030, covering market size, share, trends, and growth drivers. It segments the market by type (Standard, Heavy Weight) and application (Offshore, Onshore), offering regional insights and profiling key players. The study aims to forecast market growth and identify opportunities and challenges.

title: Renewable diesel demand expected to soar in next two years
summary: Renewable diesel production is projected to significantly increase in the next five years, driven by new facilities and biofuel policies, which is excellent news for canola growers. Canadian production is expected to reach 4.5 billion litres by 2027, with five new plants in Western Canada alone. This boom ensures a stable market for canola, enhancing prices and reducing reliance on overseas buyers, while also contributing to climate change efforts by lowering carbon emissions.

title: Natural Gas ETFs: Waves of Volatility
summary: Natural gas prices are experiencing significant volatility due to geopolitical events, changes in market dynamics, and fluctuating supply levels. This article discusses how leveraged short-term ETFs like BOIL and KOLD allow nimble traders to capitalize on these price swings, while emphasizing the inherent risks for passive investors. The author highlights the transformation of natural gas from a domestic commodity to an international market and predicts continued volatility, especially through the winter months.

title: Exxon Mobil Sells Irving Headquarters
summary: Exxon Mobil has sold its 290-acre Las Colinas headquarters campus in Irving, Texas, to Austin-based Capital Commercial Investments in a sale-leaseback agreement extending through 2023. This transaction follows Exxon Mobil's 2021 announcement to relocate its headquarters and over 10,000 employees to a new campus north of Houston. Capital Commercial Investments plans to redevelop the site into a luxury master-planned community.

title: SeaDrill to absorb AquaDrill and create industry giant
summary: Seadrill Limited, a Bermuda-domiciled offshore drilling contractor, will acquire its former subsidiary Aquadrill in an all-stock transaction valued at approximately $958 million. This merger is expected to significantly improve Seadrill's cash flow, bring it into a net cash position, and create an industry-leading company with estimated annual synergies of at least $70 million. Both companies' boards have approved the deal, which integrates Aquadrill's debt-free operations into Seadrill's modern fleet.

title: Woodside, Western Gas Eyeing More Australian Supply, Pluto LNG Exports
summary: Woodside Energy Group Ltd. and Western Gas have formed non-binding agreements to explore processing gas from the Equus Gas Project through Woodside's Pluto LNG terminal. This partnership aims to increase Australian gas supply and boost Woodside's LNG exports, with first cargoes from Equus gas through Pluto anticipated in 2027. The collaboration also supports Woodside's $12 billion expansion plan for Pluto LNG, seeking to maximize infrastructure utilization and extend its operational lifespan.

title: Exxon sues EU in move to block new windfall tax on oil companies
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp is suing the European Union to block its new windfall tax on oil groups, arguing the levy is "counter-productive" and undermines investor confidence. The company warned that the tax could impact future multibillion-euro investments in Europe, while the EU maintains the measure is compliant with its laws and will generate around 25 billion euros for redistribution. Other oil majors like Chevron have also voiced concerns about the tax discouraging energy supply investments.

title: Seapeak wraps up Evergas acquisition
summary: Seapeak, formerly Teekay LNG Partners, has successfully completed its acquisition of Evergas for approximately $700 million. Evergas will rebrand and operate as a wholly-owned subsidiary of Seapeak. This acquisition adds Evergas's fleet of ethane and multigas/LNG carriers, which are on fixed-rate charters to Ineos, to Seapeak's extensive portfolio.

title: Chevron sending two oil tankers to Venezuela under U.S. approval
summary: Chevron is sending two oil tankers to Venezuela, with one destined to load the first crude cargo for the U.S. in nearly four years, following U.S. authorization. This move signifies an easing of sanctions as an incentive for Venezuela to engage in political negotiations for a presidential election. Analysts believe the license could become more flexible as political talks progress, potentially allowing Chevron a more significant role in Venezuela's oil production.

title: WisdomTree U.S. Dividend Growth Fund (DGRW) Stock Price, Holdings, Dividend Yield
summary: This article provides a detailed overview of the WisdomTree U.S. Dividend Growth Fund (DGRW), including its stock price, holdings, and dividend yield. As of the latest N-PORT filing on September 30, 2025, the fund holds 301 stocks with a total value of $16.30 billion, with top holdings being Microsoft, Apple, NVIDIA, Exxon Mobil, and Chevron. The article also presents key statistics, performance data, and historical breakdowns of the fund's portfolio.

title: Exxon, Chevron, Shell Report Record Profits on High Energy Prices
summary: ExxonMobil, Chevron, and Shell PLC reported a combined record profit of $46 billion in the second quarter, driven by over a decade of high energy prices and strong oil-refining margins. Exxon posted its highest-ever quarterly profit of $17.9 billion, while Chevron also achieved a record $11.6 billion profit. The article links these record profits to rising oil and fuel production, increased energy prices, and cost cuts.

title: Oil and gas companies certify well sites as cleaned up — from space
summary: Oil and gas companies in Alberta are increasingly using remote sensing technologies like satellite imagery and LiDAR to certify the cleanup of old well sites, with Imperial Oil being the first to receive such certificates in 2021. This method reduces costs, risks, and emissions associated with traditional on-the-ground assessments, though limited ground verification is still required. While the technology offers efficiency, experts note its limitations in measuring all aspects of environmental reclamation, such as water chemistry or specific plant species.

title: What You Own in a Growth or Value ETF Just Changed
summary: A significant rebalance of S&P 500 Style Index-based ETFs occurred in late December 2022, altering the composition of growth and value ETFs. This reclassification led to mega-cap energy and healthcare companies historically seen as value, like Chevron and Exxon Mobil, being added to growth ETFs, while some former growth companies moved to value funds. Advisors are urged to re-examine the holdings within these ETFs as their sector exposures and underlying securities have changed considerably, potentially impacting future performance relative to their previous classifications.

title: Petrobras' Next CEO Seen Overseeing Strategic Shift with Renewables Focus
summary: Jean Paul Prates, a Brazilian senator and energy consultant, has been nominated to lead Petrobras, signaling a strategic shift towards renewable energy projects. This move by President-elect Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva aims to pivot the state-run firm away from its focus on deepwater exploration and dividend payments. Despite investor concerns about interventionism, Prates is seen as a moderate choice who understands the energy sector and could calm market fears.

title: Shell and APA among winners for deepwater oil & gas exploration blocks off Uruguay
summary: Uruguay's state-owned oil and gas company ANCAP has awarded deepwater offshore exploration blocks OFF-4 and OFF-5 to a consortium of Shell and APA Corporation, and to Argentina's YPF, respectively. This expands the presence of major international players in Uruguay's offshore oil and gas sector. The total nominal investment for work on these blocks is estimated at $31 million, with ANCAP highlighting that companies bear all exploration risks and costs.

title: Offen Petroleum Acquires Gas Depot Wholesale Division
summary: Offen Petroleum has acquired the wholesale division of Gas Depot Inc. and Gas Depot Oil Co., marking its entry into the Chicago market and the Great Lakes region. This acquisition adds over 150 new retail gas station and convenience-store customers, along with a portfolio of municipal customers. Gas Depot, founded by George Nediyakalayil, will continue to operate its own chain of gas stations after the transaction.

title: The 7 Best Oil Stocks to Buy Now
summary: This article identifies seven top oil stocks for investors to consider in 2023, including ExxonMobil, Devon Energy, Chevron, Occidental Petroleum, British Petroleum, Suncor Energy, and Marathon Oil. It highlights their recent financial performance, dividends, and strategic moves like share buybacks or activist investor involvement, noting that while oil prices have fallen, geopolitical tensions or an economic rebound could boost them. Each company's stock performance and key financial metrics are discussed as reasons for their inclusion on the list.

title: Skeena sells $20m royalty on Eskay Creek mine in Canada
summary: Skeena Resources has sold a 0.5% net smelter returns royalty on its Eskay Creek gold-silver project to Franco-Nevada for C$27m ($19.8m), with an additional C$1.5m ($1.10m) cash consideration. The proceeds will fund exploration and development activities at the Eskay Creek mine, as well as general administration and corporate purposes. The Eskay Creek mine, previously the world's highest-grade gold mine, is being revitalized by Skeena and is anticipated to have an annual production capacity of 352,000oz AuEq.

title: Shell, APA JV, YPF Win Offshore Blocks in Uruguay
summary: Uruguay's state oil company ANCAP has awarded two offshore blocks to Argentina's YPF and a consortium of Shell and APA, following previous awards in 2020 and 2022. Challenger Energy, an earlier awardee, welcomed the news, highlighting that most available offshore exploration blocks in Uruguay are now licensed, primarily to global oil and gas majors. Challenger also asserts that Uruguay's offshore potential is analogous to significant discoveries in Namibia's Orange Basin, leading to increased interest and substantial investment in the region.

title: U.S. Stock Market in 2022: Biggest Energy Winners
summary: In 2022, the energy sector significantly outperformed other segments of the S&P 500, with all companies in the industry finishing the year in positive territory. Driven by soaring global energy prices, particularly due to the Russia-Ukraine conflict, oil and gas exploration and production companies saw the highest gains, with Occidental Petroleum Corporation (OXY) leading with a +117% performance. The article also projects continued strong, though less volatile, performance for the energy sector into 2023, influenced by sanctions against Russia and China's reopening.

title: Phillips 66 expects tight gasoline, diesel supplies in summer -executive
summary: Phillips 66, a major U.S. oil refiner, anticipates tight supplies of gasoline and diesel this summer due to high demand and reduced global refining capacity. Despite refiners operating at near full capacity, a significant loss in global processing capacity has driven up profit margins and utilization rates, with further closures like Lyondell Basell's Houston refinery threatening to exacerbate the tightness. Phillips 66 plans to optimize its U.S. refineries and expects financial gains from converting its Rodeo, California, plant to renewable diesel.

title: Petrobras reinforces security at refineries after threats - sources
summary: Petrobras, Brazil's state-run oil company, increased security at its refineries, including the nation's largest fuel plant, following threats detected by its intelligence unit. The threats originated from social media monitoring of supporters of former far-right President Jair Bolsonaro, after thousands invaded government buildings. Despite the heightened security and collaboration with state police, Petrobras confirmed all assets were operating normally and the Mines and Energy Minister assured that fuel supply would continue without interruption.

title: Five new members named to Prisma’s board of directors
summary: Prisma Health Upstate Board of Directors has welcomed five new members, who began their three-year terms on January 1. The new board members are Robert Dye, Jack Ellenberg, Tee Hooper, Adela Mendoza, and Beverly Ward, bringing diverse professional experience to the board. They will join a group of existing directors to guide Prisma Health's Upstate operations.

title: Valero Energy Corp. stock outperforms competitors on strong trading day
summary: Valero Energy Corp. (VLO) stock increased by 2.67% on Tuesday, closing at $132.01, and outperformed competitors like Exxon Mobil Corp. and Chevron Corp. This marks the fourth consecutive day of gains for the stock, placing it $14.80 below its 52-week high. The strong performance occurred on a favorable trading day for the broader market, with both the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average rising.

title: Rigs report: BW on track to produce oil offshore Gabon; Transocean adds US$488M backlog
summary: The offshore drilling market is active, with BW Energy initiating drilling in Gabon targeting first oil in March 2023 and Borr Drilling securing new contracts in the Middle East and Southeast Asia. Transocean has also received significant contract awards and extensions totaling US$488 million for five drilling rigs, alongside preparations for a US$500 million senior secured notes offering. Additionally, an oil spill case involving ExxonMobil, Chevron, and Suncor's subsidiary in Newfoundland is proceeding to trial.

title: Wednesday's Top Analyst Upgrades and Downgrades: ADM, AT&T, Bank of America, Bloom Energy, Boeing, DR Horton, Exxon, Macy's, Morgan Stanley, Royal Caribbean and More
summary: This article details key analyst upgrades, downgrades, and initiations for various companies on Wednesday, January 11, 2023. It covers companies like ADM, AT&T, Bank of America, Boeing, Exxon, Macy's, and Royal Caribbean, providing their new ratings, target prices, and stock performance. The financial market context, including inflation concerns, Treasury yields, and oil prices, is also briefly discussed.

title: Exxon Mobil to Sell Thai Refinery, Retail Unit to Bangchak Corp
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. is selling its controlling 66% stake in Esso (Thailand) Pcl, which includes a local refinery and retail business, to Bangchak Corp. This move aligns with Exxon Mobil's strategy to concentrate on its US market operations and the production of lower-emission fuels. Bangchak will also extend a tender offer for the remaining 34% of Esso shares after obtaining regulatory approvals.

title: GlobalData: Shell dominated long-term LNG import contract volumes in 2022
summary: In 2022, Shell secured the most long-term liquefied natural gas (LNG) import contracts among key purchasing companies, totaling 6.7 million tonnes per annum (mtpa), according to GlobalData. This was driven by a significant 2.6 mtpa deal with Mexico Pacific Limited LLC. Energy companies are increasing long-term LNG contracts to hedge against price volatility and ensure supply, viewing natural gas as a bridge fuel for energy transition and decarbonization efforts.

title: Exxon Scientists Predicted Global Warming, Even as Company Cast Doubts, Study Finds (Published 2023)
summary: A new study published in the journal Science reveals that Exxon's own scientists accurately projected global warming caused by fossil fuels starting in the 1970s. Despite these precise internal projections, Exxon publicly expressed skepticism about climate science and ran a public relations campaign that questioned scientific consensus. This finding comes amidst ongoing lawsuits accusing Exxon and other companies of deceiving the public about climate change.

title: Reactions to the accuracy of Exxon's climate change predictions since the 1970s
summary: A Science Media Centre analysis examines the reactions to research revealing that ExxonMobil's internal climate predictions from the 1970s onwards accurately forecasted global warming, consistent with later observations. Experts highlight that despite this internal scientific accuracy, the company's public statements often contradicted its own data and engaged in disinformation campaigns to delay climate action. The article underscores the importance of corporate accountability and the dichotomy between ExxonMobil's scientific findings and its public communication strategy.

title: Consider QARP as Gas Prices Fall
summary: Inflation is slowing down, with the Labor Department’s consumer price index reporting a 6.5% rise in December, largely driven by decreasing gas prices. This decline in gas prices and logistics costs could significantly impact the Xtrackers Russell 1000 US QARP ETF (QARP), which includes gas companies. QARP focuses on large-cap U.S. equities with strong quality and value characteristics, aiming to identify quality companies that are not overpriced.

title: Exxon Mobil publicly denied global warming for years but quietly predicted it
summary: A new study reveals that Exxon Mobil Corp. had highly accurate predictions regarding global warming between 1977 and 2003, comparable to or even surpassing NASA's insights. Despite this internal knowledge, the company engaged in a decades-long public campaign to discredit climate science and sow doubt about the link between fossil fuels and climate change. This analysis adds to existing evidence that Exxon Mobil was aware of the dangers of burning fossil fuels while publicly denying them, leading to accusations of a deliberate disinformation campaign.

title: Consider QARP as Gas Prices Fall
summary: Inflation is slowing down, with consumer prices rising 6.5% annually in December, the slowest gain since October 2021, driven significantly by a drop in gas prices. This trend has implications for the Xtrackers Russell 1000 US QARP ETF (QARP), which includes holdings in gas companies like Exxon Mobil and Chevron. QARP focuses on large-cap U.S. equities with strong quality and value characteristics while aiming to avoid overpriced quality companies.

title: ExxonMobil predicted climate change while downplaying risk
summary: A new study reveals that ExxonMobil's own scientists accurately predicted global warming as far back as the 1970s, making projections consistent with independent academic and government findings. Despite this internal knowledge, the company publicly sowed doubt about climate change models, with executives dismissing them as "unproven" or "not competent." The study highlights the "hypocrisy" and "complicity" of ExxonMobil, which accurately modeled climate change years before actively working to spread misinformation and undermine climate science.

title: Exxon’s own models predicted global warming. It ignored them.
summary: A new analysis published in the journal Science reveals that Exxon's internal climate models from the 1970s and '80s accurately predicted global warming, matching state-of-the-art academic simulations. Despite this internal knowledge, Exxon engaged in public disinformation campaigns questioning climate science. These findings could now be used as evidence in ongoing climate litigation against the company, strengthening claims that Exxon knew the impacts of fossil fuels but actively sought to conceal them.

title: Exclusive: Exxon prepares to start up $2 bln Texas oil refinery expansion
summary: Exxon Mobil is preparing to fully start up a $2 billion expansion at its Beaumont, Texas, refinery, a project first conceptualized nine years ago. The expansion will boost gasoline and diesel production by 250,000 barrels per day and make Beaumont the second-largest refinery in the U.S. This comes as U.S. fuel stockpiles are low and amid calls from President Biden for refiners to increase output.

title: Chevron, Exxon and Total keen to invest in India, says minister
summary: India's oil minister announced that global energy majors Chevron Corp, Exxon Mobil Corp, and TotalEnergies are interested in investing in the country's oil and gas exploration and production sector. India, a major oil importer, seeks to reduce its dependence on costly overseas imports by monetizing its hydrocarbon reserves and aims to double its oil and gas exploration area by 2025. The minister extended an invitation for joint development production and investment in the domestic E&P sector.

title: Fuels, Antitrust: price irregularities for Eni, Esso, IP, Kuwait Petroleum Italia and Tamoil
summary: The Italian Antitrust Authority, with the help of the Guardia di Finanza, has initiated proceedings and carried out inspections against major oil companies (Eni, Esso, IP, Kuwait Petroleum Italia, and Tamoil) due to alleged price irregularities at over a thousand petrol stations across the country. The investigation found discrepancies between advertised and actual prices, omitted price displays, and failure to communicate prices to the "Osservaprezzi Carburanti" portal, indicating a lack of diligence by these companies in controlling their distribution networks.

title: These are the Houston companies with the most patents granted last year
summary: Saudi Aramco and Halliburton tied for the most U.S. patents granted to Houston companies in 2022, each receiving 963 patents and placing 44th nationally. Other Houston-area companies like Hewlett Packard Enterprise, SLB, Baker Hughes, ExxonMobil, and United Imaging Healthcare also made the Patent 300 list. Many of these companies, particularly in the energy sector, have significantly ramped up their patenting efforts, using patents as a leading indicator of innovation and a means to create value and protect investments.

title: San Antonio’s Valero dropping lawsuit that alleged it overpaid federal taxes during a 4-year period
summary: Valero Energy Corp. is dropping its lawsuit against the U.S. government seeking to recover over $400 million in tax refunds. The oil refiner had alleged it overpaid federal income taxes from 2005 to 2008, related to tax credits for alcohol fuel and biodiesel mixtures. The decision to drop the suit follows a ruling against Exxon Mobil Corp. in a similar case and Exxon's subsequent failure to appeal to the Supreme Court.

title: YPF se sumó a la suba del 4% de las naftas en CABA, pero en el interior algunas marcas lo hacen hasta casi el 10%
summary: YPF has increased fuel prices by 4% in CABA, following similar moves by Shell and Axion. However, in various provinces, some brands have raised prices by up to 9%, driven by factors like international oil prices, exchange rates, and logistical costs. This continues the "Precios Justos" agreement with monthly 4% increases for fuels, with further negotiations planned for later in the year.

title: 3 Inflation Risks Investors Shouldn’t Ignore
summary: Despite recent indicators suggesting a cooling of inflation, Morgan Stanley's Chief Investment Officer, Lisa Shalett, warns that investors' optimism may be premature. She highlights three key inflation risks—rising energy costs, persistent import price increases, and sticky services inflation—that could prevent a straightforward decline in core inflation. These factors could keep interest rates higher for longer and market volatility elevated, recommending investors consider overweighting fixed income and hedging portfolios with value-oriented assets.

title: PureCycle to build first European PP-recycling plant in Belgium
summary: PureCycle Technologies, Inc. is set to construct its first European polypropylene (PP) recycling facility in the Port of Antwerp-Bruges' NextGen District in Belgium. The plant is projected to have an initial annual capacity of 59,000 metric tons, with potential expansion to 240,000 metric tons across four processing lines. This strategic move aims to expand PureCycle's global footprint, supply Ultra-Pure Recycled (UPR) resin to the European market, and create 65-70 new jobs.

title: Fort Worth energy firm renames itself TXO, launches IPO
summary: Fort Worth-based oil and gas company MorningStar Partners LP, founded by Bob Simpson, plans a $100 million initial public offering and will rename itself TXO Energy Partners L.P., trading under the "TXO" symbol on the NYSE. The company will focus on acquiring, developing, and producing oil and gas reserves primarily in the Permian and San Juan Basins. Industry experts like Bruce Bullock note that TXO's strong management team, led by Simpson, offers stability for investors despite political uncertainties in the energy sector.

title: Wednesday's Top Analyst Upgrades and Downgrades: BP, Exxon Mobil, Kroger, Microsoft, RingCentral, Wayfair, Wendy's and More
summary: This article compiles top analyst upgrades, downgrades, and initiations from Wednesday, January 18, 2023, for various major companies including BP, Exxon Mobil, Kroger, Microsoft, RingCentral, and Wayfair. It highlights current market conditions, including higher futures trading, ongoing Q4 earnings reports impacting S&P 500 companies, and movements in Treasury yields, oil prices, natural gas, and cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin. Analysts are keenly focused on guidance for the upcoming quarters, with expectations of potential full-year earnings forecast adjustments.

title: TXO Energy Partners Announces Launch of Initial Public Offering
summary: TXO Energy Partners, formerly MorningStar Partners, L.P., has announced the launch of its initial public offering, offering 5,000,000 common units with an option for underwriters to purchase an additional 750,000 units. The company, focused on oil and gas reserves primarily in the Permian and San Juan Basins, expects the offering price to be between $19 and $21 per unit and has applied to list on the NYSE under "TXO." This move represents an approximate 17% limited partner interest in TXO.

title: Seapeak trials Starlink on LNG carrier
summary: Seapeak, formerly Teekay LNG Partners, is conducting trials of Starlink satellite internet services on its vessels, including the LNG carrier Seapeak Polar, which had the service installed in November 2022. Initial results show Starlink provides significantly faster speeds and lower latency than traditional satellite connectivity, enabling high-quality video conferencing and improved cloud service utilization. Subject to continued positive outcomes, Seapeak plans a fleet-wide rollout in 2023, with four more vessels already slated for installation in the coming months.

title: Dallas’ Matador Resources strikes a $1.6 billion deal in the Texas Oil Patch
summary: Dallas-based Matador Resources Co. has agreed to acquire Advance Energy Partners Holdings LLC for approximately $1.6 billion in cash, marking the largest deal in Matador’s 20-year history. This acquisition further consolidates the Permian Basin, a trend observed across the industry. The deal comes shortly after HighPeak Energy Inc., another Permian explorer, announced it was considering selling itself, indicating a dynamic period for mergers and acquisitions in the Texas Oil Patch.

title: NYSE glitch leads to busted trades, prompts investigation
summary: A system issue at the New York Stock Exchange caused widespread trading halts and busted trades in over 250 securities on Tuesday morning. The glitch prevented opening auctions for many stocks, leading to erroneous prices that were later declared null, prompting an investigation by the NYSE and review by the SEC. This event highlights concerns about market resilience and the potential costs to traders and brokers.

title: Bonos de YPF tienen “potencial de rentabilidad superior”, según Bloomberg Intelligence
summary: Bloomberg Intelligence highlights YPF bonds as a "rarity" in emerging markets due to their combination of deep discounts, relative liquidity, and superior return potential compared to other emerging market companies. Despite Argentina's fiscal challenges and YPF's exposure to national fuel price policies, the development of Vaca Muerta's unconventional reserves is seen as crucial for mitigating currency tension and increasing crude oil exports. The report notes that YPF's 2033 bond trades at a significant discount, offering an attractive investment opportunity.

title: Best commodities to invest in
summary: The article discusses the performance of commodities in 2022 and identifies five leading commodities for investment in Q1 2023: Oil, Gold, Silver, Copper, and Coffee. It examines the factors influencing each commodity's price, such as inflation, interest rates, global demand, and geopolitical events, and suggests potential investment strategies including stocks, ETFs, and CFDs. The piece highlights that commodities served as a hedge against inflation in 2022 and are expected to continue to offer investment opportunities due to ongoing economic uncertainties and geopolitical factors.

title: Exclusive: Exxon halts routine gas flaring in the Permian, wants others to follow
summary: Exxon Mobil announced it has ceased routine natural gas flaring in the Permian Basin and advocates for stricter industry-wide regulations. The company aims for a "level playing field" in emissions reduction by focusing on potent methane, planning to launch a satellite system to monitor emissions, and investing

title: News Content Hub - Rigs report: Hess reports new oil discovery offshore Guyana
summary: Hess has reported a significant oil discovery offshore Guyana with its Fangtooth SE-1 well, adding to the region's estimated 11 billion barrels of oil equivalent. This discovery, along with CGX Energy and Frontera Energy Corp's drilling efforts in the Corentyne block and TotalEnergies' upcoming Benriach well, highlights increased exploration and development activity in the area. Various companies are also securing major subsea contracts, upgrading rig fleets, and engaging in carbon capture storage projects, indicating a busy period for offshore energy.

title: Imperial Oil takes FID on Strathcona refinery renewables project
summary: Imperial Oil has given final investment decision (FID) for a new renewable diesel production complex at its Strathcona refinery near Edmonton, Alberta. The project, estimated at $560 million, will produce over 1 billion liters/year of low-carbon renewable diesel using low-carbon hydrogen and locally sourced feedstocks, aiming to reduce Canada's transportation sector GHG emissions by about 3 million tonnes/year. Scheduled for startup in 2025, this initiative aligns with Canada's Clean Fuel Regulation and ExxonMobil's lower-emission investment strategy.

title: Suape port receives largest ever GLP import cargo
summary: The Port of Suape has received its largest-ever import of Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) by a private agent in Brazil's Northeast, with 12,500 tonnes facilitated by Interco and Transportadora Gas del Sur. This operation marks a significant step in breaking Petrobras's long-standing monopoly on LPG imports in the region, promoting competition and potentially lowering consumer prices. The move helps meet regional demand, which national refineries cannot fully cover, and continuous imports are being explored.

title: Imperial Oil to invest $539 mln in renewable diesel plant in Canada
summary: Imperial Oil announced a C$720 million ($538.64 million) investment to build Canada's largest renewable diesel facility at its Strathcona refinery, set to open in 2025 and produce 20,000 barrels per day. The project aims to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by approximately 3 million a year and will be partly funded by credits under British Columbia's Low Carbon Fuel Standard. This strategic investment is seen by analysts as a neutral impact for now, but a move towards reducing emissions.

title: Chevron annual profit hits record but Q4 miss hits shares
summary: Chevron announced a record $36.5 billion annual profit for 2022, more than double the previous year, but its fourth-quarter earnings fell short of Wall Street estimates due to asset writedowns and rising costs, causing shares to drop. Despite the Q4 miss, the company plans to maintain its share buyback program at $5 billion to $15 billion per year, emphasizing shareholder returns while increasing capital expenditure for 2023, particularly in the U.S.

title: Imperial Oil to build $560m renewable diesel facility in Canada
summary: Imperial Oil, an ExxonMobil affiliate, plans to invest approximately $560 million to construct Canada's largest renewable diesel facility at its Strathcona refinery in Alberta. Scheduled for commissioning in 2025, the facility will produce 20,000 barrels of renewable diesel daily from locally sourced feedstocks, incorporating low-carbon hydrogen and carbon capture technology. This project is expected to create 600 construction jobs and reduce greenhouse gas emissions by nearly three million metric tonnes annually, aligning with ExxonMobil's broader investment in lower-emission initiatives.

title: White House blasts Big Oil stock buybacks again as Chevron profits double
summary: The White House criticized U.S. oil companies for prioritizing shareholder payouts over increasing supply after Chevron announced its 2022 annual profit doubled to a record $36.5 billion. Chevron plans to triple its share repurchases to $75 billion over five years. The administration argues that oil companies have the necessary resources and permits to boost production but are choosing to funnel "windfall profits" to executives and shareholders instead.

title: News Content Hub - LNG imports to China tumble 20% in 2022
summary: China's LNG imports plummeted by 20% in 2022 due to stringent Covid-19 lockdowns and a pivot towards increased domestic natural gas production and pipeline imports, including from Russia. Despite a December surge in imports following the easing of Covid restrictions, analysts at Poten & Partners anticipate only moderate growth in LNG imports for 2023 and 2024, as China continues to re-sell existing cargo contracts and relies more on domestic and pipeline gas. This shift suggests China will likely remain out of the spot LNG market for most of 2023.

title: bp Energy Outlook 2023 explores key trends and uncertainties surrounding the energy transition
summary: BP's Energy Outlook 2023 (bp.com/energyoutlook) examines the energy transition up to 2050 through three scenarios: Net Zero, Accelerated, and New Momentum, incorporating the impacts of the Russia-Ukraine war and the US Inflation Reduction Act. The report emphasizes balancing energy security, affordability, and lower carbon while highlighting the growing importance of renewables, low-carbon hydrogen, and carbon capture technologies. It projects oil demand declines but continued significant role for 15-20 years, and a decarbonizing power system led by wind and solar.

title: ExxonMobil awards FEED for world's largest low-carbon hydrogen facility
summary: ExxonMobil has awarded a contract for front-end engineering and design (FEED) for what is expected to be the world's largest low-carbon hydrogen production facility. This project aims to produce one billion cubic feet of low-carbon hydrogen per day, capture over 98% of associated CO2 emissions, and enable a significant reduction in Scope 1 and 2 emissions at its Baytown integrated complex. A final investment decision is anticipated by 2024, with startup planned for 2027-2028.

title: Spotlight on the evolving needs of the Middle East energy market
summary: TechnipFMC is increasing its presence in the Middle East, a strategic and fast-growing energy market, by aligning with national oil companies' in-country value programs and expanding facilities. Thierry Conti, President of Surface Technologies, highlights the company's client-centric approach and commitment to local industrialization, aiming to become the preferred supplier in drilling and completions. The region is also seen as crucial for energy transition, with significant opportunities in digitalization, electrification, and new energies like carbon capture and hydrogen.

title: Exxon smashes Western oil majors' earnings record with $56 billion profit for 2022
summary: Exxon Mobil reported a record $56 billion profit for 2022, marking a historic high for the Western oil industry. This significant profit, driven by high oil prices, soaring demand, and cost cuts, has rekindled debates over windfall profit taxes. The company's CFO, Kathryn Mikells, criticized windfall taxes as "unlawful and bad policy," arguing they discourage new oil and gas production.

title: Exxon posts record $56bn profit for 2022 in historic high for western oil industry | ExxonMobil
summary: Exxon Mobil reported a record $56 billion profit for 2022, marking a historic high for the western oil industry, driven by high prices, soaring demand, and cost-cutting measures during the pandemic. The company's earnings, approximately $6.3 million an hour, have reignited calls for windfall profit taxes as oil majors are expected to collectively reach nearly $200 billion in profits. Despite a $1.3 billion hit from an EU windfall tax and asset impairments in the fourth quarter, Exxon's full-year profit excluding these charges still reached $59.1 billion, with increased production.

title: U.S. refiners expect Russian fuel sanctions to keep margins high
summary: U.S. oil refiners anticipate that the European Union's upcoming ban on Russian fuel imports, effective next week, will sustain their high profit margins throughout the year. Executives from companies like Exxon Mobil, Marathon Petroleum, and Phillips 66 reported strong 2022 results due to high demand for diesel and jet fuel, and expect these tight fuel supplies to keep margins elevated, potentially into 2024. The ban is also expected to reduce Russian refinery utilization and lower exports of key intermediates like vacuum gasoil, further bolstering refining profitability.

title: White House blasts Exxon over historical $56 bln annual profit
summary: The White House criticized Exxon Mobil Corp's record $56 billion net profit in 2022, labeling it "outrageous" given that Americans faced high gas prices. The administration argued that oil companies have the resources to increase production but are instead prioritizing executive and shareholder profits, while Exxon's CFO countered that windfall taxes would be unlawful and counterproductive to increasing supply.

title: Biden Clears the Way for Alaska Oil Project (Published 2023)
summary: The Biden administration has taken a significant step towards approving ConocoPhillips' $8 billion Willow oil drilling project in Alaska, drawing strong criticism from environmental groups. The Bureau of Land Management's analysis suggests a scaled-back version of the project, reducing drill sites and infrastructure, thereby signaling a likely green light. Despite the Interior Department's concerns about emissions and environmental impact, the decision is expected within a month.

title: Exxon, Chevron, ConocoPhillips eye Permian Basin growth in 2023
summary: Exxon, Chevron, and ConocoPhillips are planning significant production growth in the Permian Basin for 2023. ConocoPhillips, which acquired Shell's Permian Basin business for $9.5 billion in 2021, anticipates its Lower 48 production growth to be primarily driven by this region. This focus comes after a year of substantial activity in the Permian Basin by oil and gas companies in 2022.

title: Oil companies in 2022 had their most profitable year in history
summary: Global oil companies, including Chevron, ConocoPhillips, Exxon, and Shell, achieved record profits in 2022, collectively reaching $1 trillion in sales. This surge was driven by Russia's war on Ukraine and post-pandemic economic recovery pushing oil prices to historic highs. The White House and environmentalists have criticized these "windfall" profits, with some, like the EU and UK, implementing taxes on surplus energy company earnings.

title: Calcasieu refineries described as among the worst in the country
summary: A new report by the Environmental Integrity Project identifies Calcasieu refineries, specifically Phillips 66 and CITGO in Lake Charles, as among the worst in the nation for ammonia pollution. The report highlights that these refineries legally discharge large quantities of pollutants under current permits and often exceed even those limits, leading to significant nitrogen pollution in the Calcasieu River. Environmental advocates are calling for stricter EPA enforcement and improved technology to protect public health and the environment.

title: Air Products and Chemicals, Inc. (NYSE:APD) Q1 2023 Earnings Call Transcript
summary: This is a Q1 2023 earnings call transcript for Air Products and Chemicals, Inc. (NYSE:APD), discussing various aspects of their business. Key topics include competition in the blue ammonia market, premium pricing for blue hydrogen sold to Exxon for renewable diesel production, and the impact of fluctuating power costs on European and American merchant price increases. The call also touched on the design stability and ammonia production capacity of the NEOM project.

title: BP share price rises as profits hit record high in 2022
summary: BP announced record-breaking underlying replacement cost profits of $27.7 billion for 2022, more than double 2021's figure, prompting a 10% increase in its quarterly dividend and a new $2.75 billion share buyback program. Despite missing Q4 earnings forecasts, the company generated significant operating cashflow, allowing for reduced debt and increased shareholder returns. BP also committed to rebalancing its investment, allocating equal budget to cleaner energy projects and its core oil and gas business by 2030, while slightly slowing its oil and gas production reduction targets.

title: General Atomics Aeronautical Systems Wins $34 Million Navy Award
summary: General Atomics Aeronautical Systems Inc. (GA-ASI) secured a $34.2 million modification to a Navy contract for eight mobile ground control stations and six ground data terminals. These systems will support the Marine Air Ground Task Force Unmanned Aircraft System Expeditionary Medium Altitude Long Endurance MQ-9A Block 5 Reaper air vehicles. The article also lists various other defense contracts awarded to different companies across the Army and Defense Logistics Agency.

title: BP's shares hit 3-1/2-year high after it cuts emissions targets
summary: BP's shares reached a three-and-a-half-year high after the company reported record profits and announced it would produce more oil and gas for longer, while also lowering its emissions reduction targets for the current decade. The company now plans to reduce its oil equivalent output by 25% by 2030, a less aggressive target than its previous 40% reduction goal, and has also scaled back ambitions for cutting emissions from fuels sold to customers. This shift reflects a move towards pragmatism in response to global energy demand and high energy prices.

title: Enbridge’s Line 5 threatens Indigenous land and peoples
summary: A federal judge refused to decommission Enbridge's Line 5 pipeline despite its threat to Indigenous land and the environment, requiring the Bad River Band of Lake Superior Chippewa and Enbridge to agree on a spill mitigation plan. The 70-year-old pipeline, which transports 540,000 barrels of oil daily, is dangerously close to the Bad River, threatening pristine water and treaty-protected resources like wild rice. Environmental advocates and tribal nations are calling for its shutdown due to the high risk of spills and the erosion of Indigenous sovereignty.

title: DLA Announces $3.5B in Fuel Supply Contracts With 18 Companies
summary: The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) has awarded approximately $3.5 billion in indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contracts to 18 companies for fuel supply to military bases over a one-year period. Phillips 66 and Petromax Refining secured the largest contracts, each exceeding $600 million. These contracts, resulting from a competitive acquisition process, will ensure fuel provision until April 30, 2024, across various U.S. locations.

title: Por que EUA, França, Reino Unido e Alemanha reestatizaram os serviços de água e esgoto?
summary: This article discusses why countries like the USA, France, the UK, and Germany have re-nationalized water and sewage services, contrasting this trend with Brazil's move towards privatization. It highlights that the re-nationalizations were largely due to abusive tariffs and a decline in service quality under private management, particularly impacting vulnerable populations. The Sintaema union argues that privatization prioritizes profit over universal access and quality of service, advocating against the privatization of essential services like those offered by Sabesp in Brazil.

title: Exxon Plans Trading Division to Vie for Commodity Profits
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. is establishing a new global trading division to enhance its competitiveness in energy derivatives, directly challenging companies like BP and Shell. This strategic move is part of a broader corporate reorganization that also includes creating a global business hub for finance and procurement, and a new supply-chain unit. The aim is to centralize and optimize its trading operations across crude, natural gas, power, and petroleum products.

title: Australian contractor Worley lands Canada oil sands prize with five-year deal
summary: Australian contractor Worley has secured a five-year contract with Imperial Oil Resources for its Kearl oil sands facility in Canada. The deal solidified Worley's presence in the Canadian oil sands sector. The article highlights the significance of this contract for the Australian firm.

title: Linde Contracts with OCI to Bolster Natural Gas-Fueled Blue Ammonia Project Near Houston
summary: Linde plc has signed a long-term contract with OCI NV to supply low-carbon hydrogen and nitrogen for OCI's planned natural gas-fueled blue ammonia plant near Houston. This $1.8 billion investment aims to support decarbonization efforts by utilizing carbon capture and storage for over 1.7 million metric tons/year of carbon dioxide emissions. The project will leverage blue hydrogen, produced from natural gas with CCS, and contribute to OCI's clean fuels platform to supply both U.S. and export markets.

title: Wills Group taps former Jack in the Box CEO for its board of directors
summary: The Wills Group, owner of Dash In Food Stores, has appointed Lenny Comma, former CEO of Jack in the Box, to its board of directors. Comma brings over three decades of experience in foodservice and retail fuels, starting his career with ExxonMobil. His appointment signals the Wills Group's increased focus on expanding Dash In's foodservice offerings to compete more effectively with fast-food restaurants.

title: Investors welcome Petrobras’ signing of the UN Oil and Gas Methane Partnership
summary: Investors involved with Climate Action 100+ have applauded Petrobras' decision to join the UN Oil & Gas Methane Partnership 2.0 (OGMP 2.0). This move is seen as a significant step in the company's commitment to climate action, particularly in reducing methane emissions, which are a potent greenhouse gas. The initiative aligns Petrobras with global efforts to mitigate warming and is a key milestone in ongoing investor engagement.

title: 4 key factors driving the ‘perfect storm’ in molybdenum markets
summary: The global molybdenum markets are experiencing a "perfect storm" driven by four key factors: demand volatility, supply deficits, disruptions at Peruvian mines, and production issues in Europe. This combination has led to record-high ferromolybdenum prices, surpassing expectations and historical records, with a significant spike of 18% on January 30, 2023. The tight market conditions are exacerbated by reduced long-term contracts, reliance on the spot market, and unwillingness of traders to release material, making prices highly volatile.

title: Exxon Mobil Is the Biggest Gainer in the Management Top 250
summary: Exxon Mobil achieved the largest gains in the latest Management Top 250 ranking, primarily driven by significant improvements in its financial strength and innovation scores.
