The ranking, developed by the Drucker Institute, assesses corporate effectiveness across various criteria including customer satisfaction, employee engagement, innovation, social responsibility, and financial strength. Other companies following Exxon Mobil in gains were Crown Castle and Chevron Corp.

title: Herb Vogel (MechEngr’82)
summary: Herb Vogel (MechEngr’82) was appointed president and chief executive officer of SM Energy in 2020, bringing over 38 years of experience in the energy business. He is an alumnus of CU Boulder, where he met his wife, and has been a significant contributor to the Mechanical Engineering Strategic Advisory Board and the College of Engineering Advisory Council, both through advice and financial support. The Vogels have established faculty and graduate student fellowships at CU Boulder, demonstrating their commitment to supporting education and research.

title: Exxon tells U.S. labor board refinery lockout did not target union
summary: Exxon Mobil told the U.S. National Labor Relations Board (NLRB) that its 10-month lockout of union workers at its Beaumont, Texas refinery was aimed at cutting costs and improving profits, not eliminating union representation. The NLRB had previously deemed the lockout "unlawful" and called for the company to compensate the 650 affected workers. Exxon argued that operating losses and the high cost of replacement workers in previous negotiations led to the lockout and demands for changes in job and contract terms, emphasizing that decertification of the union was never a factor.

title: Petrobras Taps Maersk, Alcatel for Mero Field PRM System
summary: Petrobras has awarded Alcatel Submarine Networks and Maersk Supply Service a contract to supply and install a Permanent Reservoir Monitoring (PRM) system for the Mero field in Brazil. The system, involving 400 kilometers of optical fibers, will monitor and optimize oil production from the deep offshore pre-salt area. Installation is slated to begin in 2024 to enhance reservoir management and increase oil recovery.

title: Flex LNG Expects ‘Massive’ Henry Hub Arbitrage to Keep Fueling U.S. LNG Expansions
summary: Flex LNG management anticipates that significant price discrepancies between global LNG benchmarks (European and Asian prices) and Henry Hub will continue to drive investments in U.S. LNG infrastructure through the middle of the decade. Despite recent slides in global LNG prices, the company expects the arbitrage to remain strong, supporting further expansion of U.S. export capacity, particularly from projects nearing final investment decisions on the Gulf Coast. Flex LNG's own chartered vessels also saw increased earnings in Q4 2022 as LNG prices fell and Asian demand began to return.

title: What to know about 'woke' public investing and why Iowa Gov. Kim Reynolds wants it banned
summary: Iowa Governor Kim Reynolds is proposing a bill that would prevent the state's public funds from investing based on environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors. The bill aims to ensure investments are solely based on financial returns, rather than "political agendas and woke ideology." Although Iowa's public agencies currently do not use ESG investing, the bill's proponents argue it is a preemptive measure to prevent future adoption of such practices.

title: Will the Biden Administration Greenlight ConocoPhillips’ “Carbon Bomb”?
summary: The Biden administration faces a critical decision regarding ConocoPhillips' controversial Willow Project in Alaska, a proposed oil and gas development projected to produce 278 million metric tons of greenhouse gas emissions. Environmental groups label it a "carbon bomb" that would undermine climate goals, while the Alaska delegation and energy security concerns press for its approval. The White House's recent cautious statements suggest internal divisions and potential for project modifications, though a full reversal seems unlikely amidst political pressures.

title: Guyana aims to change lopsided oil deal
summary: Guyana's government plans to introduce stricter terms for new oil and gas contracts, including corporate taxes, reduced investment recovery costs, higher royalty rates, and significant signing bonuses. While existing "lopsided" agreements with companies like ExxonMobil will be honored, future players will face these new rules to increase annual revenues from the booming offshore oil sector. This move aims to boost Guyana's share of profits from 14.5% to 27.5%.

title: Independent Energy Company HF Sinclair Appoints New CEO/President
summary: HF Sinclair Corp. has promoted Tim Go to Chief Executive Officer and President, effective May 9, also appointing him to its board of directors. Go has served as president and chief operating officer since November 2021 and succeeds Michael C. Jennings, who will continue in the CEO role until May 8 before transitioning to executive vice president, corporate, until his retirement in November. Jennings praised Go's leadership in the company's recent growth and in its refining and lubricants and specialty products segments.

title: Guyana Aims to Reclaim 20% of Stabroek Block from ExxonMobil
summary: Guyana plans to reclaim 20% of the Stabroek oil block from the ExxonMobil-led consortium, citing missed investment deadlines and a push for more competition in its oil sector. The country aims to remarket these unexplored portions by next year and is also preparing for its first competitive auction of 14 offshore blocks, along with seeking bilateral agreements with state-controlled oil companies from India, Qatar, and the UAE. This move comes amid criticism of the prior deal's terms and follows new fiscal policies increasing Guyana’s share of oil proceeds.

title: Suncor Taps Former Exxon Executive as CEO After Elliott Pressure
summary: Suncor Energy Inc. has appointed Rich Kruger, former CEO of Exxon Mobil Corp.'s Canadian unit Imperial Oil Ltd., as its new chief executive officer. This appointment follows a seven-month search initiated after a series of worker deaths and pressure from activist investor Elliott Investment Management LP. Kruger's primary tasks will involve improving Suncor's safety record and navigating continued demands from Elliott, with current interim CEO Kris Smith remaining as CFO.

title: Suncor names former Imperial chief Rich Kruger as new CEO amid shareholder pressure
summary: Suncor Energy Inc. has appointed Rich Kruger, former head of Imperial Oil Ltd., as its new chief executive officer, effective April 3. This decision comes after pressure from activist investor Elliott Investment Management LP, following a period of safety incidents and the resignation of the previous CEO. Kruger is known for his focus on safety and operational excellence, and his appointment is seen as a positive step by analysts for improving Suncor's performance and safety culture.

title: ‘É um contrassenso o Brasil importar mais petróleo’, diz CEO da Acelen
summary: Luiz de Mendonça, CEO da Acelen, a primeira refinaria privatizada da Petrobras, discute os desafios e planos da empresa no primeiro ano do governo Lula. Ele aborda questões como a desoneração de combustíveis, que pode comprometer a produção e capital de giro da Acelen, e defende que o Brasil, sendo exportador de petróleo, não deveria precisar importar mais devido a condições fiscais desfavoráveis para refinarias privadas. Mendonça também destaca o sucesso da privatização da refinaria e seus investimentos, além de não acreditar em uma reversão do processo de privatização.

title: by geoLOGIC | News | Former Imperial Top Boss Rich Kruger Named Suncor President And Chief Executive Officer
summary: Suncor Energy Inc. has named Rich Kruger, former chairman, president, and CEO of Imperial Oil Limited, as its new president and chief executive officer, effective April 3, 2023. Kruger previously had a 39-year career with Exxon Mobil Corporation. Kris Smith, the interim CEO, will transition to chief financial officer and executive vice-president of corporate development after a smooth handover.

title: Suncor gives all-clear after incident at its Commerce City refinery in Colorado
summary: Suncor Energy Inc. has issued an all-clear after responding to a vapor leak at its Commerce City refinery in Colorado during maintenance activities. The leak was quickly contained, no injuries were reported, and air monitors indicated no acute public health risk. This incident follows previous challenges at the refinery, including a shutdown due to extreme weather and a fire in December that injured two workers, significantly impacting Colorado's gas and diesel markets.

title: Chemical maker INEOS makes U.S. shale bet with $1.4 bln Chesapeake deal
summary: INEOS is entering the U.S. oil and gas production market with a $1.4 billion acquisition of assets in South Texas from Chesapeake Energy Corp. This deal provides INEOS with access to natural gas and allows Chesapeake Energy to exit the Eagle Ford shale basin and focus on natural gas production, using the proceeds to repay debt and fund share repurchases.

title: Equinor to divest Bahamas oil terminal to Liwathon
summary: Equinor has agreed to sell its South Riding Point oil terminal in the Bahamas to Liwathon Group to focus its portfolio on core areas. The terminal, with a storage capacity of 6.8 million barrels, was acquired by Equinor in 2009 for trading American market oil. Liwathon, which operates four oil liquid terminals in Estonia, will take over the facility and its employees, planning to restart regular operations.

title: Exxon warns of Russia risks to its $2.5 billion Kazakhstan income
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp has warned of potential risks to its oil operations in Kazakhstan, which generated $2.5 billion in earnings last year. The primary concern is the reliance on the Caspian Pipeline Consortium (CPC) line, which transports oil through Russia. Any disruption to this pipeline could result in significant losses for Exxon and other major oil players like Chevron and Shell, given Kazakhstan's strategic and geographical position bordering Russia.

title: Jim Ratcliffe's INEOS owns the rights to shale gas underneath Manchester United's Carrington training ground
summary: INEOS, owned by Sir Jim Ratcliffe, holds a 60% stake in an onshore oil and gas license (PEDL193) that includes the rights to explore for shale gas beneath Manchester United's Carrington training ground and near Old Trafford. This ownership emerged in 2015 when INEOS acquired a stake in the license and committed to exploring shale gas, facing criticism for "greenwashing" while primarily being a petrochemical company. The article also notes that while INEOS recently acquired US shale assets, the UK license remains active until the end of 2024, raising implications should Ratcliffe's bid for Manchester United be successful.

title: Infographic: Highlights of Booking Holdings’ Q4 2022 earnings report
summary: Booking Holdings Inc. reported strong financial results for Q4 2022, with net income rising to $1.24 billion, or $31.92 per share. Adjusted profit increased 56% to $24.74 per share, and total revenues grew 36% year-over-year to $4.05 billion. The company achieved its highest-ever annual revenue of $17 billion in 2022.

title: Storm Freddy could strike Sasol natural gas operations
summary: Severe tropical storm Freddy is forecast to make landfall in Mozambique as a tropical cyclone, potentially impacting Sasol's natural gas operations near Vilankulo. The storm has already caused the port of Beira to halt operations and has prompted flight cancellations and school closures in affected regions. Experts predict widespread flooding and significant impact due to months' worth of rain falling in a few days.

title: Dutch gov't, Shell and Exxon ignored Groningen risks for years, inquiry finds
summary: A parliamentary inquiry has concluded that the Dutch government and energy companies Shell and Exxon Mobil ignored the risks of gas production in Groningen for years, leading to significant damage and distress for residents. The report states that the companies and government "gravely underestimated" the problems caused by gas extraction, which generated substantial profits while residents suffered from earth tremors. The committee urged the state and oil companies to reconcile their debt to Groningen's people.

title: Ethylene Oxide Adds to Toxic Burden for Memphis Residents
summary: The article highlights the plight of South Memphis residents, particularly Rose Sims, who face severe health risks from industrial pollution, including ethylene oxide emissions from Sterilization Services of Tennessee. Despite a history of environmental injustices and recent victories against other pollutants, the community struggles to get action on ethylene oxide, a known carcinogen. The Union of Concerned Scientists' report, "Invisible Threat, Inequitable Impact," underscores the urgent need for updated federal regulations and local intervention to protect vulnerable populations.

title: How Have the Top U.S. Asset Managers Voted in 2022?
summary: This article analyzes how the top U.S. asset managers voted on key environmental and social shareholder resolutions in 2022, comparing trends across 2020-2022. It highlights a significant increase in social and environmental resolutions and varying support levels among major asset managers, especially the "Big Three" (Vanguard, BlackRock, State Street). The report also examines how sustainable funds within these managers voted compared to their wider fund ranges.

title: Vaca Muerta revive la esperanza de Argentina en la producción de shale
summary: Argentina is constructing a 573-kilometer gas pipeline from the Vaca Muerta shale formation to its eastern cities, a move aimed at significantly reducing the country's reliance on fuel imports and potentially re-establishing itself as a key energy exporter. This project, coupled with planned expansions, addresses infrastructure bottlenecks that have hindered production from the Vaca Muerta basin, one of the world's largest shale deposits. The completion of the gas pipeline, named Presidente Néstor Kirchner and expected by June 20, is critical for meeting winter gas demand and is seen as a pivotal step towards stabilizing Argentina's economy and attracting further investment in the energy sector.

title: Chevron boosts share buyback program, hikes U.S. spending
summary: Chevron Corp. announced an expansion of its share buyback program to $17.5 billion annually and plans to significantly boost its U.S. oil and gas production by 750,000 barrels per day by 2027. The company aims to achieve this growth through increased investment in shale basins and the Gulf of Mexico, with an overall goal of raising global output by 3% annually. This move reflects a broader trend among U.S. oil companies to focus investments domestically, driven by cost reduction efforts and geopolitical considerations.

title: PR News | Trump's New Witch Hunt Target - Tue., Feb. 28, 2023
summary: Donald Trump's media company is seeking congressional action against SEC chairman Gary Gensler, alleging that the SEC's "endless investigation" into its merger with Digital World Acquisition Corp. is politically motivated due to Gensler's past involvement with Hillary Clinton's campaign. TMTG claims the stalled deal has destroyed billions in enterprise value and seeks Gensler's impeachment and agency budget cuts. The article also touches on Ignitis Group's appeal for energy companies to donate profits to Ukraine and Rupert Murdoch's admission regarding Fox News' election coverage.

title: Yinson Production Inks Deal For Project FPSO Agogo In Angola
summary: Yinson Production (YP) has secured a firm contract with Eni Angola S.p.A. for the provision, operation, and maintenance of a floating, production, storage and offloading (FPSO) asset for the Agogo Integrated West Hub Development Project in Angola. The contract is valued at approximately USD5.3 billion for a 15-year firm period with a 5-year extension option. This marks YP's first offshore production project in Angola, its eighth FPSO in West Africa, and will increase its total order book to around USD22.4 billion, with operations expected to start in Q4 2025.

title: BP to Sell CF Industries 2.2 Bcf of Certified Natural Gas to Decarbonize Ammonia
summary: BP has agreed to sell 2.2 Bcf of certified natural gas to CF Industries Holdings Inc. this year, marking the first time certified gas will be used in industrial manufacturing to decarbonize ammonia production. This move is a significant step in CF Industries' decarbonization efforts, aiming to reduce Scope 3 emissions and enhance the appeal of low-carbon ammonia as a clean energy source. The independently certified natural gas, verified by MiQ for lower methane emissions intensity, will help CF Industries track supply through its ammonia production process and further its goal to reduce 10% of its Scope 3 emissions by 2030.

title: Chevron to update production targets during investor day
summary: Chevron is expected to update its operational plans and production targets during an investor day, balancing oil output and shareholder returns with lower carbon emissions. Investors will focus on updates regarding Chevron's renewable fuels business, carbon emissions goals, and natural gas discoveries off Israel, especially given challenges like inflation in the Permian Basin and political risks in Kazakhstan. The company's expansion in Venezuela and its substantial share buyback program will also be key discussion points.

title: Schwab U.S. Large-Cap Value ETF Holdings List (NYSEARCA:SCHV)
summary: This article provides a list of the top 25 holdings of the Schwab U.S. Large-Cap Value ETF (NYSEARCA: SCHV). The ETF's holdings include major companies like Berkshire Hathaway, JPMorgan Chase & Co., and Exxon Mobil, detailing their current price, weight within the ETF, and shares held. The data reflects the closing prices as of January 2, 2026.

title: Pure energy The fast-paced business of marketing and moving hydrocarbons
summary: This article details ConocoPhillips' Commercial business unit, which handles the marketing and transportation of hydrocarbons after they are produced. It highlights the roles of various teams, including crude oil schedulers, gas and power marketers, and financial analysts, emphasizing their focus on maximizing value, ensuring efficient delivery, and maintaining a strong reputation in the industry. The piece also touches on Commercial's strategic initiatives, recent LNG deals, and commitment to employee development and risk management.

title: Enbridge commits $1 billion to company turning food waste to energy
summary: Canadian pipeline operator Enbridge Inc. is investing $1 billion into Divert Inc., a U.S. company that converts rotting food into renewable natural gas (RNG). This commitment will fund the expansion of 30 facilities across North America, with an additional $80 million equity investment from Enbridge and $20 million from other investors. The move is part of a growing trend in major energy companies investing in biogas, spurred by U.S. subsidies for capturing climate-warming emissions.

title: Exxon starts new crude unit at Beaumont, Texas refinery -sources
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp has started a new crude distillation unit (CDU) at its Beaumont, Texas refinery, with plans to reach full capacity of 250,000 bpd by the end of Q1 2023. This expansion will increase the refinery's total crude oil processing capacity by 68% to 619,000 bpd, potentially making it one of the largest in the United States. The $2 billion unit, built to process Permian Basin crude, will increase Exxon's total refining capacity by 17% and supply diesel and other motor fuels to meet high demand.

title: IXC Top Holdings List & Exposure (iShares Global Energy ETF)
summary: This article details the top holdings and exposure of the iShares Global Energy ETF (IXC). It lists the top 25 stocks by weight, including Exxon Mobil, Chevron, and Shell plc, which together constitute 84.31% of the fund. The report also breaks down IXC's geographic, currency, sector, industry, sub-industry, and coupon/maturity exposures, showing a primary focus on the U.S. energy sector.

title: Indigenous community accuses Imperial Oil, Alberta Energy Regulator of covering industrial spills
summary: The Athabasca Chipewyan First Nation (ACFN) is accusing Imperial Oil and the Alberta Energy Regulator (AER) of concealing significant failures of tailings dams and toxic leaks at the Kearl mine. Chief Allan Adam stated that it took almost a year for Imperial Oil to inform downstream Indigenous communities about four separate tailings pond failures that began in May 2022. The ACFN is calling for a thorough investigation, suggesting the multiple failures point to a systemic issue rather than mere accidents, while the AER has stated it has issued an Environmental Protection Order and is investigating.

title: Lula bashes Petrobras dividends, says firm invested 'almost nothing'
summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva criticized Petrobras' dividend payouts, arguing the company should have invested more in internal growth rather than distributing over 215 billion reais to shareholders in 2022. He suggested half of these dividends should have been reinvested in Brazil's naval and oil & gas industries. Lula's comments followed Petrobras' announcement of a significant surge in fourth-quarter earnings and a plan to pay 35.8 billion reais in dividends for the period.

title: The Fossil Fuel Industry’s Own Poll Found Most New Yorkers Support a Gas Ban in New Buildings
summary: A poll commissioned by a fossil fuel industry advocacy group, New Yorkers for Affordable Energy, found that 57% of New Yorkers support banning natural gas hookups in new buildings starting in 2025. Despite this finding, the group's press release focused on concerns about electrification costs and reliability, highlighting Western New Yorkers' opposition. Climate advocacy groups accuse New Yorkers for Affordable Energy of cherry-picking data to obstruct climate policies and safeguard the fossil fuel industry's interests.

title: Brazil's Petrobras faces legal risks after halting asset sales -lawyers
summary: Brazil's state-controlled oil company Petrobras faces potential lawsuits for breach of contract after halting over $2 billion in planned asset sales at the request of President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's government. Legal experts warn that suspended deals, which include sales to 3R Petroleum and Seacrest, could lead to litigation as existing contracts contain clauses that must be fulfilled by all parties. This move marks a significant shift from the previous administration's policy, aligning with Lula's Workers Party's stated intention to cancel such divestitures.

title: Tanzania completes negotiations with Shell, Equinor on $30 bln LNG project
summary: Tanzania has completed negotiations with Norway's Equinor and Britain's Shell for the construction of a $30 billion liquefied natural gas (LNG) terminal. The project has been delayed for years due to regulatory issues, but a framework agreement was signed last June, with a final investment decision expected in 2025. Experts are now drafting contracts, including a Host Government Agreement, vital for developing Tanzania's vast offshore gas resources.

title: OPEC Chief Dines With US Shale Bosses as Supply Issues in Focus
summary: OPEC Chief Haitham Al-Ghais met with US shale executives, including CEOs from Occidental Petroleum, Pioneer Natural Resources, and Devon Energy, to discuss global oil supply concerns. This meeting, the first for Al-Ghais since leading OPEC, highlighted the ongoing challenges in the oil market, including global demand outstripping supply due to Russia sanctions and China's reopening, while both OPEC and US shale companies face constraints on increasing production. Despite the tradition of such dinners under Al-Ghais's predecessor, this particular gathering showed little clear alignment between the two sides, with one CEO noting that "nobody controls the market."

title: PR News | FTI Consulting Recruits ExxonMobil’s Soper - Mon., Mar. 6, 2023
summary: FTI Consulting has hired Steven Soper, formerly ExxonMobil's US state government relations practice lead, as a senior managing director in its strategic communications group in Dallas. Soper brings extensive experience from ExxonMobil, Burson-Marsteller's Direct Impact unit, and political roles with the Bush-Cheney campaign and the Republican National Committee. He will focus on helping clients navigate complex policy and communications challenges in the growing Texas market.

title: U.S. sues Exxon Mobil for racial discrimination after 5 nooses found at Louisiana complex
summary: The U.S. government has sued Exxon Mobil for racial discrimination after five nooses were found at its Baton Rouge, Louisiana refinery complex between 2016 and 2020. The lawsuit, filed by the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC), alleges that Exxon Mobil failed to take sufficient corrective action to prevent further harassment, creating a racially hostile work environment. Exxon Mobil reportedly disagrees with the allegations but encourages employees to report workplace harassment.

title: CERAWEEK Exxon seeks to unblock stalled sale in 'challenging' Nigeria - top executive
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp is seeking Nigerian government approval to finalize the sale of its shallow-water oil production operations. Despite the "challenging" operating environment in Nigeria, Exxon plans to retain its deep-water assets and views them as an attractive long-term opportunity that needs to compete with global investments. The company's top executive, Liam Mallon, expressed hope for the sale to proceed before the new Nigerian president takes office, emphasizing Exxon's commitment to staying in Nigeria through its deep-water operations.

title: Growth stock vs. value stock? It's all in the eye of the beholder
summary: The article discusses the increasingly blurred lines between growth and value stocks, particularly in the context of index investing. It highlights how major index providers like S&P reclassify stocks such as Microsoft and ExxonMobil, challenging traditional definitions due to factors like price momentum and earnings changes. The piece emphasizes that different index construction methodologies and rebalancing schedules can lead to significant performance divergences among growth and value ETFs, urging investors to understand what criteria their investments are based on.

title: Shell, Chevron and Petrobras weigh Guyana oil auction bids -sources
summary: Guyana is offering 14 offshore oil exploration blocks in an auction that has attracted interest from major oil companies like Shell, Petrobras, and Chevron. The country aims to accelerate economic development and reduce Exxon Mobil's dominance in its oil sector. Winning bidders are expected to be announced next month, with new contract terms increasing the government's share of profits and royalties.

title: |Enbridge earmarks $2.4 bln in infrastructure, renewable projects in U.S. | NEWS
summary: |Enbridge Inc. plans to invest C$3.3 billion ($2.4 billion) in natural gas, liquids infrastructure, and renewable power in the U.S. this year, driven by green energy subsidies from the Biden administration's Inflation Reduction Act. The company aims to capitalize on better investment opportunities in the U.S., focusing on gas transmission modernization, LNG export business expansion, and renewable energy projects including converting food waste to energy. Enbridge expects a significant increase in its renewable portfolio by 2028 and an annual core earnings growth of 4%-6% through 2025.

title: CERAWEEK Eni CEO says gas market will be "difficult" for Europe through 2025
summary: Eni CEO Claudio Descalzi stated at the CERAWeek conference that Europe's natural gas market will face difficulties through 2025. This is primarily due to the complete cessation of Russian gas supply, which previously accounted for about 80% of Europe's supply until mid-2022. Descalzi highlighted the coming winter and the subsequent two years as particularly challenging for the European energy market.

title: CERAWEEK Exxon says it is reevaluating Europe strategy after windfall taxes
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. is reevaluating its European strategy due to new windfall profits taxes, according to CEO Darren Woods at the CERAWeek by S&P energy conference. Woods stated that such taxation discourages investments, while the company increasingly focuses its investments on the U.S. The U.S. Inflation Reduction Act has positively impacted Exxon's strategy, enabling it to launch a new business for decarbonization.

title: Eastman Chemical Co. stock outperforms competitors despite losses on the day
summary: Eastman Chemical Co. (EMN) stock experienced a 1.92% loss on a generally grim trading day for the market, closing at $82.42. Despite this decline, the stock managed to outperform some competitors, such as Exxon Mobil Corp. (XOM), which also fell. Eastman Chemical Co. is $32.55 below its 52-week high, and its trading volume was below its 50-day average.

title: Are Enough Young People Entering the Oil and Gas Workforce?
summary: Experts from Petroplan, The Birmingham Group, and Piper-Morgan Search discuss the challenges of attracting young talent to the oil and gas industry. Factors cited include a negative perception of the sector, a significant drop in petroleum engineering graduates, and the appeal of careers in renewable energy. While some believe the industry can always attract talent through competitive compensation and benefits, others emphasize the lack of interest among young people due to volatility and environmental concerns.

title: J&J, 3M among companies seeking 'basic due diligence' in multidistrict litigation
summary: Over 30 companies, including Johnson & Johnson and 3M Co, are urging the federal judiciary to implement a policy that would require "basic due diligence" from plaintiffs' counsel in multidistrict litigations (MDLs) early in the case. This proposal aims to prevent a large volume of unsubstantiated claims from being "parked" and intends to streamline the resolution of MDLs for meritorious claims. This move could face pushback from plaintiffs' firms, who argue it might create a significant burden of proof just to file a lawsuit.

title: Muncrief: Devon Energy Taking Slower Approach to LNG
summary: Devon Energy Corp. plans to take a measured approach to supplying the global LNG market, initially committing about 10% of its gross gas volumes while still primarily focusing on oil production for revenue. Despite anticipating a gassier mix in its portfolio over time, the company intends to remain "as oily as we can for as long as we can," according to CEO Rick Muncrief. This strategy is influenced by current market conditions, including expected lower gas prices in 2023 due to limited LNG export capacity and rising U.S. gas production.

title: ConocoPhillips bid team delivers lasting value with Qatar LNG deals
summary: ConocoPhillips' Qatar North Field Expansion Bid Team received a 2023 SPIRIT of Performance Award for successfully securing two LNG agreements with QatarEnergy. These deals, for the North Field East (NFE) and North Field South (NFS) projects, build on a long-standing partnership and are critical for global energy security, including providing long-term LNG deliveries to Germany. The success is attributed to extensive teamwork, strong relationships, and ConocoPhillips' reputation and expertise in the LNG sector.

title: Federal judge rules in favor of ConocoPhillips to keep Willow drilling data secret
summary: A federal judge has ruled in favor of ConocoPhillips, blocking the public release of exploration data from five oil wells within the Willow project in the National Petroleum Reserve. The decision overrides a state law requiring data disclosure after two years, citing federal law that mandates release only after ConocoPhillips' federal lease expires. The Willow project is still under environmental review but is expected to produce significant oil and tax revenues, while opponents warn of its substantial contribution to global climate change.

title: Exxon Mobil sued as 5 nooses displayed at Louisiana facility
summary: Exxon Mobil is being sued by the U.S. government for allegedly failing to address a racially hostile work environment at its Baton Rouge, Louisiana facility. The lawsuit claims that five hangman's nooses were found at the complex, starting in January 2020, and the company did not take adequate action to investigate or prevent such harassment. Exxon Mobil denies the allegations, stating it thoroughly investigated reported claims and has a zero-tolerance policy for harassment.

title: BP recommends vote against climate activist resolution at April 27 AGM
summary: BP's board has recommended that shareholders vote against a climate activist resolution seeking more ambitious emissions cuts by 2030, calling the proposal "unclear," "simplistic," and "disruptive." The resolution, co-filed by activist group Follow This and several institutional investors, asks for absolute emissions cuts in line with the Paris Agreement, including Scope 3 emissions. This recommendation comes after BP scaled back its own emissions reduction targets last month.

title: Imperial Oil faces federal order to stop seepage as tailings leak deemed harmful to wildlife
summary: Federal inspectors have ordered Imperial Oil to stop an oilsands wastewater seepage deemed harmful to wildlife from its Kearl mine. The leak, first noticed in May, was not reported to First Nations or federal officials for nine months, causing widespread anger. Imperial Oil states it is complying with the order, installing pumps and planning to collect fish as a precaution, while Environment Canada continues to monitor the situation.

title: B.C. approves Indigenous-led Cedar LNG project, announces new ‘energy action framework’
summary: British Columbia has approved the Indigenous-led Cedar LNG project, which is set to become the largest infrastructure project in Canada with majority Indigenous ownership and one of the lowest-emitting LNG facilities globally. To reconcile this with its climate goals, the province also announced an "energy action framework" which includes an emissions cap for the oil and gas sector and a directive for all proposed LNG facilities to have a credible plan for net-zero emissions by 2030. While hailed as a step towards reconciliation, the project faces criticism regarding its reliance on the contentious Coastal GasLink pipeline and concerns from other First Nations about increased marine shipping.

title: US Labor Board judge rules Exxon must repay workers for suspended 401K match
summary: A U.S. National Labor Relations Board (NLRB) administrative law judge has ordered Exxon Mobil Corp to repay 1,800 employees for lost earnings due to a suspended 401K match in 2020 and 2021. The judge ruled that Exxon engaged in bad-faith bargaining with United Steelworkers (USW) union locals during the suspension, which was implemented to save money during the COVID-19 pandemic. Exxon has stated it disagrees with the ruling and plans to appeal.

title: Argentina's YPF Looks To Double Oil Production Within 5 Years
summary: Argentina's state oil and gas company, YPF, aims to double its crude oil production and boost natural gas output by 30% within the next five years, focusing on the Vaca Muerta shale formation. This ambitious plan includes a potential $60-billion LNG project with Petronas and a new oil pipeline project, despite Argentina's economic challenges. YPF reported strong financial results for the last quarter of 2022, driven by increased production and higher oil prices.

title: Exxon Mobil illegally halted retirement contributions, NLRB judge rules
summary: A National Labor Relations Board (NLRB) judge has ruled that Exxon Mobil illegally stopped making 401(k) contributions. This decision comes after the company halted contributions, a move deemed unlawful by the NLRB. The ruling addresses an important issue regarding employee benefits and corporate actions.

title: Exxon considers selling stake in LNG terminal offshore Italy
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp is exploring the sale of its majority stake in the Rovigo liquefied natural gas (LNG) terminal offshore Italy, consistent with its strategy to divest noncore assets. The terminal, co-owned by QatarEnergy and Snam Spa, has recently expanded its regasification capacity. While verifying market interest, Exxon confirmed no decision has been made, and any transaction would not impact its LNG imports or gas supply interests in European markets.

title: Snam CEO says Piombino FSRU terminal on track to start operations in May
summary: Snam's CEO, Stefano Venier, confirmed that the FSRU-based LNG import terminal in Piombino, Italy, is expected to begin operations in May. The Golar Tundra FSRU, purchased last year to enhance Italy's energy security, is nearing its destination. This will be Italy's fourth large LNG terminal, and Snam is also open to increasing its stake in the Adriatic LNG terminal if ExxonMobil sells its share.

title: Venture Global Gives Green Light to Plaquemines LNG Phase 2
summary: Venture Global LNG Inc. has approved the continuation of Phase 2 construction for its Plaquemines LNG plant in Louisiana, a 20-million tonne/year facility. This decision follows securing necessary permits and a significant $7.8 billion project financing for the plant, which has an estimated combined cost of $21 billion for both phases. The company has also begun marketing and production activities for its third plant, CP2 LNG, after signing sales agreements with major oil companies.

title: ExxonMobil Boosts Fuel Supply with $2 Billion Beaumont Refinery Expansion
summary: ExxonMobil has successfully started up its Beaumont refinery expansion project, a $2 billion investment that adds 250,000 barrels per day of capacity, making it the largest refinery expansion in the U.S. since 2012. This expansion increases the refinery's total processing capacity to over 630,000 barrels per day and will help meet the surging demand for transportation fuels, supported by crude production from the Permian Basin. The project was completed on time and on budget, demonstrating ExxonMobil's commitment to providing reliable and affordable energy.

title: Exxon starts up new Beaumont, Texas, crude unit -executive
summary: Exxon Mobil has successfully started up a new $2-billion crude distillation unit (CDU) at its Beaumont, Texas refinery, adding 250,000 barrels per day to its capacity. This expansion, built between 2019 and 2022, allows Exxon to process crude oil from the Permian Basin and supply motor fuels to U.S. and international markets. The company expects the unit to reach full capacity by the end of March, boosting the refinery's total capacity to over 630,000 bpd.

title: With oil below $75 per barrel, what’s next for the Woodside share price?
summary: The Woodside Energy Group Ltd (ASX: WDS) share price is rebounding despite recent declines, influenced by the price of Brent crude falling below $75 per barrel. Analysts from Goldman Sachs, OPEC, and the IEA predict a significant rise in oil prices in the second half of 2023 due to increasing demand and underinvestment in exploration, which could positively impact Woodside's share performance. The article suggests that despite current volatility, the Woodside share price is expected to trade significantly higher in the coming year.

title: Exxon Mobil starts up $2B Beaumont refinery expansion
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. (NYSE: XOM) has announced the startup of its $2 billion refinery expansion in Beaumont, Texas. This expansion, which adds 250,000 barrels per day to its capacity, is noted as the largest refinery expansion in the U.S. since 2012.

title: Hess Corp. stock underperforms Friday when compared to competitors
summary: Hess Corp. (HES) stock fell by 2.04% to $118.33 on Friday, underperforming the broader market as the S&P 500 Index and Dow Jones Industrial Average also declined. The company's stock also trailed competitors Exxon Mobil Corp. (XOM) and Chevron Corp. (CVX), which experienced smaller percentage drops. This trading session saw Hess Corp. close significantly below its 52-week high.

title: Chad says it has nationalized all assets owned by Exxon Mobil
summary: Chad's energy ministry announced it has nationalized all assets belonging to an Exxon Mobil subsidiary, including hydrocarbon permits and exploration rights. This action follows the Chadian government's dispute over Exxon Mobil's $407 million sale of its operations in Chad and Cameroon to Savannah Energy, stating the final deal terms differed from what was presented. Exxon's assets included a 40% stake in the Doba oil project and an interest in the Chad/Cameroon pipeline.

title: Delek’s chief operating officer to step down this year
summary: Delek US Holdings announced that its executive vice president and COO, Todd O’Malley, will depart in September. His responsibilities will be divided between Patrick Reilly, EVP and Chief Commercial Officer, and newly hired Joseph Israel, EVP of Operations. Additionally, Nithia Thaver, EVP and President of Refining, is also stepping down in May, with Tommy Chavez named as the new Senior Vice President of Refining.

title: Halliburton and Honeywell in talks to develop oil fields and refineries in Libya
summary: Halliburton and Honeywell International Inc. are negotiating $1.4 billion in deals with Libya's National Oil Corporation (NOC) to develop an oil field and construct a refinery in southern Libya. The initial agreement for the refinery's design is expected soon, followed by a $400 million contract for its construction. This development follows U.S. Secretary of State Antony Blinken's statement about reopening the U.S. embassy in Libya to support elections and comes as American firms increasingly view Libya as a safe environment for investment.

title: B.C.’s Cedar LNG approval sends mixed messages
summary: B.C.'s NDP government approved the Cedar LNG project, a partnership between the Haisla Nation and Pembina Pipeline Corporation, then hours later announced new emissions regulations for the oil and gas sector, sending conflicting signals about its climate commitments. While supporters hail the project as an act of reconciliation and economic self-determination for the Haisla Nation, critics and climate activists decry the approval of another gas export terminal given global calls to cease new fossil fuel projects. The article highlights the tension between economic development through fossil fuels, Indigenous rights, and environmental protection, as the new emissions rules do not fully apply to the newly approved project.

title: Comcast Stock Is a Buy
summary: Morningstar analyst Michael Hodel rates Comcast stock as a buy, citing its undervalued status, attractive yield, and stable dividend. The article highlights Comcast's strong core cable business with competitive advantages and resilient broadband provision, despite challenges from competition and the evolving TV landscape. Key metrics like a $60 fair value estimate and a Wide Economic Moat rating reinforce the positive outlook, while acknowledging risks such as regulation and technological obsolescence.

title: Chad approves bill to nationalise assets ExxonMobil sold to Savannah Energy
summary: Chad's parliament has approved a bill to nationalise oil assets that ExxonMobil sold to Savannah Energy, with 172 out of 175 lawmakers present backing the move. This decision follows Chad's challenge to the $407 million deal completed in December, with the Chadian minister stating the actions of Savannah and ExxonMobil pose threats to public order and stability. Savannah Energy has vowed to contest this nationalisation.

title: ConocoPhillips partners with UT to research renewable energy, prepare for Willow Project
summary: ConocoPhillips, leading the controversial Willow Project, is collaborating with the UT Energy Institute on renewable energy research, aiming for near-zero methane emissions. This partnership highlights the complex balance between fossil fuel development, environmental concerns, and the transition to renewable energy. The project faces criticism for its potential environmental impact, particularly regarding "scope three" emissions, while proponents emphasize its economic benefits and contribution to energy independence.

title: Schlumberger Rebrands as SLB to Drive the Future of Energy
summary: Schlumberger has rebranded as SLB, signaling its evolution from an oilfield services company to a global technology company focused on driving the energy transition. The company's new strategy centers on new energy systems, industrial decarbonization, digital solutions, and oil and gas innovation, all aimed at achieving a balanced energy mix and a lower-carbon future. SLB emphasizes the critical need to balance energy demand with rapid decarbonization, focusing on a carbon curve approach to meet its net-negative carbon goals post-2050.

title: Par Pacific to take over Montana refinery on June 1
summary: Par Pacific Holdings is set to acquire Exxon Mobil's 63,000-barrel-per-day Billings, Montana refinery, with the takeover expected on June 1. This acquisition, valued at $310 million plus inventory costs, will increase Par Pacific's total refining capacity to 218,000 bpd across four refineries. ExxonMobil is divesting the refinery to focus on facilities integrated with chemical plants.

title: As Suncor restarts its Commerce City refinery, neighbors demand a plan to prevent future pollution incidents
summary: Suncor Energy's Commerce City refinery is restarting operations after a three-month shutdown caused by a December cold snap, which led to fires, worker injuries, and significant pollution incidents. While the restart has lowered Colorado gas prices, local residents and environmental groups are frustrated, demanding a comprehensive plan to prevent future pollution and advocating for a "just transition" away from fossil fuels due to ongoing health and environmental concerns. The community seeks more transparency from Suncor and state regulators regarding the incidents and their impact on air quality.

title: Stock split history
summary: This page provides the stock split history for Exxon Mobil Corporation (XOM), including details for ExxonMobil, Mobil, and XTO Energy. It lists the split dates, ratios, and company names involved in each stock split and merger event. The information covers events from the mid-20th century up to the early 2000s, detailing significant corporate actions like the ExxonMobil merger and the XTO Energy merger.

title: The Search for Yield – Equity Income Whitepaper
summary: This whitepaper explores strategies for investors seeking yield during times of economic uncertainty, particularly in a potentially recessionary U.S. market. It emphasizes focusing on quality dividends, defensive sectors, and flexible equity income portfolios. The article also discusses the benefits of preferred stocks, covered calls, MLPs, and REITs as solutions for generating yield and managing risk in various market conditions.

title: Hess Corp. stock outperforms competitors on strong trading day
summary: Hess Corp. (HES) stock rallied 1.74% on Tuesday, closing at $144.80, outperforming major indices like the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average, which saw mixed trading. The company's stock also surpassed competitors like Exxon Mobil Corp. (XOM) and Chevron Corp. (CVX). Hess Corp. is currently $15.72 below its 52-week high.

title: RBC surpasses JPMorgan as top fossil-fuel financier: study
summary: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) became the world's top financier to fossil-fuel companies in 2022, surpassing JPMorgan Chase, according to a report by the Rainforest Action Network (RAN). RBC's fossil-fuel funding increased by 4.2% to $42.1 billion, while U.S. banks like JPMorgan, Citi, and Wells Fargo significantly reduced their financing in this sector. The article examines the implications of RBC's increased funding and its climate goals amidst criticism from environmental groups.

title: Chevron (CVX) to Outperform Exxon (XOM) as Oil Prices Rise, Scotiabank Says
summary: Scotiabank predicts that Chevron (CVX) will soon outperform Exxon Mobil (XOM), despite Exxon's significant gains over the past year. While Exxon's shares rose 33% in the last 12 months, Chevron's remained largely unchanged. However, with rising oil prices, Scotiabank analysts expect Chevron's stock to reach an all-time high of $200.

title: Exxon declares force majeure on crude liftings in Nigeria
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. has declared force majeure on oil liftings from several terminals in Nigeria due to industrial action by its in-house workers union. This action comes as Nigeria aims to increase its oil production to 1.6 million barrels per day, striving to recover its position as Africa's largest OPEC producer, a goal made challenging by ongoing issues of theft and spills. Exxon is also in the process of divesting $1.2 billion in shallow-water assets in Nigeria, citing "challenging" operations.

title: Elevated Demand for Oil Could Push Commodities Even Higher
summary: Global oil demand is projected to reach a new record this year, primarily driven by China's reopening, even amidst the transition to renewable energy. This increased demand, coupled with supply cuts from OPEC+, is expected to drive crude prices higher. Investors seeking exposure to this trend can consider diversified commodity ETFs like the Neuberger Berman Commodity Strategy ETF (NBCM), which actively manages a portfolio including crude oil and other commodities.

title: 4 Gold Stocks to Consider
summary: Morningstar has recommenced coverage on four senior gold miners: Newmont Corp (NEM), Barrick Gold (GOLD), Agnico Eagle Mines (AEM), and Kinross Gold (KGC), providing fair value estimates and analysis. The article notes that while gold prices are rising, concerns remain about increasing interest rates and cost inflation affecting miners' margins. None of these companies are assessed to have an economic moat, with Newmont and Barrick Gold shares currently considered undervalued.

title: How to Invest in Commodities: Complete Guide 2023
summary: This guide offers an in-depth look at investing in commodities, including what drives commodity prices, the benefits of commodity investing (diversification, inflation hedge, outperformance), and specific strategies for investing in gold and oil through stocks and ETFs. It also highlights specific ETFs and companies such as iShares GSCI Commodity Dynamic Roll Strategy ETF (NASDAQ:COMT), iShares Gold Trust (NYSEARCA:IAU), Barrick Gold (NYSEARCA:GOLD), United States Oil Fund ETF (USO), Exxon Mobil (XOM), and the Energy Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLE).

title: Chevron, Exxon developing cleaner gas as alternative to EVs
summary: Chevron and ExxonMobil are developing renewable gasoline blends as an alternative to electric vehicles, aiming to reduce emissions from conventional cars to competitive levels. These fuels, partially made from non-fossil feedstocks like soybeans, could extend the lifespan of the gasoline market by allowing the existing U.S. car fleet and gas stations to continue operations. However, commercial availability will likely require government support, similar to incentives for other renewable fuels, according to Chevron.

title: Chevron, Exxon pursue cleaner gasoline as alternative to EVs
summary: Chevron and Exxon Mobil are developing and testing renewable gasoline blends that they claim can significantly reduce emissions from conventional vehicles, offering an alternative to electric vehicles. These cleaner fuels, derived from non-fossil feedstocks like soybeans, could extend the lifespan of the gasoline market, but their commercial viability depends on government support and incentives to reach affordable pricing and scale. The initiative comes as the U.S. administration proposes new pollution standards that favor EVs, highlighting the oil majors' efforts to innovate within the evolving energy landscape.

title: U.S. oil refiners to post strong Q1 earnings, but demand outlook dims
summary: U.S. fuelmakers are projected to report strong first-quarter earnings due to robust fuel exports and margins, despite a slump in domestic diesel demand. However, analysts predict a weaker second quarter for refiners, citing declining exports and increased global capacity, alongside long-term demand concerns. Major companies like Valero Energy, Marathon Petroleum, Phillips 66, and Exxon Mobil are expected to show significant profit increases for Q1 compared to the previous year.

title: 30% of Dow Shareholders Urge Company to Study Future With Less Virgin Plastic
summary: A shareholder resolution filed with Dow Inc. by As You Sow, requesting the company report on the impact of reduced global demand for virgin plastic, received support from over 30% of shareholders. This proposal highlights the growing concern over single-use plastics and the need for companies like Dow, a major producer of plastic resins, to assess their reliance on these materials. The resolution also sought disclosure on the cost-effectiveness, efficiency, and environmental soundness of chemical recycling technologies Dow plans to use.

title: South Korean Companies Snap Up Opportunities to Advance Floating Nuclear, Nuclear Hydrogen, SMRs
summary: South Korean companies are actively engaging in partnerships to advance nuclear technology, including floating nuclear power plants, nuclear hydrogen production, and Small Modular Reactors (SMRs). Notable collaborations involve Korea Hydro & Nuclear Power (KHNP) with TerraPower and Samsung Heavy Industries, NuScale with Doosan Enerbility, and Ultra-Safe Nuclear Corp. (USNC) with Hyundai Engineering and SK ecoplant. These efforts align with the U.S. and South Korea's shared goals of establishing energy security, reducing carbon emissions, and expanding their influence in the global nuclear reactor market.

title: ExxonMobil Guyana Advances Fifth Offshore Guyana Development
summary: ExxonMobil has made a final investment decision for the Uaru development, its fifth project offshore Guyana, following government approvals. This project is expected to add approximately 250,000 barrels of daily capacity starting in 2026, representing a $12.7 billion investment. ExxonMobil aims to have six Floating Production Storage and Offloading (FPSO) vessels online by the end of 2027, increasing Guyana's production capacity to over 1.2 million barrels per day.

title: Eni mulls second floating LNG platform in Mozambique
summary: Italian energy company Eni SpA is considering building a second floating liquefied natural gas (LNG) platform in Mozambique's Rovuma Basin, aiming to replicate the success of its Coral Sul project. This move would leverage Mozambique's vast gas reserves and strategic location to contribute significantly to European energy security and global energy needs, while maintaining a competitive edge in emissions performance.

title: Questions over accounting and inclusion mar Guyana’s unprecedented carbon scheme
summary: Guyana has launched an unprecedented carbon credit scheme, selling credits from its vast, intact forests to Hess Corporation for $750 million, with 15% allocated to Indigenous communities. However, the initiative faces scrutiny from climate experts who question the methodology used to calculate emissions reductions for forests already under low threat of deforestation, arguing the credits are overstated. Additionally, disputes have arisen among Indigenous groups regarding the adequacy and legality of consultations prior to including their lands in the carbon market.

title: Imperial Oil hoping Cold Lake carbon capture project will be running before 2030
summary: Imperial Oil announced plans for its Cold Lake carbon capture project to be operational before 2030, ahead of the larger Pathways Alliance carbon capture and storage network. The company reported strong first-quarter earnings of $1.25 billion and increased its quarterly dividend. This initiative is a key part of the oilsands majors' commitment to achieving net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050, despite industry concerns about the federal government's 2030 emissions reduction targets.

title: Exxon delivers record first-quarter profit on higher output
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp reported a record first-quarter profit, surpassing analyst estimates due to increased oil and gas production, which also pushed its shares to an all-time high. Despite softening energy prices, robust output from its Permian Basin operations, Guyana fields, and the Beaumont refinery expansion contributed to a significant rise in net profit. The company's cash balance reached $32.7 billion, with executives focusing on organic growth rather than acquisitions, while anticipating even higher cash reserves in the future.

title: Curtiss-Wright signs subsea canned motor pump agreement with Shell
summary: Curtiss-Wright Corp has secured an agreement with Shell Exploration & Production Company to manufacture, test, and provide operational support for an Electro-Submersible Pump (ESP) for an offshore platform in the Gulf of Mexico. This initiative aims to demonstrate Curtiss-Wright's canned motor technology as a reliable alternative to current subsea pump technologies, reducing outages. A test facility will also be constructed to demonstrate the pump's capability before deployment, with the first ESP expected to be ready for delivery by year-end.

title: Energy ETFs to Bet on Solid Q1 Earnings From Exxon, Chevron
summary: Exxon Mobil (XOM) and Chevron (CVX) reported strong first-quarter profits, surpassing analyst estimates, despite a decline in oil and natural gas prices compared to the previous year. These robust earnings are expected to positively impact energy ETFs that heavily allocate to these two oil majors. The article highlights several such ETFs, including Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE), iShares U.S. Energy ETF (IYE), Vanguard Energy ETF (VDE), Fidelity MSCI Energy Index ETF (FENY), and Strive U.S. Energy ETF (DRLL), detailing their holdings, expense ratios, and risk outlooks.

title: Exxon Mobil not quitting exploration in Brazil
summary: Exxon Mobil clarified that it is not abandoning oil exploration in Brazil, contrary to recent reports. Alberto Ferrin, the company's Brazil country chief, stated during the Offshore Technology Conference that Exxon is actively looking for exploration opportunities in the country due to its favorable conditions, similar to its successful ventures in Guyana. The company maintains an 89% success rate in Guyana and sees Brazil as offering similar exploration enablers.

title: BCI calling for increased climate disclosure at Imperial Oil, Caisse pre-leasing Chilean mixed-use development
summary: The British Columbia Investment Management Corp. (BCI) is advocating for increased climate disclosure from Imperial Oil Ltd. by filing a shareholder proposal requesting greater transparency on climate risks and liabilities. Separately, the real estate arm of Caisse de dépôt et placement du Québec, Ivanhoé Cambridge, is pre-leasing a mixed-use development called Somma Asturias in Santiago, Chile. This development, a joint venture with Greystar Real Estate Partners, includes apartments, office space, and retail facilities.

title: State Street CEO: Divestment Will Slow Clean Energy Transition
summary: State Street CEO Ron O’Hanley stated that pressuring large asset managers to divest from polluting companies will hinder the clean energy transition by politicizing the issue and cutting off necessary investment for these industries to innovate. He argues that polluting industries require continued investment to facilitate their shift towards cleaner energy and reduce carbon emissions. O'Hanley's comments come amidst criticism from environmentalists urging financial firms like State Street to divest from oil and gas producers.

title: Welcome to the DIG Drilling Intelligence Group moves into new space
summary: ConocoPhillips' Drilling Intelligence Group (DIG) officially moved into its new, redesigned space in Midland, transforming a former storage area into an advanced technology center. The new facility, named the DIG, allows directional drillers, operations personnel, and engineers to monitor drilling activity, analyze data, and provide real-time support to enhance overall drilling performance and leverage rig-automation capabilities. The space was designed for future growth, with plans to integrate more disciplines to further improve learnings and performance.

title: World’s first oil tanker shipping ETF starts trading in New York
summary: John Kartsonas-led Breakwave Advisors has launched the world’s first tanker shipping exchange traded fund (ETF) on the New York Stock Exchange. The Breakwave Tanker Shipping ETF (BWET) offers exposure to the crude oil tanker shipping market using near-dated futures contracts. This launch capitalizes on high demand for oil transportation, limited vessel orderbooks, and geopolitical disruptions affecting oil markets.

title: 5 Biggest Oil Companies in Texas
summary: This article discusses the top oil companies based in Texas, highlighting their revenue, hedge fund interest, and operational specifics. The initial entry covered is EOG Resources Inc. (NYSE:EOG), emphasizing its financial performance, production capabilities, and commitment to shareholder returns.

title: Strive Asset Management fills leadership vacuum created by CEO's run for president
summary: Matt Cole has been appointed CEO of Strive Asset Management, taking over from co-founder Vivek Ramaswamy who resigned to pursue a presidential bid. Cole, previously CIO, will continue Strive's mission to prioritize shareholder value over stakeholder value, emphasizing an "anti-woke" approach to investing and proxy voting. Strive has launched eight ETFs totaling over $700 million and aims to offer an alternative to traditional ESG-focused asset managers.

title: The Alaskan gambit: $44 billion LNG project decades in the making
summary: A planned $44 billion natural gas project in Alaska, decades in the making, aims to pipe gas from the North Slope to an LNG terminal near Anchorage for export to Asian markets. This initiative, supported by the Biden administration, seeks to revitalize Alaska's declining oil and gas industry and provide a reliable energy source to allies like South Korea and Japan, despite environmental concerns and financing challenges. The project faces questions about its necessity amidst a flood of Gulf Coast LNG projects and the long-term demand for natural gas as nations shift to renewables.

title: Formal investigation into Kearl oil sands leaks begins
summary: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) has launched a formal investigation into the tailings leaks at the Kearl oil sands project, co-owned by Imperial Oil and ExxonMobil Canada. This follows accusations from the Athabasca Chipewyan First Nation that Alberta regulators covered up the spill and failed to alert downstream Indigenous communities for a year. The Alberta Energy Regulator (AER) confirmed the presence of naphthenic acids in a lake feeding into the Firebag River, as Imperial Oil implements mitigation systems and asserts drinking water safety.

title: MODEC Confirms Its First FPSO Order in Guyana
summary: MODEC has secured its first FPSO order in Guyana for the Uaru project, following a final investment decision by ExxonMobil. The FPSO, named ‘Errea Wittu’, will be the fifth in Guyana and MODEC's first for the country, with the company also providing operation and maintenance services for 10 years. This project marks a significant return to working with ExxonMobil for MODEC, showcasing their continued collaboration in major offshore developments.

title: Elliott Target Suncor's New CEO Plans Long Stay at Helm
summary: Rich Kruger, Suncor Energy Inc.'s new CEO, has come out of retirement to lead the struggling Canadian oil producer, with input from activist investor Elliott Investment Management LP. Kruger has expressed his commitment to the role for the long term, even selling his Texas home to relocate to Calgary. His priorities include improving Suncor's safety record, though he does not plan to revisit selling the company's Petro-Canada retail business, a previous recommendation by Elliott.

title: B.C. innovators charting routes to greener fuel options for the global marine industry
summary: B.C. companies, including Methanex Corp., Atlas Corp. (Seaspan), and Robert Allan Ltd., are leading the charge in developing greener fuel options for the global marine industry. Methanol and LNG are frontrunners in the transition to low-carbon shipping, with a mix of fuels expected to be the long-term solution. These innovators are addressing the challenge of decarbonizing the international shipping fleet through technological advancements and strategic partnerships.

title: LNG is surging. Can FERC reviews keep up?
summary: The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) faces challenges in reviewing natural gas export projects, with legal observers noting ambiguous directives and a lack of clear guidance in the Natural Gas Act, which governs FERC's oversight of LNG. This ambiguity creates debate among lawmakers pushing for quicker approvals and environmental advocates concerned about the climate impact and thoroughness of assessments. The issue is critical as U.S. LNG exports surge, driven by European demand for alternatives to Russian fuel.

title: CRC Goes Big on Carbon
summary: California Resources Corp. (CRC) is investing heavily in carbon capture and storage, with plans to spend $2.5 billion over five years to inject carbon dioxide back into the earth, particularly in mature oil fields like Elk Hills. This strategy is a response to environmental pressures and aims to demonstrate the oil industry's commitment to carbon neutrality while continuing operations, and potentially pre-empting stricter state regulations on carbon capture projects. The company has already secured several agreements to sequester over 600,000 metric tons of CO2 annually and is seeking permits for significantly more storage capacity.

title: Indonesia’s coal gasification plans hit as Air Products withdraws
summary: Air Products and Chemicals withdrew from a $15bn coal gasification investment in Indonesia, including a $2.3bn plant, less than two years after the project was announced. This withdrawal signals deteriorating financial prospects for coal-to-chemicals projects, further complicated by rising US interest rates and questionable economic viability without massive government subsidies. Attention now turns to whether a Chinese company might step in, despite concerns about environmental impacts, increased debt, and the potential for stranded assets.

title: Govt may mandate 1% green jet fuel in all commercial flights by '25: Puri
summary: India's Petroleum and Natural Gas Minister, Hardeep Singh Puri, announced plans to mandate 1% sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) blending in all domestic commercial flights by 2025, potentially increasing to 5% in the following years. This initiative aims to boost local SAF production to meet India's de-carbonization goals and prepare for global carbon offsetting schemes in international aviation starting in 2027. State-owned IOCL is planning a large-scale SAF production plant with Praj Industries' technology to support this mandate.

title: Guyana approves Local Content Annual Plans for ExxonMobil, Halliburton, TechnipFMC, Saipem and Baker Hughes - BNamericas
summary: Guyana's Ministry of Natural Resources approved the 2023 Local Content Annual Plans for five major oil companies: ExxonMobil, Halliburton, TechnipFMC, Saipem, and Baker Hughes. These plans outline procurement, employment, and capacity development efforts aimed at ensuring local content investment. The companies also received Certificates of Compliance, marking the first time these certificates have been issued under Guyana's Local Content Act.

title: Chord Energy acquires Williston basin assets for $375 million
summary: Chord Energy Corporation has acquired assets in the Williston basin from XTO Energy Inc. and affiliates, subsidiaries of Exxon Mobil Corporation, for $375 million. The deal includes approximately 62,000 net acres with 123 estimated net 10,000-foot equivalent locations and current high-margin production, funded by existing cash on hand. This acquisition expands Chord's inventory, enhances capital and operating efficiencies, and is expected to be accretive to shareholders.

title: Chord Energy Announces Strategic Acquisition of Williston Basin Assets
summary: Chord Energy Corporation announced the strategic acquisition of Williston Basin assets from XTO Energy Inc., a subsidiary of Exxon Mobil Corporation, for $375 million. This acquisition adds approximately 62,000 net acres, primarily undeveloped, and current high-margin production to Chord's portfolio. The company expects the transaction to be accretive to cash flow, free cash flow, and return metrics, while extending its inventory life.

title: Exxon Mobil subsidiaries selling Williston Basin assets to Chord Energy
summary: Chord Energy Corp. is set to acquire approximately 62,000 net acres in the Williston Basin from Exxon Mobil subsidiaries, including XTO Energy Inc. This acquisition comes after Chord Energy was formed through the merger of Oasis Petroleum Inc. and Whiting Petroleum Corp., aiming to create a leading operator in the Williston Basin.

title: This Ultra-High-Yield Stock's Deal With ExxonMobil Could Drive Its Dividend Higher
summary: Chord Energy has agreed to acquire 62,000 acres in the Williston Basin from ExxonMobil for $375 million, a strategic move expected to boost Chord's cash flow, free cash flow, and potentially increase its dividend payments. ExxonMobil is selling these assets as they no longer align with its focused upstream investment strategy, allowing it to reallocate capital to its core, high-return assets in other regions and strengthening its financial position for future strategic acquisitions. This asset sale is seen as a win-win, benefiting Chord Energy's dividend capacity and ExxonMobil's long-term investment goals.

title: ExxonMobil Sells Williston Assets
summary: Chord Energy Corp. has entered a definitive agreement to acquire hydrocarbon development areas in the Williston Basin from ExxonMobil Corp. for $375 million, adding approximately 62,000 net acres. The acquisition will be funded through cash on hand and is expected to close in June, significantly expanding Chord's inventory runway in the low-cost, tier-one asset region. This deal follows Chord's previous acquisition of Diamondback Energy Inc.’s assets in the Williston Basin and comes as Chord also divests non-core assets.

title: Canadian oil sands output expected to reach 3.7 million barrels per day by 2030, S&P Global says
summary: S&P Global forecasts that Canadian oil sands production will reach 3.7 million barrels per day by 2030, an increase of 140,000 barrels per day from its previous outlook, marking the first such upward revision in five years. This growth is attributed to an "era of optimization" where production focuses on high-potential areas near existing developments. Although record production is anticipated, growth is expected to slow in the mid-2020s and decline in the early 2030s due to the flat production profile of oil sands assets.

title: Norway's Wealth Fund Sides With Activists Against Exxon, Chevron
summary: Norway's $1.4 trillion sovereign wealth fund, the world's largest, has announced its support for shareholder proposals at ExxonMobil and Chevron's annual general meetings. These proposals aim to introduce emissions targets, marking a significant stance against Big Oil companies by a major institutional investor. This move follows similar climate activist victories and protests despite a previous shift in investor sentiment favoring energy security.

title: Italian citizens and organisations sue fossil fuel company ENI for human rights violations and climate change impacts
summary: Twelve Italian citizens, Greenpeace Italy, and ReCommon have filed a lawsuit against the fossil fuel company ENI, alleging human rights violations and climate change impacts. The lawsuit also targets ENI’s main shareholders, the Ministry of Economy and Finance and Cassa Depositi e Prestiti S.p.A., accusing them of complicity in policies that violate the Paris Agreement. Plaintiffs, from regions severely affected by climate change, are seeking for ENI to revise its industrial strategy to reduce emissions by at least 45% by 2030.

title: Equinor Delays Bay du Nord Canada Oil Project up to 3 Years Over Rising Costs
summary: Norway's Equinor ASA has announced a delay of up to three years for its Bay du Nord Canadian offshore oil project due to rising costs and volatile market conditions. This decision impacts one of Canada's most significant oil projects, despite prior support from Prime Minister Justin Trudeau's government. The company plans to re-evaluate the project for further optimizations, while environmental groups like Sierra Club Canada hope for its cancellation.

title: ExxonMobil Clinches CCS Deal for Nucor’s Steelmaker Site in Louisiana
summary: ExxonMobil's low-carbon business has secured its third carbon capture and storage (CCS) deal in seven months, contracting with Nucor Corp. to manage up to 800,000 metric tons/year of CO2 from Nucor's Louisiana steelmaking facility. This agreement, along with previous deals, brings ExxonMobil's total CCS commitments to approximately 5 million metric tons/year. The Nucor project is scheduled to begin operations in 2026 and will connect to the CO2 storage infrastructure being developed for the CF Industries project in Vermilion Parish, Louisiana.

title: Chevron produces first gas from Gorgon Stage 2 development off Western Australia
summary: Chevron announced it has commenced gas production from its Gorgon Stage 2 development project off Western Australia. This expansion enhances the existing subsea gas gathering network of the Gorgon Project, which supplies liquefied natural gas (LNG) to Asia and domestic gas to Western Australia. The Stage 2 development involved adding 11 wells and related subsea infrastructure to maintain gas supply for the processing facilities on Barrow Island.

title: 2 Alabama-based companies make the Fortune 500
summary: Two Birmingham-based companies, Regions Financial and Vulcan Materials, have been included in Fortune's 2023 list of the nation's largest corporations. Regions Financial ranked 483rd with $7.5 billion in revenue, while Vulcan Materials placed 494th with over $7.3 billion in revenue. The Fortune 500 list, which ranks companies by their 2022 fiscal year revenue, features 52 companies led by women CEOs, an all-time high.

title: Governments Must Start Walking the Talk on Fossil Fuel Subsidies Phase-out
summary: This article argues that governments must move beyond pledges and actively phase out fossil fuel subsidies to combat climate change, especially as the UN assesses global climate progress. It highlights that current indicators are poor, with fossil fuel subsidies reaching USD 1.1 trillion in 2022, far outweighing clean energy investments. The author suggests concrete steps for governments, including improving transparency, strengthening global commitments, withdrawing all public support from fossil fuels, planning at the national level, and building public support for reforms, all of which are crucial for accelerating the transition to climate-compatible economies.

title: Exposing Texas’ Excess Emissions Problems
summary: Texas industrial facilities have released an estimated 1.1 billion pounds of pollution beyond their permit limits since 2002, largely categorized as "excess emissions" that often go unpunished. This investigation highlights how these emissions, exacerbated by extreme weather and increasing industrial activity, disproportionately affect nearby communities and reveals loopholes in reporting and enforcement. Despite federal rulings deeming these exemptions illegal, state regulators often fail to penalize companies, and firms sometimes downplay emission events to avoid violations.

title: Regions Financial, Vulcan Materials make Fortune 500
summary: Two Birmingham-based companies, Regions Financial and Vulcan Materials, have been named to the Fortune 500 list, ranking 483rd and 494th respectively. Regions generated $7.5 billion in revenue, while Vulcan amassed $7.3 billion during the 2022 fiscal period. Vulcan Materials was also recognized as one of the top 200 Best Companies to Work For by U.S. News and World Report.

title: ACB Earnings Infographic: Aurora Cannabis Q3 2023 revenue up 27%
summary: Aurora Cannabis (NASDAQ: ACB) reported a net loss of C$87 million for Q3 2023, despite a 27% year-over-year increase in total revenues to C$64 million. The company achieved adjusted EBITDA of C$0.31 million, a significant improvement from a C$10.03 million loss in the prior-year quarter. CEO Miguel Martin highlighted approximately $400 million in annualized cost savings from business transformation initiatives, which led to a reduced cash use in operating activities.

title: Recent decision leaves ExxonMobil responsible for only part of Guyana oil spill costs, leaving Guyanese people on the hook for the rest
summary: A recent court decision regarding oil spill cleanup costs in Guyana has limited ExxonMobil's liability to $2 billion, transferring the remaining financial responsibility to the Guyanese people. This decision, which overturns a lower court ruling that demanded full insurance coverage from ExxonMobil, allows drilling to continue but raises significant concerns about the nation's financial exposure to potential oil spills. Critics argue that the Guyanese government and EPA are prioritizing oil revenue over environmental protection and the public interest.

title: As San Miguel Corp posts bumper profits, Filipino communities demand end to its fossil fuel financing
summary: Ahead of San Miguel Corporation's annual stockholder's meeting, fisherfolk and farmer groups are urging the conglomerate to stop its fossil fuel investments, despite the company posting record profits in 2022. They argue that SMC's energy arm, SMC Global Power, is a major coal financier whose operations harm health and the environment, and warn shareholders of the financial risks associated with continued fossil fuel reliance amid global supply volatility and depletion of domestic gas reserves.

title: A corrida entre Brasil, China, EUA e países da Europa para explorar ‘novo pré-sal’
summary: Petroleum companies from seven countries are investing in the exploration of the "Equatorial Margin," a region between the coast of Rio Grande do Norte and Amapá in Brazil, which the Minister of Mines and Energy calls the "new pre-salt." This region is believed to hold significant oil and natural gas reserves, potentially comparable to those found in Guyana, Suriname, and Africa. The exploration faces environmental challenges, as seen with Ibama's denial of a license for Petrobras to drill in the Foz do Amazonas basin, sparking a debate within the Brazilian government.

title: iShares Global Energy ETF Review and Aggregate Rating (IXC)
